text:
I somehow misplaced the USB dongle for my Logitech K350 keyboard. Funny because I put a note on the original box which aparently reminds me of where the original actually is, but I can't read my own writing! This replacement worked fine and it will also accept certain models of their wireless mice. Carrying the Unifying certification, I would think it would work with all their USB input products, as well as those of other manufacturer's. It's not mentioned in the instructions but I would be interested in knowing.

BTW a warning. Windows 10 update has affected some systems; the keyboards have slow response. You litterally have to hold a key down for some 3-5 seconds before you get a response. I spent time researching this and apparently the most likely cause has to do with the EASE OF ACCESS section of your Control Panel. If you don't use the fully itemized version of Control Panel, select Control Panel and then from the old, normal control panel screen, go up to the file name and click the right arrow or down arrow that follows "Control Panel." If there is no arrow next to the name, just click on the name Control Panel at top and one will appear. Then select All Control Panel Items. You will now see a list of some 25 individual items rather than the old screen which has about six main categories. Now select Ease of Access, then "Make Keyboard Easier to Use." You will find a category regarding Filter Keys. It will read Turn On Filter Keys. If it is checked as being ON, uncheck the box. You don't want the filter keys on because that is the usual problem of having the slow response from the keyboard. Oh, one warning. Hit Apply. I forgot to and wasted another half hour trying to find a solution in the Registry which didn't work. I went back to Ease of Access and found the filters still being checked as ON. After trying three wired keyboards and one wireless without success, this was quite a good feeling!! If this isn't your problem, and you've already replugged in your USB cable, you are probably going to end up in the registry which is a place of last resort. I have no idea how the filter key got turned on but there is a suggestion that it may have to do with a Windows update. This seems to go back to Windows 7, but I have had Windows 10 for more than a year.

title: Remote works but the button/screen layout is horrible
text:
I have been a Logitech Harmony user for nearly a decade now and this is the first time I've ever been unhappy with a remote. My most recent remote had a bulging battery and wasn't holding much of a charge anymore so Logitech sent me an Ultimate One as a replacement even though it was far out of warranty. (I couldn't just replace the battery since it was bulging and stuck in the remote.) The Ultimate One remote itself works just fine once it is configured, but there are plenty of things that I still don't like about the remote.

I have problems getting the MyHarmony software to work at all most of the time and I'm not really sure what I've done to get it to work the few times it has worked. It usually just sits there on the splash screen on the computer and doesn't do anything. Once I got the remote configured it works but the button layout is atrocious. Once in the software, I feel like this newer software isn't as easy to configure as the older version that I used in the past.

The way the remote sits naturally in your hand, the most accessible part of the remote is the touch screen which is also the most useless part of the remote since you have to look at it to do anything. I like having the screen there when I need it, but nearly everything I use the remote for can be done via the physical buttons. The only well positioned buttons are the directional pad, ok, volume, channel, and menu. The exit button is ok too but I'd rather have something more useful in that spot like previous channel. The fast forward, play/pause, and rewind buttons are what I probably use the most with my DVR recordings and you have to hold the remote in a weird way bridging the gap over the LCD screen while making sure to not hit the LCD screen at all. The info and previous channel buttons near the very bottom are the worst positioned buttons though since they are near the very bottom of the remote and you have to be careful not to drop the remote when going for either of those buttons.

I don't really miss the number pad that much like I thought I would but Logitech should have made it feel more natural to hold the remote at the very bottom by putting the battery bump right at the very bottom. They also needed to leave the LCD panel at the very top of the remote with just the power button above it and the other more used buttons all below the screen. I am going to continue using the remote since I don't want to spend the money on replacing it but you can bet on the fact that next time I need to replace my remote I will be looking at other brands if Logitech hasn't vastly improved the button layout on their remotes by that time.

title: Been using this for 4 years - works well. Recommended. Although one keyboard had a sporadic delay problem, the other does not
text:
Keyboard #2 of this model for me. I purchased it 4 years after the first keyboard. Overall, I give this keyboard model 4 stars because the first keyboard had the sporadic keypress delay problem that others have mentioned.

But the feel, ergonomics, operation and battery life is good and the delay problem was only a minor annoyance. I used the first keyboard with the sporadic problems for 4 years for personal and work use. I can definitely recommend this keyboard now that the second one does not have the delay problem. The problem started from day one so you know if you have the problem right away or not, and it never goes away without bringing the receiver much closer the the keyboard.

The delay problem happened sporadically a few times a day, everyday for four years. When I was typing, there would be no response for a 3 seconds and afterwards the typed letters would appear, sometimes a few letters would be duplicated, sometimes the first letter of the group would be missing. My first keyboard was still working fine, except for than that delay problem, so I'm donating it instead of recycling it.

It seems the problem was the distance of the keyboard from the receiver. The solution I found on the web was to keep the receiver 3 feet or less from the keyboard which did work temporarily. But my computer is 7 feet away from the keyboard and is under another desk so I can't keep the receiver that close to the keyboard permanently. The included USB extender helped quite a bit which I held three feet up a wall with masking tape to have better line-of-sight with the keyboard. My mouse also had unresponsive problems but that happened only a few times a month instead of a few times a day like the keyboard.

The delay problem was annoying but obviously not enough to get a replacement from the manufacturer or buy another keyboard right away. I had previously used a Microsoft Natural keyboard but I like the price on this Logitech as well as the non-split keyboard layout.

title: The good and the mediocre and the not-so-great
text:
I travel by motorcycle a lot and carrying a small laptop has a few problems: the computer gets abused by the travel, laptop keyboards suck (especially small laptops), and my tent and a lot of motels don't really provide a work surface. So, I've carried a wireless Logitech, USB adapters, and my Android tablet for a year or so.

When I discovered this keyboard, I thought I'd solved "The Problem." Mostly, that's true. The keyboard is designed for typists, which means it does NOT have backlighting but it does have clear ID for the F and J keys. The keys are spaced nicely, too. There is no pad, trackball, or mouse, but that's no real problem with a touch screen tablet.

For some reason, Android programs are marginally compatible with the keyboard, though. For example, Google's Blogger editor does not recognize the keyboard's arrow keys. Cut and paste does not work between many of the programs, which really sucks. Since I do a fair amount of blogging on the road, the work-around is a pain-in-the-ass. I almost feel like there should be a driver for Android tablets.

The Bluetooth function works flawlessly, even for an old dude who has never fooled with Bluetooth on anything. I even yanked the Bluetooth adapter from my car stereo. Some people bitch about the rotary switch for swapping between devices, but I can't see that as a real problem.The keyboard works fine on MacBook Pro, (relatively, since Macs aren't really designed for keyboard operation).

The rubberized slot for holding the phone/tablet is beautifully designed. You can work on your lap, on a desk, on the ground, or whatever works for you. The device stays in place until you intentionally remove it.

As a Windows keyboard, it is Logitech excellent. I'm on Win 11 and as you'd expect it works fine and predictably. My current Windows laptop is an HP and HP has decided to copy the Apple anti-keyboard operating standard, so having a decent Bluetooth keyboard to use when I actually want to write something is wonderful.

title: An excellent mouse at an excellent price

This mouse is awesome. It works on any surface I throw at it, battery life is excellent, and the built-in bluetooth support is flawless. I especially love that the charging port is on the front of the mouse, so you can plug in a micro USB charging cable and continue using the mouse normally while it charges (where the retarded Apple Magic Mouse 2 I was using has a charging port on the _bottom_ of the mouse, rendering it useless while charging).

It's an especially nice touch that Logitech also includes a USB RF dongle, in case the device with which you're using the mouse doesn't have native bluetooth support. The thumb-rest area has an almost hidden button that lies directly beneath your thumb; just apply a little downward pressure and the button gives a subtle, yet satisfying click. I also like the little thumb-accessible scroll-wheel for horizontal scrolling, but the two smallish buttons nestled behind the scroller take a little getting used to.

THERE IS A TOUCHPAD ON THIS DEVICE WITH TWO ADDITIONAL MEANS BY WHICH TO MAKE THAT OCCUR???!?!?! You must have been the same crew that put case badges on your machines and expected them to go faster.

All in all, it just lacks focus. Fix the items I mentioned, included just opening up that touchpad to the full range available by Win10, and you might be ok. As it is, it's kinda crappy. title: Small handed individual who had to return the mouse.
text:
First impressions were mixed when I bought this mouse. I liked it but it was a little large for my hands (I'm half Korean and my hands are smaller than the average American male hand size). This mouse is chocked full of features. It is the first mouse I ever owned with adjustable weights. I learned very quickly that I prefer my mouse as light as possible (just received a Rat 3 and that thing is perfect weight wise for me by comparison - if you haven't felt one, it weighs almost nothing). Dpi buttons are in a terrible spot... they are a little too easy to access. Changing dpi accidently is super easy and of you let someone else use it like I was a few times. Be ready to fix your dpi settings. Dpi shift button I could see useful it I played fps games.

Also the mouse by default does not have a default dpi button set. As I mentioned it's really easy to accidently change dpi so default dpi button is necessary.

One of Logitechs greatest creations is their super easy to use gaming software (crushes my beloved cs storm mouse software) so it's really easy to set a button to default dpi. This fact is why I keep trying to go back to Logitech mice for so long even though I haven't found one in their catalog that fits my small hands.

The scroll wheel was the best I've ever used on any mouse. Very responsive and easy to use. Lot of things made me want to love the mouse. I put like 100 hours into Darkest Dungeon and was like, "Okay I'm keeping it." Then I played one game of League of Legends (much faster paced game) and before the game even ended I had finally officially made up my mind... the Proteus Spectrum was going back...

So in conclusion. I am sad because I had to return this. If it was a little less pricey I would have kept it and kept it for slower games (mmos Diablo, stuff like that) and used my Xornet II or Rat for stuff I need to be quicker on. If this mouse fits you (which it wasn't uncomfortable until I played a much faster paced game) I do highly recommend this mouse along with anything Logitech (their customer service has always been amazing in my experience/awesome software/can find it on local store shelves if you're into that kind of thing/etc.) But for the people with small hands such as myself I don't recommend it if you play fps/rts/mobas. It was awesome for browsing the web or any non gaming thing or like super chill gaming stuff like Darkest Dungeon (game is turn based if you've never heard of it).

title: The best mouse I ever used was my first Revolution
text:
The best mouse I ever used was my first Revolution. It eventually died, and the Performance MX that replaced it was NOT its equal. Yes, it had standardized charging (the Revo used a cradle) and yes, it had the unifying receiver (Revo had the weird giant dongle) but everything else about it was inferior. Not bad, mind you - still better than most devices - but just not as good.

All that changes with the MX Master. The design is great - I wasn't a fan of the Anywhere MX 2, which is this same redesign. It felt lighter than its predecessor and lower to the table which was uncomfortable. This one has none of those problems. I can sync it with three devices using Bluetooth, OR use the unifying receiver. It has enough functions (zoom, scroll, forward and back, window toggle) to be useful without being distracting (gaming mice, I'm looking at you here). Tracks smoothly, feels weighty but not too heavy. Lasts a long time on a charge.

All in all a heck of a mouse for the money.

Pros:
- This mouse is solid, heavy (due to the AA batteries) and decently curved for my hand.
- The darkfield laser works on any surface.
- Unifying receiver means it can be paired with my other Logitech stuff.
- I really love the fact that you don't have to find some tiny switch to turn it on, you just flip it over and slide the nice chunky slider with your thumb. If the aperture is open, the mouse is on.
- Comes with a cute carry bag.

Cons:
- Requires Logitech SetPoint software, which is always a crapshoot.
- This mouse was redesigned and has a shiny surface instead of the matte surface it shipped with from 2011-2013. The shiny is inferior and picks up oil and fingerprints more readily, but mostly that's an aesthetic consideration.
- The button will fail, just like every other Logitech mouse from the last 6 years, in a spectacular "double click of doom" manner.
- Odd placement of holder for receiver INSIDE the battery compartment. Not sure why this is even here, you don't want to take the battery cover off all the time, it will wear out.
- I wish this had the automatic/programmable clutch like the other mice from this generation, or even the "click the button under the wheel to release the clutch". Instead it has the "click the wheel down hard to release the clutch" design, which is not great.

title: Best mouse for my desktop needs.
text:
I love this mouse. The MX mice from Logitech have always been great, this is no exception.

I originally was going to get the MX Master, which is the latest (as of this writing - Q1 2016) iteration of the mouse, but after trying one out at Best Buy I decided to get last year's model.

Pros:
- Fits my moderately large hands REALLY well.
- Unified adapter. These things are super useful and interchangeable and reprogrammable, so that's awesome. No more separate dongle.
- Darkfield laser, pretty much works on any surface.
- The "all windows" button is more useful than you think.
- I really like the automatic clutch. That's programmable and can be disabled if you hate it.
- More rechargeable than previous models.

Cons:
- Logitech's software is always pretty questionable, and nowadays pretty much mandatory. Sometimes you can get a Logitech mouse and not need Setpoint, or Logitech Preferences, or whatever they are calling it now. Not so much here. My biggest gripe with Setpoint is that the scrolling acceleration profile never seems as nice as the Microsoft or Apple defaults.
- It will die a horrible "clicks register as double clicks" death just like every other Logitech mouse made between 2011 and 2015. It's a design flaw.
- Kind of bulky to tote around. This is definitely a desktop mouse. That's ok, I have the Anywhere MX for my laptop.

title: Reminds me of the legendary old Microsoft red ball trackball mouse.
text:
I use to have Microsoft trackball back in the late 90's. It was a way for me to get use to a new way of working. I absolutely adored that mouse. It only took me a week to figure out how to use it, and I can honestly say that I worked better with that then a regular ball mouse at that time. I honestly don't know why I stopped using that trackball mouse. I think I might of dropped it one too many times, or moved and lost the ball. Or maybe I got on the whole optical mouse train.

Well, I purchase this for my cheapest laptop that I have. For just browsing things. I missed using it. I missed not having a wrist that hurt after using it. And let me tell you, as much doubt I had about this unit, I am in love with this thing. I have gone through basically all of the mouse types over the years. The trigger kind, 15 button gaming laser mouse, adjustable mouse, presentation mouse, and I think this is the mouse for me.

Ergonomically, it's beautifully crafted. Although the ball rolled little rough at the beginning, which worried me from the get go, I knew eventually my man oil will smooth things out with the ball.

Overall, this is an excellent trackball mouse. The rubber grip on the bottom is solid, where on any solid surface or even my leg, it holds nicely.

The only thing that I want is to program the top left two buttons, so one can be an "Enter" button, instead of it having it permanently left or right page scroll.

I can say, this thing is built very well as well. I dropped it about 10 times so far, and nothing broke yet. Everything is working perfectly. The range is also very good too. I can use it about 20 feet away.

title: Makes life easier
text:
I love this logitech keyboard. I gave it 4 stars for a couple of reasons, but in general, it has made my life easier, which was what I had hoped for.
We have a tablet, but no laptop, so I ordered this to make typing easier in conjunction with my tablet. It is extremely simple to set up. I use a Samsung tablet and the only things I had to do to connect the keyboard to my tablet is search for the bluetooth device with my tablet and hold in the top right keyboard button that is labeled "PC (Android, Windows, Chrome OS)". My tablet recognized the keyboard right away, and I was all set to type. This device allows me to connect up to three devices at a time (such as cell phones, other tablet, etc..), but I have only been using it with my tablet.

I read some reviews complaining about the keys being difficult to push. To me, this keyboard is really comfortable - the keys feel just like those on a regular desktop keyboard. It is powered by battery and there is an on/off switch underneath the keyboard.

My only complaints are the following: I wish there were a usb charging port so that I could charge my tablet while I am using the keyboard, but there is not one. Also, the slot where my tablet rests (or where any device would be placed) - the flourescent green/yellow part, is a little wide. My tablet almost leans back too much so that it is difficult to see. I wish there were some type of rubber in the middle to allow different devices to fit and also hold the device straight up. Lastly, I may have a defective keyboard, but the battery cover keeps sliding off. It really isn't a big deal, because I just slide it back on, but I am really not sure why it is doing this since the keyboard is not very old.

Overall, I do definitely recommend this item to those looking for a keyboard to use in conjunction with their tablet. You can't beat it for the price, and it does the job well.

title: Get your wallet out and pay for better speakers
text:
I love Logitech and their products. I have 5.1 speakers that are great, my previous speakers were 2.1 but way better than these, a couple wireless mice, a game controller that I have had since like 2006 that still works, and I'm sure I'm forgetting something. The price was so low that normally I would be skeptical, but I thought "But it's Logitech, they have to be good :-D"

Nope.

I can tell you that these speakers suck. There is no volume control on one speaker like most speakers but on that stupid little hand-held thing. The maximum volume is very low. I bought these with an adapter to plug in my grandfather's TV because the TV speakers sound terrible and he can't hear well, and I'm not paying $100+ for a soundbar like a sucker. The speakers were NO LOUDER than the TV speakers, only sounded better. I ended up plugging them into the cable box directly. Same thing, no better.

The cable box was set to 75% volume with no way to change it (Comcast is awful), aside from calling customer "support" and wading through hordes of idiots with scripted dialogue until finally getting on the phone with someone who could tell me the 5 buttons to push to make it happen. Once I got it the volume up, it was sufficient for my grandfather, but still only slightly louder than originally.

The wires are so short that the subwoofer and the speakers had to stay on the bottom on either side of the cable box. Pretty unacceptable.

Bottom line is I would have paid an extra $10-20 more to save myself from 1-2 hours of frustration. You are letting me down, Logitech. If you want to add some ambiance to your bathroom with a speaker setup on top of the back of your toilet, I suppose these speakers would do. Otherwise, get something better.

I had also been concerned that it might be rather complicated to learn to use the new remote, but at the end of the second night, I was pressing all the buttons like a pro and navigating the television set, the DVR, and the DVD player like I had been doing it for months.

If you are nervous about this being complicated or difficult, don't be! Highly recommend this awesome little remote control.

title: Good in some areas, falls short in others.
text:
The high points of this product are decent sound, comfort, and a fairly long battery life. The lows include microphone sound quality, its implementation of phone audio, and its frequent disconnection.

I'll explain the lows in some detail. Microphone quality is similar to other gaming headsets, which is mix of often too low and muddy. It's easy to chalk it up as being a gaming headset, but it's an expensive gaming headset. Its phone connection is a 3.5mm 2 way wire with a potentiometer to control volume. It only works with both microphone and audio if it's plugged directly into the headset. Also, while the cable works plugged directly into the USB dongle, only audio is transmitted. That means your phone will still register as having a microphone connected. Connected directly to the phone, audio is okay. Occasionally, I'll have to repeat something because it wasn't heard well on the other end. The quality of the phone will also effect the quality of calls. I have an HTC One M9, and audio is decent with other devices. In short, its phone implentation could use some work. Including the option to plug the phone directly into the USB dongle, or adding bluetooth to the dongle/headset would be better.

Last, I'll include the disconnections. I somewhat expect this from a wireless device, and left to go in sleep mode sometimes it will sometimes unpair. This wouldn't be a problem if the USB dongle had an ordinary pairing button. Instead you have to use a pin and plug it into a tiny hole is in the USB dongle. When on, the device will usually maintain a good connection. That leaves the user with two options to prevent unpairing. The first option is to disable sleep mode, which will cause the headset to drain at the same rate as receiving continuous audio (8-13 hours instead of days), or the option of keeping a pin nearby for unpairing events.

In short, this would be a 4 star item if Logitech had an ordinary pairing button and a way to receive microphone information from the phone that was truly wireless (either Bluetooth or connecting the 3.5mm jack to the USB dongle). I would make it a 5 star item if the microphone was superior to other gaming headsets. It's certainly not the worst microphone I have ever used, but it is on-par with other gaming headsets I have used from Logitech and Creative.

For those times I want to kick back and listen to music, watch a video on my PC, or game solo, this product is amazing. It does fall short in other areas. An updated USB dongle with a pairing button (not a hole), and ability to receive audio from the phone would be ideal. Dedicated call buttons, bluetooth, and better microphone would require a more extensive upgrade, but Logitech should consider these options in their next model.

title: Literally The Worst Thing I've Ever Bought
text:
I hate this thing so much. It's been nothing but trouble and I'm still using it because I basically have to.

So I bought it because it's supposedly compatible with Photoshop and other Adobe applications. That's not strictly true, though - you actually have to download and install Logitech Options, a free program which reads the mouse inputs and then issues commands to the programs. IT sounds great, like a programmable mouse that'll do anything, right? No way, not a chance. This thing works wirelessly and it's constantly jittery for no reason. I have an amazing rig, I've never had a mouse stutter before, let alone one this expensive. Also, despite what the website says, it's NOT Win10-friendly. It works the same as any other plug-and-play mouse, which defeats the purpose of buying this particular model and spending this much money.

Specifically, when I try to use it with Photoshop, half the time it doesn't recognize commands until I force-close and re-open Logitech Options, and even then it only works for about twenty minutes before I have to do it again. Occasionally, it doesn't work even after that, in those cases it makes the "zoom" and "pan" functions so glitchy that Photoshop crashes. At least once (but typically multiple times) every day, it loses total connectivity with the PC. What I mean by that is that the cursor begins skipping in a time-delayed manner when I move it, as though the movement is "loading" in bursts or something, a characteristic of shoddy wireless connection. It's not a rig issue, I have an absurd amount of RAM, an excellent graphics card, and a fantastic processor, and no other mouse has ever had this issue. Only this one. The issue becomes slightly less frequent when I leave the mouse plugged into the computer (the charging method), but I have confirmed that it doesn't form a wired connection this way. The improvement may be psychosomatic, I might be clutching at straws.

The real kick in the teeth, though, is Logitech's customer service. When I contacted them with my multiple problems and gave them all the information they asked me to provide, they emailed me back a week later asking for the exact same information (apparently, they randomly have people respond, so the new person didn't know the original problem somehow). Then, they blamed me for not properly researching it - and when I pointed out that it says both on Amazon AND on the Logitech website that the mouse is compatible with Adobe programs and Windows 10, they told me I could just use it like a regular mouse without the additional functionality I paid for. As if that weren't enough, they've been emailing me for months since the purchase asking "if my customer support experience was satisfactory" and "if my issue was resolved" - I made the mistake of replying the first time, I got sent back through the same cycle of being treated like an imbecile and eventually just shut down, and then when I asked to never be contacted again I was told they would open a support ticket to help me with that issue. As in, they opened a support ticket to address me wanting to never talk to their support crew again.

Seriously, give this piece of garbage a miss and if you know anyone who has one, take it from them and destroy it.

title: Best remote ever!
text: It's been about 6 months since I purchased this remote. I held back on writing a review because I really wanted to see how it held up through daily continuous use.  Well, the jury is out now and I absolutely love it!  It was extremely easy to program.  I just connected it to my desktop with a simple USB chord and entered in all my devices by brand and model.  If you're using a amp/receiver that all your devices plug into for sound, you will need to have a little knowledge on how you're inputting them; the same goes for your television.  Have this information handy, and when you go through the programming app for your remote, the app will navigate you through all the necessary steps, easy as pie!  I didn't have to memorize or search for any device codes or go through a whole sequence of button pushing.  Literally, it took me less than 5 minutes to program the remote.  After the first month, I did have some issues.  The remote would still light up, but the button functions stopped working.  It happened very spontaneously...at one moment everything was fine, and the next moment, it just totally stopped working.  When I tested the batteries, they seemed like they still about a 70% charge on them, so I ruled that out.  I tried reprogramming the remote several times, but still did not have much success. Finally, on a whim, I put a fresh set of batteries in it, and VOILA!  the remote began working again. I felt like 1 month was a pretty short time for batteries to go out, and for the remote not to be able to operate well on a 70% charge.  I was able to tweak the remote's power usage by changing the LCD light setting.  I think the default was set so the light automatically shut off after the remote has been set down for between 20-30 seconds.  I changed the setting so that it would automatically shut down after 10 seconds.  This change has greatly increased the battery capacity and life.  It's now been close to 4 months since i put in that 2nd set of batteries and the remote is still going strong.  Overall, this remote is pretty great.  Even my wife can use it without too much confusion.  I would highly recommend this remote to anyone tired of shuffling between multiple remotes in their home.  Life is so much better and easier now!

The Logitech Wireless Touch Keyboard K400 Plus is a good wireless keyboard for your TV-connected computer, Raspberry Pi, or Alienware gaming system... but it's not perfect.

The process was fairly easy, I guess, but I had to exchange emails back and forth with them several times before they shipped the replacement. I guess it happens sometimes, but Logitech was quick to send a replacement out.

The keyboard itself is a little flimsy feeling, but you get what you pay for... it's only $30 currently on Amazon. The trackpad is very responsive and worked really well, but the keys were a little spongy for my tastes. Still, it works pretty well for the price. I didn't notice any lag when pressing keys quickly, as I have with other wireless keyboards.

Overall, the Logitech Wireless Touch Keyboard K400 Plus is a good wireless keyboard for your TV-connected device.

Very nice and much better than my old Logitech Harmony 700 that was IR-based. No more exact pointing and aiming at the TV/FiOS box/Receiver/DVD player to turn things on or off. This new remote is much more forgiving of bad aim but will occasionally still get out of sync. That's the only negative about this remote because when things go out of sync, you need to load up the app on your smartphone and fix it from there; there is no screen on the remote. Other than this minor inconvenience, this remote works great and can even be controlled over the Internet. I turned on the TV from out of state one time and scared the crap out of my wife and daughter. Good times.

It's also important to note that this remote comes with 2 components: the remote itself and a small powered 'base station'. You do need to keep the base station within line-of-sight to your devices (in other words, not behind them), and it needs to be close to a power outlet. I'm not sure about the max range, but I keep mine about 15 ft away and 30 degrees to the side of my devices.

title: Much better solution for PC gaming than the other controllers out there.
text:
While I love gaming on my PC, I hate using the keyboard/mouse. I played on consoles for many years and this controller suits me better. The only reason I gave this controller 4 stars is due to Logitech not offering any driver support for Windows 10. I have found that if you just use the drivers for Windows 7, it will work just fine. Just go to the actual Microsoft website and download the XBOX 360 driver. After installing the new driver, plug in your usb sensor/dongle whatever it's called and then you will need to open up Device Manager and confirm that your computer recognizes it. It should list "Xbox 360 Peripherals". If not, don't worry, there is a crude workaround: unplug the usb sensor, then flip the switch on the controller to "D" and plug the the sensor back in. Wait a second, then unplug the sensor again, only this time flip the switch on the controller back to "X" before re-inserting the usb sensor. Go ahead and re-insert the sensor again and it should show up as "xbox 360 peripherals" this time. If not unplug the usb sensor and re-insert a few more times. It will eventually show up and you'll be good to go. It sounds like a bit of a hassle but it takes less than minute to get it working. It's a minor inconvenience but worth it if you like having a functioning controller that works with most games. Hopefully Logitech will offer a fix for this in the future or at least offer a newer, more windows friendly controller for us to use.

I even use this controller to play all my Steam games because I absolutely hate my Steam controller with a passion. For Steam games, I found that using big picture mode to setup the controller works with like 98% of the games I play...even the ones not designed for controller support. Here's how to do that: Go to Big Picture Mode and find the game you want to play in your library, then click the following: Manage Games---> Configure Controller---> Browse Configs----> Templates---> then select "Gamepad". That's it, you're all set. Enjoy your games! You can even use the community settings under templates to find a setup that suits your style if you wish, but I found that just the plain 'ol Gamepad settings works fine for me.

Strange Humming - It starts for no reason and continues to get louder until you can't hear anything but the humming. After turning them off and on a few times, sometimes the humming goes away.
The annoying power off - Nothing more annoying than putting headset on to realize it's decided to power off for no apparent reason. To power them on you have to hold the power button down for an unknown amount of time. (You may be thinking he owns 4 of them how does he not know how long he should hold the power button down?) Easy, it's different every time. Sometimes it turns itself back off, sometimes it hangs as it powers up sometimes they come right on.
The mute light - one cool feature is there is a red light to tell you the microphone is muted. Unfortunately it has a mind of its own. Sometimes it's on when it's not muted and vice versa.
Cracked Head band - so far only 2 of these have cracked but they crack. The design is awkward and soon you may have a dangling ear muff as it breaks itself off.
USB only - not a flaw just a pain. With it requiring a usb port there is no listening to music on your phone.
Charging - 3 out of my 4 headsets have never fully charged. At least the charge light has never turned green like it did on the 4th headset.
7.1 Surround sound - this is virtual surround sound. Which means it's not actually surround sound. I wish they'd spelled that out as it was a big factor in my initial decision to go down this road.

Summary:
I buy a lot of Logitech products and love them, This was not one of them. No matter how cheap the price goes on this I'd say clear.

P.S. I have sent these back to Logitech, the wait was so long I ended up buying spare headsets because it took so long. This is why I have 4 terrible headsets.

title: Was pretty easy to setup but there are a lot of ...
text:
Bought to control my TV/AppleTV/FireTV etc. Was pretty easy to setup but there are a lot of little problems that make using the thing problematic. If you try to do any voice control of the Apple TV (4th Gen) for example it will automatically press your enter whenever it receives a command. If you have an app selected it will open, if you have something paused it will start playing, very bad integration here. I was also getting a "that device doesn't work on Fire TV" error when I would try to turn my Fire TV on. Sometimes when I give a command Alexa says "That command does not work on device (name)," despite it working correctly. If I want to actually use the Harmony App I'm going to have to make at least 2 activities with some devices, one that just changes my AVR input that doesn't include the device itself for the Alexa Commands and one that contains the device so I can actually control it from the App. Seems to just be a lot of bugs and bad control in the Harmony/Alexa integration front.

Discovering devices on your Alexa App adds some of the activities you have listed in the Harmony App, but not all of them. Can't get a generic On/Off to be recognized by Alexa for example. Additional names for all your activities are also added which is quite annoying. I didn't want these "automatic names" as they seem to get confused with each other. Every time you discover devices they are added again. Some of the automatic commands that were added would turn devices off but were not recognized to turn them on, others just didn't work. For a device designed to make control of your entertainment center easier these "automatic" devices just cause a headache and defeat the whole purpose.

Voice commands also only work for turning devices on/off, that is mostly what I was after but having pause/play functionality would be nice and I'm hoping it gets added in the future.

Edit - They've added a 2nd Alexa skill which now allows more voice commands including volume control.

title: You've Found Your New Headset
text:
9/30/16
This headset is without a doubt, the s***. It is the best headset I've ever owned, and over the past 20 years between gaming and mobile devices and work, I have owned A LOT of headsets. This is the first wireless one, and the last wireless one, unless Logitech manages to trump themselves and make an even better headset down the road.

Set up on this is basically non-existent. Plug in the wireless receiver, turn the headset on. If you already have Logitech gaming software installed, which you do if you're already using one of their other excellent products like mouse or keyboard, the installation is already done. The only thing you'll ever have to do is connect using the included mini-usb cable to install a firmware update. Obviously, in the future, you'll have to charge the headset, which is effortless if you have USB 3.1s because they quick charge.

7.1 surround is a gimmick without an actual 7.1 speaker setup, but this headset reproduces the effect very well. It's excellent for watching movies or playing games - especially first person shooters - where sound is extremely important to the experience. Music is also wonderful on this headset, and the equalizer included with the software does a sufficient job of letting you tweak. The only reason I say sufficient is because there aren't default sound profiles built in for music, but that's no problem.

Again the software allows you to create custom profiles and switch between them, so you can literally make a different sound profile for every game you have,or make one for games, one for movies/tv, and one for music, etc. In addition to this, you can program buttons on the headset, although I haven't found any purpose yet for them. You can also turn the, honestly, needless lighting off completely - although it seems to always revert back to being on when you power the headset on after turning it off. Turning the lighting off nearly doubles the battery life. On that note, the battery has a compartment on the right ear and it can be easily disconnected if you ever end up needing to replace it because it loses capacitance in the future, though I can't vouch yet for whether or not Logitech covers this.

In the days I've had this headset, I've kept it on my head as much as possible. The earphones are comfortable enough that you will actually forget you're wearing them after a while - unless you just seriously don't like clamshell type sets. I have had some issues with the headset where it will desync/unpair with the computer if it stays on without playing sound for a certain period of time, but this was easily solved by just unplugging the USB receive and plugging it back in.

As someone who always used wired headsets and always broke them - almost always unintentionally - I couldn't be happier with this purchase, even at the normally steep price of $200. I got it for $139.99, and you can find it refurbished for about $120. Now I'm sad because I want one for work and there's no way I'm bringing mine or paying for a new one, yet.

*Update* 10/16/16
HOWEVER, after weeks with this headset, I would honestly tell you not to buy it. It is a constant pain in the ass. The drivers never work correctly on Windows 10, for sure. Literally every time I turn the headset off and turn it back on, the Logitech gaming utility doesn't recognize it - it thinks the headset is on sleep. The wireless receiver has to be removed, and plugged back in, and the power cycled on the headset. On top of this, the built in profiles literally never work. The second you re-sync the headset, it defaults back to factory settings meaning it turns the lights on. It's impossible to know whether they're on if the headset is on your head - where headsets go - without checking the utility. Even after you turn the lights off, if you X out of the Logitech Gaming Software GUI, it instantly reverts back to the default. It is so infuriating dealing with this product. I think it's probably worth it, but a lot of people are a lot less willing to deal with bullcrap than I am.

Update 1/19/17

While I don't feel anything I've already said needs to be rescinded, it's been almost 4 months and I have to say this headset isn''t holding up well. I've taken to just plugging it in rather than using wireless but even so, I do drain the battery and recharge it properly. I have never dropped the headset or damaged it in any way. Now, however, it just cuts out at random. It doesn't matter what the audio source is, local or network. The wireles receiver no longer has any range. I can't even go 20 feet now without the sound cutting out. I used to be able to go outside, now if I do - the headset completely stops receiving signal.

It's still a great headset but buy at your own risk and make sure you keep the receipt, as there is at least a 2 year warranty.

text:
I just picked this up from Best Buy, because amazon didn't have it available.

Anyway, I've never had more trouble with an electronic gadget than I'm having setting up this Hub. For reference, I've had to different harmony remotes in the past and set them up just fine. I got this Hub because I wanted to try to pair it with an Echo Dot to try controlling my Home Theater with Alexa.

Anyway, I've been trying to set up the Hub for over 2 hours and have run into failures almost every step of the way.

1) Using the iOS app, the hub sync fails 100% of the time, so the set up won't finish.

2) When I try to finish the set up on the desktop app (tried on a PC and a Mac), I can't even open the hub's settings. it just keeps spinning on a blue dot wheel.

3) I can't even look online for help because all logitech support pages are apparently broken now (just says "page not found").

4) The manual does not say how to do a factory reset, although I tried pressing and holding the pair/reset button, but it didn't seem to do anything.

5) Now I gave up on setting up the Hub as a new device, and am trying to pair it with my current harmony touch remote. The desktop app goes through the process, but it keeps failing on downloading my account info. Then it says to disconnect the remote's USB cable for a few seconds and try again. Tried that about a dozen times with different USB cables, but it always fails.

I am SO frustrated right now, I've never encountered any consumer electronics device so apparently broken, especially one that has been on the market a long time. I am honestly in disbelief it's so bad.

title: Nice keyboard, some safety/sanity concerns.
text:
[[VIDEOID:a571d5611cd57584cf51fa1103e6f8f7]] Do y'all remember when Logitech iPad keyboards weren't the literal worst? I sure do!

I use my iPad a lot. I bring it to meetings at work in lieu of lugging my laptop and I use it at home, too. I bring my iPad all over the place with me - meetings, waiting rooms, the couch, my bed, etc. Because I use it so much for work and writing, a keyboard is pretty much a necessity for me. While an iPad will never replace a computer for me like some hopeful tech enthusiasts like to claim, a keyboard sure does get it close.

Here are the pros about this keyboard:
- Quiet keys (for real, I had an Anker one that, while being significantly less expensive and more sturdy, made a ruckus I didn't appreciate when I was trying to surreptitiously tweet about Chris Evans on Twitter during meetings).
- Dedicated keys to bring up search, keyboard, take a screenshot, show your apps.

Cons:
- WHY. Why on EARTH did you do this to what was previously an amazing keyboard?
- Remember when these keyboards used to have nice magnetic bars that wrapped around your iPad, creating a low-profile juncture between your keyboard and your iPad? Remember how the magnet would very easily snap into place? If you've ever wished that joining your keyboard to your iPad was a much more delicate, precise, and unforgiving process, I've got great news! Half the time the magnetic bar on this new one doesn't even notice you're sliding your iPad up to it. Sure, you can't easily flick the magnet on it like the last one when it doesn't work, but you CAN exercise your fine motor skills every time you go to pack up.
- When it does work as intended and raises up to snap around the magnetic edge of your device, it has the handy feature of also acting like a weapon. Why, you ask? Well, because instead of being a nice, rounded bar that hugs the edge of your iPad, it comes to a bizarre rest at a diagonal angle to the side of your iPad and features a razor-sharp edge that is sure to absolutely wreck anyone you pass in the hallway. If your 2016 work goals include: Be able to defend myself against attackers with basic office supplies, this is the keyboard for you. Sure, you may get fired for slicing your coworkers flesh straight down to the bone with your keyboard/katana, but hey! At least this design makes absolutely no sense at all, so you can seem really edgy and mysterious.
- With past bluetooth keyboards, you may have had an issue with the angle that your iPad sits in the cradle. Logitech addressed this by making the cradle adjustable. This sounds like a great idea, until you realize that the new starting angle is about a half an inch further tilted away from you than the last model. No problem, because the cradle is adjustable, right? Yep, sure is. After applying an amount of brute strength that I was sure would either break my iPad screen or the keyboard, the cradle moved! It moved further away. It only tilts back. So the options on your screen angle are: further away than the old one or even more ridiculously further away. I'm including a photo that shows both the difference in starting angles and the extreme angle that the new keyboard will extend to. Who, I beg, is using their iPad at that angle? Are they anticipating users will be riding a stationary bicycle while typing meeting notes? Are they anticipating aerial acrobats will need to be able to hang from the ceiling AND use their handy keyboard to make shopping lists? I am at a loss as to why you would create an adjustable keyboard that only moves one way, and starts further away than the old one to begin with. This is only my second biggest complaint. My biggest complaint:
- THIS THING DOES NOT HOLD MY IPAD IN. There is maybe a 2mm depth of plastic holding my iPad into its cradle. On previous models, I could pick up the keyboard, tap the screen, even breathe near my iPad and it would stay snugly in its cradle. On this new model, the slightest movement causes my iPad to pop out of the cradle and slam backwards. At best, it goes sliding across the slick surface of the back side of the keyboard and onto my soft blankets, because I'm using my iPad to play Kim Kardashian Hollywood (still) and tapped too hard on a cute dress that I wanted to add to my collection. Slightly more upsetting, I sneeze in a meeting and send my iPad crashing across a conference table. I've included a handy video illustrating this absolutely ridiculous design.

I use my iPad a lot - probably more than I anticipated using it when I bought it. I use it in a variety of situations. I use it in meetings, to display recipes while I cook, to watch TV while I'm doing my makeup, to play games/write in bed. I use my keyboard as both a keyboard and a stand, because it sturdily holds it at a nice, comfortable angle. iPads are expensive, and I know that I shouldn't be manhandling it. I also know that I have owned two iPads, with at least three different keyboards (the older model of this same keyboard and an Anker), and this is the only one that is both dangerous to me (RAZOR SHARP EDGE) and to my iPad (flips out of the cradle at the slightest provocation). I want to keep purchasing Logitech keyboards, because they do offer great features and historically have been high quality. I just can't get over these positively baffling design choices.

Photo/Video descriptions:
1) Comparison of old joining mechanism vs. new (new on bottom).
2) Difference in angle of screen. New closest to the camera, further from your face because ergonomics are just quack science, right?
3) New, razor sharp edge that can be used to fight off assassins in the event that you come across assassins. Very difficult to convince to please, PLEASE pop up and grip your iPad. A fun challenge and a thrilling sense of danger to amp up your workweek.
4) Old, lovely, rounded connector with strong magnet that easily attaches.
5) The full reclining angle of the adjustable cradle. Because your iPad needs to kick back, it works really hard.
6) A video demonstrating the quick-release insanity of this new grip compared to the stability of older models. Because why would you want your keyboard to actually hang on to your very expensive device?

title: POOR Case Design - NOT worth the money or aggravation
text:
The Logitech Pro Protective Case with Full-Size Keyboard for Samsung Galaxy Note Pro and Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro is a HORRIBLE case design. And I would urge anyone thinking about getting this case, to go with something different.
I -wanted- to love this case, but it just couldn't happen. The way this case was designed was not thought out very well at all.
The only thing holding the table into this case are basically 2 side plastic clips and the 2 upper plastic corner pieces, that barely come up and over the side of the tablet, which is the reason it does such a -poor- job of holding the tablet in place. And with the heft of this particular tablet, it NEEDS the support.
I attempted to use this case for 1 month, and quickly replaced it. My tablet would pop out of the clips almost every time I went to open the case, and I was always afraid that the tablet itself would fall. It is not worth the aggravation for me to go through all the time, just to have a keyboard built in to the case. I was constantly having to make sure the tablet was still clipped under the plastic tabs, and slide the tablet back up under the other plastic corner pieces.
The keyboard itself was nice, and easy to use. The keys were nice and I liked the tactile feel of them. They placed small "bumpers" on the corners of the case so the keyboard wasn't able to rub against the screen.
Over-all, for the amount of money I paid for this case, and it's now sitting in it's box in my closet...I'd say, don't waste your money, time, or aggravation. Buy another case and utilize a wireless Bluetooth keyboard / mouse.

title: Nice feel. Works right out of the box. no caps lock indicator light. puzzling icons. Only worked great for 2.5 months
text:
Im downgrading this from 4 stars to one. I purchased it Dec 2, 2016. today is February 25, 2017. Ive had it for less than 3 months.

In the beginning it charged super fast and never drained. It was amazing. However, in the past few weeks it drains in less than a day and no longer charges unless I pop it in the window. And then only charges nicely if the sun is shining.

there is no way to know when the caps lock is on or off and this is pretty critical element. My guess is that its not an oversight but a battery saving design element. after all a light on would drain the solar battery faster.

the board is super thin but doesnt feel cheap. actually feels nicer than my official thin mac keyboard which I hate because it has no numeric keypad. yes, I know you can order one. but what person in their right mind wants two pieces to a keyboard sitting on their lap board?

Because Ive used a logitech mouse for many, many, years (instead of that lame small mac mouse) I already trusted this brand.

They keyboard started up right out of the box after peeling off the right plastic bits. That parts super intuitive for getting started. The product box was also intuitive and easy to pull out the keyboard and its USB stick.

TIP: if you can find the solar app it will help you keep track of the battery usage. Unfortunately the link on the site does not take you to the solar app. I found it on the apple website. This little app is works with the puzzling icons. You press a button and if the app is installed on your computer it will tell you how much battery life is left. really did love the app. wish Id known about it out of the box instead of stumbling across it when I was looking for reasons why the keyboard is no longer charging like it used to. Apparently it takes TWO days to fully charge IF you do not use it for two days and put it in a sunny window. But I never had that problem in the beginning. And now of course...its simply drains faster than it can charge. It used to be so good it charged by lamplight!

The so called "manual" that comes with the keyboard is a tiny bit of paper with microscopic text that you can not read without a magnifying glass.

All in all I was happy with the purchase. But now that it cant keep a charge its pretty much a waste of money. Ive ordered a new NON-solar keyboard.

title: Not surprised by my disappointment.
text:
This is the second programmable remote that I've tried, pretty much without success, although this one I had professionally programmed.

To be fair, the problem is probably not the remote, but rather the expectation (or hope) that it would be possible to lose the four (and counting) remotes that control our home theater system.

The holy grail, although hardly an unwarranted expectation, would be to have one, simple remote to control all the components. But, alas, with all the various hardware offerings and an industry's reluctance to support a single standard that coordinates hardware and software, my expectation continues to be illusive.

Does this remote eliminate the need for all my separate remotes? Yes, well, sort of. The problem is that there are functions available on the individual remotes (including the hand voice recognition commands available on my Apple TV and XFinity remote) that are unavailable on the Harmony.

As a result, I usually have to push many more buttons on the Harmony Remote to produce the intended result than if I had used the dedicated remote that came with the product I'm trying to use.

And then there is the "Help" button. When all else fails, press "Help". Usually, but not always, after pressing buttons multiple times according to the instructions that appear on the remote's screen, the problem will be fixed. It's taken up to 10 minutes for success, however. And, more often than not I have to manually turn off each device and start from scratch.

This has not been particularly helpful for the health of my marriage. My wife always used to shout "Tech Support! when she couldn't get our system to play nice. When the Geek Squad arrived from Best Buy, I asked the Geek in Resident whether we could eliminate her cries by having one, programmable remote. He assured us that the Harmony remote would solve the problem.

Well, regrettably, it doesn't.

Perhaps I should be grateful that my wife still needs me to make everything work. Fortunately, I'm retired, with plenty of time on my hands.

My advice? If you don't mind mediocre sound, skip all the bells and whistles. Use the sound that comes from the TV and have a simple system that only includes a TV, a Cable box and, perhaps, a DVD or Apple TV player.

In the meantime, I continue to pine for the holy grail system that allows me to experience high quality home theater from one, intuitive remote.

A postscript. My high tech son-in-law also purchased this item a few years ago. He used it for a few months before dumping it. When the Geek from Best Buy suggested that I buy it, I thought that perhaps my son-in-law perhaps didn't know how to program the unit. But my Geek-for-Hire didn't provide a better experience, which suggests even more respect for my son-in-law.

The advantage to this Z625 is that the cords are separate from the system itself and can be replaced if necessary. The cords ARE included in this set, so you have everything you need as soon as you open it. The bass is very strong, so this system is great for music. But it works just as well for listening to podcasts, news apps, and streamed TV/movies while puttering around the house. If you want something you can move around the house, get a bluetooth device. title: Works great with iPhone and Macbook, touchy set up
text:
I can finally type documents, emails and text with ease on my iPhone. It's amazing!

***It comes with batteries so you can use it out of the box!!!***

I've tried other Bluetooth keyboards, but with little success. See, I learned to type on a typewriter 25 years ago and keyboards today have keys that are too close together, or they are so sensitive you barely click them and you suddenly have a whole line of the same letter. They are also very flimsy.

The keys on the keyboard are appropriately spaced. They click slightly - reminding me of my beloved typewriters - and are not too sensitive. The keys press down easily, but not too easily.

Those other keyboards were also very poorly made. I was shocked when I picked up the box for this unit. It was super heavy. This keyboard has some staying power and I want to make sure I have a protective case for it.

I LOVE that this has a numbers keyboard on the right side, too. I use this constantly when entering data into spreadsheets.

It took a few times to hook up to my iPhone 6 Plus, but it connected better once I propped the iPhone onto the back of the keyboard.

That is another bonus feature. There is a space to cradle your mobile device. Now, I have a case on my iPhone, so it didn't fit all the way, but I just propped up the back with my coffee cup and away I typed! Purists will want to remove the case so it nestles just so. I spill too much and would rather protect my device. It might work with other cases, thought.

I wanted to test the claims that you could switch between devices with ease with this unit. I have a Macbook Pro and plugged in the USB pin. It works with that, but it does not work with Bluetooth on a Macbook running 10.9.5.

It shut down the Bluetooth connection on my iPhone when I attempted to use Bluetooth on the Macbook, which was irritating. I tried following the diagram inside the box without success.

I did submit an email to Logitech's Vine email account, but only got a ticket number in response. The Knowledge Base did not offer any solutions, but does provide good, basic information for new users.

I am still not quite certain how the buttons set up for both the iPhone and the Macbook. They just worked, so maybe the keyboard automatically configures? Or maybe those times I was pressing the buttons down when following the diagram did something. It just started working.

When I have the USB plugged in, it does not kick off my iPhone's Bluetooth when switching devices.

I did have a few instances where I had to turn the keyboard off and one to get it to connect to Bluetooth. This is not a terrible thing, as I have had to do this with other bluetooth devices.

One item of note for quick keys - like for copy/paste and printing. For Mac users, the "alt" button servers as the Command button. It is clearly makes and works just fine for standard shortcuts on Mac products.

Overall, I love the look and feel of this keyboard and while some of the set up with the Macbook was shaky, overall it does a good job of working between devices.

title: A PTZ 1080P conferencing system for under $1000? Incredible!
text:
The new Logitech Group HD conferencing system opens up a whole new world of audio and video conferencing options, at a fraction of the cost of the competition. Previous systems from the likes of Vaddio and Lifesize usually run around $3500-$4500 for a basic PTZ setup. This Logitech system offers the AV controller with remote, PTZ 1080P camera and one mic for under $1000. The system is compatible with almost every video platform, including Skype for Business (previous Lync), BlueJeans and more. To clarify - this system still relies on a laptop or desktop with USB to initiate the call, whereas some of the larger systems offer fully stand-alone setups (like Cisco).

Call and video quality are great - but they are greatly dependent on your platform of choice. I made several calls using Skype, and they looked fantastic, mostly thanks to a robust connection on either side of the call. Regardless of the hardware you use, a bad connection will render it useless.

All in all, Logitech has delivered something amazing here - a true HD PTZ conferencing system for under $1000. Best of all, the system is relatively modular, so you can add additional components as your setup grows. Operation is easy, you have a system keypad and a remote, it interfaces with all major platforms. The camera stand is a little weak, but you can mount it in a variety of ways using additional hardware.

title: The first (finally!) worth successor to the MX Revolution.
text:
I had been keeping my one working MX Revolution alive for years with parts salvaged from a spare (A defective one that was to be thrown out after I got the replacement, but I never threw it out because I don't like to waste things.)
I'd swapped out buttons, wheels, batteries.... even bought replacement batteries for it... and the thing kept running! I think I was at 12 years with it... and finally, FINALLY.... Logitech came out with a replacement.

I had heard before that there were MX revolution replacements, but they never had the auto-shift scroll, and I live by that... so no dice.

Now, the positives first.... it actually fits my hand BETTER.... higher arch... but I have really big mitts. Battery life is amazingly superior... and I love that you can plug it in and use it as a "wired" mouse while it's charging. (With the old Revolution I had to plug in a crappy wired mouse while it sat on the base to charge if I neglected to realize it was getting low.) Also, the software is superior

The negatives... well, they're things I can adjust to. Mainly, I don't use a single button on the thing for what it was intended to do (same with the revolution). They are all customized to my needs. My main pet peeve is that there's no easy thumb button to use. On the Revolution I used the in-click of the thumb wheel to switch windows... on the Master I use the "gesture" button... but it's a down motion of the thumb, rather than inward, which makes it far less ergonomic. Might not matter to most, but I'm on this thing all day and switch windows every several seconds, so I can see it (or rather, feel it) being a much larger micro-movement that feels less natural. Other than that, the "back" and "forward" thumb buttons are absolutely useless... at least to my big fingers. I can't hit one without hitting the other, so I just programmed them identically... but would have preferred to just have one large button there that I could trigger easily rather than with an awkward backwards and up maneuver.

Overall, I'm sold. Other than thumb buttons, ergonomics are improved (for me, at least) in the way your hand rests, and it's only a minor step back in functional ergonomics... which I'm sure I'll adjust to.

title: Needs more attention to detail.
text:
Needs more attention to detail.

My version is 8.81.15, on a Windows 10 64 PC, used primarily for my Home Theater (I'll probably never need the microphone).

The audio is wonderful, and the fit is perfect (for me). But, there are some design problems.

1st - The power button operation. It's nice that the button is flush with the surface to prevent accidental shutdown (or startup). I can even appreciate the need for holding the button in for a few seconds to activate/deactivate it. But the power off operation is a little frustrating. When powering it off, you have to hold the button down (support site says for 5 seconds, but I've managed it after about 3 seconds). The problem is that it does not begin to actually power down until you release the button. You could hold it down for a very long time if you want, and the headset will stay powered until you release the button. It may seem to be a silly complaint, but after only using them a dozen times now, it is getting annoying to have to guess that I've held it down long enough (or count to 5 to myself), and then watch lights when I release it to be sure that it actually did power off. Instead, it should power off after the required amount of time held down, and the lights should just go out as soon as it has accepted the command.
Also, with the power button being rather small and flush with the body, it's hard to locate the button in a darkened room. I use my headsets for my Home Theater, which I keep dimly lit.

2nd - the volume control is rather sluggish. I get that it is actually sending the volume command to the PC and it is changing the Windows volume, not the actual device's volume, but there are times where it can take 10 or more seconds for volume to finally settle. You rotate the dial and then leave it alone, and the volume will creep up or down a little at a time until it finally stops.

3rd - the biggest problem is that the headset will randomly power itself off. I've noticed that it does it most often within a minute of being turned on initially. Battery indicator on the Gaming Software screen says fully charged and my lights are all green, yet it turns itself off. And, sometimes about 30 to 45 minutes after powering them back up they will turn off. After that, they stay on.

Also, there have been a few times where the headset didn't power off, but lost connection to the PC for about 20 seconds. I'll take the headset off to see the battery light is green but the power light is off.
Logitech support site says that version 8.79 and higher of the software fixes this. My version is 8.81.15, but I still have the problem

I've tried going through the Logitech support site for this, but it doesn't take me where I need to go to troubleshoot or get further help.

title: Really nice little mouse I bought to use with my HP ...
text:
Really nice little mouse I bought to use with my HP Folio. I bought a Microsoft Wedge Mouse earlier, then got this, but I prefer this Logitech. Nicely weighted, not too heavy and not too light, and feels very high quality and well made. This mouse has a rechargeable battery and an included USB cable for the purpose. The charging port is on the mouse's underside, and you cannot use the mouse while it's charging. Battery life seems decent, though too early to tell, though there is no percentage indicator, just a small battery graphic in the SetPoint utility software and a message in the Windows task bar saying the batteries are "good". Looks like after a few days, the battery is about 1/3 depleted, which is faster drain than in my Mac's Magic Mouse, but still not bad. The Apple Magic Mouse shows % charge remaining and seems to last longer, but then costs about $30 more, too.

All in all, a nice little mouse that seems to maintain bluetooth connectivity well, better than the Wedge Mouse, and I like the handy software utility (had to down load that from Logitech's website). Pointer movements are very accurate and well controlled. Has touch-scroll and functionality is very similar to that of the Apple Magic Mouse. A good purchase, and I would recommend for someone wanting a minimalist mouse for travel, etc.

title: Good size for bigger hands (updated Nov 2018)
text:
I have bought 8 of these mice since 2015. I've tried the MX Master too and have one sitting on my desk that never gets used. When I first bought the Performance MX (this one), it was nearly double the price it is now. And I was still happy with it. The extra ones that I've bought includes three that I have at my office away from home. We have multiple people who pick up random mice and disappear with them for hours. Everybody knows, when they see this mouse, it's mine.

I'll tell you the biggest reason. Most of the people who work with me are older than I am. I'm around 40. They are from that first generation of techies. You give them a small mouse and they become a nervous wreck. They want the full-sized mouse and even though I'm younger than them, I also much prefer the bigger mice. This one is the best for daily use, I don't know how they are for gaming but the Darkfield technology is excellent. You can use this mouse on glass and various wood and even on your pants or shirt or chair arm. It also comes with a rechargeable battery that on average needs charged two to three times a month. You can charge it with the USB cable that comes with it. It takes 1-2 hours to fully charge it AND you can use it while it is charging. It has the programmable buttons where you can change what every button does and you have 3 extra buttons too. The best part, it works with the Unifying Nano Receiver and up to 6 devices can be used with just one of those receivers. At the price it's going for now (around fifty) there shouldn't even be a question about which wireless mouse you're going to get. Unless, you like small mice. It even has the switch to change your scroll wheel from free-flowing to the more ratcheting style. I don't know why they make the higher end ones than this one. Having rarely played computer video games with a mouse, I'm guessing it maybe has something to do with that but if you're just looking for your everyday, easy to charge, no buying batteries, mouse, this is the best one. As a side note, if something happens and your rechargeable battery completely dies, you can use any AA battery in it but you can't charge those with the USB cable. I mention that because my oldest one, nearly 4 years old, stopped charging a few months ago and I've been putting regular AA batteries in it and that's why I just bought a new one.

title: Fantastic mouse, adjustable weights, long USB cord, very comfortable, tunable.
text:
Item: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Mouse
The way this mouse feels in my hand is amazing. I have medium sized hands and I can game using this mouse for hours. On the top of the mouse, the G logo is frosted, with an LED light underneath it, and it slowly and smoothly cycles through the the RGB spectrum within 8 seconds and repeats. You can set the color, the brightness, and rate of color change using the Logitech software. Just download it from their site. Using the software, you can also set the surface that you are using your mouse on (fabric mousepad, hard mousepad) and add new surface profiles to choose from.
The scroll wheel can be set to click with every scroll, or have no click at all and scroll completely free and smoothly. Both are fantastic. The button behind the scroll wheel will set it to click scroll or smooth scroll.The scroll wheel also shifts slightly left/right for scrolling left/right. The scroll wheel can also be pressed as a third button. There are two buttons on the left for thumb use that are Forward and Back buttons. They can be used in gaming or for navigating webpages. The forward button is the button closer to the front of the mouse. The second button behind the scroll wheel will swap through the three profiles. The LED marks near the G logo signify the profile in use. The rubber grip where the thumb sits is slightly textured, and feels great. Even the thumb rest is perfect. The cord is braided fabric. The mouse is really built for a right-handed user. The thumb rest is on the left, and the mouse even arches slightly to sit perfectly in the arch of the palm. Two buttons near the front on top allows you to set the DPI up and down.

Profiles: You can set three profiles for the mouse. You can also load profiles on the mouse's onboard memory, or load specific profiles from your computer for specific games.

Weights:
The mouse itself weighs 4.4 oz or 127 grams. There are five weights included, with each weight weighing 3.6 g. Underneath the thumb rest, where the glossy part is, the bottom portion pops off easily, and there are slots for the weights. Be sure to push the weights in completely, or else the bottom will not lock on properly to the mouse. It is a magnetic lock that holds the bottom portion, so it should lock on easily and stay locked on, and flush with the mouse. The weights do require slight effort to push them in completely into their slots. With three weights, the mouse weighs 137.8 g, and with all five weights, the mouse weighs 145 g.

The software works really well and allows full customization of the lighting and allows tuning of the mouse. Runs without any issues on my Win 10, 64 bit OS.

title: Very Good Remote System - Reliable and Reasonably Priced
text:
We looked for a reliable remote control that costs less than a 60" Flat Screen TV for years. We tried other Logitech products with miserable results. One of our clients even changed out his home theater system trying to get one to work. We started testing this remote hub and remote control early in the summer of 2015. It is great. Extremely reliable, reasonably priced. It is very nice.

It needs a couple of things. One is that you must buy the hub and remote control together. I made the mistake of buying the hub and attempting to use it with my iPad - not a good idea. So, I have $100 invested in a nice door stop. There are three controlling keys with icons. A short hold and a long hold start different activities. That's just not intuitive. Theoretically you can add a QWERTY keyboard, but I've not been able to do that.

Still, it's the best remote going, regardless of the price. It was easy to set up with my iPad - not so easy with a PC running Windows with any kind of security on it. It has a wide selection of devices that it can control, from Roku to Smart TV's, even BOSE systems.

title: Better than several prior Logitech products but use the downloaded Harmony software and avoid the web interface
text:
I posted a review for this product after trying to update it and subsequently learned that the prior generation downloaded software still works fine. So I'm revising this review a little.
I've had at least 10 Harmony remotes and ever since Logitech took over the company, the product has become less and less useful. I have a 600, a 700 and a harmony hub with a the simple remote and a nearly dedicated iPad. My wife and kids have reverted back to using the Tivo remote because the Harmony stuff simply doesn't work the way it used to. I love the Harmony Hub, but the latest generation of remotes do not manage DVRs, particularly TiVos, veryt well.
I was attempting to update my Harmony 700 with a new device and was directed from the downloaded software to a web based interface. It was broken and kept asking me to install the Silverlight and the Harmony plug-in. Both are already installed. A little link on the bottom of the page says "what to do if you are asked to install silverlight and harmony software after it is installed. Click on it and you get a 404 page-not-found error. Nice.
I tried the downloaded Logitech Harmony software a few more times and it eventually loaded WITHOUT referring me to the web interface. This is the old version of the software where I originally set up my remote. It worked perfectly and allowed me to add my new projector. Odd that Logitech is referring people from a working piece of software to a broken web based interface that may pre-date the downloaded version.
If at all possible, avoid the web version.

I have had 2 different 700 remotes and can tell you that they are a little more rugged than the previous Tivo-remote-shaped models. I have been using one of them for 3 or 4 years and, although the labels have rubbed off the rubber buttons, it still works! It also appears as though they fixed the start-up lock-up problem where the device would sit there for 15 seconds even though it only took 3-4 to run the routine. Now it returns to home state for the activity almost immediately. That is a big positive change.
So, this device is still very nice overall but avoid using the web interface to program it and seek out the downloaded version of the Logitech harmony software.
