title: Design and Quality Control Could Use Improvement
text:
I've had an aluminum Apple keyboard for years. I liked it so much that I ended up buying a spare one to use at work. Ever since I've seen the K750, it reminded me of the general layout and style of the Apple KB, plus some nifty solar panels. I've been eyeing this unit for a couple years and finally picked one up for my office.

First impressions, not great. The keyboard came well packaged, with protective film over the glossy covering between the keys (more on that later). Upon peeling it off, I was disappointed to see residue on the plastic underneath the solar panel area. When I went to clean it off, I realized the dirt was on the backside of the plastic. I bet my KB was built after someone ate their lunch. I now have permanent marks by the solar panels that I can't clean off. I also discovered that even when cleaned relatively gently, the glossy finish picks up fine scratches.

Speaking of clean... This glossy finish on the top of the KB was a poor choice. This thing is a magnet for fingerprints. I've ended up bringing a microfiber cloth to work so I can wipe down my keyboard every day. It looks pretty awful after just one day of use. The keys aren't glossy, but the areas in between are. Unless you're perfect with hitting keys, you'll quickly turn the KB into a crime scene.

The typing feel is actually pretty good. I consider it a "hybrid" between the low-profile Apple keyboard (like a laptop) and an old-school mechanical, which is what I'm currently typing on. The feel is pretty light are the keys relatively quiet. The wireless has worked well thus far and don't notice lag. I don't game, so i'm referring to regular typing here only.

CONCLUSION: Logitech needs to improve their quality control and the glossy finish was a horrible choice for a keyboard. If you don't care about that stuff, you'll likely be pleased with the keyboard itself. It's pretty nice to type on, but may require some adjustment, depending on how much key travel you're used to.

DATA: Being an engineer, I couldn't resist to take some speed tests between this KB, my old trusty Apple, and my new Logitech G610 mechanical (Cherry MX Brown keys). In short, no difference once you've taken statistical sampling into account (20 samples per keyboard). I can type just above 70wpm on all three keyboards. The long travel of the mechanical feels a bit unusual to me, as I've spent years on short-travel keyboards. So far, key travel has shown little difference in terms of speed. Accuracy results were all comparable as well.

title: Great product, not many downsides.
text:
The Logitech Type+ keyboard case for iPad Air 2 is a great case to have for an iPad Air 2. This case fits perfectly on my iPad Air 2, and even though I don't have an iPad Air 1, I am sure that it would work fine on that as well. When my unit arrived, it came in a very nice box that had a few big bubbles to protect it during shipping. The box inside of there was just fine as well. My unit came in a plastic sleeve that nicely keeps the product well protected. It also came with a USB cable for charging and a not too helpful but OK instruction manual. The case itself has a paper insert to hold it in place during shipping, and there were a few protective pieces to keep the case from getting scratched or dirty. Setting up was simple. First I charged it via my computer and it charged in under an hour. I am not sure how charged my unit was but it was charged in under an hour. Then pairing. Pairing it was very fast with my iPad Air 2. I just put it into the case, which holds it very well, and connected it, then I went into Bluetooth on my iPad and connected it to the keyboard case and it was working just like that. The design of the case is very good. It has a very slim profile, which is very nice. The outer material was a little greasy at first, but that went away with a couple days use and now is very easy to hold. The case does not obstruct the speakers, lightning port, camera, volume rockers, or the power button or microphone, which is very nice. It is easy to plug the iPad in as well. The case connects when you open it and put the iPad on the magnetic strip, which holds the iPad in place very well. The status LED is nice to have as well, telling you if the battery is charged or not when you connect it. The keys are very responsive, and having the command, option, control, function, and tab keys along with arrows and having a power button and home button on the keyboard is very nice. It also has a screen shot button, volume buttons, a Siri button, and even a multi-tasking button. The only thing that I wish it had were brightness keys. The keys feel very nice to type on, I could type on it for hours if I actually had anything to type about for hours. The keys are also very responsive and work very fast and there is no lag at all. It is quite easy to take the iPad out of the case and put it back in, which is a nice feature for me especially because I have to keep my iPad clean a lot. The durability of the case is outstanding. It protects the iPad from a lot of things. Another thing that I noticed is the area around the outside of the keys is very easily scratched, which I noticed after a few days of use, but it's not that noticeable when you look at it. I noticed NO flex at all in the keyboard or the case.

So, In summation, this is a very great keyboard case and I would definitely recommend it for anyone who has an iPad Air 2 or iPad Air. With great durability, very nice to type on keys with no lag, and almost instant Bluetooth connection, the Logitech Type+ Keyboard case for iPad Air 2 or iPad Air is a great choice in my opinion.

title: Wish I had spent a little more on the remote with the screen
text:
I like this remote a lot. It simplifies my A/V experience, and as long as I have my phone with me, it is super convenient. It is when I do not have my phone that I run into a few challenges, which I believe would probably be alleviated if I had the more expensive remote with the screen.

I bought this to control my A/V system, which consists of an old Panasonic plasma TV, a Denon AVR-X2200W, an Xfinity X1 DVR/cable box, a Playstation 3, an AppleTV, and an Nintendo Wii. Since this one has the Home Control, I also connected it to my Insteon SmartHome hub, even though I don't plan on using it for that.

My hub is on the mantle with my TV, and the other equipment is nearby on an open shelving unit. The setup was pretty easy through the app. You get the hub connected to your wifi, and then you start to connect your devices to the hub. The hub had no issues sending IR signals to the TV, cable box, and the receiver, and the PS3, AppleTV and Wii connected via Bluetooth, all with no problems. The app then walked me through setting up activities, which are the main reason for this device. You press one button, and the hub takes care of turning on/off the necessary equipment and changing inputs if necessary. You then get to test the activities and adjust settings if needed. In my case, I had to adjust for my 8 year old TV because it apparently powers on/off slower than today's equipment.

Using the remote via the app has been great. I do wish some of the screens/ buttons could be moved or modified but not a big deal. For example when I am watching cable and want to either use the Last Channel button or input a channel by its number, the Enter button is on a different screen than the number pad screen or the DVR buttons screen, so it takes an extra swipe or two. Not the end of the world, but an Enter button on all these other screens would be nice. The hub responds quickly to signals from the app, and the app has the option to stay on, but also dims itself while not in use, which probably saves a little bit of battery on the phone.

The physical remote is ok. It has buttons for three activites, and a few home automation buttons as well, which I used once to see if it would turn on/off the lights I have set up with the Insteon SmartHome hub, and it did. The buttons can be reassigned via the app, which was nice because currently my TV is the speaker for my system, and during the activity setup, the app set up the receiver as where volume should be controlled. I was able to reassign the remote's volume button to control the TV volume for all activities. I'm not sure this option is available for buttons in the app, but it's just a couple taps to get to the TV remote section and modify the volume there. This brings me to my one gripe with the physical remote. If for some reason things get out of sync (say your TV was supposed to change input for watching TV, but it didn't), I haven't figured out how to have the physical remote change to individual components. I can try to run the activity again to hopefully get it in sync, but if it doesn't then I have no way of changing to control the TV since this activity ends with controlling the cable box. Again, I could probably reassign some buttons to accomplish this, but then I have to remember that a button with a different picture or word under it now does this new task, and explaining that to my wife is not going to fly. I think the remote with the screen, if it is anything like the Logitech Harmony 650 that I bought for my mother, would rectify this issue for me. I may pay the extra money for it at some point.

The hub has been pretty stable. I did go through a period where I would have to unplug the hub and plug it back in order to get the app to see it after some unidentified period of inactivity, but I'm assuming an update fixed it, or it stabilized on its own. Either way, I haven't had to manually reboot it in over a month. If you look at the reviews for the Harmony app (at least on iTunes), it got terrible reviews for stability. I haven't had any of those issues on the app side.

I am definitely happy with the purchase, and hopefully I'll get some extra spending cash to get the remote with the screen, which should give me an even better experience.

title: Built to break, unreliable.
text:
So these headphones, while they work well when they do work, have three huge issues:

1) The biggest issue with these headphones is that after a certain amount of use, they will cease being able to be charged. Research indicates that the mini-usb connector separates from the rest of the device. I had to RMA one after six months, and then the replacement broke after another three, and I don't have two weeks to go without a functional headset every couple months. With my job I need this kind of communication capability, and when it stops in the middle of the day and I have to dig out backup equipment, it costs me time and money.

2) Every once in a while, the headphones start playing a buzzing sound that gets louder and louder until it drowns out all else. The headphones can't be shut off while this is happening, they must be unplugged and/or reset with the reset button using a paper clip. Sometimes this needs to be done multiple times before they'll function properly again, which happens about twice a week.

3) The macro buttons were the entire reason I got these headphones, being able to use push to talk communication from a distance, and every once in a while the macro keys default back to their original functions (play/pause, back, forward media keys) while the Logitech control panel still shows the user-defined functions. The control panel has to be restarted in order for the macro keys to work again, and this happens about three or four times a week.

All in all, while good in concept, they're not worth it when you have to deal with the constant interruptions that the device malfunctions cause.

title: A great mouse for productivity on the go
text:
The left click on my Logitech M305 failed after 4 years of dutiful service, so I figured I'd give another Logitech portable a try as my on-the-go mouse. I haven't been disappointed so far.

The mouse has a slightly larger footprint than the M305, which I was a bit bummed about, but still definitely packable. However, the mouse is substantially slimmer than the M305, which means it takes up about the same space in my bag. A nice change is that they've moved to a wedge shape and chopped off some of the useless plastic on the backside, which reduces the effective volume. Comfortable in the hand, most of the weight comes from the AA battery that runs the thing. The nano receiver continues to be my favorite wireless peripheral adapter, and there's a storage pocket inside the battery compartment for it.

Buttons are pleasantly "clicky," scroll wheel is nice enough. The surprise with this mouse was how useful the gesture button (the square guy below the scroll wheel) is combined with the new Logitech software. I use it to drive multiple desktops, but you can use it for media controls, photo editing... Was expecting it to be a gimmick, but it's turned out to be tremendously helpful. You can also overload the left and right scroll to defined shortcuts (defaults are forward and back web browsing), which is also a neat feature.

On the whole, a great portable mouse with some clever productivity tricks. Great for anyone who needs a laptop mouse to throw in their bag.

text:

I recently talked to a co-worker about their device, and they have none of the same issues. I got one of these for free and one for half off, and still don't feel like I got value for my money.

It's great for checking on the dogs. The "Day Summary" is so pointless it's almost comical, and it compacts 24hours worth of video into mere seconds and moves so fast you can't see a thing going on....waste of a 'feature'.

We bought a second one only because it was 50% off on Black Friday, otherwise 200 for this product is absolutely absurd, but our garage door opened on it's own a couple of times and with $25,000 in bikes alone in the garage I got paranoid and want to be able to check if it is is open or not throughout the day.

If you can't leave it plugged in, the battery lasts MAYBE 3/4ish hours....but not generally making it pointless without power. They are easy to set-up and I guess it's cool you can "talk" through them. Certainly wouldn't have paid money for one if we hadn't received the first for free, but I also didn't want to have two apps to check on the home place.

title: Logitech 4 Lyfe
text:
Once again Logitech has surpassed expectations, Supplying me a superior product for a fair price. I'm upgrading from my G500 that I have had for... I think 6 years. As soon as I plugged it in, Even without the Software I noticed a huge performance increase. After installing the software I was again surprised at the new options, Such as, Tuning a custom Mouse pad. They have 3 default presets, Cloth, Hard, and Factory default which would technically turn off the setting. If you choose to tune your own mouse pad, Which I highly recommend. It is easy and only takes 1 minute. This reads your mousepad and draws a map of sorts to tell when elevation and speed is varied, Giving a more even and accurate reading. The lighting settings are amazing, You can select Lighting Zones, Logo and DPI lighting. Choose a lighting effect which is limited but cool, Your choices are.
Color Cycle.(Switches between Blue/Green/Red/Yellow/Purple colors in a fading/breathing effect.)
Breathing.(Choose a color of your liking and it will fade in and out at the pace of a humans breathing.)
You can choose practically any color, You have 16.8 Million Colors to choose from. No problems matching your build.

For a high performance mouse you should never pay more than $60... Check mark! <$60.
What you should look for in a mouse is performance over all, Although other areas are important too.
So lets break down in terms of my own opinion what a mouse should have.
1. Performance.
2. Durability.
3. Fit and comfort.
4. Advanced settings.
5. Visuals.
You can check every one of those at 5/5 stars.
Overall this is the best mouse ever owned, The Laser increased movement tracking greatly resulting in a better gameplay and higher KDR. If you are like me and have kept the same mouse for 5+ years it is time to upgrade.

So in conclusion this is the best mouse I have ever owned, I would suggest it to Gamers and Graphic artists or anything that requires a very accurate mouse reading. Logitech is the best and any bad review you read is fault of the user.

First Impressions.

I will try to make this brief, But also effective.
Logitech is well known for their PC Gaming products and always give you quality, I have never bought a bad or cheaply made Logitech item.

So, Lets start with the look. Silver and Black looks great, However the Button Numbers should have been a brighter color. It is a very dull gray making them very hard to see. If you can't see them why are they even there then. Everything else is very appealing.
This joystick has many functions and abilities. It has a Profiler Program so that you can further customize it, Allowing you do adjust sensitivity, Add mouse and keyboard commands to a button, You can also setup a macro for the buttons within the Profiler. This profiler also helps to keep the joystick calibrated and should always be running when playing a game, So in a sense this is NOT PLUG & PLAY. Many people complained about calibration issues and I believe they do not have this Profiler Installed or Running during their gameplay.
This joystick is Right Handed, If you are Left Handed you will need a different joystick, I'm unaware if this model comes in both.
There is 3 Axis's on this, Tilt Front/Back, Tilt Left/Right, and the Twist(Left and Right). The "Controller Joystick" you see on the top is not like one you would find on your average PS or Xbox controller, It has 8 buttons that when you move it in a direction it will click on one of the 8. This might sound bad, But it acts nearly the same as your average controller joystick, While also adding the option of giving you 8 more customizable buttons. So you can consider this 20 buttons rather than 12 depending how you utilize that 8 directional joystick.
The feel is great, It has an internal spring along with a rubber type spring externally. The internal spring will take the pressure of all movement and the outer rubber one will help during heavy movement, Decreasing wear and tear on the internal spring, Assuring a long life for the product.
Every button performs as it should, And always responds quickly. There is never a stick or hard to press situation, This goes for the joystick as well.
There are 2 trigger buttons, Your conventional trigger and the one on your thumb, Which can be triggered with a squeeze on the joystick or movement of your thumb. The Conventional or Front Side Trigger could have been made better, The plastic feels cheap and loose. I expected more from Logitech in this regard, This is the only thing I think could have been done better. However that does not hinder your gameplay in anyway.
The THRUST Lever is especially useful, In certain games this will allow you to maintain a certain altitude, In others it will allow minor adjustments to Thrust/Altitude. In BF4 this will allow minor adjustments, Helping you maintain altitude while at the same time providing a softer landing.

My conclusion for this review and a summary is that, This is a Quality made and Effective Product. It will support the Oldest to the Newest Games and has ALL The functionality that you would expect from it plus more. It will last at least 1 year with HEAVY gameplay. It will not become outdated anytime soon, Meaning it could last for 4 years. Hope this has helped someone, If you were looking for a Joystick look no further.

title: Constant Disconnections at Random
text:
Oh man where do I begin. First off, I've owned this product for over a year now and throughout my year of owning such a product, I've had CONSTANT USB recognition issues. I've gone through support four times and through those times they've sent me a replacement. The first time was sending mine in and receiving a new one. The next three times was sending me a new/refurbished unit. Makes me wonder why they sent me free units without the need of sending in mine again. Because of this, I gave out three of those units to my brother, gf, and my friend. And all of them have had the same issues I've been having, constant USB disconnection. Let me rewind a bit. When I first received this error on my end, I thought "ok, it's my camera." So I contacted Logitech support (Logitech makes it hard to find the support I need and needs to have a simple "email/call" system rather than a "submit your device in order to get a hold of us" system) and they requested me to send in my device, no problem. After a week and received the new unit, I plugged it in the same USB port and the device was recognized, yay right? Well, there's more to it. I've noticed that there's been a pattern. Every time I go onto Skype to call, I realize that my camera is not recognized. So I initially go into Device Manager and find out that there's an exclamation point, stating it's not recognized. Ok, so I pull the USB and plug it back in. I hear the sounds of it being detected and it's detected. Great! So I go back onto Skype and see it still not being recognized. So I then restart Skype and go back on, and seeing the camera icon still not showing. So that's when things get a little interesting. When I go to unplug the USB, I realize that before I unplugged it, I can hear my PC making the sound of a USB being connected/disconnected. So after playing with the cable I thought it might've been a short. Well, I then went to support and they sent me a new unit. Great. I plugged in that unit and it STILL gave me the exact same issues that the previous camera gave me. I toyed with it and tried every USB port on my motherboard and still received the issue. I then thought to try the USB ports on top of my PC case. Surprisingly it didn't disconnect. So at that time I thought maybe it was my motherboard. But what doesn't make sense is how come every other USB plugged into my motherboard is fine but not the camera? However, at that time I tried contacting support and they sent me another unit for I thought it was that unit as well. They sent me the third one and tried it and it STILL persists. By this time I was fed up and confused as to why this was happening. I then tested all three cameras on my brother's PC and it still does this. However, it only acts up on the motherboard USB ports (our motherboards are different) and not on the PC case's USB ports. So I then tested all three on my mom's laptop. Surprisingly they were all recognized and not disconnecting, even though I was moving the cable to see if there was a short. So back to the drawing board. I put my camera back, my bro's back, and mailed out one to my gf. When she received it, plugged it up and such, she too had issues (she has a different motherboard than what I have). So I thought to myself, "what is causing this? Why is this issue so persistent?" Then a month later after ignoring the issue for awhile, I received another camera and decided to give it to my friend (he has the same motherboard as I do). He too had issues with the camera. So after a year of debating why this issue is happening and how to fix it, I have no idea. I'vs just given up on it and continue to use the camera till I find a better camera online that doesn't have this issue.

TL;TR

I've given out three cameras, to my brother, my friend, and gf, and everyone had the same issue that I've been having. It seems to only effect the motherboards and not the PC USB ports. All of our motherboards are different, except my friend's. So in the end, I just sucked this issue up, as we all did, and continue to use them and witness the constant video disconnections on Skype and having to replug the USB cable every time this issue happens.

A fix? Just unplug and plug the camera USB back into whatever port you used and wait till your computer recognizes it. If it doesn't work, just keep on unplugging and plugging back in the camera USB till the camera is recognized. There's not much else I can do at this point.

EDIT: bumping up from 3 to 5 stars. The problem is you cannot use this through a USB hub. Connected directly to the laptop, it works great. Bought another one (red) for another laptop - couldn't be happier.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

This was a great mouse - I can't stand laptop trackpads, so I always try to have a mouse packed in my laptop bag. Last year I was away on business and without a mouse, so I went to a store where you BUY things that they claim are the BEST to pick up a reasonably priced wireless mouse, and it worked great.

The problem is that I actually very rarely needed it, generally having my computer locked to my desk at work when I'm not traveling, so it basically sat idle for about 10 months. When I started needing it again, it still worked flawlessly - Logitech makes a great mouse, no doubt. But suddenly after about a year (total) of use, and only maybe a month of "serious" use, it just decided to stop working. When it's moving the mouse at all, it's erratic. Yes, tried a new battery; the power light often will not come on (it doesn't stay on anyway, to save battery, but when you're actually using the mouse - moving and clicking, the light should be on, and this one does not. The laser on the bottom does not turn on; if it does, it's very low power.

So it was great while it lasted - ergonomic, responsive, tracked well - no complaints; but it should last longer than one battery.

title: Excellent replacement for a Harmony One
text: I purchased the Logitech Advanced Remote Harmony 950 to replace an aging Harmony One. When I started reading reviews of the 950, it seemed like it might be a good choice as a replacement.  I finally decided to order it, and have been quite pleased with it so far. It took a little time to learn the new feature set of the 950, but it is fairly intuitive.  Button layout is good, the size is smaller than the One, the touch screen is snappy and scrolling/swiping are easy.  I find that it starts up my devices faster than my One.  After a day's use it feels quite comfortable and I find my fingers fall easily on the correct buttons.  It charges vertically, so takes up less space while in the charger.  I have it working with my Samsung Smart TV, a DirecTV DVR, an Oppo BD player, a Pioneer AV receiver and a Roku Stick that plugs into my Oppo.  All in all it has been a good experience so far.

title: I really like the hub and remote all by themselves
text:
I really like the hub and remote all by themselves. But once I add in my Echo and SmartThings Hub, the combination is amazing. I can control my entertainment system with the Harmony remote or with voice commands via the Echo. I say "Alexa, turn on TV" and the TV turns on; if I say 'Alexa, turn on TV Time" the TV turns on, the room lights turn on at 60%, and all other lights on the first floor turn off; if I say "Alexa, turn on Sleepytime", the foyer light turns on immediately, then 30 seconds later all lights turn off, the Harmony shuts down all activities (TV, DVD, Fire TV, etc), my door locks and the home alarm is set.

Other than the voice commands to turn on and off the system, I mostly use the Harmony remote to control the entertainment system. (I have voice commands as well, but the remote is more convenient). It is very customizable.

NOTE: There is a way to get around the 8 device limit if you have an older Harmony remote. My older Harmony had 12 devices associated with it. At setup of the Harmony Hub I was given the option to use the configuration from my old remote. This allowed me to associate all 12 devices with the Hub. A week after setting up the Hub, I purchased a Fire TV. I was not allowed to add the device to the Hub as I was over the 8 device limit. So, I added the Fire TV to the older Harmony remote (even though it could not control the bluetooth Fire TV) and re-ran the Hub setup. Now I have 13 devices associated with the Harmony Hub.

NOTE 2: Setting up Activities can be tricky. Not necessarily due to the Hub, but due to the way the devices themselves work. For instance, I had two issues when setting up my Vizio Soundbar in all my Activities. For some reason, the input source had to be entered a second time as part of the Activity. But, the Harmony software does not allow you to manually enter the input source a second time into the Activity startup. So, I had to create a new input source to use in the Activity after a 2 second delay. The second issue was with the Vizio on/off coordination with other devices. Sometimes it went out of sync and would power off when everything else powered on (and vice versa). My workaround was to use the volume down and volume up key presses (briefly) to wake up the Vizio (and turn it on).

title: Logitech MX Master: looks before function
text:
The MX Master is purportedly Logitech's top-of-the-line offering for power users, successor to the likes of the Performance MX and the venerable MX Revolution, both of which I own and use. Suffice it to say, whenever Logitech slaps an "MX" on a mouse it's meant to be their top-tier mainline offering, and their flagship mouse.

--In my opinion, this mouse is inferior to other mice Logitech has had over the years, in multiple respects.--

First, the mouse's contour. Honestly, this is a fairly comfy mouse overall, but it's got an unusually-high hump around where the user's palm would be, and there is a fairly sharp dropoff on the back end which doesn't make for good gripping area. The previous Performance MX has a more smooth profile.

Secondly, the mouse's thumb wheel, thumb buttons and gesture button are 100% useless and nonfunctional without Logitech Options software, which is mostly-painless to use and install, but it's a bit of a letdown considering that lower-grade mice like the M705 don't need any kind of software life-support to allow them to function. The thumb buttons, when depressed, register perhaps the slightest impulse of a Mouse4 or Mouse5 press, even if the actual mouse button is held. I'm a gamer, and I find this VERY disconcerting, as I use the "back" mouse button- Mouse4, that is- in first-person shooters to have my character move backwards. When I tried to use the button bound to that on the MX Master, my character would maybe take the slightest, briefest step backwards. To most folks, this is a non-issue but to me it's very disappointing. I was expecting a top-tier product to deliver the same kind of functionality I've expected out of Logitech products for years, and the Master does not deliver. I'm aware this is an issue with the software, not the hardware, but even SetPoint had the option to have those thumb buttons act like they would without the software (it's rather obtuse- one must set the thumb buttons to "generic button" mode. They will still act EXACTLY the same.) They won't even work on the Master without the software.

The adaptive scroll wheel, a large selling point of the mouse, has a very nice feel to use in the click-to-click ratcheting mode, like almost every mid-tier or higher Logitech mouse does, but in adaptive and free-spin modes the wheel feels far more restrained and sluggish when compared to a mouse such as the Performance MX or G700s, with Logitech's more pedestrian "marathon" wheel. When my scroll wheel is going to free-spin, I'm not expecting the wheel to feel like it's constantly got some sort of mild friction- I'm expecting that thing to spin 'til the cows come home. I'd describe the wheel's lack of free-spin duration as it being "sticky", for lack of a better, more accurate term. Also, the wheel in a fair few of these mice has a habit of breaking or screwing up in some way.

"Perfect mouse for power users"? Yeah, maybe if you're obsessed with mouse gestures and that adaptive scroll wheel. If you're like me and don't usually bother with gesture controls, I'd suggest you don't waste your money on an MX Master, and go for something like a G700s or a Performance MX if you can find a good used one. If you're crazy, lucky or both you might stumble upon an MX Revolution for less than three figures.

Logitech- where the older products are almost always the better products. If they were ever to make a G602 with the G700s's dual-mode scroll wheel, they'd have the perfect mouse for a power user.

Sadly, that ain't gonna happen.

EDIT 10/2/16: I have given this mouse to a friend, and he loves it. The mouse wasn't that bad to hold and use, honestly, but Logitech's habit of making mouse4 and mouse5 into momentary buttons, even when held, is a very annoying thing in their mouse-options software pieces. This bad habit of theirs was a carryover from the earlier SetPoint software, as I learned when using it to configure a Performance MX I bought to replace the MX Master. Though the Options software is very low-key, it's annoying that a mouse this expensive would require software life-support to function as anything beyond a three-button mouse with a fancy scroll wheel.

EDIT 10/26/16: Options and SetPoint also both have a bad habit of gimping the scroll wheel's side scroll functionality. Really, most of Logitech's "general consumer" software has some kind of annoying habit that reduces mouse functionality unnecessarily.

EDIT 1/25/17: I can safely say that the Performance MX and MX Revolution are far, far superior products to the MX Master. I own both of the former, and still use both on and off. DO NOT BOTHER with the MX Master when there's better stuff from the same company. My best recommendation would be the Performance MX, simply due to its availability, usability and the fact I worked out that side-scroll and thumb-button BS in SetPoint. (The "generic button" option is your friend.) If you're crazy or lucky enough to be able to score an MX Revolution, note that you *WILL* need SetPoint to get the most out of it, much like the Master. I managed to score two MXRs at roughly MSRP--exceedingly lucky, I'd say.

EDIT 4/21/17:
The friend I gave this mouse to still likes it, but its scroll wheel is giving him all different kinds of grief. Like so many others, the ratchet/freespin mechanism busted and he's leaving his locked to ratchet scrolling. Review downgraded to one star.

Furthermore, some of Logitech's gaming products provide similar usability and adaptability, if not the battery life. The M705, MX Revolution, Performance MX, G602, G700 and G900 are all better, superior mice in my opinion. Yes, I said M705. That's a $25 mouse, and it's better than this supposed top-of-the-line piece of trash.

TL; DR:
Don't buy this, get a Performance MX instead. If you're a gamer, go for a G700s.

title: Good mouse aside from the middle mouse button
text:
I got this mouse mainly because the trackpoint on my ThinkPad external keyboard wasn't great for gaming or SolidWorks (CAD). While I love trackpoints, and find them much better than having to reach for a mouse for coding, web browsing, or writing, they are rather useless for games, and design programs. So I got this bad boy because I have had good previous experiences with logitech devices and this mouse looked rather comfortable. For the most part, for the price that I paid for it (I bought it used), I am very satisfied. I'll start with the cons:

CONS: the middle mouse button is weird: So there are 2 modes for scrolling: this hyper mode, and regular scrolling. In hyper mode, you don't feel the slight tactile bumps you normally get when moving the mouse wheel, its just totally smooth (honestly don't understand the point of this as you can just hit PgDn or end to fly through documents). In regular mode, it feels like any ordinary mouse wheel. But the weird thing is this: in regular mode, when pushing down on the middle mouse scrollwheel, it feels like there are 2 stages for this button. But in reality there is only 1 stage. You have to press the middle mouse wheel farther down than you think you have to in order to middle mouse click. The first "false" stage feels like a normal middle mouse click, but the second stage, which is what is required for a middle mouse click to be registered feels really mushy. Not really a big deal, but this seriously annoys me more than it should.

PROS:as you can see, I only have 1 negative, which isn't really that big of an issue.
1) the design: extremely comfortable and ergonomic. Very comfortable for a right hander. Buttons like backpage are exactly where you want them.
2) works great: tracks wonderfully, button clicks (aside from the middle mouse button) feel nice and satisfying. The middle mouse wheel gives satisfying clicks when your scrolling with it.

Overall, have to recommend this mouse despite the lousy middle mouse button. Overall very satisfied with my purchase. Can't comment on the battery life though, I did just buy this keyboard.

title: Top Quality Remote at Value Price
text:
This remote is my favorite remote I've owned. I've tried out the Harmony One and other top end Harmony remotes but this one is the best one when looking for the sweet spot between value and performance. I would only suggest a more expensive remote if you are looking to control many actions (10+), need a RF remote, or are looking for whole house automation. Otherwise, this remote will be a workhorse for your electronics.

I have the following set up for my electronics: Watch TV (tv 1), Watch Smart TV (tv 2), Use XBox One, Play Music

Setup: You use a computer program to input every device you want to control (have your model numbers handy), then choose what to control with each activity. Basic setup will easily get you up and running, but the program allows for more fine tuning if you need it.

Use: The remote works very well. The most common mistake that people make with the remote is not holding the remote towards to electronics while it turns on everything. My dad sometimes gets frustrated when his remote (same model) doesn't turn on everything properly but he blocks the remote's signal sometimes. This is something you must be conscious of - the remote is not instantaneous, it needs time to send power signals to each device, then possibly send other signals depending on if an input or other function needs to be changed. With complex activities, it might take 10-15 seconds to fully get the devices all lined up.

Help Button: The nice thing is that if you block the signal or a device gets out of whack on its own, there's a simple solution. The help button is the answer to any problem 99% of the time. Press it once and it'll try to fix the issue. If that doesn't work, the remote screen will walk you through each device asking if it's properly set up, with the user clicking yes or no each time. It's a simple but very effective tool.

Batteries: Batteries are two AA and they are used up relatively quickly but it's to be expected. So have some rechargeable ones handy. I'd estimate the batteries need replacement every few months depending on how much I use the product. There is a rechargable version (Logitech 700) if replacing batteries is an absolute no for you.

Bottom Line: It's a quality remote that is so much better than the standard issue ones and the $20 ones from local box stores. If you don't need RF or numerous whole house activities, this is the clear choice. It's well worth the money.

Side note: The remote is pretty durable as my puppy found it one day and started to chew. It held up really well to the jaws of a 6 month golden retriever. So that's another positive, it seems pretty sturdy for a piece of electronics (just don't go dropping it from a skyscraper or anything).

text:
First -- Logitech apparently listens to your complaints/suggestions. Several of my original problems were resolved the last time that I used the update software!

But it still has problems.
My biggest is that it's anemic -- has no IR power. I have to point it exactly at my devices to use it. Anything that's on an angle is iffy.

Activating and switching activities is my next problem. It assumes that all of your stuff is in one place and tries to turn everything on and make the appropriate settings when you push the activity button. If you're switching activities and a box only has a power toggle, it'll turn the box off instead of on. If your stuff is not all in one place (my audio equipment's in a different rack across the room from the video), then it sometimes turns it all on, sometimes not, and it'll also leave things in an uncertain state depending on what commands were strong enough to be received depending on where it was pointed. You have to go to the individual devices and make sure they're set right. I wish that I could have multiple "on presses" for different directions or just be able to skip that step. I usually push the remote hard into the sofa to block the IR sender when I switch activities so that it doesn't mess things up!

title: Great in Many Ways, Occasionally Frustrating
text:
This is a tough item to write a review on. In many ways this is a 5-star item, but in others, it's more of a 2-star gadget. There's quite a bit to like--it's sleek, the haptic feedback works well and is useful, the software is easy to download, comprehend, follow, and use (I am using a MacBook), it's highly functional (you can add 15 remotes for literally hundreds of thousands of devices, 50+ favorite channels, and due to the software it is adaptable and dynamic), comfortable, has the right buttons (guide, dvr, info, up/down, vol, exit, menu, record, play, pause, stop, fast forward, rewind, select, direction controls, etc.), and a reasonably sized touchscreen with buttons large enough that it's easy to hit the correct ones. In addition, it easily works the input controls for the tv and makes one remote a breeze to use when often you might need at least two and probably three. I thought the software (you'll need to download it from the myharmony website; east to do) was surprisingly intuitive and very easy to use--download was fast and adding devices was quite easy (10 minutes total). In short order I was able to control a Cox cable box and a Samsung tv without issue and with one remote (which isn't really such a big deal since I could already do that with the Cox remote). Only now, I had a cooler looking more functional remote at the ready. The remote allows you to choose a device (tv, cable box, dvr, streaming device, etc) or an activity (watch tv, watch Apple TV, etc.). All this is great and the biggest (pleasant) surprise was how good the software was at making set up and troubleshooting easy.

Now for the negative...Adding a Kindle Fire Stick is not possible (at the moment). Adding an Apple TV is not trivial and took way more than 10 minutes and a bit of research online (more than I wanted to do). Although the initial set up only requires the device identification (tv make/model, cable box make/model, Apple TV generation)--and it's best to write this down before starting--and entry into the myharmony app is easy and, for the most part, things work after correctly identifying the model type, this is not always the case. There is an option to train the 950 remote with the remote you're trying to mimic, but I found this to be imperfect. The bigger problem was with the Apple TV. Whether correctly identifying in the app or training the remote with the little silver AppleTV remote, I've not been able to get the Harmony 950 to do everything the simple Apple TV remote does (moving up and down would work, but sideways wouldn't for example). The online users guide and several forums are helpful, but for the 3rd gen Apple TV, this took more effort than it should. Nevertheless, overall, this is a very good, sleek, functional, and dynamic remote. But setup can be time consuming and occasionally frustrating.

title: Surprisingly useful, comfortable, and flexible. Useless joystick.
text:
I bought this on a whim and acknowledged then that this purchase was frivolous at best and outright wasteful at worst. A separate, tiny, keyboard for gaming makes less sense than a keyboard that's designed for gaming (like a Corsair K70 or something). I don't much care for single-use things but when it comes to PC peripherals uni-taskers can bring some value so I thought I would give it a shot.

To place things into perspective, I use an MS Sculpt Ergonomic keyboard as my primary. This has been good for working and gaming--although decidedly much better for work. And it's because I like the typing experience on the MS Sculpt so much that I couldn't bring myself to buy a brand new keyboard. Just a little something to supplement my gaming was needed.

So I tried out the G13 because I was just getting in to my first MMO and I've been gaming on my PC a lot recently and I thought that something specifically designed for gaming would help alleviate some of the issues introduced by the Sculpt. Specifically that the split design of the ergonomic keyboard causes some buttons to be too far out of reach, such as every key to the right of 6, T, G, and B. And the row of number keys are a bit odd to work with as well.

The G13 places more keys in easy to reach places and very effectively gives me more freedom to customize my controls for the keys accessible by my index, middle, ring, and pinky fingers go. The rows of keys below WASD are less than optimal because the device narrows and reduces the number of keys per row. As a result the spacebar key, just under where my thumb naturally rests, is too small and a bit too difficult to press down. And the keys to the left of that are even more difficult to reach and activate.

The joystick and two small buttons are almost completely useless. Or, I should say, I have yet to find a practical application for the joystick and buttons. The first problem is that the joystick is a bit too low to fully replace WASD while still providing easy access to the rest of the keys on the board. So if I'm using the joystick for movement (WASD) then I'm not really able to use most of the keys on the board, mostly because using the joystick puts my hand in a position where my fingers are where they need to be but my wrist is in a position that restricts how much pressure I can apply with my digits. The joystick pad itself is very small and comes to a point, it's not designed like an XBOX thumbstick and this makes it a pain to use and gives me the feeling that I have far less control over the stick. This part of the device is my least favorite but at least it doesn't get in the way.

Overall the device is pretty comfortable. I get the feeling that my grip is wrong, though, because I do feel some discomfort when I start using it but that goes away after a bit of time. Keep in mind that I use a crazy ergonomic keyboard which has a profound effect on how I rest my hand on any keyboard so it really must be my approach and not the ergonomics of the device itself which really has been put together quite nicely.

The Logitech software that runs in the background is effective but very ugly and sometimes difficult to understand because of it's asinine layout--seriously Logitech, please design a UI that looks like it's from this decade. It's not immediately apparent that each of the three M buttons along the top of the device not only change the color of the backlight but can also switch button functions within a single game profile. I would think that most games only really need a single set of buttons mapped anyways so this isn't a huge issue but it's worth mentioning as it's emblematic of the types of issues that you may have with the Logitech software.

I would call this purchase a win. No, it's not necessary, by any means. But it does what it's meant to do quite well. That said, I will most likely buy a Corsair K70 or K95 very soon and set this thing aside or hand it down to a friend.

title: Great Gaming Mouse
text:
Previously had a G500, so this seemed like the logical choice to buy once it bit the dust. The mouse is highly rated by those who use it, and it's easy to understand why once you use it. The LEDs are a nice touch since the color can be customized.

The mouse has a good layout for all hand sizes. You'll find that your hand will naturally rest where intended, unless you have a slightly different grip (e.g. claw). During long usage, the mouse doesn't become nasty from hand condensation and remains easy to use. The optical sensor seems quite responsive and accurate; gamers will like that there is no mouse acceleration used.

This mouse is definitely worth the purchase, especially if you are considering this for PC gaming. This will definitely become my recommendation to anyone in the market for a new mouse.

Pros:
+ Has a natural feel when your hand is on the unit
+ Insanely high DPS, if that's your thing. Can be customized to any level of your preference.
+ Optical sensor. No mouse acceleration.
+ Buttons have nice "clicky" responses. Benefit to those who need resistance to accidental double clicking.
+ Removable bottom plate for weight adjustment.
+ LED is color changeable, and can be modified through software.
+ Additional programmable buttons on the mouse. Logitech's software makes changing any of the mouse functionality quite easy.
+ Adjustable DPI, with 3 specific profiles to swap through depending on what is necessary.
+ Braided cord

Cons:
- The mouse wheel is somewhat slippery. Not too big of deal, but I can see some people becoming annoyed at it.
- Sniper button will constantly be hit by those who have their thumb up more than others. I personally did this while getting used to the mouse.
- White LED is blueish in tint. Those expecting true white LED lighting will not achieve this.

title: Comfortable and great quality for the money
text:
My husband is a dedicated PC video gamer, devoting much of his time to playing "Left For Dead" online. Having a comfortable, high quality gaming headset that he can wear for hours at a stretch and talk clearly over is a high priority for him. He's tried other brands of headsets in the past and not liked them, mostly because they were either too heavy or had on-ear attachments that weren't comfortable. His previous headset had been a Logitech G430 model, which he had had for years and been very happy with. All of a sudden the microphone stopped working on it, so we were delighted to have the opportunity to try the G231.

The G231 looks identical to the G430, other than being a different color. It took us a while to test their quality, though, because when we first tried it on my husband's computer, the microphone also didn't work. I took it to my computer, and at first I couldn't get it to work at all (mic OR headphones). Here is where I will complain about the documentation provided with the headset: All that was provided was one of those "setup guides" that lack any words, and it indicated that all we would have to do was plug it in the appropriate jacks. Well, on my computer, that wasn't sufficient; I had to reboot the computer for the device to be recognized. So that was a bit frustrating, and it would've been nice for the instructions to include that as a step. However, I was able to establish quickly that the headset worked fine on my computer; I still couldn't get the mic to work on my husband's computer. There ensued a couple of long frustrating weeks in which we sent the computer (newish, still under warranty) back only to be told it was working perfectly. Then I called Logitech service, and here is where I will give credit where credit is due: My call was answered promptly, and the agent on the line was knowledgeable and able to walk me through diagnostic steps in a clear manner to attempt to get to the bottom of the issue. Alas, the tech was left as baffled as I was.

Bottom line: It was only after I googled "mic doesn't work on headset" and researched a gazillion threads with people having the same difficulty that I discovered the solution: My husband's computer--even though we were running daily scans with Windows Defender--had been infected with malware (yeah, I know, in hindsight that should've been an obvious cause! What can I say? We're not computer geeks.). Once we removed the malware, both headsets worked perfectly on his computer, and my hubby was happily killing zombies left and right. Phew.

And he loves the G231 headset as much as he did the G430--the sound quality is impressive, the mic works well, and the mute switch is easy to operate. So I'm happy to give it a 5-star rating, including a shout-out to the quick and easy technical support, despite my sad tale of the long process to figure out the malware issue--which, obviously, is not Logitech's fault but which I included here just in case anybody is shopping for a new headset because their microphone suddenly stopped working. Before you buy, go ahead and do a scan with Malware Bytes just to rule out the possibility of malware.

title: Great Quality!!!
text:
I've been using an older 1080p logitech webcam for years, and have been very happy with it. The C925e, however, blows it out of the water. The video quality is amazingly clear, and the field of view (FOV) is perfect for capturing a single user in front of the computer. Speakers and microphones both work great as well. The added lens cover is a great added feature (no more tape sticky notes in front of the lens when not in use!).

Integration in windows 10 was easy, and its recognized instantly by all videoconferencing software I've tried.

The unit is a little pricey, but the quality you get justifies the price in my opinion. However, this is likely overkill for most users (especially if you just do the occasional videoconference/call). That said, if you're a heavy user of videoconference software I think this is a great buy. The FOV isn't going to be great at capturing large groups of people, though - you'd need the c930e for that ... but if its just you I think this is a better buy for FOV reasons.

title: Absolutely abysmal for gaming
text:
I didn't purchase the MK350 from Amazon, but often use Amazon's reviews even when this is the case.

This keyboard and mouse combo is perfectly serviceable for home and office use (providing you don't type fast enough for the input lag to wreck your flow)

As for gaming...No. Nope. No way, no how. Run screaming. This thing is just horrible beyond the capacity for words to describe. There is an input lag that simply can't be overstated.
I have tried moving the unified receiver. Still has a savage input lag.
I have tried changing the batteries. Still lagging.
I changed the batteries again. Lag.
Removed receiver, removed batteries, rebooted the computer, re-installed everything (fresh batteries) and said a tiny prayer to the keyboard gods. Lag.

I have had great luck in the past with Logitech Keyboards and Mice, but this combo has clearly put an end that run.

If you're looking for a basic wireless keyboard and mouse combo, this has some nice features for the price. If you're looking for something with a little bit higher performance look elsewhere. If you're looking for even the most basic of gaming functionality and are given the choice of stabbing yourself in the foot or getting this combo, make sure to clean the knife first to avoid infection.

title: Absolutely the best HTPC keyboard yet made...
text:
I have used several wannabe HTPC keyboards over the years. Frankly, I think the K400 is one of the best options (for the price) if you don't care about the illuminated keyboard. But for a true HTPC environment, an illuminated keyboard is almost essential. It has a nice heft, incredible battery life (I use it every day, and charge it not more than every month or two), fantastic range (I sit about 20 FEET away from my HTPC), great feeling keys on an ILLUMINATED keyboard, and a responsive touchpad. At a hundred bucks, I think it is overpriced, but the product is so good, I can't even bring myself to take away a star because of it. I have the older (non-Bluetooth) version of this keyboard, and if I needed another HTPC keyboard, I would get another one without hesitation--I wouldn't even look at anything else. The new one with Bluetooth support just ups the ante on a nearly perfect product!

UPDATE: This keyboard went on sale, so I DID buy another one. But my first unit is still going strong--it has withstood several drops onto my tile floor, and still only needs the occasional charge to keep going and going. This keyboard is so easy to use that I most often use my HTPC just to surf the web, or any other non work-related task. And a big reason why is because of how good this keyboard is. There are very few products that I gush about, but this is definitely one of them. Get this keyboard, especially if you see it anywhere near half off retail (like it is as I write this update). You won't regret it. I don't have a lot of money to throw around, and I don't regret buying another one as a backup!

I LOVE this headset. I work from home so much of my time is spent on teleconference calls.I use this headset with Skype, Skype for Business (formerly Lync), and my Cisco softphone. All sound great. The headset has built in noise-cancellation which works really well. I have a window air-conditioner less than 4 feet from me and my coworkers not only cannot hear it but say that my voice is loud and clear. Also, I live in the city - 1 block away from the LifeFlight helipad of a major hospital. I used to have to close my window when a life flight was landing/taking off and coworkers could still hear it rattling my house. Not with this headset - no interference at all. And it's so great not to be tethered to my PC with with a short cord - the freedom this wireless headset provides is great! And the range is super! My house is 2 stories; I can walk from my office on the second floor/front of the house out to the end of my back yard with no loss in call quality. VERY impressed. In fact, I convinced my manager to get one - she loves it.

For someone who is often on the phone, this headset is well worth the price!

title: Our 3rd set since 2011, it's all about that bass!
text:
This 4th of July and we were watching Independence Day on our LED TV. The poor blah sound from our TV just about ruined our favorite movie. Since we had two of these awesome speaker systems already, I knew one more could solve our sound problem on our TV, cheaply and efficiently. My son has one for listening to music in his room, we have one for his record player in our music room, and we finally just bought one for our TV in the living room. Now with the Logitech Z623 200 Watt Home Speaker System, we get to rumble the house while watching a movie the way it was meant to be! We love that! The sound is that good, as there is nothing quite like THX surround sound! We watched Independence Day again after the speakers arrived. What a huge difference! Gotta have that bass!

I almost left a 4-star review simply because it doesn't have a remote, which is our only complaint. We're so lazy about getting up to control the volume and bass. Also, since it lacks a remote, the only way we can turn down the volume when we get a call or need the volume lower is to pause the TV. So not much fun there, but the great Amazon price, the superior sound, and excellent quality make it worth the trouble. We bought our first set in 2011 for listening to music, we were blown away, and that one is still going strong.

title: Wasted So Much Time Trying to Get This Remote Installed/Working - DO NOT BUY!!
text:
I bought this remote from Best Buy, but wanted to leave my feedback as I have had a HORRIBLE time trying to get this remote working! I initially bought this remote per the recommendation of staff (this was meant to replace my lost Samsung Bluray remote).

For starters, the website is horrible to navigate and not very user friendly (this coming from a 20 something who is more than computer literate). Upon downloading the recommended software, it does not respond and will only show a blank screen. If you spend an embarrassing amount of time hunting around on the website/clicking on various links, you can try to download an "alternative" older version of this software - which did not work for me either. The software seems to hang up without even recognizing the USB connection to the remote.

Don't bother calling the support staff, you will waste more of your time being asked ridiculous questions such as "Did you try rebooting your machine" and "did you double click on the application"?? Was given no real answers, except the suggestion that something is wrong with my Mac and to contact Apple as to why THEIR software won't run. Shouldn't Logitech be more knowledgeable of the quirks in their own software? Why can't they make the process more streamlined and user friendly to set up a dang remote?

I am going back immediately to return this remote. So disappointed that I spend $40 and wasted an entire night for utter crap.

*** There is an app that you can purchase off of Google Play ($9) called MYAV (listed in Google Play as "Remote for Samsung TV/Blu Ray"). It allows you to control devices through your phone. There is a trial version you can try first. At first I was hesitant to buy the full version after the trial expired, but after wasting so much time with this horrible remote, I decided to buy the app. Works great and SO much faster to set up!! **

text:
I liked this mouse when I first tried it out, and still do, with a few exceptions.

After less than two months the ratchet feature of the scroll wheel just stopped working. On top of that the Logitech customer support was fairly non-responsive. They agreed to replace the mouse, but it took them days to respond every time I emailed them.

Pros:
- Looks nice (i.e. not like a robot). It's probably one of the highest quality mice you can get before you get into ridiculous looking gaming mice.

Cons:
- Terrible customer service
- It broke in under two months (you may have better luck)
- Thumb pad button is a little tough to press. It's not an issue if you're using it to toggle menus or gestures, but it doesn't work very well for anything that requires precision.
- Forward/Back buttons are hard to reach. I can't bring my thumb back to press them without changing the position of my hand. This makes these buttons pretty much useless.

title: Try Your Luck Somewhere Else - Look Elsewhere for a Minimally Decent Headset
text:
As an audiophile, I feel that the bass and music volume and quality is just literally O-K, not great and not bad, just meh. If I'd have known this I would've just ordered another Turtle Beach x12, but I wanted something wireless so my dog wouldn't chew through the cords. You miss out on immersing yourself in video game sound effects and soundtracks. You also have to hold the power button down for 5 seconds to turn it off or on.

Speaking of wireless, it's hard to keep a connection unless you literally have the thing right in front of the left side, which is pretty annoying. I can barely turn my head to the side without it disconnecting and messing up the audio.

If you're looking for a quality wireless headset, don't skimp and go for something that's actually worth your time and money, even though it might be over $100.

Edit 4/17/16: The headset is now turning off by itself randomly now...

Edit 6/19/16: This started happening weeks ago, but the connection keeps disconnecting and reconnecting every 5 seconds when you first plug it in for around five minutes. I would toss this thing in the trash if I didn't dump around 90 bucks on this failure.

Edit: 3/21/17: I factory reset my computer, the surround sound switch doesn't work even thought I have the program installed, but now it connects very easily. I'm still annoyed by how long I have to hold the power button to switch it on and off.

I ended up pairing this with a Samson Meteor Mic USB Studio (http://www.amazon.com/Samson-Meteor-Studio-Microphone-Chrome/dp/B004MF39YS) and that made a world of difference.

I had mine for about a year before I destroyed the the LB button. No fault of the game pad. Fault unto Dark Souls. Buying another one of these...maybe 2 if I decide to try to play Dark Souls again.

Seriously though, the gamepad is stout, feels like a Sony controller (plus for me, PS kid growing up), and has a decent chord length. I really liked that for all the games I play I didn't have to map anything, it was just plug-in and play.

Edit after a month of use: Bringing the review from 5 stars to 3 stars. This controller feels like an absolute work out to try to use. The buttons feel very laggy, they tend to stick, and the trigger buttons have to be pressed hard to register most of the time. The buttons are also so obnoxiously loud that I hate using it. I don’t know what happened between my last controller and this one, but the build on this is just not what it was, and I’m shopping for a new controller now.

title: I am happy that we got 4 years of heavy use out ...
text:
I am writing this review as someone who is about to buy my second 700. The one we have now we bought 4 years ago and the "4" button doesn't work anymore. I am happy that we got 4 years of heavy use out of it.
There is a learning curve to this remote. To program it you download Logitech's program to your computer and plug the remote into the computer. You give it all your device product numbers and there is a wizard to help you decide what the buttons control. For instance, you can tell it what devices to turn on and set up when you press "watch TV." This feature works great. It will even change channels on the TV automatically. So, for instance, when I press "Watch TV," it turns on our Dish receiver/DVR, turns on the TV, and makes sure the TV is set to HDMI 1. And, the remote is set up to work the TV volume and Dish functions. If we want to watch a movie, I press "Watch Movie" and it turns on the TV, the Surround Sound, receiver and the Blu-ray player, and it sets the TV to HDMI 2. Literally ONE button to push to start watching something. And,, of course, when you press the top left power button, it turns everything off.
We almost decided not to get a new Harmony remote because we just bought a new 4K Samsung TV that comes with a smart remote. Trouble is, the smart remote won't perform all of the functions of our Dish/DVR receiver, like skip or info.
Also, the rechargeable batteries that came with the 700 had to be replaced after a couple of years. We got some Envelope rechargeables that work fine in the 700. In other words, the rechargeable batteries are replaceable.
Obviously, since I am buying it again, I would highly recommend this remote.

title: Good mouse overall, just some minor issues I ran into
text:
Overall good mouse, as I am a Logitech fan. However there are a couple issues I ran into (see below).

Review:
Small mouse convenient for carrying around. The small USB that you plug into the computer is docked nicely on the bottom of the mouse (have to remove cover where battery is to access it).

The cosmetic condition of the mouse is actually not "new" as I saw scuff marks around the mouse as if it was used or refurbished. Also, the mouse doesn't seem to work well with a mouse pad (normal padded one with a fabric on top). The laser on the mouse picks up the small thread patterns and makes it annoying to use the mouse on the pad. What I mean is, the mouse cursor does not move in a straight line but often angles while moving the mouse side to side. Over time, this gets very annoying. I just stopped using the mouse pad and just use it on the hard surface of my desk.

PROS:
* Great portability (small) and USB dock inside battery area makes it easier to not lose the little USB that comes with it
* Good battery life
* Can work on almost any surface, like a desk, with no issues
* Works right out of the box - plug and use
* Comes with a battery (AA)

CONS:
- Does have some scuffs on the mouse (exterior) as if it were used
- May be too sensitive to use on a regular mouse pad - randomly angles your mouse cursor so making it very annoying to click on anything small on the computer

title: Okay Hardware, Okay Software
text:
From a hardware standpoint, the K400 accomplishes what it sets out to do, which is be a lightweight keyboard/trackpad combination for use with an HTPC or other scenario where you may not be able to sit at a desk.

The keyboard is okay, not something I'd want to do extended typing on but fine for typing stuff into a search box. The function keys default to "special" keys that do things like open your e-mail program and control volume; if you want to use them as standard F1, F2, etc. keys you have to hold down the FN key, something I dislike. The trackpad was a little clunky and didn't seem to always pick up my finger movements. The trackpad buttons feel mushy. You can't tell by feel whether your finger is on the left or right mouse button, something that led to a lot of mis-clicks for me. The trackpad also has "touch click" turned on by default, something I find incredibly frustrating as it constantly causes the pointer to click when I didn't want it to.

Although it's not required, to get the most out of this keyboard you need to download and install the Logitech Options software from the their website. This will allow you to do things like turn off the touch click and set the function keys to default to F1, F2, etc. However, the Options software would not install on my main computer. When I searched for ways to solve the problem I found a lot of other people having the same issue, with a myriad of suggestions on how to fix it. It took me a couple of hours before finding the solution: I had to restart my computer in "safe" mode, then install the software, then restart again to finally get it working. Once you get it running, the software is pretty easy to use and I liked the number of options it gives you. One quirk is that it does not let you access settings from a taskbar icon, something that all other Logitech mice and keyboards I've used do.

I was not impressed with the K400, but I didn't really need to be. It gets its intended job done, but not much more. That, combined with the buggy software and relatively high price, is why I give it three stars.

title: Exceptional value for the money UPDATED 3/7 to DO NOT BUY THIS CAM
text:
I found the green tint that some here are complaining about is the effect of my particular room lighting. In full sunlight streaming through the windows with no lights on in the room, the picture is beyond reproach. Crisp, clear, natural warm tones. I could not be happier with this camera. In fact people have often commented how amazing the picture is. At night with overhead room lighting, it's still exceptional but that's where the hue subtly changes, but nowhere near the green tint some are complaining about as per their photos here. I've also found at night, lighting from a table lamp is much better than an overhead, but obviously not as bright. It al depends on how you want to use it. I have no problems with mine and for the extra 30 or so dollars for the better model up, I don't see how you can improve on this one. Glad I picked this up for the price and not top of the line camera in the range. It's a steal. But I just hope it lasts!

One gripe, it came with a USB extender. Nowhere in any of these Amazon reviews or the product description I found was a mention of this, only that the fixed length of USB cord was only 3 feet long and too short for many people which it certainly is. I went ahead and bought my own separate extension adaptor which I do not need now and wasted 10 bucks. Can't believe everyone here missed that feature, unless this is something brand new and the manufacturer is now adding this because of the complaints of the cord being too short. Oh well, you live and you learn. Now everyone here knows the deal.

UPDATED 3/17:

DO NOT BUY THIS CAM. This failed 7 months after I purchased this and with extremely minimal use. The problem with this cam is that you cannot change the USB cord, it is attached permanently. The cord has failed now. Before the cord failed I noticed in the past 5 months that browsers would intermittently not recognize the cam itself in preferences. After awhile, all browsers stopped recognizing for good. On a MAC, the preferences defaulted to the Facetime cam and on a laptop that is not the always the most desired cam. That means I got 2 months of good use out of this using it once a week. A RIP OFF.

I am waiting patiently for Logitech to get back to me for support so I can send this back to them. It is warranteed for 2 years. In the meantime, I am looking for another cam. I will not buy any cam that has an attached USB cord ever again.

Please be aware that Logitech is posting technical comments on this page about how well this cam works with Macs. They are false. Logitech has not updated the software for this cam since 10.6, 4 years ago. They are misleading customers into thinking this works on present day Macs. It does not, and the poor cable quality turns this into a complete piece of junk. I WANT MY $40.00 back Logitech!

title: Works Great! Except...
text:
Works Great! Except...

This vastly simplifies using your devices and it works pretty well. The only issue I've come across so far is when you don't use the remote to turn off your devices - say you use the Sleep timer at night to turn off your TV, or you walk up and press the TV Power button on your way out the door. In these cases, the remotes thinks the TV is still on because you didn't use it to turn it off. This means that when you go to turn the TV back on with the remote, you don't have the option to select an Activity (like Watch TV); instead you have to select Devices, then TV, then Power, then turn on whatever else you use to watch TV separately (Cable box, Apple TV, etc.).
The only other option is to trick the remote into thinking you used it to turn everything off by cupping your hand over the remote's IR sender window and pressing "All Off". Then the remote will give you the ability to select the Watch TV activity on the screen or by using the button.

So that's sort of weird, but I suppose I understand the logic behind it...

To our delight, it is!

This mouse has a mini USB plug in that is housed inside the bottom of the mouse. When you wish to use it, simply plug the USB into the computer or device and the mouse is ready to go. Pretty simple!

This is a great size for travel, or in our case for little hands. Since our 5 year old was using it, our 3 year old wanted to as well. He was able to figure it out quickly and use it easily. Day one and he could drag and drop like a champ. Technology!

The pictures included are of a 5 year old's hands. You can see this is tiny. Probably too tiny if you're a large handed adult. By for my hands and for our kiddos, this is perfect!

title: Decent headset
text:
I was satisfied for years with my wired Plantronics headsets. I had a hutch on my desk and used that to keep the wire out of trouble and the headset proper out of the way when not in use. However, I moved and had to lose the desk for a more austere setup. I started running over the cord with my chair and figured I would destroy it and all replacements unless I found an alternative. Decided to go wireless with the Logitech G930's generally positive reviews.

Excellent sound quality. Lower response seems limited, but my EQ preferences have always favored a heavy low end that usually press my sound systems to maintain fidelity. Battery life is good. I don't use the controls built into the cups, so I'd rather they weren't there to be accidentally bumped and mess with my volume. But they're probably nice for those who use them. Few lights and nothing really extraneous or "blingy."

My only real complaint is that I'd prefer the ear cups to be made with fabric. The "pleather" used here just makes my ears hot and sweaty. I don't really care for "noise-cancelling" this and that. Really just complicates use in that the user can't really hear her own voice, so she must go into the software to turn up the "Sidetone" and have her voice piped through the microphone and back into her own ears. This has the added irritation that the mic picks up ambient noise you might normally just filter out and pipes that directly into your ear. Fabric cups would be more comfortable and less complicated from a tech standpoint.

Still a good headset if you think you need to ditch the wires.

title: Functional Remote with More than a Few Frustrating Features
text: This remote replaced my venerable Harmony One, which I loved dearly.  The Ultimate One's dock does not have a light, which I miss when returning the remote for charging in the dark.  The remote has a lot of annoying features.  The most noticeable is the lock screen, but that can be disabled.  The location of the play, fast forward, and rewind buttons do not fall within the natural arc of your thumb like they did with the Harmony One.  The Volume and Channel buttons are only illuminated in the middle, not on the ends where the up and down buttons are actually located...this makes it more difficult to press them in the dark.  With the previous remote, my projector would never turn off automatically, even though I programmed separate 'off' and 'on' codes.  I simply copied the programming from the old remote to the new using the web site, and in less than 10 minutes, the new remote was operational, and the projector problem was gone!  I have love-hate relationship with this remote.  Logitech should move the play/forward/back/stop buttons back below the screen where they're more readily accessed by one's thumbs, and illuminate both the up and down buttons, and you'd have a winner.  I've gotten used to the remote, but given its frustrations, I consider it over-priced.  But the Logitech Harmony software and approach still make it easier to use than separate component remotes.  Conditionally recommended.
