title: Beware:  Great...Yet Macabre!
text:
Contrary to my two-star rating, this is a great remote. For me, anyway, because I don't often add remote-controlled tech to my life, so setting up the remote was a once or twice fiasco that, for me, is worth enduring.

The problem is, the sync technology relies on old (outdated) browser plug-in technology as well as old hardware driver plug-and-play technology. Yes, I know this is an older remote, but it's not that old! It's as if this tech was written by a high school comp sci student - no offence to high school comp sci students the world over...some of whom really +do+ understand the Cookie Monster algorithm.

Anyway, to really test the tech before writing this review (and perhaps with a little too much time on my hands and Adderall in my nervous system), I've tried various versions of the software (all downloaded from the Harmony website) on several different machines (both Mac and PC) and different Windows versions (7 and 10; 8 is dead to me) and found the infamous compatibility ballet to be something out of the early 2000s plug-and-play tech: a clumsy performance with plenty of missteps where at least someone always lands on his or her ass. If you're really good with computers (willing to try different versions of the software*), have patience to perform the connection tweaks between computer and remote, or, if you're lucky and don't have any issues at all, this is the remote to buy. Otherwise, buy it, try it, and be prepared to return it.

FYI - I didn't return mine because I got through the setup process (though I'll never be able to unsee that macabre ballet; it'll haunt my dreams forever) and don't plan on adding more remote-controlled hardware anytime soon.

*Make sure that you fully uninstall the software (via your system's Control Panel and NOT the program's) and then reboot. This is necessary because the installation procedure adds drivers that rely on that old tech I was talking about.

The wheel acts like it is top heavy, or unbalanced. I'm about to throw it out and get a Microsoft mouse.

I see online that other people have seen the same problem, and it's not limited to this model. Try searching for Logitech unbalanced wheel. It appears that Logitech does not know how to build a working scroll wheel. They should stick with keyboards, and stop selling shoddy products like this.

title: Possibly the most expensive mouse you could own.
text:
The left button WEARS OUT VERY QUICKLY. Mice used to last for years, but these last about 3-4 months before the left switches start to wear out and give double-clicks or no click. Don't buy this for daily use, but for occasional use it should last a few years. I like that you can download Logitech Options and change the button functions. I have the thumb buttons assigned to copy and paste. A real time saver.

Update 2020-01-14: Logitech support had me re-pair the unifying receiver with the flaky mouse. I told them that it wouldn't matter (I've designed wireless USB pointing devices for specific applications). All of the other features were fine- just the left mouse button failed- AS ALWAYS. So after wasting about 10 minutes of my time, they escalated it. Logitech has now sent me a replacement under warranty. I'm not putting up with this anymore. I am using another m510 that I spent over $20 on because I need a mouse that works. I put a label in that one too. When they fail, I'm going to get a warranty replacement instead of spending more money on this junk. It's a pain. But- someday, Logitech might arrive at the conclusion that it's better to make quality products.

Update 2019-12-18: The mouse I installed on 9-1 is failing after a bit more than three months. Left-click often means double-click. So If I keep using these mice, they'll be the most expensive mice I have ever used, having to replace them every 3-4 months. That is simply ridiculous. Logitech can and must do better unless they want to be known as the really nice cheap mice that fail quickly. I have uploaded a photo of the label I put on the inside of the battery cover that has the date I first connected the new mouse to the PC. It was put into service on September 1st for a PC named AC7. That's 110 days. If this were typical, I would go through 3.3 of these a year, or 33 new mice per-decade, per-machine. WOW! That gets expensive fast.

2019-09-01: I just replaced another one of these and have quite a collection of unifying receivers now. The "old" one was about 8 months old. I used it all day, every day. But still- this is way sub-par. Logitech mice used to last for years under the same conditions.

UPDATE: I bought my current mouse in April, 2018. The left button's failing as of 6/15/2019. That's pretty crummy quality.

UPDATE: I replaced that 2018 mouse with another M510. This one has a defective thumb button. It works if I press the button really hard. Not sure that Logitech even tries anymore. I went to their download page to download the latest software. It had a hodgepodge of Options, and SetPoint software of various dates and versions in no particular order (both 32-bit and 64-bit versions) even though my OS was (supposedly) detected. When I installed and ran Setpoint, I was presented with a dialog box that indicates that I need to use Options to configure the M510. Setpoint installed itself into my tray and runs continuously anyway. I will manually remove it and disable the unnecessary processes. It's sad that Logitech has fallen so far. I've been using their formerly wonderful products since the early 1990's.

title: Better than I was told it would be!
text:
It took a day or so to get used to it, but now I have the motions down and it is intuitive. A great little device.

I use it with a Google Pixel C. I was told that some features of the mouse would not work with a Pixel C. But, it works great! It has a toggle on the bottom so that you can pair it with different devices. It always pairs up in about 5 to 30 seconds.

It fits the hand nicely, is light, but has enough weight to give a nice "techie" feel. If they had made it from plastic it would be too light, and probably would take less of a beating.

If you stroke the surface front to back it moves the screen up or down in relation to the pointer. If you move your finger to the right across the surface, it pulls in things from off screen to the left. (This is the feature I was told would not work on a Pixel C, but it does anyway). To move them back you have to right-click and hold to drag them back off the left side of the screen. Within some programs that feature does not work, but I think that is because there is nothing there to drag, but in others it works both to the right or left side of the screen, and in those programs either there is content off screen or the content snaps back to center. If you can drag something with your finger on the screen, then you can with this pointer. At least that is how it has worked on mine.

It makes using some tablet or phone versions of "desktop" programs feel more like their big brothers. For the price it is a great deal. It has already taken a beating of a few months being dragged around in a soft side briefcase. It shows no wear to the appearance, and works like it did out of the box.

I am pretty spoiled and am dreading the day that, as with all mice, it gives up the ghost and goes to that great recycling heap. I might buy one and stick it in my spare parts locker against that day.

The long version.

I've had this mouse for many, many years. It is quite a great little mouse that has been adaptable across different computers, from a MacBook, to a MacBook pro, to a MacBook air. The multiple buttons are easy to program and can be very useful for many applications. The design of the mouse is very ergonomic, especially if you have a small hand like me. I tried out the large Logitech mouse (the typical one most people go for) and it was way too large for my hands. This is the perfect balance. In case you do lose it, I believe you can always get a replacement, which is great. The battery section of the mouse has a slit for the adapter for safekeeping to prevent any loss from happening. The only (tiny) downside is that after years of use, the mouse does lose the logitech logo, but this is not a big deal at all. For the extensive durability of the mouse, and the compact design, this mouse gets 10 starts, only if I could rate it that high!

title: Good in theory, bad in practice
text:
Nice looking and reasonably priced. Has some notable flaws however:

Driver software is notoriously crash-happy. Microphone noise cancellation ahs to be turned off or you will find the drivers crashing multiple times a day, requiring a reboot to work properly.

Charging jack is notoriously fragile. Leave it plugged in to be safe, because the micro-USB port has no stress relief to speak of, and so plugging in or removing the cord causes strain on the solder points. This is a well-documented flaw in this product's design.

Every few hours the driver/headphones malfunction, causing odd beeping and screeching noises to occur before the sounds shuts off completely. This will require unplugging the headphone and doing a reset by holding down the power button until the unit flashes, then replugging it in and leaving it powered off but charging for at least 2 minutes before attempting a reconnection. I have verified this behavior with two friends who have the same headset, and have contacted Logitech support to be told it was a known issue.

Save your money and don't buy a wireless headset unless you REALLY need wireless. There are bood headsets for under $40 to be had from multiple manufacturers.

title: Best computer mouse I've ever found, and being wirless makes it better.
text:
I love the tracker ball mouse, it seems to alleviate some of the wrist pain from excessive use of the mouse. Being wireless is great. No wire to get twisted, kinked, bent or pulled. Has not interfered with any other wireless devices and I don't have to worry about a short cord.
This is my second M570, I wore out the "click" button on the first after about 4 years of use. Very durable mouse.
One word of advice to new "ball" users: If the ball starts feeling like its getting sticky turn the mouse upside down, hit the mouse into your other "cupped" hand so that the ball pops out into the palm of you hand. In the socket there are several sensors that the ball rolls around on. Dirt and dust can accumulate on those sensors. Take your clean index finger and GENTLY run your finger tip across the sensor, then gently blow into the upside down socket. This should clean out the socket. Now, take a very soft, clean cloth and gently rub off any dirt on the tracker ball. Now, gently push the tracker ball back into the socket. This should alleviate any sluggish felling of the ball movement.

title: Bright idea that lost all potential to shine due to poor design insight.
text:
Quite possible the worst keyboard ever designed for internet TV usage. I bought this keyboard to use with my Samsung TV, which was delayed on shipping for 2 months, but I had ordered the keyboard at the same time; nonetheless, the keyboard sat in it's box till the TV was delivered. Finally I was able to pair the two and enjoy internet TV at its greatest. What a disappointment this keyboard was! Honestly, it's my fault for waiting to use it, otherwise I would have returned it strait away and choose a keyboard with more user friendly features. If you like browsing the internet or are a computer multitask-er avoid this product, it's too clunky. What a shame, this is yet another product that had potential, but it's functionality was sacrificed for looks. Back to the think tank on this one Logitech.
Negatives:
- The mouse pad and mouse buttons are NOT illuminated! Considering that the entire purpose of having an illuminated all-in-one keyboard would be to make full use of the device in a low-light environment, why wouldn't the mouse pad or buttons have some sort of illumination? If no light then at least make the mouse buttons easier to locate in a low light room with a raised mark of some sort.
- No control on how long the keyboard stays illuminated. The timing is too short, specifically for a someone with poor typing skills like me.
-Key layout is awkward. Simple keyboard functions like home and end require the use of the FN/function button and un-intuitively placed, undersized arrow keys. Oddly enough the FN key is NOT illuminated!!!!! What kind of keyboard was this supposed to be again?! Should be renamed as semi-illuminated.
Positives:
- There is a small niche out there for used "semi-illuminated" keyboards, hopefully I can recoup a few bucks and use the proceeds to buy a keyboard that preforms as well as this one claims it does. Maybe I should delay posting this review till I sell mine?
- There is always a lesson to be learned from every experience-lesson learned!

title: They have drawbacks.
text:
Fake tweeters? Really Logitech? Sad, very sad...

UPDATE 5/2020: I originally bought this set about 4 years ago (apparently, based on what Amazon tells me) and the only problem I've had in that time is that the external volume control bit the dust. For some reason, it no longer controlled the volume in the headphone jack. Anyway, I only needed the remote volume control knob replaced but it's hardwired into the sub, so I opted to purchase a new set because I prefer this kind of speaker control setup. $59, but cheaper than the newer version with Bluetooth, which I don't want or need.

The new kit arrives, I plug it in and it works as it's supposed to. However, the volume control dial puts out nowhere NEAR the power the other one did. I used to keep the old dial at around 20% max for headphone use, and now I need to dial it all the way up to around 80% to get full volume (in both cases, with internal computer volume turned up to 100%). The pot is also very choppy, increasing volume in chunks instead of a smooth increase. I would absolutely not recommend buying this speaker kit.

I haven't even plugged in the new speakers, as my old ones are fine for the limited use they get. I now have pair new units should I need them.

Previous review:
Why would they cheap out on the cables? My desk, like most, is loaded up with stuff, heavy, and pretty much permanently in place - up against the wall with about 1/2" to 3/4" of clearance behind it. Should be easy to drop some cables behind it to connect to the subwoofer underneath, right? Nope.

The volume control knob on these speakers is permanently attached to the sub; the sub that needs to go under the desk. So how are we supposed to get the volume control knob UP the back of the desk when the desk is already up against the wall (in most cases)? So the sub has to sit on the desk. BUT the power cable for the sub isn't even 3', making it very difficult to find a nearby power outlet.

I really need this separate satellite volume control option, and I really liked the design of this speaker set. But if I saw this in a store (saw that the volume control cable is permanently attached) I would pass on them. It's not a big enough problem to go through the hassle of repacking and returning the speakers, though. I'm just disappointed that Logitech - who otherwise makes good, affordable products - has gone cheap with cable options, removing an installation option for end-users.

title: Colorful alternative to standard keybpards, with gaming features to boot.
text:
I'm not a hardcore gamer, but welcomed this as a lighted keyboard for my desktop Del. I've become accustomed to the lighted keyboard on my laptop and enjoyed the idea of a colorful keyboard to replace the very standard and flat Dell stock keyboard. I also like the higher keys and traditional feel of this keyboard.

I will say that I was not impressed in terms of this being a premium gamer keyboard, it's more of a regular good quality keyboard elevated to gaming. This fits with the "entry-level" fit in Logitech's lineup. However, the configurability and color controls are definitely a step in the right direction. The keys are not mechanical switches or anything to write home about, but they have a positive feel. The lighting is very nice - you can configure it a number of different ways. I like to just section it off with different colors, which helps me instantly recognize the sections in a darker room. Though I have not yet dumped coffee in it, I have on other keyboards and it's nice to know that this one will survive it.

Overall, this would make a good upgrade for someone getting into gaming - there certainly are many more expensive choices for later. My primary use really is just having a lit keyboard, and the color controls are very nice for me. I like to change things up from time to time, so being able to select virtually any color when I feel like it is nicely cool. The media controls are nicely set off and easy to work and it's nice that they don't blend into the rest of things as on some keyboards. The cord is a nice robust one, with a fabric covering. It's probably no better than any other, but looks premium.

The software is easy to install - nothing comes with the keyboard except for a small piece of paper which directs you to Logitech's web site - and it's very intuitive and usable. There are lots of options for keyboard programming and putting it in and out of game mode.

My only complaint is that the actual lighting of each key can look a little uneven, no doubt due to the nature of projecting the light into many keys at once. But, this is entry level, so it's not perfect but very usable. Looking at priice though, you may want to consider a step up - but a buck's a buck to many and there's no reason not to save a few of them on this keyboard if you're not in competition class. All in all, I think this is a solid choice for someone looking for a standard keyboard with colors, or to get into gaming class without spending a lot of money.

title: Finally, a good full-sized Bluetooth mouse!
text:
I've had a Macbook Pro for a couple years now, and as anyone with an MBP will know, Apple doesn't supply their new laptops with many USB ports. So, naturally, I went searching for a Bluetooth mouse to free up a port. Until I got this mouse, I was faced with a choice with no clear good answer. I could use a tiny, travel-sized mouse that wasn't good for long-time use, or use Apple's Magic Mouse, which although works very well, is so low-profile I was constantly rubbing my wrist and the side of my hand against my desk while I used it.

Now, the Logitech MX Master has come along, and it's pretty much as close to a Holy Grail of Bluetooth mice as anyone could find. First off, it's a big mouse, and raises my hand up to a comfortable position while I use it. It's also incredible precise, so working in things like Illustrator or inDesign is incredibly easy.

Another really cool thing about the mouse is the wheel. Most mice offer either a click-style scroll wheel or a free-spinning scroll wheel, and some of Logitech's mice have previously offered a mechanical switch that lets you choose between the two, but the MX Master goes one step further to offer a wheel that dynamically changes based on use. If you're doing slow, precise scrolling, it will use the click-style wheel, but if you push the wheel hard enough, it disengages the click-style switch and changes over to a free spinning wheel. It's pretty amazing and futuristic when you first use it.

After a long time of agonizing over mouse options, it's really great to find one that does everything I want, and more.

title: Great gamepad plauged by buggy software.
text:
LEGACY POST (UPDATE AT BOTTOM)
-------------------------------------------------------
I've spent a lot of time using various peripherals over my 19 years in the computer industry, and numerous years tinkering before and, as soon as I opened this, I could tell I had bought a quality product. The first sign was the plate on the bottom that offered extra weight while at the same time, just plain looking nice. Before I even plugged it in, I slipped my hand over it and this thing is as comfortable as they come. The pad at the bottom grips your hand while still being comfortable and they've placed the keys in the perfect positions; even the thumb switch seemed to align perfectly.

I've been using other Logitech products for some time now, so was already familiar with the software and quickly took to setting up my keys. I went for a macro approach at first, but that quickly became overwhelming so I scaled back to a keyboard style layout, with the first setting holding some function keys and all of the letters on the left half of the keyboard, the second setting holding the same function keys and the right half and the third holding some more task-oriented keys and macros for opening applications.

The LCD screen is another great feature - I've begun using it to keep a date and time up, along with CPU and GPU stats. It's been great to be able to see when my graphics card throttles down or when my CPU spins up. I can't say they've done a great job of letting you know what applets are available out there, but, they are out there. Although, I'll tell you in advance, be prepared to sort through fifty applets that tell you what your CPU and memory usage are!

As for the actual function, I've used it heavily for work and gaming and haven't experienced any ghosting or malfunctions of any sort. Why then, you might ask, have I given it four stars? Well, my problem with these types of products in the past has been that they offer no clue as to what the keys do, outside of the software display. I've done my best to make these keys resemble the main keyboard layout so that memorization isn't a huge problem, but, still, it's tough.

Why in the world hasn't someone put LCD screens on the keys themselves? I want to see what each key does. Heck, if anyone else were to use my computer, they'd have no clue what G15 does - none. If they said, "Hey, what does G15 do?" I'd say, "Um, eh, let me put my hand on it and I can tell you," or, "Let me pop open this software, one sec..." I can't say I love that. It's time someone solved for that and, yes, I'm docking them a star for giving me something with 25 keys, an LCD screen and nothing to tell me what those keys are in the device itself. Why haven't they added an applet that tells you how the keys are mapped? Why?! It's madness!

Otherwise - I love it.

UPDATE
-------------
After using this pad for a bit longer I've grown to, well... not use it. The configuration profile on my computer gets reset to defaults for no apparent reason on a fairly regular basis now and the profile I copied to the unit has been lost twice - it just disappears. So, if you do buy this, save your profile and be ready to import it again, again and again. I've stopped using it almost entirely. It wasn't until I would attempt to use it that I would find the profile issue, and, by then, just wanted to get on with things so would just ditch it for the keyboard. I began to realize that the only time I spent with the thing was to fix it. I've just given it up and will probably hand it off to a nephew who has the time to worry about it. I can't in good conscience sell this to some unsuspecting soul.

title: Logitech quality, even at $25
text:
I've bought a lot of speakers over the years and got exactly what I've come to expect from Logitech with this purchase: A well-built product that delivers all you could expect for the price-point.

I produce music and play games using my personal speakers, but my wife needed a set for her computer and didn't want anything so extravagant. We looked through the Amazon listings, saw this set going for a great price and pulled the trigger. I was fully expecting that I would be upset with what I heard after plugging them in, but we wouldn't have purchased them if I felt my wife's experience was going to be the same. When producing music, you need speakers that are able to faithfully reproduce all the original frequencies, or you end up with a song that has sounds in it you didn't even realize were there. This is a high mark for a set of speakers and, since I knew these would fall short of that (simply by virtue of price), was completely expecting my wife to be happy with them while I cringed.

Well, I'm happy to say that I don't grimace when I hear her music from across the room. She's completely happy with them and, from what I can hear, they do a great job of producing mid-range, something usually lacking in products at this price-point with a separate subwoofer. I'd gladly buy this set again given a similar set of circumstances.

So, while I'm not going to buy these for music production, I'd quickly recommend them to anyone seeking a better sound experience that doesn't have studio quality expectations. If you want to play games, listen to music and watch movies, and these are in your price range, you won't be disappointed! The amplification is wonderful, the subwoofer is decent and the clarity of sound excellent. If you're listening to your computer through anything less and you move up to this, you'll be blown away. These are the best bet if you're aiming for a set of speakers that cost less than $30.

title: It Works Well to Annoy You...It works "okay" at it's Main Purpose
text:
I purchased a better Logitech universal remote at a big box store a couple holidays ago. That remote was fantastic and survived some drops, falls and normal living situations until.........apparently my beloved soon to be wife dropped it in the sink while doing dishes. Why was the remote in the kitchen next to the sink while the TV is in the living room? No one seems to know BUT...that (also beloved) remote didn't survive. So...shopping for a replacement at another big box store I was NOT liking the price tag to replace it with the same remote. I saw this remote and used the Amazon app to scan a price check. Amazon was cheaper, prime shipping was free, have it in two days. I placed the order while in the big box store.

I got the remote, had to use my computer to get it up and running (minor annoyance) and then on first impression I was happy with the remote for the price. However, we've had it for some time and are both incredibly annoyed at how long you have to point it at the TV to get everything to turn on. I should have known something was "amiss" with a HELP button being top dead center on the remote. It's as if they know the product sucks and decided to try and add a button to fix it. Well, it doesn't. It sucks.

If you stop space and time while pointing the remote at the TV there's a good chance everything will turn on or off properly. If not...some things turn on and others don't and if you repeat the button function you just tried other things happen or nothing happens all the while blood pressure increases and fight or flight responses begin in the brain.

BOTTOM LINE - if you have a Logitech universal remote and need a replacement on a budget this product will do the job. If you are use to one of their better remotes this thing will annoy you almost as much as dropping a good remote in the sink.

title: First, the gooey buttons.  Now, resets constantly
text:
First, I basically love Harmony remotes. The new Windows software is easier than the old version. And their tech support replied to my emails and helped me with a few things. That's why I'm giving this 2 stars, rather than a 1 star (despite my remote being unusable after 2 months).

All of my problems are with the remote's hardware. Maybe I received "a bad one," but here are my symptoms:

1. From the beginning, the buttons were hard to press reliably. They're "gooey." I could never get to the point where I was sure a button would engage after I pressed it (although I had pretty good luck pressing the OK with my fingernail rather than my fingertip).

This is a real problem when, for example, the TiVo is speedsearching through commercials and I want to stop it real quick as soon as I see the show come back. That delay of "Oops, my first button press didn't work; I'd better try again" overshoots the show by so much that I end up seeing what's coming for the minute or two after the commercial while I slowly work my way backwards to the commerical-end point.

2. "Resets constantly." I have to assume that I got "a bad one" when it comes to this happening. If this happened to everyone, there wouldn't be a single review over 2 stars.

This started happening about 2 months after I bought it. I suppose it's possible that at some point the remote fell the 2 feet, or 30 inches from the couch to the carpet below. Maybe that's what started it?

But now, as others have said, it resets constantly. If I come to a commercial while watching TiVo, and grab the remote, the remote is about 70% likely to reset to the "All devices are turned off" state. That means the Mute button won't work (since the remote thinks the TV is turned off), the Pause and Speedsearch buttons won't work (since the remote doesn't know it was on the TiVo Activity).

The lid to the battery case feels a little loose, as though it's not quite on correctly.

Again, if this was the result of the remote falling to the floor at some point, it couldn't have fallen more than 30", and onto soft carpet. I'm sure our 9-year-old Harmony 550 has fallen that far many times, as have iPhones, Kindles, other remotes, etc. It shouldn't have been enough to make the Harmony 650's battery case feel loose, or for it to contantly lose battery power (or whatever the heck causes it to reset).

We have completely given up on this 650, and downgraded ourselves back to the old 550 it was supposed to replace. The couple of problems we have with our 2007 Harmony 550 are nothing compared to the problems with our December 2015 Harmony 650.

text:
I liked this setup, but when I took it out of the box, I was a bit dismayed to find out it is not wireless. I mean, I get why they call it that. The connection from the source audio to this device can be wireless. But the thing CERTAINLY IS NOT wireless in and of itself.

There’s cables connecting from the subwoofer to power (OK, that one you don’t have a choice on, really). There’s a cable going from each remote speaker to the subwoofer. There’s a cable going from the subwoofer to the “control pod” thingie (a technical term - haha) that is part of the system.

On top of that, the cables that are connected are not the longest out there. Given my desk and the way I have things set up, the included cables simply weren’t long enough. I did get it going, but I had to cheat, and stand the subwoofer on a box. The under the desk spot that I keep things like that is too low to just be on the desk. I had to put it on the box to gain another few inches to connect everything. The “left” speaker has no slack as it is, I barely could get it to where I wanted it. I’m using this with a 27” iMac computer, and it’s a stretch. Additionally, the little control pad is not something you can disconnect to run through cable management holes in your desk. The control pad is HARDWIRED to the subwoofer, and as such, I can’t squeeze it through the hole in my desk. I had to run the cable hanging out the front of the desk, which is a disappointment. More than once I’ve bumped into the cable and knocked the thing off my desk. The cable situation on this device is a disappointment both in that they exist, and how they’re physically laid out in length and connections.

Having said all that, I do like the device and how it sounds. Once I got it hooked up, it works quite well. Makes the default sound on my iMac sound much better. I’ve hooked up my iPhone 6S+ to it as well, but these speakers serve primarily as the sound system for my iMac, and they do the job QUITE well.

I just really wish the cables were a) not there, or b) longer / more flexible, or this would be a five star review.

text:
I have been using this keyboard for 5+ years and for the most part feel it is fantastic.
Pros:
This keyboard just feels so light and easy to the touch and it most parallels the feel of a laptop keyboard so that you don't feel out of wack when switching back and forth from desktop to laptop. I truly love the design and feel and would rather not have any other keyboard. I really wanted to give it 5 stars.
Cons:
Had I known they replaced the windows "MENU" key (not the LOGO key) with the function key I would not have purchased it. This truly would have been a deal breaker for me as I am a keyboard heavy user and highly appreciate the ability to keep my hands on the keyboard when accessing the mouse right click menus. The function key has taken its place and then you must press function and/+ the "Print Screen" button to access this menu, which I find takes two hands. Another reason I did not give it five stars is originally I tried to use the "Setpoint sotware" to manage settings but it was too buggy.
I will try a newer version of the software to see if I can make the function key access the menu key with one key press. For people like me who rely more on keyboard than mouse, it cannot be stated more clearly how important the menu key is for quick access to spelling corrections and adding words to the dictionary etc. For the life of me, I cannot imagine what their engineers were thinking when they moved it.

I found a solution to the Menu (appskey) removal. If it is very important to your writing productivity, you can get a program called "Auto Hot Key" and use the following script to create a keyboard combo for the Menu key that is easy and quick to use.
^!m::send {AppsKey}
This script uses Crtl + Alt + m keys combo to open the context menu. This combo is much more comfortable than trying to use my thumb on the function button and middle finger on the print screen button. I hope someone finds this useful and if you do please upvote it.

title: A good camera, but for one small issue.
text:
This camera worked fine, right out of the box, up until Windows 10 Anniversary update. That's because Microsoft removed support for USB streaming of HD video, along with a lot of other things like serial, and parallel ports. Anyway, you can regain your camera's functionality by editing your registry, reboot, and you're back in the saddle, again. Here's a link to the Learn Windows 10 channel in which the producer outlines the regedit steps need to correct for Anniversary Update's blunder:

[...]

My only major complaint regarding the product is that the threaded mount pulled out of it's plastic socket. I tried gluing it back in, but the plastic is of a type which does not bond well with glue. So, out the threaded mount came, again. My solution for mounting the camera on a tripod, or boom was to order a test-tube clamp which grips the camera's monitor / laptop grip nicely. Since I teach the theremin, I have to move the camera from one position in the studio to another quite often. So, I just mounted the camera onto a simple microphone jib boom, which I clamped to a video lighting stand with a professional filming camera clamp that accepts video lighting stand studs, and bam! Boom mounted web cam, no problem!

I only wish the USB cord was about 6 feet longer. No matter, I just ordered a USB 3.0 extension cable, which is 10 feet long, so now my camera is footloose, and fancy free.

I may try roughing the hole in which the threaded mount resides to allow a better bond, and then I'll use liquid nails, or Gorilla Glue to see if that works a treat as far as retaining that threaded mount goes. I'd really like to use a more flexible camera clamp, than a test-tube clamp, but for the time being, it'll get me through.

On skype, this camera really does shine. My students all could now see more of my studio, and pointed out how much better the 16 by 9 aspect looked compared to my older camera's 4 by 3 aspect.

The colour, and contrast both looked good, as well as focus. The lighting works very well, even in mediocre lighting.

I've not tried face tracking with this camera, as I usually set up the camera for particular shots.

A friend of mine in the U.K. has started using this camera, and now we both get to enjoy HD, 16:9 aspect during skype calls.
The compression artifacts seem minimal, and about average for any skype call. That totally depends on your interned speed plan, though.

title: Excellent Handsfree Device That Is Also Eyes Free
text:
This Logitech ZeroTouch is a great device for anyone looking to be totally handsfree while driving. The device consists of a magnetic bluetooth mount that works with a special app that you download to your phone. The mount is fairly strong and should be able to hold most cell phones securely. The App that you download to your phone is really the true gem in this product. The app allows you to activate your phone with a wave after which you can speak simple commands that allow you to call, text, or navigate. It truly is handsfree and more important eyes free. The one downside is that while this product is great it really is a powerful application that is unnecessarily tied to a bluetooth mount. If Logitech sold just the app alone it could work really well for most people especially if you already have a mount in your car. Logitech has still done a terrific job in making this handsfree App... you just wonder if the device could be cheaper if weren't tied to unnecessarily to the bluetooth mount.

*** Positive Points: ***

- Excellent voice recognition that allows you speak your texts and commands
- The app clearly reads your incoming texts out loud to you
- The Mount is magnetic and easy to use
- The battery that operates the bluetooth can last about a year
- You can connect your cars handsfree mode in addition to the bluetooth mount

*** Negative Points: ***

- The bluetooth mount seems to be more of a gimmick to ensure you don't use the app without the mount
- The instructions are minimal (you need to download the App on your smartphone to get true instructions)
- The mount has no speaker so your phone needs to be close enough for your microphone to pick up your voice

title: AVOID THIS MODEL !!!
text:
This model is a waste of money.

Read the other reviews and you will quickly discover that Logitech incorporates planned obsolescence into their mice. Specifically, the click button (usually the left one) will prematurely fail and render the mouse difficult to use. Once the failure occurs, single clicks sporadically become double clicks, which results in strange behaviors occurring while you're trying to use your applications. At first you'll think it's you. After a while you'll realize it's the mouse.

I've been nursing this mouse for about 3 months now. But the inconvenience of having to deal with the inadvertent double clicks has worn me down. I'm now at the point of giving up and buying another mouse. Which, BTW, is the only solution that will actually work once this failure has set in. There are people who say otherwise but, trust me, any fix you administer will be temporary at best.

My last mouse was a Logitech M510 and the same thing happened.
I bought this mouse figuring that the longer battery life meant, a longer-lasting mouse: WRONG.

Hey, you will get EXCELLENT battery life with this mouse. I've never had to change the batteries. Unfortunately for you, the batteries will far outlast the functionality of your mouse.

IMHO, if you've become addicted to the feel of this model, the M510 is basically the same mouse, same feel; and anywhere from 8 to 10 dollars less. There's no point in buying this model. The manufacturer's promise will never come to fruition. What's the point of paying extra money for a product that promises to deliver three years of battery life when the product itself will only operate properly for one?

You want to own a Logitech mouse? Fine. But, for heaven's sake, AVOID THIS MODEL !!!

UPDATE:
I bought a Logitech M510. The feel is slightly different, but you'll get used to it in no time. I'm perfectly satisfied with the M510 and will never go back to the 705. Why pay extra money for a mouse that you know will inevitably fail you !

title: Mouse in the House? Get on the [track]ball and call the exterminator!
text:
This is a review of the Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball.

The 8,000+ people who gave this a positive review before me are right. If you’re reading this, clicking the “Buy Now” button is not likely to be a decision you’ll regret. I paid full price for this on Amazon about 9 months ago. There’s many excellent videos and photos already; I couldn’t do any better.

♦BACKGROUND: Although I’m relatively young (early 30s), when it comes to using computers, I try to maximize keyboard use and minimize mouse (or trackball) use. From what I’ve observed, those who are most efficient in working with computers are this way, and I try to emulate that. I LOVE keyboard shortcuts and regularly challenge myself to adopt more (increased use of the Alt key is my current focus).

♦WHY A TRACKBALL: I took a new position at the same company recently, which involves using more web-based applications (boo). Unfortunately, most of these are not keyboard-friendly, and I was using the mouse much more to the point of experiencing hand and wrist discomfort regularly.

I remember my father having a trackball for ergonomic reasons when I was a child. It was the kind with the huge ball in the middle. I disliked it intensely then, but thought it was worth a try if it could help me avoid developing serious or permanent problems with my hand and wrist.

♦WHY THIS TRACKBALL: When I searched Amazon for trackballs, I saw the best-seller tag on this and decided to look further. I’ve had good experiences with the other Logitech items I own. The design appealed to me: it is completely different than the one from my childhood.

Prior to purchasing this, I deliberately avoided buying wireless mice or keyboards that take replaceable batteries. It’s probably irrational, but I thought I’d be having to change batteries frequently, which would be extra time, money, and an inconvenience. If the wired version of this trackball wasn’t ten times the cost of the wireless version, I definitely would have chosen the wired one.

P.S. If you’re just beginning your search and you noticed and are curious about the *slight* price difference, from what I’ve read, there was a copyright/patent issue with the wired trackball and Logitech isn’t allowed to make it anymore. The difference in speed between the wireless and wired versions is enough to be noticeable to gamers; and the wired version is valued highly by the gamer community.

♦LEARNING CURVE; ADJUSTMENT PERIOD?: This is silly, but I was somewhat worried that I would hate the trackball and not want to use it. I wondered if using the trackball would make me less efficient and if it would be hard to get in the habit of using it. Since I use it on a desktop and there’s no shortage of USB ports, I kept the mouse connected and plugged the Logitech Unifying receiver into another one.

For a few days (not longer than a week), I used the trackball when I wasn’t in a time crunch and switched to the mouse if I needed to speed up to get something done. Although I still keep the mouse on my desk, I eventually got to a point where I wasn’t using the it at all. If the trackball is slowing me down, I don’t notice. Overall, switching to the trackball was far less traumatic than I feared.

Side note: I’m left handed. I’ve always kept the mouse on the right side of the keyboard and used it with my right hand. I would consider myself on the lower end of the spatial-kinesthetic intelligence scale, but using the trackball with my right hand and moving the arrow with my right thumb is a breeze.

♦WHAT I LIKE
•SPEED: As a non-gamer, I noticed no difference in speed from the wired mouse I was using and the trackball.

•PLUG ‘N PLAY: There’s no software to install (for reference, I’m using this with Windows 8). I could have gotten another ergonomic evaluation and had my work order and pay for some kind of mouse-alternative, but I didn’t want the hassle. Since I don’t have admin rights at work, I like that once the receiver was plugged in, the trackball was recognized right away and ready to be used. For convenience, the receiver can be stored in the battery compartment.

•BATTERY LIFE: Having used the trackball at work for 40+ hours a week for 9 months, the original battery is still going strong. Another worry of mine washed away. If battery life was a concern, I could always use an Eneloop (rechargeable) battery. Side note: this gave me confidence to purchase a wireless Logitech mouse for home use. I don’t use the computer much at home, so I wasn’t concerned about hand and wrist strain there.

•DURABILITY: Clumsy would not be an inaccurate word to describe me. I’ve knocked the trackball off the keyboard tray where it sits *many* times already. Usually, the ball comes out when it hits the ground. Despite this abuse, the trackball doesn’t show any wear and tear, and the ball pops right back in. The compartment where the ball sits picks up some dust and debris but it’s easy to clean out. (Other reviews provide more detail on cleaning and maintenance).

•PAIN-FREE ME: The discomfort I was experiencing in my hand and wrist has vanished. Shortly before deciding to order the trackball, I would see the carpal tunnel center advertisements on television and wonder if that was my future. That no longer concerns me.

♦CONS(IDERATIONS)
My hands are on the small side. For a reference, with my hand outstretched, I measured the distance from the tip of the middle finger to the bottom of the palm (by the creases where the wrist starts) as 6.75”. I spread my thumb and pinky fingers out as wide as I could and the distance was 8.25”.

Until recently, the fleshy part of my palm (the bottom part, under the pinky finger towards where my hand met my wrist) would get red by the end of the day on most days. At first, I was thinking that I’d prefer the body of the trackball to be made of something more comfortable. After more thought, I came to the conclusion that the redness was a result of my palm resting on the body, causing the pressure and redness. If my hand was larger or the body smaller, the weight of my hand wouldn’t be on the body.

I have a spare mousepad with a gel wrist rest and decided to start using it with the trackball. Now that the gel piece supports my wrist, the weight of my hand isn’t on the body of the trackball. After a couple of weeks, the issue has largely been resolved. After re-reading some reviews today, I’m thinking about making a foam wedge as described in another review.

There’s only one other annoyance for me. I assume that the index finger and middle finger are supposed to rest on the buttons surrounding the scroll wheel. Although I don’t use the back/forward navigation buttons, my index finger has a habit of resting on them, and I’ve been “left-clicking” with my middle finger. It works, I suppose, but I’d be happier if those buttons weren’t there.

Recently, I’ve been using the trackball rotated about 45-90 degrees counter-clockwise. In this position, my palm doesn’t rest on it and I naturally use my index finger for the left-click button and my middle finger for the right-click button. Manipulating the trackball with my thumb is still comfortable.

title: it is a great mouse, and I enjoy the back and forwards ...
text:
I have owned this mouse for nearly two years and it has always functioned well for me. Under heavy office use the battery will last a month, and for at home use, I can get a half a year or so depending on how I use it. I have dropped it probably 30 times or more and it has survived without any noticeable scratches or damage and that has not reduced it's effectiveness.

This mouse greatly reduced the carpal tunnel pain that I had in my hand from making numerous, tiny motions with my wrist using an old fashioned mouse at work. If my thumb got tired, I'd use my pointer finger if I had to. There is a bit of a learning curve to using this mouse, but with a little time it can be used just as fast or well as a traditional mouse. The right and left click buttons are right where you'd expect them to be so you just have to learn how to move around with your thumb.

Pointer: if the track ball starts to move roughly or takes more effort to move around, pop it out and wipe off the points where it sits as they can build up with gunk.

The only thing this mouse doesn't have that I wish it did was a left to right scroll. Other than that, it is a great mouse, and I enjoy the back and forwards buttons for internet surfing. Also, who doesn't enjoy having one less wire hanging around? The mouse will work from the opposite side of my apartment (approximately 25 feet).

Oftentimes, single devices will quit responding while others continue working fine, making for a difficult troubleshooting process.  The smartphone app is a great idea but EXTREMELY unintuitive (for example, simple TV commands are spread over at least 4 swipeable screens) and surprisingly limited in flexibility in terms of setting up routines/activities -- power on/off and input are about all you can hope for on many activities. title: I do not like to write bad reviews out of the 100 or ...
text:
I do not like to write bad reviews out of the 100 or so that I have done only a couple have been negative and I really like Logitech as a company so this hurts equally bad.

I bought the Logitech G933 wireless headset to replace my G930 wireless headset which after nearly 5 years were beginning to show a lot of wear and tear. I thought about buying a refurbished pair of G930's but I figured its been 5 years maybe they have improved them. Overall they did not.

Good:
1) The headphones have a really long range you can walk about 50 feet line of site from the base more than double the old G930's
2) The headphones work with just about everything PC, PS3, 4, Xbox 1, 360 and come with the hookups as well

OK:
1) The batteries last as long as the batteries on the original G930's I was hoping for an upgrade but eh...
2) They sound as good as the G930's
3) The lights are pretty for about 15 minutes and then you turn them off to conserve battery life

Bad:
1) They feel cheap like they could break at any moment
2) The are heavy
3) They are uncomfortable to wear for long periods of time
4) The band that fits over your head is glued with cheap glue mine came off the second day I had them and I have to keep pushing it back into place
5) The microphone sounds worst than the original G930's
6) My ears get hot after about 10 minutes of use the G930's I could wear for 3 hours or more comfortably with no heat build up

In conclusion if you are on the fence about a new headset buy the G930's or look elsewhere the G933's are just not what they should be, what I really wanted them to be. Sorry Logitech

title: Intermittent mysterious stuck z key kills what otherwise is a great keyboard
text:
Features are awesome - can pair with up to three computers and has an illuminated keyboard. Sadly, this worked great for a while with mac but I think with the latest logitech software this keyboard has been crippled due to an issue where the z key seems to mysteriously get stuck even though I'm not pressing it. I can't seem to figure out what is causing it exactly but I have tried resetting the bluetooth and re-pairing several times but the issue still persists... if anyone or Logitech has a way to fix it please comment!

Update 12/5/16: Keyboard is now completely unusable... any time it's connected to my mac pro I just get a string of z's... I've tried resetting my bluetooth module, resetting PRAM/SMC, removing and re-adding... nothing appears to work to fix it... Such a shame for such a great keyboard... I've written Logitech support so hopefully they'll send me a new keyboard under their warranty. For now I'm using my old Apple bluetooth keyboard and have zero issues. If I don't get anywhere with Logitech I'll probably give the new magic keyboard a try.

Update 1/22/17: Logitech has replaced my keyboard under warranty and I haven't had the same issue pop up but I do get some random connectivity issues but nothing that isn't out of the ordinary for third party bluetooth keyboards. As such, I've been using my Apple keyboard more, which is rock solid.

title: Connectivity Issues Galore with Apple...  Don't expect longevity.
text:
Use this between two macs... a mac pro and an air. For some reason on the mac pro after the latest updates to Logitech Options the cursor would jump around a lot but after messing with the settings in Options and the built in mouse options in system preferences I think I've found a sweet spot for the settings... that is, until Logitech Options gets updated again.

Settings (may vary for you)
- In system preferences mouse screen set tracking speed to a slower speed. I have mine set to right around 3-4 bars.
- In Logitech Options, set the Pointer speed to about 85-90% of the slider bar.

With the two settings above, the pointer has a lot less skipping and jumping around on the screen on my mac pro... for some reason my air does not have the same issue. My guess is because of a different bluetooth chip in the air vs mac pro.

** UPDATE 11/7/16 **
Forget what I wrote above... it may help a little bit to do as I said but my bluetooth on my mac seems to have a mind of it's own. Luckily whenever it starts acting up I just switch the mouse over to the other input option for the unifying receiver and then turn bluetooth off then on again on my mac. This seems to clear up the issues for a while but is not a permanent solution. Been reading up a lot about USB3 interference so I may try to move some things around to see if that helps.

** UPDATE 2/28/17 **
Now I get another strange thing with my mac pro... sometimes the mouse will not connect. Strangely enough when I open the bluetooth preferences using a trackpad, the mouse connects by itself... doesn't work all the time but this mouse seems to have a mind of it's own. My apple branded keyboard and trackpad never seem to have any issues connecting... my mouse is now a few years old so it may just be time to toss this one and start over...

title: Disconnects Frequently from Bluetooth? Not anymore (for me)!
text:
Originally, with an issue I had, I would have given this mouse 1 star.

I bought this because it was the best Bluetooth mouse I could find, but the Bluetooth would suffer from frequent disconnection. That was a huge issue when I was trying to use this to game and I would have to wait for a few seconds for it to reconnect. During worst case scenarios, the mouse would not reconnect and the trackpad would not respond, so in those circumstances I had to use key presses to reboot the laptop.

Note: This was for my MSI GT602QD. Maybe if you have a similar Bluetooth setup (note that Bluetooth is built into this laptop), this may work for you.

That all being said...I fixed my MX Master issue!

Windows 10:
Type in the lower left corner box: Device Manager.
Press the Enter key.
I quickly found 4 items had Bluetooth in their name (or names); there may be more, but this is what I found from quickly skimming the items.

1) Bluetooth >> All items here are Bluetooth.
2) Human Interface Devices >> Bluetooth Low Energy GATT compliance HID device.
3) Network Adapters >> Bluetooth Device.
4) Other devices >> Bluetooth Peripheral Device.

Only 1) and 2) had power save check boxes in their Power Management tabs.

From 1) Bluetooth >> Intel(R) Wireless Bluetooth(R) >> double click on it >> Power Management Tab >> Allow the computer to turn off the device to save power (UNcheck this box).

From 2) Human Interface Devices >> Bluetooth Low Energy GATT compliance HID device >> double click it >> Power Management Tab >> Allow the computer to turn off the device to save power (UNcheck this box).

OK, so now Bluetooth power management, or mismanagement, is disabled.

Everything worked perfectly for about 5 minutes with both items UNchecked (no disconnect happened; error would have happened by now), so I tested both items UNchecked and then alternated Check marking them.

When testing with 1) Check marked, the disconnect error popped up within about a minute or two, on the lower right corner, so I UNchecked it again so both 1) and 2) were UNchecked.

I then tested with 2) Check marked and no error happened for at least 5 minutes, so 2) was not the issue, so I left my computer configurations like this, from this point forward.

It has been a couple weeks and still no disconnect issue with this mouse! It used to disconnect every few minutes when using Bluetooth, so I can definitely say once the issue was resolved, the mouse went from 1 all the way to 5 stars.

Great huge grip, it charges quickly, it's Bluetooth (and also functions with Logitech's nano receivers), and it's just easy to use.

We used this on a 1000+ mile drive recently, and I found myself going back to my other cell phone holder as often as using the ZeroTouch.

title: Updated: You're really going to like the keyboard
text:
Updated 5/16/2016

I said I be back. I've had time to experiment with this keyboard and have become more impressed. It still keeps its 4 stars though. The lack of instructions really bothers me. There are so many features on the keyboard but no way to know them because they don't include a manual or they forgot mine. Luckiest I found a Logitech manual at Logitech.com. Believe me that helped a great deal. YouTube also offers a few demos. Secondly: do not turn off the keyboard. You'll be forced to reconnect to the Bluetooth each time. The batteries are said to last up to 2 years or 1 million keystrokes. I believe it as my wireless Logitech keyboard has been going now for more than 3 years on the same 2 AA batteries. Thirdly: is there such a word ? You only have to depress the connection button until the blue light stops blinking. So the only things I don't like is it's not backlight capability and it lays too flat making it pretty rough on the wrists. Other than that I'm in love with the keyboard and have no trouble giving it a great recommendation.

This is a very preliminary FIRST IMPRESSION review of the Bluetooth K480 by Logitech. I'll be back with a revised review after I get to know the keyboard and it's features.

It works!. I purchased the Logitech keyboard for one reason. I due to some medical problems find myself in rehab hospital quite often. I like to stay in contact with friends, write in my diaries, check and write E-mail and correspond by using a word program loaded on my iPad. I find the iPad much easier to use while in hospital as it's much more portable than my notebook due to size and weight not to mention the accessories. Using the built in iPad keyboard is fine for brief notes and E-mail but not for writing a long email or even an Amazon review. . I decided to break down and purchase the Apple keyboard for the new iPad Pro 9.7. The day I was going to the Apple site I thought I would check out pricing here at Amazon. I alway check the specials and on this day they were offering Logitech products in the Warehouse. Being a long time fan of Logitech I decided to look what was on sale. At the end of the list popped up the Bluetooth keyboard which caught my immediate attention. Bringing the description up and reading through the reviews and of course the pricing, under $25.00, Check the price. I found three different prices here at Amazon. From the $24.95 I paid to two different prices. One of the descriptions is for a refurbished keyboard so be careful. I decided to go ahead and order this to see if I could save about $125.00. I figured Apple wouldn't starve if I went a different route. Now I have seen other companies offer keyboards for the iPad but nothing was being offered for the new iPad Pro that I could find and as a long time satisfied user of Logitech keyboards, mice and other products I felt relatively safe with the purchase. With Amazons return policy it even makes it a safer buy. The keyboard arrived actually a day early using Prime Shipping, there were other items ordered, which has only happened once before which was a surprise. The package is the standard Logitech white and ocean green retail box well sealed without all the plastic and was easy to open. I know that's not too important to most of the shoppers here but those with certain handicaps will be appeciative. It's simply protected by a plastic bag and cardboard raised platforms. There is the guarantee sheets and surprisingly no instructions. Looking closely the instructions are posted on the keyboard in very small print. '
Logitech includes 2 AAA Duracell batteries installed which is a nice jester as who really uses AAA batteries. Enough about packaging.

The keyboard is heavy. Actually heavier than my wireless Logitech keyboard K350 which was a little disappointing. I'm sure to the iPad users this could be somewhat annoying. The great thing about iPads is they are so light. The keyboard is not a standard layout either. This should not be a problem as anyone using a notebook or ultra notebook knows it's almost impossible to put the full keyboard features found on regular desktop keyboards in a smaller configuration. It will take a little practice but indeed is very usable. My keyboard has all the functionality but just an a different layout. The letter keys and function keys are pretty standard. There are extra keys for different features. Some I'm still trying to understand and am sure I'll get to know them when I start using on a regular basis. As mentioned, Logitech included the batteries which like all Logitech products are placed in the bottom. I found the battery door easy to remove but had a horrible time replacing the door into its tracks and cutouts. Doesn't seem to align properly and took way too long to replace. Perhaps it is my unit and hopefully you'll have an easier time. The keyboard sits flat with no way to raise for easier viewing. Sitting straight up in a chair and the keyboard flat make you lean over and after awhile my neck and back started acting up. I think if the keyboard had a couple of adjustment legs it would have been a better design. There is a slot to place the iPad either vertically or horizontally. Once again there could have been a better design. The iPad can't be tilted back and sits straight. Wit the keyboard flat and the iPad straight it's for me impossible to use as is. There is definitely no way the iPad if in a case will fit the slot. This is another design flaw. I use a UAG case which has a built in tilting feature so it will not cause any problems. To solve the above mentioned problems I have propped the keyboard temporarily with a few posted notes pads and I'm using the built in tilt feature of my case to make it work a bit more comfortable. I found that the weight of the keyboard is actually benificial. It stays in place while typing. I have one wireless keyboard that I use that I have to chase all over the desk because of it being light weight and have to use a rubber backed place mat to keep it steady. You'll have no trouble with this keyboard shifting. The setup was simple. I went to the settings, clicked Bluetooth and while pressing the IOS key on the keyboard my iPad found and connected. No codes or anything. You do have to push the IOS key continually to connect I found. There is an on off switch on the bottom of the keyboard which if turned off after using requires Bluetooth connection again. A real nice feature is the multi connection knob. You can connect to 3 units at the same time. I had the old iPad the new iPad Pro and the iPhone all connected. By turning the control knob you connect to whatever unit you choose and it worked flawlessly. The keyboard is not back lit which I'm sure is because of the price point. Should cause no problems in a well lit room under normal use. I have a rechargeable and portable lamp by Boyon and purchased at Amazon which I'm sure will come in handy. The keys have a great feeling and react very well with light pressure. Even with my fat fingers I found the keys easygoing due to the good spacing. I've only tried the keyboard with messages and a brief test letter using Microsoft Word on the iPad and iPhone and both programs worked flawlessly. As stated I've just started exploring the keyboard but I'm quite excited. I'm sure the Apple keypad and the other more expensive boards when available will most likely be lighter and yes have better features but for the price of this keyboard I feel you can't go wrong. I'll be back after some further use with additional information.

The keyboard like all my purchases are at full Amazon retail. No free product or discount was offered for this review. If you have any questions please feel free to ask. I reply to all reasonable and pertinent questions.

title: A really well designed system!
text:
The camera was well researched before any decision was made to purchase. I research just about everything I purchase. I first research the different available items on the internet. Then to Amazon to check prices and the reviews. Then back to the Internet for further reviews and then to YouTube for further information. Luckily this system has proven to work about 90 to 95% of the time. Once again my system worked out pretty well and the decision to purchase at Amazon was made. Amazon doesn't actually have the best price for the camera. Taking into consideration the cost of shipping ( Prime ) and Amazons return policy usually sways me. The camera arrived in anticipation of the arrival of a new computer system. I'm handicapped and must rely on computer service companies to do the take down of the old system and installing the new one. Because of cost for that service I wanted to make sure everything was here to avoid additional charges. Along with the camera there were additional items purchased for the new computer. Those have been reviewed at Amazon as well. Everything went as planned and the new system worked great. Everything was installed and I retired for the evening in anticipation of exploring the following morning. I checked each and every add on to make sure it all worked. The camera was mounted on the monitor by the technician who told me it was a well designed for mounting just about anywhere. It's a simple USB connection and the Windows 10 OS picked it right away and added it to the Apps column, control panel system layout. I'm not a computer wiz kid so excuse me if I get some things wrong. Went to the all applications column and double clicked. There I was dead center in the monitor staring at myself. Now I'm not the handsomest person in the world but I must say I looked damn good. It sets itself at the highest resolution so everything is sharp. The auto focus is right on and each movement didn't cause the camera to try and refocus. There aren't any written instructions and no software included with the camera. I ended up first going to YouTube and found instructions. Then I went to the Logitech web site where I was told that there was no software needed for the camera. There are some simple settings you can work with but they just didn't seem to be enough. Went back to YouTube and found there are software drivers available. Went back to the web and in the search I typed Software got Logitech C920 camera. Yes indeed there are quite a few down load sites. Make sure you go to the official Logitech site to avoid private download companies who try to sell you the world before letting you get close to any software. Been there and done that. Just look up the camera and download and expand the files. I opened the installed drivers and followed the simple instructions to customize my camera. There is a big difference when you take over the default setting. Another quirky thing I found. I've had other Logitech products that once connected requires the registration of the new item. It wasn't until I was into my fifth or sixth use of the camera did the registration window appear. So I registered only to be told that the E-mail address I put down was already in use. Ahh I said it must be from my previous purchases. So I went in as a registered user only to be told that my password was incorrect. Well I write all passwords in a special place as getting on in years I do forget. Sure enough the password I used was the right one. Retried and again was denied. Finally I gave up and found forget password box. The funny thing is that they sent an E-mail telling me my password which was the exact thing I had posted originally. Registration is easy. Put the information in and then another problem. They ask for the serial number. I checked everywhere on the device, the package material and the box. They don't give you a serial number. After a few calls to Logitech and some hold time I was informed the registration doesn't need a serial number. Just bypass and hit the enter box. Sure enough it registered and on I want. Shortly after I received an E-mail from Logitech welcoming me and stating if I include the serial number I'll get free updates and better tech help. By this time I was so infuriated I decided to move onto something else. I'll call back and straighten it out in the next couple of days. As far as the camera is concerned it's everything I hoped for. As far as the rest just be prepared to do a little work to find the available software and the agony of registration.

The product was reviewed without any financial considerations. The product was purchased at full Amazon retail.

title: A serviceable (but blind) Mouse
text:
I have several Logitech mice, including the M185, M510, and M705. This Logitech M330 mouse is somewhere in between the 185 and the 510, in terms of size and comfort. Personally, I prefer a bit of a 'heavier' mouse, so to that point the 510/705 work better for me for regular, everyday use. They are also a bit larger. The M330 is billed as a 'Large Mouse', but I found it a bit small. This is important if you have larger hands and plan to use this all day. I personally found this mouse to be a bit 'petite', and was surprised by how light it is.

The M330 is described as an 'Ultra-quiet' mouse "with 90% reduced click sound and same click feel". I will agree that this is perhaps one of the quietest mice I have used! My 510 and 705 are very 'click-noisy' mice. This would definitely be a good option if you need to use it in a quiet atmosphere (library, perhaps?) or somewhere where noise can be an issue.

In terms of setup, the M330 mouse paired easily with the unified receiver that came with it. I generally had no issues with it connecting or with the range/distance of usage (I did not try from across the room). The mouse tracks well on pretty much any surface I have tried, including dark surfaces. I have never had an issue with battery life in any of my Logitech mice, and thus far this mouse has held up fine to regular use.

BUYERS, BE AWARE: This is why I removed one star - I have a Logitech K270 keyboard and wanted to replace the M185 mouse I was using (which I find to be small and featureless) with this one. Unfortunately, the keyboard receiver would not accept the 330 mouse, and the mouse receiver would not accept the keyboard. I tried shuffling others around but could not get it to work as desired. That was frustrating, and I could not figure out what the issue was. However, after some research, I found that the M330 DOES NOT come with OR WORK WITH the Logitech 'Unifying Receiver' that comes with the majority of their other products. Instead the 330 comes with a "Nano Receiver". Strangely, the M325 mouse DOES come with a Unifying Receiver. I do not understand why Logitech would not just use ONE receiver that would allow all of their devices to be compatible.

Honestly, I considered dropping two stars for the issue noted above. However, I decided that many folks are likely still using a wired keyboard or are just needing a 'laptop mouse', and for that purpose this works fine. In fact, I have settled into assigning this as the dedicated mouse to use with my Chromebook, and for that purpose it has worked well. But folks should be aware that if you are planning to pair this with an existing Logitech KB, it won't work.

title: The buttons go bad, but so what. . .
text:
I've had at least four of these (maybe six). The left mouse button always goes bad eventually. I suspect that people who dispute this either don't click a lot, or don't use the mouse all that much. If you mainly just browse the internet and read your email, this mouse might last forever for you.

Because this mouse it popular with gamers, some users do a *lot* of clicking. In my case, it's programming and Freecell, which means a lot of both clicking and dragging.

If you click enough, the left mouse will start to double-click when you single click. You might not notice it if you're just typing text, but it will show up very fast in computer card came like Freecell where a spurious double-click has dramatic and unpleasant results. It also becomes almost impossible to highlight text, because the button won't stay down. These are the same symptom, really. When you press the button down, it will alternately click and unclick because the top of the switch under the button is dented, and though the button is down, the switch may or may not be at any given moment.

So, why five stars? Because this is, ergonomically, the best mouse on the planet, it's very reasonably priced, and it has a three-year warranty.

Seriously, you need to at least try this mouse. Once, in a period of extreme boredom, I used this mouse to play Freecell for seven straight hours. No discomfort, no carpal tunnel, no ill effects at all as far as my wrist and hand were concerned. I have the mouse sensitivity set at its max. It takes a little getting used to, but I can move the mouse from the beginning to the end of this paragraph by moving my thumb less than half an inch. This makes highlighting text a dream once you get used to it.

I use a keyboard drawer under my desk because it keeps me from aggravating my elbow and shoulder. That means the mouse goes on the little pull-out table on the right side of the drawer. When I used a conventional mouse. It kept either making me bang my hand against the keyboard on the left, or falling off the right side of the pad. This mouse never moves. When I reach for it, it's always exactly where I expect it to be.

As for the button trouble. I have not had any luck getting the mouse apart to try modifying the microswitch. And you can forget about the solutions suggested by Logitech. If they work, it's only for ten minutes or so.

However: I just read a comment here from someone who fixed the problem by putting a piece of note card stock under the left button. It fixed the problem but, understandably, made the button difficult to click. I just tried fixing it with a piece of very thin paper from a cash-register receipt. It worked! The button is a tiny bit harder to press, but it's still pretty sensitive. If the fix doesn't last, I'll just shell out the money for a new one. I often buy two at a time so I'll have a spare to use when the button goes bad -- this is handy when you have to get it replaced under the three-year warranty.

Seriously, give this thing a try.

title: Breathed new life into my old computer
text:
[[ASIN:B003VAGXZC Logitech MK320 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Long Range Wireless Keyboard and Mouse]]

I bought this keyboard to replace an older Logitech wireless mouse/keyboard (model K520) that came with a computer I bought the end of 2012. The computer is running Windows 8.1. The older keyboard frequently lost communication with the PC; I'd have to shake it around the desktop to get it going again and a battery change didn't help.

I was pleased right away with the performance of this product. It comes with no software, no directions. Just removed the dongle for the old keyboard, and inserted the new dongle for this product into a USB slot. This was done while the PC was running. The keyboard and mouse worked instantly.

Mouse and keyboard work in BIOS mode, i.e. before Windows boots, so that's not a problem.

Both are comfortable and responsive and so the old computer is a joy to use again.

There are "hot keys" with no directions on what to do about them. Their default actions on my PC:
app switch icon: Task Switcher
Email icon: Chrome (default browser). No page loaded. With each repeat, a new, empty Chrome window.
Home icon: Chrome loaded without loading any page. 2nd press: Same Chrome window loads its Home page.
Music icon: Loads Windows Media Player
Desktop icon: Shows Windows 7 desktop
FN-F5: Opens Windows O.S. search box
FN-F6: Locks PC
FN-F7: Opened File Explorer to "This PC" view
FN-F8: Puts computer into Sleep Mode
FN-PrintScreen: equivalent of clicking mouse button 2 in the active window
FN-Pause|Break: Toggles Scroll Lock ON/OFF

So - how do you configure these keys:
IN Control Panel\Hardware and Sound\Devices and Printers:
Under "Devices", there is "Logitech Unifying Receiver". Click it with mouse button 2 for mouse and keyboard settings.
You get the standard Windows setup dialogs for keyboards and mice.

So - the answer to hotkey configuration: Logitech Setpoint Software.
Go to [...] and download Setpoint Software Smart Installer for your version of windows. Install

My reassigned keyboard settings:
App switch icon: Control Panel
Email icon: opens Chrome to GMail page
Home icon: Could not reassign to open Setpoint. Probably not a useful thing to do anyway because Setpoint has installed a new "Mouse and Keyboard Settings" icon in the System Tray. So I assigned it to open my Notepad++ text editor.
Music icon: Spotify

One MINOR drawback: as with my old Logitech keyboard, there is no CapsLock LED or indicator. Logitech recommends disabling the CapsLock key, so that's the probably why there's no indicator!

I recommend this product!
