title: Superb keyboard with a short life
text:
Many reviewers have extolled this keyboard's virtues. Although I appreciate every one of them, I won't take your time by repeating them here save for one that requires extra emphasis -- the ergonomic advantage of a flat keyboard.
One of the urban myths that is so widely believed that it drives me practically insane is the idea that it's best to have the back side of a keyboard elevated higher than the front. This utterly stupid concept arose, I presume, when early electronic keyboard manufacturers foolishly tried to make them resemble the old-fashioned mechanical typewriter keyboards on which almost all early computer users had learned to type. The typewriter had to be made like that (more later) for mechanical reasons, but it's literally ANTIergonomic. The physiological position of the wrist is slightly flexed downward. Neutral is worse from an ergonomic standpoint, but having the wrist dorsiflexed (with the hand pointed upward relative to the forearm) is absolutely awful for both comfort and repetitive stress injuries. The [[ASIN:B004SUIM4E Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 4000 for Business - Wired]] actually gets this right, including an attachment to raise the FRONT of the keyboard relative to the back so that the typist's wrists will be bent slightly downward into the physiologic position of rest. However, that keyboard is not great for use with a Mac. Next to this raised-front design, the second-best format is to have the keyboard flat. Note that even the bluetooth keyboard that comes with your Mac is constructed in the antiergonomic format with it's rear edge higher than than its front.
This Logitech K750 is therefore second best in terms of ergonomics, but that means that it's better than 98% of the keyboards in use today. If you can't get a keyboard with the front higher than the back, at least don't opt for the traditional raised-back keyboard that is both uncomfortable and injurious to your health!
I most definitely recommend this product to friends -- often and emphatically. It helps that it works so flawlessly; it's almost like magic in that it works forever and transparently without batteries, but the reason behind the enthusiasm of my recommendation is its wonderful ergonomic properties. Flat is "phat."

Parenthetically, I'd mentioned that early typewriters required tiered keyboards for mechanical reasons. Ironically, there was no reason that they couldn't be made with the top row lower than the front row. I think it just never occurred to engineers in the days before the word, "ergonomic," had even entered the language. Even when typewriters were electrified so that the keys were electrical switches rather than the ends of lever arms, those manufacturers very unfortunately persisted making the keyboards in the antiergonomic format.
UPDATE: I've reduced my rating to 3 stars because of the limited lifespan of the K750 in my experience. I started using these keyboards in 2015. Six years later, I'm on my third one. The keys are durable. The Achilles heel of this keyboard, I suspect, is the battery. It's solar powered, true, but the solar energy serves to keep the battery charged, not to power the keyboard directly, and Li-ion or NiCad batteries have relatively short lifespans compared to the length of time we expect keyboards to last. Since the batteries are not user-replaceable, once the battery can no longer take a charge, the entire expensive keyboard goes into the dumpster. When this one falls, I'll replace it with a wired keyboard or perhaps one that works with simple AA or AAA batteries. And it'll be as ergonomic as the K750.

title: Still the best after all these years.
text: Bought Mine new in 2006. I had a corded ball mouse at first, hated the drag and it was a dirt magnet. Switched to a cordless optical, better but needed to swap out the two AA cells periodically. Then I found this little gem. I immediately liked the shape and weight of the mouse. Wish it was a little larger. The mouse gets used for 14 plus hours a day at home and it's still comfortable at the end of the day. I replaced the factory feet with Teflon mouse skates twice so far. Once when the original feet wore down from being on a fabric mouse pad. And again when I replaced the original lithium ion cell. Battery life was great for the first 6 years or so. I usually charge it once a week. The replacement lithium cell came from Amazon, I got it as a gift. Yes you can replace the power cell in these, did mine myself. The mouse just unscrews. The cell has a short cord and a plug, so an easy swap. I replaced the number one switch at the same time because it was double clicking. I like the mouse that much that I would rather repair it than replace it. So far the mouse has migrated from one machine to the next and is on it's third computer out lasting them and a cheap rubber key keyboard too. I have tried other brands of mice and even other Logitech mice and still find the MX-1000 to be a superior product. It glides very easily and smoothly on my UHMW mouse pad. I like the power indicator LEDs, no surprises about remaining battery power and they also indicate charging activity. The button placements all work good for me, easy to reach and operate. I usually don't notice the clicking noise it makes because it's fairly quiet and easy to 'Tune it out.' The mouse had an on/off switch on it that I only used once to turn it off during power cell replacement. Likewise the reset button on the bottom I only used once during the initial install on the first computer I tried it with. On every machine and windoze OS I have tried it with 98SE, XP, and 7 both 32 & 64 bit I always got basic functionality with the mouse and full functionality once the Logitech mouse software was installed. I really like this mouse.

title: Very nice basic gaming keyboard.  Keys have a high-quality feel.  Spill proof!
text:
This is an excellent keyboard.

I'm a very casual gamer so I don't need many fancy bells and whistles. That this keyboard offers as much and more than I need and is also an excellent keyboard for work and daily tasks means I'm very satisfied. Although serious gamers might want more features such as USB ports for peripherals, this is the best keyboard I've ever owned.

The best feature for me is the lighted keys and buttons. I can see everything no matter the lighting in the room. You can program the lighting scheme in several ways: by sections of the keyboard, in programs that change the light colors over time, and a combination of the two. This is particularly helpful if you have dedicated keys for certain gaming functions or appreciate having the visual aid of color-coded keys for even faster execution of complex game functions. A more mundane benefit is that you don't have to worry about decals or paint wearing off.

Another thing I like about this keyboard is the key feel. The key action is deep, so if you tend to get more physically involved when a game becomes more intense, this may be a help. I have large hands and strong fingers (years of piano lessons) and so I can type very quickly when I need to. The key action is really great for me but if you're used to a very shallow bed such as found on a typical laptop, you will need an adjustment period to get used to this keyboard.

The palm rest is greatly appreciated and once the kickstands are up, the angle is perfect for me to kick back and type or game. The keyboard is also spill proof. I haven't tested this feature and don't plan to but if true, it's good to be prepared.

This is a quality keyboard that has all the basics covered. The lights look great and function well and the key feel indicates quality as well as a great environment for someone with large, strong fingers. It's literally plug-and-play: my computer recognized it, downloaded the latest drivers, and I could use it almost instantly.

If any issues develop, I'll update this review but so far, this is an excellent keyboard for my purposes.

title: A necessary evil
text: I'll start by saying I have 4 or 5 of these around my house. I, on average, have to replace one about every 6-12 months and have been using the M570 as my primary device since it's debut and the wired trackman before it back to the late 1990's. Being that I primarily use a trackball and there are virtually no alternatives in existence to the M570, it is the go-to choice for people like me. This trackball has some major shortcomings, short bumps & falls are notorious for destroying the buttons (all of them). My cats have knocked a few over that immediately lost use of buttons or developed an inability to maintain button press. Over time mouse 1 and mouse 2 tend to develop issues regardless but drops will hasten issues dramatically. The unifying dongle can be glitchy, the newest one (this very one I'm reviewing) intermittently lost connection every 30-60 seconds and switching to another dongle (I have tons laying around but other poor souls may not) immediately resolved the issue. Too many devices on the dongle can mess with it as well and it doesn't help that it runs on the 2.4ghz range that can interfere with other Logitech devices like headsets. The laser lens that reads the ball itself is extremely inconvenient to clean if debris manages to get on the lens, a tightly twisted Q-tip is about the best thing to use. Also, super annoying, the Logitech software for mice and related devices doesn't automatically start with admin rights so your additional buttons don't work in many games/applications that do require those rights so every time you restart you have to close out and start with admin rights. On the plus side, battery life is great and range is good. Also, the M570 is very precise

title: The best basic trackball on the market!
text:
I was surprised and kind of not surprised to find that Reseil had expressed my exact sentiment about this in their title "This is the best replacement for Microsoft's Trackball Optical". I held on to my MS trackballs much longer than I should. This one glides around quite easily, and doesn't seem to need as frequent de-fuzzing as the MS variety. It is every bit as comfortable with the main features I became accustomed to: the typical 2-button + click-wheel and back/fwd buttons, Setup is easy, just plug in the USB receiver, turn on the track ball, and go.

I don't like reviewing right away. This has been in use for over a year. I actually ended up buying another couple for other systems. The battery lasts quite a long time. I've only had to change it once - right around the 1yr mark on my work system. The one annoying aspect is that a trackball will only work with one Logitech receiver unit at a time. You can tie multiple HIDs (keyboard, mouse, trackball) to a single receiver though. To change devices between receivers requires Logitech's special software and is a bit of a PITA.

For the price you can't beat the functionality and quality.

title: Condenser cardioid pattern mic but picks up entire room. Noise suppression 'fix' defeats purpose of being a condenser mic.
text:
Ok this isn't a BAD mic really. But it is not great at all if you don't want sound from the room in your audio, or people yelling down the street for that matter.
There are ways to 'fix' it with noise suppression software. But that defeats the purpose of getting a condenser mic in the first place. That also makes you sound like you are under water.

What I was looking for is high sensitivity in one directional cone. If you're looking for that then pass this by.
It advertises as a condenser mic which is supposed to be sensitive for detailed audio, and it is definitely that. But it also says it's a Cardioid Pick-up Pattern.
A cardioid is made to pick up sound in one general direction. But this mic picks up your entire room, and people outside of it, regardless.
Returning it and going back to dynamic mics.

text:
Was debating between this or [[ASIN:B00JUHDYSO Logitech Bluetooth Mouse M557 for PC, Mac and Windows 8 Tablets (910-0 03971)]] and I'm happy with my choice. This is a newer model and I definitely think it looks better. More ergonomic, new slick wordmark, matte black finish. I needed a Bluetooth mouse for my Surface Pro 3 so the single USB port would be available for other peripherals. I've had many Logitech mice in the past and I've never been disappointed. This is no exception. Paired quickly and easily. Tracks well on many different surfaces (can't be too reflective). Connects immediately when turning on computer/mouse. Does take a little wiggle to wake up after sitting for a bit, but that hasn't been an issue for me.
Other Logitech mice I currently use: MX Master, M705 Marathon Mouse. The M535 is more compact than the M705 and slightly less precise than either. It's very obviously flatter than the M705. I have medium-large hands and it's no problem. However, I've noticed different mouse movement styles among others so I think I should mention that when mousing, my wrist rests stationary on a pad and movement is done with my fingers and wrist with somewhat high-sensitivity. On-screen, far left to far right is only about a 1-inch movement on a desk/mousepad.
A month in, battery is still good. We'll see how much longer it lasts. Will update when battery dies. If I remember to. Probably.

title: Not perfect, but you'd have to pry this from my cold, dead hands
text:
We use this quite a lot. I have it controlling a projector, cable box, audio receiver, and Roku using the Android app from a tablet. I never use the included remote. It makes switching between live TV, Netflix, Plex, Amazon Video, HBO GO, Chromecast, etc. pretty much idiot-proof. I set up "activities" for each and it automatically does what it has to knowing the current state of each device. If I walk into the room with everything off and I press "Watch TV" it turns on the projector, cable box, and audio receiver and changes the receiver to the correct HDMI input. If I then decide to watch Netflix, it know to turn the cable box off and change the receiver's input to that of the Roku AND it launches the Netflix app on the Roku. It doesn't get any easier.

However, despite numerous update to the Android app over the last year it crashes fairly often when I come into the room and turn on the tablet. It's always the last app I used so it simply has to resume. It also fairly regularly fails to turn on the projector and I have to use the "Fix {activity_name_goes_here}" function to turn it on. Same with the cable box when I want to watch TV. Often the fix for that is to unplug and replug the HDMI cable, so I can't necessarily blame the Harmony for that. Since I don't use the remote control I don't know if that would have the same problem, but I expect so. I don't think it's a failure of the Android app to tell the hub what to do.

title: Great concept, but problems with implementation.
text:
Let me first say that I have owned two G930 headsets before this G933, and all of my peripherals on my PC have been Logitech brand for two generations of my home PC setup. The G933 doesn't appear to have any of the strange audio timbre and disconnecting issues that plagued the G930 and I think audio quality is better, but there are some new issues that I hope Logitech will correct for the G933 instead of waiting until the next model. I like what Logitech does, and I only want to see them do it better.

I've had some minor issues with this headset since purchase less than a week ago. As of this writing, I'm currently waiting on a reply from Logitech Technical Support after calling them about the issues I've been having. I've not been able to reproduce these incidents, but sometimes a feature of the headset will become unresponsive. As an example, one time the buttons on the back stopped working and the headset would beep once when I touched them, but audio was still playing fine. Another time, the microphone was muted and the mute indicator light was on, and I could not unmute the microphone using either the button or folding and unfolding the microphone. In both of these examples, powering off the headset and powering it back on solved the problem. The G930 had similar problems from time to time, but it was much harder to get the G930 to reset. Perhaps these minor issues with the G933 will be fixed in future software/firmware updates, but only time will tell. The more pressing issue to me is the headband.

My G933's headband pad, out of the box, comes loose on the right side of the headband. The pad has tabs on both ends that slip under a cover to keep the pad in place, but the pad seems to be a few millimetres too short for the tab to stay in and the adhesive is too weak to keep the pad in place. I have looked online and found a number of redditors with the same problem. Overall, the G933 is even more comfortable than my previous G930 and I expect the lack of fake leather material on the earcups will mean they will not suffer from the same cracking and peeling with age. The rest of the headset feels more solidly built and durable and the easily serviceable battery is a plus, but the headband pad obviously leaves something to be desired.

Based on information I could gather online, it appears that while I am not the only one with a loose headband pad, there are some users in those threads speaking up to say that their own headsets are fine. So, take my experience in context--not all G933 headsets may have this problem, but quite a few more than one G933's headband pad is falling out of its slot. I don't know yet if I'll end up with a full RMA or a parts replacement, and will try to remember to update this when my problem is resolved.

title: Decent in some ways
text:
-I purchased the G933- Stating this since all the reviews/Q&A show up on both this one and the G633

**Update**
Took the rating down from 4 stars to 3. I've had the headset for about a month and finally stopped using it and switched over to my other PC headset after comparing the two. Things I would say I was unsatisfied with was the distance this headset could handle. My computer sits at a desk at the end of a hallway on one end of the house. I can walk down this hallway to about the door to my room and it begins to disconnect. If I turn into a room to the left or the right in the mid of the hallway or even close to my computer it cuts out. But straight down the hallway is fine. I can make it to my back door or my front door (30 ft) but any further outside and it cuts out. Compared to the other PC headset I have listed below, that one I can walk into my backyard, take the trash out in front down my driveway and go anywhere in the house, even to the back end of my room and it does not cut out/disconnect from Bluetooth.

The Other issue is battery life. I charge it overnight and at 9am start using it, and about 6 hours later I can tell how low its getting if I have to walk to a certain area of the house real quick. If its fully charged I can walk down the whole hallway. If its close to charge life getting real low/needing to be charged again, it starts to cut on and off midway down the hallway. My other headset I can charge overnight and it will last a day and a half.

So I have gone back to my other PC headset instead for the time being. The Loggitech G933 I will use for the PS4 most likely, though I'm rarely on it as much as my PC. Again depending on what you are looking for will depend on whether this item is what you want or not. For me it was close to what I was wishing for though it is lacking.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I was about to write a disappointing review due to some odd malfunction but glad that it luckily worked itself out. I prefer to give good reviews than bad.

My main reason for buying this headset was so that I could speak to two groups at once over two platforms. I know some people would think this is a ridiculous thing to want or do but the main reason why is there is a group I game with. Mostly on PC but at times some games come out on console before PC and half of the group can't wait for the game to come to PC while the other half can. So sometimes we end up split and I like to be able to keep in contact with both at the same time. I am able to share information to both sides (Teamwork) plus my Boss is apart of the side that cant wait so I'm able to cover work issues while I play with him, depending if I end up playing on my PC of PS4. I'm able to mix work and pleasure.

When I bought this headset at a near by store, I opened it up and plugged the USB Bluetooth in but did not use it yet. I made sure to download the software first, then let the update install as well. I made sure to restart my PC as well. I made sure to go into my audio setting and make sure it recognized my headset and that it was selected for the mic as well since it was usually set to another PC headset that I've used for the past year and a half. Everything looked good. I got into Teamspeak to test it with my buddies and they told me I did not sound anywhere near as good as I do on my other headset. Also when they would talk they sounded like they were sitting inside a huge metal tin can. So I went into the advance options for the software and did my best to adjust it to help with the way they sounded. As they talked I could adjust it and hear the difference, though the changes were only subtle. They still dont sound great but its better than before.

So once I knew the headset works with the PC, I took out the 3.5mm cable and plugged it into my PS4 Controller. For some reason it did not want to work. The PS4 stated it recognized the headset and mic but when I went into the settings to adjust the mic bar, it did not pick up the mic at all. This made me a bit sad. Since a cheap pair of ear buds that came with my cell phone works with the PS4 controller just fine along with the mic and no extra gadgets to get it to work. Come to find out for some reason the wire decided it wanted to get its act straightened out when I was at the point of thinking to return it to the store.

I then decided to test it on my phone. Again the 3.5mm cable did not work with the mic for some reason the night before as I tested it. But when I played music through my phone this morning, it sounded amazing. I wanted to grab a towel, go to the beach and say forget the world when I heard how awesome it sounded over these headsets. It wasnt till a few hours later I stood up at my table and heard something in the sound change. Not sure what did it to make the 3.5mm cable start to work properly but now I could hear the background sounds around me and myself mumbling "what the heck" over the headset. I decided I test it out and call a friend and sure enough the mic starts working out of no where.

So at this point I hook it back up to the PS4 and it works!!! I am so happy at this point because my time and money has not been wasted. I went into PS4 settings and the mic bar showed I was talking and I was able to adjust it. Then I jumped into Teamspeak as the USB bluetooth was still in the PC. The mic worked on both ends. Sadly no one is on the PS4 at the time to test out how I sound and how they sound when they talk but the ones who were on Teamspeak said I sounded a lot clearer now as well. Again I didn't touch or change anything, just stood up while the 3.5mm cable was connect to my phone and heard the sound change a bit, so guessing just some faulty kink in the wire.

I was tempted to buy it off Amazon because the warranty that you can add on with this headset, when hitting the purchase button, goes as long as 4yrs but a lot of the reviews over people having to return items through "that warranty program", sound bad and just not good. I know the store by me offers one, though half the years as the one on here but I know if something goes wrong, I will get all my money back or I can just exchange it for a new one, or the next best thing and pay the difference. It was also slightly cheaper, where usually I find the better deal on Amaszon. Plus there is no time to wait for anything to be sent off and received. I always try to look at things from as many angles as possible. Though I love amazon and prefer to do most of my shopping through them.

I don't have many things to compare these headsets to besides the headsets I have, which were a gift a year ago, so I will use that. The other headsets I have are the Afterglow Universal Prismatic Wireless Headset

Pros to Logitech G933

Material used for the headphones: I prefer these to the artificial leather like covers of my other headset. With these the area around my ears don't get warm/hot after a while and I don't feel I have to take a break from the G933. They are comfortable to ware for a long time.

Snug fit: These headsets fit my head very snug. I was worried at first when trying to fit it over it might break. I take my time putting it over my head because I don't want to force it open to much and it messes something up.

Audio off cell phone and PS4 Sound great: I can't believe how great it sounded. The bass was awesome but the only thing I listen to music off my phone with is some rinky dink headphones that came with my cell. But the PS4 and cell phone sound outstanding audio wise with music at least. I havent had a moment to test how my friends sound or how I sound to them yet but I hope to update this when I do.

I love the fact that this can be use simultaneously with more than one item: Most headsets I come across is either wired or wireless. With this you sort of have both if you want it. You can listen to music off your phone with the 3.4mm cable and chat while you play on the ps4 with the bluetooth or so many other options with the fact you have to connection choices. My Afterglow Universal Prismatic Wireless Headset does have a line in plug and a plug for xbox but the issue if the USB plug is to fat to fit into the USB port in the PS4 due to the design case of the PS4. Otherwise my older headset would work for PS4 but still It would not be able to talk to two groups on two different platforms.

The wires that plug into the headset are great: Not only are they long but they are not made out of rubber to where they get tangled easily. They are covered in what im guessing is braided cotton/nylon. The Wire to charge the headset is longer than the 3.5mm cable but they are made with the same material so again they dont get tangles up with each other either. It's nicely made, very firm and material does not look good cheap.

Simple flip up mic: I like the fact the mic slides back into place easily. Though the headset is still new to me, finding it when im looking at the headset in my hands is another thing, because it blends in so well. You can easily flip it up to mute it if you like or flip it back down to start talking again.

--Cons--

The audio on the PC does not sound as good: Whether its my friends talking on Teamspeak or playing a video or music off my computer, the audio just does not sound as good compared to playing music over the phone or playing audio over the PS4. I don't have this issue with my other PC headset. Bass sounds fine, other peoples mic's sound good, and video and music sounds great. So not sure what could cause that and again I adjusted the equalizer that comes with the software and it seems no matter what I pick and adjust it just doesn't sound that great. Videos sounds like they are being played down an empty hallway off my PC.

Headset fits better backwards than the way its suppose to. Some people may find that these headsets slide off easily if you look straight up for a while or straight down for too long. Though it feels like it fits snug, for some reason it slides easily. To help a bit with this I have to make sure the top of the headset is closer to the front region of my skull, like where a girl would wear a headband. If its too close to the center or a little bit more towards the back, quick movements may send them falling off. Its not entirely comfortable with that band so far forward but its not a deal breaker for me.

--Overall I am giving it 4 stars at the moment. I will would like to see in a few months how it plays out. If anything changes, both good or bad I will update. I wanted to give it 5 stars but since I use my PC far more than anything else, I was a bit disappointed with the sound quality and for the price I would expect the quality to be outstanding an all platforms. But still there is no headset out there yet that is perfect and can do everything all in one. But this one is fairly close. If my other PC headset's Bluetooth connector didn't have such a ridiculous design it would work with the PS4 (Will include pics of the comparison of both USB adapters) . I've seen some people even cut away parts of it so that it can fit into it but im not that desperate to destroy something to make it work. Again this headset does what I was looking for, which is hard to find in other headsets. If you are willing to give up some quality over what it can do then this headset is great. Had I wanted just huge headphones with mic capability for my cell then I'd definitely give this a 5 star. If you want it just for PS4 then I'm sure you will be pleased.

This keyboard is perfect for a multimedia center, either with a Desktop or a Console. I would not suggest using this as an alternative to a keyboard for gaming or for typing. All in all, great buy!

3. Connectivity. We've never lost connection since we first set it up, and everything has worked flawlessly. All of the different functions that you could possibly need from a keyboard (and more, like the zoom and video playback options) are there, making your life so much simpler and easier.

Whether it's for a desk top or for an entertainment purpose like ours, this is a great buy, and we hope you enjoy it just as much as we do!

title: Isn't perfect, but makes up for its quirks with great sound quality, variety of extra features, and a superb wireless experience
text:
My previous headset was a HyperX Cloud, and while I love it, I decided that I wanted a wireless headset. My decision came down to the Razer Man O' War and the G933, and ultimately I went with the G933 do to a sudden 25% price drop.

So on to the review, which will only include the headset's PC experience.

I'm no audiophile, but the sound is great. The surround sound sounds strange (say that 5x fast) at first when watching videos, but I grew accustomed to it and then stereo sounded empty. The Dolby Surround sounds much more accurate that the Razer Surround that I was previously using, and overall just sounds "cooler" for lack of a better word. Explosions were deeper and lighter sounds were distinct, yet still accurately positioned.

The Mic is a few steps down from the Cloud, (and with the wireless that's to be expected) but I have an AT2020 so that isn't an issue for me.

The wireless is phenomenal. I can go to the other side of my house through multiple walls and the connection stays strong. I was blown away. I get probably 10 hours of battery with the lights on a slow breathing. Very impressive.

The comfort of the headset is also really solid considering how big the thing looks. It feels light and while it might not be as good as the Cloud for marathon sessions it is still very comfortable. The rotating ear cups makes it harder to scratch your ears, because instead of the headset simply lifting up, it tries to rotate and gets pushed off your head. I got used to it though. The build quality itself feels low, but that might be do to the removable back plates on the ear cups. Also coming from the HyperX Cloud, which is mostly metal, plastic is going to feel lower quality.

The buttons are kind of hit and miss. I often press the wrong ones but I've set them up as media keys so I can walk around my house and keep jamming to tunes, but still be able to pause it if I need to talk to someone. The volume slider is also very sensitive and I find myself nudging it accidentally. I also find it annoying that it is simply a glorified shortcut to changing your computers volume, rather than being a volume control for the headset itself. (When used on PC at least)

I've heard (and seen) lots of people having issues with this staying on their head. I have had zero issues. While it isn't as snug as my Cloud was, I still never had an issue with it falling off. I was even able to do push-ups without losing it. The extra cables are nice (including a very quality braided micro USB, that was a nice surprise) but I haven't tried the mixing between multiple devices.

Final Thoughts:

While the G933 isn't perfect, it more than makes up for its quirks with great sound quality, variety of extra features, and a superb wireless experience.

title: Could someone help me with this?
text:
I just received this Webcam yesterday and it will not work with my computer. Before I return it maybe someone here can help me, since I can't seem to find Logitech support on the issue. The sound works perfectly. The video doesn't work at all.
My computer has both USB2 and USB3 ports.
The device is detected (the model pulls up fine in the logitech software, but when photo capture is clicked, it says "No Logitech webcam detected").
In Skype, it says, "install a webcam to use video".

In Device Manager, the Webcam shows up in Imaging Devices (which goes away if the webcam is unplugged from the USB), as well as in the Universal Serial Bus Controllers. I have both Logitech Mouse and Keyboard, both of which perfectly plugged into USB ports.

In Control Panel>Devices and Printers, the HD Webcam C525 shows up with image of a webcam. Using Troubleshooting, it says: "Logitech USB Camera (HD Webcam C525) is an older USB device and might not work with USB 3.0", below this, "Plug the device into an available USB 2.0 port and click Next". It is plugged into the 2.0 USB slot (Legacy USB is enabled in the BIOS).

I have tried plugging it into every single one of 8 available USB slots on the computer, with the same result in each, and at least some are USB 2.0 slots. Both Logitech Mouse and Keyboard are of the same age as this webcam model, I've been using them since Windows 7.

There is nothing wrong with the Webcam functionality. I tested it on my Microsoft Surface Pro, the original model, and it works well and is instantly recognized. There is a built in webcam and microphone in the Surface Pro however, so I have no need of a webcam on it. I need one for my desktop PC.

Is there ANYTHING I can do to make this webcam work on a newer PC system using Windows 10? I would be really grateful, because I would rather not have to return it to Amazon. Thank you.

title: Amazing QUIET keyboard!!!
text:
VERY QUIET KEYBOARD.

I had to start my review by stating that as those were the key words I was searching for across the internet and that tidbit of info was always buried inside the more in-depth description of products, so I thought I would make it easy anyone looking for a quiet keyboard.

Back to the review. I cannot express how much I love this keyboard. I've been searching for a quiet keyboard for months and have come up empty until one of our IT guys suggested this one. For those that are not looking to drop this kind of cash for a WIRED keyboard - unless you absolutely need a wireless keyboard - GET THIS!!

PRO's:
-Super quiet. I can type an email while not muted on a conference call and not be "that person" typing away.
-It is illuminated. Do you know how hard it is to find a QUIET illuminated keyboard that is NOT made by Apple? HARD.
-The keys have a great feel to them. I don't really know how to elaborate on that - I feel like I type faster and more accurately now, but that is probably just in my mind. :)
-I've seen some reviews stating that there is no way to tell if the CAPS lock key is on - this is not true. There is an indicator light towards the lower right side of the keyboard that lights up if CAPS lock is on.

CON's:
-A bit pricey for a keyboard. This is a non-issue for me as I have searched high and low for months.
-It is wired. Again, a non-issue for me since I'm sitting at my desk 98% of the time.
-I miss the "Calculator" hot key that opens the Calculator automatically. Annoying, since I am used to Logitech having that feature, but not the end of the world.
-The delete button is bigger and placed differently. Again, annoying to re-learn, but not a deal-breaker.

I use this with a Dell Laptop, have not tried it with my MacBook and probably won't. No connection or driver issues thus far.

COMPLETELY WORTH THE MONEY!

title: Very difficult to set up, but worth the hassle
text:
I was really looking forward to consolidating remotes. I have a pretty simple setup:
- LG Smart TV
- Roku 3
- Yamaha soundbar
- Comcast cable box

I am a very technically savvy person and this remote was nothing but problems. I definitely wouldn't recommend it to someone who isn't savvy enough to troubleshoot when something goes wrong.

When I initially went to set it up on my phone, my phone could see the Harmony hub but refused to connect. After several restarts of the app and a reset of the hub, it still didn't work. I gave up and used the mac client on my computer instead. The mac program is just awful. It's silverlight based and had my fans roaring. I was able to find all of my devices in the app and set up my activities fairly quickly. When I went to use the remote, it only intermittently worked. I decided to try setting it up again via the mobile app a day later and it finally decided to connect. Again, I set everything up fairly quickly but found that it was just way too slow. It took about 10 seconds to get my TV turned on, and then another 20 seconds for the arrows on the remote to work with the Roku.

Edit: I was about to return it, but then found a setting to reduce the time delay on the TV (30 seconds, set it to 5 instead). The UI here is terrible - you have to change the setting, then hit the forward button to save it. If you try to go back, the setting gets lost.

Now that everything is finally up and working, I'm pretty pleased with it. Do not buy this unless you are very comfortable with technology and trying to do things several different ways.

title: Good once configured on a mac
text:
I'm a mac user, and didn't care for this mouse at first. I found it too sensitive and the middle buttons didn't do what I expected. I downloaded Logitech's driver for the mouse, and initially thought I couldn't configure any of these options. It turns out, everything can be configured, but the UI kind of stinks. The options are as follows.

Middle/Windows button: Mission control, app expose, launchpad, look up, middle button, smart zoom.
Horizontal Scrolling: switch between pages, switch between desktops, horizontal scrolling
Scroll button: Smart zoom, app expose, launchpad, look up, middle button, mission control

I selected mission control on the windows button, horizontal scrolling on left/right press of the scroll button, and middle button for a regular click of the scroll button.

There is also an option to reduce the pointer speed which I used.

I use this mouse for travel use. I don't find it all that ergonomic and wouldn't want to use it daily. I have small hands and find it a little difficult to click on the middle button.

I've only had it a few weeks and I haven't yet had to replace the batteries.

Overall it's not bad but not a contender for my daily mouse.

title: it's a mouse and it's built pretty well. But it's smaller than a traditional desktop ...
text:
So, it's a mouse and it's built pretty well. But it's smaller than a traditional desktop mouse. How much so? Well, the full sized laser USB mouse it is replacing is 4.75 inches long, 2.375 inches wide, and shaped like a smoothed rectangle with rounded edges. You know the type. This little lady is 4.00 inches long and 2.5 inches wide and shaped a bit like a chicken's egg sliced down the middle from top to bottom. The fat part of the egg is in the back of the mouse, and sits in your palm. This is a smallish mouse, especially if you have large hands - something I'd expect to see being used with a laptop. It is, however, made well and sports the typical Logitech quality & features.

It has very good DPI resolution for fine control and a laser that isn't the ubiquitous red. In fact, when I first plugged it in & turned it upside down expecting to see the laser light up as indication my OS had found it, I saw nothing which is what it puts out when its running - "invisilaser."

All in all I'm happy but it's smaller than I expected. Five stars for operation, four stars for size.
-----
So, it's 20 April 2017 & I've had this mouse for some time now. It continues to operate flawlessly with one minor detail that isn't a mouse problem. We have two dogs and their shedding hair is something we have to routinely deal with. One area where the hair ends up is on my mouse pad. A couple of times over the last couple of years a dog hair has ended up inside the laser well of the mouse and that causes the mouse response on screen to become erratic. Basically the hair reflects the laser light back into the receiver and that confuses the sensing algorithm. At first I thought the mouse had gone tango uniform. When I discovered the problem and understood the fix (remove the hair with tweezers) all was copacetic. It is still running hard and a great pointing device. 4 + stars!

title: Better than your average remote
text:
Due to the large amount of customer complaints and confusion, my local cable company (TimeWarner/Spectrum) decided to remove the All On / All Off button from their remotes. Now you have to turn each device on individually. Moderately annoying so I purchased this All-In-One remote. Since it does the job better than the old cable remotes it gets four stars. It turns everything on and off faster however it isn't perfect and has already led to the dreaded some devices off when they should be on problem.

Programming was simple enough using a computer and internet connection although, if you haven't saved your AV equipment manuals, prepare to go behind the equipment to get the exact model numbers. My Sherwood SB-308 SoundBase is not in the Logitech database so I had to use the Sherwood remote to program the Logitech remote. Not hard and the on-sceen instructions are very clear. The set-up process requires Microsoft Silverlight which I had to download, not a big deal in itself but the program caused my laptop to heat after a few minutes and the computer fans went to maximum. Once I quit Silverlight the laptop cooled off and went to normal.

Some of the Netflix functions of my Visio SmartTV either aren't there or hidden in buttons I don't recognize yet. However finding Netflix programming and playing it is easy enough. Getting back to the submenus not so easy.

The main problem so far is when I switch from Netflix back to cable (going from cable to Netflix is perfect). The remote turns the Sherwood speaker off which requires me to go thru a couple of menus on the remote to rectify. And then a couple menus back so the remote behaves normally again. A small annoyance.

title: Outstanding!
text:
I am very pleased with this remote. As with almost everything I purchase, I looked at many different one's and checked out some reviews before I made up my mind. This is perfect for me as I only have 4 devices that I need to operate, as well as the fact that anything too advanced would have my wife pulling her hair out if she tried to use it. It has a very straight-forward layout/design and is very easy to use. I love the fact that I can have full function control over all of my devices with one remote, something that has been sorely lacking in other universal remotes I've purchased in the past.
I had to do a small amount of customization to the controls to have that with a couple of my devices but, it's very easy to do and having full control over what buttons will do what is just awesome. In the software you have a picture of the remote along with a list of all of the commands from each device and you can drag and drop commands to the button you want to assign it to. If a command is missing it's extremely easy to teach that new command to the remote from the original and you have the same control over the new command/commands.
The one I received is the glossy black, which I thought someone said was the 300i but, I ordered the 300 so, I don't what's up with that. The only negative points I could make are that it's pretty slippery and can be difficult to hang on to at times and when selecting my TV input I can't just hit input then use the directional buttons to choose what I want, I have to hit input repeatedly to get it to where I want it, which is something I don't really like but, it's a very small drawback.
At first I was having trouble getting it to complete the sync within the software so I couldn't do any customization, it had done enough that it worked but, I wanted and needed to customize a bit. I soon discovered that I just needed to pull one of the batteries out for a few seconds then put it back and try again, it worked perfectly after that. So, if you're having trouble give that a try.

title: The Search Continues for a Microsoft Trackball Alternative ...
text:
First off, let me say this - I REALLY wanted this thing to work. I'm on the computer a LOT. Video & photo editing, website design, writing ... my life revolves around interacting with my Thinkpads. Having a good mouse and/ or other input device is critical.

Also, I used to own the [[ASIN:B00005853Z Microsoft Trackball Explorer]]. It was perfection - almost 20 years ago! And now we've regressed back to Dark Mouse Ages. Those of you who've used the Microsoft Trackball can actually understand why they're fetching $650 USED. <--- That's right - USED.

PROS of the Logitech M570

* It's cheap. If you don't like it, you're not out a fortune. You can write the dang thing off.
* Looks Okay - The black and blue colors are kind 'a cool.

CONS (and this is when comparing it to the Microsoft Trackball)

* Too Small - The ball is too small. It needs to be larger.
* Thumb Ball approach is Bad Idea - Having to use the thumb instead of fingers to move a ball doesn't work. It's too twitchy. You simply don't have the control you do with a larger ball that you an move with your fingers or palm.
* Angled Wrong - One way to SLIGHTLY improve the way it works is by sticking a wedge under the left size. It makes the wrist position somewhat more comfortable. (This is when the device rises from being a 1-star failure to a 1.5-star "almost barely usable"

Bottomline: If you're wanting a really good trackball on the order of the Microsoft Trackball, this doesn't even come close. :-(

The controls worK great. Volume, pause, play, stop, forward, and back. I live the slim profile, which I haven't found a suitable replacement yet so I'll stick with these until they break. I also use then when biking and in the cold. Although not THE BEST for, they make decent ear muffs in chilly weather. title: Perfect Mouse For Fun and Work
text:
I work from home on a MacBook Air and I wanted a mouse that would not only get the job done, but brighten up my desk as well. After looking at what seemed like a hundred mouses, I settled on this one, and I'm so glad I did.

The packaging was great and even included an easy open tab in back so that I didn't have to cut through all that plastic to free the mouse. Once I got it out, I literally followed two steps to get the mouse up and running - pull tab to activate the battery and plug in the receiver.

I literally was up and running in seconds! I didn't need anything fancy (trackball, etc.), so this mouse works perfectly. It does run a little on the small side, so if you want your entire hand to rest on the mouse, then you'll want to look for a bigger one. For me, I like the smaller style and find that it works perfectly with my MacBook Air.

The mouse also has an on/off switch on the bottom so that you don't waste the battery, though the reported battery life is really good.

One important note: The receiver is NOT unifying. If you are looking for a unifying receiver, don't get this mouse (or make sure you already have a unifying receiver - one that connects your Logitech devices). I didn't need one so this didn't impact my purchase decision, but definitely keep it in mind if that's something you want.

Overall, I'm really happy with this mouse and love the fox design! The colors are vibrant and it actually makes me want to use the computer more.

title: Good Mouse.

Totally awesome feature and I absolutely love this mouse now!

Works on pretty much all of the surfaces I have used it on. Including the counter, couch, wood coffee table, blanket, and book. I haven't tried it on a glass surface.

I will definitely purchase this mouse again for my desktop.

title: Fantastic Webcam for Streamers
text:
I bought this camera because a lot of streamers on Twitch suggest it for use, and because my older webcamera was also a Logitech, albeit a much, much older product.

I'm really happy with the camera itself. It was a bit confusing at first because I didn't realise the base unfolded and turned into either a stand or a clamp to use on your monitor or laptop; the fact that it does have its own clamp was really helpful, because I was looking into stands and clamps, and a lot of them just weren't compatible with my desired set up.

The clarity of the C920 is pretty amazing. When getting into the advanced options, you can really combat a lot of issues with your lighting without having to resort to 3rd party programmes or buying additional lighting right away - you always can buy special lighting set ups, but the advanced options can narrow down the amount of additional lighting you need.

It works great with OBS, which I've been able to use it with myself. I've had only one glitch with it, and it came from the fact that I had accidentally cloned a scene and it had the camera running in two different places; once I deleted the extra scene, it went back to working as intended. I've seen it working with ElGato Capture via friends' streams, but I haven't gotten my own ElGato just yet, so I can't 100% state how well it works with it just yet.

I strongly suggest the C920 to anyone whose considering using a face cam for streaming, because the cost for the camera and the features and flexibility are worth it. While there has been one more upgrade released since the C920 has come out, the price just kills the worth of the newer camera right now - leaving the C920 as a worthwhile option for someone just starting up their stream.

title: A fantastic keyboard with customizable lighting effects and programmable function keys
text:
Installation:
1) Download and install the Logitech Gaming Software (LGS) from the Support page at the Logitech website. Be sure to select the current version of the Operating System you are using.
2) Following installation you can register your new keyboard if you wish. Restart your computer if necessary.
3) Plug in your Logitech G213 and the software should detect and install your keyboard automatically.

Positives:
1) Plastic, but sturdy compared to some other brands. You'll need to put some effort into your ragequit to break this.
2) RGB keys with lighting effects. Included with standard fixed colors and breating effect is a new Color Cycle feature. This keeps all the keys lit but cycles the colors from one color to another. A similar Color Wave effect allows you to cycle colors from right to left, left to right, and center-out. Personally, I like the Color Wave the best. You can also adjust the speed as which the collors change.
3) The mainstay of any gaming keyboard, the "Game Mode" key in the shape of a joystick is included. Often it is used to disable the Windows key from knocking you out of a game. When used with LGS, you can select any button or multitude of buttons you want disabled.
4) Media keys work out of the box and increase, lower, and mute volume. The Play, FF, Rew, and Stop buttons located above the 10-key pad also work on my media player, in my case I use MPC-HC Player. These buttons do not work with YouTube because YouTube uses the J, K, L, buttons for some dumb reason.
5) Easily change the brightness of your lit keys with the button above the pause/break key.
6) The LGS allows you to create custom profiles for every game on your system. It will also autoscan to find your games if you wish.
7) Comes with a TWO year warranty.

Neutral:
1) Some people don't like the "futuristic" font used on the keys but I don't mind it. Take a close look before buying.
2) Membrane keyboard.
3) While lights appear to indicate Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Game Mode button is pressed. You can't see which light pertains to which button.
4) Can't rebind every key, just the F-keys.

Negatives:
1) No separate G-Keys compared to other Logitech Keyboards. Instead, you are reprogramming the functions of the Function Keys (F1-F12)
2) This also means you cannot record macros on the fly, however, you can reprogram keys while in game as long as you can pause your game, Alt-Tab and open the Logitech Gaming Software (LGS). Not the most fun, but it's a workaround.

For most gamers, the F5 and F9 button are going to be used for save and load functions. Having special designated keys that are not bound to anything in advance is a nice feature that will be missed. Otherwise, I have no complaints about this keyboard. So far it has worked flawlessly.

title: Drivers are small vs other competing headsets.
text:
My review after a few years of owning these.

The drivers on this headset are smaller, 40mm, compared to competing headsets that are 50mm. Found only after I had bought these... And for about the same price at the time I'd purchase this a few years back. That's what I get for not researching, but honestly I bought it out of loyalty to Logitech as they consistently provide great products. (Was also discounted).

A few cons:
First: I never use the stereo option (stereo sometimes makes it sound like the left speaker is muffled). I think the surround sound is best.

Second: sometimes when turning on the headset during mid game, depends on the game however, I can't get the audio to sync with the headset and must reset the game. About 1/3 of my games experience this issue and may be more of a problem with the game.

Third: The headset has a tendency to disconnect for a couple seconds and reconnect at any random given moment. Playing CS: GO you may understand why this is annoying. This causes the side tone to reset despite my efforts to change it in the application and reset the app. Sometimes it stays and sometimes it resets. I have no idea why it can't stay at the level I desire. I found the configuration file and changed the actual text setting where you can change things from 0 to 1 etc. The situation improved but sometimes it still resets. I just hate when I resets to default because I can't hear myself talk.

Pros: Great noise cancelling.

I still love the surround sound quality and design. It doesn't feel cheap, and love the rolling volume changer, but i do wish it had the head band from its wired sister headset. Had to turn in one pair for warranty because of a faulty mic hinge which didn't hold up anymore. Received a replacement and it's been working great.

title: this duo is really great. First off
text:
I was initially hesitant to buy this. It's a few $ more than the rectangular shaped keyboard/mouse combos out there and I wasn't sure if the "wave shape" would work for me. I was so wrong, this duo is really great. First off, having both a wireless keyboard and mouse is amazing, and it really decreases wire clutter around your desk. Both the keyboard and mouse communicate with a single, tiny USB stick that you can hardly notice sticking out of your computer.

Keyboard: I don't think I will ever be able to go back to a "rectangular" shaped keyboard ever again. The keys for this keyboard all point verrry slightly inwards. This means that your wrists don't have to be parallel to eachother and your elbows can flair out a little. The keys are also verrry slightly elevated and depressed in a wave pattern that makes it so your wrists don't have to be perfectly parallel with the floor. All of this makes the keyboard insanely comfortable and easy to type with. It will take you a day or 2 to fully get used to but you'll be glad you stuck with it. This thing feels very solid and looks legit. Oh and the key strikes aren't very loud either but depress the perfect amount (definitely look elsewhere if you are used to pure mechanical keyboards though).

Mouse: This mouse looks very high quality and could easily be sold as a stand-alone product. Don't think because they are in a combo it will be lower in quality. It has a great weight to it (not too light and plasticy feeling like a lot of wireless mouses out there.). Like the keyboard, it has a very ergonomic shape that really helps you rest your hand and your thumb on it. It's also very smooth and and glides along my mousepad or table very easily.

Cons: Honestly can't think of any other than having to explain the shape to people when they are visiting. I know this probably reads like an infomercial but it really is that good.

title: Very high pitched frequency (whine/whistle) coming out of right speaker.
text:
Very high pitched whine/whistle coming out of right speaker....

When the unit turns on there is a high pitched sound coming from the right speaker. When you power it on and off it sounds like a capacitor or something powering up and just staying at that high pitch sound. I found a YouTube video of a guy who had the same problem. He equated the high pitch sound to a dog whistle. I can agree with that. When you increase the volume it does not change. So...if I turn the volume way up, I don't hear it and the sound quality is great, but I should not have to do that with a brand new system!!!

My husband has the same system (I loved it so I bought one for me).

Here is what we did to troubleshoot it. We removed any harmonic interference. The noise was still there.

We tried different outlets. Noise still there.

We took my husband's right speaker and plugged it into the back of my sub-woofer and his made the same high pitched noise. We put my right speaker into the back of his and there was no high pitch noise. (Ruled out the right speaker being defective).

So...it is not the L/R smaller speakers, like some people may think, since we ruled that out by using my husband's. Something is not right in the sub-woofer. Possibly bad capacitor or circuit board or channel for the right speaker.

I am not sure. I did not build it and I am not going to take it apart. I just got it today and spent over $100 bucks to have good quality music to listen to. Not a high pitch whine/whistle.

I submitted a ticket to Logitech tonight in regard to mine. I hope they do something about it or at least someone does. It seems to be a problem that I am not alone in...So defective for sure. I hope that they have had enough issues that they have troubleshot it on their end and know if it is just a bad batch off the assembly line. Human error or bad parts. Hopefully I will get an answer.

Update: I talked to Logitech and They were not all that helpful. He told me that I could do an order replacement with them or that I could return it though Amazon. I asked him, "Will you have UPS come to my door and pick it up for me like Amazon will?" He told me "NO." So I told him that I would just try to return it with Amazon. I love that Amazon will have UPS show up at the house. Based on the reviews that I spend hours reading last night and talking with the guy on youtube how was having the same issue, I opted for a refund. The guy on youtube was returning his second set because the sub-woofer was DOA.

I hope they do better quality control on their future products. Looks like it has gone downhill recently. THX is awesome and the sound quality of these being THX certified was what had me buy them over other speakers.

title: It works great, but has some critical issues.
text:
This headset has great sound, and is incredibly durable. I have had one for years now and the actual headset itself has no damage whatsoever. Anyone posting these pictures of damaged headphones stating it is flimsy, probably ran over them with a lawnmower.

This all being said though, there is 3 issues that made this go from a 5 to 3 star for me, those are..

1. The battery life is in my opinion, way too short. I average about 8 hours of use before they have to be charged again, for most this may not be a big issue but if your like me and forget to hook it up every time your done with it, you can expect these to lose power and cut out often.

2. No removable/replacement batteries. The internal rechargeable battery is all you get, and when that is done, you have to forfit use of your headset until it has a chance to recharge, no swapping out batteries to continue on.

3. The charging/receiving station's usb cord is very flimsy. I did not touch it for my first year and left it as it was the day it came out of my box, just connected it to my computer and left it except to connect and recharge it. The day I uncoiled the cord to try to play with it attached to the charger, was the last day it ever worked correctly, ever since then it would not charge correctly on it's own cord.

I do think this is worth buying, especially given there is very few alternatives, but I strongly caution, do not uncoil the usb cord.

title: Excellent update of the MX1100
text:
I was a big fan of the previous MX1100, with its switchable scroll wheel, ergonomics, heft, and ease of use. Sadly, that was released prior to Logitech's decision to release subsequent mice with their Unifying receiver, so the dongle was rather sizeable and obtrusive. I used the heck out of that mouse for years, and replaced it with an MX Anywhere since I'd switched from a desktop to a laptop and needed something a little more portable.

When the MX Master was announced, I was happy to see that it took many of its cues from the MX1100, and could be used either with a Unifying receiver or Bluetooth. The price was a bit high when it was initially released, as most retailers were charging retail or fairly close to it. Once it went on sale, I snagged one.

The MX1100 had a user-switchable scroll wheel, so the dynamic wheel on this takes some getting used to. Once you do though, you'll wonder how you did without it previously. The overall design and feel of the mouse is very good. It's a little lighter than I was expecting, and there are no additional weights to adjust on this model.

All reports indicate that the built-in battery lasts for quite a while, but it'll be interesting to how well it holds up in the long-term. I've been using this on & off for several weeks and haven't had to recharge it yet.

Overall, I'm fairly pleased with this mouse. It's not quite as svelte as the MX Anywhere, but it feels more precise is easier to use for longer sessions. I'll keep the MX Anywhere as my traveling mouse, since it's smaller, built like a tank, and working just fine.

title: The first universal remote I've tried that really WORKS!
text:
I'm a veteran of the quest for a Universal Remote... one remote to rule them all, so to speak. I've bought a number of these over the years and they've never failed to disappoint.

Some remotes had code numbers to enter for each device I wanted to control, and a long list of devices that somehow never included at least one component in my system. So then I'd begin the process of trying to find a compatible component with codes that would work, and I'd hit about 75% on that score with some basic function, like "power on" or "mute," not working.

I tried a couple that would "learn" remote codes by putting each original remote and the universal remote nose-to-nose and teaching the universal remote each command. Which worked, EXCEPT for the one or two commands that were "outside the range" of the universal remote, which tended to be a function that I used frequently.

One by one the universal remotes were decommissioned and relegated to a cardboard box.

After a decade or more of remote-juggling, I was looking at the eight(!) remotes it took to work my system and decided to jump into the universal remote pool again, maybe one last time. I saw that you could use your smartphone as a remote control, but that system was only as good as your home wi-fi and required a "hub" to translate the wi-fi signals into the infra-red signals that most remote controls use. Seemed too wonky.

Luckily my research turned up the venerable Logitech Harmony 650 programmable universal remote! It's an all-in-one solution that works as long as you can see your components (i.e. they aren't behind a cabinet door).

Basically: You log onto the internet, create an account, and download some software. This software resides on your computer, so at this point, you're done with the internet. You log on to your software on your own PC to program the remote. You type in the model numbers of your components and add them as "devices." You can then create "activities" such as "Watch TV" or "Play Blu-Ray" or whatever. You can name the activities anything you want (subject to a limit on the number of characters), and create as many activities as you need. There's a limit of eight devices. You can customize the remote to add functions that aren't part of the standard programming or to fix commands that don't seem to work by using the nose-to-nose "learning" method.

Now you use the provided USB cable to sync the remote with what's on your computer, and you're done.

Well, of course you AREN'T done. You'll find new activities you want to create, and you may need to do some troubleshooting. I had to call Logitech Technical Support to walk me through the customization process, but they were friendly, patient and helpful.

Three buttons on the remote can be assigned a frequently used activity. They have icons for a TV, a movie, and music. There's a button for "other activities" that you push to navigate to a menu and click through to the activity you want.

Ultimately, after trying a number of universal remotes over the years, this is the first one I've found that WORKS!

Now to get to some details.

Logitech boasts a very large number of supported devices: 250,000+. I guessed, going in, that my Costco-specific Panasonic TV wouldn't be included, and I knew for dead certain that my Monoprice HDMI switcher wouldn't be on the list. I WAS WRONG! TV and switcher both appeared as I typed the brand and model numbers. The codes control both devices perfectly, allowing me to set up "activities" for all of my components.

Here's an example of an activity, one I call "TV/Speakers." Once programmed, with a single press of the "Watch TV" button, the remote selects the HDMI output from my switcher, turns on the TV, turns on the cable box, turns on the receiver, selects the proper input on the receiver, and mutes the TV sound.

Setting up an activity is a simple process: Name it, choose the components you'll be using, and then answer basic questions: Which device controls the volume? Which one selects the channel? Etc. After a very few questions, you're ready to go.

If you want specialized functions, you need to program some buttons individually. You'll be shown a picture of the Harmony remote and a list of functions, then you simply drag a function onto the button you want to program. If a function is missing or doesn't work, you can add it with the nose-to-nose learning method where the device's remote teaches the command to the Harmony remote.

You can also add steps to any activity. For instance, muting the TV sound was an added step in the "TV/Speakers" activity. Again, easily done by selecting the device and the function you want to add.

I had to call Tech Support because I didn't quite grasp the concept of programming buttons. Turns out you need to program each activity separately, which makes sense when I think about it.

There's also an assistant on the Harmony 650 remote for when things don't quite work--if a component doesn't come on or doesn't turn off, etc. I also appreciate that the LCD screen on the remote comes on when you move the remote and turns off when it's just sitting there.

You do need to point the remote at your devices and keep pointing it until everything comes on, which can be a few seconds.

So far I'm very happy with the Harmony 650 and recommend it to anyone with two many devices, too many remotes, and a direct line-of-sight (no cabinet doors) to their equipment.

title: Great remote, well done Logitech!
text:
I really love this remote. I had an older Harmony remote, I forget the model but it had a screen on it and a ton of very tiny buttons that were hard to push and confusing to use. This remote is very basic (but totally useful) and very nice looking and feeling (some kind of rubber coating). It has no problem controlling my TV (Toshiba), receiver (Onkyo) and PS3. I can also use my Android phone or Ipad to control my devices. The inclusion of the IR blaster is very nice as you can set the Hub in your cabinet then string the blaster outside to be in range of your TV and/or other devices.

The setup was really easy. I used my computer to do most of it as it's easier for me but you can also use your IPad or phone. I haven't run into any devices that the remote can't control (I took the set to my moms house and tried it on all her devices as well). The software will even give suggestions if you mistype a model number or something (which I did for my TV).

Being able to turn everything on or off with one button push is awesome. No switching between multiple remotes or any of that! Also, depending on your devices and how you set them up, it's cool that you can change channels, adjust volume and move between option on your PS3 (or whatever) without having to do anything but hit the right buttons on the single remote.

The only gripe I can think of is that the remote is not lighted so if you are in a dark room you will need a light until you figure out the button layout by feel, which is no big deal.

Looking for a Universal remote? I can't recommend this one any higher than I have, it's great!

Terrible! Total waste of my time and money. I searched for countless hours, way to much time reading reviews and comments about remotes, trying to choose a universal remote that worked with out tv, roku 4, and sound bar - that. is. it. I think that is pretty simple. We watch TV, but it is not a huge priority so we didn't want to spend a ton of money. BUT the power button on our tv is broken and we can never locate the other 2 remotes as it is. The caveat was that I was unwilling to spend a lot of money on a remote that I just needed to turn the tv on and adjust the volume. The other issue was that all the reviews I read on the remotes, include the more expensive models had little to say to support the use with the Ruko, especially the 4, some had no mention and others said it lagged or didn't work at all. Which is the whole reason we were purchasing a universal remote as recent cord cutters.

So the problems - it took forever to set up....forever. I have technical skills, I can set up anything we have purchased without issue. The software for this remote crashed constantly, it had to have taken me 1-2 hours just to put in our 3 sad machines. All of which I had the corresponding and required info (product numbers, etc.) because the software was SO. SLOW.

Once I was done wasting my life with that part, I thought we were finally on a roll - yay we are headed toward a life with one remote! I was so wrong.... I think it actually worked twice...TWICE. At one point I gave up and went to the APP, maybe that would work and let me change the channel before Hulu continues to play nonsense. It worked maybe 3 times, and then would never connect. I would have to restart the hub and try to reconnect. It was so much fun, I gave up.

The only plus is, I read a lot more now. :)

This entire endeavor was a futile and a significant waste of my time. I would not suggest buying this unless you want a way to stop yourself from watching TV, which I feel like may not be the intent of universal remote control.

title: Not as nice as the M510 by Logitech
text:
Admittedly I was taking advantage of a Goldbox sale and needed a new mouse for my office computer since I keep my Logitech M510 with my laptop. So at $15 I gave it a go.

Pros:
-Quality wise, it's a pretty nice mouse, it looks nice, the scroll wheel is metal and smoother scrolling than the m510, so overall it's a better built product.

Cons:
Disclaimer: I'm a stubborn man and once I find something I like it's hard for a new thing to replace it. So this was quite the up hill battle for this mouse and as such kind of taints my review and its objectivity that I try to maintain.
-It is slightly smaller than the M510 so for bigger hands it might not be as comfortable
-The matte paint job is affecting my tactile sensitivity and kind of causes my skin to crawl (I'm autistic, so I have a texture issue)
-This mouse is made for Windows 8, so the buttons have been mapped to make it easier to navigate. This is also a problem. Where in the M510 the side buttons acted as a forward/backward button, now they're
Side: Near Front - Start button
Near Back- Minimize/Maximize All Windows
Top: Window 8 Edge Menu (The thing that pops out on the right side when you hover the mouse to the top right corner)
So with my M510, I downloaded a program to allow me to reprogram the side buttons to ctrl and shift for consolidating and cleaning hard drives of duplicates. I can't do this with this mouse, which is a shame since there's that extra button. Also Logitech updated their SetPoint Software to not support remapping their mouse from said software, so you have to download another one, that has a lot less features than the SetPoint one did. With that said I don't know how those buttons act on other OS, sorry.
-The Plastic is connected at the top instead of having it split to differentiate between the left and right button. So it makes it require more force to push
-The same can be said about the middle click button is a lot harder to press
Edit: Ah, there isn't a middle click button, it's actually to toggle between click wheel and smooth scroll without resistance, that's worse
-Since the side buttons aren't forward/backwards, the mouse wheel tilt is now that, with left=back, and right=forward, before it was scroll left or right.
-Cut down to 1 AA battery, which is annoying for many reasons since most things use even number of batteries, so there's that issue and it cuts down on the battery life. The M510 has a 2 year battery life and this has 18 month one.

With that said, I wouldn't recommend it, I would go with the less windows 8 friendly M510 for a bit more. It's not a terrible mouse, but it is limited. As I said, if it wasn't 10 dollars off, I wouldn't have bought it and would have gone with the M510 again. Can't mess with perfection.

title: gave up hope...
text:
I was close to writing a scathing review. My unit arrived and I was ecstatic, tearing open the packaging like a kid on xmas. That's where the fun ended...

Approx. 4 hours on the phone with support before they were able to tell me that the device was supposedly doa. Not sure why it took 4 hours, but giving up an entire Friday night to learn that sent me into a rage. Immediately I filed a return with amazon and had a new unit sunday.

Well upon trying to connect the device to the internet it was giving me the same troubles. Without calling support I tried all the troubleshooting methods I learned about on the previous Friday and nothing. Begrudgingly I called support, and actually got someone that new what they were doing. Turns out my router, even though I do not have 5ghz wireless, still sends out the signal and the hub doesn't work on that band (return it now if that's all you have). He instructed me to see if there was a master turn off in the router settings. I found it, disabled it, and everything went smoothly from there on. If I didn't have to go through that motion it would have been set up in 20 minutes.

The instructions leave a bit to be desired. There is no real instruction booklet in the box and everything is done online or on the phone app. It takes a little getting used to when programming complex activities into, let's say, the ps3 but they work every time. You can even time them to turn on at a certain time of the day if you're really lazy.

For those that just want a quick one button turn on of everything, that's easier. It basically sets it up for you.

I'm only using it for tv, av, and ps3. I have no cable box or dvr (all tv watching is done on ps vue) so I can't comment on those, but the physical remote buttons all work great with no added programming for things like start, pause, etc. (There is no R1, r2, l1, l2 but the color buttons act as those for vue).

I'm currently trying to hook it up to our on wall ac, which I kind of have working but I don't have the exact model number so it's a little buggy. If I had the original remote I could program off of that.

Overall it's a great product. The model I have only works with up to 8 devices, holds 6 activities, and will work with things like nest thermostats and other home automation. The next model up gives you more options and room to grow your set up, but for $100 I can live with this.

Will update my experience as time goes on.

*UPDATE #1*

If you have a PS3 and lose internet connection or power, it's a pain in the arse to reconnect the PS3 to the remote. If you have spotty internet your remote won't work 100% (we have WOW! internet with a *supposed* 30mbps d/l and like 5 mbps upload, and sometimes the internet gets so slow the remote refuses to respond). The only reason I am sticking with this remote is because for some stupid reason NO OTHER MANUFACTURERS WILL PRODUCE A UNIVERSAL REMOTE THAT WORKS WITH EVERYTHING including a PS3/4. Why bother going through the internet to change channels? it makes no sense to me.

Feel free to message me if anyone has a BETTER solution, this is an over engineered yet half-assed device.

UPDATE #2 after a year and a half the hub has completely failed. It doesnt correctly control anything anymore and it refuses to pair with my ps3. I thought it was the ps3 at first because it froze mid-Netflix binge but after resetting everything and trying to re-pair the hub and ps3 absolutely nothing works now. The ps3 controllers are Bluetooth and work perfectly fine. The hub kinda control the receiver and tv when it wants to but I'm not holding my breath that any further resetting are going to get it to work.

Complete garbage if you have to replace it every other year. Ill go back to using 46 different remotes before going back to a harmony product. Hopefully someone else makes a better universal remote in the future
