title: Three Kind (of) Mice
text:
Yeah, I'm totally hopeless with these types of products, and really have no idea what I'm talking about when it comes to things like this, so that makes me expertly qualified to give a review on Amazon! This is a mouse, but not the kind that gets chased by a cat, like in the cartoon Tom & Jerry, which was banned in some countries for being too violent, because some people are too dumb to realize that it was a cartoon and not real and that, contrary to what some people thought thought, their kids would not grow up to become Charles Manson if they watched it, nor would they go around smashing each other in the face with frying pans or suddenly get an overpowering craving to eat mice. So it's not that type of mouse, got it.

It also isn't the type of mouse that's a quiet, timid person, who doesn't talk to people much and stays home themselves a lot. I feel sorry for people like that. I often go round to their houses, knock on their doors, with a dozen beers, and invite myself in. I then spend the rest of the night – and sometimes well into the next morning - eating their food and making them engage in conversations about subjects that interest me. Sometimes they don't answer the door and I have to kick it in and talk to them while they sit shaking in the corner – but it's for their own good. It's really is quite amazing the lengths I will go to in order to cheer people up and make their lives better. Anyway, this is not that type of mouse either.

No, this is the type of mouse that moves your cursor around your computer screen (do they call it a cursor because you curse at it when it doesn't go where you want it to?). So, if you want to watch a cat chase a mouse or you want to watch people you don't know sit shaking in the corner, then this won't work. But if want a mouse that helps you to watch online videos of cats chasing mice or people sitting shaking in a corner, then this will help you do that. Just don't get your type of mouses mixed up, it could get messy.

title: Nice sound, great range, pretty comfortable... when they work, that is
text:
I have owned 3 pairs of these headphones. Yes, 3. All purchased brand new. But I just can't deal with it anymore.

Pros:
- Great sound with decent audio range
- Excellent wireless range (usually, see below for more)
- Comfortable, over-ear design (might be subjective)
- Almost zero noise when there is no audio
- Decent battery life

Cons:
- VERY sensitive to wireless noise. Depending on the environment, constant crackling/popping and or disconnecting. This happens far too often and at this point is my main complaint. I am having to constantly pause/rewind content and wait for the headset to reconnect. We have a microwave at our office that is ~60 feet away with 2 walls in-between. When anyone uses the it, the headphones cut out completely.
- The Logitech gaming software kinda sucks and doesn't always see my headphones. In which case, I can't adjust any settings other than volume.
- The plastic bits WILL, over time, begin to crack and break off. This happened to my first pair and I used 5-minute epoxy 5 or 6 times to repair the broken bits. Then I just gave up and bought a replacement set. (See Attached Images)

So why do I have 3 pairs? Initially I was happy enough with pros that I bought replacement set for work after the thing basically shattered into too may pieces to easily repair. And then I wanted a pair for home use and thought I may not have the same signal issues I had at work, so I bought the 3rd pair. While my issues aren't nearly as severe at home, I do sometimes have crackling. It's enough to distract from the content I'm trying to enjoy.

Fwiw, the adapter is literally a few feet from my head. I've tried directly connecting to the pc (usb 2 and 3), and using the provided extension. The results are always the same.

Microphone recording quality has worked just fine for doing turk hits and using teamspeak/vent.  I wouldn't necesarrily suggest them for professional purposes though as they pick up ambient sounds quite easily.  The wire is nice and long though, but I wish it came with some sort of stand to hold when not in use.

text:

And it's approx the same size as your laptop keyboard. I was able to use it over the laptop keyboard easily and prefer this keyboard to laptop one.
Another complain - it's heavy.
Yes it is. It has a steal plate inside - so I think it was made by a reason. But if the weight is your second important option - maybe this one is not for you. Take a look to K380.
My personal issue with this keyboard was the device switcher.
It was completely not working: whatever position you select - it's pointed to the latest paired device.
And I saw several reviews when it's definitely working as expected, switching devices like a pro in a second.
But not mine.
So, if you're going to bye it - first check the switcher works property.
And if it's not - return it and get another one.
You'll gonna love it :)

UPDATE: After I returned my buggy K480 I decided to buy K380 to compare.
So, what can I say... I'm going to return K380 and buy K480 back (hope with no issues this time)
From my point of view, K380 is pretty much the same feeling as laptop keyboard, maybe even more lightweight keypress - personally I don't like it in the keyboard.
So, yes heavy, yes noisy - but I like this noisy click much better than K380 almost silent click.
And I like K480 keypress depth and feel much better than K380 shallow one.

title: Great product on its own, integrates with Alexa now
text:
I love this product. I have owned numerous Harmony remotes and bought them as gifts for relatives, including the 880, 650, and 700. The Harmony hub is the ultimate. Now that it easily integrates with Amazon Echo and Amazon Dot, it is even better. If you are buying this, you might as well just go ahead and buy a Dot to go with it because it is a cheap voice remote for the Harmony even if it could not do anything else.

On its own, the Harmony Hub is a great product. Using the Harmony app on any of the smartphones in our house, we can select from any of these activities:
Watch TV
Watch DVD
Computer
Chromecast
Watch Fire TV
Watch Antenna

Whichever activity I choose to start, the Harmony Hub knows exactly which devices to turn on or off, which inputs have to be selected on the TV and the A/V receiver, etc. and it just does it.

There is only one thing that I do not care for about this product: No backlight on the included remote. I darken the room to watch movies, and when I do, I then revert to using my smartphone as a remote rather than the simple remote that comes with the product.

Where this unit really shines is its integration with Alexa. When you integrate it with Alexa by adding the Harmony skill to your Amazon Echo or Amazon Dot, you can also configure it to automatically navigate to certain favorite channels that you may have using your voice. So in addition to everything that the Harmony can do in terms of starting and stopping whichever activities you set up, you can now also do things like:
Alexa, turn on ABC.
Alexa, turn on AMC.
Alexa, turn on Disney Channel.

As of this time (12/13/2016), you cannot mute, change volume up/down on the TV or A/V receiver, channel up/down, or use the program guide on your cable box using only your voice. However, I don't doubt that eventually those functions will come as it is still early in the integration of these two great technologies.

title: Perfect for VoIP conference calls
text:
I purchased these for VoIP conference calls and I've already used them for at least 30 hours in 1 week! I have been on calls literally all day this week!

The are much more comfortable than an ear bud which is what I was using before. After a couple of hours of wearing them, they do start to feel like they are squeezing my head. I get sore around my ears but I think that is due to the face that I wear glasses. I tired pulling them off and tried stretching them a little and I was fine to continue. But be very careful if you do that, as you could break them. So far I've done that a few times and haven't had any breakage but I don't plan on making a habit of that since they are made of plastic.

My calls were very clear and sounded even better than calls over landline or cell phones. I have a pretty weak internet connection (around 5mg down and 1 up) at home and I didn't have any issues at all.

A big selling point for me was the fact that there is only one side of the ears that has a cord instead of two. This keeps them from getting twisted and tangled. I've had double corded head sets in the past and they get twisted and are more restrictive feeling.

Another selling point was easy access to the mute button. I like the location of the mute and easy operation. There is also volume control. These functions are combined in one easy to use button and is located and your waste where the cord can be clipped to your shirt. It's important to be able to mute quickly if you have a cough or sneeze. This is my first week of using them and I had a cold so I am really really glad I considered that feature when choosing to buy this headset.

I would highly recommend buying these if you are looking for a corded option.

I will likely look for a wireless Bluetooth set in the near future for freedom to walk about while on calls. When I am ready for that purchase, I'll look for the Logitech brand since I am very pleased with the quality.

title: Logitech removed functionality from the M510 to try to make people by $80-$100 mice instead
text:
I've had Logitech M510 mice for years, and have been happy with them. I'm not a power user, but they track fairly well and you *used* to be able to program application specific behavior for the buttons (for example, internet forward/back in chrome, but switch worksheets in excel). However, the M510 I received was an "updated" version which uses the new Logitech Options software (instead of the old SetPoint software). Options does not support application specific behavior for the M510. I contacted Logitech support, and their response was that I should purchase the "MX anywhere 2" mouse (~$80 from logitech) or the "MX Master" mouse (~$100 from Logitech). I'm sure those are great mice, but that's WAAAAAAAAY outside my price range.

User HowdyDoody posted some pictures showing the old version (which works with setpoint) and the new version which uses the awful Options software.

I was able to get around this by purchasing HydraMouse software for about $22 (there are other free options, but HydraMouse was easier for me to figure out). This software purportedly works with just about any mouse, so the main advantage of not returning the M510 I bought is that it uses the same Unifying receiver as my keyboard. Except for that, I could have bought a cheapo $7 wireless mouse with thumb buttons and gotten the same functionality.

title: Excellent value, makes me *slightly* less terrible at games.
text:
Easy to use, with a plug-and-play software installation. Perfect if you're technologically challenged like I am. The price point really can't be beat for someone who has only a very casual interest in gaming. I don't own any consoles, but occasionally enjoy playing games online with my friends. My friends, however, don't always enjoy my constantly "breaking" games or stalling gameplay by getting stuck in doorways or not understanding how keyboard controls work. I had a PS2 growing up, and this is exactly the style of controller I had for that, so I know where the buttons are and have a general idea of what they do. I'm still terrible at games, but this controller helps get me to a level that is less "rage-quit" inducing fury and more "haha look what Chriss did again!" amusement for those patient enough to let me join their games. A definite improvement for me!

It's lightweight, and the perfect size for me. I have fairly small hands, so I don't like big controllers where I can't always reach the buttons easily. Really anything that makes gaming harder for me is going to be a turnoff, but I don't have any problems like that with this controller. The option to press a button and have the computer recognize it as different types of gamepads makes this compatible with almost all of my favorite games, which is great because I'm not the kind of gamer who can justify having more than one of these lying around.

I searched a few forums to figure out which gamepad would work best for me, and this was the one that came most highly recommended for casual gamers looking for a reasonably-priced tool that would be compatible with the most modern games. I'm glad I went with this one, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for an easier way to not constantly "break" their games trying to use keyboard controls.

title: Best Harmony Yet
text:
I recently bought this remote/hub to replace an aging Harmony 650 with cracked display, and to finally complete set up and configuration of my home theater after a recent move.

My initial impressions are very positive. Set up is a breeze with the mobile app as opposed to doing it with the desktop app for the 650 and not having to connect the remote to a computer is a big time saver as well. The Harmony app quickly located profiles for all of my devices and automatically configured them. I think it took all of about 15 min with some breaks in between.

What I really love is the fact that I no longer need a line of sight to turn on and control devices. This was a huge problem with my old 650, especially with certain components. I would constantly have to run the help feature to wake devices after beginning an activity. Because my TV stand is low to the ground my AVR and DVR are often blocked by the coffee table and other objects in the room. An add on IR blaster is also included for devices that are hidden in a cabinet, but I haven't needed it yet. The other really cool feature is built in support for bluetooth devices like the Playstation.

The included remote is small but it has a nice feel to it and the buttons are not hard to press like on the 650. It would be nice to have more activity buttons, but 3 covers most basic activities and the mobile app can list more than 3 if needed. At this point, it's hard to tell if the physical remote will be the go-to remote, but I have a strong feeling it will be. Employing your smartphone as the primary remote would also waste battery power that could be better used for talking, texting or web browsing.

All in all I would say that this is a huge improvement over the older 650 model.

title: I have bought 4 of them!
text:
This is my second one in about 3 years. Plus I bought my wife and I one each to use on our laptops at home. I really like this pointing device.
Pros
*Great* battery life. The battery that came with the trackball lasted nearly the full three years.
Less hand fatigue. My primary use is to make models and drawings in AutoCAD, which requires highly precise cursor placement. Doing that with a mouse, my pinky finger and ring finger would be numb at the end of the day. This was originally and experiment to see if it helped. I was amazed at the difference. Minute adjustments with my thumb do not cause fatigue like my mouse (Logitech Performance mouse MX) did. I had very little issues adjusting to the different method of movement.
Programmable buttons! After the Performance mouse.with it's 9 buttons, I was glad to see at least 2 programmable buttons on the wireless trackball. I use them extensively.
No wires means that the wire won't be moving the mouse, and the cursor, when I let go of it to enter a ACAD command on the keyboard.

Cons
The middle mouse/scroll wheel button doesn't hold up well to the trackball being slammed on the table when Windows and AutoCAD decide you don't need to be working in that drawing anymore, and crashes. (OK, maybe it's just me, lol)
They also do not appreciate the cat constantly knocking them off of the arm of the recliner at home. Everything else still works, so I will keep using that one.

Overall impressions, I really like this device. I wish it had a few more buttons on it, but what I have is adequate for now. Other trackballs with more buttons don't have a thumb ball. I think that is critical to this devices operation. The movement of the cursor is smooth and predictable.

This unit is high up on my recommend list.

title: let me say I love this mouse
text:
First, let me say I love this mouse. Ever since I used it at a job one time, I fell in love with it immediately. So, shortly there after, I purchased one for my personal use. After six months, I started getting the phantom double clicks much like a lot of the reviewers here. I dealt with it for a month or so, but being a programmer, it became very frustrating, very quickly.

I decided to disassemble the mouse and see if I could figure out what might be going on. Once I had the mouse cover off, I used the mouse by clicking the button on the control board with my fingernail. I tested probably fifty clicks with no phantom double click. I decided to test another 50 clicks. No phantom double clicks. This led me to believe it has something to do with the button on the cover. I inspected it and sure enough, there was a divot on the tiny plastic bridge that presses the button on the control board.

So, I grabbed some Scotch gift wrap tape, cut four 1/4" squares, and stacked them on top of each other, then put that on top of the little bridge with the divot in it. I put the mouse cover back on the mouse (without screws just to test it). Guess what. No phantom double clicks! So, apparently that little plastic bridge isn't worth a crap. They should have manufactured it with much more durable plastic.

I took pictures, but I can't upload them to this review. So, here is a step-by-step on how to fix your phantom double clicks:

1) Remove the battery cover
2) Remove the batteries
3) In each battery compartment, you will see a sticker showing which way the battery should go in. Peel that sticker back a little bit (from the rear of the mouse) to reveal a screw. There is one in each compartment
4) Peel off the rubber sliders near the front of the mouse on the bottom. There are two screws underneath these as well. Be careful peeling these off if you want to re-use them. They probably won't look perfect when you put them back on, but if you take care, they will be near perfect.
5) Once you remove the four screws, just pull the top off the mouse. It should come off fairly easy.
6) If you want at this point, put your batteries back in, the battery cover back on, and test your button on the control board (it's near the front. It looks like a rectangular box with a tiny button on top) by clicking around and see if you experience the phantom double clicks. If you don't, then you have the same problem I had. If you do, then you have a different problem probably not fixable by this method.
7) Grab the mouse cover you pulled off and look underneath it. Press the buttons in and you will see the bridge that moves up and down to activate the button on the control board. In the middle of that bridge, you should see a noticeable divot. Make sure you are looking at the correct button (at first, I had them backwards because I was looking at it upside down).
8) Get your Scotch tape and cut 4 pieces of 1/4" squares.
9) Stack the 4 pieces on top of each other. This just makes a thicker layer of tape.
10) Put that stack of tape on top of the bridge with the divot in it. You're essentially just creating a new surface for the bridge and filling in that divot.
11) Place the cover back on the mouse. Without putting the screws back in, test your phantom double clicks. If you clicks are working like they should, then you are good to go.
12) Put the screws back in and carefully put back the rubber sliders.
13) Now, enjoy your mouse again.

title: Awesome video quality... and not 'just for the price'
text:
These little gems are amazing. I see people on video podcasts using them, and with decent lighting (and a little care in settings) they look like they're in a network TV studio. That the camera sells for well under $100 is beyond my understanding. I've worked in television since the early 70's. I'm used to being critical of video cameras that cost upwards of $100,000. Today I shoot with far better cameras than those pro cameras of 20 years ago, and they 'only' cost between 1 and 2 thousand dollars. I guess I'm not taking the C920 on shoots (no optical zoom, no recording medium... it's a webcam, after all), but for the job it's designed for, it's awesome.

You can screw it up. The automatic settings are adequate, and for a Skype chat with your buds, that'll do fine (in fact, it's overkill, but hey, it's fairly cheap and probably way better than the crappy camera in your laptop, which, by the way, looks up your nose when you have it sitting on your desk or on your belly). To look semi-pro, you need to use the manual settings, and they can get wonky fast, so use a light touch. And shine a light in your face. And don't have that window behind you in the daytime unless you WANT to look like you're in witness-protection.

The biggest CON I can think of is that I haven't found a good way to actually just look at the video from the camera full-screen. Maybe something's out there now. The microphone is also adequate for casual chats, but has that "roomy" sound unless you get close enough that the camera is taking a closeup of your nose. OK, remember, Gary... it comes included with a really good video camera for well under $100. Quitcher Bitchin. But really, if you're a guest on a 'professional' podcast, get a real mic or a headset so your audio can match the quality of your video. In my pro career, I've always said it's way harder to get good audio than good video. But do they listen?

So why only 4 stars. I'd do 4.5 if it were offered. But like the Olympic judges, there's got to be headroom for something better. "For the price," I don't see how, but that's their job.

title: Great sound, optical input!
text:
The Logitech Z625 Powerful THX Sound 2.1 Speaker System is my second Logitech 2.1 speaker system. The other, [[ASIN:B003VAHYTG Logitech Z623 200 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System (Black)]] impressed me for its generally strong sound qualities (including good bass response when placed correctly) and sufficient power for desktop use. The Z625 ups the ante with more available input connections, including an optical input AND a provided optical cable.

I had a specific problem I was trying to solve with the Z625, specifically how to route sound from a new Directv Genie receiver that only has a couple of options for sound output on the back (no RCA!). I run this receiver to a projector via HDMI, but that projector does not have a pass through for sound and I was stuck with a substandard onboard speaker. I use this system in an exercise area so it has to be loud and clear enough to get over the din of other equipment. In addition, since it not a dedicated viewing or listening area, I did not need a big solution, but rather a medium sized one.

The obvious solution was to run sound and video through a receiver with HDMI inputs and outputs and use standard speakers. That solution was just a bit too “large” for me. I was hoping that I could use the Z625 optical inputs to run audio from the Directv receiver. The short answer is YES, it works!

Unpacking was easy. Everything you need to know about connections and set up are right on the inner folds of the product box. Logitech provides a 3.5 millimeter and optical cable, with the optical being a nice touch. (no RCA cable however). Connections are intuitive as are controls. Once set up and turned on, if there is no detectable signal to the speakers they beep for a short period. I heard that beep multiple times as I pondered how to make my DTV receiver send the proper signal. (I had to adjust the audio output on the Directv receiver to PCM).

The speakers, a front main right and left, along with a subwoofer are driven by a 400W amp which is more than sufficient in a small room to produce loud and clear sound. Bass in an open space is not super punchy, and even muddy, but it is present and you can feel it. The main front speakers are well balanced and produce even treble and midrange. For the price? They are great!

Many of the deficiencies that close listeners (or audiophiles of specific tastes) may pick up on for speakers of this sort are overcome by the placement. Most people are listening to these fronts literally in front of them on a desk, while the sub is under a desk. This is an ideal configuration, producing excellent stereo imaging, along with providing an improved sounding board or surface for the subwoofer. In my own configuration, I initially had the subwoofer on the open floor and the fronts right next to them quite a distance off axis from my listening position—not ideal. Pleasantly, the front speakers have sufficient connection cord to allow me to place them directly balanced on the handle bars of my stationary bike-- right in front of me, and exactly where they will sound best. Bottom line, if you find the sound less than optimal try a different position.

I love these Logitech Z625’s. They sound great for the price, and provide the right connections for multiple setups, including solving my own particular DTV receiver sound output issue. You can spend more money but why? Recommended.

title: User-Friendly, High-Quality Webcam for Reasonable Price
text:
Webcams sure have come a long way since I last had to buy one. Before now all but one computer has had a built-in webcam in the monitor. The only one that didn’t was over 10 years ago. So this is the first time I’ve purchased an external webcam in over 10 years. Before purchasing this one, I looked at several comparable brands online and compared the different versions of webcams by this company side by side. It seemed that based on reviews and specs this was the best webcam for the price. I have to say I am very pleased with the results so far.

Pros:

1. At 44 dollars and change, this is an incredibly affordable webcam.
2. The camera is very easy to install and to mount onto the monitor. All I did was clip it to the monitor and plug it into the USB port and it was up and running.
3. I love that it rotates easily, is small and compact, and is easily clipped and unclipped from the computer monitor.
4. The picture and video quality is pretty comparable to most. I have used this flawlessly on Skype, Yahoo!, and Facebook video chat with no problems.

Cons:

1. The software that came with the webcam was a little less exciting than the ones I’ve used in the past with my webcams that were built-in to the monitors. There are no fancy features that you can use to spruce up the picture, such as adding in costumes or animations. But for the price I really can’t complain.
2. The only real issue I’ve had with this camera is that it turns itself off on occasion if I have left the computer on for a while. I have to actually reboot the entire computer to get it to turn back on again. I am not sure if this is a computer issue or a webcam issue.

All in all, I would definitely recommend this webcam to a friend, and would buy again.

[[ASIN:B004WO8HQ4 Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus]]

title: I bought this to play Bluetooth music in my car and it works great!
text:
There are a few features of this product that make it idea of use in a car:

* It automatically powers on when power is applied and shuts down when the power is cut. There's no battery in this receiver.
* Once a devices is paired with this receiver, it never needs to be re-paired.

I have a set of RCA jacks in my center armrest console for audio input along with a 12V power port. This unit does NOT have a microUSB jack like most modern devices, but it does run off of 5VDC. I used an inexpensive USB car adapter and a USB to 4.0mmx1.7mm cable to supply power to the unit. It costs less that $2 here on Amazon, but ships from China, so allow time for shipping. The Logitech adapter powers on when the car is started and my Android phone connects to it automatically. When my car shuts down, the power is cut to the Logitech adapter and my media player automatically pauses. When I restart my car, it connects again and I can resume playback.

There's a free app on the Google Play Store called "automate" that can autostart your media player as soon as the phone connects to the Logitech Bluetooth adapter.

Only issue I had was due to a grounding issue between the power source and the audio system. Luckily, I had a spare Ground Loop Noise Isolator. Search for "PAC SNI-1/3.5 3.5-mm" on Amazon. This cleared up any humming/noise.

title: I am very pleased with the Harmony 700
text:
I am very pleased with the Harmony 700. Setup took about 15 minutes. It helps to have all of the brands and model numbers of the devices you want to control before running the set up procedure. But, once the remote is synced, you're ready to go.

There's no such thing as a perfect universal remote control. It takes some digging through some menus to access certain functions that are otherwise easy to find on the remote that originally came with the component. But the button is in the Harmony 700 somewhere - usually. But the main goal was to eliminate clutter while providing quick and easy access to the controls that are most needed, and the Harmony 700 does this perfectly.

Build quality feels solid enough, although I certainly wouldn't want it to be thrown around or dropped. The remote lights up once you pick it up, which is very nice in dark viewing rooms. It feels good in the hand and can be easily operated with one hand. The amazon ad states the Harmony 700 can only control 6 devices. In fact, it can control up to 8.

I currently have a Samsung TV, Samsung Bluray player, Marantz A/V receiver, Sony CD player, Xbox 360, Xbox One, and an LED light strip being controlled by this remote.

I'm glad I snatched the Harmony 700 up when I did since it has been discontinued by Logitech. The fact that the batteries are rechargeable on this and NOT on the Harmony 650 is what sealed the deal. Removing battery recharging capability on the Harmony 650 is a step backwards. I should buy a couple more for backups just in case.

title: These are awesome!!
text: Are you kidding me? These are awesome!!!! I connected these to a 55inch tv using the included headphone jack(green) and there is absolutely no problem with surround sound. All speakers work great and the surround sounds perfect - NO OTHER WIRES NEEDED. Base pumps like crazy (if you want it to) great replacement for previous logitech speakers which I had. Previous system was two computer speakers and a base speaker, however I attached a second base speaker from the same but separate speaker system for more thump. The sound is clean I can hear things not previously heard (assuming its the surround sound effect which makes music clearer). I just don't get the negative reviews. The TV is newer bought last black Friday its a TCL Roku ready, the tv provider is Verizon. Whoever rated these low are crazy or have old tube style tv. Buy these its at a great price and you really do get a great set of speakers and a great sound.

title: Harmony's worst offering.
text:
No. I am not a verified purchaser. Ugly truth....bought it at Best Buy.
But this is where I review products, because this is where I do most of my shopping.

At time of purchase this item was listing for $50.

I already own a Harmony 650. I needed a remote for another room and the black cover of this ensured the remotes wouldn't get confused. At time of purchase this cost more than the 650, despite being a lower model number. The buttons look similar so I mistakenly believed that those buttons would perform the same functions as on the 650, they don't.

Pro's
+ easy programming through My Harmony online app on your computer. Not usually a fan of having to go online to use a product, but this is a very functional app. By being online I assume they can constantly update their compatibility with devices you wold control.
+ nice black appearance.

Con's
- costs more than the far more functional 650 (at time of purchase 650 was selling for $45), despite lacking the features of the 650.
- only a single "one touch" function that is for the tv. 650 can one touch at least 3 functions tv, movies, and music. As well as I guess two touch features (hit "other" then select programmed function from the lcd screen. On the 350 the buttons near the top of the remote that resemble 650 one touch buttons are in fact not. They are simply buttons that turn on other devices, they do not do the impressive one touch functions.
-buttons are not back lit.
-often have to use original remote control in conjunction with this in order to switch the tv input.
-no lcd screen for additional functions and controls.

I know I spent a lot of time comparing to the 650, but when at time of purchase, this cost product more than the 650 it is extremely relevant. Disregarding the mind numbing questions as to why Harmony would release a vastly inferior product to a previous offering in the same price range, the real world implication is that there is no reason to purchase the 350 over the far more useful 650.

Bottom line: Do not buy. Instead you can get far more convenient, efficient, and useful product from the same manufacturer for the same price range.

title: If you find one at Goodwill or a second hand store, BUY IT. these things bang! user friendly to a fault.
text:
Walked into the local Goodwill, and one of these was sitting on the shelf minus the remote and power adapter. Immediately negotiated the price down from 5 bucks to 2 dollars.

Got home, found a 3 amp 12v adapter, plugged it in, did the WPS to connect to my network, downloaded Logitech squeezebox software to my media pc in my livingroom, installed it, allowed it to scan for files, loaded the remote control apps on my Android phone and iPad, and literally within 15 minutes I had a small 5 lb brick of a device blaring some of the cleanest and powerful sound I've ever heard from such devices. Crisp room filling highs, decent and stable mids, and a nice powerful punchy bass with zero distortion at 95% volume...

For 2 U.S. dollars...

It is in flawless condition, and while missing the remote and power cord, just looking at it and seeing those speakers hidden slightly behind the grilles, and the heft of the thing tells you its worth every penny. (Well, much more than the 2 dollars I spent- that's a fluke)

I have a satellite radio boombox, which I thought sounded good, nah, it's junk compared to this. Add a powered subwoofer and frankly it's at the level of Bose quality. It really sounds that good.

The setup ease is almost intuitive if you have a decent amount of pc experience, and I did it with no instructions whatsoever. Let it find the network and it found all my pc's, and files. Download the squeezebox software to PC or Mac and it'll scan and find your media, and send it right to the squeezebox... Further, creating an account on squeezebox will allow you to access your media from anywhere, as well as control the units functions and playlists.

5 stars, this thing rocks! I honestly cant get over the powerful sound coming from this thing... $2 bucks....lol...

title: Significant issues with installing the camera under Windows 10 Pro - It works with Skype but Logitech software does not work.
text:
I purchased this to upgrade a much older lower resolution Logitech camera on a PC I use as an adjunct my main iMac. I installed the camera and rebooted the machine (Windows 10 Pro) and was rewarded with a locked up driver download. A reboot restored normality (a standard Windows behaviour). Skype found the camera and microphone. I decided to install the Logitech software which installed and seemed to work but then when asked to reboot, Windows said it had an unrecognisable device on a USB port and nothing would see the camera or microphone (Skype or the Logitech software). I could not get anything to see the camera (a reboot, unplugging and reinserting the camera USB connection). I uninstalled the Logitech software and rebooted and Skype would see it again but I have no other functionality. I suspect that if I spent time on the web looking for why this occurs I would find the reason, but I see no reason why I should have to do this. As far as I am concerned at this time, it serves its primary purpose to act as a higher quality Skype camera but nothing else.

I am not sure whether this is Logitech (who generally provide high quality products (I use their mouse and keyboards extensively)) or just Windows, but if you are expecting to get a plug and play product this is not going to work for you. Very disappointed ( and I tried it on another Windows 10 Pro machine with exactly the same results - the Logitech software does not work, period) with this product. I am considering returning it but will spend more time trying to debug the problem before doing so.

Added Note: Having reviewed internets posts on this camera, I can see that this is not an uncommon problem. Also note that I had problems with Skype after removing the Logitech drivers. A simple reboot would not always work. I often had to unplug and replug in the camera to get Skype to see it. Based on my experiences I have reduced my rating to 2 stars from 3 stars.

title: A lot of Bass for your Buck
text:
There are better options out there for a lot more money, however for the cost these are very good.
I previously had a Cambridge Soundworks 'PC Works' from late 1990s which, until recently, was the best budget speaker system i'd ever heard and if they still sold them, i'd get the same one again.
I use these for my PC/Gaming/music.

PROS:
+ Subwoofer: it's hard to capture in a video, there's little point, but the woofer really does a great job. I've never used the bass level more than 50%, or the total volume more than 75%, there's been no need to. even at low/mid volume I can hear/feel the sub from another floor in the house.
+ Volume controls on the speakers: Since I use this as a desktop setup, i much prefer the volume controls on the speakers than the wired remote that so many sets are using now.
+ Cost: you really will be hard pressed to find similarly priced speakers that sound this good. I've checked out countless ones at stores or even friend's speakers. There are definitely ones that are better, but

CONS:
- Subwoofer size: Not a huge deal for me but the subwoofer is large. If you are limited in space, you may have trouble finding a placement for this.
- Clarity: Most people probably won't even notice, especially if you're just looking for affordable speakers. For me, i'm still trying to get these to sound as crisp as my old speakers. I'm able to get pretty close using the PC's soundcard adjustment presets/equalizer, but it still doesn't quite have the crisp clarity my old ones did. Just when one song sounds perfect, you can subtly hear it in the next song where it is lacking.

Tip: if you are putting the sub on a carpeted floor, place it on wood or a piece of cardboard to create clearance, so the carpet doesn't interfere and muffle out the woofer.

title: 5 star review literally slipped away
text:
80% of this mouse is perfect. the remaining 20% is enough bad for a 2-star reduction which I suppose is more like 60% in a 5 star rating system.
For reference, my most recent and prior mouse was a Logitech G500 which is a 4.5 star mouse for me, but has had years of MMO and FPS use and was ready for replacement.

PROS:
*Almost* everything about this mouse is fantastic and if it weren't for the cons below, this would have been a 5 star mouse. the 3 things below seem minor but (for me) have a huge impact on usability and feel.
+ The mouse feels great in the hand. The weight modifications are easy to access and swap out, and allow you to adjust perfectly to how hefty you'd like it to feel.
+ The L & R click buttons are solid.
+ The programmable buttons are all sturdy and have a good feel to them.

CONS
- 1/2 Star: G9 button. this button is in a place that is not usable under normal circumstances. Maybe that is the point. I believe the default for this button was to switch mouse profiles, and you certainly don't want such easy access to that behavior that you'd accidentally choose alternate mouse profiles, however, if you don't care about profiles, this button's placement is in a terrible position to use during nearly any kind of game play.

- 1/2 Star: The forward thumb button which has no G#, just a circle is too far forward. With the base of my palm resting on the most rear part of the mouse, i am very comfortable with the two side G4 and G5 buttons but the forward thumb button is barely reachable. If I reposition then the G4 button becomes difficult to reach as it's like touching the base of your palm with your thumb. The default setting for this is related to switching DPI settings, so if that's what you want it for, maybe this is OK so you're not easily and accidentally jerking your DPI around mid-play. but for other button assignment it's use feels limited.

- 1 giant star: The mouse scroll wheel. Previous Logitech mice I've owned have a solid rubber, or rubber inlay over the center circumference of the wheel making it very easy to scroll with the lightest touch, even with the notched scrolling engaged.
The G502 mouse wheel feels like solid slick plastic, and while it has groves in it, the plastic is very smooth which makes scrolling have a slippery feel to it, and sometimes actually slip if you do not apply what seems like firmer than usual pressure downward while scrolling. Because of this slipperiness, for me this is the biggest score against the mouse. The other buttons I can live with because they are always reliably in their weird positions, but the mouse scrolling action with the notched scrolling engaged seems to allow you to slip occasionally while scrolling, which is inconsistent. The wheel scrolls perfectly when the notched scrolling is released and you're in Free/Spin scroll mode, but I rarely if ever use that function.

Summary:
Hind-sight, I looking at the G700s, I think it would probably have been a better choice from the G500. It has a nearly identical scroll wheel, very similar button placement with an extra index finger and thumb button all easily within reach of the existing ones.

title: Worthless Piece of Junk
text:
I've been cycling through Logitech wireless mice for a couple years looking for one that would accurately handle the "Middle Button" pan & scroll in Autodesk. Totally pointless. They work for a while and then go Zooming nuts one day when you're under the gun. Add a Logitech wireless headset broke the camel's back. There's no way you can get both the mouse and the headset to work. The guys at Logitech are clueless.
So, stuck in Pleasanton I had to get a corded mouse at OfficMax and I opted for the simplest wired major branded mouse I could find. In retrospect I should have bought the MS Mouse.

What a piece of trash this thing is!

I'm a heavy mouse user and have to switch hands to stave off carpal tunnel. This mouse is totally RH only. Using it LH it's impossible to avoid accidental clicks on the side buttons. Easy; I turned them off in Set Point. Works fine in Autocad but turning them off does absolutely NOTHING in browsers and Office documents. POS!

I do training and tech support vids regularly. What a pleasant surprise when I found this worthless machine doesn't work in Techsmith's Snagit or Camtasia. The cursor disappears entirely or is restricted to horizontal movement only. As part of the fun it doesn't fail until you hit "Record". What a treat! Actually with enough time using you'll find the 500 locks up in either horz or vert every once in a while for god knows what reason. The "Laser" tracking similarly will intermittantly shut down on any darker surface. When that condition is at it's worst you can only mouse on a pure white background. Luckily I have two printers in arms reach most of the time so I can slap down a pile of letter size paper to replace my mouse pad.

For now I'm limping along with the Logitech monkey on my back while I debate which upscale CAD/Gaming mouse I'm going to pop for. No more sub $100 POS for me. No more Logitech for me either. I'm done with those guys. I can pay the freight for better built equipment, thank God.

title: I really enjoyed the M60 for it's "Sniper" button that would change ...
text: I'm still getting used to this mouse. My old Corsair M60 died after 4-5 years of use. I really enjoyed the M60 for it's "Sniper" button that would change the DPI to a predetermined setting. I changed this button to act as a CTRL button instead of a DPI switching. I was happy to find another mouse that could continue with this function with the (G502). So to continue with the comparison I'd say the 502 has better tracking. On all other aspects though, the M60 and 502 are on par with one another. The ergonomics of both mic are great, but in different ways. The M60 is wider and allowed my hand to have a more relaxed "Palm" grip. The 502 has a more narrow shape, but the thumb rest allows for a very comfortable "Claw" grip style, and manages to make the mouse lighter. The scroll wheel is much nicer with the 502 since it has the option to be a free spinning scroll wheel. I find that it's staged scroll wheel mode, the clicks are far to heavy and see this more as a hindrance unless I'm gaming. This is where I enjoyed the M60's scroll wheel more. Both mice have good feed back when using the left and right click buttons, the standard weights to change the balance of the mouse, build quality, intuitive software, etc. Over all this is a great mouse. If your okay with the price, and want a great mouse that can handle both office work and heavy gaming, this is the Mouse for you. Though if you're a die hard palm grip kinda guy, this might not be the mouse for you. I'd check out the M60 or M65, maybe check out the Monix Caster mouse.

text:
When this webcam works, I love it. The picture quality is great, and it works well with Skyping, streaming, and even recording random videos. However, a few months after I purchased it (which has been about three years now), I have had issues with computers not being able to detect it, so I have probably only been able to use it about 20% of the time that I have wanted. I have used it on an Alienware laptop, a Dell XPS 13, a iBuyPower PC, and now my custom-built PC. There is no pattern of when it does and does not work; it just usually does not.

Logitech's customer service has been less than stellar. Whenever I try email correspondence, it takes probably 7-9 business days to receive an acknowledgement of my support request and then an additional 2-3 days per additional email. title: Very disappointing
text:
Very disappointed with this unit. I bought this primarily to work with the Amazon Echo. My intention was for it to work with my entertainment system which includes a TV, AV receiver, Roku, Amazon TV and a Blu-ray player. I am currently using a Harmony 650 programmable remote. The goal was to use the Amazon Echo to control the devices. What I found was that the Echo/Harmony Hub combination is really only capable of turning the system on or off and switching from one system to the other. Although this has some use, you still need a remote for volume control, muting, switching channels or modes. This cannot be done using voice control with the Echo. In addition, if you turn the system on with the Echo you will find that your programmable remote is out of sync since it still believes the system is off. Basically it is a total hassle and doesn't make my life easier which was the whole point. The Harmony Hub is actually designed to work with an app on your smartphone. The Echo capability is merely an add on and is only good for impressing your guests once.
I have used the Smartphone app and it is pretty good, but it requires you to use your smartphone as your remote. This means it must be charged and be with you. It also means that it will be annoying when you are using your smartphone for other tasks -- surfing the internet, let's say -- and then you need it to control your TV. This means toggling from whatever you're doing back to the remote app. Again, a hassle. Also, you will run into the same out of sync condition with your programmable remote should you choose to use it. All in all, they've got some work to do on this. I have returned my Hub.
A note on the remote capability of the Harmony Hub. I was very impressed with the infrared signal from the Hub. I thought I would have to put it somewhere with line of sight to all my devices, but the infrared signal will bounce of walls and windows and allow you much more freedom with the placement of the hub.

title: Pretty Sweet!
text:
This keyboard is fantastic! My Dell came with a cheap, extremely basic keyboard. The keys were super low and gone were keys to control audio functions, like I had been used to on my dearly departed Macintosh. Setting this gaming keyboard up on my Windows 10 PC was a breeze. Not included in the box is the software needed to really get the party started when it comes to the functions of this keyboard. You'll have to visit their website for that software. Once downloaded, you have the options of changing the backlighting and adjusting the function keys to your preferences. Now, here's the thing-- I am not a gamer, so some of the features of this are currently lost to me. But, know that you can adjust the function keys.

My favorite aspects of this keyboard are the colorful backlit keys, the tactile feel of the keyboard and palm rest and the click of the keys! The keys are high on the keyboard and offer the perfect clicking sound, in my opinion. The keys, very tactile and almost 'soft' feeling, are a lot easier to type on than the silly flat keyboard that came with my Dell. Onto the backlit keys, the software allows you to control the color and pattern. You can have the color spectrum change on its own, choose one stationary color or turn off the lights completely. I don't mind the bright and colorful keys (currently changing on their own every few seconds), but other people who use this computer don't love them as much. (Since it's my keyboard, though, the crazy colors are staying put!) Another fantastic thing this keyboard has is audio controls. You can lower/raise your audio, pause/stop your audio or mute your computer completely. I love that you can control the audio quickly without messing with your speaker's controls.

Overall, I love this keyboard. It's so much better than the basic one I was typing on previously and has a much better look and feel to it! Totally worth checking out!

text:
I purchased the G930 and had been pleased with them for a long time. Eventually, they began to suffer significant interference in normal operations (even having direct LOS to the receiver) and I had to do away with them. Apparently I was one of the lucky ones for the G930's, most didn't work. Naturally, I was far more than just skeptical when I saw the G933's. After significant research I found that Logitech had completely rebuilt their headset and claimed that all the problems were removed. They did not lie.
This product blows the G930's out of the water (even my working pair)! For the price this is not really unexpected, but given Logitech's history with headsets, this is a major improvement. The headset is durable, with a fusion of hard plastic and metal, yet light enough to not provide any discomfort, even given long (8+ hr) sessions with straight use. I quickly found my settings on the adjustable headset sliders (10 on one side, 11 on the other), and have felt the foam conform to my head, now fitting very naturally. It took about a week to really get them to fit perfectly, but now I can place them and have them stay on without a second thought.
The wireless connectivity is solid. Even through walls with lead paint and some steel beams I can still use the headset without disruption through an entire floor and a few rooms. Don't get me wrong, there are some dead zones when I walk around like this, but if they are kept in the same room there is zero distortion. Microphone clarity is (I'm told) crystal clear over Skype and Curse. The battery seems to last for about 8 hrs before beeping for recharge, but its not a real problem.

Overall I am very thrilled with this product. It made up for all the problems its predecessor had and restored my faith in Logitech Headsets. I'm sure there are "better" products out there, but in this price range (~$200) I would certainly recommend this product.

title: No instructions included, but you should be able to find them online
text:
Last year I purchased a Chromebook to use in my home "office" (aka shed). I like it, but sometimes when I'm typing longer documents, I've wished for a "real" keyboard. Having worked as a word processing operator for almost 25 years. I'm just more comfortable typing on a PC than on a laptop or any other type of device.

While browsing at an office supply store the other day, I saw several of these Logitech Bluetooth keyboards. They all felt really good - almost like the full-sized PC keyboards I'd been accustomed to. I checked online and found that Amazon's price was almost HALF of theirs, so decided to order it and give it a try.

When it arrived, I had a little difficulty figuring out how to set it up with my Chromebook. That's why I've deducted one star, because there are NO instructions at all included in the box with the keyboard. However, I did a search online ("K480" plus "Chromebook") and found out how to set it up. That's probably what you'll have to do as well.

Once it was set up, I was pleased. It works well and has a good feel to it. I also purchased a stand for my Chromebook, so I could easily see the screen while holding the keyboard in my lap to type. In fact, I just used it to type this review!

So bottom line for me is: it's a very good price here on Amazon, it has a good feel to it for those of us who remember the olden days of "touch typing" (!), but it does require a little work on your part to figure out how to set it up. If that doesn't scare you off, I do recommend it.

title: Good sound but poor design leads to easy breakage at stress points over time with no way to fix.
text:
Headset worked properly however both ear cup hinge supports broke due to fatigue after 24 months of use. The right side went first, becoming progressively looser over time, and finally could not stay attached to the plastic mount. The left side quickly followed by the left.
The inside plastic cover held by four small screws are weak on this design and split up vertically and completely failed to keep the ear cup attached. Taking the cover apart to see if I could fix it uncovered a broken plastic ring inside which is not surprising given how thin the plastic supports are. Clearly, no reinforcements at the hinge points that will see normal stress points from regular usage.

I cannot recommend this headset for longevity and would opt for a sturdier design that is preferably all metal, not metal and plastic for the main stresspoints. It's unfortunate because the rest of the earphone is working properly.

title: Comfortable  Logitech combo
text:
Edit: I knocked two stars off my initial review below due to longevity issues. Overall I would tentatively recommend this to a friend, but there are likely better options for the price on the market since the combo will likely only last around 2 years of daily use.

Initial Review:
I enjoy both the wireless keyboard and mouse. The keyboard and mouse are both comfortable to use. The mouse feels to be about the right size. The padding on the keyboard gives it extra comfort and the stands on the back give different keyboard height/angle options. The best part about this combo is that they are are configured through a single usb slot which frees up other slots for other devices or make it easier to switch between computers (the reason I purchased this product). I only needed to change the batteries a couple of times over the nearly 4 years of use, even though I pretty much never turn them off and they are being used almost all day. Overall very happy with this purchase.

Longevity issues:
I bought this combo in January 2015 and again in June 2017. Meaning the first lasted around 2 years and 5 months while the second lasted a little less than 1 year and 6 months The first and second started having connectivity issues.

The first started having slower response times (laggy/missed keystrokes and delayed mouse movement). Batteries were swapped, different usb slots and computers were used, but the issue persisted. This combo was moved around a lot so it may have been damaged during transport as i was not careful in its transportation.

The mouse on the second system started randomly disconnecting from the computer and the usb would need to be removed and reconnected to reestablish a connection. The same solutions were attempted as with the first one, but the disconnecting got worse over time. I now have swapped the system out with a wired keyboard and wireless mouse and the connection issues disappeared so I can only guess another component was failing in the MK550 combo.

title: I like the microphone can be moved out of the way ...
text: I took me a while to find a pair of wireless, Bluetooth headphones that didn't give me a headache(hat size about 7-1/4) when I put them on. I am basically a field service tech and work in lots of computer data centers. I wanted to be able to have a pair of headphones that I could pair with my phone and listen to music while I work, be out of the way, but still be able to hear my phone ring through headset and be on customer calls and still work, hands-free. I like the microphone can be moved out of the way while listen to music, but easily bring it down while I talk on the phone. I was always concerned with the built-in microphones picking up too much noise from surrounding area that people couldn't hear me and I couldn't hear them. No one has complained to me they can't hear me. Added bonus is they are fold-able so I can tuck them away in my laptop bag. I picked up a small nylon bag from the Container Store so I could keep them from getting snagged on stuff and keep the USB cable with them. When I listen to music only, I can get a good 8hrs off the battery and remain comfortable. If I talk on phone, it seems to suck the power a bit more, but if I'm not moving around too much, I can plug the USB cable in to charge while I work, listen to music, or talk on phone. I do have a hard time hearing any beeps when the battery is low. If I'm listen to music, it sounds like music just kinda of pauses for a second which I think is normal delay especially when listen to Pandora radio. If I'm on the phone, I don't hear the beep and then suddenly the phone just disconnects as if I'm in a dead zone. I like the foam-like earpieces. They are soft, don't feel scratchy, and don't make my ears sweat like leather-type version. I didn't want to have noise-canceling headphones and these are not noise-cancelling due to the foam material sitting on the ears, but if I turn the volume up when I'm in a data center environment I can hear music and not as much noise. It has nice big buttons on the right-side earpiece for volume control, play/pause, answer/disconnect for phone, and a mute. I don't use the wireless receiver with my laptop, so it is neatly tucked away inside the left earpiece if I ever need it and it doesn't get lost. I strictly use it with my phone and its Bluetooth capabilities. I have a Samsung Note 4 and it paired up with no problems. Since these don't give me a headache when I wear them, they are a bit looser on my head so if I bend over to work on computer equipment, I have to adjust them so the band over my head is slightly on the back of my head to keep them from falling off. I can live the moving them on my head if I need to. Its better than having a headache and not being able to stand them on my head for more than a half-hour. It also has some foam-type padding on the headband so that helps keep it on my head as well. The battery in the headphone is special, not standard AAA or AA batteries, so I'm curious how long it will be before I will eventually have to replace it because headset is not keeping a long charge on it. The battery is also kept in the left earpiece along with storage area for the receiver.

I'll start this off by saying I've been using strictly Razer DeathAdders for at least 7~ years so I can only compare this mouse to what is considered one of the best mice available for the last decade.

That being said this is probably the best mouse I ever used. It takes a little bit of time to get use to the side button, it's very sensitive, but once you do everything comes completely natural. You can hold the mouse in a number of different ways, coming from using a deathadder for so long it was just as comfortable (if not more comfortable) for me to use it. The mouse wheel is without a doubt the best mouse wheel I've ever used. That being said the deathadder's mouse wheel is probably the worst I've ever used (they routinely break every 2~ years).

As of now this is a great mouse I would recommend to anybody willing to pay the price tag. I've only had it for about a week now though, so my opinion could change if it isn't very durable (the biggest flaw of the deathadder).

title: Chintzy, Bulky, and the Keys Kinda Suck

Logitech had an opportunity here, and they missed the mark. The option to connect up to 3 devices is awesome, pairing it to devices couldn't be easier, and it usually responds to input very quickly, although I've noticed some lag with my tablet (I haven't used it much with my desktop or FireTV, the other 2 devices I've connected it to).

THe keys are raised a bit too high, feel cheap, and while they have a click when pressed, it's not a satisfying click. It's a rather dull, awkward noise exasperated by the keys rocking in their spots. This makes fast precise typing difficult on even my desktop (I'm currently using the keyboard now to type this).

For the price, it should be better quality. For a portable keyboard most likely to be used on someone's lap, it should be less bulky and the keys should be more stable in their cutouts making typing more comfortable.

All in all, I am not overly impressed with this keyboard (and have constantly had to go back and edit my review for accuracy because of all this). The back key is going to get used on this a lot, I can tell already.

text:
I was not paid nor did I receive any discount for this review. This is genuine.

I can't say enough good things about this speaker. It is loud, sound quality is great, and it is super durable.

One of the unsung perks of this speaker is the bungee cord on the back. It's set up in a way that allows for a lot of versatility in how you strap it to something. Loop it through a backpack strap, hang it off your shower head/rack, strap it to a tent post. I haven't found any scenario where I wasn't able to strap/hang this thing how I wanted.

I saw some complaints about battery life and bluetooth range on here, but I did not experience either of those. Quite the opposite, actually. Last weekend we went camping, and we got every minute of the promised 9 hours out of this thing. I can also leave my phone pretty much anywhere in my 850 sq ft apartment and still have full bluetooth connection with no breaking up.

I've had a Bose Soundlink Mini for a couple of years, and I really loved it. After a few weeks with this one, I hawked the Bose on Craigslist. Sure the Bose sounds better, but not by much. After experiencing the versatility, durability, and loudness of this speaker, I didn't even touch my Bose. This is no knock on the Bose speaker - also a really phenomenal product - but the UE Roll sometimes goes on sale for 1/3 of the Bose price, sounds almost as good, and is just more versatile all around.

title: Perfect for Twitch/YouTube streamers!
text:
I upgraded to this webcam from an old Logitech Quickcam 3500 (with a manual focus). I am beginning to stream on Twitch on a more solid schedule and needed a cam with a higher resolution and more clarity. Paired with a [[ASIN:B004OAFO0I Polaroid 8" Heavy Duty Mini Tripod With Pan Head With Tilt For Digital Cameras & Camcorders]], it works perfect for my new streaming set up. The auto-focus and face-following technology is really cool, but I feel it would be distracting for the current state of my stream, but I may utilize this feature in the future. I currently use a green screen ([[ASIN:B0108TW4OC ePhotoInc 5 x 7 Feet Cotton Chromakey Green Screen Muslin Backdrop Photo Photography Background G57]]) for a background, and this camera can chroma-key (or even color-key) it out perfectly.
The base is weighted unlike the Quickcam series cameras giving the camera more stability without flopping around under the weight of the USB cable, and can attach to tripods/mounts with ease. The LWS (Logitech Webcam Software) installs automatically on Windows 10 as it auto-detects the driver for the camera, and functions with great ease in OBS (Open Broadcast Software). I did find that the automatic lighting does a fairly excellent job, but had to turn off some features due to my green screen (it was turning my face orange to try to contrast).
As I am not using this for audio, I cannot comment as to the quality of sound.

Overall, this has greatly improved the quality of my stream, and the response/resolution is phenomenal compared to my old camera.

text:
I bought this to use with MS FSX / MS FSX-SE (Microsoft Flight simulator X, box and Steam Edition). My Windows 7 Professional computer recognized it with no additional messing about needed. This is my first joystick (hard to believe after decades in the computer industry, but I've never been a big gamer) and I was impressed with its construction. It is heavy enough to stay put on my desk, and it also works in my lap -- I am using it to fly the J-3 Piper Cub from A2A Simulations and it works wonderfully for that.

Even though I have rudder pedals on my setup, I have the option of using the joystick's twist axis for the rudder if I wish. The throttle paddle on the left rear of the joystick base provides input to the throttle. There are other buttons which get mapped automatically in MS-FSX, including a hat knob on the top that is used to change your viewpoint inside the virtual cockpit.

I read the reviews on at least a dozen joysticks, and for me, this was the best bang for the buck. If I get heavily into FSP's or dog-fighting I didn't spend so much on this one that I would be reluctant to buy another in the top echelon of joysticks -- but those can get into the multi-hundreds of dollars and this will work well enough as I learn. If I upgrade later, I have some grandsons that will happy to take this one :-)

title: A solidly built magnetic dashboard mount, with a surprisingly capable app
text:
A generic car mount / dock is naturally a compromise. Some phones have NFC. Some phones have wireless charging. Almost all phones have Bluetooth, microphone, and a proximity sensor (to make sure your face don't press buttons accidentally when you're talking on the phone), however, and this mount makes use of that, together with a pretty amazing app, to provide hands free convenience. The only thing it does not provide is convenient recharging, but you can always connect a USB cable.

I got a dashboard mount holder for review, and I tested this with my OnePlus One (with OEM thin case) running Cyanogen OS 13.1 (Android Marshmallow) - factory, unrooted.

It took a while for me to figure out how to adjust the mount. Reason for that is because it is extremely stiff and needs more force than I was initially comfortable with exerting. The suction cup mounted very firmly to my car's dashboard, even though it is not completely flat. In fact, in the last 3 weeks, despite temperatures in the car exceeding 100 degrees F, it has not come detached.

The Zero Touch comes with two self adhesive metallic patches. This is what the mount's magnets hold on to. The round patch is meant for phones with flat backs, and the oval shaped one meant for curved back. (aside: Wikipedia tells me that the shape is called "stadium"). I chose to stick it to the back of my thin plastic case instead of the phone itself.

The mount appears to be a Bluetooth Low Energy beacon that is turned on when the phone is magnetically attached to it. There is a small battery in it that should last at least a year since BLE is really efficient with power. The phone's app wakes up when it detects this, and it has a number of tricks up its sleeve - reading new text messages to you, allowing you to control your music, control volume, control navigation, and other tricks I'm still learning about.

Following the app instructions setting it up is straightforward and painless. I recommend doing this in the comfort of your house, where you can look up additional information on your laptop if necessary, before mounting the Zero Touch in the car - it makes no difference to the app.

Under music settings, it lists Spotify and Deezer. I don't have any of them installed. Instead, I use Poweramp to play media that I store locally on my phone. To my surprise, it does start playing from Poweramp when I ask it to "play music".

It has not been completely smooth sailing, but I think it has more to do with my phone than with the Zero Touch. It occasionally did not detect the dock when I mount it on, and I've had to re-pair it to the dock once already, and it lost its pairing again today. My Pebble watch also got unpaired every once in a while, which is why I don't think it's a problem with the Zero Touch.

I'd like to have the ability to launch a few apps of my choosing, and also the ability for it to read back certain types of notifications to me. Other than that, it's not perfect, but it is a nicely built accessory that should make the road a little safer for everyone.

The invisibility of their names would not be so bad, except that their red lettering on the keys has such a low contrast with the keys' blackness that the names are invisible without a Kleig Light. Also, the backlighting switches off almost instantly, once you stop typing.

I believe that Logitech also should have assured that the underside of the keyboard met a flat surface on ALL four corners. Instead, it is slightly tippy. Logitech should realize that a customer might buy this particular keyboard, not only since Logitech expects it to be held on the lap. A customer may also buy it, wishing to use it on a flat surface, or may have a smallish desk and desire the smaller "footprint" and greater portability this keyboard has, or they may find that the feel of the keys is superior to anything else out there for the same or lower price.

title: Looks Great In Some Places, Bad in Others. Sounds Wonderful
text:
This is without a doubt the best and most fun to use microphone I have ever used. When I received this, I tested it on the Skype thing that lets you hear your own mic, and for some reason it sounded much better than reviews on here and YouTube lead me to believe. I do very much like this mic, but it does have a couple design flaws that are just really annoying.

Pros:
The stand is very nice. I've seen some reviews giving the stand a bad rep, but that's kind of..dumb. It's a stand, it works, it has rubberized feet so it doesn't scratch up your table. What else do you want it to do, preform back flips or manipulate time and space? The legs are made of steel and the body is made out of a very nice and thick plastic. It's not made of solid gold and you're only paying $50.

The snowball can be easily disassembled. You can very easily screw the snowball onto a boom stick if you so choose. I like the fact that I can just unplug it very easily after I'm done using it. I'm a little paranoid and feel safer when I don't have the mic on and someone potentially listening to me.So being able to easily remove the power cable and again, easily, put it back in when I need to use it, is wonderful.

The device itself is gorgeous. Opting to pay $10 more for the black version (I do feel like I was scalped, though) was a great choice since it easily fits in with everything else on my desk.

The audio quality itself is pretty gosh darn great. I've very glad I opted for this instead of getting one of those XxxM0nTaInD3wxxX pro elite mlg gaming headsets, like what Razer makes, where you get poor headphones and a rather poor mic for $100. I'd recommend my route and get great headphones and this microphone. I plan on doing voice overs eventually for mods so this is going to be good for many things. But for the time being I use it for communicating with friends when playing games.

Cons:
The red LED. It looks terrible and is very intrusive. Yes, it lets me know that it's on. Know what else would've let me have this information? Any program that I'm using it for. Or, even, the microphone section under Recording Devices when you right click on the speaker icon if you're using Windows. I guess putting electrical tape over the light would work, or just not putting the light there in the first place would be even better.

The power cord. The cable you get in the box to power the snowball doesn't even match the device. In my case, I got a brown cable. Brown. Cable. Doesn't match a single thing, it would match my desk itself but it's such an odd and ugly tone that it doesn't even match that.

Overall, I really do like this product. If it ever dies, I will be using it to play catch with my friends.
4/5

title: Smart Remote is Truly a step up from the old Harmony 890
text:
Wow. I replaced an older Harmony remote with this one and am absolutely thrilled with it's performance.

I replaced an older Harmony 890 remote and here's my comparison between the two:

Setup

The Harmony 890 required a proprietary USB cable and a locally installed program on a PC in order to configure components. Over time it was a royal pain to find the correct cable to program. In addition, if you replaced the computer where the logitech program was installed, you lost your configuration and had to start over

The Smart Remote setup was very simple and uses an app on your phone to configure (I'm using the iOS version) over your home wireless network. The app stores the configuration in an online account with logitech, so you don't have to worry about losing your configuration.

Battery Life

The Harmony 890 would lose charge after a few days off it's base station. In addition, mine had a propensity to cause the lithium ion battery to swell causing the battery cover to pop off. I replaced the battery 3 times over a span of 6 years for that reason. It would swell to the point where it was impossible to place the cover back on.

The Smart Remote uses a simple button battery. I'm unsure it's life as I've only had it 3 months, but button batteries are cheap at Amazon and easy enough to pop in and out.

Ergonomics

The Harmony 890 was comfortable in my hand and I liked the soft key programming functionality. By today's standards it is a little bigger and heavier than you would want.

The Smart Remote is much thinner and lighter and feels good in your hand. The outside covering has a soft feel to it.

Functionality

The soft key programming functionality on the 890 was nice and needed before for my setup. For whatever reason, I often had to use the 'help' feature because frequently one or another component would not do exactly what was desired. The IR blaster and extensions were properly located.

On the Smart Remote, I thought I was going to miss the soft keys that were on the 890. However, I realized the Smart Remote actually has keys for all the functions I used to have to program special - things like the satellite remote colored buttons for special functionality. In addition, it flawlessly operates all the components now.

title: I would not recommend this headset, look elsewhere..
text:
I got this headset to replace a pair of G930's. While I like them overall, they have a few major shortcomings.

Main Pros:
Comfort - Most comfortable headset I've ever worn.
Speaker / mic quality - both are extremely high quality and perform well
Range - The range on these things is amazing. I live in a 3 story house, and I can go to the edge of my backyard or to my mailbox and still hear.

Main Cons:
Connection - The connection seems to drop out every 10 minutes or so. One time when the connection dropped, the headset ceased to function at all. I had to force a firmware update through the command prompt to make them work again. Other times I have had to disconnect and reconnect the battery to get them to turn back on.
Limitations: The connection to my phone through these is wired, which didn't bother me, I just kept my phone in my pocket and was still wireless from my computer. However, I got constant complaints about sound quality when using the phone cord, so I had to go back to taking my headset off and sacrificing that convenience which was big part of the reason I got these in the first place.
Software: The Logitech software is terrible. The UI is not intuitive and some of the features do not work, at least not all of the time.

Overall, the cons outlined above were deal breakers for me. I don't have time to mess around for 10-20 minutes trying to get these things to turn on and function properly. When they work they're unparalleled on PC, unfortunately they don't work all the time. I ended up ponying up the extra cash for the Steelseries Siberia 800's for a truly wireless experience on both phone and PC.

Additional Note: Logitech's phone support was terribly rude and unhelpful in fixing my issue. Ended up hanging up and googling the problem to find out that it's fairly common, and forcing a firmware update through the command prompt fixed the issue. This shouldn't be a thing in consumer electronics. I work in the tech industry, but I would hate to have to walk someone through the process involved in fixing this issue over the phone. Simply unacceptable for a headset at this price.
