title: OUTSTANDING Warranty and unfortunately I have to be happy about it.
text:
This is an updated review of the Logitech F310 controller. My Son and I play Final Fantasy XI and use the F310 (wired) and F710 (wireless) controllers in digital mode every day. Sometimes we use them for only an hour or so and other days it can be for over 14 hours.

Over the last10 years we bought ten (10) F310 controllers via Amazon. They last about six months to one year before something happens, such as a stuck key or a key that won't function. What typically breaks? This time it is the Y (orange) key, while other times it will be the X (blue), A (green), LT, RT, or one of the d-pad keys. Each of these key are important to FFXI play.

I'm surprised these controllers don't last longer given Logitech offers a three year warranty. I can't believe Final Fantasy XI is harder on controller than other more recent games.

My Son doesn't like using a less than perfect controller, so he'll pay for a new one instead of waiting for Logitech's warranty replacement. I just finished buying a replacement (today, September 6, 2022), with overnight ($2.99) delivery (7AM to 11AM) on his behalf. This is our 10th F310 since 2012. (From March 2004 to 2012, we were using either a Sony PS2 or PS3 with PS2 support to play FFXI. We moved to FFXI on Windows in 2012.)

Over the Labor Day weekend, I started working with Logitech for a replacement. They're wanting a video showing a stuck key. I'm not sure how to take a video of a key that won't quickly pop back up. I sent a photo of the key in the stuck position instead of the video. I'm sure I'll figure something out should Logitech insist on a video. Bottom line is my Son doesn't want to wait for Logitech to make up their minds and send a replacement. I can understand because a broken controller makes game play next to impossible during battle.

I'd give the F310 a 5 star rating, if the controller would last longer than six months to a year. I'm giving it a 3 star review because, while Logitech stands behind the product, it is still time consuming to go through the replacement process. Sometimes, I don't even try to get a replacement.

On recommending the F310 controller, I'll say we continue to buy it. After all at US$16 each, they're easy on the allowance I give to both of us. My Son says he'd be willing to spend US$80 on a controller if it would last 6 years plus.

title: Favorite mouse

I own two of these mice and insisted that my employers buy this model for my use at work. It works with MacOS, Windows, and Linux, pairs with the Logitech universal dongle.

I really like that I can program its buttons and wheel to be however I like. The wheel tilts left and right, doing whatever you want (I have it send keystrokes that switch desktops on my Mac) and I programmed the "hidden" thumb button for doing region screen captures to a file. The button just behind the scroll wheel (dis)engages a detent mechanism so you can spin the wheel freely or have it silently "click" as you move it, and the wheel is also a third mouse button.

title: Excellent keyboard
text:
I love this keyboard as well as the Mac version that I use at home and at work. My prior employer and current employer both buy the Mac version for their Mac users. I bought this PC version to use with my Linux boxes. They use the Logitech Universal dongle and are easy to pair. (I found a program written in C that runs on Linux and starts the pairing process.) It is solar powered and maintains a good charge just on the light in my office (CFLs and Florescent). The "PC" and Mac versions are virtually identical on the outside, differing in mainly in the keys around the space bar, the labels on the F keys and the keypad. The feel of both keyboards is the same, so I can switch between computers without adjusting my typing.

These are powered by a rechargeable battery which has lasted for nearly two years in my Mac keyboard. There is an application that runs on the Mac, and so I would assume on Windows, that gives you stats on the current power level and light level. The keyboard will maintain power for weeks without charging, as in being in the dark, depending on your usage. However, even the light from my monitor seems to help charge the battery.

Cons - this is a "chicklet" keyboard, it does not have the full action of a traditional keyboard, however, my personal preference is now slanted to this style (v. a typewriter style).

title: Works better with some devices than others - but a great gadget that revitalized my dated audio equipment
text:
Great deal - would be five stars if I factored in the low price.

Works perfectly with my dated but wonderful [[ASIN:B000V2FJAS Bose SoundDock Portable 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock]], which is in excellent working order but lacks wifi or Bluetooth connectivity. I've been streaming Spotify and Pandora from an Android phone to the Bose using this adapter over the last 4-5 hours, and the only interruption I've experienced is when other audio from my phone, as from notifications, cuts in (not sure how to program the phone to limit the streaming to just the radio app --?). The audio quality is great - not quite as good as when my phone is wired directly to the Bose, but more than adequate.

Set-up took less than a minute:
(1) Connect the included RCA-to-3.5mm cable to the adapter, using the RCA plugs (the standard old-school red/white plugs..)*.
(2) Connect the other side of the RCA-to-3.5mm cable to the Bose speaker dock, using the 3.5mm plug*.
(3) Plug in the adapter to a standard outlet using the included charger/power cord.
(4) Ensure Bluetooth is enabled on my phone, then pair the phone to the adapter (you're supposed to push the pairing button on the adapter, but I didn't have to do this - it just flashed blue and paired automatically and pretty instantaneously).
(5) Open my Spotify app, log in, and start streaming!

*The included cable can be used the opposite way (i.e., with the 3.5mm plug connected to the adapter, and the RCA plugs connected to your receiver/speaker) to accommodate the jacks/sockets of your particular device, since the adapter has both a 3.5mm and RCA jacks.

The adapter makes it unnecessary to upgrade my Bose, as I'd initially planned. I actually prefer my Bose to the newer models, so I'm thrilled about this. I might get an additional adapter to work with my equally dated [[ASIN:B004JO1ZO8 Bose® Wave® Music System with Multi-CD Changer -- Platinum White]], which can also operate as an output speaker for various DVD and MP3 players.

On the downside, I wasn't able to make this adapter work well with my 1990s Kenwood receiver (connected to passive B&W speakers). There was considerable interference, possibly due to the nearby router, which unfortunately can't be moved. Also, the adapter continued to buzz even after I turned off the receiver, and there is no switch on the adapter to turn it off (you basically have to just unplug it). I might play around with it some more and try some of the tips offered by other reviewers - e.g., try a high quality RCA to RCA connector and/or remove the adaptor's internal metal plate that some have reported to be the problem.

All in all, a wonderful device, and an amazing deal given it has essentially brought back to life my antiquated (but beloved!) audio systems!

I pulled this keyboard out of its box about 20 minutes ago, and I already love it. As another reviewer said, it feels like typing on a really nice laptop keyboard. I also like Logitech's unifying technology in the receiver - my existing mouse was also on a unifying receiver, so I can connect the keyboard and not take up an extra USB port. Big bonus.

I won't know until I've used it for awhile how the solar charging works in terms of battery life, but it shipped with a full charge and there's an app you can download to see the charging/battery status. title: Mostly great keyboard for home use
text:
I needed a bluetooth keyboard that would work with a iOS and Android devices in my home and this seems to be exactly perfect for that use. Because I like physical keyboards, I'll give a bit more info if you are unsure if this is for you. I am a fan of Logitech items. I own a Logitech Type+ for iPad and it is fantastic for use away from home. This multi-device keyboard is not ideal for travel. It is however great if you need a keyboard for multiplle devices in your home or office.

Pros:
- Keys are large size with a good amount of space between. For those who learned to type on a full-sized keyboard, you will be fine. If you are used to the more condensed portable keyboards then your fingers will need to adjust to the spacing.
- Works perfectly for 3 devices - IOs and Android tested perfectly. It's great to have this for my phone.
- Steady on a solid surface. It is holding an iPad Air 2 (I'm using the keyboard to type this) and it is holding fine. There are no magnets to hold the device in the slot, so I would be careful if using on a lap or other unstable surface
- Nice response to presses. There seems to be no lag from the time that I press a key to when my device responds. So far no mistakes either - each button does what it is meant to do on my devices
- At used item prices this is a deal
- Can be used without supporting a device - meaning you can use the keyboard while the device is in it's own stand nearby. This is helpful if you require a specfic viewing angle
Cons:
- not ideal for travelling. It's not heavy, but it is not light either due to the fact that it needs to support a device in the slot.
- not ideal for unstable surfaces like a lap. It can be done (I'm testing that now) but I'd be concered that the device can fall out if bumped hard. It's a deepish slot and well designed, but I don't take chances with expensive tech.
- a bit of a key click. It's about the same volume plastic key sound as my desktop keyboards. I think they went with this design as this really is more of a use it at home or office sort of thing where people will understand the sound. It's not for stealth blogging. The keys are well made and they make a sound.

Overall I really like this keyboard. It's a great stay at home/office keyboard that seems sturdy enough to last. I also like that it uses standard batteries so you can just buy new if you need to while out and about. I have enough devices to charge without having another charger. I opted for the white keyboard as I'm usually a neat freak and it looks great with my devices. The main feature that I really like is that I can have bluetooth profiles for three devices and just switch between them with the wheel on the left. This could be ideal for families with 3 users.

If you are looking for a portable keyboard for use on the go, this may not be your solution. For those of us who are working at home or office this keyboard is one of the better out there in my opinion.

title: CAUTION. Not Compatible with Any iOS Devices such as iPad, iPod, iPhone. 5 Star Otherwise
text:
The only reason this is given 2 stars is to put it into a category of review that might make it more visible to some, who might make the wrong assumption that I did. This is a FANTASTIC Bluetooth wireless mouse BUT, it can't be used with any iOS devices...that is any iPads. I am somewhat new to the world of Apple with my first purchase of an iPad Air 2. When the product description said it was compatible with any Bluetooth enabled PC's, Mac, and Windows 8 Tablets, I thought that "Mac" meant any Apple devices. Naive me. But you learn by doing. I had to call Apple support to find out why this new mouse would not connect (since it connected effortlessly with my desktop PC), and found out very quickly that none of the iOS devices (iPod, iPad, iPhone) have mouse cursor technology built into the operating system, since everything is built around touchscreen. Thus there are no wireless mouse products out there that can work with iOS operating systems.

I asked Amazon for a return credit, since I felt the product description was mis-leading since it did not have a disclaimer regarding the iPad. Amazon promptly processed a return authorization and gave me credit. So I have no ill feelings about my lack of knowledge, leading to disappointment.

As far as the mouse itself goes, I did try it on my PC to try to find out why it wasn't working with the iPad, in order to determine whether it was defective (prior to discovering that iOS devices are not mouse capable). When I turned on my PC, I found the M557 to be instantly recognized by my PC and ready for use, without any effort on my part. In fact, this mouse and my other Logitech wireless mouse which I have had for some time, were simultaneously functional, so I could go back and forth between the two and my PC did not hesitate to respond to either (just an interesting side note which is inconsequential). So, for all of its features, I would give the M557 a solid 5 Stars. I have four computers (between desktops, laptops, etc) and have always purchased Logitech keyboards and mice. Logitech is the best on the planet when it comes to this category and I have had several Logitech mouse products which have functioned flawlessly for over 10 years. So, buy it if you have a Mac, PC, or Windows Tablet. You will not be disappointed.

title: My favorite mouse ever, but short switch life
text:
This is probably my favorite mouse I've ever owned. It's a comfortable size to use, but unlike its bigger, more expensive, desktop-oriented sibling, it's not over-ergonomic so as to make keyboard/mouse context switches more difficult. The click-on / click-off flywheel scrolling works so well that its not difficult for me to use a mouse without it, and I prefer the dedicated middle-click button on this mouse to the wheel-click button on the Performance MX.
The standard AA batteries last remarkably long (even when I used cheap ones), and they're wired in parallel instead of in series, so it will operate off a single battery if you need it to.
It has a compartment for storing the Unifying receiver, and a well-built, conspicuously placed power switch on the bottom that can easily be operated with one hand to avoid accidentally waking up a PC.
The tracking is completely flawless, and the sensor is neatly located in the center of the device.
I've used it with PCs, Macs, and Linux machines with equal dedication over the years, and experienced no major problems with any of them - though I do recommend passing on the bundled-in browser plugins for "smooth scrolling" on the Mac/PC versions of the support software. Honestly, there's no real reason to install the support software at all.

I've noticed a number of other reviewers cite that the buttons start to fail after about a year or two of normal use. Having used this mouse for about two years, I can confidently claim...they are correct. The microswitches for the left and right buttons in this mouse are cheaply made and fail.

I'm comfortable with a soldering iron and have done switch replacements before, so I attempted to homebrew this guy back to life. I've generally found that with very little exception, mice use rugged little through-hole soldered Omron micro tactile snap switches. They're easy to source, and you can generally just steal them from otherwise broken mice.

The Anywhere MX uses a surface-mount version of a Zippy Technology Corp (zippy.com.tw) tactile snap switch which appears to have been discontinued from their catalog, making the switch unreplaceable. It's a much smaller footprint than other switches that do the same job, so it may not be too surprising that it wears out so quickly.

With that in mind, I definitely got my $30 worth of value out of this thing in the two years since I got it, and I'll happily pick up another one and drive it until it dies (based on the other reviews I'm reading here, I should expect that to take another year or two).

title: Some nice features, and some not so nice features
text:
This keyboard performs well in the HTPC environment it was designed for, and has some nice design features. But it also has some problems.

1. The keyboard is silent to type on - very nice - but this gives the keyboard a very mushy feel. You won't want to use this keyboard for any kind of serious typing, ever. Not even medium serious. This is by design, so be aware: it's meant for the minimal amount of typing you need to do to find the next episode of Walking Dead, not for anything more.

2. The keyboard is meant to be held in your hands or on your lap. When sitting flat, it is FLAT on the surface - there are no adjustable feet. But when you are holding it the way it's meant to be used, there's a left-click mouse button conveniently located on the top left edge that makes it easy to use your right hand to scroll and left hand to click.

3. The manufacturer is very consistent in its denial that Linux exists or that Linux users would be interested in its products. They just don't care. So, there end up being things that can only be configured using a Windows program. This can be inconvenient and frustrating if the last Windows box you owned was running Win3.1. Fortunately most of these things don't seem too critical, but one that is for me is that the touchpad will click far too easily - even if you push down a few milligrams too heavily while scrolling. Apparently this is configurable, just not for us insignificant Linux users. Also, the "enhanced gestures" won't work with Linux. Although, not sure exactly what those are...

4. The backlighting and room-lighting sensor work well (although my first unit had a failure with this feature and had to be returned). It's easy to use and navigate with in the dark or low light. There is no Caps Lock indicator so you can find yourself Caps locked without knowing it.

5. The keyboard and touchpad collect grease and fingerprints like it was a magnet for them; just seems to be a function of the kind of plastic being used. My high quality keyboards and touchpads don't exhibit this phenomenon. If you eat while watching TV, some of your food is gonna end up as a streak on the touchpad.

6. It's kind of expensive for what it is. To me $100 seems unwarranted, and even $80 seems a bit steep. They appear to be marketing this as a higher-end luxury product, but it's really not. Premium textures and metal-like finish, pffft, not really.

7. The battery in this keyboard requires periodic recharging via a USB cable. Unfortunately the connector is a USB mini-B connector, which is well-known to have high-failure rates after being plugged and unplugged too many times, so be careful when charging or you will trash your keyboard over a stupid USB jack.

8. I've not yet tried the Bluetooth connection so I can't report on how that works. The Logitech mini-USB dongle connection works fine, and they include a USB extension cable in case your TV or computer has USB ports that block the dongle's wireless activities.

All in all, nice to have a combination keyboard/trackpad like this in my own HTPC setup because for the most part it works well. I just wish it wasn't presented (and priced) as such an upscale luxury item.

title: Decent with Pros and Cons
text:
I debated returning this for a few reasons. First, it's small and noticeably so once you get it in your hands. Honestly, it's sized for a child. Next, it's ergonomically odd. With any mouse ever, you arch your hand over it. Oddly, you'll do that with this mouse too, but it's just a phantom arch since the mouse is flat, but laying your hand flat on it is something that's just plain uncomfortably weird. However, the main reason I drop a star is the clicking sound. Every mouse makes noise, but this one is loud enough to annoy. When you press down on it, the center of it is what gives in to click. So there are no right or left click buttons like on a normal mouse, the center underbody gives in to click. Not really a design flaw since that's how it's meant to be, but since it's structured this way, the click will be naturally louder. Once you get over that annoyance though, it's alright.

For the benefits, the number one reason to buy this mouse is the fact that it's a rechargeable bluetooth mouse. That's it. The touch features aren't that unique. Any precision touch pad on windows 10 is better than this mouse. If you have windows 8, this mouse is fantastic because it can do more, but with windows 10, it does enough to just get by. Scroll, middle click, right click, windows menu, and maybe notifications if you tap it right. Installing the Logitech manager to update your preferences is also a breeze. Furthermore, another added feature is that it works with MacBooks and Tablets without any modifications. Don't expect it to work with your Apple iOS devices though because it won't. Couldn't get it to work with an iPod or iPad, but Android will play nicely, as will Windows Tablets.

Main takeaway is that it's nice to have a mouse that can switch from your Computer to a Tablet with the switch of a button, which this device gives you. Battery lasts for a decently long time that will get you many hours of use before the need to recharge. Just remember that it has a loud click and basic touch features. At $38, it's not awful either and will transport nicely. Any micro-USB cable will charge it too so you don't need to use the tiny cable only that comes with this device.

title: Very poor product fraught with design problems (do not buy).
text:
Avoid this product unless you like having lots of audio disconnects and broken parts due to a faulty design by Logitech. I'm a long-term Logitech customer and have many of their products, but this gaming headset has been a disappointment. The wireless design is plagued with regular audio disconnect issues sitting just two feet from their transmitter. The ear muff attachment points will eventually break and be dangling by a wire. Just Google "G930 cracked plastic" and you will see many discussions and pictures of that particular problem. Lastly, getting Logitech to respond to a warranty replacement has been an exercise in frustration. They are very slow to respond/act and I'm still waiting after (2) weeks of getting confirmation that they received the warranty request.

This wireless product (as designed) is a waste of your money, but there are much better (wired) products right her at Amazon. I highly recommend the HyperX Cloud II as a much better choice than Logitech.

My wife was looking for noise-cancelling headphones that don't insert into your ears, so I gifted her these headphones. She has enjoyed them and says they work well. When I've used them, the sound quality is pretty good but I've heard better, especially on the extreme tone ends (high and low pitch). The noise cancelation is acceptable but not as good as mine that insert in the ear. They are more comfortable than other "cup" headphones but no matter the design, if you wear them for hours there will be some discomfort.
In the end, I still prefer the ear insert headphones but these are pretty decent - I would actually give them a 3.5 star rating; gave 4 instead of 3 for good customer service and longevity as we've had these for a while, and they're not as pricey as high end versions.

title: Over-hyped camera with some issues
text:
The image quality is good. It records well even when there's not a lot of light in the room (much better than my previous $20 Chinese web cam I bought from Amazon). Overall it's simple to use. However it has some driver issues.

The video settings will frequently not save, so at times I can use it at full 1080p and other times it will only be recognized at square resolution. This happens in multiple programs that I use it for. If I'm lucky I can use the 1080p but that's lately less than half of the time and I'm forced to broadcast with a square-sized web cam. This is very unprofessional.

Also the drivers themselves aren't very good for this camera. Windows will frequently not recognize the device, so unplugging and replugging it into a different USB is a common thing I have to do daily in order to get the drivers to "stick." This part might be related to Windows 10, but the other problems are likely just due to this camera's poor driver support.

Overall, not a bad camera, but this thing won't mow your lawn and clean the sink. A bit over-hyped in my opinion.

text:
I finally got one of these remotes and I just love it. It controls 7 devices and (currently) 4 activities and was very easy to set up using the downloaded software. Now, the wife and kids can easily control everything with the press of a single button that actually makes sense like "watch a movie". Everything just seems well thought out and easy with this remote.

The only drawbacks (from my perspective) is that 1) The sync often fails. Closing the software and re-opening usually solves that problem. 2) It can't control non IR devices. title: Great headphones for the price! Great sound, range, connectivity, and function. Limited Battery Life.
text:
I've used this only for the last week. So far comfort and sound quality are excellent. Battery life states 6 hours, which is limited. As long as you shut it off when not in use (there is an off/blue tooth/wireless switch an a LED indicator) it lasts all day and into the next. I mostly use it for listening to music, taking/receiving calls, and other IM voice communication. Calls were not the primary reason. I use mine with a blue tooth 4.0 receiver on my desktop and what is built into my laptop. Excellent range; about 60' where the first break happens, but I can go to about 80-100' before it becomes bad. My desktop receiver is elevated (USB extension) above the cube walls which helps with range. I do not use the included wireless, but it's a nice touch that it has a place for storage of it in the left ear piece where the battery compartment is also located. Overall the features and design are very good. Battery life could be better. The left ear piece could hold a large battery and would be welcomed. At least the battery is replaceable and you could have one charging and one in use, but that is not very convenient. Overall, I really like these. Comfortable for long term wear, great sound, folds for easy travel, very light, and connects to both blue tooth or through the included Logitech wireless dongle.

I wish it had a wired jack to use it without wireless if the battery runs out. A bigger battery (or option) would also be a welcome plus. A case would also have been welcomed, but that's asking a lot for the price. It also will not activate (answer/hangup) my Shoretel Softphone with the play/pause (which also has an image that indicates that it's intended for that purpose) which would have been nice; that maybe more a software issue than a problem with this headphone. It's easy enough to mouse to the popup and click answer; just would have been nice. The Off/BT/Wireless is hard to move smoothly; that's both good and bad.

Charges only through USB cable. Not a negative since you can plug it into an computer or phone charge.

Because they are so light (good feature and also concern), I am concerned they will not last as long as others. I feel like if I'm not really careful they will easily break. However, for the price they are well built and function very well.

Overall impressed and happy with the purchase. Price was excellent for features and sound quality.

title: Bad battery system mars an otherwise excellent mouse
text:
This mouse might be a 5 if it weren't for the power system. Awful design. First of all, it doesn't use replaceable batteries; it's built in. I am a fan of replaceables. I have a lot of rechargeable AA and AAA and keep them ready. Swapping out a couple AA takes seconds and I get hundreds of uses from them.

This mouse has the rechargeable battery built-in. So what? Well, I'd be fine with it if it were a better battery. But first of all, it doesn't last. Every week or two it seems to go dead and I have to recharge. OK, so what? Well, I could live with that too if it gave you some notice. Then I could hook it up to the USB cable and recharge overnight. But it gives you NO notice. You just suddenly have a dead mouse. Click on something, it works. Then you try to move the cursor...nothing. No warning. But what makes that really bad is there is no way to know how much charge you have in the battery. There are three small LEDs on the left side of the mouse, and when it's plugged in to USB the lights blink in sequence to let you know it's charging. Wouldn't you think they'd use those lights after it's charged to let you know the status of your charge? Nope. No way to know. Logitech decided that it's most expensive mouse should just work until it doesn't, with no warning. You can't even press a button and see the charge condition of your battery.

So, I'm happy with the mouse in every other respect. But then that's a little like saying you love your car if only the engine would work. You really can't average your star rating for dozens of features and come up with an overall rating. This is a 5-star mouse in most respects, but I'd probably rate the power system a 2, being generous. So with the other features being so good, I'll give it a 3.

All of this can be rendered moot if you can form a habit of plugging it in to charge every Sunday night, for example. Maybe set a weekly reminder in your phone alarms or calendar. Without that, you'll be constantly annoyed when it just dies on you.

Logitech, you couldn't come up with a better thought-out battery system? Really? Very disappointing.

title: This is a very nice feature that most modern TVs have
text:
This product has potential but the product managers missed two obvious features that this product that make it frustrating to use. First, there is no "no action" power off timer. This is a very nice feature that most modern TVs have. But, if your TV's "no action" timer times out, it will turn off, and then be out of sync with the logitech hub which thinks the TV and current activity is still powered on. Anyone whose every used universal remotes in the past knows what a pain being out of sync is. This problem exists with all of Logitech Hub productions, even the expensive Elite. This leaves the user with needing to manually set the sleep timer each night (for those of us who need the TV on to go to sleep).

Second, this remote has no backlights, so it is worthless in a dark or dimly lit room. Silly.

Those in charge of deciding on the functionality of this product should be fired. There is customer feedback on their forum that is years old informing them of the need for the "no action" timeout issue, but they've simply ignored this obvious feature. Just another case of lack of competition causing lack of innovation.

title: Good but needs improvments
text:
Pros
------
1. The remote uses RF and doesn't require line of sight.
2. The remote is very 'slick', well build ('rubberized') and comfortable.
3. The blaster is very 'strong' and does reach every equipment in the room.
4. The configuration apps can identify almost any equipment.
5. Option for two more wired blasters.
6. Support for IFTTT.
7. No need to charge the battery each time (like the more expensive one) and it lasts for a very long time.
8. Good Android & Ios configuration applications.
9. Hub is small and slick, well build.
10. Support for Hue lighting (but basic), Nest thermostat and other home automation devices.

-----
1. No self-lighted remote which is very annoying using it while watching a movie.
2. Sometimes there is a lag in the response to a button push.
3. No support for LG air conditioners
4. Sometimes the hub isn't available through the WiFi net which is needed to update its configuration. A reset to the hub (which takes 30 secs!!!) is needed, sometimes more than that - i.e. pressing the sync button on the hub).
5. No windows OS support!!!
6. Sometimes the equipment power is out of sync and it is very difficult to correct it.
7. Hue lighting support is basic (on/off or dimming) - no support for scenes.
8. Not enough home automation devices support.

title: Great Value, Only Minor Critiques.
text:
Great speaker system all together. I've been using the Z506 set for a long time. It was okay for $60 but it's under-powered and I was only able to hook it up to my TV by 3.5 aux cable. After many a house party with the Z506, it just can't produce clear audio when it's cranked up.

I'd been holding off getting something new for the TV because I wanted 5.1 surround but this idea of a separate receiver seems insanely antiquated. No good reason a TV can't send audio right to a unit that runs the speakers. Thankfully I came across this system which does just that. My TV is about 4 years old and was on the lower end of high-end TVs at the time. It has an optical audio out and that's fine for this system. If the source audio is 5.1, the Z906 recognizes it and switches to 5.1. For stereo sources like music from your iPhone, the 3D effect is nice. It moves the sound around the speakers in an appealing way which gives the impression of very rich audio.

Dolby 5.1 (when your source audio makes it available) is great. I frequently spin around with my heart pounding because I think someone is in the house. Then I realize it's just the rear speakers doing their job. The sound often seems like it's right behind you, even though I have my rear speakers mounted at 7.5ft above the floor.

I love the ability to tune the audio level of the rear satellites, front satellites, center speaker, and sub individually from the remote. The lighting system on the control pod makes this intuitive and easy to do from the couch. This is especially nice if you switch to vastly different audio sources that change the way the sound comes across. Once you're used to it you can adjust the balance in 10 seconds to make it right.

Regarding volume, these are perfect for a moderate-sized living room with a high ceiling. The sub seems like it barely has to operate at half speed to do its job just fine. I'm not a fan of a ton of base but it's definitely capable. The speakers are clear and sharp all the way up to about 9/10ths volume. At 10/10ths they don't get grossly fuzzy but they do lose some of their edge.

If I have one critique, it's depth. I spend about 20 hours a week wearing Bose QC15 sound canceling headphones (I listen to music and consume other media while I work). I've become accustomed to the deep, [maybe even artificially] rich sound from Bose. The Z906 seems a touch flat by comparison. I think this is more my point of reference than reality, but there you go. Not enough to knock off a star.

Setup was easy and the wires were long enough for my setup. If you think you're going to need to run a rear speaker a little further — or maybe need to run your wires all over to keep them hidden — you might want to order extra speaker wire. I used the [[ASIN:B001QNBUA4 VideoSecu 5 Black Universal Speaker Mount Brackets for Walls and Ceilings 1XZ (Black, 5 Pack)]] to mount my speakers. The mounts worked great without adding much cost.

I'd say this system is a great value. No, it's not a $1600 adaptive Bose system. It doesn't try to be. For a bit over $300 (and saving you money on a receiver), I think this is the best you can do. To get a better system you'd likely be in for $600+ when all said and done. If you're looking at $200 speakers and you're not sure, just spend the extra and get these.

title: Would return if possible: Complete and utter trash, which is rare for a Logitech product - Win10 Compatibility is CRAP!
text:
My personal background... I've been a System Builder and Network Engineer for the last 28 years. I know how to troubleshoot.

Decent driver support for this is limited to Windows 7. If you try to use the G930 on Win8/8.1/10, the driver is glitchy and sometimes non-functional. I have tried about 5 versions of this driver, including the most recent. In Windows 10, the device manager even goes so far as to say that driver enhancements need to be disabled for compatibility reasons. Bye-bye Dolby 7.1 Surround.

The battery is limited, and basically useless for periods of extended use. I work from home and needed these for my VoIP telephone, but they cut out constantly. I spend most of my day with the charging cable plugged in during use because the battery just won't stay charged, even after powering them down and leaving them to charge all night.

Then there's the static and channel switching problem. Forget using these headphones if you have any degree of 2.4GHz wireless networking in the general vicinity of your computer (802.11b/g/n). You'll get constant static and interference, and then the headset starts playing games with trying to find a clean channel. You'll hear a beep and they cut out for about 5 seconds as they switch frequencies. If this was only once in awhile, it wouldn't be bad, but today they were doing it for 3 hours, at least once every 5-10 minutes!

I'm trashing these, and digging out my PX22 amplifier to use with my Samsung Galaxy headphones with mic (PX22 headphone earcup plastic is broken).

Honestly, why can't anyone just make a decent pair of gaming headphones w/ mic in the sub $100 range anymore?

title: Great mouse when used properly (gaming is not recommended).
text:
Aesthetically he looks alright, not a good or, bad look just kind of there. You have a total of 5 buttons with your normal left and right click with the scroll button in between. Toward upper left part you’ll see the forward and back button with the battery LED just below those. It is designed for your entire hand to rest on this device comfortable and for me it accomplishes that. My hand rested on this mouse entirely and comfortably.

The far left side of the mouse is where the trackball exists. Rolls comfortably, appears that you can replace this with the same size of trackball and has a cool color to it. Like I mentioned before the sensor is just below that trackball and allows you move your mouse without actually moving the entire mouse.

On the bottom we have 4 rubberized feet to help keep your mouse from moving with the Logitech unifying symbol and the on and off switch.
The material made on this mouse is all plastic except for the trackball and it is a thin type plastic. At least I don’t believe it is made of plastic it very well could be.

These type of mice are super helpful for anyone that has little to no mobility from their shoulder down whether it was broken, strained or anything that is has caused. It does have the Unifying Sign on it which means you can use any USB with this symbol on it to connect the mouse to your computer. This mouse will work on Windows, MAC OS and Chrome OS. You’ll need 1 Double A battery to have this work. Their website claims that one AA battery will live for 18 months. I’ve had it for close to 3 months and it is still going strong.

The Mouse weighs in (Including the battery) at 5.01oz or 143 g. since this does use a AA battery you’re way to connect this to your computer is via USB only no ports anywhere on this device to connect to your computer. You have a 3 year limited hardware warranty.

Using this mouse takes some getting used to however, it is not bad by any means. It isn’t meant for gaming, definitely more of an office or home type mouse gaming is the last thing you’ll use this for. The trackball of this mouse was comfortable to use with my thumb. For me it was a smooth and pleasant experience.

That is the review I have for this mouse; tell me if you think if this is a mouse or not for you in the comment section below that like button. Thanks so much for watching guys and I will see you in the next video.

title: Incredible time saver
text:
This is the top of the line, ultimate TV lover's dream remote. It has all the modern convenience of a smartphone with its touchscreen capability, and I especially love the swipe and tap control (like swipe right for fast forward, swipe left for rewind, and tap for pause) so there's no need to even look for any specific buttons. All of that is great, but what makes this remote so useful to us is its programmable functions. Like the picture shows, you can program it do anything you need from "Watch a Movie" to "Play a Game" and so on. More importantly, it's not a one-size-fits-all command but you can program it to do whatever your specific system needs it to do to, for example,"Watch A Movie". Before, in order to watch a blu-ray or dvd we'd have to grab the blu-ray player remote, turn it on, then grab the TV remote and switch it over to HDMI 2 just to get to the home menu of our blu-ray player (and of course do it all in reverse to watch TV again). Now it's an easy as can be single tap of the screen and the remote does all those things for me (plus fully operates my blu-ray player and all its streaming services too). It's brilliant.

Now as one can imagine, it did take a bit of time to initially set it up because, though amazing, the remote is not a mind reader so you'll need to tell it which commands you want on there and what specific things need to be done on your home theater to accomplish this, but it really wasn't difficult at all to do. The software walks you right through it (which you will have to install on your laptop and connect the remote to said laptop during this initial programming).

The remote itself is dark and sleek and perfect to blend with modern electronics. I have the charging base on our end table and it looks great. Yes, this is pricey but you just have to ask yourself if you think the convenience and time saved is worth that price, and while asking yourself that consider how many times in a day, week, month and so on this would save you time and hassle. For our home, it's been revolutionary and we would highly recommend it.

title: Powerful and a bit flakey during setup
text:
If you have the simplist of applications and/or are completely non-technical, then you may wish to stick to the Harmony 350. The IR transmitter on the remote appears powerful, so multiple retries shouldn't be an issue during everyday use.

title: The Cadillic of computer mice
text:
This is by far the best mouse I have ever used.

I have used many types of computer mice in my years and this MX Master is thee best. As a programming, the customization, features, and battery life are bar-none.

For starters, let me say that the Logitech has hit the nail on the head with the hybrid scroll wheel. Giving both the use a ratchet mode for step scrolling, and free mode scrolling for those lengthy documents is superb. What makes this scroll wheel even better is it has a hybrid mode. This mode allows you to ratchet scroll, however, with enough force un-ratchets on the fly. Like one of those sleeper Yo-yo's!

Next, the addition of the horizontal scroll wheel. Wow! I don't know how I managed without one for so long. This allows me to utilize Windows snap features with various applications and easily navigate them as my monitors get cluttered.

The gesture button is on the same note as the horizontal scroll wheel. Absolutely love it.

The battery life in the MX Master is no joke. It will last days even with heavy use.

As for gaming. It works, and quite well. The only sacrifices here is that there is not "On the fly" DPI selector, and the mouse caps out at 1600 DPI. With that being say, however, I am still able to adjust my speed through the Logitech software and windows settings. NOTE: The Logitech software does not come with the product. It must be downloaded from their website.

The only gripe I have about the MX Master is the location of the forward and backwards buttons. They are quite small and located behind the horizontal scroll wheel. On top of that they are stacked and not side by side. This causes your thumb to be at a weird angle to press the buttons. I have since got used to their location so it is not a problem now.

I highly recommend for productivity first, gaming second, but can not recommend this product if you are a hardcore competitive gamer (Only). Personally, I use it for competitive games all the time, but if you are the type that does tournaments style gaming I suggest against its purchase.

title: Great Choice - Transitioning from the Revolution MX
text:
Ok - I am only a day into owning this mouse, but so far I am really liking it. The fit to my hand is really nice and everything works after the initial setup is complete. The software had a small niggle where it said it didn't pair successfully, but then it started working when I closed that window. I am coming from the MX Revolution. I wore out the Revolution's buttons and was getting the unintentional double click. Also - scrolling on the Revolution never quite worked right. I have had that thing for many years - and the way I see it, it did its job and I just plain wore it out.

This mouse is smooth as butter. The click on the buttons is not too shallow, not too deep. You can hear and feel the click. The Back and Forward buttons are a little odd and will take some getting used to, but they work as expected. The wheel works great - which is a welcome thing coming from a non working Revolution. Click the wheel to scroll by moving the mouse, ratchet scroll, fast spin to free wheel, mode button to change between smooth and ratchet spin... it all works just like it is supposed to work.

As far as ergonomics go, it is very similar to the Revolution, and the fit is spot on for me. I have medium sized hands (average). Over the years, this mouse style has definitely helped with reducing my pain from poor hand / wrist position when using standard mice.

The ONLY thing I miss from the Revolution is the cradle. This has a plug, much like a cell phone or android tablet. I have some minor concerns for the longevity of the plug... but I am hoping it will be fine. title: This is an actual review for the 9.7" Create with Video
text:
[[VIDEOID:591d5ffa034dfa26dcd2184a7465eba0]] CREATE for the iPad Pro 9.7 inch

Review by Ronald Epstein
August 2016

The Logitech Create for the 9'7" iPad Pro brings more functionality to the table over the Apple Smart Keyboard at a lower price point.

March 31st of this year was a very exciting date for me. I had just received my 9.7" Apple iPad Pro, announced earlier in the month. I was very anxious to own this device knowing the success of its larger 12.9" sibling. I rushed to buy as many accessories as I could, including a cover and Apple Pencil.

The one item I opted not to purchase, however, was the Apple Smart Keyboard. I gambled on the fact that Logitech would follow-up with their highly favorable reviewed Create Keyboard Case for the 9.7" model. Unfortunately, the arrival of that product would not be until 5 months later. As of the writing of this review, Create is now available for purchase on Logitech's website and arriving later on Amazon for $129.99.

The Create is about $20 less than the Apple Smart Keyboard. What Logitech brings to the table with this device is a lightweight case that wraps around the entire iPad for protection, a row of shortcut keys and keyboard backlighting. To me, that sounds like a great deal of added functionality at a lower price point. Oh...and the icing on the cake? It has a holder for the Apple Pencil built right in.

The Case

Let's begin by talking a little bit about the iPad Case. I'll list the overall dimensions at the end of this review, however, let me say up front that the most surprising thing about the Logitech Create is that it doesn't add much weight to the iPad. This is startling for me as I have bought many competing keyboard cases for older iPad models over the years and all of them add a significant amount of weight and bulk to the product. I can easily just pick up the Create in my hand and carry it around like it was nothing. It's insane that Logitech was able to fit everything into such a rather small, lightweight form factor. The iPad Pro with the Create case still comes in under 2lbs. For those that complain about the added bulk (and it's not much), one really needs to think about how this case is transforming your iPad into a powerful laptop.

Available in blue or black color, the case itself is made of water repellent fabric. It totally encases the iPad, leaving its most vital access ports open (camera, speakers, microphone, headphone and power). The inside features a lightweight polycarbonate frame with keyboard module. I would be very confident that, if this was accidentally dropped, the iPad would be well protected.

Along the front of the case are two hard "+" and "-" buttons that control the volume. I really like the way Logitech designed these buttons, and since they are perfectly placed on the case, they work flawlessly when turning the volume up or down.

Installing the 9.7" iPad Pro into the case should be a no-brainer, but for some reason, it took a little working. Instructions inside the case prompt you to slide the iPad into the top portion of the case. However, it took several times to accomplish this successfully, It doesn't "snap" into place as most iPad cases do, but instead, you have to insert the device properly into the grooves of the casing in order to secure it. This is probably the only gripe I have about this product.

The Keyboard

This is a great point in the review to talk about the most important and gratifying aspect of Create...which is...the power and pairing, which are completely effortless. One simply tilts the keyboard forward until the 3 dots (smart connector) on the landscape side of the iPad line up with the three pins on the Create case. Pairing is done automatically with no further settings to deal with. It's plug and play unlike anything I have seen before. The keyboard isn't powered by batteries, nor does it need to be charged. The power comes from the iPad Pro itself. The cover also effectively awakens and puts the iPad to sleep as you open and close it magnetic latch.

Once you connect the pins, however, the keyboard comes to life. A full array of backlit keys brighten, inviting you to begin typing on them. The keyboard, while visually cramped, has 1.4 mm of key travel. That may not seem like much, but it's larger than Apple's Smart keyboard, and the response I received from the keys beneath my fingers was very assuring. It takes a few minutes to get used to the smaller keys, but I was soon able to comfortably type a Word document with considerable speed and little mistakes. The more I have been using the Create, the more my typing speed has increased while mistakes have decreased. I was able to type this entire review using the iPad and Create keyboard, and it felt as if I were on an actual laptop --- and that's exactly the effect one should be looking for in a product of this kind.

The top row of keys provide iOS shortcut functions. One of my favorite keys on the upper left, acts as the HOME button. Pressing it will bring you to the lock screen where you can unlock your tablet. Press it down firmly and it summons Siri. The other keys control screen brightness, volume, media playback, bring up the Safari Browser or even Spotlight Search. There is also a lock button to the far upper right of the keyboard to lock down your iPad should you need to walk away from your desk for a few minutes.

The Bottom Line

It would be a very difficult thing for me to travel without my MacBook or MacBook Pro in my luggage. I don't think I have gotten to the point yet that I would trust my iPad as a laptop replacement. That's more of an OS X vs. IOS issue. However, for means of traveling in tight places, such as a plane, bus or train, the Logitech Create is the perfect means of writing documents, answering email, and allowing your iPad to perform as closely to an actual laptop as possible. In fact, the Create worked so well for my purposes, I will probably use it on my next flight before even considering removing my MacBook from my travel bag.

By far, the Logitech Create brings more to to the table than the Apple Smart Keyboard, at a lower price point. This is one of the very few times that I would say that Logitech's pricing falls in line with the actual value of the device. For $130, I think one gets an exceptional product.

PROS

Well constructed case made of waterproof fabric
Protects the entire iPad
With Create and iPad, less than 2 lbs. of hand carry weight
Keyboard needs no pairing nor charging
Top row of function keys includes home button, Spotlight Search and media playback controls

CONS

iPad does not easily slide into place. Often comes loose when opening and closing until proper fitting is accomplished.

Height x Width x Depth: 7.0 in (178 mm) x 9.8 in (248 mm) x 0.9 in (23 mm)
Weight: 15.0 oz (426 g)

3.) I'm about 6'-6" and little over 200 lbs - this thing fits my giant hands fairly well ;)
4.) Lights are cool & people will like it, but for me I use them to visually see the mode I'm in.
5.) Fully customizable RGB LED, you can set color, cycle speed & mode indicators.
6.) SUPER accurate, it is better then my Laser and I find that surprising.

:: CONS ::
1.) The cord hangs up until you get it 'use to' your desktop setup.
2.) Really miss the cordless days, but this mouse catches every signal & the slightest movements.
3.) The RGB is usually not prominent as it's under your hand or in sleep mode.

:: OVERALL :: I HATE CORDS, but I love this mouse so I am torn. I need to be highly accurate in my video, photography & gaming life, the Proteus Spectrum enhanced all my computer work & play! I have bought 2 of them now & dropped them both several times hard....they still work perfectly and remain accurate. Seriously this mouse brought my K/D up to new highs, it's so much better then the cordless laser I am still kind of in shock. It's a gaming AND business must have. Using this for websites, photo editing & detail alignments in Adobe is a dream come true.

DON'T FORGET IT's EVEN GOT MACROS!?!? I don't use them to their full potential, but the few macros I have are awesome!

title: Not like a ordinary mouse, but great, you should get one!
text: I got this to go with a Yoga Pro ultrabook, which has a perfectly fine track pad, but I find I just like a mouse better for some things. It's certainly a class looking mouse, and is visually complimentary with the ultrabook, if you care about such things. I wasn't sure I would get used to the thinness and  it did take a bit of adjusting at first. I am comparing somewhat to a Microsoft Arc Mouse which I have for my Surface Pro at work. This thin mouse doesn't fill your hand like the Arc does, but the resulting grip turns out to be really good for fine precision and doesn't seem to be fatiguing even after a full day of  use. The buttons  took getting used to, they are actually on the bottom so you click the whole corner of the mouse down. That works much better than I expected, after you get used to it feeling a bit different it's no problem, although it does turn out to be a bit louder than a typical mouse click. I was skeptical about the "wheel" being a sort of track pad on the top of the mouse, but in practice that works great, way better than I expected and in fact way better than any mouse wheel I ever used.  While I am not using it at present, the ability to switch between 2 computers is well done and something I have wished for in the past. Battery life seems excellent, and there's a nice app that lets you check that easily from your computer. All in all, this mouse was a good purchase and is worth the money.  There's a case available (probably in your  "people who bought this also bought..." list) that's a perfect fit and very protective but does make it significantly thicker than my ultrabook for storage.

title: Worked well for the Mac while I had it but... you feeling lucky?
text:
I used to think this was the best keyboard for the Mac... until I also bought the Windows version.

What could possibly be a very good keyboard -- the springs feel great and the keyboard mostly works well -- this product is hampered by a company with the second-to-worst warranty experience yet (Sony still being the worst). Given the number of complaints I see regarding a poor battery in this keyboard, I would therefore be very wary about risking buying anything else Logitech. My keyboard has a key that fires repeatedly at the slightest touch. Keypad 0/Ins. A key that shouts "000000000000" when you rub might be funny if I didn't rely on this key so much for copying and pasting.

Talking to Logitech support has been a lot -- and I mean A LOT -- like talking to a wall. It's like they don't even speak English (and probably don't). They have repeatedly made it abundantly clear that they are driven by greed and not by what is right. They won't consider my claim because my receipt indicates I bought it new as an open-box item. Their warranty policy doesn't exclude this scenario but, still, they couldn't care less that their product doesn't work right. If anything, they think the seller should absorb the shipping costs of this item to make up for something they failed at. That doesn't make any sense to me. They have a warranty policy and they should honor it. But they won't. So... you feeling lucky?

I would definitely recommend getting this and if you ever have any trouble with your product, contact Amazon Support and I'm sure they'll find a way to help you out.

title: Excellent Except for the "N" Key
text:
Update - one year later - the keyboard has performed like a true champ - and gone on a few travels as well. I remember to turn off the keyboard about once a month, it has had no impact on it. It never slides around, doesn't bounce or vibrate, and has a quick response to the touch. The keys have not gotten stuck and the "silver" background - which apparently is one large sticker - has remained intact. I've gently wiped it down a few times with a wet cloth, but that's about it. I have been pleasantly surprised at how sturdy it is, how well it has stood up to daily abuse, and how well it traveled on some pretty rough trips.

The only con - the printing on the keys has worn off considerably. I don't need to see the keys to know what letters I am typing, but some other people sure do - like my teenager. And the two newest, brighter pics I have attached makes it look like the letters show up more than they actually do - essentially the "N" key is all but gone, "M" and "I" and "C" are close behind, and "V and "S" are difficult to make out, and the rest won't last the rest of the year. If you do not rely on sight to type, this isn't a problem. I glance down once in a while to see where my fingers might be if they have left the keyboard, but, other than that I am okay. I'm keeping this keyboard until it collapses - it really has served me well so far.
*********************
I like the low profile of this keyboard very much. It is perfect with my MacBook, the bluetooth signal works several feet away from the laptop when needed. The numeric keypad on the right hand side is what sold me on this product - my job requires a lot of use of that section of the keyboard! Yes, the keys are exactly like those on a Mac. The silver is a close color to the Mac - slightly on the cooler side of the color spectrum. And it's solar - and it works like a charm. That solar charge works, and works well. My office does not get much natural lighting, I rely on that lamp over the desk to do the daily charging, and it does fine.

And I almost always forget to turn the keyboard off - not a problem so far.

*But*, and here's the only thing that I am not thrilled with thus far, is the "N" key printing has worn off already. I have had this keyboard about three and a half months, yes, I use it full time for my job at home, and then it also gets extra use. Personally, I don't need the imprint to find the N key, I don't look at the keyboard when I type. But my youngest kid does, and that kid had a heck of a time typing out a short report because that N key was worn off. In the photo it doesn't look as bad, but in the daylight, it is really hard to see.

Other than the N key, it's a great keyboard.

title: Great for digital art.
text:
When my Photoshop hotkey needs outgrew the five buttons on an Intuos tablet, I did some research and bought this G13. I've used this near daily for a few months now and it's become an absolute staple for my workflow. A few random pieces of feedback related to uses for digital art:

Good stuff:
+ I use this with my right hand and have no complaints. I'm a little sad that I can't comfortably utilize the joystick, but I haven't really needed to.
+ Plays very well with Photoshop CC 2015. (In some cases, you might need to record an "Action" in Photoshop, bind that to an F1-12 key, and then bind that F key to the G13, but that's more about the headache of Photoshop keybindings than the G13 proper.)
+ Seems to work well with Paint Tool SAI, Corel Painter, and Maya 2016 as well. I'm not as much of a power-user with these programs, though, so your mileage may vary.
+ No problems using this in conjunction with my Wacom's programmable buttons.
+ No indication of lag between a button press and the resulting action, even when dealing with very memory-intensive documents.
+ Profiles are easy to save and reliably switch around based on the program I've opened.
(+ For what it's worth, my OS is Windows 7 Professional 64-bit.)

Less good stuff:
- Maybe I overlooked something obvious, but I had a hell of a time trying to figure out how I could add mouse clicks in the "Multi Key" tab of the Command Editor. (Solution: Right click in the black box under "Keystrokes" to pull up a menu for what kind of mouse click to add.)
- "Repeat Options" can be spotty/jittery in Photoshop and Corel. Regardless of whether it's set to "Toggle" or "While Pressed," sometimes the programmed action doesn't carry out as expected.

Overall, as a digital artist, I couldn't recommend this enough. Being able to readily perform routine actions (creating new layers, merging layers, selecting colors, switching brushes/erasers/tools, moving the canvas, zooming in and out) without grabbing my mouse and clicking around Photoshop has greatly improved my workflow.

title: Has problems
text:
I have to say this is by far the best mouse I have ever used/purchased. I use it with a MacBook Pro mid 2010 with Yosemite. It is the perfect larger size mouse to fit ergonomically in hand, and is a good weight. It is not too light, like many cheap mice, and it feels substantial and well made. Workmanship is excellent. The left and right button click is a pleasing sound, and the free-wheeling scroll wheel is easily changed to a classic ratcheting wheel with a convenient button. I personally like the free-wheeling scroll mode. In addition, I like the side-to-side scroll wheel on the left side of the mouse, which the thumb can easily operate. It worked perfectly right out of the box. I also have high hopes for long battery life since it is a lithium battery.

One important note...I have previously purchased the cheaper optical mice by Logitech, and two of them had a substantial problem with the mouse 'skipping' large amounts of the screen instantaneously and unpredictably while moving the mouse around. This happened so frequently that those mice were essentially unusable. I decided to try the MX Master mouse because it has a laser sensor. I have been using it for about a week now and it has not skipped even once. Perfect tracking. I am very happy with this purchase so far. Will update this review if I have problems.

9/2018 Update. Unfortunately, this mouse has developed the same problem as previous Logitech mice. The cursor skips randomly across the screen when moving, such that it is unpredictable and causes you to click in the wrong place. You have to continually adjust. This mouse is garbage. Very disappointed in Logitech. No other mice do this with my computer...Microsoft, Apple, Lenovo, Dell. What a piece of nice-looking crap. 1 star.

title: From 4 remotes to 1 in a single afternoon
text:
This is my second experience with a Harmony line remote, the first was an IR only model (350 line I think) and I liked that one, but it was far from perfect. I wanted this one because I also use a Fire TV box a lot for streaming services, along with an audio receiver, blu ray player, cable box, and of course an LED TV. This let me go from 4 remotes to one that works flawlessly every single time I push the buttons.

First, let me point out that everything you need is in this package: The remote shown, the all important hub, 1 additional IR blaster, and the power supply. The instructions are as bare as possible; for a tech guy like me this is no issue, but my parents might have been turned off by this. Even the instructions in the app, while much better, needs improvement for non-tech people to follow. Even I got a little lost in the app trying to figure out how to customize some buttons, but I did figure everything out.

The hub is simply placed on a shelf in my entertainment center, which is open faced. It does not have direct line of sight with my receiver or TV, but controls them with zero issues. My understanding is that it blasts IR 360 degrees in the room and in most cases will bounce until it gets to the desired devices. So you'd really only need the additional IR blaster if you have some devices closed inside the entertainment center.

The remote feels very well designed. The buttons feel sturdy, the textured back is excellent for grip, and it's simply light and easy. It lacks some more advanced features like backlit keys and an LCD screen to customize, but whats there works well. It runs off a smaller watch-style battery, so I'm kinda glad to not have some of those features for battery life.

The remote itself is NOT an IR remote. It will not do anything without the supplied hub. All this does is tell the hub to give the commands and the hub does all the magic. It works off a radio connection to the hub, which means you don't need line of sight to the hub for the remote to work. This I consider a strong positive, no more having to point the remote and occasionally missing the sensor, especially when performing a multi-phase action like turning on multiple devices and setting the inputs and channel. Hit the button, and as long as your hub hasn't been moved since the last time, it'll work every time.

The hub allows for control from a smartphone or tablet. This is ok for some people, but I consider the app probably the weakest part of this system. It DOES work, and you need to set up the system from a smart device before everything will work well, but I've never been a fan of controlling my entertainment center like this. Like the Amazon Fire TV app, it does work, but for me personally it doesn't replace a real remote in my hand. For those that like it though, at least I'm confident that it will work if I lose the remote or the battery dies.

Once configured, this is a great setup. I don't use every feature available since I don't watch TV as much as some might, but there are features for setting favorite channels on the app, but I'm not sure that's very helpful from the actual physical remote. If you've grown accustomed to that from more expensive versions of the remotes with LCD screens and some customized menus, you might be disappointed that this remote won't do all that. You'd need to upgrade to the better remote for that.

I also connected this to my Amazon Dot device through the "Skills" section of the Alexa app. This allows me to do some basic things like activate an activity using my voice. It works very well for those basic commands, but it won't do more advanced things like changing volume. Maybe with more updates it'll get more intricate, but I like the basics so far and enjoy being able to set up and play music without looking for a remote.

Pros:
- Replaces multiple remotes very well
- Handles bluetooth control as well as IR, the 2 most common control methods today
- hub grants smartphone access and smarthome configurations
- included remote works without line of sight
- many ways to customize activities
- Haven't found a single device that it couldn't support yet

Cons:
- A little difficult to setup if you aren't already familiar with similar tech
- App seems required if things get out of sync, which might be an issue for some

title: Nice keyboard with one fatal flaw.
text:
There are many things to like about this keyboard and one that makes it a "don't buy." That one main thing: the battery doesn't last. I bought the keyboard seven months ago and now it's not holding a charge. I noticed a low charge right away when I bought it but thought it was a matter of the battery needing to be fully charged. But even after all day in the sun, the indicator light on the board flashed red instead of green showing it had a good charge. Then last week on was working for about four hours when suddenly I could no longer type anything. Today, I was working for only about an hour when it happened.

I'll try to send it in for a replacement because otherwise I like the device. It has a nice touch for the keys and I love that it's an extended keyboard. It's low profile and measures up in just about every other way when compared to a wired Apple extended keyboard. The only drawback is that there's no indicator for when you're in caps lock mode. I'll give Logitech another chance because for the other reasons, I do like the keyboard.

title: Best Keyboard for iPad
text:
This device is wonderful. It turns your iPad effectively into a laptop. The extra keys, arrow keys, forward/backward delete, etc. all work like a regular keyboard. Plus, it has function keys that handle the "Home" key and another for showing all open apps, equivalent to 2 clicks of the Home key. Also has volume control and other function keys, all of which help make the iPad a lot more comfortable to use.

This one is better than an earlier version for an earlier iPad, because it actually tilts at different angles. You can tilt it back more, and it still holds it tight. I use that all the time, and even after months of use, it has shown no signs of wearing out.

The hardest thing about it is to remember to turn off the keyboard when you close it up. If any key is pressed, the iPad will come on. If you close it up and put it in a bag without turning off the keyboard, the keys will awaken the iPad which will drain its battery in your bag. Seems to me that when you close the iPad against the keyboard, there could be a sensor to turn off the keys. Other than that, I find this keyboard to be the apex of its genre. This is the best. Your usage may dictate other preferences, but for me it's absolutely unbeatable.

title: Excellent mouse; just 2nd to one.
text:

Power management must be incredible. You rarely ever have to charge the battery. Seriously, this is an amazingly efficient device. It fits in the hand very well, with easy reach for all buttons. It's incredibly sensitive, and there is near zero latency. You will feel like it's plugged in. Nevertheless, I give it four stars. Why? Because it sits on my shelf, hardly used. I use an Apple Magic Trackpad, and there simply is nothing that compares. But when I need something that's not Bluetooth, this is my go-to device.

title: Works good at first, but after a year, not so much
text:
I purchased this keyboard after spilling beer all over my desk, and most importantly on my original apple keyboard for my iMac.

At first, I was thoroughly pleased with this purchase because I didn't have to worry constantly replacing batteries. I started using rechargeable batteries but then had to recharge them way more than replacing regular alkaline batteries. I thought that this was the perfect replacement/resolution. The addition of an actual numeric keypad was very welcome.

After after about 8 months, the battery would continually die. Now the instructions do say to make sure that this keyboard receives bright light. My home office isn't all that bright but I would charge it with my desk lamp, which was more than sufficient for the task.

Now about 1 year and 3 months of owning this, even at a full recharge, 2-3 days later it dies. The worst part is that I've let it die completely and then left it all day under my desk lamp and could never get it to charge above 88%. Having left it for an entire day (10 hours) under the light, I figured it would at least last one full week. Nope, two days later it's dead again.

If you have an under desk keyboard tray, good luck getting this thing to regularly charge. I like the ability to do away with cords as wireless removes a lot of clutter, but it looks like I'm going to have to go back to apple's wireless keyboard. As power inefficient as theirs is, I'll deal with charging batteries.

It would be nice to be able to replace the solar battery in this keyboard, but from what I've read, you can't.

My personal recommendation would be to stick with Apple's keyboard. Apparently Apple has come out with their own rechargeable keyboard, but I'm going to guess that it will suffer the same fate as this in that you won't be able to replace the internal battery once it's reached the end of its life.

title: An awesome keyboard if you follow the directions... ;-)
text:
I've had the keyboard for about two weeks now and it's been fabulous. I love having the numeric keypad, as I frequently work on spreadsheets with numeric input.

With respect to those reviews commenting about "bubbles in the solar panes"... There is a plastic protective covering over the solar panes (and the rest of the keyboard) from shipping. When this is removed you should not see any bubbles.

As another reviewer commented, the "Solar App" mentioned in the setup instructions is not available on the Logitech site anymore, but you can download it for free at the App Store. The app is a fantastic way to track the power performance of the keyboard as well as see how effective your light source is in recharging the battery. So far, my battery has remained at 100% since I started using it. Other reviewers have commented that the keyboard would not recharge after a few months. I will certainly return to update this review if that is this case, however, based on the performance so far, I don't anticipate this occurring. I wonder if this might be due to not removing the protective plastic film from shipping as well?

I highly recommend the keyboard. It is not aluminum like the apple keyboard, but it is well constructed and certainly does not look cheap. The keys are soft touch, quiet and easy to use. Not having to worry about recharging or replacing AA batteries every month or so will be a welcome change. The value for the money on this keyboard is very high.

title: Still takes up a USB port, gives up built-in USB hub, no caps lock light, but no more wire.
text:
So, Apple still only offers their extended layout keyboard in a USB wired version. I really wanted to try going wireless again, but I just can't give up my numeric keypad, editing keys, and inverted-T layout arrow keys. I'm a software developer and use that side of the keyboard quite a lot when editing code, writing comments, and of course, any time I need to enter more than one digit. The downside with the extended layout is my trackpad is further away from the main QWERTY portion, but I don't mind that.

What the Logitech keyboard buys you for $10 more than the Apple USB keyboard is wireless functionality and solar charing so you, in theory, will not have to be replacing batteries. In addition, the Logitech does not have a Caps Lock LED, unlike Apples keyboards (wired and wireless). The Logitech, however, still requires a USB port for its receiver, and you give up the built-in USB hub of the Apple solution... all this to get rid of a wire.

My goal was to have a keyboard plugged directly into my Macbook Pro in clamshell mode, yet not have to plug/unplug the USB every time I wanted to go mobile. Instead, I have power and Thunderbolt for an external display LG Ultrawide display (which also includes a USB3 hub and second Thunderbolt for my wired Ethernet adapter). I tried plugging a USB keyboard into the LG display, and while that works most of the time, there are times when the wired keyboard through the Thunderbolt hub is not recognized, but is recognized when plugged in directly to the Macbook. Primarily this occurs a restart when needing to log in, which may have to do with having FileVault enabled. Occasionally it also happens after waking the computer from sleep. Having a small USB receiver taking up a port on the Macbook is a small compromise vs. another cable.

Others reviewers have noted the build quality differences between Logitech and Apple, such as plastic vs. aluminum, and that Apple has a more precisely crafted look. I think most concerning is the silkscreened keycaps of the Logitech, vs. the (I think) laser-applied keycaps for Apple. The latter is far more durable over time. In addition, the Apple keyboard is significantly nicer looking with real machined/anodized aluminum, precise fit and finish, and lack of a logo. The Logitech does offer two typing positions. Both are slim enough to take with you on a trip.

I have not and will not install the poorly reviewed Logitech Solar app. Not only does it allegedly fill your console log with diagnostic output every keystroke, but it is difficult to uninstall. I can only presume Logitech forgot to turn off debug in their build. You can easily see the keyboard charging status with the test button on the keyboard. A green LED next to a happy face indicates the keyboard is receiving enough light to charge.

Overall, I think the Logitech is nice to type on, but I'm not really sure the downsides are worth getting rid of one wire vs. the Apple USB extended keyboard.

text:

My macbook keyboard had just quit working (in the middle of the semester mind you) and I was looking for a patch to get me through the remainder of school. When I found this keyboard one of its solar panels was cracked and the keyboard was slightly warped. Now that said, I'm pretty sure that the keyboard belonged to my douchey neighbor, he's very careless with his possessions and quite wasteful. I though at best it was unlikely to function; additionally it was missing it's wireless adapter.

So I grabbed it and began to investigate the keyboard I discovered that with little work I could use the unifier for my logitech mouse to also connect my newly acquired keyboard. After only minutes of configuring I turned the keyboard on and to my amazement it worked. Now at this point I was impressed but still skeptical, I figured it would not charge properly with one of it's solar panels completely shattered: this was not the case.

I have now been using this keyboard for several months and am ever more impressed with it. One thing that surprises me is how little light is needed to charge; I often use the keyboard in my room while watching movies. The k750 is so good at charging on minimal light that I often give little though or even forget that it is a solar powered keyboard. The batteries have never died and the keyboard always connects very quickly. There is little to no lag when typing, I type at a consistent 87 wpm and have had issues with responsiveness in the past with other wireless keyboards.

Overall I am very pleased with this product and would consider buying another if the one I currently posses were to break. The reason I gave it four stars instead of five is because of the shallow keys ( they just don't quite have that satisfying downstroke). Thanks be to my wasteful neighbor!
