title: Excellent product that works for a programmer
text:
Ergonomic Key Setup
I always buy ergonomic keyboards. As a programmer, I do a lot of typing on a daily basis so I am very concerned about carpal tunnel and other issues related to typing on a keyboard. The board is slightly angled in a winged fashion from the middle of the keyboard with a small indentation in the keyboard making the keys surrounding the D on your left hand and the K on your right hand slightly lower than the other keys. To be honest, I never quite got used to this particular feature of the keyboard. I am good, not great, typist but I found that I miss keys in this indented area fairly often. But I miss keys on no matter what keyboard I use and I wouldn't say I miss more on this one. Such is the life of a flaky typist!

Connectivity
I love the way this connects. I have a logitech M705 mouse so I did not use the mouse that came with this set. The reason, by the way, is the mouse that comes with this set does not have the Hyperscroll feature that I absolutely must have in any mouse I use. Only certain Logitech mice have it. So I had my other M705 mouse already hooked up to my computer and inserted the batteries into this keyboard and turned it on. Boom. Windows 7 found my keyboard, installed the driver and done. No hassle. Didn't even have to use the micro usb plug receiver that came with this device. Can now use the same one for both my keyboard and my existing M705 mouse. Be aware however that this could cause a problem if you have another of the same keyboards in close proximity of this multi-device micro usb plug receiver. Not sure how to handle that but I'm sure you can. Also note that I replaced my old Microsoft 6000 v2.0 with this keyboard. The 6000 had a real problem missing keys because of connectivity issues. It's like it missed the signal. I did not have that problem with this keyboard.

Keys Issue
My C key paint has completely rubbed off and I've read that others have had this issue with other keys. It's not that old and should not have this issue. That actually is very irritating.

Mouse
I cannot tell you much about the mouse as I haven't used it. As I said, I don't use it because the lack of the Hyperscroll feature found on certain Logitech mice.

Peripheral keys
The function keys are bit lower than the number keys and I found that a little harder to get to.
I really like the up down volume keys and the mute button placement.

Conclusion
All in all this a solid keyboard with good functionality. I like the feel of my 6000 better than this one but I couldn't stand the missed keys so I'll be staying with this one for a while.

title: For me, the best mouse available.

title: Ready to go out of the box, low-cost, and works all the time
text:
A wireless mouse should turn on instantly and have a battery that lasts basically forever. I bought this last year when I ordered a Chromebook for use on same, since I don't like touch pads. The wireless dongle/receiver is very low profile and because I treat the Chromebook with reasonable care, it's safe to leave in all the time, rather than to take in and out repeatedly.

The mouse is powered by a single AA battery accessed via a slide-out battery door (not a screw-secured one). There is a place to put the wireless receiver in that compartment, as well.

Chromebooks turn on and are ready to go very shortly after you lift the lid, so my concern was that I'd have to wait for the mouse to do the equivalent of wake-up and stretch exercises before it was ready to work. Not so. By the time the screen is on, the mouse is working. I have several Logitech products that have worked for years, in one case, a decade (their roller-ball mouse model T-B/C21) with daily and hard use.

I'd recommend this product to anyone who wants a low-cost wireless mouse that punches above its weight class.

title: These performance mice seem to get much cooler, yet less functional, with each iterartion.  Great programming though.
text:
I have been using Logitech mice since the beginning of my computing days. I still to this day think they make the best Mice and Keyboards, however since the days of the old performance mouse, I feel like they are drifting further and further away from what makes a great mouse. Great intentions. So-so execution.

Pros:
This mouse feels gorgeous and ultra-premium. A little light and plasticky, but a definitely upgrade from past mice.
The programmability of the buttons is very thorough. You can pretty much make any button do whatever you want it to.
The packaging is nice and the unifying receiver continues to be a winning combo.
I love the double scrolling wheels, though to be honest, horizontal scolling is something I do like .01% of the time.
Wheel action is smooth and feels great.

Neutral-
With much programmability, comes much learning. Reconditioning your hand to a new type of mousework takes some time.
Just as comfortable as the Performance MX, slightly wider.

Cons:
The new thumb gesture button is an AWESOME item, but it is really hard to press and is awkwardly high up on the pad. I would have loved to have made this gesture button programmed to BACK instead, but it's too awkward to use frequently.
The BACK/FORWARD buttons are annoyingly small. Misclicks are common.
They've moved away from the ENELOOP battery. And while this might give longer life, still can be annoying when the battery goes dead and you have to charge with a cable and not pop in a new battery.
The carbon effect on the thumb portion does not look nearly as cool in real life as the photo.

Overall I think this is a nice next generation mouse, but I wish they would figure the thumb button out better. Would be so much more useful is it worked like a thumb trigger, than having to depress downward with your thumb. Just not a smooth gesture.

title: Can be hard to program
text:
Works easily with my DIRECTV Genie. Duplicates original DirecTV controller. With my 3rd generation Apple TV also works fine, but must use MyHarmony app to teach the Hub the Apple commands and then map them onto the Harmony remote. Duplicates original Apple controller. Tougher with my Sony Blu-Ray Home Theatre which I set up to run through a sequence of steps to select one of 6 "Activities", watch TV, watch Amazon, watch Netflix, watch DVD, play FM, and play music. That took me three days to figure out, but works beautifully once set up. Before buying, decide how complicated your aims are, and whether your objectives will require you to spend days getting it going.

I'd like to add a few details about set up. You can set up an "activity" (say, 'watch TV') that uses one button to turn on all the needed units (say, the TV, the DIRECTV Genie, and the Sony Blu-ray Home Theater). You then have to get the Home Theater to select the right output to the TV from the Home Theater (say HDMI 2). Once that is done, it is easy to use the Harmony remote as your TV remote that acts just like the DirecTV remote. (Likewise for the Apple TV, which in my setup uses Home Theater output HDMI 1.) However, when the Home Theater turns on, it chooses an initial setting that depends upon what you did last, or whether there's a disk or a DVD in the unit , or so on, so the initial output to the TV from the Home Theater usually is not the one from the DIRECTV Genie. However, the MyHarmony app lets you set up a sequence of instructions inside this 'Activity' that makes the Home Theater pick out the correct output. I found this programming to be a learning experience, in part because you want to select the correct output from the Home Theater, and you don't know where it will start out when it turns on. That programming is what took me days to straighten out, because you have to create a separate sequence for each 'Activity' to select the output peculiar to every activity you want. A sequence that works may involve inserting delays between steps so the unit has time to respond. Saving a program sometimes is inaccurate, skipping steps, so reprogramming and re-saving is necessary.

title: Cheap, Reliable, Comfortable
text:
I've purchased two. These are cheap and reliable. I use mine on the arm of my upholstered chair. Feels good. My preference is simplicity -- no extra buttons on the side to hit accidentally, just left, right and thumbwheel.

The thumbwheel has left-right switches and a press-down switch, as expected. The wheel doesn't offer any friction, but you can feel very light detents as you roll it. This lack of friction takes some getting used to.

The size is relatively small. I wear x-large men's gloves and am comfortable with it. The sides are indented just right for my hands; if it weren't for the indentations, it would be hard to hold onto. The tip of my Index finger lies even with the end of the left button. My second finger overhangs the right button about half an inch. The pressure to click is light enough that this is not a problem.

These don't work well on my glass desktop, but they'll work on clothing or on the corner of my laptop.

Update: Using my older laptop to scan and edit pictures, I learned that I wanted slightly more sensitivity in dpi. I still think this is a fine device and a good buy, and I used it happily for several years. "Microsoft Wireless Mobile Mouse 4000" improved sensitivity.

title: I Wish I Had Bought This Case to Begin With...A Goldilocks Story.
text:
Once upon a time (two months ago to be exact), I bought an iPad Air 2 and wished to pair it with a keyboard for productivity purposes...

First I got the Belkin QODE Ultimate Lite case: the quality of the case was good but the keyboard itself (small keys and non-standard layout) made typing awkward. (e.g., there were many a time I was typing a text message and instinctively moved my right pinky one key over to the right to type a apostrophe or quotation mark but ended up hitting the "enter" key instead.)

"This one's too frustrating."

Next I got the Inatek Ultra-Slim case: I thought the trade off between a having cheaper case but a standard keyboard would be acceptable, but I was wrong. In the upright position, the iPad wobbled nervously with each tap and the keyboard had a very sub-par tactile feel (unsurprising given the price).

"This one's too cheap."

Finally, I decided to bite the bullet and pay a premium for the Logitech. I am typing this review using the Type+ and they keyboard is very much to my liking: the size, layout and overall feel are very similar to a standard keyboard, which means there is no awkward learning curve like the Belkin. The case material itself looks and feels great, although I do wish it framed the iPad entirely like the Belkin and Inatek; still, it does appear to hold the iPad securely enough. Interestingly, there is no "Bluetooth lag" (a one-second pause before the keyboard syncs with the iPad). I wonder if this is due to the iPad making direct contact with the magnet. Definitely another plus over the previous two cases.

"This one's just right."

I am very satisfied with my purchase. I should've just sat in this chair/eaten this porridge/slept in this bed first.

Goldilocks out.

text:
I'm not used to track balls, and this one is taking me time go get used to. I purchased it over a month ago and I'm still getting used to it. I really like the fact that I don't have to move my hand around on the table, but I was so much more accurate with a mouse than with this gadget. I will keep it because i bought it, but it will take a while for me to get fully proficient with it.
The motions are not equally sensitive, depending on the position of your thumb. I know that sounds strange, but try putting your thumb low, middle, and high on the trackball to see how it behaves as you move your thumb. It is not a linear response because you are not always actuating the ball from a point directly opposite the sensor. Yes, it's simple geometry regarding displacement along a sphere and point of rotation, but my mice don't move differently depending on how I hold them so I mark this as an unpleasant phenomenon.

There is nothing inherently wrong with the product. The build quality is fine, battery life is good, and the integration with the unifying connector is great. I just don't like how it moves as much as I expected I would.

text:
This battery is physically a spot-on match for the old one in my Harmony One remote. Replaced it without a problem, but this "new" one never fully charges. The charging symbol on my remote will get up to halfway tops. I even tried a couple of complete discharge cycles to "reset" the battery, but to no avail. At least it's better than the old one, which was down to lasting about 24 hours per charge. I can leave the remote on the coffee table now for about 3-4 days before it needs to be charged again. It's a far cry from when the remote was brand new and I could leave it for 2 weeks before putting it on the charger.

UPDATE 6/1/2017: After using this battery for a little over a year now (the original lasted over 7 years) I could no longer leave the remote off the charger for more than 24 hours without it dying. Perhaps it was the seller I purchased it from (MNR_Store) and not the battery that is at fault, but the fact remains, the battery I received was NOT as good as the original. I replaced it with a new one for $7: [[ASIN:B00N89FZF0 R-IG7 Battery for Logitech Harmony One, 900, 720, 850, 880, 885, 890 Pro, H880 Universal Remote (950mAh 3.7V Li-ion) (ALL VERSIONS)]] and so far it has worked FAR better than this Logitech battery ever did. It charged fully the first time I put the remote on the charger and has been off the charger for 3 days now with the battery icon still reading full, and that never happened with this battery.

title: Unusable - Constantly loses connection
text:
When these things work, they're fantastic. I REALLY wanted a wireless headset. I hate cords. I've got a bajillion cords around my PC, and was hoping not to add anymore.

So let's be clear:
These things sound great. The surround is really nice. They're really comfortable, and nobody has complained about my mic, so it seems to do the job.

The problem? Losing connection! Sometimes I go 5 minutes. Sometimes 30. There's only one thing certain: I'm going to lose connection at least twice an hour.

I've read that this is often due to wireless interference. So I do have multiple bluetooth devices, my cell phone, a wireless mouse, and a wireless router nearby. Perhaps one of those devices is causing interference and by shutting them off or changing the channel on my wireless router these would work. There's only one problem with that: NONE of my other wireless devices on the 2.4GHz spectrum lose connection. As great as these are when they work, they aren't so great that they take precedence over my mouse, bluetooth devices, or cell phone.

(Full disclosure: I'm only guessing the problem is interference based on what I've read. The headset or transceiver could potentially be defective, but I don't have the desire to troubleshoot. Even if I discovered interference from another device, they are essential and these headphones aren't. Sure wish some sort of logging utility were included... There is no straightforward way of troubleshooting connection issues)

title: Good product, poor documentation, abysmal Logitech customer service.
text:
Ergonomically, it fits my giant hands perfectly.

I do have some issues with the programming interface. Specifically, I wanted to map the keys to simple character keys and did so. G3 = 3, G33 = E, that sort of thing. But when I got in-game, the keystrokes were sending (if I opened a chat window, I could see them), but the commands didn't fire.

It took me about 12 hours of fiddling with the interface, downloading different game profiles and examining them, before I found that to get what I wanted, I couldn't make G3 = 3. I had to make it Press-3 followed by Release-3. In hindsight, that sounds simple enough, but there's absolutely no guidance on that sort of thing available.

I did try to contact Logitech about it. I got one "Javier" on the line who listened to my description of the problem, got some details of my system and the game I was trying to use, and said he needed to go away for a bit to research and would I mind holding. He also took TWO call-back numbers for me. I sat there with the phone on speaker for 25 minutes before I head him click back into the line and half a second hang up on me. I waited for a moment and, sure enough, I got that fast-busy tone that indicates a hang-up.

At that point I was ready to DRIVE to their HQ and return this thing ballistically through a window, but thought, "Hey, he's got a callback number or two. Maybe he did it by accident and he'll call in a minute."

I waited another hour before I tried calling back in. I never got through again.

I registered at the site and filled out a lengthy problem ticket with as much detail as I could and when I saved it, there was the ticket from my phone call which just said "Waiting on customer." "Javier" apparently dumped that first call on purpose and lied in the log to cover his butt.

So, I knocked off one star for the poor documentation of the programming interface and one star for the abysmal customer service provided by Logitech. Otherwise, it does what I need it to do.

If you have smallish hands, expect to do a lot of micro-movements of your arm to reach all the buttons. That may or may not be a problem for you, but with big old gorilla hands like mine, this thing fits like a glove (pardon the pun).

A wireless trackball doesn't provide any advantage - it doesn't matter if it's connected to the computer by a cord since you're not moving it around like a regular mouse, so the presence or absence of a USB cord makes no difference.

I wish Logitech would bring back the wired trackball, as prices for the remaining ones are outrageous, but if they have to go wireless, Bluetooth would be much better as it wouldn't require a USB dongle. I'll be hanging on to the one I have now until it's completely unusable, and unless Logitech takes my advice, I'll probably have to settle for something else. I was concerned, because that mouse isn't made anymore; had good ergonomics; and, most standard, Microsoft mice are uncomfortable for me, and cause fatigue in my hand. Update June 2020
I’ve had this mouse for almost 6 years now. It still works, despite being dropped countless times. I have mostly use it on non traditional surfaces, since I mostly use it on the couch or in my bed. It tracks well on most surfaces. But like any optical mouse, there are certain surfaces it doesn’t do well with. With this mouse, the laser isn’t visible to the eye, so it took some getting used to. But I like it.
And the batteries last forever. I once had to change the batteries, and didn’t have any fresh ones. So I robbed the AA batteries out of a flashlight. They barely had the juice to run the light on the little flashlight, but ran the mouse plenty long enough to get fresh batteries.
As for reliability, there have been a few times the last few months where it has kind of gone a little crazy with scrolling, or registering more clicks that I input. But I’m not sure if that is on the part of my computer (8 years old), the mouse, or some damage from all the drops it’s suffered in it’s like.
The surface is holding up well. A little shinier than it was new, but that from 6 years of use. The structure around bottom thumb button has given way just a little. So their is a slight soft spot in front of the button. Aside from occasionally missing the trigger for that button, it doesn’t really effect anything.
All in I do love this mouse. I miss it badly when I use someone else’s computer and mouse. I love all the buttons traditional mice don’t have.

title: It's OK - Look Around
text:
I guess gamer people and animation folks have displaced design professionals as the target for high end pointing devices. That's fine, but I think trying to make a wondermouse is the reason the VX Revolution is just OK.

For reasons I'll never understand gamers seem to be squeezing their mice all the time. Instead of looking for the problem they prefer a mouse like this with terrifically exaggerated shapes. I suppose the constant squeezing is also why they like the mouse to be lightweight with low push force buttons and borderline unstable on dedicated work surfaces.

The CADmouse from 3Dconnexion is half the price, but corded, and is far less taxing to use. I'm sure this mouse is great for somebody, but in a building full of AutoCAD Mechanical users only one person uses a VX Revolution (he's a gamer at home).

It's really worth exploring the actual source of ergonomics problems if you intend to be sitting at a CAD workstation for your working life. I'm old so I can say stuff like that and know nobody will listen. But I also get to say I told you so when your arm gets all gimpy and you spend 15 years paying for the surgeries.

If your employer will let you provide your own tools (mouse, monitors, chair, etc...) they are tax deductible. Look around at everything you use and don't get it stuck in your head that your hand, arm, shoulder and back are uncomfortable because of your mouse. The mouse might be the issue, but maybe not.

title: Cheaply made wheel breaks easily, rendering mouse useless. Awful support. Waste of 75 bucks!
text:
I've always loved Logitech mice, and when my trusty old MX 518 started having USB connection issues after years and years of (over)use, I thought I'd upgrade to this model.

BIG mistake.

I wanted to love this mouse so badly. It's excellent in almost every way. The precision, the size, the weight, the grip, the clicking, and the horizontal scrollwheel are all excellent.

But the main scroll wheel is bad. Really bad. It's got two modes--smooth scroll, and ratcheted scroll, with a button that moves the ratchet inside the wheel to switch between them. But the ratchet comes loose so easily that after a few weeks of use, it barely sticks. You can just lightly feel it applying pressure as you scroll, which--to someone like me who prefers a ratcheted scroll--is maddeningly frustrating.

Even worse, because it barely sticks, you sometimes can't even tell if you've stopped on a sticking point or between two sticking points. So a second after you take your finger off the mouse, it'll JUMP toward one of the sticking points. This means you'll scroll to a point on the page, start reading, and then the page will jump a little bit. Or even a lot! Due to some weird quirk of momentum, it'll CONSTANTLY bounce back or forward (randomly) over half a page on my Macbook. Absolutely drives the user nuts and makes the mouse a hindrance. I've gone back to trackpad control.

Don't just take my word for it, Google "logitech mx master ratchet" and go read the numerous posts on Logitech's forums from users incensed about the same issue.

UPDATE: Had an open ticket with Logitech for two days now and their support has been totally unresponsive. Defective products and poor customer service is a real cool combo! So far there's no indication I'll be able to get them to honor their 'warranty'. Waste of $75. Logitech ain't the company it used to be.

title: Great relief from shoulder pain
text:
Love it! Love it! Love it!
Some background:
==============
I have severe shoulder and neck pain every time I operate an optical mouse. It takes 5 minutes after using any normal mouse, for the pain to kick in and then I spend the whole day in pain which is easily a 8 on the scale of 1 to 10. I have spent the last 2 years suffering. My performance at work has suffered quite a bit because of low productivity owing to constant pain, doctor, PT, Chiropractor, acupuncturist appointments. I have even thought of quitting so many times but I love my work and want to continue for as long as I can. The source of my pain is still a mystery to all the doctors I have seen so far. The part of my shoulder from the neck to the shoulder joint has been swollen since last one year. It has limited me in so many ways.
My shoulder still hurts after a day's work and I spend hours pacifying it at the end of the day.

Come in this trackball mouse:
======================
I am not scared of using a mouse anymore. My shoulder still gets sore and tired but I have been saved from the burning and mind numbing pain that I'll never wish even on my enemies. Now for the pros and cons:

Pros:
====
1. Easy setup using the Logitech utility on Mac
2. The trackball feels natural
3. Does not take more than a day to get used to when switching from traditional mice. (But check the Con 2 below)

Cons (My reasons for deducting a star):
====
1. Even though the cruise control setting is available for the smaller buttons for which the speed and acceleration can be configured, it is hard to switch the hand position from operating the bigger buttons. I which there was a better way to scroll using the trackball itself.
2. It needs more practice for finer control when trying to position the cursor or click on tiny controls on screen.

title: Worked even better than expected!
text:
It's rare when the hype truly matches the results, but this is one of those products. I had read plenty of positive reviews, but honestly it worked even better than I expected!

It was bought for a number of reasons but mostly to simplify all the other remotes that needed to be used for our entertainment system. For some functions, like watching movies on the XBox One, if anything it it works BETTER than the standard controller, which let's face it is made for games not movies.

The setup took awhile, but not overly long, and from my experience, if done carefully it will work perfectly. This is a definite situation NOT to rush thing! It hooked up just fine via the USB cable to my PC, and the steps we fairly simple to get going. The main takeaway I got was you absolutely need to take things step by step. And if all your devices go through a complex surround receiver, make sure you have all the HDMI ports and receiver functions correctly lined up, as this is a big part of getting this remote to work flawlessly.

The only initial hiccup was our Xfinity 1 box seemed to pull up additional menus that were not called for by the remote. I restarted everything again and after that the problem no longer was an issue. As other have noted, it sometimes requires that you hit the All Off button on the remote if by chance you manually turned off some devices, because the remote will assume everything is still on and will not properly connect. A simple thing really, and everyone in the house is MUCH happier with one (not 3-4) remotes now.

title: Best choice in features and price point
text:
Update, February 2019:

Bumping up the review to 4 stars. I'm still using the second headset (purchased 3ish years ago, as noted below), and it's still going like gangbusters. The flexible boom mike has gotten pretty mangled, but still works. I think the issue with the plug not gripping is, I think, an artifact of aging USB cables as I've had the same issue with phones. I'll happily purchase another when / i this one goes bad, if it's still available - at this price point, you really can't argue over getting 2-3 years use out off a single unit!

Why it's not 5 stars:

When using it for music, I've had no luck finding a way to pause playback just on the headphone. The nano receiver works better than Bluetooth (when using with a computer) but Logitech has, for some reason, never included this in the "unifying receiver" program (where you can use a single receiver for keyboard and mouse).

------------------------------------------

I wanted a wireless headset to use for my frequent conference calls, and there is a surprisingly small selection under a hundred dollars, especially if you want to stick with a better-known brand. This model comes with a nano-type adapter that you can leave plugged in all the time (assuming you can spare the USB port); it also works with Bluetooth so you can use it with your cell phones or if you just misplace the nano adapter. Battery life is decent - I can usually manage several hours a day of calls without plugging it in, so I've never really pushed it to its limits there. All in all, it has a pretty good set of features for the price point.

What isn't great:
- Logitech makes a "unifying receiver" - the tiny wireless dongle - to be used with keyboards and mice - but their headsets don't work with those. So you have to use two USB ports if you're using a Logitech wireless mouse along with this as I am.
- The boom microphone swivels which is good, but it's quite bendy as well. While that is a good thing in some ways, I'm always worried I'll flex it too much by mistake and destroy it.
- It can be a little slippery - as in, won't stay quite in the right ear position - either it'll rotate forward / backward, or the sliding part of the headband will slip.
- The plug to attach the USB cable for charging quit gripping a while ago. So I plug it in to charge, and it's kind of a crapshoot as to whether it'll actually be at the right magical angle to charge. or how long it'll stay attached. This has led to quite a few instances where I'm on a call and the annoying "feed me" beep starts up, forcing me to scramble for the USB cable. What I've taken to doing is attaching a Velcro One-Wrap cable tie to the USB cable, then I plug in the USB cable, and loop it up to parallel the headband, where I fasten it with the one-wrap. It doesn't look too elegant but it works.
- The "feed me" beep goes BOOP BOOP BOOOOOP nonstop until you plug it in. A single sequence, repeated every minute or so, would be less likely to have you flinging it to the ground and stomping on it in frustration.
- The range is OK for pacing around the room the computer is in, but when I try walking into the next room - no more than 10 feet away - it becomes staticky very quickly. As my house is not made of steel girders and mesh, this is a bit surprising.
- aaaaand, it broke after 2 years - that boom microphone quit working. Admittedly it's seen fairly nonstop use, and it hasn't always been treated that gently, so I can't honestly complain too much about that, it's just an annoyance. I'm actually just about to place an order for another of the same model since even 2 years later, there's nothing else as good in the same price point.

text:
Update - Jan 2022 - yes 2022 and its been 10 years with this little marvel of a streamer. While Logitech unashamedly abandoned it and haughty streaming services like Spotify stopped support, there are still many like Pandora, Tidal, TuneIn, Slacker, Podcasts, BBC etc that are supported. Of course it’s own media server can play your private collections. The SQ is awesome both digital or Analog. Will keep it till it dies or rendered absolutely obsolete… this has been the Toyota LC of Streamer DACs / music servers with Touch interface . Flawless !

Have owned it now for 5 years, this little gem of a streamer still stands up to the most modern DACs and Streamers in market. Only one device off late has caught my attention. The Auralic Aries Mini. People we are talking of audiophile quality devices under $500 and not the uber ones that break your bank. The Auralic does almost all of the stuff Touch can do sans its touch screen. You need a second device to control the Auralic Mini. Tidal was one I had trouble if Squeeze Box will support, but with ickstream plugin problem solved! Still my go to device for DLNA streaming, Usb, SD card streaming, touch runs its own LMS within the device, internet streaming - Spotify, Pandora, Slacker, Tunein and 40000 other searchable stations. Just awesome. The ipad, iphone controller is great to control the device remotely, pause, skip, mute, station select, search etc. as long as the third party community keeps this device supported, will have it. Unless one looks at extreme Hi-Res, this device is as great as they come! As many many owners of the touch would say, you need to pry it off from their cold dead hands!,

What a pity Logitech chose to kill this line of great products. i have the Radio too for lounge and Kitchen duties.

title: Pros definitely outweigh the cons
text:
This is an amazing controller for the price. I have bought this controller 6 times at the sale price of $12.50, but when it is $20.00 I'd still buy it.

This controller feels great to hold. The wire is plenty long, the buttons are all very responsive, and its drivers have the computer recognize it as an Xbox controller, so no having to configure input settings for hours like you'd have to do with those strange third-party controllers that have unique layouts, such as "buttons 1, 2, 3, and 4" in place of ABXY. Also, I've dropped it plenty times on hard flooring and it stays together.

1 controller that I've owned had its RB button start going loose, where I'd have to press RB really hard to have it be responsive. Even after opening the controller, screws and everything, I've only been able to fix it temporarily. All the other controllers I own have been working fine for over a year now.

Pros:
Great value
Feels great
Xbox layout
Responsive
Triggers have axes
Has D-input and X-Input switch
Has a home button for Steam (but doesn't work in some games)
Works on every single Steam game that has controller support
Has a mode toggle button that swaps the D-pad and Left Analog Stick inputs

Cons:
Not the most durable controller on the market
No rumble
Wired only

The pros definitely outweigh the cons. If you're on a budget, this controller is the way to go. If you got a bit more, I strongly recommend the wireless F710 or Xbox One controllers in place of this one.

title: Overpriced hunk of junk
text:
Logitech has lost my support. They've mad some terrible products over the years. I won't buy Logitech peripherals again if I can help it. After two years of using this product, I've had nothing but complaints. The only reason I keep using it, is because I want to feel I've gotten my money's worth of the product I've bought, especially one that runs well over a hundred dollars.

So here's the things that absolutely suck about this product -

The programmable buttons interfere with the volume and the power CONSTANTLY, even if you don't press them
The power button is infuriatingly bad, as it will go to sleep (the only way I can describe it) on random, and not work
The volume control is the same as the power button, and again, the timing on when it "goes to sleep" is completely random
The wiring internally is messed up, sometimes the power button will control the volume
The microphone's mute is an NSA wet dream, if you think it's muted, think again, even if the light is red
If you unplug the headset from the charging cord, the microphone will unmute
The numbered settings for the headset adjustment is necessary, because they'll slip in and out of place if you so much as look at it wrong
The charging cord is some of the cheapest material Logitech could've gotten, and it tears with minimal effort
Sometimes when turning it on, even if connected to the charging cord, it will turn right back off, and sometimes it will not turn off at all

The only pro is that it's lasted two years, even though questionably at best. The sound quality is nothing home to write about, but it is much better than a ten-dollars set of those that rest on your ears. But that doesn't make it worth 160 dollars. The sale prices for this thing are actually more than I would pay for it if I had to buy it again. I would say this product is worth 40 dollars full price, and should be picked up for if you see it on sale for 20 or less.

Logitech, you need to rework your QA. Or if your QA has been hassling your engineers, then you need to tell your engineers to take a hike. My guess, though, is that leadership needs to get out of the game, because this is far from the first Logitech product that's been just pure garbage. I remember their products being decent about 10-15 years ago. Not anymore. Walmart brand quality, now.

title: Hands down, the most comfortable mouse I have ever used.
text:
I purchased this mouse about two months ago and have been using it non-stop since. I do a lot of video editing and my previous mouse was not only uncomfortable, but I was sure it was on it's way out as it had been randomly disconnecting from my system (Apple Magic Mouse). Since the mouse was so uncomfortable and I had always used a laptop prior, I wanted to use a trackpad regularly. So I purchased the Apple Magic Trackpad 2. It was not a bad device for navigating the system, but for anything pro-level, it was terribly uncomfortable. I had always heard that the Logitech MX Series was the best so I decided to make a trip down to Best Buy and purchase it. The first mouse was broken, which gave me great confidence in it, but I went ahead and traveled to another store to pick it one up. I am so glad I did.

I thought the side wheel was a little gimmicky when I purchased it but when I got it home and actually edited with it, the wheel's position totally made sense. I was worried that the mouse would be too small for me, as I have baseball glove-esq sized hands. It fit perfectly and all the controls were comfortably in reach. The customization software has a great UI as well and is easy to understand. Battery life is amazing: in the two months that I've had the mouse I've charged it twice with heavy usage. It's become my primary input device and the trackpad is now stored away in a drawer. I wish though that macOS had an option to zoom within a window using a mouse (like to pitch to zoom). The only option was able to find for this was to have the whole screen zoom in/out, but that is entirely the fault of Apple and not Logitech.

The only issue I have had with the mouse is that it randomly decides to go into power saving mode. It doesn't seem to have a time-out timer, instead it's almost like it does it every so many minutes regardless of wether or not it was just used. It's a minor annoyance as it usually turns back on very quickly (within 2 seconds) and picks up where it left off. I haven't had it happen while mousing around, only if it's been sitting idle, but it can happen at any interval (5 secs or 10 mins after moving my hand off the mouse). I can tell it's not the system because when I attempt to move the mouse I can feel the ratchet mechanism clicking into place and the battery indicating LEDs turn on briefly.

I can easily say though that if I had something happen to this mouse - it dies, I loose it or something to that effect - I would definitely buy another one. Having used multiple mice over the years as a computer tech and video editor, this one is hands down the most comfortable pointing device I have ever used.

title: Excellent media center keyboard, full of features, user-friendly, zero issues! Highly recommended!
text:
I recently built a custom machine at home in preparation for the upcoming Oculus headset, and to control this computer I opted to go with this Logitech keyboard. I've got my computer connected to my 70" Vizio 4K TV in the living room, so I needed a keyboard that functioned as both a keyboard and mouse in one. I wanted it to be light, and easy to use, with separated buttons for sound. This keyboard hit all my marks, and did it quite well. Here's my two-cents on this keyboard, the good, the bad, and the returnable!

Quality:
It's solid, I mean it's plastic, so if you decide to throw it at your TV it will most likely shatter, but for us normal users its very well built. The buttons are quiet, don't feel flimsy, the keyboard doesn't crash or makes any noise. It's a well built device.

Features
The biggest things for me is the backlit keys which is a must have for an entertainment system setup. I watch movies in the dark and would like to see the keys when I need them. The dim away after a second or two of no use. The second must have feature for me was the separate volume keys. Again the scenario is me watching a movie, I like to be able to reach over and find the volume up/down and mute without having to look for them. There's also a left click button on the top of the keyboard, it's a single click where your index finger would rest, this is a cool feature, but not one I ever use myself.

Rechargeable
The keyboard is also rechargeable via USB, the charge holds up I'd say for about a month, and then I usually do an overnight charge and I'm good to go for another month. There's an thing LED light that will light up red to indicate the battery is getting low and needs a recharge. I've found I can use it for a few more days to a week once that lights comes on. So much like a gas light, there's a reserve.

Cleaning
It's also very easy to clean. I'm a pretty careful and clean user, but fingerprints and smudges are nearly unavoidable. However, this is very easily cleanable as well. Just turn off the keyboard using the switch on the top, and then I take a microfiber cloth, spray some glasses cleaner or screen cleaner on the rag, and just wipe the whole keyboard with it. I love that everything comes off with ease, and after a few wipes you get a brand new looking keyboard! It's awesome, and I love how new it looks even after months of use.

Software and Keys
You can also download the software that goes along with this keyboard. This allows you to assign specific functions to the buttons along the top—the F-buttons. It does come pre-programed with decent functions, but some I wanted to customize to launch my Plex for instance—this was easily done.

BIOS
Another great thing about this is its functionality during boot. Some keyboards won't be recognized until Windows launches the desktop during boot up, but in the case I'm able to use it immediately, which is great for launching into the BIOS. The keyboard comes with a bluetooth dongle which works great! So this was a great addition. I've done a lot of custom work and had to deal with a lot of boot changes which require a keyboard, and not once did I need to use a wired keyboard. If it helps I've got the X99A Motherboard from MSI.

title: I can easily say right off the bat that this keyboard is ...
text:
Pros: I can easily say right off the bat that this keyboard is a logical step towards solving the one weakness all wireless keyboards had: a battery life. It also looks so stylish on the computer desk that isn't cluttered with wires. (Seriously, google some pictures. It looks modern and minimalist)
+ It is powered by the sun.
+ Very slim keyboard.
+ Very comfortable to type on. (For a rubber dome keyboard)
+ Looks very sleek.
+ Price is not insanely overkill for what it is worth.
+ Has a check charge button. (Which is expressed by a smiley and frownie face.)
+ Charges well. (When a direct light source is available)
+ Can charge while the keyboard is switched to off.

Cons: While it does solve the wireless keyboard problem, this keyboard isn't perfect yet. It actually requires direct light to charge it, not ambient. This is normally not a problem for those who use a computer with the lights off, but it is a problem for those who do. People generally will close the blinds to shade out the sun in order to see, this is enough to prevent a positive charge.

Another thing: when the keyboard loses some of it's charge (< 80%), it actually starts to lose it's connectivity a bit which causes some keystrokes to not register. I also noticed that the signal is not as strong as it should be. Having the receiver plugged in the back of the computer causes keystroke loss. So I had to plug it in more pain sight for it to fully work.

These two reasons were only enough to knock off one star. The keyboard is amazing when it is put to use in the proper environment. But for the clique gamer or hardcore computer user, wired keyboards are the better way to go.
- Weak receiver compared to other wireless keyboards.
- Requires direct light for it to work.
- Needs a strong charge for it to be fully functional.
- No back light? (Not a con for me, but is for those who need to see the keys in the dark)
- Drop it once, acts funny forever.

title: Nearly the same as the Harmony Companion, but cheaper
text:
This remote combo (hub/remote control) is the same as the more expensive Harmony Companion, with the exception that some of the buttons on the Companion RC are designated for smart-home devices, whereas all the buttons on the Smart Control RC are designated for home theater devices. The hub is the exact same for both products. Logitech no longer sells the Smart Control, which is probably why it sells for less than the Companion.

If you've used a Harmony remote before, setting it up is very similar, except you do it via your mobile device instead of a computer. If you have an older Harmony remote you can merge the settings into the Smart Control. Otherwise you set up your Devices and Activities. I have 6 devices and several activities. It took about an hour to get it all set up, although I was familiar with the process.

I was concerned whether I needed extra blasters. The Smart Control comes with only one. My shelf unit is not enclosed, but the TV is on a shelf above the rest of my components. I placed the hub under the top shelf, on top of one of the components. I am not sure how, but the hub controls all the devices without a blaster at all. It even turns on the tv, which is sitting on the shelf above. Amazing.

My strong advice: Use the money you save by buying the Smart Control rather than the Companion, and buy an Echo Dot. It pairs with the Harmony hub, and you can then control all the activities, and also select favorite channels, via voice. It's certainly no hardship to press a button to turn on your tv, but once you do it by voice ("Alexa, turn on the TV") you won't want to do it any other way.

The only remote I can't replace with the Harmony system is the Apple TV, because the Apple TV RC has a mic built in to control siri, a small touch pad to move around the screen and a long press on the home key to put the Apple TV to sleep. The Harmony RC can't do any of that.

The Smart Control RC is used for basic functions - channel selection, volume, play, pause, etc. If you want to go deep into the settings you'll need the Harmony app (phone/tablet). If there are special features that the RC isn't set up for, certain RC buttons can be programmed via the Harmony app. Unfortunately, for TV only one RC button was programmable. The number of programmable buttons varies based on the Activity and Devices you use.

This is my third Harmony remote, and by far the best one. The combination of Harmony and Echo really make this seem like you've stepped into the future.

By the way, at the moment there is no native support for Sonos speakers and the Echo. But the Harmony supports Sonos. You can create an activity that starts one of the Sonos Favorites and plays over the Sonos speaker. You can trigger the activity via the Echo, either with an activity name ("Alexa turn on Tunes") or via IFTTT ("Alexa trigger Led Zeppelin"). Very Very cool.

title: Top Value in an Excellent Remote
text:
I've owned a lot of universal remotes over the years, including several from Logitech and this Harmony 700 is one of the best.
I previously had a Logitech 1000 with the large touchscreen which finally died after 5 years of use. While the touchscreen is nice, it can be awkward to use because you have to be looking down at the screen rather than forward towards the equipment. May sound like a small thing, but it can become a pain to use.
The Harmony 700 has a small screen (not touch sensitive) which provides access to specific devices and additional controls. The programming couldn't be simpler. Go on line to the Logitech harmony site, tell it what devices you have and then what activities you want to set up (watch a movie, watch tv, watch ROKU, listen to music, etc), and you are pretty much done. Very simple, very quick and it makes all your activities a single button affair.
In my opinion, even though this remote has been discontinued, it is an excellent value. Lots of control, lots of flexibility simple to setup and use, at a very cheap price. You can spend a whole lot more, but you won't get a whole lot more.

title: Portable, Immersive, and fun!
text:
I purchased this to bring sound quality up a few notches from the audio out quality of my BestRunner Projector (See my Review). This was the ticket to great simulated surround sound. I use a computer with HDMI out to the projector. My sound is piped out through the analog out to the Logitech Z506 speaker system. It is not "true" 5.1, but it is damn immersive. I teach a night class and needed something portable and easy to transport. I can set up the projector, computer, speakers, and projection screen in about 30 minutes total. It transforms my classroom into a movie theater.

So why the 4 star rating? Here are the reasons: The subwoofer is a downward firing 5 inch bass driver. It is ported and tuned well. It does provide some boom, but it cannot defy the laws of physics. It also does not have a decoder on-board to decode true 5.1 surround sound.The cords for the speakers could be longer. Still, the system is priced under $100.00. What you do get (often times, for much less than $100.00) is a system that sounds very, very good. The satellite speakers are simply excellent. This is an excellent upgrade to help your TV, computer, and projector sound excellent. I honestly don't think you can do better for the money.

title: A decent wireless headset, I think best for the price range.
text:
So I'm on my second pair of these (technically third, more on that later) and am willing to call these headphones a good investment. I bought my first pair in 2012, and they lasted 2 years before the fake leather had peeled off of the ear cups almost entirely. I emailed Logitech about purchasing new ear cups, but instead they just sent me a new pair as I was covered under a 3 year warranty. My second (free) pair lasted about 2 years before the battery seemed to refuse to charge and it would randomly disconnect and refuse to reconnect to my PC. I bought a new pair in January of 2016 and accidentally sat on them, breaking the connector from the cups to the band, but was able to tape and superglue it back together (been holding together for a few months now). So I would say to expect at least 2 years out of these headsets (and another 2 if they still have the three year warranty) if you use these every day for a few hours (like I do).

On to the actual use of these headphones. You really should install the software for the headset... it isn't great, but it works much better than not installing the software. It allows you to do the customization of the buttons, which if you spend the time to set it up, works decently well. I really love the audio profile on these headphones, some of the best for a WIRELESS headset that I have used in this price range. The mic is decent, certainly good enough for gaming, which is what it was made for.

Issues: With every headset I have owned I have had sporadic disconnection/drop out issues, or issues where it seemed to refuse to turn on. These issues are usually sporadic (sometimes a computer reboot clears them up) except on my second pair of headphones where it disconnected constantly at the end of 2 years of use.

title: The decline and fall of Logitech
text:
Logitech's frictionless scroll wheel has been around a while and is terrific for scrolling through documents. I've used several Logitech mice with this feature over the years.

But the scroll wheel on this model acts erratically. It does scroll, but often will move slightly on its own for no apparent reason, or will "snap back" a little after a flick of the wheel. This means having to constantly monitor and correct the mouse's motions. The need for all these corrections means that that using the mouse for long stretches can be tiring despite the comfortable shape.

Buy this mouse only if you absolutely must have the frictionless scroll wheel. Otherwise there are much cheaper mice that are more reliable and have a better quality "feel" than this one.

Logitech used to be a maker of high-quality products but not any more. This is not the only Logitech product that has been cheapened over time. Read other reviews and you'll see complaints about poor quality switches and other issues. At this point it seems like they are coasting on past reputation.

title: BT 4.0 Gotcha - Beware
text:
Bluetooth "Smart" technology in the MX Master is not compatible with all currently operating Macs. While Macs currently shipping already have Bluetooth 4.0, older ones won't. This makes connecting by Bluetooth a non-starter on those machines. Yes, you can still use the "unifying receiver", but check before you buy if you were thinking of connecting this mouse using Bluetooth.

You can check this by going to your apple menu and selecting "about this mac". Go to the more info button and into the system report. Select Bluetooth from Hardware and look for Ox6. A number lower than 6 means you've got an older Bluetooth radio in your Mac, and this mouse won't connect to it.

You might get a BT 4.0 dongle to work, but it's another dongle. This would be a 5 if it had dual BT compatibility. For the price, it probably should.

title: Great customization, horrible ergonomics.
text:
This mouse has several buttons that can be individually customized for each and every application on your computer, or you can simply set how you want the mouse to respond in general for each button. Buttons include three thumb buttons, left and right click, and scroll wheel click. The scroll wheel allows for free scrolling our the traditional scroll and you can change between each mode by the push of a button located just beneath the scroll wheel.

I appreciate the rechargeable battery, but this is a feature that really needs improvement. I use my computer for about 5 hours per day on average and I have to recharge the battery in the mouse every 8-12 days. My previous mouse ran on AA batteries and I replaced those once every 1.5-2 months.

This mouse has a slightly curved shape that is supposed to help keep your hand in a natural position, but here it utterly fails. The thumb button located at the base of the mouse prevents your hand from resting naturally on the mouse. A natural hand position would place your thumb just above the thumb scroll wheel, and you'd need more of a sloped mouse as it tapers off to the right. I find that my wrist hurts after extended use, mostly because the reach for the thumb button is actually a small stretch from the naturally position. For this reason alone, I would not recommend this mouse as your ergonomic choice.

title: Great universal remote
text:
I bought this remote to replace four remotes that were always scattered about my living room, and it is working great. This one remote replaces a Sony TV remote, a Marantz receiver remote, a DirecTV remote, and an Apple TV remote. Set up was fairly simple and the Logitech software is easy to understand, but I agree with other reviewers that said it probably helps if you are a bit tech savvy and understand how all the components in your entertainment system work with one another.

The remote feels very good in my hand and the buttons have a nice feel to them. Definitely an upgrade over the other remotes I had. The buttons are backlit but the backlight is very subtle. I wish there were a way to turn it up but I suppose this would run down the batteries faster.

A nice feature is how you can set your favorite channels with icons of the network logo, but one thing I thought was odd is that Logitech itself does not provide the icons. You need to go to a third party website and download each icon you want to use. It would have been nice if the Logitech software could handle this.

Finally, you should know that this remote will not work with bluetooth components such as the Playstation 4. I knew this going in so this was not a surprise to me and I was still able to set up a "Play PS4" activity which switches my receiver and TV to the right settings to play my Playstation but it would be great if this remote supported bluetooth. To get bluetooth you must upgrade to a much more expensive logitech remote with less physical buttons and a rechargeable battery. I personally like having lots of physical buttons and like that this remote uses standard AAs since I already have too many things to constantly charge.

If you are looking to simplify your remote set up and you are tech savvy, then this is recommended. My wife and children are very happy to not have to juggle four remotes any longer.

title: Not for iPad Pro. Ok keyboard otherwise.
text:
Bought it for a iPad Pro as the Pro and the Air2 have the same dimensions. Although it works to hold the Pro up in the slot, the magnets in the Pro are in a different place so the cover does not attach to the iPad.

The slot is ok. It is shallow, so I've had the iPad pop out once when trying to tap the screen. It's stiff so that you can adjust the angle of the iPad about 10-15 degrees front to back.

The keyboard is decent. The cupped keys are a nice touch, but there's one big negative - the lock button is positioned exactly where the delete button was on the Logitech that I've been using for my Air (1st gen). So I keep locking the iPad when I mean to delete a character. Very annoying.

I do like how I don't have to recharge this unit. My other Logitech for the 1st gen Air has a mini-USB for charging. The new keyboard has 2 watch-size batteries that power it. They slide out on a tray and are easily accessible.

I'm going to keep this unit to have as a backup. I also have an Apple Smart Keyboard coming, but I wanted something with a rigid base to balance on my chair's arm or elsewhere. I will keep an eye out for a new design for the iPad Pro from Logitech. I hope it mirrors the old Logitech Ultrathin design.

text:
Not bad. Lasted quite a while, but failed in the most bizarre way. One day, Skype audio (and only Skype audio) just got extremely quiet. I couldn't imagine a headset failing in a way that some audio was quiet while other audio wasn't. So I did quite a few tests... No other headset in the house had that problem. And two other computers that did not have recent updates, etc, did show the problem with this specific headset.

So, although it is puzzling as to why or how this could happen, it is pretty clear that it is a headset failure. IP packets and audio do have metadata to allow communications audio to get priority, etc. The DSP chip must have failed in a way that caused communications audio to get blocked.

Anyway, 4 stars because there are clearly better options in the same price range (see the Sades SA903 for example).

title: Great remote / Horrible setup software.
text:
Received a shiny new Harmony 650 Remote Control for Christmas. It was something I had requested after doing some homework on competing products. The features available on the Logitech remotes are excellent. The software for setting up the remote for your devices. WOOF!

It would really be more fair to break my rating into 2 sections;

The Remote:
PROS: The remote has the buttons that we use the most often and for the buttons that we want that aren't on the face of the remote may be set up on the LCD screen. The back lighting is a bit dim but not bad. Build quality isn't bad.
CONS: Only real complaint for the physical unit is the Green and Blue buttons don't really look that Green nor Blue.

The Software:
PROS: Logitech has built a lot of great functionality into the remotes. They use an approach they calls 'Activities'. Basically it allows you to send a string of commands across a group of devices. So, you can set an Activity play your XBoxOne on your TV and control the sound through your stereo. It will send a string of signals powering on your TV, setting the input to the proper input, power on your XBox, and your stereo. You may add additional commands. Their database of codes for devices is extensive.
CONS: The software for setting up your remote is insanely frustrating. When trying to sync my device it will fail 5 or 6 times before it will update successfully. The software is lacking rudimentary functionality such as copying an activity. Setting the order for activities to show up on the LCD screen. The forums say to delete all your activities and then recreate them in the order you want them to be displayed. REALLY? And it didn't work.

My closing thoughts is that this is a good remote IF you have the time and patience to work around the inexcusable deficiencies in the setup software. I say inexcusable because these remotes have been around for years and Logitech has had more than enough time to create a simple clean interface for setting up a remote. They just haven't bothered to do it and at the price point for these devices I just feel it is inexcusable and thus only a 2 star rating.

title: Great solution for integrated control of your home entertainment system,  and this version doesn't need the costly remote.
text:
Installation was straightforward, and a couple of questions were quickly handled by a call to tech support. Particularly appreciated was the ability to import settings from our old Logitech infrared remote.

The Harmony software, which we use to control the Hub from our iPhones and iPads, works well. A more legible character size for the iPad implementation would be helpful. Note that the Harmony software keeps the iPad awake with screen running, which will run down the battery. The work-around is to close it when not in use. However, a better-behaved app would be appreciated.

One advantage that isn't mentioned in the product literature: The Hub sends out a very bright infrared (invisible) control signal in all directions, and so does the IR Mini Blaster (emitter) that plugs in. Between them, I was able to easily find positions that controlled all my equipment.

One limitation: the Harmony Hub does not work well with weak wifi signals. My Apple TV 3 has no trouble with the low signal level in the needed location, and neither do the iOS devices running the Harmony app. But positioning the Harmony Hub was very touchy, with a lot of trial and error. The solution found was to place it on the opposite side of the room from the devices, where it could hold a solid wifi connection. The hub's infrared pulses are very bright, and have no trouble controlling the media devices from 15 feet away.

Some day, I'm hoping that Apple will add functionality to HomeKit to allow the Logitech Hub to be controlled by it. But we aren't there yet.

title: Great headset, iffy software.
text:
This headset is wonderful. Freeing myself from wires around my desktop was one of the best decisions I've made. I love being able to get up and walk around the room while still hearing what's going on on my computer. Speaking of, the range on this thing is great. I've been probably 30+ feet away from the base and haven't had any problems with choppy signals or dropping. I've found the headset gets about 6hrs of battery life with heavy use, which for me is perfectly acceptable. You can also use the headset while it's charging, and the supplied cable on the base is long enough for easy use (the base is basically a USB hub/passthrough that holds the receiver in an upright position).

The sound quality on this thing is pretty solid. Sure it's not $500 studio monitors amazing, but for the price I was very pleasantly surprised with what I heard. Tweaking the EQ just a bit in the Logitech software would definitely be recommended to open up the higher frequencies a bit. The bass is also very impressive, turning that up gives a feeling of power or "oomph" without becoming muddy. The Dolby 7.1 is the real deal on this thing. Playing a game or watching a movie that has all those channels is really a trip, you'll swear things are coming from behind and around you. It makes FPS games a breeze too, I can tell more where enemies are coming from on sound than ever before. Almost feels a bit like cheating!

The foldable mic is a very nice touch. It never gets in the way, and I've always had people say they can hear me just fine even if I'm speaking softly. The LED indicator for mic status is very appreciated, and the ability to throw the mic up to get a quick mute is yet another great feature. I like that Logitech did this instead of a dedicated mute button, I've often found myself forgetting that my mic was muted without the proper visual feedback. There's no question as to weather or not this mic is on.

I don't use the programmable G-Keys that much (I have plenty of media keys and the like on my keyboard), but they are a nice touch. I have bound them to games like Skyrim for features such as Quick Save/Quick Load and it's very handy.

Wearing this headset is an absolute pleasure. The pads on the headband and earcups are very soft and don't get uncomfortable after extended use. The earpads also sit loosely enough on my head to not cause me to sweat with the headset on. The earcups also fully engulf your ears which is great for isolation.

Now, onto my one caveat. The Logitech gaming software is a bit of a nuisance. In the newer versions there is a big problem with volume ducking. What this means is that the volume level will randomly drop and come back up as things go in and out of focus, or sometimes seemingly randomly. I found this to be very annoying and almost wanted to return the headset for this as I couldn't use the EQ features if I wanted consistent volume (I had to close out of the Logitech software completely to alleviate this problem). However, after some online digging I was able to find a solution. If you install an older version of the Logitech gaming there will be no volume ducking issues and you'll still be able to use the EQ. The version you'll have to search for and download is "8.40.83". This is the last update before the volume ducking issue became apparent. Although this was an issue, it's with the software and not the headset. You don't absolutely NEED this version of the software as the headset works fine without it, so I won't take off a star.

title: Repeated disconnects make this headset frustrating and useless
text:
This headset disconnects repeatedly and constantly, leaving about a 10-15 second disconnect every time it happens. After much research, I found out that it is caused by radio interference in the 2.4 GHz spectrum. What uses 2.4 GHz? Practically every wireless consumer device from the last decade. If you live in any reasonably crowded area, you can count on this headset to disconnect repeatedly.

Some people have tried plugging the USB dongle into different ports with some success. I've tried almost all of the USB ports on my PC and haven't had any luck. In fact, I have better performance when I use this headset in a different room than when I'm 3 feet away from my rig. I don't know why, but it is extremely frustrating. I won't be buying another Logitech wireless headset.

title: Not so perfect **UPDATED REVIEW**
text:
UPDATE: I contacted Logitech about the problems with my folio. It was under warranty. Logitech support was very responsive and accepted the receipt and other information I sent to them. I received a slightly different product - possibly a newer model. The cover is not cloth, but vinyl with a fine texture to give it some grip while you're holding it. The new material also prevents the cover from slipping when I fold it back to use sans keyboard. This was a problem with the old cloth. Also, the cloth frayed at the edges and was hard to clean. This material is easier to clean but it does pick up dirt easily. However, the plastic clips that were the issue with the previous cover are the same hard plastic clips. My iPad synced with the keyboard without having to do anything on my part expect make sure the bluetooth was turned on the iPad. The auto sleep and on features work flawlessly. I really hope the clips hold up this time because I REALLY like this case.

UPDATE: I've been using the folio for two months and recently had an incident that I need to share. The folio dropped off of a side table onto a carpeted floor, and my iPad popped out, breaking one of the corners that hold the iPad in the folio. Its a pretty serious break and it's also cracked. It still holds the iPad in the folio but sometimes it pops out. I have to handle it more carefully than usual. The crack is worsening and I'm afraid at some point it's going to be unusable. I guess the good news is that it did protect my iPad to a point, but I would not say that this folio will protect your iPad when dropped. If this folio allows the iPad to pop out, it could be disastrous on a hard surface. Logitech needs to redesign how the iPad is held in the folio. It seems that it's designed so you can take it out easily, but that is at the expense of protection and long term use. Although I like the keyboard itself, which has worked flawlessly and always connects to the iPad automatically, I'm not sure I would replace this with the same. I will shop around and find something with a sturdier case.I did a lot of research before buying the Logitech Keyboard Folio. I wanted something that would protect my iPad, provide a good usable keyboard, and still allowed for touchscreen use. I get all of that with this folio.

The folio is very sturdy. The keyboard is responsive. I'm typing this review with the keyboard. It took a little getting used to but once I got used to it it's very easy to use. Sure, I hit the wrong key sometimes especially the delete key in the upper right. But overall it's a breeze to type. My iPad synced immediately. I didn't have to do anything to connect it to the keyboard. The iPad fits perfectly in the case. When open for typing, the iPad locks in with a magnet that holds very well. The iPad is sitting on my lap as I type this, and there is a little bounce but it's minor. The folio folds so I can use the iPad vertically with the keyboard either out or in. In the out position it kind of feels strange feeling the keys but if you hold the iPad with your left hand there is a smooth surface to hold. With the keys inside, the hinge slips a little. You'll just have to try both positions to see what feels best for you, and the good thing is you have the option.

The outside of the folio is covered with a textured cloth. It's a little difficult to clean if you get something down in the texture but with a little work you can keep it clean. The corners of my folio arrived with the cloth a little frayed, but I trimmed them with small scissors and it looks fine. Only if you are really picky will this bother you. Bottom line, I love this folio and I'm very relieved that I chose the right one.

title: A tip for Mac users
text:
After trying various mice and trackpads, I've settled on a trackball. I picked one up immediately from a local brick and mortar store on the strength of the sales rank and the stellar reviews on Amazon.

The other reviews pretty much covers everything. I just wanted to share a couple things about this trackball.

1. As primarily a Mac user, I found that setting the tracking speed under mouse settings at 60% gives me the best tracking accuracy balanced with speed. Higher than this, I find it pretty annoying when you hover around a text, button, what have you on the screen while your thumb is still on the trackball. With a higher sensitivity, the minor movements of your thumb translates into too much movement of the pointer, which often makes it annoyingly difficult to keep the pointer over a text you want to highlight (for example).

2. I wish the buttons (left, right, middle) were a easier to press, because I have pain with prolonged clicking of the mouse buttons. The middle mouse button which I use all the time to open new tabs is especially hard to press.

I do like it because it feels ergonomic, my hand feels well supported resting on it, and not having to use my wrist is great for pain and is space-saving. If the buttons were easier to press, this would be a "I love it" 5 star product.

For those who are concerned about how long it'll take to get used to a trackball, I think a few days would suffice for most people. I've been switching between the trackball and the mouse for a few days and I find myself reaching for the trackball more.

text:

title: Desktop + Gaming usage. My go-to pointing device, trackballs are under-rated IMO. This one is a solid value.
text:
I have always exclusively used trackballs. Never have liked mice. I have the wired version of this also, and for anyone curious, there is a slightly different "feel" to the ball movement between the two, but it's not an issue. This is my 2nd one of the wireless ones I've purchased.

WHAT I LIKE:

* Wireless, and the battery lasts a year or more of daily use
* The wireless operation is flawless and instantaneous
* Very easy plug and play
* Very easy software setup and tweaking
* Easy to integrate into games and programs (programmable buttons are great)
* The ball is easily popped out with any finger, for cleaning. They made the hole larger in this version.
* The wireless dongle can be programmed for multiple wireless Logitech devices, including more than 1 trackball, so no need to change the dongle

WHAT I WOULD CHANGE OR MAKE BETTER

* I'd like to see more programmable buttons. I use this for gaming and development. A lot of mice these days come with several buttons. I'd like to see at least 2-3 more within easy reach; for example, buttons could be placed around the circular base on the left side of the ball, where the thumb naturally sits.

ISSUES OR OTHER THINGS TO NOTE

I've only ever had 1 issue with the wireless model. My RMB (right mouse button) got a little weird after a year of use. While holding it down in games (and some applications), it would intermittently release/hold/release/hold, as if the contact was wearing out. This necessitated purchasing another one. I verified it was the button and not the battery or software.

title: DOA and Terrible Customer Service from Logitech
text:
I have a pair of these I got back in 2013 after extensive comparison shopping and they worked great the last couple years. Recently they started dying very quickly and people I was voice chatting with started complaining about the microphone making horrible static noise, and since the padding on the ear pieces was starting to fall apart, I figured they were at the end of their lifespan and it was just time to replace them.

I ordered a new pair a few weeks ago and they would not work straight out of the box. Receiver and headphones just will not pair, and the receiver is recognized as some other type of device by my computer. I went through all the troubleshooting steps possible, including updating and restarting my computer, uninstalling drivers, and specifically downloading the software for the headphones directly from the Logitech site. They still will not pair, and my internet sleuthing uncovered people with similar problems who ended up just getting a replacement receiver under warranty from Logitech. So I emailed Logitech support and explained the issue, hoping to get a replacement receiver.

It took Logitech TEN DAYS to respond to my initial email, and the only thing they did was tell me to perform the troubleshooting steps that I had already detailed. I responded that none of those steps worked, and it has been another 5 days and I still have not heard another response. I have never experienced such atrocious customer service in my life, and I kind of wonder if they're stringing me along until some 30 day warranty coverage is over and they can tell me to screw off.

Buy these at your own risk.

title: Very, very good with just a couple minor problems.
text:
*****UPDATE 5-30-2016*****

I have now been using this headset just about every day for about 2 months, and I have changed my rating from a 4-star to a 2-star.

The pros are still pros, the sound is great and the surround is even better. It's comfortable and blah blah, all that is still good. But the issue with the buzzing and random shut-offs is getting progressively worse. It does it 2-3 times a day now, and there is no obvious way of fixing it. My previous method of plugging it in and leaving it alone for a few minutes no longer works. It stops eventually, but I never know how long it will be before it starts up again.

If I wasn't already out of my return window, I would return this headset and buy something that actually works. If you get it and don't have hte buzzing, then you'll love it...but I wouldn't take the risk, personally.

*****UPDATE ENDED*****

This headset is very, very good like 95% of the time, and downright frustrating the other 5%.

The Good.

Comfortable! Very, very comfortable. Fantastic sound quality - especially in 7.1 surround sound mode - totally changed the way I listen to music. Was very surprised at how good the sound quality is because it's supposed to be a gaming headset, not something an audiophile might buy. Microphone quality is also excellent. I also like how it had a microphone mute button right on the left ear cup. Very easy to hit when you're using voice activation mode on whatever voice client you prefer, but you don't want to have people hear you burp or cough or whatever. It also mutes if you move the microphone to the up position, which is really cool.

The range is fantastic. I don't have any problem walking to my kitchen to get a glass of water while continuing my conversations or listening to music.

Setup was also pretty simple. You plug the USB dock into your computer and plug the wireless receiver dongle into the dock. Drivers should download and install automatically, and if you have any other Logitech peripherals, you probably already have their software suite installed. This headset will add to that automatically.

The software suite, by the way, is just fine. Nothing really special, but you get some options for defining what the G keys on the left ear cup do, and for messing around with the 7.1 surround sound.

The bad.

Sometimes, and I have no idea why this happens, my headset won't charge while it is plugged in. I'll unplug it expecting it to be fully charged and it just straight up isn't. No idea why this happens and I can't find anything online about it.

Also - and this is the much worse thing - I occasionally get instances where it starts putting out a somewhat high pitched buzzing sound. I think this is a battery issue, but holy god it's annoying. Resolves after a few minutes of being plugged in and turned off, but it's a major problem when it happens during gaming.

Overall, I really like this headset, and I'm glad I upgraded from my G230 wired headset. It's not perfect, but it's definitely good.
