title: Very nice mid-tier headset
text:
This is a very good mid-tier headset. The audio quality is superior to computer / earbud speakers, and the microphone is good. It does not completely block out all noise, but it blocks out enough to be able to focus on what you're doing (which I prefer over not hearing anything at all). I haven't timed the battery life, but it lasts at least 5 hours from a full charge. It can be charged via USB connected to the computer or via USB connected to wall charger adapter. I probably haven't used all of the features this headset offers, but the volume control/mute buttons on the headset are quite convenient.

As for the wireless range, it's pretty impressive. I can walk to the other side of the house through two walls (about 40 ft), and it still works. When I go downstairs, it works as long as I am within a ~15ft radius beneath it before I lose signal. I'd imagine that the range would be even greater in an open area.
That being said, I live in a fairly secluded area (no houses within 100 feet). I have a friend who owns this headset and has sporadic wireless connectivity issues. This may be because he lives in an apartment where there are numerous wireless signals within a concentrated area.

A couple downsides: it's a bit awkward using it while it is plugged in because the cord is pretty short. Also, when it runs out of battery, it shuts off without warning, which could be problematic during voice calls/gaming...

Finally, If you're concerned that the headband might break - it's not that fragile. Treat it nicely, and it won't break that easily.
I have used it regularly for 6 months so far, and there are no signs of wear.

title: Small laptop/tablet BT mouse that works with built-in BT radios
text:
I purchased the [[ASIN:B01B16MXLU Lenovo Thinkpad Yoga 2-in-1 Convertible 11.6-inch IPS Touchscreen Laptop(Tablet), Intel Quad Core Processor, 4GB DDR3L, 128GB SSD, HDMI, Bluetooth, Webcam, AC Wifi, Windows 10 Professional]] and this mouse to be used together. Both came the same day and set both up at the same time.

NO receiver is packaged with this mouse. My Yoga laptop/tablet had a built-in BT card combined with the WiFi radio module. The BT version is 4.0 compliant. This mouse works with that BT compliance.

Switched on the BT, ran discover on my laptop. Following the directions set forth by Logitech, I was able to instantly get the mouse paired with my laptop. No "0000" code required.

Then a problem. The mouse stopped working. Long story, very short -- Windows 10 has a power save option in Device Manager for BT connections. After a short period of time, the BT portion of the WiFi/BT card goes into power save and shuts down. Others here have complained about this problem thinking it was the mouse that died.

Solution: Go to Control Panel > Device Manager > BT Adaptor > Properties > Power Management. You can open advanced properties with your admin password. After opening advanced properties, look for "allow computer to turn off this device" and uncheck the box next to this line. This will not allow the computer to turn off the BT setting by itself, unless you so designate. One more thing, any major Windows 10 upgrade will reset this power saving function back on again. You will have to go back and redo what I described again. One quirk of Win 10 that ignores what the end user's preferences are. I hope this glitch gets corrected in future updates.

No additional software is needed to operate this BT mouse. It works with the default Microsoft BT drivers. The Logitech software (downloaded from the Logitech web site) gives you extra functions. For me, it works just fine as is. If you are left handed, then to switch orientation of keys, you will need the Logitech software to switch keys and buttons.

After fighting my issues, I really like this mouse. NO dongle to keep track of or break. NO software install, unless you have special need. It just works after I found the solution I listed above.

Want a good BT mouse, reasonable price and long life, look no further. Take it home and you will not be sorry. The advice I gave above will save you frustration and a needless return defect for something done by the operating system of the computer.

One last point -- this mouse has an invisible laser light for movement sensor. This is unlike the red glowing light from other laser type mice. It is not broken, it is using a laser light beam outside the sight range of humans. Also, DO NOT stare into the light port while the mouse is on. You could have problems with vision being burned.

This mouse gets my full 5 star rating and deservedly so.

title: Decent keyboard with easy switching between multiple BT devices.
text:
This is a really great keyboard if you have multiple Bluetooth devices that you might want to use with a keyboard, but want an easy way to designate which device to connect. While there are a lot of great affordable keyboards, the multi-device feature on this Logitech is what really makes it useful to me. The newer Bluetooth versions will automatically pair with the last device connected to it. That's generally very convenient - except when you want to change devices and then need to manually disconnect the offending device. Not so with the K380 - I have setting #1 tied to my iPad Pro and #2 to my iPhone. With a single push of a button you can connect and even switch back and forth.

If 4.5 stars were an option, I might give it that rating because of the circular shaped keys. There's nothing strange about the layout of the K380, but I seem to struggle a bit with the circular keys. Key presses that might hit the edge of a square key may miss a circular one altogether. It also seems to be laid out a little narrower than some keyboards, and I have large-ish hands. But these are minor annoyances, and I would probably adapt to the keyboard if I used it more than my laptop keyboard.

Overall, I think this is a great mobile keyboard with easy connectivity and a convenient device-switching option.

title: Best Keyboard I've Used
text:
I Love this keyboard but the reason I am writing this is because of my successful dealings with Logitech.

I first bought this keyboard from Best Buy in red. The outside of the case had a cloth cover. I loved the way it worked. The smart keys are super useful and the keys are smooth and well spaced, very easy to use while touch typing. It has a very long lasting battery and there is not really an on/off switch which makes it easy to use. The keyboard is activated by attaching it to the magnetic space above the keyboard and activating your iPad's Bluetooth.

Sadly it lasted about a month before the clip that holds it on broke so badly that the iPad would just fall out. It developed a crack which eventually spread through use. I am very easy on my cases and this should not have happened so quickly. If you can't connect it to the magnet at the top of the keyboard then it is useless.

I researched Logitech's warranty policy and filled out all of the necessary forms in there online website. The website itself is a bit cumbersome but the forms were easy. I was able to provide them with my receipt (I bought it originally online) and a picture of the damage. Within a day or two I received an email back that they'd opened up a case. In another couple of days they asked for additional information which I provided and shortly thereafter they provided me with shipping information.

I've only just received the keyboard but already I can see a difference. Black was the only color available which is fine with me. The case has more of a rubber feel rather than cloth. The clips seem way more sturdy. Of course only time will tell how long it holds up.

I highly recommend this case if you can buy it new from Logitech. They seem to be a great company who stands behind their products. I will always consider their products in the future.

title: Logitech: Dark Age Incompetence
text:
The drivers for this thing are a nightmare. I can not believe that Logitech is still in the business of manufacturing these frustrating and outmoded pieces of technology.Here are some things to know:

1. If you are a legacy user of their remotes, the new software is not backward compatible with the old one, and in fact, they conflict with each other. Anytime you want to reprogram your remote or update the firmware, you need to uninstall the old software and reboot, install the new software and reboot, and then do you thing. That is, of course, unless you run into #2.

2. The USB drivers for the remote are borked. I opened this, uninstalled the old software (reboot), installed the new software (reboot), and loaded the new remote. It took all of the info, synced to 99%, and got stuck. The Logitech forums have about 5 different potential workarounds that might get you up and running, including messing with the entries in the device manager, hitting buttons on the remote during sync at just the right time, multiple reconnections of the USB cable, unhooking all other USB cables from the machine, and so forth. The last time I messed around with this sort of nonsense was in 1998 when I was dealing with 3Dfx and Glide/OGL wrappers. I thought we had moved past that sort of nonsense. Not Logitech.

3. The timings of device on/off to accommodate HDMI handskaking is terrible. I have to turn devices off and on again to get my TV set to see them. It's a Samsung, only 2 years old. Should this be happening? Who should I blame for this? I currently blame Logitech.

Anyway, this is one of the few options you have to get rid of multiple remotes and get them in one device. It is a terrible pity that it is just plain awful.

text:
I am really digging this mouse. It's super-ergonomic/comfortable and really smooth and accurate when using the included unified receiver. Bluetooth performance is a bit less smooth, but completely usable for non-gaming applications. I have ordered a second unified receiver to ensure super smooth performance on both my Mac and PC.

I really love the button on the bottom of the mouse that allows for switching between connected machines. Previously, I used a Razer mouse with a USB splitter/switch to toggle between computers, but the fact that this feature is built into the mouse lets me get rid of the desk clutter caused by the USB switch.

The other primary reason I ordered this mouse to replace my Razer is that the Razer lasted 1 day on a full charge. This mouse is supposed to last 40 days of moderate use. I figure even if I hit 1/2 of that, it's totally worth it, so I'm very stoked on this mouse.

For those of you asking about gaming usage: I am a moderate to heavy PC gamer and I think this mouse is more than adequate, but not necessarily ideal. Here's my observations when comparing to the Razer wireless Mamba:

- The Mamba's ergonomics are a BIT more suitable for gaming, with the device being a bit lower and it's symmetry allowing for a TINY BIT more accuracy in fine movements between the the thumb and ring finger. That said, the MX Master is also very good in this regard.

- Razer allows a high level of sensitivity tuning, but I had no problem getting the MX Master to respond exactly the same way I liked the Mamba to be set.

- The side buttons on the Mamba were both more plentiful (4 vs. the MX Master's 2) and more ergonomically accessible. This is the major advantage the Mamba has, but it's not worth the extra money and the need to charge the thing every day (or even several times on heavy days).

title: Helpful Hints for Windows 7 connection from a Mac person
text:
Size, build quality, looks... all that REAL nice! My set up is complicated and I thought this thing would be too good to be true:
My personal computer, a Mac Pro, a new iPad Air2, and my work Laptop - a very recent Dell running Win 7, all sharing my desk. Before I had separate keyboards for the Mac and the Dell, and none for the iPad.

Mac Pro on #1, check! iPad on #2, check! Dell on #3 uhhhhhhhh.... took a few hours of jumping thru hurdles on this one.
Another complication, I have a Logitech (Unified Receiver) Mouse on the Dell. Step 1 is update the Logitech Options software (yeah I know this keyboard is bluetooth, but it WILL manage both this keyboard and the RF mouse! Eventually...)

1st Problem: add Bluetooth device - Windows would see it, accept the Passcode, then... Nothing. Problem was Generic Bluetooth Drivers (see Device Manager) instead of Intel Centrino whatever drivers. Only clue that Bluetooth Radio was Intel was that generic driver noted Manufacturer #2 = Intel (thank you Google). Fortunately someone else had this problem and posted a link to the Intel drivers. That got me connected and the keyboard typing! Hallelujah! For about 1 minute.

Next problem: there's a setting in device manager for the Intel Bluetooth Radio "allow computer to shut this off to save power" - MUST UNCHECK THAT. Now I had connectivity for 2 minutes! ARGH!!!!!

Turns out further down the list there's an Intel BLUETOOTH NETWORK device - that ALSO has a checkbox about saving power - MUST UNCHECK that one also!

Finally, it works! Really nice to use the same keyboard for all 3 devices, and switching connections is surprisingly fast - only a couple seconds. In Logitech Options there's even an "easy switch" view that shows the keyboard recognizes Mac OS on #1 and #2, and Windows on #3. It figured that out all by itself. Thank goodness.

title: Great build quality
text:
I've had several bluetooth keyboards in the past that weren't exactly quality or as high quality as I would like. They would bend or feel flimsy when carrying around, or the keys simply didn't have that nice "feel" to them. Fed up with all the no-name brands I decided to try out the king of keyboard makers - Logitech. I'm so glad I did. My requirements were to be able to pair with multiple devices (laptop at work, iPad at home), high build quality (no bending or flexing when typing) and the nicer laptop style keys, similar to my mac book pro. I bought both the K380 and the K480 to hopefully end my search.

The K380 was everything I was looking for any more. At first I was taken back by the circular keys, but the more I used it, the more natural it felt versus square keys. I also absolutely loved the tactile feedback from the keys. It was just the light pressing style I had grown to love with my HP laptop at work and my mac book pro at home. The arrow keys were a little hard to use at first, but I got accustomed to them relatively quickly after an hour or so of use. The K380 was also very well built. When typing on other no-name brands, the whole keyboard would flex and bend while typing. It make it rather difficult to focus as I couldn't stop noticing the keyboard give with every key stroke. The K380 wouldn't move, flex or bend at all even with my most furious typing. That's exactly what I needed. The ability to pair the keyboard with multiple devices simultaneously has made it effortless to switch between inputs - press a button and boom I'm sending key strokes to a different device. Love it.

I won't go much into the K480 here, except that I found it heavier, clunkier and my devices with cases didn't fit inside the pre-existing slot. It may be better for you if your devices have no cases, however I loved the K380 that much more.

If you're looking for a great quality bluetooth keyboard, to travel with or just keep at your desk, I highly recommend the K380. I've had it for months now and wouldn't want to use anything else.

title: Great keyboard for convenience and portability.
text:
To quickly summarize, I would recommend this keyboard as an extra keyboard for traveling or a backup. Also if you like to switch between Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, or Linux a lot then this keyboard is a very affordable option. I would not recommend this keyboard as your star player for typing. There are better options for desktops.

To start off, I mainly use any keyboard for web browsing, some video games, and extensive code writing. Specifically for this keyboard, I use this keyboard as a backup portable keyboard for my tablet/laptop (Surface Pro 2) for mostly web browsing, homework assignments, and writing code.

This keyboard is almost the same size as the wireless Mac keyboard. It's pretty thin just like the Mac keyboard. Build quality is very impressive in my opinion, not like the Mac keyboard though. Though this keyboard feels heavier than the Mac one, it is still light in my opinion. This keyboard is overall compact. I like to put this keyboard in my backpack, forget it's even there sometimes, then take it out whenever I need to.
Specific Mac keyboard that I use right below.
[[ASIN:B0113AOSUI Apple Wireless Keyboard with Bluetooth - Silver (Certified Refurbished)]]

Of course, can't review a keyboard without discussing the typing experience. At first when I saw this keyboard I thought, "typing on this is going to suck." The main reason I thought this is because it looks kind of cramp. This keyboard's feels prove me wrong. The keys are circular which actually feels different from typing on any other keyboard with square keys. I can feel the edge of my fingertips touch the keyboard whereas any other keyboard if I press a key my finger only maintains contact with the keys themselves. As for key traveling, for me it does not reach a level of satisfaction, but it's almost there. In simpler terms, whenever you press a key on this Logitech it doesn't feel the same as a keyboard meant for desktops. But, it's almost there. This keyboard is small and good for portable use so 'almost there' compared to full sized keyboards is good enough in my opinion. Typing on this keyboard is also very comfortable. I write code for endless hours and my fingers and hands are not bleeding by the end of the day so I consider that a victory in my book. It also helps that this keyboard is shaped like a right triangle to take the pain out of typing. There are of course useful media keys on the function key row so that's a plus.

Out of the three keyboards in my images, the most comfortable to least comfortable is Mac, Logitech, and Surface keyboard. Logitech however is a close second so it's still very comfortable to type on compared to the flat Surface keyboard.

And lastly, another important aspect of this keyboard is the ability to switch between devices. I have my keyboard registered to my Surface Pro 2, iPad Air, and Mac Mini 2012. It works perfectly for all these devices. Switching between devices is extremely easy. All I have to do is press a button and bam, it's like I'm controlling three airships. Feels great to be in control. There are three lights each light representing a device you are connected to. A light will blink when you are connected to a particular registered device. What else can I say about the bluetooth part, it works and it's quick. Though there are no battery indicators that I know of for this keyboard.

I like this keyboard. If someone told me to use this keyboard every day for the rest of my life, I wouldn't mind it.

The images contain the Surface Pro 2 detachable keyboard, Mac keyboard, and of course this Logitech keyboard.

title: Fantastic image quality, no drivers needed for macOS use
text:

Oh, and if you see just one of the blue lights come on during usage, don't worry -- that's how it's supposed to work. The right-hand "light" isn't a light at all, but merely microphone in the same shape as the left-hand light.

title: Best available compact Bluetooth keyboard, though not without flaws
text:
I'm somewhat obsessive about keyboards, so I went through four before settling on this one for daily use with my iPad. Only after I decided to keep it did I discover that The Wirecutter, my favorite online review site, also considers this the best overall Bluetooth keyboard. So, yay.

First the good, and in this case it's really good: the Bluetooth radio on this model is rock-solid. This was the most maddening flaw of the other four keyboards I tested, including Apple's own brand-new Magic Keyboard. The radios would randomly cut out after less than a minute, presumably to save battery power. But it became clear that the problem was a bug, not a feature; two of the keyboards would wink on and off after only a few seconds of disuse. The Logitech not only never demonstrates this problem, its radio remains on in a low-power mode for up to half an hour. Other great features include the ability to switch seamlessly between iOS/Android/Mac OS X/Windows, the ridiculously long battery life (up to 2 years with a couple of AAA batteries), and the solid key feel compared to off-brand budget keyboards.

Now the bad. There's LED on the no caps lock key, which doesn't sound as if it would matter but is a regular annoyance. There's no hard-coded key for device sleep on iOS. And the iOS/Mac OS X labeling on the modifier keys is really faint, so it's tough to see at a glance.

And that's it. Unless you like pulling your hair out waiting for Bluetooth to reconnect multiple times per day, this is the one to buy.

When I type a word with the combination "ous" it forgets the "s." So, house is houe, mouse is moue, fabulou is not fabulous... you get it. I was the only person on the internet I could find with this problem, so I figured it was a hardware failure unique to my unit. I got in touch with tech support, went through the whole thing with them, they couldn't fix the problem, so they sent me a replacement unit.

Same thing.

NOW, for what it's worth, it only happens when I'm in my groove, which is about 70wpm. When I type slower, it's fine. 70WPM isn't lightning fast but it is faster than average, so if you're a slower typist, I heartily recommend this keyboard. It's wonderful and I love it, but it apparently does not love me. It's okay; I handle rejection well.

I bought an Anker Ultra Slim keyboard which I absolutely love, so all is well. I am sad not to be able to use the K380. It's a wonderful keyboard, until you want to type houe.

title: Quality keyboard, great for portability and simplicity.
text:
I was desperately looking for a keyboard for my iPad Pro that (1) wasn't the price of a body part (I'm looking at you, Apple), (2) was compatible with all my devices if I needed to switch, and (3) one that had a good feel when typing on the keys. This baby fits the bill very nicely.

Price: Very reasonable. It's about $30 in the retail stores and on Amazon, and the quality is ahead of many of the similarly-priced Bluetooth keyboards. Big plus for being compatible with Mac AND PC devices, and not being crazy-expensive for that capability.

Compatibility/Bluetooth Connectivity: Compatible with both Mac and Android/PC devices. My partner has a Mac laptop and Android tablet, so we tested it out on his devices. Works solidly, just make sure your Bluetooth drivers are all updated.

The keyboard has three keys at the top-left that allow the user to switch seamlessly between up to 3 connected devices. I didn't think I would be using this much, but it's actually quite useful. I had my phone next to me while I was typing something up on my iPad, and all I needed to do is click a button to instantly start typing away at my phone. I've calculated my average wait-time for the switch, and it ranges between 3-8 seconds of delay (usually closer to 3-5 seconds).

Quality of Keys/Size: The keys are rounded (shown in the photo) and have a slight dip to them. They're very comfortable to type on, but just remember that the keys are closer together than a normal keyboard due to the size. They spring back easily and make a soft click (similar to the keys of a Mac laptop)

Overall I highly recommend this keyboard. Logitech is always reliable and provides a great bang for your buck for many of their products.

title: Love this Keyboard!
text:
I've been using Logitech keyboards for many years from the Solar wireless, illuminated, K380 along with some of their gaming keyboards and this is probably my favorite non gaming keyboard so far!

Here are some of the things I liked about this keyboard:

- Compared to my k810 gaming keyboard the round keys are normal sized and doesn't feel cramped at all This is a huge relief because the k380 felt a tad too small even though I ended up forcing myself to get used to the smaller size anyways

- There's a numpad on it! I don't really use any spreadsheets or anything like that at home but this is handy when I want to type numbers or do a quick calculation on occasion. The type number keys are fun, but the numpad always feels nice :) This is the one thing I wished my wireless Magic Keyboards had.

- The dock is really nice. It's got a bit of weight to it so I can put my iPad air 2 on it and I have to say it's really, really nice being able to set this on my lap and do a little journaling/writing on it with a full sized keyboard. It's much more convenient and faster than using my Macbook, and being able to type something out in seconds (vs using the touchscreen) when I'm not on my computer is nice

- It's bluetooth and Unifying wireless. it comes with one adapter to pair with Logitech's reciever so if you don't have one already with another device then this will work great with pc's that don't have bluetooth. Mine doesn't, and I had to buy a bluetooth adapter for the k380. Supposedly the battery life lasts a bit longer on the unifying receiver but with 24 months of battery life on 2 AAAs i'll just have to take their word on it

- Mac and Windows keys! Logitech has been doing this for a while since the k810 I believe and it's great to have the command and option key in its proper place. I like to switch between windows and my mac often on the same monitor for gaming and productivity and I doubt I'll be replacing this one for a while.

Here are some things I didn't like about it:

- The Bluetooth pairing took me a few tries on my 2012 mac mini. When this keyboard is being used after being idle on my mac mini I noticed that it took around 5 seconds of delay to wake up and display the keys i typed in.I didn't notice this on my PC and found this to be really annoying. With the unifying receiver I do not have this issue so keep that in mind. Without it then this would've been a deal breaker for me.

- This really isn't a con for me (at least yet) but the middle section keys where insert and home aren't on this keyboard so keep that in mind. The only key I used in that area was probably either delete or print screen on windows and I'll live without it

- The Function keys and multi function buttons are on the same key. This might not bother most people since they probably use the F keys. But for me it's a little annoying if I'm playing a game that uses a controller and want to use a function key to do a quicksave without holding down the FN and F key at the same time. Now logitech does give you the ability to use the Function keys with a single press but then you lose the ability to quickly change the volume unless you hold down the FN key.

- There's a small round rubber piece on the bottom middle that can easily fall off if you are moving the keyboard around. It's to hold this thing in place from sliding around the desk, but even if I did lose it then there's already 4 rectangular ones in each corner that can still support it. It's not a huge deal, but kind of annoying. If you don't plan on moving your keyboard around to different areas (i like to type in bed at night with my iPad) then you won't have this issue.

I highly recommend this keyboard if you are a mac/windows/tablet user and still like using the numpad!

title: Great multi-computer keyboard, with one big flaw
text:
I bought this because it's the only multi-computer keyboard out there made to work with both Mac and Windows. It also works with the latest Linux distributions. I've tested it with Windows 7, Windows 2008R2 Server, Windows 10, Mac OS El Capitan, Centos 6, Centos 7, and Fedora 23. Thus far the only issues were with Centos 6 and Centos 7. The problem there is that when you switch the keyboard away, Linux decides you're no longer paired, and drops its connection. Then you have to re-pair when you switch back to Linux. This is not the case with Fedora 23, so the lesson is to run a modern version of Linux if you intend to use this keyboard with Linux.

ALl in all it works flawlessly. The buttons do what they're supposed to do on most operating systems. There is only one flaw that gives it less than a five-star rating: the location of the left CTRL key. Most keyboards put the CTRL key right by the Start/Option/Alt key. That way your little finger can drop down and hit it, which is convenient when you're doing cut-and-paste on Windows or using Emacs on Linux. This is what the Mac keyboards do too, their compact Bluetooth keyboard, for example, puts the Control key right there by the Option key, and then the Fn key is to the left. But this keyboard and most other compact Logitech keyboards puts the Fn key where the Control key belongs. So I reach down with my little finger to hit the Ctrl key to copy and paste, and end up inserting a 'c' character into my document instead. Annoying!

Of course, if all of your keyboards are compact Logitech keyboards, you'll eventually get used to it. But I use a variety of full sized keyboards (including full sized Logitech keyboards) including a couple of laptop keyboards in the course of my job, and *all* of them have the Ctrl key where Logitech puts the Fn key (and the keyboards with a Fn key put it where Logitech puts their Ctrl key). What this means is that my day becomes annoying in short order as I keep hitting the wrong key because Logitech puts it in a place that nobody else puts it.

On the other hand, the keyboard otherwise works flawlessly. It never "loses" characters and syncs quickly when you switch to different systems. *If* all of your keyboards are Logitech compact keyboards, you become swiftly accustomed to the weird location of the Ctrl key way out in the wilderness. If not... well, you will be annoyed. So it goes.

title: Best Multi-device Bluetooth Keyboard for the Money
text:
Originally, I bought the Logitech k480, but immediately returned it for the k380. Best decision!

Pros

- This keyboard is way lighter, yet still full sized.
- The keys are much quieter and feel better to type on than the k480.
- I am a touch typer, and have had no trouble transitioning to this keyboard.
- The bluetooth switching works flawlessly. It takes less than 4 seconds to pair with a new device, and then it switches between all three really smoothly.
- The color scheme (dark grey/yellow) does not look like a toy!
- The price is hard to beat for a keyboard that can be hooked up to three devices and lasts 2 years on the included batteries.
- The weight of this all-plastic keyboard helps it to feel like a more premium product.
Cons

- No backlighting, but for me this doesn't matter, since I'm a touch typer.

You really should try this keyboard out. If you need to connect to your computer and your tablet, this is the keyboard to try. Definitely the best deal for your money. This is an example of name brand electronics being completely worth it.

text:
I bought this keyboard, and although it performed exactly as advertised, I had decided to return it within 2 days. Here's why:

- I intended to carry it around with me for my standing desk set-up, but it is very heavy. It's doable, but I'd recommend using this mostly on a desk where it won't move much.
- While the keyboard is full sized (nice feature), the keys are pretty loud. Some reviews have exaggerated this way too much, but I was going to use it in my classroom, and it was definitely a distraction.
- The feel and look is intensely plasticky. While this isn't the end of the world, it isn't my favorite quality for a keyboard.
- I was intending on using this with my iPad some, but I already have a smart case that lets it stand up. Another important point: If you have a case on your phone or tablet, there's a pretty good chance it won't fit in the slot in this keyboard.

For $30, this is probably not the best deal. Check out the Logitech k380 if your tablet already has a case with a standing feature!

title: Great keyboard, with some little things to get used to
text:
This keyboard was recommended on Wirecutter, so I decided to check it out. Typing on it right now.

Pros: Very lightweight, seamless pairing, and I can switch between multiple devices with ease! I use it at work to switch between messages on my iPhone as well as to type on my work laptop (HP Elitebook). It's easy to throw into a bag and take with me. Easy to type with on my lap, although it slides around a bit due to how small it is.

Cons: It doesn't have any legs to incline, but that's probably expected in a keyboard this size. One issue is the F1-F3 keys are for bluetooth switching, so to use those functions as shortcuts, you need to hold down "Fn" first. A bit cumbersome when using such function keys in MS Excel, etc. Same applies to all the other function keys.

The round shape of the keys is also something that takes a little getting used to, but once you get the hang of avoiding the spaces in between the keys, the typing is very fast. I achieve 110-120 words/minute on this keyboard, which is 10-20 more than I had on a more traditional keyboard in the office.

All in all, a great buy, worth checking out especially if you do travel or move your keyboard around often.

title: Great quality mouse but ergonomic and configuration issues for me
text:
I purchased this to replace my MX Revolution. I really wanted to like it but after a week of use I returned it.

I'm giving it 3 stars because my issues were mainly ergonomics not quality. This review is based on OS X Yosemite.

Cons:
- overall comfort was terrible, my wrist and hand had a 'burning' sensation from the start and no improvement after a week.
- the 'touch-based gesture' was difficult for me to use. Trying to hold down and move the mouse left/right/up/down wasn't intuitive. I tried using it to switch desktops but it was never graceful. If it had an setting to be a toggle-click that might have worked.
- it would not connect via bluetooth using OS X. I knew this could be an issue before purchasing it, however it paired up to my iPhone and iPad just fine... weird.
- the laser did work on glass but it felt jittery or chunky. I also tried it with a quality mouse pad with the same results... maybe using bluetooth would have improved this?
- it offers app specific configurations but for me Parallels would not recognize the optional buttons and so setting shortcuts or anything else did not work. Big issue for me. I ended up using speedmouse since my VM would recognize all my button configurations. I also came across issues being reported for people using photoshop, can't confirm though.

Pros:
- quality and look was awesome.
- during the week I had it the battery level never seem to budge and I use my mouse a lot.
- option for bluetooth or usb is nice if it works.
- paired up with my other devices just fine.

Other:
- the usb cord for charging was a nuisance or maybe I was just used to the charging cradle from my MX.
- there are conflicting reports of whether you can use the mouse while it is plugged in. I never actually tested this.
- logitech does not seem to listen to their customers. After years of the community requesting options or tweaks and all you get is some canned response it's frustrating. This can apply to any number of products, so logitech is not unique here.

The main reason I purchased this was because I was having double-click issues. I had found many posts that said it was a hardware issue but for me I found that it was an os issue. If you run OS X I found a terminal command that seems to be a good work around, however you will have to run this each time you reboot. You may be able to write a startup script for it.

defaults write .GlobalPreferences com.apple.mouse.doubleClickThreshold -float 0.33

Windows users can check out this link: http://www.metalvortex.com/blog/2013/09/14/1348.html The author says that it may no longer work may be worth a try.

Use any of these commands at your own risk.

Again it's great quality mouse and many people love it, this was just my experience.

title: Cyber Acoustics has features that these don't, but these are still very good.
text:
Was replacing some good Cyber Acoustics. Of of the speakers fell and broke. Debated between these and sticking with the CA brand and decided to try something different.

The good: The sound is everything you'd expect. The sub is fairly powerful. I haven't really "cranked them up" yet though. Easy to set up.

The fair: The speakers deliver but that means they're a tad bulky on my desk. The speaker itself is at the very top and since I want them behind my monitors, it means I have to turn them on their side. This won't bother many. Depends on where you want them.

I don't really have anything bad to say about these speakers at all. I can only make the comparison to CA's.

There are 2 things that I think make the CA's better functionally:
- On the Z323's, the power and volume are controlled by the same knob. Turn all the way to the left to turn them off. On the CA's there's a power button and volume control is separate.
That is much better in my opinion because the volume will stay exactly where you left it if you turn them off. Can't do that with the Z323's.

- You can't control the bass level locally. If you want to change the bass output, you have to reach down to the subwoofer. On the CA's, you could control the base either from the right speaker or from a separate control that sits on your desk.

If the Logitech's had those two things going for them, I'd give them a 5. But I think those notes are what buyers should be aware of.

I tried to FORCE firmware update with _v27 and that did not work.

I opened a ticket with Logictech and no response yet. I found 100's of posts from many users with the same issue. I am running Win7 Pro Service Pack 2 and loaded the latest version of the Logictech Gaming Software (LGS). I followed some tips from other users to no avail.

I have to tell you for the price and reputation of Logictech it is pretty disappointing that they have taken a less than effective approach to resolving connection problem with the 933. The forums go back months. Tech support consistently gives the same useless fixes.

title: Very Good Remote if Programmed Correctly
text:
Everyone loses remotes, don't they? Heck yeah.
I bought the Harmony 650 to replace a Panasonic remote and after following the instructions exactly online to download the software and activate the remote, it didn't work. Sheesh. Not having had a positive experience with universal remotes in the past, I thought "here I go again".
But, I backed up the process and reset the remote to work from an hdmi setting instead of a tv channel setting, and went through the steps exactly again and the remote worked fine.
Do follow the instructions exactly online.
If it doesn't work, follow their reset instructions exactly. Each device can have different ideas about how the remote signal will be accessed, so if you have problems, try another setting. They profile different settings and you can choose another if your other choice doesn't work. Don't give up. This remote works fine if it is programmed properly. If you don't have online skills, ask someone to help you. I have limited online skills and I figured it out.
I almost gave it 4 stars because the setup required me to actually think but chose 5 stars because Logitech's directions were quite accurate when I followed them exactly. You will need a computer to program this device.

title: Great equipment for the price, if it works
text:
Logitech is by far my favorite company for peripherals. As such, I was excited to receive this. In my experience, mid budget gear like this by Logitech goes the distance. This item did not, however. As soon as I plugged everything up, I was met with a loud buzzing noise from every output. After some troubleshooting, I discovered it was due to the angle the wires are placed. Yes, me getting the correct sound depends on me basically having a ritual with the wires to get them to bend just right in the appropriate direction. Whats worst - normally I would just buy a new wire but its hardwired in so I cannot replace this without replacing the entire speaker system.

I am extremely disappointed in this product for what I paid. I have gotten used to getting so much more with Logitech for paying less than I did here. The wires are just... bad. Even as I type this I've been having to constantly hit my desk to juggle the wires to stop the occasional buzz. The only reason this system gets an extra star at all from me on this review is that when it is not buzzing, with the wires all magically in place, the sound and bass is perfect. As of now, I am most likely going to look into a refund. When just typing on your keyboard sends enough vibrations across your desk to make your speakers buzz, there is a big problem.

UPDATE: I received my replacement and none of the prior problems, or new ones, existed. Everything looks and sounds great. If this had been the first model I received, I would have likely given it a full 5 star rating. Like most Logitech gear, this is great equipment for the price paid. But, I cannot in good conscience do that because of the first mishap. Faulty models like that should not be able to make it out of the factory.

However, I later built a new computer and upgraded to Windows 8 and then Windows 10, and Logitech still hasn't released drivers that work. There's a workaround (use the Microsoft XBox Controller drivers), but it doesn't work reliably for all games. With this product still being available and Windows 10 nearing 25% market share, the manufacturer really has an obligation to make sure it will work. title: Good quality with a Google Chromecast Audio
text:
Bought these for my son to use with a Google Chromecast Audio. It's being saved for a Christmas gift, but we went ahead & opened it and tested it out to make sure it worked properly and was of good quality. Overall, it will be perfect for a 9-year-old that loves music.

I was worried that the speakers were damaged during shipping, because although they were packed tightly in the Logitech box, there was no Styrofoam or padding of any kind. Then the Logitech box was packaged inside an Amazon box that was a bit big and instead of putting the normal air-filled plastic to fill up the space, there was just a crumpled up piece of brown paper on one side. I don't get it - Amazon ships my toilet paper with a dozen of those air-filled bags, but they send me my $50 speakers with no padding?? Sorry, I digress. Luckily, they were perfectly fine without a single scratch on them.

The first time I tested them out, I set them up in our living room (large space, but only an 8' ceiling) & I used my Samsung Galaxy S7 to play some Pitbull on the Google Play Music app. I turned the bass and volume all the way up on the speakers and the volume on my phone about 2/3rd of the way up. It sounded just okay. The treble seemed slightly tinny and the bass was good but not great. And for $50 I was actually disappointed and told my husband to please check them out himself because I was of the opinion that they should be returned.

Well, he hooked up the Google Chromecast Audio to them (since that is what my son will be using) and set them up in my son's room (smaller space than the living room, but has a cathedral vaulted ceiling). It sounded GREAT!

So overall, I think the quality you get out of these is going to be dependent on what device you have them hooked up to. Maybe my phone's sound is not at the optimal settings. But if you hook a Google Chromecast Audio to these speakers, you won't be disappointed. They obviously don't sound as good as our 6 speaker surround sound system, but for $50 I think these are a good value.

text:
They aren't perfect but they are a bit more than great for low budget-entry level; it's why I chose this. The sounds are good given its size and for its price range.
Here are some things about this product: The visual illustrations and instructions are simple and easy to understand.
The Left speaker line is 5 Ft; connect to Subwoofer that has 5 Ft of power cable; the Right speaker line is 6 Ft; connect to Subwoofer; the 3.5 mm line from the Right speaker is 5 Ft; my point is that you can get up to about 16 Ft wide if you connect the 3.5 mm line to your source which would be way off to the right. The Left and Right speakers are about 3.5" x 8.5" x 4" (XYZ from front view) while the Subwoofer is 5.5" x 8.5" x 8.1" (XYZ from front view and give another 1" or 0.5" for cable connections for Z)

title: Boy small PC speakers have come a LONG way!
text:
I had an older but very nice Monsoon MS-1000 2.1 set of speakers hooked to my desktop. They finally died out and I was rather sad... I was walking through our local warehouse club store and saw this system for a reasonable price and figured it would be a good buy to get ok sound until I could figure out what expensive speakers to get. It's not that I do any particularly critical listening at my computer but I do like decent sound.

When I un-boxed the speakers my first thought was - CRUD, that's a TINY sub-woofer. I already imagined in my head the 100hz or so bumpy bass that would come out of it. I would have been alright with that honestly but after hooking them up and playing some music through them... WOW! The bass is MUCH lower than this thing should be capable of producing. I turned the "sub" over and noticed that the little driver has a TON of travel.

They have definitely tuned this little thing for range and as expected, the downside is that after you do run out of volume a little quicker than the satellite speakers do. This means that after about half volume or so, you will probably want to turn the sub down a bit.

The inclusion of the back firing drivers on the satellites is nice. If you were to put these down on a table at a party and hook them to a phone or something, they would give good sound all around. On my computer desk, the sound bouncing off the wall behind them is a nice little effect.

These speakers have fulfilled every requirement I had for a set of computer speakers and they did it for a great price and in a small package.

text: Amazed by the volume out of a relatively small speaker set. I purchased these as a replacement to my old desktop speakers and couldn't be happier. Thankfully, Logitech's old cheap plastic controller and interference issues have been replaced by much nicer materials and what appear to be higher quality connecters. The sub has a L/R RCA connecter and a 3.5mm jack for audio in. The sub adjustment knob on the back of the speaker was set just below half, and I have not needed to adjust so far. The right speaker has the volume adjustment, a 2nd 3.5mm jack in and a 3.5mm jack out. The left is a separate unit (like the right) and has both a front and rear speaker like the right (this is for  "360" sound). I have tried a few genres of music and the speakers provide a sound that is crisp enough to hear the details in the music while the sub provides enough boom to fill the rest in. Im not entirely sure how much the added "360" speakers are actually helping, but the speakers sound very well balanced. At only 30W, its not going to fulfill a rock concert, but its more than enough to get some complaints (living in a dorm). Overall, I'm very happy with my purchase.

title: Buy something else. Buggy to the point of being unusable, and support is practically nonexistent.
text:
This used to be a great (but somewhat buggy) headset until Logitech abandoned support. Since mid 2014 this thing is just unusable trash. Take a look at the logitech support forums if you don't believe me. Something changed - either an updated USB driver with Windows, or a bad Logitech update, or both - but basically the headset doesn't stay connected, flakes in and out, and is generally unusable. I've tried many versions of the Logitech software but nothing works for me. It stopped working with Mumble. Audio will drop in or out. The headset will disconnect or power off randomly.

End result: I want to play a game with a friend. I fiddle with the headset until it works. I'm in a game for 10 minutes, and suddenly it'll stop working. I won't be able to hear, or I can't talk to my friend, or both. Sometimes alt-tabbing out and fiddling with things works, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes I have to kill everything or reboot or unplug/replug.

Some people claim that rolling back to an old Logitech Gaming Software version like 8.55 works better. Some claim you need to use a USB2 port instead of USB3. Some people say you need to buy and install an expansion USB card in your computer to fix it. Some people claim you need to modify config files in the logitech software.

Long story short, this once nice headset has been reduced to a pile of buggy crap. Logitech hasn't fixed anything in the last year and a half. Don't bother buying this.

The size and shape is ideal for either left or right-handed use and I like the overall feel in the palm. The color options are nice and I went with the red matte color which looks refined on a desktop. I was worried it would be a red glossy color. The weight of the mouse is nice and hefty which is desired to minimize any clicks or movements in error. The grip of the mouse around the thumb and ring finger are good as the areas are rubberized and dimpled to maintain maximum grip.

The overall construction is top-notch, including the left/right buttons, scrolling wheel, and side buttons. I have had some other brands of mice from Microsoft and lesser-known names; Logitech makes the best in my opinion. The functionality of the mouse is outstanding. The mouse tracks accurately and smoothly. The clicks are very confident and just feel right. I also like the unifying receiver included with this model. With the Unifying software download, I’m able to connect it to an existing Logitech wireless keyboard by just using only one receiver, which means only using 1 usb port as opposed to 2. The unifying software is user-friendly and works great in connecting up to 5 keyboards/mice. A Logitech keyboard and mouse are the perfect combination when it comes to going wireless for me.

I also downloaded the Logitech Options software to reprogram the side buttons and click wheel(left, right, middle click) if needed. By default, the side-buttons are back/forward for use when browsing on web pages for example. The click wheel is set for left/right scrolling and middle click by default. The sheer number of options to assign these side buttons and click wheel is mind-boggling to say the least; I’ll probably stick with the defaults for now though. But it’s nice to know that I can change the button assignments as needed and I applaud Logitech for providing this easy-to-use software from their downloads section of the Logitech.com website.

Also, the wireless connection to the PC has been flawless just like every other Logitech mouse I’ve used like the m325 travel-size mouse that I use for a laptop. I’ve had a bad experience with a Microsoft bluetooth mouse before in terms of connection and build-quality(mouse buttons would stick and stop working entirely) and will generally avoid bluetooth mice in general as I feel that these 2.4 ghz mice are much more reliable in terms of connection like instant-on and overall performance.

Other features of the mouse that I like are the on/off button that instantly connects to the pc and the fact that when the mouse is idle or when you have turned off the pc and forgot to turn off the mouse, the sleep mode kicks in on the mouse which prevents unwanted draining of the 2 AA batteries. Also, if you’re using this mouse on a laptop for example and wanting to store the usb receiver, there is a handy slot within the battery compartment that keeps it safe to prevent loss.

There are really no cons for me and I appreciate the 24-month battery life of this model and outstanding reputation for reliability of their products. I have used Logitech products for years; from keyboards, mice, computer speakers, cases, sleeves and everything in between. Logitech is definitely a brand I recommend and this m510 is no exception.

title: One Fatal Flaw: Sensor Placement.
text:
It's a real shame. This mouse has really, really good hardware, and the build quality is top notch!

The wheel is nice and heavy, and is very accurate. The buttons are nice, and they aren't too loud. All the buttons are easy to access without being accidentally pressed. If you download Logitech's software, you can remap ALL of the buttons to whatever you want. It's nice to hold with a palm or claw grip, and it feels very comfortable.

Now, the flaw. I use the mouse with a claw grip with my right hand. With my old mouse (Logitech M315? the numbers wore off) the sensor was on the left side near my thumb. Because of my grip, if I wanted to make small adjustments, I could 'twist' the mouse my moving my thumb in order to move the mouse up on the screen. This worked very well, and I'm not sure if it's part of the standard use of a mouse, but I got used to it over the past 3 years. This mouse has the sensor really far to the right near my pinky finger, making my previous strategy not work at all. If anything, it actually inverses the direction that I would normally want to go. I could re-learn how to do it, but it seems like moving the right side of my hand to move the mouse up and down would be a lot less effective than my thumb. You can see a comparison between the two mice in the photos below.

All this is because I use the mouse this way. I noticed that if I use the mouse with a lower sensitivity and just move the mouse instead of twisting it like I do, it seems to work fine.

I don't think I'll be able to change my mouse method, though. I may end up returning it.

title: After years of experience with this thing, I hate it
text:
This webcam is way more popular than it should be simply because a ton of amateur streamers use it, don't realize how bad it is, and then recommend it to other amateurs. I have been streaming for over 3 years now and I can promise you this webcam is a cheap, bug-riddled piece of crap.

- Proprietary driver doesn't let you have two of the same camera. You have to use the generic USB drivers from Microsoft in order to use two of these. This is an infamous issue that you conveniently don't hear about anywhere on the product page, but Logitech even has a video explaining the issue on YouTube.
- Forgets its settings constantly, has to be set back up every time you reboot (especially if you use the generic driver)
- TERRIBLE focus range, anything after ~2 feet is blurry. Apparently this is a manufacturing defect and to fix it you have to open the thing up and manually adjust the lens. Both of my cameras have this defect, and it's apparently extremely common.
- Requires insanely low exposure, which means bright lights, to get smooth FPS. I have 3 very bright LED panels shining in my face plus four background lights for my green screen and of course my ceiling light on just so that I'm well lit enough to get the full 30fps. And that's with exposure at -6, it goes as low as -10. What's -10 for, the surface of the sun?!
- Sometimes freezes randomly and requires a reboot to fix
- Mic quality is mediocre (not like I use the mic but hey if this matters to you then there's your warning)
- Doesn't even work with OBS Studio 24.0+, until I find a suitable replacement for my two c920s I am stuck on 23.2

My old review from back when I got started streaming rated this as 5 stars because I didn't know better. Well now I can tell you I was a fool, this camera is bad and I cannot wait to replace mine.

text:
50% of the time this product will actually work as intended. My advice is that if you do purchase this headset (which it is still quite cheap at its current 79.99 and would be an instant return if it were any more) is that you should ditch the driver software as it continues to disappoint me time and time again.

Common software/driver/hardware issues I've experienced and fixes-----------------------------------------------

Headset rapidly turns off and on (about once every two seconds): This issue like most of the others has still not been fixed by Logitech. Occurring when you start your computer up with the software suite, the program will attempt to connect to the headset and will actually succeed. However, a second or two later the software will suddenly not recognize the headset and try to find it again (this happens even if the headset is plugged in). This cycle continues for between 5-10 minutes or longer and can only be solved by exiting out of the software suite (which is disabled by default for me now). If you attempt to restart the suite, the cycle will continue again.

Headset turns off and then back on every 10 minutes: A fix for this one involves editing the sleep settings in a text file and is documented on a few forums (found with a google search). With no option on the headset or the software itself, this just shows the laziness that went into the design of this product.

Buttons no longer work/ Do not preform the intended function: This one actually cracks me up a bit every time it happens (about once a day). In this glitch, the volume wheel no longer works and instead all the other buttons seem to change the volume. For example, a few minutes before writing this review, pressing the power button lightly lowered the volume by one degree. The volume slider was not responsive at that time and plugging the device in actually caused the volume to jump a degree as well. Clearly there is some miscommunication with the headset and the drivers. All you can do if this glitch occurs is hold down the power until the headset restarts.

I can hear myself through the speaker: This problem is easily solved in the software through the "sidetone" slider. The bigger problem is that if you cannot use the software like myself and many others, you will have to learn to live with it due to the fact that sidetone is enabled by default.
-----------------------------------------------
I am not going to say I hate this product, simply because it does work without the software and with only a few annoyances. I feel that if Logitech could work out a few of these simple bugs it would be a 5 star product. I can't speak of the quality of the headset straps and their supposed frailty, as mine have not broken...yet.

title: Logitech -- what were you thinking???
text:
Logitech was the first to come up with a remote control that was truly universal. Instead of forcing you to handle individual devices, possibly tied together by macros, they centered their remotes around the same thing real people do -- ACTIVITIES! They truly made using my home theater system simple...enough so, that my wife really enjoyed it. After loving my two current remotes, I decided to replace the oldest one, which had been abused for around 10 years, with this "Ultimate" remote. Big mistake. Here are some of the "features" I found with this remote:

1) No matter what I tried, I couldn't get it to toggle power to my mainstream Sharp LCD TV, even after training it with the original remote; neither of my two previous remotes had any problem whatsoever, but that simple task was beyond this remote's abilities.

2) Even after switching to a new activity, it takes up to a couple of minutes before it will control the volume of my Yamaha or my Sony receiver. Want to turn it up to hear that hot news story or turn it down so it doesn't wake up your sleeping spouse? Well, if you need to do it before the wait period is up, you'd better hop on over the the receiver and do it by hand. That's exactly why you bought a remote, right?

3) The play and pause buttons are at the front end of the remote! Yep, two of the most used functions are way at the top, so you have to reach across the touch screen to activate them...and probably accidentally activate something on the touch screen as you try to do that.

4) No separate chapter skip buttons! By default, you have a fast-forward and a fast-rewind button; if you want to do a chapter skip, you have to hold the corresponding button down until you feel the remote vibrate. Want to blast through the commercials? Nope! You have to click and hold, release, click and hold, release, etc, making it nearly as fast to just watch the commercials. Sure, I was able to custom program two buttons on the remote, but REALLY -- this is where you decide to cut corners?

5) The full-color screen uses white writing on a light green background. Sure it can do brilliant colors, but the clever people at Logitech chose to make the default as difficult to read as possible.

On the up side, the buttons that do exist are excellent, with an easy, short throw, and excellent tactile feedback. The build quality seems to be fairly high, too. The included hub is touted as being able to control home automation devices, something that attracted me, since I have a number of those in my house. The touch screen works well, and when used with proper colors, is easy to read.

Because I've loved my two previous Logitech remotes, I'm not ready to give up on them yet, so I purchased a Harmony 700, a lower-end model, that so far seems to beat the socks off this sad remote. This could have been a great remote; instead, I consider it a "Don't waste your money!" epic fail.

text:
As with most of the reviews here my feelings on concept are excellent but the mechanics of it all needs improvement. I purchased the mounted unit. Trying to find a good place for it with flat surface in my car was a challenge and the only spot available was on my dashboard. Ok so we put it there. I am a shorter person hence short arm reach. While driving I found it difficult to get it to wake up without having to look at where I was putting my hand. That means taking my eyes off of the road if I happen to be on the freeway and need directions. Putting it anywhere else wouldn't work since there were no other flat surfaces that the suction cup would adhere to. The windshield wouldn't work since it would be in my line of site.

Ok on to the next issue. It seems that the adhesive holding the metal connectors doesn't like to stay put thus creating a hazard. The phone falls off the pad even though the pad is still stuck to the mount. I had to start off with the smaller of the two since I have a Samsung 7 Edge and use the charging pad. With it being stuck nearer to the bottom of the phone it made it top heavy which in turn made the phone fall off of the sticky pad. So I put on the larger one. Now I can't charge on the pad very well which leads me to my next issue.

Now I don't know whether or not this is due to the charge pad on my phone or not but have to assume. It seems that from the day I put it on my phone the battery drains very quickly. text:
Let me start by stating I have and use 3 different wireless Logitech keyboard/combos on three computers (1 laptop, 1 HTPC, 1 high end gaming rig)

The Bad : Not very happy with this keyboard. Keys are too closely spaced together and I am have issues hitting wrong keys. Keys have little tactile feel of key's edges (too flat). Even worse is the keyboard has really bad ghosting of the key strokes, that is when pressing the keys often times strokes are delayed and the same letter appears 2 or 3 times in a row, a real irritant. Palm rest is too low profile be effective. Bought and sold from Amazon, was going to return but Amazon was going to charge me $9.90 to ship it back (unopened package), not like i live in the boonies, I live in San Diego, Not cool Amazon. Decided to keep for the mouse and have a keyboard I don't care about getting damaged for traveling with my laptop.

The Good : The mouse works well. The unified transmitter is nice, being able to pair and unpair / mix & match my other logitech wireless devises is quite nice. The logitech software can be downloaded from their website and is easy to use. The Logitech software allows for customization of key bindings. Windows recognized and installed drivers automatically. Includes batteries.

Conclusion: I recommend getting a better combo. I replaced this with Logitech's MK550 "wave" keyboard combo for only about $10 more and has a unified transmitter. The MK550 combo comes with the K350 "wave" ergonomic keyboard and the fabulous M510 laser mouse which is a joy to use. The "wave" isn't perfect either but much better than the MK520. Second pick for a budget Logitech combo would be the MK360, good working reliable combo with decent keyboard and mouse. If I had known all this now, I would have gotten the M510 mouse on it's own and bought a good mechanical gaming style keyboard on it's own.

title: H390 stopped working after 6 months
text:
My H390 headset worked flawlessly for 6 months on 3 different computers running 3 different OSes (Win7, Win10, & Ubuntu Linux 10.04). All 3 OSes recognized headset as "Logictech USB Headset" and load the correct driver. Then one day, I noticed headset was no longer working on my Windows 10 computer (e.g., no sound from the headphones). Upon checking device manager, I noticed Windows 10 now recognized the headset as "Lync Audio Device." I checked headset on my Windows 7 & Ubuntu computers and noticed the same problem.

Logitech tech support personnel have no idea as to why this is happening. Since my headset is still under the 2-year warranty, they're sending me a refurbished replacement. Since this is clearly a hardware and/or driver issue, unless new Lync drivers that work with this headset become available, I speculate the replacement will also stop working (that is if it works at all initially), requiring yet another replacement. Logitech should either provide working drivers for the various OSes or take this piece of junk off the market. If you googled "lync H390 problem," you'll find others reporting this same problem, including reports of problem on computers running Mac OSX.

I gave this headset 2 stars instead of 1 star because it did work well for 6 months. Sound quality was good.

Huge, bulky, short battery life with 5 second warning before turning off. It would require me to disable/enable input adapters to get this to work everytime I booted up. They sound was incredible, sounded 3D.

The cups are soft and cush, but get hot after a while. The microphone only points down at a slight angle, just enough to be in the line of vision and be annoying (friends said my voice sounded clear as a bell, though, best they've heard over internet). The set is heavy and likes to slide backward.

It's Catch 22. It's well-made and cush, but due to that, it's hot, heavy, and really mutes the outside world (a good thing for headsets, but you can't just pull one ear off to hear someone talking to you, the whole set tries to fall off your head then).

Again, quality is great. The connectivity had glitches, though. Not for me and I returned them.

title: Perfect replacement for the Y-UY95
text:
Since I spend a lot of time online, between my Etsy shop, and other e-commerce sites, I spend a lot of time typing, and since my primary computer is a laptop, typing on that keyboard for hours on end is less than enjoyable. About five years ago my husband purchased the predecessor to this keyboard for me as a birthday present. I am a touch typist, so keyboard feel is very important to me, and I fell in love with the original keyboard as soon as I plugged it in. Quick response on the keys, and very few mistypes due to clunky keys you may find on inexpensive models, unless of course my fingers decide to not play nice.

But fast forward a few years, and the original keyboard had gotten a lot of use, and the Y-UY95 had been discontinued, but luckily my husband was able to find another one on eBay for me. I used that one for a few more years until most recently the Z key started to break. Apparently one of the tabs that holds the key in place snapped so if I didn't hit the key solid, it would bend to one side, kind of like a teeter totter. I could kind of work with it, but if I was in the process of typing a lot of text, the key would sometimes trigger both a z and x to be typed at the same time, which caused tons of problems, and resulted in my quest to find a replacement.

Knowing that the original model no longer existed, I still went on the hunt for the Y-UY95, which is the model # listed on the back of the keyboard, I no longer have the box so I cannot remember the Logitech model number. In my travels across the web, I came across the Logitech support forum for the old keyboard, and in it this model was referenced as a similar model. Upon further research it appeared to be the replacement for the original keyboard that I fell in love with so many years ago. Once it arrived at my door I am happy to say I am thrilled with my purchase. It has the same look and feel, of the original. I am almost tempted to buy a few more to have in inventory for when this keyboard finally dies since I type so much, at hubby's suggestion of course. Hopefully Logitech keeps this style in their product line because I do not know where I would be without it!

title: Not up to par with modern tech
text:
Doesn't keep up with the modern technology. Takes too much effort to setup as there's so much effort to customize the remote to make it work properly. If you have Xfinity X1, this will not be an improvement. It does not provide the voice recording feature. It couldn't even import the correct channel numbers for my cable network. Also the X1 remote is very fast, it sends simultaneous commands to my TV and Receiver so they turn on/off instantly when I press the power button. The Harmony takes seconds just to turn on or off the TV which is annoying because you sit and wait to see if it registered your button press for several seconds before seeing anything happen.

The software they use has a low resolution GUI (Silverlight) that is hard to look at and is slow. Every change you make has to be Synced that takes up to a few minutes, even for a minute change.

The remote has a rounded back which makes it impossible to control while it's on your coffee table with one hand, while say you're eating some food.

The device is very presumptuous to a detriment. For example if you want to set an activity up to change a receiver function, it always assumed it must turn on and turn off to run then turn off the device to stop. So you can't make a routine that just changes settings of the TV or Receiver on it's own. This is important for usage with IFTTT. I found it odd also that an activity for just my receiver turned off the power to my TV when my TV wasn't specified as a device for that activity.

I can't seem to change the order of the device page on the remote which is odd. Also don't know why the device page must have a white background and not match.

The remote is rather slow.

title: The hardware might be good, but the software is worth less than fertilizer...
text:
The software for this product is absolutely a pile of fertilizer. It is one of the most tedious, poorly planned, user unfriendly, time consuming, ill conceived, GUIs I have ever had the displeasure to work with. Let's take an example. I want to add a new activity for a local TV station that is not on the favorites list. The favorite stations list, by the way, seems to require a channel search for each new activity, even though it is probably a good assumption that all activities will be run from the same zip code. But let's put that terrible interface aside to discuss adding a local TV station.

I start the harmony app on my iPhone. There is a screen that is entitled Harmony. On the left appears to be an Activities tab and on the right Devices. I click the Activities tab. A list appears, but the tab is not highlighted. At the bottom is an Edit Activities button. I click that. At the top of the Edit Activities page are two columns, on has "Tap to edit activity" on the right "Drag to rearrange", under which are three bars for each activity. I guess those are supposed to look like sliders. They don't. I click the add activity button at the bottom of the page and am taken to the Activity page. The instruction indicates that I should select an icon for this activity. I do so and it is highlighted. There is a text box at the top of the page with no apparent purpose. Apparently that is for the name of the activity. On the top of the page are two arrows, on the left and another on the right. I assume the right arrow means to increment the step and the left go back. Words would have been nice, but I'm sure the user experience designer thought they were being creative. I click that and am taken to a page that says Select Devices. I choose TV and click the right arrow again. Nothing happens. I click it again and am taken to the Power On Devices page. My TV is on. So I pick the My Devices Are On button or the right arrow? It is not clear. I click the arrow to go to the next step, which is Input Settings. I click the TV and am taken to Select Input. There I choose TV and then the right arrow. I am taken back to Input Settings. I guess the right arrow meant OK and the left Cancel, but it is not clear. The arrows are definitely creative though... not really... I click on the right arrow and taken to Input Testing. There is only a left arrow on this page and a question if all of the devices are on. I click Yes. The app takes a few moments to Sync Your Changes and then a test page shows up. I opt to test later. I am taken back to the original activities page. However, the activity is not done, since no channel has been chosen. So I click Edit Activities once again and then tap on the new activity that I just create. I am taken to an Activity Summary with a number of options. I choose Edit Start Sequence and am taken to the Edit Start Sequence page. On it are TV power on and TV. The power on step cannot be edited. The TV step has a right arrow on it. Tapping the arrow brings up a list of input devices. I choose TV and then the right arrow. Clearly I need to add steps to the start sequence, but the button on the bottom of the page says Edit Entertainment Devices. I click it anyway. Now an Add a Step and an Add a Delay appears. I click Add a Step. Under the Add a Step page is a Device line and a Command line which is inexplicably disabled. I click on the Device/Device Name line. I am taken to a screen called Select Device. I choose TV. The screen hops back to Add Step, but now the Command line is enabled and there is a text box for a channel number. Now, my channel is 24, however my TV can display several HD channels on nine, 24-1, 24-2 and 24-3. I try to enter 24-1 in the channel field and am told it is an illegal channel. I try 24.1 with the same result. I opt for using the Command line to enter the actual key strokes. Clicking command reveals a list of commands that correspond to the keys of the remote. I click on 2. The app hops back to Add Step. It is not clear how to add another step. I click the right arrow at the top of the screen. Nothing happens. I click it again. It takes three clicks for the app to hop back to the Edit Start Sequence Screen. I click Add a Step. I go through clicking the device line and then the Command line as before. I click the '4' command and the app hops back to Add Step. I click Add a Step. I go through clicking the device line and then the Command line as before. I click the '-' command and the app hops back to Add Step.I click Add a Step. I go through clicking the device line and then the Command line as before. I click the '1' command and the app hops back to Add Step. I click the '>' and the app hops back to Edit Start Sequence again. One more click of add a step, click device, TV, back to Add Step, Command, -, back to Add Step, >, back to Edit Start Sequence. Add a Step. Device and choose TV. Command and OK. Back to Add Step. This should be the key pushes on the remote to change the channel to PBS. I click the right arrow at the top of the page. The app hops back to Edit Start Sequence. I click the right arrow. The app syncs my changes and takes me back to Activity Summary. There is no arrow at the top of the page. Does the arrow save, since arrows were always used before? Well, it is the only choice, so I click it. Now I am back to the first page which lists all of the activities. PBS is highlighted so I click it, assuming that it will be tested. The harmony turns off the TV. I click the PBS activity again. A starting screen is displayed and the PBS is displayed on the TV. My TV is a bit more complicated because it automatically rotates through all of the channels available, such as 24-1, 24-2, etc. But that's another problem to solve later. I've got a local channel that was not on the favorites entered into the harmony.

title: Not the best ergonomics per my opinion
text: Well. The concept for this mouse design was great but implementation is not. The idea of the good mouse is that your hand , wrist and mouse locked together for precise movement  and need minimum re-alignment when you next time put your hand on the mouse (muscle memory). In reality , if your hand is not very small but normal or large than the left buttons for your thumb are not on the right place and you need to move your finger back or shift your hand back to be able to click on them. The lower button on the mouse foot is practically not usable since you need too much effort to press it down while bending your wrist left. Terrible ergonomics per my opinion. Battery charge gone in a few days and you will need to keep micro- USB cable attached to mouse some time while it recharges . I find it not very friendly since mouse is not your cell phone that yo need to charge all time and i buy a wireless mouse to eliminate wires clatter on a desk. Another issue that i discovered is that mouse won't work on polished portion of your desk . It just getting lost and you need to use some paper or mouse pad to use it. It is a common problem with most laser mouses but some of them work just fine even on the glass or reflective polished material. Mouse is not from the lightest so if you used to having a light mouse you will need some time to adjust. I would not recommend this mouse for 10 hours a day drawing related work but some people find this mouse  pretty comfortable.
