title: 3 years and still going strong...
text:
I've had one for 3+ years now (this newer model...the older model I had one that lasted 9 years) and I'll still never go back to the regular kind of mice or other 'trackball' types. This mouse, once you've gotten used to using the thumb, is nothing but *THE* best mouse ever to own.

The first year or two of these new models there seems to have been a bit of cruddy hardware making the different buttons stop working correctly. I was bitten by this myself - twice - with my first two. If you still get one, make sure you use the warranty to get it replaced!!

Once you get one of the good ones, you'll also never go back to regular mice and you'll wonder how you ever got along without this mouse. The comfort and quietness and no-need-to-run-your-hand-or-arm-all-over-your-desk is amazing. Need to sit back from the desk? No problem, I can operate the cursor on the screen at the other side of the room without a hiccup.

I honestly can't say enough good things about this thumb-operated ball mouse.

By the way, this mouse works just fine on Linux, except maybe for being able to program the buttons to do a number of different things, the middle button *wheel) acts as 'double-click' just perfectly and the 'back' and 'forward' buttons do just what they're supposed to. So, Linux users, don't shy away from the best mouse you'll ever own and get this one.

Ease of Use: /5
Functionality: 4/5
Design: 2/5
Build Quality: 2/5

I definitely have an issue with a line across the top of the screen where the case meets the screen when folded up. This might have been avoided by constructing the keyboard to meet outside the active screen area or even mitigated by rubber feet at the corners, so I'll count that as a long-term design oversight I'd expect fixed in future iterations. I also have intermittent issues with the smart dock where it won't want to connect until I've closed & reopened all apps, or sometimes restarted the iPad. All my users have reported the same, though it seems to be fairly infrequent. Finally, and this is probably the biggest issue I have, it looks like normal usage puts a lot of stress on the bit that connects the iPad to the case. Granted, there's not a lot of area to work with for this design, but this is an area that could have used better construction. One of my users is on his 2nd replacement and mine is nearing the point where I expect it'll stop holding the iPad in place soon.

title: I didn't read a single bad review reporting this issue on Amazon
text:
Ok, this unacceptable and people should be aware of this issue before buying this product. There is a huge section on Logitech forum titled "MX Master Scrolling issue." There are hundreds of reports of related scrolling issues. However, I didn't read a single bad review reporting this issue on Amazon. So, is Amazon deleting user reviews now?

This issue is not minor like Logitech have said in the past on their forum. If you are a habitual web user or if you constantly use online maps, google sheets and a number of other applications online where the scrolling capabilities are important, this mouse is useless.

In fact I'm returning my unit since this item is defective and there is no solution for the current scrolling problem.

Also, this mouse feels cheap in comparison to the MX Revolution. I own 2 MX revolution mice and one of them is more than 3 years old. I normally put one in my laptop case wherever I go. When I first got the MX Master, I did the same thing put it in my case, but when I took it out the bag the 2 buttons have come out of their sockets half way. All I had to do was pushed them back in and everything was fine but since then I don't dare putting that mouse in my case anymore.

The scrolling issue was first reported more than a year ago - ‎04-17-2015 11:07 AM - and nothing has been done, in the mean time. Tech support's only advice is and I quote:

"Hello,

This is LogiLaurie, the Community Admin.

We have seen that a few users are experiencing minor scrolling issues while using the Logitech MX Master Wireless Mouse in the free spin mode.

For those who are using a Windows PC, we recommend that you disable the Smooth Scrolling option in the Logitech Options software to resolve the issue.

For those who are using a Mac, we’re currently working on an update to the Logitech Options software to include the ability to disable smooth scrolling and resolve the issue.

Best regards,
LogiLaurie
Community Admin"

There are very rare days or evenings for me where I can play online games with friends for more than 4 or 5 hours. The sound quality is great, they feel great on my head, and those that can hear me say I sound great. There's really nothing bad to say about these. Okay I can think of a few things I don't really care for but they aren't bad enough to knock any stars.

1) I don't like that I have to install the Logitech software in order to properly use and configure them. I'm very particular about what gets to use my RAM at any given moment.
2) I don't like how Microsoft processes audio and I have to constantly switch back and forth to what sound device I'm using. I found a way to merge all sound through one channel, but that caused other issues so I am back to just switching back and forth manually.

I have a lot of wireless devices in my home and these don't seem to have any conflict with anything. The range is great. I can make it all the way to the toilet and back to the computer.. which is probably 30 feet. That's about all I need, and from what I hear in the headset sound from others, that's about all they need too. It's become a joke, hearing each others toilets in the background.

title: Easily 5-Stars...This Sucker is TOUGH as Nails and Highly Responsive
text:
This took me some getting used to, as you'd imagine. But once I did, I really grew attached to it and don't want to go back to a traditional mouse.

Firstly, it just sits in one place, wherever you need.....with it being wireless, I have it on a glass desktop and no pad. Which I'd never get away with in a traditional setup.

Second, this is one tough hombre! I'm notoriously hard on my mice....as I frequently work late into the night and early morning, and I'll begin falling asleep at my desk. As this happens, I continually will have my hand slip off the mouse and effectively drag it onto the floor with a loud 'SMACK!" What's worse, and scary, is that about 1/3 of the time the battery door flies off and the battery pops out, so then I have to go digging around under my chair to find each. This may happen 5-6 times....every night! And that sucker still works like the day I got it.

The only thing you need to do is pop out the trackball about once a month or so, and using a wet wipe, clean the 3 inner sensors well and wipe the outside of the ball. It may take all of 15 seconds as you turn it over and can push the ball out from the bottom through a small hole that my pinky fingertip just gets enough through to push the ball out. You'll know when it's needed, as the ball will just stop being as responsive as you've grown accustomed to, but it's easily remedied.

I'd recommend this item to anybody, and it's clearly and easily a 5-star review.

title: This is the one for HTPC fans
text:
This is the perfect size for an HTPC (home theater PC). I use mine to kick back on the couch and conjure up music and video much more quickly than the usual remote- plus it is vital for web surfing. I would not use this for a workstation but on the couch it makes so much sense!

Everything is as small and light as possible while still remaining useful. You can easily lift this with one hand or have it on your lap without noticing. The touchpad has buttons which some may not like but I appreciate. The touchpad certainly could be bigger, but I wouldn't want the unit to be heavier or bigger overall. Same applies to the keyboard- it seems to find a perfect balance between function and reduced size. You also will find handy media buttons such as volume control- very important for HTPC users. The keyboard is good enough to write an email on without feeling like a toy.

The installation is super easy and it works well for PC or Mac. Logitech's software even lets you use compatible devices with the same receiver. I added a marathon mouse to mine in less than a minute. The receivers are unbelievably small which is great as long as you never lose them. The range is great and it still works from the other side of the room. The batteries last for a really long time (weeks to months) with daily use.

To sum up, I have used MANY a keyboard, mouse, etc. in my day and this one is the perfect size and layout for living room usage. Smaller ones are not useful to me, but any bigger and it would be too big or heavy. Combine that with the reliability, ease of setup, and long battery life- it's about as good as you can hope for!

title: for now I am happy and would recommend this to others.
text:
I got this to use with my macbook pro so I can sit back and type without having to reach for the keybpoard or keep the whole laptop in my lap[. Another reviewer mentioned the keys seeming closer together because they are not raised, and you can see this is causing some typos. Also, complaints about they keys not being backlit, doesn't seem to bother me, but not having a light for the Caps Lock is annoying; I left in previous typos to verify my last statement but had deleted half a sentence accidentally written in all caps. The right shift button position doesn't bother me, but damn does it bother some other reviewers. The trackpad works okay. The sensitivity has to be adjusted in system preferences by clicking on the mouse but still it is no where near the quality of the macbook's built in trackpad. It's nice to have two finger scrolling but it would be great to also have the other three and four finger trackpad gestures, like forward/back page and spreading the windows. The scrolling, though, is either too fast or too slow it seems. The tap to click was way too sensitive and had to be turned off (just hold FN and press the left button to turn off or back on, if the keyboard is switched off, then it will reset to default settings and tap to click will need to be turned off again). Another reviewer mentioned setting up the windows and alt key to be command and option, but this seems to already be so because when I click window+q it quits the app, or window and =+ will zoom in the screen so I can see it when I'm sitting across the room using the keyboard. I like having the back/play/skip and mute/quieter/louder buttons work like they do on my macbook keyboard and open iTunes with the play button. Seems to have a strong wireless connection because I was able to play and pause my music from down the hallway in another room. The other Function Keys don't work though. F1 is supposed to show desktop but it creates a bookmark instead, at least when Chrome is the app in use. The F4 button is supposed to "share" but it minimizes the window instead, at least it minimizes Chrome but no other apps; doesn't minimize iTunes. Holding Ctrl, FN, Window, or Alt along with the Function Keys does nothing but make an error noise. If anyone knows how to make the Function Keys work with a macbook, I would greatly appreciate it if you shared your knowledge. Overall this is a nice addition to my macbook and a great alternative to paying around $150 for an apple keyboard and magic trackpad with the connector...the connector alone costs almost as much as this logitech keyboard/trackpad combo.

This is only my first night using it so I will update if it fails on me and I change my mind, but for now I am happy and would recommend this to others.

Update: I have found that the arrows up/down work much better than two-finger scrolling; much smoother. Also, holding function while pressing up/down (labeled in blue as page up/down) it will scroll a full page length at a time, not holding function will scroll smoothly but only if clicked on the screen; if the curser is anywhere else, such as a text box, the up/down will not scroll but the FN+up/down will still scroll page lengths.

title: Very useful keyboard
text:
I was looking for new ways to give my old laptop life, and came across a good idea. I ordered a small solid state drive (32gb) and put it in my laptop and installed windows on it again. I have my tv mounted on the wall, and behind that wall is the kitchen, and it happen to have cabinets directly behind the wall that I had installed my tv on. So I took down the wall and drilled a hole thru the wall and ran a HDMI wire (plugged one in one of the HDMI inputs on TV, and other end to laptop), and ran a power cord to the laptop. Then mounted my tv back up.

I went to cabinet that had the wires, and mounted the laptop to the wall (w/ the use of a some metal i bent to the shape i wanted to w/ pliers and made a stand (see pic)).

I then hooked up HDMi wire, and put the Bluetooth dongle for the keyboard into the laptop. So whenever I want to use internet to watch a movie, I dont have to bother w/ the extremely slow netflix app on the smart tv apps. I can simply turn on my laptop and sit on my couch and use this keyboard. It also can be used for doing homework, but I use it mainly for entertainment. It can be used to watch your online shows and you can stream them directly to your tv. Just imagine anything you can do on your 14" laptop screen, now you can see that on your tv (i.e. 55" v 14")

Pro's:
- Very inexpensive, I picked it up for about $16
- Well built for how cheap it is.
- I have sat upto 20 feet away and it has yet to ever give me a problem w/ range.
- It has a power button so battery doesn't drain fast, I cannot even remember the last time I put new batteries in it.

Con's:
- For minor use its okay, but it wont be the keyboard you can put on your laptop to type an essay. It is too lightweight for that unless you put it on the table/desk.

text:
Not too many Bluetooth headsets that are also relatively inexpensive. I have a gaming headset that works great, but doesn't support Bluetooth so I can't use it on my cell phone for work purposes.

It isn't noise cancelling, but is loud enough to use in an office and can use both on my computer and phone (just need to manually disconnect from the device to connect to the other). Good voice tone and the microphone seems to pick up well during Skype for business or cell phone teleconferences.

The bad part is that the controls do not work at all on the PC. On the cell, the on-board mute works, but only has a "tone-up" or "tone-down" beep to let you know you are on mute...which makes you paranoid a lot during meetings to be sure you're muted and you'll be hitting that button a lot "just to be sure". Wish there was an LED on the microphone boom to let you know like my gaming headset. Can't hang up the call from the headset, control the phone mute so you'll have to have the phone handy and the headset. So in general you can't be too far away from your device when in a call in case you hear your name and gotta run and click/press the mute to answer.

Haven't tried the Logitech dongle to see if this at least fixes the phone controls on the PC, got too many RF dongles for Bluetooth, keyboards, mice and the like and rather not add another to the PC and run Bluetooth to be compatible with the phone.

So, yes, it works with good sound and mic and Bluetooth compatible which I guess is the important part. But the controllers are wonky and may/may not work on your PC and/or phone.

Once you pair it with your device it constantly is searching for your device and auto connects.

If you come within range it disconnects you from whatever you are using and steals the signal.
If you try to connect with another bluetooth item within range of this box, it stops your join with the other item and steals the signal.
If you come within range and it connects, it beeps once and never tells you.
If you are listening to music on your car's bluetooth and you come within range, it will steal the signal and start blasting the music in your house.
If you leave bluetooth on at night, it will steal the signal and then your alarms will be broadcast to this box.

Pretty much the only way to stop this thing from being YOUR ONLY bluetooth item is if you unpair, turn off the box or turn off bluetooth.

And don't get me started on multiple devices.

title: Good call quality, a bit uncomfortable after a few hours
text:
This device is a basic solution to using online meeting programs like Google Hangouts or Skype. I find that in an office setting, most people if they are not given explicit instructions on how to set up their audio, will have some kind of issue with their audio. This headset solves the problem for me since it provides clear audio through the speaker, and the microphone is excellent for general purpose use. Aside from the quick access buttons on the USB cable, there are no other special features. Its designed to be a plug and play solution for anyone.

I haven't had anyone complain about my audio levels on the various meetings that I attend every week. I do not have to repeat myself often, or adjust how I sit in order to get a good transmission. The speaker is loud enough that I can hear others even if their microphone levels are low or they are not speaking loudly.

I preferred the single-ear headset because in an office setting I think it works best to keep one ear open in case I leave them on and must hear someone else who has walked in to my office. I can also play music and people will not have to tap my shoulder to get my attention.

This headset is comfortable enough to wear for hours, but after about 4 hours I find that I'll need to take them off or continually adjust them as they begin to bother my ear. This discomfort is the reason I took off one star. Although I have similar problems with other headsets, I feel this is a problem that should be addressed given that these are intended for daily workplace use.

You'll want to flip up the microphone if you are drinking a coffee, I've made that mistake a few times to the dismay of my co-workers.

title: Spend the money to be more comfortable
text:
A mouse is one of the things I use most frequently and for the longest spans of time. I decided that in order to combat the daily discomforts of sitting in an office chair that I would invest in things that felt more comfortable (along with getting some more exercise). This mouse has been one of the most successful purchases in improving my daily comfort level. Combining good posture with a relaxed hand has mitigated the pains I'm used to feeling throughout the day.

One of the most important design features that has allowed me to maintain a relaxed grip is the thumb rest. Without a thumb rest I find that eventually my thumb drags along the surface and gets under the mouse when I need precise control. The geometric shapes cut into the design provide a welcoming tactile feel. It also doubles as a button that can be programmed with the logitech software to execute a few different types of actions.

A significant portion of my time using a mouse is spent scrolling. This mouse has two options, one that clicks, and one that freely spins. I always keep it on the free spinning modes, but having the option to switch to more specific inputs is nice for switching weapons when gaming. Although I'm not sure that I like the shaped ribbing on the wheel as it starts to irritate my finger after using it all week. The mouse is large enough that I can comfortably use my middle finger to scroll, which can be nice.

Bluetooth connection works well, as well as the wire for recharging and the wireless dongle. The battery lasts a very long time. I think I have used it for two weeks without having to recharge it.

The piece of the design that I think needs to be improved is the side wheel. I have it set to scroll left and right, which could be useful in programs like excel, except that there is no tactile response so it is impossible to know when excel will respond and scroll to the next cell. title: A step in the right direction that ultimately falls short of its potential
text:
Purchased from (and returned to) newegg.com.

Pros:
-sleek design
-cool lights (although not particularly useful or practical)
-software interface on PC is reasonably intuitive
-multiple simultaneous sound inputs
-good overall sound quality

Cons:
-extremely uncomfortable. Clamps VERY hard on your head. The padding on top pushes into your skull horribly.
-lights aren't particularly practical or useful and drain the battery.
-no way to control the mic input volume wirelessly
-only one of the multi inputs allows for 7.1 simulated surround sound
-no way to mix the audio on any non-PC platform. For example, lowering game volume and increasing voice chat/party volume
-virtual surround sound was not particularly impressive

I was extremely excited by this headset primarily because I have a dual-screen gaming setup so I can have PC access while playing games on console (primarily PS4), and I was thrilled by the idea that I could route sound input from both my PC and PS4 simultaneously. That way I could play games and Skype/Teamspeak with friends while enjoying the 7.1 virtual surround sound on my console.

Unfortunately, the cons listed above outweighed the pros, and I didn't see enough value to hold onto Logitech's $200 Flagship headset. I spoke to a tech support agent prior to returning to see if I was overlooking some necessary features, primarily, the ability to turn up the volume of my microphone. All friends I played with using this headset via PS4 said I was always extremely quiet, almost too quiet to hear most of the time. I was told that I can raise the volume of the microphone using the included 3.5mm cable plugged into the headset, but that utterly defeats the purpose of a wireless headset. The representative awkwardly agreed.

Additionally, I'm sure these headphones would have eventually become broken in somehow, but I just found the horribly uncomfortable from day one. I am of skinny stature with a fairly small head, and they clamped my ears horribly and the padding on the connecting bar bore into the top of my skull to the point of consistent pain every time I wore them.

The lighting is a neat feature, but it's pretty much a gimmick because 1) you can't (obviously) see the lighting at all when you are wearing the headset and 2) it's a needless drain on your battery.

The sound quality in stereo seemed fine, I have no complaints there. The virtual surround sound, however, seemed rather lacking compared to my other VSS headset, the Sony Gold Wireless headset.

It's because of the Sony Gold Wireless that I think I ended up returning the 933s. For less than half the cost, the VSS is excellent, and the headset offers features that I find rather essential when in use on the PS4, particularly the ability to crossfade the volume between the game and the chat party.

As a bit of a tangent which is partially applicable to the product review, it's my hope that Logitech (or anyone really) will one day create a headset that can receive 7.1 VSS input from multiple devices simultaneously. As it is, the 933 will technically only receive 7.1 on a single input, and 2-channel stereo on the other possible 2.

In summary: not a terrible headset for the money, especially if PC is your primary machine. But for primary use with console, there are better options with better surround sound, that are probably far more comfortable and practical.

title: Perfect for dumb TV + computer combo
text:
Update 2016-03-01
I found out by reading another review that the F1-F12 keys can be made to behave in their default Windows mode by installing the Logitech SetPoint software and clearing the Keyboard "Swap F key functions" checkbox. I had to unpair the keyboard and receiver and then pair them again in order to make the Keyboard tab appear in the SetPoint application. Since that corrected my major complaint about the product, I have raised the review to 5 stars.

Original Review
On Windows systems, I like almost everything about this keyboard touch pad combo. I do occasionally miss the small SHIFT key and hit the UP key instead, but that mostly happens after having typed on a full sized keyboard for awhile. The keys have good enough tactile feedback but no click, - that's OK by me. The touch pad is convenient and has nice big Left and Right buttons. There is also a secondary Left button at the upper left of the keyboard that I often use. The computer is about 10 feet from the keyboard.
My major problem (minus one star) is the normal function keys (F1-F12) are overridden by other functions such as volume controls and video playback controls and the like. To access the usual functions requires pressing a "FN" key in combination with the desired function key. So if you want to access Help you must press FN+F1. or FN+F2 to rename a file. Other key combinations work as usual ALT+F4 closes an application, CTRL+F4 closes a Tab/Child Window.
I wish it worked with my Android table but it doesn't get much use anyways. Overall I'm very happy with the keyboard and recommend it.

title: 1. Bad cursor pointing 2. Bad precious pointing. 3. Poor ergonomic design. 4. Additional info. 5. Conclusion.
text:
1. Bad cursor pointing 2. Bad precious pointing. 3. Poor ergonomic design. 4. Additional info. 5. Conclusion.
1. Bad cursor pointing: for some reason on the bottom, at the optical sensor Logitech has made this long (1cm) narrow hole. The pieces of dust and hair occasionally go into this hole and then it becomes possible to point the cursor. This happens to any mouse but to this one it happens much more often and because of narrow hole it is impossible to remove the dust! It is extremely annoying! Very bad design!
2. Bad precious pointing: I am returning M100 and I bought Logitech M500 instead. Laser precision pointing of M500 is sooooo much better then than the poor optical pointing of M100.
3. Poor ergonomic design: go to the store and check for yourself: all mice above $30 have a different ergonomic design (most are similar to M500). M100 has a poor ergonomic design - it just does not feel comfortable in the hand!!! The hand gets tense and tired. But all hands are different so do go to the store and try different mice for yourself to find the one that fits you comfortably!
4. Additional info: I am 43 years old. I have been a computer programmer since 19 and I never had a tunnel syndrome (Praise The Lord).
I think the secret is to point mouse with your fingers muscles (not shoulder muscles). M100 just does not feel comfortable in the hand - I believe one of the reasons is both buttons are at the same height. I had to go to the store again and try 15 different mice - Logitech M500 has much better ergonomics - I believe one of the reasons right button is lower than the left - which follows the tilt of the hand.
5. Conclusion: Many times I heard the advice - never buy the cheapest product in the line. But I did buy M100 because it was Logitech - the old reputable famous solid company. But unfortunately this advice stands for Logitech also.

At first I could never understand why anyone would buy this remote as it only has one activity available on it, but then I helped them set up their new TV and honestly it is perfect for them. An activity means that the remote will turn on your devices to the correct input and will control whichever device you tell it to during your programming of the remote. In this case, the WATCH TV activity will turn on their TV to the HDMI 1 input, and when you press the channel, menu or other buttons, you will be controlling the CABLE Box. The volume will still change on the TV... etc. If they need to turn on their surround sound, they have the DEVICE button which can control the surround sound, but they do not like to have it on all the time and most of the time us it just for listening to the radio anyways. text: A solid and quality mouse.  Good heft, solid buttons, doesn't feel cheap.  But, the design is a bit odd for my very average hand.  I have average-sized right handed guy hands that will fit most any mouse, and this mouse is not designed for them.  I think the primary flaw is that it is designed with a thumb cutout on both sides for ambidextrous use--which is stupid, since the thumb buttons are only on the right-handed side.  This creates a hollow on the outer side of the mouse that makes handling awkward, and makes it difficult to get a comfortable 3-finger/3-button grip.  The middle and ring fingers are crammed too close together.  I also find that the thumb buttons are set back too far.  Essentially, the only way to hold this is to do so with just the fingertips, with the hand laid nearly flat, which leaves the base of the mouse not in the ideal palm, but at the base of the fingers.  One of the main reasons to get a mouse this large is to be able to hold and grip it--if I just wanted to use fingers, I would get a smaller one that is light and nimble enough to easily move with fingers only.  So, unless you have really long, narrow hands, I'd look elsewhere.  All that being said, the build quality, fit and finish, are excellent; and if this fits your hand, great. title: Keyboard cannot be used if you're going to remap keys (basic feature in Windows)
text:
There's a major problem with this keyboard -- it doesn't support re-mapping certain key-combinations. Remapping keys is a standard feature of operating systems, including Windows. Logitech claims it's not supported. What they're really saying is, they have a bug and they would rather not fix it because they can't justify the cost of doing so. That's fine. They don't have to have my money.

Here's the specific problem:

Operating System / Device Platform: Windows 10

I am using this keyboard on a Windows computer. The problem occurs when I remap the caps-lock key in Windows. The behavior after that is strange and I believe is a bug in the keyboard software. Windows allows the user to map modifier keys. Internally this is done via the registry key System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Keyboard Layout . You can use software to help you do the mapping, such as the free tool: (...) What I've done is map the caps-lock key to the "right" control key. When I do this, other keyboards connected to the computer work fine. The Logitech 750, however, works except for two specific keyboard sequences. If I use one of the two following keystrokes, it doesn't work: Ctrl+Shift+F or Ctrl+Alt+T . Of course, instead of using the Ctrl key, I'm using the Caps+Lock key because that's how I have it mapped (it's very common to do this among software developers. just Google "remap caps-lock key") I've tried this with two different Logitech 750 keyboards. I've also restarted my computer in Windows 10 Safe Mode just make sure some other program wasn't doing this. I have the usb key plugged into my computer directly. I tried the most basic scenario on a bare-bones system .

Remapping keys in Windows is normal and supported by the O.S. There are applications that require this type of thing to be done (kiosks, HMIs, etc.). This is just a keyboard. It shouldn't be so complex that basic things don't work. It should be 100% compatible with any other keyboard.

text:
I've used a previous version of the Logitech rechargeable mouse that uses a AA battery and wasn't very happy with the length of time it worked on a charge. This mouse uses a lithium battery and lasts weeks without a charge solving that problem.

The real upside of this mouse is that there is a smart wheel that allows you to have the normal wheel clicks when you want them and when you flick the wheel to scroll a great distance, the click releases and allows the wheel to free-wheel allowing you to cover a lot more distance. This has been the single most useful feature of this mouse.

The buttons for the thumb were mentioned by some to be useless, but I haven't found that to be the case. The wheel for horizontal scrolling could have a little better acceleration but overall, I've been happy with the mouse.

title: It can be a little loud but still a contender
text:
I am currently typing on my Logitech MK520. I am not really sure how to feel about this keyboard as the keys seem a little more loose than other keyboards. Maybe loose isn’t the best way to describe it, but there seems to be some free play when pressing each key, as if it were wobbly before being pressed. If that makes sense? The keyboard is also not very quiet. I am a light typer and I feel that the keys still make a lot of unnecessary noise. It won’t wake up someone sleeping in the next room, but it’s definitely not quiet. The loudest keys, as you can imagine, are the space bar and the backspace. Two of the most frequently used keys I would argue. A quiet space bar is not to be found on this keyboard.

Anyways, if that sort of thing does not bother you, then this keyboard will very likely suit your needs. For me, I am OCD about the sound the keys make, how each key feels when pressed (tactile feedback), if the key requires a firm press or feels mushy, etc. I feel like I am on a never ending conquest to find the perfect keyboard. While this keyboard has pushed me closer to my final goal, I still have yet to find the perfect keyboard.

The good things. Well, the design is sleek and will complement other sleek items on your desk. I have had no issues with any wearing of the letters or anything so far. The media keys seem useful and there aren’t too many. Your essentials: volume control, playback control, calculator, favorites, etc are all at your fingertips. I like the fact that there is a power button located in the top right of the keyboard. The battery life is up to three years (we will see) but the power button allows you to extend your battery life. Good job, Logitech! The FN keys are available if you enjoy using those shortcuts. I personally do not, but they are there if you do.

Logitech makes a quality product and I have many throughout my home. I count 4 Logitech items on my desk currently. If you want a good but not great keyboard, the MK520 is perfect for you. If you are looking for something that will wow you and last for many years, you will be better off investing a little more money into a better product.

title: Makes things better in every way, great experience
text:
I have been a long-term Harmony user, 12+ years, and really wasn't sure that I wanted to change, as the remote that comes with this unit is simpler/reduced functionality than the Harmony remote I use now, which has a screen and more activity buttons, and I doubted the hub would be able to control all my devices sitting in my entertainment center, and was concerned about how the family would react.

After using this for a week, I and my family are 100% sold. Best experience w/a remote/entertainment center we've every had. Caveat: Takes a little massaging to get everything up and running.

Pros:
1. Setup was a breeze...everything worked well and no surprises. Existing activities were imported and ready to use.
2. New smaller (and dare I say sexy) remote looks great, feels great in hand, is easier to hold and use (especially for my wife w/her smaller hands), and does everything we need.
3. Control via phone app is well done (not fantastic but easy to understand and use) and family members were excited about having the remote control on their own smartphones. When in the app I can control the volume of the receiver w/the phone's volume buttons! Love that.
4. Alexa and Google Home integration (also using Smartthings Hub) is convenient and fun. I can start/change activities and start specific content via voice.
5. Zero issues w/control over devices. The hub is sitting on top of my DVR in the entertainment center. DVD player behind door w/window on one side, receiver behind door on the other side, DVR & ROKU in the middle open shelf. IR blaster positioned next to the receiver. All devices are controlled, including the DVD player that is behind a cabinet door with a window. I've never had a lost signal to a device. I'm really impressed - I frankly didn't think it would work, but it works perfectly.
6. When someone is visiting and wants to watch something I don't have to teach them about pointing the remote at the entertainment center until the activity is fully started, and don't have issues with some devices not starting or switching on, etc.

Cons:
1. Had to tweak one of my Activities after importing - had some odd behavior when switching back to my SmartTV view on my Sony Android TV. Some of that may be due to the TV itself, as I had some issues w/it using my old Harmony remote.
2. Sometimes when left to sit running for a long while the mobile app loses connectivity w/the current activity/devices and won't control the devices. I close the app and open it again. App opens back up to the current activity and everything works again.

I was hesitant, but am now a cheerleader. Buy this. :)

text:
First of all I wasn't expecting much from these speakers for $9. I have a nice 5.1 set with a great subwoofer in my computer room and I certainly wasn't expecting any comparison.

I watch movies at work overnight, either YouTube or downloaded, on my laptop and with the background noise at work it was hard to hear the laptop speakers. Some laptops have better speakers, but I figured buying some cheap speakers is cheaper than buying a new laptop.

These work perfect for my situation. The sound is nice and clear, and can get loud enough for normal listening. I even tried some music and they are pretty decent. If you buy these speakers expecting much more, you will be disappointed.

One thing I was worried about, I use Linux and these speakers don't have the usual 3.5 headphone jack, they are digital, which means the sound card is basically built in to the speakers. So the sound transfers from the computer to the speakers through USB, as well as the power. I didn't read enough before I bought these to know that, and Linux can be finicky. But I was able to go into the sound mixer and change the output device to USB speakers and they work perfectly. Anyone using Windows won't have any problems, this would probably be done automatically when you plug in the USB cable. 1 less cord to get tangled up is a good thing.

I would recommend these speakers to anyone who is not looking to shake the walls, but just requires decent sound at a great price. And they are small enough to pack nicely in my backpack along with my laptop.

title: Comparison vs. Harmony hand-held remote.
text:
I had an old Harmony hand-held remote that required programming on the website. I replaced it with the Hub, now using my iPhone or iPad as the remote. Here's pros/cons. (For consistency, "components" refer to TV, amp, cable box, and other things you are controlling; "device" refers to the phone, tablet, or whatever you are using to issue those commands.)

Both the Hub and the Hand-held require extended time to program. What components do you use with each activity? How are they set up? And a bunch of questions you hadn't considered, like when you hit the volume button, which component's volume should that affect? Plan on spending a few hours with either system for the initial set-up; this is the Harmony world.

The Hub doesn't require you to point your device at components. This was VERY problematic with my hand-held (and why we got this instead), as all the devices for an activity may not be at the same location. How this works: the device sends a wifi signal to the Hub, which then sends infrared to the components. So you need line-of-sight to each component from either the hub or an [[ASIN:B00ITEPKIG Original Logitech Ir Mini Blaster (Emitter) for Logitech Harmony Smart Control Remote]] which is, in turn, hard-wired to the Hub. (The Hub includes one emitter and sends a signal itself; it has an additional plug for 1 more emitter.) This means I can select "Watching Tivo" while still in another room, so it's all set by the time I sit down. Particularly nice: turning on the stereo in the entertainment center without leaving the kitchen while I'm cooking.

You can set up a Harmony hand-held remote to have a single button issue a series of commands to your component(s) to, for instance, send various arrow button commands to get to a specific activity on your cable box. The Hub does NOT allow this for your phone or tablet, so plan accordingly. It DOES, however, still issue a series of commands upon starting / stopping an activity to get the right components talking to each other. You just can't program a string of activities to a "button" on your device. Instead, there are slabs of virtual buttons which you can program to a specific single-button activity (play, pause, mute, channel up, etc). Many are already set up, but you can edit/add/delete as you wish. Also, if you have more than one device, each programs these buttons independently. This is a pain in the butt for one person using different devices, but for a multi-user household, each can use their own device as a remote with the same activities (activities are programmed into the Hub), but can have each activity's buttons set to their own preferences.

Using the Hub with your phone/tablet as your remote has a few unforeseen implications:

1) You've probably become touch-sensitive to your remote; you don't have to look at it to know what button you're about to press. This will NOT be the case with your phone/tablet. You just have a flat screen with no way to know what you're about to press without looking at the screen. This can be mitigated by setting up the touch-screen feature for each activity. This turns your screen into a blank surface. Single- and double finger gestures (tap, slide, etc) can be set to handle your most commonly-used commands. These are also programmed by device.

2) You most likely set your device's screen to turn off after a few minutes without use. This means when you want to pause/stop, by the time you've woken up your device and hit the right buttons, you'll want to rewind a bit to get to where you wanted to stop. The solution is in app settings to prevent sleep while the app is active; this, however, eats up your device's battery. So consider keeping it plugged when using it as your remote.

3) Your device isn't speaking directly to your components; the Hub is the interface. This means your commands take a bit longer to execute, even with the screen kept awake. For instance, with my Harmony hand-held, if I was fast-fast-forwarding a show I'd recorded, if I hit the "skip back a few seconds" button, it would start playing right where I'd originally pressed the button; with the Hub, I have to press "skip back" 3 times to get to that point.

Overall, I'm pleased with the Hub. The flaws I found aren't things I believe can be "fixed" (except programming sets of commands to a button -- that's holding back the 5th star), but are the consequences of this kind of architecture. So you'll have to decide whether to go this route or keep a remote.

text:
(Using Microsoft Windows 7 Enterprise on a 2015 HP Elitebook)
If this mouse wasn't so unreliable, it would be perfect. I have had two of them now and they have both broken within the first month of use and had to return both. The way the scroll wheel works causes a lot of stress on the electronic "brakes" that stop it after it starts to free-spin. Both of my mice stopped clicking after about a week because of this and eventually the scroll wheel stopped responding on-screen all together after a month.
The side scroll wheel would be great, but it hardly ever works right with the programs I use for work (Excel, Word, any proprietary software). It is never sensitive enough, even on the lowest setting.
I do love the programmable button setup and the overall design, but the fact that I had to return not one, but TWO because of how fragile they are, makes me give it two stars.

title: Comfortable Grip - Even for Large Hands
text: I've used several different mice, but this one is the best. I use two at home (desktop/laptop) and I'm buying a third for the office. I have large hands with long fingers, so a lot of mice are just too small. I could actually use a slightly bigger one, but the size is sufficient and it fits well enough. The  sides have a soft-touch, rubber-like texture, so it's easy to grip. The other problem that this mouse solves is that the side buttons are positioned high enough so that my thumb fits below them. I've had trouble with other mice because my thumb would keep hitting those buttons. It feels solid and well-constructed, and it's a little heavier than some others that I've used. (Again, big hands, so heavier is good.) The battery life is good, operation is very smooth, and the wireless functionality simply works (no manual pairing involved). title: Perfect.
text: Even if I tried, I wouldn't be able to find a flaw with this case. What I love most about it is, the keyboard turns off automatically during inactivity, even if you haven't locked your iPad or have resorted to the touchscreen for a while, so I rarely ever have to charge it. Actually, I think I've only had to charge it once so far, and that was when it first arrived with a powered-down battery, and it's been nearly 3 months. The keyboard responds immediately whenever you switch it on, too, and you never have to re-pair it with the bluetooth. If you forgot to turn off the power switch, it still shuts off on its own as soon as the iPad is locked and automatically activates *only* if you've unlocked the iPad *and* pressed on a textbox that would prompt a QWERTY screen. As soon as that happens, the QWERTY on the screen automatically disappears to allow the keyboard use, and if you happen to prefer screen-touch typing at that moment, the conversion is extremely fast and easy when you flip off the keyboard's power switch. Brilliant! And the icing on top is, the case is extremely thin and light, with a weight and width comparable to some of the regular heavy duty portfolio cases they have out there for iPads, and with a keyboard that types with ease with great traction on the plastic keys. And what's more, I find the magnetic prop-up stand very useful when watching videos and the curved, concave edge of the case along the right side of the iPad a wonderful grip to hold onto when viewing vertically (I spend much time on Kindle) and best of all, the iPad folds naturally over the keyboard with cushioning so it doesn't hit the keys, when you hold it vertically to read off the screen. I cannot for the life of me criticize this case. It's perfect!

title: Logitech Wins Again!
text: This is an incredible unit!  It pairs easily with three of my devices, and it has a three position switch so you can change instantly between three different devices.  I use it all the time with my Windows laptop in position A.  I have an Android tablet made by Onda that sits comfortably and at an ideal angle so I can see my larger screen monitor and my 9.7 inch Onda tablet at the same time. It is set-up with position B.  Then when I want to use it with my I-PAD, all I have to do it turn the switch to position C.  This keyboard is heavy and solid.  Never-the-less, it is still a good choice for me when I travel because a tablet together with this Bluetooth keyboard is still less weight and bulk than my laptop.  Initial pairing is easy and reliable-- amazing with I-PADS, since there is no password code requested like with Android.  Note that the slot that holds your tablet is not suitable if your tablet is in a protective case.  I have my I-PAD in a Defender case, so I simply set the I-PAD standing up in its case immediately behind the K480.  This arrangement is almost exactly like using a traditional laptop, but you can separate the two units with no effort. The touch is next to perfect.  In the month or so I have used it, I have never skipped a character as the result of a problem with the keyboard.  If you want the ultimate in portability you would want to look at a different Bluetooth keyboard.  It works on a pair of two AAA alkaline batteries.  While units that work with a built-in lithium ion battery are more convenient in the short-run, eventually these batteries wear out.  Two AAA alkaline batteries seem to last for months.  Carry an extra set of them for good measure, but it will probably be a very long time until you need to replace your first set.

title: Stellar wireless gaming headset, LOVE IT (but maybe some long-term battery quality issues)
text:
This has been a great wireless headset! It is comfortable, has good sound, and enough range that I can run to the kitchen and still hear if the next round is about to start, etc. I also really like the auto mute/unmute when moving the mic boom between the deployed and stowed positions.

Unfortunately, regarding longevity, after just a couple years of ownership, it started getting periodic cut-outs while using it wirelessly. The audio will just cut out for a few to several seconds and then come back again. This can occur even within just 30 - 45 minutes of play despite have had it plugged in and fully charged before starting. Plugging it back in while playing seems to fix the issue, I think, and the power cable that it comes with is plenty long and has a nice cord keeper design, but then why have a wireless headset?

Despite this one rather annoying long-term quality issue, I am still giving it 5 stars because it otherwise shines (maybe I just ended up with an under-quality battery).

title: A good keyboard for your living room
text:
This is a nice keyboard for living room PCs. It gives you both keyboard and pointing ability in a single small package. The wireless connection works well across a room. It has dedicated volume buttons just above the trackpad; they are very useful in an HTPC setup. The Unifying Receiver lets you add a Logitech mouse without using a second USB port on your PC.

It fixes the biggest layout problem of the original K400, the placement of the right shift key; that made the earlier version unusable for me. But it comes at the cost of making the arrow keys harder to use; the up and down arrows are now half size. The lower-contrast labeling of the keys makes them harder to read in low-light situations. The touchpad is OK; I still prefer a mouse, but it gets the job done for occasional use.

title: SET-UP INSTRUCTIONS
text:
Harmony remote set up
==================

Step-by-step **easy** set-up instructions (and a review)

I was going to write a review but when I realized how many steps there were to getting this thing set up properly I decided to write instructions instead, as they seem like they are needed the most. But just to be thorough here is a mini-review (unboxing first):

Please see pics. This is a truly beautiful remote. As much as it needs to do (controlling everything) logitech has somehow managed to use less buttons than either my TV or Cable box remote—but nothing beats the Apple TV for pure minimalism. It also feels good in your hand. Now, that is all fine, but does it work? Well the first thing I did was opened the box and looked inside at everything. Not too bad . . . three layers of stuff (empty the box entirely because there are three plastic trays stacked on each other. the charging base is in the bottom tray, and apparently this is where logitech wants you to put the remote when it is not in your hand. As funny as that sounds to me, it does mean that this thing will *never* need batteries, so that’s a good start.

This thing comes with two chargers: one for the charging unit (that plugs into the wall) and another USB to USB mini. That means you can charge the remote from your computer—BUT it also means that before you can use this at all you have to download some software from logitech and install it on your PC/Mac (no support for Linux it seems). This was only a minor PitA. The website has several remote control downloads available. Look for the one that specifically says “950” and ignore the rest. If you have a Mac you have to go into your Apps and search out an app called “MyHarmony” (which does not appear in alphabetical order for some reason btw). PC users can ignore this. Coming to Mac from 20+ years on a PC I mention this as it was frustrating to have to guess what happened after I installed the software and it did not launch automatically.

I am reporting my findings as I go through the software set-up. The first thing you do is to plug your remote into your PC/Mac. Then open the software (MyHarmony app). It is extremely patient, and appears like a slide show, where you click through each screen as you complete the tasks. They chose a friendly blue as a background which for some reason actually makes me feel like I can do this (set up a touch screen universal remote) without the assistance of a 12-year old or a $75/hour “hire-a-nerd.” Side note: 99% of you will click “New Set-up” and not “copy settings.” As simple as this screen was it confused me for a while (it’s the picture).

Grrr . . . for this next part you are going to need a pen and paper. The next screen is a bit cryptic. It says to “Enter your device information.” naturally I grabbed the remote (still plugged into my macbook for set-up and looked on the back side for a serial number. Just in case you are as confused as I was, this is where you gab a pen and paper and write down the brand name (“Manufacturer”) and “Device Model Number” for *everything* you want you remote to control. Okay, so . . . monitor, Apple TV, Sony DVD player, Comcast cable box (did I forget anything?) — I will be at this a while. Hint: So will you :-D

(Yes, that is me laughing at your pain)

Okay, so that was (not) fun. I would imagine that if your electronics are in an entertainment console (large cabinet) this will require some help. The only model number I could not find was for the Apple TV, so here is a link that will help (if you need: [...]).The rest of this set-up will take you 45 minutes to an hour, just at your computer, so you might as well settle in. One thing that I found extremely useful is that you can rename the devices on your remote after you add them. DO THIS. Instead of my Comcast Cable set-top descrambler box being labelled “Motorola Model DCH70 /2089” it now reads “Comcast Cable box. Make your “device names” user (that would be “you”) friendly because this is how they will appear on the tiny screen of your remote. If you do this now you will avoid a LOT of hassle later.

Okay, activities all set and “manage devices” is easy enough to understand (just play around with your remote a bit). Don’t throw away your old remotes just yet. When you first try out each new setting you will get a haptic feedback (the remote will buzz) and it will ask you if everything is working properly. DON’T make the mistake I did. make sure (100% not a guess) that everything is “off” when you try an activity that turns on your TV (or whatever) and changes the channel/settings, otherwise you will spend another 30 minutes frustrated and trying to figure out why some things work and others do not.

You will have to manually power things off (with the remote) unless you set up a “Kill all” command, which I did not see under activities but might just try.

Other than that this thing does what it says and it works amazingly well. Now I can DUMP four (4!!) remotes in a drawer and forget about them for a while. I will update this review if this thing breaks or if I figure out how to make my (non Bluetooth) lights go on and off with this remote.

title: A very poorly executed product that will give you hours of frustration and will never successfully work
text:
Note: I purchased mine at Bestbuy because Amazon was out of stock at the time.

This is a hair-pulling product that is not ready for prime time. It's an endless stream of frustration, malfunction and error messages. There is nothing exotic about my tv and av system and all components are in the Logitech data base. However, in actual practice, the system simply could not set up sequences of commands that would operate the devices successfully. The individual device controls worked well but when programming an activity (sequence of commands to multiple devices), the Harmony just couldn't set everything correctly.

Also, the Logitech server was unreliable and was down all day, preventing any setup activities. I don't think I'll ever be more tired of endlessly typing in my user id and password on my little smartphone screen than I was with this server.

Last, but most important, I purchased the Harmony to work with my Echo system. I had to wait until Logitech restarted their server to enable the Alexa skills for the Harmony. Once I could set up the harmony with alexa, IT JUST DIDN"T WORK. The support information is very vague and the commands shown to work with alexa DON"T WORK. Echo just blinks and does nothing. The only thing it would do was turn the tv off and on, which is not worth the money and a whole weekend of frustration.

I know the hub was reliably sending control signals to my components because when I used the individual component remote control features, everything worked perfectly and my inputs worked. With my DVR, the Harmony actually worked better than the components' included hand remote. Alas, though, sequences didn't work reliably. What that means for me was that with the Harmony Hub, I had to add my smart phone to my pile of remotes to do things that, at least with the remotes, can be done without drama or guesswork.

I returned this product. If it actually functioned as the hype claims, it would be great, but at this point I'd rather go back to my big pile of remote controls, which at least work reliably and don't require hours of fruitless software manipulation. I really wanted to like the Harmony, but it wouldn't let me.

text:
I own several of these as I am a Nerd. The best price for these is on Amazon, as WalMart wants $40 plus tax and Target wants more than that.
If you have never tried a track ball, then you are likely not a Nerd and you are missing out on the benefits of not having to wave your arm everywhere while using a computer. The track ball only takes a couple hours of use at most to be quickly and effortlessly using the mouse like a real-live-Nerd. Also, there are programs you can download for free that will allow you to customize the mouse buttons and additional options in many different ways. (I have not yet tried this, as I am not yet a 33rd degree Nerd...maybe in the future).
Also, the receiver with this mouse can be used with multiple other devices, freeing up USB ports and also USB plugs! Logitech provides instructions for pairing up various devices to the Logitech Unifying Receiver that comes with this mouse.
In all seriousness, no special tech ability is required to use a trackball mouse like this. It saves you wrists, and makes it easy to work in any position, in any area. When I get tired I wind up in a recliner, sometimes with a machine projecting to the big screen TV in the living room, with me 20' away and asleep in my recliner with the track ball mouse still resting on my chest.

title: Great remote, however, requires Internet access to program
text:
I've always been a fan of the Harmony series of remotes. They are generally easy to program and their database of hardware it has the frequencies to is insanely large. But I can't give it 5-stars for the one serious flaw they likely won't fix, in that you have to have an internet connection to program them.

From a product management standpoint, they should allow an offline option where the list of devices can be downloaded to your local machine so that if you're internet goes down you can still program your remote. Requiring users to connect to their online service in order to do anything to the remote is a pain and a waste of bandwidth for making small changes such as button mappings and things like that.

We had our last Harmony for over 6 years, before going without for a couple years. After getting this, I forgot how nice it was. Highly recommend this remote even with that product flaw.

title: Wish It Worked as Intended
text:
We've had this remote for a couple months now and although I've tried in every way to make it fit with our needs, this is a very half-hearted attempt at a next generation remote device. We are tech savvy and are not super critical understanding that everything new usually needs patience and some improvements. Our hobby is home automation but still 90% of the time we're using this thing with just the TV/Netflix/AppleTV/Prime. We've had Harmony remotes of the past which I've loved but none that used my smart phone.

Notice how I put 'We' in this review. This product really flat out sucks when pairing it with multiple smart phones.

Devices:
- RCA Tv 4k 70"
- AppleTv
- Amazon FireStick
- Hue Lights
- August Lock
- Amazon Echo
- Nest
- IFTTT

Our Smart Phones:
- iPhone 5s
- iPhone 6s

The Good:
- Easily sets up with basic all remote devices.
- The remote feels great.
- The remote is about twice as fast as your typical Comcast remote so you can actually flip through channels.
- The app is powerful enough to offer many more features with IFTTT
- The app has a cool 'favorites' option which allows you to program in your favorite TV channels and associate the correct icon. Super nice touch.

The Bad:
- App frequently loses connection (even with a dedicated Wi-Fi no further than 15 ft away)
- When the app loses connection the remote is useless.
- There's no display on the remote to know what activity it may be set to. Not a big deal if you have your phone, but a problem for the next person that enters the room.
- Devices turn on only about 50% but its better at turning them off at about 75% of the time (and yes the IR blaster is right in front of the devices)
- Takes forever to program activities especially if you want the remote to have customized buttons. Seems good about the basics though i.e. volume and channel
- When using the programmed Activities (which is the common way to use the remote) it may take up to a minute to begin the activity. (again I've suspected Wi-Fi connection the whole time but at this point I've given up on this notion.)
- Multiple phones cause problems. It seems to only work fine with a single device and prompts us to re-connect the other device. If we do that, the previous device no longer works. Over and over again.

Conclusion:
The amount of time spent 'maintaining' the remote makes it worthless. Constantly messing with the app, the hub connection, the app waiting to connect, the app losing connection, that in the end it seriously makes this thing almost useless. Its sad because if it worked as advertised and intended, this thing would be awesome.

Save your money. Buy a basket for all your remotes and set it on your coffee table. The only remote it actually does better than out of all our other remotes, is the clunky Comcast remote.

text:
As someone that is particular about the keyboards he will use, this one provides a great experience. For me the most important aspects are the general shape of the keyboard and the feeling when pressing a key. I type without looking, so I like when I can feel that the key has been pressed, and I also like the spacing to be just right so that I don't hit the wrong keys.
For reference, I also use a Logitech K120 and a Unicomp Spacesaver M. The circle shape of the keys looks weird at first, but I find them natural to use and even comfortable.
On the topic of connectivity, I enjoy having three different connections accessible with the press of a button. I have already set one for a tablet and the other one for my main computer, I might set the third one for my smartphone. Configuration itself isn't hard, but depends mostly on the device you are connecting to than on the keyboard. For me in both cases I had to activate the keyboard, set it to broadcast a bluetooth beacon by pressing the corresponding button (F1 to F3), activate it on my device, which would then show a pin for me to type on the keyboard. After that the keyboard was ready to use, but I did change the keyboard configuration on the Android for something that fits my tastes better. This part is more of a personal matter.
All in all, it works well and I'm happy with it.

title: No longer the company they were. Logitech has abandoned the concept of customer support.
text:
Update: The worthless thumb button got worse. It collapsed one day under the apparently prodigious weight of my right thumb, and took the rest of the mouse with it. Support took literally 3 months, after having me dig up photos of receipts, to tell me that they didn't even want to inspect the mouse because I bought it over a year ago. Drink that in. Logitech now expects you to pay 70$ per year for mice. If it fails 4 months past the "warranty," You're SOL.

Did I buy a mouse or a WoW subscription? I am NOT buying a new high end mouse every year. I could understand if this were a crappy little travel mouse. But a flagship mouse? One year? No. I'm not spending 80$ a year on mice. For that money I could have a high end gaming mouse with a lifetime warranty or 10 cheap mice to use in sequence over the next 20 years.

I'm sure I can recover some of my money selling it for parts since it's only the thumb button that failed and the battery alone is worth something. But this is shameful and I'm honestly sad to have been failed like this. I sung Logitech's praises for over a decade. I remember as a child being excited when I got my first high end Logitech for playing Total Annihilation with. It was corded, and used a ball. That's the loyalty they've squandered and betrayed.

Update: Battery life has dropped a little. I'd say it needs a charge every 9 days or so now. But I'm a very heavy user. YMWV. Still love the mouse. It's a definite step up from the previous MX.

Side scrolling wheel is neato but I actually don't use it much. Maybe because it's kind of hard to spin, like dipped in honey.

Back and forward buttons work perfectly and feel better than they look. Ignore reviewers complaining about them.

It'll last 15 days of all day use between charges.

The issue that makes this mouse 4 stars is that it's not actually bluetooth. It's actually BLE or "Bluetooth low energy" which saves power apparently but also isn't compatible with things that can't support this variant specification.

My android 4.2.2 phone can't support it. That upset me as no where on the device is this made clear. The mouse should support both specifications. Oh well. It's still an excellent mouse and I'll have it for years hopefully. (Nope.)

text: I'm a huge Logitech fan--I trust the brand (recommended by my PC repair people)--and this keyboard is up to the company standards.  In fact, it's a more solid typing surface and feels better than my full-sized (with number pad) USB keyboard (also Logitech). I have to take my Kindle Fire tablet out of its silicon case to get it in the groove, and my phone (Droid Mini) doesn't have a case; the groove holds both tightly without cases.  The only problem I've had with the keyboard is that, while it came in a nice box (like all Logitech products), it came with no instructions except a picture strip above the command keys.  I had to figure out how to turn it on by trial and error, but there is a good video on the Logitech site.  Some reviewers have mentioned the noise the keys make, but it's no worse than any keyboard (remember, you're not typing on a touch screen, and that's the whole point of an outboard keyboard). title: Fun, Useful and Easy to Set Up
text:
I was looking for a keyboard for occasional use with my Samsung Galaxy Tab. I read dozens of reviews for several products and everyone was saying the same thing-the keyboards were OK, nothing to rave about. I did not want a cover with a keyboard, it is for occasional use with my tablet in place of my laptop.

I stumbled on one reviewer who mentioned that, although the keyboard he was reviewing was perfectly acceptable, he kept going back to his Logitech K480. So I took a look at this one.

This is a handy add-on. It accommodates 3 devices-I have it set for my Samsung tablet, my Samsung phone and my Samsung Smart TV. There is a dial in the upper left corner so you can switch between the 3 devices on the fly. Linking the devices was very easy. My tablet and my phone can sit in the slot at the same time if that is what I want. The keyboard itself is easily the size of a regular laptop keyboard so it is not small, measuring in at 11-3/4" x 5-3/4". Yet if I did want to take it traveling it is light and still fits nicely into my tote bag along with my tablet and my Kindle and anything else I am carrying. But it is especially handy for home and at the office.

One reviewer mentioned that the keys are "clickety" and noisy and I agree with that. If you are using it in a quiet environment like a dead-silent cube farm or on an airplane this would be very annoying. None the less, I like it very much. It is quick to set up and the keys are large with spaces between them so typing is easy. The slot to hold the tablet and the phone simultaneously is slick. I give it 4.5 stars with the mark down for the clickety keyboard noise.

title: Great compact combo track pad/keyboard device. Good for HTPC.
text:
This works great with my home theater PC/gaming rig running Windows 10 Pro 64 bit. I also have a wired keyboard and mouse plugged in and running along side this and they do not interfere with each other. Installation was easy; plug and play. I downloaded the configuration software from Logitech's site to turn off track pad tap-to-click gestures. The software for this new version has lots of options.

If you want to sit on your couch or in bed and use your computer from a distance, like if you have a large TV or projector, this is the best wireless keyboard/mouse out there.

PROS: Easy setup, ample configuration options, LONG battery life (apparently 1 year), track pad supports gesturing (pinch to zoom, tap-to-click, etc.) and long range (I use mine about 20 feet away and its behind a curtain).

CONS: slightly too small for average hands with the track pad crammed into this device. I found it hard to get used to using on my lap, but I DID get used to it. Only other con is that every now and then the cursor will jump across the screen, probably from signal interference. But this is so seldom that its hardly worth mentioning and definitely not worth taking a star off.

title: they are also programmable which is a nice feature if you have a use for them
text: I got this mouse as a replacement for the MX-518 corded gaming mouse. It is similar in shape and features but I prefer this one. As for differences, this one lacks the two buttons above and below the wheel for adjusting the DPI on the fly which isn't a big deal to me as it wasn't really required. This mouse also adds two buttons to the wheel by tilting it left and right which the other didn't have, they are also programmable which is a nice feature if you have a use for them. The two programmable thumb buttons are also more proud on this mouse and have a longer throw and more distinct sound and feel than the MX-518. The power switch on the bottom is easy to use and as I use the computer extensively it will be interesting to see how long the two AA batteries (surprisingly included) last. Internal storage of the USB fob is nice but I'll only use it when traveling. Overall, it has a great shape and solid feel. Many mice case my hand to have cramps but this one is extremely comfortable and I prefer it over the MX-518. There are several software drivers that you can download from Logitech but you only need the LogiOptions one to configure the mouse and buttons. There is a smooth scrolling option but I prefer to turn it off as it scrolls the screen but then "coasts" to a stop after you stop using the wheel and I like it to stop when I actually stop. I'm very pleased with this mouse and regret not having converted to it sooner. Only time will tell how long the battery situation vs. corded mouse will play out.

text: I did an absurd amount of research before buying this item, and I'm glad I did. For me, it's not about value, so much as the fact that I might be spending 5,000 hours typing on this device. I don't think there's any such thing as the perfect iPad cover/keyboard. Nobody wants a lot of bulk, but everybody wants a lot of functionality—and a lot of protection. Also, anything less than a 5-star Amazon review? Well, people see that as a put-down, or reflecting serious reservations about the product. So far as I can tell, a fully functional iPad cover/keyboard, made of Mac-grade materials and of similar build quality, would cost about $150-$200. This Logitech item is not that cover/keyboard. However, it works great. I've had no disconnect issues. Yes, it permits only one stand-angle, but that's well chosen. If you type a lot, and if you really don't love doing that on a touchscreen, then this is an excellent choice. Please note: If you drop your iPad on concrete, with this as the sole protection, your iPad will break. That's true of virtually all these cover/keyboards. When I travel, I carry mine in a sleeve. Btw I also bought mine on Amazon Warehouse, which I recommend when purchasing tech on Amazon. Many people return tech for no grave reason. Headphones, Mac devices—a lot of these get opened, tried, and returned. Price—as in this case—can be half "Amazon retail."

title: If you thought the MX Revolution was the last great mouse, this review is for you
text:
Oh man did I want to write a 5 star review here, alass 4 star it will have to be for one things and one thing only.

THE ONE AND ONLY THING BAD ABOUT THIS MOUSE:
The thumb back button on the mouse is far too towards your body causing a pause while you bend your thumb to reach it. Even once you reach it its so small its entirely possible to him the button above it by mistake. I will post back in a few weeks to tell you if this gets any easier as I use it every day.

PAST LOGITECH MX HISTORY
I discovered the MX line with the "Revolution". Honestly the Revolution is still the best mouse every made. It was the first model to have the scroll fly wheel and was modeled perfectly for at least my hands. Its upsets me to no end that it's taken so many new models to finally bring back the thumb wheel (which I use for volume control) and the spirit of the Revolution.

THE GREAT THINGS ABOUT THIS MOUSE THAT MADE ME SWITCH FROM THE MX REVOLUTION:
-Its solid, great feel in the hand.
-Great feel, the clicks just feel right
-Its functional, finally another mouse that I can control the volume from with my thumb for quick mute and volume adjustment. The software is also great, total control over how you would like this mouse interact with the OS
-Better fly wheel, its pretty awesome. I can feel the improvement over the revolution.
-Works with my desktop and my notebook without having to carry around a dongle (thanks to bluetooth and multi-profiles)

FINAL THOUGHTS
The MX Revolution is still my favorite, in fact if it wasn't for the eco-unfriendliness of the idea I would dig a hole in the back yard and give it a proper burial. However, in all 4 of my MX-R's the battery is a day and a half at best, the precision of the tracking is starting to go, and SetPoint (the older software) is barely working on my PC. These reasons plus a damn good attempt at proper design of the Master has made me switch. The few things I wish Logitech would do for a future mouse are as follows:
- Move the back button and thumb scroll further away so the thumb doesn't have to bend to hit it
- Give us back a charging Dock (how about wireless charging)

Great job Logitech, I really didn't think you had the ability to design things anymore. Whoever lead this project's design needs to be promoted.

title: Fantastic portable keyboard, but fabric gets very loose over time
text:
Oh, how I long to give this keyboard five stars! It's by far my favorite portable keyboard I've ever used. I use this version with my iPad, and the combination has virtually replaced my laptop. It's super light, extremely thin, and easy to toss into my iPad carrying case. I try to always have it with me.

I type pretty fast generally - over 130 wpm, with bursts up to 150 - and at first I was a bit worried that the small nature of this keyboard would make it harder to type accurately. But those fears were unfounded; this keyboard keeps up every time. In fact, I have come to really like the slightly condensed style of the keyboard. The keys seem to be full-sized, just spaced a little closer together than most other keyboards. It's come to the point where I much prefer this closer style; when I went to check out Apple's new Smart Cover with built in keyboard (for a potential iPad Pro purchase), I was honestly taken aback at how widely-spaced those keys were! I had gotten used to the form factor of my Keys to Go, and going back to a full sized keyboard meant that my fingers were suddenly flying all around the keyboard to keep the speed up -- it was actually more tiring.

I have used the Keys to Go to take notes at work, to write articles and emails, and really to do everything you would use a keyboard for. I've typed at least tens of thousands of words on it, probably over 100,000 words. The only time I felt VERY slightly cramped was when I had to transcribe somebody talking for several hours... At that point I wished for a slightly bigger keyboard so that my fingers could spread out a bit. But other than multi-hour transcription sessions (which comprise an exceedingly small percentage of my keyboard use), this thing is great. I'm typing on it right now, of course. :)

Before I get to the one major flaw, I want to extol its praises a bit more. I'm a radio journalist so I often take notes while people are speaking into a very sensitive microphone. This keyboard is so whisper quiet, that even my incessant transcription has never interfered with the sound recording. A non-fabric based keyboard would make clicking noises and be unusable in a recording session. This one works just great.

OK, now for the single-star subtraction: The fabric used to cover the keys just isn't up to the task. The more you use the keyboard, the looser the material gets until eventually it is literally bunched up and lifting off the keyboard. I first noticed this with the space bar, which developed two big fabric budgets where my thumbs would hit the key. It was annoying, but it didn't affect usability in any way. But then as the months passed, I started noticing it with the other keys as well. Now my keyboard looks like tiny mountain range, with undulating peaks and canyons. Again, this doesn't affect usability at all -- I can still type just as fast, quietly and accurately as I could when it was pristine - but it's really annoying. Check out the attached pictures to see what I mean.

Maybe if you only plan to use this keyboard once in a while, the fabric wouldn't loosen and bunch up nearly as much. But when you use the keyboard for hours every day like I do, the fabric becomes loose within weeks, and the problem only gets worse over time. I'm going to contact Logitech to see if they can do anything about it or offer me a replacement. But if they say no, I'll probably still keep using this one, because even with that flaw, it's still my favorite keyboard ever. :) And if the fabric ever gets so loose as to become a hindrance, I would immediately go out and purchase another Keys to Go.

HIGHLY recommended!
