title: Beware of Poor Quality / Reduced Cost Manufacturers: But Logitech Honored Warranty
text:
--------------------------------------UPDATE (March 21, 2017)-------------------------------------
I have now received the replacement warranty keyboard. The warranty process was not difficult to initiate, though there were some hoops to jump through and it took a while. Logitech was pretty good about following up during the process as well. Kudos! The replacement keyboard appears to be of similar manufacturing quality as the previous one (see items 1, 2, & 6 from the original review below). It is clear to me that the original manufacturer of the this product for purchases made in 2014-2015 is likely not being used anymore, but I'll give this replacement keyboard a chance. Perhaps the last one was just a "dud."

In summary, I recommend this keyboard based on the design (look and feel is great), but caution any buyers that you may run into issues within several months. Again, I'll update this review in a few months to let the Amazon community know how this replacement keyboard is performing. If this keyboard ends up being fine after 6 months, I would say that my experience may have been an anomaly. However, if the same thing happens, then there may be a systematic problem. Stay tuned!

--------------------------------------UPDATE (March 9, 2017)-------------------------------------
As of March, 2017, the keys on the keyboard are now failing and require more pressure to push, resulting in many missed characters and more typos. I'm incredibly disappointed... Amazon has NOT responded to my original inquiry, but I contacted them today by phone and they were more helpful. They suggested that I contact the manufacturer and file a claim against the 3 year warranty.

Also, I now think that a more likely scenario than the product being counterfeit is that Logitech changed manufacturers or reduced costs in some way. Unfortunately, their cost reduction has resulted in a lousy product and tarnishes the Logitech brand name. I no longer blindly trust the Logitech brand with regard to quality. I will update this review once I know where Logitech stands in regard to customer service and honoring their warranty.

One last thing: The item in the Amazon photos is not identical to the product I received.

-------------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW (November, 2016)------------------------
I believe the product that was shipped to me was COUNTERFEIT and not actual Logitech. I have purchased this same keyboard made by Logitech for multiple computers and this one is different for several reasons, albeit it looks pretty close:
1. Keys are made of coarse plastic (not smooth)
2. Logo looks wrong
3. The mouse is already falling apart after a month
4. Keys don't press smoothly
5. Range is much poorer than previous ones I've owned
6. The paint on the keys is clearly poor quality

I have an open inquiry with Amazon regarding this item/seller. It is possible that Logitech decided to save money on costs and reduced quality, but the item doesn't feel right. Will update review accordingly.

Thanks!

title: What they DIDN'T TELL YOU will cause DAYS of frustration
text: There's been huge hype for this thing around the gaming circles I'm in, I don't see what's so great about this. Yes, it allows you to create profiles and assign keys and things, but none of that STICKS. I can create a profile, get all my keys set up, and the INSTANT I close out of the Logitech window the profiles are reset and I have to re-assign the keys again. So, what, Logitech can make it do everything but run in the freaking background? And what they DON'T tell you is that you have to sign up to the support section of Logitech to even run the thing, and they also don't let you register the product (to make the profiles stick, I guess) if you buy it from Amazon's website. Fan-freaking-tastic. Why did I buy this again? For that "ease of access"? Except this isn't easy at all, it's repetitive to keep dragging the macros back and forth, and the thumb stick doesn't work in way too many games, every one you use a keyboard for in fact. Steam's controller is way better, AND it works for just about every steam game out there, AND you can assign it buttons just like this, AND it's cheaper, AND it's wireless, AND it can still work with the mouse. The only thing Logitech has is the profiles that don't work. Sorry, Logitech, I'm NEVER buying another thing like this again, especially not from you. I'm only giving this two stars instead of one because the thing actually turns on and creates profiles.

title: REVISED REVIEW:  LOVE THIS KEYBOARD!!
text:
I received my K780 two days ago from Logitech (purchased, not given to me). First, this keyboard is heavy. On my kitchen scale my old solar powered K750 weighs 750g (I have extra rubber feet glued on, so a bit heavier than spec). The new K780 weighs 870g. The angle and size of the slot for holding a phone or tablet is perfect. If I could get the keyboard to actually handshake with my iPhone 6 plus, I might like it. The keyboard easily connected with my Nexus 7 (2013), and my Windows 10 tower. It has a bit of trouble with the 2012 (Sierra) Mac Mini. It first recognized it as a K760 (maybe it sees the K750), but after turning the Bluetooth off, then on, the K780 popped up and was easily paired. Last device to try - the iPad Mini 4. I got the same error as with the iPhone. Logitech has a support page for the K780 which has instructions that are clearly not for this model keyboard - referring to a wheel, a blue flashing "i" key and an on/off switch on the bottom. None of those features are on these keyboard.

The keyboard is a bit mushy and I find the round keys to be odd. The delete key is moved up to the F-key row. I think regular Mac users will find this awkward.

Bottom line - my experience with connecting to Windows 10, Mac OS and Android all went smoothly. My two IOS devices (10.0.2) never did connect. I'm sticking with this keyboard for a while to see if I like having one keyboard to switch between the Mac and Windows desktops. My idea of having my iPhone in the mix is not happening. No doubt Logitech will fix it at some point, or at least change their support page instructions.

UPDATE. I had another go at pairing the iPhone with the K780. I turned off Bluetooth on the phone, turned the keyboard off entirely using the switch on the right side. Then turn the keyboard back on and the iPhone bluetooth. From there it used the typical pairing scenario. Note, this extra process was not needed for the other devices.

UPDATE #2. Changing my review to 5 stars. Other than the goofy setup for IOS, I just Love this keyboard. I have a Windows desktop on one side of my desk, a Mac Mini on the other and set my iPad mini in the slot on the keyboard. Now I'm down to a single keyboard plus I have the iPad right in front of me for messaging without interrupting tasks on the Mac. Even if you just have a desktop and a smartphone - buy this keyboard!!

title: Thumb Buttons-  Not raised enough, and too close together.
text:
Short version, great software (at least for Mac, the M510 and the this mouse). But if you’re moving up from the M510, you may be disappointed with the button placement/feel of the MX. I am. I need the additional buttons, so I’ll keep it, but I definitely like the button ‘feel’, of the 510, much better.

Guess my tactile feel is fading, but for me, compared to the M510, these buttons (Thumb Fwd/Back) are too close, and not raised enough, so I'm never sure just which one I've got. Someone else mentioned that, and I agree!

Update- Initially I couldn’t program any button for ‘Escape’. It took Logitech a week to respond, but when they did, the recommendation was to uninstall/reinstall the Logitech software (Mac). I initially thought "ugh-lot of work". Wrong- I was pleasantly surprised how easy this was. Logitech’s software includes an "uninstaller", so the whole ‘reinstall’ job was done in less than 5 minutes (3 of them were for the 2 restarts needed :) The only downside was having to reprogram the buttons. But true to their recommend fix, I can now program a button for 'Escape'

So in fairness, I’ll reemphasize a “PRO” here - Logitech’s software package is excellent, at least for the Mac (ElCap). From the M510, to adding the Perf MX, all I had to do was turn off the M510, turn on the PerfMx, program the Mx buttons- and job done. Nice. That, and making the config reinstallation so easy, is as close to ‘Plug n Play, as you can get.

Summary- If you like the M510, but want more buttons, try this one, but be sure to check it out throughly before Amazon’s return policy expires. Maybe you’ll ‘get use to’ the MX button feel. If I do, I’ll gladly bump this up to 4 or 5 stars,

title: Pleased, but with room for improvement...
text: A vast improvement over the built in speakers in my flat screen TV!  The satellite speakers are equipped with both mid-range speakers and actual tweeters, which makes voices on the TV far more intelligible.  The clarity of sound is impressive, especially for a speaker system in this price bracket.  The sub-woofer provides plenty of base, which is fully adjustable.  The depth of sound is incredible.  The flat screen is connected to both a PC and a satellite box.  The speakers are connected through the PC.  My only criticisms are these.  The speaker system has it's own on/off switch and volume control on the right front speaker.  It would be so much nicer if there were a remote control for those purposes.  While the source is the PC, playing a DVD or Netflix/Amazon Prime through the browser, the remote for the PC sound can be used to adjust the volume of the speakers.  But if the program source is switched to the satellite box then there is no remote that will adjust the sound volume.  With either program source the speakers must be turned off using the switch on the right front speaker.  It would be so much more convenient, and worth a higher price, if the on/off and volume of the speakers themselves could be controlled independently from the program sources with a remote.  But, overall, I am quite pleased with the quality of these speakers.

title: Very nice case and keyboard, but the keyboard layout is not standard (the A key and caps lock key share the same spot)
text:
This is a Bluetooth keyboard test to see how this keyboard works. ( I wrote most of this using the actual keyboard for ipad and the edits were made on my laptop!) The only qualm I have with it is that they keys seem to be moved in a different orientation than normal to accommodate the iPad and keyboard in a flush fashion (to keep the dimension of the keyboard and the iPad the same). Other than that it seems to be operational. However, because of the strange orientation, it will take some getting used to for people who are accustomed to the traditional layout of keyboards (especially those using full size keyboards). The magnet located on the keyboard top is a nice touch to ensure that the iPad does not move, as it locks the iPad into place when using the keyboard. It seems relatively strong to ensure the iPad remains in place. It also adds a nice close function to the keyboard case. When closing the iPad, the iPad turns off, and the aforementioned magnet ensures the iPad stays closed against the keyboard when not in use. This is a very nice perk. When opening the iPad back up, there was no reconnection period where the bluetooth turned off and I had to reconnect, which is a huge plus considered similar units do not have that feature. All in all, albeit the strange layout of the combination of the "a" key and caps lock key to save space, I feel this keyboard is invaluable to any ipad air user as the virtual keyboards are extremely frustrating to use because of their slow speed and clumsiness. title: Great lapdesk that works!
text: I already had the older "spartan" model of this Lapdesk (Logitech N315) for my household personal laptop...and we love it. There's merchants that are trying to sell the old N315 lapdesk tray for $189 ( that's 6x the originally MSRP of $29.99). However, since Logitech is no longer selling the N315 I decided try out the N600. The N600 is a smart lapdesk that comes with an integrated wireless touchpad. A nice bonus for people that have laptops with terrible touchpads (Like the Lenovo U430 Touch Ideapad). Additionally, I was pleased to learn that the N600 lapdesk is reversible.  Just flip the lapdesk over and you can use your own mouse on the bottom of the pull-out touchpad. Nice! The only issue i had was the batteries that are included with the N600 had exploded inside the battery cover. So I had to remove them and clean up all of the dried batter acid from the battery cover.  I installed four new AAA batteries and I was back in business. Everything works perfectly with the new touchpad. No special software or drivers needed to be installed to use the touchpad on either of my Windows 7 Pro and Windows 10 Home Lenovo laptops. The colors of this lapdesk aren't too manly (black bottom, white top, and purple touchpad\mouse pad). The N600 is about 2 Inches wider and twice as thick as the older model it replaced(N315). These changes in the new model make sense because most new laptops are wider and more space was needed to house the touchpad\batteries. Overall this was a great deal for under $20.

title: Of all "portable" keyboards for the iPad, this is the best I've found.
text:
Amazing keyboard.

I agree with other reviewers in these negatives:
(1) I wish the keys were angled (kind of like a staircase from the space bar up to the numbers)
(2) the kill switch is just above the delete key, causing me to turn off the iPad involuntarily (though pushing the same key turned it right back on!)
(3) I kind of wish it had back-lighting, but then that would drain the power out of my iPad too fast, so this is not a big negative at all.
(4) I kind of wish the cord came out of the top right corner, instead of 3-4 inches from the right corner, because as it is, I have trouble pushing the keyboard right up flush against my iPad (but this is not a big inconvenience).
(5) It would be neat to have a flip-down stand on each back corner so the keyboard would slant up. (BUT I typically use this on my lap, since that's where I usually use my iPad when I'm away from my computer, so this is not a big inconvenience, either.)

I give it a strong four stars because:
(1) I never need to charge it (it gets its charge from the iPad)
(2) A key did come off when hitting other things in my backpack, BUT UNLIKE MY OTHER TWO PORTABLE KEYBOARDS, the key went right back on, and was completely back to normal. (Those other two keyboards were permanently damaged -- one the first day, the other the first week.) In fact, I pried off another key to show my wife, and it snapped back on completely.
(3) It is totally portable, and RESISTANT TO DAMAGE.
(4) It has all the keys laid out where they should be (and not pushed this way or that happens with other "portable" keyboards' needs to be folded).

IF YOU'RE LOOKING FOR A PORTABLE KEYBOARD TO GO WITH YOUR IPAD, THIS IS IT. I'M HAPPIER WITH THIS THAN ALL THE ONES I'VE HAD SO FAR. I WISH I COULD GIVE THIS 4½ STARS!

title: Way overrated...
text:
This mouse does seem to live up to most of what people are saying—though it seems this is one of those products people get hyped about and write a review for after 5 seconds of use, so I wanted to contribute something I DIDNT get to read when i was researching the mouse.

First of all, its bulky and pretty much forces you to cup it with you entire hand. I'm 5'11 and my hands aren't small... I've used a Razor Deathadder for years and love everything about that mouse, except the crappy construction that almost guarantees it will be double clicking within a year.

The size/ergonomics is definitely a subjective complaint, but people seemed to rave about them even in comparison to other slim mice, which is confusing to me after having used it. If you're used to a fingertip grip, high DPI with minimal wrist movement... you'll hate this. The feel of the mouse moving on the screen feels "rubbery". Not sure how else to describe it. Just less accurate and quick than the death adder. I think you're paying a premium for their branding and that crazy promo they made about this mouse.

I noticed when i barely tapped the side scroll wheel, the primary scroll wheel stops responding (for a while). This seemed to happen more and more often as I used it. I researched it and apparently its a problem with like .... a LOT of people, and its still unresolved. Based on the forum post I read, which was 9 pages long and multiple years worth of posts, it seems like it may be more than just a driver update. I returned the one i ordered and bought something else.

text:

I'm not using it for a cord cutting computer in my living room. I tried building a cord cutting computer last year and used a different Logitech keyboard, I think this one would be an even better fit for that usage. However, my experience with cord cutting computers is they really want to work with a universal remote and limit keyboard usage to necessary things like web browsing or google docs. So, even if I used this for a living room computer it would be my secondary input.

I was concerned about touchpad. My experiences with touchpads on a laptop have been less than stellar. However, I think positioning it off to the side prevents most of the accidental repositioning of your text cursor that so confounds laptop keyboard/touchpads combos.

At the same time, the Logitech Type+ is stylish and functional. The built-in keyboard is easy to use, and it turns my iPad into something approaching a regular laptop. Unlike a soft envelope case, I don't have to unzip and remove to start using the tablet; instead, I flip open the cover and start to work. In all, this case is more than worth the price

title: great mouse! infrequent problems lead to painless RMA
text:
this is my favorite mouse I've ever owned. but it breaks about once a year.

it takes two AA batteries and that should last a few months at a time after constant use. I change the batteries infrequently enough that I don't really notice it. because of the two batteries, it adds quite a bit of weight to the mouse, which I really like.

the toggle-able scroll wheel is really nice for scrolling long distance on web pages or when gaming. if I find myself waiting around for a meeting or something, I'll toggle to free-scroll mode and just spin the wheel. it's a neat feature. it does take some time to get used to not clicking the wheel for middle click but that's an easy habit to break, and having the middle click on its own button prevents you from accidentally scrolling when you click. I LOVE the side buttons for forward/back.

on the mouse breaking:

I'm now on my third or fourth mouse since my original purchase in June 2014 (it's now April 2016). eventually they always fall to one of these problems:

1. the left click actuator desensitizes and starts double-clicking or not clicking at all
2. the power frequently turns off for no good reason

both of these issues are terribly frustrating. the homebrew fix for #1 involves disassembling and soldering components, and #2 can be remedied by a little piece of index card under the power switch.

HOWEVER, Logitech is really fantastic about replacing the mouse when this happens. each time it breaks, I've filed an RMA and received a brand new mouse within a few days. Logitech does not require you to send the original back to them (I guess they're aware of the problems) and the whole process is very hassle-free. because I like the weight and feel of this mouse so much, for me it's worth it to deal with the issues for < 1 week and come out with a brand new (and clean!) device. YMMV depending on what you're doing with your mouse.

I've complained to Logitech that if they would just get better quality internals they probably would do less RMAs, but I assume that most people probably would buy a new one rather than go through the RMA process. honestly, it's painless.

my last advice is to record your serial number ASAP when you get the mouse (you should probably do this with any hardware you buy!). in my original purchase, one of the batteries leaked a bit and of course it ruined the sticker with the serial number listed on it. fortunately I recorded the SN info so I was able to get an RMA no problem.

I'm not really fond of the placement and rearrangement of the thumb control buttons and I find the use of the top one mildly difficult to get used to and more difficult to 'feel' with my thumb and large hands.
Personally I can't seem to use the 'gestures' button effectively and I reprogram it to other things. The 'SmartShift' setting on the main scroll wheel requires me to change my attention from my work to how the scroll wheel is activated and stopped, so I'm not a fan of that and turn off that function. I'm quite content to change it's function with the traditional mode change button.
My older Performance MX was requiring much more frequent charging even with new Ni-MH batteries so I went with the MX Master which has a longer charging cycle but I've been disappointed that it's nowhere near what is advertised, though I admit to extremely heavy usage. It's still a solid performer and I hope the switches last longer than it's predecessor's which I've taken apart and repaired a few times.

title: Competent but for the premium price lacking premium functionality
text:
Okay, semi expert here. This is my fourth Harmony universal remote in about ten years. Perhaps that leads to conclusions about issues of longevity? I'm a little torn on that. Yes, they do get daily work, but a little more in the build quality, especially for the steep price, seems warranted. Battery life on the previous models was also not good - I am talking about rechargeable models.

Sadly, nobody makes as usable as a remote as Logitech/Harmony. If I am wrong please tell me in the comments - I am willing to switch!

While easy to use, easy to set up is not the same thing. If you are tech savvy, it is not too difficult and the biggest challenge is first, getting all your correct model numbers for all your gear, second, knowing enough about how you have all this set up in terms of both audio and video inputs and outputs. Advice, write it down and keep it on file. That is a fair amount of work and takes some knowledge. Unlike my last model, the default button setup for this and my different devices was a bit off. I had to "customize" button settings for my cable box (FIOS) to properly use the Favorites guide and a few other things including On Demand - that's right, no default button set up for On Demand. In actual use my wife was able to start using it right away, but there are some quibbles here and there on having this be the only remote we need. Back to cable, but some often used functions, like search, are more cumbersome with this than the FIOS remote. We can live with it and let that stay in a drawer, but again, for $250 I think we can all demand a bit more thoughtfulness and user testing. Not to be AV elitist, but I don't think your average person with an average set up is going to shell out $250 for a remote. We want ease of use, but also versatility. title: This mouse has 6 months to live
text:
I really wanted to love this mouse, and I did...at first. It feels great in the hand and the button feels great. Probably my favorite feature is the free-spinning scroll wheel. You can scroll through an enormously long site in a second.

After a few months the problems began -- and here they are:

1. Battery Life & Charging - The first few months of use gave me many hours of consistent use without the need for a recharge but after that time I had to keep the mouse plugged in via USB at all times. I could unplug it for a few minutes but then the battery light would go red. I switched out the battery with a new rechargeable one and got the same result. I finally just resolved to keep the mouse plugged in permanently so I lost the mouse's wireless capability.

2. Jumpy - The pointer on the screen would jump from point A to point Z while skipping points B through Y. This was incredibly aggravating. I thought it was the surface so I switched the one I had with a different, brand new mouse pad (no glossy finish). Same result. Looked it up online and apparently this is a pretty common problem with this mouse.

3. Logitech Customer Support - I contacted Logitech customer support and had no luck getting them to replace or repair the mouse. I buy lots of Logitech devices including mice, keyboards, speakers and web cams. I only mention this because that can sometimes be used to sway a customer support rep in your favor. No luck. This was not the first problem I had with Logitech customer support nor was it the last. Had a problem with an $80 illuminated keyboard -- wouldn't help me.

Just know this mouse may only last you 6 months. If you're OK with that, go for it.

title: Dirty keyboard that's impossible to get clean...unless you compromise some keys!
text:
Back lighting is awesome and I will never go back to a keyboard without it. The feel of the keys is also good as they press down enough to get a feeling of satisfaction (like the one you get with a mechanical keyboard), but without excessive noise.

5 stars means the product is flawless, which this keyboard is not. There are two things which hurt this review:

1. The keyboard gets extremely dirty even if you have a "no food or drink at the keyboard" rule - which is unwritten because I'm the only one that uses this particular KB - and you clean it with rubbing alcohol like an OCD meth addict, but with extreme care.

2. Because it gets super dirty super easily, you want to clean it, especially beneath the keys. I was cleaning it, very carefully, with some Q-tips and a key popped off and the cheap, plastic mount broke. I spoke to Logitech and they were less than helpful. I was happy to pay for a new key mount but they still wouldn't help. I had to go on eBay and trying to reinstall this thing is like putting together an Ikea bedroom set. This is apparently such a big issue that a guy on eBay makes good money selling individual key mounts and posts long YouTube instructional videos.

Point is, Logitech has poor customer service. Logitech should have spare parts for a keyboard with a widespread issue. They should ship them to customers for a low price. You pay $60 - $90 for a keyboard, you'd expect better service.

If you don't mind a dirty keyboard or at least one missing key, you're in luck!

title: Harmony Home Control > Universal Remote
text:
The first day I had this, I didn't like it. I was upgrading from a dying Harmony 350, and thought this might be along the same lines. This is much more/different compared to standard universal remotes, even lower tier Harmony remotes. Be warned that there is a steep learning curve to using this remote. However, once you figure it out, it's amazing! I've only had it a couple months, and I can't imagine giving it up.

So, by the second day, I had a better understanding of how it worked, how to program it, and how to tweak the programming. Unlike a typical universal remote, you aren't pressing a device button and then having the remote control that device. You press or long press a button along the top, the hub goes through a sequence (turn on TV, change source of TV, turn on soundbar, etc.). Once the sequence is done, your remote controls the main device. So, if I press the button for Watch TV, it now controls the cable box for channels and the soundbar for audio.

Pros:
- You can point the remote anywhere or nowhere. The hub blasts out the signals needed, so no need to point the remote at the device you are controlling, or anywhere at all.
- Remote feels great in my hand and buttons are arranged well.
- Your phone and/or tablet can be used as an expanded remote and allows access to even more sequences and controls. It also allows for easy reprogramming of the whole system.
- It can do bluetooth as well as IR, so it controls a multitude of things. I have it controlling my TV, soundbar, cable box, PS4, Wii U, Nexus Player, Amazon Fire TV Stick, and an HDMI switcher. There is a web site to search if a device is supported: https://support.myharmony.com/en-us/compatibility

Cons:
- It's limited to 8 devices. I thought that was a lot (and it is), but some might have more than that. I don't know why there is a limit, so that's why this isn't 5/5.
- That learning curve...
- Battery is CR2032. It comes with one and supposedly lasts a long time, but it's not likely you will have a spare lying around unless you plan ahead.

NOTE: I don't have any smart home items, like WiFi light bulbs, so I can't comment on how those work with this device...yet.

title: Wonky/iffy/maybe connectivity and bad mic design.
text:
I have had three of these sets over the last few years, but no more. All the headsets died due to the same problem - broken mic-wire in the mic-stem. The last set died at only 2 months old. I think moving the mic out of the way so it's up over my head causes the little fine wire to break. I've done an autopsy on all the dead sets, and that has been the case in all 3 of them. I actually repaired the wire in the last one so it's working again, but you KNOW it's gonna happen again! When they work, they sound great, but they suffer from one other major issue which I experienced constantly from all three sets.

The other problem is that their wireless connectivity is wonky/iffy/maybe - but usually they connect. By that I mean that sometimes it just plain wouldn't connect. None of my other wireless devices have had any connectivity issues, just this headset. I would have to pull the little USB dongle out and plug it back in... sometimes several times. Sometimes it would disconnect while in the middle of a conference-call, game, friend-chat etc. Then I'm scrambling to get it to reconnect. It's maddening. I've even taken to keeping a hard-wired headset at arms length just so I can get back into the conversation.

This headset can optionally use Bluetooth instead of the Logitech wireless - you select which to use with a switch on the side of the earphone, but it still demonstrated the same wonky connectivity issues under Bluetooth -AND- the sound quality under Bluetooth was so bad that it wasn't usable, so I always used the Logitech wireless mode. This connectivity problem was present on all three headsets, in the same manner, under all versions of Windows I use - Win 7 and Win 10, both 64-bit. You should expect the problem with all versions of Windows, because it's not a Windows problem, it's a Logitech problem!

If the wire doesn't break early, and you can tolerate the touchy connectivity issues, you should get about 12 to 18 months of full functionality out of it, otherwise I recommend you choose something else. It took me a while to learn my lesson.

title: Great fit, hyper-scroll, with poor switches
text:
I have owned two Logitech M705 mice for the last 4 years – one for each computer. I've rated this 3-stars because that is the average between 5-star and 1-star. Here's why I'd give it each:

5-stars: I love this mouse for two specific reasons: 1) hyper-scroll and 2) how comfortably it fits in my hand. Logitech does have other mice with their hyper-scroll wheel, but only this mouse fits my hand without cramping by the end of the day.

1-star: If you've ever Googled this mouse, you'll see that it fails from ghost left double-clicks (double clicking when you did a single-click). It also suffers from not holding the click – making drag-n-drop a real nightmare. Many people have resorted to opening the mouse, the switch, and performing various fixes. Over the past 4 years of owning these mice, I've taken them apart at least twice and have sprayed contact cleaner into the switch mechanism. It helps for about 3 months, then you have to repeat the process – which lasts half as long, etc.

I'm now at the point I don't feel my repair attempts will help this mouse an further. Logitech simply used cheap switches with a short click-life cycle (in my opinion). Before purchased two replacement mice, I did take a fresh look at the current mice available. They all have issues.

Yes, it may appear stupid of me to buy two new mice that I know will fail – but you will notice that I'm not complaining. I'm accepting responsibility for Logitech's poor quality because the fit and hyper-scroll are more valuable to me. If I get another 4-5 years out of them, they would have been years of comfort and happiness.

Would I love to Logitech to make a product with high-quality switches that would last 5-10 years? Yes! But my boycotting them isn't going to change their company, and I'm not really skilled at making my own mouse – so I'm kind of at their mercy.

As with all my reviews, I'll provide updates over time if the product degrades or fails earlier than I expect it to.

title: WARNING: Defective bulk product
text:
First, I am the owner of two Logitech M705 mice for each of my computers. I have owned both mice for about 4 years, and love the way this mouse fits my hand and the hyper-scroll feature.

About a year ago, each mouse began exhibiting the well documented issue of ghost double-left clicks, and the button not holding (drag-n-drop was impossible). Since each mouse was way beyond the warranty, I had nothing to loose by taking them apart. I used contact cleaner in the switching mechanism and this worked for several months. Then I'd have to repeat the process again a few months later. But then even that didn't work anymore, so it was time to replace each mouse.

After looking at the options available on Amazon, nothing compared, so I bit the bullet and purchased two new Logitech M705 mice. Even with their known problems, I figured if I got another couple of years out of them, I'd have comfortable hands, wrists, forearms along the way. This mouse is that comfortable for me (I have big hands - well, big enough to reach an octave on the piano). But my wife and kids like the mouse too - so it seems the form is adaptive to different hand sizes.

Unfortunately, both new mice had broken hyperscroll locks, which engages/releases the scroll wheel to alternate between hyperscroll and traditional (slower) scrolling. I immediately requested a replacement, and two new mice arrived two days later. They too had inoperable hyperscroll locks. So if 4 mice have the same identical problem, then there's something seriously wrong with this product lot. (It does make me curious, because these are "bulk" products and do not come in the retail packaging. Did someone buy a lot of defective/clone mice and are trying to pawn them off on Amazon?)

Currently, when you search Amazon, 3 options are available for this Logitech M705 mouse. Yes, they are all by Logitech. However, they each sell under a different model number. This review is for model number 810-002525. Amazon should remove this entire lot. I'm returning all 4 mice and am going to give Amazon one last try with a listing with model number 910-001935.

title: fundamental design flaw, although not so detectable by users less needing of precision
text:
Wow, I need to do a better job reading negative reviews before I purchase something as personally important as a mouse.

The mouse seems well constructed, pretty, etc. But it feels incredibly clumsy in actual use, as judged by where the pointer actually winds up on the screen. I couldn't figure out why. It's as though sometimes, it would only go about half as fast as it should in the vertical direction. But not other times. What gives? I turned it over.... And there's the problem. THE OPTICAL SENSOR IS ON THE SIDE, INSTEAD OF THE CENTER. What this means is that any yawing motion of the mouse will increase or decrease the speed of the y axis. Another way of saying it is that when you spin the mouse about it's center of gravity, when spinning to the left, the pointer will go upward, and when spinning to the right, it will go downward. And that will hugely impact left-handed vs. right-handed use. What an incredible bug in the design. Completely ruins its use for fast-paced video games, although is probably eventually overcome-able for office use with some practice.

-------
Addendum after writing the above: After researching, am astonished to see so many mice with the sensor located so far off center. I don't know when that became fashionable, since I don't buy mice all that often. It's a horrible idea. Whatever. Seems like Logitech gaming mice still keep the sensor in the middle, so will probably go with one of those.

title: Totally recommended, Awesome headset
text:
I was able to get this super cheap because it was on sale here on Amazon but I couldn't wait so I bought it at a store that matched internet prices, It's served me very well in the last 4 months, the surround sound sounds great in games, I don't really play competitive multiplayer so I can't speak to any advantages it might give you, but in Fallout 4 it helps with immersion. Sound quality is not something I really notice but for games it seems pretty darn good, music doesn't seem all that great but not terrible by any means and movies or tv shows (which I don't really watch anything that takes advantage of the surround sound) again seems ok although other than gaming I usually just use a sound bar I bought for my tv. Noise cancelling it pretty decent too, with my phone right next to me I can barely hear the ringer which is just enough so I don't miss calls but otherwise I'm pretty immersed in whats coming through the headset.

I heard a lot about the charging port on the headset breaking so I've just been careful and mindful whenever I'm plugging it in and haven't had any issues, breaking the charging port would be a major disappointment though so fingers crossed I never have this problem, the micro USB charging cable has a battery picture on one side so I always know I'm plugging it in the right way and never need to stress it by trying to plug it in backwards.

One issue I didn't realize is with your computer because this is a usb headset not one with the two auxiliary jacks you can only use your headset or speakers but not both at the same time, not a huge deal but if I wanted to use these while showing a game off to a friend they either have to watch a silent screen or I can't use the headset, not really a big deal though, audio switcher is a great program for switching which audio device you want to use on the fly by the way and I was able to hotkey the buttons on the headset to switch between my sound bar and my headset. Now even though I think it'd be nice to have audio play through my speakers and the headset while it's turned on, Having it be wireless usb is AWESOME! I can run to the bathroom during cut scenes or hear tv while washing the dishes, or get up for any reason without worrying about ripping out a cable, it more than makes up for this little issue which is in no way the fault of Logitech simply how computer audio works.

title: Great value if you pay $40 or less - average sound quality and mic
text:
I have had these headphones for a few years and the volume dial started acting up about a year ago, and the other day when the ear pads finally wore off, it was time to find new headphones. Since I liked these so much, I went looking for them on Amazon and decided to buy a USED pair for much less than the main listing. The original price of these headphones was probably around $30-$40, so I was not going to be paying twice that, no sir. THESE ARE NOT WORTH $80. Do some searching around for other sellers, seriously.

For the $15 I ended up spending this time, these headphones are great. I love that they are behind the head, and the ear pads are small and do not enclose the whole ear. I do some casual gaming, so the mic on these is great for me. If you're looking for high quality sound or mic, these aren't for you. The sound isn't tinny, it's just average. Nothing mind blowing here. The cord is 8 feet long, which I find to be a huge plus. I wrap the excess behind my keyboard when I'm at my desk so it's out of the way but it's also easy to get up and move around my desk area without having to take off the headphones or discontinue a conversation I'm having on Skype.

Overall, I love these headphones. They're perfect for me - casual use and no worry about needing high quality sound or mic. Very good value if you get them for $40 or less - the first pair lasted me years and I expect this one will too.

title: New Logitech Options software killed this mouse
text:
My Logitech G700s suddenly started giving me fits. The left button switch was acting up, not registering clicks is bad, not holding while you drag and drop is down right dangerous. Thats the 2nd G700s in a few years to have this problem. So I decided time to try something new, like the shiney new MXMaster that Logi is hawking. Logi, the new coke of Logitech, yeah that lasted what 2 weeks? Anyway, I got my new MXMaster home drooling in anticipation. Setup was fast, easy, almost too easy. Had to go download latest Setpoint ... wait, no ... Maybe the Gaming Software package from my G700s works ... nope. You get Logitech Options, a brand new logitech mouse support program because new and shiney is better, right. Eh, no ... just plain no.

Now, the side scroll is cool, I can't deny that. Can't way to get that function on a gaming mouse. The gesture button, meh, akward to use and usually does the wrong thing anyway, remapped it to F5. I must say, I spend way too much time on my computers. Many times I change hands to relieve hand cramps and such. While not great for lefties, the G700s is usable, the MXMaster is not. Its painful to even try using lefty, even for a few seconds. The scroll on my G700s already had the freewheel or clicky scroll function, the MXMaster takes it to the next level with a e-magnetic switch instead of simple click (I'm guessing). The ability to auto change from clicky to free wheeling when I scroll fast was interesting, sadly not enough to save this fail of a product. 2 extra buttons ( + Gestures! ) instead of 7-8 on the G700s really made me question why I paid more for this thing, let alone why I thought it was a good idea.

So, the real reason for this review. Speed. You see, I have a 4K monitor, love it. My G700s had great adjustments for DPI and mouse speed. When I first started up Logitech Options and made my tweaks I ended up maxing the pointer speed option, something that usually makes for a crazy impossible to control mouse. In fact, after a few minutes I was trying to speed it up more. It was taking 3 sweeps across my oversized mouse pad to traverse the screen. A few online searches quickly informed me that there was no way to make it faster, that was as good as it gets. After a few reads on Logitechs forum pages I knew it was a pointless search. The Logitech Options software was to blame and the new mouse will not be recognized by Setpoint or the gaming software package. Even the default windows options were of no help.

After 10 minutes, my hand hurt. It hurt much less as I returned the MXMaster to its packaging and set it aside for returning. I used my old malfunctioning mouse for the rest of the evening and was much happier ... thats just sad Logitech, you should be ashamed. But then again, this is from the guys who came up with Logi

Stopped by Amazon today to order a new G700s and leave this review ... if that tells you anything more about how I feel about the MXMaster

title: Great mouse, very good price for this quality
text:
Logitech Corded Mouse offers great value, awesome precision, at a very attractive price.

I am a retired gamer and I take my mouse precision very seriously. Let me just start by saying that if you are a serious gamer, look somewhere else! This mouse does not offer enough laser precision for FPS games. But I'm assuming the rest of the review for the office workers and infrequent light gamers.

Comfort - win! the shape of the mouse is very good for maintaining good grip and lessen tension in your hand. I generally like mice with a bit of depth to it that helps with the grip. The thumb area also offers rubber grip, which is awesome! This is small on paper, but really annoys me when other mouse do but pad grip area with rubber to add friction.

Precision - amazing precision at this price point. The precision is adjustable with software. Again, this is no gaming precision, but for regular day to day tasks, this precision level is perfect. I never quite feel that the pointer is not going to the spot that I had intended. In comparison, I tried to use a wireless mouse from Logitech (M510) and I cannot stand how imprecision that mouse is! I just had to deal with the fact that if I want good precision level without breaking my bank I should stick with wired mouse.

Buttons and scroll - you can customize what the buttons do and the scroll affects. They work very well. And the clicks feel comfortable, the feedback level is nice. You feel the actual click, and don't have to guess whether the click went through. And you basically never accidentally click with these buttons. For the scroll you can turn on infinite scroll, but I personally find that rather annoying.

Setup and software - just plug and play! I use a 15-inch retina macbook. Mouse worked perfectly the second I plugged it in. For the average user, I think this is pretty much all you need to do! I'm sort of a power user so I installed the logitech setpoint software to customize the buttons and the mouse acceleration. These software are intuitive and work like a charm.

Weight - the mouse is pretty light weight. This is a matter of personal preference. I actually think this mouse is a bit too light that it causes me to overshoot sometimes. But I think this came from the fact that I used to have a heavier mouse and I just need to adapt to a different weight. I think if you never used gaming mouse before, this weight is probably gonna be perfect for you.

Overall verdict - this is an amazing mouse at <$30. I'm definitely keeping this mouse for my day-to-day tasks. I recommend a buy.

title: Better than expected
text:
Logitech has made computer speakers for a long time, but they were never an audio company. They specialize in making computer peripherals. Since I have not heard a set of Logitech speakers in over 15 years, I was interested in seeing how far they have come.

The Z625 THX computer speaker system comes with 2 speakers and a huge subwoofer. The right speaker controlling the volume and bass has a very thick cable that attaches like old printers. The other speaker has its own dedicated wire, and both plug into the subwoofer. The subwoofer is plugged into the wall. Setup took seconds, and I plugged it into the computer.

I have to say, I was impressed. The sound, power, and the feeling of the bass surrounding the room was better than I imagined. Logitech has indeed come a long way in sound quality. I tried several games, movies, and songs on my PC, and these speakers handled all of it. The sounded is well balanced—even though I could hear sound coming from the individual speaker (such as footstep coming from the right), the entire sound mixed perfectly in front of me. The bass had no distortion and was also properly balanced with the speakers. Overall, these are very good speakers and I was happy with the overall quality.

One advantage these computer speakers have is that they can take a fiber optic cable from another source. This means you can use the fiber optic connection from a video game console (such as the PlayStation) and have digital sound. This is a huge bonus for these speakers because most computer speakers only have the traditional sound inputs. I applaud Logitech for having this feature (keep in mind that if you use these speakers for a video game system or a TV, there is no remote control for them, which might be a deal breaker for some users).

Overall, if you are looking for a high quality, flexible, 2.1 computer speaker setup, I would recommend the Logitech Z625 THX system.

title: Just ok (Bluetooth is terrible!) ... (Does not support voice volume pass-through to the headphones!)
text:
Pros:
- Lightweight
- Two modes (usb dongle and bluetooth) with a physical switch to switch between the two.
- Mic/call quality is great with the dongle, bluetooth is terrible
- Fold away mic

Cons:
- No option to bring mic volume to the earphones when on a call (details below)
- Bluetooth connectivity is a joke, mic sound quality makes it is unusable (Galaxy Note 8 or laptop BT adaptor).
- Sound quality isn't super awesome (not so much a con, but expect more at this price point).
- The door to stash the usb dongle is hard to open and close
- feel kinda cheesy for this price point

The sound quality isn't bad, definitely not audiophile quality, but good enough for calls and background music.

The one thing that is nearly a deal breaker is the fact that there is no way to feed your own voice (mic volume) into the speakers when on a call as most other plugin usb headsets allow. Typically there should be a mic level adjustment in the playback devices levels dialog. With these you don't have that option, so you can't hear yourself in the earphones. This may or may not be important to you, but it is to me as without it I find myself trying to talk louder as one inadvertently does when wearing isolating/over-ear headphones. I haven't tried many other wireless headphone/mic combos, there doesn't seem to be too many out there with the same convenience features that these have.

One nice thing is that you can use the usb dongle (which conveniently stores inside one of the ear pieces, although not the easiest to open and close), or use bluetooth, and here's the nice part; There's a switch on the earpiece to switch between the two. Very nice as you can use it with your computer (using the dongle) and very easily just flip the switch to use with your phone. In my opinion this feature brings it up to a 3 star from 2.

Tempted to return because of the mic pass through problem, but will probably hang onto them.

title: A reliable and versatile mouse with excellent build quality.
text:
I got this in 2012, and I am still using it as I type this review. The quality is just superb.

Notes:

- The battery life is amazing. I turn it off every night when I turn off my computer, but I still think the battery life is nuts. I remember in the 2014, I was using the mouse, and I wondered: "why hasn't it run out of battery yet?" The mouse was performing as usual, but when I checked out the batteries, they were starting to leak a little bit... Screw the "Marathon Mouse", this thing can easily last two years of multi-hour daily usage. I've only had to replace the batteries twice in the time I've had the mouse (I just switched them out again).

- The build is almost perfect. This mouse does exactly what it needs to do. The scroll wheel is great w/ it's ability to side scroll. The forward/back buttons are perfect for web-browsing. The left/right clicks are crisp and consistent... both still perform like day one! The laser sensor never bugs out (on a mouse pad/reasonable surface). The balance of the mouse is just perfect with the batteries (heavy side where your palm rests, so less fatigue). The size is also perfect (I'm a 5'8" or 1.72m male; approx. 7.5" or 19cm from wrist to tip of middle finger).

- The mouse is super reliable. I mean come on. I've had it for almost FOUR years. It doesn't disconnect or feel like it's going to break. The mouse still glides perfectly, and the grips are still grippy. (Side note: the middle click did start to act up, but that's due to my constant usage of it. I just put a piece of duct tape above the switch, and it started to work again. It really isn't meant to be used as much as I use it...)

- The mouse has great compatibility. My operating system of choice is Linux (Xubuntu), and it works without a problem. When I use Windows, there are no issues either. I have also tested it on Mac OS X without any issues. It is also instantly recognized on all the OSes.

- The current price is awesome. I paid a bit more than the current price, but if Logitech still manufactures these the same way that they did back in 2012, the mouse is worth every penny.

tl;dr: A reliable and versatile mouse with excellent build quality.

Although I love the mouse, there are some minor, and completely non-essential tweaks that would make this perfect (for me):
- Logitech's "infinite scroll"
- thumb/ring/pinky finger supports
- soft-touch plastic (maybe)

title: Apple Magic Keyboard vs Logitech K811 - Logitech Wins. Easily.
text:
Short and sweet for Mac Users - Right now I have Apple Magic Keyboard and this one. Last week I used the Apple Keyboard for a few days. My feeling on the Apple Magic Keyboard [[ASIN:B016QO64FI Apple Magic Keyboard (MLA22LL/A)]] is frankly that is isn't very magical. The keys feel floppy/flappy and the travel is so short that it makes the Apple keyboard feel smaller than it is. Simply not very comfortable. I'm male and will say if you have the slightest bit of fingernail, based on your angle of attack on the Apple Magic Keyboard they may hit the aluminum. Annoying.

Logitech K811
I've had a 15" Late 2011 Macbook Pro since it was released and became very used to that keyboard. I tend to hit the keyboard fairly hard and key travel and resistance on the K811 is _very_ similar to that one. There is a little resistance when a key is pressed to decelerate our finger and a satisfying pop/push back. I'm also spoiled by a back-lit keyboard which makes perfect sense on the K811 (which is utterly missing on the Apple Magic keyboard). The key feel/softness of the keys, from the 2011-2014 era Macbook keyboards are also very similar on the K811. The K811 keys have a soft roundness and while the 2011-2014 Macbook's keys are more square than the K811, it isn't as stark of a difference than the 2011 Macbook Pro to the new "magic" keyboard.

Verdict:
The K811 wins easily if you're looking for that same tactile feel and operation of an earlier era Macbook. I really like the backlit keyboard since my office is dark. +2 for Logitech for knocking this one out of the park!

The new mouse was fine at first but after about a week it became very erratic, particularly when scrolling. I tried a wide variety of troubleshooting steps, Logitech's forum and FAQs without success. After about a month of frustration I tried Logitech support again. This time they sent me a return label then, after they received mouse #2, they sent me another new mouse. So far so good until about day 4. You guessed, this one is erratic too. At this point I'm just going to tell Logitech that it's going in the recycle bin and I'll stick with my M510 which has always been reliable. The only reason I'm giving 3 stars rather than 1 is because of their customer service.

title: Unable to charge batteries
text:
Purchased to replace very old Harmony 650 who's buttons stopped working reliably. Got the 700 because it has the same button layout and programming as the 650, but comes with (allegedly) rechargeable batteries. After I got the 650's programming copied over to the 700 I used it OK for about a half hour, after which it gave the message "Charge batteries."

So I used the enclosed USB cable and charger block to charge the batteries. After about 2 minutes the remote said "Unable to charge batteries". So I removed & reinstalled them and tried again. Same results. Next I took the USB cable with remote attached and plugged the USB cable into a wall-mount USB outlet I use for my cellphone (I know this outlet works OK). Same results.

I Googled "Harmony 700 unable to charge batteries" and found a number of postings from people having the same problem. But there were no solutions posted. The best info I could find was "old batteries need to be replaced". So I figured the rechargeable batteries that came with the remote were just old and bad. I replaced them with standard AA's and the remote seems to be OK.

At least I got another USB cable and charger block.

title: Slamming Issue Major Promlem...
text:
I am so unbelievably disappointed in the keyboard/case! I've had this since March of 2016...At first it was the obvious choice. I actually bought every keyboard offered for the iPad Pro and tried them out before returning the others to the retailer I got them from. Within the first 45 days or so my first Zagg Glass broke because SO very often when I would go to adjust the volume the screen would slam shut, I was always checking to make sure I had the iPad correctly in the case. It is a major design flaw. Luckily, the retailer I purchased the case and screen protector from could see the obvious flaw and replaced my Zagg glass for free..I became accustomed to holding the case in place before trying to adjust the volume because I knew it would continue to happen. It was still happening but I'd grown accustomed to holding the case differently...until I forgot a few times and SLAM....another broken Zagg glass and a few weeks ago during one of the volume adjusting slams the plastic around the case cracked...I've NEVER dropped my iPad, always keep it in an additional protective case when I am transporting it, I can confidently say this is a real and aggravation design issue...
I started typing this review this morning when I could no longer ignore the Logitech keyboard case was not sufficiently protecting my iPad as it had totally lost the capability to hold the tablet inside. I knew it was time to stop in at my local electronics store and get a new case ASAP! The iPad slipping out constantly was really stressing me out, I didn't need additional stress on election day :/..so, I'm now typing on my new (VERY EXPENSIVE) iPad keyboard, I was thrilled to learn that since I made this initial purchase Apple released a protective case that slips on the back and integrates flawlessly with the keyboard...well, of course it does it is Apple and they make you pay! $100 more for the combo then what I paid for the Logitech but the typing experence is amazing, kinda ironic that my review for this is being finished on it. The keypad response is devine, I can push the volume buttons as hard as I want and it is not going anywhere. So~after owning the Logitech since last March I can confidently say I am a seasoned user of the product and sadly I've thrown $150 out the window :( Oh..plus the two Zagg glass covers I've lost. I forgot to register the last one, my bad so I will be ordering a new one and replacing this cracked one due to the slamming issue. Really aggravated I missed the return window. I will probably reach out to the company and let them know of my experience. If you are on the fence, dive in...get the Apple keyboard and protective case. I will try to update in a few weeks, I need to use it and travel with it some. So far I LOVE it.
(The photo shows the cracked case and the piece that eventually totally broke off, NOT what I would expect for the price)

text:
*READ BEFORE YOU BUY!* Prior to purchase I verified with the Harmony website that this product would work with the brand/models of my AV gear. The Logitech Harmony 650 will not, WILL NOT work with a Panasonic DMP-BD87 Blu-Ray player! After over an hour on the phone with Harmony support, and jumping through SEVERAL hoops, I gave up.
Harmony later sent me information that would address the problem. It did not. The information (based on their research) had NOTHING to do with the problem.
If you're willing to gamble then give it a shot but even in current consumer electronics today there is no standardization. Chaos reigns ULTRA supreme. With 'work-a-rounds' suggested by Harmony for SOME of the remote commands, other commands (like basics) needed way too many steps to make all this worth while.
I plan on returning this item, & hope I get my money back without a struggle. Buyer beware.

title: Nice Keyboard...
text:
I own a few of these. One at home connected to my 27" iMac. The other goes with me to work. I do contract IT work so I take one from job to job. This is a long term review as I bought them in 2012.

The backlighting is really cool and the lettering is sharp. After four years it still works great even though my powered hub at home keeps it lit 24/7. Logitech replaced one because a key broke and there have been no problems since. I can type so much faster on these than on a standard keyboard and the wrist rest placement is perfect. There are no problems using it with Mac or PC.

I'm writing and deducting one star however because of the rubberized coating on the wrist rest. Like many products, Logitech decided to spray on a rubber coating which over time turns sticky and eventually scrapes off. It always looks dirty and is impossible to clean.

At work, I keep my work area clean with Clorox Disinfecting Wipes. No, they don't contain bleach and are very mild. I've never seen them ruin any surface.

Lately, I've cleaned my trackball, keyboard, phone, and desk frequently because I've had a cold and today I came in and realized that the wrist rest had a very sticky/tacky feel. I rubbed on the area and the rubber started to come off. I wasn't surprises because I've see this on mice, universal remotes, older IBM Thinkpad laptops, cameras... It always comes off in time.

So I proceeded to spend a long time with cleaning wipes, rubbing alcohol, a towel, and my finger nails and got it all off. To my surprise, the feel is better and it's easy to keep clean! The bare plastic surface underneath is nice! So why??? And it's kind of funny how Logitech printed their logo ontop of the rubber coating and underneath on the base plastic... They knew it would come off but wanted their logo to remain.

It is my favorite keyboard on the market, they've lasted me years, and I highly recommend it. Like so many products it just could have been better without the coating.

text: I love this remote control.  I am an old guy who has purchased universal remotes and programmable remotes for the last 30 years.  THIS ONE IS TRULY INNOVATIVE, AND MINE HAS WORKED PERFECTLY SO FAR.  My previously owned remote controls were "device based" and you had to change from device to device to operate all of your equipment.  Let's say you have 5 devices, the old remote controls were better than 5 different remote controls and all of the clutter they caused.  AND it would take forever to program all of the functions that you want on a single remote control.  This Logitech Harmony 700 is "ACTIVITY BASED" and it was so easy to setup using my computer and the myharmony website. An example:  "DirecTV + Sound" as an activity does all of the following with the press of one button on the remote.  It turns on 3 devices; my TV and AV receiver, and the SAT receiver.  It sets the TV to the right input, it sets my sound amp to the right sound input, and device controls are for the DirecTV SAT receiver, and yet the sound and mute buttons affect my sound amplifier. It is wonderful.  I like the 700 better than the 650 because the batteries are more powerful and they are rechargeable.

title: Slightly short but very functional
text:
I bought this to replace an almost identical Logitech mouse that I bought several years ago, and which has no model information on it. The biggest differences were that the button to activate the "microgear" or ratchet action on the mouse wheel was underneath on the older model, by the batteries and laser sensor. Having it on top for this model obviously makes it a good deal more useful.

My lack of a fifth star is purely subjective. The model I replaced was a good inch longer, which allowed me to rest my palm on it more fully, whereas this one, my hand has to hover above it, a less comfortable position for daily use. For folks with smaller mice and/or hands, this won't be an issue, but I'm going to upgrade (already) to the MX Master for the bigger form factor, and the auto-ratchet gear on the wheel.

There is a small button built into the housing at the base of the left side of the mouse. It's not a physically distinct button, per se. It's more a place in the housing where you can squeeze to ignite whatever functionality you assign in the Logitech software. I won't have had the pleasure of using this function, but I can tell that in using it, you have to squeeze the mouse somewhat awkwardly, which causes the pointer on the screen to move ever-so-slightly, unlike a good ol' fashion right- or left-click action.

For the money, if you're OK with the shorter wheelbase, it's a fine mouse to use.

title: Buying This Product is Only HIGHLY Recommended.
text:
I have this unit connected to my Vizio 4k television, Onkyo AV receiver, PS3, XBOX 360, Nvidia SHIELD TV, AT&T Uverse receiver, and Nintendo Wii U and it is great!

I prefer using a remote while on the couch and this device can set up macros to automate my TV, receiver and device all turning on and going to the appropriate inputs with one touch (or long press) of the remote. My only gripe with this feature is that there are only 3 buttons to achieve doing this on the actual physical remote and with the exception of "Watch TV" they aren't really intuitive (aka Wife Approved). For Example, I use Kodi to stream movies from my SHIELD TV, and for 4k Netflix, so I programmed that as "Watch Movie" There's a button that has a clapperboard on it which indicates a movie; simple, but my PS3 is under the music note which makes no sense. For my 360, I have to long press the button with the TV on it, and likewise with the Wii U but with the "Movie" button. That being said, it's certainly no deal breaker and finding and adding devices is super-simple.

My goal with this remote was to remove my A/V components from my living room into a closet, and based on my testing, I will be able to do this and even use the IR blaster extension ports on the back to add functionality into an upstairs "Game Room" which I am excited to try out. I had hoped that the unit would be able to control my Logitech Revue (which I love and STILL use in my Game Room) over WiFi. I can control it via IR, but it would have been nice if the two Logitech devices played nicer together and perhaps even having the Revue act as another hub, but support for that product was dropped long ago, so I'm not bitter.

I am also excited about the possibility of using this product in conjunction with the Amazon Echo. This opens up many possibilities on the home automation front. The Harmony Smart Control can control things via WiFi, IR and Bluetooth; For example, it connects to my Nexus Player in my bedroom and I can control it with no direct line of sight and through a few walls If one had Philips Hue lights, control over those lights could be achieved with this device even if the hub wasn't in the same room. With the Amazon Echo, the Smart Control and Hue lights you could ask Alexa to turn on your TV, turn down the lights and play some music; it would send the command to your hub and the hub would do it's thing and you wouldn't even need to touch your phone, remote or anything.

So all-in-all it's a fantastic device. The only short-comings are that if you have a lot of IR items and you want to control devices in multiple rooms, you're either going to have to invest in multiple hubs, or commit to running IR blasters into a couple of rooms (you can only add two), and the macro buttons can be confusing. The only reasons I see for not buying one, is if you A) love collecting and using multiple proprietary remotes, B) You've already spent many hours coding applications and devices to do the same things this can, or C) You already have one or more of these.

title: Excellent! Setup a "Smart Theater" on a budget!
text:
I've had this remote for 11 months. It has performed flawlessly. The basic functionality was quick and easy to setup. It took a couple tries to get the correct signal to turn off my BenQ W1070 projector and integrate lighting control.

With this remote and hub I have setup a routine to "Turn on Theater". The routine powers on the projector, AV receiver and a Fire TV (front end for my Plex Server), it also sends a command to my Smartthings Hub to turn the lights off at the same time. Pressing the off button powers down the system and turns the lights on.

With a recently added skill the Amazon Echo will run the routine by simply saying "Echo, Theater On". It works the same in reverse by simply saying "Echo, Theater Off" - obviously the routine must be setup and named appropriately. Once paired to the Hub the echo triggers the routine, the Harmony Hub carries out the routine and passes a trigger on to the Smartthings hub within the routine it is running.

As a remote and hub only, I would highly recommend this unit. Integration with the Smarththings Hub and Amazon Echo makes it exceptional. It's hard to describe the WOW factor when someone walks into a home theater and you can control it with your voice.

text:
I was going to buy a foldable Bluetooth keyboard to take on a cruise to do some writing on and then found this.
This works great for my Note 4 and my Tab 2. I enjoy writing a lot and this way I have the best of several world's with lots of options rather than just have a notebook.
The size and weight are fine, it functions as a table for for the devices at a really comfortable angle.
The Android buttons are perfect.
The clicking is a little louder than usual. But it was odd last night when I was trying it out.
My 19 year old son was sitting on the couch and he heard me typing and said how cool that is to hear the clicking of the keys.
It sets up easily to Bluetooth devices and you simply toggle between them and do what you need to. Text, email, surf, email, Facebook, write reviews, listen to music on one.
Then flip to the other to continue writing your book.
I wished that it came with a cover though. I'm just going to buy a sleeve for it and move ahead.

This product solved the problem! It worked very well during my first conference call. I would give it 5 stars but for the fact that I found it difficult at first to determine if the device was on or off and I didn't think the instructions were very clear on that point. Also there has been a slight echo on some of, but not all of the calls. The set up was easy as well. You do have to be fairly close to the device when your are speaking, but you can hear the person speaking on the other end from a good distance. Additionally you can use this as a speaker for your computer as well. All in all I am pleased with this purchase.

title: Best headset I've ever owned.
text:
I bought this headset back in 2011 and it is still working fantastic. I actually came on amazon today just to buy replacement ear pads because the original ones have just about had it. the outer covering is falling apart and my wife keeps trying to get me to buy a new headset, but I love this one so I found the replacement ear pads for $5. Seeing some peoples pics of their headset after a year makes me wonder how they treat their stuff. Mine looks as good as it did when I bought it.Minus a few scuff marks from setting it down on the desk.

If you take care of your headset and don't throw it down or have rage fits with it then it should last you easily 3+ years.

Sound quality is still the same as it was when I bought them, the charge life is still about 10 hrs on a full charge so I don't think it has gone down.

the voice changing software is kinda fun to use but nothing to really drool over. I love walking around the house in between matches and being able to hear my friends in TS while I get something to drink or use the bathroom. The mute for the mic is nice and I set the 3 buttons up to control my itunes music while i play.

you really can't find a better headset out there for twice the cost of what this one is.

I hope this helps anyone on the fence about getting them. You will not regret buying these.

title: The gold standard for non-HOTAS joysticks.
text:
Amazon won't say I'm a verified owner, but I am. In fact, I've owned mine since before Amazon was as ubiquitous as it is now, and I can vouch for this thing's quality. The spring response is good, the number of buttons is exceptional, and while the throttle may seem diminutive, it is fully functional. Personally, I keep my left hand on my keyboard and my right on the stick, but some people like having their right hand on the stick, and their left down on the base, with their fingers controlling the six pad buttons and their thumb on the throttle. Both are effective methods.

Put simply, there is a reason this has been on the market for so long, and it isn't because Logitech is lazy; its because this hit the sweet spot for gaming joysticks.

All that being said, this isn't going to give you the same immersion in flight sims as a proper HOTAS setup, but this is a cost effective solution for most people who don't want to pony up several C-notes for a robust HOTAS configuration.

text:
The Harmony operates as advertised, fits well in the hand, has enough buttons to handle all the functions I need, and simplifed my multi-remote life. It is robust enough to accommodate my odd situation.

Wish it had a backlight.

I had a unique situation, because [I didn't realize this until I bought the Harmony] you can't just pick a setting on my model of Samsung DVD player -- you have to cycle through each setting in sequence. So I couldn't simply assign a command on the Harmony and have the DVD player switch to the right setting. for, say, Smart TV or cable or DVD.

I actually had to call Geekatoo, and it took a guy who knew home theater really well about 2 hours to figure out how to program the Harmony so it cycles through each DVD setting to get the one needed for each different function. So there's a really annoying delay each time I turn the TV on as it cycles through 5 settings. I can't switch functions without turning the whole thing off first. But like I said, I'm an outlier.

A long way of saying: If the Harmony can handle my one-off situation, it's pretty flexible and good. When I replace my DVD player I'll bet it's easy to set up.

Now, to the current one that I just bought 35 days ago... The + sign key popped off and is broken! Its not going to kill me but jeez, the return policy is 30 days. Go figure. The new one still has the same design with the small plastic feet that pop out to prop it up a bit. They aren't the best, but it will do.

This is the absolute best feeling keyboard I have ever had, it's wireless and holds a charge. The keys feel very soft yet sturdy, and I bang while I type. It is nice and small, so it doesn't take up a huge amount of desk space like most keyboards. I'm really irked about the plus + key breaking so soon, so low rated!

title: This keyboard has been the perfect answer for me
text:
I was looking for a portable way to do some writing with my Samsung Note 3 phone, and this keyboard has been the perfect answer for me, paired with the Google Docs app. It connects quickly, and does the job well. It's light and completely portable, but feels substantial enough that I don't worry about damaging it in a bag. I wonder how the flocked surface will hold up over time, though.

I love its small size - the keyboard is close to the size of my Dell Mini 10v's keyboard - it's perfect for my small hands. I find the tactile 'click' is all I need, it doesn't feel mushy at all to me... but then again, it's nothing like my Macally Icekey that I use with the Mac Mini, which is also a much 'easier' keyboard than the usual corporate model. My hands are dainty, and I make way more mistakes when I have to pound on a heavy-duty keyboard than this one.

It took me a little time to get used to the key spacing, but after a few minutes I'm touch typing at full speed. I think this is a great bit of tech for someone on the go, who doesn't want (or need) to lug a laptop around everywhere.

This case (and Logitech) irritate me to no end. I received this case as a gift in June of this year (less than 3 months ago) and while the keyboard itself has worked fantastically as other have mentioned the left side holder broke! I called Logitech to see what they could do for me and they informed me that since the product was over 3 years old they would not do anything for me and that my warranty had expired just one week ago... No, not a month or two, one week ago. They indicated that the purchase date is irrelevant and regardless of when it was bought new they warranty off of the manufacture date which was 3 years ago. I have never had an issue with Logitech support but it has completely soured my lips to them as a company. I offered to send a receipt to prove the age of the product and it did not matter, they would not assist. I even asked to speak to a supervisor and they would not transfer me. Fortunately Amazon has offered to make it right by crediting me for the product, but I will not likely be purchasing anything from Logitech in the future. How good is a 3 year warranty if it's based on manufacture date??

According to other reviewers it sounds like they've fixed this flaw, however even though I bought my case 3 months ago it still had it, clearly it was old stock, but regardless.

title: Does everything as expect as a SMART TV controller but feels a bit cheap.
text:
Does everything as expect as a SMART TV controller but feels a bit cheap.
It also works fine with the Kindle Fire TV (don't forget to disable USB debugging).

The reason why it does not deserve 5 stars is because it feels cheap, when holding it on your lap while typing it bends and twists. When holding the edge in one hand, it warps and you hear the plastic squeaking. I tried to make it more rigid by tighten the tiny screws at the back but that did not really help. Probably I open it some day and just glue the edges.

They used a standard notebook keyboard, that is fine for desktop usage but I expect that most people use this keyboard in their living room to control their TV appliance. The cursor keys are some the most used keys but that layout is not really practical for handheld use. There is enough space to have separate keys for that or just a d-pad. Try to hold it like a huge game controller, it is obvious that adding a d-pad to the top right would be a huge improvement for navigating through menus.

Some tips for Logitech to improve the next iteration of this product:
* Make it more rigid.
* Add key back-lights or at least phosphorescent (glow-in-the-dark) ink.
* Add a D-pad (Joystick directional pad) mapped to the cursor keys at the top right.
* Add shoulder buttons mapped to Z and X keys.
