title: Buyer Beware, Manage Your Expectations
text:
Buyer beware on this one. When I saw that this was the #1 best seller in this category on Amazon I thought I was buying a slam dunk product. Perhaps my expectations were too high but I've been disappointed after using this for the past couple of months.

PROS
The sound quality on this is great. I'm very pleased with both the volume control and the quality of the sound itself.

The range is pretty good too. I'd estimate that I can walk at least 25-30 feet away before I start having problems.

CONS

The battery life on this headset is very disappointing. I find that I get maybe 2-3 sessions in at my computer before I need to charge these again. I'd estimate that my sessions last anywhere from 1-4 hours.

The software for these headphones is TERRIBLE and suffers from crippling issues. First and foremost, someone at Logitech decided it was a good idea to add a feature where the headset will randomly turn off at times. I assume this was intended to be some sort of sleep mode/battery conversation functionality but it is so poorly implemented that it happens at almost any time, including while you're playing sound through the headset. And the best part? There is absolutely no Logitech-created way to disable this feature. There are a couple of homebrew work-arounds but its incredible that you can't even disable this function. Second, the software provided by Logitech gives the user almost no guidance as to how to set up and use the various features on the headset. Third, the headset plays terribly with any other sound output devices you might have. I have analog speakers attached to my computer and thought it would be easy to switch between those speakers and this headset. I was terribly mistaken. Often, Windows won't even acknowledge that the headset is connected. I don't know who's fault this is (Logitech vs. Microsoft) but it's ridiculous that this isn't as seamless as it could be.

The base station also leaves a good deal to be desired. Logitech has designed it so you plug in a base station to your desktop via USB and then plug another USB into that base station that acts as the transmitter. I guess this makes sense so you have a place for a charger cable but generally seems weird and clunky to me.

On the whole, I much prefer my wireless headset to my old wired pair but this headset reminds me of what life was like in the cellphone sector pre-iPhone (e.g. clunky and buggy).

text:
The technology and sound is great and has, personally, worked flawlessly. The physical construction, on the other hand, is severely lacking.

I've now owned 5 or 6 of these headsets over the course of a few years for at least windows 7 and 10 (possibly Vista). I've never had a technical hiccup, aside from a 2 second turn-off and turn-on issue with connectivity once in a while. The thing is plug-and-play. If you want, you can download a software package that unlocks some cool features, but the headset, for me, has just worked.

I'm no audiophile, and I don't listen to music. I just use this for gaming and streaming. But, even I can tell that the sound quality is good. There's a good range. The treble is clean and the bass is deep enough that you never want to go to max volume. The 7.1 surround sound is certainly better than stereo sound - just remember to activate it using a toggle on the side of the headset.

But, before you buy this headset, invest in electrical tape and Krazy-Glue. I hate this headset because it seems they hired a ton of ergonomic and technical specialists, but no manufacturing specialists. The headset is plastic junk.

The headphones that fit over your ears are great; some of the most comfortable I've ever used. But, they're attached to a series of plastic apparatus which sucks. Sure there's a thin steel head band, but the rest is junk plastic and fake leather. The fake leather actually seems to last longer than the plastic.

The manufacturing problem is manifold. The plastic is junk. The pivot points of the headset are held in place by 2 or 3 milimeter screws - watch screws. These screws can't hand the pressure of a big head.

Yes, I dropped a pair and broke them. So, I bought another. It broke because the plastic was junk. My next pair broke because the plastic gave out. Then, I accidentally stepped on a pair. One pair just fell apart and I didn't warranty it, because I was an idiot. I am now on my last pair, held together by glue and some electrical tape.

Nonetheless, for the price of 69.99 for at least a year of great sound? Buy this. Just expect creaks and cracks at some point. It will all depend on your use. I abused the headsets. I wore them tight, I kept the headset on the floor, I shared the headset with my pals - maybe one was Charlie Brown. But, I have had headset after headset fail and I am on no. 4., which is held together by electrical tape and crazy glue.

title: Another superb remote by Logitech/Harmony.
text:
I previously used a Logitech Harmony 670 remote for over 8 years. It worked very well, despite abuse by family members and friends. The original one would have been 9 years old, but the USB port on it stopped working after 1 year. It was just out of warranty, but Logitech still honored the warranty, and sent me a new one, which I consider to be excellent customer service. Because of both their product quality and customer service, when it came time to replace it, I knew that I wanted another Logitech Harmony.

This remote is functionally somewhat similar to the 670, although the buttons and screen have different layouts. The remote has a tilt sensor, and turns on the color screen automatically when picked up or moved. The buttons also backlight when the screen is on (Logitech calls this the "glow" function). However, the backlighting is so weak that it will only be visible in a dark room. This is not great, but it is acceptable, as when the room lights are on, you can see the labels without the backlight. The screen light/backlight turns off after 20 seconds by default, but this can be changed to whatever value you choose, via the setup program.

Note that if you have poor vision, you might have a little struggle reading the buttons, as they are small. A backlight which was bright enough to light the buttons when room lights are on at normal levels would have helped here. Also, the top few main function buttons (red buttons) have no backlighting at all, even in the dark. This lack of good backlighting is my only complaint with the product as designed (my old 670 had good backlighting).

Response sequence delay times are customizable for device power-on/off and button presses, directly on the remote, which is a great feature. Basically, when programming the remote you enter your devices and then define the "activities" you desire ("Watch TV", "Watch Movie", "Play Game", etc). Appropriate activation/deactivation sequences and delays are then automatically set for power-on/off, and for between button pushes. Then during an activity such as pressing "Watch TV", the remote will instruct you to keep it pointed at your devices for the entire time that the activity sequence is being run. The default delays can be modified easily, directly on the remote, without having to again hook the remote to a computer for reprogramming.

For example, initially it was taking 10 seconds or more for the remote to execute all the "Turn On" commands when selecting "Watch TV"; some of these involved turning on my AV receiver, selecting the AV input, turning on the TV, etc. I was able to shorten this quite easily, on the remote, to just a few seconds for the sequence.

Another excellent feature was the ability to import most of my settings from my old 670 remote (even though Logitech had revamped their site, which required me to generate a new user logon for the new 650 remote). During the setup for the new remote, the software informed me that I could import my information from the old remote. The program then stepped me through creating the new user account, then entering my old user account logon (which it quickly located). After this it quickly imported the settings from the old remote to the new, even though they are not matching models. Excellent! I did have to go back and redefine a few activities, but these were marked as needing information, and I was able to modify them without too much effort.

And for those of you not familiar with how Logitech designs their Harmony remotes: if you should ever need a replacement, it is very easy to simply add the replacement device to your user account, and then quickly port all of the settings from the original device to the replacement. This is because all the remote data is stored on their website. The software app you download to your computer for programming the remote simply accesses the data stored on Logitech's servers.

Admittedly, to realize the benefit of some of the remote's advanced features requires a little study of the programming software. However, the majority of users will simply add their devices, and allow the remote to create common activities, which is a fairly simple operation.

I would not hesitate to purchase another Harmony remote.

title: Stick with the Harmony 600. The Harmony 700 has problems with its charging components.
text:
The remote works well for controlling my devices. The ability to use the Logitech database to look up products by model number is a great perk to Harmony remotes I've long enjoyed.

For as long as I can remember, Harmony remotes have been plagued with battery problems. My first Harmony, years ago, came with a cradle, and the thing would not stay on the cradle to save its life. It got to a point where I had to use rubber bands to keep the remote on the cradle. Eventually ,that one went in the trash, and I upgraded to a Harmony 600.

Oh, the Harmony 600--what a wonderful little remote. It was pretty straightforward. There was no built in battery charger, so when the batteries died, it was just time to replace them. That was simple. It was easy. Then the sad day came when my Harmony 600 died.

I was doing better on money by that point, so I decided to step up to the Harmony 700 because hey, that sounds cool--plug it in to charge the normal AA rechargeable batteries. Awesome! So I bought the Harmony 700. All was well until...

One day, while watching the Doctor save the world for something like the eleventy billionth time, the Harmony's screen displayed a low battery warning. Uh oh. Time to charge it. So I plug it in and... oh... what's this? "Please insert batteries." Odd.

I removed the batteries and replaced them. Same thing.

Removed the batteries, threw them out, and replaced them with new ones. Same thing.

Thought, "Oh, might be just a glitch." I left it plugged in for two days. It didn't charge.

Tried a different cable. No go.

Different wall charger? Nope.

This thing won't charge--at all. So I consult the great oracle Google on this message on the Harmony 700. Apparently this is a common problem with Harmony 700s. I feel like I paid an extra $20 for a useless USB port on a Harmony 600.

The remote still works fine for its primary use, but considering the charging capability is the main thing that set the 600 and 700 apart, I'd say save your money and get the 600. At least then you won't feel like you've wasted money when the charging component goes haywire.

The Good:

title: Shielded Against WiFi Interference, But High-Pitched Ringing, Overbearing Sub
text:
I bought these Z623 speakers to replace my Altec Lansing VS2421 speakers, which sometimes suffer from WiFi and cell phone interference.

Good News: These speakers are immune to WiFi and cell phone signals!
Bad News: These speakers emit a constant, high-pitched ringing sound when turned on, even when not connected to a computer. The sound is unchanged by fiddling with the knobs or reconnecting cables. I thought I would be able to tolerate it until they hopefully got broken in, so I used them for a week. Then the right satellite speaker started to warble at the climax of songs and the ringing drove me crazy. I ended up switching back to my trusty old speakers and returning these.

Also, the VS2421 are lower-end speakers compared to these (28W @ $50 vs 200W @ $150), so I was expecting better sound. All I really got was an overbearing sub-woofer - something which seems to be a Logitech trend, since my brother's X-240 set is similarly unbalanced.

title: Just what I wanted
text:
I echo the other positive reviews. Here are a couple tidbits I couldn't find documented elsewhere.

It automatically connects to your iPhone after the initial pairing. It does this quickly. This suggests the unit has Bluetooth version 4.0, possible up to v4.2 (the latest version as I'm writing this).

The middle button on the top acts as a play/pause button. Overall the buttons are very responsive with very little lag. They are covered by rubber/silicone with no gaps around them so I feel confident pressing them while in the kitchen with wet hands.

The volume controls change the volume on your iPhone. The speaker doesn't seem to have its own, separate volume.

The power buttons turns the unit on and off with a single tap. You don't need to hold the button down like with many Bluetooth units.

The only thing missing are skip forward and skip backward buttons. Also, the battery level does not display on my iPhone next to the Bluetooth icon.

title: Poor Support. Hope it works for you without any issues.
text:
I was considering the Elite but opted for the 650 due to reviews and my first experience with Harmony remotes. Good thing as I quickly learned that Logitech support is non-existent. Setup and Sync did not work out of box and I even question if the setup app supports Windows 10, likely root of the problem. The installer only installs the App for single user instead of All users.

Sync continues to hangs at 99%. If sync does not complete you cannot use the remote or make any changes. Searching the Forums it appears to be a very common issue with customers, posting questions over several years, yet there was no definite answers from Logitech just possible work arounds by other users.

I finally was able to get the remote to sync completely by removing the batteries. But that work around only worked once. I made a change then tried to sync and it failed. Will try on a Windows 7 machine.

Another issue if you want any support (forums) you have to create an account which is different then the account you have to create to program your Harmony remote so that your setup data can be stored in "the Cloud".
I would have preferred to store locally on my Laptop as I am now a future victim of planned obsolescence. When Harmony decides to drop support for the 650 it will no longer be able to be configured.

My initial impressions, will update if any changes.

title: Much better than the Performance MX
text:
I purchased this mouse after trying out the Performance MX, which is an outstanding mouse in its own right. The Performance MX feels great, is ultra smooth, and is less expensive than the MX Master.

The big, and apparently very common, problem w/the Performance MX though, is the noticeable whine they emit while at idle, that only gets louder when it's moved. The sound will fool you into thinking your ears are ringing.

I returned the Performance MX in favor of picking up a lightly used MX Master elsewhere, and I was immediately more impressed. The MX Master feels even better in the hand, moves slightly smoother, and improves on the ratchet-vs.-free-wheel scrolling by auto-switching between the two based on how fast you scroll. And, happy to report the MX Master is dead silent.

Additionally, the MX Master also has a very light rubber matte finish across its surface, improving grip and overall feeling over the Performance MX.

The only tiny issue I have w/the MX Master are its noticeably *louder* mouse clicks. Based on some quick research it sounds like this is a common sentiment other MX Master owners complain about as well. So despite being the best mouse I've ever used, it's also the loudest clicking one, by far. Though in its defense, I relay this fact as a strong silent-pc enthusiast; I value quiet operation far more than the average user.

Overall highly recommended, you won't be sorry.

title: Outstanding mouse, if it didn't whine
text:
Well, the mouse has an outstanding design and feel. But I've decided to return it. I can't get past the constant whine it emits while at idle, and the even louder and more high pitched whine it emits while being moved.

The first day of use I thought my ears were constantly ringing, but on the second day of use I pinpointed the whine to the mouse. About a week later and no improvement; it's driving me nuts. No difference regardless of the battery's charge, using a mouse pad or not, or changing the USB port I have the receiver connected to.

title: Fully compatible with G510
text:
Epic!

So when i first got my hands on my early Valentines gift (wifey and I spoil each other!) I plugged it in and saw the profiles are the same between the Logitech g510 and the G13. I paniced. Both have G1-G18 and the only extra G keys on the G13 are G19-G22, I was kinda bummed that I would only have another 4 hotkeys to play with. Not that I have them all set on the keyboard anyways.

Some forum searches later, I thought I had confirmed that the G1 on the keyboard would sent the same command as G1 on the gameboard. Everyone spoke about changing the settings on one only to find it would change on the other as well.

I am here to tell you that is not the case!! The G510 and G13 are fully compatible and do not mess with each other. Maybe you need another profile for some reason? I cannot imagine why but I don't.

With banks M1 M2 M3 and 18 hotkeys on the keyboard plus M1 M2 M3 plus 29 on the G13 (including the thumb control, pressing the thumb button and the two keys beside it.... you will have hotkeys for DAYS! I don't care to do the match because I know I won't use them all. I'm thrilled! The only thing that could make it better for me is if I could change the LED behind each key and even change it from saying G1 to saying what the key does. Or some other custom text.

Time to go nerd out.

title: Great mouse but has a common design defect
text:
I purchased this mouse in November of 2013. I have been using it quite regularly for 2.5 years up until I write this review. Prior to me purchasing it, it had been on my radar to purchase due to stellar reviews. I hadn't read about the major caveats at the time. One day the price was right (sub thirty dollars) and I jumped on it.

I want to LOVE this mouse. I really do. It's a great size for laptop use, has a nice weight, and I got it for a decent price. The issue here is the DOUBLE CLICK/CLICK & DRAG defect. You can read more about this via google search/other reviews. I started experiencing this problem probably 1.5 years into use. It was also very sporadic. Sometimes I had the issue, sometimes not. This mouse was not my primary mouse, so I just dealt with it. I seems this is a widespread issue which leads me to believe there is a defect in the design. Logitech needs to fix this. I have initiated my warranty claim (standard 3 year warranty on this unit) and will see how the replacement works.

Again- I really want to love this mouse. I do not think it is anywhere near worth its MSRP of +$50 so get in on sale. But be aware of the potential defect. If the defect wasn't present, I would absolutely give this a 5/5- no questions asked!

UPDATE 07/27/2016: So I finally received the warranty replacement in June (1 month ago). No issues (yet). I am moving my review from 3 to 4 stars. Still docking a star for Logitech should have addressed these issues through rigorous testing before selling it to retailers.

title: Apple Schmapple, Works Great on my Android Phone, as well!
text:
Like many, I live in mixed universes, Macbook Pro and Android Samsung S7 Edge. I got this because I wanted a backlit keyboard to work with the MBP. (Apple, why don't you sell a backlit keyboard?) The lighting was the draw, not the "easy-switch" functionality. The keyboard works and feels great, generally, and the backlighting works as hoped. A day after I bought it, it's sitting on my desk and I figured, since it has the easy-switch thing, lemme try my phone. The keyboard paired instantly with the Edge, so I can jump between devices quickly, and now, if I travel and want to take only my phone, I've got a thin keyboard I can take with me. It shouldn't be any surprise that this worked, but all the hype is about Apple devices. So, those of you running an Apple/Android mashup, this is your keyboard.

Everything about it is great, but for due diligence, here are the minor cons, so far:
1. The keys are a little more slick than the Apple keys. There is just a hint of slippage when you type vs. Apple. This is mitigated by the fact the keys are concave and your fingers naturally go to the bottoms. I stopped noticing quickly. I like the feel.
2. Adding the Bluetooth switching keys meant they had to remove a couple of the standard F keys. They picked Rewind and Fast Forward on the the media control buttons. Up to you if this is a problem. Now that I have a second device paired, the sacrifice is more palatable.
3. I'm concerned about the non-replaceable rechargeable battery. I've owned several higher end Logitech keyboards over the years and, even in the rechargeable versions, you could replace the batteries, which I have eventually had to do on every model. The manual treats battery death as the time to throw the keyboard away. This planned obsolescence of a great, pricey keyboard seems stupid. I hope the battery lasts for years.

Overall, I really like it so far and highly recommend!

title: Best keyboard with proper key feedback and quietness
text:
I have had 5 keyboards in the past year alone, as I have been searching non-stop for a keyboard that I can type without effort. My search stopped with this keyboard, Logitech Illuminated K740.

This keyboard has the old school scissor switch feel from the first generation of laptops, and the key strokes are crisp, responsive and effortless.

Another feature I like a lot is that it is really quiet. It is not completely silent, but it is quiet enough that almost none of the keyboards I owned matched it (unless you are using the Macbook pros 2015 model)

Although I don't care much about the illumination, it is a nice feature.

The layout of the keyboard is practical and standard (except for the insert key, which I have no problems with). The hot keys are elegantly placed, and only the useful hot keys are included, which is also a thoughtful design.

I know this keyboard was designed years ago probably for Windows Vista, but in the age of Windows 10, it still outperforms the competitors by a long shot.

Finally, for reasons I can not comprehend, keyboard makers have been swarming to the "gaming keyboard" market and started making gaming mechanical keyboards as their mainstream lines. This is a little disappointing, as keyboards aren't meant for gaming. In addition, I got a lot of complaints for using the clicky mechanical keyboards I had (I owned an IBM mechanical keyboard that I have been using for 10 years, before it was replaced by another mechanical keyboard) from my colleagues and I basically stopped using them. If you type a lot and don't want to affect others, go for this one.

title: Best mouse under $100
text:
You may wonder why I say it is the best for mice under $100. That is because I owned a lot of mice spreading the range of $10 ~ $100 and my opinion is that a $80 mouse doesn't give you anything better than this one that is practical for day to day office use.

If you are looking for something that clicks right, scrolls right, moves quickly, this is your mouse. In stark comparison, I owned a Microsoft mouse for business (which I threw away once this one arrived) that cost me a whole lot more, the scrolling wheel on that one was just flat out terrible. It didn't have the discrete clicks this one has (the clicks are silent but can be felt by your fingers), and the pages constantly flicker or roll back against my will.

The only pre-caution for this mouse and all other mice that use red LED tracking is that it doesn't move well on some surfaces. Blue LED's work better. That said, it can be easily overcome by having a mouse pad.

title: No double click issue yet, but the mouse wheel in click-to-click mode occasionally acts erratic.
text:
Despite the large number of poor reviews due to the "double click" issue and the issue with the mouse wheel continuing to scroll when in the freewheel mode, I went ahead and purchased this mouse in January. I like the form factor, as it fits my medium size hand really well. With one Logitech unifying receiver and software, I use this mouse and the logitech K360 keyboard. Taking up only one USB port is excellent.

I still don't have any trouble with the buttons. As to the complaint about the overly sensitive scrolling in free-wheel mode, it's designed that way. Upon Google research, someone advised taking the mouse apart and making the wheel scroll slower by applying objects (tape, sticks, anything really) to resist spinning. It's a rather silly solution, and I personally don't care. Just mind your trigger finger. I almost always keep the mouse in the click-to-click mode anyway.

However, I noticed a different issue with the mouse wheel about a month ago, and this is why I'm giving it a two star review today. My mouse wheel is set to scroll 3 lines. About once an hour, it decides that it wants to scroll about 50 lines. I'm almost certain that it's a hardware issue because if I continue to use it as is, the erratic scrolling continues about once or twice a minute. If I turn the mouse off, and give it a couple fast and hard scrolls up or down, the erratic scrolling ceases for a while.

I have uninstalled and reinstalled the driver software, adjusted the mouse settings including scrolling size and smooth scrolling, and confirmed that the erratic scrolling happens in all of the software I've tried (Google Chrome, IE, Adobe PDF, Microsoft Word, Google Maps, and more). The erratic scrolling is not dependent upon the battery level or distance from the receiver. I took the mouse apart, and inspected the wheel mechanism, hoping I would find a piece of dust stuck in between the wheel and the sensor. Although everything was clean inside, I used a can of dust blower to blow the area off. The only other thing I haven't done is rule out the computer, but I do not have another computer I can test the mouse on. All the while, the K360 keyboard works flawlessly, by the way, so I think the receiver is not to blame.

With the huge number of complaints of this beautifully designed and perfectly sized mouse, I would recommend you to look for another mouse. As much as I don't want to buy another mouse so soon, this scrolling is driving me crazy and makes me want to throw the mouse against a wall. That is not good for my wall, however, as a hole in the wall will only make me more frustrated. I can guarantee that no mice were harmed during this review (it was taken apart and put back together), but I can't promise it will stay that way if the mouse continues to misbehave. If the issue becomes more frequent, the mouse may just become a shooting target.

title: Excellent But Logitech Needs To Upgrade This To Wireless
text:
A standard mouse has never been my friend. After a short period of use, my right hand and wrist start aching. Numerous studies have shown that a standard mouse is a major factor in RSI (repetitive stress injury).

I've used this Marble Mouse trackman for a number of years now. Even though I'm right-handed, I use it with my left hand to further reduce stress on my right hand. Figure it out: most people are right-handed, which means you put more stress on that hand doing everyday things, and even more so at the pc. Switching to the left hand just makes more sense. Ditto if you're left-handed: switch it to the right.

It's also the right size and shape for my hand.

Logitech is a good company, but they do some strange things that don't make any sense. They insist on keeping the marble mouse corded instead of wireless. I would gladly pay more for a cordless version, and I'm sure many people would buy it, but they don't. They did make a few wireless trackballs, but with the ball on the side - and one with the ball off-center -instead of right in the middle. I tried both of those, and all it did was work my thumb a lot and start it aching. Other reviewers have noted the same or similar experience with the Logitech track ball wireless versions. They don't sell well. Logitech, wake up and make an excellent product even better!

I've downgraded this by one star simply due to Logitech's stubborn refusal to offer this marble mouse in a wireless version. Wireless isn't the "new" thing any more, so update your good product to the 21st century.

title: Piece of garbage keyboard. Logitech weasels out of warranty.
text:
Piece of garbage keyboard. Letters on keys are starting to wear after less than two year's use, where keys are not readable - keys are essentially scratching through on white translucent part and black opaque parts so that letters are not legible in some instances. This keyboard has 3 year warranty. When I call Logitech Customer Care, they state that the letters on the keys wearing so that one cannot read the letters anymore, in less than 2 years of use, is a normal use issue and is not something the warranty covers. They would only cover this as a warranty item if it happens in the first 4 months or less of use. So much for the 3 year warranty.

After further discussion on this. Logitech Customer Care tried to reason with me why they would not honor their 3 year warranty. Logitech Customer Care absurdities such as: 1) I should remember where the keys are after two years of use anyway, so the keys being legible is not important and hence is not an eligible warranty item. 2) They than asked me how much I use the keyboard (hard for me to be precise on this ridiculous question - some days the keyboard gets no use, other days it might get several hours use) On this basis - they state that I used the keyboard too heavily, so the warranty does not apply - being less than 3 years old does not matter, if I use the keyboard 'a lot' then the wear is to be expected and is not a warranty item. I was expecting Logitech Customer Care to then ask me how often I press they keys that are wearing to the point where their legibility is gone or fading (the L and the F), expecting that their warranty does not apply based on the use of specific keys, i.e. I type the word Loofah or Fully to much, so the warranty does not apply.

All in all - Logitech is more interested in weaseling their way out of a warranty claim than standing being their products - shame of you Logitech.

I know people like to do that to test the limits, but they are plenty loud at low to mid volume! This is my favorite speaker set of all that I have owned. I have been using them for just over 2 years, and they still work great. I have never had the volume over half way, and they are plenty loud.

A couple things more to say. First, the headphone jack lowers the output volume a lot. I have to turn the volume knob to almost half way to get moderate volume out of my headphones. Not a big deal, but worth mentioning in case you listen your headphones really loud. Second, my set has developed a bit of crackle when adjusting volume. This is typical of stereos in my experience, but disconcerting none the less. It has never crackled loudly, but it is a little annoying. The Circle requires an internet connection, charging station and a phone app.  I love that I could see my live feed as soon as I turned on the camera.  I have the free trial of Circle Safe, but figure the free 24 hour storage is enough for my needs.  The 30 second day briefs are just a click away and alerts are simple to set up and maintain.  The security camera is not intimidating in the least, and maintenance is at a minimum.  For someone with minimal wall plugs, the 10 foot charging cord was a plus.  I'm happy with this purchase and would recommend to friends who would like to monitor a small indoor space.

title: Fairly solid headset

The microphone is fairly crisp quality, nothing too spectacular except that after approximately six months it stopped staying upright and will constantly just be in front of my face. It's a bit inconvenient as I enjoyed being able to put it up to mute the mic, but now I have to remember to hit the button or toggle the mic on my actual computer.

title: Excellent mouse while worked. Seriously quality issue.
text:
This mouse was really great while it worked. But Logitech has some serious quality issues with this mouse, especially the scroll wheel. How serious? For the three MX master I've used, two failed within two weeks (lucky enough to be still in return period). My first MX master worked amazingly until I lost it in a bar. I didn't hesitate to order a second one. However the scroll wheel totally failed for the ratchet mode after two weeks of use, always giving a freespin. I ordered a replacement and again within two weeks, the scroll wheel failed, this time unable to switch to freespin mode.

Major issues experienced with this mouse:
Scroll wheel failure with the two supported scroll mode.
Serious bluetooth connectivity issues with Mac. Often ended up not recognized by mac and needed to pair again. (Not sure if it's a mac problem or Logitech's. My old Microsoft Sculpt Comfort bluetooth mouse works fine with mac)

I've also seen other people commenting on the same problem and now believe that it's a widespread issue. I'd avoid this mouse until Logitech addresses the quality issue.

title: Worth Every Cent and BETTER than Apple's own "Smart Keyboard"
text:
***Preface--Skip to next paragraph for full review*** I don't review stuff here very often, but I've had this keyboard case for 2 days and I am so impressed that I felt compelled to share. I originally purchased a faux leather case that came with a bluetooth keyboard. It was ok, the first one fit, but the keyboard was always losing it's bluetooth sync with my ipad or not holding a charge. It's annoying to have to sync it several times in the span of a few minutes. After a month, I got annoyed and because I had exceeded the return period, I posted my review of the product which, as you might guess, was pretty bad. In a strange turn of events, the seller contacted me and without me asking, sent me a replacement with the hope that maybe I just got a lemon. I was thrilled and praised the seller for replacing my lemon at no cost to me. Hey, that's great customer service! Sadly though, the second case was even worse, not only did it not sync up consistently but the cutouts were not aligned so I couldn't use the case at all. Fast forward 2 months. I'd be considering buying the Apple ipad keyboard, you know, the one they want $140 for? I stared at it online, wanting to buy it because I knew it would work, but after reading reviews and looking closely at the product, I was not convinced it provided enough protection for the back of the ipad and the keyboard looked pretty flimsy, similar to the MS Surface.

So, here I am, on Amazon searching for third-party options. I knew I wanted something that made use of the smart connector feature (that connector on the side that enables the ipad to both charge and communicate, no bluetooth or synching required). I also wanted something that provided coverage for the back of my expensive ipad pro, was easy to use, and if at all possible, a secure place to store my Apple iPencil. I had hoped to find something in the $50-$60 range, but after the fiasco of my first two cases, I found it really hard. I came across this product and after reading the reviews, staring at the photos, and several hours of arguing with myself about spending $130 on a keyboard/case, I bit the bullet. I eagerly awaited for my smiley-faced box from Amazon to arrive, and immediately opened it up. The packaging was on par with what you would expect from an Apple product. Not that this really mattered, but it was a great first impression. I opened the box and found the case with a simple instruction sheet showing how to install the ipad. In 30 seconds my ipad was docked and the keyboard INSTANTLY turned on and I was off and typing. The smart dock works perfectly and easily enables quick placement at a perfect viewing angle for typing. I can't say enough great things about this product. It is lightning fast (no more going to settings to sync/re-sync EVER!) and even has backlit keys (which are a bonus as I wasn't looking for this feature) that you can adjust using the hot keys you'd find on any Mac. I was a bit concerned that the backlighting might reduce the battery life of my ipad, but they automatically dim 5 seconds after you stop typing. You can control the brightness of the keys by selecting one of the three options provided by the hotkeys: 100% on, 50% on, or off. Yep, they included a full keyboard with all the hot keys you'll need, including volume up/down, muting, screen brightness, video FFW, REW, Play/Pause, lock, and power down. The keys are made of a soft and smooth texture that doesn't show finger prints. That might sound weird, but have you ever typed on keyboard that have that slickery plastic and know exactly what you typed because the oil from your fingers shines? The keys are responsive and are spaced much like a laptop, and for anyone who doesn't hunt peck, this is a huge plus! The case itself is sturdy and has a slot where I can securely store my iPencil WITH the cozy (plastic tip cover with ring that ensures I don't lose the cap). The automatic sleep/wake feature works great and the case closes magnetically and securely. It has a slim profile for a case with a keyboard that also houses the pencil. All of the exterior buttons work well with the case. The only down side is the volume buttons are a bit on the flimsy side due to their "+" and "-" shapes and honestly, they look a bit corny, but a they seem to work just fine. I'd suggest future iterations emulate the buttons they protect. As for charging, the keyboard automatically charges through the ipad so I only need one cable to charge both. The exterior texture is great in that is both practical and easy to keep fingerprint free. It looks a bit like a canvas finish, but is made of high quality plastic (I think it's called TPU) though it doesn't look plastic.

Overall Impressions---
PROS: Sturdy, well constructed, responsive design, easy to use, convenient hot keys, backlit keyboard, secure magnetic closure, slim profile, multi-functional as a case, keyboard, and iPencil storage, does not require separate charging and synching via blue tooth
CONS: I don't really have any complaints. The only thing I would change are the volume buttons, they're white and in the shapes of a plus and minus sign that take away from the overal exterior aesthetic, but they function just fine.

text:

Everything on it just started to catastrophically fail after a while. First it stopped pairing with the dongle and required manual pairing before each session. Then it would randomly lose pairing during use. Then the mic wouldn't shut off when you close it. Then it wouldn't turn off when you hit the off switch.

The audio quality also isn't that good. If you have the volume above 40%, you will hear a white noise or buzzing sound.

The headset is also heavy. Honestly for this much money, you are better off getting a pair of Sennheisers.

I am not the only person who has reported these issues with the product. A quick perusal of the Logitech forums will show that the exact same issues are extremely common.

title: Allows me to type lots of stuff and move this little arrow thingy around my computer screen.
text:
I got this Keyboard/Mouse combo to replace a heavily outdated (but still quite functional - keyboard anyway) Microsoft bluetooth combo.

This thing gets relatively heavy use on my desk at work. The mouse has seen more use than the keyboard though as I will bring that with me when I travel, while the keyboard gets shut off and left behind to keep the other desk decorations company.

I'm extremely impressed by the battery life on this set compared to my previous setup by Microsoft. I've gone days (maybe even weeks) with the mouse even after it starts telling me the battery is low. In over three years, I may have replaced the keyboard battery once or twice.

I really like (and my co-workers probably highly appreciate) the ability to set the mouse wheel to free-wheeling mode to quickly and (relatively) silently scroll through long documents/spreadsheets/webpages.

The keyboard is quite comfortable to use, but the printing overlay on several keys, primarily on the left center have been worn away. This isn't an issue for me as I'm not a hunt-and-peck typist, but the quality in that regard is lesser than most keyboards I've used and is worth mentioning. I'll try to grab a photo if I can remember to when I'm back at the office provided I can add one to my review after posting it.

Overall, this is a good, solid product that has served me well so far and I expect it will continue to do so for many years to come.

title: Buy this one only if you can't find a K-400r to buy.
text:
It works better than most touchpad wireless keyboards but the plus isn't a plus. The K400r is actually a better model. This one doesn't have a single key system lock and shrinks the up/down keys into two half sized keys. The F-keys are smaller too even though they are all dual function. There is no color anywhere to indicate alternate functions on keys so it's nearly impossible to see what they do. On the K-400r the left mouse button is bigger than the right one. On this K-400 Plus I keep doing right clicks that I don't intend to since the left button isn't wider anymore. I also don't like that the on/off switch is placed further than a finger length from the right edge of the keyboard. I wrap my finger around that corner but then i have to move it just a little further left to turn it off. Does this all sound pretty trifling? It really isn't. If you can still find a K-400r buy that one and use it for a while before you buy one of these. You'll find that I was right and these are not small complaints at all. The one thing that I have come to like is the dedicated mute/up/down volume keys directly above the touchpad. On the K-400r these were the primary functions on the F10/F12/F11 keys. That's right PRIMARY, you had to use the alternate function key with your F12 if it was F12 you wanted. But there weren't ANY buttons above the touchpad on the K-400r so they could have just added the buttons and called it K-400 Plus and it really would have been a better keyboard (Plus). Sorry.

Oh, I just wanted to add that I bought the K400 Plus because I had worn the paint off of several keys on the K400r. The keyboard and touchpad both still work perfectly but it had been hard to find a good combo like this and so I decided to make my move before some idiot discontinued the series completely. You know, there's always idiots making decisions at every company.

title: ... has sound quality come from $1500 speakers if not better. I am an experienced audiophile that spent tens ...
text: These $15 speakers (Logitech Z130) has sound quality come from $1500 speakers if not better. I am an experienced audiophile who had spent tens of thousands on audio system in the past and yet these little dinky Logitech computer speakers have just as good sound. The treble sound is insanely crisp. It is clear and VERY crisp. There is no discernible noise and muddiness. It doesn't have that same level of wide stereo imaging-effect and openness like the high-end mid-range drivers speakers (Adam & Focal for example) have, but the crispness and freshness of treble sound these Logitech speakers provide makes up for it. It is great for near field listening obviously you can't turn up the volume too high as these have 5 watt music power. I was really surprised how much hidden details these speakers put out in the highs. It has unique quality and characteristics of sound that no other speakers have. Something is seriously wrong with the Logitech manufacturer only charging 15 bucks for this thing... it should've been priced $1500.  Prior to purchasing these speakers I didn't have anticipation getting such great sound but I was dead wrong after listening to them. They are stellar. I was going to upgrade my speakers to Audioengine A2 speakers in the near future but forget it.... I'll stick with these $15 speakers.  These speakers deserve 6 stars in this review but it does not allow me to choose 6 stars but 5 stars... Take my words for it these speakers are really that good.

title: my only regret is not buying it sooner
text:
The remote to my A/V receiver had some buttons that weren't working, and my DirecTV remote had seen better days, so I bought this, my first universal remote.

Setup:

I connected it to my computer with the supplied USB cable, went to the website, and the experience was mostly smooth. I had to install software for setup but that was easy. It would be nice if they gave a dropdown list for models when you choose a manufacturer, but I had the info so it wasn't a problem. I had an account created and my devices registered in under 10 minutes. The hard part came when I wanted to assign buttons. You get an image of the Harmony remote and click on the button you'd like to assign, then choose the command from a list for the remote it's replacing. What they don't tell you is that you have to click on the word "assign" which appears to the right; I kept trying to click the name of the button when it highlighted and getting no response. After you do assign buttons you then have to click "sync" for the changes to be programmed to the remote. That was 15 total minutes of needless frustration. After that it was all done, I could make use of the 5 favorite channel buttons to choose my input source. There's also one button which powers everything on or off with a single press, though the remote has to be far enough back for all my devices to be successfully targeted.

Ease of use:

The type on the source buttons is small so I took a minute to commit to memory which one controls what, and now it's intuitive. The remote itself is extremely comfortable to hold, and I like the feel of the volume and channel buttons in particular as they can easily be identified in the dark. I'm easily able to do everything on my DirecTV box I could with the original without any reconfiguring needed. Button presses register very easily and consistently provided you aim reasonably well.

What could be better:

I really wish this remote had Bluetooth functionality so I could use it on my computer and Playstation. I wasn't willing to drop a fortune on one of the high end Harmony remotes and have a cradle, hub and other such things creating clutter. I'm not sure why it can't do what a $25 PS3 remote can without all the extras.

Final thoughts:

I paid $39 for this and it's well worth the price. It feels fancy, looks nice and is highly responsive.

title: What could be the best mouse on the market is crippled by a severely broken scroll wheel system
text:
In so many ways this mouse is amazing, and i'll get into all of that in a moment. But there is one flaw, that I find quite significant that is crippling this mouse from being likely the best on the market. My review of the G502 Proteus Spectrum:

Let's talk about all of the positives, because there are so many in my opinion of this mouse. I just recently built a new high end PC for gaming primarily, and wanted to overhaul all of my peripherals including my mouse. I've been a long, long time Logitech fanboy ever since my first gaming rig well over a decade ago. To this day, I still use my MX518 (One of the best mice ever) at work full time. So for me this is incredibly hard to rate a Logitech mouse lower than a 5 star.

The PROS:
+ The best optical sensor currently on the market as of mid 2016. This sensor is amazing and reacts far better than you can likely even fathom.
+ Weight tuning - If you like a heavier mouse, this will be perfect. That being said, even without any extra weights added from the removable compartment, it's still quite heavy. I utilize this mouse with a 'Control' mat (cloth type vs plastic/pvs) and it's so far been great for all around genres of games, yes even including FPS's.
+ Buttons - If you want a mouse with a boat load of buttons, but not as many as an MMO specific mouse, this is by far the best choice on the market.
+ Design - This is super comfortable for mid to larger sized hands. As I mentioned earlier, I still use my MX518 and it's a natural progression from that mouse I believe.
+ RGB Lighting - This is a cool feature in which with the Logitech software you can edit basic functionality as well as colors for the "G" logo and dpi switch lights. They can breathe, switch colors, or just be static one color.

The CONS:
- The mouse button furthest up from your hand (the dpi hold) is a bit of a stretch unless you're playing full palm grip. I'm more of a blended claw/palm natural grip so I find that button usually just out of comfortable reach. Everything else is a breeze to reach.
- Semi-frequently i'll accidentally tap the dip up button instead of the right-click button. They are close together and depending on your hand posture this may accidentally happen.
- THE BIGGEST CON....The mouse wheel is awful. Here's the thing, it has a 'infinite scroll' lock feature that could be awesome, but it's completely non-functionally good. When you have infinite scroll enabled, the wheel is terribly unbalanced, meaning that it'll roll the opposite direction when you stop scrolling just enough to scroll several lines up or down on whatever you were viewing such as a webpage. It's obnoxious and there is no easy or even moderate way I've found to fix this (some people have hybrid tore apart this mouse with the Proteus Core that doesn't seem to have this issue!)
When you have the infinite scroll disabled, you get a very tactile click, but it's quite loud and feels very clunky. It functions yes, but by far the worse 'normal' scroll method I've ever used.
And lastly with the scroll wheel, and most importantly - IT RATTLES! There is a gap that makes the scroll wheel not sit in firm, so it actually moves left and right before engaging the left/right mouse wheel click. This means that during normal, average use, my mouse wheel bounces left and right by a few centimeters, and since it's not a rubber wheel, you hear it rattling (you can Youtube this to hear what i'm talking about). This to me is entirely unacceptable and what in my thought completely cripples this mouse from being the best on the market still.

So here's the deal - I've started an RMA with Logitech on this. Amazon wouldn't do an exchange (for some reason) only a return, and I purchased this mouse on a $20 discount from normal MSRP. I wasn't about to pay more for the same mouse in case this is a known feature, which i'm having trouble confirming entirely.
Logitech support has been painfully slow, days sometimes an entire week go by before I get a very basic response. They've stated that this isn't a known feature or issue of the mouse, but here's the thing...I went to a local Best Buy and had them open one too...It also had this issue!! Crazy rattling scroll wheel! I then proceeded to look into Logitech Forums, and there are a few others that have also posted about this, but Logitech claims this isn't intended behavior. So at this point i'm super skeptical. It's either a known issue with the Proteus Spectrum only (NOTE- Proteus Core users don't seem to have this issue at all). I'll keep plugging away with the RMA to see what happens, but this really bites as I want to love this mouse.

So here's my closing - Once this RMA goes through, if my new Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum doesn't have this scroll wheel rattling crap, I'll update this review and sing the highest of praises and 5 star this review in a heart beat. I'm skeptical, but still hopeful a bit.

text:

So, the problem was the Bluetooh unit, I didn't want to buy another Bluetooth unit receiver, so I decided to get a Wireless Keyboard, not Bluetooth.

And I found this one!
It's really really really good! I really like the keys, they feel well, really soft, the keyboard has a small hole to put in there the usb nano receiver while is not in use (really helpful to not to loose it). It has the button On/Off at the back, and it also has two little kicks to stand up the keyboard better. It also includes three caps from different colors, that you can change. This is the cap for the AAA batteries.
What I like the most is that sometimes I leave my laptop hibernating if I go to drink coffee meanwhile or just doing another thing away from my laptop, and I really like that you can turn off the keyboard to save batteries, or just leave it On, and as soon as you start using it again it works immediately, you don't have to press buttons to start it again.

It's really a wonderful keyboard! I wish I had found it sooner! And avoid all the Bluetooth problems I had.
I recommend this keyboard and I think Logitech is a very nice brand, I also have a wireless mouse from this brand and both work as a charm.
I have had this keyboard for just a few days, but hopefully it will continue to work well.
I'll update this in a few months!

If you're in this for advertising or anything similar you DO NOT need the pro! This will suit you just fine! Yes, the pro can record at a much higher quality, but your recordings will always be limited by the quality of the speakers your clients will listen to them on and, in 95% of households and businesses, they will never have a full blown, amazing sound system. So, all that extra quality is totally lost. In the rare case they do have an awesome sound system, they will absolutely never hear the difference. Honestly, they just absolutely will never know the difference.

In conclusion. Get this mic. Stop searching, stop deliberating, just get this freakin' mic. Thank you.

Programming was quite simple using the App for my Ipad. Was was able to program almost all functions as needed. I lost one thing, the voice button for my Amazon Fire Stick. The Amazon remote operates via Bluetooth and did not have the voice button feature built into the programming. I contacted tech support via email and received a prompt reply. (this feature was not already in their database and could not be added at this time.)
During my troubleshooting, I did find that you could learn any IR function from any remote, but couldn't learn any Bluetooth functions. You only get what they have already in the data base. Which in my case everything worked except for the one voice button.

I like the basic remote. It is fits just right and give you the ability to do 6 different settings for what I need. If you need more then 6, you will need a different remote. The hub and IR blaster took a few tries to get the proper placement to control everything, but once I found the proper spots everything operates as it should. With the hub in addition to using the remote, you can use the app on any smartphone or Tablet to control the components. Its a really nice feature.

Overall I am very happy with the remote, however I deducted a star due to losing the voice button on my Amazon Fire Stick.

title: Fantastic controller works for most any game.
text:
First off I have owned one of these for around 5 years after going from a Microsoft sidewinder and it is night and day difference. Of course the sidewinder was OLDER technology. I no longer need to use anything but my mouse and this controller to play virtually any game I have. It is so easy to use I had to get one for my wife. The screen on it will display info on the game your playing like DPS, HP and other things *game dependent* and when your not playing a game it will scroll between news feeds and computer info like CPU usage and RAM usage. It will also display songs you are listening to if your using media player.

Pros: First off the controller is very well made and comfortable to use even when you have somewhat inflexible fingers like I do. The programming options are endless. The controller will import the standard key profile for dozens of different games. So if you have a game like say Call of Duty the profile it imports will automatically assign the various keyboard and special key functions to the controller automatically and assign it as a profile that you can change the key layout any way you choose. It will also recognize when you launch one of the games that are in the it's profile list and switch to the key profile for that game. You can also change the default key mappings for each key of a any of the profiles to how you want them or just create your own custom key mappings. The smaller buttons above the keys allow you to switch the current profile to a different one and you can set your favorite profile as default and even lock it so you have to push one of the small buttons to change to a different one. It allows you to change the color of the display as well as the keys. The thumb stick takes a little getting used to but anyone that has used a game pad will be okay with it. I use it for strafing and forward and back controls it works a lot easier and is more fluid than using the keyboard imo. You can store your key mappings for you favorite games on the controllers memory so if you plug it into a different computer your profiles will be there.

Cons: None really except that occasionally if you haven't been using it for awhile and you launch a game it might not do anything but if you unplug it and then plug it back up it works fine.

title: Sound great, but.....
text:
First off I want to say that I really wanted to like these headphones. I originally, bought them to use on my Xbox One console, but unfortunately I did not have the adapter I needed to plug them into the Xbox One's controller, so I decided to use them with my PC while I wait for a decent completely wireless headset for the Xbox One to be released....but that is a different rant. Anyway, back to the PC.

After having them for a couple months I can say I like the physical aspects of the G933s. The headphones are comfortable, decently light on my head during extended gaming sessions, and I have become proficient with accessing the controls on the headset by touch instead of taking them off and looking at which button I needed to push. Even the auto-powering down after 5 minutes is acceptable since all I have to do is adjust the volume and they turn right back on. Additionally, after tweaking the sound settings, they sound amazing. Listening to music while doing my chores or working on my PC is fantastic. Getting surround sound effects while playing my first player games like Skyrim, and Fallout 4, is totally immersive. The rotation of sounds and the deepness of the low frequencies is awesome. Multiplayer games....not so much.

I don't know if it is my Windows 10 setup, the G933s themselves, or just bad mojo....but I can't get these headphones to work consistently while trying to chat. I bought the G933s so that I could talk to my friends on Xbox, but like I said I haven't used them on that system. Trying to use them for Skype, online Chat in Steam, or just trying to record personal notes to my PC has been a nightmare. I've opened a support ticket with Logitech, but other than some automated responses they have been unhelpful to say the least.

These issues the G933s are having while trying to chat, none of these issues appeared on the other two wired headsets I use on my computer. Basically, I just want to be able to chat with the G933s and I am hoping an update in the next few months will sort out these problems until that time I guess I am stuck using my old wired headphones.

title: Awesome
text: I have purchased three of these.  I have two older Harman Kardon receivers and a Kenwood, all of which lack Bluetooth connectivity.  I hooked this Logitech receiver up to the "TAPE/PLAY" inputs on the receivers to remain consistent throughout the house, and plugged the power adapter into the "SWITCHED" input on each receiver.  Once paired, this setup is awesome!  Connects instantly to my Galaxy S5 as soon as I power the receiver on.  I renamed each BT connection in my phone to reference the room the receiver is in (i.e. "Logitech BT Bedroom") to eliminate confusion.  I can tell no difference between the audio from my phone and my CD players.  The range is very good too.  I can be in my upstairs bathroom and control my HK receiver downstairs in the living room flawlessly.  I really like that this device has RCA outputs rather than a 3.5mm jack leading to RCA's like most of these receivers, because the 3.5 connection is a poor one that can introduce static and other problems.  I had three sets of good quality gold plated RCA L/R cables in storage, so I used them to make my connections.  I read about a lot of people having real problems with the connection tone the Logitech makes through the speakers when pairing or unpairing.  By hooking my three up to the switch on the back of the receiver, my phone only pairs when I turn the receiver on, I hear the low volume tone once, which I don't mind at all, and then when I turn the receiver off, that cuts power to the Logitech, so I don't even hear the disconnect tone.  Not only do I not mind this irrelevant tone, I'd much prefer it than not, because it confirms my Galaxy S5 has connected properly.  This device has brought all three of my receivers up to speed with current technology.  They lack HDMI connectivity too, but I solved that with the Kinivo HDMI hubs and a J-Tech HDMI digital audio extractor. Both are a must have for older receivers when you have lots of HDMI devices like I do.  Overall, I am thrilled with these Logitech units and hope to get years of use out of them.

title: Cheapest Feeling Logitech Mouse in My Brood
text:
Having used a HP Spectre with only two USB ports for two and a half years, and having to unplug the Logitech nano unifying receiver for my mouse whenever I need to review the contents of multiple USB drives, I thought it was time I got a Bluetooth mouse. (Well, at first I considered a USB 3.0 hub, but there are some scary stories about those corrupting USB drives.) Getting a Start button that can be set as an application switcher would be a bonus.

I have used Logitech mice exclusively as long as I remember. My daily mice are: an Anywhere MX (at home), a M560 at work, and a M325 in my laptop bag. (I have a collection of M325 mice because I almost always buy more when they are on sale for $10.) I have an old wired laser MX 400 (in case of emergency), and an unused T400 (that I never got used to due to the touch strip) on my office desk acting as a decoy. This M557 looks and feels cheaper than all of them.

As other reviewers have commented, the M557 mouse has buttons that click too easily. While I have not used it very much so far, this does lend to a very cheap feel. All of my other Logitech mice, even the $10 M325, have a textured rubber grip on both sides; the M557 has hard shiny plastic sides. This mouse also has a strangely designed bottom cover that is almost impossible to latch after replacing the batteries.

title: Great replacement
text:
Great replacement for my old keyboard which had been through the wringer. The best part about this keyboard is that it has a very clear "on/off" switch. So when you spill a glass of soda over the keyboard and then try to wipe it off as fast as possible you don't accidentally hit that one crazy combination of keys that turns your computer permanently into something indecipherable. That's what happened to my old keyboard. Backspace had turned into \. Delete typed an "H". One key shut the computer down. So I won't kill this one the same way! The price is definitely worth the peace of mind.

And if you do completely lose keyboard functionality? Win + U will bring up an onscreen keyboard that you can use to try to get your computer back. I'm glad I have this and I'm planning on getting another one as a backup....just in case I forget about the on/off switch! It is very clear and the light lets you know that it's on but only after you've flipped the switch. The rest of the time the light isn't on, so it isn't distracting. Great job Logitech!

title: Best One Yet
text:
I have been through a lot of these HTPC keyboards. There's always some kind of issue. The last brand/model I had I actually smashed to pieces in a fit of rage. I was having a bad day and the keyboard wasn't co-operating. So good anger management. The roller ball was lagging and it was randomly clicking on stuff.

After that, I actually switched to a standard wired USB keyboard and mouse. Partially due to wanting to avoid the EMF exposure. But I decided, when I'm watching TV on my 55" LED, EMF is sort of a wash anyways. I can't be a purist and I don't seam to be as EMF sensitive these days due to improved health. The long USB wires across the room were making me crazy so convenience won out. I mean if someone trips on a USB cable and breaks their nose, would being EMF protected be really safe? Anyways! I love the switch on the back of this keyboard for this very reason (EMF). It's a nice compromise. You can kill the keyboard when not in use. Saves battery and cuts the wireless chatter. I never checked it with a meter but in theory it seams to fit.

About the actual keyboard. I love that it uses NORMAL batteries. I've had it with rechargables. Every rechargeable battery I own holds less of a charge every week. I'd rather use normal batteries and not have to worry about it. I recycle all my batteries so no guilt.

The keyboard is weighted perfectly. It's not cheap and flimsy. The keys are firm but not too much so. The track pad is a little slow but I'm thinking that could probably be configured in mouse settings. No problems connecting and staying connected. No missed keystrokes. No phantom clicking. Keys are in a compact arrangement but not too cramped. A lot like a small laptop. I think a lot of thought went into designing this. I can dig it.

The long-term test is how it does over time. We shall see. I seam to go through one keyboard every 8-10 months. Hopefully this one lasts longer.

text:
Last time I bought a Logitech camera was years ago. Have been using the Microsoft Lifecam Cinema and Studio.

Bought a C920 two days ago in Miami as everyone seems to be using it. Hooked it up to my HP and right away saw that I could have saved my money.

1/ Looks ok indoors if using for video chatting. Outdoors is another story, not suitable as a weather cam. Seems not to be able to handle the bright sunlight. Colors off, image looks washed out and all the messing around with the software won't get it close to what the Lifecam Studio produces.

2/ Sharpness is not all that sharp. Much finer detail with both versions of Microsoft cameras.

For me. another one of those "file it away" products.

UPDATE: Have since discovered that the video sharpness can be greatly improved by uninstalling the Logitech Drivers and using the built-in drivers in the Windows Operating System. Go to Control Panel / Programmes and Features. Double click Logitech Webcam Software. Choose the 3rd Option, Uninstall Drivers and execute. Unplug the camera, plug it back in and you're good to go.

text:
The headset itself is decent. It is pretty comfortable, has good sound, and is easy to use. I would have to say, I would probably consider this a good buy if it were half the price. Unfortunately, for the hefty price tag it carries I can't with good conscious give it sparkling review. It is very comparable to headsets that are 1/4 the price as far as audio quality and unfortunately the short battery life and the fact you have to plug it in to charge is just too much of an inconvenience.

Finally, let's talk about the customer service Logitech provides. I have owned this headset for about a year now. I went to put it on the other day and one of the ear pieces literally fell off in my hands. Now, I have owned well over 20 headsets in my life, some of them expensive and other pretty cheap. Out of all those headsets, I have never had this happen. I stepped on one before and broke it, but I have never had it fall apart during everyday use; especially in less than a year! So, I promptly put in a service ticket for support complete with pictures, a receipt of purchase, and as many details as I could possibly provide to help them verify and complete the service request. And I waited ...

About 5 days had passed without so much as a "we have received your ticket and are reviewing your case. We will follow-up with you in x days." nothing ... Just the automated reply that the ticket had been created. It was at this point that I decided to follow-up with someone via their live online chat. I spoke with someone who did not offer any information on how long the process would take, what I should expect as far as how the RMA process worked, anything ... They simply updated my support ticket with the fact that they put in a request for replacement. Isn't this what I already had done? I followed up with them and absolutely nothing. At this point it has been over a week since my initial request, with absolutely no idea how much longer it is going to take. Long story short ... I will be ordering a replacement headset and am leaving this review.

title: This mouse = NOT READY FOR PRIME TIME!
text:
I wanted to like this.

Somehow my Logitech Wireless M510 mouse disappeared from my desk at work. While I'm not making any accusations, somehow I don't think the mouse came to life and scurried off my desk by itself while I was off to lunch. So, I went on here (Amazon) and ordered the M325. It was a bit less expensive, and was - after all - a Logitech.

I received it via Prime two days later, hooked it up, and… Not impressed. It felt funny in my hands… a little small. Certainly not as comfortable as the M510 I enjoyed before. Having only one battery, the "life" would be shorter, meaning replacing the battery sooner. That's not so bad, because I'm sure it still lasts a long time. Other than feeling a little weird (in comparison to the more comfortable M510) and being too small, the smoothness of the tracking itself on my clean mouse pad was a few levels worse than my beloved M510. It seemed like the optic window wasn't as effective as Logitech's (albeit more expensive) offering.

So, what do I do? Return it? That can be a hassle. No, we have a very nice and young office receptionist who is somewhat short and has tiny hands. We had given her a laptop for Christmas because she is such a wonderful employee. I asked her if she was enjoying her laptop (she was) and asked if she was using a mouse with it at home. She said she didn't have a mouse. *** BOOM! *** Now she had a mouse. Nice and small for her tiny hands.

If you are a user of average or better height with average or better hands, and enjoy a mouse with near perfect tracking capabilities… I urge you to purchase the M510 instead. Sometimes paying more is worth it.

title: Bad range, strange queuing of input system
text:
I tried to use this in my living room, about 6ft from the receiver, but the signal was so inconsistent at that distance. Now I use it in my office, where it sits 1ft from the receiver (with a plastic table in between the keyboard and receiver), but it still occasionally doesn't seem to register. It says it uses 2.4Ghz wireless, but it almost feels like IR, because objects in between the keyboard and receiver greatly affect it's ability to function.

- Additionally, it has this strange way of sending the input when it doesn't have a good signal, If it is "out-of-range" it seems to queue up all the keys I've typed, and when I move the keyboard "into range", it sends all the queued up keys. It seems like it would be a useful feature, if the signal was cutting in and out, but it seems to always forget the first key I typed. This leads me to believe it is in a standby mode when it's out of range, then switches to a logging mode after a key is pressed and starts logging the input, until it is brought into the range of a receiver.

title: Third Time's The Charm
text:
I had been using a K360 with my Mac, but I decided that I'd like a wireless keyboard built specifically for Apple machines, so I took the plunge and bought this.

I originally purchased the silver model, but it had a defect, so I returned it. The plastic above the Logitech logo was warped and wasn't fully attached to the outer casing. The font on the buttons also looked a little different than it did in the images on Amazon, so for a second I thought that maybe I had received a knockoff. When I re-ordered, I decided to try the black version since it matched a little better with my setup.

Within 5 seconds of opening this second unit, I was unhappy. Why this time? There was an air bubble under the right solar panel that couldn't be removed. At first I thought that I had missed removing some of the plastic that covered the keys, but upon closer inspection, it was definitely an air bubble. I looked around online, and discovered that some people have encountered this before. The bubble didn't impact the functionality of the keyboard at all, but for almost $60, I felt like I should get a unit that's as close to perfect as possible, so back this one went too.

I got my third one today, and I'm happy to say it looks and works fine. The keys are just deep enough that you can easily type without looking, as opposed to Apple's who I feel are just shallow enough to be unsettling. All of the keys do exactly what they say they do, and it paired up without a problem.

My only question now is durability. I've never had any issues with past Logitech peripherals, so I'm hoping to continue that run with the K750. As of now, the ambient lighting in my office seems to be enough to keep it charged, and I don't have any lag from hitting the button to seeing the character on the screen. I had read some reviews about the battery not being able hold a charge after a few months, so time will tell. For now though, this is an awesome keyboard, and I would recommend it.

title: Waste of My Money
text:
I've been looking for a food HTPC keyboard and the K830 seemed like a great option but it didn't support Bluetooth, it seemed silly to waste a USB port for a custom wireless technology when every computer since forever has built-in Bluetooth. When Logitech finally updated the K830 with Bluetooth support I decided to take the plunge. Unfortunately, this won't connect to my Windows 10 PC via Bluetooth (it's a Kangaroo mobile desktop PC, which supports Bluetooth 4.0 and LE). There's also no support for this issue! A few other people on the Logitech forums have the same problem but the responders either explain how to connect via Bluetooth, which are exactly the same steps in the manual, or they say it doesn't support Bluetooth. Well, it has a Bluetooth symbol on the del key and it connects to my iPad mini and my iPhone. Neither of those devices support Logitech's Unifying dongle but they do support Bluetooth, so my K830 clearly supports Bluetooth. (It won't connect to my Apple TV or Xbox One either. It doesn't advertise that it will so I'm not disappointed, just putting it out there in case anyone reading this was curious about other devices).

To make matters worse, it does work via the port-wasting proprietary Unifying adapter, but it won't wake my PC so I have to find an alternative method of waking it, and then I have to re-pair the keyboard. Every time.

So...the keyboard works, just not for me. If you buy it, be aware that there are some PCs out there that the Bluetooth won't work with. The issue is probably very limited (based on the lack of useful support) so it was a waste of time and money for me, ymmv.

The keyboard itself is ok. The keys are a little mushy but not bad. The trackpad is accurate and the multitouch gestures work fine, but the space is a bit limited. The backlit keys are what I was looking forward to the most and they don't disappoint. Unfortunately since I can't reliably connect it, they serve no purpose. I'll be returning this.

title: Defective Product, Ripped off by Logitech Support
text:
I rarely leave bad reviews, but this experience has been interesting to say the least. This review is as much a criticism as the keyboard as it is a criticism of Logitech Support. This keyboard was great for a month. It is compact, stylish, medium-travel on keys, quiet, and just overall well-built. However, at exactly one month after purchase, my "A" key ceased functioning. I am excellent with technology and underwent every conceivable troubleshooting step to identify that the key was in fact broken (different usb ports, different computers, reinstallation of drivers, etc...). The keyboard had never been submerged or washed before the key stopped functioning.

I called Logitech Support and, after troubleshooting, they agreed that the keyboard was in fact defective and eligible under the one-month warranty for replacement. Logitech support said that the product is discontinued (no indication of that given upon purchase), so instead of a one-for-one replacement, I had to select a keyboard of equal value. As far as I'm concerned: fair enough. Here's where it gets good. Logitech support told me to select a keyboard valuing at $29.99 or less, since their "system" reads that the MSRP for this keyboard is $29.99, even though I bought it for $79.99 from the Amazon Logitech store and had the receipt to prove it. At this point they're trying to move the rest of these discontinued keyboards, so the going price has fallen to ~$60 over the course of the last month and continues to fall. This product is rapidly becoming cheaper as retailers are trying to move it, but when I purchased it in August, the going price was $79.99. Logitech Support has left the case unresolved and refuses to honor the original purchase price. If you buy this, and yours holds up, I'm sure its a great keyboard. However, if you get a lemon like I did, expect to get the runaround from Logitech and then ultimately end up with an inferior replacement product due to the arbitrary MSRP adjustment.
