title: Good home entertainment control system, but not for Chromecasts and Fire Sticks
text:
The Logitech harmony remote and hub is a good system. I wish the Amazon rating system can do 1/2 stars, so I could give it 3 1/2 stars, but I'm going to give it the benefit of the doubt and give it 4 stars because it truly does work better than most other systems I've tried. Although there is not much documentation, I did find the system relatively easy to set up. For reference, I will say that I have this Net Gear router: [[ASIN:B00MRVJY5C Netgear R7500 Nighthawk X4 AC2350 Dual Band WiFi Router]] .I had no trouble connecting the Harmony hub to this router in my house. I also have the Lutron Homekit hub: [[ASIN:B00XPW67ZM Lutron L-BDG2-WH Caseta Wireless Smart Bridge, HomeKit-enabled]] and the system found all the lights connected to this hub as well. Any lights that are on can be seen in the IOS app on my phone and tablet.

For setup, the system asks you the manufacturer and model number of your device. Then it loads the codes needed for the device to work. If you input a model number that it does not know about, then you can use the existing remote for that device to program the hub. To do this, you just need to connect the hub to a laptop, with the supplied USB cable, and then follow the instruction on the screen. The instructions tell you point the remote to the hub and press and few buttons so that it could figure out what codes the remote uses for your device. I had one device that it did not recognize and I had to do this step. After I did it, then my device was connected to the system and worked properly. The hub also recognized that I had an Amazon Fire TV connected to my TV and guided me through setting that up to work with the hub as well. I also have a Chromecast Video and a Chromecast Audio in the house and the system found both of them. However, the hub got confused about which one was a Chromecast Video and a Chromecast Audio and I still haven't figure out how to tell it to distinguish one from the other.

Setting up an activity was also not too bad. Connecting my receiver, TV, and cable box together was not too bad. I can setup and activity that turns on the TV and power on the receiver, as that is the way my Av system currently works. I can even schedule the activity to come on at a certain time of the day. The scheduling feature also includes controlling devices at Sunrise and Sunset. However, what is missing is the X minutes before/after Sunrise/Sunset feature. The other note worthy thing I found that can be done is turn on an activity, or a device, when I'm not on my home Wi-Fi. This was a welcomed surprise as I have not seen this mentioned in a lot of reviews I have read.

The big issue I have is with the Amazon Echo IFTTT integration. Basically, it's hot or miss. Sometimes the trigger works and sometimes it does not. I can definitely control the all devices with the IOS app. But using Echo to trigger an activity just doesn't work reliably. I can hear the "ding" notification on my phone when the IFTTT trigger happens, but the activity sometimes does not happen. I wish there was native Alexa integration as the Echo integration was one of the primary reasons I bought this system. So, the faulty IFTTT and Echo integration is really a bummer for me.

Also, I find the user interface dated. It doesn't feel like something that was written for the year 2016. It feels clunky. It feels like something that was written in the 1990s.

Also, I wish it had Apple Homekit integration so that it could recognize all the other Homekit appliances I have. However, besides the faulty IFTTT/Echo integration and lack of Homekit support, I still recommend the system.

Update 11-02-2016:

After using this device for a while, I've lowered my rating for the following reasons: First, when the software finds a Chromecast or Fire Stick, it does not use the name that is associated with these devices. Further, when it finds multiple Chromecasts and multiple Fire Stick, it names them Chromecast 1, Chromecast 2, etc.... Fire Stick 1, Fire Stick 2, etc. So now, it's up to the user to figure out which device is which. If Logitech would do, what all other software does in this case, which is query the devices for the names, then this issue would not come up. Bu they don't, so it's up to the user to rename the devices back to what they originally was named. If the software finds Chromecast Audios and Chromcast Videos, then the system really gets confused. It simply doesn't know what to do with Chromecast Audios.

Next, Logitech does not realize Chromecasts and Fire Sticks implement HDMI-CEC. This means, sending these devices a signal will make them turn on the TV and switch to the right input. You don't need to associated a TV input with them in this software. It's just not necessary. Logitech forces user to associate a TV with these devices, and does not give the option not to do so. When adding a TV, to an activity, you don't have a lot of flexibility as to what you can do with it. For instance, when I tell Alexa to turn off a Chromecast, or a Fire Stick, I'd like the option to switch the TV input back to cable, instead of turning the TV off. This option is not there. The whole system is very inflexible when it comes to controlling Chromecasts and Fire Sticks.

The new Alexa integration is good, but the user interface is flawed. Once you go to the Harmony Alexa Skill to set it up, you have to go back to the Alex app to disable, re-enable, and reconnect the account, just to make changes. It's not a great user experience.

title: Harmony 650 - hallelujah!!
text:
We have an older Bose CineMate Series II that no remote code exists for and no other universal remote will control.The tiny remote which controls it constantly gets lost in the chairs, couch, pockets. FINALLY we can control it perfectly from the same Harmony 650 remote we now use to control every feature of our Samsung 60" Smart TV and various international DVD players, Roku and ATV.
Why we didn't buy this utterly wonderful godsend years ago I don't know but I'm never going back to six remotes piled on the table.

1. Setup was simplicity itself using the computer (Win7Pro) and downloaded Logitech Harmony software. Take some pictures of your devices (DVD, Roku etc) exact model numbers with your phone before you start and you're done with the hardest step in my opinion. Setting up the 7 devices we use was a breeze following simple onscreen flow steps. No need to point our old remotes at the Harmony etc. Total time to perfectly working Harmony 650 - 20 minutes.
2. Ergonomics - button layout is excellent. Imagine the transport buttons (play, rew, f fwd) and main arrow keys right under your thumb where they should be instead of the awful Samsung remotes and ATT Uverse mess. Keys are beautifully placed and satisfying to press with great spacing.
3. Screen on the remote is very good - not something I've had to pay much attention to so far but it's well lit and easy to read. Having the extra "did everything turn on? If not press.." is helpful for my younger kids who may need it.
4. Construction and quality - it feels like a solid remote that can survive the drops and bangs all remotes endure. Ours was nicely finished cosmetically and nothing tacky or gimmicky whatsoever. I'd be happy having it out even in higher end home theaters.

I've used models above this one briefly and they just failed to accomplish things any better or more efficiently for most home TV and entertainment systems. I am not experienced with Alexa enabled models but we often use iPhone and iPad apps to control Roku, Netflix, Samsung.
To me this remote is a must-have and outstanding value. Gets the job done beautifully without requiring too much time or ability to get it all up and running.

title: You can spend a lot more for a mouse, but why?
text: This is probably the fifth or sixth M325 I have bought, not because they break down, but because I buy them for friends and for additional equipment (tablets/notebooks/home video security system/etc.)  Long ago, I started out my computer use with a trackball because back then the mice were wired and didn't respond to movement all that reliably (and I absolutely hate moving a mouse with no corresponding cursor movement).  The resolution required one to pick up the mouse and drag it some more on a crowded desk or mouse pad to get the cursor across the screen.  Very inconvenient and a trackball worked much better.  For the longest time I was very much "anti-mouse."  ...Until my girlfriend needed help with her computer and I used her mouse.  It was a lower end model (M-317), but I was immediately surprised at how well it worked.  It was wireless, sensitive to movement, and had enough resolution to make picking up the mouse unnecessary.  That afternoon we went out and got a couple of the M-325s because they have the tilt wheel (very handy for surfing the Internet) and a longer battery life.  I have been using mine ever since then, to the point that I've worn the little slider pads off the underside, but it still works very well, and with approximately 18 months on a single AA battery I very rarely turn the mouse off (it has an auto sleep mode after a period of no movement).  Over the years I've used other brands of wireless mice while helping friends with their computer woes, but I keep buying the Logitech brand because I have been spoiled.  They are a superior product in my experience.

title: Scroll wheel may work on Windows PCs, but it fails on Mac OS Sierra on MacBook Pro
text:
The scroll wheel is unusable for me with Mac OS Sierra 10.12.1 on my 2015 MacBook Pro (Retina, 13-inch, Early 2015). Sometimes scrolling one "click" will race forward multiple lines of text, sometimes scrolling ten clicks doesn't scroll the page at all. It's completely unpredictable and unreliable.

The Logitech Control Center for Macintosh OS X doesn't include support for this model, M325. The wizard recognizes the USB dongle, but the wizard doesn't find the mouse. The Advanced tab can be used to pair the mouse manually, but none of the Logitech Unifying Software features work (battery level, upgrade firmware, etc.).

While the product description reads, "Logitech Wireless Mouse M325 with Designed-For-Web Scrolling", it should also specify, "... except on Mac OS Sierra."

I wouldn't recommend this mouse for use with Mac OS at all, and I won't buy another Logitech mouse for use with my Mac.

text:
Bought one of these two years ago at Walmart for $5 during a sale. Still works great. However, only 4 stars because I think the $15 price tag they currently have is too high. Would definitely buy another $5 one though. More than worth it.

Had a problem a couple times where it stopped working (Cursor stuck, not moving). I just turned it off, took out the battery, put it back in and turned it on and the problem stopped. But let's be honest, you're not going to use this for gaming or anything serious, so the occasional stuck cursor, as easy a fix as it is, isn't going to cause you problems.

Item is very light, which I love, and has a high enough DPI (1000DPI) that I never have to pick up and move the mouse just to move across the screen. I just use it with my laptop, since track pads are awful. And it is the perfect weight/size to just keep with you for laptop use.

Basically, the conclusion is, if you can find it for a little cheaper, maybe even $10, definitely pick one up, you'll find some use for it.

title: Good little mouse but scroll wheel and clicking sounds are a bit annoying.
text:
The good:

1. Small, portable, and feels sturdy
I bought this mouse because I wanted something that's not too bulky and portable to carry around. This fits comfortably but is a bit on the smaller side (there's room between the bottom of my palm and the back of mouse. (My hands are pretty average sized, FYI).

2. Scroll wheel is smooth
Most mouses I've used have those little clicks when using the scroll wheel that makes you scroll in increments, but this one is smooth. My manager at work has the exact same mouse and I find it hilarious how she aggressively scrolls/flies through her documents as the wheel makes this whizzing sound (this sound could be pretty loud for those who care to know).

The bad:

1. Scroll wheel is smooth
Although I've grown to like the smooth scroll wheel, it always makes me over-scroll when I'm working on something that's really zoomed-up. Scroll wheels with the little clicks actually prevent me from over-scrolling.

2. Tad glitchy
On the rare occasion, the mouse decides it doesn't want to work for me anymore and refuses to move. It's rare but happens enough for me to develop the habit of popping out the batteries and reinserting them to make this work again.

3. Thin/flimsy clicking sounds
The clicking sounds coming from this mouse are thin, high-pitched, and - dare I say - unsatisfying. I personally prefer Microsoft mouses in this aspect.

4. Non-ergonomic
This was not a factor in deducting stars because I knew this was not meant to be an extremely ergonomic mouse (plus I bought it for its portability). After months of use, I've developed pretty bad cramps which means I'm going to have to move on to an ergonomic mouse.

title: BEWARE: Rip Off by selling you defective device!!!
text:
Amazon and their 3rd party seller, NetZero, have both refused to exchange our defective device or refund our money to purchase another one, so we are left with a defective Harmony All In One unit and out all the money spent on the device. This was my email to Amazon and NetZero, and neither will make things right. As a regular, dedicated, and loyal Amazon customer, I am extremely disappointed. I guess Amazon is getting so big that they no longer care about their customers. And NetZero sells DEFECTIVE PRODUCTS AND WON'T STAND BY THEIR PRODUCTS!! Shame on them both!!

"We have had a technician install and deal with this, but without luck for more than a day or two before something goes wrong again. He has come back to tweak things over 10 times, but things are so complicated and difficult to get to work (if at all!) that we are disgusted with this situation all together. This Harmony system has failed us when having company over several times and embarrassed us, b/c then, with company, we can't get our Direct TV to work, Amazon Fire Stick to work, our Netflix to work, etc.

The specific issues (we believe) about why this product hasn't worked since we received it, are usually surrounding the TV inputs changing all on their own, which controls our Amazon Fire Stick and Direct TV, not being acknowledged at all, and therefore can't use our TV at all. The actual Harmony Remote acts like it is possessed and starts changing the channels all by itself and keeps scrolling through the channels without stopping or will not respond when we push a button at all.

We have given up on this particular Harmony unit. We are on the fence about ordering another Harmony unit (thinking our particular device is defective, rather than all Harmony remotes are garbage), or just going back to life without a Harmony system, and using all our device's remote controls (which are dependable, at least).

I do not understand why, after going into such detail, trying to explain all the problems your product has been giving us and how we even hired a professional to install and teach us how to use it...you do not want to do the right thing and stand by your product?? This device is a lemon and has problems; this happens with electronics and we understand that. We do not understand why you want to keep our money and leave us with a defective product?

Please do the right thing and allow us to ship our product back to you so we can purchase another one. Maybe you can repair ours and sell as refurbished?"

I wasted hours of time calling Amazon, NetZero, and Logitech looking for help with my problem, but no one will help. Logitech tried to trouble shoot over the phone, but ended up telling me that there is in fact something wrong with the device.

title: A Thumb Trackballer
text:
There are enough reviews here espousing the greatness of the M570 from Logitech, so I'm just going to briefly describe my experience.

I've had mine since 2010 and have been using it every day at work. I've found that, for productivity, it beats a mouse hands down. Over the years I have had absolutely no issues with this wireless trackball and it continues to perform flawlessly. The ball tracks smoothly and evenly. But as others have mentioned, you do have to give it a cleaning every month or so as the bearings tend to trap and accumulate gunk over time. The ball can also attract and have stuck to it the errant hair strand or lint glob that will cause the movement to feel gritty or stick and skip. It is easy to clean though. Pop out the ball, give the bearing a good wiping with a microfibre cloth (or other lint free cloth) and likewise with the ball, pop the ball back in and you're golden. I've probably changed the battery twice. The size is just about right for my hand (about 8.5 inches around at the knucles) and the contours felt natural from day one with my fingers aligning right in the groves, over the buttons, and my thumb placed just right on the ball.

I've ordered a second M570 to use with my tablet PC (MSI WindPad 110W). I'm currently using a Kingston Orbit. I tried the Orbit because it was smaller than the M570 (not by much though ... those product pictures sure are deceptive). But, I just cannot get used to the position of the trackball on the Orbit. I guess I'm a thumb guy and not a finger trackballer!

2017/03/17: Logitech, if you're reading any of this at all, please consider a G version of this! If the G900 Chaos can be wireless, then we can have a G version trackball. No need to deviate too much from the design, but a free-scrolling middle button, some more programmable buttons, a gaming sensor, a spiffy RGB LED layout to sync with the rest of the G stuff, even a removable cord for charging ... I'd go for that!

title: Giving Logitech Another Chance
text:
I had used Logitech IR remotes years ago and found that they did not last very long and thought they were just ok. I have been using a URC R50 for the past 7 years and loved it. The URC involves "macros" and can be programmed in unlimited ways & can be highly customized. However, after 7 years of heavy use the buttons have worn out so I was in need of a new remote. Amazon still sells the URC R50 but I though I would try the Logitech again. The Logitech Smart Control will control a Bluetooth device such as a PS3 whereas the URC R50 will not. URC has bluetooth enabled remotes but the cost is $$$$. So I gave the inexpensive Smart Control the nod. The box arrived the next day (PRIME) and it was extremely easy to set up. I think it took me less than 15 mins. I have a faily basic system of TV, cable box, stereo, PS3, Wii. So I only need 3 "activies" of "play TV", "play PS3", "play Wii". All I did was follow the app prompts and it all worked seamlessly. NOW, it is a matter of will this thing perform over time? Many of the bad reviews state that the device does not always work correctly and IF that happens, there is no way to recover. for example If the stereo does not turn on when "Play TV" is pressed...well there is no way to easily turn it on with the Smart Remote because the remote only has limited buttons and "real estate". It is not highly cutomizable like advanced remotes such has the URC. Also, the remote depends on an internet connection, so if that goes down, the remote will not work. But I will give it a try and report back in a few weeks. After one day, it has worked perfectly each time and the ease of setup was quite nice. To program a beast like the URC takes a few hours but it is a one time commitment.

Update about one month later....I really like this remote. I have had few issues with it but overall it works very well. It is not perfect, but does the job. I have 2 minor issues; one can be fixed & one cannot. First is many negative reviews have reported that occasionally not all the devices turn on/off when command is sent. So if your "Watch TV" command has to turn on 3-4 devices, sometimes not all of them turn on. This has happened to me but it is because of the placement of the "blasters". This unit comes with a main base "blaster" & an auxiliary "blaster". The "blasters CANNOT go thru hard-wood cabinets or at least that is my experience. My set up is TV sits on top of cabinet & then cable box, PS3, Wii, etc sit inside a nice hardwood cabinet. The devices are split across the 2 sides of the cabinet and there are 2 doors. So my main blaster is on inside of cabinet on one side & aux blaster is outside next to TV. One side of cabinet does not have a blaster. If the doors of cabinet are complete closed tight, the equipment in the cabinet that does not have the blaster may not receive the signals. I just leave the cabinet doors slightly open so the signal can bounce off the cabinet doors and into other side of cabinet. However, this can be fixed IF I shell out about $15 for another auxiliary blaster so that each side of cabinet gets a clear signal. The main unit has inputs for an additional blaster but only comes with one. If Logitech really wanted to avoid negative reviews, they should include the additional blaster as I think a cabinet setup is very common.

The other negative is no backlight on controller. After using it for a few days you can remember by "feel" where the buttons are, but you cannot see the buttons in a dark room, It is by feel only. Adding backlighting would really put this over the top.

This is a fine product and very glad for my purchase. Still 4 stars and could be a 5 star product with slight improvements.

text:
Bought this refurbished from Amazon warehouse. Looks good as new and works pretty well. The picture quality is good as well as the microphone. Setup was a breeze and running this is simple, as well. Even my 3 year old knows how to click on the icon to get the camera running.

Update: this camera has a macro auto focusing problem when you want to record something up close. For example, if you're recording yourself at about a foot or 2 away (arms distance), your image is clear, but if you hold something up to the camera, the image will be blurry because it doesn't auto focus. What you'll need to do is pop open the camera cover, remove the 3 tiny screws with a Phillips head screwdriver, remove the 2nd camera cover to expose the lens. You'll see the lens has a circular cover that has ridges or a dial, if you will. Point the camera to a close object and slowly turn that dial either clockwise or counter clockwise until the image is focused. I believe it was clockwise to zoom closer. Don't focus too clearly because your images that are at arms distance or further will be blurry. You need to create a balance between close objects and arms distanced objects. Now hold your camera at the usual distance and refocus the camera until you get a balance. When you find a balance, replace the 2 covers and screws

title: The damn buttons!
text: This is my 3rd Harmony remote.  I love how powerful they are.  This one frustrates me though.  For one, the power button is located right above the rewind button, and I frequently accidentally push power instead of rewind.  This has spoiled many evenings for me.  I may have paused live TV on my DVR while I did something else, and came back and while trying to rewind, I power it off.  All that paused program gone, wiped out forever.  Why is the rewind/play/FF up at the top anyway?  I wish it were down below.  I also wish there were actual number buttons instead of the touchscreen numbers - they are very difficult to enter.  The touchscreen is not very sensitive, or is too picky, and by the time I enter the 2nd or 3rd numbers, the target device has given up waiting for my input.  Also, sometimes while watching TV, when I press volume up/down, the remote does something weird and rewinds, or tells remote controlled (not programmed in my Harmony tho) fan to oscillate...  Seems to be a glitch.  I'm hoping the next one will be better, but as much as these things cost, I'm going to have to live with it for a few years before I can justify buying a new one.

title: Consistency issues
text:
I think the setup must have changed significantly in the past year or so. I was able to get all 5 of my devices entered through my phone and working in less than 15 minutes, which included me having to redo my Wii U because I left the Wii on during that process and the hub paired the Wii twice instead of getting the Wii U. I didn't need to learn any buttons, all the buttons on the physical remotes were available automatically. I could also turn the system off from anywhere in the house, which isn't at all necessary, but pretty cool.

9 month update...
When the hub actually does what it's supposed to it's really nice. However, very frequently I have to close and restart the app to get the TV to respond. I'm not sure what the issue is since I can see the hub lights registering my commands, but nothing happens until I close and restart the app. It's not the phone either I see this behavior on all 3 phones. It's also not the TV since it happens across all devices as well. So this leaves me wanting desperately to change the volume because it's really loud (since Netflix can't regulate show volumes for us) and I have to run to the TV because the hub isn't sending the commands a couple times a day, which is the entire point of having a remote. And in my opinion, a "remote" that works 90% of the time (especially for this much money) is a terrible remote.

Also, I synced a Wii and WiiU to it as well. It's nice that you can do this, but it's completely useless because the phone becomes controller 1 but can't actually control the the system. I tried to resolve this with customer service, but nothing worked. According to them, if you hit "Disconnect" it will remove the phone as a controller, but it does not. This means you have to re-order the controllers on the Wii. So I've removed turning in the systems in the action since it takes longer to re-order controllers than to turn it on with the controller.

There is potential here, but a lot is missing in this application. The game system thing is annoying but livable. Not working 10% of the time is unacceptably high for me.

title: DO NOT BUY INTO THE HYPE.
text: The biggest issue you will read about is the scrolling wheel.  Some of you might know that it comes with the option to ratchet spin or free spin.  Many people have reported the ratchet suddenly not working.  I opened the MX Master and found the reason it doesn't work is due to the plastic mechanism which loosens up too much.  There is no way to tighten it as it is a mechanism which ALWAYS moves.  This is just poor quality on Logitech's part.  Don't believe me?  Google "Mx Master Wheel" and you will see all the posting of the ratcheting not working.  At most Logitech thinks its software related, but software will not let this device tighten loose parts.  Please don't buy into the hype.  It's not a mouse worth purchasing.  This happened on my first week with this mouse.

I am looking at using it as a fixed camera in other settings to record many views simultaneously using several cameras, so I can edit it all later. title: It is the best and easiest universal remote to manage multiple devices and an HTPC w/Kodi, Plex, or Windows Media Center
text:
I use this in conjunction with the [[ASIN:B00BB0ETW8 FLIRC FL-09028 USB Universal Remote Control Receiver for Media Centers Components]]. I don't know how to beat the combination. The FLIRC is seen by the OS as a keyboard, and the Harmony has software that knows what to send for thousands of different devices. It also makes macros based on questions you answer so that if you want to watch a Blu-ray, it will turn on the TV, set the correct HDMI port active on the TV, and turn on the Blu-ray. Same thing when you shut it off. HTPC software is designed to work with a remote.

At first, I was a little sorry I bought it because I would like to have something with an air mouse, keyboard, voice, and IR channels to turn things off and on, but the only one even half good is the MINIX A2. However, the MINIX A2 is designed to work with their set top boxes, so people have not been successful getting some of the buttons to work with PCs, and it is murder on batteries. Also, practicing with my phone, I find that aiming and remaining steady while pressing buttons is a lot harder than you think. So if you are using Windows Media Center or Plex or Kodi, this beats the stars out of anything else. I also have a [[ASIN:B014EUQOGK Logitech Wireless Touch Keyboard K400 Plus with Built-In Touchpad for Internet-Connected TVs]], and that may be what I use for web navigation. On the keyboards, you would probably be better off with the [[ASIN:B00ZOPVSKW Logitech Illuminated Living-Room Wireless Keyboard K830 and Touchpad for Internet-Connected TVs (Unifying and Bluetooth)]] if they weren't so expensive because your living room may not be dark, but maybe not well lit as in for reading, so the illuminated keys would be better.

title: Simply The Best
text:
Holy Mother of God.

Let me first state that I know headphones. I have a number of sets of pro studio monitor headphones, including the venerable Sony 7506's and Sennheiser HD280's at home, as well as AKG, Audio Technica, etc. I have a thing for headphones. I'm also a musician, and do digital audio production, with KRK reference studio monitoring as my main go-to's. I've used in-ears by UE extensively: UE500's, SuperFi 5's and TripleFi 10's for live performance & pleasure listening. I've used in-ears by other manufacturers, but have always found them either woofy or not detailed enough. I have a set of Etymotic Research balanced armature earphones, and while they have great detail and clarity, they sound distinctly one-dimensional.

These UE900s phones are, without reservation, the best-sounding earphones/headphones I've ever heard. The detail and high-end openness is phenomenal, and the low-end accurately reflects the source material. It will give you what's there, without artificially boosting and boominess. On material that has tight kick and bass, the response is sharp and quick. With material that uses deep synth and kick, the bass is expansive and thick. The midrange is fantastic - guitars, snare drum, and vocals all come through sounding distinct, crisp and layered across the soundstage.

If you're a "bass head" and like artificially-boosted low-end, a la "beats", you'll be disappointed. These are much better and more accurate phones; the problem will be your source material, not the earphones. Garbage in, garbage out, so to speak. I plan to try these puppies out with some laptop-based audio mixing, "in the box." Usually, I don't like headphone mixes, as they tend to accentuate some frequencies & require re-mixing in the studio with proper monitors. I'm not so sure with the UE900s IEM's, though. These might be the ones to break the rule. A true audiophile will be in heaven with these things, and the untrained ear will hear these phones reveal things in familiar music that you probably weren't aware were always there. Seriously, they're that good, even for balanced armature IEM's. The crossovers are wonderful, and the 3-way, 4-armature setup delivers the goods. These things will grossly outperform IEM's 2 or 3 times the price. The packaging and accessories are first rate, and scream "QUALITY" in every direction.

Buy them at this price while you can. You will not find better.

title: I loved it so much that when I decided to get ...
text: I own the Logitech K811 and have been using it at home for a while. The 3 Bluetooth switch feature is genius. It really makes you wonder why it’s not included on other devices. I loved it so much that when I decided to get a laptop stand for my office and a keyboard to go along with it, I decided to look at it again. Unfortunately, the K811 is currently listed at $90. With that you get the Bluetooth switching, a rechargeable battery, thin profile, backlit keys, and Mac/iOS specific keys. All these features are great and I’d definitely suggest that one as well, but the truth is that all of those features aren’t necessary for a stationary keyboard at my office. Fortunately right next to the K811 is the K380. It has the 3 Bluetooth switcher buttons, but isn’t backlist or rechargeable. The profile is slightly thicker due to the fact that it runs off of 2 AAA batteries. In exchange for losing these minor things, it only costs ~$20 and I get it in a slick blue color. Considering that it’s literally less then a third the cost of the K811, I really have to highly suggest the keyboard. My one singular gripe? Round keys?? Not my personal favorite. Takes a little bit of getting used to. Certainly not a deal breaker, but considering that it’s something you’re gonna be using daily just be aware.

title: With a Raspberry Pi
text:
This works fairly well with my Raspberry Pi 3 and the Raspbian OS for a baby cam project. The bit rate, when using the cam's own H.264 encoding, is fixed at 3 Mbps. The picture is very clear and the audio is good. I am able to use a number of resolutions but I elected to go to a 720p. title: Great boom for your buck
text:
I bought this along with the Bluetooth adapter (sold separately) to set up as a small home theater system for my tv, and for anything audio related. This is what I have discovered with my testing. My room is 12x30. I listen to a variety of music that puts it to the test in every possible way.

Aesthetically is inoffensive, and the light is orange and dim which is great for dark room usage.

Lots of inputs which is great. RCA goes to my tv output, and actually pairs well with the flatscreen tv speakers to provide better dynamic range (if you configure the tv properly). One 3.5mm on the sub output goes to the Bluetooth adapter, and the 3.5mm on the satellite remains free for other devices which is like having an aux input in your car. Then there's another 3.5mm output right next to that for headphones and what have you. You don't have to manually switch between the inputs which is great.

Sound clarity and volume is good enough to handle the room. It's not glorious, but the next real step up would be spending $800+ on a home theater system. Don't turn either the volume or bass knob past 12-1 o'clock if you want to maintain clarity on a standard mobile device playback at full volume. Bass knob above 12-1 o'clock and you start to muddy the satellites so it's best to keep it there for full depth without noticeable distortion. That being said, I could still feel the bass enough to be happy.

My only complaint: The satellite speakers are angled upwards slightly as you can see. Normally you want to aim speakers at your ears. If you have it directly in front of you on a TV stand, you'll lose a bit of clarity on the couch. However, it isn't really offset enough to cause much loss as the highs aren't super clear anyway. I assume they're meant for a computer desk, but even so, it's an unnecessary feature that doesn't help unless you never move from perfectly upright in front of your monitor. It would be cool if there was a cradle under them to adjust the angle, but maybe that's wishful thinking for $110 speakers.

As far as listening using the Bluetooth adapter (sold separately, but suggested), it complemented the system just fine, but remember that when using Bluetooth, the adapter does the audio processing, not your phone or tablet etc., so you're almost guaranteed some loss of quality. So don't judge the speakers solely through Bluetooth. Maybe there are great adapters out there that I've never used. That's a different topic. But I was happy with the result and it did me a slight favor of mellowing out the highs on audiobooks.

Overall, it's a very good alternative to a home theater system. It produces good sound and volume for the price and with all the inputs and outputs included, I'm very satisfied. I can only imagine it would be a beast on a computer in an office.

title: Great performance and comfort, from mic quality to headphones, even for music, totally worth it
text:
These are great, they can be adjusted to fit on your head comfortably. Well, my head. They're very light, yet they don't move around. So once you find your position, they just stay. I use these for hours as I do transcription work.

I have tested them with music and they sound better than the Sony Pro "studio" headphones which retail for $100 and have no microphone. Those headphones have a pronounced treble and lack bass. It seems like they are made for old people. Anyways, in music, these have a nice balance of midrange, bass, and highs. They don't make you say WOW but they also don't piss you off with frequency peaks at various places, and you may find they sound quite a bit better than your average stereo.

I just tested the microphone on my Mac Laptop Pro or whatever it's called, using ScreenFlow and the words are crisp and clean with no caffeine, as that old advert used to say. I will say though, that wind protection is not very good. I recorded outside, where I work, and you could hear low tones of wind coming through. However, the voice was completely crystal clear, there was never any doubt about that, so even with the wind sounds (and unless you work outside, this mayn't be a bother), I could still record my voice loud and clear.

If you only can buy one set of headphones and one microphone, you should definitely consider this offering. It seems plastic and cheap and yet you can tell by the way it's put together, and the materials used, that it's actually going to last a long time, and for $30 that can't be beat. Pair that with the above-average sound quality of the headphones and the above-average quality of the mic, and you have a total winner, for less than $30. I think this demonstrates technology really working for the people, when a company like this can make such a great product for so cheap.

Edit: the sound in these is somewhat "hall"-y. It sounds like you're in a boring auditorium. It's fine, but I tried the Sony cans I just dispagaged above, the pro ones, and even though their treble is at first annoying, if you turn them down, they're way better than these. So for sound, these are not offensive at $30, in fact they're rather nice. But the $100 Sony Pro Studio monitors end up beating them out by a long shot when I compared them one after the other.

title: Deeply flawed due to Logitech cutting corners
text:
I've gone through two of these already. Both times, the left mouse button began giving out after around 6 months of use. Because the internal switch "sticks," single clicks are sporadically registered as double-clicks, or no click at all. This problem starts off as a moderate annoyance (especially if you use this mouse for work), and eventually renders the mouse unusable.

This is a well-known flaw and is caused by Logitech using cheap Chinese switches for the left and right mouse buttons.

If you are handy with a soldering iron, and are willing to make a project out of it, you can open it up and replace the switches with quality Japanese switches.

When you buy this mouse, just know that you will either need to replace it every so often (how long it lasts depends on how much you use it), or you will need to replace the Chinese switches inside of it with Japanese replacement switches that you will need to track down online (or in another mouse). If you decide on the latter option, a bit of Googling will uncover at least one detailed tutorial on how to do the swap.

title: Inconvenient shortcut buttons, stuck in landscape mode, flimsy. Samsung keyboard case is better
text:
I've used this as well as the Samsung keyboard case for the Tab S 10.5". The pros in comparison to the Samsung keyboard case seemed apparent at the start:

- Softer outside material.
- The keys are slightly bigger and feel quite nice to type on. I prefer a keyboard where the keys feel sturdy and you can feel some resistance when you press down on one.
- Might be slightly lighter.
- The tablet is completely covered and protected when the case is closed (whereas with the Samsung case the tablet closes onto the keyboard so that the entire back of it is exposed.

After using the Logitech keyboard case for a little while, however, the cons started to appear:

- Combined number/function keys. In comparison, the Samsung keyboard has separate Function keys which have their own shortcuts. I really struggled with adapting to the Logitech one where I have to press the FN key plus the Home key to access Recent Apps (and they're on opposite sides of the keyboard so it's hard to do it with one hand), or press the FN key plus the volume keys to change the volume (even further away). On the Samsung keyboard, these are all one-press shortcut buttons (Home, Recent Apps, Screen brightness, Volume, Search).
- Once you slot the tablet into the case holder, you're basically stuck in landscape mode. If you want to view a website or app in portrait mode, you'll have to flatten the case, turn off your keyboard (so the back of your tablet won't press buttons accidentally) and turn the tablet around. Then you'll have to use the on-screen keyboard if you need to type, which is a pain when you're typing a lot and prefer to type on a physical keyboard.
- It's very difficult to pop the tablet out of the case holder. I was worried that the tablet would bend so much that it would crack. I've since worked out a method to remove it more quickly, but it's still not optimal.
- Say you're Skyping with someone and you need to tilt the tablet forward a bit more so the other party can see more than just your forehead. With the Samsung keyboard, the way it's propped up on the case makes it easy to push something weighty against the back of it to tilt it forward. With this one, the case bends outward at the bottom, so even this dodgy workaround isn't really doable.
- After 4 months of use, the magnet from one of the corners of the case holder has come loose so that I often open it up to find the magnet and the little plastic cover sitting stuck to the other magnet under the Ctrl button.

I use my tablet a LOT. I rarely boot up my laptop because I do pretty much everything on my tablet. So, for me, I feel that the Samsung keyboard is much easier and more convenient to use. I regretted getting this one, to be honest. I have always loved Logitech products, but for this I have to say that Samsung has made a better product.

title: Good product...I recommend
text:
Good product. I am really enjoying using it. I especially love the joystick compared to the directional pad some of the new gaming pads have. I’m just not a big fan of directional pad. There are plenty of buttons so you shouldn’t have any issues with macro’s and or hotkeys. The keys sound great when you press. Some people have a preference for mechanical keys but I really don’t care…as long as it feels good (mechanical or not) when I hit the keys is all I care about. It is sturdy and well built, it has some weight to it so you don’t have to worry about the device moving around when playing. Cable length is very reasonable; for those that like to game in their living and your couch is a good distance to your console, you might need to get an USB extender. Your WASD keys are indented versus the home row key where you have a bar for your middle finger button but this is not an issue for me. I got used to well in the first 30mins.

Now for the con’s:

Ergonomic design – really this is the only problem that I have with the product. The hand placement position is not in a very comfortable position over a period of time and the pinky finger buttons can be hard to get to. Another issue is the joystick. I find that the joystick is a little high and the tip too pointy. I play FPS and prefer the claw grip finger placement on my WASD keys which would help me better hit the pinky finger buttons with ease but the drawback to this is not being able to properly use the thumb stick as it is a little too far back if I use the claw grip finger placement. I think it would have been better if the joystick was shorter with the tip having more of a thumb rest shape, so you can almost place or most like rest your entire thumb on it (for reference, view picture of the joystick of the Hori Tac device (see link below)

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01F9HMO2K/ref=wl_it_dp_o_pd_nS_ttl?_encoding=UTF8&colid=38YII0GZP0KDV&coliid=I1V5Y8U0F33M8A&th=1

Now with that said, I rate this a 4 star solely based on ergonomics design and the current price (less than $40.00). I have taken into consideration how long this market has been on the market which is about 7yrs now. I do not believe it is fair do a 1 for 1 comparison with the more recent and current gaming keypads that have been on the market for much less time that have improved ergonomics design and joysticks..

title: Disappointing mess of a product, terrible support
text:
I've never been this disappointed with a Logitech product before.

First the good points. The sound quality is excellent, no one has ever had a problem hearing me. I never got a 10 hour charge out of the batteries as advertised, but got 5 or 6 at first. They are comfortable, they don't weight too much, they wrap securely around my head without being too tight and do a good job blocking out outside sound. They give you a really long USB cable with a base you can wrap it around to shorten to whatever you desire. At first it really appeared to be a fantastic product.

Then came the problems. Right off the bat I noticed it had problems staying connected. Probably 5-6 times per day, it will give out a short beep and lose the connection for about 5-10 seconds, and give me a double beep and reconnect. Since it always reconnects on its own It isn't terrible enough for me to have returned the product, but over the 7 months or so that I've owned it, it started to make me hate the thing. It was frequent enough that it would often make me have to rewind in a movie or show I was watching, or I'd miss an important moment in a video game, or I'd have to ask someone to repeat themselves when I was on a work call. It wouldn't be so bad if it only happened when using the headset wirelessly, but it has this problem even if you have the USB cable plugged in, as it only seems to use that cable for charging and not to send data over USB like their wireless mouses.

Even worse, about once or twice a week it will start making a low humming sound that gradually builds into deafening buzzing. It sounds a lot like feedback but it happens even if the mic is muted so I have no idea what the issue is. Turning the headset off and then back on a few minutes later fixes it, but if you turn it off and back on quickly it's still there, you really do have to wait a few minutes which is absolutely unacceptable if you're using this thing for a work call.

Battery life has gotten bad quickly. I know rechargeable batteries have a limited life-cycle but I expected it to at least be decent until I was past the warranty period, but I've only had it for 7 months. I feel like it only gets about 2.5-3 hours after charging all night now. I'll have to do a test and come back and edit this with specific results.

The last straw was the mechanism that keeps the right headphone tight and in place broke. Since they wrap fairly securely around my head and ears, I typically remove the headphones by grabbing the right side and pulling it off my right ear then sliding the headphones off my head. Apparently this was too much strain on the piece of plastic used there, because it just snapped off and flew across the room one day, leaving the right headphone loose and making the product no longer comfortable or secure around my head. (Picture of the broken product attached to this review) I'm still well within the warranty period so I decide to RMA these things and hope for better results with the replacement.

Logitech support, which used to be incredible, has taken a real dive apparently. Here is my support horror story: I opened my first support ticket 10 days ago, no response. I did a live chat a couple days later, the agent told me he was going to get me an RMA and to hold on, then I got kicked out of the live chat for taking too long to respond to the agent even though he told me to "hold on" while he processed my RMA. There was no way for me to get back into the live chat or even start a new live chat under the same support ticket, so I had to open a new ticket and start a new live chat with a different person, explained the situation to her, she said she talked to the other agent and he was going to process my RMA request and that I'd get an email within an hour.

I waited 2 days and never got the email (checked spam, etc.), so I called their support phone number. Unfortunately during that call the headphones started doing that loud buzzing/feedback thing and I had to turn them off, and I guess while I was unresponsive the agent hung up on me. So another 2 days later I tried a live chat again and got that first agent, and I referred him back to the prior ticket and chat and he said he didn't know why the RMA didn't go through before but their new system has some bugs that haven't been worked out. He started the process over again but this time we had to make sure to keep talking while he processed the RMA. He would type something like "I'm typing this so the chat doesn't kick us out" and I'd respond with "I'm responding for the same reason". This exchange went on for 36 minutes (I have the chat logs), which was going to make me late for an appointment, so I had to get in my car, remote into my computer through my phone, and every few minutes type something into the live chat so I didn't get kicked out and have to start all over again, while driving. Finally he told me my RMA was processed and I'd get an email within an hour.

I never got that email either. I wait two more days and try another live chat. I explain to the new agent, give her all my pending support tickets for reference, she apologizes, says she will escalate this to the senior level, and says someone should contact me within 48 hours. I tell her "okay, what do I do if no one contacts me? Because this keeps happening." She responds, and this is a direct quote, by saying "I will make sure, you will receive a response on this matter."

48 hours later, no one has contacted me. I try phone support again (I use my cell phone this time since I can't trust this headset), and I tell the agent all of the above and give him all my various pending support tickets ( I now have 7 pending support tickets for this one issue, because there is no way to open a live chat under an existing ticket and starting a new live chat creates a new ticket ). The agent on the phone says "wow this is a real mess" and I agree. He promises to send me an email and stays on the phone with me, I get it instantly, proving I'm capable of receiving emails from Logitech support. The email requested a bunch of information that they already have because I registered my product to my logitech account and provided the proof of purchase and a picture of the problem and everything in my first support ticket, but I filled it out again and responded. That was yesterday. As of today, one of my 7 support tickets says "RMA pending". I'm still waiting on the actual RMA, at which point I will have to ship my product to them and wait until they ship a new / refurbished product back to me. Hopefully.

This is the kind of support experience I expect from Comcast, not Logitech.

title: Unreliable to the point of uselessness.
text:
It is rare that I post a one-star review on a gadget. This may be my first.

The product itself COULD be great. It has a great interface, the app is fantastic, and it integrates well with other Smart Home accessories. But it has one giant glaring issue, and it's unreliable as hell.

The product relies heavily on your WiFi and Internet connection. Even when using the IR remote to control IR devices, it still needs to get to the internet. This is where the product falls apart. Every few hours, the WiFi signal drops, causing the red light on the hub to turn on. It'll correct itself in a few hours, but that's a few hours in which you lose all control of your devices. It always seems to happen when I need to mute the TV for one reason or another. At first I thought it was just me. Then I started googling. This is a VERY widespread issue. The number of tested routers is limited to a handful at best. I have a very common Netgear N600, sold at Best Buy. I was able to replicate the issue on an enterprise-level Cisco AP, and an older D-Link router.

Frustration caused me to revert back to my 7 year old Harmony 880, which has had its own history of hardware issues. A few weeks later, I decide to give my Hub another shot. I moved it to the same room as the router, and realized it now doesn't connect to WiFi at all. Ever. I tried 3 other untrusted networks near my house. Nothing. It's toast. Does Logitech care? Of course not! They already got my $99.

title: Great Entry-Level Joystick
text:
Bought this after my old Microsoft Sidewinder joystick finally died. The Extreme 3D Pro is a very good stick for one on a budget, like myself. It has a rubber-padded, weighted base, providing decent stability when the stick is pulled hard to its extents. The 12 buttons are easy to program with most games, the 8 way hat-switch is a nice plus, and the stick is three axis, allowing for yaw control without third party pedals.

However, it does have some minor issues. First, while 12 buttons is plenty for most flying games, for hardcore study simulations like Falcon 4, it is woefully inadequate. Also, the stick has a little bit of play, but the sensors, for better or worse, are sensitive enough that they pick up this play, leading to minor control inputs when your hand is resting on the stick. I have found that it still occurs even with the dead zones maxed out on all the games I play. Finally, I have issues getting it to interface properly with some games, namely Kerbal Space Program, though that may be to the technical issues with the game rather than the stick.

Overall, it is a very good entry-level stick, and I can only hope it lasts as long as my old Sidewinder did. For the price it is hard to beat.

Upon powering on, I immediately noticed a high pitch whine on the background. I have turned them off, reconnected them, changed the power outlets, and even just powered it on without connecting to PC. One thing remains constant - the high pitch whine.

It seems like I am not the only one who has had this issue, and after 3 ours of using it, the noise is really getting to me. It sounds like the ringing in your ears after getting hit hard in the head - and gives you the same head ache, lol.

I am assuming this is a defect, so I will be returning these. Not sure if I want to risk getting another defective model, especially considering my last set died unexpectedly. I think it is time for another brand now.

title: Best Mouse I Have Ever Purchased
text:
SYNOPSIS
I purchased my first of these in 2009 a couple of months after their release, and the second toward the end of 2010 so that I would have another one handy for traveling and going back and forth to college classes. Here we are in 2016 and both of my Performance MX mice are still working perfectly.

DURABILITY
Over the years I've used and abused them, thrown them in bags, dropped them on occasion, and put them through their paces ten times over as a graphic designer and web developer. I have used the rechargeable battery that comes with them, I have tried custom rechargeable batteries to get more life out of them, and unsupported or not I have had to run standard non-rechargeable alkaline batteries through them. As a guy who prefers a little length on his nails, I have caused premature wear in a few places, especially under the zoom button. This has simply worn away the rubber and has had no effect on the functionality of the mouse. Both mice have had the pads replaced once, and I'm getting ready for round number two. The pull tab under the battery is as good as new, and the mouse has never given me any problems with leaking batteries to ruin the battery compartment. All functionality of the mouse is as good as it was the day I bought it.

BATTERY LIFE AND CHARGING
Charging via a low-power USB port on my computer takes around four hours for a full charge (during constant and heavy use), high-power usb ports halve this time. To this day the battery they came with has proven to be the best battery to run in them. As a person who uses their mouse for eight hours a day, I get a minimum of two weeks off of a charge when I am diligent about turning them off at the end of my shift.

DARKFIELD
I have never had any problems with the mouse not being accurate on any surface, even glass. I spent a year on a glass desk with no mousepad and suffered no significant side-effects. I have on several occasions simply used my leg as a mousepad and the mouse performed admirably. I have only ever tried this mouse on one surface that it threw a fit over, and that was carpet filled with glitter. And even then it still worked well enough to be usable.

CONS
There is literally only one CON I can say this mouse has. When charging via the USB cable, the dongle must still be attached for the mouse to function (does not function as USB mouse when plugged in directly). This is so minor of an inconvenience that I'd long forgotten about it until I decided to write this review.

title: Started out great, now they're a paperweight.
text:
I've used these headphones on two different PCs, and like I said, they started off great. Only complaints I had initially were:
(1) Default settings (have to edit a device driver inf file to change) powered the headphones off after 3 minutes. Sort of an odd setting to even HAVE on a wireless device, but ...
(2) My G930 wouldn't hold a charge overnight, or the control app for it just showed the wrong data. I could charge the headphones for 3 hours, get to a full battery in the control app, then use them unplugged for 1-2 hours, and the next day the app would say I needed to charge them for 3 hours to get back to full, when they should have been at about 75% or more..

If you have a Windows 7 PC I suspect these will be great. I don't.

Now - the paperweight part. After updating either of my gaming laptops to Windows 10 "Threshold 2", i.e. build 1511, these headphones will no longer work as the default audio playback device. If the built-in speakers are set as the Default device, the G930 will make sound if you do the control panel audio playback device Test command. If you set the G930 to default, they not only don't make the sound, you don't even get the fake VR/level bars to move. This has happened on the 1511 update on both last year's laptop (Gigabyte P34Wv4) and this year's model (P34Wv5).

Unfortunately, the games I play don't allow you to select anything other than the Windows default sound device, so these are now useless to me for their intended purpose, and are sitting on my work desk to let me listen to music on my work's Windows 7 PC.

I've reached out to Logitech on multiple occasions and their responses (typically taking 2-3 days to even GET a response) were to "try a different USB port", which failed to work, or "try a different PC" i.e. see if it's the G930 hardware, which I did (as said above, they worked great on the 2nd PC until the 1511 update.).

I even sent Logitech support specific details on how the driver initialization is failing on Windows startup, but I guess Logitech is just too small a company to worry about a Windows version that's been out for 6 months (/sarcasm off.) The one time I went ahead and did a system recovery to roll one of the PCs back to the original Win10 version (pre-build 1511), the G930 miraculously came back to life.

************************
UPDATE 2016-04-25
************************
I've since installed these on another PC (Surface 3 tablet actually) that already had Win10 v1511 installed, and lo and behold, the headphones work fine (as stereo headphones). However, I haven't installed the Logitech Gaming Software on that PC yet, so that may be the culprit. Will update again once that's done.

***** Update 2 *****
After installing Logitech Gaming Software on the Surface 3, the headphones changed from Default (playback) to only Default Communications Device. After re-setting the G930 to Default device, they're working fine, even after a couple reboots (which killed it on the 2nd laptop after my initial delight in it working after one update...).

Now to see what happens if I can find and delete every single reference to the device on my main PC and re-install :|

***** Update 3 *****
After removing Logitech Gaming Software (LGS) and removing all of the Logitech headphone and mic devices in Device Manager (via View -> Show Hidden Devices), I'm back to square one. I can get sound from the G930 as the Windows Default Playback on my laptop if I don't install LGS, but then it's stereo (not 7.1 surround), I can't monitor the battery level, and I lose the customization of the additional buttons on my Logitech G602 Gaming Mouse.

If I install LGS, the playback device changes from Speakers on Logitech G930 Headset to Earphones on Logitech G930 Headset, and sound only works from the sound control panel interface (and I'm assuming from other apps that let you specify the sound output device outside of the Windows Default device.

I'll keep these in Stereo mode for now and hope that Logitech provides an update that addresses this issue, or until I get fed up and buy a new gaming headset from someone not named Logitech.

title: Easy set-up, works great, has a very long range antenna
text: I wanted a Bluetooth adapter to stream audio through an older receiver.  The Logitech Bluetooth adapter works like a charm.  I have the Logitech's output connected to the aux input on the stereo and the power connected to a switched outlet on the back of the stereo so the adapter powers up when the stereo is turned on.  You hear a couple of beeps through the speakers and that's it.  Setup was a snap.  I don't remember reading the manual.  I just plugged the Logitech adapter in, paired the Bluetooth to my phone and it worked.  It pairs with our phones almost instantly.  The signal quality is good with no hiss or other noise.  The antenna is very strong with long range.  My phone will connect from basement on the other side of the house - through 2 floors and numerous walls - to the stereo above the garage.  The connection is so strong that I need to remember to un-pair my phone or shut off Bluetooth if I want to stream audio (or watch video) in any other part of the house.

title: The miracle of vanishing remotes
text:
This is the first universal remote of this kind I've owned - it required a little learning and getting used to, but in the end I'm very pleased.
Build quality is excellent, typical of Logitech products - and so is the industrial design; the components are beautiful and unobtrusive - although the interface design could see a little improvement.
In the package comes the "Hub" - heart of the system, an IR blaster (or repeater, to direct the IR signals to where the Hub can't reach), a small remote and cables for power.
The Hub is supposed to be positioned in a certain way depending on your home theater layout, and if that was a concern for me at first, it quickly went away: there's plenty of IR and RF power to reach everything near, far and out of direct sight with the hub alone (although I don't have anything inside closed cabinets). For reference, I control a TV, a cable box, a receiver, a PS3, a projector and a projection screen.
Take your time to set it up, especially if you have several devices to program. The step-by-step process is not hard, but I would also not call it easy or simple. Basically you use the Harmony app on your phone/tablet to create an account and run the setup process and later on to tweak the settings. What wasn't completely clear to me in the beginning was that setting-up and configuring the settings are separate procedures - you first make the remote work with the devices and finish the basic setup and then you can edit the different activities to change stuff around. Once set and customized, it works wonderfully well.
The app is intended as the main controller and can be used to control everything: activities, which combine the main controls of all devices in use, or individual devices alone. The control interface is good, the customization interface not so much.
The physical remote is secondary, it only controls activities and not necessarily individual devices alone and needs to be configured using the app, but is my preferred method because it's simpler and more convenient. It has two drawbacks, though, in my opinion: no backlighting, and small buttons, especially the numbers at the bottom. With time you learn the layout and the backlight becomes less of a problem, but the small buttons will make it hard for certain people to operate, I'm sure.

All in all, I'm very happy and would recommend.

This will actually cause sound issues with modern games like Watch Dogs 2. Which uses 24 bit audio at cut scenes or ingame sounds. You wont hear them!
Here is an from a reference review of the problem"

"Moving on to high-resolution music files required the use of the 3.5 mm input, which was fine with me as I needed to test this out anyway. It is unfortunate however that those seeking greater bit depth won't have a choice in the matter, as the internal DAC is unfortunately limited to 16-bit audio (with a sample rate of up to 96 kHz). This won't pose an issue to most users, but it's worth noting that a wired analog connection will be required for not only high-res music, but also to hear uncompressed 24-bit/48 kHz Blu-ray audio (Dolby TrueHD, DTS Master Audio) without downsampling."

title: Want a scratched screen?  Buy this
text:
I was offered this case as a rebate replacement for a different defective Logitech case, the FabricSkin Keyboard Folio.

Con: Though the keyboard works as intended, you WILL scratch your screen if you don't place a cloth between the screen and the keys. It's unavoidable. I recommend the Shaggymax cloth for a MacBook Pro, as the Shaggymax cloth for the iPad is ill fitting on the width of the screen and not long enough for the length. The MacBook cloth will be way too large way you can at least cut it to size.

I can't help but feel the screen scratching quality could have been alleviated with some better rubber bumpers on the keyboard side that cushion the screen rather than allowing the screen to sit directly on the keys. Still construction wise it is a much better offering than previous attempts with the FabricSkin Keyboard Folio. That product broke repeatedly (I went through three) where the iPad secured to the case. If they'd have created that soft key case with the securing corners of this product they'd have a hit. I sound especially critical but many of the problems with their products would have appeared and been resolvable with ANY degree of product testing. All around poor design on most Logitech cases.

Pro: On the upside this keyboard has an excellent battery life and connects instantaneously. If combined with the cloth protector, you will actually have a workable keyboard case that is relatively durable.

title: Love this Keyboard. (Update after a year of use)
text:
I have had this keyboard a few days now and REALLY love it.

Some of the reviews have stated that the iPad Pro was difficult to get into the keyboard. I do not know if Logitech has done some minor modifications to the keyboard or now to address this problem, but I found it extremely easy to get into the keyboard. It was more difficult to get out, but not impossible. However, it is not something I will be doing often, so this is not a problem (I took the iPad out to put in the sim card).

I truly love the feel of the keyboard. It feels much like a regular laptop keyboard and is MUCH more responsive than the old "bluetooth" keyboards on older iPads. It feels solid and robust and is in many ways a joy to work with. I wish my regular Apple laptop felt as well. The back lighting is a wonderful feature.

I have no problem with the single angle of view for the iPad. The screen is large enough and there seems to be little glare on the screen, so there is no complaint there for me. I take it to dinner and read while I am eating (if I am alone) and can type and use the Apple Pencil just fine.

I also have no problem folding it over and using it just as a straight tablet. Taking notes in meetings with the pencil works perfect (although I have learned just how much my penmanship sux). Drawing in this mode is also very easy and comfortable.

I also appreciate not having to "recharge" the keyboard. Previously this meant having a totally DIFFERENT charging system and was a pain. With the new docking feature of the iPad Pro, this is all done away with. I don't see much drain on the iPad battery.

The ONLY con I have is that the keyboard does make the device a bit heavy. But that is something I am getting used to quickly.

All in all, I love this keyboard and am giving it a 5 star review.
--------------------------------- Update 03/17/2017. After a year of use.
I still love this keyboard and have had no problem with it scratching the iPad screen. However, here are some problems with it.
1) I dropped the case and it cracked right where the right speaker on the iPad is exposed. Now, the iPad will not stay put in the case. This causes me to have to re-seat it almost every time I move. Very annoying.
2) If the angle of attack between the keyboard and the iPad smart connector changes (which it does now that the case is cracked), it looses connection. And often a dialog asking me to "update the driver" for the keyboard pops up. Very annoying.
3) I wish there was some kind of holder for the iPencil. It would be nice to take it with me when I'm just carrying my iPad. There are several solutions involving buying a loop or something like that, but it wore out after a few months and was just not worth replacing.

Other than those three factors, I still LOVE this keyboard and have ordered another to fix the problem of the cracked case. The backlit keyboard is wonderful. It doesn't drain my iPad. I don't have to have a Bluetooth connection (which DOES drain the iPad). The keyboard is very comfortable even for my big hands. I sometimes think I'm on my Laptop (I even like this keyboard better than my laptop).

I will take better care of it, this time and will update this review if my opinion changes.

title: Not as customizable as I thought it would be. Buy the Anywhere MX 2 if that matters to you.
text:
Having owned and used several Logitech mice, I am used to having lots of customization with regards to the buttons via Logitech's Control Center software. But this mouse uses a different configuration tool entirely called "Logitech Options" that you have to download from their site.

Unlike Control Center, Options only has very basic customization. You can not assign any keyboard shortcuts as you can with the Control Center, nor can the buttons have different actions for different apps as they can in Control Center.

For example, with Control Center, I can assign the left and right action of the mouse wheel to handle Back/Forward in my browser of choice. And when not in the browser, those same button actions can slide to different workspaces. With the Options software, the buttons can only have one action and that action is global.

Apparently the Options software does support 'Application-Specific' controls, but the m557 mouse is not supported in that respect. The Anywhere MX 2 mouse apparently does, however. In hindsight, I would have bought the Anywhere MX 2 instead.

Other than the limited customization, I find the device build quality to be decent and the performance accurate as expected.

title: My favorite recent computer accessory (Edited)
text:
To preface: I'm utterly sure that for the price, I could have gotten a better sounding set of headphones.

So here's why I decided not to get a pair of Sennheisers or Beyerdynamics:

1. Wireless is amazing. I've never used a set of wireless headphones before, and these are a fantastic introduction. The signal is strong and shows no degradation moving several rooms away. Acquisition is very quick.

2. I'm a bit of a basshead. These are closed back, and that helps with the bass. I know, the sound isn't perfectly accurate. But these are a very good set if you like your music tuned a little bit towards the bassier end. I use the "flat" equalizer setting (default), but there are several more preprogrammed and you can always drag the sliders yourself.

3. Surround sound. I consider it to be somewhat of a gimmick. Yeah, these only have two drivers, so it's all postprocessing. But I think it gives a tangible advantage in fps games, so I like the option.

4. Included microphone. It's pretty good. It's not dedicated desk mounted microphone good, but it's better than webcam microphones.

5. Low impedance. My Moto X drives these almost as well as they drive themselves. It's nice to have the fallback to 3.5mm when the batteries are dead.

6. Everything is RGB in the future. Fuuuuuuture.

Cons of these cans:
-Slightly annoying that they go to sleep after 5 minutes of no sound. I'm sure this helps with battery a lot, but it's a tiny bit more effort to press a button. (EDIT: Since the time of this review, Logitech has now made this a programmable setting. Awesome.)
-Heavy. I get a lot of pressure on my head from the padding on the headband.
-Slips off somewhat easily. Not a big deal at the computer, but you can't angle your head forward or backward too much.

title: Expensive torture device
text:
The curved keyboard is totally not ergonomic. Look at the key layout and then look at your hand. Your pinkey finger is the smallest and likely the weakest, and the keys to be operated by it are angled inward, so in order to press those keys you have to press down and outward. Your joints are designed to push down, not to the side. The key spacing is all wrong as well and there are large gaps between the keys, so you have to really reach for them. Mind you, i'm 6'3" with proportionally large hands, i work on cars for a living, and type 83 WPM. I'm not using little wimpy kid hands here.

The wrist pad is nowhere near your wrist when you play. It takes a sharp turn down, and has no provisions to cradle your wrist. You would need to have the top of your desk at face level for your wrist to need that sort of bend, and at that point, the tendons of your fingers would be so far stretched that it would be difficult to press buttons. The wrist pad doesn't even transition smoothly into the bezel around the keys. It's just a lump that applies pressure to the underside of your wrist and does nothing to support it further up the arm.

Another issue is the joystick. Again, look at your hand and where the joystick is. An average sided thumb would have to be attached somewhere near the wrist to operate that stick. The guy who designed this thing must have been seriously deformed. If you suffered a horrific industrial accident, this pad may be for you.

About a week into using this pad, the X- axis of the joystick failed and i rejoiced because now i could return it.

title: Good wireless mouse that works with LG Smart Television sets
text:
Good wireless mouse that works with LG Smart Television sets.

All I had to do was plug in the dongle to an available USB plug on the Smart TV and it recognized it right away and started working. I liked it so much I bought a couple more and put them on other Smart TVs as well. I have never lost connection, except for the time when the batteries were dying, and the TV finds it immediately. There are many wireless mice but many of them will not work with Smart TVs since the TV has to recognize the mouse to work. I tried a Dell wireless mouse first and the TV never saw it but when I plugged in this wireless Logitech M185 mouse to my Smart TV it worked flawlessly.

PROS:
- Recognized by LG Smart TVs
- Has switch on bottom of mouse to turn it on/off if you want battery to last longer
- I've left the mouse on for months and the batteries last a good long time
- Works with rechargeable batteries (uses 2 AA)
- Good range (using from 15 feet away without a glitch)
- Allows me to read emails, newspaper, etc on my TV

CONS:
- No indicator when batteries get low, you know simply by having to move mouse closer to TV to work or it doesn't work at all

text:
Just picked this up after a long and arduous hunt for a scissor key feeling board. The keys on this board are different from all the other K series that logitech puts out. They feel crisp, responsive, just... perfect, honestly.

...unfortunately, this keyboard does not have 3+ key rollover. If you are attempting a running jump, for instance, in an FPS that requires SHIFT+W+SPACE, the space will not register. Max 2 keys at a time.

This is not a drawback for most people, and in every other respect it is such a great feeling keyboard. I cannot dock it any stars for this, as it's not an advertised feature. title: Best of the many universal remotes that I have tried.
text:
I have tried just about every universal remote out there in an attempt to make controlling a complex system easy for my wife. Caavo Control Center... Harmony 650, Smart Control and Elite... Inteset INT422-3... One-For-All 4 and 8 device versions... Philips... GE... RCA, etc.

None of them do everything that I need. I love the GE layout and backlighting, but there are no macros or activities. Inteset is very good, but more difficult to program. One-for-All is good but only the 8 device version supports enough devices, and it's mostly not backlit. Harmony Elite is too complex, and expensive, and the backlighting is poor. The commands don't seem to be as reliable as the smaller Smart COntrol either. Caavo is just not ready for prime time yet. It has some intriguing features, but the layout is strange, it depends too much on their proprietary guide service and has too many dual function buttons.

So far, my favorite is my Harmony Smart Control. I wish it had one extra activity button, but there are workarounds. Also, wish it was backlit for use in the bedroom at night, and was a bit larger with more space between buttons. But it controls everything, has a familiar layout and is easily reconfigurable using the phone app.

If it was a little larger and was backlit, it would have been a 5.
