title: Bottom line: It's quiet. Logitech has my mouse and keyboard business.
text:
I wanted a mouse specializing in two features: (1) quiet and (2) big.

I am using the mouse primarily for the purpose of playing a few classic computer games. Those games require a high amount of clicking, and therefore I wanted a quiet mouse! This mouse delivers on that feature. It is practically silent. Basically the sound you hear is just quiet confirmation that you've clicked. I also had positive experience with using a big mouse from Logitech in the past. The bigger size gives you easier control of the mouse. It is more comfortable and less taxing on your wrist. This mouse as not as big as the 10-year-ish old model of the MX Master I used to own and my dog proceeded to destroy in puppyhood. However, this mouse is bigger than your "average" mouse. I am happy with the size. Any smaller I'd be disappointed with the size.

Those were my two primary features of interest and Logitech delivered. This mouse does not have buttons that integrate with web browsing or multi-tasking. There is a quiet scroller.

Other features:

- I like the design on the mouse grip. It is subtle and modern. I chose the Silver color to match my MacBook Air.
- I purchased this item at $20. My research of the mouse market suggests cost goes up as you want more buttons on the mouse that you can use for web browsing and multi-tasking. You would consider a model like the MX Master in that case, which those can get up to $60. If you don't need that additional functionality, and you want a quiet and comfortable mouse for recreational use, then I highly recommend this model. By all means, the MX Master was a great product in my experience, but I need that convenience of button integration on the mouse.
- Came in durable packaging that was 'frustration free packaging' vs a lot of those hard plastic casings you come across.
- Battery included. Between that and the frustration free packaging, those two things were small value-adds that made the product experience a little more enjoyable and convenient.

Logitech makes durable, effective, and attractive products in my experience. My experience with the old MX Master model was excellent. I have a wireless logitech keyboard and basic wireless mouse (similar to this one with the exception that it does not have quiet clicking). Now, I have this mouse for home recreation use. I rarely feel like I have to change batteries with their products. They have my business for life until I have reasons otherwise.

title: Specs on this model changed since 2014.  Disappointed in Logitech
text:
I've now had this mouse for almost 2 years, and I love it. I use it for creative work (Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, After Effects) as well as gaming (Team Fortress 2, Watchdogs, Diablo III, Life is Strange) and works great in all aspects. When I purchased this, I was worried about battery life, but in two years I still haven't needed to replace or charge the batteries yet. I was also worried about lag, being a wireless device, but I don't sense any. I'm very happy with this mouse, and would buy it again.

UPDATE: After almost 4 years, the mouse started having problems with the switch under the left-click. Not a complaint, because I love this mouse. It was time to order a replacement one, so I did. I ordered THIS model, the same one I purchased 4 years ago. I plugged the replacement mouse into my iMac (OSX 10.13.6) and expected it to simply work. After all it was exactly the same model, right? It did not work. The Logitech drivers claimed that it could not detect any Logitech devices. What the ?! I had the latest drivers installed, and my old mouse was working (minus the click problem) just fine moments before.

After some research, I come to learn that the M705 has changed. Different weight, different laser, missing the hidden button. Essentially it was a different mouse. I am very disappointed in Logitech, and angry about this deception. If the specs of a specific model of mouse change, you should create a new product for it. I can't order this mouse, because now I won't know if I'm getting the older version I loved, or the new version that is useless.

*sigh* . Very sad. I used to love this mouse.

**Photo shows my old mouse on the left, and the replacement on the right. What the photos won't show is the weight/feel difference. The new one is lighter and cheaper feeling.

title: Wears Out Too Fast!
text:
I've had one of these for years. When it was new it worked very well, although I didn't like the heavy spring. I replaced it with a lighter one and was happier with its feel.

The problem I had was that after a relatively short time it would no longer reflect the position of the stick accurately. The calibration software takes you through a series of steps. First you tilt the stick in every direction to establish the limits of its motion. On screen an indicator shows how much the stick has moved. The indicator can't reach the four corners of the display area. If I hold the stick all the way in one corner the indicator on the screen jumps around a little. My guess is the sensors that detect the stick position are noisy. So I can roll rapidly to the right but only slowly to the left. That's pretty much a sure-fire recipe for getting shot down.

I've had similar problems with other inexpensive joysticks. I suspect it's due to using cheap potentiometers as sensors. They are cheap electro-mechanical devices that are suited to controlling the volume of a transistor radio but aren't up to the heavy wear and tear of a joystick used for gaming.

If you don't mind buying a new one each year it's a fine joystick.

title: Excellent Keyboard/Case For iPad Pro (Retiring After Nearly 5 Years of Use)
text:
After using the Apple keyboard for the iPad Pro since I first purchased my new tablet, I found it had a number of annoying shortcomings.

So I decided to try the Logitech Create which was my secondary choice when I purchased my iPad.

Several things that I like about the Create are:
* integrated keyboard & case
* backlit keyboard
* strong magnetic hold to keep case shut to protect the screen
* stronger magnetic hold to side of the iPad compared to the Apple keyboard
* easier to clean than the materials used on the Apple keyboard

Yes the case adds bulk and weight compared to the Apple Keyboard, but it is minimal and the improved magnets used make up for it.

I travel internationally on a regular basis I and need a case/keyboard that is rugged and versatile as well as to provide protection to my iPad which has replaced my Mac Book as my travel companion.

If you are looking for a case/keyboard for your iPad Pro, I highly recommend the Logitech Create keyboard case

***UPDATED November 2016***

After having used the case for several months now, I still love Logi compared to Apple's keyboard cover.

There is however one short coming I have found with this case that I am not pleased with.

The volume controls protrude enough from the edge of the case to allow for snags that can pull the button away from the case and rendering the external audio controls worthless with the buttons still extended for further snagging.

** MAY 2020 UPDATE **

I originally purchased my Logo case for my 1st Gen iPad Pro about 5 years ago in order to use my iPad as a replacement for my MacBook Pro and Air since neither were convenient with my extensive international traveling for work.

Pros:

1. Excellent iPad protection
2. Relatively light weight
3. Highly functional keyboard with good tactile feel and backlighting
4. Stays closed and does not interfere with camera or speakers
5. Superior to products offered by Apple

Cons:

1. Had a quality issue within a few months of purchase (replaced by Logitech that took some work and time)
2. Fabric outer material attracts dirt and hair, hard to clean
3. Can drain iPad battery quickly if used heavily
4. Logitech stopped supporting firmware updates

Overall this has been an excellent product that has worked well for me and lasted long enough until I was ready to finally upgrade y iPad Pro to the Gen 5 model.

So in the last few weeks as I was waiting for my new iPad to be shipped, a few keys stopped functioning and the plastic button for the power button fell out.

Since I found that the Logi product worked so well and lasted for so long, I decided to order the new Slim Folio for the Gen 3/4 iPad Pros over the cool new Apple Magic keyboard which is like x3 the cost and appears to lack the function keys.

I am looking forward to my new keyboard and hopes that it lasts as long as this old trusted work companion has.

I game at a desk with a mouse and keyboard in front of me, so placing it front and center isn't an option. I ultimate decided to return to using my headset.

I also tried using this microphone with my PS4, but all my friends begged me to switch back to my headset because it sounded like I was talking to them through a tunnel. It's not the microphone's fault. It provides great sound quality. It's just a problem inherent with using a stand alone mic as opposed to one that's placed right next to your mouth.

I'd recommend this microphone to anyone looking for a cheap starter microphone for doing Youtube videos or podcasts, but not for any form of gaming. If you're going to be pushing buttons at all, that's all your friends will hear.

title: Works great for controlling media devices
text:
I have used the Logitech Harmony One for years. I found the Hub much easier to set up and operate using an android app. The Hub does a better job of controlling my devices with a lot less setting up and configuring devices than the Harmony One. I use the Hub to control my TV, amplifier, streaming devices (ROKU and Fire TV Stick) and Happauge USB Dual. I have connected the Hub with Alexa, using the Echo Dot. It works well, but has limited application. I am hoping for expanded control support in the future.

I was surprised to learn that the Hub only supports 2.4G WiFi. I live in a condo with 162 units. So, the 2.4G WiFi band is over-crowded. So far, though it does not seem to be a problem. Also, the Hub needs to be placed in very close proximity to the devices for the IR to operate successfully. In spite of the fact that my entertainment devices are on a open shelves, I had to place the Hub within inches of the IR receptor on my TV to get it to operate the TV. My other devices are working on lower shelves without a hitch. I would like to see dual band WiFi and a little better range for the IR.

I am very happy with the Logitech support. I had to contact Logitech support twice. In both cases the support agent help solve my problem quickly.

I am very satisfied with the operation and functionality of the Harmony Hub. It takes time and patience to set up the Hub and to get it to operate optimally. Once it is set up you will not need to fiddle with it again unless you add or change devices.

Logitech updated android app 11/22/16. The updated app is working much better than the prior version. It used to drop the WiFi connection. Now is maintaining the WiFi connection and operating better without glitches that appeared in prior version.

text:
Initial thoughts as I test the keyboard out.

Hi I’m testing out a new keyboard that might be the best typing keyboard ever made!
So far it is very responsive and feels rather nice to type with, although, the keys maybe a tad bit sensitive. It is not loud at all, hardly hear myself typing. I was told this is a mechanical keyboard, which I wanted, but it does not appear to be the case. I also read that this is a good quality keyboard, but I question the quality: the keys have stickers that identify them instead of being painted on. Rubbing alcohol will probably remove them so be careful. I wonder how long they will last as the finger residue builds up. I have always liked keyboards that were island based and this is no expectation.

The layout is nice, and even though it is a smaller keyboard, I feel as though I would be ok typing a postgraduate paper with no problem. Would be nice to have a little bit of wrist support, but, I understand this is more of a portable keyboard as opposed to a stay at home keyboard.

I will be using it for stay at home due to the size of it. My last keyboard, a normal size, took up most of the space and crowded into my mouse (wanted my keyboard and mouse on the same sliding out tray part of my desk. Now they fit just fine. I just might get another one for my laptop!

So my test is complete, I have typed everything I intended to type, aside from some spelling issues, all keys pressed typed what I wanted.

I'll update in a about two months so, by that time I will have completed two postgraduate courses.

title: Gets the basics right and looks cool in the process.
text:
I've been using this mouse for the past 4-5 days and can honestly say that it's a new favorite.

There are lots of options and configurable bits here, but it's the basics that Logitech really got right...

1. The things tracks like a dream. I've used it on my reclaimed wood desktop and a large mousepad with equally good results. The wide footprint and the big slider pads on the bottom made it much easier to use on the rougher surface of the reclaimed wood desk. It was much nicer, of course, on the mousepad. The 'laser' tracking is very precise and predictable, meaning it does what a mouse needs to do very well... move the pointer around your screen accurately.

2. The primary scroll wheel has a nice clicky ratchet feel, but you can still spin it fast if you need to (aka: selecting 30,000 rows on an excel sheet). You can click a button and the wheel turns into a free-spinning wheel, which is nice. It also has an adjustable clutch mechanism to automatically switch from ratching click-click-click spinning to freewheeling, based on how fast you spin the weel, but I found that to be kinda fussy, so I just turned it off. I like the ratchet feel, but like being able to click a mechanical switch on the mouse to switch over, should the application demand it.

3. Ergonomics: I usually dislike the mice that you have to 'palm' (put your whole hand over 'em instead of just holding with fingertips), but I decided to give this one a try anyway. This is the first one that fit my larger hands (I wear a glove size 'large' or 'xl').

The other stuff: This thing looks cool and well made. It blends right in next to my DasKeyboard 4s (matte black). The gesture controll switch is pretty cool and, if I can program myself to use that feature without having to think so much about it, I can see it being very handy. I also like that it uses a micro USB cable for charging... I hate having a slew of propritetary design charging cables rolling around in my desk drawer, so using the same one that my power bank, headset and other devices (except my phone, curse you Apple) use is very appealing.

title: Problem with the background software for older computers, fast, smoother hardware, better than the C922 for 40 bucks more.
text:
I have the C920 which I just bought from Amazon a few weeks ago to do some Skyping for job interviews. I also used it to communicate with my friend George who is teaching computer science in Saudi Arabia. The frame rates are supposed to be identical on the C920 and the C922 for the 1080 P resolution. The C922 is supposed to be double for the 920 P lower res, so I thought the hardware must be a little more capture accurate, and I put both side by side and swapped the USB plugs. I waved my hand fast to make it blur, and I could definitely see a better picture (less blurring) on the C922 at the full 1080 P resolution rate.

My computer is a bit older about a 2009 Alienware machine running Windows 7, so when I tried to load the background replacing software and it came up and complained it needed to have a particular instruction set (processor assembly instructions I believe) to work. Since my machine is too old to have that there is no way to make it work, so I couldn't test that aspect. I don't really intend to do anything with the XSplit license, but I suspect it would have similar problems with the older computer hardware.

Bottom line given the 40 dollar difference in the price, you have to go on the faster smoother hardware to want to pay that over the C920 model. Unless you want to use this as a continuous streamer or to take quality motion videos with, save the cash and go with the C920 model over this C922. If you are going to stream or take video to make a home movie or business presentation, then the newer model C922 is the better choice. As for the software, I don't assign much value to it, if you have a newer machine you can probably run it, but if doing a professional streaming task with your webcam look to get something that works well and is well rated for that.

Recommended if you want one of the faster webcams with clear picture and easy to use and set-up. Like my C920 if all you need is a clear picture for Skype, you don't need the extras. I do like the design of both of these they easily perch on top of my monitor, and you can fold up the mount and use the tripod threaded mount to perch this up high, to monitor an area away from the computer.

title: Sound quality and volume nearly the equal of the high end systems in a medium priced 2.1 system with movie quality THX.
text:
Wow, this is great, I have super sound now for my Dell Mini Tower Computer, my Blu-Ray player, and my Flat Screen TV all connected at the same time in the back master bedroom. In the living room area of my house I have my biggest flat screen TV, and a Boston Acoustics sound system. In my front bedroom, I have my Alienware tower, connected to a 2.1 Klipsch sound system. My Dell Mini Tower from the VINE has been connected to a high quality but mono bluetooth speaker until now. I connected up the computer using the 3.5 mm pin connector, then added a Blu-Ray player with the optical cable, and then connected my Polaroid 32" Flat Screen TV with RCA sound cables. In the past and with my other sound systems you can only connect one hard wired set of cables. The BA system allows bluetooth connections too, but that's a bit different.

Sound we did some good bass sounding games with tanks, bombs and machine guns, then tried out a number of CD's. I compared it with my Klipsch and my BA system, and the sound was equal in power for the most part, and the distortion was similar as the volume went up, but I'd have to say the other two systems were a bit sweeter sounding if that makes sense. Smoother, much like my Bose Alarm/CD player. Still, the sound was excellent, the bass was strong and the high notes, guitar mistakes and horns came out true to life. Brothers in Arm's Album "I Want My MTV" was almost mind blowing for such a small system. While it may not have been as refined as the other systems I have, they cost 400 and 500 dollars, and this costs 170 dollars, so I can live without the sweeter sound so long as it's not overly harsh or distorted, and it is not.

Maybe this is not quite as high end as the high end speakers of this type (but it's close), you can see the quality construction, fit and finish of the system is very good, as good as the high end brands. The base may be a bit more imposing than on the higher ends too because neither of my other systems are the theater quality THX, and I really like that for hard core gaming. Recommended for gamers, and those who want a good computer sound system for their desktop computer, but without the high end price. Would work as well in the living room for those of us who like good sound, but can't fathom how someone can install seven speakers and a subwoofer all around the whole room, too many wires for me. I like the 2.1 systems like this.

UPDATE: Someone asked me a question about this, and I tried to find the a picture of the back of the SubWoofer online, but they must have searched too, because for some reason Logitech did not publish one. It seems to be too new to find a PDF manual online, and I didn't want to dig my SubWoofer out from under the desk where I set it up at, so I did the next best thing. I took a cell phone picture of the back inputs printed on one of the box flaps. I'm posting in there so you can see where the three inputs are for optical, RCA, and 3.5mm pin connections.

title: Impossibly thin and light while maintaining good key action feel!
text:
Are you kidding me? - That's what I thought when I first pulled this out of the box. I could not believe how thin this thing actually was. I didn't think I could possibly like it until I tried it and realized that yes, you can still get good key action and a great typing experience with something that could almost give you a papercut. Logitech has hit another home run as far as I'm concerned with this keyboard. I have owned several different types of portable/bluetooth/travel/iPad/iPhone keyboards before and this one is King of Keyboards in my opinion! Here are a few things to note about this keyboard:

- The thinnest/lightest keyboard you will find that still provides good key pressing action and rebound. Incredible! I keep it in my backpack with my iPad Air 2 at all times and it would be impossible to tell the difference in the weight and girth of my bag with or without it.
- It is not flimsy in the least! Just because it's impossibly thin doesn't mean you're compromising on durability and sturdiness. Somehow, this has both! This keyboard does NOT bend at all.
- The keys are full size! Typing on this is SO much better than relying on the iPad keyboard, especially for busy students or professionals or travelers who rely on their iPad rather than a laptop for writing emails or drafting documents.
- The battery seriously lasts forever. It has an on/off switch and a small light indicator showing when it's on, connected, fully charged etc. I go months without charging this!! When it is time to charge, it does so quickly and with a mini USB that everyone has 10 of laying around.
- Your device will remember it and pair automatically within seconds of switching the keyboard on.
- The feel of this keyboard is unlike anything I've ever felt before. It's made of a really soft material that almost feels like fabric somehow, but it's durable and easy to wipe clean. Over the years some fading has occured on some of the keys, but all of the letters/numbers/symbols remain entirely intact. I'm sure it's just normal wear due to the oils in our fingers. As you can see from the pictures, it hardly looks bad enough to put it out to pasture just yet.

I have owned and heavily used this keyboard for about 2 and a half years now and I still love it as much as the day I first connected it. Besides my case and screen protector, this is the next most important iPad accessory that I own. You will NOT be disappointed if you purchase this. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

And for the record, I did NOT receive this product free or at a discount. I paid full price for it and am writing this review just to help other people who pay full price for stuff too!

title: Incredibly bulky, but gets a specific job done.
text:
Designed along with help from Apple, the Logitech CREATE Backlit keyboard is the first third-party keyboard available that connects to the iPad Pro's Smart Connector. While other keyboards from Logitech and other brands rely on a built-in rechargeable battery and connect via Bluetooth, the Smart Connector means no batteries are needed, as the keyboard gets all of its juice from the iPad itself.

There are really only two types of keyboards to pick from currently with this Smart Connector. The CREATE keyboards and Apple's own Smart Keyboard. I own the Apple Smart Keyboard, and so a comparison is easy between the two.

1.) The CREATE is incredibly heavy. It literally doubles the weight of the iPad Pro when connected. The added bulk is immediately apparent, bringing the iPad Pro's weight in line with a 13" MacBook Air. That's not really a flattering comparison...

2.) Getting the iPad Pro into the CREATE is pretty terrifying, requiring a bit of force and "wedging" of the iPad. Once it's in there, it's not going anywhere, and getting the iPad out is an equally daunting process. Certainly not for the faint of heart.

3.) The keyboard feels great to type on, and unlike the Apple Smart Keyboard, you have full access to iPad brightness and volume controls, something the Apple keyboard really could use.

4.) The backlighting system also works great, and has several levels of brightness, plus off. The Apple keyboard doesn't.

5.) When you don't want to use the keyboard, it's just kind of dangling there, in the way. And then you're holding a ~3lb device in your hands, which isn't fun.

Overall, there's no two ways around it - this is a keyboard designed to be attached and your iPad Pro, and the device used as a traditional laptop computer. At this point, depending on your uses, you may be better off using a MacBook Air, which is about the same price as the this keyboard + iPad Pro...

Conversely, the Apple Smart Keyboard, while not backlit, and missing some of those media keys, is removable/re-attachable in just one second (literally), is considerably lighter, waterproof, and might just be more useful to you. It's certainly worth checking out both...

3.5 stars out of 5. Good, but with plenty of caveats...

- The settings you can program in the software are amazing!
- The interactive scrollwheel is amazing. You can change it's settings, but basically the rattle on/off is now electronically controlled, which adds the future that it can automatically disengage (and re-engage) with fast scrolling
- For some reason the scrolling is not accurate; it sometime does 2 lines, sometimes 0 per click. I may need to play with the settings.
- The multi-device feature is great (finally!!!). Which they had the button accessible on the top though for fast switching...

Overall: I am amazed that they were able to add so many improvements to something as simple as a mouse.

title: Good product but 3.5 mm mini-plug audio output is lacking
text:
I've had the Logitech 980-000910 Bluetooth adapter for a couple of months now and it's been working flawlessly.

It comes with both the 3.5mm-1/8" female mini-plug connector and traditional two port RCA red and with female ports.

I was hoping to use the 3.5mm mini-plug into one of AV ports of my Yamaha RX-A730 receiver however it sounded horrible. "Tinny" as if I was listening to one of those old AM portable radios from the '60's.

However when I switched to a standard two wire (red and white) RCA cable to input the analog signal from the Logitech into the same AV port on my receiver the sound quality was exceptional and was exactly what I was looking for with my Spotify.

Obviously I was a little disappointed with the failure of the 3.5 mm mini-plug hence only 4 stars. But by using the old RCA audio ports I can still have great high fidelity sound through a bluetooth connection to enjoy music through my 5.1 surround sound system.

title: I feel that it deserves a bit more than just a negative review and after using some more headphones that are now considered mid-
text:
I honestly have a hard time recommending this product, but from the others that I have used that are at this price range, I feel that it deserves a bit more than just a negative review and after using some more headphones that are now considered mid-budget headphones in 2016 (H2100’s for instance) I can actually recommend it.

+ Comfort... I think it’s perhaps the most comfortable of the wireless headsets around that price point. The faux leather is actually very soft and does not create a sweat ring around my ear, the shape is actually perfect for my hear and covers the whole thing without touching at all.
+ Sound is fine for the price point that it’s at now. The bass is kind of blown up a ton in DD 7.1 mode and can come across almost distorted, thankfully not distorted. Everything else is fine.
+ Buttons! It has buttons that made it really convenient for using things like Netflix, Spotify, things that respond to play/pause commands. The mic mute is seriously awesome since I do use this as a VOIP headset at work (have for over a year now), one of the biggest reasons that I’m sticking with this headphone actually. The other buttons are also programmable and I’m a bit of a Powershell nut so I can set them to do things like answer my VOIP, open my case file and OneNote at the same time. And they are context sensitive buttons, so they change depending on the app that’s running.
+ Microphone is good, comes with an indicator light on it telling you when you’re muted or not. It picks up my typing, but so far every other wireless gaming headset has. My Plantronics bluetooth earpiece doesn’t, however, so I’m sure there’s the tech out there and perhaps some higher-priced and newer tech cans might come with a better mic. Rotating the microphone upwards does mute it automatically, a kind of standard feature from headsets that have rotating mics.
+ Wireless range is actually pretty good compared to H2100s, Turtle Beach Stealth 500 and ManO’Wars. I was surprised by this fact that I can go downstairs, into my garage and to the outside beer fridge, get a cold one and not have to worry about disconnecting or losing a call or hearing stuttering from Spotify, just about everywhere in my house it will work.

- The buzzing noise. It happens perhaps once a week and is quite annoying (understatement). This happens sporadically, I haven’t found any triggers for it, but when it does happen there is a very loud buzzing sound that overwhelms the audio very quickly and a underlying tone that sound like perhaps the things are getting interference from something. At work these cans don’t do that, so it very well may be a setup at home that causes the buzzing noise, but still they shouldn’t do this. My other wireless cans don’t have this problem at all. It will go away if I turn off the headphones for about 2 minutes.
- Disconnects. These don’t happen all too often, but occasionally (once every other week) the headset goes through a fit of disconnecting and reconnecting over and over for about a minute; I have to play around with turning it off and plugging it into the charger.
- A standby mode? After not using them, the things go into standby that they don’t actually wake up from. You have to turn them off and back on.
- Off button doesn’t always turn off. You have to hold down the power button for about 5 seconds and sometimes longer if the button doesn’t seem to press right. That’s to turn them off. Thankfully they turn on quickly.

Other things of note:
I used these things heavily, 10-12 hours a day for over a year (Aug 15 to now). Here’s the wear and tear stuff that has happened in that time:

* Recently the left joint where it rotates cracked, allowing the left earpiece to swivel in both directions so that it can do a full 180. This happened about a month ago, however.
* Battery life lessened quite a bit. I used to be able to go almost an entire day without needing to charge them (I used them for over the advertised hours by the way). But now they only last about 6 hours, and the decline happened about 6 months ago. Now I leave the things plugged in a lot.
* The headband pressure was light to begin with but only got lighter with use. I actually like that a lot as it’s more comfortable. The headset doesn’t fly off my head, but I’m not tossing my head around. If I lean back a good bit the headset will fall off, just looking up doesn’t do it. My Corsair H2100’s felt like they weren’t going to fall off even if I was crawling around headbanging, but they are newer and the pressure they put on my head makes me want to take them off often.
* The microphone boom started to loosen up. There’s an easy fix to tighten it by removing the ear pad (5 small screws in the red plastic just under the pad, and then tighten down the screw on the boom. However, do not undo the screw. There’ s a nut on the backend of it and if you unscrew it too far the nut comes loose and you have to take apart the whole earpiece to get to the nut again.

Logitech support was actually very good to me. I got a replacement of these after about a year and the newer set didn’t have the above problems immediately. I can’t say that they won’t develop the same problems, but support was really good about it. I’m not a fanboy, but I do happen to own a bunch of Logitech stuff. These headsets were great except when they weren’t… and they weren’t great often enough that I was giving them 3 stars and only because of their price point now. Had I paid top dollar, I’d probably be more upset. Given support’s quick responses, I give them another star, plus the things have a 3-year warranty, which I didn’t know until I went to get my stuff fixed.

Bottom line:
For the price that I find these things at now, I recommend them over similar products just for the convenience of them, the comfort and the quality of support that I have experienced from Logitech (even non-gaming stuff). The only headphones that were more comfortable were my broken-in, ATHm50x and those are also more expensive.

I used a Turtle Beach Earforce stealth 500, Razer ManOWar, Corsair H2100s and Creative Tactics3D Rage wireless and of these I prefer to use my G930’s and the ManOWar the most.

title: It sounded like I was grounding in feedback and there was an ...
text:
The main 1/8" cable that connects it to the computer is poorly (if at all shielded). It took me 5 minutes re-arranging my desk to get rid of all of the distortion. It sounded like I was grounding in feedback and there was an electrical short. But once I isolated the main audio cable and moved the subwoofer from the other electronics on my desk it sounds fine.

Now the unit is producing excellent bass and mid range. The lack of tweeters is noticeable if you pay attention, but isn't otherwise. All said and down, I believe these speakers are worth the ~$111 I paid for them.

If you have a lot of electronics under your desk (it really seems to hate power supplies), then I'd recommend investing in a shielded cable to replace the crap cable it ships with. Or maybe you could try wrap the audio cables in foil. As said, physically isolating the audio cables from the power cables uder my desk did the trick for me.

title: The perfect mouse with the worst flaw.
text:
Pros: Incredible design and features. Absolutely adore the feeling of the mouse in-hand. Perfect weight. Wireless. The auto scrolling fast-scroll is a dream. The side-scrolling makes using OSX with a mouse a must-have. The buttons feel tactile and have a very nice click without being too loud. The thumb button is absolutely incredible for setting gestures. The Logitech Software, for once, is amazing even if it doesn't have a ton of power user options, setting gestures and buttons are great. Multiple wireless profiles is a fantastic feature, great for switching between computers.

Cons: This is a really big one and it explains why the rating is so low. Everything above is what a perfect mouse should be, but the biggest downfall, which absolutely ruins the entire experience, is the polling rate of the mouse reporting to the computer. With Bluetooth, it polls around 45-85hz. With the 2.4Ghz wireless dongle, it polls 80-125hz. I tested the polling rate on my Macbook and my PC with same results. What does this mean exactly? It means the cursor isn't smooth and jitters around on the Bluetooth connection. (Bluetooth-LE is able to handle a 150hz polling rate). The polling dips below normal screen refresh rates (60hz) so the cursor isn't precise and stutters about. It just feels bad. There's also an 8ms delay in movement because of Bluetooth. Even when connected to the 2.4Ghz dongle, the mouse smoothness was still not great. It wasn't worth the compromise paying $80 for a Mouse that was less than a perfect experience.

It's absolutely a shame.

title: Absolutely Amazing with Alexa!
text:
I love this device! I recently set up a home theater in my basement with a huge projector screen. I didn't want to have any of my electronics near the screen so I created a shelving unit to the side using plumbers pipes. The only problem I had was with the Logitech Harmony 650 remote I was using and a structural beam in my basement. I would have to hold out my arm with the remote in order to get a signal to my devices around the beam. It was a HUGE pain, and family members couldn't quit figure it out.
Then I found this remote/hub and thought it could solve all my problems and it did. Not only did it solve the problems I knew I had but also solved problems I didn't realize I had. No longer did I have to point the remote in just the right way to get everything to work just right. In fact I could point it in the complete opposite direction and it still works. Solved the problem of family members pointing the remote at the projector screen and nothing happening as well.
Not only did the remote solve the issue I knew I had but also solved the issue of having to press buttons! This is where Alexa comes in! I never had an Amazon Echo Dot before this, but now I'm not sure what I would do without it! I EASILY set up an Echo Dot to control the powering on and powering off of all my entertainment devices. I can simply say "Alexa, turn on Netflix" and it will power on my projector, my receiver, set proper inputs, and tell Roku to open the Netflix app. I never knew this was possible, but I was happily surprised. Now even my mother-in-law can't mess this up, well she can but she is talented at doing so.
I have now bought several other Amazon Dots to place around my house for listening to music and turning on the smart lights I have started to buy and I couldn't be happier.
Overall I would say that this is a great product for both control your devices, as well as interacting with Alexa through the Amazon Echos.

Perhaps the long "palm rest" makes that worse. having to raise the back so much does put the whole keyboard up higher. This may be the deal breaker.

I think that from now on I will stick with the $20 keyboards.

title: No instructions included... by design (not for those with unsteady hands, but that didn't affect my review).
text:
First off, a caution that has nothing at all to do with the poor review score I gave them. This will not likely work if you do not have a steady thumb. I have a slight tremble, so I need to stick with a mouse. Now the reason for the rating.

Two stars is all I'll ever give a company that does not include a basic instruction manual and puts any of the information that might be of value in a seriously small font. In a much smaller font than the part number is, there is a link to a website that includes the model in the link. You get there and then you still have to search for your model. The product does come with 4 very small pictures on one page though. I get that they want to save paper, but there was plenty of room to put the link to the website in the same size font that this review is written in. The part number is 3x larger type than the web site link, which you go to and then, and then find out you need some software too. You can't adjust anything in control panel. I don't mind needing software, but they could have put something about that in the hieroglyphs. Despite having entered the specific product in the link, you still have to search for your product. Stupid. Logitech is to cheap to spring for a couple of extra drops of ink to make their stuff easily readable. In the picture, find the word "Unifying." Thank you Amazon for a great return policy!

Update. The top of this page is the only place you will find a description of the buttons. Yeah, I know what the left and right button are, but I didn't know what the ones that turned out to be forward and backward were. You'd think they would have a small (small is all they do) diagram on the page for the device, but all they have are drivers and an entry saying that there is no user manual.

title: I love how the software (which you download from the Logitech ...
text: I'm actually quite impressed with all the things this mouse can do. I use it with Mac OSX Yosemite (10.10.5).  Here's my experience: I love how the software (which you download from the Logitech website) allows you to map the buttons and wheels to so many different functions. I currently have the side wheel mapped to audio volume control, the thumb gesture button set to screen capture, the two side buttons set to switch desktops (left/right).  The scroll wheel is pretty cool too; it has clicker mode (the wheel's motion is resisted by a clicking) and it can be switched to smooth scrolling mode (where the wheel spins freely).  It's a physical analogue of scrolling momentum which OSX uses when you scroll on the Apple track pad; in this case it's physical momentum of a spinning wheel - which is pretty cool.

title: Caveat Emptor
text:
The sound quality is good when there is no interference. Unfortunately, it is a lot more sensitive to interference than other wireless headphones I've used. But when it works, it works well, and they'd be comfortable enough for extended use if that were an option anymore.

Unfortunately, my unit began to wear out within a matter of months. The battery began to die faster and faster, but it would turn on and off every few seconds when charging, so it would only be good for less than an hour at the best of times, then it had to charge without being used for three more hours. I knew I had wasted my money when I plugged in the cheap earbuds that came with my phone in order to finish watching a single episode of a tv show.

And the best part is, despite the warranty, Logitech was completely useless. Every time I contacted them I got a list of tips to try and questions to answer, even when responding to a nearly identical message with all the information they requested. They did not honor their warranty, and I will not trust them as a company in the future. I expect this crap from the sketchy people selling $10 to $20 headphone, but Logitech should know better.

Don't waste your money. Get something reliable from a company that cares about their customers.

text:
I have 2 of these. Something you won't learn from YouTube videos is they have poor quality control. My 2 webcams have COMPLETELY different video quality, even down to the zoom.

When I only had one, I noticed no real quality issues. It wasn't until I got a second that I realized they were absolutely nothing alike, no matter WHAT I did with my settings. This means whether you get one with wide angle or a tigher one, a warmish tint or bluish one, is a roll of the dice. Because at ANY matching settings, these two webcams look nothing alike.

You won't notice this with just one. But if you have a specific need and expect this budget webcam to fix it, be warned they vary greatly. Sitting 3 feet from my webcam, one placed upon the other, both zoomed out to max, my arm leaves the edge of one screen a full 8" before it does the other, tested playing themn side by side with OBS and manually adjusted controls to match. It's THAT bad.

title: Hey Logitech, it's 2016.
text:
There is no reason why any home automation device that relies on Wi-Fi in 2016 should (1) only be able to communicate on the 2.4ghz band and (2) fail to connect if you use a 5ghz/2.4ghz dual radio access point with a single SSID.

My network is a mix of devices that prefer 5ghz and 2.4ghz. In order to get a Harmony Hub to work, I would need to:
- rename the 5ghz network for the poor little confused piece of plastic
- reconfigure all my devices that I want to move to the newly named 5ghz network
- move my Echo and phones that prefer less congested 5ghz into noisy 2.4ghz so they're on the same network as the Hub

I have 31 devices on Wi-Fi from a mix of vendors and across both bands. Logitech Harmony Hub's failure stands alone. These radio chips are probably made by the same people who did the fans for Logitech Revue.

title: Fits my big hands. Tracks smoothly and accurately, incredibly comfortable. Battery life has been a little disappointing.
text:
One of the best mice I've used. Having spent several years as a PC gamer, I spoiled myself with excellent mice. This bled over into work, and I simply could not abide the crappy wired mice most employers hand out with machines. I work in IT, and am in front of a computer most days and this puppy is a pleasure to use. It fits my big hands perfectly, and is incredibly comfortable. The ability to adjust the DPI works great and the tracking is smooth and accurate. While I prefer a tactile response to the scroll wheel, the ability to turn it on/off is pretty nifty. My couple criticisms are that the forward/back buttons are a little higher up than I'm used to, but I'm already getting used to it. Also, after a couple weeks of use, I am noticing I get about a week of charge before I have to plug it in again. It's not that big of a deal since if I forget, I can still use it while charging, but I certainly expected a little better battery life.

The Good
- Large and ergonomic, it fits my big hands perfectly (which is a feat).
- DPI and tracking is smooth and precise.
- Rechargeable, and ability to use while charging, is fantastic.

The Bad
- The forward/back buttons are a little higher up than I'm used to reaching for. I would have preferred they were placed where the zoom button is, but I'm already getting used to the difference.
- Battery life is surprisingly short. Using at work (M-F, 8-5) I get about a week's worth. I expected better.

I really love this mouse. Sadly, my employer's policy is not to allow downloads on company machines so I haven't been able to play with the finer points of functionality the mouse offers but what I can say is that despite not having the software the mouse works perfectly, and the major functionality I need from a mouse is there.

I'm going to order a better battery to see if that fixes the battery life issue, and will update with results.

If you're looking at this mouse, you already realize the difference a higher-end mouse brings to the table. This is a great choice, and I couldn't be happier.

title: fairly well pleased.
text:
So far so good. It shipped quickly, in fact arriving a day early. Very well packaged.

I bought this one because I've had good experience with Logitech products before, and this folio/keyboard meets expectations. For being so thin, it has a pretty sturdy feel to it. The magnets do hold it shut very well, and the one that holds the ipad in the propped up position is impressively strong, too. I do question the ability to put your ipad mini to sleep just by shutting the cover. I tried it, and I can still see a blue glow around the edges. You will want to play it safe and use the sleep button. Also, the sleep/wake button is completely covered and requires a definite effort to engage. You have to press just a bit harder than you think. I was surprised that the side buttons on the ipad are not covered when the folio is closed. This isn't a deal breaker, but surprising considering how thoroughly the sleep button is covered, and it might leave your device vulnerable to being accidentally muted, or the volume adjusted, if you just have it tossed into a tote bag or something.

The keys are of a surprisingly decent size. Of course they are a whole lot closer together than the average typist is used to, a given considering the keyboard can be no wider than the device, and that requires that you give it some real attention, double checking the 'home' position of your fingers and practicing with the half sized side keys. But I really think that you can get used to the positioning in time. And they feel like real keys, which I consider a strong point.

The surprisingly low price makes up for the few drawbacks. Maybe if I were completely dependent on my mini for all my typing/computing, I might want something a bit more; but for how I use it, just emails and browsing, I think this will work well.

title: A NICE, SOLID NO NONSENSE KEYBOARD FOR IPAD
text: I read a lot of reviews here on Amazon on many clam shell type keyboard/ covers for iPad. I had a Zagg that came with my used iPad3 and had finally worn it out after nearly three years of continuous use and wanted to try something different. The reviews on the Logitech Keyboard Folio seemed generally positive so I decided to try it. When it arrived I opened the well designed packaging and was at first not certain that I'd made a good choice. My old Zagg seemed heavier and more solid in comparison and I wasn't sure about the molded plastic interior, but my apprehension was unfounded. This has proven to be a really well designed, solid piece. I love the larger size of the keys, they're smooth to operate and the keyboard commands are logical and easy to access. The magnets hold the iPad securely at a good view angle and hold it in the closed position very solidly. Battery time before needing recharging is excellent. The outer cover (I got the black covering) is tough, looks good and is easy to clean. I didn't require an ultra light unit, I rather like the solid heft of it, and it doesn't feel any heavier than my old Zagg. We ordered a second one of these for my wife and she's happy with it as well. We had ordered a different make for her but it had issues with linking through the blue tooth connection. The Logitech links up immediately and does not drop out. I'd recommend this keyboard/ case to anyone who desires a good solid, dependable piece of gear to enhance their iPad experience.

title: Good for the price!
text:
Right. So I am very unkind to headsets. I've gone through them like tissues in the past. It's not something I'm proud of, but it's a thing.

I've recently re-ordered these after 2 1/2 years, which is a personal record for me. Technically, the headset I have still works, as well.. It's an ugly mess, and the faux-leather WILL wear out on you after a time, as cheap faux-leather tends to do, but this thing has been incredibly hardy. It's only just now started to stop holding its charge well, which along with the cosmetic issues is why I'm simply replacing it, even if Logitech is actually pretty good about having replacement parts for you.

Here's a bit of a breakdown:

PROS
- Holds at least a 10 hour charge, pretty consistently.
- You can use it while it's charging. A good bonus.
- Comfortable
- Pretty good wireless range. I've been able to hold conversations halfway across a one-story house with little issue
- Good sound quality, good mic quality. No pops or hissing.
- Side buttons and volume control are nice and very convenient
- Microphone can be muted either with a button, or by lifting the mic itself up. Convenient.

CONS
- The faux-leather is garbage. It's gonna wear off in about a year with regular use.
- The power button, for some reason, is very finicky. I've often had to hold it down rather hard to get it to power on and off. Considering how small and awkward the button is, it's kind of annoying
- Mic is a bit fragile. Not horribly so- it only started giving me problems around the 2-year mark, which isn't bad in comparison to past headphones
- Not a huge con, as it's very typical with most wireless headsets, but you will have moments where the signal cuts out. It's gonna happen.
- There's an indicator on the side that lets you know when your battery is dying, but if you're wearing it, you're obviously not going to see it. I believe it's supposed to make a beep when it'd dying as well, but mine never has. Also when it dies while you're talking to them, it'll make a sound like a demon has escaped it. The software monitors your battery life, which helps a bit, but only if you're paying attention.

All-in-all, this is a good headset for the price range. Overall, this headset has treated me well, though I have no doubt that some higher end headsets probably blow it out the water. Would recommend if you're wanting a relatively cheap wireless headset.

title: Reliable, Flexible, and Strong Signal-ed Wireless Mouse
text:
I bought the Logitech Wireless Mouse M185 as a college student looking for a mouse that would work easily while being durable enough to handle my hectic college lifestyle. After working with the mouse for over three months, I am in love with this product. A great two piece set of a mouse and a USB port connector that works together; this product is perfect as it is reliable, flexible, and has a strong signal. The ideal user for this product is someone who has a busy lifestyle such as a college student or a business person. Additionally, a person who works with computers on a daily basis may enjoy the wireless mouse as it is easier to work with than a corded mouse.

Reliable: This product is very reliable and works like a charm. After buying a first Logitech Wireless Mouse two years, and losing the mouse, I had to buy another one. Traveling across the country, I have taken the mouse everywhere I have gone and it has worked at every location I have been at.

Flexible: The mouse is very flexible and allows you to work on your device from anywhere in your room. I like to use my mouse with my TV screen to help ease movie browsing options on Amazon and Netflix. Also, I have been able to plug the mouse into different devices and use it with same reliability and precision as the original device.

Strong Signal: The mouse has a very strong signal for being such a small, compact mouse. I can get a signal from the mouse in a different room and through walls in my house. This signal strength may be a downfall if you lose your mouse or someone steals it from you, however that problem can be eliminated by unplugging chip from the USB port of your computer.

Overall, this wireless mouse is a great product at a great price. High quality, low price, and very reliable for such a convenient product.

title: Barb Tested - Dan Approved
text:
I didn't buy this mouse from Amazon (at least I don't think I did) but I wanted to leave a review for this amazing piece of quality engineering from Logitech. I have a co-worker who uses this mouse on a daily basis. She frequently becomes frustrated with her PC when it freezes or when an application takes more than a millisecond to respond. She becomes so frustrated that she begins to slam her mouse repeatedly into the desk. She will slam it into the desk several times until the page eventually loads. She does this AT LEAST 10 - 30 times per hour, depending on the length of the application load time. Let's do the math!!

Let's assume she uses this mouse for 6 hours per day. She works 4 days per week (since we have a day where we aren't in the office every week), and let's deduct 3 weeks for vacation, Christmas, and sick days on an annual basis. 49 weeks in a 12 month span + 24 weeks in a 6 month span (deducted 2 weeks for time away) = a whopping 73 weeks of solid beatings. 4 days per week = 292 days of destruction. 292 days * 6 hours = 1,752 total hours of pain. Let's assume she slams this precious little creature against her desk 10 times per hour (we'll aim low and be modest), and we can safely assume that she has man-handled this sturdy electronic device about 17,520 times.

If you want a mouse that could theoretically survive World War 3 (or a coworker obsessed with extremely fast load times) then this is clearly the mouse for you!!

text:

Yes, there are only 3 activity buttons (but a long-press for each expands this to 6) and you can't directly control a single device (sometimes useful to get to setup menus), but for day-to-day use it's amazing.

It comes with a hub that actually transmits the RF signals, and also works with WiFi Direct devices like the Roku. The remote doesn't need line-of-sight to work - you just have to put the hub in a good place where it can 'see' everything. Mine is on top of the TV stand tucked under the TV - the signal bounces off the back wall of the lounge and back at the devices. Rarely had a problem with that.

You know what else is awesome? When your wife messages you from home saying something isn't working, and you are able to REMOTELY (ba-dummm) use the Logitech Harmony app to connect to the hub through 'the cloud' (we used to just call it the internet) and fiddle with the devices to make everything work (change inputs, cycle power etc.). title: Almost a home-run, case only, no attached keyboard Logi Create Case
text:
After thorough use of this case, I am fairly satisfied with the product. I am using it with an IPAD Pro 12.9inch (without keyboard) and the Logitech Keys-to-go keyboard (details later).

To provide context about my rationale on this purchase, I wanted a case that would allow me to change orientations and adapt to the many positions I would find myself in whether its sitting, laying in bed, or standing. In addition, I wanted something that would provide enough resistance to the very many pushes, taps, swiping, pinching, and pulling that I would inevitably be doing with the screen so it wouldn't tip over or be too flimsy. Also, I wanted a case that would be able to provide an average amount of protection to the front, sides, and back.

To start, I looked into getting the Apple Smart Keyboard but after playing with it a few times in store, I decided against it. The reason being because the screen position was in a fixed position and didn't quite meet my expectations. The Logi CREATE not only allowed me to be flexible with different screen orientations but it also allowed me to fully utilize the Logi keyboard. The various screen positions are comfortable and convenient. I haven't found myself in a position yet that I couldn't adjust the screen to a comfortable position. I find the lowest angle most comfortable when editing pictures. The screen stands its ground satisfactorily through the many taps, swipes, and presses through the time i've had it. When closed, the case looks sleek and provides minimal protection (which is to be expected from a portfolio case like this) but it's a welcomed addition as I don't intend on taking this iPad hiking or through adverse envronments that would require better protection.

A couple gripes. First, the volume buttons aren't very tactile. In fact, I wouldn't know that I was decreasing or increasing volume if the volume meter didn't pop up during the changes. Second, same story for the lock button. There is hardly any feedback to know you're actually pressing something. Lastly, and this is more of a concern more than a gripe, but there is a certain stiffness to the back of the case where it bends and flexes. This stiffness is most appreciate; however, I wonder how long it will last after heavy, tong-term use.

All in all, with everything conersiderd, I love this case as it checks all my boxes and the pros definitely outweigh the cons. For the most part, the cons can be remedied through some minor home adjustments. With the use of the Keys-to-go, I am able to take full advantage of the portability of the ipad and being able to be in a position I feel. I removed one star for the lock and volume buttons lack of responsiveness.

text:
I use the mouse as a backup to another Logitech mouse and as an alternate for a laptop which means I currently almost never use it since my laptop is currently dead. These comments are strictly about the K350 keyboard.

This keyboard is by far one of the best multi-purpose multimedia keyboard designs out there. It never ceases to amaze me that other people haven't caught on to the fact that arranging the multimedia keys/buttons in a grid rather than a linear arrangement just makes sense. Perfect example: the volume keys are arranged (top to bottom) up-down-mute, all together rather than having the mute separated by other multimedia keys and all in a line as on other keyboards. In addition, it is both slightly ergonomic without ruining the continuity required by gaming. If it weren't for the serious impediment below I would easily give this product 5 stars.

The problem with this keyboard (and I have had several... repeat buyer) is that it is not uncommon after a while to have a mild to serious lag between when keys are pressed and when they actually appear. It comes and goes but it is really a pain when it happens. Too often the receiver does not pick up the key presses at all. Words will appear with missing letters or key-presses won't register at all because the receiver did not pick them up. At a certain point the keyboard needs to be turned off and then on again (and sometimes that doesn't work either). There is no wired version which would allow me to get rid of this problem altogether. The mouse (and my regular mouse) NEVER has any issues with signals so it is something with the keyboard alone.

EVERY K350 keyboard I have had for the past 10-15 years (4-5 altogether which have all been this model) has had this problem. The "fixes" that are recommended both by tech support and other users have never worked for me on a permanent basis (though one has improved performance so that it isn't quite as bad).

"FIX": For those who are experiencing this issue and want to know what the "best" fix is: Buy a USB extension cord that allows you to plug in the receiver a significant distance away from your computer (and the keyboard). It may not get rid of the problem but it will not happen as often and may not be as pronounced.

EDIT/UPDATE: This keyboard has been out for 10 years and they STILL HAVE NOT FIXED THIS ISSUE. The above fix helps but does not get rid of the problem which has been repeatedly encountered by people who use the keyboard for an extended period of time. It IS a manufacturer/design defect because simply hitting the thing over my knee hard enough for the batteries to come out fixes the problem (temporarily). I have talked to logitech and they do not acknowledge the issue. My guess is that there is some sort of buildup of charge or something that gets in the way of working properly and whatever it is gets discharged with physical shock and loss of power. I have to do this periodically throughout the day and I am REALLY getting tired of it. I am changing my rating to 2 stars and if they do not fix this soon, I will change it to one star.

title: Review for Gamers
text:
REVIEW FOR GAMERS

I feel the high rating on this keyboard is warranted for the majority of use cases. It's a great set.

I've logged 260+ hours in-game on this keyboard mouse combo because it's a perfectly fine set for a casual gamer. Here are some reasons I finally decided to replace it with a mouse and keyboard made specifically for gaming.

KEYBOARD:
-Does not have anti-ghosting. This means there are certain key combos that will not register. For example, In Overwatch I cannot press forward (W), sideways (A), and melee (F) at the same time. However, I can press forward, sideways, and jump (space bar) at the same time. So it's not necessarily a three key limit, but certain combos may have trouble.

MOUSE
-Does not register very quick movements. In my case, I play on low mouse sensitivity, so to move my character 180 degrees it takes a mouse/arm movement of about a foot or more to the side. The faster i move my mouse across the pad, the less likely I am to make that turn. At worst, i'll sweep the mouse the full foot to the side and my character will continue looking in the same direction and just wiggle a bit, even though the movement of my hand should have resulted in a speedy 180 degree turn. So for the majority of gameplay, this isn't an issue. It's just the really intense moments where you've got to react instantly to something outside your field of view. That's when it matters, and that's when it fails.

WIRELESS:
-Wireless dongle experienced very bad signal drop when plugged directly into the PC. In my case, this was caused by interference from the motherboard. Must use the provided extender to separate the dongle from the PC tower so it's out of range of interfering signals, which adds to cable clutter, but resolves the issue. (note: not all users experienced this)
-With this set six inches (or less) from the dongle, the wireless signal dropped keystrokes/movement/signal VERY RARELY (aside from the keyboard ghosting scenarios described above). I'd guess it happened under 5 times in 260+ hours, with two of the times being pretty dramatic and lasting a second or two. It's possible it was a battery issue, but when you're in game and you lose a second of keystrokes or mouse movements, you don't really care if it was the hardware or the battery. You just don't want it to happen again. So yes it was annoying, yes it cost me some in-game lives, but keep in mind this is five seconds out of 936,000+ seconds of play, which is perfectly acceptable for a casual gamer in my opinion.
-I also tested this keyboard/mouse seven feet from the dongle. The signal dropped too much for me to play games, but was fine for browsing the internet.

title: This is just a great product. The mouse and keyboard both have great ...
text:
This is just a great product. The mouse and keyboard both have great shapes to them that feel good to the hands. Particularly useful and nice is the thumb indentation in the mouse - it feels really natural to just rest your hand in the indentation. The built in wrist pad on the keyboard is just the right firmness/softness and prevents your wrists from getting sore after typing for a long time if your wrists were resting on a hard table. The rubber gripping surfaces on the mouse are nice too.

Buttons are of good quality and feel. The mouse glides easily across mouse pads. Battery life is pretty good with rechargeable batteries - with the batteries I use (EBL brand AA) I get about a month or two of use on a charge - it's hard to gauge exactly because I don't keep close tabs on battery recharge frequency.

My only slight beef is the relative slight noisiness of the keyboard keys when struck, but that's to be expected with keyboards of this button type, which I prefer. It doesn't bother me at all - I'm used to it. I like this style keyboard because the slightly concave surfaces of each key self-center your fingers on the buttons, and the small gaps between the keys make it easier for the fingers to discern each key and to avoid striking unintended keys vs. chiclit-style keyboards.

One other small thing to note is that the little indentations in the wrist pad and mouse grip rubber collect dust over time and take a little scrubbing to clean maybe twice a year - not a big deal - their benefits to look and feel outweigh the cleaning aspect in my mind.

Logitech really hit it right with the "WAVE" concept. It feels a lot nicer ergonomically typing with this keyboard's finger-length attentive key height variance. At the same time, it takes very little getting used to typing with this keyboard and contributes less to finger muscle and joint fatigue after long hours of typing versus a standard non-ergonomic keyboard. It's similar enough to a standard keyboard that when you're using one instead of this keyboard you won't strike a ton of unintended keys.

Small holes are even built into the bottom of each keyboard section - so that, should you spill something across your keyboard, the liquid will drain out, making it less likely that the keyboard will be shorted out as a result.

I used this set for my computer all through college. I liked it so much I bought another set for my work computer. Just a very nice, well-designed product. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

title: Recommended, BUT CONSIDER AN EXTENDED WARRANTY!
text:
Good compromise between ease of use and ergonomic design. The keys have a good action, and are fairly quiet. The built in wrist pad makes long term use more comfortable. Battery life seems good. I never really used any of the grey keys, so I can't comment on those.

This is the second unit I've had. The first lasted about 2.5 years of heavy use: about 7 hours a day, 5 days a week. After lots of use the keys were not working quite as smoothly, although all of them still functioned.

2017.03.03 UPDATE. My second unit failed after about 10 months of heavy use: about 6-8 hours per day, 5 days per week, in a clean office environment. Mechanically it was in good shape, but it increasingly began to skip characters or hesitate in transferring data to the computer, resulting in me often having to go back and retype characters or words. It was subtle at first, but increasingly frequent. When I swapped it for an old, USB wired keyboard, the problem disappeared entirely.

I notice that the keys on the new unit are noticeably stiffer than the old unit, but I remember seeing other comments that the keys seem somewhat stiff initially but relax after a little use. This seems consistent with my experience.

I like this keyboard for its ergonomics and performance, but two of the four units I've purchased required replacement: the latest one, after only 10 months use. For that reason, I've dinged my review rating from 5 down to 4 stars.

I recommend this model, but if you buy one, consider getting an extended warranty, and keep your receipt.

title: Latency Issues (when not using included extension cable)
text:
When I first received this product I put it together like I would any other USB keyboard/mouse combo. It has a tiny USB wireless dongle that plugs into the back. However, it also included an extremely long USB extension cable which I thought was silly at first. I had a great deal of latency issues for quite a long time until I tried using that extension cable and ran it to right behind my monitor so that the signal is going just a few inches from the keyboard. After that the latency issue stopped completely which is why they included the cable to begin with.

So if you don't mind depending on a USB cable this product is great. Still, I have to wonder why they didn't make the dongle a little better. Seems like the included USB cable was a short cut solution.

In any case, since it works for my needs, I restored it to 5 stars.

text:

My only complaint would be that sometimes there's a very slight delay when I first start to type after my computer has been asleep for a while, but it goes away quickly after that and I haven't had any issues with connectivity or lagging otherwise. So obviously, if you're a serious gamer or someone using the keyboard beyond "ordinary" purposes (like work or school), you're probably going to want a nicer keyboard that will hold up under strenuous use for long periods of time and never lag. Not being a gamer myself, I can't say how well it holds up under those conditions, but I can say that for the majority of users (including busy, working grad students like myself), I think this is a really nice keyboard and I love it. title: They're serious about "receiver in clear sight of the keyboard and mouse"
text:
The quick specs for this combo say "Operate up to 30 feet (10 meters) with the receiver in clear sight of the keyboard and mouse" - and that's important.

I'm using this combo for an HTPC setup where the computer is about 8 feet away from the couch, on a TV stand's bottom shelf. If I had the receiver plugged into the front panel of the computer, the keyboard and mouse worked sporadically if I sat on a chair 2-3 feet away and not at all if I was on the couch. Once I used a male-female USB extension cable to move the receiver to the top shelf of the TV stand, still as far away but now straight ahead of me and with no obstructions, the keyboard and mouse worked fine.

Before using it for the HTPC, I'd been using it for months on a desktop micro-PC and chose it because it only needed one USB port and provided two devices. There it worked solidly, with the keyboard right next to the computer.

title: Comfortable But Noisy
text:
I just received the Logitech MK550. I am using it with an Asus Zenbook laptop running Windows 8.1, and with a Logitech trackball (not the mouse that came with the keyboard).
Setup: The User Guide/Manual/Instructions were not included, which was frustrating. But I was able to find them easily enough on the Logitech website. More frustrating was the fact that, although Logitech's advertising for their "Unifying" hardware makes it seem that you should be able to "plug and play" multiple Unifying-compatible devices as easily as one device, this is not the case. The Logitech website informs you that you need to download software to connect multiple devices, and provides a link to a page with these downloads. (Word to the wise: You have to scroll down the page to find these downloads. I have my screen blown up to accommodate my eyesight, and the first half of the page tells you that there is no software needed for the MK550.) Then you download two different executable files and install them. *Now* you can pair multiple devices! I also had to add an extension to Google Chrome (per the instructions from Logitech's site) to "enable smooth scrolling."
Use: The layout of the keys allows me to type much faster and with more accuracy than I could do with my laptop keyboard, so I am very happy about that. My wrists are in a much more carpal-friendly position, too. The feel and sound of the keys, however, are both like cheap plastic, and the "cushioned" wrist rest seems to have 1-2mm of spongy stuff layered over a rock. I can live with these limitations, though, because this keyboard is such a huge improvement over using the keyboard on my laptop. Still...I can tell that the clacking sound of the keys is going to get on my nerves, and I'm glad I'm not using this keyboard around other people. If someone were using this keyboard around me, I would probably need to wear headphones (but then I'm easily distracted).
"Wave" design: I love the design. It is less extreme than the "super-ergonomic" keyboards on which your hands are on opposite sides of a small mountain, but more carpal-friendly than the standard flat keyboard.
Tiny, petty gripe: No light on the Caps Lock key.
On the whole, I would say that this keyboard is worth the money if you want something easier on your wrists than a standard keyboard and you (and anyone who works in your vicinity) can tolerate the plastic-y clacking of the keys!

For the price I was expecting better quality and reliability.

WHEN IT WORKS - everything sounds great, and output is high quality.

But when it's not working properly, the headset shuts off randomly, has tons of static or other audio artifacts (glitchy sounds, buzzing, etc).
The switch to and from Dolby doesn't work right either. The mute doesn't always work, making for some awkward situations in Teamspeak or Skype, etc.

The buttons on the side don't always work. Most notably, the volume dial hardly ever works.

The big pro's to this device is that the lasting time off the charger. And, again, when it works, the sound quality. The Logitech Gaming Software that you can download with it can be great, but, honestly, I had to go through hell just to get it to pick up my headset at first. You can get other voice profiles (voice changers). A few are included, but, surprise: you have to buy more if you want more.

I expected much better for the price. As long as they don't die out within a couple of years, I guess ill be okay with it. I suggest potential buyers do some more research and find an alternative. Unless these happen to be on a huge sale.

title: Skip this and get something better
text:
First, a complaint about Amazon's shopping process. This isn't the first time this has happened, but it's been a while. I had decided to buy the Logitech H110 headset because it had separate headphone and microphone plugs, which would work with my desktop computer's front audio ports. I had the H110 on the screen and I clicked the "Add to cart" button. It was only after my order had shipped and I got the confirmation email that I realized Amazon was sending me the H111, which has a single TRRS plug instead of two TRS plugs. Instead of sending it back, I decided to order an adapter that would split the single plug into the two appropriate plugs, since it would avoid the hassle of a return, and I would be able to use the H111 with my cellphone as a full duplex headset. This solution worked fine for my purposes (chatting while playing Rust and other multiplayer games), but I was not happy that I had to spend an extra $7, nearly the cost of the headset, to be able to use it.

Anyway, on to the actual product review. First the good: I've had reports that my voice sounds excellent in game, and my own testing with recording software has been very positive. The microphone is great at picking up my voice and attenuating surrounding noise, and has adequate pop filtering via the foam guard. The bad: The headphones sound terrible. There's simply no way you're going to enjoy the sound coming out of these earpieces. It seems like Logitech never thought someone might enjoy music or any kind of lifelike background sounds. This would be fine if they were tuned for voice reproduction, but even voices sound like the person is shouting into a tin can from across the room. Bass? What bass? With this headset, enemy footsteps are indistinguishable from innocuous nature sounds in Rust, which can get you killed pretty quickly.

The headset is fairly comfortable to wear, though after about an hour it can start to press on the earlobes a bit. Some shifting around every now and then helps with that. They are lightweight and the cord is more than long enough.

Overall, unless you just need a casual gaming headset with a TRRS plug for modern laptops or phones, you should avoid this set and spend a few dollars more on something that will be more comfortable and sound better.

title: Read the Logitech website if you're having trouble!
text:
When it arrived, I connected to my MBP using 3rd party USB-C hub, to USB 3.0 port. And soon I noticed the intermittency delay. I tried everything to my knowledge; swapping to different USB 3.0 ports, new batteries, re-pairing using Logitech Unifying Software. Nothing. As for last resort, I went to Logitech knowledge base and start reading every troubleshooting articles. And guess what? I had the solution all these time. Logitech website clearly states that USB 3.0 port can interfere the wireless signals, thus we should use the included USB 2.0 extension cable to use it with USB 3.0 port.

Now, my mouse and keyboard work flawlessly! So before you complain, try Logitech's website and see if you can find a solution too.
