title: Decently comfortable and works with Logitech keyboards
text:
If you're experiencing wrist pain/fatigue from using your mouse too much, a trackball mouse can certainly help.

And it is actually pretty comfortable and easy to use. You can tell it was actually shaped to someone's right hand. I will say that the two extra small buttons can occasionally get clicked by accident, but that could just be a matter of getting used to it.

The reason I am not giving it 5 stars is because sometimes it feels like the trackball doesn't roll as smoothly as other times, and I don't know why. It doesn't seem like there is dust or any other obstructions, but then a few moments later it will roll smooth again. So not the biggest of issues by any means, but it is an occasional annoyance (not more than taking a break to rest my wrist though), and it would be great to know the reason for it...

I'll also add that I purchased this to use with the Logitech Wireless Wave K350 keyboard that comes in the MK550 combo. In order to connect it to the same USB receiver as the keyboard, you must first unlink the M510 mouse that comes with the combo, then link the M570 Trackball, and to do so you need to use a wired mouse (I could not find keyboard commands that worked, and neither could tech support). So have a wired mouse ready if that is in your plans. Also, afterwards, I linked the M510 mouse with the USB receiver that came with the M570 Trackball, and now use that with my Chromebook. So the Logitech USB receivers are really interchangeable (unless you get a defective one).

title: Initial frustration, but works well now...
text:
I like the keyboard. I don't use all the extra shortcut buttons, but I like the keyboard. I got it to replace an older similarly curved microsoft combo set because the keys of that keyboard were slowly giving out one by one. I didn't want the full ergonomic split in the middle, so this seemed like an appropriate option. And it was especially appealing because it presented the option to link a wireless trackball mouse to the same USB receiver, should I get one like the Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (which I did). Given the price, I didn't expect that the combo would be the most high-end piece of technology, but I was hopeful it would work and not fall apart quickly. With those expectations in mind, I would like to give it 5 stars, but there was one major issue...

As I got it setup, the positives of the combo were readily apparent:

- It's a comfortable keyboard. Maybe it is because I was already using one of a similar design, but I also enjoy/appreciate the pad along the bottom below the spacebar to rest my wrists on (which my old one did not have). The pad does collect some dust, but only if you let things get dusty.
- The mouse works as expected, and is fairly comfortable as well. And while I haven't really used the extra preset keys on the keyboard, I have used the added buttons on the mouse more and more. I also really like that I can take the mouse and USB receiver and connect it to my Chromebook from time to time.
- As I mentioned before, I have also purchased the Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball to link with the usb receiver and use in combination with the keyboard. I had to unlink the mouse that comes with the combo from the USB receiver, then add the trackball, and ultimately I got it to work as I wanted (both working on the same USB port).
- I like having the option of the extra preset shortcut keys, maybe I will use them someday.

The one issue with the combo, was a major one.... The keyboard and mouse did not work correctly initially. The mouse would jump around randomly and trying to type even the simplest of emails (like to Logitech tech support) was oh-so frustrating. It appeared to be an interference issue, but given that the USB receiver was plugged in to the back of my desktop PC immediately next to the desk I was attempting to type on (less than 5 feet away), that was simply not acceptable as it was advertised to work up to 30 feet away. After a few frustratingly repetitive conversations with tech support as they worked to determine the issue, they eventually agreed it wasn't working correctly and sent me a new setup. Sometimes flawed products are shipped I suppose...

Since the new setup has arrived, I've been skeptical of it (I've kept most of the packaging), but it seems to work decently as I don't have significant interference issues. But I am not too certain of the 30 foot/10 meter range. The room I use it in is about 18 feet long, and I will occasionally notice small hiccups if I use it near that distance. But the vast majority of my use occurs within the 5 to 10 foot range for me, so it's not a big deal for me. I was frustrated for 2+ weeks, but 3+ months since then have been good... hoping for more good times.

I'll also add that if you want to connect something like the M570 Wireless Trackball, you will need to have an extra wired mouse to do the installation. This is because you have to unlink the mouse that comes with the combo, then link the Trackball afterwards, and to do so you need a 3rd wired mouse (I couldn't find a way with only keyboard commands, and Tech Support didn't know of one either). This is a little annoying, but I suppose it makes sense and is only a small annoyance in the grand scheme of things. One bonus I didn't expect though is that since the Trackball comes with its own USB receiver, once I unlinked it from the Trackball, I then linked it to the mouse from the combo and now use that with my Chromebook while I use the Trackball and keyboard with my PC.

And, like everyone else I imagine, I was also disappointed to read about the security issues with these wireless devices, so you should probably keep in mind the type of environment it will be used in.

The mouse works fine. The keyboard has a serious issue with lag. It will intermittently hang up where no keystrokes register, then it will "catch up" by spilling out a lot of characters at once. Many of the characters will duplicate, and many will be missed. Backspace will either not work or erase a lot of extra data. Makes this a totally unusable input device.

This is seriously one of the worst keyboards I have owned. I got this because I have been a loyal Logitech user for years. I've never had issues with their hardware, be it a mouse, keyboard, speakers, universal remote, or laptop pad. I've done my homework on this, and I know this is defective hardware. Other people with the same problem have gone to Logitech and have received replacements, but the issue is with the K350 keyboard itself. I did try new batteries. I'm within 5 feet of the receiver. I tried multiple USB ports, powered or otherwise. I've tried on 3 separate known working computers. I work in technology support. I know my hardware.

I first noticed this when I was using the keyboard to game. I was suddenly unable to effectively control my character movements and actions, so I switched to a wired device. Wireless used to be bad for gaming, but the tech has improved over the years so I thought I'd try. Mouse was never an issue. Then, I reconnected this keyboard to my media center. I'm back to wired now because I couldn't even type this review. I got this back in Nov, and now in Apr it is just going to be tossed in the garbage. I guess I'll have to buy a Microsoft product. I'm not getting burned again. This product should be removed from inventory and no longer sold. it is a tarnish on the company reputation. JUNK.

Update:Received replacement unit from Amazon, hooked up the new subwoofer and they are just as bad or worse. Emailed Logitech support about them. Waiting on reply.

Random times on login, the volume will be at 75%. which I never have it at. I use a SBZ soundcard. I am at my wits end with these. title: The price was fine, and the seller got this out to me ...

As I said, I bought this mouse for its scroll wheel. I have a wireless Logitech mouse with this same scroll wheel, but I have never been satisfied with wireless mice because I find too many things interfere with their movement tracking and button clicking detection. Also, that mouse's buttons' microswitches have started to go.

The M500 works perfectly. It has a nice side grip finish, and the wheel, being weighted, spins forever when it's in free spin mode, yet reasonably solidly moves with a nice, physical increment when the ratchet mechanism is engaged.

I'd buy another one in a heartbeat from this same seller if I needed one.

title: Great product!
text:
I have two MK330s -- one I use at home, one I use at work. I love it!! I see people referring to a software installation in other posts. Mine did not require a software installation. I am wondering if the feedback is being posted for the correct product because there is no need to install software for this combo.

Regardless, this product is great. My colleague and I did a test to see how far I can walk away from the computer and have the keyboard still register keystrokes in Notepad. I walked 60 feet away and the keystrokes continued to be recorded. I had to stop our test because I couldn't walk any further.

It never fails. It behaves as well as a wired keyboard, but without the wire. The battery lasts a long time. I don't think I put new batteries in it this year -- that's 9 months and counting for battery life.

The only time I have been frustrated is when transporting it from one building to another. For some reason, the K key has stuck after transporting it in my car (meaning, I would hit the K key but it wouldn't send the signal for the K press). Maybe I was a bit rough in transporting it? The problem resolved itself over time. I still love it.

I am very happy with it.

I had a Logitech C910 that I sorta liked except for the close up lens: no wide angle. I found this C920 and it seemed like a good idea. However, when I first installed it on my Win 10 PC the picture was really jerky, a problem that is quite common according to the web.
I thought I would keep it anyway so registered it and downloaded the software, something that maybe shoulda been included in the first place, installed it and problem solved. i do love the improved lighting and picture quality on this. And it has a much wider angle lens resulting in a vastly improved image. i have tested the photo function, wow, and the video function, sweeeet, and really love this thing now. The stereo mics are an improvement too.
So I do recommend this as an upgrade as long as you install and use the Logitech lws280 file available on the site for the capture software. i understand the Quicktime can be used too.
And, hey Microsoft, fix that darn autofocus problem with the lifecam, k?

title: good product.. but quite a few flaws
text:
so i've had 3 of these since i first purchased the first one 2 years ago...
i don't know where to start.. but here we go:

pros:
1. convenience, obviously. the fact that i'm not restricted to my pc is amazing. the battery life is pretty good i can go about 8 hours before needing to recharge.
2. the sound quality is really good! definitely better than my siberia v2 that i had before this.. and that i still use once in a while for other reasons (see cons.) the audio is clear and everyone i talk to thinks the mic sounds really clear, as well.
3. the ear muffs fit my ears perfectly with just enough wiggle room that i don't feel like i'm sweating profusely like with other leathery-type muffs. the buttons on the headset are amazing.
4. the buttons on the headset! i love the volume control. i love being able to mute by a quick button press or just lifting my headset's mic up. i love that i can control things like for instance, spotify. i can easily go back, go to the next song, or pause/play whenever (and this is straight out of the box, no programming) i can also pause/play movies on my VLC player.
5. i love that the program tells me if i'm fully charged yet or still need charging.

now for the cons (i wish there weren't so many)

1. not THAT convenient. if i go downstairs, i'm okay.. certain parts like the kitchen, it will cut off.. no big deal. but some days are better than others (i'm not sure why) sometimes i can go downstairs just fine, other times it keeps cutting off just from walking outside my room. and MICROWAVES, oh god. I guess mine is old and leaking because anytime someone turns on the microwave, it just cuts out completely until the microwave shuts off.
2. DO NOT trust the charger. just don't. i've learned the hard way that using the charger it comes with loosens and eventually breaks your headset from being able to charge at all. i didn't know that til after it broke, had to contact logitech for a replacement and then researched online that it's a common thing. it uses a mini-usb to charge so i just ended up just using my android charger (and eventually just purchased a separate mini-usb cable and outlet) and leaving the charger/transmitter sitting there on top of my desk connected to the pc. been doing it for 6 months now and it works great, no problems with that situation so far.
3. the comfort level could be a lot better. i often find myself switching back to my old headset because wearing these for a long time will give me really bad migraines. i've also made the mistake of falling asleep with these on one night, i ended up having to get a prescription for muscle relaxers and ibprofens to help with the neck pain. of course this could just be my own issue but i figured i'd mention it.
4. the buttons on the headset. sometimes they work, sometimes they don't. when they don't work, i have to disconnect/reconnect the transmitter.. sometimes i have to restart the logitech software.. sometimes i have to keep trying to hold the on/off button down until i'm able to restart the headset.. sometimes i have to just wait for the headset's charge to die out so that the buttons can work again on the next charge. a bit of a hassle.
5. the program isn't always accurate. sometimes it'll say it needs 3 hours to charge.. and then after 30 minutes it'll say fully charged, so i'll stop charging it and it'll only be at half bars. sometimes it'll say i have 2 more hours before it dies, and then it dies 10 minutes later... ???
6. this is the MOST FRAGILE piece of equipment i've ever owned. the first time i returned it for a replacement to logitech was because the piece above the earmuff on one of the sides was cracked and eventually the headset broke apart from it (a known issue that happens for whatever reason, there's lots of posts online about it and even reviews here about it) - the replacement was the one that stopped charging (due to the mini-usb it came with that caused it to loosen, as previously mentioned) which i then had to RMA again to logitech. and now this 3rd one i'm wearing has tape around the top of the left earmuff because one night the plastic just randomly snapped in half without warning and there happens to be wire inside that plastic so i have to tape it to hold it together (and now i'm already past the warranty timeframe so my only choice is to purchase a new one, sigh)

the picture attached to this review is what happened to my current headset.

title: The Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard is an excellent product. It features 25 programmable buttons and 3 ...
text:
The Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard is an excellent product. It features 25 programmable buttons and 3 on board buttons to switch between profiles.

The Good: The G13's ergonomic design provides a comfortable alternative to the traditional gaming keyboard. The main four keys (meant to mimic the classic WASD keys) are indented and are a natural resting spot for my fingers. The buttons are laid out such that they are easy to reach no matter where my hands are situated on the keypad. All 25 of the G13s programmable keys are extremely responsive and fully programmable. The top right "MR" button is extremely useful in a pinch. It allows you to program any one of the 25 keys without using the software. The software that controls the G13 is fairly user friendly and with a bit of practice I was able to program any of the keys with ease.

The Bad: Nothing to Report

The Ugly: I would argue that this device is well constructed and quite good looking.

The Verdict: The G13 Programmable Gameboard is a great piece of technology. For the price, it beats the comparable Razer gameboard in both price and performance.

title: They have changed the product. Less features, not noted on the packaging.
text:
t's great to do so much on a computer with just the mouse. Plus, you find one that is the right weight and feel and it becomes like part of your hand. But if you're buying one to replace your old one, it does NOT have the same features. If you want to use the wheel to middle click and zoom in and zoom out you are out of luck. Yes, I'm saying it does LESS than the old mouse. This page says it has a zoom feature. I guess that is technically true as you can set it up to zoom in OR zoom out. You can NOT set it up to zoom in and out using the wheel, like you could on the old one and like you can on almost all their other mice.

I had one for years. Loved it actually. The mouse would get balky and I'd clean the laser port with a q-tip and it would work again. Eventually a few months ago this no longer worked. I got tired of messing with it and bought a replacement M-510 mouse identical to the one I had. THE PROBLEM IS, IT IS NOT IDENTICAL.

Mentioned nowhere was the fact that the new M-510 will not work with the setpoint software. As soon as plugged it it a prompt for new software popped up. I tried to ignore it but the software on my machine would not recognize the new mouse. The unifying software I had would NOT recognize the mouse. The mouse worked but i could NOT set up the buttons. It FORCED me to download the new software which included separate software for the new M-510. I had simply bought the exact same mouse expecting it to have to work the exact same way. It did not. So I downloaded the new software and tried to set the buttons up like I like. Simply this... thumb buttons page forward and back.. tilt wheel scroll left and right.. and the big one.. middle clicking the wheel enables Zooming in and out.

The Zoom feature does NOT work. You can now set the M-510 mouse to zoom in with the wheel OR zoom out. How fricking insane is that? You can not longer hold the wheel down in a center click and zoom in and out!!! There is a check box for zoom in, OR a check box for zoom out.

I've spent over an hour in 3 different calls to tech support and at least a dozen emails. The ADMIT the Zoom in and out feature is gone.

Things I have tried. Delete the software and reinstall. Delete mouse and unify it again. Search of 3 different old versions of the software. Tried all the above on 2 different computers!!!!

It's not the software. It IS the hardware.

The responses I get from tech support are variations on "sorry 'bout your luck sucker". They didn't offer to replace it because they knew the replacement would work the same way.

I don't think it was an unreasonable expectation to replace and old product with a new one still carrying the exact same model number and expect it to work the same way. I'm now using an M-710 from my other computer but it is NOT as good a mouse. It has the absolutely necessary zoom feature but it's too light, doesn't fit my hand as well and is not as stable as my old M-510

I have used Logitech product as far back and Windows 3.1. Never used anything else. I've even praised their products. Now I feel like taking both keyboards and both mice, all spares and anything I can find in the house with the Logitech name on it, including the web cam I bought with a lousy microphone and no way to pair it with a good one, busting them up with a hammer, boxing them and sending the back. In some parts of the world people spit when they have to say the name of someone they hate. That's how I feel about Logitech now. I will post this review everywhere I can.

They dominate the market and have developed a Microsoft style arrogance.

If someone can prove me wrong about this please contact me. I haven't taken a hammer to it yet.

title: Great headset for games, music, and looking cool
text:
This is a review of the Logitech G933 Wireless headset.
Pros
-Comfortable for 5-7 hours
-Battery lasts ~10 hours
- You can customize the side panels by buying other ones ( whenever a company decides to make some i have yet to find any)
-Re-aquires signal like a radio.
-Customizable LED
-Lots of features
-Good Bass for your music listening
-Invisible microphone when you don't need it
-Volume wheel gives you a nice little feedback tone when you turn it up or down
Cons
-Static hiss on power up
^I really only have one thing I don't like about these, if you put them on and then flip on the switch you get an uncomfortable, Kind of loud, static hiss. It's just like a split second but I don't appreciate it. That's all I dislike!

First Impressions
I've had this headset for almost a month and I love it. It comes with a 3.5mm cable with volume controls, a USB charging cable, a RCA to 3.5mm cable, and a 3.5mm to 2.5mm adapter. I was happy to see all these things ship with the headset, you basically don't need to worry about having to get anything else, it's great!
The microphone is invisible! When I first got the headset in my hands it took me a few seconds to find where the microphone was, there is a insert in the headset and the mic folds into it, you can barely notice it, which is handy especially if you aren't going to be using it. The headset also has two panels, the one's with the "G" that are removable. They have two magnetic points that are attracted to two of the screws in the headset on each side. Under the left panel the Wireless USB dongle is inserted there, great for if you're going somewhere you can just put it inside the headset and you won't lose it. Behind the right panel you have the battery, which looks like you have to unscrew two screws to be able to get it out. Shouldn't need to though. The Wireless USB dongle also has a little 3.5mm jack on its end so you could plug the cable it comes with into that.

Comfort
This headset is really comfortable. I was able to wear it for about 5 hours the first time until i got off my computer. They were tight at first, they really clamped onto your head, they still do but not so hard. They don't fall off my head, I remember watching a video by Linus tech tips and they were saying it would fall off, oddly enough at first when I did it they did, but I adjusted them differently and now they don't fall off.
The headset has a nice soft breathable material. It's not the imitation leather like the G930s. I game for longer periods at a time and only have had comfort problems about two or three times. Those I believe were very extended periods of time, my regular is about 5-7 hours, so it was more than 7 hours. Though you shouldn't be using them for longer anyways right? I'd say they do their job!
Features
These has more features than a casual gamer like myself will bother to mess with. Using the new software that if suppose to be for all your logitech devices (I may be wrong) you can adjust the LED color, it's RGB so you can really customize it. It also has the option to set light pattern. You can make it "breathe" which is where its fades in and out on a solid color, You can also make it cycle through all the colors with the breathing effect. Also of course you can set it to just a solid color of your choice.
There are different presets based on what kind of game you're playing. I haven't played any of the games that with their presets yet so can't tell you much about that. You have different mixer presets as well such as Bass, or Flat, FPS, things like that. I mostly just use flat. You can also manually change things using the mixer with the software. You have your 7.1 surround sound as well as a different option which is surround, but based on some other settings, which I haven't messed with yet. One day I will.
Sorry I couldn't go in depth in this, I'm sure someone else has/will.
The customizable G keys can be used for many computer functions and are configured with the software. They have commands by default such as surround sound, LED function changer(solid, breathing, color cycling), and the preset mixer options. One thing to note is that the software isn't required to be able to do the preset changer and LED function changer. So you can do this on any computer or on your phone even. The only thing is that you can't see what preset on the mixer you're using. The headset doesn't need to be on to play sound through auxiliary, but you do have to switch it on if you want the LED lights to turn on and the mixer changer.
Durability
I have yet to drop these and don't plan on it happening. They seem flexible. I would say that they could handle the occasional drops. My only concern is the side plates breaking if they fall on a hard surface like tile or wood. Though they would have to fall just right for that to happen , perfect storm type of thing.
Connection
I love the connection on these, I don't see much of an improvement from the G930s in terms of range, I'd say they are pretty much equal. Though, I do like how they handle the signal. They aren't as prone to disconnecting or distorted signal due to microwaves. My G930s would lose signal if I was near the microwave, even if I was closer to the computer than the microwave was and 10 feet away from the microwave. Also when they do lose a signal, its almost like a radio. The headset won't turn off, it just goes quiet for a second or two and then the signal comes back (aslong as your not going even further from the computer, or standing next to the microwave. This is a big improvement if you're like me coming from the G930s as you know they'd turn off for like 5 seconds then turn on and try to get the signal back.
Battery
The battery has been able to last me a couple of my avg 5-7 hour sessions with LED lights on. Love it, other than that nothing to say.

title: Decent, with a few big misses
text:
Overall, the Logitech G933 is a pretty decent headset. I compared this headset to the SteelSeries Siberia 800, because for my needs I required wireless connectivity, good audio fidelity, strong transmission strength, and (most importantly) mute features including onboard mute button and mute LED indicator.

Pros:
* Good transmission strength. Better than Siberia 800, even though both advertise 40-ft range. Transmitted through the walls in my apartment with little difficulty.
* Far cheaper than the Siberia 800, almost by 50%.
* Great sound quality. I don't claim to be an audiophile, but if you're not the type of person who buys $100 gold cables then these will probably sound great to you too.
* Earpieces swivel quite nicely, although the headset is not quite flat when the earpieces are rotated a full 90 degrees, so I'm not sure if they'd travel too well.
* USB connector is a simple dongle, although it's somewhat large & wide and won't fit in tight spaces such as a USB bay on the back of a desktop.
* Power button is a simple slider switch, which makes it a lot quicker to use than a button that must be held for several seconds.
* I very much like the USB connector compartment inside the right earpiece. Big plus for travel purposes. Great idea.

Cons:
* The mute button is located on the left ear, on the same side as the mic. It also makes a terrifyingly loud click sound that the mic quite faithfully transmits to your listeners.
* Likewise, swiveling the mic up/down in order to mute transmits a loud scraping sound to your listeners.
* The mute button is also located right next to the volume wheel, which is easily bumped when reaching for it.
* Even after installing the software from Logitech's support site and ensuring the drivers were updated, I came through sounding quite garbled and scratchy to listeners on Discord. I don't have Skype anymore so I'm not sure if it's a driver problem or a hardware defect with the headset, but neither of those is a great option.

Overall, if the drivers can be fixed so that I don't sound awful for my audience, then this would still be a good headset for gaming; however, due to the problems with muting I wouldn't recommend anything but recreational use, so if you're looking for a device to double for both work and fun, look elsewhere.

title: Exactly What I've Been Looking For
text:
I've spent more money on keyboards that I'd like to admit. One thing that the new Logitech K780 and MX Master mouse do very uniquely is replace simple KVM switches. It also has a very good light key action. The keys have very little play in them and are soft yet firm in their action. Actuation pressure is fairly light but doesn't feel cheap at all.

I like the key layout. I actually do use insert, delete, page up, page down and the arrow keys quite a bit. I do prefer a TKL layout but this is also not bad. I can easily adapt to the alternate layout and can use the numpad as directional pads with all the aforementioned keys laid out on the numbers. I think it's important not to have too much space between the right edge of the enter key and the mouse. This allows proper centering of the keyboard without having to use the mouse way out to the right of your workspace.

The keyboard is also heavy. This allows it to be used as a base for heavier tablets. I use it with my iPad Pro 9.7" in tablet or portrait mode easily. They definitely spent some time on this because it actually angles devices down quite a bit. This is the proper ergonomic angle since this allows you to look down on the iPad without crouching.

I've used a couple mechanical keyboards and I plan on keeping them for a variety of uses, but this will probably be my main desktop keyboard. It is just so versatile and has the perfect layout for me.

Some key points of the keyboard I like:
- 3 device switcher (can use any combination of Logitech Unifying receiver and Bluetooth). Works great to switch between my Mac and Windows PC.
- Full sized key spacing. (Although this looks like the K380, the keys are more widely spaced and are definitely of a higher quality)
- Number pad
- Customization of keys.
- Reduced width for better ergonomics for right-handed mouse users.
- 24 month battery life. I basically only will have to replace the batteries once, maybe twice before I get a new keyboard.

title: Sometimes, sort of, maybe (not Universal) Remote for those with very basic AV systems, and small hands
text:
There is a distinction between the remote itself, and the "universal" nature of the Logitech software that controls it. First, the remote has positives and negatives.

REMOTE PRO: Good overall design, sleek and looks "modern" and not like a 90's throw back with garish ugly buttons. Fits well into a contemporary or modern home. The feel is nice with it being not too heavy nor too light. The curved design fits into most hands.
REMOTE CON: 1) This device is NOT made for large hands. The buttons are WAY too small, especially the number buttons at the bottom. The "off" switch is barely identifiable and made for those using a fingernail. 2) The remote is NOT backlit! What a design flaw, especially for the price. Since the buttons are tiny, and there is no way to distinguish one from another, the lack of a light is unacceptable. 3) the remote is NOT rechargeable, so be sure to buy batteries for it. There is no indicator on the remote for when the batteries are low so, good luck. 4) the remote should not be heavy, but this one is feels lighter than most, so it doesn't have the heft of other (say, Bose) universal remotes. 5) It has only three visible macros to "watch movie," "watch TV", etc. It can have up to six commands if you press and hold one of the three buttons, but that is not intuitive and visitors will never know unless you go out of your way to tell them. I purchased a universal remote for international guests who rent my place and shouldn't have to spend time tinkering with devices. It's a design flaw!

SOFTWARE PRO: 1) You can set up your system/device functions online (after you set up an account. see YouTube on issues associated with that!). 2) You can add most, but not all, devices in your system using the Logitech search (just know the manufacturer and model number of every device). 3) You can change your device settings using the app, on the fly (so you don't have to plug in the device IF you are using wi-fi to do your setup).
SOFTWARE CONS: Many many, but I will list the most frustrating here! 1) If you do NOT have a AV Receiver and do not plug most of your HDMI devices into your TV (which Logitech assumes you do), you will most likely NOT be able to have full "universal" functions. I use an HDMI switch (not an AV Receiver) and my TV only has two HDMI inputs, not the FOUR I need. So getting the Remote to recognize my J-Tech HDMI switcher or my CD (not HDMI) was impossible. So the "universal" is nothing of the sort. 2) As mentioned, my Sony CD player was completely NOT recognized by the Remote, so when I want to listen to a CD, I have to do it manually. 3) The Remote gives the option of "testing" the functions before they are saved. VERY limited troubleshooting if devices don't work correctly. 4) Assigning a command to the [tiny button] remote was futile. I wanted the remote to skip/reverse 10 seconds (or 5 minutes) like my Comcast remote. Futile, never happened. 5) The Remote allows you to move the sequence of device functions (on/off) within an Activity (e.g. Watch TV), but it only allows some of the devices to be resequenced, so my TV would switch to a dead output and create very loud static until other devices switched to the appropriate input. Switching from TV to DVD should not mean hearing LOUD TV static until the DVD gets a signal from the TV. Super annoying. Logitech should allow any sequence on any device to be set by the user. 6) You must keep "old" remotes nearby during set-up and troubleshooting. The tests required so many edits that I used my old Logitech universal remote just to get devices to function properly.

In Summary: PROS: Sleek physical design that fits into contemporary decor. CONS: Not backlit, tiny buttons, incomplete software, NOT UNIVERSAL control of Audio/Video devices. Consider whether your system may have too many devices for this Remote to control efficiently. If you needs extend beyond "TV/Cable DVD and Apple TV, Amazon or Sonos", plugged into the TV itself you may want to look elsewhere. I DO NOT recommend this if you have any switchers, spitters or adapters.

2. Secondly is that the IPad fits in real tight, so tight that once you put it in, it might break taking it our . . . But I found a solution, I simply pealed off the rubber pressure pad placed near the clips. I think it's there to ensure the Ipad fits tight. 3. Third problem is that once you close the keyboard case, the covers have a little slip and play . . . Which will eventually do damage. I wish there was a way to clip the top and bottom so there's no slip. I'm thinking of putting some velcro strips or possibly some elastic tape in the outside to ensure the whole thing stays put. This one is a big minus for the case.
4. Finally many others have talked about the keyboard eventually scratching the Ipad. I'd like to have a felt cloth to separate the two sections so as not to scratch my Ipad. I have a a glass screen on it, but even that can get scratched. I wish the keyboard was designed to take care of this problem, and came with a felt pad just as a precaution instead of me having to go figure out how to get a 12 inch felt pad.

All that said however, the keyboard is really responsive and has a very good typing feeling . . . It's a joy to use, and for me solves the problem of what to do when I'm on the road and need to write long reports. It's much, much better than the Apple foldable keypad . . . Even though it adds some weight to the IPad. And the keys are backlit. I've also typed all this in bed with the keypad balanced on my lap - it works super!

title: Confusing Functionality
text:
This is a good webcam but its touted functionality, of zoom, pan and tilt, can be confusing to a user, as it is not explained by the manufacturer. The zoom function is digital and the pan and tilt functionality depend on the webcam being zoomed in. The default configuration for the webcam, when it is plugged in, when applications that access it get started or even when a connection is made within an application, is of the webcam being completely zoomed out, at its widest angle setting. In that configuration the pan and tilt do not work. In fact, even to activate the zoom, the user may need to run Logitech Camera Settings software and apply the settings there, in parallel to any other primary software using the camera.

Beyond that, the good aspects of the camera include its good operation under varying lighting conditions, good autofocus and the tripod base that allows to use it with camera mini and full-size tripods.

The Logitech support website is poor. In fact it may be impossible to access it in Firefox or PaleMoon as it goes into an endless reload. This often happens also under Explorer. After access is made it is unclear which software needs to be installed and why.

title: Great 5.1 setup for the money!
text:
Update 2023: My set has finally died after about 8 years of daily heavy use. It died during a power surge in my house, so I can't really blame it for dying on me given that it has survived countless brown/black outs in the past. I happily ordered another one. For better or for worse, the entire PCB is in the subwoofer, so all I had to replace was the sub and did not have to touch the satellite speakers or even the console unit and it works as before. Unfortunately Logitech does not sell replacement subwoofers, so I did have to buy an entire new unit, but again, no regrets here. The unit is still the most affordable option I've found if you are looking for a big surround sound for movies with deep, rumbling bass. I pair it with soundblaster Z to my PC via optical cable and get dolby digital sound out of my PC. The satellites perform decently well, lacking some treble extension, but I have audiophile grade headphones when I want to do some critical music listening. This thing is just pure joy entertainment upgrade for your movies, anime, whatever.

Update 2022: It has been nearly 7 years since I set this up for my PC and I have been literally using it on a daily basis without any issues thus far. I'm not sure why there's so much bad review for this product, but I just wanted to throw out that mine has survived for years and the sub on this thing continues to impress me. Dolby support works great with soundblaster z as well

Great theater sound for movies and games, which is the primary reason I purchased this product. The bass hits hard and deep and does not disappoint. I am not sure if they revised this product, but I have this system on 24/7 without any additional cooling agent and have even stuffed the subwoofer inside of an enclosed cabinet and it does not get anywhere near hot, or even what I would call warm really, so I either got lucky or the issue with overheating sub is no longer a thing.

title: I would not  buy it again if I had the choice.
text:
Purchased it last week. Replaced a different Logitech keyboard -using same wifi hub.

+ The keyboard is nice -typing experience is very good. Also, I really like the spacing between the keys -very forgiving.
+ The keyboard charges using the solar cells perfectly. It holds a charge from either room or sunlight very well -virtually always at 100%.

Now my dislikes.
- it is very thin & a bit heavier than some other keyboards. The combined weight, hard edges and thinness, make it not sit well on one's lap if you are typing at a desk and want to put the keyboard on your lap, lean back and type for a while. I can use it that way, but it is the least comfortable keyboard I have used that way. Not easy to grip. (It is sort of like holding a giant, long and thin ipad on one's lap. . .just doesn't sit well.)

- most importantly: the keyboard has lag. I have "re-paired" the keyboard twice to the receiver (since I saw that as a recommended fix on the Logitech site); but the keyboard simply stops working every now and then -maybe as often as once a day or certainly once every two days.
Sometimes typing and nothing will show then a flurry of letters as the buffer catches up. Very poor and sometimes misses a letter or two when that happens. I don't think that it is caused by the ambient light -since this has occurred in low light and bright light.
This is paired with an I7 Surface Pro with lots of memory and generally zippy performance. Previously never had any keyboard lag with other keyboards (MS and the prior Logitech).
(BTW I tested my logitech trackpad and it does not have any lag --even when the keyboard is lagging.

- Oh, right now the function keys don't work so, <function key> sound up or down for example (or any function) simply does not work. I don't think they ever worked -even brand new out of the box. . .For my previous keyboards I did not have to do anything special about this to get them working, but I am still looking for a fix on this.

So, I would not recommend buying it. However, you may have a better experience than I if you take the risk.

title: Great mouse with one major flaw for the OCD people like me.
text:
Ugh, I want to give this 5 stars badly but first the good. This mouse is awesome. Ive tried a lot but this one I like the most. The 3 side buttons and top buttons have really worked out for my style of game play. The back most thumb button on the side is the only one Id like to see modified a bit. Its very far back and sometimes hard to reach. If they made the buttons shorter in length on the side I think it would be a big improvement. But not why I gave the 4 stars. Accuracy is great. I love the weight as well, but I use ALL the weights as I just like it like that. Its also VERY comfortable to hold. The configuration software is good but one thing I don't like is its a little confusing on how to store your settings. The mouse can handle 3 separate profiles that can be switched between with a button on the mouse itself. So for the most part 3 games in one program. HOWEVER, I can't seem to figure out how to simply save a configuration to call up later. Not intuitive and I just stopped messing with it. I am only usually playing 3 games at any time but I had an ANKER mouse that made it VERY easy to just save a profile and call it back later. But Im sure there is a way I just haven't taken the time to figure it out so Im not removing a star (yet). Currently I just replace one of the 3 profiles key by key when I need to.

The reason for the lost star is the ANNOYING rattle sound Im getting when I release my finger from the main mouse buttons! I don't notice it at all when playing a game because Im usually using headphones but I am also a graphic designer and I use the mouse with my work and the button will stick to my finger ever so slightly that as soon as I lift away, it RATTLES into place. I mean seriously, it sounds like a spring loose! This is not a cheap mouse. All they need to do is put a little rubber piece in there somewhere to dampen the vibration. The only way I can describe the sound is if you every have flicked one of those spring-like door stops in you home,(barraanngannngge) it makes that kind of sound! Its extremely annoying and almost makes me want to leave 3 stars because I can't possibly understand why such a good mouse would make this kind of racket by simply using it. Anyway, because I can't tell if its just me or this particular sample I have, I felt like 1 star was enough to deduct. Even though, Im starting to hate the sound lol!

title: saw it had pretty good reviews
text:
When my previous HP speakers crapped out, I was forced to go looking for another set. I was used to high quality sound, so I knew I needed something comparable. I work from home as a Software Engineer, so music is critical for my daily function, otherwise I get highly irritated. I came across this set, saw it had pretty good reviews, and decided to give it a try. I'm glad I did.

Pros:

- It's sleek. The speakers/woofer don't leave a huge foot print and they look fairly trendy. ie. They don't look like crap sitting on your desk
- They are built solid. I have an 18 month old who is constantly grabbing and yanking at everything on my desk. A couple of times, he has grabbed a speaker and slammed it into the side of the desk. The speaker takes the beating like a champ. No dents, scratches, or loss of sound.
- They really do sound great. As soon as these speakers arrived, I turned up the woofer as high as it would go and cranked the volume as loud as it would go, and fired up some rock music. No distortion or crackling in the speakers what-so-ever. The bass sounds great and the mids sound great as well. The speakers do not squeal or rattle. My wife, who was on the complete other side of the house, even said they sounded good from her distance.
- You adjust the bass on the speaker, not on the woofer. This is a big deal to me since I slide the woofer well under my desk. Having to climb under there and turn the woofer around to make adjustments would be unbearably annoying. Not to mention, I don't have to worry about my toddler crawling under there and messing with any knobs.
- Both speaker cables are plenty long. My desk is about 6ft wide and I can sit a speaker on each end and still have some play in the cables.

Cons: (I honestly cannot think of any negative features with this speaker set. I've had them for over a year now and have ran them every day for at least 8 hours. If something should arise, I'll update my review.)

If you're looking for a set of really good speakers at a reasonable price, then I would highly HIGHLY recommend this set.

And I thought about how much and how long I've used the K400 for and a mere additional $60 investment felt like nothing.
This is a keyboard for the lazy anyways - one that I have connected to my multimedia computer connected to my big screen.

Yes, I occasionally drive my mouse on the mousepad with my thumb and use that top-left left-click key.
Yes, I watch movies in the dark so the illumination helps.
No, I do not want to have to worry if I have batteries if they drain out and have multiple micro-usb cables all over the place.

In that case, it's well worth it.

This is so stupid, as the two small buttons can be configured to do all kinds of other action, just you can not make the right little button do middle click. This problem would be completely avoidable if Logitech allowed this in their SetPoint settings application. Also, a simple option to swap functions from left to right would make it much easier to use the mouse with both hands as needed.

=========================================================================================================

So, Logitech support suggests to install uberOptions which is a third party application which manipulates Logitech software, to fix a stupid problem which can be fixed by Logitech by editing a few of your XML files. That is what the third party software claims to do.

title: Highly recommend for kids and adults alike!
text:
Last year our school district provided all students with ipad air devices to help them with their schoolwork. My kids of course were thrilled, but my youngest struggled during his writing assignments. So we experimented with a cheap keyboard and case I found locally with the thought that if it helped him we'd invest in a better keyboard at a future date. The addition of that greatly improved his writing experience and assignment completion rate, so we decided to get him a much nicer keyboard before the new school year began. I started trying to research what to buy on my own and frankly I found myself overwhelmed by so many choices. So I contacted one of the district tech guys and asked what he would recommend and this keyboard is the exact link he sent me. Anyway, now that my son has used it at home and at school for a short time now I feel its time to leave my own review for those looking for similar products.

Here's what you should know right away.
1. It doesn't come with a case. I initially wanted both,but after a lot of research found very few of them that met what my expectations would be and none of them were in our price range.
2. This keyboard attaches to the ipad itself. You plug the cord into the charging port to power it up. It is not a bluetooth one. Our first one was, but I have found we don't miss it at all.
3. This is super easy to use. My little guy is just shy of 10 and is super speedy with it and enjoys it a lot.
4. It comes with a small list of shortcuts so you'll want to read it if that interests you. Otherwise there are basic instructions for setup, but even that us super simple. Plug it in and off you go.
5. There is a lot of space to personalize it for yourself or your child. I wrote my son's name pretty much all over it because it is the same keyboard the tech people have admin using at the schools.
6. Keep the box the keyboard comes in as a travel case. My son takes it to and from school in the box so it doesn't get damaged. You'll probably want to do the same thing if you have a child using it.

So I had to give it 5 stars and would definitely purchase it again if my other children need one. Its easy to set up, use, and is very sturdy so its perfect for on the go use and in the classroom.

title: Bad Triggers Ruin An Otherwise Solid Controller
text:
I've had this controller for around a year I believe. I haven't played too many PC games that I want to use a controller with as I typically go with the keyboard and mouse. The few that I can think of offhand are Batman Arkham Asylum, Batman Arkham City, Tomb Raider (2013), and most recently Middle Earth: Shadow of Mordor. I didn't have any issues with the Batman games or Tomb Raider that I can recall. However, with Shadow of Mordor (SoM), I've had nothing but trouble using this controller.

I now hate this controller and will be replacing it with an authentic Xbox 360 controller. The controller has only been used lightly since I play most of my games with the keyboard and mouse, so it isn't worn out. I haven't noticed any dead zones with the analog sticks like a lot of reviewers mention, but I haven't played any driving games or anything where I think that would be easily noticed. The issue that I have is with the triggers. In SoM, you need to HOLD the left trigger to enter ranged mode to fire your bow and perform some other maneuvers. If you TAP the trigger, it throws a dagger. You also need to HOLD the right trigger while in ranged mode to charge an arrow in order to fire it at full strength. If you TAP the right trigger, it will shoot a weak arrow that is only useful for interacting with the environment and pinning an enemy to the ground. You also HOLD the right trigger to go into stealth and sneak around. What ends up happening constantly is that the triggers will depress and then release constantly if I don't hold them down with extreme force, which is very tiring and cramps my fingers. I try to hold the left trigger for ranged mode and it keeps releasing and throwing daggers, which alerts the entire camp to my presence. I try to charge an arrow and it fires 4 or 5 weak arrows in rapid succession which doesn't kill the target, wastes my limited ammo, and alerts everyone. I attempt to sneak through a camp and the trigger randomly releases and my character stands up out of stealth and is detected. This makes the game extremely frustrating and basically unplayable with this controller. I tried my roommate's Xbox 360 controller and did not have any of these issues.

I do not have any other issues with the controller. It seems to be sturdy and well-built minus the triggers. It has been compatible with every game that I've attempted to play with it, and is always recognized as an Xbox 360 controller in the game and in Windows. I've used it with Windows 7 and Windows 10. I have not used the direct input mode, but the Xinput mode has always worked and gets it recognized as an Xbox 360 controller requiring no configuration. I haven't installed the Logitech software, so I can't comment on that. I knew it didn't have a rumble feature, so I can't complain about that either. Overall, I wish I had spent $5-$10 more and bought an actual Microsoft Xbox 360 wired controller.

title: No More Logitech Products For Me.
text:
After all these years I should have known better than to buy another Logitech product... Here's what you need to know about the MX Master: The shape of the mouse is pretty good and I haven't had much of any trouble with repetitive motion or ergonomics. Also the number of controls and ability to customize them is more than I have seen on any other mouse. That's it for the good, now here's the bad... First the cost of this mouse is very high and the poor performance makes it a bad deal. From day one I have had to click the mouse multiple times to wake it and often just to execute a click. Also some of the customization features just don't work. I have a Mac and with the most recent OS Sierra, several of the mouse functions stopped working. On Logitech's knowledge community site I see that many people have complained and that Logitech is aware but after 2 more OS updates Logitech still has not released an update fix for the problem, so typical of them. The mouse is unusable for me in this condition. My experience with other Logitech products (like Harmony Remotes) is don't hold your breath waiting for them to release a fix or offer a refund. My advice to you is to look for a top quality remote from another manufacturer.

12-7-2016 UPDATE: I am happy to say that Logitech has finally offered a software update to fix the Mac OS Sierra problem. Unfortunately no notification of this fix was sent registered users, nor was the update pushed in any way. I had to just keep on continually checking with Logitech to find out. Also the issue with difficulty waking the mouse from sleep mode has gotten worse and now whenever I restart my Mac I have to plug a corded mouse in and re-pair the bluetooth connection to the MX Master to get it to reconnect. Unfortunately my review stands at 2 stars.

title: Unbelievable piece of crap... Logitech Wireless devices are decent until a few short months later, they are garbage.
text:
Sorely disappointed with this Logitech Wireless Trackball.

I have been a fan of Logitech devices for almost 20 years and have, for the most part, been very happy with everything that I have used of theirs. I've always had mixed feelings about wireless keyboards/mice, whether Logitech or other manufacturers, due to eventually needing battery replacements and just gradual loss of reliability leading to much frustration.

This trackball is no exception! I purchased it four months ago and it worked pretty well for the first couple of months. The last month or two I've seen very herky jerky response when using it, so I tried replacing the battery and it made a little difference for a few hours, then started acting up again. I regularly cleaned the contact points where the ball touches and that would also help for a while. Sometimes just bumping it against the desk would also 'jar' it enough to work.

That all rose to a head today when it just wouldn't work to an acceptable level no matter what I tried. I couldn't place the pointer with any precision without it lagging/stopping during movement. So I removed the battery and promptly slammed it into the garbage pail, resulting in several pieces.

I had a similar experience with a Logitech wireless travel mouse that worked fantastically for almost a year, then it started double-clicking on everything I wanted to single click on. This is a well-documented problem with that device and I should have learned my lesson, but alas I ended up wasting more money on another wireless Logitech device like this one.

Sadly, I will probably never purchase another keyboard/mouse made by Logitech (wired or wireless again) which really is a shame, but I won't lose sleep over it.

title: Another winning gaming mouse from Logitech
text:
This mouse is just plain excellent. Coming from a G303 Daedalus Apex which is my current favorite mouse (see my review on it's page if you're interested), this is a larger, fuller sized mouse, but is still a little smaller than some full size mice, such as the huge G602 which was definitely too big for my hands. As a full size mouse, it is primarily designed mostly for a palm grip, but I find it works pretty well with a modified claw grip as well. The G502 is a bit on the heavy side for me, even without the optional weights, but then some people like their mice heavy.

The sensor is top of the line (the G303 has the same sensor, incidentally), and the software (download from Logitech's website) works well and is pretty easy to use, although some things could be explained better (game profile setup can be a little confusing, for example). But it is nice to have one single application to control all my Logitech accessories (I have a G710+ keyboard as well). I do like the up and down dpi adjustment buttons as opposed to a single or no button, and the dpi shift button on the thumb grip is nice as well.

If I can come up with any negatives, I'd say the scroll wheel is a bit clunky- it's metal and very ratchety- it clicks heavily and roughly, although you can press a button to release the ratchet and let it free spin, though it feels less responsive that way. After some time with the G502, I don't think it will replace my G303 as my #1 gaming mouse (again this is a personal preference), as I like smaller, lighter mice, but the G502 is still of superb quality and I'm sure I'll find a use for it even so.

title: Can't beat it for the price
text: For the price you can't go wrong with these. 40W RMS is great in this price range. Peak is 80W but RMS is key. The speakers get get loud without distorting and the same goes with the sub. Totally fills the room. To get the most out of these speakers you're going to want a dedicated sound card (Sound Blaster, Xonar, etc) with software EQ options or at the very least have EQ available with your PC's on-board Realtek to fine-tune things. You really need to tweak a little to help bridge the audio gap between the satellites and the sub. Once you achieve that, these speakers will sound great through all volumes. They're really nice. I'd totally give it five stars but there are a few factors that could be improved that wouldn't necessarily affect the quality/cost. The shortcomings (literally in one aspect) are that the power LED is old-school, outdated, lime green (no blue/white?). The satellite RCA cables are also fairly short for a 2.1 system which can really limit speaker/sub placement without the use of RCA, 3.5mm, or power extension cables. The other downside is that the sub is forward facing vs side-facing. This would be a much better layout if the plugs/controls were on the short side opposite the port rather than the large side opposite the woofer. Still, for the price, this is a great system.

title: Amazing Headset, Shoddy Software.
text:
Me and this headset have a love-hate relationship going on.

So I really, really like the headset. It's comfy, the sound is great, the mic is fantastic, it has great battery life, charges very quickly and has fantastic range. Now, with a review like that you're probably wondering why i'm giving it 3 stars.

Well, its because the software is prettttttty s***. I upgraded from Windows 10 awhile back and have been having nothing but issues with the headset. When it works, its amazing. But after awhile it will either shut itself off (which i've tried to fix) or start power cycling to which there is no way to fix. I've found that the only thing that remedies the constant shutting off and turning on is to turn off the Logitech control center. The headset will work without the software running but it won't have 5.1. It is really annoying to be in the middle of a movie or a game and have the headset start to endlessly power cycle.

Beyond that, its a great headset. Just wish Logitech would fix whatever problem is causing the power issues.

title: Great Sound, Poor Build Quality
text:

Before I bought the Z506 I had a very old Logitech Z-640. title: You're better off saving your money and getting a pair of ...
text: Short version? If you're looking for comfort, sound quality and mic quality but don't care about the wireless feature? You're better off saving your money and getting a pair of Cloud 2s. If you're looking at more expensive wireless options like the SteelSeries Siberia 800 the Astro A50 or the Razer ManO'War? These are a great value for the money and sound just as good as the three aforementioned pairs. With that said, this is a TERRIBLE headset for audiophiles or people who don't want to sound like they're underwater. The serious gamer knows that you need to be heard clearly the first time and this mic just doesn't deliver in that aspect. It's short, inflexible and of just awful quality. The sound is good, but not well balanced and the Logitech software can only do so much. It doesn't communicate enemy locations well in FPS and for other games that require stealth? You'll be too distracted by the grating sound of your own walking through grass, crackling fires, etc to be able to zero in on the enemy position. The buttons are not intuitively placed and in my opinion - poorly thought out. You can only, for instance, cycle through the preset lighting schemes and cannot customize them to turn off the RGB lighting at the press of a button to save on battery life. The power button is the most inconveniently placed of all - way at the top. The earcup covers are held in place by magnets, which means you can reasonably expect to lose them if you're not babying them every step of the way. The earcups are UNCOMFORTABLE. Great size, love the square shape - but the material used is itchy and hot as all heck. Finally, and perhaps worst of all, they are made of a cheap and glossy plastic that attracts fingerprints, scratches and disappointment everywhere they are seen.

Hardware - Unlike some previous reviews, I found, if you are used to a laptop touch pad, you will have no problems feeling at home here. Using this touch pad without a physical button is very possible and exactly like most laptops. That being said, I found out the reason the hardware keys are not very responsive. title: Wireless dropping and mic arm issues.
text:
Let me start by saying this is 3 stars and not a 1 star because the audio and voice quality are top notch. The manufacturing quality and wireless technology are the issue here though.

I had issues with my headset after about a month. I ended up using the manufacturer warranty after 3 months and swapping it out for the corded G35 version. For some reason the headset dropped signal for a few seconds would beep a few times then reconnect. This created a problem while gaming since hearing and communication with the mic are key. I tried a million fixes, many others reported the same issue. This would sometimes not happen at all one day and happen a billion times the next day. The cause I never figured out. Some even theorize that wireless routers and cell phones may interfere. But this wasn't enough to use the warranty.

Thankfully whatever holds the mic arm in place went out at that 3 month mark. The mic would not stay in the up position, it was loose. Fixing it yourself would void the warranty. So at this point Logitech was very helpful and I sent in my G930 on their dime and they are sending me a G35 at my request. It's $15 cheaper so I am losing $15 on the deal but I can not deal with the wireless problems. It was nice being able to get up and go to the fridge or something without taking my headset off but I wasn't walking away from my PC with the headset on enough to justify the wireless requirement anyway. Now lets hope the mic arm holds up on the new one and the plastic cracking problem doesn't haunt me. Once the 1 year warranty is up on this one I will most likely switch to a different headset from a different company.

title: Great Video, ZERO audio
text: I only have one complaint with this webcam in that the downloadable software is primitive and the microphone stuck on zero volume. I can record excellent quality 1080p video but no audio whatsoever with the Logitech software. The microphone level slider does not move at all when you attempt to adjust it despite Windows settings being maxed out. With third party software such as ManyCam I was able to record using the built in stereo microphones and they are really nice quality, far better than the previous Logitech unit I have and far better than the Windows one I also tested. Auto balance, face tracking, auto focus work very fast and retain image quality and quickly refocuses on objects, such as moving something in front of the camera for a close-up. I feel for the price that Logitech should include a webcam suite for recording and effects or at least a discount for one since they supply such a poor one themselves. I have to steal two stars from the review for that reason. Software is nearly as important as the hardware and I have to invest in a software package to record 1080 resolutions, that adds another $30-$80 dollar cost to this unit. I have not found a free recorder that supports the resolutions and VideoLan is choppy and messed up for some reason. I needed to record reviews now not later so I had to go with a lower resolution than I wanted.

title: Gamer Review: G213 is way better than G710+
text: I use this for gaming. Everything about this keyboard is better than my G710+ that I bought during the Black Friday 2015 sale. The G710+ has a bunch of features that I find annoying because I don't need them and don't use them, like "on-the-fly macro recording," extremely loud keys (mechanical keys), 3 macro modes, 26 key rollover (WHO NEEDS THAT?!?), 50,000,000 key lifespan (really..? no one will ever hit any key 50 million times). The main annoyances I had with the G710+ were the extremely loud keys because it's a mechanical keyboard and all of the extra keys/buttons I don't need and never use. This keyboard (the G213) has all of the basic keys with gaming performance behind them. That's all I ever needed... a normal keyboard with gaming performance. The G213 has membrane keys, which are much quieter than mechanical ones (like the ones in the G710+) and beautiful RGB back-lighting. Right when I plugged it in (G213) the keyboard lit up a solid color and then slowly cycled through all of the other colors of the rainbow. I know it has other color scheme options but I haven't tried them because I'm enjoying the default one too much to care about the other options lol. The palm rest is so much better on the G213 than the one on the G710+. The 710+ palm rest is hard plastic and removable (it snaps in place), but the G213 palm-rest is built in, a better feeling plastic, and cannot be removed. Also, the little kick-stands under the keyboard are way better on the G213 as well. I seriously like the G213 way better than my G710+ in every single aspect. If you're a gamer and you hit more than 5 keys at the same time, you may want the G710+, but there's VERY few gamers out there that hit more than 5 keys at the exact same time, so I really can't recommend the G710+ to anyone unless you're one of those rare dudes. Keyswitch lifespan on this is supposed to be 20,000,000 and it's pretty safe to assume you'll never hit any key 20 million times. 20 million is a ridiculous number; it's just a marketing pitch. Unless they hooked up a machine to rapidly tap the same button 20,000,000 times, the key lifespan has never been tested for it's real limit and considering my keyboards from the 1990s still work just fine, I'd imagine this 2016 keyboard will last just as long or longer. But hey, maybe not since my 1990s keyboard was built in the United States and now days everything is outsourced to China and 3rd world countries. Either way, I'm done ranting about Logitech's marketing scheme. This keyboard is great (so far).

title: Feel the Power
text:
No batteries? Check. Numpad? Check. Comfortable layout with crisp, clicky keys? Of course. This keyboard take's Logitech's excellent line of wireless (non-bluetooth) keyboards to the next level by truly cutting the cord. Solar power means you never need to think about charging. To give you an idea of how little juice this keyboard needs, this winter mine has been living in a dark room with one small north-facing window. It gets about six hours of indirect sunlight a day, and I usually have my keyboard tray tucked under the desk and I never turn it off. It's been holding steady at a 57% charge, which is enough to last a month anyways. In slightly better lighting conditions, it never dropped below 100%. In two years of ownership I've never been without power, and I don't expect I will.
A few other notes: the wireless is excellent and connects near-instantly. It's not Bluetooth, and suffers none of the connectivity issues I seem to run up against again and again with that technology. The keys have a great feel, with crisp clickiness, just a little bit of a noise for feedback, and a slight depression in each one to make sure you never miss a stroke. Some people may not like the space between the keys, but I am entirely used to it, and that seems to be the standard in keyboards these days, led by Apple's design cues.

title: Best USB Mic I've found
text:
I've bought 3 USB microphones to use for podcasting; Samson Meteor, Blue Snowball, and Blue Yeti. Far and away, the Yeti is the best.

I'm not an audiophile or very electronics-savvy. So, all of my comments are based on "out-of-the-box performance".

Sound quality is amazing. There is little to no of that annoying electronic recording sound. Sound is clear and crisp. The Snowball is good in the sound area, but the Yeti is 30%-40% clearer in my opinion.

The features on this mic really set it apart. I love the mute button. I use it a lot when I sniff or cough. It saves a ton of time on the post production end.
The different recording patterns are great. With a turn of a disl you can change the recording area on the mic. It can record 1 direction (just record the person directly behind it), 2 directions (record a conversation of two people on opposite sides of the table), or 360 degrees (record the whole room). This is extremely helpful for interviews when you don't have a whole mixer setup.

All in all, this is a great mic that I can't recommend enough. It is the best USB mic I've found. It is definitely worth the extra cost over the Snowball and Meteor.

title: I hope your M187 will work for 8 years like mine did.
text:
My M187 is about 8 years old. I found that the first symptom when it stops working is that the mouse suddenly stops responding. I can make it fail by mousing really fast for a few seconds. I can get the mouse going again by disconnecting the battery for a moment. It started happening yesterday.

Until I get a replacement, I will try to remember to mouse s..l..o..w..l..y so the mouse won't crash. (Little tiny mouse crashes.)

The USB receiver is connected directly into one of the laptop's USB jacks.

I tried a new battery; same problem.

I uninstalled the domestic-spying Logitech utility along time ago (it reports to Logitech every time the computer boots up), so I don't know what it might report about the mouse. All it reports is the battery condition, but I know that's not the problem, so I am not motivated to re-install the utility.

I just read a review where the mouse only lasted a few months, Logitech replaced it, and the replacement only lasted a few months, so the reviewer gave the M187 only one star. The reviewer did not confess to being a gorilla, so who knows if it's a case of real bad luck. I hope your mouse works for 8 years like mine did.

PS: Normal man's hands, not big enough to palm a basketball (unless I put a big wad of chewing gum in my hand first), and the size of the mouse was fine for me. Never had a problem with over-sensitive buttons and wheel, a trouble other reviewers have reported. But maybe they don't make them like they used to.

Or maybe the reviewer with the over-sensitive wheel had the wheel-settings turned up too high. When you switch from one mouse to another, you have to go into windows' mouse settings to get them comfortable, again.

title: ... the trackball when using my laptop - I don't like touch-pads; it's especially good when there is no ...
text: I prefer the trackball when using my laptop - I don't like touch-pads; it's especially good when there is no solid surface for a mouse (e.g., in bed).  It takes a little getting used to but it is very effective once you get the hang of it.  I advise caution when using for first-person shooter-type games or applications with tons of movement - your arm is stationary and may be prone to forearm tendinitis (esp. if you're over 40...).  The only issue I have discovered is that there is no ground strip internal to the button/switches - so, static electricity builds up (via triboelectric effect) resulting in 'misreads' of mouse clicks.  The effect is more prominent in low humidity environments and may take about a year of use before you see it.  I have successfully disassembled and manually discharged the hammer/switch assembly with a metal probe thereby extending the life of an otherwise good mouse.  Note that this problem is not unique to this mouse (I do wonder why Logitech hasn't fixed it yet on their designs).

title: SO LOUD, and working perfectly after 5+ years of use and abuse
text:
Holy moly, I LOVE this speaker. It's seriously one of my favorite things I own.

I've had this bad boy for at least 5 years. I've traveled with it, I've lent it to friends for presentations, I've dropped it, I've stepped on it, it mostly lives on the floor when I'm not using it, and it's still chugging away at 100%. It's built fantastically well, despite being an all-plastic build.

It gets SO LOUD. Like, amazingly, shockingly loud. I normally listen to it turned up to around 30%, because more than that is just too dang loud and I'm worried about disturbing my neighbors.

The sound quality is also super solid. Good bass, tremble, highs mids and lows. Of course, you can't expect audiophile-quality from this, but as someone who doesn't sweat that kind of stuff, these sound fantastic to me. It does well both with music and with movies/audiobooks - no muddy sound, no distortion, no pops, no cracks.

Really, the best thing I can say about this speaker is that when I pull it out and my friends see it and hear it, their reaction is always, "OMG where did you get that I want one!!!"

If you are thinking about getting yourself one, do it! (Actually, when I looked this item up to review it, I was SHOCKED at the price here - $149.99 as I'm looking at it now, but reading reviews, it seems the price fluctuates. I swear I bought this for like $40 back in the day!)

One thing - this works instantaneously when I plug it into my PC, as the OS detects it and switches output. However, when my boyfriend plugs it into his MacBook Air, he has to go into his settings and manually change the output. Not a huge deal, but a strange quirk, and definitely not the speaker's fault.

title: Software Hamstrings an Otherwise Promising Device
text: The programmability of the Harmony Hub is ridiculously limited.  Their Activity system is designed to take you from one kind of activity to another, but the activities are incredibly broad, and you can't customize them in the ways that you should be able to out of the box.  Activities are a vision of someone sitting down expecting to do a single thing with their remote for a while, and then switching to something else - as a result of apparently dummy-proofing activities, you are forced to turn off EVERYTHING from the first activity, and then turn everything on in the next activity.  It's an outmoded way of controlling such devices, and could be remedied by simply including an advanced control option that lets the user program how the remote should act at any given time.  Instead, Logitech assumes its customers are idiots, and something that looks like an incredibly promising device for home automation turns into a frustrating exercise in working around its built-in limitations, where possible.

title: Add this to your existing logitech hub!
text:
I owned the basic logitech hub. I wanted to add the ultimate remote but didn't want to buy the $350 version with hub.

While it is super hidden on their website you can absolutely add this to your existing hub, here is how.
1) update you hub to latest software
2) buy this remote
3) ignore the instructions it comes with, charge it, ignore the instructions on screen
4) open your harmony app on your ipad and choose 'harmony upgrade'
5) choose add remote
6) click ad now
7) follow the prompts to add remote (press mute and menu on remote)
8) one this is finished you will need to connect the remote to your PC to update firmware, but that's it.

now you have all the features of the most expensive remote for less money than buying new and not waste having multiple hubs - woo hoo. I hope this helps someone.

Note each hub can only have one touch remote + one smart keyboard + one non-touch remote, while the hubs get different names they actually all seem to be identical - i bought my first smart hub when they came out with the smart keyboard. This is working find with those.

alex
PS great remote, much better weighting and layout, you can customize what buttons appear on the LCD in activities and devices and re-order all from the remote.
