title: I LOVE THIS HEADSET so far..
text:
I would give this a 4.5 if I could.

So I've spent MANY days searching headsets, trying to figure out which one would be best and the best price. There are lots of applications I use headsets for (which I will list) and had questions about which ones it would and would not work with, but no one really had them listed.

First- the sound quality is GREAT. I am very pleased with the sound. Sometimes it cuts out, but through the various use of applications with other programs running and with only one program running, I've found that its either the application or my connection (depending on how many things I have running at once). There's no feedback and I've been told that I'm able to be heard clearly, no echo, no static.

Second- the feel is okay. I have an average size head (its not big.lol) and the headset...it doesn't feel tight, but it aggravates my ears, after being worn for a while. The cups (ear pieces) are a little weird. I haven't seen/felt any like these before. Usually its the foam pads or the material is close to the material of the entire headset. They don't feel bad, but just a little old. I have small ears and they cover my entire ear. I included a picture of my ear so you could gauge better.lol {This is the reason I didn't give 5 stars, but again, if I could have given 4.5- I would have}

So. So far, I've used Five9, Skype, Blackboard/Adobe meeting rooms with this headset. Everything (sound and compatibility wise) works just fine.

***I saw where people were complaining that the answer call button doesn't work; on the instruction sheet that comes with the set, there is an asterisk that says you may have to download drivers in order for it to work. There's also something about another company, Cisco maybe?, but I can't remember. It may say something like it doesn't work with them or you HAVE to download the drivers for it to work. I can't find the instructions right now, but when I do, I'll update it with what it says. After you've done that and it still doesn't work, you should contact Logitech.*** I've only needed to use my volume buttons, so those are the only two I can speak on. All applications I use have mute options, so I haven't needed to use the mute button.

In one of the pictures, I extended the side all the way out so you could see how far it would extend. In that same picture I bent the mouthpiece so you could see it's flexibility. The piece does flip around so you can use it on the left or right side, but you have to flip it over and not under. It tells you that in the instructions as well. *****See picture*****

I can't think of anything else. I hope I didn't leave anything out.

**Update July 22** So my new headset came and it, too, is flawed. The amount of feedback in the headset is ridiculous. I lowered my rating. I did 2 stars because when it worked- its great! It was a constant buzzing in my ear. I had to stop working because of the sound. I'm pretty peeved and did NOT order a replacement. title: Strong Performer on a Budget
text:
Good and powerful remote with few limitation when compared to the top of the line Harmonies.

This is our 4th Harmony remote, and the most basic model. But it doesn't lack performance. Our favorite model is the Harmony One, with its touchscreen and nice, large buttons. But this Harmony 700 is still very competent. We do miss the touchscreen and not having six buttons on the screen, but it does get the job done. And the soft, silicone-like buttons are an improvement over the old generation, top of the line Harmonies, like the 880 and 688 models.

The 700's buttons light up when the remote is woken up with movement, and the rechargeable batteries are charged with the common micro-USB socket; very handy. We had the remote for about two months, and we have yet to charge it, even though we use it daily.

The online programming site has become way more user friendly since when first Harmonies came out, but it still takes some learning. Once the user becomes accustomed to the system, making small tweaks to the remote becomes a simple task.

Overall, the 700 is a strong performer, and if you're on a budget and can grab one for under $80 like we did, since it's a discontinued model, there is no need to go for the $250 Harmony.

title: LOVE this keyboard, with 2 tiny-tiny"flies" in the ointment. (They're so small, these flies, I'm telling you. Buy the thing!)
text:
After my MPB gasped it's last, I was in the market for something new and portable. My sister had gone the iPad/keyboard route, and had glowing things to say, so I thought I would try it myself. Since my biggest concern was keyboard comfort, I took my sister's for a "test type". I was was so impressed, I went out and bought an iPad Air 2/ Logitech keyboard at Big Box the next day. (Sorry Amazon, I couldn't wait, although I should have, as I proably would have saved $40 or so.)
Anyway, that was six months ago, and I haven't looked back. It's really, really comfortable to type on, especially if you are used to the flat Mac keys. It feels sturdy, and (mostly) stays in it's case when I am commuting to and from school. (The iPad has popped out of the "frame" once or twice, but mostly seems secure.)
Did I mention it's a dream to type on?

So, here's what bugs:
1~ The no backlight thing is a minor annoyance, it's true. That said, I wouldn't want to see price, weight, heat out-put or battery life affected in exchange.... Honestly, the battery life is incredible- my sister has gone 6 months without charging hers. 6 MONTHS! And that's with daily use. (With all the other gadgets I have to charge, it's a relief to not have to bother about one more thing.) Anyway, I got a white keyboard thinking it might help with visibility in low-light situations, but after 6 months, I came to realize I pretty much know where the keys are anyway, and it hasn't been that big a deal.

2~ This is really my only gripe, and it mildly annoys me a few times a week: The "lock" button- which makes the iPad go to the lock screen? I hit it all the time when I am going for the the "delete" button, immediately below it. I am sure the lock button comes in handy... Like, perhaps if you are a spy typing secret documents, and your nemesis just walked into the cafe where you shouldn't be typing on unsecured interwebs, anyway, well, you have a button to make the screen go dark. More likely, you are watching something not kid-appropriate on Netflix, and your little darling just walked in, wondering why she can' twitch Jessica Jones, too. I don't know.
All I know is that I hit that damn thing all the time when I don't mean to, and perhaps in future incarnations, Logitech can find somewhere else to put that darn thing.

In the meantime, I sure do love this keyboard- I'm typing on it now, in fact- and I'd buy it again, in a heartbeat.

title: Best [non gaming] Mouse I've Ever Used, in over 20 years.
text:
I think this is the best mouse I have ever used - it works so well, and I can even set the speed at which it 'travels', etc. (After years of frustration with Microsoft mice, I tried Logitech.) I have never had a problem with my Logitech mouse - I've used 2 models; and this has been over several years. The company's support staff is always friendly and always works to resolve any difficulty or problem you might have with their products. (I thought my mouse wasn't working at one point, and I called Logitech, and their staff person walked me through some things to check / try. We then found the 'issue', and it was resolved.

{I'm not an online gamer, so I can't comment on this, or any other mouse, in that situation. I suspect this would not be the 'right' mouse for gaming; but that there are an array of specialized mice for that venue.}

&Note: I suffered something like "Tennis Elbow" a year ago, but I wasn't playing tennis. My doctor suggested it was from using the mouse for too many hours day after day. Happily I found a mouse with a 'non-standard' design*, which when I use it puts my arm and wrist in a vertical alignment [like when shaking hands]. Happily, after using this mouse for a little while, my pain went away. So now I can still use my Logitech mouse - it's the "better" one for me, but if I start to feel that pain again I can switch for a time.

(* There are several of these 'handshake' mice on the market. I use one by ANKER. I've had it for nearly a year, and am quite pleased with it.)

text: I've had this headset for almost a year now, and at first I thought that it was a good one just to start with because of its cheaper price range. I got it so I wouldn't have wasted much money if I didn't end up liking my new job that required its use. I teach online classes and this headset is great! Totally compatible with Adobe Classroom, which I use with Google Chrome. I've never had any tech issues on my end with it, that's for sure. The sound cancellation isn't the best, but the headphones are cushiony enough that I have no problem wearing them for loooong stretches of time on my busy teaching days (yes, sometimes for about 8 hours total in a day). They don't make the arms of my glasses dig into the sensitive skin behind my ears, which was one of my biggest concerns initially. The cord is nice and long, so if I have to go get a new pen or something, I can discretely do it without taking my computer down accidentally. The mute button is my lifesaver! Students just think I have a really quiet house because they can't see it's muted through the classroom controls. The button is the only thing that has worn down over the past year, but it's still fully functional. I just have to make sure I feel a little click when I push it and check to make sure the little indicator light is blinking so I know it really is muted before I go ahead and bite into a crunchy snack or take a loud slurp of coffee =P.

title: A durable no-frills remote
text:
I have purchased several Logitech Har. This one is by far the most durable. It has been dropped numerous times onto my hardwood floor and continues to work. The downside is I am maxed out on devices - but I probably have more than the average person. The other downside is that it's not color, or terribly fancy. For me - that's not really a negative. My fancier remotes have died the first time they fell on the floor, while this simpler model has proved to be very rugged.
Adding a device or activity is very easy. It takes a bit of trial and error for certain activities - but I have managed to get everything programmed just as I want them. I have used this remote so much that the buttons are starting to fade, and more importantly, one of the buttons needs a hard press to respond, so it's time to replace it. That said, this remote has had a LOT of use, so I'm still pleased with it. One of the upsides of going with Logitech is that their software is able to pair to pretty much every device that has a remote, and they are constantly adding new ones. I'm not worried that this remote won't work on the tv that I purchase next year (OLED :)).. If you're looking for a remote to make your life easier and you don't need the bells and whistles, this is a durable no-frills remote that will do what you want it to do for many years.

text:
Yeah, this mic was probably overkill for me since I'm not using Skype, doing a podcast dictating to the computer or anyother worthwhile thing like that. I'm just playing games, watching tv (cable card) or streaming radio stations (Boomerradio ftw).

The problem I needed to solve was this: I use Voice Attack and some voice packs for Elite Dangerous. I have a cheap headset/microphone combination. First problem was that even with the attached mic, voice commands had to be repeatd to be recognized. The other, and more important to me, problem was that I hated having to either switch all audio to the headset or leave it coming from the speakers and have the headset mute. With the headset mute, I still had to hang it around my neck to use the mic.

Blue Ice solved this. I have the mic set about 7 or 8 inches in front of my left speaker. I've tested this with an audio recording program while streaming a radio station (Boomerradio) fairly loudly through my speakers. When I played back the recording I could hear my voice quite plainly and plenty loud, and heard absolutely nothing that was coming out of my speakers. I did have a panic moment when Windows speech engine appeared not to understand me, but it turned out I just needed to retrain the thing with the new mic. Now all is well.

I love this mic. I'm considering getting a boom for it just to clear up some desktop space, but I may not. It really doesn't take up that much space. At night, when I'm at the computer in a dark room, it does look like a cross between Hal the Computer and some kind of Terminator. I swear it's staring at me So that's maybe the only 'con' I can come up with.

It's also nice that it is USB. I have a powered USB hub so have no problem running the mic from there. With the usually audio plug I would be worrying about running out of places to plug audio thins in. Also, my experience with regular plugs is that occasionally either the plug or the hole isn't quite right and you have to move them around a bit to get a good connection. This never happens with USB.

All in all, I'm very glad I decided to go with this Blue Snowball Ice. :)

title: Great audio in/out. Dysfunctional extras.
text:
I've been a Logitech loyalist for quite a long time. They 'were' one of the very few companies that I would list off the top of my head that I thought were synonymous with 100% quality. Then I bought the G930 a few months ago. The audio quality of both the microphone and the speakers is fantastic. The ability to plug in the µUSB cable at any time, in use or not, and have it charge is wonderful. I'm glad that I can leave these plugged in and be able to use them and unplug when I want that freedom of wireless. I definitely enjoy those parts about this headset which account for all four stars of this rating though I really wish I could rate it more of a 3.5. Not quite a three, but definitely teetering on that fence.

I'm too tired at the moment to go into depth about the cons but it basically breaks down to this: At first, the headset liked to completely turn itself off for no reason, regardless of being fully charged and/or being plugged in and the fact that it's 4 feet away from the transceiver, until I tweaked a setting in an XML file that supposedly gets broadcast to the device for configuration (Found this via Google and Youtube). That seemed to fix the issue for the most part to the point that I am pleased with it. The next problem is the function buttons. They're supposed to be programmable with either the nicely made GUI as well as a more advanced route which requires actually writing a script that runs to interpret the control signals coming from the headset. There were functions that should have been trivial that I simply could not get to work outside of it's testing environment. I tried setting it up via the GUI and even writing that scripts for it and it worked as long as I was testing it within the testing environment but nowhere else. That frustrated me. If you only want to get a nice quality wireless headset for the audio aspect then this headset will deliver for sure. If you want more out of it, I suggest looking elsewhere.

title: Poor quality- started falling apart within 4 months and sound quality sub par.
text:
I work online as a teacher and was desperate to find a behind the head wireless headset. I have always had Logitech products and many of my headsets have lasted a year or more, but I really needed a wireless set.
I bit the bullet and bought this very expensive headset.

So the good news is that they are wireless and behind the head. The rest is bad news.

1st- the sound goes in and out for my students. They say that I at times sound like a robot or the sound disappears and comes back.
2nd- about 2 1/2 months ago they started to disintegrate. The top at the neck connection first looked cracked and then it crumbled and fell apart. At this point I have cardboard wrapped with electrical tape just to keep it together.

I can't afford a new pair and I can't afford to send them back, plus, I don't know how to find out whether the regular warranty would kick in as I have no information who to contact.

If I could find another pair that will last and be worth the price, I'm all ears. Right now, it is a lesson in disappointment and frustration.

UPDATE: Amazon support is fabulous trying to help me get a replacement, but Logitech Customer Service is the absolute worst. After 1 hour on the phone, I was told they would replace my headset with a new set which is $99 (They told me that they were never really that expensive just priced that way because they aren't sold any longer (say what?) Then, they told me that before they will replace them, I have to send them in at which point they will determine if they will replace them and then I can wait for the determination all the while, I would have no headset to teach with. text:
I had the Harmony 800 and it performed fairly well except for buttons breaking. I've been disappointed however with the 650. When everything is working, it does the job OK but it has the following characteristics that I hate and which make me wish I had chosen a different remote:
* It feasts on batteries. I'm used to remotes where 2 AA batteries last 1-3 years. In this remote, you'll get a few months, maybe.
* Poor button feedback. The buttons do not have a satisfying "click" or "pop" when you select them, but just feel squishy. On top of that, when you want to select an activity or power things off, I often have to hold down the button for around 1.5-2 seconds to have it take effect. That doesn't seem like much time, but it's way longer than you would expect on a remote.
* It's slow. When you select an activity, the remote is generally locked out for ~25 seconds where you can't do anything with it. This continues even when all devices are turned on (and sometimes device modes still aren't correct even after that time).

title: Made my mom smile
text: Bought it for my mom to use on Skype. She has a new Win 10 Tower and an older flat screen that was almost too thick for this webcam. But it did perch up there pretty steadily. When I turned on the computer there was no software to install and Skype recognized the webcam right away. I called my mom over to the computer and had her run a Skype Echo test to make sure the volume was okay. At first the test did not work, and then I realized her old stand-alone microphone was still attached. So we disconnected that mic, and then the Echo test worked great. My mom spoke fairly softly but the mic test worked flawlessly. I showed her the video image using Skype's video settings tab, and she said that the camera made her look good. The image was bright and crisp. Finally we ran a Skype video call from her desktop to my iPad's Skype app. I was in a different room of the house to avoid any mic feedback. The call was very high clarity and great sound, though of course, we were on the same wifi network at the time. The next test will be when my mom uses Skype to visit with her daughter, her grandkids, her sister, etc. But all in all, five stars for ease of setup and use. And for the quality of the image, the sound, and my mom's smile.

title: The MX Revolution is still the best Logitech has made yet they seem to ignore the ...
text:
Update: 12.06.2017
--------------------------------
Just a paper weight on my desk now. No left/right scroll (customized buttons) has proven to proven to be a no go for me.
I simply can't use without missing the feature. While the mouse itself is really good, the lack of physical buttons has left me no choice but to give 2 stars.
1 star for the quality, multiconnect, battery with cord charge while using.
1 star for the original SmartScroll

Original Review
--------------------------------
The MX Revolution is still the best Logitech has made yet they seem to ignore the voices of their customers.
This mouse could have been the new MX Revolution just like the MX Performance could have been the new MX Revolution too.

Likes:
1. The mouse is a beauty as it fits nicely and has a nice feel. I am still unsure if it is as good as the MX Revolution but no complaints.
2. The Smart Shift Scroll is back (awesome) - Main reason I bought it.
3. The top scroll has a nice feel and is wider than the MX Revolution. The other scroll feels nice too.
4. Charge and use simultaneously.
5. The Vertical Scroll wheel is neat. Works pretty good as Back/Forward.
6. Thumb Button on the thumb rest.
7. MutliConnect

Dislikes:
1. No Left/Right on the top scroll wheel (SERIOUS disappointment as I had these as programmable keys).
2. Back/Forward side button is kind of weird to use. I think this should have been placed above the vertical scroll wheel in a linear form.
3. Software is not as good as SetPoint although it is prettier and opens faster. The mouse speed is slow but I'm hoping this can be changed in the software in a future upgrade (if not, then another star deduction).
4. The number of buttons is less than the MX Revolution.

Suggestions (additional - what was not mentioned above)
1. Add back the Thumb Wheel.
2. I would like another button behind the top scroll wheel.

Wake up Logitech! Make what people want. You had the best mouse in the MX Revolution. All you have to do is fine tune it, not re-invent it.
Your pass two (2) attempts have been pretty much failures. Third time the charm I hope :-)
Also, in case you haven't realized it as yet, people will pay if they think it's worth it. However, when you keep short changing them they get annoyed.

title: Best mouse I've ever used in 15+ years. Extremely well designed & made, extremely comfortable to use. Feature loaded.
text:
Best mouse I've ever used in 15+ years. Extremely well made, extremely comfortable to use. Feature loaded.

The Logitech Options software is surprisingly well designed and easy to use to configure the myriad custom functions of this mouse. The fact that you can pair it to 3 computers simultaneously is awesome, and if you have bluetooth issues, the RF transmitter can also be used with multiple Logitech devices simultaneously using only one USB port. I did experience interference caused by the mouse on my Bluetooth earbuds, so I've been using the RF transmitter. It does seem smoother and more responsive (as much so as my USB Razor DeathAdder gaming mouse) with the Logitech transmitter.

The mouse is extremely comfortable to use and conforms to my hand perfectly. The scroll wheel is great, and it's something that seems a little odd at first, but once you get used to it (a day or two), other scroll wheels will seem primitive by comparison. The buttons will quite literally save you hours of time over the lifetime of the mouse, because you can program tons of mouse-intensive or even keyboard shortcut functionality into them. For example, I've mapped mine to several powerful keyboard shortcuts to save time. You forget how many times you take your hand off the mouse to use the keyboard, or how many times you use your mouse to hit tiny on-screen buttons that can be mapped to mouse buttons.

It is cross-platform, so all the functionality works with Mac and Windows, and you can even program all the buttons to do different things on your Windows machine than your Mac, and switch between the two machines with the press of a button on the bottom of the mouse. Really a great modern mouse that is designed for today's computer-heavy homes and offices. For example, you can pair and configure it for your work computer, your laptop, and your home theater computer – regardless of operating system – and connect to each instantly without re-pairing.

Overall, this is an absolutely fabulous product, and I highly recommend it.

title: One remote to rule them all
text:
This initially took some time to get exact model numbers and how things were all connected. Once I had that information to begin, the process to set up the remote with each activity was pretty easy. You can fine tune later, but it’s pretty much just checking boxes and the software does the rest.

For example: A single press of the “Watch a Movie” button on the remote turns on my TV and sets it to the correct input, turns on the receiver and sets it to the correct setting for the Roku and, lastly, sends the OK command to the Roku to take it out of standby. From there, we can watch NetFlix, Amazon or content on our HTPC via the Roku Plex app.

(The OK command to the Roku was added to the activity in the Adjust Settings for this Activity feature in the Harmony software)

My wife, who has hated all the individual remotes and figuring out what to do with them, almost cried when she saw yet another remote come into the house. I assured her that in the end, there would be just this one remote and she would only have to press one button to watch a movie, etc… and that’s where we are now. We’re both very happy with the results.

My details might help someone decide if this is for them. I’d guess that mine is a pretty standard arrangement, except for the exact models of the equipment and *maybe* the Home Theater PC:

- Samsung TV
- Yamaha RX-V467
- HTPC running Plex
- Roku 2 XS
- Playstation 3

The Roku, PS3 and HTPC all feed via HDMI into the Yamaha receiver. From the receiver, there is a single HDMI going to HDMI 1 on the TV.

*** NOTE: I had problems with the receiver going to the correct input and then within seconds switching to AV4. To be clear, this was NOT a problem with the remote, but apparently with the settings between Samsung TVs and AV receivers. (Google “receiver switches to av4”)

The fix was to disable AnyNet+ in the Samsung TV options and then it all worked as expected; the input/output STAYS where it should.

THE REMOTE:

First step is to get the exact models from the devices. For example, my Roku 2 XS is actually a 3100X. So, giving the setup the correct and full information will make the setup go more easily.

Also, you should know how your devices are connected, what inputs and outputs are used.

Plug your remote into a USB port on the laptop and create or log into a Harmony account.

The software saves the configurations, so you can easily go back and tweak or even copy to a new Harmony remote.

title: The Best Mouse for $25
text:
The Logitech M510 Wireless Mouse is a great wireless mouse. After using the M510 for about 3 months, it is clear that this purchase was a wise decision.

Proves and Contras:
The mouse is comfortable, period. I have large hands and use a claw type mouse grip and this mouse feels wonderful. My wife has very small hands and uses a full palm mouse grip, yet this mouse is extremely comfortable for her as well. Regardless if you are used to large gaming mice or small wireless mice this mouse should feel comfortable. The mouse has a lovely weight and solid feel; the buttons are firm and feel distinct when pressed. The scroll wheel has soft clicks you can feel when scrolling a webpage, text document, etc. The left and right scrolling options were a nice unexpected touch. The left and right clicks feel crisp and are audible but not overly loud. The mouse’s finish is smooth and soft with firm rubber grips on each side that work well with my particular mouse grip. The backwards and forwards buttons are also firm and I do not have any trouble accessing them or with accidentally pressing them. Plug and play means no setup is required simply plug the mouse into your computer and start using your mouse. The Logitech unifying receiver is great if you have other Logitech wireless accessories. For example, I already had a Logitech wireless keyboard. Using only one receiver, I am able to use both accessories with a single dongle freeing a USB port. The mouse also tracks extremely well and is accurate for sensitive applications such as Photoshop work or causal gaming.

The only complaint I have about the M510 is the absence of an adjustable DPI button. I game frequently and having the ability to change DPI during gameplay would be great. That said for the price you really cannot expect everything.

Verdict:
For under $25 dollars, this is the best mouse you could hope to purchase hands down. My wife and I have ordered two now and we are both extremely happy with our purchases. I will reserve a full 5 star rating, but this is only because the DPI is not adjustable, which would have served my personal needs better. However, this is a well-made, comfortable, and accurate mouse. I give the Logitech M510 a solid 4 out of 5 stars.

title: "Double-Click" Defect Still Exists in 2016 - Avoid this Mouse!
text:
The top reviewers for this mouse give low ratings due to the "phantom double-click" glitch that this mouse (apparently) frequently exhibits. The reviews are from 2013, so after 3 years I thought it may have been corrected since then. Nope. After a few months of use, my mouse has started failing in the exact same way described by the other reviewers - a single click randomly becomes a double click, making PC work nearly impossible. And hugely frustrating.

This is extra sad for me, because otherwise this mouse has a great design. It tracks perfectly, you can use one battery or two (allowing weight adjustment), and the shape fits my hand / grip style exactly right. Plus, the "middle" mouse button (the small metal tab on top) is the best I've found, since it seems to be ideally suited for CAD work without accidentally scrolling.

But regrettably, I'm forced to advise you to stay away from this mouse, and don't be fooled by the high overall ratings. Listen to the warnings, like I should have (but didn't), and save yourself headaches. It's clearly defective in its hardware design and/or components.

title: Good but not great.

I would be a lot happier if the playback buttons were moved below the screen. I sometimes would like to pause playback while the remote set down on a table or the couch, but the bulb like shape on the back of the remote causes the remote to tilt, and feels awkward.  I do like the touch screen, it allows for direct tuning to a specific channel, and me not having to remember what the channel number is. I do enjoy not having to switch between several remotes while watching tv/watching a DVD/or watching appleTV. Alexa is supposed to work with Harmony through IFTTT, but I would not recommend it. Charging the unit did nothing - in fact, keyboard didn't even acknowledge that it was hooked to power. When I tried to find a resolution through the Logitech web page - all I got was that the coin batteries needed replacement - but the two halves of the board were glued together so there was no way to pursue this remedy. I filed a claim but never have received any sort of acknowledgement so tomorrow, the case goes into a box that will be delivered to UPS to be returned to the company. I suspect that the non-functioning keyboard will quickly disappear into the abyss and that no resolution will ever happen, but, the keyboard is of no use in its current state so need for it to be cluttering my house. title: Works intermittantly in machines with a mixof  usb3, usb2+ and USB2 ports
text:
This thing would be great if it worked. They have some kind of incompatibility with newer computers... they work intermittently. When you look at places where people talk about this, this is a common problem. I have 4 or 5 of them here, as my wife keeps replacing her's because she thinks it is dying. Now she finally believes me that this is a software issue. You plug then in fresh they work fine for a while, anywhere from days to minutes. This time her new one lasted about 4 minutes. I have the same problems.

The receiver that you plug into the computer fails very quickly if you plug it into a high-end powered usb hub (a place it should work the best). But not only that, when it is messing up, it causes my wired keyboard to mess up in a really weird way... it delays whitespace and special characters while not delaying text, so it rearranges what I time... intermittently. When it becomes unresponsive or glitchy, it is messing up everything on usb. I unplug everything, no hub, only trackball and dell branded wired keyboard on usb... works great for 10 minutes, and then it is messing up again. Does the same thing on my desktop and three laptops, my wife's old and new laptop, and desktop too. My wife uses the logitech wireless keyboard on two machines, the keyboard seems to work, but both the trackball and keyboard are connected through thesame wireless link, so at least they are compatible... but regardless of which USB2, USB2+ or USB3 port we use, the trackball is intermittently unresponsive. This has persisted through both windows 7 and windows 10 environments. Turning offal l wireless in the house does not help (our office machines are both hard wired, so no wireless is involved, and we are well shielded from any outside wireless and, I can turn my phone off too. My spectrum analyzer shows that no signals strong enough to use are active in the house. Every other sentence I type I have to go re-edit because spaces are all bunched together after blocks of joined words... This only happens when the M570 is connected. When I unplug it I can type as fast as I want and no spaces or special characters are delayed, everything types perfectly. kind of howit works when I use a wired mouse. There is a serious software flaw, and logitech is in denial, blaming it on everything from dirt to little green men. I would switch back to the wired version, but logitech discontinued it, so the remaining ones for sale are selling for $200 or more.

Logitech knows they have software issues, but they have yet to address this issue or release software that fixes it. None of my other usb devices have any problems, and my keyboard works perfectly until I plug the logitech wireless dongle in. (and yes, we have tried multiple wireless dongles, we get a new one with each M570 and wireless keyboad.).

title: Controller That Controls it all: PS4, XB1, TV, DVD, Receiver, etc
text:
I have the following devices that I use on my TV: PS4, Dreamcast, Xbox One, Receiver, VCR, Cable TV & DVD Player.

Using the remote controller I am able to control all the devices (including the ps4) with the exception of the dreamcast.

PS4 note: My TV is a HDMI-CEC tv, which means I can control the PS4 using the TV remote since the TV & PS4 are synced. I can go back, open apps, go left and right, select netflix movies (get out of them), pause movies, play them, etc. Now the trick is you add the PS4 option as if you are "Watching TV" and have it select the correct HDMI input (this means the TV controller IR signal will be giving all the commands and control everything - both ps4 and TV). If you try to add it as a console or a device it will not work. Do not even bother adding the ps4 as a device at all. This is not perfect as I cannot turn off or on the ps4 console but neither can the $350 bluetooth enabled remotes. This is very care as this means the Harmony 350 & 650 controller can control the PS4 without the need of a bluetooth enabled device if your console has CEC. This works great on netfix, amazon prime, watch movies, etc. You have to have the CEC HDMI option enabled on your TV for it to work as well. Many people can control the PS4 using their basic TV remotes and don't even know it. The $350 harmony bluetooth version does not control the PS4 any better than this. If you do not have a CEC enabled TV your only option is a bluetooth enabled Harmony device that costs the price of a ps4 or more than it.

Xbox One works even nicer as you have full control of everything including on/off. Other devices work fine.

So its great being able to automate and customize everything. Overall its not perfect. The easy setup you have to trick to get it to work right. The all off command works about 50% of the time (usually hitting help next will fix it).

Overall it was a draw between the Harmony 350 & 650. In short, the 350 has a better control layout that is simpler and does everything this one does. The 650 is a little more complex and needs extra steps (such as the missing input command in which you have to go through the digital menu) but it does have additional activity options that partially makes up for it (but doubles the costs). Overall, the 350 vs 650 is all about multiple activity queuing.

Listening to Jamie xx (nice reference material for clean bass), I found a few of tracks that didn't make me cringe the whole time as the bass swept in an out of the speakers' "sweet spot".

title: Get these speakers.  Then throw on some Drake and let them rock! You will be impressed...
text:
I have these installed at my desk at work. The quality FAR exceeds the price point. Very pleased with the product - no regrets. Bass response is phenomenal, and middle and high frequencies are true. You will hear extreme EQ settings that you set on your source material, but do not have to have extreme settings to get a great sound with this system. My primary data source is my iPhone using the supplied 3.5mm cable. The cable is long enough that I can swing it around and occasionally use it with the headphone jack on my work PC. Installation was easy and all cables are long enough for me to position the speakers where I want them.

Received the unit at work - much heavier than anticipated which, if you are a speaker geek, you know that means heavy magnets on the low frequency speakers and better sound. The weight is the subwoofer, and it does NOT disappoint - the sub is better than a lot of home theater systems I have heard. Audio playback on my Spotify account is set to Extreme, and you can hear the enhanced clarity and spatial detail with this set. EDM and pop music uses effects that make sounds appear to be coming from outside the speakers and these effects translate well on this set. Guitar and vocals on country music is super detailed, and made even me a fan! (Spotify playlist - "Country Coffeehouse" is the bomb!). I have the subwoofer on the floor and the satellites on my desk about 3 feet apart. The sound is amazing!

Given that these are used in a work environment, I especially like that I can turn the subwoofer off completely via the control knob on the right speaker, next to the volume control. This results is a sound you would expect from typical office PC speakers - but highs and mids are better. However, the knob is variable, not just an off/on switch, so I can adjust to my liking at the moment.

Get these speakers. Then throw on some Drake and let them rock! Even if you do not like rap or hip hop, you will be impressed!

- The programming interface is terrible. I'm trying to make a button on the app that clicks a few buttons, but I'm dragged through some interface that wants to set up power on and off, input switching, etc. It's like they have never used their own product.
- The app appears to talk to the server, which then talks to the hub. It's all super slow and clunky. I could possibly be wrong about the communication method, but not the slow and clunky part.

text:
I tried this gamepad after buying several cheaper ones that weren't compatible with the games I play through Steam on my PC. After several attempts at saving myself some money I decided to go for this which I've seen is a fully recognized xbox controller through all the games. I've been using it for almost a year and I've had absolutely no problems getting it to work with any of my games. It's comfortable to use, and it does everything I need from a PC Gamepad. The only issue I've had with it is that sometimes the top triggers don't register unless you push down a little harder than normal on them. The issue is likely specific to my controller so I doubt everyone experiences it with these controllers but I haven't bothered to try to get it replaced. If it wasn't for that defect I'd give this a full 5.

Pros: Great controller for a good price. Easy to use - plug and play. No driver issues or compatibility issues with any games I've played. Comfortable grip, easy to use buttons, durable.
Cons: My top right and left buttons need to be pressed a little harder than normal to get them to register in game.

title: Perfect for travel or to save space
text:
I absolutely love this mouse. It is exactly the small and compact size I was looking for. When I am at home (not at school) I really dislike using the track pad or touch screen unless on a whim. Let me rephrase that, I do not like HAVING to ONLY use the track pad and or touch screen lol. Call me old school I guess, I just find the mice much easier and precise to navigate with.

The previous one I had from 3-4 years ago was just a little too big and the wireless adapter was as big as a full size flash drive. I needed something more compact that has an adapter I can leave in all of the time. Searched around Amazon and came across this little beauty. It is so small, if I want to bring it with me somewhere, it easily fits into the little accessory pouch my laptop sleeve came with. The adapter is like one of the mini flash drives. It is so small I just leave it in almost all of the time. When you do want to take it out there is a place to store it in the closed compartment where the battery is (one AAA battery required) so it does not get misplaced or damaged. There is an on/off switch on the bottom of the mouse as well, always a considerate feature and handy to have when you are traveling with it.

I have been using it everyday for a couple of months now and have not had any issues. Once in a while I get tired or lazy and I have to change the way I am resting my hand on the top of the mouse because I have accidentally hit the right click. I suppose that would be expected with such a tiny mouse though, it is not a big deal. I did learn though after starting to use it, I needed to get a mouse pad. I mostly use it on a desk that has a glass top on it and the mouse would not work unless it was on a piece of paper or another object that is not translucent. I was slightly irritated but I ended up getting a really beautiful and good quality mouse pad that I love, on Amazon of course. So it worked out well.

If it holds up anything like my other Logitech branded items, I am looking forward to many years of use without having to worry about replacement. If you are looking for a small and compact mouse for around the house or travel, look no further.

text: I own an older set of Logitech 2.1 speakers that I used for my computer and absolutely loved them.  In fact, I connected them to my Vizio 1080p HDTV and the sound is fantastic.  When I purchased a new Samsung HDTV the sound was HORRIBLE!  So I bought these newer Logitech speakers to connect to the Samsung TV &  I am very disappointed in them.  The maximum volume is quite low and there is no way to enhance the high and mid ranges.  The base is amazing, but it overpowers the mid & high end, which I really appreciate.  There is no option for an equalizer to customize the sound, and there is not enough modern connectors to hook to a HDTV; just RCA.  Unfortunately, the TV will not allow the use of it's remote for sound volume when you use an external source!  Needless to say, I am NOT happy with either these Logitech speakers or the Samsung TV (that everyone raves about)!  I did buy another Vizio soundbar, and the volume and sound are VERY good.  They allow customization of the frequencies most desired, and the maximum volume is louder than I would ever need where the TV is located.  I was expecting much more in a 200 watt system.  But putting most of your wattage into the subwoofer and not providing adequate volume or equalization options renders this model a dud, in mho.

title: Highly recommend. 1.) uses regular batteries. 2.) Good quality 3.) wireless dongle & storage. Avoid Bluetooth only (see below)
text:
First I want to point out that this gamepad uses a dongle when connecting to a PC (which is a good thing). I have had issues with several Bluetooth gamepads that are only Bluetooth for PC gaming. There is a strange issue with windows 7 and windows 10. At some point depending on how many times you install/uninstall the Bluetooth only gamepads windows will not install it correctly and the joysticks no longer function under windows. I have researched this extensively and contacted a maker of another gamepad and the only solution I found once this happens is to reinstall windows because once you do this they start to work again (not a practical solution). This is NOT an issue with this gamepad since it uses a dongle when hooking up to a PC. In fact it shows up in the control panel like a xbox 360 controller and even though the Bluetooth gamepad no longer installs correctly this one continues to work. So in short avoid the Bluetooth ones when that is the only method of using it with a PC. I would also recommend getting a copy of Pinnacle's Game Profiler which will also you to map the gamepad if needed with certain games.

This is a great PC gamepad. It is a little heavy but that is probably because of using regular batteries. I definitely would prefer to put up with some additional weight and have a device that will last longer because you can swap out the batteries yourself. An internal rechargeable battery will eventually fail to hold a charge and then you will not be able to use it wireless maybe corded (providing you can use it that way).

Build quality is great and here is one feature all the other makes of dongle using gamepads should include: dongle STORAGE. Which for this gamepad is in with the batteries. Thank you Logitech for thinking of dongle storage. It drives me crazy when you have a device that uses a dongle and which is large enough to have had a place made in the device to store the dongle and yet there is none.

So if you are looking for a PC gamepad that uses regular batteries and not an internal rechargeable battery I would recommend this one. It just depends on what you prefer; but as mentioned already all internal batteries fail eventually it is only a matter of time.

title: An incredible mouse but Mac Users should read this before buying.
text:
I've now had this mouse for about a year a it is BY FAR the best mouse that I've ever owned. I started using it on Windows 7 but later upgraded my PC to Windows 10. Both worked extremely well. However I did have some problems when I tried to use Synergy to allow for the mouse to be used between two different PCs at the same time. That is one little thing to be aware of.

Recently, I started a new job and got a brand new MacBook Pro. It started off as a total disaster. The mouse was barely useable as the mouse pointer lagged horribly. I searched logitech's forums and today I finally found a solution.

It appears that the MX Mouse's BT connection is being interfered with by the MBP's Wifi transceiver. I did some testing to confirm that this was indeed the issue. I simply turned off my WiFi and the mouse started working perfectly. I then used my Thunderbolt ethernet adapter for my networking connection and once again everything worked incredibly well. After some more investigating, I read that running WiFi at 2.4Ghz causes the interference. Check your wifi routter/access point to see if you can change it from 2.4Ghz to 5Ghz. Doing this allowed me to use my mouse and continue using my wifi connection...

In summary:
MX Mouse + 2.4Ghz Wifi = BAD LIKE FIRE!
MX Mouse + 5Ghz WiFi = GOOD LIKE BEER!

As to the operation of the mouse on Apple OS X, we dammit, it's frackin' awesome! Don't shop for any other mouse. Stop right here because this is THE ONE!

title: I still miss my Klipsch, but...
text:
I bought this as a replacement for the Klipsch 2.1 that I'd had for less than a year when the amp for the satellite speakers went out. I loved that Klipsch system, but for the price ($40 less) I'm impressed with this sound system. They're both THX certified, which is nice. Here's my comparison:

The Klipsch seemed to have more volume to it. 1/2 way on the volume knob with 1/4 turn on the sub was plenty.

The Logitech's amplifier is a little different, but I cranked it up right out of the box, and still no distortion. The sub's halfway point is plenty, but you can crank that up, and it still doesn't distort.

The Klipsch seemed to have more of a Marantz-style richness to the sound.

The Logitech seems a bit crisper on the high end than the Klipsch.

The Klipsch's sub can't handle lower frequencies like the 7" sub of the Logitech can. Nice, rich, deep bass, lending itself well to games or movies.

Bottom line. I hated having to waste $150 on the Klipsch to have it die a little over a year later. If I had it to do over again, I would get this Logitech and save some cash. It's handled everything I could throw at it and more. Great purchase!

title: Worst Harmony remote I have ever used
text:
I have owned quite a few Harmony remotes over the years and loved them all -- except for the Harmony 350. Either save your money and buy a cheap $10 universal remote, or spend a bit more and get the 650 or one of the more advanced remotes.

While it is true that the 350 can control up to 8 devices, it only can control a single "activity", which is pre-selected to "Watch TV". This is great for controlling your cable box and TV, but useless if you also have a DVD player or other media devices. For those you have to keep pushing device buttons to switch the remote between the devices, say if you want to start playing a DVD, then change the volume on the TV, then pause the DVD. There is no way to associate the TV volume with the DVD player. There are also no macros on this remote, so to switch do your DVD player you have to hit the following sequence - DVD button, DVD power (which is oddly placed to the side of the device buttons), TV button, Input button one or more times to select the correct input, DVD button, Menu or Play button to start the DVD.

In addition, once you leave the "Watch TV" mode, there is no way to get back to it without powering everything off and on again by hitting the "Watch TV" button twice.

I purchased this remote for an aging parent thinking that it would make it easier for him to switch between watching TV and his DVD player. After a few minutes of working with it, we both realized that it is easier for him to use two remotes than it is for him to use this single one.

Logitech apparently upgraded their receivers, because it was a slightly different shape with a newer logo that matches the website. They may need to update their software, if this is a driver issue.

title: I forgot how amazing logitech mice were for gaming, the G502 is like coming back home for my hand
text:
I've been using a Razer deathadder for the last two years, the first I'd used a non-Logitech mouse for gaming. The G502 is the first gaming mouse I've used from Logitech, and I've been really impressed. A lot of the features I'd assumed to be gimmicks turned out to make a real difference. Messing around with the metal weights and weight placement really changes how the mouse handles. I preferred placing two weights in the slots that form a ring around the sensor. I tend to use a more relaxed claw grip, and the weights gave the mouse a nice heft and felt good moving side to side. I also didn't expect to use the sniper button...turns out that being able to drop my DPI on the fly greater improved my accuracy for certain moments in Overwatch. The profile manager is decent, and being able to switch from a 2400DPI MOBA profile to a 1600/800 DPI shooter profile is a nice thing to tweak and play around with. The button placement takes some getting used to as there were initially more buttons than my giners knew what to do with. The two buttons to the left of the leftclick button are tricky, and those are the ones that let you cycle DPI settings. I'm adjusting though. Still, I felt like my accuracy improved with this mouse. I don't know if that is due to comfort or one of the key features, but I'm excited to continue to experiment with the vast functionality of the G502

Overall, I'm really glad I bought this mouse, and I won't miss the Deathadder at all (even if it is also a great mouse).

title: Rubbish for any serious typer
text:
I am an efficient blind-touch typist, who appreciates a well laid out keyboard as it allows access to most shortcuts I normally use.

This keyboard just does not cut it for me. The problem other reviewers mentioned is not such a big deal really - Yes, you can switch between F and special keys on the top row if you download logitech software. Here's the list of real issues for me:

1. The keyboard is small - keys are squashed and the layout is actually smaller than on my 13' laptop. It is a small keyboard. Tight and uncomfortable.
2. There's no dedicated Pg Up and Pg Down keys - I cannot switch between Excel or Firefox tabs, i cannot even scroll pages efficiently. This is a major handicap.
3. A pressed key does not necessarily means that the key has been detected - this is generally ok for the keyboard keys, but the mouse keys (both by the track pad and on the left top corner of the keyboard) fail miserably. This is another major handicap.

The trouble with #1 and #2 that most other modern combo keyboards on the market suffer from the same poor layout. You can see that Logitech, Microsoft and other smaller brands have the same issue - they are pressured by miniaturization and hence compromise on the usability of the keyboard.

Two stars if you just want a remote for using a TV set - it will probably do. For any serious work where productivity is critical this is a piece of garbage. Very disappointed.

I LOVED this mouse, and am a big fan of Logitech mice, but have only ever really used their gaming mice in the past.

Why I'm considering tossing it after two months: I configured the thumb button to minimize windows, and use that button very regularly. I've had the mouse for a little less than two months now and the button has settled about a millimeter under level with the adjacent metal trim. I don't like the rough feeling on my thumb and it is somewhat more difficult to press now. I would've expected this button to last considerably longer.

I'm considering asking Amazon/Logitech to refund the mouse. In retrospect, even though I don't use this mouse for gaming, I now wish that I would've bought the G700s because it has more programmable buttons that I would use for things like forward/back/cut/copy/paste/enter.

Other thoughts: It looks sharp. It feels great and is comfortable to use (as I would expect from a high-end Logitech mouse). Middle click is a little difficult to press. It has programmable buttons. If you ever overcharge and destroy the battery it takes standard rechargeable AA batteries (score). The included SetPoint software does not let you create macros using the Windows button, which is sad; lots of great keyboard shortcuts use the Windows button, but I think this can be accomplished with third-party software.

title: My new favorite Wireless Mouse/Keyboard Combo
text:
I was a bigger hero than I realized when I bought this for my wife. The lit keyboard feature alone (it senses your presence...oooo...and lights your way to delightedly substantial f and j pegs...ooooo). Never again will she (nor I - I bought one for myself... at home... one for my office, so that's three...). Never again will we have a keyboard that doesn't light at our touch (near touch is even cooler) no matter the lighting in the room. It's amazingly rock solid for it's very thin profile. It hugs my desk like a race car on asphalt, but travels around the room like a tablet.

The window view offered by the mouse (thumb-down) is pretty sweet, a nice Alt/Tab alternative (my wife didn't alt/Tab). It worked flawlessly across two monitors as needed without any tweaking at all.

Seems you can program anything you want, but I didn't go nuts. I want the forward/back buttons to be comfortable (they are), the clicks to feel right (they do), it needs to be silky smooth on all surfaces (one laminate, one textured plastic, one wood - all good), it needs to be comfortable (I'm half again her size yet it suits us both)... that covers it. I'm playing with the zoom (careful on your scroll speed or you could open a wormhole). I should rtfm as there's another button that I don't need but it might do something cool... another reviewer no doubt touches on it.

Love it. Home run. Easily my new favorite keyboard and mouse combo (hers too - better!). Expensive. Worth it, IMHO.

text:
I rather like this thing, but the other people in my life using television in my house still cannot get it right, which is about 90% of the reason I got this: so I could stop having to fix the TV every single time my mother-in-law or parents turn it on.

Going from power off to everything on basically never works correctly. I have spent literally hours and hours working with the timing and delays and every setting I can possibly tweak, going through the Logitech forums for hints, and yet somehow one device or another doesn't turn on. Or the input switching gets out of sync and then chaos ensues. The most frustrating aspect is that the TV will never turn off in sequence, even though I go through the on-remote help tool right after it fails to turn off, and every time the remote is perfectly capable of turning it off.

Once everything is changed for an Activity and all the problems are sorted out, having channel control and volume and everything on one remote makes it almost worth it. Being able to assign anything to a button is cool, too. But the constant hassle of having to fix whatever went wrong with changing between Activities is pretty much more frustrating than it's worth.

When I read about these, I figured they were too good to be true. So, it's about as disappointing and frustrating as I expected, but still sort of worth it. #firstworldproblems

title: Scroll wheel just spoils what could have been an awesome mouse
text: Ok this mouse is awesome in every respect. Sensor, buttons, ergonomics. It's almost perfect... but man! The scroll wheel... it's just terrible!! I don't understand why they would design such a good mouse and neglect one of the most important parts. The scroll wheel is slippery, there is no grip to it and if you flick it hard it will skip a lot unless you use it's hyperscroll mode which is a really nice feature for scrolling through long documents or websites (I'm looking at you Reddit). It's very sensitive but it's completely useless because the scroll wheels they put on these mice are all unbalanced and they tend to turn on their own until they find a balancing point. Trust me it gets really annoying after a while. A lot of people are going to say "well I don't use hyperscrolling so it won't be a problem for me". True, you won't get annoyed by the scroll wheel moving on it's own but for the other reasons I mentioned above. Slippery and un responsive. One more thing, the mouse's weight is unbalanced as well, towards the front. You can use the included weights to balance it but beware it will become quite heavy for FPS games. I returned this and got a Razer Mamba TE which I'm really liking. It has a similar price, it's light, comfortable, well built and the scroll wheel works! It may not have hyperscrolling or weight management but you will also won't have the headaches they will give you!

title: Best Wireless Headset Currently (2016)
text:
Lets start with I have about 7+ headsets total: Wired and Wireless e.g. Corsair H2100, DT770 Pro 32 Ohm.

Pros:
- Comfortable
- Consistent Connectivity
- Surround sounds is good
- Good customer service
- Lasting batter
- Swapable battery
- Can Mix up to 3 devices
- Amazing microphone
- Compatible with consoles (at least PS4)
- Sturdy even when its plastic. Lightweight
- Pull up mic to mute

Con
- Depending on your headsize, sometime they do slip
- A big large
- When mixing between 3.5mm source to USB dongle, there could be static or volume limit
- Require LogiTech Software for full functionality.
- Battery status needs to be checked from the software and is not always accurate (e.g. drop from 50 to 15% when it updates)
- During charging stage, Logo lights cannot be turned off as its indication of charging.

Mixed:
- 95% of the time, my connectivity is good. But once in a while, it does dropped. This is from using on multiple PCs. Could be due to USB 3.0 per Logitech Support
- Expensive, but overall best wireless headset with great mic
- No point of having lighting on the device as you can't really see it and reduce battery time significantly. But looks very good and can be customized
- USB dongle is quiet big . But light status is clear for connectivity: Solid for connected. Blinking for standby.
- Buttons on the back are all on one side and close to each others. Difficulty to identify which is which. But can be customize to macros and commands on your PC.

Overall. Best wireless headset I have used. There are some draw backs and negatives, but that is just me being nit picky or just opinion. Very comfortable, but of course, long terms can be uncomfortable. The material for the ear pads are cloth like and soft, so it does trap some heat but absorb your sweat, which can be washable. Range is very very good in open area, but does cut off if you're through a wall. I have a router near one of my home set up and its not been interfering with the headset or vice versa. Having the backlight LED is very good looking and can be customized, but it does drain the battery very quickly, from 10 hours to approximately 6-7 hours from full. It does shows a status from mute to unmute as well, but you won't see it since its in the back, but there is a red LED light on the tip of the mic that will shows red as mute.

Pretty much all plastic, but it is very sturdy feeling and like its made out of quality materials. Light weight as its plastic. A bit bulky but does cover your ears completely. So its a bit outward feeling since its large, unlike something like Astro A50 where its flatter and closer to your head.

Comes with component adapters, 3.5mm headset cable which you can use that as a mic or the headset's mic. USB dongle of course. USB cable for charging.

I have had this headset for almost 3 months now.
And lastly, Logitech support/warranty in the past has always been great if you have any problems.

Pros:
Excellent sound.

Built-on volume control is great when you're gaming and can't alt-tab (and don't have a volume control on your keyboard).

title: Last gaming headset I'll ever buy
text:
I'll come back to write another review in 3 months just in case, but for now, it gets 5.5 / 5.

Edit: After using the software for awhile, honestly, it works perfect. I have no issues with it, and it's never intrusive with popups or stopping randomly. It's quick and responsive, and lets you change profiles on the fly (if you don't want to use the quick profile swap on the headset itself). The EQ works great. The DTS Surround option or whatever makes no sense to me, I can't play around with it to make it sound normal, it just makes everything worse for every application. But whatever. The regular 7.1 surround is perfect, and customizable with sliders for each digital "speaker".

Sound quality is amazing. Even hooked up to my phone and no driver/software, the 35mm sounded fantastic. I tested out a song I have in FLAC that I've listened to thousands of times and know what I should and shouldn't hear. I used a recent bluetooth earbud purchase, wired stock earbuds, a headset with mic (cheapo), Grado S80s and some old nice Sennheisers all one after another to test this out. And the G933 hands down wins. It consistently puts the most correct bass out while still letting me hear the subtle guitar notes, background vocals you can't really hear or make out normally, and all sorts of neat little sounds I forgot about when not using quality headphones. I love my S80s, but they leak sound and have no bass. Tthe over the ear pieces in the G933 help keep sound in/other sound out, as well as put out the most magnificent bass I've heard in a long time.

The 7.1 makes games feel like whole new experiences. That, and the bass. But mostly the 7.1. Seriously, it sounds amazing if the game you're playing can take advantage of it, and you have it setup correctly.

Mic: haven't had a chance to test this out with multiple sources. I can add this to my next review/update. I'm sure it sounds fine, it's USB and wireless, not a whole lot of room for error here. It has fold-to-mute, nice!

Controls: awesome controls on the headset, the inline is pretty nice too if you're using the 35mm cord. I muscle-memorized the locations of the buttons on the left headset quickly.

Looks: obviously awesome. A bit wide if you have a big head, but whatever. It glows in oh so many colors, so that makes up for it I think. My coworkers thought they looked "pretty sweet".

Comfort: super super comfort. Used for hours at a time, no sweat, no discomfort. Ears fit perfectly inside. No sore top of the skull area. Product isn't really that heavy.

Logitech software: Make sure you play around with the settings and don't overlook anything. There is a lot of power under the hood for the software, just make sure you test your sound when playing around with it. Don't make a lot of changes and then test it, otherwise correcting will be harder. It's pretty awesome!

title: Not perfect, but not bad, so far.
text: I bought this for work, doing a fair bit of CAD and home interiors layout work (cabinets, countertops, etc).  I used to have the Logitech Trackman Marble FX, and since it is no longer available, this was the closest thing.  Let me just say, it is nowhere near as easy to use or precise as the Trackman Marble FX, and the mouse buttons are not in as good of a position.  The FX was the best design ever, period, because with the larger trackball and its position, you could use thumb and forefinger to the wheel and control the trackball. Much better idea.  The M570 is a little too small for me, and I definitely don't like using only my thumb to roll the trackball.  With some adjustment of the speed and movement settings, it has gotten better, but still a tradeoff.  I read some of the other reviews about putting wedges of foam under it to improve the wrist angle, and am experimenting with that right now, and it seems to improve performance and comfort.  Have also read the other reviews about durability.  We'll see how that plays out as time goes on.  Overall, it's still definitely no Trackman Marble FX, but it is far superior to the aggravation of dragging a mouse around on my desk all day to do design work, and it is the best of what is available right now.  I've tried several others.  The wireless speed is good, and it works well on the Unifying USB plugin for running this and my Logitech keyboard.

title: This is a good BUDGET keyboard. Most important for me was no lag and good range and non directional for Keyboard.
text:
**Just a thought for people with lag\connection issues----In Windows change the USB settings in "power options". Depending on which version of Windows you'll have different selections. Enable them all\set always on, ect. Then go from there. it MAY help**

I'm reviewing this as a BUDGET wireless keyboard but with all the features and functionality of higher end models

It isn't what i'd hoped for but it will work.. You should just plug and play but If you have problems, downloading Logitech setpoint will solve many of them. It also has a tab in the program to change\add devices to the unifying receiver. Setpoint is also useful for the programmable keys,disable CapLocks,ect

Well, it certainly isn't as nice as the old Pro 2000\2800 set I had. Not by a long shot. This keyboard feels and is very cheaply made. It's very thin and simply feels a fragile. Durability might be an issue for some depending on how you use your keyboard...The Pro 2000/2800 was a solid, well built keyboard. It had a great feel, solid construction and much thicker build.

This kb is about as thin as it gets yet still having real keys. It also is an in between min\full size key board. Layout is not standard for center(home,end,pg up\dn)

It has 6 programmable keys along with the playback\sound buttons. it also has 4 fn keys I have yet to figure out how to use. This is all customized through the setpoint software which I had already been using with my old kb. I might be in the minority, but I like setpoint. Very handy to keep CapLock key disabled as there is no light on the kb.

I've read a few reviews on here of people who experience lag with this kb so I think it may be up to the individual set up and other devices(phones, routers, ect) in the general area. All I can say is how it functions for me..I almost didn't buy based on those reviews

This kb doesn't suffer from dropped keys or lag nor is it directional. It has very good range as I frequently type with my kb on my lap with my legs bent up and sitting 6 feet or so from the computer. I can put random stuff in front of the keyboard and it has not one bit of lag or delay and doesn't drop any keys. This uses the unifying USB and the newer k330 kb. Not the mk320 that used the larger usb stick receiver

Fast forward 3 weeks.

I initially paired this with my old m570 trackman and it's unifying receiver. Paired right up and worked flawlessly although i did miss my pro 200/2800's full size and feel and traditional layout(the home,delete,end,pg up,pg down area is different)..

All of a sudden after 3 weeks the mouse started very minor freezing. Almost unnoticeable but i'm a bit obsessive about stuff. What was noticeable was the the kb started dropping keys at the same time. I ended up, not wishing to troubleshoot anything, simply added the second unifying receiver and put each device on it's own receiver. I don't use the included mouse so it's not paired

Not in the least bit an ideal setup, both devices do work perfectly again. I'm sure it has to do with something interfering as I have MANY devices running wireless in close proximity at same frequency.

When I get around to setting them both back up on a single unifying receiver i shall update this review. I will also update through out the life of the kb is anything comes up regarding connectivity and durability.

The mouse.
Small. I have small hands and it's a bit smaller than even I would prefer. It feels about the same as the keyboard--a bit fragile. Note--there is a button on bottom of mouse to release the battery cover. You still have to pull the cover off with some force though. Not the best design

For a budget wireless keyboard I suppose it's about what you can expect. It checked all the boxes that were important to me-No lag, non directional, good range, full sized bottom area many kbs lack nowadays. When typing in your lap it's essential to have that space.at the bottom. If you're on a budget it's a prefect keyboard for everyday use. This isn't a gamer keyboard.

If not for the 3 year warranty which Logitech has always honored throughout my 20 year history with the company I might have knocked another star off. If this lasts 3 years I'll be happy.

title: Works but with very stiff, hard to pull trigger buttons
text:
These feel sturdy and they are very responsive. Logitech did a great job with these, but the only problem i have is that the trigger buttons are extremely hard to pull. It literally feels like 6lbs of pressure just to pull the trigger. It's great if you need to finesse how much you pull the trigger button down (can't really think of too many situations tbh), but if you have to pull it all the time your finger will tire out really quickly unless you're like some kind of finger... push ups ...triathlete... or an all-star championship shooter. or like a freaking marine, i don't know.

Also, the shape of the handles are such that it makes it difficult to place the index and middle fingers on both bumper and trigger buttons at the same time. Sometimes you want to do that, but if you do with this then it leaves your ring finger hanging in midair in kind of an awkward way and you don't have a strong grip on the controller anymore.

So that's why it doesn't get 5 stars. 4 stars for being a cheap workable controller. I am keeping mine. I'll accept its flaws. It seems more real that way.

title: Recommended
text:
I grew up using a standard mouse and mouse pad for my daily computer needs. At a certain point, the standard mouse becomes a pain in the rear end. If you are working in a cluttered area, your hand may bump something on the side of the mouse pad or run out of space. With a wired mouse, you need to be close to the computer and that wire is a pain.

With the M570, that is no longer the case. You no longer need to use a mouse pad. You no longer need to be within the cords reach of a computer. I use one of these on both my laptop and desktop. I can sit on my couch and play on the computer (using my television as a monitor) at the same time without any hassle.

Pros:
- Excellent Performance - This trackball performs all the same features as a regular mouse. There is no lag due to being wireless. Once someone is to use to the thumb control, the movements are precise.
- Easy Installation - There is a connector piece that plugs into the computer. The system then recognizes and installs the required drivers and you are off and running.
- No cord hassle - There are no cords to limit where you can use this. You can literally place the trackball in a cabinet when you are not using it.
- Requires very little space to use - Since the mouse never actually moves, you require no space to really use this. This is perfect for things like being in a car or incase you do not like the standard pad on a laptop.

Cons:
- Frustrating when first learning - After using a standard mouse for so long, its hard to break habits of wanting to move the hand instead of the thumb. This is the worst part about the product. Using this involves a way of doing things that are bodies have been trained to do something different.

Do you like mics that pick up actual audio? Do you like headsets that let you listen to things on your computer? I hope not.
if it was possible I'd probably post a video with feedback about this ... Magical little piece of equipment, but seeing as the new laptop I got has everything but proper audio quality (hence I bought a new headset in the first place) I can't. I bought this thinking the people with bad experiences seemed to be significantly less then those with positive ones, but I can say with certainty that it was the biggest waste of 12 dollars I've ever spent.
As soon as I got these I tested them out by watching a video on my computer, the first thing i realize is that they make the audio sound like well.. It sounds like you are trying to watch a video with a person talking to you in a robot voice through a waterfall. It's really bad. and the only way to make the audio semi-normal is to have them half plugged in, they don't stay that way, and even if they did, the term "semi normal" is being polite, because then it just sounds like the person in the video is whispering to you from across a football field.
The microphone just.. it's not good, It works, barely, but it's not much of a step up, it makes everything weirdly high pitched, and distant sounding, and again, it's just really kind of bad. I was trying to game wearing these and, it just did some really weird things, like plugging them in cut out the audio in the game sometimes..
I honestly just wanted something I could use to record audio if I needed it, or had a mic around if I wanted to skype someone or whatever. This doesn't accomplish either of those goals. Maybe it's just that some of the sets are better then others or something, but I should have been more careful and maybe next time will consider spending more for something better. Before you buy this, read all the reviews carefully and note that you are taking a risk with this one.

title: Great headset but don't really have much to compare against.
text:
After 5 months I'm ready to review this. Keeping in mind this is the only "gaming" headset I own, the only thing I have to compare it to is my Seinheisser momentum 2.0's and a couple of other cheaper headsets. It really is great for what I need it for which is mostly hand free headset.

Being honest I found half the features of the headset useless as I already had a logitech keyboard with set G keys so I never really need to use the ones on the headset. The connectivity is very inconsistent and sometimes even crashes. 2 months in the battery life went from lasting around 13 hours on a full charge to around 7-8 hours fully charged. Battery life isnt too much of an issue yet still because of the long cable that came with it that lets you charge and play, still kinda defeats the wireless part but lets you use it while charging.

It is inconsistent with how it stays connected with the dongle. Sometimes while I play right next to my computer it will randomly crash and restart. Sometimes when I go to another room right next door it will flat our stop working (around 6 feet away from dongle) even though the wall is thin.

It is however comfortable which is one of its best features. The cushions feel soft. However those with a bigger head might feel more pressure.

Mic quality isn't anything special. It is better than the cheaper headsets but does not beat the quality of my snowball Ice.

Customizing audio profiles per game is a huge plus. 7.1 is great but also sometimes falls flat in games where you can turn. If you rely on it too much sometimes it will mess you up because of driver issues or problems with the game.

RGB is kinda whatever. It does have lots of colors and a breathing effect if that is what you're into.

Overall I would recommend this headset to anyone looking for a decent gaming headset. However I recommend you do more research.
