title: One of a family of decent media / TV / troubleshooting keyboards.
text:
How much you will like this keyboard depends on what you're using it for. For "real" keyboard use, I find it hard to use anything but mechanical keyswitches, with the Cherry brown switches being my favorite. The K410 would never replace a mechanical keyboard, but as an occasional keyboard for TV/media center computers it is great. It's very convenient to have the keyboard and touchpad in a single lightweight unit.

Generally I'm using it for setup or troubleshooting duties on the TV computers, so I prefer the layout of the K410/K400r to the compacted arrow keys of the K400 Plus. All of them have the media and other shortcuts as the primary functions of the top row of keys, with the traditional F1-F12 keys accessed with the FN key. I wish that were reversed. When I'm trying to get into the BIOS of a PC I'd prefer to just hit F2 or F8 or whatever, instead of having to do FN-F2 to get there. Again, it depends on what you want. I'm sure most people like it the way it is.

Owning all of the K400 family, here are the differences I see:

K400r Black: My favorite. The FN key legends are in a fairly bright teal blue. Matte finished. Full size arrow keys. White base.

K400r White: Identical to the black model, but FN legends are in a gray/blue that's impossible to tell from the main legends in low light. Gray base.

K410: Black: matte black base, gloss black top. Fingerprint magnet. FN legends are light gray, better than the white model, but not as good as the blue legends on the black K400r. Otherwise identical. All three include a 1.75" USB port extender that can be handy on some computers.

K400 Plus: A different keyboard. Compressed arrow keys, full size right shift key. Dedicated Volume Up / Down & Mute buttons. Missing the dedicated Music, Home, Lock and Power buttons from the K400r/K410. Smaller touchpad buttons. Left mouse button larger and yellow. F-key functions are different, F1-F12 still require the FN key. FN legends are in 3rd place for legibility, only ahead of the K400r white. No USB port extender.

All of them have storage space for the Unifying receiver. All of them use 2 AA batteries. All have a power switch on the keyboard.

Besides TV / media center computer duty, they are also handy for working on various computers that I need to troubleshoot from time to time. Again, it's very handy to have both "mouse" and keyboard in a single, portable package.

I would also suggest looking at the Microsoft Wireless All-in-One Media Keyboard, Part #: N9Z-00001 [[ASIN:B00IICMUWS Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard (N9Z-00001)]]
It's a similar design, with a larger touchpad.

title: Too Heavy, Bulky, and Difficult to Remove iPad from Case, Fast Backlighting Timeout
text: I used the Apple keyboard for about a year before buying Logitech's Create keyboard.  The Apple keyboard was excellent and its only weakness was the lack of backlighting.  When used on flights, especially late at night when it's rude to turn on overhead lights, Apple's lack of backlighting made typing difficult.  Unfortunately Logitech's keyboard, while very good at typing, makes the iPad more bulky than a MacBook Air and comes close to a 13" MB Pro.  The ballistic nylon material used for the outside cover is awkward and doesn't match the sophisticated fit and finish of an iPad.  Also, the backlighting times out far to quickly and isn't configurable.  Worse yet, using the iPad in reading mode is cumbersome and removing the device from the case requires lots of patience.  I read about screens getting damaged from this case but after a few weeks of business travel, I didn't notice any problems with my iPad.  Ultimately I returned my Logitech Create and switched back to the Apple keyboard.  This product gets 1-star for poor fit and finish, rough materials, difficult insertion and removal of iPad, ridiculously fast backlighting timeout, and a bulky and heavy design that turns the iPad into something the size of a 2010 Dell Latitude.

This one continues to have problems regularly. It frequently (more than once per week) becomes unpaired from the receiver and I have to re-pair the headset to the receiver. Also, the power switch on it doesn't function as one would expect a switch to function. Sometimes off is on, and on is off. Sometimes both the on and off positions are on. On top of that it is now starting to have charging problems like the first G933 I had. If you want a comfortable, albeit slightly heavy, wireless headset that will last a month or so before having a wide array of problems go ahead and get the G933. Otherwise just get the Logitech G930. I had a G930 before this and it lasted much longer, and I only sought to replace it because the plastic cracked in a few places yet there were no actual functional problems with it. The G930 is lighter so it's easier on the neck. The earpads aren't quite as comfortable of a material, but overall it's a superior product for a better price given the problems the G933 has.

title: Broken, buggy, and unsupported
text:
Absolute rubbish quality.

Before I go full rant, here are the good qualities:
Sound quality is on par with most wireless headsets I've owned, although not the best surround sound.
The auto-mute feature of the mic is really nice, as is the light indicator
The Gkeys are nice, although only really practical for use as media keys
Battery life is pretty good

Now for the bad. I've had nothing but problems with this product since I bought it. First I found out there is a well know, well documented and unfixed bug with the battery indicator. Basically if you have it enabled the low battery beeps will occur at a fixed interval (ie every hour) regardless of the true battery state, making it a completely useless feature. If you research it this problem has been a day 1 bug for most people experiencing it, yet Logitech has done nothing. This was a minor inconvenience, but something really shocking to see going unfixed for this long after coming to expect good quality and support from Logitech with all their other products.

And then things got worse... More recently the battery has had a shortened battery life, which exacerbates the first problem I had because I can no longer predict when my headset might fail, forcing me to keep it on charge unless I need it to be wireless. Worse yet the headset has become prone to weird freezing and glitching where it won't turn on unless I try numerous times. this is especially common after the headset dies from low battery. It somehow ends up with light showing it's on but no sound comes out. A quick reset removes this problem, but is quite annoying to deal with. Most recently my headset has added in a new "feature" where the audio will randomly introduce a loud buzzing noise independent of the volume control that is almost impossible to get rid of. Unplugging the headset seems to change the tone, but the only way to completely get rid of it is to turn it off and leave it off for a while, reset the headset and the transmitter both, a lengthy and obnoxious process to have to do at least once ever week or two.

I love my G700 mouse and have never had a bad product from them before, but this has made me decide I'm never buying another headset from them. This is a strong Do not buy.

title: Great Headset once the shut-off is fixed (Instructions within)
text:
I am giving a 4/5 because these headphones are a great deal, as long as you know how to fix them. That's what I'm going to explain here. As far as quality and all that stuff, they are wonderful Clarity is great on both speakers and microphone, but there is one enormous problem...they literally turn off exactly every 15 minutes.

The reason for this is that they are explicitly set to do so in the configuration. They also provide no way to change this configuration easily. Here is how you fix these and make them great:
1) Download a good xml editor, I personally used notepad++ which is free and heavily used in the software industry.
2) Turn off the Logitech Gaming Software (right-click the windows tray icon and hit "Exit")
3) Navigate to your config directory, likely: C:\Program Files\Logitech Gaming Software\Resources\G930\Manifest
4) Move, don't copy, that file to another location for now (like the Desktop)
5) Open Device_Manifest.xml with your xml editor (right-click and "Edit with Notepad++")
6) Find where it says <battery turnOffInterval="900"
--Change that to be <battery turnOffInterval="36000"
--This changes the turn off time to 10 hours instead of 15 mins
7) Save the file, close it, and move it back into the folder it came from: C:\Program Files\Logitech Gaming Software\Resources\G930\Manifest
8) Restart the Logitech Gaming Software

That SHOULD fix it. Make sure you closed the software before messing with the file. Now you have great headphones that don't constantly turn off.

My only other annoyance is that for many games/programs, i need to keep switching my default audio device to speakers or headphones to get it to play where i want, which is tedious. Especially when i need to restart the program/game for it to take effect, but I think thats a product of having USB audio headphones and 3.5mm speakers.

title: Good but not great
text:
The Logitech K830 accomplishes what it aims to do, bring keyboard and mouse control to the couch in a single device. However having used other Logitech devices I have to say I was a little disappointed by the fit and finish of this particular keyboard. I was hoping the K830 would be just like the K810 with a trackpad, unfortunately this is not the case. The K830 connects via bluetooth or 2.4ghz via Logitech's proprietary Unifying USB receiver. I use bluetooth, but if you don't have bluetooth, you can use the usb dongle. I don't use this for gaming so I can't speak to it's performance for that. I use the [[ASIN:B0041RR0TW Logitech Gamepad F710]] for casual gaming.

I'll review the keyboard and touchpad separately.

The Keyboard:
Previously I was using the [[ASIN:B0099SMFVQ Logitech K810 Bluetooth Illuminated Wireless Keyboard for PCs, Tablets, Smartphones - Black]] and [[ASIN:B00DR8LA6U Logitech Ultrathin Touch Mouse T630 for Windows]] in the living room which using a regular mouse in the living room is not ideal. However, the build quality of these two devices is top notch, they absolutely changed my opinion of Logitech. The K810 as a keyboard is far superior to the keyboard of the K830. The backlight of the K810 responds to touch and proximity, as in, if you just get close to the keyboard it lights up. This product, the K830, however, does not. You must touch the touchpad or press a key to light up the backlight which essentially makes the backlight worthless as you have to click the mouse or random keys just to see critical buttons like pause/play, volume, mute. Also the K830 doesn't remember it's backlight level and reverts to the lowest setting every time you activate the backlight. Which is one reason I returned my first K830, as the backlight at it's lowest level caused the keyboard to emit inverter/coil whine that was positively unbearable. The second K830 produces a slight whine but it's not obtrusive. As for the quality of the light, it is nice, white and even. The light only illuminates the printed letter of each key. It does NOT illuminate around the edges of the keys like most backlights. Also, the Function Keys only illuminate their "alternate" function (pause, play, next) not the F1-12 so if you need to see F1-12 in the dark, you're out of luck. Also the Fn key doesn't light up so even if you memorize which F key is which you'll be hunting for the Fn key in the dark. And just to rub salt in the wound, the spacebar doesn't light up, once again due to the fact the light is only emitted through the printed letters on the key caps and not the perimeter of each key.

The keyboard of the K830, for typing purposes, is decent, however once again the K810 is far superior. The keys of the K830 are chicklet style, but the key caps are completely flat, and the spacing between the keys is quite narrow. This leads to a situation in which you absolutely cannot use the keyboard by feel. This is made worse by the fact that the backlight, as mentioned above, doesn't illuminate around the edges of each key. So what you have is a keyboard you can't see or feel in the dark. The K810 on the other hand is an island style keyboard with indented key caps and slightly more space between keys which lends to the all around better keyboard experience.

Fit and finish of the K830 is good compared to your average $10 usb keyboard from walmart. Compared to other premium products though it lags behind. It's almost as if two totally separate design departments at Logitech designed the K830 and K810 because the K810 is once again far superior. The K830 is nice, smooth plastic without any large seams, gaps or visible screws. It is of moderate thickness, thicker than I was expecting but overall it's not bad. The K810 again destroys the K830 in build quality and finish. It is made of aluminum, feels much more solid, and is considerably thinner.

The touchpad:
The design of the touchpad of the K830 is somewhat of a mystery. The touchpad of the older [[ASIN:B01F5U5OZ0 Logitech Wireless All-In-One Keyboard TK820 with Built-In Touchpad (Certified Refurbished)]] is much, much larger and doesn't have separate clunky mouse buttons. Compared to most new laptops the touchpad of the K830 is average in size and feel. It is responsive enough, however I find myself often wishing it was larger seeing as there is so much wasted space below the touchpad for mouse buttons and blank space. Compared to using the T630 ultra thin mouse on the couch it is generally a better experience. It lacks some of the gesture support of the T630 but that's ok, the gestures are mostly important for web browsing which I don't do too much of on the couch. The mouse buttons of the K830 are, a mystery as to why they're included, nonetheless they're there. They cheap feeling, wobbly plastic, clicky buttons. They could have been omitted for a larger clicky touchpad like the TK820.

Battery life:
I haven't really had to recharge it more than once in a couple weeks of sporadic use. I believe bluetooth uses slightly less power, but this will mostly vary according to use. The one, and really only one, area this keyboard improves over its predecessor (the TK820) is the battery. Gone are the days of hunting for AA and AAA batteries and tossing them in the trash when they're spent after just a few weeks of use. The K830 (like the K810 and T630) uses an internal rechargeable Li-Ion battery that is easily recharged using a standard micro-USB charger you probably already have lying around for your phone. I honestly don't know why any wireless devices still use AA and AAA batteries anymore when lithium batteries are so light, compact and ubiquitous.

Overall:
If you've never used a mouse and keyboard in the living room you'll probably be pleased. If you've experienced some of Logitech's superior products you'll be underwhelmed. The K830 gets the job done, but with lower quality fit and finish, and some odd design choices compared to other Logitech products. It won't disappoint but it won't leave you speechless either.

title: Versatile, good sound, easy switching, sturdy
text:
Update (4/29/16): I've been using this for months now in a call center setting. It has held up perfectly. I spend about 8 hours a day with this on my head during the week. I toss it on my desktop tower under my desk when heading out. There are no signs of cracks or stress damage. It still holds a charge that lasts for most of the day. title: Best Bluetooth Mouse?
text:
The successor to the MX Performance, so is it any better?
I bought the MX Performance mouse when it first came out because of the "Dark Field" technology being able to track on pretty much any surfaces and no doubt it was a great mouse but I hated the fact that I had to waste one port to a dongle.

When Logitech came out with this MX Master mouse and mentioned that it has Bluetooth, I knew I had to get it, so I got one.
Ergonomically, it's ok, I don't usually believe in that sort of hype, as everyone has different hand shapes and sizes.

My main computer is a Macbook Pro Retina 2012 and everything was working fine when I had Mountain Lion as my OS until I updated it to Mavericks and that's when I started having trouble with the Bluetooth cutting out every 10 minuets or so. This happened throughout the updates from Mavericks until El Capitan and I'm kind of reluctant to update to Sierra for now. If someone has found some sort of fix, do let me know.

I know it's not the mouse issue, but more so a Mac issue because I've tested it on my windows computer and it works flawlessly.

Things that I like:
- Bluetooth when it works
- Being able to switch to dongle
- Side scroll
- Customization of the buttons
- Thumb rest button
- More refined ratchet scroll wheel
- A little more ergonomic than the MX Performance (your comfort may vary)

What I don't like:
- Short battery life
- In-built battery
- Back and forward button are awkward thin strips on top of each other.

If you don't need Bluetooth and can spare a USB port, I'd say the MX Performance is the better buy for the money, otherwise if you really need the Bluetooth, then this is probably one of the best Bluetooth mouse out there.

Other perplexities include a wrist rest at the base that immediately and noticeably gets covered in my hand oils. I hate that greasy look it constantly has, though that might be more of a byproduct of the black color than anything else. Worse, they decided to put two tiny cracks above the wrist rest that are beacons for dust and debris to collect in. I have no idea why they wouldn't have made the wrist rest flush with the keyboard.

Don't get any ideas about cleaning this keyboard. After owning this for only two days, I was trying to get a piece of dirt out from between two keys and accidentally popped off my 'K' key. I discovered that the keys are attached with very cheap and flimsy plastic, which broke. Logitech states that the keys are designed to be non-replaceable and does not sell replacements. I was able to find a replacement key on that popular online flea market and was fortunately able to reattach it. But you might not be as lucky. Avoid this keyboard if you're going for a clean look.

title: Great for typing, terrible for gaming
text:
[[ASIN:B001F51G16 Logitech Illuminated Keyboard K740]]
This keyboard's design is nearly perfect in my opinion. It is ergonomic, sleek, and stylish. Over the years it also proved to be reasonably durable. While its software may require windows it is basically a plug & play device (which made it perfect for Linux, my preferred OS). I loved this keyboard so much that I have purchased three of them in the last ten years or so (one for home, one for office, one for my husband). My home keyboard finally broke after many years of use so I thought I'd replace it with the same model (which I purchased on 03/17/2016) since it served me so well in the past. So why do I hate it now?

While I am a software developer by trade and typing comfort is paramount, I still enjoy gaming in my free time. The most recent model I purchased does not permit the common W + SHIFT + SPACE combination anymore which is a tremendous inconvenience when playing games. Gaming keyboards are typically gaudy and not very ergonomic and since I never had this problem in the past I figured I could safely purchase this again for work and play. However, I would have realized that this is a pervasive problem/complaint if I had researched this keyboard a little more. Logitech even responded to others who have experienced this problem on their own forums to basically say "This is an office keyboard, you should have purchased a gaming keyboard instead."

I don't think it's foolish to expect that a keyboard which costs $65 would be able to perform such a common simultaneous key stroke (especially since my older models didn't have this limitation). Furthermore, keyboards which cost 1/3 as much with similar form factor typically do not share this design limitation. I sadly cannot recommend this keyboard any longer; as much as I love everything else about this keyboard this built in limitation is a deal breaker for me and I will be replacing it with something else.

title: Logitech Illuminated Keyboard K740
text: A straightforward, elegantly-designed, rectangular and wired keyboard with backlit keys so you can see what the computer buttons are that you want to depress when you're typing in a darkened room. I decided I wanted a wired keyboard -- since wireless keyboards are more fragile in comparison, and, wireless keyboards that have backlit keys will drain their rechargeable or removable batteries much too quickly.  Thus, I settled for a wired one that's, "low maintenance."  And if you're looking for a keyboard with multiple colors and wild housing designs to appeal to the eyes and minds of gamers from ages 10 to 17, this isn't the keyboard for you.  All the alphanumerics are backlit with white L.E.D.s. -- looks more professional, more elegant (and in my opinion, it's more appealing to practical-minded adults) to keep the color scheme limited and consistent for its backlit design. The alphanumerics themselves are laser-etched for a precision appearance. All the keys have a shallow depth and a responsive, light touch with a near-muted, click-tactile feedback for ergonomic finger strikes; they're part and parcel to its overall low profile. Like a lot of electrically-powered backlit keyboards -- don't get it wet -- otherwise, keys simply won't respond for shorting it out. (If this keyboard was waterproof I would have rated it with the full five stars). Function keys on the top row are either software-programmable, or they have preset functions enabled via the same software.  Even if you didn't use the keyboard's software that comes with it, Windows recognizes it as a standard keyboard device anyway, and it starts working as soon as you plug it into any viable USB port. A nice, clean, fast feature are its manual adjustments for key brightness and sound volume, and these four keys are located in one row in the upper right corner. After I wore out the first keyboard after using it for several years (I shorted out the backlighting of a few keys for accidentally spilling drinks on it over the years), I decided that this keyboard was good enough for me to purchase this exact same model, again ...and I did just that.

title: Pretty, Fluid, and practical
text:
This is the holy trinity of keyboards, in my opinion.
Honestly, when I opened this baby up I was going from a scratched up dollar store keyboard to this beast.
It's kind of like going from your 1999 Camry to a Tesla V35.

Now enough of the analogies and praise, here's how it breaks down.

This keyboard has some wicked aesthetic with the rest of the things in my little computer corner, it has a black and white color scheme. Seriously, there's no reason for you to not have this guy maxed out on the backlit keys. It's got a hint of orange for the array of f1-f12 keys and an orange FN button. There's s slick thin black bar running across the bottom of the board above where the bottom of your palms rest on the board. This bar is for the Caps lock-num lock keys, and it just looks fantastic.

What's even better, the black matte finish DOESNT collect an absurd amount of dust over night, or while you're not using it.
The key strokes are fast, really fast. If you're one of those mechanical keyboard nerds who love to get off to the clickety clack of your slower keyboard, then this board isn't for you.

Overall:
This board rocks, in every way I could imagine, the colors mesh, the keystrokes are responsive and it just works.
His thing is a sex machine and I love it.

title: Great keyboard, but QC is gradually deminishing
text:
Opinions:
I've been using the K740 keyboard since it first premiered several years ago. I like everything about it. It has a positive feel to the keys and still remaining quietly unobtrusive.

Pros:
The keys layout is perfect for productivity.
The additional (orange) function keys work well with multimedia and productivity.
The oversized Delete key should be the de-facto standard for all productivity keyboards.
There are 3 levels of illumination.

Cons:
I use the K740 all day long on all of my productivity PC's. They wear out sooner than they should... especially the Shift, Ctrl, Back, Del, C, and Z keys.
Not all keys are set perfectly... some may wobble more than others.
For the price of the keyboard, the key retainers should have more durability (see image).
Backlighting dims after a couple years.

Conclusion:
I've purchased several K740's in the last few years. Since I consider them the best productivity keyboard made, I'll continue to buy them until a better model takes its place. I just wish Logitech would up their Quality Control standards.

title: Beware: The quality of this keyboard is NOT what it used to be.
text:
I love what the K740 used to be, and recommended it to everyone because it was solid and well built, nice features, sleek, etc. However, I just replaced my 4-ish year old K740, and it's obvious the build quality was reduced.

My experience with this K740, as directly compared to my old K740 (which received constant use for 4 years):

- The keys feel loose and wiggly on the new one.
- The keys feel less responsive on the new one, i.e. you have to press them harder.
- The keys make a lot more noise and sound clunky on the new one.
- Several keys (the left control key in particular) stick slightly as you press, so if you don't hit it right, the press doesn't register.
- The plastic of the keys themselves feels thinner and lower quality on the new one.
- The new one *is* cleaner than my old one, so I guess there's that.

I even gave the new one the benefit of the doubt and have been using it for a couple of weeks before writing this review, just to see if it needed to "break in." I'm quite disappointed. Sure, it isn't a super expensive keyboard, but it is at a higher price point than the cheap end of keyboards and I expected reasonable quality. I'll have to reassess whether Logitech is still my keyboard and mouse company of choice.

If it weren't for some of the pads being worn out on my 4 year old k740, I'd return this junk and keep using the old one. That says something.

title: Durability review from a 2010 buyer
text:
Not sure if this review applies for the latest model but I bought this keyboard back in 2010 for $40. This review serves as a durability test. Every key stills works perfectly fine, no ghosting, and three stages of illumination work for every key. Works perfectly for gaming, typing, and everyday usage. Keyboard rests wore out a while ago but there is a smooth finish underneath the rubber when it wears out. Feels even better than the rubber rests it originally came with. Others have said that the keys are flimsy but in my experience, no keys have ever popped out even when using toothpicks and tissue to take out dust between keys. The lazer etched keys prevent the key labels from wearing out and are exactly the same since day one.

Also accidentally spilled cup noodles and water numerous times until it was dripping from the keys but the keyboard is still going strong. No issues encountered since day one even with rigorous use of 8+ hours a day. So in conclusion, the keyboard still works perfectly fine with no problems at all. Hopefully it lasts another decade!

title: Pretty good gaming mouse
text:
This mouse replaced my aging Logitech MX510 (red) for my secondary gaming PC. Having explored much of Logitech's gaming line-up, this mouse is most similar to the Logitech G500 I once owned. It checks all the boxes: removeable/configurable weights, on-the-fly DPI adjustment, 3 thumb G-buttons, and 2 index finger G-buttons, and killer looks. Unlike the G500 though, the G502 has a "G" shaped RGB light that can be tuned via Logitech's software to match your color scheme. In the case of my secondary gaming PC, I achieved a wicked black/orange color motif and I couldn't be happier with this mouse's aesthetics. I like this mouse so much, if my G602 ever fails on my primary desktop, I'll probably replace it with a G502.

Only reason I'm knocking it 1-star is because I've started noticing strange scroller behavior. It appears randomly, but sometimes when down-scrolling, it shoots me back to the top of the window. This also occurs in Photoshop when I use the scroll to zoom, it suddenly scrolls 1000% in the opposite direction and zooms me way out. I may have a defective unit, but the scroll hasn't bothered me to the point of replacing it.

title: Overall good for the price.
text:
I replaced a more expensive g700s with this one and was fairly OK with the transition. the g700s is a better mouse in many ways, but it became "My favorite wired wireless mouse" which eventually got old. Mostly because I couldn't find a soft braided wire.

The g502 is a fairly good replacement, over all. Unfortunately it is a very light and flimsy feeling mouse, even with all of the weights added. The aesthetic is fairly whatever for me, but there was one design flaw that really bothered me. There is a raised pattern on the bottom and right side of the mouse that has a mildly sharp corner. This just happened to be exactly where my pinky naturally rested. Within a day I was going crazy with this little pointy spot and had to grab an exact-o knife and carve this area flat. Once I did this the mouse was very pleasant to hold (even if a tad light).

Overall a good mouse for the price. If the braided wire could unplug from this and into my g700s I would probably just do that, but it is what it is. If you're considering this mouse because of the price point, I think you'll be fairly pleased with what you get. It beats other mice within this price bracket, but still falls short compared to more expensive mice.

title: Logitech K740 illuminated keyboard not a bright buy outside the USA
text:
Amazon had exactly what I wanted at a fair price and shipping - a corded illuminated keyboard [[ASIN:B001F51G16 Logitech Illuminated Thin Keyboard K740]]. I was impressed with the speed of delivery to Western Australia and at first use the illuminated keyboard appeared to be just what I wanted. Then I realized the white F1 to F12 keys plus the PRINT SCRN and PAUSE BREAK white half keys were not illuminated (the orange FN part of the keys are illuminated).

Checking reviews of this keyboard I noted "Cons" comments that these keys are not illuminated (however all keys on the K800 wireless illuminated keyboard keys are illuminated). I considered it strange that only some keys would not be illuminated so to check whether the review comments were accurate I contacted Logitech Support, including photographs and they came back saying ALL keys on the K470 should be illuminated and mine was a Warranty matter. Unfortunately Logitech cannot process a replacement to Australia, they process only within the USA (place of purchase). Logitech suggested I arrange Warranty replacement via Amazon (the Retailer).

To ship the faulty keyboard back to Amazon is time consuming and difficult. I have yet to decide whether I can be bothered - or just cut my losses and buy an alternative illuminated keyboard.

I am now sorry I purchased this Logitech K740 keyboard and am disappointed that the K740 was dispatched from Logitech factory with such a basic fault - especially when older reviews show this as a problem. It has put me off Logitech products.

I caution buyers to be aware of the long winded process to return faulty product back to Amazon from places outside the USA. When the manufacturer provides a Reference number (as for me) to quote to Amazon, recognizing the product is faulty, I would like to see Amazon have an arrangement with Logitech where the product is simply replaced and the buyer trashes the faulty product. This would save time and money for all parties

title: Product is fantastic BUT arrived dented!
text:
First of all, let me say that i rate this product a 4.5 so far (half a star ding for the crappy shiny black plastic i don't like because it picks up smudges far more easily than it wipes off). I'm rating it a 3 because of the condition it arrived in- the silver back has a dent despite having a little green "QC pass" sticker right next to it! That said, the seller was very prompt in getting back to me to resolve the issue- i just didnt see his message until a month and a half later.

More details below:

Positives first: It pairs and works flawlessly with my iPad 2nd generation and my 2010 iMac (i connected it to the iMac because it is connected to my TV and i like having a bluetooth keyboard so i can sit on my couch and control the computer). I will test it with my Android smartphone later as well. The silver back material matches the silver of my iPad beautifully and feels great to the touch. All keys were tested and work well- Logitech really maximized the space to make the keys large as possible while still fitting the size constraints of an iPad. I also love that the white stand slot has a magnet in it which keeps the iPad very secure when inserted.

Neutral: I haven't had a chance to test out the battery power yet since i only got this hours ago, but can update this review once i do. I fully charged it tonight and will see how long it lasts on normal usage. The keyboard did not arrive with any kind of instructions or booklet, but luckily it's fairly intuitive. Green light above the top right of the keys blinks green when it's charging and becomes solid green when fully charged. Originally i couldn't get it to pair with my devices, but then quickly realized there are two buttons on the right side edge which you need to be aware of: 1) the power button. Switch it on (so some green color is showing). 2) a tiny little bluetooth button next to it that you need to push in order to pair your devices.Make sure your device's bluetooth is turned on, and then press the bluetooth button on the keyboard. A blue light will come on to indicate the bluetooth is on.

Negatives: As mentioned, the only thing i don't really like is the shiny black plastic. It smudges too easily and then doesn't wipe off nearly as cleanly even using special device-cleaning fluid and/or microfiber clothes. Also where the white slot is, it looks like a rubbery sticker was placed along the inside edge (I imagine to protect your iPad where it sits in the stand)...which is fine except whoever put the sticker on mine just sliggghhtly mis-aligned it enough so that the top edge has blackish lint stuck to it that i cannot get off. And the biggest negative for the seller: my keyboard arrived "new" with a dent on the silver back despite having a little green "QC pass" sticker affixed to it right near the dent! Really? Who QCed this item? For a $40 keyboard, I expect better!!

title: Fantastic mouse; great for general use and gaming. I would expect this level of quality out of a much higher priced mouse.
text:
I have had two of these mice over the last eight or so years. I cannot speak more highly of them. The precision is good, the DPI is plenty for my purposes, which include general computer use as well as gaming, and the two extra buttons seems to always come in handy. While the first one that I had did eventually start to wear out (the left click began to occasionally not register a click, maybe 1 in 50 clicks, just enough to be annoying), it took about four years of heavy use before that happened. The second one I have had since and have had zero issues with (actually, I still have the first as a backup. aside from the occasional missed click, it still works just fine).

The range on the receiver is great. I once took my laptop over to my neighbor's apartment, and could not figure out why my cursor why skipping all over until I realized I had left the mouse on my living room table, and it was getting bumped around and still registering from 50ft away, through several walls. Being able to combine multiple peripherals is also a great feature, so I can leave all but one usb port still free for other things.

Battery life is excellent. I frequently don't change the batteries for several months before it starts to warn me that they are low.

The only cons are minor. mousepad gunk tends to catch in the little recess in the bottom for the laser, necessitating blowing the gunk out every once in a while. Not a dealbreaker, but it happens. Also, a replacement dongle is like 75% the cost of the whole mouse, which just seems silly to me. If you lose it, you might as well just buy a new mouse and dongle, and keep one of the mice on a shelf for later, as you can always re-bind it to whatever dongle you want.

Long story short: Great mouse, good for everything, excellent range, good battery life. Seriously can't complain, especially for the price.

title: Harmony 700 gets rid of the RC clutter
text:
Purchased a factory re-furbished unit on a different site. The Harmony 700 is a quality product like the majority of Logitech's items.
Pros:

2) Unit is fairly easy to setup via MyHarmony website
3) Once programmed and tested, it will quickly activate your TV, DVD, Cable box and AV Receiver in the order you programmed the unit

Cons:
1) Control buttons are a little on the small size. Would have preferred them bigger
2) While programming works well for standard features like volume, channel changing, pause/play on DVD player, you will have to read the manual to understand more advanced features like switching to secondary audio track, activating sub-titles, configuring your AV Receiver audio settings, etc,. Then again you would have to do this for the original remotes anyway. I found myself still going to the original remotes for these advanced tasks.

Overall I am satisfied with my purchase of the 700 and I would recommend it to someone who wants to get rid of remote control clutter.

title: Less "wear and tear" on my wrist
text:
I bought this trackball based on SO many reviews from happy customers who were using it prior to my purchase. I've messed with these trackballs on occasion in the office supply store, but never actually purchased one.

I've now used this trackball for several hours a day for maybe the last week. I often work in places where I do not have much desk space, which is part of my personal reason for trying it out. "Mousing" around without adequate desk space is even more uncomfortable on my wrist than mousing WITH desk space. And I spend so much time using my computer, that I am now going out of my way to switch around with different types "mouse" devices, including this trackball mouse, my laptop trackpad, and even just "mousing" to the right place with my right hand ... and hitting the track pad ... with my left hand ... just to take some of repetitiveness off my my right index finger.

Overall, I like the this trackpad quite a bit. It is easier on my wrist, and requires less desk space.

I read several review comments about the track ball seeming to have some "friction" while moving it around. I experienced this. So I removed the ball from the case, and simply rubbed the ball against my hands. Maybe I got a bit of oil on the ball, or maybe I "smoothed" the ball out a bit? At any rate, this definitely made a difference, and the ball has been very smooth since then. However, at least for me, and not being accustomed to this type of a mousing device, I almost preferred the LESS smooth surface of the trackball ... to my "modified" more smooth surface. What I found is that with the ball so smooth, I have quite a tendency to "oversteer" with the mouse. I suspect that as I get more accustomed to it, everything will be fine. But, for users who have never used this type of a trackball, you might try it out, first, with MORE friction ... and if you want it to be smoother, you can easily make that modification.

title: Good system hampered by poorly designed remote
text:
I wanted to love this product for a long time but now feel I need to warn others about its shortcomings.
First, the pros: if your system is turned on with this remote, it does a nice job of managing all the components and setting them correctly. The iPhone app works okay and is really the best remote for the system. The hubs is a good device, connected by RF to the remote and then driving the components by IR blasting that seems to be able to go around anything. So there is no line of sight requirement for the remote to work, which is very nice.
Now the cons: if someone turns on the TV with the TV remote, the TiVo remote or any other remote, this device becomes worthless. It doesn't know what has been turned on and isn't ready to operate any of your components. The design of the remote presents a huge likelihood of a really annoying problem. If you look closely at the picture, you'll see that the rewind-play-fastforward "control" buttons, which you use constantly, are about 1/8" from the "launch" buttons that turn components on and off, and I'm not even sure why they turn them off - there's an Off button for that. The problem is that if you try to use the control buttons and accidentally touch the adjacent launch button, you system shuts down. If you are rewinding your TiVo and then try to hit play but hit that middle launch button, you TV and other components shut off but your TiVo continues to rewind while you fumble with the remote to get the system launched again. They need desperately to put more space, or at least a little plastic ridge, between those rows of button to give more tactile feedback that you're about to trash your viewing pleasure.
Also, while the iPhone app remote avoids this problem and is easier to use, it is a bit of a crude design with no resemblance to the look of the factory remote for the devices it's managing and requires a lot of scrolling left and right to find the screen that holds the control button you want to use. Yes, there are other Logitech Harmony remotes that are probably better to use than this one, but they cost up to $200, doubling or tripling your investment.
The hub is a very useful device but it is seriously compromised by this remote.

text: I really like Logitech products, they are great, well at least 95% of them are great products! I think this is a very good keyboard, built tough for many years of continuous typing, but with the following concerns. 1. The On-screen display to tell you the battery level does not work on some Mac's. I have a MacBook 12" Laptop (Early 2015) model and it will not display the LogiTech K750 battery indicator. I have used the keyboard on 3 of my MacBook Pro's and on my iMac (2014) Desktop Computer and it works fine. I switched the keyboard over to my MicroSoft Surface 2 Pro, then to my ASUS Laptop and had no problem with the keyboard battery display. I think it is just like all electronic products, some work on some devices, some don't. 2. The keys are a good size, perform well, but a little clicky for my taste. They make a clicking noise even when laying your fingers on them without pressing the keys. If you will remember back a couple of decades ago when we seniors were using the old IBM clicky keyboards that made a lot of noise...well this keyboard is not quite as loud, but it's certainly just as clicky. 3. I have used this keyboard for the last 3 years and it has not failed me. The battery still holds a great, long lasting charge and the solar panels do a fairly fast job of recharging it even in somewhat low light. I would recommend that when using the keyboard, that you use it under a desk light, or in a brightly lit room. This will keep the battery charged and you won't have to worry about charging it all the time. 4. Finally, I do recommend this keyboard and I would probably buy it again if I had it to do over. There are a lot of great keyboards out there these days, and this one is no exception. Logitech, keep up the great work! I am a long time fan of your products and there will be no doubt that I will buy other Logitech products in the days and years ahead.

title: Disconnects galore
text:
So with this review I want to state that I've owned this product for about two years now. In this time I have gone from loving the product to being absolutely frustrated with it. I loved it because, upon receiving it, the device worked almost flawlessly. I could walk all over my one-bedroom apartment and get no disconnects at all. Now, seated a mere foot or so from the USB dongle that sends and receives the wireless ONLY connection (even when plugged in this device is wireless only; the plug is only for charging, a major flaw if there ever was one) I get random disconnects and NUMEROUS ones at that. I've literally tried to hold a conversation over chatting services and had to pause once every thirty seconds for the device disconnecting and taking a few seconds to reconnect. What should have been about four sentences took me about five minutes to complete because of this device repeatedly cutting its signal and leaving me deaf and mute to my machine.

Let me say that I'm giving the product three stars because when it works it REALLY works well. I come in clear as a bell to anybody listening, the sound quality is great and it deafens me to most sounds around me and really helps immerse me into games, movies, and music. But when it doesn't work this device is an absolute pain.

As a note yes, I have spoken with Logitech Support, followed their numerous 'fixes' for the issue and sent in my headset, received an all new one and still have this issue after only about a month of having it around again. I don't know whether it's poor workmanship, poor luck, or just Logitech's software being garbage (they have you modify the device 'manifest' file to change the battery turn off interval value, a fix that by the by has not worked for me.)

Before you buy consider the idea of whether you NEED a wireless headset 24/7 and consider seeing if there are any others out there that allow for both wired AND wireless connectivity (I don't know if they exist but it certainly would make the disconnects far more bearable if they only happened when I'm 'mobile' around my place instead of when I'm actually seated at my desk.) If you do consider that if you've had ANY problems with wireless devices functioning improperly in your home you probably should shelve this one and just go for something wired.

title: They sound fantastic and are a great value - as long as you receive a good unit
text:
These speakers are fantastic. They sound great and the subwoofer is surprisingly powerful. The sound is clear, crisp, and strong when it needs to be. I thought the speakers seemed a bit weak given their size and weight, but they do not disappoint at all. Even the subwoofer looked small to me, but it delivers great bass.

I use these on my PS4 setup, which is hooked up to a computer monitor via an HDMI to VGA converter, which has an audio jack built in; as my monitor has no port or built-in speakers, this is where I plug the Z213 in. I note this because I cannot adjust the volume as liberally as one might on a traditional computer (which I assume most people would use these for), yet I can crank up the volume on the control pod without compromising the sound quality. It's possible that it can still perform well past the limits I am restricted to, but I've not tested that for fear of breaking something.

All of that being said, I did have an issue with the set I received initially. After about two weeks of use, sound in one of the speakers cut out intermittently (just the satellite speakers, nothing to do with the subwoofer; that was fine). It would be working, and then all of a sudden, it would stop. Several hours later, it started up again. When setting them up, I was very careful not to damage anything, so something in the wiring was likely the issue. I say this because the speaker that went out wasn't the one that had all of the main cables going into it; it was the one speaker that had one wire going into it, connecting it to the speaker that had everything going into it.

I approached Logitech directly after checking everything I possibly could myself - the state of the speakers, the connection points, visible damage, etc. They were very formal and requested information on my specific set - which I provided - and also questioned me on the basics. They asked me about checking the connections, both between the components in the set and with my device (PS4) and other related questions. After informing them that everything was correct and there was no damage, they issued a replacement, which was sent out the same week at no charge whatsoever.

Really, you have nothing to lose with this product and everything to gain. It's a great set for a small gaming setup (like mine) and absolutely perfect for a computer setup, especially if you watch a lot of movies on it. Plus, you can't beat the price for two satellite speakers and a subwoofer. If you experience problems, just spend a little time talking to Logitech customer support and they will gladly help you out. This product comes highly recommended!

title: Good all-around mouse once you scrap the hand-sensing.
text:
I've had this mouse for a long time, and I constantly had problems where the mouse would intermittently stop responding. When it worked, it was a good mouse that works on many surfaces, but the intermittent response made the mouse nearly unusable.

I was completely unaware of the "Hand Sensing" feature, which is designed to prevent accident inputs from the mouse being moved inadvertently.

Even once I was aware of the hand sensing, it was still very annoying, as the way I hold the mouse would occasionally cause the mouse to think no one is touching it. It's not a bad idea, but with a less than perfect execution, it simply becomes a hindrance. Logitech eventually released a little program (Windows only, as far as I know) to disable this feature.

My only other complaint is about the middle mouse click button, which takes a little bit to get used to. Rather than having it as part of the scroll wheel, they give you the option between a clicky and smooth scrolling wheel, forcing the middle mouse click to be its own button. I would gladly give up that choice of scrolling style to have the middle mouse click on the scroll wheel.

Overall, I'd rate 1/5 with hand-sensing enabled and 4/5 with hand-sensing disabled (1 star taken off for the middle mouse button).

title: I was never very happy with them
text:
I previously had the G930. I was never very happy with them, but having wireless was a big deal for me. This review will compare the G933 with the experience I had with the G930.

The G933 seems to have noticeably decreased range. There are places in my house where the signal no longer reaches.
The microphone repeatedly permanently mutes itself. I need to unplug and replug the USB dongle every time.
The headset goes to sleep mode and is unintuitive to wake up. I haven't really figured out when it does this.
The sound quality is worse than the G930. It sounds like an echo chamber with surround turned on, and just empty with it off. These are no good for music at all.
Battery life seems to be less than I got with a brand new G930.
Build quality is better than the G930, but it's far more bulky and less comfortable to me.
The buttons are hard to press and hard to find when it is on your head.
The volume on the headset spins too freely. It's too easy to bump and jam up the volume by accident.

Honestly, this is a terrible product, well below Logitech's standards. The G930 wasn't much better. That said, there are barely any options in the wireless headset space, so this is one of your few options.

title: Now It's a Steal. Go Get one.
text:
I've only had the camera for five days now, so this obviously will be more of an "initial impressions" review, as opposed to something more extensive; be that what it may, I'm a little confused as to the more negative comments regarding the camera, so perhaps I can offer some sort of karmic balance here: all is not lost. It came beautifully packaged, as several reviews have noted, and un-boxing it couldn't have been easier; the quality is Apple-like, and once everything was out and on my desk, I understood why there is no manual or instruction booklet included: you really don't need one, except for one reason: some people need to be able to convert symbols (words) to actions--everyone learns differently--so for those folks, here are the steps:

1. Download the apps onto your mobile device, or go to the website. (If you don't know how to find it, type, "Logi Circle" into Google, and it will be the top link on the page.)
2. Plug the camera in. Put the camera on the ring with the cable with the metal bands facing up. Put both the camera and the ring atop of the magnet. The magnet is very strong, so it's best to put it onto a place where you could easily lift it off for now.
3. Open the app. Take the camera and look underneath, and you'll see a little switch; turn it to "ON", and ouch the "SET UP" button. You should see a "GOT IT" page, and you'll automatically go to the the next page; that says, " MAKE SURE CIRCLE IS NESTLED ON ITS CHARGING RING" (We've already discussed that), then hit, "OK"; you'll be taken to the next page that says, "LET'S CONNECT", and putting your network name and password. Hit "OK", and the next page will say, "JOINING NOW." It will then connect to the cloud, where it will keep your recordings for 24 hours, or 31 days if you so wish. The first 31 days are free, so check it out. Next, put in your email and password for the account you've previously created, and hit, "OK"; afterwards, you will see a, "WELCOME TO CIRCLE" page; hit the, "GO LIVE" button, and you'll see what your camera sees.
4. The first thing that you will probably see on your mobile device will be a notification regarding a "firmware update"; this might be a little frustrating for some, but if your camera is not sufficiently charged – and it probably won't be – it will not install the firmware updates. So hit "LATER", and worry about the updates in a few hours. This goes for any changes you'll ask the camera to do when you go into settings, so don't worry about things: put the little sucker on the charger, go away for a while, and when you come back, it'll be ready.
5. Time to mess with the settings: first, fire up the app, and you'll go to the "Live" screen automatically; on the top left, you'll see a little "hamburger", or three little horizontal lines; touch it, and you'll be presented with a menu; on the right, you'll see an icon for the camera, under that, a bell, and under that, something that looks like a person; touch the camera one, and you'll be presented with, from left to right, top to bottom: Power Save, Rotate View, Firmware, Camera On, (Next Row) Speaker, Microphone, Night Vision, LED, (Bottom Row) Resolution, Add Another Camera, Remove a Camera. On the right, if you touch the bell, you'll see it ask you if you want to be notified if the camera senses movement. Try it, don't try it, it's up to you: but based on what I've read, you'll get a whole bunch of messages sent your way if you have a pet. Not my thing, but your mileage may vary. Last, touch the person icon on the bottom right, and you'll be taken to your account.
6. As far as camera settings, it's pretty easy: power save extends the life of the battery, so if you're going to remove the camera from the charging ring for more than a couple of hours, turn this on. Rotate View just means that if you're going to mount the camera upside down, use this. Firmware is just that: once you have adequate battery power, if you see a number above the little cloud, it means you need to download something. Speaker and Microphone are self-explanatory. Night vision is too (note: it works really well!) LED on/off means do you want the lights on to let people know you're recording or not. Resolution is a little trickier: 360 is low res, but takes less bandwidth; 1080 is hi-res, but takes more. You decide. The add/take camera buttons are just that. That's it in a nutshell.

For those unsure about your internet system, here's the quick and dirty: it all depends on what you have. Think of broadband like plumbing, where the bigger the pipes, the larger the volume of water it can carry. The more faucets that run off the main pipe, the bigger demand on that water volume, and as for broadband, the more devices you use, the less data available for each one. Time for a personal story: I'm a nurse, and one of my patients is a young boy whose parents wanted to monitor him via webcam; their house was fairly large, their router fairly old, and they had a 12 Mb/s package from a certain phone company; needless to say, their system couldn't handle the data load (they had two teenagers as well), and the camera went offline constantly. So remember: things like 24-hour monitoring takes a large amount of bandwidth (data), so if your system isn't up to it, it's not the camera's fault; either upgrade your system, or don't purchase the camera. In the end, the aforementioned family changed their service to one with 200 Mb/s, with a modern router and a repeater, and they're really happy. If you have adequate pipes, you will be too.

I tried to duplicate the issues people were having--mostly connecting to the camera--and when I deleted my app, re-added it, and tried to re-establish a connection, there it was: I couldn't connect to the camera. I tried several times to do it the easy way, but I couldn't. So here's what you do: Just reset the thing. It's a pain, as you'll have to reset your settings, but it's quick and effective. Don't get mad, just reset it. Three minutes, tops.

As to the issues with retrieving your stream, I haven't had that at all, so I'm going to reiterate what I said previously: it's probably an issue with your not having the broadband available to run it; I could be wrong, but I can't think of another reason. Every time I've used it, it's worked flawlessly--but I also have 240 Mb/s available to me; if you've got something rated at 25Mb/s, and have four people using it at the same time, it's probably not going to be enough.

And once you've got the setting to where you what them, you'll be thrilled: Logitech, in the year the camera has been out, has already done several upgrades (1080p, Desktop app, etc.) that make it easier to use--the company is obviously committed to making it better for some time to come. In short, it's a great little camera (and I mean little: think tennis ball), and it does everything you'd want., and the fact that it's now 25% cheaper than when it was first released (Upgrade coming soon? I don't care.), makes this a steal. Buy one.

title: Great USB Controller for Steam and Mac Games.
text:
I didn't buy this controller myself. I hope that's alright with some people to still consider my review helpful. I actually got this controller as a gift from someone so I'm not sure where they bought it. Anyway, I feel that this controller is so good that it merits a review either way.
The controller has some weight to it. It does not feel cheap like a Mad Catz controller. I like that the joysticks are across from each other like a PlayStation 3 controller. But I am not a fan of the D-Pad. They are not individual buttons, they're all attached to each other like a 360 controller. The wire is long enough to connect to the back USB ports of my PC. Since it is a USB cable, I can connect it to my Galaxy S7 Edge through and OTG adapter. Not every Android game or phone is compatible with a controller, but it is possible for this controller to work with some Android phones and games. I don't really play games on my phone but I thought I should add that in.
I use this to play mostly Steam games on Mac and Windows 10 through my dual-boot Hackintosh. For it to work on Mac, I have to change the slider on the back of the card for games to detect it. Some games like Deus Ex: Human Revolution and Bioshock from the Mac App Store only recognizes the gamepad as a 360 controller. So the button scheme for the D-Pad and the left joystick are swapped. Depending on your games you can remap the buttons individually or change the whole preset of the button layout.
First/Third Person Shooters don't feel ideal to me with a controller but they still work. For example, the Metro Redux games, Spec Ops, and Tomb Raider 2013 work with it.
I feel that I do play better with the controller in fighting games. Some newer titles that work well with the controller are the Batman: Arkham Series games, Shadow of Mordor.

title: The king of keyboards!
text:
I've been wanting a keyboard like this for awhile...my setup at home is my home desktop and my business Surface Pro, and of course I also have my phone (currently a Note series Android device). I currently use a USB Switcher which I have my wireless mouse / keyboard connected to and switch back and forth between the two devices. For typing on my phone, no luck :(

I saw a review for this approximately 2 weeks ago and have been checking daily for Amazon to actually get this in stock to try. Having a bluetooth keyboard that worked paired with three devices simultaneously seemed like a godsend. I happened to be on the BB website and realized that they already had it in stock and went down and picked up two of these (thinking if I liked it, I would take the second one to my client site and leave it there).

Well, I've had it for one night so far and yes, I do love it! The keyboard paired easily to both my phone and Surface (haven't tried my home desktop yet) via bluetooth and works exactly as expected. To switch devices, you only have to press one button and it automatically switches over...this is exactly what I was looking for.

I didn't realize this from the pics online, and as the other reviews mention, the "middle" keys are missing (home / end / delete / insert / page up / page down) so that kind of sucks, but I wanted to have the number keys as I use them daily. The keys are mapped with the function keys, so maybe I'll learn to use them that way eventually.

Using this keyboard on my Android phone is also great - you can use the arrow buttons to navigate from screen to screen (similar to a mouse), and the typing is flawless. My Note phone fits in the tablet holder even with the S-View case on.

If you need a single keyboard to rule them all, this is the one!

title: Losing sound all the time.
text:
I bought this headset a few years ago and lived in a cornfield surrounded by nothing with a house full of people who didn't use electronics. It was great! Then I moved to the suburbs and thought my headset was just malfunctioning (admittedly the dog used it as a chew toy for the five seconds I left him alone in the office) when the sound would randomly go out after a beeping noise. When I received the new headset (same make/model), the sound issue continued...

If you live in a remote area where the wireless signal won't be affected by anything, then this would be the headset for you. Unfortunately the sound cuts out randomly (sometimes five times in two minutes here) whether the headset is plugged in or not. If you need to buy this for the usb plug in as I did, spend a few extra bucks to get an adapter instead for another headset, this is not worth the aggravation of losing sound all the time. This was not an issue of losing battery charge either as the sound would come right back on after 5 seconds. I googled how to fix this issue and none of the suggestions work. The fit, sound, mic quality, and battery life are all great though.

title: I prefer the orbweaver.
text:
Comparing this to my Razer Orbweaver.

The rubber dome switches are annoying to me. The... Key "wells" (I suppose you could call them?) Are deep and since they're rubber domes, you have to push them all the way down to activate the switches. I'm used to mechanical switches where you don't have to push them all the way down.

The domes feel rather stiff and take too much pressure to depress, giving them a nasty "pop" feeling. This isn't so much an issue with three of my fingers, but my pinkie tends to have a little trouble pushing things down.

I feel that the keys have terrible placement. The lower keys are difficult to press in a natural and fluid way.

The "wasd" equivalent keys have depressions in them, meant to give you something to tell you which keys they are, but all keys are concave, so it's difficult for me to quickly and easily tell where I am.

Since I play an mmo where I'm constantly switching hot bars and dodging things, I don't have the time to check my placement. I need my keys to have low pressure and in a good position with good key caps so I know where i am and so i can keep my fingers on the movement keys for quick responses. This keypad failed these criteria.

The thumb buttons also have terrible placement, they're too close to the palm rest and are difficult to use comfortably.

The analogue stick felt terrible. I replaced it with a normal stick from an old controller I had lying around. It made it better, more comfortable and natural, however it's a normal stick with a circle gate. This made it difficult for me to tell which direction exactly I was pushing it. I had more than a few botched hotkey switches because of this.

The Orbweaver has good key placement, good feeling, low pressure switches with keycaps that don't confuse my fingers. I never have to double check my placement. The thumb switches are in a natural place, the stick clicks and is easier for me to tell which direction i'm pushing it.

I got this to replace my Orbweaver since it was starting to fall apart and the thumb button is malfunctioning a bit, but this key pad won't be my replacement.

I have no brand loyalty, so I'll use whatever feels good. If I could buy or try all of the keypads to find one that would replace my Orbweaver, I would, but I can't. I'll probably try another one in the future, but for now I'll continue using my Orbweaver.

title: 5 Stars as an MMORPG game pad.
text:
I got this as a Christmas gift (2015) and have waited about 3 months to give a solid review. Honestly I love this thing. It won't make you a great gamer, if that's what you're thinking. It has allowed me to be marginally better because I can make each button do exactly what I want it to without worrying about fat fingering that dastardly Windows button or whatever else. Personally I'm horrible about fat fingering things and still do all the time on this thing, but it is a little more forgiving. World of Warcraft is pretty much the only game I play (because it's all I have time for) and I do a lot of PvP which requires being a little quicker than I was able to be on my keyboard alone, and that's where I think this has really helped me the most.

Something you should know about the thumb stick button, I've seen some other reviewers say this too, it is better used as a directional spell hotkey as opposed to trying to use it to move. For instance, as a BM Hunter I have arcane shot bound to the up-directional button, so when I'm ready to spam it (b/c it's instant cast) I can just flick it forward over and over. Same for moonfire with my druid. As for moving, I changed that up a little too. The pad comes with a standard keybinding when you first go to use it and the ASDW buttons are where the finger indents are. I basically moved them all down one button and left the top row for casting. It is much more familiar since when I was using my normal keyboard much of my bindings were the number keys. Plus it leaves the one indented button on the top row easy to find so you kinda always know where you're at. I have made the button just to the left of the directional toggle my space bar button (for jumping) and the one below it for my mount.

One of the best things about this pad is that you can easily program each button to do whatever you want it to. So if you already have hotkeys setup on certain buttons, when setting up just use that button. This also helps in the event you aren't using the pad for whatever reason, you haven't messed up anything to do with your present keybinding layout.

FLAWS: A couple I've noticed are one, it seems like there is a slight lag when jumping (ref which button I'm using above). I'm not going to change that to a different button b/c it's in a familiar place, but you might be inclined to do so. Two, I've noticed something strange that happens from time to time. My "oh shoot" buttons are G20-22. Sometimes I accidentally hit 20 & 21 at the same time and it closes the game, which you can imagine is all kinds of frustrating. Three, the directional toggle can be pretty sensitive. Sometimes I'll flick it to the left and whatever I have bound to the down position happens. Probably my fault with the way I fat finger things, but it just isn't super forgiving that way. Btw, the toggle also has a binding for if you press it down. I'd recommend just leaving that alone.

Something else worth mentioning is that I have wrist issues and part of the reason I asked for this was to help with that, to be a little bit more ergonomical. Well, it hasn't really helped. And the buttons are definitely not the smoothest things to press, which is probably the real issue of how it hasn't helped. Sometimes it almost takes effort to push the keys, depending on the position of your hand.

Overall I think this is a great product and the display even tells you certain things. You can also change the colors to whatever you want. I have 3 lvl 100's that I PvP with and have different setups for each one. I change between them with the M1-3 buttons at the top and each one is a different color. I chose to ask for this as opposed to the Razer Tartarus that was the same price at the time mostly just because this one had more buttons to program. Plus its Logitech and I have some of their other products that I like. Despite its minor shortcomings I would recommend this. But I do think certain parts of it could be made better.

title: Excellent webcam for serious users, if you ignore the new gimmicky feature
text:
PROS:
+ Can now record 720p video at 60Fps
+ Excellent low light performance
+ Automatic Video/Light Adjustment
+ Easy to use software
+ 1080p Video Capture (30Fps)
+ 16MP Still shots
+ Good microphone audio pick-up
+ Accepts Tri-pod mounts or easily attaches to most monitors

CONS:
- Background removal doesn't work very well
- No built-in privacy cover
- No RealSense (i.e. for Windows Hello)
- Only minor improvement over C920

SUMMARY:

if you've used the C920, there is very little change moving to the C922x. Basically you get the same design and excellent still/video capture. And they've improved video capture at 720p to 60fps. Yes, there is background removal via free software download. But it really doesn't work well. I'd ignore that feature. Basically it's all software based and does a poor job of determining what should and shouldn't be in the foreground. Hair for example, darker it is, the most likely it will cut it off.

Otherwise the features that made the C920 one of the best web cams for serious users is still there. Fantastic low-light images, great detail at higher resolutions, and just a solid overall camera. I do wish it had Intel RealSense for Windows Hello. I think that'd be far more useful that software-based background removal. In either case, I still give this a webcam a 4.6 star rating and consider it highly recommended.

title: Excellent All Purpose Remote...just be sure you know how to add DELAY if you need to.
text:
This replaced an older Logitech Harmony 1100 which initially, I thought was a very advance remote for it's time, but found that it's rectangular tablet shape wasn't ideal for a remote control. Form doesn't necessarily beat function in this case. Ultimately, and with good reason, the standard stick design is the ultimate shape for a remote control. In hindsight, the Logitech Harmony 650 was probably the best remote that ever existed.

Saying that, I really like this remote for 2 reasons... 1) the stick shape design as previously mentioned, and 2) the Harmony Hub capabilities.

Until the day comes when ALL remotes are bluetooth based (which really should be the case sooner than later), the Harmony Hub does provide a similar convenience factor, where you don't need to point the remote at an IR receiver. I also appreciate the mobile app you can use for even more detailed control (like managing each device individually if needed); BUT I would've preferred to have a small LCD display on the remote, which you can get with the more expensive Elite and Ultimate One remotes. I still think I will upgrade to one of those remotes considering how excellently this basic remote works with the Harmony App and the convenient Hub capability. I will say I haven't had any issues with powering up, switching between, or shutting down activities with the basic remote; with one caveat as I will mention below...

One very important point i'd like to make. If you're used to adding delay to your activities, unlike the older software where you can insert delays in any part of an activity, it works differently in this version of the software. You add delay as a customization of the device itself. Thus the delay is built in to the device, rather than a step in the activity process. I admittedly was going to throw the remote out the window, thinking I couldn't do this anymore, until I realized it was just different. Thanks goodness, since I went from a 1 star rating to 5 star because of this.

I highly recommend this remote which provides excellent value for the cost.

title: Overwhelmingly Happy
text:
I've owned the G933s for about a month now, and I've got to say that I am incredibly happy with them. I'll give a quick pros and cons list, but there is an extended review afterwords if you'd like to read more about my experience:

Pros:
- Fantastic sound for a gaming headset, and great sound in general. Music, gaming, and everything else is just a joy.
- 7.1 channel surround sound is generally great, but the game has to support it. Some games sound better in 2 channel. Otherwise, very immersive and very helpful in games such as Battlefield or Devil Daggers.
- WIRELESS WIRELESS WIRELESS. Seriously, I fell in love with wireless after buying some JayBirds, and these don't disappoint.
- Great battery life when you turn off the LEDs on the headset.
- Software is great, for the most part. Some bugs. More in the cons.
- Option to connect your phone through a 3.5mm jack while listening to whatever is coming from your pc. In other words, talk on the phone while gaming or watching a video or whatever else you might be doing with no hassle.
- On board buttons are customizable. I set mine to Play/Pause and Next for music, while keeping one for surround sound on and off.
- Easily removable battery is a fantastic addition in the case that I ever need a new one.
- Very sturdy build.

Cons:
- Make no mistake, these cans are very big. This might put some people off. Definitely won't be taking them around with me on regular basis.
- It took me about a week to adjust to the fit of the G933s and be very comfortable, but it's been no looking back since.
- The LEDs are a great idea, but they really serve no purpose when you're sitting at home, and they drain the battery considerably faster. I just turn them off, though the do look great when they're on.
- At $200, these are rather expensive. You could go for the cheaper wired version if wireless is not that important to you, or buy a pair of dedicated audiophile cans for perhaps a less expensive alternative to getting the same or better audio quality, sans the extra gamer features.
- As mentioned in the pros, the software is great, but a little gimmicky at times. When I first attempted to install the update for the G933s, the software locked up and I had to manually abort it. I couldn't get my headset to connect again, and I had to search the internet for some troubleshooting help. At that point in time, I was quite frustrated. Alas, I resolved the issue, and it's been smooth sailing since.
- Something that doesn't happen too often, but can happen from time to time is the headset not connecting properly to your USB dongle when you turn it on. Not a big deal, just turn it off and on and you should be good, but it is a bug nonetheless.
- Finally, the on-board buttons are customizable, except for the Mute button, which is rather curious considering that the mic will auto-mute if you push it back up. Not a huge deal, but it would be nice to utilize that extra button.

Extended Review:
I was a little concerned prior to ordering these because I typically only purchase products with at least a solid 4 star rating or higher, but I decided to give it a go. After using these every day for a month, I must say that a lot of the negative reviews on this headset really did come from people who were not happy with the previous model and came here to complain. In fact, I noticed a lot of those reviews were posted prior to the release of the headset, so the intent of the reviews becomes quite obvious at that point.

Getting back to the headset, it's been a long while since I owned a really good pair of cans. I used an old pair of Turtle Beach's for gaming for years, but they finally wore out, and I wouldn't really consider those high quality anyway. I've mostly just stuck to buying ear buds that would be easy to take on the go over the past few years. I was satisfied with the sound I was getting from the ear buds, but I somehow seemed to forget how far a good pair of cans can go. It's almost as if I'm listening to a lot of my music for the first time again. The bass is deep without dominating the soundscape, the mids sound great, and the highs are very crisp.

Of course, if you invest in a pure set of audiophile cans at the same price, you're most likely going to get even better sound, but I like to game and I fell in love with wireless after purchasing a pair of JayBirds. The wireless range is fantastic; I can walk all the way across the house and still have little to no interruption with these on.

This headset has hit the perfect medium ground of great sound, wireless, and gamer oriented with an on-board mic and great software that allows you to tailor your experience to whatever soundscape you'd like to have. Nothing is perfect, but the cons I stated previously are only minor annoyances on an otherwise overall fantastic product. Highly recommended.
