title: Would be perfect except.... (Edited)
text:
I wanted to love these speakers, I really did.
I can't find any set of speakers with a similar output at this price point, and furthermore, having the bass knob adjacent to the volume knob is awesome. For once, being able to adjust the bass volume without having to crouch to the floor and reach behind the subwoofer. I live in an apartment complex, and for the few times I DO play music relatively louder, I turn down the bass, and it's nice to have that knob RIGHT THERE.
However, with both the first AND replacement unit, there was a constant high-pitched whine.
This was independent of the volume settings, whether or not any source was actually plugged into the unit, and what outlet or surge protector it was plugged into.

Side note---if your intent is such that 'if these are on, then they are playing music loudly', you might actually be okay---at moderate volumes you kind of lose the high-pitched whine in the mix. But if at anytime these are on but not playing music, and you're in a decently quiet environment, the whine will be quite audible.

It's not literally dog whistle range, but it's up there. Perhaps it is in that range that becomes inaudible as one grows older. Aside from this problem they DO seem like decent speakers.

EDIT: After receiving a refund after returning the second set, Logitech customer service service sent me a replacement set, free of charge, and this one does not suffer from the whine that plagued the previous two. Although I can't offer any comments on reliability over time at this point, this particular set seems to be working at 100% and I do like how it sounds.

title: I Just Replaced Four Remotes with ONE!
text:
There are four devices connected to my Harmony remote. They are:
- LG television
- Panasonic Blu-ray player
- LG soundbar
- Directv

All were easy to link to my Harmony remote and all are easy to control with the remote. My favorite option is "Activites." I simply pick "Watch TV" and all of the components turn on or off simultaneously. Then it's possible to choose any of the components and manage them with one remote. Even the Directv commands are easy to use. Before I moved to my new home, I had TiVos connected to each TV. I do not think I would want to use the Harmony with my TiVos because of the familiarity and ease of use of the TiVo peanut remote. text:
I am totally not a gamer, so this is from the viewpoint of an old woman with vision problems who types too fast for a lot of software. The first thing I love about this keyboard, however trivial it might seem, is that the keys light up, and the characters are large. I can see the keys I'm looking for! Yes, I touch-type my alphabet, but sometimes not so much the numbers and symbols, and now I can find them quickly and easily. The lighting effects are fun and useful - definitely download the Logitech software from their Web site. You can color-code various zones on the keyboard or just let it change colors in various ways. I turned on the Wave effect for now.

I can also create macros very easily, like for key combos that I use often but have trouble executing without looking or with one hand. I can set up the function keys for all kinds of stuff.

I have a great big gaming laptop, also for the power and the big screen, and I like to watch video on it when I'm not working. The media keys on this keyboard allow me to pause, start, stop, mute, and skip without having to use a mouse or the touchpad on the built-in keyboard on the laptop.

The wrist rest actually helps these old hands, and the spill resistance means I'll actually get to keep this for a while.

Incidentally, Captain Carrot the ginger cat hates it when I put the big laptop in my lap, but right now I'm using it on the side while resting the keyboard on the cat, and he seems quite content: see?

title: Great sound with powerful bass but won't take sound from newer bluray players
text:
These provide a huge sound improvement for our TV, and are ideal for a computer where you want a lot of bass, such as gaming or digital sound/video. The adjustable subwoofer is the best part of this system, though the mid-range and treble are also surprisingly good. You might do better for classical music, but even there these aren't bad. For gaming or computer use, there is even a headphone jack on the right speaker making it easy to switch.

Unfortunately these don't have optical digital input, which is the only sound output most newer low and mid range bluray players have. I tried [[ASIN:B013KE5Y9Y this audio converter]] to convert the optical sound output from my new bluray player to RCA analog sound that these speakers would take, only discover converters like these converters won't handle the multi-channel sound output by bluray players. So I'm back to an older player for now until I find an affordable solution.

The right speaker has the power, volume and bass controls, so with the subwoofer under the desk (or TV stand), you have ready access to what you need. I've found I need to adjust the bass control for every movie/show as it has a huge impact and needs to be fine tuned so it isn't either overpowering or underwhelming. The quality is great too; we've had an older version of these speakers for five years and they are still going strong: the less powerful [[ASIN:B002FU5QMK Z523 speaker system]], which I'd also highly recommend.

title: A Terrific Camera For Keeping An Eye On My Dogs
text:
If you are looking for the perfect pet camera, I highly recommend the Logitech Circle Wireless Camera. I was so impressed by this camera, I bought two of them. They are basically plug and play. No muss, no fuss, no bother. I have one pointed at my dog door and pointed the other one at my dogs' favorite spot in the den. I can check in on them anytime I'm away from home to see what mischief they are up to. There are settings for different resolutions (360, 720, and 1080) one can choose depending on how clear of a picture you want to see. I have a slow internet (dsl) and use the 720 setting which still gives me a clear well-lit picture on my phone.

Each time one of my three dogs leaves the dog door, the camera records it as an event. It keeps recording for a minute or so and sometimes captures them coming back into the house in the same clip. These clips are time-stamped and can be viewed anytime I log into the app during the day. The app also features a day brief button where you can view the entire day in one viewing in fast-forward speed. It's a great way to tell what your dogs have been up to all day. I couldn't be happier with these little gems! They offer me peace of mind that my pets are doing well while I'm away.

title: The last remote you will need. Wish I could give 6
text:
Man, I haven't written a review in a while, but I love this remote and hub that much.

I've had previous Logitech harmony remotes that were OK, but this one takes the cake. It controls everything in my house - it can even do the air conditioner.

The blaster setup is ideal, and I've been able to hide all my components except the tv, speakers, and turntable. The app works great, and is a big improvement over the Logitech software required for their other remotes. I had everything set up in minutes through the app, where the old software took a lot of tweaking and adjusting. The punch through stuff is so smart it automatically knows what to do for all devices. It's currently running two TVs, a PS3, a PS4, a stereo receiver, two Amazon fire sticks, the A/C, and probably something else I'm forgetting. The only thing it can't do is flip a record to the other side or turn on the PS4 (that's something that Sony locks out, and is not really a big deal because the controller does it and my other devices make everything on the PS4 but gaming redundant).

I got a second blaster and a few mono 2mm male to female extender cables available here on Amazon, and was able to control everything in the bedroom, too, so now it's the only remote in the house. And even then, the phone can work the hub too, so I technically don't even need the remote.

The remote proper is great. Simple, sleek, and lightweight. No more explaining to visitors or houseguests how to use it. You just press one button and everything's good to go. Tweaking the extra commands is extremely simple. The battery is said to last a year, and you can get a five pack of replacements on Amazon for like 2 or 3 dollars. So, I never have to change or charge the batteries or use a bulky port. It can reach the hub from practically anywhere in the house, so I'm having to teach myself not to bother pointing a remote anymore.

Very happy with this purchase. Worth every penny.

title: Almost perfect, but not quite. Two issues subtracted one star.
text:
First, the reason I docked one star. This is an excellent mouse in nearly every way except one major annoyance. They shrank the forward and back thumb buttons (which I use heavily) and stacked them above one another, rather than being located forward and back. They did this to make room for the left-right scroll thumb wheel. BAD move. I can't tell you how many times I've clicked forward when I meant to click back and vice versa. A -much- better placement would have been to make the thumb wheel slightly narrower, then put the forward and back keys on either side of the thumb wheel. The button in front of the thumb wheel would be forward. The button behind would be back. That's the bad. Now, the good.

The new scroll wheel has an automatic clutch which scrolls differently depending on how fast you move the wheel. If you roll it quickly, the resistance of the wheel is turned off and the wheel just keeps spinning and quickly scrolls through long documents. If you roll the wheel slowly, the resistance remains engaged and you get precise control while slowly scrolling. I didn't think I would like this feature, but it is intuitive and addictive. Now, I can't imagine not having that feature.

The mouse is also rechargeable now. You plug it into a powered USB port and it charges. I had the previous model of this mouse and it wasn't rechargeable. I used rechargeable batteries in it, but because they start out at a lower voltage than standard AA batteries, I had to swap them out for a fully charged set every few days. This mouse has a real rechargeable battery pack at the proper voltage, so this mouse lasts much longer between charges. I haven't tracked it specifically, but I'd estimate I charge every 12 days or so. That's about 4 times as long as my previous mouse lasted on a charge. Plus, you can keep using the mouse while it is charging (although reverting to a mouse on a cord hurts.)

Lastly, I actually do like the new left-right scrolling side wheel. My gripes are that it is too wide and messes up the forward back buttons. Also, when I move the mouse forward and it hits something on my desk, it presses one of the mouse buttons. The reason is that the left and right mouse buttons actually extend past the front end of the mouse slightly. Having accidental clicks from bumping into my keyboard or water bottle can be annoying or even dangerous, especially when you are running stock market client software doing live trading.

I hope the next version of this mouse addresses the forward/back button issue and the buttons which wrap over the front of the mouse. Both are poor designs in actual use, but I still keep using the mouse for the other improved features, which outweigh the problems.

title: but I hate using the wheel as a button

title: I really hate this remote.
text:
I upgraded to this from a Harmony One, which I loved but was just starting to feel kind of old. I read a lot of reviews and complaints about this model's button layout. I figured people were just exagerating, how hard can it be to learn a new layout and get used to the play-pause controls being at the top of the remote instead of the middle. You have to hold the remote by the top to use the commands, but thats not the big problem for me. Instead its the brain dead designers that put the power button millimeters above the similarly shaped rewind button. The number of times I've accidently shut my whole system off while trying to quickly rewind something... extremely frustrating.

Another issue with holding the remote at the top to use the play-pause controls is that your thumb or hand will often press the touch screen. This is a design flaw they tried to solve by putting a lock on the touch screen. When the touch screen activates you have to slide the lock screen over to use the touch buttons. This got old real fast, it adds an annoying extra step to trying to use your fancy (supposedly) convienent universal remote. Disabling the lock screen, however, means that my remote's touch screen is constantly ending up on the numeric or favorites page for some reason. Two pages I never use and wish I could just turn off or hide, but cant.

And finally, the biggest problem with this remote. The battery. The Harmony One's battery lasted forever and when it was running low, the remote would smartly remind you to recharge it. This new Harmony lasts a few days if youre lucky, and has no charging reminder. So I'll use it for two days the battery indicator around 70%, then the next days its completely dead and wont even turn on. So you cant use your remote until its gotten enough charge to function. If you remember to ALWAYS put the remote on the charger when youre not using it, this wont be an issue. But for me its a constant and frustrating problem with an overall poorly designed and bad upgrade of a once excellent universal remote.

title: Nice option for lengthy text editing on iPad. Multi-device is nice, if you actually need it.
text:
This is a pretty nice Bluetooth keyboard for use with multiple devices. I've had it hooked up to an iPhone, iPad, and a Windows 10 device. While it was fun to switch around, it has mostly been dedicated to use with the iPad, where it makes some text-heavy apps quite nice. On the iPad, for example, you get all the additional real-estate of not having the on-screen keyboard showing. Typing is far less prone to mistakes than on-screen. Of course, the keys aren't awesome for day after day of typing, but it's great for those times when you need to type up a lengthy document and all you have is an iPad sitting around. You even get Cmd+Tab support to switch apps. As well, you can select text with Shift+Left/+Right, which makes editing nice.

Note: if you are ever using an iOS device and can't seem to get the on-screen keyboard to show up, make sure this isn't still connected to it. Your iPhone or iPad will prefer the hardware keyboard when it sees it as available.

Additionally, if you want to use a keyboard on a PC where you need Function keys regularly, you may want something else. Device switching takes priority over the F1, F2, and F3 buttons. That isn't a big deal in many uses, but it does mean that pressing any F-key requires the fn modifier key. If you need those keys a lot, it might be better to find a keyboard where the top row of keys defaults to those Function keys instead (which Logitech doesn't appear to offer).

title: Classic infrared remote with modern features; compatible with Harmony Hub
text:
The Harmony 950 This is a classic Harmony remote, refreshed. It's got a responsive touchscreen, haptic (vibrating) feedback for the touchscreen, and the ability to accept gestures to control your devices. Out of the box, this unit will control only infrared devices; but you can also connect it to a Harmony Hub to control devices in cabinets if you buy one separately.

Unfortunately you cannot program this remote using a tablet or smartphone, you must use the Logitech Harmony software which is available for Windows or Mac OS.

Setup is easy, I was up and running in about 10 minutes including the time needed to download and install the software. The setup program will ask you for your equipment's model numbers and then will suggest activities to match (e.g. watch TV, watch a movie, etc.) Most users will find the remote sets up almost automatically, there are customization features for power users, such as the ability to control delays between keypresses and to set up macros or custom sequences.

The remote comes with a cradle that takes up much less desk or table space than previous Harmony remotes--instead of laying flat in this cradle, the remote sits upright. I've found that the battery doesn't last very long if you don't dock it--maybe a week--so you will definitely want to keep the dock handy.

title: Best Harmony I've Owned!
text:
I have owned several Harmony models (One, 550, and 700), and while all offered slightly different features, they were all equally effective. All were infrared, of course, and while more convenient than using a handful of different remotes, they all suffered from the same issues with getting out of sync when starting or stopping activities due to missed IR commands. So when I stumbled upon a good deal on the Harmony Smart Control and reading some good reviews, I figured I'd give it a go and see for myself.

And boy am I glad I did. This is unlike any of the Harmony remotes I've owned before. After setting up your configuration, the remote works surprisingly well--almost flawlessly. Having owned it for a few weeks now, I can remember only two instances of activities getting out of sync. Resolving the issues was a breeze. And you can customize the buttons as you would expect from any Harmony remote.

First, let me explain what comes with the unit, because it wasn't entirely clear to me when ordering. The unit comes with a remote, a "hub," and an IR blaster. The IR blaster connects to the hub, and there is room for an additional IR blaster, too, if you find you need it. The remote is light, thin, and has a nice "textured" feel to the bottom of it that gives it a good feel in your hand. The remote connects to the hub via RF, so you don't need to point it in the direction of your entertainment center (a habit which I'm having difficulty breaking), and the hub sends the IR signals to your components. The hub itself sends a very strong IR signal. I was skeptical it would work with my TV since my hub isn't in a location that has a direct line-of-sight position relative to my TV, but the IR signals are strong enough that they reflect around the room and hit the TV. My entertainment center has four "quadrants," and I have the hub and one IR blaster connected--both in the top two quadrants, and they reliably send signals to all of my components (receiver, Xbox One, Xbox 360, Tivo, and Apple TV) in all four quadrants. And there is negligible lag in component response time after pressing the button on the remote. It's all quite impressive.

Also worth mentioning is the app connectivity. The app (iOS in my case) works exactly as described. It connects to the hub via wifi, and the hub again sends the appropriate IR signals the components. I personally find it more convenient to just grab the remote and press the physical buttons, but when I can't find the remote (these things happen when you share a house with a two-year-old), the app fires up quickly and is a suitable substitute for the physical remote. Some people felt the simplicity of the remote (no screen and no backlit buttons) was a drawback, but I personally like it. The remote works extremely well, and I expect excellent battery life.

Simply put, I strongly recommend this remote. There's just something to be said for a product that works so reliably. My greatest concern when purchasing this was the lag time and the ability for the IR signals to get to all the components. Those concerns were quickly lifted after using the unit myself. You can buy the hub without the remote, but I recommend getting the remote, too--just for the convenience of it. Treat yourself and pick one up today!

title: Awesome once you get it working
text: I bought this to replace an older cheaper harmony universal remote which had broken after a few years.  I love this remote it is so nice not to have to point it directly at the TV and hold it there, you just press the buttons facing the remote any which way and everything works as expected.  The only reason this is getting 4 stars instead of 5 is that it was a bit tough to set up and get working properly at first.  One of my components was not responding properly, my sound bar.  I emailed technical support and I got some instructions but they weren't very helpful.  It wasn't until I spoke to someone and they stayed on the phone with me for about an hour until we determined that the issue was that the hub had to be positioned better including an extra extension mini hub.  So this isn't something that you will always be able to just take out of the box and it works perfectly.  I'm pretty tech-savvy and even for me this was complicated.  But the tech service on the phone was very helpful and since the remote uses wi-fi they were able to make adjustments to it from their end.  The remote, itself, has a good feel to it also.  It almost always works perfectly now, but when something goes wrong, it is a little annoying to fix the problem like if one component doesn't go on properly.  The best way to fix when that happens is to use the app on your smartphone to fix.  The remote itself doesn't have a good way to fix things when they go wrong, it's not like you can select a component and then press 'on' or anything.  Again, for me this remote is great but it was a bit frustrating to get working at first, at least for me.

title: A great controller to give to someone you want to frustrate
text:
This thing was supposed to be the be-all end-all of analogue stick controllers within a reasonable price range. Unfortunately, it not only has very stiff triggers that don't like to report full 100% depression without squeezing them extremely hard, but the control sticks suffer from a ~15-30% deadzone across all 4 axes, turning the analogue sticks essentially into an 8-direction D-pad. And no, I have not confused the "swap D-pad and stick input" button for something else. It reports .3 to 1.0 fine, if a bit on the nonlinear side. After calibrating, recalibrating, and downgrading my Logitech software to be compatible with this thing, I've still not been able to get this controller to report anything between .0 and .3 on any of the stick axes. It makes flight games unplayable. As for an arcadey game like Need For Speed Most Wanted, while "drive straight" is now an option which wasn't available with a stock '360 controller, I would have been better off simply using the D-pad to steer.

Finesse is not an option with this controller. If you're okay with a controller that requires you to really hamfist the controls, then by all means purchase this one. I have, however, purchased a HORI controller at a higher pricepoint which is of much higher quality all around. I'm planning on buying more of those the next chance I get, so I can throw this controller in the trash.

title: Excellent Camera For Home Monitoring. Very Simple To Set Up
text: I found this to be the perfect camera for home monitoring. It will record to the cloud for free for 24 hours at a time. After 24 hours it will erase the footage then start recording again. You have the option to view your footage and save (download) any portion of the video incase you need it. Personally all I need is 24 hours to view my footage after that I don't need it anymore. If anything happens and I need the footage I can easily save it to my phone to view later or show to the police. Out of the box this is the easiest camera I have ever set up, and I've set up quite a few in the past both at home and at work. It connected to my wifi very quickly and has stayed connected ever since. It has quite a few options built into the app like you can turn the LED indicator light on the camera on and off, you can turn the camera's speaker and or mic on and off, you can change the video resolution, you can turn night vision on and off, you can flip the video 180° incase you mount the camera upside down, you can turn push notifications on and off, you can rename each camera and finally it has a battery charge indicator within the app. I really like the Day Brief feature which will show you all the recorded activity for the day in a short time lapse video clip. You can also navigate to any time of day that footage was recorded. Video quality is very good at 720p and 1080p. You can remove the camera from its charging ring and place it anywhere in your home. I'm not sure how long the battery will last but I'm sure you can get a good portion of the day recorded providing you don't have too much activity to recored. I would use that feature while not home if I suspected something happening in a certain part of my house where I do not have a camera. I can remove the camera from its charging ring and place it anywhere for the day to see what's happening, then put it back in it's original location, on its charging ring, at the end of the day. I have two Logi cameras and adding a camera is very simple. The app practically does all the work for you. Once you place the camera on it's charging ring it will give a short sound to indicated it's connected and charging. The charging ring also has a magnetic ring that will allow you to mount the camera upside down like under a shelf or to a wall. The charging ring comes with a flat 10' usb cable which plugs into the power adaptor. since it's flat the cable is easy to conceal and snake through small areas to a power outlet. All in all I feel this is an excellent camera for my home monitoring needs. Personally I would not use the Logi camera for monitoring a business. For a business I would recommend purchasing a hard wired system with a DVR. They are much more reliable then wireless and if you have the DVR you would not need to pay for cloud storage. I purchased both Logi cameras at Best Buy on sale for $149.99.

title: ... this with a Spigen Mouse Pad and I'm so happy with it
text:
I bought this with a Spigen Mouse Pad and I'm so happy with it. If you're into the gestures and different swipes you can do on a trackpad for the Macbook Pro or anything else, this mouse is a great addition!
I used the 3-finger swipe on my Macbook Pro Retina trackpad all the time. I still do when I don't choose to carry this mouse around in my bag while I go to my classes. With the gesture button (or any other button you choose; you can program them with the free downloaded software) I can do the exact same things without ever having to take my hand off the mouse. I even have the mouse programmed to "force click" things like my trackpad can do. This mouse also feels really, really great. It contours my hand really well and the thumb rest feels awesome. The back up and down buttons behind the horizontal scrolling wheel (also a godsend) is a bit far back for my taste, but I use those buttons to control the volume of my computer, and I seem to have enough dexterity to know what I'm doing with it. That kinda says a lot because I'm a total klutz.
It's definitely pricey, but if you want a good-feeling ergonomic mouse with excellent programability, this one's for you.

title: Good headset, some flaws.
text:
I've never had issues with Logitech in the past as I have a mouse that I use from them that is over 10 years old.

My first experience with this headset was the creaking plastic noise when you move it or add any flex to it. One side the plastic creaked and made a lot of noise while the other was fine. After 4 days of use the battery no longer would hold charge. I've tried changing chargers and everything. Sent it back to Amazon and got a replacement.

The new one doesn't creak as much, but does feel very flimsy. Although you can tell the head band is sturdy, when it flexes it feels like the plastic will break. I think the effort into making it lightweight also made it very flimsy.

The other thing that before buying you must know, is that while running on the batteries, around 45% battery life it will start beeping for a recharge.. and the beep comes every few minutes, and gets very annoying. Even on the latest firmware. I would much rather the warning be around 20% or 10% rather than 45%.

Last but not least, sound. The sound is surprisingly good. It's the reason why I gave this headset a 3 not a 2. The Bass and Highs are there with a nice presence and the Mids are adequately balanced. This is not a audiophile grade headset and it doesn't sound flat at all. Just perfect for gaming.

Battery DOES last about 10-12h of use if you turn the lighting off. Which is great.

title: Great Headset, Bad Software
text:
I ordered this product around 5 months ago and since then I have had a very mixed experience with this headset. Although the product seems great right out of the box, the annoyances in the software really take away from an otherwise flawless headset.

Comfort / Build Quality - 4.5

All in all, it is a very comfortable headset. I’ve never been picky, but this headset goes above and beyond. I have worn this headset for up to 10 hours before without complaints and the earcups fully encompass your ears so people wearing earrings get a very comfortable fit. It is, however, a little bigger and heavier than other headsets I have worn which can be inconvenient if you are gaming on the go. The band is a pretty durable plastic, but when the price tag is so high, I honestly expected a more premium material. Ever since I snapped a pair of turtle beaches, I have been nervous and have been VERY cautious with this pair. So, I have yet to find the limits of this headset.

Sound Quality / Connectivity - 4.5

Although this headset boasts 7.1 surround sound, I have heard better. That said, if you aren’t an audiophile, chances are you won’t notice any flaws from the audio. As far as connectivity goes, the range on this headset is actually quite impressive. I can head out of my room, down the hall, and into the bathroom without breaking conversation with my friends in discord. Heck, most of the time they don’t even notice I’ve moved! Music and video sound great in this headset. I usually use this pair when listening to music because the simplicity and convenience completely outweigh and flaws to the quality.

Features / Customization - 5

Honestly, I haven’t even gone through all the features. With the Logitech software, you can customize the buttons to do several different things. A lot of these choices relate to how the lighting on the headset works. Since most of the time I’m wearing the headset, I haven’t really cared about the lightning, but for others who like to coordinate their setup, there are numerous lighting patterns and colors to pick from.

My favorite feature for this pair of headphones has got to be the microphone. The foldable mic is awesome for the times that you don’t need to say anything and folds up seamlessly into the headset as if it were just a part of the earcup. The mic automatically mutes when folded up, but the headset does also have a dedicated mute button on the left earcup, above the volume controls.

Software - 2

I know I lauded the customization of the software in the earlier section, but frankly the software sucks. It honestly feels like they tried so hard overloading the features that they overlooked some serious annoyances in the software. As a person who has multiple audio outputs and uses switches to manage all of these audio devices, I have come across the problem many times when the mic will be permanently stuck on mute and I have to pull out the battery of the headset and then plug it back in for it to fix. That’s just one of many annoyances. I’ve also suffered through situations where the on/off switch doesn’t really work and the device is stuck in a pseudo sleep state (at this point I don’t shut off my headset anymore, I just leave it plugged in when I’m not using it). In my first month of using the headset, there would be times that everyone in my discord call would hear deafening static on their end and it was due to the headset. Although their software is slowly improving, it pains me to see an otherwise perfect headset rely so heavily on such a lacking software.

Overall, I’d say this headset has many great features, but with bad software and a high price tag be cautious with your purchase and do your research!

title: I hate that I love this mouse so much, despite its big flaws.
text:
I would like to start this review by saying that it's a near perfect mouse for me. It fits my hand perfectly and the feel of it is exactly what i want in a mouse. I love the scrolling wheel and functions of it, and even like the simplicity of the software that you have to download in order to customize the mouse and keep it's firmware up to date.

HOWEVER, I have two massively annoying gripes that each detract one star from this mouse. The Bluetooth feature is non-existent. It's such a shame because I thought I was moving into a modern computer setup by including my mouse in the upgrades I was doing. I have all drivers up-to-date on my computer (literally went down the device manager page in window 10 and made sure every single icon was up to date). I couldn't use it at all, but the USB unify thing fixed that issue; fine. I put the receiver on a port located in the back so I did not have to see it and think how crappy the Bluetooth is.

The second and hands down; the most annoying feature, is that IT SKIPS. I bought this mouse because I thought it was a high-end mouse that had come down on price. I honestly had no idea that skipping was an issue on a mouse that originally sold for over $100 and the main objective of the device was to TRACK MOVEMENT. I play videos game a lot and sometimes the mouse will start getting choppy and skip. I'm not someone that will easily get upset, but let me tell you how frustrating it is to perform simple tasks like walking around in a video game and have the cursor go bananas as it's trying to track your movement. WHAT IN THE WORLD? it's an absolute pet peeve that I did not know I had until I bought this mouse. However when I exit my video games and things calm down, the mouse goes back to normal, like an overstimulated cat that walks away from too many pet scratches. Yes I compared this mouse to a cat (no pun intended) but this mouse HATES video games and will get over-stimulated and not be able to handle everything. I purchased another Logitech mouse because of their quality is amazing in the mean time while I figure out if this is fixable. I haven't found evidence that hooking up the mouse to computer via USB port will hard wire it (as opposed to only charging) but if that is the case, hopefully that will nullify the latency issue.

The caveat to all of this, is that I've tried many other mice; cheap and expensive. They ALL feel like a bismol hunk of junk after using my MXM for four months. I would give it one star out of anger, But hot dang this is probably the best electronic gadget I've ever purchased. I love you MXM, but I hate you as well.

title: Logitech Stood Behind Its Product!
text:
Revised Dec. 2, 2016:

To its credit, Logitech replaced my keyboard, whose battery door had broken on first use. It took several weeks, but the company acknowledged the delay and, to apologize, didn't ask me to go through the hassle of returning the original keyboard. (I had mailed the broken battery door with a note requesting replacement of that small part only.)

The battery door is flimsy (slide one side first, then the other, to limit the force applied), but I've upped my rating to 4 stars because the keyboard is quite useful.

Although the K780 supports Bluetooth, there are advantages to using Logitech "Unifying" USB receivers, one of which is included. First, a USB receiver is essential if your computer has an older Bluetooth chip. Bluetooth 4.0 is the minimum for "Bluetooth Smart", which this keyboard requires. Second, once you've paired the keyboard with a USB receiver, the keyboard will be available the moment you power-on the computer. This is handy for changing BIOS settings or pressing modifier keys, for example, to boot from a data DVD. Bluetooth drivers aren't loaded until much later -- so late that on some systems, you cannot type your Windows password from a Bluetooth keyboard!

The K780 can be paired with three devices. Good computer stores sell, or can order, additional Unifying USB receivers. A cheap way to get them is to wait for a sale on Logitech wireless mice. (Look for the red Unifying star symbol on the package, because the cheapest models have single-purpose, non-Unifying, USB receivers.)

To use the K780 with a computer that doesn't support Logitech's Unifying software (computers running older versions of Windows and MacOS, and computers running Linux, unless customized), plug a Unifying USB receiver into a computer that has the software, pair the keyboard and the receiver, unplug the receiver, and plug it in to the old computer. With Unifying, the keyboard (or mouse) remembers the identity of a specific USB receiver. Logitech's software is necessary for initial pairing, not for ongoing use.

Initial Review:

You wouldn't expect a keyboard with a $79.99 list price to break before first use, but that's what happened with my Logitech K780.

Usually, a battery door has ridges, so that your fingers can slide it open easily. Logitech, however, opted for a smooth surface.

On my K780, the plastic claws that held the battery door closed were tight. The tiny, smooth, rounded indentation made it difficult to generate enough force to slide the door. When I did get it open, the plastic claws snapped. The battery door no longer locks closed.

It's also amusing that the instruction sheet inside the box was designed before the keyboard. It shows a door that slides toward the top, and straight off. The actual door slides the opposite way, with about 2 mm of travel before it has to be pulled out.

I'm mailing the broken battery door to Logitech and will update this review if I receive a response. I doubt I will, as Logitech seems to have been reduced to a Chinese manufacturing operation with a skeletal North American sales and marketing presence. Make no mistake: despite the steep price, this is cheap, Made in China junk.

(Before you ask why I opened the door right away when batteries are included, I always install those horribly expensive long-life batteries in my wireless keyboards and mice. It's worth it to avoid having to re-pair devices so often. The K780 is, after all, a 3-device keyboard. Before you point out that the door on your K780 slides easily, plastic molding is not an exact science, and tolerances vary from one unit to the next.)

I have a variety of other bluetooth headsets, from cheap in-ear designs to expensive DNR designs, that don't suffer from this issue. If your computing environment involves a number of Bluetooth and WiFi devices, consider something that hasn't been on the market quite so long. Bluetooth chips have improved. The H800 has not.

title: Great build quality, great optics, absolutely worth the money.
text:
Simply put, the quality on this camera blows all other webcams out of the water. It's not going to compete with a true DSLR pro setup, but it's probably as close as you will ever get at this price point. That's right-- I'm comparing it to DSLRs, not traditional webcams-- that's the level this thing is on.

What I really like about this camera:

- The stand is well built and surprisingly versatile. It has rubber backing so you can easily set it up to sit on top of your monitor without having to screw anything down-- and it stays in place. You can also tilt it to a bunch of different angles / setups and even screw it onto a stand if you wanted to.

- Although I don't use the microphone on this thing (I have a dedicated setup for mics), I did try it out and the audio is pretty clear without being too sensitive to background noise. Used it a few times in audio calls and got no complaints. The fact that you get a mic "for free" is a pretty good deal.

- The optics quality, again, are just awesome. The camera has good auto-focus and a low aperture to capture a lot of light, but that also means it creates that really nice looking depth of field effect when it focuses in on your face. The result is professional looking DSLR-type video that you just won't get on a conventional webcam.

title: Good quality keyboard, worth the money
text:
Had this for about 3-4 months now and it's a good keyboard. Nice to type with, good quality construction and of course it has that "chroma" effect.

It isn't as nice as the new Razer Ornata, but it's close. The definition of the key letters is a little blurry when you look at it from any angle except straight down - so you lose some of it's "wow" factor. The other slight downgrade from the Razer product is you can't program the lighting effect for each individual key, there a few pre-defined lighting options to light up banks of keys with different colors, but not many. It has multiple color wave type effects, which you can slow down or speed up as desired. Cosmetically it's 4/5 compared to a Razer Chroma effect. The colors are bright and easily visible in daylight.

Overall it's a very good product and worth the money. It had media controls, a game switch to disable a few keys that could take you to the Windows desktop accidentally while playing and the response time of the keys is good.

This is no mechanical keyboard, but it feels nearly as good as one. Typing takes a week or two to get used to, but once you do it's natural and feels solid. The response time for keys is good, again not mechanical, but far better than a $20-$30 keyboard. It's also spill proof - accidentally tested with a full cup of coffee - which is a definite plus.

TLDR 5/5 build quality, 4/5 cosmetic (chroma), 4/5 features and 5/5 value for money. The only thing it's really missing is a USB port for the mouse.

I'll leave my initial post below for reference but I'm glad I got a replacement that works.

I want to like these speakers, I really do, but they simply DO NOT WORK RIGHT. They sound awesome, and look great, and the price is nice, but I can't enjoy them with the insane amount of hissing going on in the right speaker. It's ridiculous. Apparently it takes one even two replacements to get one that doesn't hiss, but even then I hear people say they stop working within 2-3 years of owning them.
Pros:
- Looks great
- Great sound
- Spectacular bass
- Headphone jack on right speaker
- Power switch
Cons:
- Incredibly loud hissing noise in right speaker than ruins the whole thing
- Apparently if you do get one that works, it stops working in less than 3 years
- Right speaker has proprietary cable
I don't understand how these speakers can look so good and sound so great but have such major quality control issues, and how they fail so quickly. Doesn't make any sense. If I don't get a working unit then it looks like I will have to get a different set of speakers, and I don't want to because these speakers check all of the boxes for me.

title: Defective, disappointed, was not offered replacement unit when returned.
text:
I have never been let down by a Logitech product until I received this adapter. I purchased this to replace Logitech's previous incarnation of Bluetooth adapter (which served me faithfully for years until one day it died). I was excited about the upgraded features of this model. I own Logitech's Z623 speakers (The THX with subwoofer and two bookshelf speakers), which are physically connected to an all in one computer that I use primarily for music, streaming video, and my PS3.

I have many devices that use Bluetooth - IPad Air, Amazon Fire Kindle, iPod Nano, Headphones. I only need one connection at a time (however having two available was a big draw for me).

Issues I encountered: Easy pairing but either a) no sound, b) faint sound with loud static, or c) ear splitting feedback like sound.

I assumed I received a defective unit, so set up a return where normally I am offered a replacement. However, this time I was only offered a refund. So, either Amazon is not replacing defective products anymore, or, there may be an issue with this particular product.

I searched for other adapters, and settled on Etekcity Unity Adapter, which was cheaper but has limited features (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00KXYXXK2?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detail-page_o01_s00). Received that yesterday and it works perfectly. Easy to use. I recommend this alternative until Logitech sorts out its issues with this model.

Cheers, and I am glad to see this product has worked well for others. Just not for me. Two stars for the quick pairing.

title: Solid headphones with poor battery life, seriously consider the newer variants of the G930 or a wired equivalent
text:
These headphones are such a shame because on the whole they are fantastic, but there are some serious hits to functionality and usability that make them pretty mediocre and occasionally frustrating.

First off, what they got right: These are the first pair of headphones where the cups are deep enough that they don't press on my ears and hurt after long periods of wear. All together they are pretty comfortable. The swivel boom mic it has pretty good quality, and, build-wise, seems nice and sturdy while still being adjustable. In addition the ability to flip it up and automatically mute it is nice. There are enough buttons on it that it's useful and functional and they have a nice resistance, but stick out enough to be easy to find without seeing them. I'm a big fan of the matte black aesthetic with subtle branding. I'm not one for the gaudy yellows on Corsair or the recent trend of obnoxious LEDs on everything. The stereo sound is great, but with the surround sound on it really does sound pretty fantastic.

What they didn't get right:

The wireless functionality is beyond mediocre. The enormous USB dongle is a pain and seems fragile. Would definitely prefer one of the tiny Logitech dongles or, ideally, just Bluetooth pairing functionality. Sometimes I'll have to pause my music and check that I don't have mics on because the interference sounds like someone breathing into the mic.

The crowning irritation for me has to be the battery life. It is absolutely abysmal. The software will say "10 hours left" which is atrocious on its own, but manageable. But not even 2 hours later it will start beeping and if you check the software, it will notify you that there is about an hour left. However in a couple minutes, it will flicker and tell you there's 24 minutes left. It will shut itself off substantially before this time limit. Honestly this is the quality that drove me to write this review. It's just such a huge let down to have to plug the charger in twice a day, usually once while using it. And I'm very religious about turning it off when not in use.
In fact, I just heard a beep while I was writing this and I charged them fully this morning.

On that note, the power button is far too flush against the case, and you have to hold it down for an indiscriminate amount of time and then let go before it will turn off. There is no LED or any signifier that tells you it's about to turn off or that you've held it down for long enough, it simply waits for you to let go. And if you let go before then nothing happens.

My final note is that the software is pretty clunky. It's extraordinarily unattractive, feels legacy on Windows 10, and is surprisingly hard to find. But its functional and for the most part does what I want. I take it all with a grain of salt considering it's a couple years old and so isn't really comparable with recent software suites.

title: Thought this was a single-activity Harmony remote, turns out it doesn't really support any activity at all
text:
I've used various Harmony remotes for close to 10 years. From the 880, to the One, to helping my parents set up their 700. All of those are fine and capable remotes, but the 350 in my view should not even count as a "Harmony".

I thought the 350 would be perfect for my bedroom TV because the only things I had connected there were a receiver and a Roku 2. I only needed a single activity (watch the Roku), which the 350 is designed to handle, so what could go wrong?

As it turns out...a lot. Unlike real Harmony remotes, it is not possible to program buttons for an activity. This is a huge problem, and defeats the entire purpose of owning a "Harmony" remote. For example, in my singular activity, I would like to map the remote's directional buttons to the Roku's directional buttons and the remote's "Red" button to my TV's picture mode button. In a real Harmony remote such as the 880, one would create an activity called "Watch Roku", and map the activity's directional buttons to the Roku's directional buttons, and the activity's "Red" button to my TV's picture mode button. As a result, I press a single button (Watch Roku activity button) to turn on the TV, receiver, and Roku. As soon as the devices are on, I can press the directional buttons to control the Roku, the Red button to change the TV picture mode, and the volume buttons to control the volume via the receiver.

In the 350, however, things work in a much less intuitive way. It is not possible to program buttons for an activity, only for a device. So, I can map buttons just like I did with a real Harmony, but they are useless unless I switch to that specific device. Following the same example above, this means I press the "Watch TV" button to turn on all my devices. Once the devices are on, the directional buttons are useless because the default device is the TV. So if I want to control the Roku, I have to press the Roku device button first. If I want to change the TV's picture mode, I can't just press the "Red" button, I have to make sure to press the TV device button first. In other words, this works just like any other cheap universal remote.

The 350 also doesn't support custom power-on or power-off sequences to allow you to add additional button presses to deal with special circumstances that require it. Given how the 350 doesn't even properly support the notion of activities, I guess this is hardly shocking.

For anyone who's used a real Harmony or is looking for the Harmony experience and expected the only restriction to be the single activity, prepare for massive disappointment. For anyone else who wants a universal remote, there are much cheaper alternatives elsewhere.

After doing two weeks of in-depth research, I decided to go with the Logitch Z623's based on positive customer reviews, fewest reported problems, build quality, sound quality, and the fact that they were THX certified. My instincts proved correct. After some initial setup, the Logitech Z623's have exceeded my listening expectations. Stereo separation is excellent, crisp treble, solid bass, and transparent mid-range that doesn't sound muddy.

My only recommendation (if you are super-picky, like I am) is to make sure you are using a good audio card, and a 10-band equalizer to tune the audio to your listening preference. For example, I used my computer's Realtek audio, Win 7 built-in 10-Band Equalizer to compensate for the room's acoustics and for maximum dynamic clarity. Not everyone may think of that, which may affect your overall satisfaction. If you don't have built-in equalizer on your computer, you can download one for free from the internet. Just Google it...

Bottom line, Logitech's Z623's are well worth the money and a safe choice if you are picky about music. You will not be disappointed.

title: Annoying rattle. Here's how to fix it.
text:
This mouse is good but the little on/off switch rattles. I fixed this by taking it apart and putting some tape underneath the switch. If you are like me and the rattle bothers you, here's how to do it:

1. Remove battery cover.
2. Pop rear of top black shiny piece where the logo is out and up away from unit, but be careful not to pull up too hard because it's still attached at the front.
3. Push the top black shiny piece forward to remove it.
4. Remove the battery and using a tiny Phillips screwdriver, remove the screw below it.
5. Pop rear of grey piece up, and slide it forward to remove it, just like the other piece.
6. Lift the left-click-button side of the circuit board and gradually pry it out, being careful not to break the two prongs that hold it down.
7. Note the orientation of the switch and maybe take a picture. You'll want to align the switch on the circuit board and the plastic piece when you put it back together.
8. Remove plastic switch piece.
9. Apply some tape in the area where the switch piece goes, sticky side down. Make it bigger than the switch piece so it won't come out, but make sure it doesn't interfere with the rest of the unit.
Cut a hole in the tape where the switch piece hole is, and place the switch piece back and make sure it can still move.
10. Put it all back together.

It's pretty easy, just take your time. Should only take you about ten minutes.

The curvature of the board is both nice and annoying, as it fits your hand great, but is hard to adjust to when coming from a flat keyboard. Then there's the standard spacebar button on the pad, which is not really where most people hit the spacebar, but actually represents the left 3/4 inch of the spacebar, so you have to actually push your thumb under your palm to hit it. Setting the top button next to the thumb stick helps but it's somewhat awkwardly placed as well. So far, this is mainly just issues adjusting to the design of the device, while being accustomed to a keyboard. My other issue is the thumb stick, which has a really small top/head that is somewhat awkward to use as well. I've seen a ton of tutorials where users replace this stick with the one from the Logitech game pad, which is basically the same style as those found on Xbox or PS gamepads, and have a more ample thumb area. I used to use a Belkin Nostromo which had a better thumb stick, so this is the one real flaw in my opinion. Other than that, the pad feels great, the keys, while not mechanical, are feel basically like those on the Logitech non-Mech boards like the G105, and the screen is quite useful once you set up applications for it.

title: it's great. The problem is that it's sold as a ...
text:
For what it is, it's great. The problem is that it's sold as a "Keyboard Cover" so I was expecting something that covered the iPad and helped protect it from drops. It is definitely NOT a cover. The keyboard magnetically sticks to the front of the iPad, so it will protect against something impacting directly on the front. But the iPad is still completely exposed to the far more common edge impact or corner impact during a drop. And those are the ones that break the screen. It wasn't clear to me from the images that it did not have some kind of protective cover for the rest of the iPad. And because of the design, there's no way to add a protective cover and still have it work with the keyboard.

As a clip-on keyboard, it's excellent. Good feel on the keys, very thin, adds minimal weight and thickness to the iPad. If you like using your iPad without any protective cover, and you want a good quality, attractive, minimalist keyboard, this is it! But if you want some protection from drops along with your keyboard "cover", look elsewhere. The Belkin Qode Ultimate is a good choice, but at a higher price.

title: the sound quality is great and it's very comfortable
text:
I've had this headset for about a year and a half, and it's full of problems. When it works, the sound quality is great and it's very comfortable. That said, this headset has some massive driver issues that Logitech has refused to address. When I first got this headset, I used it on a Windows 7 machine and had problems with constant disconnecting which required manually resetting the device sometimes as frequency as every 5 minutes. I was able to follow some sketchy guides to modify some of Logitech's configuration files to get it useable, but it is not consistent. I have since had it on the same machine with Windows 10, and a new machine with windows 10, and on all 3 iterations I have had stable connectivity issues in one form or another.

If the connectivity were the only problem with this device, I would give it a higher rating. But the main problem is constant interference and crackling that is a known issue documented by hundreds of users. I bought this device from Amazon unaware of these reviews and have regretted it ever since. Simply put, Logitech made a great piece of hardware but absolutely terrible software. I have tried everything from multiple versions of drivers to adjusting the broadcast frequencies of my modem/router, and nothing has resolved the tendency for this device to constantly and randomly have sound crackling and distortion. This distortion can get so bad at times that it will trigger the device to start disconnecting and reconnecting to try to fix it, and can get to the point to render the headset un-useable. I've checked new solutions repeatedly for years, and there is literally nothing you can do.

I've also recently started to have issues with the battery, and it's barely a year old. Sometimes during use a huge electronic noise will start filling the headset, and it needs to be disconnected from the computer and manually reset in order to stop. This can happen even after being plugged in for days, and after this happens the battery will be totally drained and require recharging.

It's frustrating because I've been a Logitech customer for over 20 years, and have always used Logitech peripherals for all my computers. All these issues are known if you are aware of them and go to look for them, both on their official forums and elsewhere. Logitech has yet to actually patch their software to fix them, meaning that either Logitech just doesn't car, or it's firmware level problems that they are unable to patch, and instead of announcing this they just have remained quiet. While I want to remain a loyal Logitech customer, this sort of shady dealing on an expensive headset really doesn't sit right with me. Good headsets are an expensive investment, and I feel like Logitech has totally shafted their customers on this one. The problems with the headset have been getting progressively worse from month to month, to the point where I am considering replacing it soon.

Perhaps I just got a dud, but I'm certainly not alone. Stay away from this headset. Shame on you, Logitech.

title: Do NOT buy, very poor quality
text:
As a long time supporter of Logitech Products, I have to say I've been very disappointed with my G930. Over the past few years I have gone through a total of 8 of these units, all for various reasons.

My first clue should have been when I got my first set home and plugged them in... The sound quality was excellent, the features worked fine, but the headset would drop connection every 15-30 seconds, even when plugged in. The receiver sits less than 3 feet from my head so there's no reason there should be such poor signal quality. I ended up exchanging this unit at the store (per Logitech supports advice) with another one which ended up having the same issue.

By headset number 4 I finally got one that held a stable connection and it worked great for about a year. Then it started not holding a charge. I expected this to some extent since batteries to wear out (I also noticed some cracking around the headphone pivot points) so I had it replaced under warranty. Unlike other Logitech hardware I've had to RMA before, they didn't simply send a replacement, I had to ship them the broken device and wait 2+ weeks for a replacement (that's 2 weeks with no sound on my computer). Upon receiving said replacement though, I had the exact same problem that my first several devices did, where it would constantly drop connection. So 3 more RMAs later I finally got a pair of headphones that work.

Fast forward to today, the headset is now out of warranty, both of the plastic retaining tabs on the headphone pivots have broken (just from the stress of being on my head, I've never dropped them and they just sit on my desk most of the time), and I'm trying to use my 3D Printer to make replacements for the cheap plastic parts Logitech used on the this headset because Logitech doesn't sell replacement parts for the most commonly broken thing on these.

Don't get me wrong, when they work they work great, but good luck getting a pair that works and lasts.

text:
I've had this headset for 2 or 3 years now and they're still going strong. You don't realize how annoying wired headsets are until you get used to using this headset. Not only do I not have to deal with a wire being stuck to my head but it also means you can get out of your seat and do other things in the room and not have to worry about taking the headset off. This is great if you have a roommate who you don't want to bother with your music or if your cleaning your house and you want to be able to hear music while you walk around. Some minor complaints: the battery life is good for one long session or two short sessions but besides that you're going to need to charge it. You need to hold the power button for an unusually long amount of time to turn it off. And when you have the volume high, other people in the room can hear them too, pretty easily. title: Way too many issues to make it worth your money
text:
TL;DR
The headset is nice in construction and looks, but has way too many technical issues for it to even be usable. Do not recommend.

I'm going to break down this review into a bunch of different categories where I explain what is good/bad about it:

1. The Sound: As a whole, the sound on these headphones is actually pretty good (while they are working properly), and the base on it is nice. While playing PC games, I felt that the audio sounded very crisp and clear.

2. The Design: The design of this headset was also pretty nice, combining a good balance of style and comfort. I could wear this for hours on end and not feel the slightest bit of discomfort. The headset also has a bunch of unique features on the side of the left ear cup which are quite nice and useful. Being able to mute your mic by simply raising it all the way up is quite helpful.

3. Technical Issues: Okay now you will see why I gave this headset a 1 star rating. The amount of issues this product has is so ridiculous that I cannot possibly recommend this to anybody. I spent more time looking up how to fix certain issues rather than actually using the headset comfortably. The worst part is that these issues were all so common, with very few and reliable ways to fix them. That goes to show that Logitech is probably aware, but just does not really care. Here's a list of the many problems I had with this headset

- Crashing: This is the most frequent issue that I get (In fact it's happening to me as I am writing this review) and it is also probably the most frustrating one. While I am using the headset, it will randomly shut off, and then turn back on after 5-10 seconds. This happens to me about 8 times every 30 minutes, and is especially annoying while I am in the middle of an online game, or watching some kind of video. I've tried about 20 different methods to fix this issue, and nothing seemed to work.

- Mic bugs: Sometimes the mic will say that it is muted (the red light on it will be on) but it would actually not be muted, and even if you pull the mic all the way back, which is supposed to mute it, it will remain functional. When the red light is constantly on, nothing you do will mute it, which is very annoying.

- Rapid crashes: Sometimes if the headset is low on battery, and I am using it while it is charging, it will completely bug out, and start just turning on and off over and over again very quickly, and I would have to manually reset it to fix it.

- No Sound: Sometimes the headset will just not get recognized on my computer (an issue I never had with previous headsets) and I will not be able to hear any audio coming out of it whatsoever. The only way to fix this issue was to restart both my pc and headset, and hope for the best.

- Static noise: Sometimes the headset just wants to punish me even more for wasting $100, so it will just muffle out all the audio it is outputting, and instead replace it with a VERY LOUD static noise directly into my ears. One of the worst technical issues I've ever personally experienced.

- Not charging: Sometimes this headset will refuse to charge when I plug it in to my charger, which is also very irritating. Manually resetting it multiple times will sometimes fix it.

- The Software: The Logitech gaming software that you can download with this product is not very helpful, and is known to cause even more problems. It will sometimes solve some issues that you may be experiencing, while simultaneously creating new issues for you to deal with.

FINAL VERDICT
I do not recommend you buy this product due to the insanely long list of issues that I have had with it. I have noticed that most of these issues are very common with other users of this headset. If you are planning on purchasing a wireless headset that is worth your money, stay away from this one.

text:
The Logitech G930 headset is a my daily driver for both PC and PS4 gaming. The construction is quality, it is comfortable, and its easy to use. I bought this after finally retiring an old GameCom 380 headset that broke, and this has been an amazing upgrade. I have now had this headset for a few months and these are my impressions as a heavy user of electronics, especially headsets.

Pros

The ear cups are comfortable faux leather, allowing the user to wear the headset for al long as they want without any discomfort. My longest gaming session was about 12 hours straight never taking off the headset and my ears didnt get hot, nor did my head start to hurt at any time. Top marks for comfort. The USB dongle is easy to use, just plug and play between my PC and PS4/. Your really do get about 10 hours of battery life, much more than a lot of other headsets. It adjusts to fit any head shape or size, but it will feel snug at first. This took a few hours to get used to but was very nice once I was accustomed to it. While not completely noise canceling it does a great job to muffle outside noise, which makes the surround sound experience that much better. The mic and surround sound are very good quality, and tests over multiple communication platforms such as skype, steam chat, oovoo, PS4 group chat, and in game chat have all confirmed that the mic sounds crisp and clear. The volume buttons and macro buttons on the side are easy to program with Logitech software, and easy to find even n the dark after having had a few drinks. Side note, one of my favorite features is the mute light, and the ability to mute your mic just by raiding it up.

Cons

Turning on the headset takes to long and the button does not always register a press. It can take up top 10 second to get any feedback that the device has been turned on. The USB dongle is easy to use but does not always connect to the headset even at small distances. When connected to my PS4 I experience frequent disconnects between the headset and USB dongle. The sound will just cut out without warning and may cause some miscommunication between you and team members of the game is heavy influenced on chat. It can take some messing around with your router setting to fix this issue as it seems to be related to interference on the 2.4 Ghz wireless signal that the headset uses. No problems when connected to the PC through the wireless dock though, so it seems isolated to when the headset is wireless and not plugged in for charging.

Overall the product is solid. Without the disconnect issue it would have gotten a perfect 5 stars, hopefully Logitech fixes this but the headset has been out for a long time so I doubt they are concerned with it anymore. Great headset, fantastic sound, with a few minor issues makes this a great buy for around 80 Dollars US. You should be able to find it for that on amazon, but I do NOT recommend paying the full $150 retail price.

title: Bad, unless you NEED a wireless gaming headphone
text:
If you absolutely must have a wireless headset with an attached mic, then this is probably not the worst choice in the world. However, I would strongly recommend getting something else. If you want a gaming headset, then the HyperX Cloud ([[ASIN:B00JJNQG98 HyperX Cloud Gaming Headset - Black (KHX-H3CL/WR)]]) Is probably your best bet. If you're willing to use normal headphones (which is what I'd recommend), get a decent headphone and an attachable mic or a desktop mic. I would recommend the Philips SHP9500 [[ASIN:B00ENMK1DW Philips SHP9500 HiFi Precision Stereo Over-ear Headphones (Black)]] and a V-Moda BoomPro [[ASIN:B00BJ17WKK V-MODA BoomPro Gaming, VoIP Headset Headphone with Mic (Black)]]. This combo should have much better sound and give you a better mic. If you have more money to drop, you could get something like the Sennheiser HD558 or HD598 [[ASIN:B0042A8CW2 Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory]] and get a ModMic and attach it to them.

As far as the actual quality, I found the build quality shoddy. My first pair broke (no sound out of the right ear) after 6 months, and the required warranty number was conveniently worn away by then, because the plastic that contains the unit number happens to rest on your head and get worn away over time. Logitech still took the warranty request, but it was very annoying. These headphones just scream cheaply built, with cheap plastic and weak joints in a lot of spots, so I wouldn't expect them to last for more than a year.

Another problem I have is that the wireless connection cuts in and out when I use it in environments that have any interference, so they would not be suitable for an apartment or dorm. This problem is much less noticeable in a place where there are less wireless signals being broadcasted, like a house in the suburbs.

The comfort on these is OK. They get a bit hot for me, but that is pretty expected on a closed headset. The clamp force isn't too heavy, and they isolate well.

I got into headphones a year or two after buying these, and I've learned that the sound quality in the vast majority of gaming headphones (outside of the HyperX Clouds) is really bad compared to equally-priced headphones. I've also learned that 7.1 surround is a gimmick (especially on PC) that shouldn't have any positive effect on audio. Any well-made game will supply good positional audio in stereo without an additional USB dongle.

There are also many annoying problems that happen from time to time: sometimes audio only comes out of one earpiece when surround is turned off, because the channel that should be going to the left ear is instead going to the right ear (this happens in League of Legends a lot). The mic will continue to broadcast my voice even when it is muted. The surround sound will turn off even when the switch is set to on, and then the annoying problem with sound only coming through one ear will happen.

If you absolutely need a wireless headset with a mic, then this might be the right choice, but if you can deal with wires, there are far better alternatives for the price.

But it keeps cutting on and off and we found out that the frequency the headset and USB dongle ride on is the same frequency our WiFi network and it interfere against each other. It's very annoying when I'm in a sync meeting with my Engineers and my headset cuts off. Very irritating.

If this headset works for you and doesn't interfere with your home WiFi. To keep your headset from automatically shutting off. Go to the Logitech g930 folder and find an xml file called "manifest.xml", copy that file to your local C drive, open that up in notepad++ or Windows notepad. Change the shutoff # to 0. Save it and copy and paste back to the g930 folder and overwrite the old one. Than reboot. That should fix the auto shutdown.

title: GOOD SOUND QUALITY, TERRIBLE LONGEVITY
text:
I purchased this product about a year and a half ago. I have used mine for an average of about 4-6 hours a day as a college student. I decided to write this review after because I am in the market for a new headset, and I feel that I've run this pair through their paces and I would like to give some feedback.

I am giving it a 2/5 stars for the following reasons:

Pros:
-The sound quality is good, despite some audio glitches when in 7.1 surround mode
-The mic quality is good as well, for a headset that is
-The wireless range is good

Cons:
-The swivel joints break ridiculously easily due to the terrible design choice of making flimsy plastic joints for cans that are this freakin heavy. This is the same problem I've had with the 2 g430's that I've owned from Logitech. In this case mine broke after 8 months
-The plastic forks that hold each can are made of terrible quality plastic that also break easily, mine broke while moving back to school after 10 months.
-The programmable buttons are difficult to program as the software will sometimes not recognize what function you want it to be set to, likely because of buggy software.
-The wireless dongle is finicky with what usb port it will work with
-The included coiled wire died 4 months after purchase
-The connection to the dongle gets worse over time, mine now has issues connecting to the headset on start up and will lose connection randomly or when near too much interference from other signals like if you sit next to a wifi router and I have tried this on several devices.

In summary DO NOT buy this headset if you intend to use these heavily because, like most products from Logitech, they will not last very long. Mine are barely being held together with duct tape and gorilla glue. And that does not warrant the full price, luckily I bought mine for under 90 bucks, so BUYER BEWARE if they are not on sale. I have since decided to go with a Cloud II headset due to its all metal design and lack of swivel joints.

title: Power button unreliable (needs a power switch)
text: I dread using these headphones due to one major design flay, the implementation of a power button instead of a power switch. Getting these headphones to turn on/off usually takes me multiple presses of the button until it registers and in some cases it registers with a delay in which case I end up getting stuck in a vicious and frustrating cycle of pressing the button, waiting a few seconds, then trying again until finally getting it powered on/off. After having a pair of headphones with a power switch and now having this pair with a power button, I will never again buy a pair of headphones that doesn't have a power switch. I absolutely dread using the power button. If it worked reliably 99% of the time it wouldn't be an issue, but in my experience the power button on this pair of headphones is reliable only 25% of the time where it will register the button press without delay. Also on some occasions the headphones will suddenly just shut off on their own for no reason and I have to go through the whole process over again. This random shutoff might happen in 5% of my gaming sessions. The audio quality of these headphones is fine and the wireless range is excellent.

title: DO. NOT. BUY. THIS. HEADSET. IF. YOU. PLAY. CSGO.
text:
I'm making this review with hopes for an issue for this headset to be solved although, after searching the forums, it seems that
Logitech isn't going to do much about it...

This headset is a COMPLETELY wireless USB 2.0 headset with the only thing wired is the provided cable used to charge the headset.

Pros:
Great Sound
Great Range
Matte earpad surface that reduces possible cosmetic oil smears from the hands
Three shortcut buttons on the right side of the headset, useful for speaking on push-to-talk applications when away from the computer
Slightly flexible microphone that will lightly prevent your microphone from cracking if pushed a bit

Cons:
Feels fragile
Crackling audio when streaming videos
Earpads become uncomfortable and will hurt the ears after sometime of gaming(3-4 hours)
Headset WILL cut off due to wireless interference. Happens sporadically with a minimum of 5 seconds and lasts for an
INDEFINITE amount of time. This is horrible and unacceptable for sound-dependent games such as CS GO
When turning the headset on mid-call, a certain beeping/buzzing sound will occur that you or your friends may hear. This happens in
applications such as Skype

Conclusion:
To establish credibility, please keep cognizant I am an owner of this headset that has owned a total of THREE g930 headsets after receiving TWO replacements from Logitech. I have also lived in two separate households during the two years I have owned this headset.

The product is given 1 star solely because of its inability to produce sound CONSISTENTLY. The headset cuts off randomly during gameplay, and it seems that it will cut off even more often while streaming videos from sites such as Youtube, Netflix, Facebook, etc. When cutting off, the minimum time it cuts off is 5 seconds; however it is possible that it will cut off until it is turned off, which has happened to me countless times during my use. Customer support is not helpful for this issue, as I have listened to their troubleshooting with no success; the fixes on online forums will help minimally and will ease nothing but your mind temporarily. The issue will arise again.

If the headset did produce a consistent sound, the headset would be a solid 4 stars with the only thing holding it back is its fragile feel and uncomfortable earpads, since it does not serve well for long gaming sessions.

Why did I not return it when the issue happened? Partly because is a gift from my parents, which was bought online; the hassle of returning wouldn't be really pleasurable for my parents, and partly because I was ignorant of the lasting issue and was hoping for a fix from Logitech.

DO. NOT. BUY. THIS. HEADSET. IF. YOU. PLAY. CSGO.

title: Five years of use and still going strong!
text:

The top cushion vinyl cover on the headband has disintegrated over the years, although the earcup vinyl has held up okay. I made the earcup vinyl last longer by sticking some thin pads onto them. The [[ASIN:B002XKBBSA Howard Leight by Honeywell Cool Pads for Earmuffs, 100-Pack (1000364)]] are made for Howard Leight electronic earmuffs but will fit a variety headsets and headphones with over-the-ear designs. These pads make the earcups even more comfortable in all conditions, warm or cold temps. Sadly, the pads are now very expensive.

I don't know if I'm just lucky but I'm still really happy with the Logitech G930. It's held up for just over 5 years with no issues other than headband wear. Battery life is still good. No issues with the USB wireless 'dongle'. I'll buy these again when they do eventually wear out or break.
