title: Please Skip These - They Will Skip on You
text:
I've had this headset for a year, so I feel like I can give an accurate and fair review. This headset is junk. The number one most important thing for me in a headset is that it gives uninterrupted service. Unfortunately, the G930 does not deliver in this regard. When I first, purchased the headset would cut out about once every 10 minutes. It has now grown to be about once every 3 minutes.

Now one might think this isn't that bad, a 5 second cut out over a 3-10 minute period doesn't sound THAT bad does it? I would disagree. Logitech calls this a "gaming" headset, As gamers can tell you, losing voice and sound at ANY point can be a deal breaker.

I tried many solutions. Google Logitech G930 cutting out and you will see manythe people with the same problem. It seems like around half of the people do not experience an issue with this headset, but its simply not worth the risk. Please exercise caution when considering this headset.

title: Bad Drivers, Good Product
text:
I've only had this product for a few weeks, but I thought I should review this product.

Out of the box, and installed using the link they provide, I give it a 4/5 stars. This is for three reasons.
1) When you try and use the Headset while it is charging, the charging cable is rather short. This is a minor annoyance, and not something I would usually take a full star away for, but it contributes to item 2/3.
2) When the headset is not plugged in and Charging, every so often it randomly disconnects completely from the sound, goes silent for a minute or two while it is making the "Out of Power/Disconnected" beeps, then recovers without any interaction by me and goes on it's merry way.
3) Out of the box, unless you press a button on the headset every 15 minutes or it is plugged in, it will automatically turn off after 15 minutes of use to "Save Power"

That being said, Items 2 and 3 are fixable through a little internet digging. I don't have the link on me, but the problem with the disconnect seems to have something to do with the unified drivers for the Logitech G930 and every other Logitech gaming tech that exists. If you find and then install the drivers for ONLY the headset, which I was able to download from the Logitech website using a link from a 3rd party website this problem goes away.
If you google search for the G930 randomly turning off it will take you to a website which provides instructions for Disabling the Auto-Off Power saving features. While this means it does not turn off while you are using it, it ALSO means that the G930 will not turn off on it's own at all, which would deplete the battery if you forget to turn it off.

Overall it's a good product. If you think you can figure out how to do the above items I would recommend it.
The sound deadening of the headphones is very good, and I can barely hear someone talking to me within the same room when the headphones are off, let alone when something is actually using the headphones. They are very comfortable, and the mute light near the microphone is a nice tip for when you forget to unmute yourself.

Edited 2/23/2016 - So the new drivers worked for about 3 days, then the problem came back with the Shutting off and turning back on again. I did uninstall the drivers and am using the default Windows Drivers which has reduced the Frequency of the occurrence, but the Headset continues to do the shutting off and back on again, if at a reduced occurrence rate. I've tried what I've found online to solve the problem and it doesn't seem to help. What I am seeing online basically says it's a Crap shoot on if you get a good product or a bad product. Some Headsets Work well, some don't.

TL:DR - Bad Default Drivers, Find better drivers, slightly better product, still not so Good Product overall.

Edited: 9/8/2016 - I tried the new software that was commented on down below in the comments. While the problem is reduced, it is not eliminated. I continue to stand by my statement that their is some sort of problem in this headset. Item 2 from the above review continues even with the new drivers.

However, knowing about that before I purchased it, this performs exactly as I expected it to. I got it not for the most perfect audio experience, but for being able to stand up and get something from across the room without having to remove a headset first.

A few other issues I have noticed with this. Occasionally the power button doesn't want to turn off the headset, sometimes the headset will not send any sound even though I'm talking. It will show that I'm transmitting on voice detection, but won't actually send anything. It was also quite difficult to get the EQ right.

As far as a wireless headset goes, this one is great for the price. Know what you are getting, and realize that it will not be as good as a wired headset. I'm not sure if I would purchase it again, but I'm not disappointed by this purchase.

EDIT:
After having used this for several months I now have to say that I'm not quite as pleased with it. When it works, it's amazing. However, the audio likes to cut out and reset fairly often. Yes, I'm close to my wireless router and that can explain some of the static, but this just has too many issues. I still use it as my primary gaming headset, but I'll probably buy a wired headset when I replace this, and it'll probably be before this one wears out. If I wasn't close to my router it would probably work a lot better.

title: Some issues with signal quality but overall a fantastic headset for this price.
text:
Well, the other reviews didn't lie. This is a quality headset. I came from a set of Siberia V2's to the PS Gold headset. After my USB dongle bit the dust (my fault, chugged a vodka bottle at the PC and somehow managed to bend the dongle 30 degrees - it still worked for 2 more years!) I decided I needed to upgrade and get a slightly more functional headset than the previous.

Out of the box, materials are excellent. It comes with a USB dongle as well as a little station that you can use to set up on a desk for more accessibility options. The finish looks great and everything moves/rotates smoothly and with confidence. The feel is quite comfortable especially with the box-sized cutaways which should be able to wrap around most ear sizes. As a wearer of glasses I don't get too much pressure, although you will probably have to adjust your glasses a bit to make it truly comfortable for longer sessions. The earmuffs rotate on a swivel so that they can be set down on a table flat, which is a nice feature. Hopefully the mechanism holds up over the months/years. More parts typically equals more breakage.

Sound wise, I am no audiophile, but I appreciate clarity in sound and music. I'm not really a fan of virtual 7.1 but this does perform adequately, especially for FPS and games where having that situational awareness can give you an edge. My benchmark for music quality goes out to J Dilla's instrumental "So Far Gone" and the bass, treble, and overall quality was pretty darn nice. You might need to mess with the equalizer settings to fine-tune it to be just right for your preference. After I slid the bass and treble up slightly I was in another world.

The advertised charge time is about 10 hours, and so far I haven't had to charge the headset after multiple gaming sessions lasting a few hours each. Be wary of charging this headset while wearing them as the mini-USB port doesn't seem to be very solid. As far as signal quality and the wireless feature I was expecting a bit more. Using the little USB station I have my PC set up on my living room screen and I use a wireless mouse/keyboard. The USB is about 10-15 feet away from where I sit, and quality at that time is perfect. However, I have noticed that if I move to my desk which is a bit to the left of where I sit, the signal cuts out completely even though I am still the same distance away. I rotated the USB hub to face that direction, and the sound came back on. I'll still need to test this more, but it doesn't look like the signal will keep if you walk into another room with a wall separating you. A bit disappointing coming from Logitech, but then again, this headset looks to have been out for a while.

Since I'm still in the "honeymoon" phase of this headset I'll have to update my review after some time has passed to see how these hold up. But, so far so good!

Somewhat noticeable background noise when you have them on w/o any sound playing
I find the buttons on the sides completely useless. It comes with software to customize it, but seriously, if you are a gamer, are going to really bind some in-game functions to your headphones?
The range is just about 20 feet.
The power button. This power button is what triggered me to go and write a review. One would think, how you can possibly screw up the power button... well... buy it and see, it is actually possible. The button itself appears to be working just about 50% of the time. Well... most people are ok with that. Another twist on it is that you have to hold it. Another plot twist is that it will only tell you that it worked or not in few seconds after. Now putting all these amazing engineering decisions together - you pressed the thing.... wait... nothing... maybe I pressed it not well enough.... press again... doesn't work... maybe I need to press it for longer... hold... hold... nothing... press again OMG, I retried too soon, my second press actually turned it off. title: they work brilliantly; but when they don't oh my goodness
text:
I've had this headset for 2 1/2 months now, and when they work, they work brilliantly; but when they don't oh my goodness. The first problem I had were the updated drivers the headset used. It caused the headset to automatically turn off after a set period of time, (30 mins-60 mins) I can't remember specifically but there was no way to change this unless you changed the actual coding of the driver. So I uninstalled the software and used them without it, which caused the buttons on the side to switch between the functions they use. Sometimes the volume bar would forward a song, sometimes the pause button would turn off the headset. Well the drivers were updated recently and so far the problem has been fixed by Logitech.

Next we have the hardware. The headset worked well, up until this last week. After only two months of use the screw that connects the mic to the headset became loose, causing the microphone to not stay in the upright position. I figured it took just a little bit of tightening down, and all fixed, but that was not the case. The nut that holds the screw in place came completely off the screw, and fell back into the plastic headset. The first layer of the headset is easy to remove with a small Phillips head screwdriver, but the Allen screws they have below it are some obscure form of metric Allen wrench that strip faster than my high school girlfriend after prom. So I wasn't able to retrieve the nut, the screw was loose, and I have this headset that I regret buying. I ended up jerry-rigging the microphone with some double sided tape to at least keep the microphone in the down position so it wouldn't be flopping around when I moved my head.

All-in-all, go fork out the extra money for a better and more well engineered headset. I wouldn't recommend this to my worst enemy.

title: Does its Job very well but is physically lacking
text: I have owned 2 pairs of G930's and I have really enjoyed them. The sound quality is great as is the mic, its easy to charge, it has a pretty far connection range even passing though walls and such and it's very comfortable. However... although all the software quality are great the actual physical hardware is meh to say the least. My first pair the ear joint broke in travel, well I do admit it was partly my fault for not packing it a little better I figured with the lower price and the great experience I had with my first pair I would go ahead and get a second.... now this second pair has been somewhat of a nightmare when it come to physical quality. the first few months were great, sound was great, no disconnects, nothing breaking, absolutely awesome. However around the third or fourth month of owning them the left swivel joint broke. Now well it didn't really effect the quality of the mic in the sense of make it uncomfortable to wear or damage the sound/mic performance it was kinda annoying. Cue the next month where I started having disconnection issues. Whenever it was plugged in it would lose connection the the computer for some reason, finally changed out the cable and that seemed to fix the problem. However tonight I think its finally finished, I think one of the wires is loose on the inside which is rather frustrating considering it was working earlier today and I had just set it down on the desk to do something else for all of 2 hours. When I got back I tried turning it on. Resting on the desk I could hear sound from a video coming out of the speakers however putting on my head I head a loud zap like sound and the headset shut off completely. I tried plugging it in thinking maybe the battery wire had just been disconnected and I figured that if I had it plugged in it would not require the battery and I could save it. Unfortunately it just made the problem worse and caused this horrible screeching noise plus long loud beeps and then would shut down for a few seconds then do the whole thing all over again. So in conclusion, The G930's function as a headset is great the sound quality is awesome and user friendly. However for the price the actual hardware is not really worth it, to many weak points cause it to be a bit of a struggle to transport and lower the life of the headset by quite a bit even if you leave it at home. It seems the cord has a longer life than the headset itself considering I was still using my first G930 cord for my second G930 long after I had purchased my second headset. My first headset lasted about 6 months but that was partly my fault. My second however didn't last a full year and that was with extra care to prevent damage. All in all good headset in terms of software but horrible when it comes to the actual hardware.

title: An Expensive Headache; Not Worth the Trouble
text:
There are two good things about this headset: the noise-cancelling of the ear pieces, and the quality of the mic. But those two features are not worth the headache or hassle that comes with using this headset.

The software for the headset causes it to shut off periodically every ~15 minutes; fortunately, this can be fixed manually by editing the XML file in the Manifests. Unfortunately, the charge doesn't last long enough, even if you leave the headset plugged in 24/7, because my headset is constantly shutting off because the battery keeps running dry despite the fact that it is never unplugged from the charge station. This is a serious problem, because it interrupts my conversations and subsequently interrupts my work.

I often hear trace static while using this headset. Sometimes I even get this shrill whine that rises in volume and can only be fixed by unplugging the headset, which for some reason forces it to shut off despite the light indicating it has a full charge. Which brings me to my next point: I have to jump through hoops to turn the headset on in the first place by finagling the wire connecting it to the charge station several times.

The reason I wanted this headset was because I sometimes have to get up and move around, and didn't want to have to remove my headset or stop conversation every time in the event I was in the middle of something important when I had to get up. Because this headset refuses to work when unplugged, I basically threw money away on this thing. This headset will be going into my back-up box for when the cheaper, more-reliable headsets break and I need something to hold me over until their replacements show up.

Do not waste your time or money on this infuriating thing.

text:

This lead me to believe that the product had been opened previously.
My suspicion was confirmed when the box just opened on its own and the product almost slid right out, but I was fast enough to stop it from falling to the ground.
Even the little plastic snaps that held the headset in its enclosure were not snapped together.
Upon first use I noticed some a minor tinny feel to the audio and wasn't that bothered by it.
I tried playing CS:GO with it and the audio took a dive. All sounds were unbalanced, NO bass, way too quiet with 3rd person sounds, WAY too loud with 1st person sounds.
I decided to get the configuration software provided by Logitech specifically FOR the headset.
Upon connecting to the software, the headset repeatedly disconnected and reconnected, over and over.
I found about 3 different fixed online that didn't work, including instruction to change actual code for the software itself.

Overall:
The headset was ALRIGHT, not impressive or even that great. Quality takes a dive when in use with actual games, quality disappears when connected to the Logitech software.

Just returned the headset for a refund, I'll continue to use my Sony Pulse Elites, which, after 4 years of excessive use and a snapped left ear-cup connector, still sounds CRAZILY better than these.

title: Forgo the bells+whistles of the G930 and get something more reliable.
text:
Pros: the volume and button controls are quite nice, sound is decent enough, mic does its job. The wireless combined with the controls makes it quite convenient for using when away from the keyboard.

Cons: Garbage construction quality, the thing has broken in a dozen ways for me. Its complicated design makes it an absolute pain to repair. Audio quality is mediocre, really poor base. The software often crashes. The wireless occasionally cuts out (tho only for split seconds). The headset will occasionally bug out, preventing proper use of some features until a full reset; sometimes the headset will even lock up, forcing me to find a pin to press the tiny manual reset button. To top it off, the weight of the headset feels unbalanced towards the left, which can be quite annoying at times.

One of the wires in my headset seems to have gotten frayed, causing audio for the right ear to often cut out, whether partially or completely. For most simpler headsets this would be an easy home fix, but do to the overcomplexity and tight formfactor of the internals, it can't be easily done. as a result I have to occasionally shake the headset like a madman until it for whatever reason stops shorting out and hope I don't bump it to make it quit working.

If you *really* are set on a wireless headset under $100, you could certainly do worse, but I would recommend forgoing the G930's bells and whistles for a simpler more reliable set of headphones and external mic that would have better quality for the same price. Everybody said this to me when I bought the G930, just get quality wired headphones, and didn't listen, now I wishing I had.

title: Very good headset, would recommend if you understand computers.
text: I'll rate this 4/5 headphones for several reasons. Although this is an extremely good headset, has great sound quality, a good distance for wireless sensor, and very good 7.1 surround sound, I had a lot of problems when i first got it. For one, logitech gaming software, has a problem that causes the headset to shut down every 15 minutes and in order to stop this, you need to go into the system files of the program in order to change this. Although this isn't a very difficult task, it could be very annoying for someone who is not very tech-enabled. Another problem i had, was that the headset's sidetone feature would go to 10% every time the 15 minute shut off happened, which can be very annoying since the headset is very dense, and cancels out a lot of noise, including your voice, so sometimes the feature would shut off, and I would be yelling because I could not hear myself very well and would try to compensate. FInally, for a solid week, logitech gaming software would not boot up for me, even after reinstalling it in 64 and 32 bit versions several times, however after contacting logitech support, I found that instead of putting the wireless receptor on the hub that charges the headset, put it directly on the computer. I did this and at first i saw no effect, however 10 minutes into a gaming session, the headset shut off and on again, on its own, and somehow all my problems were fixed. Would rate a 5/5 but the first 3 weeks of having this product were really stressful during a time of day that was supposed to be relaxing, and were it not for that, it would be a 5/5.

title: for the love of God do not buy these if you're using ...
text: Ok, for the love of God do not buy these if you're using Windows 10. There are significant issues with the Logitech gaming software and drivers on windows 10 with certain usb controllers that cause random disconnects, problems charging and other problems (e.g. the buttons randomly stopping working until you restart the software, making wearing these around the house pretty worthless).  I was eventually able to get mine working by randomly switching usb ports, turning off selective suspending, changing the xml file associated with these headsets, summoning and killing Cthulhu to appease some great power, and I still had to sell my soul and the souls of my first 11 children in order to get this to work properly.  Do yourself a favor and buy something with better driver support.  I've been through multiple battles with cancer, and I'm still unsure whether or not that was worse than purchasing this headset.

title: Nice sound, short life, have bought 3 over the years
text:
The Logitech G930 is a capable, great-sounding 7.1 surround wireless headset but it does NOT LAST. Be prepared to buy another one later. Several of my friends, and I, own this headset. I've personally bought three of them and would again, with these important notes:

The plastic housing and the wiring, even on the USB cord, is very flimsy and breaks easily and often. I've had to replace two G930's outright for broken plastic and refurbish another one myself. Extended use with natural oil on the skin around the ears will also break down the padding of the earpieces, a faux-leather type material. Battery life starts strong when purchased but diminishes over time with daily use.

All that being said, it's a good value, comfortable to wear for long periods, and you can't go wrong with the 7.1 surround sound. Just wish it were more sturdily built and reliable. But I guess that's why there are more expensive headsets out there.

Don't spend more than $75 on this; it should always be on sale for that price or less.

text:
I have this headset for a few weeks. and have had a lot of issues with it. So I will list them.
#1 the headset has a built in timer that powers it down after 15 min of not hearing anything. sounds good. except I use it every night for 4 hours. The only was to keep it running was to plug it in. The issue is not the battery it is the software. After searching Logitech Forms I found that you can edit the Device_Manifest.xml file found in the Logitech file folders. to set Battery autoshutdown to 0 was set at 900. I did that and problem solved.
#2 The mic mute Button will sometime mute the mic and sometimes not.. mute.
#3 headset work great with Vent and TS. but the game sound will be great then sound static.. not great. the fix set game sound to speakers. not what I wanted but worked.
#4 Headset and Transmitter lose contact with each other. and will only reconnect if computer is restarted.
#5 The headset fits so tight on my head I can not hear myself talk. so the next thing I know I'm yelling. My fix was to notch the Ear cushions looks funky but works.

title: Stunning 40 mm range, crystal clear disconnects and sound quality so rare one can only sample it for seconds at a time.
text:
After four G930s, 2 gen 1 (2010) and 2 gen 2, I have to call it quits. I just purchased my fourth and I'm going to return it. The 7.1 is functional but not flawless. The new 'LGS' software has its share of problems and doesn't seem to like WIN 10 very much. But there's absolutely nothing I can do besides tape the cable with transmitter to the side of the unit to make it work. This headset is plagued with two problems: 1) the plastic plates that secure the overhead band to the earpieces and 2) the intolerable disconnect issues. My first unit worked fine, but eventually the battery wore down and the on/off button became stuck because it requires a lot of 'holding' to turn it on. I replaced it with another and that one had the earpiece retaining plate break. Logitech replaced that one under warranty with a new 2013 version and that worked fine until it snapped in the same place. There was always intermittent disconnects, but I survived in spite of them, mostly out of laziness to locate an alternate product. However, with the newest version of LGS, the drivers or the new hardware I'm experiencing disconnects every few seconds unless I hold the transmitter next to the headset.

Sorry Logitech, can't do it anymore. Unfortunately, if I'm going to spend $200 on the new 933s, I'd rather just upgrade to units with better reviews. Great promise as a budget headset, but not to be used within 30 miles of electricity, magnets, people, radios or indoor plumbing as they all cause tremendous interference. The MSRP isn't worth it, for $70 you can try your luck.

I give it an extra star because Logitech CS is still the best in the industry, but I can't .... deal.... . break.....and .....furth....... ..aid........a........no........

title: Sound is ok, but design is terrible.
text:
Logitech generally makes decent products, so I was pretty surprised at how terrible these are. First the good--the sound, when they work, is pretty decent. But that is completely outweighed by the terrible wireless connectivity. Every time you turn them on, it's like playing the lottery--they *might* connect almost immediately, or they might spend several minutes trying to pair with the base station. Once they *do* connect, they will periodically lose connection minutes or hours later--there's no predicting it. I've tried moving the base station, I've tried moving myself--they simply will not connect reliably and predictably.

In addition, and this is a small point, but still infuriating--the power button is terrible. You need to hold it in for at least several seconds to get the set to turn on or off--but as with the connectivity, it's unpredictable. Sometimes 2 seconds is enough, sometimes it takes 15. And you get no feedback on whether you've succeeded until you let go. It's really beyond me how Logitech ever let this design out into the field.

title: Unacceptably poor reliability
text:

70% of the time, this headset is 5/5 stars. The other 30% consists of random disconnects despite the headset being less than three feet away from the receiver. I have tried placing the receiver in pretty much every possible location within ten feet of me and placement seems to be totally irrelevant. At this point it is guaranteed to disconnect several times on any given day and to sometimes go through a prolonged period of disconnecting every few seconds. The period of constant disconnects can last anywhere from two minutes to over a half hour of the headset being unable to maintain a connection.

After going through countless threads about these issues and wasting many hours trying to find a resolution, I'm replacing this headset and am very much discouraged from considering Logitech for this type of product in the future.

title: Good headset - Good price
text:
What you get - Headset, USB adapter, and a USB charging cable/extension to plug in USB adapter

Reliability - I've had this headset for about a month. In that time nothing has broken and the build quality is pretty good.
Audio quality - The sound quality of this headset is good. For the price, you won't find better sound quality in a wireless gaming headset. My one complaint about the audio quality is the microphone. If the microphone isn't within about 1 inch of your mouth it comes with a heavy dose of static.

Ease of use - The headset has its own mute button and volume control which are simple to use. The microphone automatically mutes if u raise the mic up as well. The microphone even has a red light on it to let you know when it is muted. There are 3 additional buttons on the headset which can be programmed to do a number of features, but the Logitech software has to be installed in order for them to have any function. The battery life of this headset is consistently about 10 hours from a full charge.

Comfort - The headset is padded everywhere it touches when you are wearing it. When I first bought the headset, it felt like it was clamping my head (it didn't hurt, but it felt tight). It also made my ears feel hot (not to the extent that it was uncomfortable). After wearing the headset for a couple of days, I don't even notice that anymore. This headset isn't particularly light or heavy for a wireless headset either.

Connectivity - If you are using this headset at home, you will have minimal connectivity issues. The range is great, and it rarely disconnects. If you are using this headset in a call center (like me) or at a LAN party or anywhere that there are tons of people using wireless headsets, you will experience connectivity issues with this headset. At work, my headset disconnects about once every 15 minutes and stays disconnected for about 1 second. When I am at home, it almost never disconnects. I should also mention that about 1 in 10 people at my work have a wireless headset so that makes for a lot of interference.

Pros - Cheap for a wireless gaming headset, good sound quality, great battery life

Cons - Not a great headset if you're going to be around others that have a wireless headset.

title: AVOID LOGITECH HEADSETS AT ALL COST!!!
text:
AVOID LOGITECH HEADSET AT ALL COSTS. NOT WORTH THE TROUBLE!

I rarely ever write a review but I felt it was necessary to warn anyone even considering a logitech headset. I have own this particular headset for years now and the ENTIRE time I have had problems with it.

First it was the crackling noise problem. Find out it is because of driver issues and interference with the wireless. If you search on the forums for this problem you will see what I am talking about and how users fixed the issue. WHAT YOU WONT SEE IS A LOGITECH EMPLOYEE EVER RESPONDING TO ANYONE ANYWHERE ABOUT THE ISSUES!!! They have known about this issue for years...not a single response or attempt to fix it.

Second problem, buzzing sounds while gaming. Come to find out, yes it can charge while you play but if you do so it will definitely cause interference and an annoying humming or buzzing sound while charging. Again...well documented by other upset customers.

Three, and the most important one of them all...the drivers flat out dont work. I repeat this to you...THE DRIVERS DO NOT WORK PROPERLY AT ALL!!! This issue has been around since DAY ONE. It is 2016 now, years later...and still no fix. In fact the ONLY way to fix the issue is hunting down a link to someones personal storage where they have an older driver that still only works 50% of the time. Otherwise you will have a device that disconnects and connects over and over again SLOWING DOWN YOUR COMPUTER. The newest drivers remove most of the benefits advertised for this device AND STILL DONT FIX THE PROBLEM.

The whole reason I say to avoid Logitech at all costs is because this driver issue is in ALL OF THEIR HEADSETS. Not just wireless too. They ALL have problems, including their new 933 and 633 series. title: "Expensive Wireless Wired Headset from Logitech!!"
text:
OK. This headset is literally the worst purchase I have made towards my computer since I bought it. I had researched headsets for a very long time when trying to find a new one to use. I previously had a wireless stereo headset designed for the PS3 that I bought somewhere about 3-4 years ago. Best headset I ever bought. They were tough, reliable, and had reasonably good sound quality (not as good as the G930s though). But this review is not about the headset I bought 4 years ago.

The G930s looked promising and I have two friends that also own these headphones. The 7.1 surround sound looked very cool and considering all the other products that I have owned from Logitech (mainly mice and one keyboard) I was hopeful.

Got the headphones and was incredibly excited to have some nice quality headphones only to realize I got cheaply made horse crap that lasted just under two months.

Pros:
.The headphones are incredibly comfortable, I could game for quite a few hours before finding myself having to take them off.
.They block out sound very well
.The NORMAL sound from them is pretty incredible, not the 7.1 feature. It'll be covered in the cons area.
.Cool feature with the boom-mic where it auto-mutes when it is raised up.

Cons: (HOLY HELL HERE WE GO)
.The Logitech Gaming Software is an abysmal excuse for a "driver program". It is literally worthless, with the exception that you can only turn on 7.1 surround sound when the software is installed and running. Which is still pointless. I had some issues with my computer at one point during these 2 months where some memory got corrupted or something. I had to update a few drivers for my motherboard etc restart the computer a few times, when suddenly I realized that my headset was not working anymore. No sound at all. The mic was being picked up because my friends over skype could still hear me. So something weird was going on. I spent three days not being able to play with my friends because I was stuck with no sound trying to figure out what to do to fix the issue. I have no idea what messed the headset up but the only fix that I could find was to completely uninstall the Logitech Gaming Software. (which isn't a big deal considering the software is 100% worthless to begin with.) So basically the software that is supposed to make the headset work and have more functionality is what broke them for a couple of days. Good job Logitech.

.For the first few weeks the headset was constantly cutting itself off, forums stated that it is because they might almost be dead etc. where the aforementioned gaming software told me they had 10 hours of life left. I felt reason to believe that the headset was not almost dead considering I had them charging most of the day while I was out working. One solution I found was to leave them plugged in charging while I used them, effectively making them what I will call them from now on, the "Expensive Wireless Wired Headset by Logitech". I finally found a permanent solution, go into the driver files and find the config for the G930s and change a setting called something like "battery_power_off_interval 900" and change it to "battery_power_off_interval 0". In all honesty the pure stupidity of this line of config even existing makes me feel like I have lost brain cells so I will not comment on it. Hopefully you the reader will understand why that is so stupid.

.The 7.1 surround sound is a joke. I don't know all the gizmos and gadgets and tech behind how the surround sound is supposed to work. All I know is that it only sounds like you are in an empty wooden room with sounds echoing off the walls. This in my opinion is not "surround sound" but hell what do I know. If you want to experience the "7.1 Surround Sound" feature of this headset just buy like two or three speakers and an empty wooden room and play music/ sounds from them from your phone. BOOM $80 worth of 7.1 surround sound.

.The mic boom broke near the end of the second month. From what? I don't know. It seems that a screw or something broke and it doesn't hold itself in the up position anymore, which is sad because that for me was one of the coolest features. I wasnt that distraught over it though I was planning on just seeing if I could fix it myself and tighten said loose screw. That is, until the mic stop working completely. About 2 days after the mic boom broke, the mic stopped working. So I'm guessing there was something more wrong than just a simple loosened screw. The only thing I can even conceive that might have broken it is occasionally when going to the bathroom I would lightly toss the headset with the mic boom in the up position onto my bed from less than 1 foot away. The max airtime they might have had would have been 0.5 seconds. If this light toss onto a pillow-top mattress broke the headset then they definitely were not built to be sold as an $80 headset. This sorry excuse for Chinese engineering leads me to believe that all of Logitech's microphones are made from delicate baby tears and toenails. Simply put without the sarcasm. If the headset broke from this light tossing they were built with absolutely awful quality materials.

Summary:

This headset is not worth $80, the "feature adding Logitech Gaming Software" is useless and a pile of garbage, the software was also programmed with the most ignorant config setting that I have ever heard of, the quality of the material it is built out of is trash, the auto-muting mic boom is really cool though.

Basically do not buy these headphones unless they are lowered to a price more worthy of their build quality, something like $15 sounds fair. Sorry Logitech you dropped a ball bigger than the craps I get from my local Mexican restaurant. I will be taking my business elsewhere. Maybe Razer will have something worth the money.

title: Where's the serial number on these things?
text:
I bought these headphones about 3 years ago and have loved them. The sound quality is good. The fit is good and the leather pads are comfortable. If you had asked me after the first year, I would've suggested this headset to anyone.
Then the problems started. Here is a list of the issues in order of occurrance:
* Constant disconnections - this happened from the start. They are wireless and they lose their Bluetooth connection randomly about once ever 30 mins. Not a huge deal but the brief moment where you lose sound is annoying.
* Retractable microphone became loose - It would not retract up anymore. The screw that holds this mic tightly had become stripped and so it was always down. Tolerable but again, annoying.
* Right earphone had started to lose sound - I think there is a loose wire somewhere. The right ear would cut in and out randomly. This was a big issue so I decided to contact Logitech support.
* Logitech Support, what a joke - For the life of me, I could not find the serial number on these. I took high resolution pictures of every inch of the headset and send it to the Logitech support staff. They just kept telling me to keep searching. Despite my best efforts and 4 weeks of telling the same guy that I could not find the SN, he kept repeating the same "you need to look closer" (yes... 4 weeks and about 20 messages back and forth). Needless to say, I gave up.
In summary, this headset is a great value for the price, if the build quality (or engineering mistakes) weren't such an issue. I hope that I just got a bad pair and others had more success. But a huge caveat is that Logitech support lack the skills to do much of any problem solving. So you are rolling the dice a bit when getting these.

title: Great product but a word of warning...
text:
Just as a heads up this operates on the 2.4 GHz band so if you live in a place that has a lot of wireless density it is likely to struggle. At my house it works great I can walk about 45 feet away and it works fine, until I turn on the Mircrowave, which also spew out tons of 2.4 Ghz electromagnetic radiation. That's right your wireless router and microwave run at the same frequency. So in theory you could cook a hot pocket with your wifi router, but I am getting off track.

However at my friend's apartment complex I have issues staying connected. I have resolved this by having the headset plugged in to power. It has more power to draw from so it can boost the signal gain and I don't have any issues. Until I forget that I am plugged in and want to grab a beer out of the fridge. I then pull my laptop and taco bell into my chair because wires attach things like that.

I also pull my laptop off my desk at work because I am so use to wireless and just getting up and walking away. That I forget anytime I have a head set on that it can attach to things. That is when I decided I need one for work too!

If it hasn't been made clear I wear this thing a lot. It might be my new fashion statement. Upwards of 16 hours a day for the last 14 months. It is extremely comfortable. I love it. 'Nought said.

Oh and if you are wondering about the wifi and hot pocket thing, don't try it, most wifi routers emit 0.25 watts of electromagnetic radiation whereas your standard microwave is around 1100 watts. You are going to lose heat faster than you create it in the hot pocket. You are better off setting it on your phone while writing amazon reviews. Phones get hot when you do that with the brightness turned all the way up of course.

title: GREAT when working ANNOYING when not Basically
text:
GREAT when working
ANNOYING when not

Basically, when it works, it's good. The sounds are good, and the mic is good. It being wireless is a good thing - but also it's fatal point.

Although not using a unifying receiver (it has its own dedicated one), the connection can be really bad. I've had times where I game 2-3 hours without any disconnects. I've had times where I got disconnected 10 times in 15-20 minutes worth of gaming. FYI the transceiver is only 1 foot away from me (I bought a wireless one because my setup was different before).

PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE search for "Logitech G930 disconnects" and look over the results. These are the problems you might face. There is no one single working solution that solves everyone's problems.

For me, I've tried switching my wifi channel (in case of interference) - did not work. I did pinout it down to one factor - WIFI. When I game, I tell everyone at home to stop using wifi. When they stop, I got only 1 disconnects in 1 hour or so. If they continue using wifi, I was disconnected 3-4 times per minute and it just got so annoying.

So, be careful before your purchase and consider facing these problems. You might start seeing problems after warranty kicks in.

p.s. I've used other logitech devices (my TV keyboard and all my mouses are logitech) and they are generally quite good. I hope this is an exception only...

title: Pretty Good Product Ruined By The Most Fatal Flaw of Headsets
text:
Okay. So. There's a lot of good things to say about this headset. I know, I'm only giving a single star. But I'll get to that.

The good stuff is as follows: The headset is pretty comfy. I've had the set on for several hours on end and not felt the need to "take a break," or readjust for comfort. Additionally, the headset breathes well, there's no sweat or heat build up over the ears.

The second thing I like it the sound quality. It's pretty damn good. I'm not a big audiophile, but I feel like the sound quality is solid. Bass is good, and the high end comes through just fine. Spoken word sounds great too. Basically, nothing that I've thrown at it sounds bad.

Third thing I like a lot is the "portability" of the unit. The other end of the USB cable that attaches to the computer is attached to a hub. This hub has space where you can wrap the cord and keep it tidy. The hub is also where a USB dongle attaches. This means I can simply remove the USB dongle and plug it into any other USB port on a laptop, etc, and use the headset there.

Okay. After all that praise. Here's the rub. Intermittently, the headset completely drops connection for 5-15 seconds. Sometimes two or three times in a row. Sometimes the headset will not have this problem for an hour, other times it's once every 5 minutes. So, while all the things I love about the headset are definite positives, I simply cannot recommend this product. It doesn't matter how good the sound, portability, or comfort of the headset is if I can't get *sound*.

Sorry Logitech. I've liked a lot of your products, but buyers, give this one a pass.

title: The Logitech G930 headset is most likely the best wireless headset out there for the cost
text:
The Logitech G930 headset is most likely the best wireless headset out there for the cost.

CONS: 1. Poor construction
2. Software Support
3. Wireless connection issues
4. Replacement parts

Pros: 1. Range
2. Ease of use
3. Comfort
4. Programmable buttons
5. 3rd party replacement parts.

OK here is is I am the proud owner of two G930's(1 first gen and now current 2016 gen) the first one I had nothing but issues with its construction and the ability to find replacement parts and connection issues(since being able to find out the the headset is 2.4 GHz and my WiFi router was causing issues). I find this headset very useful and convenient to use. I however do find the construction of the device lacking and the company should have taken the time to make sure that the device in question was sturdy in its build. Logitech should have been more conducive in the ability of users ordering replacement parts for its device.(in this I mean all parts of the device should have been order-able from Logitech or from a 3rd party from release or as soon as customers started to complain about poor build quality of certain parts.) Software support is an issue after finding that the software did not take into account the interference of WiFi networks frequencies of the headset after many users complained about the issue. Also the causes of disconnects and stoppage of signal reported by users from the firmware of the device and the computer(ie shutdown at random and disconnects caused by software timers in the software)

With all the cons reported the pros are listed below:

The range of this device is fantastic. From the base station to my kitchen is about 50 feet through 3 walls and I still have connection without issue and I think that is fantastic. This also works with the programmable buttons.

Ease of use is pretty simple: Plug into computer, install software from Logitech website and use period. Anyone else that says otherwise has no experience in using computers and needs someone else to do it for them.

Logitech software allows you to program the 3 buttons on the headset with different functions. This option is most like the number one pro that gamer's need when it comes to a wireless headset other than sound quality(this includes positional audio and surround sound . As a gamer I like the ability to get up from my computer and still be able to communicate with people on different audio chat programs, this headset allows that. Also the buttons can be programmed for other computer programs.

Since this headset has been out there for a while there are companies that will 3d print replacement parts for the headset that seem to have the most issue. If you already own one of these headset you know if not the mounting brackets where the headband meets the speaker are weak and break often and Logitech has no replacement option on their site. But you can order them via 3rd party and they are fantastic.

Final Thoughts:

I originally bought this head (G930) on original release and loved it with the exception of build quality. I have since bought it again and am loving every dollar and minute spent in it. If you as a user want a headset that preforms well(with some tweaking of your wireless channels on your router), with the ability to orders parts third party for broken replacements (out of warranty) then this is the headset for you. Cost vs issue of this headset vs usability is a no brain-er. Are there better and newer headsets on the market of course. However they cost 4 times as much and sound performance is the same. If you do not mind to tinker a bit and are computer savvy then this is the headset for you.

title: The best headset ever. Easily.
text:
First off, this is the best headset I have ever owned. I have had only four headsets since I started really gaming back in 2005. I usually take great care of my things and they last me a long time.

Things I loved:
The sound quality was terrific on this headset. I love listening to music on it, and I could hear other instruments or things I never noticed before. I could pick out footsteps easily in Counter Strike, or even Team Fortress 2, and hear everything. The surround sound worked very well. I could pinpoint where any sound was in a game. It was very accurate.
Gaming was so much more immersive and intense, Amnesia was absolutely terrifying, Skyrim was that much more real to me, somehow. I felt much more into my games.
The Mic was clear and loud, but not over the top. Very adjustable, and can move out of the way when not in use, and automutes itself when in the up position. I really liked that a lot.
Side buttons for music are cool, but I never used them, because I have hotkeys on the keyboard, so sort of a useless feature for me, but a neat idea.
The range. Oh my goodness. I cannot describe how impressed I was at the range on this headset. I have never owned a wireless headset before, but I am not so sure they all work this well. I am not over exaggerating at all when I say I could go use the bathroom with this on (Yeah I tried that okay?) and much more impressive was I could still listen to my music, and my friends and talk on Mumble while checking the mail outside. I lived on a small street and so I had to walk up the street to go and check the mail. (While on Mumble a friend asked: "Mike is there a car in your house?!" "No dude, I'm checking the mail.") I still was loud and clear to my friends. It doesn't make sense to me how the range could be that good though. Never had a problem with my signal ever.
Charging station was no problem to have plugged in and using it while charging was no different. The headset lasted maybe 8 hours or something while fully charged. Plenty of time for a marathon session.
Earpads are over the ear, much better than anything else you could get. They were comfortable, and did not bother me when I used them for very long marathons(6-12 hours, yeah pretty disgusting I know.)

Thing(s) I did not like..?:
I'll have to say the only thing I can remember that I did not like was the headband was not as comfortable as I had hoped. It bothered me head, and I had to have the headband out to the maximum size, but my head is extra big so that's probably why. I had a headband cushion from an old Sound Blaster Alpha Tactic 3D headset that broke (terrific headset as well) shoved into the top with the original cushioning for extra softness. No problems with that in place.
This is me trying to be critical, but I suppose I may mention that the headset may have been a tiny bit tight and small on my head, but again, big head here. Probably totally fine for everyone else.

While I am very stingy with my money typically, I splurged hard and bought this. It has lasted me 4 years. It was awesome, despite the intense nerd level when you wear a headset like this. Worth.

I would definitely recommend this to someone. To you. To everyone. It is simply awesome. I bought it on sale for $100 back in 2012 so it was like $50 off. Logitech has always impressed me with the quality of their gear. This is a terrific product.

title: Major connectivity problems
text:
I've had this headset for about 3 years now, and I'm finally posting a review in the hopes of saving others from the pain and suffering that this abomination has inflicted upon me. If you're thinking a wireless headset sounds great, and the negative reviews can't be right, wrong. Walk away now while you still cling to your sanity. I'm convinced my life is going to 6 months shorter for having owned this.

To be fair, there are good things about the headset:
- Very comfortable
- Very effective at muffling other sound
- Sound quality is good

So why one star? Well, none of those things really mean much if it can't stay connected. And mine can't. Since day one, I've had major connectivity issues, and they've gotten worse over the life (such as it is) of the headset. After literally years (years!) of tweaking settings, trying different drivers, changing USB ports, trying with different computers, trying with and without Logitech Gaming Software™ running, moving my wireless router around in an attempt to reduce interference, I give up. Just when I think I've figured it out, that dreaded disconnect comes and crushes my soul anew. I may get 10 seconds, 1 minutes, or 30 minutes (I swear it happened once!), but it's always coming. Every raid boss, every split push, every close match comes with the added stress of this sword of Damocles hanging over (or in this case, resting upon) my head.

I like everything else about the headset enough that I was hopeful that I'd finally find the trick to making it stay connected. But all along it's been a trap to drive me further into madness. Oh, how I've longed for a wire, a thin strip of coppery goodness that, while preventing me from talking to my gaming buddies while sitting on the toilet (don't tell them), would actually transmit data to and from my head. Please don't buy this. Don't make the mistake I made. I want to tell you to never buy another Logitech product again, but that would be unfair. They do still make things that don't constantly ponder taking your own life. But this one...just no.

title: After 2 years of use, my warnings.
text:
I've had this headset for MAYBE 2 years. It was a huge letdown. It was a the first "expensive" headset i bought. I mostly used the cheap wired logitech 20-30 dollar headsets before this. I was expecting a decent product upgrade for the price. Instead i got a flimsy janky headset.

Would like to start off by saying i could really care less about audio quality. If i can tell direction sound comes from the help me in games, i don't give a crap how clear and crisp it is. I was fine with the sound quality on my cheap headsets. So as far as any of that goes, this headset did fine in this department. 3 very major downsides though, and 1 huge annoyance.

Right off i noticed that the usb charging cord had issues connecting and actually charging the headset. For some reason it was not solidly connected and could jiggle. This has only gotten worse as time went on. I now have to lay my headset at an exact angle at the edge of the desk so the cord hangs down and the connection stays. Any other way and it just won't charge. I don't really know how batteries work, but i think due to the issues i had with charging, the battery life died away really fast as well. It went from about 8 hours of gaming life to 4ish within 8 months. I raid in WoW and it lasts a little longer than the 4 hours of our raid before needing to be plugged in. Once plugged in, since the dongle jiggles, you will find it turning off and on as you move and it connects and disconnects. Each time it reconnects it powers off and then back on. SUPER ANNOYING. When doing said power offage, it makes a ping to everyone in discord/mumble for me to let them know. Its a huge joke now. They all know when i have it plugged in.

The other issue i had was because of how i had to position the headset so it would charge, it put stress on the plastic that connected to the headband and cracked. I had to rig it with some nice electrical tape so it wouldn't break further. It has held, but don't feel like its a good design or craftsmanship here.

The software the the programmable buttons is fairly nice but it comes with a downside. The buttons seem to work until the unit powers itself on then off. After which point the buttons no longer work. To get them to work again.... i must restart my computer. Much more a hassle than it is worth to even use the things. It was one of the selling points to me, and i never even get to use it anymore.

The annoyance comes from the power button. This thing powers on and off as i said above at will when you have it plugged in, and even if u turn it off, if u plug it in it will randomly power on. Well sometimes after it dies, and you plug it in, u have to press and hold down hard to get it to power back on. Seems fairly random exactly how long you have to hold it. Sometimes 5 seconds sometimes 10. If you don't do it exactly right you can hold it down till you are ready to smash it to pieces. Its a power button, make it simple and do what its supposed to do, holy crap.

I have since seen that many others have had this issue and a few people i play games with have had the same issues with the breaking point and the charging dongle. Figured after this amount of time i should write a review letting you know our frustrations.

text:

After doing some research, this has been an ongoing problem with this brand of Logitech headsets for 4-5 years now. Try googling "g90 keeps cutting out" or "g930 losing signal." No fixes presented, such as changing the channel of your wireless router, editing xml files for the Logitech software, or even editing the registry helped. Many, many others echo this experience.

Logitech has given canned responses and generally only offered replacements for the headset.

No fix has been offered to anyone, and no amount of drivers would fix the problem. I would demand a refund but I'm past the 30 day period, so I'm stuck with these garbage headphones.

title: A good headset for the price but not really a good one for gamers
text:
A good headset for the price but their gaming software really sucks.

The headset itself is good. The earpieces fit over the ears nicely and they are very comfortable. I'm able to wear them for hours with no discomfort. Sound quality is good but if you are a audiophile and plan on using them just for music, you'd be better off looking for a more expensive pair. If you just plan on gaming with them, then the sound quality is just fine. The range is very good with them as well. I was able to get up, go to the bathroom (With the door closed) with two walls between me and the transmitter and not have it drop audio once.

However...

In order to use the 7.1 Surround Sound, you need to go to their website and download their driver software and this is where things fall apart. The software is totally buggy and a piece of crap to put it mildly. It's ok if you are only planning on running one thing at a time but, if you are a gamer, it's going to cause you some heartache.

If you are like most gamers, you will have a voioce chat service up like Teamspeak while running your favorite MMO or FPS. My MMO of choice happens to be Lord of the Rings Online. I fired up Teamspeak and then Lotro. What I found was that I could chat on Teamspeak but I could not get any audio from Lotro. Subsequently, if I fired up Lotro first, I found that I could hear Lotro fine but I couldn't hear anyone on Teamspeak. And it isn't just MMO's or FPS's that have this problem. With Teamspeak up, I could not hear any other program I launched after Teamspeak be it game or muic.

The only way I was able to fix this was to uninstall their software (Which itself was a pain because AU_.exe kept crashing in the middle of the install. I had to keep trying until I was finally able to get lucky enough have it uninstall before AU crashed). So now, I have a good wireless headset with no Surround Sound and I am unable to adjust the vol on the headset itself. I have to use the vol control on the computer to adjust the vol.

In short, if you just want to do one thing at a time, this is a great headset. If you are a gamer however, the software leaves much to be desired.

That all said, the headphones were functional and had acceptable audio. I was happy to be able to move around the room. They continuously connect and disconnect which is pretty inconvenient. When you do reconnect and happen to by on a voice chat your friends get a very loud beep on the other end.

title: 1 surround being weaker than I would like. With 7
text:
This headset is definitely a more budget version of higher-priced headsets. The sound while listening to music and other media with an audio focus is rather weak overall, with the non-7.1 surround being weaker than I would like. With 7.1 surround sound turned on, the sound does get significantly louder, but in both modes, bass, mids, and highs are all fairly muddy. I have not adjusted the audio settings at all so perhaps this is a fixable issue, but out of the box it is not particularly great. This is not a headset for anyone with an audiophilic nature.

For gaming, the 7.1 surround is still rather weak, with directional audio still there, but rather weak in actual direction. You'll get a tiny boost in directional audio, but not enough to significantly impact gameplay. The soundstage is rather subpar as well, with no real distance for anything happening around you apart. It definitely has better sound when listening to in-game audio, though; while listening to music leaves something to be desired, in-game audio works just fine, The noise isolation is fantastic, even without audio playing, which really helps to immerse you into the game world. There's just the a tiny bit of audio hiss when no audio is present, but its hardly noticeable unless you're looking specifically for it.

The wireless connection works perfectly. I had no problem hearing audio with the USB wireless transmitter within line of sight, which has a decent length of cord for charging (which can be done while the headset is in use) and plugging into your PC's USB jacks. It also works like a charm when not in view, even several rooms away with closed doors in-between. Going out of its advertised range will lead to audio distortion and drops, but within the advertised range it works great.

The headset design is a little unbalanced in my opinion. The left earcup has three media controls(defaults being pause/play, forwards, and backwards), volume wheel and mute button for the microphone, which is also attached to this side. The media controls are all well-spaced and have good tactile feedback when pressed, and the volume control has a weak but noticeable click when adjusting sound levels. At the bottom of the let earcup is the micro-USB jack, which I found rather stiff when plugging and unplugging the headset for charging. The right earcup has...nothing. I would have liked to see some buttons moved to this earcup, as personally I have a tendency to release the mouse rather than the keyboard when I want to grab or alter something in-game and am, like the majority, right-handed.

I haven't used the microphone a ton, but when I have there have been no complaints on the other end for sound quality. It helpfully has a red LED on the end to inform you if you have muted it, and automatically mutes when in an upright position. It bends very nicely side to side, with a stiff enough hold to not shift after positioning but easy enough manipulation when altering the curve. The clamping force of the headset is fine, though it does have a tendency to slide backwards and forwards when I look too far up or down.

Overall, this is a decent budget headset. The sound quality while listening to music leaves something to be desired and the headset's controls are lopsided, but great noise isolation and in-game audio in addition to an excellent wireless connection make this a good solution for anyone looking for a wireless headset specifically for gaming.

title: This was useless and had no change to the behavior
text:
I had this headset for ONE evening. The connection would drop intermittently (about every 2-3 minutes) and reconnect after about 30 more seconds. There are a few different threads on Logitech's support site specifically talking about this issue. The first one recommends changing the .XML file associated with the software that will set the timeout settings for the connection to 0 rather than 900. This was useless and had no change to the behavior.

The second "fix" was to load an older version of the software (LGS_8.87.116) which did help but the disconnections still remained consistent enough to render these headphones useless. I think the underlying issue is that this headset utilizes a 2.4GHz wireless connection and I live in an apartment which is, I assume, saturated with wireless connections. I did notice some slight improvement by manually changing my own 2.4GHz channel from "auto" to a manually set channel. This worked for about an hour but then the same issue persisted.

I decided to then simply cut my loses and return the product since I have only had it one day. I WILL say that the headset itself is fantastic aesthetically and functionally (with the exception of the wireless connection). But I can't even try to deal with the issue so I can enjoy the other features since this issue basically makes the headset useless about 60% of the time. All in all this would have been an amazing buy for the price but Logitech's unusual silence with this well known (now that I researched it) problem is terrible in that there is no foreseeable solution as of yet.

title: Physically the G930 is quite nice and somewhat different from the G35
text:
Five stars with a caveat -- read this if you're having connection drops.

I am a big fan of the G35 wired headset. I've been using it for years without any issues. I picked up the G930 based on many positive experiences with the G35.

Physically the G930 is quite nice and somewhat different from the G35. It's lighter than the G35, the top headband is a little narrower and the mic boom angle when fully lowered is at more downward angle (in G35 it's nearly a 90 degree angle). Time will tell if this one holds up as well as the battle-tested G35 has.

Unfortunately, out of the box the usability of this headset would have made it a one-star product. Luckily, however it now works perfectly. Many reviews report frequent drops and disconnects. I experienced this myself, the headset would shut off on its own in increments of 15 minutes. I tried the solution recommended by some, which entails modifying the manifest config file to prevent the headset from shutting off to preserve battery power -- it didn't help.

In my case, the culprit behind the drops was the Logitech gaming software. I reverted to an older version of the software -- v.8.55, than what is currently offered via the Logitech web site, and the headset has been working flawlessly since then. I have not had a single drop.

The range of the headset is quite good in my experience but not huge. Generally, I am only 2-3 feet from the receiver in a direct line of sight and it works well. Sometimes, I also use it when I am about 10 feet away in a line of sight from the receiver for prolonged periods of time and it still performs well without interruptions. But beyond the radius of 10 or so feet, or with walls in the way I start experiencing occasional drops. So just keep that in mind when considering this headset.

To sum up, it's a bit frustrating that getting the G930 to work involves downgrading the software -- but now that it works, it's perfect. I love not having to be tethered to my computer with a headset wire.

I have a latent onset of internet gaming addiction... I found playing a first person shooter that I was being decimated over and over and really couldn't get how everyone seemed to know exactly where I was. Then another player mentioned hearing movement was key to the game. Obviously my normal 2.1 stereo speakers weren't getting the job done. I ordered these since I wanted to go wireless. They install easily. The headset connects to the base station fast and easily the majority of the time. However, every now and again the headset will inexplicably disconnect and power off. It takes a second to reconnect. This generally happens within the first minute or two of turning on, and I haven't had any problems with that happening in the middle of a game. Overall, I am very pleased. The 7.1 channels makes identifying where the sound is coming from a thousand times easier than my old setup. The mic is clear and no other players have expressed difficulty understanding me. I wouldn't mind if the volume would go a little higher. It's fine, but I have the volume turned all the way up most of the time. The battery lasts for about ten hours, and if it begins to die you can plug in the USB charger while still using the headset. I have not experienced any problems with the power supply. The headset is comfortable to wear. The audio signal is clean with no buzzing or static interference. For t he price, this is the way to go for a wireless 7.1 setup.

title: got a new one within like two days (Thanks Amazon
text:
Had this headset for two weeks, and then it basically stopped being functional. It would cut out every few seconds for up to 30 seconds at a time. "I guess it's defective. Luck of the draw, eh?" Wrong. W-r-o-n-g. Shipped it back, got a new one within like two days (Thanks Amazon!). This one worked just fine, for a few months, then every now and then it would cut out, for no reason at all. Not often, but not uncommon enough for me to go "Oh wow, that was weird!". To my friends it was a relatively common occurrence for my words to be cut-off mid-sentence just to hear a loud noise and me saying "Headset went out again. Anyway..." and continue my thought. A bit after two years of this "living" (if it can even be called that), one of the metal filaments inside the charger on the headset broke off, and it would no longer charge. "Luckily", I had a 3-year warranty. I submitted a ticket to Logitech support on a Wednesday, (November 30), and did not receive a response until the following Monday (December 5). The response I received was a clear copy-paste, which was to be expected of the first email. I filled out the information I was asked to, and then sent it back on the same day. I did not receive a response until that Friday (December 9). I again filled it out on the same day, and sent it back, and then got my final response today, December 13- a Tuesday. I understand how "business days" work, but the email I received said two business days, not four. I then opened a Live Chat to ask to do an exchange, which I tried to explain to the "Agent" as, 'Imagine that you have a rock, which you keep around. Your rock breaks, so you go to the rock supplier. You give him $5 and he gives you a new rock. You go home, take your broken rock, and bring it back to him, and he takes it and gives you the $5 back, since your rock had a warranty'. He said they did not have such services, and basically told me it would take ANOTHER two weeks to get a new headset.

TL-DR; Logitech Customer Support is garbage, and in the future, I will refrain from buying their products. I say this as a loyal customer, typing on a G19 and clicking with a G700s.

title: Good Design/Quality - Poor Reliability
text:
For a Logitech product, I'm very disappointed in the reliability of this headset. The design and build quality are typical (meaning it's good for what it is) for Logitech products but it seems you are playing the build lottery with this headset. It either works great or it doesn't so keep this in mind when you buy. On a brand new desktop system (Windows 10 Home x64) this headset worked fine for 1 day. So I let it charge overnight, ran a WiFi analyzer to ensure that the 2.4GHz spectrum in my office would be clear, adjusted the settings in the Logitech Control Panel and positioned the USB reciever on my desk so it would be just a few inches away from my chair and setup the audio profiles for it and went to bed. The next day, I was ready to enjoy some gaming so I grabbed the headset and it wouldn't turn on under it's own power. I plug it back in and the microphone would work but the speakers would not function. The evening prior it worked fine, even on the "factory charge" right out of the box so I was very perplexed as to how it would simply cease to function. I've built several custom PCs over the years so I'm no stranger to basic troubleshooting with hardware/software issues so I began a 2-3 hour process of troubleshooting the issue:

I went through all the settings, cycled through different USB ports on my desktop, uninstalled/reinstalled the drivers, reinitialized the USB drivers, you name it... I did it. I couldn't get it to work under it's own power and the device became worthless after 1 use. So... feel free to try them out, you might get one that works and it could suite your needs just fine or you may end up getting something that may not be something worthy of a Logitech logo.

title: Extremely comfortable, great sounding, excellent range, great for long gaming sessions. No Mac drivers, but still usable on Mac.
text:
Fits over the ears for extremely comfortable gaming, even for long, multi-hour sessions. They are a bit bulkier than other headphones, but I really don't notice once they're on my head, and they don't fatigue my head/ears like other headsets do. All the bluetooth headsets I've used sound great when used only for listening, but sound terrible when also using for mic input - not sure if that's changed with bluetooth 4. This headset, however, sounds awesome all the time. Great range - I can walk downstairs to my kitchen & still hear/talk on these. The mic boom bends for getting it to that "perfect" spot, and swivels up into a "mute" mode easily when I need it to. The volume knob is much better/easier than having up/down buttons. Even after years of use, the battery life is still great, lasting many hours before I need to plug them in, and if they do die while in use, I simply plug the cord in while I'm wearing them and they're up & running again, charging while I'm using them. I loved them so much, I bought a pair for my best friend to use while we game together, and he loves them as much as I do.

Only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is because I use these with a Mac, and there are *still* no Mac drivers for using the side buttons (other than volume & power). The good news is they still work great overall with my Mac, but I'm disappointed Logitech has never provided Mac-compatible drivers/software, which they have for many of their other products.

title: Good at the beginning, but then it took a Logitech to the knee
text:
I have had this headset for a couple of years now. Certainly not the worst thing I have owned, but it has many, many issues.

Pros:
Pretty comfortable
Surround sound is decent (when it decides to work)
Worked great at first.
Charges via Micro USB, so I will never, ever, ever run out of charging cables.

Cons:
Randomly disconnects and reconnects.
Battery life isn't great (this never really mattered to me, but some may care)
Logitech offers no meaningful support for this product. The newest versions of their awful gaming software don't even recognize the headset, and any new drivers I have installed increase the issues with the surround sound. The fact that I have had to install countless old drivers to try and reproduce the quality I had shortly after I purchased, is in my opinion unacceptable. Any search for issues on their forms usually have one canned response from what is probably a bot account, then the support threads just kind of die after the user fixes their issue on their own. Generally when one spends a decent amount of money on a headset, you would think that the company would offer at least some useful form of support.
Speaking of the Surround Sound, this would be so much better if it worked. Half the time, if I am watching a movie or playing a game, the surround sound switches off and on. It is very noticeable and annoying. Much of the time, when watching the movie, the surround sound kind of completely breaks and makes this clipping sound until you turn it off, at which point the sound coming out of the headset is unbalanced. At first, I thought the unbalanced issue was just a problem with the movies that I was playing, but I tried an older stereo headset I had laying around and everything was balanced perfectly. I ended up fixing the issue by uninstalling every god awful driver which ever came from Logitech and just using the drivers which install automatically when you first plug it in. That solved my balance issue, but there was no surround sound.
Most recently, the headset decided it was never going to turn off again, and ran through its battery life while I was doing other things (like sleeping or during my workday). When I returned, the stupid thing was bouncing between on and off, while murdering its poor defenseless battery. The only way I managed to fix this issue was by using a wall charger while the receiver was unplugged from my computer.

All and all, the headset used to be good, but Logitech's apparent lack of concern for customer satisfaction and inability to care what their software does to their products, make it an overpriced paperweight. For that, they have lost all of my future business, and I would recommend that anyone who has made it this far avoid them as well.
