title: Your average 5$ earbuds are more reliable
text:
Good things first.
The sound quality is what you would expect of the average wireless gaming headset, pretty good, not great. The mic is very good and the volume rocker is handy. The headset is very comfortable, coming from a user who uses it for extended periods. Battery life is pretty meh though.
Now, for the bad:
When I first got the headset, the default driver software that came with Logitech Gaming Software made it sound horrendous. Especially in surround sound mode, it would glitch out and make static at higher volumes. After about a week, I found some older drivers that fixed this up, and for a short while, the headset worked great. Until the surround sound went out.

I have no idea how and why, no idea if it was on the hardware or software side, but the surround sound DOES NOT WORK. I tried reinstalling both the older software and the newer, didn't work. The #1 reason I bought the headset was broken.

Even after I fixed the sound quality, I still have one gigantic complaint that single-handedly manages to bring down my review to 2 stars. This headset is the most unreliable, inconsistent POS on the market. It started about 2 weeks after I fixed the sound quality. I would get the occasional disconnect. No big deal, I figured I could fix it with a little research. Turns out there is a group of people just like me that bought this headset and have had the same problems as me since they bought it. One of them said they returned their pair 3 different times to no avail. Mine wasn't that bad... yet. After about another month I was having disconnects and static very frequently. I figured out that when my phone uses wifi it interferes with the g930s, so now I have to make sure I don't use my phone near the headset. Even when I don't use my phone it still disconnects, a lot. I play competitive CSGO, and I need the headset to hear and communicate with my teammates. Sometimes, when it dies and I turn it back on, it won't play audio until I restart the game. It was then when I realized that this headset wasn't worth the trouble. Right now it says it is connected, and it's the primary device for audio in the control panel, but it still won't play audio for some reason.

To summarize, this headset is not worth 70$, not even 20$. It disconnects even when being charged, it has tons of static interference, as well as sometimes just not working at all. If you are looking for a new PC headset, let me reiterate: A 5$ pair of earbuds is better than this. The only reason it earned more than one star is because of good sound quality (when it doesn't get random static), a good mic and comfort. Get a pair of HyperX Cloud II's instead.

title: Amazing headphones
text:
For amazons low price of $80, you cant go wrong with these headphones. I have had these for a little over a year and I don't have anything to complain about.

Sound quality isn't super amazing, but it is definitely good enough for me, and it is much better then most headphones in this price range.

These headphones are extremely comfortable. I have had many headphones in the past that would start to hurt after wearing them for a few hours, but these never hurt. I wear these for 12 hours straight on some days, and they stay comfortable the entire time.

These headphones are amazing at blocking noise. Since they go all the way around your ears, you don't really hear anything except whats coming through the headphones.

The microphone quality is okay, not that great. I use a Blue Yeti anyways so the microphone doesn't really matter to me.

Another thing I love about these headphones is the charging dock. The wires come all wrapped up in the dock, and you can take out the perfect length, keeping your wires really neat. I love that you can easily wear the headphones while they are plugged in, because the wire can be much longer then a lot of other headsets.

I also love that so many pieces of the headset are replaceable. My ear pads have started to wear off a little, so im going to get new ones soon. You can buy a new battery, charging dock, and all of that stuff for really cheap if anything ever breaks.

The range is amazing on these. I can go outside or to the other side of my house and still be listening to my music, and the quality sounds just as good from 50 feet away as it does from 5 feet away.

Overall, this is an amazing headset for the price. Yes, there are better headphones, but your going to be paying way more for them. These are an absolute steal and I have recommended them to several friends.

title: Best gamepad I've seen so far.
text:
My girlfriend got this for me for my birthday, and I've been using this gamepad for about a week now. Let me just start off by saying that this product is AWESOME! It is really comfortable to use, and the symmetry/ergonomics that it allows is excellent. The placement of the buttons feel very natural. The LCD screen is also a nice little addition. I also own the Logitech G502 mouse, and the gamepad uses the same software which I think is cool because they both integrate really well together. I've only used one of the profiles so far, but they seem like they will be handy to set up for different games and such. The auxiliary buttons next to the joystick work good, and they have a satisfying click to them. The joystick itself doesn't feel too bad to me, however, I probably wouldn't want to use it for a main mode of movement or anything too important. The joystick click feels nice as well.

All that being said, there are a couple of caveats. I think that if Logitech made these few improvements then it would probably be a perfect setup.

1. Mechanical switches.
-Coming from a mechanical keyboard, you can really tell the difference in quality, and I'm sad to say that the keys on this gamepad feel quite 'mushy' comparatively. Even knowing this, however, I'd still recommend this gamepad over any of the other ones I have looked at (and I did look at quite a few reviews before I decided on this one...)

2. Number row.
-Using a keyboard, you have a number row above the letter keys and many games use that row for hot-swap commands. The gamepad feels a little lacking without a number row in my opinion, but I've decided to try and augment some of the number keys to the joystick instead. The gamepad is quite wide, which isn't a bad thing, but I'd easily give up at least one column of keys on the side in order to gain back the number row up top. As it is, there are a couple of buttons to the left of the simulated 'WASD' keys that I do not even have any functions assigned to yet. So, this criticism isn't a complete deal-breaker in my opinion. We'll just have to see how it works out.

That's all I can think of for now, If I come up with anything else I'll do an update.

1/4/17
I have noticed a bug in the software. After waking my computer from sleep mode, the software needs to be restarted in order to work properly again. I don't have any idea why it does this, but maybe if I send an email to support they will hopefully fix it in an update or something.

title: The headset is very comfortable to wear
text:
I have been using these headphones for about two months now for both personal and business use. I bought them on the recommendation of a gaming buddy who used the G930 for about three years. Both of us work remotely and have used them for remote meetings and VoIP phone calls in addition to playing MMOs.

The headset is very comfortable to wear. It's relatively lightweight for its size and the ear cushions are very soft and cushy. I've had no problems wearing it throughout my workday for conference calls or for hours at a time gaming with friends. Music, sounds, and voices all come through clearly and beautifully, whether you're using surround sound or not. The microphone quality is excellent compared to the cheap work-provided headset I had been using previously. Both my coworkers and gaming group immediately noticed a difference once I switched. The microphone auto-mutes when you flip up the stem (very useful during conference calls). There is also a mute button on the left earpiece, but I prefer to flip the mic up and down as a visual reminder.

I've found the battery to last around 9 hours of constant use (close enough to Logitech's claim of ten hours). I like the design of the included wireless adapter/charging base, which neatly stores your wrapped charging cables when not in use.

Range of use may be an issue for you if you live in a large and/or multi-story house and want to move around a lot while wearing this headset. This hasn't been an issue for me as my apartment is only 750 sq. ft. I have been able to keep participating in conference calls while pacing all around my apartment. My aforementioned friend also likes to pace during conference calls (or make a trip to the fridge), however he upgraded to a higher-end headset because the G930's range did not reach from his office on the second story to the ground floor of his house. If you are primarily going to use this while sitting at your computer, this won't be a problem for you.

The sound quality is what I expected, pretty good, with good surround, but the 'sidetone' setting produces a slight static hiss at all times even if the mic is off. That's really confusing to me, I can understand if the mic is ON and picking up background noise, but when it's off?

I 'upgraded' to this from a wired G430, which is almost the exact same thing except for the buttons on the headset itself, and there are a LOT of cons in comparison. The mic quality is abysmal compared to the G430. I'm seriously considering returning it for a full refund and moving to something else.

title: Convenience and decent sound quality; abysmal battery life and random connectivity issues.
text:
Pros:
- Mic and sound quality is pretty good.
- Wireless capability is super convenient.
- Earpiece controls work great for changing songs or volume from afar.
- Construction isn't too bad (not as great as the G35s though, due to these having rotating ear cups).

Cons:
- Battery life sucks. Within the first few months of owning these it isn't so noticeable, as you'll be getting around 4-6 hours unplugged. I've had these since December and I now get about 2 hours of charge before they die.
- Connectivity issues. Sitting at your desk near the adapter with these on you'll have little to no issues with connectivity. Walking any distance away from the adapter however, expect random disconnects and reconnects from the headset. It's extremely annoying.
- Trouble being recognized by Logitech software. I've had on-and-off problems with the Logitech software program recognizing this headset, which prevents me from altering any of the G-keys on the earpiece.

Overall:
I'd say either A.) stick with the wired version of these (G35), as they're pretty much superior in every way; or B.) save your money for a much higher-quality headset that may last longer.

title: The Best Headset I've Ever Had
text:
I have a friend who has used this headset for about 3 years now I believe and so I was convinced to purchase one for myself when my old headset gave out. I've used it for over a week now and I really love this headset. A quick look at what I use it for; gaming (mmo's, various Steam games), listening to music, watching movies, chatting on Skype. Below is a little more information on my opinion of the G930.

I'll outline a few pros and cons for those of you still on the fence:

Pros:
Comfort: Headset is light enough that once you wear it for a while you begin to forget it's there. Does not touch my ears except for the slightest feather touch on the very edges, just enough to realize you're wearing a headset until you're distracted by something.
Good adjustment options to move and shape to fit your head.
Noise cancelling is very good, all noises are well muffled by headset design and helps, especially in gaming, to achieve that immersion into the world you're playing in.

Ease of use: Only took a minute of reading the quick start guide to understand the features and what the light indicators mean; the Logitech Gaming Software isn't too hefty a program and it's handy to use to tell you just how long your battery has and for programming your headset.
Roll button for volume on the headset left side is genius, easy to to quickly change volume.

Performance: Sound is fantastic, the surround sound demo on the Logitech Gaming Software scared the daylights out of me with its realistic sounds; this headset is only limited by the quality of the input it receives. The bass actually sounds like bass too, which is another plus.
Mic sounds great, keystrokes are muffled but voice comes through crystal clear even without adding background noise cancellation.

Cons:
Auto-shutoff: This was going to be the thing that knocked a couple stars off my rating, but my friend gave me a tip about how to fix it and it's been a lifesaver. The problem is that the auto-shutoff only allows the headset to stay on for maybe 15 to 20 minutes at a time. It seems to be quite determined to shut itself off whether you like it or not, no matter what you're doing. This was very annoying straight off, as I would have to scramble to find the small button to press and hold slightly to turn the headset back on, and in the mean time I was missing something. The fix I spoke of requires a bit more than the average computer user will do in their normal interaction with a computer, but it was simple enough and fixed the problem. Now, if the headset does decide to shut off, it comes right back on again; occasionally not even shutting off at all.
Not enough to knock off a star since there is a fix, but certainly a frustrating con as a new owner.

Battery Life: I wish this could be a pro, but it's a con because although the headset does run on battery for a good long while, I do find myself somewhat confused at the inconsistencies I've noticed. While the Logitech Gaming Software does give relatively accurate battery usage in real time, right now, as I write this, my has gone from 10 hours remaining, to 8 hours remaining, and it has only been 15 minutes. Now, this could be due to the fact that it was not fully charged to begin with, however, I do find that a bit odd. I have, however, used it for quite a few hours before it alerted me it needed to be charged, so all in all I really can't complain too much.

Charging: This is more of a pet peeve, but for some reason I have a real whale of a time getting the charger cord plugged into the headset to charge it. I fumble and fuss, usually taking the headset off my head and glaring at the cord trying to figure out which way it goes in, since it only plugs in one way. Occasionally the planets align perfectly at just the right moment and I pop the cord in without batting an eye (or taking off the headset), thankfully it's become slightly easier now that I'm getting the hang of it.

Honestly I can't think of anything else that I would consider a con. I really love this headset and I hope to have it for years to come, just like my friend has. If you're still not sure, it's not terribly expensive, and I promise if you're using a wired headset that you're going to love going wireless, and the sound is fantastic!

text:
This headset has been absolutely abysmal since day 1.

Pros:
* Wireless 7.1 sound is decent
* When it actually works it's nice

Cons:
* Day 1 red flag: headset would turn off after 5 minutes of no activity (including radio silence). You would be talking to yourself for a bit before realizing the headset died (no warning sounds or anything either). Eventually this was patched and now you can actually set the timer to "Never" go to sleep.
* One update managed to cause the mic to sometimes get stuck on mute. You'll see the red light on the mic, but you can't unmute it.
* Every so often the headset just becomes "unresponsive" (especially frequent on software updates) - they actually recommend you re-flash the firmware with a /force option to bring it back alive
* The headset constantly just decides to reboot on its own. When it does this and comes back alive, other USB devices (keyboard, mouse) are disabled for a good 5 seconds. No other USB device causes this issue.
* Recently, the headset's mic just decided to stop working. No amount of re-flashing or re-installing drivers has fixed this. It is still an issue and Logitech support is very slow to act on the ticket I claimed.

I would not recommend purchasing this device unless you enjoy dealing with faulty products all the time.

text:
EDIT:

I now have had the mouse for over a week and I must admit that it has charmed me. Although the original nuisances mentioned below are still present, the feel and precision of this mouse has won me over. It's pointer and mouse clicks are crisper than all winter chill gum commercials ever made.

Original:
I just left work where I was using my MX Performance and came home to unpack and commence my bonding ritual with the MX Master. Well, I must admit that the Master isn't that much of a master.

Bad thoughts:
1. If it were on Tinder, I'd swipe left. It is too angular (not that I dislike people with angular features, I love that actually, mice are different.)
2. The feel is strange. The MX Performance (and even the MX Revolution which I also had) are natural for my hand. On this mouse, the palm rest area feels steep and the thumb curve that enable me to rest my hand but rather have it awkwardly hang off of the mouse.
3. The forward/backward buttons are too high. Previously, I could use those buttons with a minor thumb twitch. Now they are much higher which isn't as ergonomic as it used to.
4. Software issue: this is a high precision mouse that can take a full-sensitivity setting. However, even on highest sensitivity with the current software, the mouse doesn't move as much across the screen as I'd like it to. (easily fixable in future updates, hope it does goes fixed).

Good thoughts:
1. Button clicks feel solid and I love the tactile response.
2. The side scrolling button is a neat feature, we'll how how it works out.
3. The software. It's light, it's nimble, it's functional. It doesn't clutter like SetPoint. <3 <3 <3
Good thoughts:
1. The clicks feel sharp

title: You can do better!
text:
Pros: Cheap, comes with tons of tips and a stylish case. Decent background noise isolation. Flat cord is fairly tangle-resistant. Having a volume dial on the cord is convenient.

Cons: This headset has probably the absolute worst microphonics (scraping noise from friction) I've ever experienced. Everytime the cord brushes up against your clothes or skin, you can hear it. LOUDLY. Running or even walking with these is near impossible. You'll hear the scraping louder than your music. Logitech must know this is a problem since their website specifically mentions this and suggests two solutions: 1) Use the included clip to attach the clip closer to your shirt to minimize rubbing (didn't work in my case and the clip went missing after like a month) 2) Loop the headphones OVER your ear and basically put them in upside down. This essentially cinches them tight to your ear. There's still a decent amount of noise but it's listenable.

All this would be OK if the sound was great, but to be honest it's muffled and mediocre, and QUIET. You have to really jack up the volume to hear anything out of these. Oh, one last thing - the tips on these pop out incredibly easy. I've had the tips repeatedly stay stuck in my ears when i took these out, that's how easily they pop off. You definitely want to use the case because quickly stashing them in a pocket or backpack will result in missing tips.

So yeah, Logitech products are usually great, I don't know what happened here. They're nice to keep around as a backup pair but that's about it.

text:
If you demand high quality sound, this is NOT the system for you. If you just want a cheap speaker system for background music with a bit of a thump, this system is great. The high end is a bit "tinny", and the voice sounds hollow. The bass box delivers a thump, but not the low rumbling bass you would expect from a bass box. When cranked up, it will really shake the room, but it's due to the hard hitting mid bass, and not the low rumbling bass.

The speakers are small, and perfect for my desk, with a volume control / power switch in the speaker line so you can place the volume control in a convenient spot (I mounted mine to the side of my desk, out of view). The bass box is smaller than a shoebox, so it doesn't take up much space.

My only comparison is to speaker systems 10x to 30x this price, so I feel the poor sound quality is offset by the cheap price.

title: Barely better than three or four dedicated remotes; glitchy app, not recommended.
text:
Logitech gets two stars from me only because I realize how daunting the development and testing of such a device can be. My overall satisfaction is truly closer to one star. I am very tempted to return the device, because while it is less bulky than three separate remotes, it is much more awkward to use, because of having to switch the context (device being controlled) of the remote all the time, and becoming accustomed to awkward button to function mappings. Buttons are too squishy. Labeling of buttons is far too small. No lighting of buttons other than the device selector button to indicate which device is the current one. Watch TV Activity is very touchy - I finally made it suitable by setting it up to leave my receiver on all the time and then fiddling with the inter device delay (which I only learned about by accident while doodling around with the menus in the app.) Instructions online in the support area, describing how to adjust input control for various devices was incorrect. And finally, I have to keep unplugging and re-plugging the USB cable, and waiting for an interval until the "hand" icon shows up while hovering the sync button before it will actually sync (update the remote with the settings entered into the app.)

The only positive thing that *may* come of this purchase is that it will probably inspire me to develop a more sensibly designed universal remote. This one is reminiscent of the amazingly convoluted user interfaces that early VCR's sported, better suited to Japanese assembly-language programmers (who tend to think in binary or hex anyway.)

title: Terrific speakers for the money
text:
Wow. I upgraded from my old Altec Lansing 2.1 compact computer speakers (5-inch subwoofer) that have been doing desk duty for the last seven or eight years to this Logitech set and I am impressed with the major performance boost. The old set was actually quite punchy for its size, but the Logitechs have revealed how lacking the high end and "presence" was.

On unboxing, I immediately powered the system up for a test drive, connected my phone's audio jack and went through my music library to flex the speakers' muscles. With the big subwoofer box one of course expects heavy bass capability and the Z623 doesn't disappoint. More important, the satellite speakers provide far better high end and "sound space" than did the satellites on my old set. Spatial awareness is vastly improved, and subtle sounds on the higher end were far more obvious than before. Overall, the new set handled every type of music, from delicate classical to bass thumper tracks that I threw at it. I was impressed all the way through.

Getting the system attached to the computer, I was able to run through some videos, gaming, and more music at the computer desk and my favorable impression remained. These speakers are powerful. They pack a lot of wattage, so the volume can be cranked to excessive levels quite easily, enough to overdrive the subwoofer. Thankfully there is the bass control to dial in as much bass response as you need, all the way down to none at all. Boost it way up for games and movies, dial it back for excessively bass-heavy music tracks; the knob is in easy reach right there on the satellite with the power and volume controls.

I compared these to the Klipsch Promedia 2.1s, their obvious direct competition, and it's a tough call. I wasn't able to do a side by side, since no store had both sets on display together, but I got the impression that the Klipsch speakers had a bit of an edge in sound quality, but the Logitechs packed more punch. Which to choose? Pretty close call, and may come down to listening to both and deciding which you like best.

Any cons? So far I've only had minor ones, for example the lack of any contrast markings on the control knobs. It's impossible to see where the volume and bass knobs are set in lower light, since the marking is just a groove the same color as the rest of the knob. Nothing a dab of white out won't fix. I also would like a bit more weight in the satellite with the controls. They have very nice tacky pads on the bottom to keep them in place, but a bit more weight would help. Really though, we're just picking nits here, I am very happy with the speakers, and I hope they last at least as long as my (still working) old set.

USAGE UPDATE: I've had more time to really put these speakers through their paces and I am thrilled with the performance. I look forward to listening to music on my computer again, and I love firing up a game and cranking up the volume and bass to literally feel that subwoofer rumble. This system hits loud and hard, and after dabbing some "White Out" on the knobs so I can see where they are set, I have no operational complaints at all. Outstanding performer, and I would definitely buy them again.

title: A great way to combine all you remotes into 1. Easy to setup!
text:
Very easy to program! Just put in your devices by model number and tell it where everything is connected (e.g. DVD is on input 1 on the TV). The software download from the Internet. Worked great on my MacBook Pro 15 (late 2013). You need to plug in the remote to program it (they call it sync) once everything is setup and it includes a USB to micro USB cable, so if you have a laptop with the new USB C connector, you will need to use an adaptor or buy a new cable, so new MacBook Pro (late 2016+) and MacBook users will need to figure out a cable solution.

The Ultime One is IR, it doesn't include the RF base, but the base can be bought separately at a later date if you decide you need RF.

We have Roku 3 and 4 players, which use RF on their included remotes, however the Roku player can receive IR too, but it's not as responsive as it is with RF. You also need to point the remote at the player, which you may not be used to if you use the Roku remote a lot. My daughter complained at first but I removed the battery from the old tv and Roku remotes (so they don't leak over time) and put them away, so she has to use the Logitech. After a few days she adapted to having to point the remote. Hopefully your significant other or kids are as flexible ;)

The touch screen is responsive and easy to use. You can swipe over from the actions screen to the gesture screen and use it to easily raise or lower the volume (swipe up or down on the screen instead of using the volume up down buttons). It works great and so far I'm very happy with the purchase.

1 star reduction because of the lower IR output requiring aiming more to use it.

title: Made for Live Streamers (YouTube, Facebook, Twitter)
text:
This Logitech Pro Steam webcam is specifically designed for professional streamers. If you "go live" on the internet or do live, online gaming where you project your head into the game, this is the camera designed specifically for your use. The camera will stream 30 frames per second at 1080p and 60 frames per second at 720p.

The camera mounts on your monitor, and has a flexing arm on it so that you adjust the camera angles as desired. The camera arm will flex up to 7" over your monitor. The camera can rotate on the arm up to 360 degrees. The power/USB cord is 6' long, with adequate reach for desktops or laptops.

Just like the other Logitech cameras I have used, the microphones are on both sides of the camera lens.

In the box, you get: camera with mount and USB cord, Setup Guide (how to mount the camera), Safety and Warranty sheet, and a trial license for the xSplit service.

The camera's main feature is the ability to remove or replace backgrounds using software. If you have used green screens in the past (think online gaming video streams), then this camera removes the need for a green screen. You will need to install software to get the background function to work (XSplit, ChromaCam, OBS). This is an inexpensive way to get green screen functions, provided your computer has the hardware necessary to support it (you're going to give your computer's hardware a workout running the software live if you don't have good memory on board, a fast processor, and swift uplink).

The camera with the six-month xSplit license is exclusive to Amazon.

It is very light and compact and is really meant to be portable but doesn’t come with a case. I don’t tote it around so that is no loss for me - I use it on a desk.

title: The angle feature works well
text:
My review is for the folio case, which does not have a keyboard. I am comparing this case to a Solo folio. I prefer this folio to the Solo folio for several reasons. While I consider this case to be better than the Solo, it is still not perfect.

My Solo folio has a denim-like exterior that I prefer over the rather plain exterior of this folio.

Installing my iPad Pro was quite easy. Indeed, it was almost too easy and I was not sure whether the iPad was really secure in this folio. The Solo folio completely locks the iPad Pro into the case, which I like. On the other hand, the iPad installs from the direction of the hinge in this folio, so the iPad is not going to fall out of the case.

In spite of a better appearance and a more secure locking arrangement, this folio beats the Solo folio in performance.

First, this folio has a magnetic cover closure, which I like. My Solo folio has no lock of any kind on the cover, so the cover can flop open if not held.

Second, this folio has a much broader range of angles at which the iPad can be oriented. Furthermore, the design of the folio is such that the iPad stays at a set angle fairly well. I used the folio while surfing, switching screens, and sliding, and the angle remained fixed. The Solo folio is limited to five specific angles, and the iPad likes to slip if you press too hard. I think the Logitech Create folio wins for these features.

The buttons of the iPad, power, volume up, and volume down, are exposed on the Solo. The buttons are covered on this folio, with buttons built into the folio that press on the iPad buttons. The buttons on the Create folio can be a little difficult to press. I believe that accessing the buttons directly on the Solo folio is a better way to control the iPad, so for button access, the Solo wins for this feature.

As you can see, this folio contains a mixed bag of useful features and less useful features. I am a fan of the angle feature on this folio, which is important to me. I am also a fan of the magnetic closure. For looks and button access, the Solo is, in my opinion, a better folio. On balance, I give the nod to the Logitech Create folio. However, both folios could use improvements. Indeed, if the best features of each folio were combined, the result could be a five star product.

Enjoy!

title: A unique keyboard and mouse combination that you'll enjoy
text: Best keyboard and mouse you can possibly use. Logitech has made a keyboard that has the buttons pop out like a wave. This design helps to type both easier and faster. All the labels and controls of the keyboard are correctly placed along with some hotkeys for easy access to the calculator, windows scrolling, shutting down your computer, etc. The keyboard uses 2 double A batteries to function/power on, you insert these in the back of the keyboard on the bottom. Also located in the back of the keyboard are 2 mini stands that can pop out and make the keyboard tilted at an angle for you to type, rather than being flat. This is good to use on a desk or any other flat surface if you choose to do so. The mouse has a unique and fitting shape for the palm of your hand. It slides very smoothly and is sensitive, but not too sensitive when scrolling or moving. The best feature of the mouse are the 'back' and 'forward' hotkeys on the left side, just by clicking either one it can send your web page back or forward without having to scroll all the way up to your browser to click. The mouse uses 1 double A battery to function/power on, this is located on the back of the mouse.

title: Great inexpensive controller.
text:
This controller is pretty much a nice basic xbox/ps3 combination feel. The controller sometimes feels a little small in my hands and lightweight but overall I am comfortable with it in my hands. The controller can work with any game that allows the use of non-keyboard devices and can be reprogrammed often through the games themselves. No need to worry about what if its a playstation or xbox port. It will still work.

The analog sticks have a nice gripped coating that your thumbs will be able to hold onto without slipping off, especially with the ole mountain dew and Doritos fingers we all love. The response time between the controller and the computer are pretty seamless thanks to the direct wire connection through a usb port. Often wireless ones will have a bit of a delay so this is where the non-wireless comes in handy. I use this a lot when I play rocket league and even after hours of use, it doesn't feel bulky or hurt my hands at all. I think that is where the lightweight feel becomes a major benefit.

The other big benefit is that these controllers are very inexpensive. You can often find a good deal here on amazon or check any local electronics store as this is the most common controller you will find near you for PC. I would definitely recommend this controller to anyone in need of one. Happy gaming!

title: Nearly a decade later, still the best.
text:
I have had this webcam for nearly 10 years now. I hope you find this review in the sea of already overwhelming support for this product because I am not just one of those I bought it, used it, liked it and reviewed it people. This camera is almost a decade old and it still works as if it were brand new freshly taken out of the box. It has gone down in price since it first hit the market so if you're looking for a deal I would say this is one already. I was willing to pay more and I don't regret having done so in the past for this truly top of the line webcam.

The built in audio mics do a wonderful job picking up sounds whether you're using them for business or personal use, speaking loudly, or whispering quietly. The sound pics up well from all directions so as you move around the room your receiving party won't get that weird sense of you walking around in an echo chamber getting quieter and louder as you move in the slightest with many other cameras.

The camera is very good at capturing your target in all lighting ranges. Ive used this webcam early on before I bought a DSLR to take some high definition photos with the supported software. The clip on the webcam is also very simple in its design yet effective, allowing it to easily clip onto any computer or device or even just on a desk nearby if you so felt inclined.

The biggest selling point for me at this point if you are considering this camera is the fact that after 10 years, this model is still leading the market, and has become cheaper while never losing its edge over the competition, thats how great this device is.

Let me start my saying that this mouse is amazing and I love it.
Pros:
-The scroll wheel is amazing and I love that it does NOT have the tilt function.
-The mouse fits my hand like a glove and is great to use for long periods of time.
-The charging port is at the top is na position that allows the mouse to still be in use even when it is charging with the included one meter cable.
-The USB dongle allows for the mouse to be used for a system that does not have bluetooth and works great.
-The material that the mouse is coated in feels comfortable and gripy (if that is a word) but is not something you have to worry about getting dirty.
-The software that accompanies the mouse allows a lot of adjustability and is almost complete control over what any button does.

Cons:
-The side scroll wheel and buttons are slightly too far back and the smaller button of the two is just not useable without repositioning of your hand.
-The "gesture" button that you press with your thumb is just in the wrong place. The moment that you use the mouse you will wonder why it is not on the side of the mouse such that you can squeeze your thumb into your palm. Instead you have to press down with your thumb in a way that is just unnatural. (Note- some say the button feels vague, I found this to not be the case, it is just not in the right spot).
-The edge of the thumb button is not attached to the frame to allow it to move properly, the downside is that I think it will collect grime rather quickly.
-The USB dongle is amazing, but the mouse has no storage space for said dongle. This is a major oversight on Logitech's part.
-The gesture feature is a waste of effort, mostly because of the position of the button but also because Mac OSX does it better.

title: The mouse charged just fine. The keyboard was completely unresponsive
text:
I had problems with this right from the start. The mouse charged just fine. The keyboard was completely unresponsive. I figured out the batteries in the keyboard were completely dead, and in order to charge it apparently requires at least *some* juice. So I took the batteries out of the keyboard and gave them a jump start by charging them in the mouse. That worked. Problem solved.

Next I noticed that the batteries don't hold a charge for as long as I'd hoped. I found I had to plug them in once a day to keep things running smoothly. It didn't take them long to charge. But I'd hoped they'd hold a charge for longer than a day.

Sometimes the mouse isn't very responsive. At first I thought it was the unifying receiver dongle being too far away. I plugged the USB extension in and brought the dongle up close - within inches of both the keyboard and the mouse. It helped, but didn't completely solve the problem. When it's acting up, this is a real show stopper.

Another show stopper - they keyboard doesn't always light up when it's supposed to. Yes, I know about the little app that comes with it and the function key you have to hit to set the lighting to max. It works. Sometimes. Sort of. I don't mind that it only stays lit for a short time. I understand that's to save battery power. But what I DO mind is that it often doesn't light up at all. It's very inconsistent and unpredictable. I don't see very well, which is why I wanted a backlit keyboard to begin with.

The look and feel of the keyboard and mouse - when everything is working the way it should - is good. Otherwise, I'm finding this a waste of money. I liked the idea of going wireless. Guess I have to bite the bullet and go back to a wired mouse and keyboard. In any case, I won't be using this combo much longer and will be very suspicious of any similar products in the future.

title: Not satisfied with Mac Bluetooth connectivity.
text:
I am not pleased with this mouse. First of all, no fault of the mouse, but it's a bit large for my smallish female hand.

Secondly, and more importantly, the Bluetooth connection is not completely reliable with my MacBook Pro. When the mouse has not been used for a bit and I come back to is, sometimes I have wait up to 30 seconds for my computer to recognize the mouse. This is completely unacceptable for professional use. I can't tell my boss, standing over my shoulder, to "just wait a sec" when I need to show him something. I do not have this problem at all with my Bluetooth Microsoft Sculpt Mouse.

Apparently, this is a known issue at Logitech because there are some recommendations about what to do about it. One of the suggestions is to use the dongle that came with mouse so you can use Logitech's proprietary unified wireless connection. This is not a useful suggestion for me. I specifically looked for a Bluetooth mouse so that I can use any and all of my USB ports for hard drive connections, not mice, and I never want to have to worry about losing the tiny thing that I need to make the mouse work.

It's disappointing to me, but if your need are different, you may be very happy with this mouse. It gets 3 stars because it's a decent mouse if the issues above are not a problem for you.

I would stay away from this speaker set.

title: I refuse to buy any other keyboard
text:
Once upon a time, I searched long and hard for a basic, practical, wired and illuminated keyboard. It was a frustrating process sifting through all of the ugly, tacky "gaming" keyboards, but I finally found this little beauty, and never looked back.

Simple, mature design, and individually lighted keys that have a nice feel, and good feedback. This model has been on the market forever, and is probably still the best wired and illuminated keyboard out there. My biggest gripe is that the F keys arent fully lit. Only the alternate functions are illuminated, and I dont use them enough to associate the alt function symbols with their respective F number.

A couple of things to keep in mind:

While it is more than sturdy enough to handle constant use, it isnt built to handle big impacts. I had to buy another one after giving my old one a hefty slam with my fist during a bout of gaming. Even though it remained perfectly functional, the J key was dislodged, and I managed to break the clasps trying to get it back in.

I also discovered it isnt waterproof after giving an even older one a bath... It can handle common spills, but if you run it under a warm faucet for a few minutes trying to clean it, you might run into some issues.

title: Great receiver, terrible experience
text:
Alright, first off, let's get the good things out of the way. This receiver has great range, even through walls and piping. The sound quality is excellent, the build quality solid, and the pairing button has a satisfying click to it.

Sounds pretty sweet, right? So why the two stars?

Simple. If you own more than one BT receiver (one in another room, a portable one for headphones, one in a home theater receiver, even one in your friggin car) this receiver will steal connection to your devices from them and keep stealing it until you either upair from it or unplug the friggin thing. Telling it to disconnect lasts, at most, 10 seconds.

That, to me, is unacceptable. In today's world where *everything* has Bluetooth, having the expectation that a user will only have need for *one* receiver is unreasonable to the point of foolishness.

Despite how well it performs, I can't use this. Its fundamentally unusable to me.

Your mileage may vary, of course.

title: The Harmony hub tries to solve all your problems in home media, unfortunately, what it really does is trade some for others.
text:
At first, this Harmony set seems as if it might be your dream come true. You can configure it with a smart phone. You don't need to be a programmer, and you don't have to cash in your 401k to buy it. Unfortunately, while the setup is simple and straight-forward, you will quickly find it lacking in important features and reliability.

Pros:
- Simple setup
- Affordable
- Nice remote controls that feel good in the hand
- Often simplifies very tedious tasks such as using four different remote controls to watch TV
- Very nice compatibility with some smart-home technologies, such as Hue lights

Cons:
- Often locks up and needs to be power-cycled
- Proprietary 2.5mm infrared "headphone" jacks, rather than the industry standard 1/8th inch that you can buy at your local radioshack
- Lack of flexibility in programming. No PC programming support without hooking up a cable. Likewise, no control from your PC. Only smart-phones.
- Lack of Amazon Echo support

text:
I would not have any other mouse type device than a trackball because it's super fast with minimal movements. Takes a little practice getting used to, but doesn't everything? I do a LOT of writing and other keyboard stuff and I cannot work on a regular keyboard and mouse. My trackball is on a little stand I built right below the space bar and between my two hands so I can easily reach it and I do not need another surface for the mouse. My keyboard is also mounted above my notebook's keyboard so I use the notebook's monitor and the whole apparatus goes - well, on my laptop! Perfect posture for typing, nice and close, and the viewing angle is also perfect, slightly down, easy on the neck. I've used the microsoft ergonomic keyboards and trackball this way for years. the ergo keyboard allows hands to be at an angle and the mouse is also oriented diagonally so that the right hand is "on axis" when I shift 4 inches left to rest my hand on it.

There are two things that would be a big improvement. First, make it USB instead of needing a separate input device. What's the big deal about freeing up a usb port because it's wireless, only to lose it to the Logitech "unifying" dongle???? Second, it takes some ingenuity to get the mouse positioned exactly right, below the spacebar and between the hands, and at such an angle that the wrist is not cramped, but rather straight, both in the horizontal plane (left-right) and the vertical. Actually it probably should get 5 stars but I gave 4 in hopes Logitech would take notice, fat chance huh?

text:
Would've loved to add 5 stars like anticipated, however, issues developed less than a month upon receiving it back in March.
POSITIVES: 1. Great crisp feeling of pressing the keys which personally helps me type faster. My old rubber keyboard case practically had me slamming fingers down on each key to type. 2. Loved being able to stand up my iPad like a laptop. Stand holds iPad extremely sturdy. All of my previous cases were impossible to hold upright. 3. Bluetooth is 110% reliable. Never disconnects from the iPad, even after using it for college classes (worst WiFi in America). 4. iPad remains lightweight with keyboard attached. Since I need my computer for to write class notes, I bought this keyboard to prevent breaking my back further by carrying a 200 lb macbook pro everywhere. 5. Duo function- keyboard plus latches as case. 6. Very similar appearance to mac keyboards.

NEGATIVES: 1. Magnetic latch- too weak, detaches effortlessly from iPad. 2. Latch causes iPad to detach when opening passed latch's max. rotation. Cannot use iPad as handheld device while temporarily fully opening attached keyboard case (ex.flips behind iPad, power off) and/or closing/utilizing keyboard later. Basically, keyboard must be detached from iPad to use as handheld device. And MOST IMPORTANTLY: 3. Only used keyboard approx. 7-8 times then keys suddenly stopped working (ex. 'X', Caps Lock, right arrow). While trying to type notes rapidly during lectures, auto correct & other alternatives don't always come in handy. Unsuccessfully attempted to reconnect Bluetooth, restart, hold down unresponsive keys,and pull them off to check for any issues underneath. Basically, Whats the use of a keyboard with broken keys?
Very disappointed..overall, this device had great potential, remains scratch marks/particle-free & suited up to my needs..until main point of "KEYboard" failed to properly function WAYYYY unacceptably soon after receiving it
Would LOVE suggestions forr fixing problems and/or recommendations for equivalent products with higher quality!!!

title: The HD Pro C920 produces some of the best video quality available in a webcam
text:
The HD Pro C920 produces some of the best video quality available in a webcam. It shoots and streams in 1080p at 30 fps, it records dynamic stereo audio and it can even produce stills at up to 15 megapixels. Features like tripod compatibility, motion detection and face tracking help make this our top choice. There are many web cameras on the market today that boast the ability to shoot full 1080p HD video. While this is technically true, many such models can only shoot or stream in 1080p at the cost of a lowered framerate. This means the footage they produce will be high resolution, but the video will appear jerky or sluggish.

As one of the best webcam companies out there, Logitech offers great support for its products. The C920 comes with a two-year warranty, so you can be confident that your webcam is protected. I actually had my camera stop responding after about 16 months. I contacted logitech and with no questions asked, they shipped me out a brand new replacement.

The Logitech HD Pro C920 is the best camera I have tested in pretty much every way. It offers the best video and audio quality, the most features, the most useful design and some of the best support in the industry. This webcam consistently delivers appealing results, although you do pay for the extra performance. However, if you want top-notch image quality, tripod compatibility and face tracking, this device is your best option.

title: If you work on a computer a lot and want to use nice equipment, then I would definitely recommend this mouse
text:
First of all: Yes, this is an expensive mouse. If it's too expensive then move along.

If you work on a computer a lot and want to use nice equipment, then I would definitely recommend this mouse. The Logitech MX series has a reputation, and this model is worthy as a successor.

I have a Razer Mamba at work, and it is a great mouse as well, but the price was even steeper and the wireless battery life was a joke. I desperately needed a mouse that was bluetooth capable and had good battery life for a home theater system.

I'm also a fan of larger mice because they are much more comfortable. At first I thought this mouse was actually too light, but after using it for a bit I think it is perfect.

For multitaskers, switching between apps using the thumb-rest button is great (similar to alt-tab on the keyboard). It's fully programmable so you can set it to do something different if you'd like.

The scrollwheel is incredible. I scroll though things just to feel it go into "free-spinning" mode, then go back into normal scrolling with a satisfactory "click" once it slows down. Great for going to the top of a website or document if you find yourself drowning and don't have the "home" key handy on a keyboard.

I haven't found use for the horizontal scroll wheel yet, but it feels very sturdy and accurate. Most reviewers mention it is excellent for video editing.

If you haven't tried a larger mouse before, go to a store and test one out before buying. A lot of people seem to have an issue with larger mice, but I think that's just because they feel so different at first. I LOVE large, well designed mice. My hands are normal sized for an adult, and I don't think it would be too large for anyone unless they are either very young or a very very small adult. It just takes a bit to get used to, and is probably much more healthy than scrunching your hand around a tiny mouse.

Bluetooth kicked right in, and has a dongle if needed. Can be used wired as well so they have all the bases covered, including pairing it to multiple devices.

YadaYada, 'nuff said! Go for it.

title: The mouse that's good at everything, but not the best at anything
text:
This is a good mouse, but I ultimately decided to return it after using it for a few weeks.

I'll start off with the pros that I'm sure you've read in the tons and tons of great reviews for this mouse (which are justified).

* Good size
* A cool thumb holder on the side
* Adjustable weights
* Lots of buttons
* A two in one scroll wheel that unlocks to allow smooth endless scrolling
* Great sensor & feet
* Solid build quality

So I'll get to why I decided to return it.

The default weight without using any of the adjustable weight is too heavy. While playing FPS games I wasn't able to swipe and crash down as quickly as I'm used to. I'm guessing that this is because of all the additional buttons, scroll wheel release mechanism and the thumb support.

The buttons are in some really weird places. There are a couple right next to the left click button, causing me to click it by accident instead of left clicking. The other also have strange positioning without any feedback as to which you are thumbing over.

This mouse seems like it would be perfect based on all the specs, but it really doesn't excel at anything. It's got a bunch of buttons, but there are mice with more buttons that have the buttons laid out in a better fashion that are easier to remember and not miss-click. So if you want a mouse for MMO's and the like, I would get one of those. And then if you want a mouse for shooters, I would recommend something a little lighter that doesn't have tons of buttons in strange places.

I feel like this mouse is a combination of a ton of great mice that are staples of their categories, but this one belongs to none. It's not perfect for shooters, role playing games or real-time strategy games, but it's OK for all of them.

title: Very surprised at the record quality coming from the microphone!
text:
[[VIDEOID:45faeadcb8bbba8efec14a3c18ea886c]] The microphone's quality is actually very nice. I recorded a short sample so you can listen for yourself (note: Amazon's video player actually reduces the audio quality just a little bit. They sound just a little better than the video on here). Make sure your recording software is recording audio at 16bit 44100 kHz or higher.

I had a ceiling ran running in my room on "high", and my dog was even barking in the next room, yet you can't hear it on the mic. The earphones are pretty standard-- not super comfortable, but I think they get the job done. I wouldn't want to wear them for hours, but for calls, meetings, webinars, etc. (my reason for buying it), I think it will be fine.

Also, I am male with a fairly large head, and these fit comfortable enough. Again, I wouldn't want to wear it for hours, but it feels fine to me. For those interested, I measured my forehead just above my eyebrows and got 23 inches. I feel like the headset can stretch a little wider too. If the earpads were just a bit softer, I think it would be perfect. But, for such a low price, you are getting a quality item.

For those that said the record quality was bad, I wonder if they had their program set to record in 16bit audio, at 44100 kHz. Sometimes the default in software (like Camtasia) is 8-bit 22050 kHz, which does sound very weak and unpleasant.

Logitech has made some real improvements to the scroll wheel--this mouse has a mode that will adjust from incremented (clicky) scrolling to smooth continuous scrolling based on how fast you spin the wheel. title: Works great!  Tips and Features of the Logitech CREATE case and the iPad Pro
text:
This is a great case!
Key stroke response: I used a Bluetooth keyboard with my iPad2 for years and the instant response of the keys of this case is SO MUCH FASTER! It is very easy to type and the tactile feedback of the keys feels solid and top quality. I type very fast and the keyboard keeps up easily.
Attaching/removing iPad from case: I snap the iPad Pro in and out of this Logitech Create case several times a week so I can mount it in the holder on my mic stand for displaying sheet music and chord charts. It is easy and very fast to snap it out of and back into the case. First, I detach the bottom of the iPad from the magnetic connector, then holding the iPad from the bottom with my left hand, I gently push at the right edge of the case (just above the home button) with my right thumb and it snaps out easily.
Holding with one hand: There's a convenient ridge on the edge of the case just behind the keyboard when the iPad is in the connected position. This makes it very easy to hold securely with one hand (right or left side) - my thumb is on top and my other fingers are splayed across on the bottom of the case.
Tablet mode: The iPad can lie on top of the keypad or can be flipped around so the keys are on the bottom. In the former position, it doesn't lie completely flat. In the latter position, it is perfectly flat, but the keys are exposed to whatever it is resting on. Either way works fine. The keys are deactivated as soon as you detach the iPad from the connector so they don't send any erroneous signals to the iPad.
Apple Pencil Holder: I bought a pencil holder on Amazon (< $6) that as a 1" elastic loop (that holds the Apple Pencil snugly) attached to a 1" adhesive-backed square of material. At first I tried to affix it to the outside of the case, but the texture of the case was too rough and it came off within a week. I then affixed it to the back of the iPad itself, directly opposite of the lightening connector. This is much more secure and works perfectly (see photos).
Weight: The Logictech Create case doubles the weight of the iPad and doubles the thickness. In exchange, it feels solidly protected.
Audio: The sound quality of the speakers on the iPad Pro is amazing - much better and louder than my iPhone 6 Plus (but no comparison when sending the sound to a Bluetooth speaker). One of the microphone pinholes (the one on the side just above the volume + button) lines up with a hole in the Logictech case so it can pick up sound. We use the iPad to record live music from our practice sessions. We did some test recordings with the iPad in the case and out of the case. While in the case, the recording was slightly muffled, which may be due to the microphone pinhole being at the bottom of a relatively deep and narrow hole in the case. When I removed the iPad from the case, the recording sounded clean.

title: Exceeded my expectations
text:
My previous universal remote was the "Re," which is basically software plus an infrared blaster that attaches to an iPhone or iPad. I loved it, but programming it was an intense affair which involved a lot of trial and error. I ended up with a brilliant remote that did everything I wanted it to, so when my spouse dropped the iPad and bent the IR blaster, I was fairly devastated. I was sure nothing could ever work as well.

So I was very pleasantly surprised to discover that the Logitech Harmony 650 remote could do everything the Re could do, but with far less setup time, and much fewer headaches. You'll start by recording all the model numbers for your equipment, as well as figuring out all the appropriate settings on your receiver for each component that attaches to it (and in my case, the devices that plug into my standalone HDMI switcher), as well as which inputs on your TV your devices plug into. Once you know all this information, you'll download the MyHarmony software from their website. You begin the setup process by attaching the remote to your laptop via the provided USB cable and inputting all the information you've recorded. As you record the model numbers for each of your components, the software lets you know if the device is found in their database. The Logitech database of known IR device codes is quite extensive, and included all my equipment, some of which is getting rather long in the tooth. My receiver, for example, predates HDMI, so I need to use a separate device to switch between all of my HDMI devices. Thankfully, the database includes the IR code for my Monoprice HDMI switcher as well. Once you record all your equipment, the software prompts you to list each device used for a particular activity. For example, to watch Apple TV, I use my Apple TV device, my receiver, my TV, and my HDMI switcher. Once you've input all this information, you sync the remote to your laptop, and with any luck, you're ready.

The first time I tested the remote, the HDMI switcher didn't respond at all. So I pressed the "Help" button. The Logitech remote asked (via its LCD screen) if a device had failed to respond, and I said "yes." It then correctly guessed that the HDMI switcher was the weak link, and tried a different code. The switcher powered on, and then the remote asked, "Is it working now?" I said "yes," and everything has worked perfectly from then on. Super simple!

I have not fully tested the remote, but what impressed me most is that when you switch activities, say, from listening to music to watching Apple TV, it turned on -- and off -- all the appropriate components. With the Re remote, I had to create a separate button to switch from one activity to another, since the steps are different when switching between activities, compared to powering up an activity from an all-off state. The Logitech just worked! The remote also provides the ability to individually control any devices used for an activity. So if the activity is to watch Apple TV, the remote turns everything on, and then allows you to control settings on your receiver, your TV, etc. I haven't yet tested that functionality, but this is the one area where the Re remote was superior, since it created a virtual remote on the iPhone screen which resembles the remote for the device you're controlling. Perhaps the Logitech remotes that include idevice apps do this, but I'm not familiar with them, so I can't say.

In any case, this remote is easy to set up with minimal leg work, and works well. At the moment I recommend it highly, but I will certainly revise my review if I find that fails to deliver in some other area.

title: A keyboard well suited for operating your computer from a distance.
text:
The Logitech K400 Plus Wireless Keyboard is well suited for those looking for comfort and reliability in a portable keyboard. Immediately upon first use, the build quality stands out as sturdy but lightweight; the soft keys give quiet yet satisfying feedback, while the solid weight and balance make the keyboard feel like it belongs on a desktop rather than in my lap, sitting on the couch. This keyboard is well-suited for a living room setup, or a situation where you want to operate your computer from a distance.

The built-in trackpad featured on this keyboard allows for ultimate portability while operating your computer. Whether you’re lying on your bed, sitting on your living room couch, or walking around your room, the K400 makes operating your PC comfortable and enjoyable. The trackpad is on the small side, and it isn’t as precise as higher-tech laptop trackpads, but it serves its purpose for the price you pay.

The layout of the keys resembles a typical laptop keyboard with the ‘FN’ keys, compact arrow keys, and lack of a number pad. If you are used to using a laptop keyboard, this will be no problem to you, but as a desktop PC user, I find difficulties transitioning from a full-size keyboard to the K400, but I have already found myself growing used to the layout in these couple weeks I’ve owned this keyboard.

In order to get the fullest experience out of this keyboard, you must install the Logitech Options driver file in order to customize the keyboard. My biggest initial complaint was that there was no option to toggle whether the FN key activated the shortcuts or the function keys. However, by installing the Logitech software, you can find this and several other options to optimize your keyboard for your usage.

Perhaps the most unique aspect of this keyboard is the left-click button located in the upper left-hand corner of the device. This allows you to grip the keyboard with two hands, operating the trackpad with your right thumb and the button with your left. This configuration, for myself, allows for more precision with the trackpad and a more comfortable experience browsing the Internet.

Pros:
• Comfortable and lightweight
• Uses very little battery power (2 AA’s)
• Functions well as a computer “remote”
• Satisfying typing feedback
• Customizable FN shortcuts
• Volume control buttons
• Sits well on any surface

Cons:
• Trackpad is less than impressive
• No Caps lock or On/Off indicators

Overall, this keyboard is a very wise purchase for somebody who needs to operate his or her computer from afar, but doesn’t want cords strung all across the room. The Logitech K400 Plus is easy to use, has an exceptionally long battery life and range of operation, and performs its duty as well as one could hope.

After running the software, there will be a window where you can select different functions for each button/wheel. If you have trouble with the side buttons (as many people do), select the side button(s) (#s 4 & 5) and click "Select Task / Select Function" to assign functions. I chose "Do nothing", which disables them, but there are many functions you can choose to assign those or any other button.

title: Broke Within A Few Months - Not Worth The Money
text:
At first I loved this mouse; it fit perfectly into the palm of my hand, the ratchet on the scroll wheel and the smooth scrolling felt great to use, and overall the mouse felt high quality.

The thumb buttons were perfect for my needs - I could map certain keyboard keys to different programs based upon need. This was great for both work and gaming.

The thumb scrolling I found a little bit more awkward to use based upon placement of my fingers (I have smaller hands). I found myself using the thumb scroll wheel much less than the main scroll wheel, however it did have it's uses such as going forward and back in browser windows. Unfortunately this didn't always work, rather dragging the windows sideways but not actually going back and reloading the last page...

Alas, after a few months, the true quality of the mouse began to show.

The ratchet scrolling was first to stop working. Over time it just clicked less and less as you scrolled. I didn't pay much heed to this - sure it was a great feature and felt great to use, but the mouse still functioned. I could handle less clicks than normal... And then it stopped functioning completely. It was just the smooth scroll. Why pay extra for the special feature of ratchet vs smooth scrolling if within a month or two the ratchet stopped working...?

Then the scroll wheel stopped working completely. At first I thought it was just a software bug (as I had just updated the Logitech Options software). I did everything to confirm it wasn't software - uninstalling and reinstalling, installing the older version, and so forth. At first the scrolling seemed like it was a slight delay in connection... but the pauses got longer and longer. In the end I could be scrolling with my finger, and waiting up to thirty seconds for the mouse to actually scroll a web page. It wasn't a connectivity issue as the standard mouse movement still worked during this time.

Furthermore, the problem persisted when the mouse was both directly connected via cable and bluetooth. I also tested on multiple computers, with no avail.

I contacted Logitech about the issue, and their only solution was to disable "smooth scrolling" feature under Logitech Options. This had been disabled for quite a while.

Since purchase the scrolling has ceased to function entirely, making the mouse quite un-useful. Considering that this occurred within only a few months - sadly outside of the warranty return period - I would not deem the mouse high quality. Especially considering I paid US$80 for the product. The issues I experienced are quite common, so sadly this appears to be some serious manufacturing and quality issues.

If you were to ask my honest opinion about purchasing the Logitech MX Master Wireless Mouse, I would honestly suggest you keep looking for better options.

title: Terrible - please read
text:
It's been discontinued so maybe you can't buy this one - but don't buy any of them. It's a less than perfect outcome but the reality is that almost all of the universal remotes stink. All of them. They all have major drawbacks. The best one of all, Universal Remote (yes that's their creative name), makes the best ones but the best of their versions must be programmed by a professional installer or you need to beg them for the complex software to program it yourself. By the time that's done - it's $500-900 for a remote control! So Harmony has always controlled the mass market sub - $200. I've owned two Harmony Remotes. Both - very disappointing and I don't expect much to change. I currently own the Harmony 700 and in almost every way - it stinks! First, the software that it uses to program the remote on your computer uses Microsoft Silverlight. This might not sound like a big deal, but it is. Why? Because Silverlight is sort of like an operating system on top of your computer's operating system. It is a little like Adobe Flash (which no one uses anymore either). While this might make things easier for Harmony, it is nothing but a pain for you. This is because in addition to installing the Harmony software, you will quickly find out that you do not have the Silverlight software (bc virtually no one does). So you will need to install two pieces of software and both will need updating from time to time. Silverlight itself is a pretty lousy platform to dole out to consumers because it is slow, and lacks many features. It is meant to be visual but the Harmony uses it there is no room for any help or support so you are left clicking around trying to figure out what to do. In essence, it ends up way oversimplifying what is a complicated task - programming a remote control that must communicate with many devices. As a result, the most important duty of a good universal remote is to generate macros that can do a single task with one click (watch TV = turn on set top box, TV set and home theater system). Harmony fails miserably at this. I honestly don't know why. My setup is super simple. I only have four devices and all are mainstream. The setup is in my bedroom and the only macros I really need are watch cable TV and watch Apple TV. I have a Samsung TV and a Cisco Set top box. But the STB is perpetually out of sync, and the Harmony can NEVER shut the entire system down. I'm experienced with this stuff and I can not get it to work. You know what did work though? I a $16 universal remote control. Not as good with macros but it works and was dead simple to program. The Harmony looks so much nicer and has the screen and macro buttons, but in terms of programming and functionality - it is a fail. This is my second one and this was my identical experience with the first one.

Second issue is the absolute deal killer to the point where i am done with Harmony forever. The battery is rechargeable in the 700 series. Great idea. I have had the remote for about 3 months now and it has been recharged only once - terrific! But now it will not recharge - I'm getting recharge errors regardless of what I do. I've tried removing and cleaning the contacts and changing the charging cable and outlets. The battery is shot - after 3 months. My last Harmony remote - about 5 years ago, same exact battery issue. That time, I called Harmony and they sent me a new unit. That one died via the battery a few months later too. Now I'm done permanently. I bought this unit at a discount so I can't be entirely upset but it was still $60 -- what a waste. When will I learn. Please benefit from my experience with Harmony.

title: If you use a computer for >2 hours a day, stay away.
text:
I'll be up front with this: I did not buy this mouse for myself. If I did, it would earn a solid 1-star, because I can't rate it any lower. I am an absolute peripheral snob, and I cannot like this product for myself. I bought this mouse for my mom, and, while I'll list a few of my personal grievances with it and its inability to let me click dots precisely, just know that my grievances have not affected my rating, and I have some objective complaints that net it its 2-star rating.

Pros: It's cheap and wireless. If you want a wireless mouse, this is an inexpensive one to buy, and it gets the job done. For a lot of people, this is enough to convince them to buy it. If it doesn't work, it was only $15, and if it does, then you got a good mouse for $15! It seems to work alright for my mom, so I guess those kinds of people will be pleased. The scroll wheel is nice, too. It's not free-spinning like Logitech's high-end gaming offerings, but is very close to it, and it's pleasant to use.

Cons: This thing is extremely small. I have moderately sized hands, and the only way I can move it is by shifting my fingers around. This means it's horrible for anything resembling long-term use. Additionally, it's quite prone to interference. You might be moving your mouse around and it'll just stop, seemingly at random, and it might takes a few minutes to work itself out and resume its pointing duties. Finally -- and this is more of a gripe than anything else -- I've never been able to get Logitech's unifying receiver to work. The concept is that you can use 1 dongle for your mouse and keyboard, but in my experience you just end up with 2 identical dongles sticking out of your computer. They're small, which is great for laptops, but isn't so great for desktops.

Honestly, I can't in good faith recommend this product to anyone who uses their computer for a decent chunk of their day, and even if you check Facebook once a day on your computer, this would still be a hard sell. If you're determined to find a wireless mouse under $20, and you don't care about comfort in the slightest, then I guess this is slightly better than something shaped like it was made from a miniature F/A-117 model.

Having owned a UE Mini Boom, I never really could understand why reviewers like The Wirecutter lavished it with such praise when it really didn't sound all that great.  The new UE Roll, on the other hand, actually does deserve all the same or better praise than was given to its predecessor, the Mini Boom.  The Roll sounds nice and clean, clear and capable.  But just like the Mini Boom, look elsewhere if you need bass.  When I first got the Roll, I thought the bungee thing on the back was a bit gimmicky, but I now use it constantly through a d-ring on my Timbuk2 bag.  Being able to turn the Roll on/off from my phone makes it all come together.  I'm only having to charge the Roll once a week and I don't have to constantly fuss with it like with the Mini Boom.  Logitech did their homework here and really did come up with a truly great little Bluetooth speaker that fits just about anywhere and that I now take with me everywhere.

title: High Promise / Low Results
text:
Great for the first hour.....

From the moment I started using this headset, everything worked fine. Battery indicator worked, charging worked, microphone worked.

Then the issues started. When playing Overwatch I noticed that my microphone was not working. I raised it and brought it back down, heard the beep to indicate the status change. But the "mute" light was still on the microphone. Took a while but the only time this issue would not appear is if Logitech Gaming software was started.

The next issue came in the form of the headset beeping over and over and over every 5 minutes or so. Figured this was the low battery indicator but the LGS displayed the battery at 50% with a remaining life time of 4 hours.

Rebooted tried some more things and plugged in the headset to USB the beeps went away.

The next day the battery was somehow at 2 percent and it would not charge or display as charging on the application. It was unclear as if it was charging while in use or not or if it was even charging at all other than the blue blinking G logos on the side.

Lastly, after a full charge the battery was only at 51 percent, and that was it.. The battery would not show as charging the software did not update correctly, and when I checked the battery status after 2 seconds, it dropped from 51 percent to 30%. Contemplating using it as a "Wired" headset since the audio quality was good in my opinion. However, for the price it is not worth dealing with all these issues.

title: Not as good as people are saying, but not necessarily bad
text:
Just recently bought this and a SS Rival 300 at the same day. I bought the Rival 300 from Amazon and then, since I'm impatient, bought the G502 on sale at another seller that is local to me. I initially tried to cancel the Rival 300 since I made another decision, but I'm glad that I didn't. Here's why:

* It's heavy WITHOUT any weights. Would be far more 'Tunable' if it were lighter out of the box. I can't imagine putting more weight into it.
* Rubber side grips are made of a harder rubber that doesn't really grip well.
* The mouse itself is pretty narrow, leaving no room for my right hand ring finger and pinky. I tried to adjust my grip but that led to slippage from the non-grippy rubber
* Scroll wheel is awful, heavy and wobbly (likely due to side to side click feature, which are kinda worthless IMO)
* Button placement was awkward for me. I found myself accidentally hitting the side button closest to my thumb, which I usually use for reloading... Not good.

I gave 3 stars due to what it does do well:

* Great sensor - lift off distance is super low (which is good)
* Tons of options to customize buttons as you like them - probably good for MMO games (which I don't play)

Please don't put too much stock into rated DPI since most people will never ever use max DPI from their mice. To put this into perspective, the Rival 300 I'm using now (4000 DPI) shows no difference at 800 - 1000 DPI (my typically used settings) compared to this mouse with a 12000 DPI sensor.

Note that I am not a fanboy of any brand, I just found what is most comfortable to me and this was not it.

* Excellent sensor, lift off distance is extremely low
* Adjustments for mouse pad you are working with (I have hard and cloth mouse pads, and it does work rather well)

text:
My buddy bought me this headset for my birthday to go with my new PC, and I've been using them nearly daily.

I have never had a problem with the audio, unless I walk past a certain point in my house, but that's due to the rebar in the walls interfering with the signal. Audio is crystal clear, microphone doesn't pick up ALL the background noise going on in my house, so I can have a pleasant professional conference call in my living room, and no one is the wiser. The dongle slips nicely into the left earpiece, and is easily removed as well. The headset syncs really quickly with any device I need. The band part with the cushioning makes this super comfortable to wear. Charging is simple, as is taking calls or playing songs through it.

The only problems I've come across are that sometimes, because I have cartilage piercings in my ears, the headset really starts hurting my ears and head after several hours. I also wear glasses, and have found that when I wear the headphones on only one ear and move one of the earpieces to sit behind my ear, the arm to my glasses presses into the padding. The padding has now torn to shreds, even though I don't drag the headset across my glasses a thousand times a day. I do really like this headset and I will be purchasing new padding for them.
