title: Rock Star Controller: Great Performers Often Die Young
text:
This is a great device and invaluable for MMO games where you need to access a lot of commands.

No complaints about the functionality of the device - I bought it when Guild Wars 2 was released and I can't play the game without a G13.

My issue is the longevity of the thumbstick. I use this for "WASD" control and after abotu 18-24 months, the thumbstick gimbal will begin to fail. Mostly it gets really gritty and refuses to self center (making you inadvertently walk off a ledge and fall to your death, etc). Since they were out of warranty and not working, I took two of these apart to see if I could fix the thumbstick but you would have to desolder it from it's circuit board and bend the casing open to check it out.

My 3rd one is arriving some time today. You glass half empty people might think 3 in 4 years is terrible, but you glass half full people will note that I keep ordering them.

I'm a heavy user, but gentle on my gear, under more normal use, you might get 3-4 years out of yours so don't let that discourage you, it's a worthwhile device, but, like everything else these days, it won't last forever.

title: and the cheaper Logitech G35s) and these are hands down the best of the bunch so far
text:
I've owned a handful of various quality headsets (Turtle Beach's PX5s and Ear Force Tangos, the PS4 gold headset, and the cheaper Logitech G35s) and these are hands down the best of the bunch so far. I bought these looking for a headset I could easily use with my PC, PS4 and Xbox One without that hassle of unplugging the optical cable and moving from one to the other, because I regularly switch between all 3 platforms and I recently put all 3 on a new shelving unit which made this very very difficult. I also was hoping to find a headset that was completely wireless when using the chat microphone, but was very doubtful I would find something that fit this requirement because each console just HAS to use their own proprietary wireless technology for some stupid reason, instead of just using Bluetooth like everything else on the planet (yeah, I know the PS4 technically uses bluetooth but it's locked by Sony so it doesn't allow devices not specifically designed for it). Well I was pleasantly surprised that this headset not only meets both of those requirements but also matches my Logitech G502 gaming mouse AND looks badass all at the same time.

Pros:
+Completely wireless and instant "installation" on anything with audio and a USB port, including all gaming devices, computers, TV (at least mine) etc. There isn't really any installation, it's literally just plugging in the USB dongle (hidden under one of the ear cups for portable storage)
+Looks badass, customizable LED colors and effects (pulsing, color changing strobe, steady, off, whatever you want)
+Easy to use customizable software, uses the same G series software as other logitech G products (like i said I also have the G502 mouse and plan on getting the G910 keyboard). This allows custom profiles to be made or downloaded, and ability to sync G products colors and effects.
+The collapsible mic is very convenient and self muting, and doesn't require any "chat cable" or adaptor like a lot of mid range headsets do for each console
+One of the more comfortable headsets I've owned. I also have quite a range of over ear headphones and for their weight, these are surprisingly comfortable up to 4-5 hours.
+Detachable 3.5mm cable is a great option to have when the mic isn't needed or you want to mix 2 audio sources at the same time. I used to have ear buds underneath my headsets in order to watch youtube/ netflix while gaming and this eliminates the need for that.

Cons:
-After that 4-5 hour mark I mentioned, they can become painful (though ANY headset you get will begin to hurt after that long so it's not a huge surprise). Mostly right in the top of the head, but also a bit around the ears.
-No bluetooth. An odd feature to be missing in such a robust headset, but I guess this design choice was made to keep the price and weight down and with the core market at gamers the USB dongle serves their purposes. But it would've still been nice to have so I could receive phone calls while gaming, like with other headsets.
-Slightly flimsy plastic material. I haven't broken or cracked anything, and it feels sturdy enough but the rotating joints and headband portion look like thin shiny plastic that doesn't seem too tough. Again, I haven't actually broken anything, and I'm using these at my desk and that's it, but if you plan on traveling with these in a bag or using them heavily I would highly recommending getting the case for them as it seems a good twist a bit too far could snap the headband-to-cuff connection.

title: Keyboad Needs a SERIOUS Redesign
text: I've owned this keyboard for 6 months. For the most part is has worked well. However, despite its fairly high price, the keyboard has some design flaws that take away from its value. First, the "feet" that pull out from the keyboard to allow it to sit at an angle are VERY thin. The amount of plastic that is SUPPOSED to support the weight of the keyboard and endure fingers making keystrokes is insufficient. The first leg broke within a week of ownership, and thus the keyboard has had be used in the "flat" position ever since. Second, the rubber anti-skid "dots" fall off as they are simply stuck on with a kind of common sticky adhesive. 2 out of 3 have fallen off and that means the keyboard skids around on my wood desk way to easily. Third, my office has low ambient light, and so the keyboard has to be left overnight under a desk light every 4 days to maintain a charge. You'd think with some keyboards claiming battery life of over a year, this keyboard's batteries could last more than 5 days without a recharge. Minor annoyances include keys that are starting to stick in the down position and commonly used keys already getting smooth, shiny and slick surface instead of the original textured surface.

text:
I started off ordering one of these for my mother. She has a tough time negotiating the different remotes (DVD, Cable Box, TV). She has NetFlix and watched it but it was a usually a call to me to explain to get the TV remote, set the TV to HDMI 2, get the DVD remote, turn it on, move to the left three rows, move down three to NetFlix .....

I got her this, went over to her house and after getting the manufacturer and models of the devices, within 30 minutes, I was done programming it. Now if she wants to watch NetFlix, she selects one of the buttons and in about 20 seconds, there is NetFlix!!!

I liked it so much, I got one for myself also.

A hint - if you are getting this for someone that is not tech savvy at all, you can install the application to program the device on their computer, then if they ever change equipment (like the cable box), there are free remote support tools to where you can take over their computer. They connect the remote to their computer, connect to the remote support, tell you what the manufacturer and model is of the new device, and you can do it all for them. Works great for me, as I am about 200 miles from my mother.

title: Great remote, easy to program and has all the features I want.
text:
For many years I have used a Harmony One remote and have been really happy with it. As it started to wear over time, I kept looking for a viable replacement, but nothing I could find even equaled it, much less topped it. At long last I came across this option, and I am more than pleased with its performance.

My main concern was its lack of the 30-second skip feature, but that was more than easy to add. I simply had it "learn" it from my Harmony One, programmed it into the FF button, and then made that the touch-once application, and away I went. I press down longer on this same button, and it will fast forward 1X. Press down longer again, then it goes to 2X FF, etc. up to 4X.

I also found that pressing this same button quickly when on the Guide screen for Comcast directs it to jump by page instead of having to scroll the channel choices.

Note that I added all my devices and activities and modifications via my computer, not via the app. I don't think I'll even bother with the app. I set up a new account for this device with Logitech, and was able to transfer everything off my other account that I had set up with the Harmony One. The user interface for this Smart Control is even better that what I experienced with the user interface for the Harmony One...really easy to use.

Really is an excellent remote. My only negative would simply be the learning curve of remembering where the buttons are....I was so used to my Harmony One I knew what buttons were where without even looking, and occasionally I hit the wrong button on the Smart Control out of habit. I'm sure I will get used to it over time. Oh, and BTW, one worry I had was that I would miss the little color screen I had on the One, but I don't....at all!

Highly recommended.

title: Apple Update 9.2 Destroys Functionality of This (Probably) Good Device
text:
I bought my iPad Pro and this keyboard on January 4. The iPad Pro came with iOS 9.2 installed. As soon as i connected the keyboard, I noticed its extreme lagging, dropped letters, bizarre word replacements before I had typed more than two letters, and near-uselessness. Apparently, Apple forgot to put in some kind of a fix-it patch in iOS 9.2 that would allow it to work with this keyboard. Not Logitech's fault... but nonetheless the keyboard can't be used with the iPad Pro until Apple decides to release an update that will allow it to pair with this keyboard. VERY POOR JOB, APPLE... and unfortunately, Logitech is going to bear the brunt of the returns on these!

There is a work-around you can find if you search online: go into settings-->general-->keyboard, and change the setting for the keyboard to US/International or something like that. This did seem to help quite a bit with the lagging problems. I also shut off all the "autocorrect" options, which are useful for a cell phone but not really necesary when typing on a keyboard. (I have all the autocorrect options enabled on my old iPad keyboard from Zagg, and experience none of the typing problems, though.)

I agree with other reviewers that it is a challenge to get the iPad into the case, and with its size, the device feels more fragile than the smaller iPad. I wouldn't want to have to force anything on the large sheet of glass. Also, the volume controls are very difficult to use because the plastic over them is bulky and thick. Those are the first things I noticed when trying to set ths up. I do love the idea that this doesn't need to be charged separately from the iPad - great feature. The difficulty inserting and removing the device would probably be a negative, though: the iPad Pro is aimed at artists, especially with the pencil, and I would want to be able to quickly have just the device in my hand when doing artwork.

At any rate, for $150 I can't wait and cross my fingers and just hope that the next iOS update will fix this, so I'm going to have to return it.

text:
The keyboard and mouse generally work as they should. I had been using a wired "rubber-dome" keyboard, and a wired laser mouse. The keyboard and mouse both broke around the same time so I replaced them with this.
Good: The mouse and keyboard work as you might expect a mouse and keyboard to work 95% of the time. The keyboard is sized well, and isn't overly large, or overly small. The keys are satisfying to press, and have a reasonable amount of feedback, and travel. Much better than a chiclet style keyboard, not as nice as a mechanical, but you aren't paying for a mechanical. The mouse, is a full size mouse, that feels durable. Neither the mouse, nor keyboard have experienced any sticking keys, or other major issues.
BAD: The keyboard saves power, I think, by turning off its transmitter when you aren't using it. This has resulted in a very significant, and very annoying delay whenever you start to type on it after having not typed for a short time, where you then have to wait a moment, then backspace, and retype everything you just tried to type. If you can live with that, no worries. The mouse is an OPTICAL mouse, and what that has meant in this circumstance, is the sensor experiences a lot of stuttering, resulting in herky jerky mouse movements from time to time. I do use the mouse on a mousepad.
This setup is entirely unsuitable for gaming, however if your just an average guy doing average stuff, it works fine.

text: This mouse is amazing. I was really skeptical about spending $100 on a mouse, but I watched some reviews and went for it anyway. As someone that has to use a computer everyday, a comfortable mouse is something that I need. This mouse is really big, which is perfect for my big hands. It is super comfortable for any kind of grip. As far as the features, it has a horizontal scroll wheel, which you can program to do what you want. On my desktop, it changes volume, and on my laptop it changes brightness. You can program it for up to three different machines and can easily switch between them with a button at the bottom. The main scroll wheel has a feature where if you spin it fast enough (you can change the speed required) the scroll wheel will loosen and keep spinning. This is useful for long web pages or documents. I use it to cheat in games that require constant scrolling. This mouse also has a gesture button, which is on the thumb rest. You hold down the gesture button and move the mouse in different directions, which of course, you can program. title: Not ideal for more than 2 sources
text:
I thought there was no way a universal remote would be more complicated for my wife and kids as the 5 remotes that were sitting in our theater room. So I ordered this without research knowing it can handle more than enough devices, how could it complicate things. Don't feel like going into the whole details but here is my setup followed by what is needed to do to preform functions, as an FYI for people with similar setups.

My setup: Epson projector, Yamaha receiver, Comcast cablebox, Apple TV, Steam Link, Samsung Bluray

What I need to do to change functions...

Watch TV: Press the AVR button, press 1, press the cable button

Watch Bluray: Press the AVR button, Press 3, press the DVD button

Watch Apple TV, Press the AVR button, press 4, press the TV button, explain to my family for the 200th time how TV, Apple TV, and TV button, are different

Play games: Wake up SteamLink by pressing button on xbox controller, press AVR button, press 2, not number 2, quick button 2. Black screen, switch to any other input, press AVR button, press either 1,3, or 4, ,press AVR again, press 2 and get picture.

Turn off everything: Press the power button (everything but the projector turns off, despite no problem turning on), press AVR1, press the little power button 3 times to finally turn the projector off. Don't press power to quick, space it 3 seconds....

These are my scripted responses to the frustrations texts and calls I get on a daily basis from my family after simplifying my five remote setup for a room we use twice a week. I hate this thing. If you are going to go Logitech, spend the $200 and get one that will do everything you need. I set my parents up with an older logitech 700 a few years back and it has been bullet proof.

I could maybe see this working for a basic bedroom cablebox/tv setup but I really have a sour taste in my mouth with this device and won't bother going down another frustrating path of getting people to figure it out. It makes esnse to me, but it is equal ammount of work as handling five remotes so is it really functional???

text:
I am incredibly disappointed with this mouse. It is one of the poorest performing mice I've ever owned. It is advertised as it "works on more surfaces than other mice--even on glass." My experience has shown this to be blatantly false. For me, it only works on a mouse pad, not even on a wooden desk surface that other mice have worked on in the past. It also doesn't work at even moderate distance from the transmitter ( <10 feet ). The cursor motion on these surfaces or distances is choppy at best, and that's when it moves at all.

Even with all this, I could use it on a mouse pad, and it worked well enough in that situation, so I did not return it.
I bought this mouse in July 2015. Now, nine (9) months later, the scroll wheel has also decided to not work correctly. The scrolling jumps from the lightest touch, in any program, and in both scroll modes. This makes using the "scroll wheel click" impossible, as attempting to click shifts the page. It also makes reading with the scroll wheel frustrating at best.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but few products, especially expensive ones, have frustrated me as much as this mouse. A much cheaper mouse would have (and has in the past) provided a better experience. I wish I had never purchased this mouse, or returned it after my initial misgivings.

title: MX > MX Master
text:
I used the mouse for a month before writing this review. I use my mouse 8-10 hours a day for design work. (lots of clicking) Prior to the MX Master, I used the original MX for approximately 7 years, and loved it, but because I use my mouse so much, I went through three of them. When the last one started to fail, I decided to "upgrade" and get the MX Master. My main reason for wanting to upgrade was because of the advertised advanced features, such as the side scrolling wheel, and also the ability to connect to multiple computers without repairing.

Unfortunately, now that I have the MX Master, as I try to implement it's new features, I feel like they are more or less marketing gimmicks, and not very useful in a practical way. To add to the disappointment, the mouse doesn't feel as comfortable as the original MX. It's slightly higher/bigger than the original MX. The new scroll wheel is somewhat spastic. Yes, I realize you can (and should) customize it to your liking in the preferences, but when you switch between smooth scroll, and ratcheted scroll, it kinda jumps and sounds bad. Almost like the mouse is going to break. On some pages when I try to zoom in with the smooth scroll, it just keeps going, even after I've stopped the wheel. It's rather annoying. Additionally as others have noted, the new forward and back button placement is terrible. They get lost when trying to use them.

When I saw the marketing video of some dude carving the mouse out of wood, I kinda felt like that was also a cheesy marketing ploy, but I overlooked it. I highly doubt that this is how the mouse was developed - but hey, caving wood looks cool, so run with it, Logitech.

The new mouse does not come with a power brick or case like the original MX. You have to charge it from your computer.

Overall, it's an okay mouse, but I don't like it. The original MX is better.

With the MX Master, I feel like Logitech spent more time on marketing, rather than on perfecting this mouse - but hey, carving wood is hard work.

In the end I'm disappointed with the MX Master. The next mouse I'm going to buy will be the original MX. (again)

If you are reading this, I suggest you don't fall for the hype like I did, and just get the original MX. (It's now less expensive, since the MX Master came out, so that's a bonus.)

title: Highly recommend, solid unit, easily connects and works at long range.
text: I bought my home stereo receiving 8 years ago and blue tooth wasn't a big thing. Now I use Buetooth for music all the time, and wanted to run music through the ceiling speakers, but our receiver didn't have the ability to receive. Now I'm perfectly happy with the receiver, it is a very solid unit and performs well, but I thought the convenience of Bluetooth would be worth the cost of a new receiver. After researching the cost of a new receiving with enough amps to run our ceiling speakers, I decided I definitely wasn't going to that route. I found the Logitech Bluetooth audio adapter, and thought at that price point it would be worth a try. And with Amazon's return policy, I felt safe that I wouldn't be stuck with an under-performing Bluetooth receiver. Well, the Logitech Bluetooth adapter has really lived up to expectations. Out of the box, it feels solid and well made. Instructions were clear, but were scarcely needed.  The range is excellent, installation was took five minutes, most of that time was spent moving the equipment around to access the back connector panel. The adapter rests unobtrusively on top of the stereo, and all of my devices have connected to it easily. Since my stereo doesn't have a Bluetooth input, I used "Stereo 3", and simply put a label on the Logitech indicating which input is being used. Very easy now to switch over to the Bluetooth, we haven't had any trouble with this device, and I'm buying another for the basement entertainment system. Highly recommend this unit.

title: Solid For What It Is
text:
If you buy this keyboard for what it is, you will be happy.

What is it? It's small. It's a lightweight, compact keyboard that has portability as its primary goal. I have 2. I bought one as a utility keyboard to pull out when I needed a keyboard to set up a new computer, or a keyboard to throw in my briefcase on long trips. It's perfect for that. I bought another one when I built a computer for my then 5 year old. Small hands need a small keyboard. Again, it's perfect.

Would I want to use it all day at length? No. The key action is OK for what it is, but I don't want to type up 50 page documents on this thing. Could I? Absolutely, but it wouldn't be my first choice. The keys are kind of chic-let style, which I don't fine comfortable for long typing sessions. Even if that's totally your bag, you'll find that some of the key placement isn't convenient if you're a power user. Look at the top row and you'll find all the keys that should be between the alpha keys and the numeric keypad. Look at the undersized arrow keys. Small is a compromise.

One thing that is great is that it uses Logitech's unified receiver. The unified receivers are AWESOME. I won't use anything that isn't Bluetooth or unified. After having purchased mouse/keyboard sets over the years and wearing out one or the other, it's so annoying to have multiple receivers. I love the unified receivers.

Also, it comes in all sorts of different graphic patterns, so you'll probably find it at different prices. Shop around.

Review typed on a K360 as my main desktop keyboard is in the process of being replaced.

Even if that's totally your bag, you'll find that some of the key placement isn't convenient if you're a power user. Look at the top row and you'll find all the keys that should be between the alpha keys and the numeric keypad. Look at the undersized arrow keys. Small is a compromise.

One thing that is great is that it uses Logitech's unified receiver. The unified receivers are AWESOME. I won't use anything that isn't Bluetooth or unified. After having purchased mouse/keyboard sets over the years and wearing out one or the other, it's so annoying to have multiple receivers. I love the unified receivers.

Also, it comes in all sorts of different graphic patterns, so you'll probably find it at different prices. Shop around.

Review typed on a K360 as my main desktop keyboard is in the process of being replaced.

title: Really Nice Mouse Unless You Have Huge Hands
text:
I've carried this mouse in my briefcase and used it on all sorts of surfaces. I have relatively small hands and find it to be almost perfect even for desktop use.

I get that some people have had button issues and left 1 star reviews. I've worn out mice in the past and had button issues, and I can't speak to whether their situations were normal wear and tear or not. What is strange to me is that I supposedly bought the "old" version in frustration free packaging but I clearly have the new version in appearance when I look at the pictures people are posting. So I'm just going to ignore all the other posts and give my thoughts:

1) I like the size. I would like it to be a little bigger, but it's nice for me. If you have giant hands, you won't like it, but if you are in below 50th percentile in hand size, you could probably use this at your desktop and be happy. It doesn't feel at all like the M325 travel mouse that I bought for my son.

2) It has some heft. Again, unlike the M325, it has a bit of mass and feels good.

3) It works on anything. Dark field laser works well, in my experience.

4) I like the feel of the scroll wheel.

5) The unified receivers are AWESOME. I won't use anything that isn't Bluetooth or unified. After having purchased mouse/keyboard sets over the years and wearing out one or the other, it's so annoying to have multiple receivers. I have used the unified receivers several places and find them wonderful.

Recently my desktop mouse went down and I moved this to my full time desktop mouse. I might just buy another for my briefcase and keep this one here.

I am a fast typist, and am able to type up to 90 words per minute on this keyboard without any issues.

Ergonomics are average. It feels comfortable to type on, and I can do so for long periods of time without having any problems.

The hotkeys worked right out of the box with my Windows 10 desktop. Volume buttons control system volume and play/pause/next track/previous track buttons work with iTunes (or pandora, whichever is currently playing.)

Huge fan of the Logitech Unifying Receiver, and that was a major purchasing point for me.

Overall it's a great keyboard. Haven't had any issues with it, and would definitely buy another one if I built another black/white system.

title: What you should expect within 90 days of owning
text:
EDITED! READ UPDATE BELOW:
1 star for product, -10 for support

I just purchased this headset from BestBuy who price matched Amazon.

shortly after setting it up, every time I tried to use the mic, there is this "buzzing"/"crackling" noise. Listeners describe it as a "Tazer" going off and they cannot hear anything I say at all. We're not talking a subtle low background buzz, but a full on Zap Zap Zap.

A google search said this can happen when plugged in to USB 3.0 ports and should be moved to USB 2.0 port.
Ok... Problem #1 right there. A $200 piece of hardware should not suffer from such a constraint, but OK.. I have an available 2.0 port.

Moved the USB receiver to the 2.0 port and presto, worked fine for a couple of hours. But then, without changing anything, the exact same issue came back.

Another Google search reveals that this is a VERY common issue with this unit and the vendor has no solution. The unit was returned to the store within 24 hours (See the update below, the unit was worth keeping after all).
As a result, my long term patronage of Logitech gaming devices has ended.

While it worked, the sound and mic was absolutely beautiful. But 3 hours of working and 3 hours of time spent trying to fix an issue; just to have the problem return without change.... That's unacceptable at this cost.
Corsair should send Logitech a thank you note. Because they are now my gaming vendor of choice.

UPDATE:
I gave it one more go, by attaching the USB receiver/transmitter to a Logitech "dongle" USB cable I don't use that came with my G700s mouse. Once I plugged it in to the dongle (which is also connected to a USB 2.0 port); the crackling issue has gone away and not returned.
I'm still extremely disappointed with Logitech for releasing something so sensitive and unable to be plugged in to USB 3.0 ports. USB 2.0 is going away and not even present on most current systems. While I've decided to keep this headset (because the mic and sounds are crystal clear); this still remains my last Logitech purchase.

UPDATE AFTER <3 MONTHS OF OWNERSHIP:
Rating drop to one star.
Unit has been having an increasing issue with going in to permanent "standby" mode. Other user's with this issue state that they have to disconnect the battery for 15 seconds, then reconnect. The issue has been slowly increasing and now the unit won't come back at all. I've had it for 2.5 months.
I contacted Logitech to replace it under warranty, and they don't even have the option to send a new unit first (with a CC hold) and I can send back the defective one. I have to wait 1-2 days for "approval", then 7-10 days to receive the replacement AFTER they receive mine.
For such a large company, this is a very archaic replacement process.

This unit is in the same category as half priced headsets. For the quality, I should have gone with something more fittingly priced, such as the Kingston HyperX. For the price, I should have gone with something of justified quality like the Steel Series H wireless.

Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this product. Its fancy, it's pretty, it has bells and whistles. It's just poorly made and supported. and simply not worth the price tag (even discounted at $150; this is not a good deal).

My RMA has been ongoing for 2 weeks now. Logitech has my defective unit, and I still don't have a replacement. I've received no notification of a replacement being shipped, tracking number, approved, unapproved... nothing. Their support is completely non-responsive to emails. The only way you get any information is by calling them directly.
I even got a feedback email on the level of service for my support case. The case isn't even closed yet! Well, they got some hard truth.

Update:
Received an email stating that the received unit (that I sent over a week ago) doesn't match the model in the case. Logitech's system matched the serial number to a 633 headset. As a part of the registration process, I had to upload the store receipt; which thankfully clearly states the proper model#. I called support (because they don't respond to emails or notes in the case); and they claim to be correcting the product mismatch. The rep stated "You'll receive an email with the replacement shipping information in 24-48 hours". I heard their 24-48 hour time frame every time I've called on the day 3 because I did not receive the promised communication.

Update:
So 3 weeks after starting the RMA process, I did finally receive the proper replacement unit. The new unit has been working properly, but this ordeal has not changed my rating or opinion of Logitech and their products.

title: The Hub provides the best Harmony experience so far!
text:
I have owned a few different Harmony remotes over the last decade, but this is my first experience with a Harmony Hub. I was a bit skeptical about it because the hub is designed for setups where most of the gear is either hidden away or behind a cabinet door. I read a few reviews and most raved about it, so I decided to go for it.

The Harmony Hub was easy to setup (plus you can import your settings from other Harmony remotes you have in your MyHarmony account) and works flawlessly. I figured since the hub is designed to fill a cabinet with IR signals that it could probably blanket a room, too. It does. I have the hub sitting next to my couch, on a table where I usually keep my remote(s). It's about 8 or 9 feet from everything. As a nice little bonus, the Harmony Hub is also able to control WiFi-Direct and Bluetooth devices such as Roku and PlayStation 4.

My only complaints are the remote is not as big as other Harmony remotes I have used which means the buttons are a little smaller and very easy to "fat finger" if you have big hands like me. Also, it only provides a way to control activities, which is fine 99% of the time, but if you need to control a specific device (like adjust settings on you TV or HT receiver), you will still need your original remote or use the Harmony app for Android and iOS.

What is cool about the app is you can also use it to add/update/delete devices and activities and push firmware updates to the hub (no more having to connect your remote to a computer via USB)!

title: Ok, not for coffee drinkers
text:
The Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse is a solidly designed product that should give you no problems. However, I feel the need to issue a public service announcement that this trackball is not for coffee drinkers or those of us who require pinpoint mouse precision (graphic designers, etc). The human thumb, which scientists tell us sprouted a mere 5 million years ago (a fraction of a second in evolutionary terms), is perhaps our most imprecise digit. Unless you're a three-toed sloth, you may find yourself as clumsy as "all thumbs" with this thing. Add some coffee and nervous jitters to the mix ("the Jameson project needs to go out by 5pm or you're all fired!"), and this thumb-operated trackball is about as useful as a hippo on rollerskates.

I purchased this mouse because I was tired of running out of desktop room and smacking my elbow into my coworkers with traditional meeses. Not to mention knocking over coffee mugs. The idea of a fixed, wireless mouse is a good one. The problem is simply that the trackball is operated with the thumb, unlike other trackballs which are operated by the index/middle finger combination.

Perhaps I need to take up hand yoga, or quit drinking coffee, or hire myself a three-toed sloth, but this thing is just aggravating. Or should I say, my thumb is aggravating. So in the end, although I have no problem with Logitech or the build of this product, I have to criticize this mouse for being a few million years ahead of its time. In other words, uh... thumbs down?

title: The g502 Proteus Core/Spectrum is one of the best mice ever created
text:
The g502 Proteus Core/Spectrum is one of the best mice ever created. Now that is a pretty bold claim, so lets do our best to justify it. The g502 at first glance looks angular, futuristic, and almost uncomfortable; however, go to your local store and put your hands on one, and you are greeted with IMO one of the most comfortable mice in the hand I have ever had the pleasure of using.

One of the 502's greatest assets is the sheer number of buttons it has at its disposal. For your thumb you have easy and comfortable access to 3 buttons, one of which is a very lovely "sniper" button which can reduce DPI for when you really need to be precise with your shots. The other two are all purpose buttons which can be mapped, or even rebound to other keys, or set up as macro's. Your middle and index fingers also get the VIP treatment here with two more programmable buttons easily accessible to your pointer finger, along with DPI shift/profile button, and the amazing Free scroll button (free scroll= the mouse wheel can have tactile standard click, or be put into a free scroll mode which allows it to spin freely). We will just say if you find yourself needing more reprogrammable buttons, then you my friend have 3 hands.

Now we will discuss the meat and potatoes of any gaming mouse......The sensor. The g502 houses the PMW3366 sensor, which has proven itself to be one of the most trusted, and accurate sensors ever created. In my almost two years using both the g502 core and spectrum I have never experienced any sensor malfunctions or even the slightest input issue. At the end of the day the sensor is probably the most important part of any gaming mouse, and in this regard, the g502 passes with perfect marks.

Finally we can discuss the aspects of the g502 which I do not enjoy, there aren't many, but they are fairly significant depending on your make or break qualifications. Firstly the mouse is quite heavy, the fact that there are weights you can add to the mouse is almost comical to me personally. For many elite competitive gamers a heavy mouse is a no go, so if you are looking for something light and "flicky" this is not the mouse for you. My second and final complaint is minor, and you do adjust to it, but I am not a big fan of the metal scroll wheel. I love the weight of it, but when gaming you can tend to slip. The solution they came up with on the new g900 chaos spectrum would fit amazingly on the g502, and should be implemented on the g502 imo.

All in all the G502 is one of the best gaming mice ever created. If you can put up with its slightly hefty weight, and come to terms with the sometimes slippery scroll wheel, you will be rewarded with one of the most feature full, accurate, and comfortable mice ever created. the following games are ones I find particularly suited for the G502 (Arma 2/3, diablo 2/3, GTAV, CSGO, Battlefield, DayZ, etc.)

TL;DR
Pros:
-Great sensor
-Free scroll
-11 fully programmable buttons
-Comfortable
Cons:
-Could use a weight loss plan
-Scroll wheel could benefit from rubber coating like G900

title: The Logitech Gamepad F310 is an absolutely fantastic gamepad especially for the price
text:
The Logitech Gamepad F310 is an absolutely fantastic gamepad especially for the price. For anyone who is looking for a bargain pc game gamepad your search should absolutely begin with the F310.

I don't like reviewing items after only using them only a few times as the review cannot speak to durability. After using the F310 for almost 2 years I can confidently say that the F310 is absolutely worth your money.

Performance: When I was searching for a PC gamepad the market was pretty simple: Pony up the cash for a Xbox 360 controller, buy a cheap knock generic brand controller that may feel uncomfortable and may not survive a year's worth of gaming, or buy a Logitech. The choice for me was clear. For only a few dollars more than the cheap generic controllers, the F310 is a budget but very robust and well made controller. The durability is excellent and 2 years each and every button still works flawlessly . In terms of ergonomics, the F310 looks a bit like a cross between a PS3 controller and a 360 controller.

Compatibility: While I don't play a ton of PC games, so far I have yet to find a game that does not work with the F310. First person shooters, rpgs, even emulators work right out of the box with the F310. My computer instantly recognizes the F310, and I never needed a second of tinkering to make the controller work with a game. In case things don't work out of the box the F310 has both Xinput an Direct Input settings, one just needs to flip a unobtrusive button on the back to switch settings.

In conclusion, if you are in the market for a budget PC gamepad don't hesitate to pick up the F310. You wont regret it.

If the set up isn't working perfectly to begin with, the remote has an assistant that will step you through the process for the remote to fix itself.  What are the negatives? title: Good product but limited when used with Alexa
text:
Before I start be aware the Harmony Hub comes without instructions for interfacing with Alexa. First thing, go the the harmony support site at myharmony.com and type "harmony and alexa" in the search box. You won't regret it. I wish Amazon would make this clear on the product page or otherwise. My initial experience setting things up was very frustrating.

1) To start off The Hub with Alexa has limited capabilities that can be aggravating if you expect more. You will still need a remote for most of the functions. For example, you still need a remote to handle details like navigating on screen menus. It would be tricky to sit there and speak, "up, up, right, select," rather than using the remote navigator keys. Controlling volume requires a remote but the good news here is the app uses the volume keys on my phone. There are lots of other stuff that demands a remote so just be aware of it. Also note that you pretty much need to use the apps, rather than the remotes that came with you components or risk things getting out of sink. The apps talk to the Hub and coordinate. It's not hard to get things back in sink but it can be annoying, especially when some of you family another family member don't understand the system.
2) The Hub works with an app for your phone, pad, etc. The app is just OK, not great. On my iPhone the default layout for some functionality is a senseless mishmash. The app is better on my iPad but still needs some work. For example, controlling my TV is reasonable as long as I use the favorites function to set the stations. Setting the stations with the numbers or the up/down is awkward. The layouts can be customized to some extent but not enough for my taste. On the plus side I can control volume with the volume keys on the phone or pad. Also, since the app works over wifi it doesn't need to point at anything. Those are very nice features.
2) There is a detail about Harmony Activities that needs mention. You can turn on your components and setup the states with a single command but it can be tricky to get everything right. It helps to be technically savvy. For example, my Bose system takes a long time to start up so I need to program the Hub to wait before it sets the input port. With the Hub at least I do not need to stand there holding the remote until the process completes. You can use Harmony Activities to voice control other things but I find this of limited value. You still need a remote anyway.

title: Superb for the "Power-User" types who love efficiency
text:
I will never, EVER, buy another mouse that doesn't have the beautiful scroll wheel functionality of this one. Being able to slowly scroll and feel the clicking, then be able to just whip the scroll wheel off and have it switch to "free spin" automatically.. I can't even begin to explain how genius that is.

Then there is the gesture button, which despite what some people have said it doesn't go off while just resting your hand on it, this thing is a life saver. I don't have to switch hand positions at all in order to swap desktops, and i can bind them to whatever i want. Another genius move.

The side wheel is another crazy good idea, but unfortunately it doesn't work all that well. I'm not sure if it's the mouses fault, or the fault of websites/programs. But it seems like half the time it straight up doesn't work (like with audacity) or it goes WAAAY too fast/slow. One site will work fine, then another site will suck donkey balls. So i really think it may just be on the app/site end of things. (you can set app specific settings, but doing that for each app is a huge time sink)

My Only gripe is that there isn't a larger version. I HATE the "claw" grip everyone seems to think mice need to use... I want to palm the mouse god damn it! My poor pinky gets so tired :'(

title: A new standard for headsets. (Plus sidetone on PS4!)
text:
Ok, so before I jump into my review here, just know that I am not an "audiophile" (and most that claim they are don't know what that word means), and I am unbiased towards any brands or styles of headsets/headphones. That being said however, I have a passion for collecting and experiencing audio products such as headphones, theatre systems, car audio etc. I know good sound when I hear it, and these definitely live up to their hype.

Audio Quality/Mic Functionality: Arguably the most important aspect of a good pair of headphones or headset. No one likes to listen to an unbalanced mess or poor positional audio precision. This headset nails it. Right out of the box, I literally plugged the usb dongle into my PS4, and boom, setup complete. My first reaction was an outloud "wow". I went through spotify listened to a few songs, as well as some shows on Netflix. All sounded clear, crisp, and very balanced with the lows, mids, and highs. The bass in particular is very tight and punchy. It makes electronic music sound amazing. So initially I was pleased, so I decided to download the Logitech sound customization software that is advertised with this headset. Oh my god. I was literally blown away. I have owned many of the higher end headets over the past few years, including Steelseries Wireless H, Astro A50's, PS Golds etc. Never in my life have I seen a customization spread like this one. You can customize every aspect of sound and functionality to your liking. EVERYTHING. Lows, mids, highs, surround, positional volume levels, driver levels, every frequency response imaginable, all can be individually tweaked. And as if this wasn't enough, every button on the headset can be programmed to your preference with a few simple clicks. Want to create 3 different unique sound profiles? Perfect, save each to the software, and map them all to their own buttons that can be changed on the fly. You can even customize the LED's on the sides of the headset. Choose from 16.8 million colors, make them fade in and out, change the intensity...whatever you could possibly think of, this has it. I could go on and on here, but check out any youtube reviews to see more info on it. Now for the mic, another very important aspect of a good headset. As far as quality goes, I will say the mic on the G933's is very good. It is not going to sound as good as a premium boom mic such as the mod mic 4.0, but it does more than get the job done. You will sound clear and crisp. A very convenient feature is the flip up mute. Once the mic is about half way up, it will illuminate red, beep once, and become muted. This is extremely convenient, as other headsets such as the A50's give no notification that the mic is muted once flipped up. Oh and remember the software mentioned above? Yeah, you can adjust all settings for the mic as well, including sidetone. Yes, you read that right, you can program this to support sidetone (mic monitoring) on the PS4. Dear Lord, has this been an overlooked and ignored problem with the PS4 operating system. PS4 supports no sidetone whatsoever, and has driven me insane. Now I can finally hear myself in intense matches online with my friends, and I no longer scream unknowingly. Thank you Logitech.

Comfort/Build Quality: This headset is one of the most unique fits I've ever felt. They clamp firmly onto your head, but not too much. The earcup have more than enough room for your ears to not touch the drivers, and the material is...strange at first. The best way I can describe the ear muff material, is an abrasive thin mesh. At first I was put off from this, but after extended use, I have never felt a headset more breathable. My ears never get hot or sweaty, nor do I get any aches or pain from the cups. The headband is covered in the same abrasive material, but has medium firmness memory foam that rests on your head. Very, very comfortable. If I had to nit pick about anything however, it would be the cheaper feeling plastic that covers the rest of the headset. It's not horrible, but the earcups will swivel and flop everywhere while you hold it. Not a dealbreaker, but slightly annoying. Another awesome detail they added are the removable faceplates on the sides of the headset. They are magnetic, and can even house the usb dongle inside one of the earcups. Even the battery is removable/replaceable. This is something all headsets should come with. Once again, thank you Logitech.

Features: So usually I would cover features of a headset, as far as extra things they can do, but this one does them all. Like mentioned above, the customization is unrivaled, even on headsets twice this price. Simple things like being able to pair this with your cell phone, and answering calls while gaming is insane, and has literally changed my expectations on what a headset should have. Even in the box you get all braided cables including; 1 usb to micro usb cable, 1 3.5mm male to male aux cable with both mic and audio input, and the rca passthrough cables. Completely above and beyond what they could have done, and for a reasonable price. Battery life is also incredible. With LED's on constantly, you'll get roughly 6-7 hours on a full charge. With no LED's on, you get over 12 hours.

Overall: I have nothing but praise for this headset. I own many other pairs, but this one makes all of them look bad. Combine that with the deep customization, quality cables and materials used, and good customer service, this should be a no brainer if your even on the fence at all. Stop looking at Astro's, save yourself $150 and get these.

I will also update with pictures as soon as possible. Thanks for reading!

EDIT 07 Nov 2016: Headset is still working perfectly. I have absolutely no gripes or complaints.

EDIT 10 JAN 2017: 0 complaints. Headset still working perfect. My wife uses it daily now and I'm using the ASRO's.(She likes this headset better)

title: May want to consider the Nest...
text:
I ordered this directly from Logitech ($30 off so I went with them).

The good?? Extremely easy to setup. No messing about and literally within a couple of minutes you're up and running. The picture quality is great (all the way up to 1080) and it has decent audio and, mic capabilities.

The bad... Well... I have had it no more than 8 hours and I have had to reset it twice. It goes off line and doesn't want to come back up. Their troubleshooting blames wifi signal strength but, it's only 5 feet from the source so that's definitely not it (and I don't have issues with anything else wireless). The app settings for alerts are a little counter-intuitive. It seems no matter what I set it to it's tracking and recording activity.

So... We will see what happens here in the next few days. If I have to keep resetting it - it will be going back to Logitech. I had an older LNC104 (lorex) that was great but, finally gave up the ghost (it was 4 or 5 years old). I had gone between this cam and the nest and, I'm already feeling like I may have made the wrong choice.

-------------------
Updated June 18, 2016

Logitech pushed a new version of their software out to IOS and, this seems to have fixed the issue with the camera going offline and not being able to turn it back on. So - I bumped up the star rating one (to 4). Really a toss up between this and the nest I think.

title: I REALLY wanted to LOVE this product...
text:
I am typing my review for the iPad mini ultra thin Logitech keyboard on the keyboard itself in order to be able to get a better feel for the keyboard,

Pros:

Very light and thin. Fits in a purse, along with my iPad mini which makes taking it out and working anywhere very convenient.

Very aesthetically pleasing. It's really cute, and like I said before, takes up such little space, it doesn't have that cumbersome feel that a laptop would have, especially when you're in a public place, like a restaurant or anywhere where you don't want to draw too much attention to your work. It’s almost like pulling out your cellphone.

I like being able to keep my iPad in its own case when using this keyboard. It would be inconvenient to have to take it out of its case and attach it to the keyboard, This could be a con for some people however.

Cons:

One of the cons is actually one of the pros. The keyboard is so small, it does take some time in order to get used to the keyboard. My hands are relatively small, and they do tend to hit each other when I'm typing. Being that the keys will inevitably be placed in a different location on a smaller keyboard, it’s obvious that one would need time to get used to a new keyboard, especially when used to typing on a much bigger traditional laptop. Maybe I’ll get used to this with time.

Like I mentioned before, I keep my iPad in the cover I purchased for it, because I like the angle it provides when I’m working with the keyboard, and because I want to keep my iPad protected, This can be a con for some people who are hoping to be able to insert the iPad into the keyboard itself and be able to work on it. The angle is too straight for my taste, and although in the pictures, both on the site and on the box, it shows that you can somewhat tilt the iPad a little more, I wasn't able to. It could be just me though.

As I am writing this review, I find the keyboard slipping from side to side a little too much for my taste. The little rubber on the bottom doesn't help keep it steady in place. For $40, I wouldn't expect to have to buy something to make it stop sliding around. I tried using it on different surfaces, and it didn't help much. It doesn't feel level. It feels like a table with one leg slightly longer than the other three, if that makes any sense.

Upon receiving the product, I also noticed that the box itself was not sealed, the way you would expect a new product be sealed. I have the feeling it was used and returned. It looks a little dirty too, which is very noticeable since it's white. :( The product I purchased says "new".

All in all, it's just OK. There are way more cons than pros. It's too bad, because it's so darn cute, and as I've continued to type in it, I feel I am getting more and more used to the keys, but the keyboard keeps sliding, and I keep pushing on the comma key instead of the period, because of the close proximity of the two.

Out of all the cons though, I have to say what bothers me the most is the sliding of the keyboard. I know I can easily fix this by sticking something to the bottom to keep it from sliding, but for the money paid, I don't feel I should have to spend more money on correcting a manufacturing flaw.

I REALLY wanted to love this, but that one flaw alone is a deal breaker for me. Maybe mine was just defective, and I should exchange it instead of just returning it and trying another keyboard, judging by all the great reviews…

If anyone who has had it for longer or loves theirs has any comments or recommendations, I would love to hear from you!

title: Great mouse for gamers!
text:
I play mostly FPS games now like Overwatch and Counter-Strike:GO so I wanted a accurate and comfortable mouse. I have a hybrid claw and palm grip ( medium sized hand ) and I find this mouse pretty comfortable. I use to play with the mx518 a long time ago and I find this to have a similar form factor and feel. I've went through many mouses in the past such as Corsair, Mionix, Razer, and Steel Series ones.

Pros:
+ Nice form factor, fits well for my hybrid claw grip
+ LED is nice and bright with a few futures through the included program ( although I do wish there were more options )
+ Style, It just looks simply sexy
+ Upgrade from the previous version since they removed the blue part so it would match the RGB more

Cons:
- The wheel on infinite mode can be... annoying sometimes as it is so slick that it moves a tad over or less more than you want it to.
- The sniper button is ANNOYING. it could be my grip, but I always accidentally press it. I simply deactivated it
- Wish it was a little lighter
- The rubber part on the right side sometimes hurts my ring finger ( could be my grip again, I hold it kind of tight ) The rubber is textured.

Overall TLDR:
+ I Like this mouse and I will most likely keep it to play my FPS games. Seems accurate and everything. Good for claw hybrid grips. Sniper button is annoying though.. deactivate it unless you really want to use it. Can be a little lighter, but it is manageable. I rate this as a BUY!

title: A simple pop off of the battery cover if it shoots out easily you are good to go
text:
Dead on replacement for the harmony 1. This is my second replacement, all these batteries end up swelling and bloating and getting stuck in. At these prices I would suggest ordering in pairs and checking on them regularly. Once they swell to a certain size they are a definite pain to get out, almost to the point of needing to disassemble the device.

You can definitely tell they are on the way out when you need to charge it daily, but sadly by the time you realize it, it might be too late. A simple pop off of the battery cover if it shoots out easily you are good to go, if it doesn't immediately come out, probably a time for a change.

title: Awesome mouse
text: This mouse is a great upgrade to the M705 for those looking for a bluetooth mouse.  This mouse can be used with the unifying dongles OR bluetooth.  Most of the new laptops nowadays have bluetooth built in so to be able to pair this with your laptop through bluetooth and not waste a usb port is awesome as some devices only have 1 or 2 usb ports. I've only ran into a few quirks when using this via bluetooth on windows 7, you need to make sure you have the latest chipset bluetooth drivers for it to work well, the generic windows 7 bluetooth drivers do not support bluetooth smart or low energy which is what this mouse uses.  This is very important and I don't recall seeing it in the description because if your device has any bluetooth version older than 4 and does not have bluetooth smart or low energy this will not work with it.  But that being said it is an amazing mouse, I use it for work almost all day long.  It's a great design, love the bluetooth, and the battery life of 2 years with 1 AA battery is great for a bluetooth mouse.  This mouse also has the mousewheel that you can have clicky or press the button and it will scroll freely for going through long pages.  Also has forward and back buttons on the side which are great for web browsing.  Just a hint if you are trying to re-pair with a device via bluetooth you press and hold the device button.  Overall great mouse and I highly recommend.

title: Decent Speakers for the Price
text:
For the price, they are decent speakers. They are a decent size form factor for a small desk as I use them on. They provide decent mid and high range, but lack in the low range (which is to be expected with 2.0 speakers at this price). I have them connected to a desktop amplifier ([[ASIN:B000KIPT30 Behringer HA400 4-Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier]]) and the low range is not improved much. The power cord for these speakers is modular meaning it is removable from the speaker, but the wire connecting the two speakers as well as the wire with the 3.5mm jack is permanently attached to the speakers themselves. This can make cable management a little tricky.
Pros:
- Good size for small desk
- Good price
- Decent Aesthetic
Cons:
- Speakers permanently attached to each other
- Non-Modular aux cable
- Lacking low range sound
Overall, these speakers are decent for the price, but there are better speakers out there.

tl;dr: Decent speakers for the price, lacking low end sound

title: This is a great bluetooth adapter
text:
I needed a Bluetooth adapter for my Yamaha receiver, since my dog destroyed my previous setup. I had been using an ipod classic connected via a 1/8'' to rca cable to my receiver. This worked fine for the last several years, until last week when the doorbell rang, my dog jumped off the couch, caught the cable, sent the ipod flying across the room, and almost pulled the receiver off its shelf. Needless to say, it was time to go wireless.

My hesitation towards devices such as this has always been based on sound quality and the compression that's used in the Bluetooth conversion process, but when I read a very favorable review of this adapter when used with a high-end system, I decided I'd give it a shot. I have been very happy with the results. I don't hear any of the compression artifacts that have been associated with Bluetooth in the past, and this unit seems to have a good dac, even though Logitech doesn't specify which one it uses.

Some of the best features: compact size, rca or 1/8" output, great sound, decent range, and easy pairing with instant connection with previously paired devices. It all adds up to a great little adapter that will keep my ipad mini on the couch, instead of the floor. Sadly, the ipod classic was damaged beyond repair.

The controller functions in the "joystick setup" menu at the FF7 start screen, but once you enter the game it doesn't work. I spent hours researching and troubleshooting to no avail. No real excuse for compatibility issues, since it's a new game, new controller with newest driver, new computer running Windows 10, etc. I suppose it might work in "x input mode" if I wanted to take the time to map all the controls, but I shouldn't have to do that. title: Waste of money and time
text:
I have fairly large hands which makes finding a comfortable mouse very difficult. After putting my palm on an MX Master in the store, I knew this mouse would be comfortable enough to use for long periods, yet functional enough to use for both gaming and programming. Also, the fact that it has both Bluetooth and 2.4ghz radio connectivity with a switch on the mouse makes this a dream for a setup where I'm constantly switching between a Macbook Pro and a Windows desktop. It would even accommodate a third connection if I had another computer with Bluetooth or another Logitech Unifying Receiver. I received the mouse as a gift and was not disappointed when I took it out of the package. Besides being just as comfortable as I expected, it connected with both of my computers effortlessly. One feature I hadn't expected to like was the middle wheel, which will switch from clicky to smooth without having to hit the mode switch button, I simply flick the wheel up or down and I can scroll through many pages of content. I also like Logitech's new software, which stays hidden, doesn't take long to load on boot, is attractive, responsive and featureful. I really thought I would love this mouse. I really want to love this mouse. Unfortunately, thanks to Logitech, I can't.

Like every other Mac user here, the Bluetooth experience is laggy, jerky, and sometimes unresponsive. Unfortunately, it's the same for my Windows desktop, which uses the 2.4ghz receiver. Aside from an infrequently used Xbox 360 game pad, the only other wireless radio nearby is my router, which is 20ft away (the Macbook is on the 5ghz network, but others nearby sometimes use the 2.4ghz connection). If Logitech can't make a wireless mouse that can handle connecting to a computer 2 feet away because of some interference 20 feet away, then they need to get out of the business. I contacted support about a week ago and have since gotten one rather weak response asking me to change the channel the mouse uses and disable all possible wireless interference (temporarily). Neither of these worked, and the last suggestion isn't actually possible. They haven't responded further yet.

What's clear to me is that the MX Master is a great concept poorly executed and Logitech is not exactly excited to help their customers with a $80 mouse. As a long-time Logitech user and someone who thought they finally had an appropriately sized mouse, I'm disappointed. As someone who is holding onto an expensive waste of space, I'm pretty angry. Judging by reviews here and elsewhere on the Internet, Logitech could be looking at a class action suit if they don't make things right.

My review? Don't bother. If you were to get one that works, it'd be great, but there's a good chance you won't.

**UPDATE**

Customer service got back to me. They acknowledged that it's a hardware problem and said they would ship me another one free of charge. This was a good move. A bit more than two weeks later, my replacement arrived. The problem is still very much present over bluetooth, though noticeably improved. With two unifying receivers, I have one in my desktop and the other in my Macbook's hub. This has stopped the mouse from randomly disconnecting over bluetooth, but it's still laggy and jerky - not nearly as much, but enough to be irritating.

About a week after the replacement arrived, I got a follow-up email from service to make sure my problem was addressed. At this point, I had tested the mouse enough to be sure that it also wasn't working, so I responded to let them know. I haven't heard back from Logitech, and they've marked my service issue as 'solved', which is kind of a joke.

Logitech used to be the champion. Now I know not to buy from them.

title: Perfect for video chats!
text: This was a gift, so in being cautious, I spent about an hour comparing webcams. Some did not offer 720p, some required USB and 3.5mm microphone jack (Those connections are analog and some mic quality and signal strength is lost when converting back and forth between analog and digital unnecessarily.), some had complex software driver installations, and other cams just cost to much to consider (I wanted to stay under $30 US). In the end, I bought the Logitech C270 as a gift for my sister and her 7 year old daughter near Seattle. Neither of them are very technically inclined, so my hopes were high that this webcam would work without any problems. Ease of use was another key factor since I am very technical, but could not be there to install it since I'm across the country in St. Louis. The C270 worked flawlessly. Within 10 minutes of delivery, the camera was unpacked, installed (No drivers needed on Win7. It uses a single USB connector, no other connections are necessary AND it keeps the microphone all digital), and we were video chatting. The built-in microphone with noise cancelling worked very well. I heard the conversation, no other noises in their living room. The video quality was also excellent. The image was clear, frame rate was smooth, and non-pixelized at full screen (we used 1920 x 1080 even though this is a 720p camera). But, keep in mind that video quality is largely dependent on network speed. We used Skype to chat and I'm pretty sure Skype auto-adjusts the quality vs. speed during a video call. Overall, I am very happy with this purchase.

title: Longtime Harmony One user unhappy with this very expensive remote.
text:
Owned a couple of Harmony One remotes which we loved because they worked so well. When one of them finally died, I decided to upgrade to a much higher level currently available one, but more expensive is not always better, it seems.

Problems with this remote are:

Not enough delineation between the buttons. They look cool, but they are so low profile and sensitive that it's easy to hit the wrong button in the dark or a combination of buttons by mistake.

Very twitchy motion control. I pick up this remote and very often the screen changes to something like "Pick a device" or some other screen other than one of the ones for the current activity.

Clicking on buttons and having something completely different than expected happen. This could be related to the first item I listed, but sometimes I can't even reproduce what happened. Bizarre.

I regret buying this as it was very pricey, but as it's too late to return it and replace it with maybe 350 or 650 model I guess I'm stuck with it.

title: Now the bad. The latest app update has completely hosed connectivity ...
text:
As a remote and an IR repeater/blaster, this works well. My only gripe is that my kids keep misplacing the remote - sure could use a locator on this "connected" device.

Now the bad. The latest app update has completely hosed connectivity over my WLAN. The device says it's connecting locally, but then flips to "connecting to hub through cloud" - every time. title: Making videos can be so much fun and so can doing live streaming
text:
[[VIDEOID:aae249ca5cb4c5661454106a197bf49b]] Making videos can be so much fun and so can doing live streaming, but sometimes it can be a bit frustrating. Having to change your camera location can be tough, or maybe you are lucky enough to have a friend or some one help switch your shots. Either way, it's not ideal. This can make videos so much better with the ability to change camera angles or zoom in and out on the fly. This would also make shooting live video so much better as well.

Well, now you can thanks to Livestream and the Mevo. I have been loving the different features it has. I truly feel like I have a large studio at my beck and call. I no longer have to stop shooting to reposition cameras or make a lot of post edits. This little device will change the way I do my video reviews.

Now streaming-wise, the Mevo is a game changer, being able to adjust the filters and angles will enhance my FB live videos in a way I could not before. I am very impressed with what this little beauty can do for my video work. My only gripe is that at least as of the time writing this, it only outputs 720p video. I just wanted to disclose, I preordered this from Mevo’s website a few months back and have only had it a few days for testing, but so far I am very happy minus the 720p. Still, the Mevo will come in handy for all of my new video work.

title: Great alexa integration
text:
This is the second one of these remotes I've purchased.

I bought the first for my aunt around 3 years ago. She is the type of person where if you need to change inputs or use more than one remote for anything, she is absolutely lost. This remote solved all of her problems and saved me from having to go to her house every two weeks to fix her TV when she inevitably got stuck on a different input.

I just recently bought one for myself to pair with my Echo. I have a projector and a HTPC and am fine with having multiple remotes. However, with the Alexa integration, I love this thing. All I say is "Alexa, turn on the Xbox" and it turns on my TV, turns on my reciever, sets the input to HDMI4 and turns on the xbox. From there "Alexa, turn on the computer" and it turns off the xbox and switches over to my HTPC on HDMI5.

Finally, when I'm groggily heading to bed I just say "Alexa, turn off the TV" and it turns everything off.

title: Yes! Works with Windows 10 (64 Bit on my rig) and with all the newer games I've played!
text:
I bought this controller through another vendor, not through Amazon, but wanted to leave a review here because for some reason it is getting negative reviews as to it doesn't work with Windows 10 (its just a doorstop for Windows 10, etc), okay people take a deep breath, go on Logitech's website, download the latest drivers if you bought this controller before they released the update if amazon will let me post the link ( http://support.logitech.com/en_us/product/wireless-gamepad-f710#download ) they have both 32 bit and 64 bit drivers available of the Gaming Software and Gamepad connect software. Set the logitech controller to the X on the switch in the back, which is the Xbox input setting not the old Direct X 9 and lower setting, install the batteries, plug in the receiver and enjoy. If for some reason this doesn't work as others have said you can go on Microsoft's website and download the Xbox 360 driver for Windows 8 and Up (Win 10) and then set the F710 as a Xbox 360 device in device manager. For the RECORD I have this controller working without any problems on Windows 10 Pro 64 Bit, yes occasionally I may have to unplug replug the receiver after the computer been in hibernate for a while, but hasn't really been an issue, and I've played dozens of games with this controller with hours of enjoyment, just use Energizer Lithium or Advanced batteries to get more playtime.

Games I've played through Steam on this Controller with full support:

Sleeping Dogs
Tomb Raider (2013 version)
GTA IV + Eps from Lib City
Far Cry
Watch Dogs
and more...

EA Games:
Need for Speed
Battefield (required PC restart after install before first time playing to recognize the controller)
Mirror's Edge (2009 version)

Older PC Games (using the D Input _ Direct X 9 ):
Tomb Raider Legend / Anniversary Edition
and more....

I've been a fan of Logitech products and in my opinion Logitech products offer great bang for the buck, and this controller IS ACTUALLY LESS EXPENSIVE than the Xbox One or Xbox 360 controllers consider you don't have to buy an extra wireless adapter for it!

Note: All games were played and installed on a Windows 10 64 Bit system.

title: Great Mouse, Maybe More So For Bigger Hands
text:
I'll start by saying that I purchased this mouse after having used both Anker and Reddragon mouses (mice?) in the past. I got rid of the Anker when I built my new black-and-red-themed PC and the blue didn't match. From that I went to an ambidextrous Reddragon mouse. It was very light (around $20 mouse), but it did its job until the thumb buttons got gunked up and couldn't be cleaned in any way. Enter the Logitech G502. OVERALL FEEL
This mouse is amazing. I'm an avid player of the new Star Wars Battlefront game (2.78KD, 200+hrs, 38,000+kills). I mention stats not to brag but to show that I've used this mouse quite a bit. About 1/2 of the total time I've spent on Star Wars has been with this mouse, and it has served me very well. It's a right-handed mouse which fits very well in the hand. I personally didn't have to add any weights to it at all. If you move to this from a cheaper, ligther mouse then you probably will have the same transition I did: having so much mouse to hold on to in my hand makes up for a lot of weight.

BUILD INFO
If you're moving from another nice gaming mouse to this, I'll mention some more nit-picky things. The mouse wheel is heavy and confident, but if you spin it and let it spin freely, it'll start to make a noise that's similar to a squeak after a bit. It's kind of annoying, but it was my own fault for mistreating it. The top two thumb buttons are well-placed, but I find it a bit hard to get my thumb (I'm 5'9" and about as "normal" sized as you can get) back down to the "sniper"/DPI change button. For people with a wider thumb it might be easier. The other 2 buttons on the index clicker (default DPI up/down) are easy to get to. I have the front one programmed to my combat roll, as it's a very efficient reach to get to it.

I also notice that I have ample room in front of my fingers on the clickers even when I palm the mouse. I play with a hybrid palm/claw grip but mostly claw. I would think someone with much bigger hands than my own could palm this comfortably. The thumb lip which keeps your thumb from dragging your mouse pad is fantastic. I often rubbed that part of my thumb raw, as I play with 950DPI and therefore do a lot of moving and resetting of the mouse.

CONCLUSION
I believe if you're in the market for a mouse in this price range, you would definitely not be disappointed with this mouse. I have several friends who use this and also have nothing but good things to say about it. They love the way you can add the weight to whatever part of the mouse that you'd like to in order to fit your personal taste. If you're on the fence like I was, just do yourself a favor and go for it. You'll be happy with it.

Happy buying!

The app works great, and the buttons are fully customizable. This is great if you want to set up "grandma mode" with just the basic buttons. I wish the iPad app wasn't just landscape though. The app is absolutely the best thing about the Harmony Hub.

No better remote than your phone IMO, since you have it with you all the time. Definitely worth the price. You can just get the hub if you don't care for the physical remote and want to save money. Great product!
