title: Bass playback through the sub has a very singular sound to it that doesn't really seem like anything other than slurpy bass nons
text:
Consider this a retroactive (and more critical/analytical) review; I owned these speakers from roughly 2010 to 2013 and used them as my desktop speakers before handing them off to a relative. In the time since, I've since pursued a career in audio, and I found myself using these as reference speakers for a recent mix. Coming back to listen to these speakers for the first time in years, I thought I'd offer up my evaluation while still giving the system a fair rating for its affordability.

It's hard to argue with the price point. At $30, these are priced appropriately. Properly mastered audio will sound decent enough, though anything with a wider than average dynamic range will suffer, to an extent. These speakers are only capable of "filling the room" with the bass from the sub, which is decent for the price. The low-end cutoff at 48Hz is something that will be noticeable to anyone used to working with the full range of the audio spectrum. The bass region, frequency-wise, is from roughly 200Hz down to 60. 60Hz down to 20 is sub-bass. Because of the cutoff, the sub -- while still producing an ample amount of bass, given the overall size of the system -- is a bit lacking in terms of fullness/punch.

Bass playback through the sub has a very singular sound to it that doesn't really seem like anything other than slurpy bass nonsense. It doesn't have the "reach" to provide the listener with anything remotely detailed, and it sounds too fluid (as opposed to solid, or somewhere in between). There's more of a loose rumble to the bass than any sort of deep impact/punch, if that makes any sense, but, again, for the price...

All that aside, I imagine that the bass should be sufficient enough for the majority of listeners. What strikes me as being a bit more universal, however, is the quality (or lack thereof) in the two remaining speakers. It's somewhat understandable, considering how small the tweeters are, that the higher midrange/treble would suffer, but anyone with high frequency loss or those who are simply less sensitive to the higher range of the spectrum should likely consider purchasing a different system altogether.

On paper, these speakers extend all the way up to 20Khz, but raw specs aren't everything. It's all about the actual 'curve' of the frequency response -- which frequencies the speakers churn out at the highest output. Typically, consumer speakers deliver a more bass-heavy frequency response with a light dip in the mid-range and light rolloff in the high treble, which makes sense for the majority of people. Above the age of 30, most of us won't be able to hear much of anything above 16Khz, and it takes more 'energy' for bass to be perceived at an approximate loudness to midrange/treble frequencies, as our ears naturally perceive these as being louder due to increased sensitivity to these frequencies. I was therefore expecting some dip in these areas, but the 'curve' to the Z313's response comes a little too soon and a little too steep.

Frequencies around 5Khz-6Khz are an area of the spectrum I consider crucial, as they provide presence and precision, in many cases -- fairly nebulous concepts to discuss, but the sort of thing that you simply feel/sense upon hearing. A discerning listener will know if it's lacking, even if they can't put their finger on what it is in specific terms. This is the area where these speakers begin to 'dip' in their response. Granted, the following determinations are made primarily through listening to material played back through the speakers and determining the approximate response of each area of the spectrum by ear rather than any 'official' measurement, but considering I was well versed in the frequency response for each track I tested and the listening room was flat, I stand by these self-made measurements. For what it's worth, I was listening at around my average listening level of 60 to 70db spl.

Around 5Khz is where these speakers 'peak', and the perceived volume of the higher frequencies take a gradual nosedive from that point on with a tiny little boost somewhere around the 10Khz-12Khz region or so. This leads to a listening experience that sounds muddy and -- depending on the content -- muffled or "small". The tweeters can't output 'detailed' higher frequency content given their small scale and design, which is understandable, but this dip is more noticeable than most other systems I've come across at similar price points in similar sizes. There's very little sense of 'air' to these speakers as a result, meaning that harmonic content and nuances in the treble/high treble range will seem lacking.

Oddly enough, I believe the signal is boosted a bit somewhere around 250-500Hz, as well -- perhaps in some bizarre attempt to offset the dip in treble response -- but adding more fullness to the lower mid-range is like trying to fix the problem by, uh, making the problem worse. The subwoofer's already thumping away with frequencies just below that region, and without the detail afforded by the treble, the slightly boosted response in this region creates more of a 'wall of sound' effect than anything else. Which could have actually been deliberate -- since much of today's music and audio content is heavily compressed I can see how this sort of frequency curve would work for an 'average' listener, I guess. When everything's compressed/limited/maximized to the point where it sounds like you're listening to one big slice of sameness in terms of volume, you probably won't be sitting there bemoaning the fact that you're missing out on the fine details and nuances.

TL;DR / Moral of the story --

This system doesn't sound 'good', but it does what it does well enough given the price.Your room and the positioning of your speakers plays a HUGE role in how you perceive the sound of your equipment -- in a "flat" listening environment, these speakers are quite bad, but a more "colorful" location could provide a potentially more enjoyable experience. If you're hard of hearing or have high frequency loss, you may want to look elsewhere; lack of detailed midrange aside, the nosedive in frequency response from 6Khz and up coupled with the ham-fisted lower mid-range and sloppy sub-bass won't be doing your ears any favors.

That's all! I don't really know why I wrote this sprawling epic, but hopefully it benefits someone in some way or another.

title: Great Product, Difficult Setup
text:
I bought this Harmony 650 to replace an older Harmony 670 which I loved, but it was developing some button issues. First, let me say these are great products that really do enable you to control everything with one remote once you get them set up properly. I use mine to control a Vizio TV, AT&T cable box, Vizio sound bar, Sony DVD player, and Teac CD player.

This would have been a 5-star review had it not been for problems experienced during setup. The first problem was the USB cable that came with the remote was defective. Because of that the software was unable to establish a connection between my laptop and the remote. That is when I called tech support. Fortunately, unlike the older model, the 650 can use any micro USB cable like you would use to charge an Android smartphone or tablet. I was able to establish a connection with one of my Samsung USB cables.

Tech support then told me I would have to set up a new online account, because the older 670 software was not compatible with the newer 650 software. Once that was done, I was able to copy all my device settings from the old account to the new one, which saved a ton of setup time. But then the software had trouble updating the new remote with my settings. Tech support revealed at that point that Windows 10 was not 100% compatible with the Logitech software and I might have to do complete this process on another computer. However, after rebooting my laptop everything worked flawlessly and the 650 remote is now fully functional and working as expected.

In summary, this is a 5-star product, but I had a 3-star setup experience. However, the Logitech support guy was terrific, patient, and resourceful during the entire process. If not for him, this remote would have been returned to Amazon for a refund. I'm glad it worked out, because the buttons on the new remote are working much better than the old one.

title: Seeing keystroke delays? Try this.
text:
I installed this keyboard with a Logitech m510 mouse using a single unifying receiver. During initial testing, sometimes the keyboard would lose keystrokes, other times it would display nothing for 3 to 5 seconds and then... whoosh, all keystrokes magically appeared. I tried updating drivers, re-pairing the devices in the unifying software, uninstalling, reinstalling, etc. to no avail. Pretty frustrating.

Then I stumbled upon a Logitech forum post suggesting that the unifying receiver likes to be the ONLY USB 2.0 device. No big deal. I moved a USB DAC that was connected to a USB 2.0 port to a USB 3.0 port. Now everything is working as expected. Not sure this will work for anyone else but it's easy to try.

I reduced the score by one star because of the setup challenges. Overall, I like the K750 (and the m510).

title: Well rounded headsets for web conferencing
text:
I bought this for work. I got them at Bestbuy at around $80. What I was looking for was a good inexpensive wireless headset and microphone for webinars and conferencing. For work purposes it’s a nice pair of headphones good boom mic, people could hear me clearly with little or no background sounds. My desktop doesn’t have Bluetooth so the USB connection is a must and the ability to toggle between my phone that have Bluetooth is fantastic.

The battery life at about 5 hours is not ideal for having them on all the time when working, however, the ability to use the headsets while charging cuts back on the inconvenience. When the battery is running low there is a highly noticeable degradation of sound quality and connection before the warning beeps come on.

As for the sound, the sound is ok for normal volumes at high volumes it cracks. Listening to music feels bland. On the positive side, I don’t get lost into the music while working. Voices come out very clear. The build quality is a low, the headset itself feels fragile, and its lightweight and very comfortable to wear for extended periods of time. Good padding and light weight makes it great for all day use. The foam cushion doesn’t feel great on your ears but they are still comfy. On ear design allows for a ton of sound leakage from my surrounding which is great in an office environment like mine that prefers to shout out commands spontaneously.

For a good webinar/conference calling headset for work the headset passable with 4 stars, I wish the battery is better.

title: Pricey and bug ridden but the only game in town
text:
A system that does exactly what I needed but 1) Expensive and 2) Very, very buggy.
The companion system was a lot more attractive to me than the touch screen version, for reasons of price, reliability and not having to to constantly charge the remote. However, it took me a long time to set up, contrary to what is indicated by mainstream media reviews.

The user interface on the mobile app is not great. It has some very deep menus for setting up the activity buttons for instance, and I found it a lot less intuitive than the desktop software. The main reason for the slow setup, however, is that several "activities" had to be deleted and created multiple times, due to bugs. For instance an activity could report that my Roku had no channel capacity, and hence I could not set a start up channel. Only way around this was to delete the activity and start over. And about deleting,... some times deletion would not "take". Then the only solution was to restart the app, and try to delete the activity again.
Some functionality is only available on the desktop software, like custom icons. Some functionality is only available on the mobile app, like Roku startup channels. And some times the settings on the mobile does not sync with the settings on the desktop software. Only solution is to restart apps and try again.
So a 20 min setup job takes 2 hours, easily. But when you have gone through all the hassle, it works like a charm. And the remote looks like it will be hard to destroy, which comes in handy for kids.

text: I would love to give this a 5 star review, but I can't. I've been playing video games for about 26 years now, never really got into the whole mouse and keyboard thing, strictly console. I did a lot of research, and apparently this is the best mouse for gaming out there. It should be noted that I'm using this for PS4, via a XIM4 adapter. Mostly, it works perfectly. But there's one huge problem: the click wheel. It works when moving vertically 100% of the time, but when I try to move it horizontally, it only works sometimes, which is frustrating. Right now I'm trying to get adapted to the mouse/keyboard combo, so I'm only practicing on one game for now: Rainbow Six Siege. I set my wheel click right to change the fire mode, and the wheel click left to ping, and being able to change fire mode in the heat of the moment is critical. I thought I may have received a faulty mouse, but I received a replacement, and same problem. The problem was there before and after I updated the firmware. I also updated the firmware on my XIM4, then reset it to factory settings, nothing worked. I don't know if this is a problem overall, or a problem because I'm not playing on a PC, but nonetheless, it's a problem that shouldn't exist.

text:
I have been using the MX Master for a little more than a year now.

I waited soooooo long to have the MX Revolution next in class. That mouse lasted me years of heavy use before it finally lost it's left mouse click. I loved that mouse and for some years Logitech never made a replacement in the line so I had to switch to a stupid gaming mouse to get that awesome functionality of the MX Revolution. Hoooray, Logitech was coming out with a new Productivity mouse, the MX Master. Needless to say I was very excited to get my "hand" on one. What a huge DISAPPOINTMENT this mouse is comparative to the MX Revolution!!!! Sooo sad. Let me first say there are a couple of things I like about the MX Master which didn't change or improved upon from the MX Revolution. Large Size is good, hyper scroll is great, design is nice looking and multi user assignment is nice but not necessary for me. I like the charge on the go capability. Here's what I loved about the MX Revolution that the MX Master has failed to live up too. Thumb Scroll, why did they mash the thumb scroll and forward/back buttons together, I got used to it, but totally not necessary. Also, I liked that the thumb wheel also acted as a push in button on the MX Revolution, no dumb button hidden under the thumb rest that doesn't work after 10 uses. Integration into Excel. Whoa, the MX Master does not play nice with Excel like the MX Revolution used to. Soooo Sad. Update after update, still didn't work. Can't switch between tabs with forward / back buttons, despite the "Program Specific" capabilities. Lame lame lame lame lame lame. Normally I wouldn't mind the price tag, but when it doesn't live up to predecessors, not worth even half what I paid, I paid full price. I remember watching the video for the mouse before it was delivered. I was sooo excited, now I just want to chuck it against the F'n wall. I'll be posting this on Amazon to help protect people from getting an over priced piece of garbage. F'n disgusted with the down turn in Logitech quality.

title: It's easy to see why this is a top selling keyboard
text:
It's easy to see why this is a top selling keyboard. It's easy to install - just plug in the dongle and pull the tab that allows the pre-installed batteries to connect. (There's no "insert this CD" or crapware - YAY!) The upside of this is immediate usability. The downside is that some features don't work, or don't work the say you'd like. To completely take advantage of the keyboard, you need to go to the Logitech web site and download their specific software. It's easy to do, but no on will tell you to do this. When you do get the software, you can customize the function of many keys. For example, you can determine what the keyboard "power" key does. Seems that the default was sleep mode, but most people (or at least "I") would assume that it would perform a Shutdown. All the media ad function keys are easily customizable, so programmers or Excel fans can use them as "F1", "F2", etc., while others can use them as their other labels, for MS Word, MS Excel, etc.
Also, this keyboard came up in response to a search for "ergonomic keyboard". I was specifically searching for a split keyboard (like the old Microsoft keyboards that had each row of keys split in half and presented at an angle). If that's what you're looking for, this keyboard will be awkward. If you merely like a keyboard that's a little easier to use and feels better, you'll be fine.

SUMMARY:
Advantages:
Reasonably priced
Easy to install - just plug it in!
Comfortable to use
Many shortcut keys for launching commonly used programs
More fully customizable with Logitech software
Disadvantages ( No real "disadvantages", but...)
Requires Logitech software to unleash the full power of all the keys
Not really "ergonomic"

This is based on a week's use. Will update if my opinion changes.

title: I have been pleasantly surprised by how good this little streaming camera is
text:
In every way, I have been pleasantly surprised by how good this little streaming camera is. There seem to be some detractors who expected it to perform miracles, so lets address the complaints:

1) The footage is grainy in low light:
Yes it is. Just like footage from any digital camera is grainy in low light. I have a GoPro Hero Black that suffers the same loss of quality in less than ideal lighting situations. Even my Canon 70D struggles indoors without proper studio lighting. That's how cameras work.

2) Short battery life:
Two and a half hours of video recording and streaming from a WiFi enabled device this size is pretty good. Not great, but certainly nothing to complain about.

3) Software isn't responsive:
This one totally confuses me - the software is EXCELLENT. I was shocked at how easy it is to set up, either over WiFi or by having the Mevo create its own hotspot for your phone or tablet to link with. Controls are simple and intuitive and the real-time preview window always lets you know what is being broadcast out. External audio is simple - you just plug it into your phone or tablet's headphone jack (so carry that dongle with you, iPhone 7 users).

4) The recorded audio is hard to hear:
Audio records from a microphone on the front of the Mevo. If you are close to it, it records better. If you are far away, it sounds like you are far away. The camera can't change how sound travels through a room, but you can add additional microphones into the recording mix. I do live home tours with an agent who is laved with a wireless mic while feeding low ambient music into the Mevo at the same time. The result is pretty magical.

5) WiFi connection is spotty:
This one is legitimate. When connected over my phone's data, the camera performs flawlessly. If I switch to my WiFi network and try to introduce audio, it (eventually) crashes every time. I am hoping this improves with a direct CAT-5 connection via the Mevo Boost.

For the $200 I paid (I got one of the early Kickstarter versions) I cannot imagine a better solution for live video. Even at the full retail $400, it blows away similar competition. If you don't expect the impossible, you will not be disappointed.

I never dreamed I could have such a solid live streaming kit that could fit in a small backpack. I can easily add the Mevo into my existing video setup and run both with no trouble. I'd happily buy it again at full price.

title: Great Christmas Present, Room for Improvement
text:
I bought this device for my husband as our "entertainment center" (not) is exceptionally difficult to work with. We have a Magnavox and it would continually cycle through the different inputs until is randomly hit hmdi2. We also have an ir switch to cycle between other components (Roku) and I thought this would work with ir devices (which it does quite nicely).

Now for the disclosure. I paid full price with no incentives. I am a 40ish mother who is probably somewhat more adept at these funky gadgets than others in my age/sex category. The most difficult part of the initial setup is that Harmony wants to "see" (or rather has to) all of your components. I'm thinking okayyyy...how difficult could this be. Well, that all depends. It wants the brand name and model number of each component. Fun. Some were really straight forward, others were written for faires and you could not discern the model number that is like .00001 inches tall. Get your glasses, a magnifying glass or , a geek, anything that will help with this.

So, now you have put in all of the information, it is time to set up actions. This is where the fun is (no, really). For example, to turn on my TV I have to turn on the tv, turn on cable, switch the ir to selection 1, then finally set the TV back to hdmi 2. Then I set my most popular news channel to switch to as the default. Yeaaaaa! This is what we have struggled with for ages. It used to take up 3-4 tries for the tv to "land" on hdmi 2 without this device. Practically worth the money for this feature alone.

To get to Roku I made a "Change to Roku" action. Turn all components on (basically copy the Turn The TV action). Then switch your ir device to wherever Roku is. At this point, you can set all your Roku Stations to pop up on the remote control screen. This is the same with the TV action. You just pick all your favorite stations and the appear on the screen. So far so good.

Just about any device you have is programmable with this remote. I also use Alexa with this which is fun. No more fumbling around at 5am looking for the remote. Now it is just, Alexa, turn on the TV, and "poof" the TV is on.

Now for the items that I feel are definitely lacking. ESPECIALLY for 300 bucks. The remote needs numbers. It needs to integrate with Roku better. I can get "on" Roku, but if I feel like channel system is totally lagging. If you actually wanted to type a few words in the search box it would take over 10 minutes because of the lag. So I still need to keep my Roku channel changer handy for Roku Surfing. Also, since you can turn on, off, and change channels with Alexa, why can't you voice scroll up and down? For 300.00 I am pretty disappointed by this fact. I really expected everything to be top notch.

Having said all that, it was still a really cool Christmas Present.

title: The M705 is a great mouse, it is everything you expect from a ...
text:
I own two these mouses, one at work and one at home. I have only owned both for a couple months. I am a software engineer and push my peripherals to the max. The M705 is a great mouse, it is everything you expect from a solid device, ergonomically well thought out, great button placement, instant connectivity to different computers of mine, no connectivity issues with Windows 7 or Windows 10 and works on different surfaces without an issue, haven't tried glass though.

Alas, there is one reason I didn't give it 5 stars. The Scroll Mode button on the top is rather high. It is higher than the pictures convey to the point I thought maybe there was a depressed lock catch from the Scroll Mode button that was being displayed in the Amazon pictures. This Scroll Mode button brushes the underside of my middle finger when scrolling and clicking the scroll button. The Scroll Mode button even touches the inside of my right ring finger from time to time in the neutral holding of the mouse. This is something many might notice, but again, I am a major geek and I noticed it to the point that I thought of filing down the Scroll Mode button.

See I have used Logitech MX610s for years, they do not make this model any more, but if you look at the top of it, there is no Scroll Mode button on top, the MX610 has the Scroll Mode underneath: http://www.amazon.com/Logitech-Cordless-Laser-Mouse-931350-0403/dp/B000BFO4OC

I can see where changing Scroll Mode on the fly is handy though, I have never done this with my Logitech mouses. I always have the smooth fast scroll mode on, but I have started trying to be mindful of switching to the line by line precision scroll mode when reading a document, and then having the Scroll Mode button on top is a nice feature. I think I decently speed read though so not sure if I would switch Scroll Mode on the fly real world.

So again, its something most might not even notice but I don't like how the Scroll Mode button brushes the underneath and side of my middle and ring finger at times and this just might be from years of being used to the Logitech MX610.

By the way both my Logitech MX610s, I think one is a decade old still work, the left click responsiveness in one seems a little degraded but the sturdiness and longevity of Logitech products are excellent. I have consider going back to my Logitech MX610s, which are sitting in a drawer on standby. I just grabbed one and rested my hand on it, and the higher ergonomic rise if the M705 is immediately missed, the part that your palm cups around, so I think I prefer the ergonomics of the M705. Now I just try and tell my mind that the Scroll Mode brushing of my fingers is part of the experience and that is working for me though I still get a little bothered by it, I am sure my monkey brain will get over it in a couple more months.

title: This is a great remote! I got this when it was on ...
text:
This is a great remote!

I got this when it was on the deal of the day. Overall it is a good upgrade from the Harmony 650, and the MyHarmony software allows you to transfer your settings from an old Logitech remote to this one.

Pros:
-Nice sleek design.
-Touch screen, good dots per inch so could be read with ease.

-App for Android is well designed and allows some modifications to the setup.

-The software on the PC is very flexible, and once you are past the initial setup you could edit your remote from anywhere without needing it connected to the PC (I changed somethings while on vacation in Egypt!)

Cons:
-The transfer from the old remote wasn't without bumps and hiccups as the remote froze twice and had to start over and didnt fully transfer.
-Half way through the setup the remote notified me it needs to be in the same room with the hub and the devices it will control, so had to abort and start again in a different room.
-The play/pause etc buttons are at the very top above the screen, they probably would have been better on the lower half of the remote (this might be more of a habit for me coming from the 650 which had all the buttons below the screen).
-Sometimes if you make too many changes on the remote to the layout of buttons and icons it asks to sync with the hub and then ends up deleting all your changes, so need to save every few steps.

title: A great addition to the MX lineup
text:
This is a great mouse and I have used a variety other Logitech product, and this one is one of my favorites. Lately I've used the MX Performance, G700s, G502 Proteus Core. I've upgraded my work mice from the MX Performance to the MX Master, while using the G502 for gaming at home.
I have really big hands and I am using the mouse with a fingertip grip and it is quite comfortable. I find that using the palm grip, I am unable to hit the forward and back buttons easily, though those with smaller hands would definitely find the mouse more comfortable to use in any grip. The unique texture pattern on the side gives it a very unique and understated look. It doesn't stand out as much as other gaming mice with LED lighting but is a great looking mouse nonetheless. The mouse overall feels solid in the hand, definitely a very solid construction and a luxurious feel. The matte texture makes holding the mice easy with minimal slippage. This mouse is a great addition to continue the superb Logitech MX line.
The battery is built in as oppose to being removable as in the MX Performance, though it last quite a long time on a single charge and can be used while charging simultaneously. The nice thing about the MX Performance and G700s is that if the battery runs low, you can just swap out battery quickly, but this is not a big deal since the battery life is much better than the MX Performance (3-4 weeks or so) or the G700s (3-4 days).
Wireless connectivity is handled via Bluetooth or the 2.4ghz wireless dongle that is a mainstream on most of Logitech's wireless lineup. The addition of Bluetooth is nice, however I have exclusively used the mouse on the 2.4ghz wireless dongle connected to my computer. Another neat feature is the ability to pair with up to three seperate computers and switch with a tiny button on the bottom of the mouse.
The addition of another scrolling wheel on the side next to the forward and back button is nice and useful when there is a need to scroll horizontally. The scroll wheel is solid, the free flowing wheel is something that I need to have in my mouse. The smart shift technology that transition from the precise, click-y mode to free flowing mode is very handy to give more control while scrolling, truly a best of both world feature baked into one mode.
The mouse requires a new Logitech software called Logitech Option instead of the previous Mouse and Keyboard setting software which has a sleeker interface, though you will still need the Unifying software to pair the mice and other Logitech wireless peripherals.
Overall, this is probably one of the best mouse that Logitech has created, and probably one of the best on the market right now for those who aren't looking for a gaming mouse.

title: the controller feels nice and has a lot of functions built in I ...
text:
I am a huge fan of Logitech and their products, so I had no reservations about getting this controller. Once you get it working, the controller feels nice and has a lot of functions built in I like. The problem is, getting it working.

I was running Windows 8.1 and now Windows 10. Getting the computer to recognize the controller and pair with it was a major headache. Short story is this, go to [...] and watch the video, follow the instructions. 5 minutes later my controller worked. This compared to the 2 hours I spent on the phone with Logitech, having a new USB pairing sensor sent to me, and still no solution.

Long story is Logitech does not offer driver support for this controller since Windows 8. Not only that, but their support department will run you through a bunch of troubleshooting steps that make it seem your machine is the issue. It isn't. The video link posted is the only solution I found, and it works. Essentially you have to fool the computer into thinking it is an Xbox controller so that it will pair. Once that is done, it will display as an f710 controller like it should. I've had to do this technique a few times, as when there are updates to the operating system pairing sometimes fails again.

The other issue with this controller is that it will lose connection randomly, causing input lag. The solution is often as simple as shifting body position by a few inches. This inconsistency in input makes the controller horrible for tournament use or games requiring split second timing. It is for this reason I am looking for a new controller.

Here's the positives:

- Feels good in the hand and is very comfortable over long play sessions. If you are a fan of dual shock style controllers, you know what I mean.
- Has a good weight to it, balances nicely in hand.
- Mode button with indicator light is a huge plus. Allows for quickly swapping input of D-pad for left analogue stick with visual indicator.
- All the button inputs have a nice spring to them, nothing feels mushy.
- 2 vibration settings, though neither is strong enough for my taste.
- Two AA batteries last a good long while. Down side is there is no indicator for when they are about to die.

This isn't a terrible controller by any means. If you don't mind putting up with it's quirks that is. Really wish Logitech still made available the f510 as that was a wired version of this controller. The f310 is wired but lacks rumble. The wireless signal dropping on occasion has finally pushed me over the edge after owning this for a year +. Main thing, should you choose to buy this controller, is bookmark the YouTube video [...] as I guarantee you'll need it's solution when the controller fails to pair to your Windows 8 or 10 machine.

title: Smart Dedicated Remote. Nothing Better Than Having a Dedicated Remote With Physical Buttons & Touchscreen
text:
Honestly, this remote is pretty great. Some argue about how the play/pause buttons are at the top but I had no issue using it that way. Besides, most of what I tried let's me use the "Ok" and directional buttons as play/pause, fastforward/rewind. The touch screen is pretty responsive and there isn't much delay accessing your devices or activities. What sucks is that there is a limitation of 15 device no matter if you add more of these remotes or add a hub, you'll get the maximum amount from the device that has the maximum limit. I wish the 8 device limit from my harmony hub combined with this harmony remote giving me a total of 23 devices. But nope Logitech just wants you to buy one of the expensive remotes to have the 15 limit. Even the Elite has a maximum of 15. So the maximum you could get from the most expensive remote is also 15. They should have at least doubled that as they did with the 8 limits.

Before I begin, I would like to say this is my first time owning a smart universal remote. I had one or two or so cheap universal remotes before. So this is a bigger difference.

Battery: Charge it for four hours. Use it for about 72 hours. Plenty of time to use this imo. Just leave it on charge when you sleep and you'll be good to go throughout the day. It has a charging indicator on the screen that let's you know when charging and fully charged. There is a battery life indicator on the top right of the screen when the remote is out of lock screen. You can charge this two ways. It has a cradle but you can also use the micro USB port below the remote to charge it up. (The micro USB port is mostly just there to setup the remote through PC but you can charge it through micro USB port as well.)

Design: The remote looks beauitful. Though, it could have been better. I do agree with people that the play/pause, fastforward/rewind buttons should have been at the bottom. But honestly that isn't an issue as most of the stuff I've tried lets you use the directional and ok button as play/pause, fastforward/rewind. But either way it's pretty easy to use and feels nice in the hands. I love having a remote that has both a touchscreen and physical buttons. Touchscreen adds more functionality and having physical buttons just feels better pressing on them. Number keys would have been nice but really not needed if you have ditched cable and don't plan on having an antenna. And it doesn't take much effort looking at the touchscreen when entering the numbers. I know some people don't like that but at least it's just 9 numbers and not an entire alphabet. :)

Interface: Not much could be done with an interface when the screen is small. It's nice for a universal remote (much better than what smart universal remotes had before). You can change the background from a preset or upload your own through the computer. Overall, it's pretty easy to use and really no delay from going device to device.

Touch screen: Like I mentioned before, the touch screen is pretty responsive. If you don't want to accidentally touch the touch screen, it's best to put the lock screen. So you can just swipe the lock screen when you want to use it and you don't accidentally end up pressing any of the touchscreen buttons when you meant to touch the physical buttons etc.

Customization: You can arrange the order of devices. For example; if you want TV all the way at top you can drag it to all the way at the top when you are in edit mode. Same with activities. What you can't arrange is Smart Home devices that are in the Plug/Lights folders. You can arrange where Plugs and Lights go but not the devices themselves in the Plugs and Lights folder. Kinda sucks as you can do that with the Harmony app but not on the remote. Also, the arrangement you set in the Harmony app doesn't get applied to the remote. You have to do the arrangement separately on both the app and remote. Also as I said before you can also change the background image to a selection from the preset or upload your own through the computer. Customization is great but could be better. At least it's there. :)

Activities/Favorites: You setup activities which lets you can turn on multiple things at once. You can also for example access your favorite channels or if you have a Roku your favorite apps. It seems like there is only integration with Roku when it comes to Alexa and "Favorites" section. So for example you can launch Netflix from the Netflix icon in the favorite sections once you hit the Roku activity.

Limitations: It kind of sucks that there is a device limitation of 15 devices only. I'm sure they could have gone with a much higher limit. I have a IR+RF Hub called "Broadlink RM Pro" that doesn't have this kind of annoying limit and it's much cheaper than this remote and harmony hub. It's only under $40 and that's when it's not on sale. I also wish they would have let us combined devices in order to increase our limits such as if you have the harmony hub which carries only 8 devices you'll have 8 + 15 from this harmony remote giving you a total device limit of 23. The nice thing though is there does not seem to be a limit of devices you can setup for SmatHome such as if you have SmartThings linked, you can pretty much put as many devices as you like.

Price: It's a pretty expensive remote. It's hard to put $200 on this remote. I guess if I paid $200 for this remote, I would have rated this differently. But since I got this during the holidays for $100, it's a much better experience to me just because of that.

Support: Logitech has email, live chat and phone support. So you have many options to chat with them. And they usually respond back and take care of your problems pretty well.

Overall: I would recommend this product when it's on sale for $100 or less. As $200 is too much to ask for. I like this over using a smartphone as a remote because it's nice having a device that is dedicated as a remote only and nothing else. Smartphones have too much going for it and the lack of physical buttons don't make it as nicer to use as a dedicated remote. Even if you voice control for everything (Echo/Google Home), using a remote is sometimes nicer. I prefer changing the volume through remote rather then through Alexa but I prefer turning on the TV through Alexa through anything else. The amount of customization is nice but could be better. Having the ability to charge the remote two ways (Micro USB and cradle) is also nice. The remote has a nice design, feels good in the hands but the device limitations are for the most part the weakest point. title: so obviously besides these issues I like it well enough to continue to use it
text:
Overall, it's a decent mouse, but it does suffer some issues that make it a pain to use sometimes.

First -- and this is a common feature of all trackball mice that I've used -- the bearings for the trackball will collect gunk, making the trackball less responsive. They require regular cleaning, though nothing fancy -- just a quick wipe with a tissue or something.

Next is the scroll wheel. It's too sensitive and doesn't have any resistance between "clicks". Even the slightest bump will trigger a scroll action. This isn't a big deal for most applications, but I use this mouse for gaming and it's frustrating when for example the scroll wheel is bound to weapon switching and I inadvertently switch weapons. It also seems to wear down over time, becoming even more prone to accidental scrolling.

Finally, there are the buttons. After a year or two of use they will start randomly double-clicking, or releasing when you're holding down the mouse button. A temporary solution for when this first starts happening is to quickly alternate left and right clicking for about 30 seconds, but this only helps so many times before they become totally unreliable.

I've owned 4 of these since buying my first one in 2012, so obviously besides these issues I like it well enough to continue to use it. But once my latest mouse wears out I will be looking for an alternative.

Logitech, please update this model with more reliable buttons and scroll wheels!

The packaging box has 3 stickers all on top of each other, could have been a rekit, refurbished or replaced parts but do not work together.

title: This is the Bluetooth keyboard to get for iOS
text:
This is the second review I've ever written in all my years of using Amazon. I just got this keyboard – the Logitech Easy-Switch for iPad and iPhone – 15 minutes ago and am totally hooked on it. In fact, I'm writing this on it into my iPhone 6, which is propped up in my lap against an old iPad 2, sitting on a Griffin folding case.

The biggest things for me are:
1. The full-size keys
2. The three Bluetooth assignable buttons
3. The key travel depth
4. The Home button
5. Not having to use AA batteries in it.

I also have an Apple Wireless keyboard - not the Magic one, but one a few years older. I love it, too, but I can only use it with one device easily because you have to make sure Bluetooth is off on any nearby devices except for the one you're typing on. I was looking for a second Bluetooth keyboard to use at home with the iPhone/iPad, so I could then leave the Apple one at work to use daily at lunch break.

I had read a bunch of good reviews of another Logitech keyboard, the Ultrathin one for the iPad/iPad 2. I bought that one, but returned it after trying it for a couple of days. The keys were too cramped and I could never get used to the small Delete key and the contortions necessary to use the Command and Option keys.

The Easy-Switch, though, is fantastic. I read tons of glowing Amazon reviews and other reivews on blogs, and there seemed to be universal love for this keyboard. I see why now. The instant I started typing on it, I felt at home. I don't have to think about what I'm doing. It may actually be better than the keyboard on the MacBook Pro Retina 13".

Pairing it via Bluetooth is super easy. It really does switch nearly instantly between iOS devices. I haven't tried to use it with a Mac yet, but I probably won't bother since I got this for iOS. And the keyboard's Home button (F5) works with the iPhone 6 (as well as the iPad). You can single-press it or double-press it and it works just like the actual Home button on the phone.

I'll see how long the charge lasts. I was surprised that it came charged up out of the box (at some level — I don't know how much). From what I've read, a full charge lasts long enough to not be annoying, and I won't need to spend extra money on AA batteries or feel guilty about throwing dead ones away.

If you suspect that you might be inclined to need a full-size keyboard, then you probably do. I didn't know it until I tried the other smaller Logitech and couldn't use it. The Easy-Switch is wonderful and I hope they never change it.

title: Amazing keyboard, questionable quality control...
text:
This is more a review of the quality control more than anything. As a keyboard for my 9.7 Pro, it's amazing. It works great and with a few minor flaws (i.e. the right arrow not being backlit which is apparently on all the 9.7 keyboards...) I would take it over the apple keyboard any day.

HOWEVER, I am on my second one. Reason being is i returned my first one not knowing that the right arrow issue was an issue with all the keyboards not just mine. But now I have this second one and it seems as though the magnets on either side of the connector (not the connector itself) are weaker and there's a noticeable downward curve near the right side that wasn't present on my last keyboard. Lifting the keyboard up, even lightly, causes the keyboard to detach because the magnet towards the left is incredibly weak.

This is a real shame because the backlit keys and the typing itself is EXCELLENT and the shortcut keys are great. I love the size, the material, basically everything else about it. But it seems that the quality control is just not up to snuff. I would recommend it over the other keyboard any day, but I would also take precautions and be prepared to have to exchange it. Going back tomorrow to exchange this second one (going to see if I can get the first one back as it was superior).

title: The Z506 in my opinion sounds better than the Z906
text:
I have owned this set of speakers for the last 4 years (and counting), and am proud to say they've survived the years (nothing has broken), as well as multiple moves in the time since I bought this system. Now, in regards to the actual sound, it has a moderately rich mid and bass profile, although these speakers don't have any dedicated tweeters, they can go to quite loud volumes without distorting as well (enough to piss off housemates, by experience, oops...). The system does play in legit 5.1 directional surround when ALL three 2.5mm jacks are hooked up properly, but not the RCA jacks, those only play in simulated 5.1. The Z506 in my opinion sounds better than the Z906, although the bigger system would be more suited to larger rooms, but I'll be honest, you should probably be spending the extra for a proper system with a dedicated receiver (Denon, Onkyo, Yamaha, Ect.) if your going to be wiring up a large room. But, that's not the point of this system, not to fill large rooms, but to fill smaller living spaces somewhere in the range of 100-400 sq.ft. (very rough guess), and Logitech absolutely nails it in price for ludicrous performance. Although, the rear speakers only have 15 ft of cable, so co-purchasing RCA extender cables is recommended, if you know where you're going place and wire these is past that length.

If you're looking for a system to fill a small-ish room, I would absolutely recommend this to you.

Being able to toggle between high-fidelity wi-fi from my laptop and Bluetooth from mobile devices is a huge convenience. The music quality is first-rate, with a rich low end. But I also can use collaboration tools such as WebEx over my Internet connection instead of taking up mobile minutes. In addition, the pull-down microphone isolates much of the background noise (I've taken calls on an Amtrak train with no problem). I also sit and watch movies on my TV using it at times.

Like most rechargeable devices, you always wish for more battery life. However, for the money (under $100) this is the best headset on the market by far. Call it the perfect headphones for work/life balance.

title: Small footprint with large sound
text: These are a surprisingly good basic computer speaker system. I honestly didn't expect much and just needed something for my desktop and purchased these. They are of a much higher quality than they appear.  In other words, their minimalist and understated design does not portray their audio performance. I used these in a sizable 12 by 12 foot dorm and they were more than adequate enough to fill the room. I don't think you can expect to host a party or to have the loudest speakers in your dorm or apartment, but you cannot go wrong with these for casual music and media consumption. text: I am extremely impressed by this remote controller. The installation recognized all of my components which included the version of my Verizon remote. So, if my wife is using the Nexus 7, she can use the ASUS tablet to control the TV. I was actually looking for a remote that eliminated the push buttons which can inadvertently be depressed when grabbing the included remote. Using the Nexus 7 or ASUS eliminates this problem. text: What a pleasant surprise this speaker is. It will be the perfect companion to the Echo Dot that I'm giving my wife for Christmas. If it were only bluetooth, the search for a speaker for my iPad would be over. No more returning lackluster sounding aluminum boxes. But this is not why I bought it. I was merely looking for something halfway decent sounding for our bedroom as the Dot benefits from an always-on speaker.  What I got was something quite great sounding with well rounded highs, mids and a fair presence of bass. While its volume is more than sufficient, bass heavy tunes may case some distortion, but only at uncomfortable volume levels. The speaker has no volume knob of its own and relies solely on what it's connected to. I haven't tested the Dot with it yet, but the audio from my iPad Pro at about 90% volume sounds REALLY great!  I'm thinking of maybe rigging a couple of these with our tv instead of a sound bar. The sound from the one speaker alone filled our downstairs very nicely. title: Pleased Overall
text: Having enjoyed the K380 for some time, I was excited to see this keyboard hit the market.  I absolutely love the feel of the round keys and the semi-silent operation.  I have average sized hands and the compact K380 has been very comfortable.  Even so,  it was nice to see the more widely spaced keys along with the tenkey.  I'm keeping my K380 for writing on the go and replacing my everyday full keyboard with this one.  I'm not a heavy user of function keys, so their dual functionality has not affected my experience.  I do still have a bit of a learning curve ahead of me due to the displacement of the 'home' and 'end' keys.  Instead of dedicated keys in the area they are expected to be, they appear as alternate keys in numbers 7 and 1 of the tenkey.  The print screen function is also an alternate of the delete key.  These along with the small arrow keys will surely take some getting used to.  But I've faced larger challenges in life.  These are minimal trade-offs for the excellent typing experience the K780 provides.  Also, the ability to take the keyboard into another room to use with my iPad is hugely appreciated.  The receiver can remain with my PC and there are no wires to fool with.  Lastly, with the touch of a button I can swap to my iPhone and respond to my wife's texts, then immediately return to my desk work.  It is this functionality that makes this keyboard worth its weight in chocolate.  It's obviously what this keyboard was created to do and it does it extremely well.  No issues are present with either my iPad, iPhone or Windows 10 PC.  I am quite pleased overall.

title: Very Impressive Camera!
text:
I will rate this product a 4.5 star. When I received the item and opened it up it was nicely packed in the box. The camera feels solid and well made on a neet base that allows the user to tilt the camera up or down. The charging ring is impressive and unique with a 10ft cord allow you enough length to charge the camera and yet hang it high enough to get the best views. The ring is slim enough to allow you to charge the camera on its mount or separate and doesn’t matter how the camera is placed on the ring.

Setting up the camera was simple after finding the app for your phone. The setup process asked that you enable your Bluetooth to first connect to the camera for initial setup to your home network but after that the camera stayed connected to the network with its own IP address. You’ll have to make a Logi Circle account to enable cloud backup service which would be nice to access the backups or at least view more than the 24hr “Day Brief’ view.
Once the camera is setup it works really good. The picture quality is very impressive and clear. The app has many options for the camera. Your allowed to turn the camera ON/OFF, turn the speaker and microphone ON/OFF, allow notification to your phone and the possibility to add another camera. This feature I would like to test out more if I could. It’d be interesting if your allowed to view both cameras at the same time in a split screen mode or select which camera you’d like to view. Also the question would be how its saved on the cloud service?
I’ve noticed when I removed the camera from its base being fully charged the and placed in the baby’s room for night monitoring that the camera didn’t stayed charged for very long, which was a disappointment. There’s mention of a 12hr total battery life and 3 hr when continually streaming but I wasn’t apply to locate those options in the app to make the battery last the 12hr.
When viewing the camera on your app there is a 2 second delay. The audio itself is very impressive and the ability to speak to someone in the room while your away is a nice feature to the app. The night vision is really impressive, so impressive that when placed in the baby’s room I was able to view dust particles floating around the camera, but the night vision was very clear.
For the most part I would recommend this camera to someone.

title: Accurate mouse, comfortable layout, tactile buttons everywhere...
text:
I purchased my first wireless mouse a year ago, and I thought it was time for change.

Coming from the most budget of budget wireless mouse (Tecknet M002), I can say the $10 difference between my old mouse and this mouse is much more than worth it.

Initial thoughts:
- Plug and play right out the box
- INCLUDED 2x AA Energizer batteries (mouse can work with only 1 AA battery)
- EVERY button on this mouse is tactile, easy to press, and is satisfying in every way. Back/Forth buttons have plenty of travel too. Wheel click is the most tactile I have ever had on any mouse.
- Accuracy and precision are on point. No noticeable skipping or judders, especially when gaming. I am using this mouse with my PC sitting 10 FEET away from me connected to my tv. Although there is some input lag to be expected in this setup, I can hardly notice it, and my Black Ops 3 K/D ratio hasn't taken a hit once.

I am a moderate gamer who plays a decent amount of FPS like Call of Duty/BF4, and lots of 3rd person games like GTA5/Dark Souls.
Finding my most comfortable DPI setting hasn't been easy. Once I got this mouse I was wondering how to change the DPI setting, only to later find out that this mouse has a constant DPI of 1000. I have no issue with a constant DPI setting because it just feels right.

I highly back Logitech's M510 mouse, there's a reason it has so many great reviews.

title: Needs Work
text:
My main headset is the Logitech G430, and thus many of my experiences will be compared to that.

This headset was very highly reviewed as a great headset for 2016, and I was excited to purchase it. Unfortunately, multiple problems put together made it a return.

The first, but smallest problem is the tightness. The headset is tight enough new that I began to develop headaches after half an hour of use, and when getting a headset for gaming that is unacceptable. I understand that given time it would stretch out, but I do not want to deal with headaches until then.

Another issue I had is the sidetone volume is really low (sidetone is playing what you say back to you to make yourself heard). This is a feature many people do not even like, but I am a loud person and having the chance to keep myself at a normal volume is great. The G430 has a perfect sidetone volume, and it is too quiet on the G933.

The biggest issue is the mic quality. I was not able to hear a large difference, but everyone I spoke with online stated that I sounded muffled and at a lower quality. I attempted to configure the mic settings to improve it but nothing I did was enough.

I love the build quality, the looks of it, and the fact that it is wireless, but the issues made it unappealing.

text:
I bought this headset for skype and voice recognition, and I have to say it performs very nicely for what I bought it for. The range isn't everything I ever dreamed of, and the microphone gets scratchy just walking 9-10 feet over to my mini fridge, but the room I'm in doesn't have very flat walls for wireless signals to bounce off of very easily.

While the microphone won't do at any kind of range, the speaker signal seems to work far better. It will transmit well enough through a wall for me to continue hearing my computer on the floor above my PC with only a respectable amount of loss.

I can easily mute the microphone when I need to walk away from my desk and continue to hear my friend(s) speaking over skype in most places of my house. I also love the fact that I can plug the headset into a charging cable (and it comes with a pretty long one) and continue to use it like a wired headset. The warning tone gives me plenty of time to tell my friends to hang on while I grab the cable and plug it in before it dies.

The audio quality sounds great to me when it's in range.

Other, minimal complaints: It hurts my ears after a couple of hours of continuous use. Also, if you want to use it immediately and the battery is dead, sometimes after plugging it in you must flip the switch to off and back on again, then wait for the activation beeps which takes less than 30 seconds.

The original came with a AA Eneloop rechargeable battery which lasted for the life of the device. Note: I use Eneloops in almost all my devices and have a good quality charger that uses a low current charge cycle and trickle maintenance mode, so the batteries will last many many years (some are ~10 years old now and still hold about 80% full charge).

The new mouse comes with a no-brand AA rechargeable and it's much more difficult to replace manually if a battery dies and I just want it to work right away. Otherwise, precision is good, wireless range is good, build quality is good, the wheel is excellent, and the buttons are very responsive with a relatively light touch. I love the ergonomic design, much easier on the hands when using continuously for a long period of time.

title: Very good speakers for the price - better value than Klipsch
text:
I bought this set of speakers with the intention of using it in my apartment connected to my laptop. I play games, listen to music, and watch movies pretty often. These speakers fit my three uses pretty well. Plenty of crisp highs and deep lows. Mid range could probably sound a little stronger, but nothing changing my equalizer settings can't fix. Once I changed my audio settings on my laptop to my liking, I have absolutely no complaints about the sound that comes out, especially given the price point.

These won't compare to $1000 home theater systems in terms of richness of sound, but they will blow pretty much any set of regular computer speakers right out of the water. Volume wise, I'm quite happy. These are plenty loud enough for a reasonably sized room full of people

Now, the reason why I docked a star is because the wires from the satellite speakers are not removable. They are hardwired into the backs of the satellite speakers. This isn't really a major issue, but it's a durability concern. You won't be able to just go out and buy new cables in a few years should you happen to damage a cable.

Overall, I'd still recommend this set of speakers. I compared this against the Klipsch set, and have decided the Klipsch speakers were not $80 better, and after buying these, am very happy I didn't spend anymore because it would have been a waste.

text:
For the first month or two, it worked perfectly. Exactly what I expected: a speaker for streaming music wirelessly via the theoretically awesome AirPlay system. Yet, since then, it stopped working. I unplugged and re-plugged it in, and it appeared to work--and then it stopped streaming. And then it started again. And it stopped. It cannot maintain a connection, which is pretty friggin' basic to being a wireless speaker. If it would just work reliably and consistently, it would be great. The sound is solid (the low end is great, although the high ends could be a bit brighter), but it's key contribution--wireless sound via AirPlay--is just so unreliable that's it's become little more useful than a really expensive doorstop.

Update: the speaker has been working better recently. The spottiness is rarer and the speaker is more useable, so I've upgraded the stars to 3. If the previous problems disappear completely and indefinitely, I may be able to upgrade my review further to 4, but as of now, I'm sufficiently hesitant that I remain at 3 stars.

title: It's a great mouse. However
text:
It's a great mouse. However, I am one of the few people who can hear the high pitched noise coming from the motion sensor. There is no real solution to this and Logitech doesn't seem to acknowledge it exists.
Here is a test. Back when tube TVs were a thing. Have you ever walked into a room with a tube TV and could tell that it was turned on just from hearing a faint high frequency hiss? The TV is at a blank screen so you can't "see" that it's on and there is no static noise or TV content playing through the speakers.
If you have no idea what I'm talking about, you probably won't hear the sound that this mouse makes.
If you do know what I'm talking about then you'll probably hear the noise this mouse makes when it's moved. Every time it's moved.
If that noise bothers you, then I would recommend looking elsewhere.

title: Rainbow of emotions before I reached my happy place
text:
I mainly use this for my TV devices and am expanding into more home devices, like my fan and the colored, dimmable light bulbs (just for fun).

Pros:
- Can control multiple different types of devices. TVs, streaming video boxes, appleTV, nest devices, etc
- Controls are organized by activity, so you can start up multiple devices at the push of a button to create a cozy atmosphere while you watch tv or relax
- Pretty good reception/relay of remote signals. The mini-blaster helps a lot when you have devices hiding in tv cabinets or behind other devices
- Can use the phone app or a computer to set up
- Can customize buttons for different devices
- Separate buttons/section for home (lights, dimmers, outlets) vs entertainment (tv, music, streaming, etc)
- The remote feels really good in my hand. It's slightly curved and has that soft, smooth texture on the front and the buttons, so your thumb slides over the buttons easily, but still grippy enough that pressing the little buttons doesn't really require fine motor skills. The back has a rough texture that feels secure, like it won't go flying across the room when you get excited and start gesturing with your hands.
- Battery for the remote is a common 2032 button cell, so it is easy to find and not too expensive. I like batteries better than usb charging because I forget to charge things and it just sucks to end up with a dead remote control when your tv show is on and you have to turn everything on the hard way.

Cons:
- Set up can be a bit aggravating. It took me a few tries to get a few devices working correctly and then I had to "teach" it quite a few commands for my Android streaming box
- Only 3 activity buttons on the remote for entertainment (tv, music, streaming, etc), but can create up to 6 activities. Short button press for the first 3 and long button press to get to the other 3
- Not for a complete noob (novice). Requires quite a bit of knowledge about how your devices work to set them up correctly. There are pictures and instructions for most things, but I still went through some trial and error to figure out how my audio amp "chooses" the input.

I'm not sure if this is a pro or con, but you do have to set up an account with logitech to set up the system and connect it to wifi, but it saves your configuration with the account via wifi, so after all that effort, it doesn't just vanish and leave you anxiously flipping between wanting to cry in the fetal position and crushing the components into a fine powder.

Overall, I really like the system. Once I got it set up correctly, I was able to put away 4 remotes, so that made me super-happy. I do wish it was a bit easier to set up.

Would I recommend it to friends, maybe. It would depend on the friend. Not family, but that's just my family. You may feel different about yours.

text:
As many other reviews have stated, I purchased this device to run my Amazon Echo Dot through my home theatre receiver and speakers. However, once a device is connected to this adapter, if you disconnect the Bluetooth connection, it will automatically reconnect. Unless you power the adapter through the receiver itself, you will not be able to use the Echo Dot without having your receiver on first (since the Dot internal speaker won't work while Bluetooth is connected). text:
Wirecutter lets me down again. It's a good thing I bought this as a secondary mouse. On the plus side, it has easy to open packaging. On the down side, it feels incredible cheap. It's very plasticky and light, even with the batteries in; the buttons feel terrible. Then there's the fact the batteries aren't fully secure in the mouse, so that they makes noise as you move the mouse from side to side "too suddenly". As, you know, you kind of do with a mouse during use. I'm sticking with the Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Mouse as my primary, this one gets 2.5 stars at best.

P.S. Plugging in the USB dongle brought up the keyboard detection wizard on macOS for some reason. I just re-set this up for my usual keyboard, just to get rid of it.

Update: The more I use it, the less I like it, I'm actually knocking it down to 2 stars. It's not the batteries that loose in the mouse, but the stupid scroll wheel. I hate the lock/unlock wheel button, who wants a free-spinning scroll, people who don't understand the page up/down keys? Logitech touts "hyperscroll" as a feature, but I strongly disagree.

Additionally, the mouse is *terrible* on Mac (I'm still on El Capitan due to work restrictions). The scroll is jumpy and impossible to control by default. You literally cannot scroll through a long email without missing content, even with the gentlest touch. You can install Logitech Control Center (LCC) to turn the vertical scroll settings way down, but this destroys all other mouse AND keyboard settings. I.e., the function keys on my MS Sculpt keyboard stop working, and if I plug another mouse in, its middle button doesn't work. So I promptly uninstalled that. In hindsight, I wish I hadn't bought this.

text:
This mouse is what has been missing from my life! I went from using $15 mouses to the Logitech M705 and finally decided to get the MX Master and it has been great!

But this isn't a problem for the MX Master. Out of the box, the back and forward buttons also don't work, but once you install the custom software there is no problem!

Every button is well crafted for usability. I use every single button on this mouse on a daily basis. Horizontal scrolling seems useless until you start using it every single day.

So. Why 3 stars and not 5? Because this mouse will break on you in less than a month's usage. Just google "MX Master wheel" and yeah... it's a known issue that Logitech has seen fit to not address.

For their flagship product, I can't believe that this type of hardware flaw exists. I had to purchase a torx screwdriver (what is a torx?) just to open up this mouse and fix the issue myself.

The issue can be fixed but next month I will have to open up my mouse again.

If the hardware issue didn't exist, I would recommend this mouse to every single working professional.

title: My favorite controller with only minor problems.
text:
I was extremely skeptical of this product due to various reviews that seem to have the common trend of the joy sticks wearing out. I do not play many joy-stick heavy games so my joysticks haven't seen nearly as many hours as the D-pad has. I would like to say though, that after 1 year my joysticks still work.

Pros: I love almost everything about the design. I really love the D-Pad. It works very well with Street Fighter 5. I used to hate these types of pads where the direction buttons on the D-Pad were all fused under one circle instead of individual buttons and now I've changed my opinion. I think it's vastly superior to controller designs like the PS3 and PS4 individual D-Pad buttons. The ability to input very distinct D-Pad shortcuts for Shoyruken's, Critical Arts, etc. at a high rate of speed without error is much easier on this design.

Con: Only two cons. The L2 and R2 buttons are just a little bit too long to pull. This makes it difficult to press them simultaneously with other buttons, at times. Trying to press something like R1&R2 together can suddenly become a very easy thing to mess up. While trying to activate V-trigger in SFV, i'll often press R1 or R2 a little too soon and not get my moves because i didn't press the buttons at the same time.

Finally, the last con, is that just inside 1 year, I am about 9 days away from owning this controller for a single year, and the little rubber pad underneath the D-Pad has torn from use. I have almost 400 Hours of Street fighter on it, and 40 hours of MKX on it and it doesn't have the same spring and snap to it and sometimes the D-Pad will get stuck in particular direction, because the little rubber nodes underneath the D-Pad have torn from repetitive general use.

I will honestly probably either A) try to use the warranty to fix it, or B) Simply by another one. This controller is cheap and it is very familiar in my hand. I have come to love it much more than any XBOX or PS3/PS4 controller.

title: Great camera for Skype, crisp picture quality and sound is perfect, with lots of features!
text:
I did a lot of research on this thing before purchasing. Basically I am having to work from home for a while and my office wanted me still "in the office" if you will. My boss bought another webcam that was supposedly plug and play and compatible with Windows 10, but it wasn't and ended up being a nightmare. I did some research and saw that Skype rated this in the top 5 webcams that work best with Skype. I also read on CNET that for the price range is was the best. If you want to pay a little more I would go with the C920. I wasn't paying and I had to keep the cost down. It was truly plug and play, the Logitech drivers popped up and started installing. It was very quick and simple. I do wish that most of these companies would quit letting Bing and all that be apart of the installation process where you have to pay attention to uncheck the boxes during installation, however thats neither here nor there for this review. Once the cam was up there is a "Follow my face" feature which could definitely be handy and works surprisingly well. The picture quality is very good and the sound/mic is excellent. I really was shocked at how easy setup was and at the quality at this pricing point. If your looking for a very good cam with a good mic at a low price, you cant go wrong with this thing.

The only reason it got 4 stars was because of the cord length. I know that seems silly and stupid, but its ridiculously short. If your using it on desktop like me, then its a huge issue, I actually had to move my PC up onto my desk because of this cam. The cord is extremely short, so to use it on my monitor as it should be, is more tricky. If they would have put a normal size cord, I would have given it 5 stars, maybe they were only thinking of people that use laptops. I am that person most of the time, just not for work. It is very compatible with Skype, Skype picked it all up very quickly and has since worked flawlessly. I keep this cam on for almost 9-10 hours 5 days a week and I have yet to have an issue with this cam now for a couple weeks. The other side says I am very clear and sound very clear, they are using the same cam, especially compared to what we were us ing.

Boxing was what I have come to expect with Logitech. Very nice, secure, and simple manuals. If my review was helpful to you, please click yes below.

The stand was easy enough to rig up provided you have a basic understanding of righty-tighty vs lefty-loosey and there is only one cord similar to the one connecting your printer to your computer (while we're on the subject of printers you should probably check your ink...I know you've been putting off buying a cartridge, but nobody wants a late night trip to Walmart to have to buy ink because your paper is due tomorrow and you procrastinated).

title: Great for pet owners!
text:
I bought this keyboard because I spent a couple hours disassembling and unsuccessfully attempting to reassemble my standard type keyboard to remove accumulated cat hair. I have three cats, but two are Maine Coons with very long hair and all three like to get on my desk. I wanted a keyboard without the giant gaps and pit below the keys where cat hair can accumulate and gum up the works. And no, I've never found a keyboard vacuum or canned air on the planet that will remove long cat hair reliably from a keyboard.

This keyboard has small, round "chiclet" type keys with little space around them, so you can easily clean the keyboard with a Swiffer. Having used small Bluetooth keyboards before, I was concerned that the key spacing would be wrong and it would take me a long time to get used to it. The spacing seems fine. The only thing I've had to get used to are the directional keys, which are small and a little oddly spaced, which only is a problem when I play World of Warcraft.

It connected fine both with my iPad and my Android tablet (I'm a techno-pantheist) as well as to my computer.

The only thing I thought I would not care for is that the keyboard is extremely thin and thus there isn't much of a rise -- it's very close to the surface of the desk. It took me no time at all to realize I loved it. It's actually more comfortable to use for long periods of time. There is no need for a built-in wrist rest (another place for cat hair to accumulate) because it's so low to the desk.

Having a full-sized number pad is a huge plus and something you don't often find on Bluetooth keyboards.

title: Excellent mouse.  Optical sensor very accurate, and the mouse it highly configurable to personalize your experience
text:
This is a review of the Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse.

This corded USB mouse is awesome. The scroll wheel can be free spinning or switched to ratcheting with the touch of a button. The sensor is very sensitive and works fabulously. The sensitivity can be adjusted to suit your taste and your mousing surface. You can also create three sensitivity presets to switch among [among which to switch?]. I use it with a basic $2 solid black nylon covered mouse pad, and it works great. It tracks perfectly on pretty much any flat surface—even a desktop with no mousepad at all; however it does not work on glass. If you are having trouble with the sensor, you can recalibrate it, but so far, I have not found that to be necessary.

It is a long and fits very comfortably in my right hand—it is not for left-handed mousing. The bottom of the mouse has a magnetic door behind which you can add weights in various configurations so that the weight and balance of the mouse can be whatever you find suits you best. It comes with a set of weights. There are 11 programmable buttons to do what you want with, and personally, I couldn’t find a use for them all, which is probably good, because then I would have to remember which is which. I am sure I will use them over time though. If you like shortcuts and buttons to simplify things, you will enjoy it.

The mouse comes with a very short instruction pamphlet that says to go to the website and download the software. The software is easy to use and you can really customize your mouse. The G logo on the top of the mouse is backlit and you can change the color of the light to just about any color you can imagine, you can have it pulse, or have it fade from one color to another (those are picked randomly though), or you can just turn it off altogether.

Overall: This mouse is fabulous, and should fit any gamer or workplace needs. The sensor is the most accurate I have found. It works great, and the sensitivity is so highly adjustable it should work for anyone.

title: Easy Setup and Smart Operation
text:
Just opening the package speaks of quality. What's inside includes a USB cable, a dedicated wall wart charger, the charging base and the Harmony 950. That power supply means it's not necessary to charge from a device with a spare USB port.

The next thing I checked out is the small (SMALL) manual. It illustrates what's in the package and tells you to connect the Harmony to your computer and download/install the Harmony app that you'll use to configure the remote.

The manual is so concise that it fails to mention that the usb port is under a rubber door on the bottom.

This is my first universal remote; maybe because I figured it would be a big hassle to configure one. That was not the case with the Harmony 950.

After a quick download of the app installer, the actual app loads in under a minute. Once you launch it you'll create an online account. The setup process ask you the make and model of your devices. It had no trouble identifying mine. You will have to know which inputs (on your receiver) are connected to which sources, so you may end up pulling some of your components out to read info from the back. It really did a good job of guessing all of the other relevant settings for my equipment.

Setup is organized in “activities,” such as TV, music, etc. Some activities are preconfigured, but you can add custom activities. Well, you can also modify some of the canned ones, at least changing the names. For each activity you tell it which components to include and assign a few functions, such as that the receiver controls volume.

Once you start using the remote, the first time you use an activity it asks if the configuration works, and gives you a chance to tweak things.

In use, you use the touch screen like a smart phone, even including a clock. There's also, of course, the usual array of buttons for common tasks.

Press the gear icon at the top and it offers help, fix it myself, settings, edit and sleep timer. Settings lock keeps the kids from messing things up.

The device goes to sleep about 10 seconds after you set it down . It wakes up when you pick it up. The feel is excellent with nice heft. It's shiny on top and has a matte, textured surface on the bottom.

I recommend the Harmony 950 with no reservations. It's a quality device and it works.
