title: A Quality Webcam Complete With a Privacy Shutter
text:
When it comes to video conferencing, I was an early adopter. At the time I was part of a team that established one of the first (if not the first) ISDN cross country video call. Video has come a very long way since those early ISDN days, but the Logitech C925e Webcam nods to one "high tech" feature that we learned to include in our early ISDN video cameras--a lens shutter.

Let me explain. Our early ISDN cameras were on all of the time and once a connection was made the opposite party could be seen quite clearly--whether they realized it or not! Case in point, I placed an ISDN video call to a colleague one day. He didn't know that I had called because his video window was hidden behind a spreadsheet, a web page and a document that he was working on at the time. I called his name several times, but he never heard me because he had turned down his computer speakers. I watched him work for several minutes (he was very well behaved) before my guilt got the better of me and I disconnected the call.

When we talked the next time, I told him what had occurred. After we both got a good laugh off of the incident, we contacted the camera manufacturer about a change to prevent unrecognized video calls. His solution was simple and elegant at the same time. He installed a plastic shutter between the camera lens and the case. We never had that issue again.

Now nearly 30-years later along comes the Logitech C925e Webcam. Yes, it supports HD 1080p video and, yes, it has a built-In stereo microphone. That's great. But it also includes a plastic shutter that gives you privacy when that unexpected FaceTime or Skype call comes your way. Thank you Logitech!

Of course, as enamored as I am with that privacy shutter, I must say that the webcam itself is very good. Installation of the camera my Mac Mini was a breeze (a non-event actually--I simply plugged it into a spare USB port on my Mac and it started working. No fuss no muss. The camera mounted to my monitor effectively and easily.

The video quality is very good as is the audio as well. What else can you expect or want in a webcam. Well done, Logitech!

title: good, better couple with Echo Dot
text: All my friends love their harmony hub but I held out on getting one for a long long time because it was just too pricey for me, I finally made the move now that pricing is down. I like the hub. It was easy to setup and is easy to use. The app works well, the add on remote works well. If I moved within 3 ft of the hub then life was good, but more than 3 ft and one device wouldn't work. I plugged in the ir blaster and then all was okay. My hub is on a shelf within 1 ft of my entertainment devices and at the same level as them. It has to be pretty finely positioned if you ask me to work very very well. If my wife moves it an inch or two or the pets bump it then often I'll have to reposition it. By itself, the harmony hub is okay to good. It works well most of the time. I'm hoping command set will get expanded.

title: Well made speakers for desktop use with good sound and flexible connection options
text:
Setup is painless and simple. 3 options to connect - bluetooth, R/L RCA, and/or 3.5mm (headphone) jack. The bluetooth setup was flawless and simple - I connected to a samsung S7 and was playing music within 60 seconds of having it out of the box: plug in power, press the bluetooth button, scan on phone, logitech showed up, connected, played.

The sound quality is very good for an office / bedroom / computer connection -- comparable to my bose wave radio that I have connected to my pc for music, with nice rich bass and clean sound at a more than adequate volume for individual use.

Note that it's a total of 4 components that are all hardwired together, so it's not like a highly portable bluetooth speaker. It's more designed for being the fixed speaker system in a room that can be flexibly attached to your computer hard wired and then your phone on bluetooth. The main unit which houses the woofer also connects to power and has the inputs for wired connections. It is also hardwired to the 2 satellite speakers and to the little round device that is the combination bluetooth receiver and volume control. Control for bass is separate on the woofer.

Overall, a very nice solution for the specific use.

title: Great for group video conference s
text:
All staff at my company have desktop video conferencing through Google for Work. Desktop video reduced our phone bills, made working across different offices easier and generally increased the level of cordiality. It's hard to think of someone as an idiot when you regularly see him face to face rather than just exchanging emails or talking occasionally on the phone. We use Logitech cameras across the board but the inexpensive models aren't particularly good when you need to get 5 or 6 people at one location on the same video call. Enter the C925e.

This camera has two advantages. The lense picks up a much larger area. At 6 feet distance we can get several people comfortably within the shot. The microphones also work well at that distance allowing for all of us to be heard well enough for extended calls.

This is a GREAT camera option for your larger meetings. It's not going to do the advanced sorts of things that the expensive high-end gear can do but it's more than good enough for most business meetings.

text:
If you're playing steam games on mac, don't buy this controller. It will only work with a small percentage of games. Most of the time, the buttons will be all wacky and you'll find you're game character doing weird, or the controller just straight up won't respond.

If you're on windows and you need a cheap controller, this one is just fine. It works plug&play, haven't had a single issue in that regard.

So why am I giving this only 2 stars? Well it's very cheaply made. It feels cheap, the d pad is very wobbly & inprecise, as are the bumpers. Well, one day I dropped it on the floor. You'd think a game controller of all things could handle that, I dropped my gamecube & ps2 controllers on the floor a million times when I was a kid and they continued to function perfectly. This one? I dropped it one time, & the right bumper came loose somehow and stopped responding. It just didn't click anymore. I figured I might as well try to fix it first, if I'm gonna drop the money to buy a new one anyway.

The casing comes apart very easily, but the way the insides are put together are so ridiculously stupid. DO NOT remove the circuit board because you will never be able to put it back together again. I don't know how they managed to jam the usb wire underneath it, but once it comes out, it's never going back underneath again, and then you can't fit the circuit board back in the case. And as a warning, if you're going to try, be careful when you first open it up because all of the face buttons are going to come spilling out everywhere. In case you drop any, these are all the pieces, 16 in total: 4 ABXY buttons, 4 white pieces that they sit inside, the 3 oval center buttons, the logitech button, plus 4 little black cylinders that fit inside the d pad. And if your bumpers are loose, those might fall out too.

But long story short, just don't drop this thing on the floor.

title: 4000 hours of use and still a champ. If I could have only one headset, this would be it.
text:
I bought the Logitech h800 from an Amazon competitor in July 2012 for about $85, to use primarily for Skype and video game chat on PC. Since then, I've used this headset an average of about 20 hours a week, or roughly 4000 hours total. Of all the headsets and headphones I've ever owned, this one has been BY FAR the most versatile and the best value.

Here's what I love about it:

As a chat headset, the H800 is excellent. I don't have difficulty hearing the people I'm talking to. As long as I remember to swivel the little boom mic down near my mouth, people tell me that my voice comes through clearly and that the volume is good. The on-ear volume and mute controls are very convenient since you can always reach them using the same motion. This is a big improvement from my older headsets that had inline volume controls where you'd have to fumble to find the controls on the cord.

As media headphones, the H800 is good. For music and movies the audio is generally pretty clear, but it noticeably loses fidelity at higher volumes, but that's pretty common for any headset with dynamic drivers.

It's broadly compatible. With the USB receiver, this headset works with no drivers required in Windows 7+, every Linux I've ever tried, and PS4. In bluetooth mode, this headset works with every Android phone or tablet I've ever tried, every iPhone 4+ I've ever tried, and PSVita.

It's very lightweight, and it adjusts to fit with minimal pressure on ears and the top of the head. The padding on the top is a very light and insubstantial-feeling foam, but it's effective because I can wear it for hours without discomfort. The ear pads are open, so they don't trap heat like closed-cup designs do. They also don't block ambient sounds - you can easily carry on a conversation with a partner or coworker while wearing these without needing to shift them off one ear. I replaced the factory earpads with a replacement from a seller here on Amazon. They weren't rotten like many earpads have a tendency to do, but there were holes worn through where the pads would rub against my glasses.

Battery life is pretty decent. I regularly get 6 or 7 hours of use from a charge before it begins to sound a low-battery alert and I need to plug it in to a charger, but it still works normally while charging. It still connects snugly and feels secure when plugged in even after years of regular use.

I have only a few complaints about this headset that are worth mentioning.

The low-battery alert beep begins to sound when there's still about an hour of charge left in the battery. As the battery wears, this beep will sound earlier and earlier - at worst, for me, I'd get a low-battery alert after only two hours. When this happened, I'd just leave the headset switched on overnight so it could beep itself to death. In the morning I'd switch it off and put it back on the charger, which seemed to restore normal battery life for a month or two. After three years, when battery life regularly fell below four hours, I replaced the battery with a Logitech-branded replacement.

The on-ear controls rattle when I shift my head. It didn't rattle when it was new, but it started after about a year. The rattle IS fixable, I just haven't taken the trouble yet to do so because I've mostly become accustomed to it.

Once in a while, maybe 5% of the time, the headset does not pair with the USB receiver when the headset is turned on. Removing/reinserting the USB receiver and switching the headset off and on resolves it.

In conclusion, there are better headsets/headphones out there. I still own and use other headsets. I have a pair of lower-end Sennheiser headphones, a Logitech h600 headset, a ThermalTake eSports gaming headset, and the Sony virtual 7.1 headset for PS4, as well as a half-dozen cheap earbuds for the gym. In the past, I've owned and worn out many headsets and headphones I couldn't remember to list if I tried.

Out of all of those, though, none have survived the use and the wear that the H800 has, and it still works just as well now as it did the first time I put it on almost four years ago. If I could only have one headset, this would be it.

title: The gold standard in compact integrated keyboard/touchpads, now with better button layout.
text:
This keyboard is a minor redesign of the Logitech K400 wireless touch keyboard, and in my opinion it's the best revision yet.

I've used these keyboards in dozens of installations, from medical exam rooms where space is at a premium, to auditorium podiums where presentation is priority, to home theater setups where ease of use is king.

The original K400 wireless keyboard had volume control buttons and a Home button on the left above the row of F-keys and was generally okay. I still own and use a few of these. A later stealth revision replaced all the F-keys with media control hotkeys, and the previously convenient volume keys stupidly became useless launch keys, and the Home button in the top center of the keyboard became a power button that only worked to turn the PC off - this was very inconvenient.

This revision eschews the stupid power button entirely, and the volume keys have moved to the right side above the touchpad. Also, the up and down arrow keys have been consolidated into a single row. This is an especially nice correction for touch-typists - it restores the right shift key to where your fingers expect it to be.

The yellow button above the Escape key is a left-mouse button, which in my opinion is the feature that makes this series of keyboards best suited for couch use. Just pick the keyboard up with both hands, put your right thumb on the touchpad and your left thumb on the yellow button, and you're all set for browsing on the big screen.

I've tested this keyboard to work at over 30' with line of sight to the USB nano receiver, and easily 15' without. The receiver can stow in a little clip under the battery cover for travel, too.

Battery life is very good - if the previous keyboard revisions have been any indication, you can expect to replace two AA batteries every 12-18 months depending on how heavily you use it.

title: 2 years on, not quite as impressed
text:
So I've had this for about 2.5 years and battery life is still great. I haven't had to change the batteries in either the mouse or the keyboard during that time (and haven't turned them off during that time, though I probably should have), but haven't ever found them to be low on a charge.
The keyboard works fine, I've no real complaints there, though it feels a bit thin for my taste.
My issue is with the mouse. More specifically, with the scroll wheel on the mouse. So the mouse has a button to switch it from scrolling a page at a time to an infinite scroll where the wheel spins freely. The positioning of this button is such that I'm always bumping it while moving the mouse around. It does click, but not loudly enough to be noticed if you aren't listening for it. I could probably get used to this, but even when in the correct position the scroll wheel sensor isn't very accurate. It's recognition that the wheel has been rolled in sloppy at best. When it does recognize it it doesn't respond correctly more than about half the time. I suspect this is a result of slop from the scroll wheel doubling as a button and also having the second (infinite scroll) functionality (essentially, I think they just tried to do too much with that one button).
If you're looking for something like this, I'd probably keep looking. That mouse is going to drive you nuts.

title: Defective product and horrible support.
text:
[[VIDEOID:9fdca43d99e7a4705da03f4bd1262783]] I purchased two of these devices. One for personal use, the other for work. One of the devices arrived defective with debris rattling around in the mouse. Indicating poor workmanship and quality control. the debris is large enough that it can work its way in between buttons and switches effectively locking out left click, right click, and middle click. It is quite annoying. Usually shaking the device can rattle it loose, but it just moves the problem temporarily. Because the device is held together with torq screws I can not repair it myself. Furthermore some of the screws are hidden underneath the Teflon skid pads. Removing them to access the screws would permanently deform them.

Defects happen, but my issue is that Logitech support is handling the problem in the most inconvenient manner. They are requiring me to ship the device back before they will issue a replacement. This is unacceptable, Their system is not capable of tracking the progress and status of RMAs and is basically email based. Thus if I ship my device it could become lost in their system and it will be my word against theirs. Furthermore, its a 65 dollar mouse, not a 2000 dollar laptop. What is strange is that I had a G602 mouse from Logitech fail with a bad middle click (similar issue, but defective switch in this case). This was replaced and handled without issue. A new mouse arrived at my door, and they didn't ask for the old one back. So they are capable of handling the issue properly, but they insist on fighting me over a 65 dollar mouse.

In the future, I will not recommend Logitech products. I have purchased two different products and have had failures with both. They have quality control problems, but their support is unable to accommodate and fix them under reasonable terms. I recommend finding a different company to handle your peripheral needs.

Update: Device was replaced but it took the device shipping via UPS ground, and arriving at their facility before they would ship out a replacement also UPS GROUND. Total turnaround time was 3 weeks. Next time I will just let Amazon handle the defective product and return it to them. At least they refund and/or ship replacement when they see tracking number post. Logitech could learn from Amazon.

title: Pretty Good for Ableton Live 9 Mac -- I compare to Apple's Magic Mouse with trackpad
text:
I have been using the Apple wireless magic mouse for a few years. I like it OK, but it often loses connection, isn't reliable, and eats through batteries fast if I don't turn it off all the time which is a hassle. Plus-- I'm not a fan of the batter hatch design on those.

But this is a review of the Logitech B120 which I must say, feels a lot cheaper than the magic mouse, but it does the things that I want it to pretty much as well at a fraction of the cost and no batteries to replace. OK so this is a wired mouse and there's that drawback. I guess I'm not in dire need of wireless although it's nice.

The main thing I wanted in a replacement mouse is the side-scrolling. I use it a lot in Ableton Live 9 (scrolling audio files left and right a lot). This does that although not in the same way as the magic mouse. The Apple magic mouse has the trackpad that lets your scroll left right up and down, and it's kind of cool how you scroll with your finger and the music file keeps scrolling and slows down slowly. With this Logitech mouse, you use the side scroll thing on the click wheel which is cool, but it scrolls one bar or one note at a time depending on how zoomed in you are. That works fine for me, I zoom out a little and then scroll, and then zoom back in when I want to scroll left/right a significant amount.

Great value, I'd recommend to anyone. I will use this over my Apple magic mouse which will end up by my TV when I use Airplay between my mac and my Apple TV.

I gave those speakers to someone that needed them and found myself upgrading to the Logitech speakers. They did arrive on date and were packaged with care.

title: Loving it!
text:
I'll be honest. I just wanted to buy this product to annoy my neighbor. Allow me to explain - my neighbors use their home theater system all day every day and even late into the night. The bass from their subwoofer shakes my walls and has woken me up from many a naps. It's also super annoying if I'm trying to do some work. After all my efforts of pleading with them failed, I decided to buy a good speaker system with a powerful bass. I also wanted something more reasonably priced because I'm not one for terribly loud music and therefore planned on using my subwoofers only to annoy my bass-loving neighbors.

Anyway, I've had the speakers a few weeks now and they work great! The sound is amazing and the bass is definitely wall shaking. I turn the bass up to max when my neighbors turn on their home theater system and two things happen - 1) I don't feel their bass anymore because of the bass coming from my subwoofer and 2) it shuts those a-holes right up.

I think these subwoofers have made them realize how thin our walls really are and how terribly annoying your neighbor's subwoofers are if you're trying to work or sleep. I love my speakers and the subwoofer. They're very reasonably priced and they've saved me a lot of heartache. I would highly recommend these if you're looking for reasonably priced good quality speakers with powerful wall-shaking-subwoofers. They work well with my Sony Bravia TV as well.

title: like some alien creature trapped in a human body that ...
text:
My gourd is big... And by gourd I mean head. I've got a massive head, like some alien creature trapped in a human body that wants to be able to talk to you and others on the internet while listening to the delicious Surround Sound quality of whatever current distraction I'm immersing myself in.

Pro :
* They are comfortable as all get out.
* The sound is amazing.
* The mic is actually really decent, and has good noise filter.
* They hold a charge for quite a while, I get a good two hours a day for five or six days before I need to charge them. (And if I forget to turn them off, they have a nice automatic "sleep" feature which can be turned off by flicking the volume button.)
* The charger is on the bottom of the left can, which is also a con, I'll go into that below.
* Once you take out the dongle and plug it in, your headset has a handy snack compartment in the ear, just remember to use ziploc bags so ants don't get into your brain.

Con :
* They are big, I mean it. If desk space is at a minimum get a headset-stand. I did, and it is a piece of s***, but it works.
* The mic doesn't pull out that far and I catch myself speaking louder than I need to because of it, that is something I am sure I will adjust to in time.
* The charging is on the bottom of the can, which is great when you are wearing them... But, if you hang them up, these are heavy big cans, if your headset-stand isn't really tall as well they will sit on the USB cable. Which, when a 9 year old comes rushing in to show you something can get tipped over and off of the desk... Which will then bend the USB port... Which will cause the 34 year old father, and 9 year old daughter to cry... (But, as an aside, Logitech replaced it free of charge when I explained the situation and that I'd only had the headset for... Say, three days? Now my headset-stand is on the opposite side of the desk from the study door, meaning my wonderful 9 year old daughter can bounce in and throw her drawings, tablet, self into my lap without having to fear anything but me accidentally smacking her while I flail as she surprises me.

Overall : I've owned the Kraken Headset (Blech), Numer Steelseries Headsets (Meh..) and my Seinheisser headphones that are like Buddha and Jesus making sweet love to your ears... But lack a mic. I would recommend this headset to anyone, and everyone. Even if they seem like they are over your budget, trust me, buying a pair of these and using them over the course of two-three years is better than buying a s***ty headset once a year and cheaper in the long run.

I like this mouse a lot. it is nice having a larger-than-normal wireless mouse. It feels pretty nice to use, and the left click, right click, and scroll wheel all feel nice. It is nice having a scroll wheel release, and for the price, this mouse is pretty fantastic.

CONS:
The 3 side buttons feel mushy and awkward, especially the lower side panel button. I never use that one for anything. The scroll wheel release often gets pressed when storing my mouse in my laptop bag. The sensor being on the side rather than in the center sometimes makes the mouse feel strange, especially when first getting used to using it. I very rarely notice this after a month or so of use, but it is something to consider.

text:
I bought this to make my ipad mini more useful at work. I'm trying to go mostly paperless, so I use this keyboard, along with Microsoft One Note, to take notes, track phone calls, etc... This keyboard is great! The battery lasts a long time, I can usually get several days on meetings in without charging it. I have to charge the ipad several times before I have to charge the keyboard. The keys do make a slight clicking noise when you type, but not as bad as most laptops and after a few months hasn't been a distraction.

This case if mostly for the keyboard, it doesn't fully encase the ipad, so a drop or something may still damage it. Since I generally carry it in my backpack or to and from meetings, it has been fine for my needs. The pen holder is nice also, I have a pen/stylus, so I have a pen handy if I need to write on someone else's note pages, sign something, etc...

I would not use my ipad nearly as much without this keyboard, it really makes it a useful business tool.

Here is my wish list: I wish the Mevo app included the capability to add titling (such as the name of the person appearing on the video). title: Nice job, Logitech! Finally a remote that works the way I want it to!
text:
We had an older Logitech remote that was programmable through their web app. The puppy decided he liked the remote better than we did, and although it still worked after the application of some CSI-style, crime-scene reconstruction forensics and super glue, it was time for a new remote now that he had grown up.

This remote and the computer-based app is remarkable. If you can follow simple directions, the application walks you through each step. I write instruction and repair procedures, and I can tell you that the instructions in the app make it easy to get the remote working how you like. well done, Logitech!

You Begin by entering the brand and model number of each device. On one of the older devices it gave a screen message that there are control variations with that model and to consult them if there was a problem. It also popped up that the Roku was IR and RF and that this remote was only IR. It even handled an old VCR and a not-quite-as-old DVD recorder. Ya... we're old. So what?

Once all your devices are entered you create "Activities." For example, for watching TV we use our receiver, the LCD TV and the antenna. It even asks if we wanted the Onkyo or the TV to control the volume and what input on the TV to use for this activity and what input on the receiver. I was easily able to create an "FM" activity to listen to the radio in the morning. With dreary morning eyes, just we only have to press the "FM" screen icon in the "activities" window on the touch screen.

Additionally, I created two "custom" activities- one for watching HULU and one for watching NETFLIX using our Roku3. I was able to customize it so that the remote would start the TV, Start the Onkyo, and select the Roku. At that point it sent the signals to emulate remote key selections for "HOME/Click Right/click Right/OK" to get to Hulu. I did much the same for Netflix. I found that these two custom Activities would not go back and forth between the two. The solution was to add a two second delay between "HOME" and "go right." The app made that easy as one of the custom items which could be selected in the app was "ADD DELAY" and you can select the length of the delay as well. Handy for troubleshooting should it become necessary. The custom items (such as the button presses) can be reordered when programming them as well. In that way, when I found the two custom Activities were not working properly I went back into the app, added a delay, and then moved the delay up to just after "Home."

If you are not sure, you can download the "MyHarmony desktop software" at the Logitech website and program in all the various devices to see how it works before even purchasing the remote.

Although I gave it five stars, it is not perfect:

- One problem I had with the last Harmony remote model and this one as well is that it is made to fit in your hand. Unfortunately, that same ergonomic design makes it very difficult to click something as simple as "Mute" when the remote is sitting on the table.
- Allowing the application to auto-program the favorite channels will work fine for most people, but if you live in a rural area and get channels from different directions (like when using an antenna rotor), you can't automatically add the channels from both directions. Pick one or the other. The solution is to add the channels you watch manually, and that can be done right on the remote. Afterwards, synch the remote on the computer and they will be saved there was well.
- Finally, the battery is not meant to be user replaceable, but a search on YouTube will show you that it can be done fairly easily, just in case the battery dies before the remote does.

If I had known these things before I bought it, would it have changed my mind! No. I have been writing reviews in the coffee industry for nearly 16 years and try to be balanced in my appraisals. This is why I added the above.

This model is evidently no longer for sale at Logitech, and I hope that this is not an indication that it is discontinued as that would be too bad. If you don't need the home automation and smart phone app, this remote might just be what you are looking for. We got ours as a refurb for under $120, delivered with sales tax. What a deal!

text:
TL;DR: Packaging was good and the delivery was on time. Thanks Amazon for that. They are heavier than I expected. Pretty solid construction. Decent sound.

So, I got these a few days ago and was pleasantly surprised with the build quality. These speakers are solid. Large subwoofer; definitely moves some air. The placement of the connections on the box are strange. If you're looking at the default stock photo, looking directly at the exhaust duct for the subwoofer, the connections are on the left towards the rear of the unit on the bottom, or parallel with the cone of the subwoofer. Kind of strange. I would have expected to see them on the opposite side of the exhaust (Is that the right word? Probably not...)

The cables on the Speakers are rather short. The cord for the right speaker, which houses the controls, is a serial cable. It is only about 4.5 feet in length, which is a stretch for where I have my speakers on my desk relative to the box. I can see this becoming an issue as other have mentioned it. Not great for sub-optimum step ups.

The sound quality is good. For this price point, I did expect them to be a little better. The base has a tendancy to sound a bit muddled compared to other Logitech speakers I've had, but it's not bad. Just feels a little bit separate from the rest of the sound until you play with it a bit.

Do not use an AMP'd signal into these speakers! It will clip and pop the audio. It took me almost two hours to realize I had iTunes amplifying the signal out. Not good!

Overall a good, not great product. I won't be returning them, but I don't know that I would buy them so enthusiastically next time.

title: These speakers are very good for the money
text:
These speakers are very good for the money. They sound rich and full, with no shortage of detail in the mids and lows. The mids are the clear tonal strong point. The lows are extremely deep (thanks to the wonderful subwoofer), and fairly detailed. You can find more expensive units that offer more lows, but after listening to several $200-$400 sets from Polk Audio and Bose, I can confirm that the lows of these Logitechs are as crisp/deep if not more so than the more expensive systems. The highs don't sing and sizzle like more expensive systems (If you care about highs and an extremely full midrange, I reccomend the Polk Audio Hampen speakers. They are exceptional for highs and midrange, and you can buy a sub to fill it up. More expensive, but not drastically), but are standard for this price range. Three negatives: 1) These speakers don't have the aesthetics of other systems. They aren't particularly pleasing to the eye. 2) They tend to emit a very quiet but high-pitched hiss when turned on but not playing sound. This isn't a huge deal for me, because if I'm not using them, then I turn them off, but if you plan on keeping them out of easy arm reach, the hiss will get very annoying very quickly. 3) They don't have a separate wired remote like a lot of other systems do. The only place to turn it on/off and adjust v volume is on the right speaker itself. 4) The chords connecting the speakers to the sub are fairly short. Each speaker is connected to the sub through a separate cable that is less than 5 feet long.

I highly recommend these if none of the negatives will be an issue for you- they sound great.

title: The overall quality of sound makes these the perfect speakers for anyone who wants to enjoy music at ...
text:
If you are looking for high quality speakers at a reasonably low price then these are the speakers you’re looking for. The Logitech Z623 Home Speaker system has unparalleled sound quality for the price. Logitech has seemingly fit a $300+ home entertainment sound system into have the size and a third of the price.
These speakers really provide a wide range of sound and and allow you to really hear every note of the music you’re playing. Typically when looking at other sound systems in this price range you will not find adequate bass from the sub woofer in the system, however the Z623’s sub woofer provides smooth and noticeable bass. The overall quality of sound makes these the perfect speakers for anyone who wants to enjoy music at a low price. The overall sound makes you feel like you are in the center of a movie theater in mid action scene. The immersive sound really fills any entertainment room and gives studio quality output to the listener.
The relatively small design allows you to fit the entire system perfectly into any TV or night stand without fear of looking bulky or out of place. The sleek design of the left and right speakers really give the system as a whole the feeling of unbeatable quality. The ergonomic shape of the buttons on the system also strengthens this feeling of quality. Also, the left and right speakers are each given a generous amount of cable distance so you can effortlessly move them to adjust to your given TV or night stand, or anywhere you choose to use the speakers.
As well as the quality and design, Logitech also has really catered to the modern day music listener by putting a 3.5mm audio jack that makes it easy for you to hook up any laptop, phone, gaming console, etc. If you are looking for more of a hands free approach then Amazon has also included top quality bluetooth adapters so you can play music from anywhere in your room. I am very pleased with my purchase of these speakers, after much research on other similar products I think it’s clear that the Z623’s have unmatched sound quality for the price.
If you are in the market for high quality and low price home entertainment speakers then these are it. I can honestly say that I am very pleased with my purchase and am positive that any owner of these speakers feels as passionately as I do about them.

The satellites have some surprising weight to them, giving off the impression that these things are built pretty well. The subwoofer is a lot smaller than I thought it'd be, but that's no statement on its power. It's built very well. title: Blown Away by Logitech
text:
To preface, I am an audiophile and have spent countless years at my father’s recording studio hearing some of the best studio monitors out there. I am by no means comparing computer/home theater speakers to the likeness of a pair of $6,000 Genelec studio monitors, but I have high regards for these Logitech speakers.

To be honest, I bought these speakers alongside a monitor for my PC not expecting much other than knowing that for a fact they will at least be better than the speakers found in my TV, which I was using as a monitor for the longest time. When I received them, I quickly set them up and played some music from my phone. I was simply blown away at the sound quality that these speakers put out even when they were not properly setup in terms of placement. Once the speakers were properly setup, I was even more amazed. I eventually cranked up the volume somewhere around three-quarters of the way and was even more surprised that these speakers were not distorting. Ever since I set them up, I have been using them not on my PC but on my Macbook Pro nonstop and have even been able to turn off my EQ in iTunes as I feel these speakers reproduced the sound more accurately.

Keep in mind that my review is based on many variables such as the size of my room, placement of the speakers, etc. But, I have found that with these speakers you need to turn up the bass knob (for me I turned it in between 1 and 2 O’Clock) to achieve a smooth low frequency response and a more overall “fuller” sound. When setting up the speakers, I recommend referencing the picture I included for placement and using a song that you know well and setting the volume to your normal listening volume and then modifying the bass knob to your satisfaction. I would like to stress that placement is one of the biggest factors for how your system will sound.

Regardless, I find that these speakers are absolutely worth the money. I have used them to listen to music, to play movies, and other miscellaneous audio related tasks on my computer. There is no doubt that these speakers are THX Certified because it felt like pretty close to being in a movie theater when it came to movies that made adequate use of the subwoofer. I am even contemplating getting another pair to replace the Bose Cinemate GS Series II that is on the TV in my living room as I feel that this system is better than the Bose. I can only find one con when it comes to this system and that is if it were to be used for on a TV, which Logitech says it can be used for, there is no remote for changing the volume or shutting the unit off. Using it on a TV could lead to having to change volume by hand as most TVs have a fixed audio output not a variable one.
To be fair, this is a minor fault considering that this system is more of a system for the computer than for the TV.

Nonetheless, don’t hesitate buying this unit. For the price, I have yet to find anything that can beat it let alone one that is comparable.

text: I purchased these speakers to replace my Logitech X-230 2.1 Computer speakers and I can say these are a massive improvement. I had owned both the Logitech Z-2200 and Z-2300 speaker systems in the past and can say from personal experience the Z-2300 had the best bass response of the three the next best being the Z-2200. I am not dismissing these speakers as for the price you are getting alot of sound. I do however want to compare these speakers to their predecessors for those who have owned them and wanted to compare them. The first thing I would point out is Z623 have a boomier bass to them and do not have the tight "punch" the other previous generations have. The bass adjustment knob at its center position is a lot flatter than the previous generations leaving the sound a bit lacking for my tastes at least when it comes to music. The next thing owners of previous generations will notice is the volume control on the new z623 is different. When turning the volume from its "off" position to about 50% the overall volume increase is a lot milder than when going from 50% to 100% where the decibel difference is substantial. Other than that these speakers are a great deal and one of the best you can buy without going all out on a studio monitor setup. My only real complaint is the choice not to design these speakers with a volume control remote like the 2200 and 2300. The satelite speakers are much larger than the 2300s and are annoying to position on a desk where multiple monitors are used or where space is restricted. I would definitely recommend these to anyone that wants a great sound system for a very reasonable price.

However these speakers do have a great sound quality! By turning up the volume music sounds great, as do games and movies. The high-pitched noise is mostly inaudible when listening to something with lots of action. Even quiet parts of a song or movie is not that bad. They deliver plenty of volume and anything past 50% will shake your room!

Concluding this brief review, I must say that for the money you get a lot of great sound and power! But for speakers such as these "THX certified" I should not be hearing any high-pitched noises! I wish I could have purchased a pair of these without the noise. I was thinking of buying a set through Amazon, but isn't worth it if I have the same problem. The question is how long will they last? Is it something that is faulty? I would be fine and live with it if I knew there isn't a problem with the hardware.

I don't think 3 stars is overly generous but they do sound great! If the high pitched noise was gone, I would be happy to leave 5 stars!

Update July 2 2016

I have been keeping this set of 623's because I was tired of returning them for another with the same high pitched noise! So far it's been a couple weeks and they are still working. The noise is there, it's worse some days then acceptable the next... I can't predict how long these speakers will last, but I wish I could... I have a set of Bose Companion 2 Series lll's on hand just in case the Logitech's do fail! Lol

Okay, design sometimes changes during the life of a product/future developments, HOWEVER as I looked over the mouse more and more, the differences were subtle but were still there. Over the years I've owned 3-4 M510 wireless mouses and looking at the brand new the logo placement on the top of the mouse was in a completely different place, again the blue color of the mouse itself was much lighter, there was no "Logitech" logo on the bottom of the mouse, the "Off"/"On"/"M510"/Unifying receiver logo were all stamped instead of painted on. The biggest and most crucial difference however is that if you look at the product description, you will see a circular hole that has "Performance Laser" or maybe even "High Performance Laser"... BUT on the mouse I just got from amazon it is a completely different cutout, and next to it it has punched text that says "Invisible Optic". But wait, this isn't an optical mouse. This is a laser mouse.

The button click noises were a bit louder than I liked (with a shaprer more audible 'click'), and the middle mouse button has too much resistance to comfortably use on a long term basis. This button also suffered from click recognition from time to time, which was doubly frustrating.

In the end, for some reason my system (Windows 8.1) stopped recognizing this mouse after only a couple weeks. I ended up taking apart the old mx310 and finding the source of it's scroll wheel problem, and am now happily using my previous 10+ year old mouse again which has no recognition issues with my system.

If the mouse had not failed to work then I probably would have suffered through using it, but it did not have the mouse quality I thought I was buying. Thankfully this m500 didn't cost a whole lot, but I still feel like the money I did spend was wasted.

If you're listening to music from far away, or perhaps even listening loudly, this isn't a problem. But if you aren't using the speakers or, worst of all, listening to any sort of quiet music, it's unmistakeable.

title: A great mouse I can't wholeheartedly recommend
text:
The Logitech MX Master is my favorite mouse. This is frustrating because despite owning two of these, getting one replaced with Logitech, and waiting almost two years since the release date, the Bluetooth issues with this mouse have not been resolved.

Everything else about the mouse is great: The industrial design is sleek and comfortable. The ability to pair three unique devices is great if you have multiple computers. The thumb scrollwheel is great for working in graphics programs like Photoshop or Sketch. The thumb button and its gestures are great. Even the software isn't that bad. Despite all of that, the main selling point of this mouse to many of us who upgraded from the Performance MX is its Bluetooth functionality, and the ability to free up one of the two USB ports on my MacBook Pro, and the MX Master doesn't live up to its promise.

Every few months I come back to the mouse and think, "instead of fishing up a Unifying Receiver, lets see if the Bluetooth works again." Every time I'm let down. From the moment the mouse is paired with the computer, its tracking is already a little bit slower than on a Unifying Receiver. Before long, usually 5-to-15 minutes later, it will start losing its Bluetooth signal and chopping across the screen, impossible to control until it regains some semblance of stability.

Don't count on Logitech Support being at all sympathetic either. The first time I tried to contact them, I went through a series of insultingly condescending tests for them, as if I didn't know what I was doing. I work with computers for a living. "Update your computer," they said. Other times, it was my computer's fault. I have a top-of-the-line 15" retina MacBook Pro and a recently built monster of a Windows PC. But besides the fact that two completely different computers surely weren't having the same Bluetooth issue, theres also the many others I've sold on buying MX Master that have the same Bluetooth problems.

So if you want a great, comfortable mouse, this is definitely the mouse for you, but its best to just pretend that the Bluetooth support exists. Its just a disappointment waiting to happen. Every time I flip the mouse over and see the "Connect" label and its accompanying button my heart sinks a little, but then I plug in my Unifying Receiver and USB hub and try to forget how nice it'd be to have a Bluetooth mouse.

I LOVE this keyboard for all the reasons every other reviewer has stated & agree with the design issues mentioned as well. That being said I have had mine since the iPad air came out a couple years and it has worked flawlessly as can be within its limitations. After so much use over the past few years some of the keys are finally starting to act up as I open & start to type. Once they start working again they're fine until I need to use the case & open it again. I may have to tap the ones that act up repeatedly to get them going again. This has only started in the past couple weeks but more & more keys are being affected, so it's time for a new one & as you can see from the pictures this one is WELL worn
The reasons I am getting another is
(1) because nothing else I've seen is as LIGHT & completely PROTECTIVELY wraps around the iPad &
(2) while not glamourous I have figured out a sutible low tech solution to the cracking frame quality issue that this product most definitely has that works for me. A cheap clip with rubberized tips that holds the ipad in place very well (see the pics).
(3) none of the other keyboard cases are able to be lightly wiped down & RESISIT DUST/DIRT like this one making it great in the field for me when in dusty construction environments.
I hope my new one works as well or better than this one has but at least I'll know what to expect from it. I'm actually using this keyboard to type this review.

title: As you volume it up or down all the frequencies and instruments (especially bass) come through remarkably even (as they would on
text:
Replaced SoundWorks12V speaker system on my computer, which was getting "tired". It had a separate bass sub-woofer, but even with the bass volume control cranked all the way over, it was not sufficient or well balance with the other frequencies.
I am a professional jazz musician and perform regularly on stage with massive audio systems, monitor speakers, ran by professional audio engineers etc, etc. I can recognize well setup and well balance audio when I hear it. Anything can "appear" well balanced when you crank it up so you can "hear it through your bones". The trick is will it be well balanced and pleasant to listen to at low volume while you work at the computer 2 feet away from the speakers. This system does it in spades with the bass control set to its center detent. As you volume it up or down all the frequencies and instruments (especially bass) come through remarkably even (as they would on a good audio board). I could have bought cheaper computer speakers or even cheaper Ligitech models, this system is well worth the little extra cost. It is a pleasure to listen through it to performers on youtube,or streaming music on pandora.

title: Great, until the sub burned out after 3 months.
text:
I have to say that I have been extremely happy with Logitech products in the past. A previous set of speakers that I owned lasted 10+ years and only stopped working because the audio cord was severed. I didn't want to deal with getting the cord repaired and I also wanted to upgrade the size of my sub woofer, so I opted to purchase the Z623 system. The price was great, they promised rich bass, the majority of reviews were very positive, and I was happy with the quality and longevity of my previous Logitech speaker system; I was confident I was making the right decision.

Once I received the system it was love at first listen. The speakers sounded great and the ability to control the level of bass was exactly what I was looking for. I rarely pushed the bass level over 60%, as even at the 30% to 50% range, the bass shook the house. The same can be said for my use of the volume dial, the majority of the time the volume never exceeded 75% for extended periods of time. I only used my speakers a couple times per week, mostly on the weekends, for 1 to 3 hours per jam session. Every time the speakers were used, I made sure that they weren't being "pushed too hard" and anytime the sound became distorted the bass and volume level would promptly be dialed back. I really wanted these speakers to last as long as my old system.

Unfortunately, they only lasted a little over 3 months. I noticed an odd burning smell one night while using the system. I quickly found the smell was coming from the sub woofer as white smoke was pouring out of the exhaust! I never had any issue with a burning smell before and the volume and bass at the time of the incident were at a very reasonable level. I filed a warranty claim with Logitech within days of the incident. My experience with customer service has been fine so far. At the time I made the claim (4 days ago), the Z623 system was out of stock but I was told that I would receive a printable shipping label to send my defective system back to them and would be notified once they were available again. I haven't received the label and according to the Logitech website the system is back in stock, so hopefully they will get the label to me soon so that I can get my replacement system as soon as possible.

Overall, I was really happy with the system until it suddenly burned out on me. I'm very disappointed that this happened within such a short period of time given how long my old system lasted with zero issues. I really hope that my Z623 system was just defective and that this isn't a quality issue with all Z623 systems.

title: A $20 dollar headset with good range for $140 bucks.Unless you need a 100ft+ range headset look elsewhere.
text:
If you're looking for good sound quality and microphone quality look elsewhere. If you want a long range wireless headset for conference calls with cheap build quality, it will work... to a certain extent. If this was a 50 dollar headset I would say it's a good buy if you're only doing conference calls occasionally on your desktop throughout the day.

Pros:
-Long Range (I can actually get 100+ feet with walls distance and be able to hear/speak on conference calls)

-Has a dedicated mute light (you can see when you're away from your desk that you're on mute) which is a really nice indicator.

Cons:

-Garbage audio quality, I can hear coworkers well enough for a phone call. Listening to music sounds worse than some $10 dollar headsets I've owned.

-Microphone audio quality while not garbage is not much better than poor. I have coworkers complain about it picking up my overhead ceiling fan and sounding like I'm in a "wind tunnel" . I've used several headsets in this office and I've never had any make that comment until using this one. I have to have have mic boost to full otherwise no one can hear me.

-Poor build quality. Although the charging stand is nice, is weighted and has a couple of light, the headset itself is cheap. I had the charging stand fall off my desk while it was charging ONCE and it broke this headset. This is a plastic headset with plastic joints, simply the cheapest materials and engineering they could throw together.

-Poor comfort. You know those headsets that feel like you're wearing a clamp on your head? Yeah, it's one of those.

-Decent/poor battery life. If I'm on a bunch of conference calls throughout the day and try to play music in-between the battery doesn't last the day. Basically you are limited to putting it on and off the charging station if you work more than 8 hours. I think I've gotten 9 hours tops out of the device.

-Limited connectivity. This device only pairs with the base station. So you can't pair it to your phone or office phone. This isn't something that everyone needs but keep it mind most of us use an office phone (or cell phone) AND a computer we would like to use.

title: This headset while seeming nice has some pretty serve product flaws which makes me ...
text:
This headset while seeming nice has some pretty serve product flaws which makes me not able to recommend to anyone.

Cons:
The biggest con with this headset is the range. While the site clear states you have a 20 meter range with this product you have something closer to a 3 foot range with RF dongle it comes with. I can easily get a 3 foot cabled headset for less than 20 dollars why would I possibly want to use this device? While the Bluetooth may be able to handle around 10 feet (slightly better than the RF) it's still less than the 20 meter range mentioned. However, the Bluetooth audio (incoming and outgoing) is horrible and sounds like everything is run through a string and can. Between these two issues Also the connectors between headphone drivers and the headset itself are held together with thin plastic which seems easy to break.

Neutral:
Flip up mic can bend and is move-able. Reasonably comfortable band. Device has on ear controls for mute with audio indicator although no visual indicator. Battery Life is a few hours which is enough to get you through some calls but not an entire workday of use.

Pros:
The device sounds pretty decent when using the Wireless RF transmitter (not bluetooth). Has two radios one for Bluetooth to pair with mobile devices and the better sounding RF for your PC.

Overall:
I can't recommend anyone buying this headset unless you REALLY hate cords and want something for a short range that can pair with your phone, tablet, and PC. There are better ranged standalone bluetooth headsets and better sounding/ranged headsets for PCs. Wired headsets will give you a much better bang for your buck for about a comparable range.

title: not even close to the mx revolution
text:
anyone who says this thing is a true successor to the mx revolution is either lying or desperate for a new mouse.

i have been using the mx revolution since it came out in 2006. i will go on record saying the mx revolution is the greatest mouse ever conceived of by man or god. however, my second one is failing, and so i decided instead of buying an old used revolution off that auction site that will probably start double clicking in 6 months, id try the mx master since its been getting such great reviews.

well...most of those great reviews are from people using the mx performance or other non mx revolution mice...because compared to the revolution...this thing is garbage.

to be fair...the mouse itself isnt too bad. i kind of like the new thumb wheel (even though it doesnt have a button), and i like the "gesture" button...which i changed to something else. the contour od the mouse is ok...i like the revolution better, but ive been using it for 10 years...i probably just need to get accustomed to it. so...yea...the actual mouse itself is alright.

heres where it all goes horribly horribly wrong:
the god awful logitech options software
that abysmal, frail, improperly built unifying receiver.

first up...the logitech options software. IF you have never used the mx revolution and set point (or even better...uberoptions) then you might actually like the logitech options software. however...if youre coming from an mx revolution and set point...be prepared to pull out all your hair as you realize that using the word "options" in the name of the software is nothing but a cruel sadistic joke.DO NOT expect the level of customization you got with set point...because you aint gonna get it. it also doesnt help that the software doesnt get added to the startup list and also wont reside in the taskbar.

now on to the unifying receiver...what can i say? its a flimsy, poorly built, pos. ive had my mx master for 3 days...and it hasnt managed to stay connected for more than 2 hours. my revolution (well 2 of them) disconnected a grand total of zero times in 10 years. the issue is that it doesnt make proper contact in the usb port...any usb port. i had to open it (which was entirely too easy to do) pull out the tiny circuit board (which wasnt even held in with anything at all) and wedge a little folded piece of paper behind it in the housing to push the board forward so it would make contact properly. sure...it worked...but i shouldnt have had to do that.

even still...the software keeps "forgetting" my mouse...which is to say that its still connected and will still move and function as a mouse (so its not the receiver) but none of the special software functions work. which means that it operates like a normal 3 button mouse. trying to get it to recognize the mouse ends in a cryptic "wireless receivers are full" message and it wont connect. go ahead...look up that message there is literally NOTHING anywhere that explains it or how to fix it. when this happens your only hope is to unplug the receiver shake your voodoo chicken foot over it and pray it connects again when you plug it back in.

soooo...no. this thing is certainly no successor to the mx revolution. logitech should just do what people have been begging them to do for the past 5 years and make that one again. theres a reason they go for $450 new IF you can find one...which you probably cant.

conclusion:
pros-
mouse itself is pretty nice.
battery life is very good
usb charging (no dock)

cons-
awful terrible aggravating buggy software
shoddy receiver
pricey for being so underdeveloped as a "power user" mouse.

conclusion:
if you never experienced the joyful bliss of the mx revolution you might like this mouse.
if youre coming from the mx revolution this is absolutely positively 100% NOT an adequate replacement

title: A great device with some minor caveats
text:
This is a very good remote with some caveats. I initially bought the Harmony Elite and returned it because functionally it just did not work for me. I had it for about 30 days and kept going back to my old remotes. I bought this one which is a much more traditional remote (and about 300.00 less) and aside from not controlling my PS3, it works great. You can set it to mimic your other remotes and you can also set it to perform activities which will perform functions across multiple devices. It will also control multiple devices on the same device setting if you programming it correctly (i.e. controlling the soundbar volume and TV input on the DVR device setting.) I use this to control my DVR, TV, BOSE soundbar, XBOX, and Roku. After programming it and working through some issues, it works perfectly for what I need.

A few things that I do not like: You cannot re-order the device listing or the activity listing. In my case this is a pain because my DVR and Soundbar receiver are on different pages on my device listing. The same is true on my activity listing. It is unfortunate that every time I use the remote I will need to press something, then hit back, open a new device or activity, and then press something else. This seems like such a simple thing to fix but I searched online and many people had the same issue and were told it cannot be done by Harmony support.

Also, the software to sync the device continually gets hung up and I need to unplug my remote, exit the software, restart, plug my remote back in, and sync again. I would say I have a 60% success rate in syncing the first time. Now that my remote is programmed that won't mean much but it was annoying. That might be my laptop or version of windows. Who knows.

If I could re-order the device and activity listing, I would give this 5 stars. However, for the 50 bucks, you can't go wrong.

title: The battery almost seems designed to fail after several months
text:
Ok, so some background on my experience with the keyboard: I received one of these keyboards as a gift initially long ago (Christmas 2012). The keyboard worked great!! … for about 7 months. After that point, it would only work with light directly over it, and then sometimes spottily (the battery would not charge regardless of the surrounding brightness, 500+ lux).

After opening a support ticket with Logitech, they agreed to replace the keyboard. That is great! … but 6 months later, another dead keyboard (thanks to another battery failure).

There is a silver lining here: you can buy the battery for this keyboard for a couple bucks (the ML2032). If you have run across this post while investigating how to fix your dead keyboard, this will probably do the trick. The only drawback here is that the case is specifically designed not to allow you to open the battery compartment, so it may take some elbow grease… be careful so you don’t jab yourself with the screwdriver/ other implement while trying to pry it open :P. In my case, Logitech did not ask me to return the dead keyboard, so I ended up with two living keyboards for the price of some frustration.

This thing is a nice keyboard when it works (hence the 3 stars), but has some flaws. Had they included a better battery to start and made them easier to replace when necessary, I would give it a 4 or 5 as it is light, the keys feel nice, and it is quite low profile.

title: Great Mouse, Would Highly Reccomend
text:
This is a great mouse. The sensor is way more than you'll ever need and feels great. The adjustable tuning weights are a great feature that you may not think is super necessary, but it is extremely nice to be able to keep it at the perfect weight. The buttons are all really responsive and Have a great feel. It is definitely made for people with medium to larger hands. Claw grip with this mouse feels great and I can easily place the base of my palm against the back of the mouse and still hit almost all the buttons extremely easily. However, the Dpi-shift thumb button I have not found very useful. If you are playing a first-person shooter, it is 1. Hard to hit and 2. Fairly useless. The idea is that you would use when sniping, but any well-designed game is going to automatically lower your sensitivity when scoped in. That being said, you can fairly easily reassign it to a different function but hitting still I find quite hard.

Other hardware notes:
-The scroll wheel is very useful when free-scrolling, but it is easy to accidently to hit the toggle in-game which can cause you to switch weapons when you weren't trying to.
-Weights can be hard to get out of mouse after you put them in
-The texturing on the rubber feels really comfortable, and I have used it four hours with getting uncomfortable.
-Ergonomics also feel great

The software is fairly well designed, but it has some things that are hard to do that would be nice if they were easier. Adjusting the Dpi can be kind of finicky and reassigning buttons is simple, but not the most intuitive. The programmable macros are really nice for both working and gaming, and the RGB software is great. The RGB options are fairly limited in comparison to something like the Razer Mamba, but overall ,the lights are really good looking and very bright. The brightness is adjustable, but be prepared: darker colors are not going to be very bright looking. That sounds dumb, but its is very hard to not make the colors so vibrant without losing brightness. The software's game recognition and custom profiles per game are great and are certainly very useful and have pretty much any in-game function you could want without having to go in and change controls in-game. But, this means that if you switch to the onboard profiles and forget, the buttons you are used to pressing are not what you expect them to be, so just make sure you check and make sure you are set to the right memory and profile.

Final Thoughts/ TLDR:
I highly recommend this mouse and is easily the best in terms of actual function anywhere near its price point. The hardware is great and comfortable, and the software, although not perfect, has no glaring issues and is mostly intuitive. The LED look amazing and are easy to customize. The programmable buttons are great and can be programmed with macros, which is amazing. All in all, you should definitely buy this mouse if you are in the market for a new gaming mouse (especially for FPS games, but MOBAs and MMOs are great with this).

title: DETAILED REVIEW, things you need to know that aren't generally stated!!!!!!
text:
I have a Samsung 12.2", 64MB, WiFi tablet bought in Dec. 2014. I upgraded (not by choice, mandated) from KitKat 4.4.4 to Lollipop 5.0.1. That said, I just bought this new keyboard & a Samsung mouse elsewhere for a lot cheaper but I just want to worn you there are problems with Lollipop (all revisions) communicating with Bluetooth & I hear sometimes WiFi too. I am one of the fortunate ones that the fix worked by clearing all Bluetooth connections & cashe on the tablet then starting fresh to connect to Bluetooth, keyboard & mouse to tablet successfully. And don't forget to hit "scan" when trying to pair! It is easy to do once understanding how to do it. Samsung does not understand even after 4 hours on the phone with a tech. In fact I had to tell him the problem & the fix. He still couldn't do it nor could Logitech. It was a woman Samsung tech at Best Buy that told me how to fixed it over the phone in 10 minutes. Well, success!!!! I have connected with Bluetooth between the tablet, mouse & keyboard.
Also NOTE: Logitech has discontinued this keyboard as a result. Google/Android has refused to send out a patch or updates to resolve this problem.

All this said & I have only had/used the keyboard for a couple of days, I will now review this keyboard.
1. Overall the keyboard is a keeper. A BIG issue is you lose spellcheck capibility. NO SPELLCHECK!!! Android spell check is really lousy anyway.
2. My second MAJOR issue is the battery on this keyboard is not replaceable period, not even by the manufacturer, Logitech. What? That's right. There is no way if the battery dies it can be replaced. So this keyboard is short lived, probably. Designed/recommended to use only a couple of hours per day.
3. It has NO indicator if the battery needs recharging or not. Recommends once a month based on 2 hrs/day.
4. You must use the back arrow on the tablet (bottom right) to move back into the tablet. Meaning to do anything but type in the page you are typing on the keyboard does not work (no going from page to page or whatever). Any other areas you want to access must be done on the tablet itself. It is NOT like a keyboard on a laptop. No real big deal but can be difficult to get used to having to use touch screen, keyboard & mouse vs just keyboard.
5. The keyboard is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard so that takes time getting used to but not lots.
6. The keys are a hard to press to type fast but that is also something to just get used to. I am already a lot better than the first day.
7. The problems of the tablet not being secure in the holders/clips... I have not had an issue with that yet but I can see that it could be. So I have no firm comment. Maybe one, I can see where they aren't "screwed in" secure but as with all electronics one must be gentle when using or carrying it around. The case is not designed for careless handliers but fine for responsible owners of a very expensive tablet.
8. I have not used all the key functions yet so I can't comment on them.
9. It is very difficult to take pictures with the case on or using it in portrait/vertical position. It really must be removed from the case.
10. The keyboard is fairly responsive although there are times it is slow/lags but not often or for long. It does not jump all over the place either!
11. I don't give a hoot about cosmetics if the equipment is outstanding. But I guess I better say something about that. It is very professional looking. It doesn't not look or feel like a toy or cutesy or out of the future. It is just very professional looking. It allows easy access to all the slots/bottons, external SD card, battery, cameras, power & volume controls. Seems it will be durable & protective too, quite functional as it should be.
12. The tablet angle can be placed in only one position. There are not any choices... so put a pillow or sock or book (whatever) under the keyboard to put it at the angle you desire. It is not necessary to do this when using it on a flat stable surface. On one's lap in bed, or legs/feet up on the the couch, yes you will probably want the back lifted to angle the tablet comfortably.
13. BEWARE this keyboard/case is discontinued so it may become difficult to find new.
14. NO INSTRUCTIONS with this keyboard. None on Logitech website either. You will have to play a lot to see how to use it. The user forum at Logitech is not very good or active either.
15. It is NOT a backlit keyboard.
16. The keyboard must be turned off after use (mouse too). It does sleep but still sucks up power thirsty Bluetooth. In fact your battery will be drained in 1-2 hours of continual use. Best to keep the tablet plugged in while using Bluetooth. Actual keyboard power usage is unknown still but revewers say it has a long life... months. Best to drain battery then charge it per instructions (the only valuable thing in the "instructions") but you canNOT tell when that is. Dumb design!!!
Note: the other keyboard that can be used with this tablet (theoretically with no Bluetooth issues) is the Logitech K480. This model has no case. I have seen it in the stores & you can use it in portrait or landscape positions but no choice on forward/back angles. It appears it would be a good choice too but NO CASE!
17. It has a stylus S-Pen carrier/tab in front of case but totally unnecessary because the table carrier/slot is easily accessible. That tab is good for assisting in opening the case though.
18. Tablet battery warming up? You can't tell! Tablet must be removed to know for sure.
19. What can I say, a real keyboard is so much better than duking it out with a finger or pen. PLUS the cursor or page doesn't jump all over the place since your hands or S-pen aren't near or touching the tablet. Major issue for me.
20. Opening the case up & setting up the tablet is easy but it can cause your grip to falter allowing the tablet to fall. Just be careful.
21. Some have complained, when set-up, the back is flimsy. Yes it is but it still prevents the tablet from falling backwards. So it works. Yes, with no problem you can use the touch screen while the case is set-up. I advise using the S-Pen since that is a gentler touch than a finger.

OVERALL: It is a keeper, many downfalls but it is a nice sturdy good keyboard & hard case. It is NOT flimsy, not rock solid either but does the job pretty well. I like it. With no battery replacement & no spellcheck... those are real bummers. This is why it is a 4 star rating... maybe even a 3 star rating.... pretty major stuff.
Please excuse any mispellings/typos... my area of weakness.

I contacted Logitech and they informed me that yes, it qualifies for warranty replacement BUT I would have to return it to the merchant I bought it from. Sounds great until you realize that Amazon and almost every other store on the planet won't allow you to return anything a year later. I guess now I'm on the hunt for something similar with a better warranty policy.

I can't really recommend this mouse knowing that it will likely break on you and you'll be stuck with a broken mouse with a "warranty" that isn't worth the paper it's printed on. This is the second Logitech M510 that broke in this way. title: Logitech makes good hardware but don't expect a consistent scrolling experience
text:
I've gone through a few bouts of hand pain over the years and each time I was able to work it out through stretching. However I decided not to put off my hands any longer and buy a trackball mouse. My great uncle had double carpal tunnel and used a trackball afterwards with great success. I was nervous about the lack of dedicated scroll but it said there was software support for it. I spent too long trying to get it to work nicely on Windows but never got it working in Windows Metro apps. Which means no Task Manager scrolling! I used the Logitech software, then an older utility Marble Mouse Scroll, then MarbleScroll which was newer. The Logitech Chrome extension was worthless but I was still feeling okay. Until I got home to set it up on my MacBook Pro.

Turns out there is no autoscroll or universal scroll support for OSX, none. The scrolling they talk about ends up taking the 3rd and 4th buttons and making them dedicated page up and page down buttons. I spent again more hours than I should have installing Logitech software and trying to figure out why I couldn't get it working like Windows was.

And Windows wasn't perfect. Visual Studio wouldn't scroll at all. Logitech's answer to that is "Therefore, it has to be something with that specific application that is not allowing the full functionality of that mouse. Where it is a Microsoft product I am going to advise that you contact Microsoft." http://forums.logitech.com/t5/Mice-and-Pointing-Devices/SetPoint-redefined-scroll-does-not-work-in-Visual-Studio-2010/m-p/624106/highlight/true#M33579

So if you're on Windows and you don't care about scrolling then this is a fine mouse. If you're on OSX and don't care about scrolling this is a fine mouse. I was on Windows 10 and OSX El Capitan

I have ordered this other mouse with a dedicated scroll 'ring' to see if it works as advertised. [[ASIN:B002OOWB3O Kensington Orbit Trackball Mouse with Scroll Ring (K72337US)]]

text:
This review is my small token of thanks to Logitech for being a customer-oriented business.

My M305 mouse continues to faithfully point and click even after four years of college abuse. Recently, I was saddened by the loss of my unifying receiver. After switching to a wired trackball, I eventually found someone else's discarded unifying receiver by happy accident. Thanks to Logitech's forward-thinking unifying technology, I am able to put this wonderful M305 mouse to good use once again.

I feel I ought to brag a bit - I was able to navigate my PC to download & install the unifying software using only my wired keyboard. It was quite a moment of pride when the mouse paired to the PC, without the help of any other mouse.

Thanks, Logitech. You're adding significant value to the marketplace of ideas!

title: Warranty Problems
text:
Pros:

- Easy to customize the functions of the four buttons w/ Logitech's SetPoint software
- Fairly smooth rolling action
- Mostly comfortable for extended use
- Logitech comes though when it comes to their long warranties
- Most classic and affordable trackball on the market

Cons:

- Lacks a reasonable scroll feature. Scroll feature is clunky and max scroll speed is a crawl even at max sensitivity.
- Rolling action is not very smooth at slow roll speeds
- Secondary buttons are uncomfortable to use often. This is especially an issue since one of them activates the scroll feature

The product is 4 stars but I'm leaving two stars for the following reason: A few months after purchasing, I experienced transient jitter effects making the device basically unusable. More than a year after purchasing, Logitech customer service helped me determine it was definitely a hardware problem with the mouse. They sent me a replacement swiftly and I got to keep the broken one too. However, it has been less than a month and the right hand secondary button has failed. I can only speculate that Logitech fulfilled my warranty with a refurbished unit. Take this w/ a grain of salt, as it may just be an unlucky coincidence.

title: Only one (major) con
text:
Pros:
- It's made of sturdy materials (no rubber grips that wear off over time, like those with the M510).
- It has good battery life (430 days left after a month of use).
- As this is a trackball mouse, there is no need for base movement and therefore no need for a mouse pad. It's also great if you have little room on your desk for mouse movement.

Cons:
- The trackball takes a bit of acclimation.
- Cursor movement is simply not as smooth, quick or convenient as with a traditional optical mouse.

There is only one major con, but it's one that turns me away from further use of this mouse. I have a triple monitor setup in my work environment, which makes a trackball unsuitable. The left-right trackball motion is pretty smooth, but it's still relatively slow across three screens. The north-south movement is not at all great, as the distance traveled by the cursor in a single scroll going up/down is much shorter than going left/right.

This product may be a good choice if you intend to use it for a computer with only a single monitor or a laptop, but I haven't had a great experience with it on multi-screen systems. I can't imagine how bad this would perform for multi-screen PC gaming.

title: It has a switcher to go from regular PC gamepad to xbox mode which you will have to play with for each game to see which one wor
text:
For the price this is the wired PC gamepad to get besides one major drawback listed below. It has a switcher to go from regular PC gamepad to xbox mode which you will have to play with for each game to see which one works best. Currently I'm play The Division on the X mode and it works nicely, telling you the correctly labelled buttons in the tutorials hints.

The big failing with this gamepad is the large joystick dead-zones and lack of ability to control them even with the logitech software. You'll find yourself compensating for the large dead-zone by playing in a slopper, "flick the stick a little and hope it goes to the target", style. I can get by but my aim would be much improved if I had control over the dead-zone settings to make the center more sensitive to small adjustments.
