text: Many of the smaller keyboards omit the side numpad to save space but this keyboard is small and manages to squeeze it in. I had read about a delay from other reviewers and figured I'd still give it a shot since I really liked the size and look of it. I'm a gamer as well and delay can mean the end for you if response time between your input and the receiver is too delayed. Now, when typing in a text field there is sometimes delay. It seemed to do this at first but as I type now there is none. In games I do not sense any delay sitting anywhere between 4-7 feet away. (Living room, bedroom, etc.) I don't play many twitch shooters that require insane precision but for something like basic WASD direction movement (for example) there is either little delay or none because I do not detect it. So if you are a casual gamer that's looking for something wireless and small with undetectable delay that you can use for gaming as well (and doesn't look like a spaceship about to take off from your desk) I'd recommend giving it a shot for sure.

title: Great headphones only during the honeymoon stage
text:
Let me start off by saying that these headphones are very nice when they work. They sound good, the wireless range is decent, and the mic is clear. They are moderately comfortable as well.

That's where the good stuff ends...
The headphones were a gift from my brother. They worked well for a few months and then not so much.

First, the battery life was pretty terrible. I came from a corsair headset which I rarely charged. These headphones are basically wired since you have to have them charging so often. I think the lights drain a fair amount of battery and that's why I turn them off. Unfortunately, they love to turn themselves back on for no apparent reason and kill my battery.

Second, The mic would not be very reliable. My voice was clear and crisp when talking to others but the mic would randomly shut off. I would have to turn off the headphones, wait 5 seconds because of the dumb power-off delay, and turn them back on. during the off phase, the mic would pick up my voice and my friends could hear it but I couldn't hear them since the headphones were off. Another thing; the headset has a functionality where it will mute the mic when you lift it up and that worked well. However, when i lower the mic back it would not unmute. The button on the headset to unmute it didn't work either so every time I wanted to unmute my mic, I had to go into the windows settings. Super inconvenient.

Third, the headset was very unreliable. I could be playing a game or watching a movie and it would randomly beep 5 times and turn off. It would refuse to turn back on so I'd have to pull out the battery and put it back in. Other times, it would without warning power down and back up for no reason.

The volume knob has almost no detent so any movement or bump causes a change in volume. When the headphones are "off", bumping them would still change volume on the pc....

Lately logitech has been severely lacking in reliability. I have the harmony home hub, harmony elite remote, the G910 artemis spectrum, and the g933s. Every single one of these has failed on me and needed to be replaced or has major issues that make it impossible to rely on them.

ALTERNATIVES: If you read this far I really recommend not buying these. I have 2 pairs of these and a set of the wired ones. None of them work properly. If you want something really good but twice the price, I recommend either seinheisers or astro a50s. If you want something a bit less expensive but good nonetheless, get some turtlebeaches.

title: An Outstanding Pair of Speakers and a real bang for your buck!
text:
First of all, the look of these speakers is great. It isn't made of wood or wood cabinets like most professional speakers are made of but instead made with plastic (a very durable one too!) The speakers all have a thin, yet strong, grill on them.

The satellite speakers were easy to set up, my only problem is that the right front speaker kept falling over because of the way the cable was packaged (folded, so, the speaker fell in the direction of the cord) I would have to say that setting up these speakers took less time then it did to unpackage them. To unpack these speakers and set them up takes a good 20-35 minutes.

The sound quality was actually quite astonishing. I made a recording in a room with a little bit of echo and if you are close enough to the speakers, you can hear the echo, kinda like you would hear it if you were wearing headphones. Basically said, it gets small auditory details very well. The balanced bass is amazing for songs and is great for when you are listening to audio with people talking because they sound more lifelike. When you are listening to something cinematic, the subwoofer works really well to make the movie feel more immersive. I do not recommend these speakers to bass-heads as the subwoofer is a bit small and if you really want bass then try something with a 10-inch subfoofer. I also would like to make note that nobody should need to go past more than about around 3/4 on the bass dial. After that, the bass can get muddy, less clear, and dominate the other sounds in the audio. So, be careful with your bass.

To conclude, these are honestly some really great, cheap speakers. If you are looking for something a little better then your average stereo speakers, then these are for you. They have more clarity, and are quite immersive if you set them up well.

title: Won't stop scrolling even when NOT SCROLLING.  Horrible design, Logitech.
text:
While the keyboard is good, the mouse is absolutely terrible. The mouse wheel on this device is about as sensitive as a seismograph. If you just rest your finger on it, which is quite normal for me, or bounce it on the pad too hard, it just starts scrolling. Yes, the mouse wheel "clicks" when you scroll it, and that is my point. It scrolls even when you haven't progressed it to the next click. You can change the sensitivity of the mouse pointer, but not the scroll sensitivity. This is only my second day at work with this mouse, but it has become extremely annoying. I am having to relearn how to use a mouse because of this mouse (keeping my finger AWAY from the scroll wheel at all times). Bad design, Logitech. Very bad. I will most likely be returning this item

UPDATE 06-13-16: After using this mouse for another week, I have decided to return it. I spoke with Logitech who told me that from what I was describing, it is likely a defective mouse. Amazon accepted my return request. I chose to replace with the exact same item. I should receive it on 06-15-16 and will update again after I find out if this was a fluke or if this mouse is, by design, as bad as it is.

UPDATE 06-15-16: Returned the original mouse and keyboard. Amazon did a great job on its return policy and execution. Received the new mouse and keyboard today. Same thing. The mouse wheel is EXTREMELY sensitive. If you do not completely remove your finger from the mouse wheel while you are working, your screen will just bounce up and down repeatedly. It has caused my eyes to hurt with a slight headache to boot. Kind of like trying to track a fly buzzing around in the air. Needless to say, I'm going to return this item for a full refund. I guess I never noticed it before, but I normally rest my "scroll" or index finger on the mouse wheel while I'm browsing or working on a document. Again, I am not going to relearn how to use a mouse because of a bad design. Don't get me wrong, I own a LOT of Logitech products and this is the first I can honestly say is a HORRIBLE DESIGN. They should have done better. Don't buy this product. Make them improve their standards of design. By the way, I've decreased this to ONE star. Hope this helps someone.

title: Setup is a nightmare, serious bugs and flaws, but still useful
text:
I'm torn on this one. Once everything is set up, it is really nice to have one button to turn everything on and off. However, that's the ONLY thing I use it for. The remote's interface is so awkward and slow that I still use the original remotes for everything to navigate menus, change, volume, etc.

Setup is a nightmare and very inflexible. Be prepared to wait 15 seconds for it to sync with the hub every step of the way, every time you change any single setting. And then on top of that, it checks repeatedly for firmware updates throughout the setup process. Everything is painfully slow.

You also can't change the ordering of some things. For instance, turning your lights on has to be the last step. I have to wait for it to turn on my receiver, TV, and Roku, and then about 5 seconds later it finally turns on my lights.

Sonos and Hue integration are both very buggy and limited. You can only control ONE room of Sonos, and it sometimes fails to start playing music. For Hue, sometimes it only turns on some of the lights it's supposed to and I have to either use another control device to fix it or restart everything. You can't use any pre-created groupings or scenes for Hue; you basically have to set up each bulb manually for every "activity."

This thing has a lot of potential if they'd just improve the software on it. Meanwhile, unfortunately I just don't know of a good alternative, and I guess it's useful enough not to return it.

title: Smooth, precise movement and very comfortable
text:
I did a lot of research before selecting this mouse, and it paid off.

My last few mice had super annoying jitter issues (where the mouse pointer bounces around a few pixels in random directions even when you try to make slow/precise movements.) It turns out that's a common issue for laser mice. The Logitech G502, however, is an optical mouse with one of the best sensors out there. Now I'm finally getting smooth and precise control.

The button placement isn't ideal, as it's very easy to accidentally press the two buttons immediately to the left of the left mouse button. Luckily, it's easy to remap what each button does so I just made those two side buttons also act as a left click. The only button you can't remap is the one that toggles the mouse week from free-scrolling to click-to-click, because that one physically interacts with the mechanism that changes how the wheel spins. I think it's actually nicer having it physically interact like that instead of depending on software to do it electronically.

This is also one of the most comfortable mice I've used, and has a great grippy material that doesn't feel like it will wear down anytime soon.

It looks every bit as sleek as you'd expect from the photos. I'd prefer if the RGB lighting showed up in one or two more places, but there's something to be said for keeping it minimal too.

Really, this checks all the boxes I care about: precise control, comfortable, and good-looking.

Full disclosure: I work for Microsoft, which technically makes competing products, but my opinions expressed here are solely my own and neither represent Microsoft's views nor are deliberately influenced by my employment.

title: Solution for a problem that nobody else in the market is really serving .....
text:
We purchased several of these at my workplace, specifically for use with a 3rd. party videoconferencing solution called "Zoom". Not only does Zoom make clients for Mac, Windows and mobile phones -- but they have a conference room specific solution called "Zoom Rooms" that lets you use an iPad as the controller for a system that runs on an Apple Mac Mini. It's designed specifically for the Logitech CC3000e as the camera it uses.

Since we don't use this camera with Skype or anything else, I'm writing this review based on how well it works with the Zoom product.

After using these for at least a year or so, now? I'd have to say they've held up pretty well. I had some initial concerns that the motorized camera assembly might wear out or seize up, but that hasn't happened yet with any of our cameras. We did have one camera where the proprietary DIN cable going from the camera to the hub seemed to have a broken wire in it. The camera would only work if you bent the cord just the right way behind where it plugged into the camera base. Annoying, but we were able to get a replacement cable for it.

The only other issue I've run into is that recently, one of our cameras seems to prevent the Mac Mini from booting once in a while. (Appears to happen most often right after a software update is done and the system is restarted, but not sure that's always the case.) The only way to get it all working again is to unplug the AC adapter from the hub piece for a few seconds and plug it back in. I'm starting to suspect that the AC adapter might be going bad and not outputting the required amount of power anymore, but will have to buy a spare one to test that theory.

Overall though, I haven't been able to find an integrated speakerphone/camera solution that's anything like this one. (They exist when you start looking at what's out there for 3-4x the price, but then you're getting into dedicated systems that don't just plug into USB ports on computers and work with any PC or Mac software.) There are little things that could be better about the CC3000e, but with no real competition -- what can you say?

I think many people would like longer cables as at least an option. (Logitech sells an "extender kit" now but it's costly and runs everything over CAT5e or CAT6 ethernet. That extra complexity can create some new problems of its own, depending on how you have everything set up in a given conference room.) And although the metal L shaped bracket is clever, in that it works as either a stand or a wall mounting bracket for the camera? When used as a wall mounting bracket, it's a little on the flimsy side. It has a tendency to allow the camera to "bounce" up and down a bit because the metal is a bit "springy". It's not a big deal but if you're a perfectionist, you'll get better results with an aftermarket dedicated camera mount.

The Zoom conferencing software does have the ability to zoom/pan the camera, and adjust the speakerphone volume right from the iPad controller, so you don't need to rely on the included remote control for any of that. (Nice because the included remote is just a cheap infrared type that needs line of sight to the camera rig to control it.)

title: Can you turn your Ipad Air 2 into a device almost as good as an iPad Pro? I think you can with the Logitech Blok case.
text:
[[VIDEOID:68e7bd0e3ae79cff54e4e318e83a4603]] Here is what I like about the Logitech Blok case.

The case uses kickstand to prop up your ipad air 2, instead of having the folio wrap around prop up your Ipad which is very similar to the ipad pro and surface pro. [insert video of those two here.] Why do I like that more? Because you don’t have to fiddle around with your case before having your laptop propped up. You simply just pull out the kickstand. One simple easy step.

The keyboard is attachable and detachable via a row of magnets on one side of the case so you can use it in the pure tablet form without having any annoying keyboard case attached to the back just like the ipad Pro and Surface pro. The Keyboard also acts as a cover for when you just want to toss your ipad in your bag.

I could also easily argue that the keyboard on the logitech blok case is actually better than the keyboard that you get with the ipad pro 9.7 model because this keyboard actually includes a set of function keys that allow you to perform universal search to open apps, talk to siri, volume controls, pause and play media, and even lock your device, something apple has left out of the ipad pro keyboard case inexplicably.

Here is what I don’t like:

The case is insanely hard to put on and remove from the ipad. Like scary hard. Everytime I try and take the ipad out of the case I am genuinely afraid that I am going to flext my ipad so hard that it will crack the screen. So you defenitly won’t be removing your ipad from it’s case often if you use this case.

The case is a little bit more bulky than I would like. You are going to lose all of the finesse and thinness of the ipad if you use this case. The trade off is that you get some excellent functionality and protection. If that is worth it to you, than I don’t think you will mind the extra heft, however, if the weight and feel of the ipad is more important than typing functionality and protection, you might want to look for a slimmer case.

I wish the case was a bit more studier. I have used this case everyday for about 3 months and it kind of looks like that. You can already see a little knick in the kick stand.

Conclusion:

I love this case and keyboard combo. The real test with this, and pretty much any keyboard - case combo is will you actually use it in real life or just go back to a laptop. I can say in my actual daily experience I vastly prefer using the iPad air 2 with the blok case more than lugging around even an macbook air. The ipad air 2 with the logitech blok case gives you a lot of the functionality of an 9.7 ipad pro without the hefy price tag.

The entry level 32GB 9.7 inch ipad pro with the apple keyboard case will run you around 700 dollars, this setup (which is an 64GB ipad air two with the logitech blok case cost me right about $500). Safe to say I think it is a good alternative for consumers who want a lightweight computer setup without wanting to shell out the hefy price tag that comes with the ipad pro or surface pro.

title: Great keyboard for those that hardly use their keyboard and mouse and don't expect perfect accuracy
text:
Here is the thing -

The first year I have had this keyboard and mouse combo, I have had no problems. It was a brilliant piece of hardware that worked very well.

The last two-three months...not so much. It started innocently enough where it wouldn't pick up inputs. Mouse and keyboard both would just kind of eat inputs. A couple keys here, a couple keys there, a mouse button down let go of early. So, I would be trying to move a file from a folder to another, and it would stop halfway through and drop the file. Most of these I chalked up to my CPU at near 100% during rendering or just a small thing that can happen. But in the last month it has gotten horrible. I have been running tests as best as I possibly can to see what it could be. Are any of my other wiseless devices interfering with the signal (plenty of wireless gaming controllers, wireless headsets, 2.4/5ghz networks running, etc)? So, I went through systematically unplugging all that I could nearest the device, then slowly arcing outward. No luck. Inputs were getting eaten by the dozen. I changed batteries. It's only been a year and it's foretold that this keyboard will last me three years on the same batteries that come with the device! Well, I do use my computer all day (work from home), and many of my nighttime activities include the keyboard and mouse (gaming, communication, etc). Well, I also never turn off the keyboard or mouse, and maybe you are supposed to to get the maximum time out of it. The battery indicator on both mouse and keyboard never went down and stated full battery, but maybe they are on a date/time situation where every day it registers it's on it counts down. So I switched batteries to brand new Duracells. No better. Energizer? No better. Eneloop? No better.

So, I am still in search for what can make this amazing keyboard tick like it used to when I first bought it.

Minor note, yes the keys do where off quickly. In the first three months "S" and "L" were pretty much gone (lots of ctrl+s took care of that very quickly, and I only assume my fingers finding home row cut the L out quickly). E, C, V, N, and A were the next victims. This doesn't bother me at all, truthfully, but for others that might need the visual aide while typing, this could be a hindrance.

All I wish is that it worked liked it did for the first year again. Simple movements like clicking and dragging, whether it be an audio slider, folders/files, or trying to select a group of things, has become a nightmare. And don't get me started on how many times I have overwritten files on an FTP server accidentally because it drops them in other folders and I have no way of undoing the damage on the remote site.

title: Used To Love it.  Can no longer recommended it.
text:
UPDATE - 8/15/2017: I reduced my stars from 5 to 2. I've used this product for many years and have loved it. Recently, my old headset was having issues, so I ponied up the $40 and bought a new one. It looks the same, but it does not act the same. The old model would connect to my Skype calls in 5 seconds. This new model does not. It takes upwards of 60 seconds to connect to my call. Half the time, I have to unplug the USB dongle and reinsert it just to get my machine to recognize the headset. This makes impromptu calls painful.

I have tried uninstalling the drivers and reinstalling them - no luck. I set the headset back for a new one, thinking I got a dud, but the new one does the same thing. It's unfortunate, because for $40, this was a great buy. Now I will have to research Jabra or Plantronics and spend more than I want because this product is no longer an option for me.

ORIGINAL:
It's not often that I get to recommend a headset, but this one is quite solid. I bought this in May 2013 and it's still going strong.

I work from home and I'm on a LOT of Skype calls daily. I love the wireless capability of it. The sound is pretty good. It allows me to wander around my office without loss of sound. I can go to various rooms and maintain audio quality. I have noticed that if there are more than 2 walls between me and the unit, that it starts to get staticy. I can move to about 80-90% of my house without issue.

I use the headset daily for about 4 hours a day. I've gotten into the habit of turning off the unit when a call is done. This helps the battery stay charged. I have to charge the unit about twice a week. I've never had an issue where it wont charge after the battery fully drains. It works like an iPhone in that once the battery is fully drained, it has to charge a few minutes before it can be useable again. In this case, I have to charge it while I use it. I bought a 6 ft mini USB cable for this purpose.

The only con I can see is the time it takes for my computer to recognize the headset when I turn it on. As I said earlier, I turn it off in between meetings. But if someone skype calls me, i have to turn on the headset and wait about 5 seconds before the computer and headset talk to each other. It's a minor problem in my book, but might be a deal breaker for you. I'm sure there are other wireless headsets out there that dont have this initial lag, but for $44, I can handle a little initial lag.

title: Decent Wireless Mouse
text:
Update (6-15-2018):
This mouse (and the keyboard I got with it) is still going strong! Right now it lists the batteries for the mouse as "fair" and states there are 706 days / 65% remaining. While I don't know if that is accurate, it's important to note that this review was posted 1-27-2016, 2 years and 4.5 months ago. To the best of my knowledge, I've never changed the batteries. The 3 year battery claim is very real -- even if the batteries died tomorrow I really coouldn't complain.

I have one for home as well and have used it successfully for gaming, including playing most of Fallout 4 with it. I'm not a championship gamer by ANY stretch but for me there was no noticeable input delay. I've experienced mice FAR worse than this one in terms of delay (early wireless model my friend had).

As for the "sensor being off to one side" issue, I really don't notice that anymore and kinda forgot about it. I think I used to sort of pivot with my right ring finger subconsciously when making fine movements, but I apparently learned not to do this since I didn't even remember that issue until I reread this.

We have several Logitech unifying keyboards at work which we use with tablets, and the unifying hardware and software are pretty flawless even with 10+ floating around.

Original (1-27-2016)
I got this for work in a set with the K350 to replace the crappy mouse my company gave me. I have used decent mice before (various Razer models, currently the Imperator).

It tracks pretty well and is great for the office environment. I wouldn't go up against a proper wired gaming mouse, though. I feel it isn't quite as responsive or as accurate, but honestly there is no blatant delay either. I'd almost like to try gaming with it just to see how it fares.

One thing I didn't initially like is that the sensor is off to the side instead of in the middle. This causes certain fine movements to be lost (as I apparently pivot the mouse slightly in these situations rather than move it straight). However, I've gotten used to it over the last week and I would no longer call it an issue.

I've paired this with the same SteelSeries mousepad I use at home. This actually makes a difference: most people are so used to not bothering with a mousepad since optical sensors came out that they don't realize the advantage of a decent smooth tracking surface.

title: Solid Keyboard
text:
I got this to replace my 2007 model cheap OEM keyboard at work. It came in a set with the M705 Marathon Mouse. I figure, I spend all day typing as a programmer, might as well type on something decent. This fills the bill.

So far, I am really liking it. I have mostly used cheap OEM or laptop keyboards. This is far superior.

The action of the keys is significantly better than most I have used. The do not wiggle, they have a positive tactile feel, and they do not have the squishy feel near the bottom that some cheap OEM keyboards have. (Early 2000s Dells were particularly bad for that last one, no idea if they are better). Its smooth travel all the way down, even if off center (which is where the "squishyness" is the worst), even on the larger keys/spacebar. On top of all this, its quieter than most, even with my sometimes heavy hand.

The ergonomic layout is different for me, but I am getting used to it. It's not too extreme. There are several additional keys for volume, zoom, etc. This is nice and I've not had this before. I especially like the zoom.

It is obviously wireless, and uses 2 (included) AA batteries. I'm honestly fine with a wire, especially for a keyboard. But with the stated 3 year battery life, I don't see a problem embracing it. It actually is nice to eliminate the wire for this and the mouse in my 5S-centric office. I don't know if the batteries will last this long, but it should be way better than a few days or weeks like older models.

The one thing I really don't like is the fact that the F-keys and the insert/home/delete/etc cluster have a non-standard layout. Had I noticed this, I may not have gotten this. The f-keys are 4 groups of 3 instead of 3 groups of 4. And the aforementioned cluster is a different layout. I guess I'll get used to it.

I know that mechanical keyboards are all the rage with the kids these days (this is not mechanical). I see the mechanicals being far superior to cheap OEM keyboards, however, the superiority to this is much less clear. Frankly, when I tried this in the store, I preferred this one. The keys on the mechanicals either have no tactile response (MX black/red) which I hated, too little (MX Brown), which I also didn't like, or OK but super loud (MX blue).

text:
Got the mouse delivered to my office today around 10am. Set it up quickly, programed the buttons, and proceeded to start figuring this thing out. By 4:00 I noticed that the ratchet on the scroll wheel seemed to be getting weaker. By 4:30 the scroll wheel stopped ratcheting completely.

I am very disappointed. I use CAD all day long and need the detent to keep the zoom from creeping. I have to go back to old M705 after barely 7 hours of use on the new mouse.

Seriously bummed with an otherwise lovely mouse.

UPDATE 3/2/2016

Got a replacement shipped last week. Love Amazon Prime for that. The one has worked well for the last 4 days. Still going to give it some time before I change my review. Hope to get YEARS of use out of the mouse, not days/weeks/months.

Wow, update later the same day, I must have jinxed myself. 4 hours after the above was posted the scroll wheel has lost all ratcheting again. How many times should I send this thing back before I try another brand?

Very Dissapointed.

Update 8/10/2016

3rd time seems to be the charm for me. I've been using this mouse 5 days a week, 8-10 hours a day since I got my 3rd replacement on 3/4/2016. Amazon returns and replacements were fast and painless. Thank you Prime!

It has been working well, with no fade in the scroll wheel ratchet. I have been getting exactly 2 weeks per charge, I never turn the mouse off. Wish it had better battery life like the marathon mouse, which goes for almost a year on 2 AA batteries. But, charging every 2 weeks really isn't a problem since the mouse still functions while charging.

I think I'll raise my rating a star, as it really is a great mouse, too bad about the defective scroll wheel that seems to plague this unit.

title: Not just for gaming!
text:
I don’t game at all - I bought this mouse to use for my everyday computing because I was looking for an ergonomic wireless mouse. I am quite pleased with this one.

***Pros***
- Battery life is great, and I can continue using the mouse while it’s charging. With my previous wireless mouse, I had to place it on a charging cradle and use something else until it was done charging.
- I like the option to toggle between two different scrolling modes (the “loose/fast” scroll and the precision “clicking” scroll)
- The shape, look, and feel of this mouse is great

***Cons***
- From time to time, the cursor will skip or be less responsive than usual. I believe that this may be related to the USB port on my PC being underpowered, but it’s worth mentioning because wireless mice can encounter issues like this whereas wired mice will never have this problem.

title: A great way to take your automated home to the next level!
text:
I bought this home controller for two main reasons:

- I wanted a good universal remote so I could avoid leaving 4 different remotes on my coffee table and confusing my girlfriend/guests
- I wanted to take advantage of the IFTTT integration to enable control of my AV equipment from my Amazon Echo.

***Tips***
- Experiment with the positioning of the IR blaster and hub itself. In my case, I had to complete lots of testing and move both of them around until I figured out the ideal position to reliably communicate with my devices.

***Pros***
- The home controller hub lets you use the remote to control Philips Hue bulbs and other popular home automation devices
- Lots of spare buttons that you can assign to your favorite AV or home automation tasks. For example, I have a “TV watching” button that I use when I’d like to watch something. It’s very handy to have a single button that will turn on the TV, sound bar, Amazon Fire TV, change the TV input to the Fire TV, and turn off most of the lights in the living room.
- Unlike some fancy universal remotes from Logitech, this remote has no LCD display. I view this as a positive thing because it doen’t chew through batteries the way those other remotes do.
- The setup process was a breeze! You can use a PC to choose your devices from a catalog and set up actions/scenes. The mobile app can also be used if you’d rather sit in your living room to try things out as you complete the setup process.

***Cons***
- The remote introduces pretty lengthy delays between individual steps. For example, it takes about 15 seconds for my “TV watching” task to finish.
- The battery is a coin cell, so it won’t be as easy to find as a AA or AAA. This isn’t a huge deal though - you can easily buy replacements on Digi-Key.

Purchase these keyboard as a replacement to my aging K400 keyboard used in my home theater pc. The only issue with my K400 was that the 7 key was not working anymore and that it had no backlight for night use making it difficult when you wanted to quickly write or use a key at night.

Pros
- The K830 fixes almost all of the issues I had with my late K400 and the main one was backlighting. It is auto adjustable based on the room light which is good and you can further change the level with a key.
- The placement of the volume and other special key buttons has better placement than other keyboards so you avoid accidentally doing something you don't want
- It has a good build quality, no cheap plastic feel here.

Cons
- The keyboard is a bit heavier because of the built quality so be mindful as usually on the couch or bed you can easily send it flying to the floor.
- Just after a few minutes of us you will notice the spots left by fingers, not fingerprints but oil from clean hands will be quite noticeable and if you are like me you will be constantly wiping it all the time.
- The still have not fix a way to properly light the function keys, so when the backlight turns on and the room is dark you will not be able to tell where is F4, F5 and so on.
- Battery compared to something like a K400 runs out faster with backlighting so there is that tradeoff as my K400 lasted months on two Panasonic eneloop batteries.
- Charges using micro USB not type C

At momento of purchase was happy with the keyboard and the only gripe is that Amazon lowered the price two days after I bought it for about $10 and overpaid for it.

LONG TERM USE UPDATE:
Same as all other long term users charging port broke off, being careful it lasted about 2 years. I have resoldered it and luckily it can charge again after having it in a box for a long time. Stay away from this keyboard if you can. The should have not cut corners on the charging port.

title: Tilting the M570 to prevent wrist stress for carpel tunnel relief / prevention.
text:
Just put my 5th M570 into use and ordered two more. They last about 2 years unless you eat fried chicken at the computer - real ball killer.
This last M570 is the only one that did not die due to greasy ball syndrome- it is difficult to clean if the grease has been there long, the plastic softens making the ball grabby on the suspension points. At a little over 2 years, the left click key started double clicking. I have bought new balls in the past, but the whole M570 is so inexpensive now that I don't bother when soap and water doesn't fix it.
Dealing with carpel tunnel and popping ibuprophen like popcorn until retirement, my modified M570 allowed me to avoid the surgery.
Back when the old mouse's had a ball they were finicky and I was ending up with a "death grip" on it to get it to work. Your wrist was always an odd angle and flexing under load when moving the mouse.
The M570 fixed the "death grip" issue and the pictured 30 degree mounting wedge fixes the odd wrist angle issue by bringing the wrist back to neutral. This block of wood has been in use for about 15 years and 5 M570's.
Attached with foam core double stick tape the opening in the the block allows access to the switch and battery. The 4 feet on the bottom are globs of silicone (bathroom) caulk applied and then the block is set on wax paper, spaced up by sucker sticks and let dry to form the feet.
The page up and down buttons on the track ball are real handy surfing. I realized this when I had to use a mouse again, drag the arrow up and point/click the arrows at the page top was a real inconvenience.

title: Has been perfect for almost 9 years
text:
Just though I'd report that this K520 combo that came with my old HP m8120n desktop which I bought in July, 2007 and has been in almost daily use, has been working perfectly since day one. No lag like I saw in some negative reviews. Maybe that is related to placement of the receiver? No letter markings wearing off the keys. Maybe those users inadvertently got some acidic substance on those keys? Or maybe Logitech has cheapened the quality of this combo since 2007, I don't know.

One keyboard maintenance trick I've adhered to is occasional cleaning by tapping. I.e., I turn it over with the base resting on the desk and the top held in one hand at a 30 - 45 degree angle, and with the other hand, tap multiple times all over on the back of the keyboard, which reveals an astonishing amount of little specks of detritus.

The mouse's minimal battery consumption has always surprised me. No turning it off and on, it just works, and needs battery changing maybe once a year or less. That was amazing tech for 2007.

title: this inexpensively priced keyboard works just fine
text:
For my purposes, this inexpensively priced keyboard works just fine. It is so much better than the keyboard that came from the computer store with my desktop PC. It has a very good feel to it. The keys have a kind of "rubbery" feel, the proper amount of resistance when you strike them. The layout is great. I like that you can plug it in to a USB slot. The keys are not especially big, but they are big enough.

If there is a drawback, I would say that, ideally, the keys could be larger.

I have had a lot of trouble getting the right keyboard and mouse. Several more expensive keyboards I have tried were a lot worse. They were supposedly great from an ergonomic point of view, but I found them very hard to type on -- configured so that it was hard to reach the keys. This inexpensive keyboard works well, which is not to say that are not better ones out there -- I'm sure there are.

Supposedly, the keyboard has a "spill resistant" design. Not true; at least, doesn't apply. Be extra careful not to spill anything on the keys. The slightest bit of liquid spilled on the keyboard will jam the keys and it will become unworkable. Trying to clean up underneath will not help.

title: Lots of Bulk for Little Extra Function
text:
I have had my eye on one of these cases for quite a while, and once they went on sale, I picked one up.

First, the good. The case itself is very well made. If you are looking for drop protection, this thing is a real tank. I can see this as providing some serious help in case of a drop or fall. The case fits very snugly on the iPad - in fact I had a heck of a time getting it in there, and I hate to think what it's going to take to get it out. The keyboard is very good, a little "clicky" with plenty of play, just how I like it. Logi has proven to me that they know how to make a fine keyboard for a mobile device, and this is no exception. Nice to have the upper row of function and shortcut keys, as well.

The bad. Wow, this thing seriously turns your svelte little iPad into a brick. It is very bulky, and the keyboard adds even more. The little flip-out stand on the back adds an additional layer of bulk to the thing, as well. The keyboard itself is wobbly on the lap, and the kickstand doesn't do much to help. Hard to get that kickstand into a good position on your lap, for sure. No backlight on the keyboard, either; seems like an unusual choice for a keyboard that retailed on launch for well north of $100. It's nice to be able to pull the iPad off the keyboard, but the connection remains - so your keyboard still is connected even when your iPad isn't. I always hated this about BT keyboards, and I had hoped they had changed this, but I guess not.

I always loved the functionality of the Surface Pro devices, and hoped this would be a good alternative for using my iPad, but it really isn't. Too much bulk and not enough added functionality for what you get. Any number of cheap Bluetooth cases can do this same thing, many of them better. Glad I kept the box, it's going back tomorrow.

text:
What makes this keyboard such a great device?

- It's solid. Even though it's made of plastic, you can pop it into your bag or backpack and not have to worry about the keys coming off.
- It has a sleek look to it.
- It's compact. It really fits nicely into a man bag or purse and it doesn't take up much room.
- It is easy to type on. I've found that the keys (which are round) are very easy to hit and they have a slight indentation that helps your fingers get centred.
- The battery life is said to be two years. That's pretty exceptional for something you might use on a frequent basis.
- You can operate up to three different bluetooth devices with it. This might not sound like much, but it makes a prefect external keyboard for my iphone and my laptop. You can switch between them at the touch of a button. It means one less keyboard to lug around during travel. And yes, it works nicely for the laptop.
- It's really easy to pair. Just hold down the blue function key for a few seconds.
- The power button is in a easy to get to place (on the side)
- It has a natural slant so the keys are not flat. This helps with typing.

Cons
- it can take a few seconds to connect to your device, especially when changing from one to the other.
- It is a little weighty, but not enough to notice when being carried in a bag.

This one cost a little more than the cheaper brands, but I would say it's worth it. The fact that it is so solidly constructed is worth the extra money.

text: It's a great idea to combine Bluetooth/WiFi and IR, it's a really bad idea to take the IR emitters off the hand held controller! There are only two ways this product can work.  First, if you don't have your components in a cabinet, you're all set.  Second, if you don't mind having the control unit (with its power cable) and its IR emitter sitting in front of you on a table, you might be all set.  Otherwise, stick with a basic IR unit.  Also, the basic models have a nice screen with your favorite TV stations, the Home Control does not, even with the smartphone app.  I have to admit the original setup was slick, I was able to copy the configuration of an older device to this device but it was all downhill from there.  I was able to get this unit to work after an hour of fiddling with placing the components and moving my gear but only if the door to the cabinet was open!  I am going to keep this device but I'm waiting for a second IR emitter so I can turn the TV set on and off.

For instance, without using it playing Spotify on bluetooth sounded great. When using it and playing Spotify over bluetooth it sounded like AM/FM radio quality, and added static.

title: Good mouse, great accuracy and feel, wheel spins weird
text: This mouse is decent for gaming. I have large hands and still can't reach all the buttons without shifting my grip on the mouse.  When gaming FPS online, speed is king and moving your grip around is a killer.  The primary gripe I have with this mouse is the wheel button. There are two modes for spinning: free spin and restricted.  Free sping is just that. The wheel spins with no resistance other than the bearing/bushing on which it spins and that things can sping for a few seconds depending on how fast you spin it.  In games (or even applications) where you need accurate wheel spin, this can be a detriment.  The solution, you would think, would be to have some kind of resistance.  In regular PC mouses, the wheels have a notchy feel to them to prevent free spin.  This Logitech accomplishes this with a push button that when activated, you get that same notchy action. However, the momentary intermittent resistance is a bit strong, especially considering the mouse surface is metal and hard to get a good grip on when your finger is a bit sweaty.  A bit less resistance (or tunable) and a rubber surface on the wheel would get the 3-star to a 5-star rating.

title: 5 Stars, but with an asterisk for us not-very-tech-savvy Mac users
text: Okay. First, this webcam does all that they say it does. Buy it!  That being said, however, if you're a not-very-techie 70-something like I am, you might discover that it doesn't work when you first plug it into your Mac. And then, when you go to the Logitech website, you find downloads for Windows software to run the thing, but nothing for Mac. And then when you read the product literature, you find that it does actually sort of say that it'll work with a Mac, but when you call the Logitech number for Support, you speak with some guy in God-knows-where who tells you that, sadly, the Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920 isn't wired to work with a Mac, so, sorry to say, you shouldn't have bought this one. So then you're faced with returning the camera to Amazon and resuming the search for a suitable webcam. Until, that is, you discover the YouTube video by the guy who says that you actually need only to go to the app for which you bought the webcam in the first place -- Skype, in my case -- go to Preferences, click on Audio/Video, and select the HD Pro C920, which will appear in the drop-down menu. I tried it and, sure enough, it works. Good thing I stuck with it for a few days and didn't immediately ship the webcam back. NOW the furshlugginer thing is worth 5 Stars.

title: Excellent value (at $15)
text:
It works as well as any other game pad, and, after around 200 hours of use and a dozen or so minor drops on the ground, it has retained all functionality. The only complaint I have is that a strange rubber band sound started occurring in the right analogue stick after about 20-30 hours of use, but that could be from it sliding off my lap during some loading screen -- it is only mildly annoying, and only noticeable when not wearing headphones or with the volume abnormally low. It is probably a combination of wear on the parts and the humidity of the south US.

I personally really like the 8-way D-pad design -- it is far superior and easier to use than the Play Station design. It is a little difficult to hold a finger on both the bumper and the trigger simultaneously, but it is feasible, and that is almost always unnecessary -- the trigger is sensitive enough and the bumper close enough to the trigger that I can rest my index finger in the groove between them and hit either with minimal vertical movement. The only time this becomes an issue is with some fighting/button-mashing games, but it is otherwise very ergonomic and comfortable to use for extended gaming sessions. The lack of vibration is in my opinion more of a feature rather than an omission -- vibration servos increase weight and are generally very annoying: the vast majority of gamers I have met disable them as soon as they find the relevant setting.

If I ever decide that I want to play local coop on my computer or need a replacement, I'll probably get another one of these. Until then, I am satisfied with the one I already have.

title: Love this remote
text:
Love this remote!! Let's just say it passes the wife test

Don't look at this remote as being too expensive, because this is worth its weight in gold. There are plenty of comprehensive reviews out there explaining what this does, and what this does well. I will just explain how I am using it, and why I love it.

I just renovated my basement - I built a medium sized room (roughly 14 feet by 12 feet), with a large closet off to the side 7 feet by 7 feet, square (you can never have too large of a closet). In this closet is where I wanted to store all my TV components, thus removing the need for a TV stand/entertainment center.

I was worried that this setup would not work with my TV being in the main room, and everything else in the closet. It turns out everything worked exactly as advertised!

What I was able to do was place the hub in my closet, on top of all my components. Thankfully due to my closet being square, it seems the hub has no issue bouncing the signal all around it, and it reaches all of my components (Xbox One, A/V receiver, Tivo mini) without issue. I had to connect the included IR blaster to a 2,5mm extension cable (I used a 12 foot cable) in order to get the mini blaster out into my main room.

I ended up placing this blaster on top of my center speaker, which was the perfect placement to get my TV to turn on and off from. I am including an image so you can see my setup (don't judge the fact I used a normal piece of wood for my center speaker, I am going to paint it later :) )

On the whole, it has worked flawlessly once I set it up.

It was somewhat difficult to set up, but I attribute that to just how different all the components work. It took some trial and error, but once you get the devices set up correctly, it works like a charm.

The remote itself is very light weight, but it feels very solid at the same time. The buttons are very "clicky" which is very nice to use. The fact that you can point this remote in any direction is a huge plus, and the interface with Android/iOS devices is just the icing on the cake

I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to simplify their TV viewing experience!

title: Much better than the performance mouse MX, found some glitches, -see bullet points below
text:
Now updated with glitches after a month of heavy use! See bottom of list. [Other notes have been added [in brackets]]

I had the performance mouse MX but of the 2 I bought, 1 had a mis-weighted and rather loose scroll wheel. The screen would jump up and down, and sometimes I couldn't get the page to stay where I wanted it! (if the heavy side of the wheel was on top where I wanted to be, it would just roll down causing the page to drift up or down a whole page-length!) I really didn't like using the ratchet to solve this problem. I scroll through long documents/pdf's throughout the day and it's a constant switch back and forth. I though the auto-switch on this mouse would be nice. But I don't think I'll need it because it doesn't have any drifting problems (although it's not perfectly weighted [I can hear it when it spins] it's much closer, and close enough - it has a tighter connection on it's bearing to make up for mis-weighted wheels).
Here's a bullet point list of the pro's and con's of this MX master vs the performance mouse MX (mainly pros). It's broken into categories:

Scroll wheel!
Doesn’t ‘drift’ on the master!
Moves only if you really shake the mouse.
Wheel seems tighter.
It’s ratchet will auto-turn off if you spin is fast enough. (Main reason I bought it, but since it doesn’t drift in the smooth mode, I won’t be using ratchet mode ever)
Ratchet is a bit hard, probably won’t need it anymore though [I turn it on in excel maybe once a month]
Forward/back
Forward is hard to push -they really could have been bigger. [I don’t use it much]
Back is easy to push, which will be used more.
Doesn’t feel as mushy, it makes a more satisfying click
Laser is centered on the ‘mx master mouse’. On the ‘performance mouse mx’ it’s actually under the thumb, and it’s noticeable if you manipulate the mouse finely by rotating it.
Ergonomics
The forward/back button arrangement is farther back on the mouse, easier to reach [Almost too far back, i use the crease of my thumb to push back, but I cannot get to forward like that]
This let’s me use the mouse with my fingertips, which is much better to manipulate, and means I can move my wrist less so I don’t have to drag my wrist around (even on a mouse pad it’s not great)
The Scroll wheel is not farther back though, so I find myself having to readjust to reach it. [I have slowly started holding this moue farther up, and it’s quite comfortable, everything fits nice - it just took time coming from tiny $5 mice]
Place to put thumb is larger, more comfortable
Charging/battery
The charging cable is shorter, 4’ instead of 5’
Cable is a plain micro-usb. On the ‘performance mouse mx’, it had a nice tall grip making it obvious which way is up and easy to plug and unplug.
Battery should last longer [It does! I charge about once a week, because I use it 10+ hours a day 5 days a week]
Li-Po instead of NI-MH (great!)
Battery won’t be as easy to replace, but contrary to reviews, there’s instructions on how to remove the battery to dispose it properly. So I don’t see why it’s not replaceable.
Software
No pointer acceleration? Would be handy when I hook up a second screen. [I’m used to it now]
Requires another program from logitech to control settings
The speed in the program is separate from the system speed. Normally turning up the speed in logitech turns up the speed in the system. I turned it up in the program and it was incredibly slow. I had to them turn up the system’s speed. Weird, odd, no biggie. [I had to uninstall the old logitech mouse. Setpoint will reset the system setting to slow to that setpoint can control it properly. But the MX Master doesn’t use setpoint to control the speed, and relies on the system setting to get a speed boost -this might be an issue if you plan to have 2 logitech mice on the same computer]
After some time with it, most of the positives remain, but I have found some glitches and easy, but not-permanent remedies.
Scrolling will randomly lag, especially on webpages, so I suspect it’s the logitech smooth scrolling extension
The extension itself cuts out randomly (I have a few profiles on my computer, and certain profiles seem to cut out more). If I click the hamburger menu, and then click the logitech symbol, it takes me to the extension page in the chrome extension store. After closing that tab, it works again, weird.
The horizontal scroll wheel cuts out. I mainly use this wheel in excel, so that’s where I notice it cut out. The weird thing is that it cuts out for a specific workbook. It will work on other excel workbooks, but not the random one that cut out that day. If I close it out and re-open it, it’ll work again.

title: Scroll wheel doesn't stay put.
text:
I bought 2 mice, one of the scroll wheels 'drifts'. It doesn't seem to be weighted correctly. As I listen to it spin, it is slightly off, it's not a smooth sound. This means that if the heaver part of the wheel is on top when I let the wheel go, it will roll back down, causing my webpage or document to scroll while I'm trying to type! Very annoying. Many times i have to turn on the slow scrolling in order to type, and then turn on smooth scroll when I put my hand back on the mouse. Thankfully one of them works right, but the other is very disappointing I'm considering sending it back, but I'm not sure what to replace it with.

Also, the wheel is loose enough, if I move the mouse fast enough it'll 'shake' the page. Not much fun if I'm clicking a lot (think excel) but don't need to scroll.

Maybe if it get's older and the bearing get's junked up it'll work better, but then it'll probably loose it's momentum.

I have to turn on the scroll ratchet to get it to hold still on webpages and documents. I read that the MX master turns the ratcheting on and off automatically, so I might return this and get that one even though it's ugly, and I don't think I'll like the forward and back bottoms on top of each other.

title: Good mouse but lack of real mac support downgrades mouse to the most basic
text:
The mouse is fine and works well enough and I do appreciate how thin the new pico-receiver is but there is misleading mac support being advertised as of the time of writing this review. On the packaging and the support website, Logitech says you should install "Logitech Options" to re-map the keys. I did so and it does not show the M545 as a supported device. I did some googling around and a post on their forums from August 2015 says that Logitech Options doesn't support the M545 and you have to use Logitech Setpoint Software, which is Windows only as time of this writing. I also have an MX Performance Mouse and that appears fine (using the same pico-receiver that came with the M545) in the Logitech Control Center but I cannot find the M545 for that either. This means the mouse's left and right wheel scrolling and the two side buttons are useless, which downgrades it to a very rudimentary mouse. The only functions are left click, right click, scroll up-down, and middle click. The middle click isn't even consistent, e.g. Firefox recognizes it and brings up the scroll icon but Chrome does not, but both recognize middle click to open links as a new tab.

The documentation is misleading the customer and if you plan on using this mouse for a Mac, I absolutely cannot recommend it at all.

P.S. Logitech, what is up with all the different software? Logitech Setpoint, Logitech Control Center, Logitech Options, Logitech Gaming Software, etc. Why even have a "standard" control application if you come up with a new one every couple of years.

After going online and making sure all the settings were for English, I was able to successfully synch. I agree that it would be better if the on/off switch wasn't covered by the keyboard corner; however, since the Ipad goes to sleep when I close the cover, that hasn't been a problem. I unhook it once a week to turn it off completely and that isn't a big issue for me.
The pictures of the Ipad laying flat are somewhat misleading. At this point, I haven't found a comfortable way to use the Ipad sitting on the keyboard in that way. It's too easy to accidentally hit the keys on the keyboard. I'm still at a 5 rating because the Ipad and keyboard together meet my needs in retirement beautifully--for a Kindle and Nook reader, Web browser, using either Gdocs or other document apps for journaling, and synching with my Iphone.

title: Worked for one day
text:
Worked for about 8 hours the day I received it. The sound was boomy, distorted and very echo-y. I wasn't sure which setting could've been the culprit, because I didn't have a lot of time to tinker with it. Directional audio was great, I booted up and played WOW for a few hours, while chatting with a friend over Skype. The Logitech Software seemed to have a problem identifying which audio source to keep in front of the other, and on occasion, the volume on both audio sources (Skype, game) would drop to barely audible for a minute or two, and then come right back. Mike dropped out twice, then popped back. So when it worked, there were intermittent issues and audio quality was surprisingly not as crisp as I recall Logitech systems to be. Very disappointing as I've owned several Logitech 2.1 systems and gaming headsets in the past, without issue.

For reference: the USB wireless key was in the front of my PC, less than 3 feet away from me and in clear line of sight. There are no other wireless devices plugged into my computer that would cause interference like I experienced.

Then I get home from work today and bootup my PC. The Logitech Software shows the headset as being in sleep mode. I turned it off, then on, then off and on again, waiting several minutes but it will not leave sleep mode. I tried unseating the USB from multiple ports, reinstalled the firmware, reseted the headset hardware to no avail. Logitech website is surprisingly unfriendly, unless you register your device. No idea why they would gate the public and community forums with a log in, but I scoured the pages for assistance and tried several helpful tips. At this point, I'm fed up and the headset is going to be going back. Very disappointed, as I heard great things about this headset.

text:
I first bought the 5.1 adapter because I needed a way to connect my television to a set of Logitech surround sound speakers.

After receiving the adapter in the mail, I couldn't wait to plug it in and be surrounded with surround sound.

Little did I know, the television I was trying to plug it into only had digital optical audio out because, I mean, why would I just be able to run a few analogs out and be surrounded with surround sound?

After running to the local electronic store and purchasing a digital optical cable, paired with an optical-to-analog converter, I was able to be surrounded with sound.

Long story short, the adapter works wonderfully.

However, whenever I power on the television there is some static, but I believe it's from the converter clearing it's throat so it can surround me with surround sound.

With a few tweaks, if need be, you too can be surrounded with surround sound.

I'll start by saying that I'm not a gamer. I use this mouse as the primary pointing device for a home theater PC (thus, it's value to me for use on a couch). I went through at least 4 other mice, including another laser mouse, before I finally got one that worked consistently. I use it to operate basic windows functions like web browsing and launching videos and music. For that, at least, it's fantastic. It's precise and reliable, and the relative motion (which is tunable in Windows) is spot-on for me at the default setting.

This one reads on every surface I've used (I don't have any glass tables, so that dark field thing is unnecessary for my needs). Also, it's well-sealed and smooth on the bottom, so it doesn't catch on the fabric, and it doesn't collect fuzz or lint. The batteries last for MONTHS. I've honestly lost count. I think I've changed them 2 or 3 times period in the 3 years that I've owned this.

Most importantly to me, though, and the reason I decided to write this review today even though I've had this thing for 3 years... is that it's damned near indestructible. Being a couch mouse... you can imagine that it occasionally gets knocked to the floor. By occasionally, I mean at LEAST once a week. I have a hard tile floor. When it lands, it makes an awful clatter, and the battery cover and batteries go flying. But you know what? When I put it all back together each time... it works like nothing happened. I swear there's not even a scratch on it! I believe, in fact, that the part scattering is likely by design. As an aerospace engineer, I know that by freely releasing those un-critical items of mass, the critical main body is spared a lot of the impact of the crash. Race cars do this. That's why NASCAR and Grand Prix crashes look so disastrous when they happen, but almost every time, when it all settles down, the driver gets out and walks away. And so it is, here.

This mouse is a trooper, and I'd recommend it even for houses with kids and animals (and ok, adults) who are... less than precise in all of their movements.

title: A audiophile businessman's review for music and phone calls
text:
First of all, I am an audiophile. I have a laundry list of headphones I have owned or still own that cost in the $500-$1500 range. I also have a laundry list of Bluetooth and hard wired headsets I have used to make phone calls in order to find a good noise cancelling microphone. One of the best, if not the best, noise canceling microphone headsets (bluetooth) also used for in music was the Logitech UE9000.
So, it came as no surprise to me that this headset had an excellent noise canceling microphone. I love that I can use this headset on my iPhone and utilize the flip down mic, instead of some crappy in-line mic. I've tested the mic in my car with radio volume up 50%, and I couldn't hear a thing in the background! It wasn't until it was up to 70% (very uncomfortable) that i heard a peep here and there. This tests better than my MB Pro by Sennheiser for the radio test. The kid screaming test and the grocery store cart crash, loud coffee shop, and grocery store intercom tests have not been done yet. appears to be lights out for the most part.
These are remarkably comfortable. I could wear these around the clock without pain. Strangely enough, it almost seems more comfortable living with them ON than off; wierd. They breath very nicely as well, so no sweaty ears!
I am more of wanna-be gamer. However, i work so much, I end up with not enough time to play :-(. But, these perform well while gaming. I prefer them over my M-100's that Ill use with the Boom Mic. I think the HD700's were a good gaming headset, unless youre looking for more bass. These have stronger bass presence, while the HD700 don't have any Mic but have better all-around sound. If you want good sound, go with the Sennheiser HD700, but it you want bass impact, features, a great mic for phone calls, and wireless capability look to these. Im VERY happy with this purchase. Im glad I wasn't swayed by the negative reviews.

Update; after 2 weeks. Headset is still comfy. I haven't been tempted to take them back. Given that I've bought SOOOO many headphones
and then sent them back because I was impulsed by something else should say something. In usage on a conference call, I had a negative experience that blew my confidence. The call started where the microphone was in the path of the A/C vent in my car. People commented that it sounded like I was standing next to a train. That's a common fail point for many headset, so it wasn't too bad. Once I moved the vent, the people commented that I sounded a little hard to hear. I took off the headset and threw on the Plantronics Voyager Legend, and they were much relieved. I'm tempted to bring my rating down to 4 stars after that call, but I'm going to give it another chance in case it was a fluke. I'll perform more noise-cancelling tests for the microphone. But, one thing remains is that its a very enjoyable headset to listen to for surround sound and thunderous bass.

2016-8-26: I've changed down to four stars after having them for a couple months. However, I'm still smitten over them. THey're extremely comfortable and the sound quality is very good. For music, it has top-tier soundstage. The sounds is surprisingly pretty well balanced across the spectrum, but maybe that's because I was thinking they'd be like the UE6000 or the UE9000; bass monsters. The range of the wireless is also very good. I really have no complaints. I put it at 4 stars instead of 5 only because I had originally given it a 5 due to its microphone quality. I will try to perform more testing for the mic and get a once-and-for-all opinion posted on it. Since last time, I had the Astro A40 headset. I liked that it could be open back OR closed back, but the sound quality seemed a little dark and didn't have the same clarity and music separation that I get with the G933. I'm keeping these. They're very cool-looking, they're wireless, they've got great sound for music, they've got top-of-the-line soundstaging for games, and a fairly decent microphone. It is a little plastic-y, but so far I haven't had any issues. The band has some give to it, which may help keep it out of trouble. These are my son's favorites to wear as well, but he's 8 and only a headphone junky in training.

text:
I Love it:

I've had this very comfortable, smooth trackball since 2011 as a gift from my family and up until mid-2015 I changed the battery 3x!. I usually use a pencil with an eraser to take out the sphere roller from the bottom hole, so I can clean it (maybe at least 3x in a quarter to remove the dust/dirt build that is seen on the sensors near where the sphere aligns.

Also in that mid 2015 time period, the left button clicking mechanism was not responding very well. As noted based I on the time line I gave, I was already out of the three-year warranty and after reading all the great reviews for troubleshooting. Unfortunately, I was not able to resolve this problem and therefore opted to purchase another.

Using this device I feel relieves the wrist and hand pain I had when I used the standard mouse. One will be using the thumb constantly with this unit, and it feels so smooth, light to the touch. It stays in one place and for the work that I do that consistency is a must. Do I wish it was bigger? sure but It fits well enough for my hand, I really have no complaints about that. Logitech continues to support this fantastic unit and so I feel it is well supported. Be mindful not to loose the tiny Unifying Receiver as it can take about $10 out of your wallet if it does get lost (I’m talking to those that travel with the trackball since one would have to be disciplined and remember to put it in the secure slot near the battery, as those that leave it at home will likely leave it permanently placed) .

Below defines my opinionated star ratings:

One (1) star = the product grossly under delivers to the point the it was a waste of time/energy and/or this was the lowest rating allowed.

Two (2) stars = the product poorly represented what is was designed for even though it works (i.e. quality, stability, below par when comparing to competition). (and the manufacturer should go back to the drawing board).

Three (3) stars = the product worked (in the middle), but never met my standards overall, but the functionality was simply okay.

Four (4) stars = the product is good and will satisfy most that use it, regardless if there is that one nagging thing prevented it from being the best

Five (5) stars = the product is the all-star/gold medal/excellent category and ether surprised me that it worked so well or it did exactly what was promised by the manufacturer.

title: Logitech's gaming controller that never loses its purpose, even though its got a soulless design.
text:
I can say that a larger part of me despises this controller, its so ugly, so completely soulless in its design, and yet, its price point, its utility, its range of supported games, its longevity, its tried and true design. I hate this controller, yet I've owned more of this specific controller than any other game based input device ever. Its pad is better for fighters than a 360 controller, its shaped like the superior PS3 controller, and simply does everything its intended to do.

My personal gripes are that the sticks are not as responsive as the competing Xbox 360 controller and it also lacks vibration. In 3D non-fps games, this causes the controller to be less than satisfactory, to frustrating to use, yet, as stated earlier, its pad is so much better than a 360 controller that it has its niche in platformers. Due to the ability to swap the use of stick and pad at anytime, it makes the left stick's usage non-issue, but in twin stick games, its noticeable, its frustrating, and the controller is a liability for competitive players seeking equipment to further their game.

I received this camera ten days ago and it has been in use for the past nine days and continues to be in use. My husband and I have been shopping for a security camera to compliment our existing security system. The Logi Circle has been a good addition in our home. Listed below are the Cons and Pros that me and my family has observed:

Cons:
-Battery Life is short, between one to three hours based on ability to access WiFi, but this is only when it is streaming and off of the charger.
-WiFI signal isn't as strong as we had hoped, it took a long time to connect when it was off the charger, in a different room. It may help if there was a small antenna on the circle to increase the signal strength or it may not, it is unclear.
-When the circle is on or off the charger, there is always a slight delay between what is visible on the app and reality. It's only a 2 second delay, which doesn't seem like much, but it feels like a lot when using the walkie talkie function-though this is a minor delay considering that the video is being streamed over the internet.
-The app may only be paired to one device which doesn't seemed unusual. When setting up the app, it asks for an email and ties the device to that email. It is internet based, so since it’s internet based, why not allow people to access it via any device or at least allow for multiple. I'm not sure I understand the reasoning behind having to pair a device to it when it’s not blue tooth capable.
-Has no ethernet port, so the only connection is via WiFi, it would be nice to have the option to directly be connected to the internet and possibly even get POE (power-over-ethernet).

Pros:
-Easy and quick set up/ installation, 5 to 10 minutes to get it ready for use
-variety of mounting options; magnet, screws, two sided tape or on its own stand
-Magnet for mounting is unusually strong and secure
-Easy to move and position
-Night vision works well
-Microphone works well on the camera, person on app can hear it well
-2-way communication/push to talk on one end (the app) and the other end is open microphone/speaker
-Has both motion and sound detection
-Provides option for push notification to the app/device upon the onset of any activity on the camera end
-has a long 10 foot usb cable giving us flexibility for where to plug it in
-Sound quality is exceptional on both ends
-Video quality is exceptional on the app
-Video is held in a cloud for a 24 hour period with the option to save it onto a computer, otherwise the video is no longer available to view
-It’s got an appealing look to it, not obtrusive and blends well with most of our home electronics.
-White light indicator may be turned off for stealth operation so an intruder wouldn’t notice it, with the exception of the infrared light for night vision, so it is most beneficial during the day
-From the app, we have the luxury of putting the camera on Motion Detection versus Broadcast. This means that we may, at any time, turn on the app to view the inside of our home, when away from home or just set the camera on motion/sound detection. The broadcast option is most beneficial when the camera is off of its charger.

The Cons listed above are fairly minor weaknesses. I would have rated the Logi Circle, a 4.5, but because I didn't have that option, I chose to rate it a four. Overall, for a new product that's recently entered the residential security sector, it works pretty well and does what it is supposed to do.

I received the Logi Circle Portable Wi-Fi Video Monitoring Camera by Logitech at no cost to me, in exchange for an unbiased opinion. This review is 100% my own.
