title: Love this mouse!!
text: I am absolutely in love with this mouse. In the past I have gone with the inexpensive wired mice, so I thought I would spurge a bit and purchase a nice wireless mouse. After reading other reviews of this mouse on amazon an watching reviews on youtube, I decided to go for it. I was not disappointed!! The back of the mouse, where your palm rests, has a nice matte rubbery finish on it, so it is easier to grip. In the past I have had mice that had smooth shiny backs, and this rubbery finish makes the mouse much more comfortable to hold. The scroll wheel that can be changed to be free spinning, or incremental scroll that can change to free scrolling if you move the wheel fast enough is also a very nice touch.I am also really enjoying the side wheel that can be programmed to do different things. I have mine set to change the volume, which is really nice so I dont need to use the keyboard any more. Behind the side scroll wheel are another two programmable buttons. Out of the box, these buttons perform the go back and go forward buttons that you see in your web browser. I feel that I would use these buttons more, but they are a bit too far back for my thumb to reach comfortably. I think that a better placement of these buttons would be underneath the side wheel. Overall, I absolutely love this mouse and I am so glad that I spent some extra money to purchase this mouse.

title: Long term 650 review - Stay far, far away!
text:
Really deserves a negative rating.
Someone need to tell Logitech it is the year 2016 not 1980.
I am very technical, have a super fast i7 Intel PC and the guy who 'programs' his kids electronic devices.
So read this carefully before wasting your money on another piece of junk from Logitech - Harmony.
My expensive Harmony 890 died and I bought this as a replacement.
The 890 was an expensive piece of junk.
Never kept the settings, took forever to sync and the software was a molasses drip. And those expensive optional signal extenders - great for Halloween decorations at best.
I suffered with the 890 for 5 years, regretting the $$$ purchase, always trying to make it work as advertised. No luck. Yes I used their 'help'.
Now the 650.
Same molasses software with incomplete setup options.
Same garbage buggy software keeps seizing and you have to restart the Harmony program.
Newer, Bigger issues -
You have no programming control over what devices do what, ie volume control from your amp and pause control from your streamer. The 890 had those options, although never kept them programmed for long.
You need to keep flipping screens for various device functions as you cannot without great programming difficulty have this. What??? I thought this was supposed to remove that need.
The only almost good news was the new software for the 650 transferred all my setting from the 890.
The bad news is I had to delete the transfer as all the controls buttons were mixed up.
If you only have 2 or 3 remotes, steer clear of this 650. If you have more remotes, get a universal remote instead. Easier to program.
The 650 is just another money grab that makes you wish you had bought pizzas instead.
Pass on this one.
You have been counseled.
You have been warned.

title: it's a sturdy mouse. Design is comfortable
text:
As far as quality, it's a sturdy mouse. Design is comfortable. The forward and back buttons are perfectly placed and easy to use. I was moving from a smaller/portable M525 Logitech and the increased size took a bit to get used to.

The problem, and the reason I had to return it, was the scroll wheel. In the hyper scroll mode, it's simply defective. You can actually watch the wheel physically "rebound" after you've finished scrolling. On a webpage that means once you've finished your scroll, it will bounce the page up or down an inch or so (depending on how quickly you were scrolling). It's a physical design defect and if you prefer your scroll wheel in hyper mode (versus the incessant clicking of the alternative mode), you're out of luck.

It's really too bad because I liked everything else about this mouse. Potentially mine was from a defective batch, but I've seen numerous complaints about this issue across a few different forums now, all with different dates and times.

title: Had to replace my old MX510 which I just love. My comments here echo feedback from other reviewers
text:
Had to replace my old MX510 which I just love. My comments here echo feedback from other reviewers: the forward/back buttons are too tiny for my normal sized hand and are annoyingly stacked on top of each other, the mouse is too heavy and does not glide quite as effortlessly, and there is no base station for charging. The button issue happens maybe 1 in 10 times I hit the back button, but much more frequently when trying to hit the smaller forward button.

Using the USB for charging is more of a hassle than I expected, since I turn off my computer at the end of the day and so the mouse wouldn't charge as the ports don't have power. The cradle from the MX510 was a simple reminder that always worked.

Rating as 4 stars since apparently the MX510 was the best mouse ever made and you just can't find it. The complaints above are pretty minor overall. I do like the large shape of the mouse, and have found it to be very accurate and reliable.

text:
The only other mice I've used for gaming have been the Mx518 and the G400 (which is just an Mx518 by a different name), so consider this a comparison to those.

-Feel of this mouse in the hand is nicer. It contours well and the little sidepiece for your thumb is surprisingly comfortable (I was worried it would just feel weird). Even without any of the weights it's noticeably heftier.

-Cord is stiffer, which I'm not a huge fan of personally, but it's not the biggest deal once you figure out optimal positioning for the cord.

-The mechanical action of the buttons is, frankly, divine. Left and right click are responsive and sensitive without being overly so, and the mechanical THUNK on the middle mouse click feels so nice I've just been randomly clicking it. It's lovely. If you like the feel of mechanical keyboards you will adore this mouse.

-I don't super love where they moved the dpi buttons to, but it's not the biggest deal.

Overall I'd hugely recommend this mouse for gaming.

title: Great Possibilities, Far From Perfect
text:
## Logitech Harmony Home Hub for Smartphone

I bought the Harmony Home Hub in the hope of connecting my new Amazon Echo Dot to my home theater system, using Alexa to control everything.
So far it appears that the Harmony Hub integration with Alexa is limited. It works perfectly to turn all parts of my home theater on and off for three different activities I have programmed — watch TV, watch a DVD, or connect via Apple TV.
I had assumed that the Hub needed to be aimed at the various components of the home theater setup. However, I was delighted to find that even with the Hub placed beside the components (as opposed to aimed at them like most remotes would need to be), the signal from the hub is powerful enough that it bounces off other items in the room and still operates every single device in my home theater setup — the TV, DVD player, set top box, receiver, and Apple TV! And that’s without using the IR blaster which is included with the Hub. (The IR blaster would be useful if some parts of the system were in an enclosed system instead of on an open shelving setup like mine.)
I’ve had a Logitech Harmony universal remote for a couple of years, so I had a good understanding of programming the Hub, which was fairly easy to do with it connected to my laptop. Pairing it to Alexa was also easy, following their online instructions.
However, options using Alexa and the Harmony Hub appear to be limited right now to basically telling the Hub to turn the system on or off. I’ve not figured out a way to use Alexa to change the channel, or the volume. Instructions on the Logitech website imply that it’s possible to do those things, but lack specific instructions to make it work. I gave up after several different tries, especially since I can easily do those things from the iOS app.
It is very nice to be able to use the Harmony app on my iPhone as another means to control the system. That does allow controlling everything a remote would do, including channel changes, volume adjustments, and much more. However the interface on the iOS app is poorly designed and can be a challenge to use. Each app update seems to make it a little better, but Logitech still has a ways to go to make this a killer system, both Hub and app.
Bottom line, I don’t regret my purchase. But if this is your first Harmony product, be prepared for a learning curve. It can be complicated to make something simple.

title: Good sound, but questionable functionality
text:
These speakers sound great, better than my old Logitech system that stopped working. However, there are some caveats.

In comparison to another speaker, the mids (especially vocals) seem to be artificially diminished by the system; sometimes the main vocalist is barely audible, while the harmonies are much louder. It's rather strange, especially given this is a stereo input through RCA. The speaker system seems to redirect sound to different speakers on stereo, in addition to any actual stereo separation in the audio. For example, any kind of percussive instruments (non-tonal) are more directed towards the rears, and the lead vocal is usually louder in the center channel.

Upon first impression, I was unimpressed by the size of the subwoofer (if you were not already aware, the description is misleading: the sub is 5.5 inches, not 10) but it really outputs a lot! Don't underestimate the little thing. The satellites are satellites, I suppose- they output sound, I don't have much else to say about them. The speaker wires on the rears, while they seem longer than the fronts, are still relatively short, even in my very narrow room. I had to purchase six foot RCA extensions, but with that they work well.

On the actual surround sound ability... I'm not very impressed. I have the trio of 3.5mm inputs hooked into my audio card, and it's been a nightmare to try to get to work properly. Usually the sound from the computer only comes out of the center channel, but when using the actual test in the device's properties, each speaker will "work". I say that because the surround input is not true surround, the speakers themselves seem to mix the sound before outputting it. Therefore, when the computer sends a signal to the rear right channel, it will come out of that speaker the loudest, but it comes out of the other ones at a relatively high volume as well. This makes the actual surround functionality of the system considerably lessened. The sub input is all but useless, because if a bass signal comes through another channel, it will still output through the sub (I am aware that most computers allow for setting of "full range" surround/front l/r speakers, but the computer's crossover should be the deciding factor, not the speaker's mixing)
Lastly, the headphone-out on my system does not work.

This system is really good for the money, and if being used as a stereo system in a smaller room, will be fantastic. If you buy it expecting very loud sound, and legitimate surround sound, you may be disappointed. I'll keep it because I don't *need* the surround and the bass is plentiful :P

title: Great Multipurpose HD Webcam
text:
This webcam works well with Windows 10. When I plugged it in, it did not automatically install any drivers or anything. You have to go to the Logitech website to download the software for it. When I installed the software, the camera was recognized and I was up and running in no time.

The camera feels very solidly built. The stand has a nice range of adjustment. I have it standing on my desk, but you can also adjust the stand to hang over the top of a monitor or another such object. The "foot" of the stand is rubberized to keep it from slipping. If you collapse the stand all of the way, you can also screw in a tripod type stand (which does not come with the camera).

The image/video quality is excellent for a camera of this price point. My office is rather dim, but it has no issues picking up details in faces or objects. The images appear bright and clear. The resolution is of course excellent at 1080p.

The software is fine. Nothing fancy. It is very similar to the Apple OS X Photobooth app. When you launch it, you have the option to snap a picture or take a video. If you take a picture, it does a countdown just like Photobooth. Once you take a picture or video, it ads it to a list of captures at the bottom of the window. Again, this is like Photobooth.

One feature that the Logitech application has that I have not seen in Photobooth is the ability to pan the image left, right, up, or down. You can only do this when you are zoomed in though. The camera does not have motors to physically move the camera in any direction, it just move around the viewing area when you are zoomed in.

Overall, I would highly recommend this camera. There are no major faults. I only wish it came with a privacy lens like the more expensive business version of this webcam, but it doesn't. You can just drape a little lens cleaning cloth or something similar over it if you are worried about privacy.

text:
It's fairly easy to program, versatile, and easy to troubleshoot when a component "misses" a command/signal, via the "Help" button.
One of my biggest gripes is that it CONSTANTLY resets, like almost every time I use it. If it's dropped, bumped, or just feeling grumpy, it will revert back to the Home screen, which means that if you're currently watching TV (for example), it won't work until you get it back into that mode. But be sure to cup your hand over the end, as it isn't smart enough to know the present "state" of a device (on, off), so it will turn it off if it's currently On, etc.
I've had this for about 2-3 years now and yes, it works, but it's only OK as far as a programmable remote. title: Excellent Sturdy Larger Portable Keyboard with FAST and Easy Device Switching Wheel.
text:
This thing is awesome. Complaining about this keyboard because it's too big is ridiculous and you should just buy a folio case for your tablet if it really bothers you so much. The wheel makes using it with multiple devices at once a breeze. It's something I've wanted for years. First time pairing to iOS is easy, Android 5.0 was easy, just had to type the number on the screen to securely pair the keyboard. Then on 3 I have it paired with a PS3. If I'm talking to someone via text on my phone I simply set it in the slot next to my iPad vertically and it takes barely 2 seconds for it to re-pair. Use the phone for messaging and browse the web/FB on the tablet, it's great. Totally seemless and natural. Just to test out the switching capabilities I paired 3 devices and gave them some good use like I was using a multiple display tower. 1) iPad 2 running iOS 9 - Facebook, Safari, calendar, Clash of Clans back and forth. 2) LG Optimus G Pro - FB Messenger, Clash of Clans. 3) Samsung Tab 10.1 - Netflix, Clash of Clans, YouTube, Chrome.. I went back and forth and it seriously takes less than 2 seconds for even my old iPad to pair up and start typing. And if you do manage to get ahead of it, Android and iOS will keep it cached and catch up to you. Don't even have to wait.

Build is like a short throw full size keyboard. Reminds me of typing on a nice laptop or something haha. It's really smooth and excellent for holding conversations. The weight is actually why I bought it. I picked it up and felt some durability. And once I had my iPad and phone standing vertically in it I was glad for it. You need the counter balance to keep it from toppling over. It's super sturdy with a 10" tablet horizontally, I walk in and outside with it in one hand. The rubberized slot is the perfect material and angle.

The shortcuts on Android are flawless. Everything matches up. iOS is about a 9/10. Almost everything works, but there is no back function in Safari. Backspace, the function plus F4, nothing. It jumps back to your home screen. FB app backspace will take you back to the timeline tho and random apps that have keyboard functionality it's just like you'd think it would work.

This is something I didn't even know I needed until I got it and now I can't live without it. If you want a larger keyboard and something sturdy to hold your $1000 devices, this is your keyboard. Even using it at your PC and having a holder for your phone so you can stay hands off, this is your keyboard. I've come to trust Logitech with their PC products and I don't doubt holding this keyboard and feeling it's keystrokes that I'll be using this thing for a long time. A+. 5 stars. 10/10. Would have bought 2 if they had a white one in the store haha.

Note: Pair this with a decent length stylus and you have the best of both worlds. Easy browsing is in your future not to mention the excellent shortcuts in photo editing.

title: Full feature Linux Mint trackball
text:
The Logitech corporation does not officially support Linux. No bother. The Linux community supports Logitech devices. We are conditioned to believe that we must go to corporations to get support for their products. However, Linux was never developed that way. Once you buy a product from a corporation you own it. The Linux community of developers produces Linux drivers to support all sorts of devices.
I installed Linux Mint 17.3 and the [[ASIN:B0043T7FXE Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball]] just worked without a hitch. However, I also bought [[ASIN:B007PJ4PN2 Logitech Wireless Keyboard K360 - Glossy Black]], and each device came with its own Unifying Receiver. I downloaded the Solaar application through the Software Manager to pair the two devices to a single Unifying Receiver and was able to remove one and store it inside the device battery compartment. Solaar is a panel applet that pairs Logitech devices and displays battery level status and warnings.
I personally prefer trackballs to mice. I feel no need to mimic cursor movement with arm movement, or pick up a mouse and move it when it runs out of real estate on a desktop. Rolling the trackball with your thumb is all it takes and the device remains stationary on your desktop. That said, long ago I purchased three [[ASIN:B00004Y7MT Microsoft D67-00001 Trackball Optical Mouse]] and one by one each died. The Microsoft Trackball devices are larger, but current versions are more expensive and plug in via USB cable. I acknowledge a personal prejudice for the size of the Microsoft device, whereas the Logitech trackball is much smaller, although wireless is a plus.
I bought the Logitech trackball & keyboard for a new Linux Mini PC [[ASIN:B018Q0GN60 Intel NUC Kit NUC6i5SYH BOXNUC6I5SYH Silver/Black]], with the intention to connect my Linux Mini PC via HDMI cable to a large panel TV on occasion for streaming video. The wireless design of the LogiTech devices allows me to do this with more convenience than devices with USB cables. I can just set my Linux Mini PC next to the TV and connect the two via HDMI cable then sit back with the wireless trackball & keyboard at a convenient watching distance. Try to control the cursor on a TV, while sitting on a couch, with an optical mouse...well good luck with that. A trackball is simply more convenient, and the [[ASIN:B0043T7FXE Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball]] does the trick on Linux nonetheless, even without official Logitech support.

title: Hardware Failure. Device Completely Unusable. Waiting for Logitech Support
text:
I can't believe this is even legal, this product is defective. it has a hardware issue that prevents pairing. my headset blinks green and beeps three times and disconnects. Now before you scroll past my review....

YES i have troubleshooted my device. for three days i have gone through logitech's website for troubleshooting. i have removed the battery, plugged it back in, restarted my computer, done a fresh driver/logitech software/firmware install, done a hard reset on the headphones and the dongle. EVERYTHING the site recommends for the issue.

Saddest part is on logitech's website there's lists of people complaining the same issue as me. and no response from logitech on most of these forums on their own website (all the forums that did have responses only had one with a list of steps that i above mentioned). i've even done manual installs of all software installs (mentioned above). i have turned to my last hope and emailed logitech customer support to either seeing about a refund or getting a new headset. i'm surprised logitech hasn't gotten sued for releasing a product with hardware problems like this.

How do i know its a hardware problem? i've followed all steps on logitech's website which mainly involved fresh software install and pushing a paperclip in the device to do a hard reset. if all the software is freshly installed manually (with latest software from logitech's website) and power cycled appropriately and the problem persists (even when using audio jacks to attempt to use wired) it has to be a hardware problem. i'm a network admin in real life and i know how to trouble shoot. this is a failure by logitech.

Currently waiting on logitech customer support. If my problem is resolved i will adjust my review.

title: Faulty first 2 times (2016 batches) however amazing quality in 2017(most recent replacement is June 2017) moving into 2018
text:
Update - March 2018:
*Have gone through two replacements since the original date of this review and the second replacement has been working like a charm since. The only warning I can give from this point out is that some people may suffer from headaches or pressure after prolonged use as well as it's bulky size when looking at it in the mirror. It may be specific to your head size or susceptibility from the followups I run on my friends when I recommend this to my friends. Only one complaint out of 12 people. Amazing run so far, wish I didn't have to come in with the original headaches but was worth it in the long run. The warranty process is simple with Logitech without any fees on your end, just some lost time with your precious FPS tool. Seems I will still be using Logitech for my sound needs moving forward.

This headset was a dream come true after I finished building my first PC. The sound was amazing allowing me to respond to people trying to sneak around me in many of the games I have begun to play such as Overwatch, Ghost in the Shell [In Beta] (until the sound service crashed for LGS within the game), lawbreakers, and many other non-FPS. The wireless range is amazing because it remains strong going 3 levels down my home compared to the H600 and H800 I once owned which would cut off in a relatively short ranged compared to the G933

However the main issue with this headset is primarily the microphone. It is locked behind the LGS program so without installing that you will not be able to utilize your mic wirelessly. How ever the most recent and upsetting issue is the fact that there may have been a short in the microphone's wiring because in the middle of a ranked match the microphone just stops inputing any sound without me even touching it or any hotkeys from within my PC. The only way to recover any use is to play with it until the wire falls into just the right place to use it but god forbid if you accidentally adjust it out of habit because you will have to play with the mic for progressively longer amounts of time until the connection just wont remain. But here the amazing part LGS, the G933 itself, and Windows still detect when the mic is in the muted or un-muted position whether there is sound input or not. Wish I could exchange the product or get a replacement from Amazon however this is far outside of either window...

Have submitted a ticket to 3 days ago with no response in sight. Despite how much I have loved this product when it did work there are far too many issues that continue to appear for me to recommend a product of this price point to anyone. Please avoid this particular unless you do not mind prolonged stress. I have given this a 1 star because without the microphone this is an overpriced headphone lacking the fuller sound of dedicated headphones.

title: DO NOT PURCHASE THIS DEVICE! (Read the Edits!)
text:
In the past, my girlfriend and I both had pairs of the old G930's. Both had the crippling issues with network drops constantly. Literally 5-6 times an hour, however it was out of the warranty period, so I pretty much dealt with it.

One of my coworkers mentioned that Logitech had resolved the issues with the G933's I purchased 3 pairs. 1 for work, one for home, and one for my girlfriend. Already 2 of 3 are showing a new fun issue, namely they reboot all the time. It's not a network drop as far as I can tell, it fully reboots the actual headset.

It is triggered by "crazy" actions such as "using the volume wheel"

I attempted to file a support ticket with Logitech, I added notes every time it rebooted. At no point did I receive any response whatsoever. I then tried calling them. After speaking with an agent for a moment, he placed me on hold, and left me on hold until the company closed, some 2 hours later.

I tried tweeting at Logitech to move the support case forward, they did not respond.

Regrettably as I purchased these over a few days, only 1 is still eligible for a replacement, so I am going to try that through amazon (heads up, this device does not get the normal 30 day return window, that bit me in the bum)

This is 2 lines of logitech headsets, over several years, with crippling hardware failures. They have 0 support. I will never purchase a logitech product again.

Buy literally anything else.

EDIT: As you can see in the replies to this review, Logitech replied quite quickly, asking that I email them to escalate. I replied the day they replied to my review. It has now been almost a month since I emailed them as they requested, and I have not heard back from them. Not shocking when you factor in the remainder of my review, but it seems particularly scummy to post replies to amazon reviews implying that they are trying to fix the situation, when they have no intention of following up. In short, Logitech support is still non-existent, however Logitech PR game is strong!

EDIT2: Logitech still has not responded to the email that they asked me to send. Since then, one of 3 headsets has fully died.

Unbelievable. Never purchase logitech, they cant make hardware.

EDIT3: Literally the day I posted that they still had not contacted me, they immediately reached out to me. The email only stated that they would "reach out to me" with no further details. It would seem that the only way to get support from Logitech is to throw a public tantrum. I don't like being that guy. I tried the normal support channels, I tried the phone support, web support, support forums, twitter. It's only after I wrote a bad review that I got any momentum, and even now, the only things I have heard from them are vague promises.

Another item of note, one of the headphones somehow destroyed it's own firmware, and I had to manually reflash the firmware. This was not caused during the firmware update process, I was listening to music, the headset went "boop" and stopped responding. The side LED's stopped functioning, and the device started ignoring the power button. Even when off, the mic muting led would stay on, and it does not respond to turning on or off. I tried removing the battery, I tried charging it overnight, it was only after digging through forums that I found a command line argument to force a reflash. Someone who is not comfortable with tech would be unable to fix this issue. This is not a good consumer product. I shouldn't have to be manually re-flashing the firmware.

EDIT4: 12.28.16. At this point, I have given up on these headphones alltogether.

They release updates to the logitech software, but the software does not warn you, or auto update, so you have to go to their webpage and confirm product versions. I regularly update my software, and have applied the latest firmware. These headphones constantly reboot, at this point several times a day. Furthermore I have to keep reflashing the firmware when the headphones brick themselves roughly once a month.

I ended up getting a hardwired USB headset for $20, and I am much happier with them. I am done with Logitech in general, and am un-trusting towards wireless headphones in general.

Fun note, while writing this review, my headphones rebooted again.

title: Too bad, the mouse MX lasted only a year for ...
text:
Bought this keyboard way back 2012 to compliment my Performance Mouse MX. Too bad, the mouse MX lasted only a year for me. Owning the keyboard for more than 3 years, I could say that this is a very solid keyboard. I haven't changed the battery ever since I got the keyboard and it's already 2016 but it's still going strong. Logitech has reached the pinnacle of battery saving technology on their keyboards. Even the overall design of the keyboard makes any bland desktop look sleek and futuristic.

My one gripe against this keyboard is that the overall key response is hard and snappy. There are times when I am typing that some letters do not register because the normal amount of force I use to type into a keyboard does not even budge the key. This in return, generates unnecessary finger fatigue since it takes much more effort to type in the keys. If Logitech has given the keys a mushy feel like most standard membrane keyboards does, this would have been a guaranteed 5 stars for me.

If not for the stiff key response I would've used the continued to use the keyboard until it gives up on me. However, since I think I have got my money's worth for what I have paid for this item, I have decided to switch to another Wireless Logitech Keyboard with a much more softer response, the K270.

text:
I first bought two of these webcams in 2013, one year after they were introduced onto the market by logitech. Out of curiosity in the past few days I started researching what was new in the market to see whether it was time to upgrade. I have been positively stunned to discover that The majority of respected rankings still identify this model as either the top rated or one of the top five webcams on the market, nearly 8 years after I first purchased it. There are few popular electronics on this planet that are not quickly superseded by an upgraded version of itself or other competitors. due to crushing demand, many unknown manufacturers have taken over the market on Amazon for the time being. title: For the most part I've actually liked the programmable features of the gamepad
text:
Bought this back in November 2014. For the most part I've actually liked the programmable features of the gamepad. My main gripe after almost a year and a half of daily use it's too large for my hand (and my hands aren't small); I have to spread my fingers uncomfortably wide. I will not buy this controller again as a result.

Apparently the controller is starting to fail. Tthe gamepad button just below the joystick just quit working tonight. With this recent key failure and with another key sporadically "misfiring", I take this as a sign that it's time to retire the G13. If you buy this controller, I wish you better luck with it than I'm having.

UPDATE (1/28/2017)--I've been using a replacement Logitech sent me for the unit described above. It's worked fine until recently, when, once again, the button under the joystick stopped working. I'm not a keyboard pounder. I don't hammer that key. I've been very gentle with it since I received it. Despite this, the same button no longer functions. This looks like a design feature flaw to me. Very frustrating. I'll be contacting Logitech again on this unit. My rating for this product here will remain the same. I love the overall design and functionality of this game pad, but when the button most often configured for "spacebar" in gaming goes bad, the game pad becomes pretty useless. That button design needs to be re-engineered.

title: Invest a week to get proficient at it and you will love it!
text:
The first M570 I purchased lasted for many years. The second M570 I purchased lasted for months, maybe a year tops.

What changed? The microswitches Logitech is using. Microswitches are responsible for the left click and the right clicks. Logitech used to use well made Japanese microswitches but along the way changed to cheap Chinese made ones.

Search the internet, or the questions, or the comments section of this trackball for "M570 microswitch" and you too will opt to shop for another brand of trackball. I say another brand because Logitech uses the same cheap microswitches in their more expensive trackballs too.

The problem you will have when your microswitch goes bad? Your trackball will become nothing more than a paperweight.

It's very sad that Logitech opted to go the el-cheapo route. I've used their trackballs since the wired trackball days, long before wireless trackballs even existed. The cheap microswitches makes further Logitech trackballs a hard NO SALE for me. For the first time in my life I will be purchasing a non-Logitech trackball. Sad.

And the fact that it connects to pretty much anything with Bluetooth is awesome, so if you are by any means mobile and have multiple devices, this is definitely recommended. The only reason it doesn't get a 5/5 stars is because I wish it came with some sort of protection. Maybe a case or retractable cover or something, cuz you will feel it to be vulnerable. It also feels slightly heavier than it should (by the look of its size), but not by much. It does feel solid however, and the keys probably won't just pop out, as does tend to happen with the keyboards of many laptops... So overall, great keyboard and was exactly what I needed.

title: There are things I very much enjoy about this mouse
text:
I bought this as a replacement for my beloved MX Revolution, RIP.

There are things I very much enjoy about this mouse, and had I not come from the greatest mouse ever built, I feel like I would have an over better opinion of it. Firstly, I am not an overwhelming fan of the thumb-button placement. I think maybe I was spoiled and this has yet to be a problem, but I'm not really comfortable when I use it; I'm always looking to make sure I hit the right one.

That said, the fact you can swap connections with a button to different PC's is brilliant. I am working with various machines and I can tell you it might be the best idea ever. Also the mouse tracks on every surface I've used it with without fail. I can run on glass, smoked glass, paper or various colors... anything I've tried. The mouse is always super comfortable in your hand. The thumb rest is one of those sneaky-awesome features you'd never care about until you don't have it.

All in all, I really like the product. If I hadn't been spoiled, I would have given this 5 stars. Nothing will ever approach my old Revolution, but this comes really close.

title: Waaay to much reliance on poor software, failed to control 'approved' devices
text:
Returned because of too much reliance on bad software that simply didn't work. This was with modern and fairly standard A/V setup (Vizio TV and Soundbar, Apple TV, Cable\DVR box, and Wii U). Repeated re-syncing of devices and 'activity' workflows never remedied the physical remote's inability to consistently turn on and control the devices I wanted nor program specific, critical button functions (the volume up\down never worked for my soundbar no matter how times I tried to re-program them).

The iOS app worked somewhat more consistently but I don't want my phone for my primary A\V control - I want solid, physical buttons with positive, instant feedback and this is unit none of those. The phone is also required to sync changes to the remote via the hub unless you plug your computer into the hub with a micro-USB - no thanks. Again, reliance on software instead just being a good, solid, remote.

The Mac software for programming individual buttons is confusing, poorly designed, and doesn't offer the customizability it claims. After repeatedly confirming successful pairing\mapping of keys to commands, they would only work for some of the re-programmed keys.

I'm next going to try one of the Harmony remotes that aren't wi-fi connected, don't need a 'hub', and don't require an app\smartphone to simply watch a movie.

My only wish is that this unit would control the PS3 and PS4 but that's asking way too much from one solid remote at this price point.
Overall I'm pleased with my unit, its ergonomics and performance so far.

title: Works with FireTV Stick. Works with IFTTT.
text:
I have long been a proponent of the Harmony remotes-- every time I see a picture of three remotes with all but 5 buttons covered with tape, I cringe, and usually point them at the Logitech page.

So when the FireTV Stick became our go-to streamer, I was irked that after years of smugly only having one remote on the coffee table, there were now two. And when I actually lost that tiny little thing, lines were drawn. This could not stand.

Thankfully, Logitech stepped up, and in a big way. The Harmony Home Hub and Smart Control not only have me back down to one remote, but I'm even now integrated with Alexa. But I'm getting ahead of myself.

Let's start with the setup. Logitech moved from the "desktop program and USB Sync" to a completely wireless model. If you've used any smart home devices, you know the drill-- download the app, give it your WiFi login information, let it find your toys. While the app isn't going to be used as an example in a design class any time soon, it was straightforward enough, and more importantly, it worked the first time.

My biggest hiccup with the app was not recognizing that I needed a new account-- if you have an existing Harmony remote, the login for that won't get you into the app.

However, once you *have* created a new account, you are given the option of importing existing profiles! This was a nice time saver, as I didn't have to look up all those model numbers again- both the devices and my activities were immediately imported. Even better, it remembered all the correct inputs on my amp for each activity- since I updated the amp to display "FireTV Stick" when you change to "Game", I saved a couple minutes by not having to poke around.

The app then scanned my network, and correctly found the slew of Chromecasts and FireTV Sticks that were floating around. A minor quibble here-- I had to click on each one to get the "friendly" name, so I could distinguish between the FireTV Stick in my roommate's bedroom vs the one I was trying to configure downstairs.

But within a minute or so, my device list was correct, and I was at the point of verifying that the Harmony Hub was positioned correctly to turn everything on and off. I was mildly worried that this would be an issue, as I have a projector that sits about 10' from the rest of the equipment, but the only device that was tricky was my 12 year old OTA receiver. After a couple of attempts, I attached the IR Blaster, and that provided the boost that I needed to get the job done.

Finally, the app asked me who was my TV provider, and allowed me to pick out the stations that I wanted to set up as shortcuts. Having gone through this sort of thing a half dozen times in the past few years, the Harmony app was hands-down the fastest way to do it-- put in the zip code, select OTA, limit it to HD, unselect all, add the major networks, done.

At this point, things *basically* worked, but I started to hit the next round of issues.

Firstly, when I looked at the button programming on the remote, a lot of buttons weren't assigned. And we're not talking about weird things like DVD Scene, I'm talking "Volume Up" didn't get carried over from my existing remote.

This was probably the most annoying part, as the app carries over the step-by-step wizard UX from the old software-- you tap on a button, you get a new screen. You tap on the device you want to set, you get a new screen. You tap on the command, you get a new screen. I would have thought that at the very least, the list of devices would have been a drop-down, rather than a round trip back to the Logitech server, but apparently not.

This definitely could be handled better, and is part of why I'm only giving 4 stars.

The next annoyance was that I couldn't figure out how to add a device to an activity, specifically, to update my "Watch FireTV" activity to include the FireTV Stick. I thought that this used to be a simple task with the old system, but as far as I can tell, it just wasn't possible now.

Not a big deal, I created a new activity, and the app helpfully had "Watch FireTV" as a hint, complete with Amazon logo. The app was definitely a bit faster than the old program, and within a minute, I'd picked out the devices, verified the order to turn things on, and was at the fun part- pairing the Hub with the FireTV Stick.

I've seen other people comment that the hub only works with the Fire TV, not the Fire TV Stick. I can assure you that is wrong-- this 100% absolutely works with the Fire TV Stick.

You will need your old Fire TV Stick remote, or the app, but the process is simple, and the app guides you through it-- you're basically going to add the hub as a Bluetooth Game Controller to the Fire TV Stick. Again, a simple process, and inside of a minute, I was back to slooooowly mapping buttons on the remote.

My last quibble with the device, and this is entirely based on my choice of remote-- I really miss the "Help" function. This was a key feature of the old remotes-- if something didn't work, you hit "Help," and it would re-run the sequence, then ask if everything was now working. If you said "No," it would walk you through step by step to find what was wrong, then fix it.

This was the greatest thing ever for less technically adept roommates, but since this is the cheap remote with no screen to display the questions, I get that I've lost the feature. At least until I shell out for a better remote. The roommates will just need to learn how to press the activity button again until it works.

I hope that this doesn't sound like a lot of work, because it really wasn't. I remembered at 11:40PM that the package had shown up that day, and by 12AM, I had the whole thing up and running, including mapping the buttons.

That would be getting four different activities (TV, BluRay, Chromecast, and Fire TV Stick) running with 6 different devices (Projector, Amp, OTA Receiver, BluRay Player, Chromecast, Fire TV Stick) Yes, I had a big head start because I could import things, but even if I started with a blank slate, I can't see that it would have taken more than 10 extra minutes.

Fortunately, I did get the head start, because I used that extra 10 minutes to add my Harmony account as a channel to IFTTT.

If you're not using IFTTT, and you have any sort of smart device, you should put aside a half hour to dig- it really is straightforward, yet disproportionately powerful for what it allows you to do.

How powerful? How about setting up your Amazon Echo to automatically turn on your TV for you while you finish making dinner?

IFTTT is straightforward-- you pick a channel, then you pick an action in that channel, then you pick a second channel and an action to perform in that channel. In my case, the first channel was the Amazon Echo, and the action was to speak a specific phrase: "start fire tv". The second channel was the Harmony, and I could choose to either start or end an activity-- so in this case, I just added my "Watch Fire TV" activity.

Sounds complicated, right? It's not. I did the whole thing from the IFTTT app, and the longest part was authorizing the IFTTT to talk to my Harmony, which was no more complicated than re-entering my email and password. Once that was done, I was able to add two new commands to IFTTT, to turn things on and off, and it was just that simple. It would be nice if IFTTT allowed for more complicated commands, like pausing the music on the Echo after turning on the projector, but the lack of complexity allows you to get that simplicity. And since the Harmony *does* allow for some more complicated actions, it won't be hard to create an IFTTT action to "prepare theater for dinner" and have the lights dim as the projector starts.

While part of me is saying "You just spent $90 so that you could have a single remote sitting on your table again," I actually don't feel that much buyer's remorse. After moving my AV rack, my old IR Harmony was hit or miss with some things- that's eliminated. In fact, I don't have to worry at all about where the remote points now. It sounds like I can expect massively better battery life on the remote. Being able to use my phone as a remote will be nice for those times where the remote is out of reach and I've got two cats sleeping on me. Not needing to drag out a laptop and plug in a remote to program it is super-handy- I probably wouldn't have set this up last night had that been the case. And being able to fire up the projector from the kitchen is really just the icing on the cake.

If you have more than one device in your home entertainment center, you need a Harmony remote. And if you've got anything using Bluetooth, like the FireTV Stick, this is probably the cheapest, fastest way to integrate it with your setup.

title: From the perspective of a Cherry Blues fan: excellent lightweight option
text:
I am more of the kind of mechanical keyboards, but the thing is that there is no way practical way to travel with a mechanical keyboard so I was looking for a compact keyboard to stuff in my backpack. I tried the cheap Anker Bluetooth Ultra-Slim Keyboard and it works, but if feels "cheap" and the tactile feeling is... wobbly, it works, but it is what you are paying for.

This Logitech feel really good, from the unpacking moment it feels solid, it is still plastic, but good plastic and aluminium and the tactile feedback is extremely good for scissor switches. It feels right, firm. Also is really quiet.

Keyboard switching between paired devices works like a charm. Hoping there was a Logitech Mouse which such ease for switching. About the other features: key distribution, function keys, illumination, charge, etc they all work pretty well.

Cons: there is no way to rise the back of the keyboard to choose a typing angle, it has a little slant but I prefer a more pronounced angle. Silly omission from Logitech, otherwise it would be truly perfect. Still giving it 5 stars as you can stick a couple rubber feet in the back as a cheap hack.

title: Have a paperclip handy
text:
I have been using this headset for a while now, and personally, I would like to say am very satisfied. The battery life is not terribly long, but considering the number of functions available and the fact that it is wireless for a very decent range makes that a forgivable failure in my own consideration. I have had no complaints with those I have spoken with about my audio quality when speaking through the provided microphone. However, take care when plugging a device into the 3.5mm audio jack found on the USB wireless adapter. I have noticed this 'feature' can create a distracting amount of static and is really a disappointing outcome from an otherwise excellent little gimmick to come with the device (yes, I have tried swapping ends with the provided dual 3.5mm jack extension provided). The speakers on this are strong enough for me to hear nearly anything in-game and the surround sound is accurate enough that I can discern the "direction" it is coming from as well. It is quite the habit of the software to regularly shut this off whenever it pleases. Regardless, in applications that do not even support surround sound, the extra activated speakers can still add an extra 'oomph' in audio volume where needed.

In all honesty, I would rather be rating this 4, maybe even 5 stars. Yet Logitech has, insofar, had a disappointing trend in their devices of theirs that I use. Software glitches and unreliability. Take care when leaving this behind and allowing it to hit the 5 minute mark for sleep mode. Waking it (or even just turning it on for that matter) has an irritatingly large chance to un-pair the headset from the USB adapter and force you to run around your house searching for anything thin enough to hit the reset switch. With how often this happens, the switch should be large enough to hit with your thumb. This is the failure that I believe was worth the two stars, as the reliability of Logitech has often proven to be consistently bad across all devices I own.

Recent update: Dropping the device review by another star. Connections between the headset and the USB adapter have only gotten worse, completely losing all pairings and forcing the use of that paperclip at least three times EVERY HOUR. This is ridiculous. The device is not damaged, firmware is kept up-to-date, there is no reason for this. Frankly, I don't care if this is by fault of Windows 8, as no other program I have ever used on my system have had nearly as many inconsistencies as Logitech's systems have. Inconsistencies that account for more software and hardware annoyances than anything I have ever used in conjunction with my PC, combined. Considering hat I have had too send that laptop in for repair to resolve a kernel issue Windows 10 had caused(Long story short, complete revert necessary using recovery partitions that Windows 10 took the liberty of deleting.), that is not a good standing. At all.

Update: Looking back on this review years later, my opinion feels rather...stale. Most of my issues seem to have been isolated to this headset and a particular laptop. I notice that a Logitech representative actually noticed this review. Unfortunately the laptop I used with this headset had six USB 3.0 and NO 2.0, so the proposed fix falls flat before I even would be able to test it. If that truly makes any difference then it was a flat out incompatibility with the system itself and it would have never worked.

In any case, my problems seem to have been limited to this wireless headset alone. I have since rebounded right back to Logitech, as after finding myself on a new system I decided to attempt other brands. It just so turns out they failed me in ways that were somehow worse and Logitech's consistency has only improved. My opinion of this headset has not changed however and I have since "sworn off" any USB wireless gaming headset. As it stands, if you were considering this set, get the 633. You'll be much happier contending with a wire.

text: DO NOT buy this product if you want to use it for any video chat applications other than those expressly listed on the box. I got this webcam for the specific purpose of using it with Facebook Messenger and found that I was unable to do so - this, despite statements to the effect that this webcam is suitable for "most" video chat applications. It turned out that I needed to download additional software in order to use this device with Messenger, but I couldn't find the right software ANYWHERE on Logitech's site.When I called Customer Service & finally found someone who knew what they were talking about, I was told that video downloads for my operating system (Windows 7) were no longer functional. I was given a link and told that if it wasn't helpful (it wasn't) I could contact FB for help. Of course FB couldn't help me - #1 how can they help when I can't download the requisite drivers and #2 FB doesn't give individual responses to reported problems anyway. For my purposes it was a waste of money.

title: Rest easy, Logitech.
text:
Since I was originally hesitant about buying a Logitech mouse (they are notorious for problems with the piece of metal that clicks the button becoming bent on the left side) I feared the worst when the M510 started having tracking problems on my mousepad after seven months.

I reset the mouse, I cleaned the mousepad, and I was frustrated that I could take it over to the hard wood of my desk and have it track perfectly.

Then I started looking around for fixes because I'd realized I was about to just go ahead and buy another for the sheer sake of it, and ended up taking a regular Q-tip ("cotton swab") and sticking it into the recession where the laser is and twirling it around.

Problem solved, the mouse tracks like it did when I bought it (maybe even better).

Rest easy, Logitech, you've apparently redeemed yourself! (Most of my former Logitech mouses started having issues around the six month mark, so this one having a simple fix was a breath of fresh air).

title: The epitome of universal remote design.
text:
This is just my personal opinion, but I think that the Harmony 700 is the best universal remote out there and it's just a disgrace that Logitech has decided to discontinue this model.
The ergonomics are very good, the back-lighting is excellent, the keypad is solid with good tactile feel, and the battery life is also very good. Not to mention the fact that it uses rechargeable AA NiMH batteries rather than some expensive proprietary solution.
Programming is done online, so you need a PC with internet access for initial set-up, but once you have done this, it's not a requirement for day-to-day use.
Nearly all the buttons are programmable to serve any function on any device in any activity and it even has learning capability for any obscure devices you may have. And a BIG plus... It doesn't have a fragile touch-screen that seems to be the norm among the latest universal remote offerings.
While the unit feels solidly built, I bought two for the sad eventuality of the first one getting broken, or just wearing out and a replacement no longer being available.

The only two cons I can point out is that there is no back-lighting on the activity or power buttons, and there is no charging cradle. Rather recharging is done by plugging it into a USB port or the included charger, or alternately putting the batteries into a NiMH battery charger, which is the method I use since I have several Eneloop [[ASIN:B00JHKSMJU Panasonic Advanced Individual Cell Battery Charger with eneloop AA 2100 Cycle Rechargeable Batteries (White, Pack of 4)]] batteries and a charger on hand.

title: More trouble than it's worth. Avoid this product.
text:
Constant issues since I received it. I am running Windows 10. To start I just want to say that I work in IT and have been working with the ins and outs of Windows and computers for over 10 years, so I am very experienced troubleshooting problems. I am a loyal Logitech customer and always by Logitech for my peripherals. This is the one product that really fell short.

When I first plugged it in the mic would not work at all. I could not get it to activate. I suspect it had to do something with a conflict with my Logitech G930 headset microphone. I eventually fixed it by uninstalling the driver completely, using a different USB port, rebooting, reinstalling the software completely. Not a plug and play experience. It was finally working, but then there were other problems.

The video for this webcam is terrible. There are blue lines like static all over the picture. I believe this only happens in low-light conditions, but the light is honestly not that low. It's like if it's not sunny then it looks like s***. Also even though the microphone functions (as in I say something and people can hear something come out the other end on a video call), but nearly every video call (primarily google hangouts) I've done the party on the other end will comment about the audio quality, having difficulty hearing, distortion, etc. I was previously using a Logitech 720p C310 which worked perfectly with audio and video for 5 years (eventually started having problems, but 5 years is plenty). I also never had problems with the C310 in low light.

To sum up, this webcam is more trouble than it's worth. Unfortunately, because the problems did not happen all at once (I was able to workaround / troubleshoot until I fixed it), I did not return this item in time. I've tried adjusting settings, reinstalling, but still I get video and audio issues. Once the video turned to s*** I was ready to throw in the towel (just a few days late...). So now it's just going to collect dust somewhere and I'm leaving this review to try and prevent others from going through my misery.

title: Terrible support! Third party software needed for recording. Missing options.
text:
I want to start by saying that I purchased this webcam to replace my old Logitech C910 which I loved but it sadly kicked the bucket:

Pros & Cons:
Pro - Excellent picture and video quality
Con - Terrible customer support
Con - Third party recording software needed to record video or take pictures. Logitech no longer has an out of the box solution. Most quality third party software adds cost.
Con - No option to turn-off recording light if you use for home security or if you are annoyed by a bright recording light.

Detailed Summary:
-There is no longer a Logitech software solution for using the webcam. You must download a third party software to record video or take pictures with this webcam. Not only is this an inconvenience but most third party software cost $. This was a simple solution that used to be included with webcams (including my old C910.
-Support is absolutely terrible! I use my webcam for home security so I was worried when I didn't see a setting to cut off the recording light so I could record video without a recording light. I immediately go to Logitech's support website to see if this is possibly a hidden setting (this was an easy setting to turn off on the old Logitech Webcam Software). I couldn't find any information in the forums so I turn to the Logitech chat support to see if i can get some answers. I chatted with three different support representatives. Twice the chat support window timed out while I was waiting on a response from support (they told me to hold and never got back to me). The third representative just kept asking what third party software i was using to record which is irrelevant because this is a logitech hardware/driver setting that has nothing to do with third party recording software.

Just purchased the C922 through Logitech's website and it's just ok. I had a really old Logitech webcam and the feedback I've gotten from my friends so far is that this sounds worse and video looks worse. I tried using the background replacement software and it's buggy and not super useful. The demo videos show some guy with a background that moves and it's super clear - but that is a different piece of software and seems to only work for video calls through that piece of software. It doesn't appear like you can do that in Skype or Google Hangouts (you can have a fixed photo background there). In both of those, the background replacement is so stuttery that there isn't even a point because then people can't really even see you. When I say stuttery - I mean like 5 fps at times. Perhaps this will get better with some software upgrades, though.

With all that being said, it still functions and still works fine for a webcam. Just don't expect this to be a worthwhile upgrade over any other web cameras.

Edit: It's worth pointing out I have a pretty solid gaming computer so it's more than likely not my specs causing the issues. (i7-6700K Processor + NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980Ti graphics card).

title: Double click hardware issue and interfering right and left click buttons make for frustrating experience
text:
I used to love this mouse but there have been several issues that will keep me from buying it every again.
1. It has a double-click issue where single clicks become double clicks. This is a hardware problem and will drive you nuts figuring out. Try reversing your left and right click buttons if you're not sure if it's a software issue. If the issue goes away, like it does for me, then it's hardware.
2. In some situations the right and left click buttons interfere with each other. I was playing Resident Evil Revelations with this mouse and that game requires you to hold down the right click button to switch to aiming mode and press the left click button to fire. You can imagine how frustrating and surprising it can be when you're in an intense gaming situation and you can't fire. The left and right click buttons are extremely close to each other and angle slightly so that if you are pressing the right click button it will slide to the left and under the left click button preventing both buttons from being pressed. This doesn't happen for short presses and only occasionally in gaming sessions but it was enough to annoy me.

For most uses it's a fine mouse but that double click issue is definitely a huge negative for me. It started out fine and wonderful and you can't believe how smooth the scroll wheel flies when you unlock it but it's just got too many flaws. Find another Logitech Mouse unless you're willing to risk these issues.

title: There is a good 10 second delay or so after hitting one of ...
text:
I use this for my TV, a Roku, and an Onkyo AV receiver for my surround sound. I use the shortcut Macro buttons to control these. The remote uses a line of sight signal, which means it occasionally misses. This wouldn't be a big deal, except that if say the TV does not turn on, the remote does not allow you to just try again by hitting the same button. You need to first turns everything off with the "All Off" button, and then try to turn everything on again. There is a good 10 second delay or so after hitting one of the Macro buttons before you can do anything else, which means if the signal misses on the first try, it'll take 20-30 seconds before you can get the TV to actually turn on. It is very frustrating.

Other than that, the remote easily paired with my devices, and the Macro buttons are a good idea. They just need to be perfected.

title: Extremely comfortable w/ ear-cup controls a big plus.
text:
The good parts: they're very comfortable over long periods, thanks in part to the fabric earcups and the great headband. The boom mic—that mutes itself when moved up, or with the press of a button on the left earcup—is well made and sounds clear. The USB (wireless) dongle is quick to pair, and I never had any issues with wireless connectivity despite being in a *very* noisy 2.4GHz area. The ear-cup volume control also works regardless of the device you're connected to: PC, PS4, etc. This is a big plus as many other headsets require their software drivers.

The bad parts: after running the battery down, they refused to charge. Updated the firmware, unplugged the battery, tried different USB cables, different charging sources, and nothing: they refuse to charge. They power up when plugged into a power-only USB source, and connect wirelessly to my PS4 at the same time, but the charging circuits are seemingly DOA. It looks like I'm not the only one with this problem. I'm considering replacing them for the [[ASIN:B01DPS4QQ2 Razer ManO'War]] that I'd originally considered as I don't want to risk another faulty pair.

Update: The Razer's were a no-go. The ear-cup controls only work on PC (via Razer Synapse), and even on a larger-than-average head, they fit quite loosely. The Logitechs, also being smaller, feel better in-hand (despite being the same weight) as they're denser. Despite the hiccup with my first pair, I'm glad I bought another. Kudos to Amazon's return policy as well.

title: This keyboard is great! I spend most of my day typing and ...
text:
This keyboard is great! I spend most of my day typing and I have a MacBook. The feel of these keys is far more tactile and smooth than what comes on the MacBook or Apple keyboards. I also usually have my iPad on my desk as well and being able to switch seamlessly between the two makes it easy for me to use my iPad as an email station and my laptop for other applications.

I've only had to recharge the keyboard once so far. I ran with the charge it had when I received it for almost a month. So we'll see how it holds up with a full battery charge now. To be honest though, connecting the USB cable to the keyboard for an hour or two to charge it isn't a big issue for me.

The backlit keys are a nice touch. Interestingly, you cannot not use the LaunchPad key (F5) unless you install the Logitech software. But since the software gives you a couple of other features, like specifying displaying low battery warnings and displaying caps lock status on screen, you're probably going to install it anyway. All other keys seemed to function without the added software.

Build quality is solid. The keyboard is solid. When this one dies someday I am certainly going to buy another. I only wish that Logitech had a track pad that could quick switch between multiple devices as well.

title: The windows key acts as the command key which is useful. I didn't have to do any crazy configurations ...
text:
This keyboard works very well with just about any device. I originally bought this for my Samsung Tablet and it ended up working for my wife's iPad mini and my iPad Air. This tablet even works on my Macbook Pro even though it has a windows set up. The windows key acts as the command key which is useful. I didn't have to do any crazy configurations for that either. Also, the carrying case is nifty even though all my tablets have folding stands on them. It is an elegant design and very functional. I've had it for a year and it works very well. The battery life on it is pretty amazing as well. I've only replaced the batteries on it once since i've had it.

The only quarks with this keyboard is that it won't save it's connection to multiple devices. It will connect automatically if you are using the same device, but if you switch back and forth between a computer, an iPad or and Android tablet, you will need to press the button on the back and re-pair it every time you cross over to a new device. It's not that big of a deal but it is a little inconvenient. Also, there have been times when the device just stopped working and it would just type a bunch of nonsense instead of what i'm actually typing. What worked for me is just taking the batteries out and switching them around and then re-pairing it. That was only really a problem in the beginning, it seemed to have worked it self out. I haven't had an issue since.

Also, for those people that want to know about the build of the keyboard, it's a very solid device. You won't feel any flex as you are typing and the plastic is pretty solid. The case is a little flimsy but once you attach it together to put a tablet on it, it's really sturdy and the build won't allow your tablet to fall down. I heavily recommend this keyboard for anyone that want's a good, reliable keyboard that works on all platforms with a windows set up. There is one that has the mac setup as well.

title: Excellent and comfortable headset and mic
text:
INITIAL THOUGHTS
The headset is lightweight and has a microphone that can be adjusted up and down so that you can push it out of the way easily. The cable is lengthy with a volume control including a mute function about 2 feet down the wire from the headset. The portion that goes over your ears are slightly larger than your ears and are not as large as say a full heavy stereo headphone that you might use as an audiophile listening to your stereo.

DETAIL
This style of headset is my preferred style given that it is light enough to wear for hours without causing any discomfort. It is one of the most comfortable headsets I have had. It is good for gaming, and you can hear very well through them without fully drowning out what is going on around you. While occasionally I wish the volume control was either higher or lower on the wire (due to occasionally muting things with my elbow, in reality I don't think it could be moved elsewhere since further up would mean the slight weight might be felt swinging as you move your head, and further down would mean more of a reach to use it.

FINAL THOUGHTS
I have had several headsets with built in microphone. I like this one so much that Wr now have 3 in our household.

By happenstance, today I noticed my MX is 10 years old. Today... This very day, 10 years ago. Amazing.

I've used my MX every single day, except for a few days (Read below to find out why), since December, 5th 2016. I've never had to do any maintenance to my MX. I've never even had to replace the battery. It could probably used one, though. It gives 10ish days of battery now. It used to be about a month, if I remember correctly.

I bought many mice over the last ~6 years expecting to find something better because of the advancement of technology in general. I even gave it away to a family member after a thought I found a replacement. 3 days later I asked for it back and traded the $200 "replacement" for my MX. I was so very happy to have it back.

Basically, I'm saying that this obscure peripheral with a cult following might just be one of the best products over the last 10 years.

If you find one, get it... Time is running short and so is the stock of the discontinued MX Revolution.

From a typing perspective, this thing is everything you will ever want.

The added feature above the Apple Smart Keyboard are:
1). The backlight
2). The short cut keys at the top
3). The back cover that protects the back of the iPad

Which leads me to the bad. As i've said, everything about the keyboard is great - as a keyboard. There is something else to desire when it comes to protecting the iPad. The case protects the iPad really well when it's stationary. Even with gentle movements, I think it's fine. With any kind of sudden jolt, the iPad falls out. I can't explain why or how, it just does. I wouldn't even dare to drop this as I know there will be no protection from a fall. So if you are looking at this to protect your iPad, look for something else.

Like I said, great keyboard, just not as a case

title: A good workhorse for a mouse
text:
I've purchased this mouse numerous times. I own 5 of them and just purchased another. I gave one to my wife, one to my son, I keep one on my desktop, and I have one for a windows laptop and one for a mac laptop. I just ordered another for a computer at work. This mouse continues to perform and holds up for a long time. I first purchased this mouse in 2013 and that one is still kicking (though I replaced the battery at least once, possibly twice).

I obviously love the mouse, but why?

It has a better fit to my hand than most mice. If you use a computer for more than 4 hours a day I highly recommend you find a mouse that isn't too small. I don't have truckasaurus hands and I don't have princess hands. My son (12) and my wife (closer to princess hands) both use the mouse without complaint.

The battery lasts a really really long time. Looking at the 3 mice closest to me they all still have their original batteries in them.

The receiver can be setup to pair with a logitech keyboard. The receiver is also fairly small and doesn't jut out too far of my laptops.

I've dropped my mouse a few times. It takes a beating.

The buttons on the side (thumb buttons) are well placed and mostly useful. They also don't accidentally get hit.

What don't I like?

The scroll wheel isn't smooth. It has stops (like gears) that feel like bumps when you scroll. I've gotten used to it but I'd prefer smooth.

The pads on the bottom can get gunked up if you mouse through something unsavory on your desktop. I have one that does this and it was pretty ugly until I just pulled the pads and sticky goo off. That's my oldest mouse too so... might be expected after so much use?

title: Good, but quick to show wear on keys
text:
I've used the Logitech Wireless Combo MK520 keyboard and mouse for nine months now, and I'm happy with it. Everything works as expected - key feel is good, mouse size and feel is good (it's smaller than some, but I don't like a bulky mouse), and the design is attractive. I don't generally care for fast-launch keys and volume controls on a keyboard, however one thing I would have never asked for but love on this keyboard is the button that launches the Windows 7 Calculator - I use it often. I can't comment on range, as both keyboard and mouse stay on my desktop.
My only criticism is that the letters began wearing off of the keys within a few months - only a little here and there at first, but now after only nine months of use, several keys are completely unlabeled: S, D, C, N and L, with a couple more nearly gone. Still functional, but I expected the keyboard to hold up better at less than one year of normal office use.

title: Gets the job done, but not great
text:
I like this keyboard, but I do not love it. I bought this for my job where I use excel extensively, therefore spend a lot of time on my keyboard.

Here are my observations:
Cons:
1. No nums lock or caps lock lights to show when one / both is activated.
2. Keys are slightly rounded, which (as a matter of personal preference) I do not like as much as keys with a more defined edge. It makes slipping between keys easier, which is not something I want to be doing.
3. I have had some technical glitches since owning this for about a month. Sometimes I will be typing, and it takes a few seconds to wake up the keyboard. I then have to re-type what I've already written. This has happened 2-3 times in the period of owning. Not excessively annoying, but it does happen on occasion. Also, there was one time I turned on my computer and even though the USB device was in, it wasn't "seeing" my keyboard or mouse. Nothing would fix it, and I had to reboot. That has happened twice since owning. This is more irritating, but again, since it happens relatively infrequently I am not terribly frustrated.

Pros:
1. I love keyboards with mute / volume down/ volume up buttons. This keyboard has that. I haven't used them yet, but they are there and easy to find.
2. The mouse is surprisingly nice. I expected a crappy mouse, but I actually think the one included is very comfortable. It has the grippy rubber on the sides, which I really appreciate.
3. I like the on/off switch on both the mouse and keyboard. I have had wireless mice / boards before with no switch, therefore I felt like I used battery much faster.
4. It gets the job done. Overall, it is a typing machine and the cons aren't enough for me to return it. If I had seen the keyboard models in person, I don't think I would have chosen this one, but it works.

title: A good start, but it will scratch your screen
text:
First off, the keyboard itself is great. The keys "feel" like a legitimate laptop keyboard, and the "function" keys (not true F1-F10 keys, but specific iPad functions like home, lock, search, keyboard and screen lighting, etc) are a great addition. The lighting of the keys is occasionaly quirky, but reseating the smart connector usually fixes the problem.

The case portion is heavy (in the protective sense) without being overly obtrusive. It will bend/flex out of the way when holding the iPad upright, and doesn't interfere with charging, audio output, or power/volume controls.

The only major negative that I've identified after about four months of use, is a pretty big one, and it costs the product two stars. The edge of the keyboard leaves some pretty significant scratches on the iPad screen. Luckily I applied a screen protector before I put my device in this case, but there is a line of scratches and abrasions across the the right vertical edge of the screen, running downward from the power button to the bottom speaker. Fortunately, these scratches are on the protector, not on the screen itself. I would be *extremely* unhappy if a case designed to protect my device had instead damaged the screen.

As an aside, if you have one of the magnet sleeves for your Apple Pencil, there is no place on this case to attach it when the case is closed. This isn't a flaw of this product, merely an FYI.

text:
I have quite some brand loyalty for Logitech, mostly due to their amazing warranty. They have never failed to fulfill my expectations and then some. That being said, I was quite worried that this keyboard would be a little too small for my comfort, but I was pleasantly surprised! I could type for an extended period of time on it if I had to, although I would prefer my K750 if a full-size keyboard was an option.

The trackpad on this keyboard performs buttery smooth, and this is from someone who really does not like trackpads at all. For the type of use this keyboard is intended for, the kb + trackpad in one really is a superior solution however. I always found my mouse falling off the mousepad, or tracking improperly when trying to use it as a remote control for my computer + TV. This is more of a pain in the butt than you might think when just trying to relax and consume some media.

An added bonus for me is the bluetooth support, I paired it with my Samsung Galaxy Note 5 to test compatibility, which works great! When mobile and needing to do some typing that proves to be a bit much for the on screen keyboard, and using jargon that the voice recognition would barf all over, this keyboard fills a niche I didn't know I needed filled. I am tempted to take it with me on the road more than I'd like to admit. My wife doesn't appreciate not being able to find the remote, however :P

The illuminated keys are very well done, bright and evenly lit. The additional left click on the top left of the keyboard is a brilliant addition, kudos to whatever engineer at logitech came up with that idea. My only complaint is the need to press Fn to use the normal F-keys, I find myself needing to use those much more than the media-centric keys. That being said, the home/back/menu keys kick serious butt on android! Hard to make up my mind on that one...
