title: Great ergonomics but combined with bad electronics makes it rubbish in real life.
text:
This product has 73% of the people rating it as a 5 star product. I suspect they all wrote the review within a week of buying it and are not long term reviews. This review comes after 3.5 years of using this mouse.

The good:
The ergonomics are EXCELLENT.

The bad:
1. Right click wont work AT ALL. I have to mash it or try weird angles to get it to register a click. For every 8 clicks I click it works once.
2. Left click wont let me drag and drop, it will let go inbetween and drop the file (basically the button stops working)
3. Left click wont let me select text (same problem as above) because the button stops working and hence the selection gets dropped
4. Left click will sometimes double or triple click when I just click once. This is very annoying when sometimes I try to close one window and it triple clicks and closes the three other open programs/windows that were behind the one I was trying to close.
5. Left click doesn't work properly most of the time.

The ugly:
All of the above problems seem to be caused by two components:
a. Suuuuuper sensitive micro-switches that Logitech used. These switches are so sensitive they respond to the slightest variations of pressure in your finger which you can't control. So when you are trying to drag files or select text the natural variation in pressure that occurs in your finger muscle combined with the super sensitive switches they use ends up releasing the switch (and then pressing it again) causing the dropping of files/text or multiple clicks though you just clicked once.
b. Bad capacitors or bad circuit design that doesn't let the capacitors discharge properly making the clicks not function. And you know what their fix is when you call them and ask them? Remove the batteries and click the buttons repeatedly as fast as you can for 20 seconds to discharge the capacitors. Come on Logitech, we expect better than this from you.

Most people (myself included) who really LOVE the ergonomics of this have taken the mouse apart and replaced the micro-switches with better ones.

I'd strongly suggest googling "Logitech M570 click problem" and reading the numerous frustrations of the current owners and DIY fixes required to get these working before you make up your mind on buying these.

A great ergonomic mouse ruined by sh*t tier circuit design and components.

title: Edit: Got a replacement. Still does not work. DO NOT PURCHASE
text:
It works with a HUGE BUT...

I purchased this with the mind of using BlueTooth for connectivity to my Mac Pro (Late 2012). I did some research on this before purchase and I saw that some were having connectivity issues with the little dongle that connect at 2.4 gigahertz, which can be a problem with things like older WiFi networks and even some Microwaves.

The idea was if it was connected via BlueTooth, I should have problems. I was wrong.
1. There is no manual in the box.
2. The dongle works but intermittently due to the proximity of my WiFi as well as my neighbors WiFi
3. My Macintosh does not recognize the BlueTooth in this mouse, be it as a Bluetooth device or specifically as a BlueTooth mouse.
4. Only way for it to work properly is to have the dongle in, as well as have the mouse wired via USB, which of course destroys the whole purpose of me purchasing this mouse.

The Good parts:
1. It's heavy for a mouse. This is good for me due to me having MS, though others may not like the weight.
2. Bigger than average. Again, good for me. It's now a replacement for an older Logitech MX mouse, wire and very light. Having a heavier mouse allows me to move it with a little more precision.
3. The scroll wheel made me keep the mouse. It clicks as you scroll and has a tactile feedback, so again, when I need it I have another sensory input for my finger. This can be turned on or off by a button behind the wheel. Most may like it better without the feedback click (slight sound) but if you need to scroll quickly, you can move wheel fast and like a clutch, the click is off and the wheel is free moving. This is good ID (Industrial Design).
4. Though not obvious, there is another button where your thumb rests. I thought I would accidentally click that all the time but I do not. Of course, it is programable as well as the other scroll wheel for you thumb as well as the usual forward and back buttons for your thumb.
5. I should also mention good ID on the forward and back buttons. They are not flush to the body of the mouse, they are more like peaks than an valley. Much easier for me to find and push.
6. I haven't fully used the side scroller just because I have never had one but must remember to use it if I come across a need.

So, in conclusion, it does work. If I can get the BlueTooth to work, I would give it four or five stars but as of now, I have a ticket in to LogiTech. It is the third working day the ticket has been in. I put the ticket in on a Saturday and so far, I have an acknowledgement that they have it.

NOTE: This next part is just conjecture on my part and is not meant to state facts...
From what I could see on the boards of Logitech, Apple and other tech boards, it seems to me that Logitech with the latest update to this particular product 'turned off' the BlueTooth and that their answer to non-connectivity is to use their dongle. Of course, if you are like me and have a lot of interference, you must have the USB cord plugged in. I have held on to this mouse because, even wired, it is an upgrade of my older wired mouse. I will keep my fingers crossed that Logitech updates the BlueTooth so that it works smoothly with all machines. I state all machines because, again, it seems like now, the BlueTooth doesn't work on Windows 10 machines. Again, this is conjecture on my part and I have been a Logitech fan for quite a long time. I even have recommended large purchases of Logitech products to replace outdated or broken OEM products when I worked for large companies and institutions.

In all fairness, this is the FIRST Logitech product I could not get to work out of the box and I have a lot of experience with Logitech products and can make some PC only Logitech products work on my OS X machine

EDIT 8-13-16: Got my new USB 3 hub today. Hey, guess what doesn't like USB 3! The dongle doesn't like USB 3 either, so I have the dongle, the mouse and my PC only keyboard working on USB 2 only.

I also have not heard from anyone from Logitech beyond the robo reply. Dropping it to 2 Stars because it doesn't work with USB 3 on a Macintosh. I actually thought it would work better! The mouse is starting to annoy me, hence the downing to 2 stars. If I switch back to my old wired mouse, it'll be one star.

EDIT: 8-19-16
Got two e-mails. I don't understand why they have to use their "Mary Casmir" auto-reply but the auto replies have some human typing within the reply. Why they don't just have a human do it, since it is being half done by one is silly. They have decided that my mouse is defective. I've given them my address and strangely, wanted my phone number. I'll keep updating as this plays out.

EDIT: 8-24-16
Two days ago, Logitech stated in an e-mail that I would get another e-mail with a prepaid return label for UPS. It now has been 48 hours. Really, what has happened to Logitech??

Edit: 9-2-16
It took two weeks to get a UPS label to send it back to Logitech for replacement. Of course it is ground delivery so it will take longer than usual. If I get another mouse with the same problem, then my first assessment that it is software and not hardware would be correct, in my opinion. I am using my old mouse again until I get a new or referred MX Master. I will report when/if it arrives. I am dropping it down to one star. I hope to bring to 5 stars once I get a replacement.

Edit: 9-26-16
So I got a replacement about a week ago. Was working on a project, so waited. I changed and Bluetooth does not work. I really don't care at this point. It's software, not hardware that is the problem. If they need to put out two different versions for the Firmware, one for OS X and one for Windows, they should.

On top of all that, they want to close my issue. I think I got one e-mail from a real person. Mary Casmir, the computer responder was more helpful than the human.

Replacing one non-bluetooth working device with another is not the answer. Whiskey Tango Foxtrot Logitech? Have the balls to state it doesn't work and fix it. Your product, own it, and fix it.

As of, hell, couple of weeks ago, I will never purchase another Logitech product because of this experience. There is no excuse.

HEY AMAZON, you might want to take this off your product listing too, it's going to give Amazon a bad rep for selling, just my opinion.

title: Good keyboard with some slightly annoying flaws.
text:
Good for the most part, and works pretty much as advertised. The two stars are knocked off for two reasons:
(1) I type pretty quickly, and when I'm typing at full speed, the keyboard tends to drop keystrokes occasionally. I assume it's because the paired device (Android phone) and the keyboard aren't doing sufficient error checking, so I'm not sure whether to blame the keyboard or Android, but I'm docking a star for this anyhow.
(2) The groove for mobile devices is too deep for my Nexus 6P phone in landscape mode -- part of the screen falls below the lip, and of course that's the part where the cursor often is located. I have another phone stand that works, though, so now I just put that next to the keyboard instead, but it's kind of annoying I have to do that (or type in portrait orientation).

Otherwise, it's a good product overall, and if your phone or tablet has a screen that doesn't go nearly to the edge like the Nexus 6P then you probably won't face the second issue.

title: A disappointed fan with a defective 1 day old headset
text:
I loved Logitech. I have a keyboard, a G602, and finally this headset. I saved up all the money I had just to buy this, but then got so disappointed.
If you are thinking of buying this headset, read the reviews more carefully. I was like most people, ignoring all the low star reviews, brushing them aside as bad luck, but when you actually receive a product as bad as the 1- start descriptions, you feel like total sh*t. The are SO MANY problems that you face when buying this product, here are just a few:

1. Every time I turn the headset off, it disconnects from the dongle. It will not turn on unless it is re-paired to the dongle by resetting it.

2. The headset will occasional have a non-functioning mic after I re-pair it to the dongle. The only fix I found out so far was to keep pairing and unpairing until I got lucky, and it would work.

3. The headset switches from a nice clear sound, to a bad quality echoy sound after 20-30 min of use. Watching YouTube videos on chrome is the worst.

4.If there is no sound, a loud static popping noise will be present, followed by silence.

These are just a few, and were supposedly fixed by the firmware update that came out a few days ago, however, they are still present. You can get another pair, but you better be lucky, otherwise you will be facing the same problems as hundreds of people who paid an outrageous price for a non functioning headset. I will probably return this for another headset, but if that doesn't work either, I will get a full refund.

title: Exceeded expectations
text:
I have had a multi-device home theater/music setup for quite some time without having a universal remote to control it with. I finally got sick of having three remotes on my table at all times and juggling them to enable different functions and use different devices. My three remotes were for my TV, for my cable box, and for my receiver.

First of all, I will explain my choice of this model remote. I considered getting a cheaper Logitech model such as the Harmony 650, but ultimately I went with the Ultimate One over cheaper Logitech models because it comes with the Harmony Hub and IR blasters, which means I don't have to have a direct line of sight to control my devices. This is very useful because I will often control my setup from across the room when I am listening to music, and my furniture is in the way. The Harmony Elite also comes with the Hub and the IR blasters, but it would cost another roughly $100. From what I can tell, the advantages to the Elite are a superior button arrangement and more convenient controls over home automation devices and lights, perhaps some improvement to battery life as well. I do not have home automation devices or wifi/bluetooth enabled lights, and for a savings of $100 I can definitely live with the slightly subpar button arrangement, so I clicked buy. From what I understand, this model will control home automation devices, however, the Elite has dedicated physical buttons for lights and such, whereas this model does not. I'm sure the Elite is a nicer device, but I'd rather save $100.

The remote was relatively easy for me to set up, but I consider myself tech savvy. I have a feeling that my father, who has a solid understanding of computers for someone his age (55), might have some difficulty in getting this remote set up exactly how he would want it. But then again, he wouldn't buy this remote in the first place. I have heard that Logitech tech support is very helpful in setting up the remote if you need assistance, however, I did not contact them myself. I think that most people who are buying this remote understand the advanced functions that it has and will have a pretty good idea of how to set it up. There was a bit of trial and error for me, but I had it set up exactly how I wanted it within 24 hours of unboxing it.

Being able to set up activities on this remote is truly awesome. When I want to watch my cable, I can just press "Watch TV" and it will turn on my TV, turn it to the correct input, turn on my receiver, turn it to the correct audio input, turn on my cable box, and, if I choose, have it immediately tune to a specific channel. You can set up these actions for any common "activities" you have. This is so much easier than juggling the three controllers I used to have. I love it.

I read some reviews that mentioned poor battery life. This does not appear to be an issue with my remote. It appears that this issue was caused by an old version of firmware that was bad, and one of the first things that the remote has you do is update the firmware to the current version. I haven't run the battery out yet (I've been putting it in the charging cradle when it gets to around 25%), but it seems like it would last a good 4-5 days between charges under moderate to heavy use.

I have only two minor gripes with the controller so far, and they are very minor because I still give it five stars.
1) I would prefer for there to be a physical number pad. It would be nice for changing channels on my cable box. You can set favorite channel buttons on the screen, so you just tap them and it tunes to that channel. That is good enough for me 90% of the time, but for that 10% of the time I want to watch some random channel, it would be nice to have physical number keys.
2) This seems to be the main reason that people don't like this controller: the pause/play/skip keys are located above the touchscreen. The placement of these keys on the Elite controller, right below the touch screen with the rest of the buttons, is CLEARLY superior.

I would recommend this remote to anyone who has a moderately complex home theater setup. It really helps to simplify controlling everything. The price tag is high, for sure, but I expect to have this device for many years to come.

title: I have had 3 Logitech M187 mice that all developed the same fault: THE RIGHT BUTTON ON THE MOUSE STOPPED WORKING PROPERLY
text:
I have now had three Logitech M187 Wireless Mini Mice that within a year or so all developed exactly the same fault: THE RIGHT BUTTON ON THE MOUSE WOULD NO LONGER WORK PROPERLY.

Although these mice were all working fine initially, after around a year the right mouse button would become increasingly difficult to activate: you would have to press the right button very hard, and hold it down for a moment, in order to create a right click. If you just pressed down and released the right click button normally, you can hear and feel the click it makes, but the right click is not actually registered, and is not sent to the computer.

I think the problem lies in a faulty microswitch in the mouse, which physically clicks down, but does not make electrical contact. So you hear a click sound, but no right click actually occurs (no right click is transmitted to your computer).

Oddly enough, this fault never appeared on the left button (which gets used much more frequently than the right button, so if anything, you'd expect the left button to wear out first). But with the three Logitech M187 mice I have had in the last few years, the fault always appeared on the right button, never the left.

Generally speaking, I like this mouse. I like its small compact size, and I am impressed by the very long battery life that the Logitech engineers have achieved from a single AAA battery.

However, with 3 mice (bought at different times from different stores) developing the same fault after around a year, I cannot recommend this product, until Logitech rectify the problem of substandard microswitches in their mice.

title: Please read this if you're having trouble with the wheel in Windows10!
text:
This mouse works great... once you DISABLE the Logitech Setpoint software!

I paired this using the Logitech Unifying Receiver with a Logitech K330 keyboard. I had ZERO problems with this mouse in Windows 7, but a lot of trouble with it in Windows 10.

The problems:
When scrolling through photos in Windows 10, the wheel would scroll through SEVERAL pics with one click instead of just advancing a single picture.
Chrome/IE/Edge --When clicking the wheel button to open a new tab, I'd often have to click 3-6 times before anything would actually happen. Also, when trying to open any bookmark in Chrome in a tab using the wheel, it just simply didn't work.

Although I primarily use Chrome, I was able to replicate the exact same problems using Edge and IE as well.

The short: DISABLE the Logitech Setpoint software AFTER you set everything up. Leave it installed, but remove it from running at login. Yes, you WILL lose advanced functionality (like assigning special functions to buttons) but it's worth it in the end.

The long: Logitech Setpoint needs updated to work better in Windows 10. Install it, if you have another Logitech unifying device select the Unifying option and allow it to pair up your keyboard and mouse with the Unifying Receiver. Once it's paired, close out of, and disable the software from running at login (Ccleaner is GREAT for easily doing this). Once Setpoint is disabled, say goodbye to the keyboard latency problems, as well as mouse problems with the wheel.

What will still work fine with Setpoint disabled:
All basic mouse functionality.
Wheel scrolling and middle-clicking will work PERFECT.
Forward/Back/Left/Right/Wheel & Wheel click still work fine.

What WON'T work after disabling Setpoint:
Anything you've assigned via the Setpoint software. For example, rather than 'Switch Applications' for this mouse, I assigned the bottom thumb button to 'Close' any application in the foreground. That button no longer works at all.

This is a fresh Windows 10 64-bit Pro custom build PC that I built myself.

Bottom line: Logitech needs to fix their software. Their hardware, on the other hand, works GREAT once you disable Setpoint!

HOPE this helps someone save some time and headache!

Overall, I'm VERY happy with this mouse once Setpoint was disabled.

The short: DISABLE the Logitech Setpoint software AFTER you set everything up. Leave it installed, but remove it from running at login. Yes, you WILL lose advanced functionality (like assigning special functions to buttons) but it's worth it in the end.

The long: Logitech Setpoint needs updated to work better in Windows 10. Install it, select the Unifying option and allow it to pair up your keyboard and mouse with the Unifying Receiver. Once it's paired, close out of, and disable the software from running at login (Ccleaner is GREAT for easily doing this). Once Setpoint is disabled, say goodbye to the keyboard latency problems, as well as mouse problems (more on that in my M705 review.)

What will still work with Setpoint disabled:
All basic functions of the keyboard
All top-row keys (Email, Browser, Media Player (all still assignable WITHOUT Setpoint).
Track forward/back Play.
Volume Up/Down and Mute
Calculator.

What WON'T work after disabling Setpoint:
Buttons you've 'assigned' and customized. --I changed the 'Show Desktop' to Media Player 'Stop' and that won't work without Setpoint running.
On-screen notifications. --The CAPS lock will not alert you on-screen when turned on/off. Volume keys still work fine though for on-screen notifications.

I've been using this keyboard now for days without any latency issues whatsoever. Yes, you are giving up advanced functionality for what is just basic functionality but you're at least still wireless.

This is a fresh Windows 10 64-bit Pro custom build PC that I built myself.

Bottom line: Logitech needs to fix their software. Their hardware, on the other hand, works GREAT once you disable Setpoint!

HOPE this helps someone save some time and headache!

Finally, one other thing to note: As others have stated, the keyboard I received states K330 as the model number on it. NO difference in features and still works PERFECT once you disable the Setpoint software.

I'm VERY happy with this wireless keyboard.

text: Received this remote for Christmas.  I find it to be nearly all Logitech claims it to be.  Set up was pretty smooth and quick.  It operates all five of the components in my entertainment system, including the Amazon Fire TV box, thereby relieving me of five different remotes. The volume and channel controls need to be more prominent to allow the user to use them without actually looking at them.  The forward/rewind/pause/play and record buttons should be below the touch screen, not above.  The touch screen should be at the top of the remote,  not in the middle.  The number pad doesn't function very well.  It seems there are parts of the touch screen, especially the corners, that aren't very sensitive, so you think you've poked in a 1, 3, or a 9 but it doesn't register.  Using the app to arrange the channel icons doesn't work at all.  I've tried in vain to rearrange and/or delete some icons.  These are minor irritants that shouldn't deter anyone from trying this remote.  Perhaps with more time and experience I'll overcome them.  In the mean time I'll enjoy operating everything with one gadget.

title: 4 stars for Simple and Future-Proof.
text:
The Harmony 650 Remote is one of the basic devices in the Harmony family. I like it because it allows me to tap into the huge list of compatible devices Logitech provides for Harmony devices and because it is inexpensive. In fact we have been using a 650 for our bedroom TV/Audio/Blu-ray setup for some time. The unit was so inexpensive we bought a second one recently so we have one on both sides of the bed. Logitech is constantly updating its software to accommodate new devices, so your remote is future-proofed. I have set up activities with obscure devices like off-brand HDMI switches from China with no problem. If you have a model number, Harmony will find it and load the device in your remote.

This remote allows you to set up all your devices on the remote and even create custom buttons for special features of the device. Once you have set up the devices, you can create "Activities" or shortcuts for specific functions like "Watch TV" or "Watch a Movie." My TV has internet access, so I have created specific activities for Netflix, Amazon Prime, and Pandora. If I want to use one of those services I can get there with just one click and don't have to bother going through layers of menus. It is very convenient.

The only limitation I've found with this remote is that it controls devices with infrared signals from the remote to each device. There is no RF capability or internet connection. Therefore, it only works if you point the remote at the device(s) you wish to control and have a clear line of sight path. The remote will not control any devices hidden in a cabinet. You need to go to one of the more expensive Harmony remotes for that capacity. Secondly, when you set up an activity, you are actually creating a sequence of commands for the devices involved in the activity. As long as you keep pointing the remote at the devices until the sequence finishes, everything works fine. However, if you stop pointing the remote as soon as the devices come on but before other commands are sent such as inputs selected, etc., the activity will be incomplete. This is easy to avoid by simply holding the remote in position until its LCD screen reports that commands are complete, but the less technical members of my family do not seem to be able to remember this and sometimes have to go back to manually issue one or more commands through the "Devices" menu.

In conclusion, I don't think you can beat this remote for a simple, inexpensive way to control multiple devices in your video/audio system. If you need to control devices enclosed in an equipment cabinet, or you are one who forgets to give the remote time to finish it's sequence of commands, then one of the more expensive Harmony remotes is for you. Either way, you are buying a remote that will continue to serve your needs as you replace components in your system with newer ones.

text:
I haven't owned a Logitech mouse since I owned a Logitech Mouseman back in 1997 which was before the mouse wheel was invented. I loved it but I switched to Microsoft mice because Logitech seemed to get cheap and gimmicky. However that is what are Microsoft mice now so I am on the hunt for a good mouse again.

After using it for about 8 months I can't recommend the MX Master.

The good:
- The darkfield laser is nice for working at night, there is no flash of light when removing the mouse from the table.
- It has a weighty feel to it
- Looks great, the polygonal texture on the side looks great in person.
- The build quality is good, it feels solid.
- The main buttons feel great, a firm plastic and some internal reinforcement work well.

The bad:
- I just don't like the side wing. You can't brake the mouse with your thumb, which is just annoying.
- There is no place on the mouse to store the usb dongle
- I never used the side buttons once, the wheel is too sluggish and awkward and the buttons are designed to look better than they are clickable.

The ugly:
- The scroll wheel clicking/clutch feel, which is different and fascinating at first, ends up just not working and is frustratingly illogical over time. There is something wrong with the manufacturing of it, as it briefly only returned to functional after accidentally dropping the mouse a couple times. There is some sort of electronic catch in it which feels good.
- The scroll wheel, after it starts to die "back scrolls" preventing you from scrolling to the bottom of documents.
- It has to install some overly complicated and bloated mouse drivers. I don't need another process that runs trying to check for updates thanks.
- It does have a rubberized coating, the kind that feels great initially but inevitably starts to get softer and sticky. I can scrape it off now with my thumbnail.

Overall this mouse is still what I don't like about mice: All gimmicks that don't stand the test of time.

I just want two buttons and a scroll wheel made out of something not cheap feeling.

title: Warning: Battery Replacement IS Required
text:
It's a nice keyboard, but what a PITA battery. I would not buy this product again. I bought this keyboard because of the promise that I would not need to replace batteries. This is incorrect. And to make things worse, the battery is not trivial to find or replace. I have to order an expensive ML2032. With my non-solar keyboards, I would just pop in a couple of AA or AAA batteries about twice a year. Now I spend more on one little battery than I ever did on all the AA or AAA batteries used for a single keyboard. Live and learn. It's like a hybrid car or solar for a house - the cost and extra maintenance does not always pay off in the long run.

I hope my new battery lasts longer than the first. I think Logitech should buy the ML2032 in bulk (10 cents each?) and give them to owners of this keyboard.

title: Great wireless performance and functionality
text:
This is probably the best wireless mouse you'll find on the market right now.

Funtionality:
First off, they brought back smartshift which was one of my favorite things about the original mx revolution and they've upped their game with gesture buttons as well. This mouse effectively has 15 buttons thanks to gestures, which means I'm able to launch almost every frequently used app I use and I have it set to close windows as well. This helps a lot when I need to use a calculator I can just gesture up, do the quick calculation, and close it instantly with no fiddling. Obviously there is more that this can do, this is just what I use.

Comfort:
This feels pretty good in hand, although it's a tall mouse to hold and may be uncomfortable if you use a claw style grip. It's definitely for palm grips which is what I have, and even still it's a bit too tall for my liking. Another pain point is that I have nowhere to rest my ring finger. I have trouble choosing to rest it on the side or change my grip to have in on the RMB, which always feels weird to me. I don't think the other iterations had this problem since the sides always had a little molded grip for your ring finger. I will note the rubber they use on the thumb rest and side with the polygonal pattern is surprisingly nice. There's something about the pattern that feels really good. The vertical scroll wheel feels amazing and the clicks are more satisfying than any other mouse I've used yet, but the horizontal one feels too smooth, and I don't ever know how fast I'm scrolling since there's no click to it. So overall, the mouse feels pretty good, but is not the most comfortable one I've used.

Performance:
This was actually a welcome surprise for me. I found this performed almost as good as my previous wired mouse, and the extra input lag was negligible. Of course if you're a pro gamer or something you probably wouldn't want this, but if you are one, you probably wouldn't be looking here to begin with. For your average game, this is more than enough. I find it's plenty fast for games like Overwatch, where modest speed is important, but I doubt it would be great for super twitchy games like CS GO. Wireless performance has come a long way in the last few years, and this mouse proves it.

Battery Life:
Can't complain, it lasts an absurd amount of time. About a month of regular use on a single charge, or a few weeks of incredibly heavy use. This has always been something the MX line has excelled in, and continues to do so.

Bottom line:
Get this if you aren't a pro gamer and can afford it. If you use a claw grip or have small hands try it out first before buying. This mouse has a lot going for it and is a great buy for almost anyone.

title: simple black with beautiful bronze/brown trim
text:
I have had the Logitech MX Master Mouse for a little over a year now.

I found it searching online for a new wireless mouse that I could use for many years to come. The first thing that caught my eye was the stunning design. The sleek look, simple black with beautiful bronze/brown trim.

I debated for a while before getting this mouse because at the time is was $120 plus tax. I went to the store and the second I put my hand over it, the way it conforms to your hand is like it was made specially for me! It fit very comfortabley in my hand which was a very important for me factor, as I was looking for not only a good quality - nice looking mouse, but one that was ergonomic as I spend a whole lot of time on my laptop. (Using the trackpad for hours on end was not that good for my posture.)

A bluetooth/wireless mouse was important to me as I did not want to have to deal with a wire, and I wanted something easily portable. The nice thing is that you can still use this mouse with the usb wire included (that is used to charge the mouse). Additionally you can set the mouse up to three different computers and with the click of a button have it connected. I use the mouse more than 10 hours a day, everyday and I am able to use it for a good 2-3weeks before needing to charge it. Connecting the wire to charge the laptop, within an hour it is fully charged again!

The only downside is I was expecting a completely bluetooth mouse (not actually a flaw in the mouse)...my 2011 macbook has Bluetooth, but supposed it was not the "correct" bluetooth. Not a problem though, as I plugged the USB-Dongle included with the mouse, and within seconds I was connected!

A great selling feature of this mouse is that you can virtually use it on any surface (greater than 0.2 millimetres!). I can use the mouse at my desk and it has great reaction, yet it works just as great if I'm sitting on my sofa, using it on my bed, my blanket, my leg! It works virtually anywhere you could possible use a mouse.

The Logitec Master Mouse has a Fly-wheel style Scroll Wheel which makes navigating through long pages a breeze. You can scroll slowly, or with the flick of a finger go through pages. Just under the scroll wheel button you will find a little square button. (I will get back to that in a second)

To the left of the mouse, where your thumb rests is a very intrinsic black diamond/triangle pattern, the "gesture" button. To the top of that still on the left side of the mouse, a Horizontal scroll wheel allowing you to navigate large pages to the left and right! Just below (close to you) the horizontal scroll wheel you will find two more buttons, a "back" and "forward" button.

The beauty of this mouse and all the great features is that using the software included with the mouse, you can completely customize every single button on the mouse to any command you want! The gesture button on my mouse brings up all pages open on my Macbook, and that little square button I talked about earlier - well I have set that up to play and pause my music. The rest of the buttons I have left to function as you would imagine, but you can literally set it up to do anything you choose. As well, as mentioned earlier you can connect the mouse to three different computers, saving your own custom settings for each one. This is great as you can have a work computer and set up the mouse to ease your work activities, then have your personal computer and set up the mouse for that with different settings.

Overall I have to say this is the best mouse I have ever bought! 5 Stars!

title: Slower to dry after rinsing than a regular keyboard.
text:
I've had this for several years. I got it at Best Buy when it was on sale down from $40 to $20. I generally avoided rinsing it because it takes about 12 hours to dry which means I do it before I go to bed and the next day go to work to let it keep drying, and then I can use it. At night I'm usually downloading something and in the morning I want to check something on my computer. So early on I rinsed it twice and then I didn't rinse it for a long time.

On my third time rinsing, I wait the long time for it to dry and for an hour it works perfectly. Then some keys stop working at all and others cause multiple keys to trigger when pressed. So I have to use a keyboard software tool where I type each key slowly with the mouse. I also tilted the "Logitech washable keyboard" to dry it faster. Then two hours later I find even more keys don't work.

I go to bed with my computer off and see if the keyboard dries.

In the morning, there's the exact same problem. So I get a high speed fan and aim it at it for hours, turning the keyboard in different directions every so often.

I also leave home looking for a place that sells keyboards. I live in a small town so there was nothing. The closest place that sells them is 40 minutes away driving 80 MPH on the freeway (10 minutes of it is traffic lights after arrival at the town). So I didn't want to go all that way. Keyboards are cheap but most places don't sell them.

So I try to open the keyboard up to manually dry it. The bottom screws are all rusted and four refuse to come out at all. So I pry it partway open and aim a high-powered fan inside for a while trying different angles. I then try again and it still doesn't work.

So I find that prying it halfway open has loosened the screws a bit so I open it up and find it mostly dry inside, just barely damp. So I wipe everything off extra well.

I then notice a clear plastic box around some computer chips inside. The box is supposed to be sealed but there is a crack. On the edges of the plastic I see small bits of moisture condensed. The box has screws holding it together so I try to open those up. These screws are not rusty, but they refuse to turn. So I find a precision screwdriver for really small screws and after a lot of work, only three out of about ten are willing to turn. I then pry part of it open and try to clean inside but can't get all the moisture. I try a fan. I eventually pry some of the plastic shell off and cut it off so it should dry. I also remove some rubber that insulates it. So now the plastic shell which is supposed to keep water out but instead keeps it in will allow water to come out. I then run a high-powered fan inside it until all the moisture is gone inside.

I then re-assemble the keyboard fully and plug it in. I start my computer. I expect to find that I have broken in my cleaning offers. To my surprise, I did not break any electronics. To my horror though, I find that the EXACT same keys that did not work still do not work and the EXACT same keys that did work still work. So I changed nothing at all!!!

I look at the clock and three hours have passed!

So after throwing the keyboard against the floor several times and then throwing it away, I head out to shop. 40 minutes there. Then time spent looking at multiple stores for a keyboard I liked and when I got back 2 hours had passed.

Now I know why Logitech discontinued these items. I had asked them once a year ago repeatedly and they kept refusing to give a reason why.

There are some small businesses that sell "waterproof" and "washable" keyboards marketed to hospitals but I have not tried those. I might in the future. There's even some on Amazon for about $25 instead of $75 which this keyboard is priced at now. They rarely have reviews sadly so I don't know about them.

title: Logitech G502 Proteus - Great mouse but took a little getting used to.
text: The Logitech G502 is a great mouse. Last I checked, it has the most accurate sensor on the market. It also has more programmable buttons than many other optical mice. It's built solid and it works flawlessly. I've read where others have said that you need to use a claw grip for this mouse. I tend to agree that I had to adopt more of a claw grip to use this mouse whereas I used more of a natural palm grip with my Mionix Naos. Maybe that's partially due to the fact I have fairly large hands and this mouse is a little smaller and its form is not ergonomic like the Mionix Naos is. I don't think it's a completely uncomfortable mouse but it does take some getting used to. One feature I'm surprised this mouse did not have is a pinky rest, which definitely would have made it more comfortable. I love my Mionix Naos much better than the G502 both in form and feel, but the G502 has more programmable buttons, which I find useful in my favorite FPS game, Planetside 2. I also like Logitech's software much better than the Mionix Naos since it is a much cleaner, more frequently updated, and easier-to-use interface. Also, since I have a Logitech headset as well, it's nice using just one program for both devices. In game, it's easy to use this mouse once you get used to it and it is extremely accurate. Overall, I'm happy with it and now have both the Mionix Naos and the G502 on my computer desk since I love both of them.

title: Good functionality for price.
text:
I am using this to replace a broken cable provider remote. Over the past few years, I have gotten used to manually switching from one device to another with the buttons on the old remote. I also used to keep each individual remote nearby for the times when the cable provider remote could not do all the functions of the TV, DVD, etc.

The 350 is a very nice change. I was a bit hesitant prior to purchasing, due to some negative comments of the remote not doing everything that the $300 model could do and not having a screen. However, I am very satisfied with what my under $50 purchase can do.

The "Watch TV" action button works correctly to start and stop everything. Most of the buttons can be overridden and the majority even work correctly for the additional devices. For example, when I watch my cable box, the buttons work correctly for the cable box, but the volume and input buttons are still mapped to the television, which makes sense and avoids having to change devices on the remote to simply change the volume. Likewise, this can be remapped to control the cable box sound or an external sound bar,

You will need to program the remote control using a computer, attached via USB during programming.

The top device buttons light up. The individual button do not. You will need to get used to the position of the buttons, but it is fairly intuitive. When you press a button (e.g. volume up), the device button will light up to let you know which device is being controlled.

The Apple TV does not work out of the box. Everything else did. For Apple TV, you will need to teach the 350 using the apple remote. (Less than 5 min activity.)

title: I was really surprised by how much I disliked this device
text:
I was really surprised by how much I disliked this device. It is just way too clever for its own good. There is too much focus on programmability, and obvious basic functionality is missing, or much harder. For example:

1) It takes several button presses to switch between whether it controls the TV, DVR, speakers, etc.
2) There is no "on/off" button - again several buttons and traversing menus are needed.
3) There is no "input" button (for switching between watching TV, DVD, Blu-ray, etc.) - once again menus and many button presses required for this simple function.
4) There is no "view recorded shows" button - a very common thing to do with a DVR.

It claims to make doing complicated things easy, like turning on multiple devices, switching TV input, etc. all at the touch of one button. Half the time it gets that wrong though, because many devices have on/off toggle, rather than just "on", and input cycle, rather than switch to a specific device.

My wife - who is smart but has no patience with unnecessarily complicated technology - never could get the hang of it. I can, but it annoys frequently. I will probably switch back to the harmony 350, or maybe a different brand altogether.

title: That is the main reason why you are getting such a quality product for a great price, because the wires can get a bit ...
text:
I have owned these speakers for a little over a month, and they bring superb sound quality to any room, large or small.
I currently live in USAF dorms, which are a little larger than college dorms. I bought these speakers when they were selling for $60, but trust me, the extra $8 you have to currently pay is definitely worth it. The setup is so simple and quick, the directions are posted on the back of the box. I was able to do it in 20 min from having the package in front of me to listening to music off of my laptop. The bass is deep, and loud or quiet if you please because it is adjustable. It brings plenty of sound to my dorm, loud enough to piss people off from the floor below and above me with ease. At full blast, you won't be able to have a conversation at all with someone next to you.
All cables lead to the subwoofer, which is powered by an outlet with no ground connection needed (the third round part of the plug).

Cons:

I really only have 2 issues with these speakers. The first being the wires. I would buy velcro straps or zipties to compensate for the wiring that comes with these speakers in order for it to look neat. That is the main reason why you are getting such a quality product for a great price, because the wires can get a bit hefty, but are manageable.
The second con is that it does not come with RCA cables. The package comes with an aux cord to play music off of a cell phone or a laptop, and a double cable to play on 6 channel settings, but it does not come with RCA cables. I had to buy them at BestBuy, which costs $18 for a good 8ft cable. Once you go with the RCA cables, I notice a better sound quality than with just the aux cord, but that could be the cord itself, or just a placebo effect, I can't tell. But I'm going to personally stick with the RCA cables hooked up to my TV so I can play youtube music videos off of my XBOX Elite.
In the end, if you don't mind a few wires hanging around and needing an extra set of RCA cables if you want to hook it up to a TV, then these speakers are a fantastic choice. Great, clear, crisp sound quality with deep bass. Great music for all of you lovely Basshead's out there.

title: Perfect in every way except for the one that really matters - CLICKING
text:
It's not easy giving this mouse such a poor review. It really is the perfect mouse in it's design. It fits perfectly in the hand for easy wrist movement. It's compact and sleek. It has just the right amount of customizable buttons. The scroll wheel can be set to be freely-rotating or click-lock rotating. Battery life is sufficiently decent - in fact, if you remember to switch the mouse off when not in use, your batteries will last forever.

But, unfortunately, the most important aspect of any mouse - clicking - falls flat on it's face with this mouse. The mouse actually went for several months before I started seeing any issues. But when the issues started showing up, it just got progressively worse from then on. It'll click when you don't want to. It'll double-click when you only mean to single-click. It'll un-click when you're holding down the button (such as when you're trying to drag something), etc.

At first, I figured I had a dud. But when I saw all the other negative reviews citing the exact same problems, I realized it's actually just a poorly constructed mouse.

title: I Hate This Remote More Than Words Can Express
text:
I wish I could give the Harmony 350 zero stars. That's how much I hate it.

Where to begin? How about this? Want to use your new remote? The one that you already paid for and thus presumably own? Well, you're going to have to sign up for Harmony's site just to do that. That's right, because that's what we all really want in life: another user name, another password to forget ... to use a REMOTE.
Why do I need a password to use my remote? What possible reason can Logitech/Harmony have for demanding my email address before I can use my remote the way it was intended? Beyond harvesting my email, that is? Can anyone think of a reason? No?
Neither can I.
Then there is this: I bought this remote to replace the one I had for my Oppo 93 blu-ray player. But when I use Harmony's code for that player, most of the buttons FAIL to work. The "return" button for instance, to go back through the menu, does NOT work. Okay, but Harmony's going to help me fix that. It says so right on their site: just click "Add or Fix a Command." Great!
So I click on that button, and this is what Harmony tells me
"You are now going to use your original Oppo remote to teach the Harmony remote more about this device."
Great! Except ... I don't HAVE my original Oppo remote. That is WHY I bought the Harmony remote to replace it in the first place. Harmony has to know that a great number of their customers are using Harmony remotes to replace their lost or missing original remotes. Of course they know this.
So what do they say when you click the "I don't have my original remote" button?
Nothing. Because there IS no "I don't have my original remote" button. Apparently, it isn't even in the realm of possibility that you wouldn't have the original remote handy.
So now I have to call support, and deal with all the hell that entails, just to get my Harmony remote to do its basic job correctly. After I already signed up with a new user name and password to use the oh-so-helpful Harmony software.
You know what? I think I'd be better off using a rock to control my blu-ray player. It will work just the same, only with less aggravation, and at least it won't cost me anything.

title: What is a projector?
text:
I recently purchased a Harmony 350 remote hoping to rid my living room of the three remotes that I currently use to watch TV. I currently have an Epson EX7230 projector, a Yamaha sound bar, and a Roku 4. I hoped to replace all of the remotes with your product however, it soon became apparent that this was impossible. After programming all of the devices into the remote, I began creating the “Watch TV” activity. However, the software informed me that I would NOT be allowed to create ANY activities since I needed to have a “display device”. Last time I checked, the main function of a projector is to project video. However, I’m assuming that the programmers of the software have not seen a projector, as most would know that it is in fact, a display device. I’m surprised that your company (based in Switzerland, a country with one of the highest human development scores) created a product with such a flaw. However, I quickly remembered that Switzerland was, in fact, the last Western country to allow women the right to vote (1990 for the whole country). Then it became apparent that maybe the Swiss had never heard of a projector, as the times change a little slower. I perhaps jumped the gun a little too quick living in the United States where most everyone has seen a projector and know that the main function is to project an image (some would even go so far as to call it a display device).
I then contacted “customer support”, which I put in quotations as there is no way, in reality, in which the customer was supported in any way. After I explained my issue (and waited 15 minutes for a response), the lady informed me that there was, in fact, no way to change the software so that the projector would work as the almighty display device. She then proceeded to tell me that in the “database” it is shown as a display device but it wouldn’t work in the remote software and that I would have to manually turn on the projector each time. I stated that I would return the remote as it would be just as useless as the both the developers of the software and the head of customer service. I could understand that there could be a “software bug” in this situation. However, the fact that customer service had zero interest in finding the root cause of the issue, left me with no faith in the company and a desire to never purchase a Logitech product again. I noticed recently that Logitech stock price was up quite a bit in the last year (high five on that by the way). However, I would rather invest my money by means of a Nigerian Prince than buy Logitech’s stock.
On the Logitech website, it states that the “Harmony” 350 provides “One-touch entertainment”. I would encourage the website developers to change the title to include an asterisk advertising that it is more likely able to provide two-touch+ entertainment. I again included harmony in quotations because, according to Merriam-Webster, the definition of harmony is, “A pleasing combination or arrangement of different things”. I’m assuming, however, that the creators of the remote have not investigated the definition of the term, as at no point was there a “combination of things”, much less a “pleasing combination”. The only harmonious part of this process was watching what could have been recorded as revenue on your balance statement, have a “pleasing combination” back into my bank account. I look forward to returning the product and informing my friends of it obvious superiority over other remotes (that’s sarcasm, by the way).

title: Awesome Mouse, Nearly Perfect with One Small Letdown
text:
I love this mouse! I recently purchased a Corsair M65 which I returned because I was very unsatisfied with it, and when spending this much on a mouse I expect pretty much every aspect of it to be superb. Except for one small problem in this mouse, which I'll get into later, it fits this description. It's very comfortable, customizable, and the software is unobtrusive and easy to use. And, unlike the Corsair, all the settings can be saved to the mouse itself so you don't have to be running the software to use the custom settings. Like many others, I bought this to replace my aging Logitech G9X, and it is a worthy successor I think I'll be happy with for a long time.

The only problem I've had with it, and the reason it got knocked a star, is the fact that the mouse wheel is not well balanced. One side is heavier than the other, so when the mouse is in freespin mode a lot of times you'll scroll to the part of the page you want, and when you let go of the mouse wheel it spins a little bit, the heavier side falling to the bottom, which scrolls the page a bit. This is a pain and pretty much makes the free spin mode unusable. In doing some research not every mouse has this problem, but enough that I easily found other people. Apparently it's a quality control issue, and it's a shame because otherwise this is pretty much a perfect mouse.

If free spin is important to you you may want to look at another mouse, but otherwise this is a great buy!

title: Catch this mouse...
text: Ah...the elusive and rare wired mouse.  This species of mouse has proven to be more difficult to track down even in it's natural habitat of online electronics retailers. Once the wired mouse roamed free on mouse pads across the world but these days, they slowly are becoming extinct as the wireless mice have encroached into their territory, leaving fewer and fewer to survive in this wireless world.  Ok, you may have figured out that I am fan of the classic wired mouse ( though I enjoy the wireless variety for certain uses) and this Logitech model is perfect for 90% of my needs including Photoshop, Video Editing, Music Production and regular computer stuff. I'm not a big gamer so I don't need 50 buttons on my mouse with neon lighting and a cooling fan. Ok..I made up the cooling fan part. I was tired of changing batteries in my Apple Magic Mouse and this simple ...er....classic wired mouse does the trick. This model is a well made unit with scroll wheel functionality, side scroll plus two forward/ backward side buttons and it's a decent size for most hands with a comfortable height for wrist support.  So I am doing my part to conserve this slowly fading species...won't you help?

title: Great sounding portable & rugged bluetooth speaker
text: Every bluetooth speaker is a compromise. Even the big JBLs, which sound booming, don't compare to a home stereo. If you are looking for a bluetooth speaker that packs easily and is light for travel, plus can be handled rough and get wet - this is the winner. Anything smaller or cheaper is going to sound cheap (like the Hydra Photive). Anything bigger (like the other UE speakers) will sound bigger, but cost much more and be harder to pack. Plus most big speakers seem designed to stand on end, and good luck with that happening in the great outdoors. This speaker sounds big and warm, packs easy, and straps to most anything - including your iPod if your end up using the mini-plug with a non-bluetooth device. It can even tell you in plain English how much charge you have left! I haven't tried using two of them yet, but you can pair them for stereo even without using the UE app. We like it enough to order a second one, so we'll soon find out. Typically with outdoor sound, spreading multiple speakers gives a much better distribution than turning up a single speaker too loud. So I'm going to get a second one of these and the total cost will be less than the cost of one bigger speaker.

title: Great mouse, but annoying scroll wheel extra functions
text:
Great quality mouse! Logitech always makes really good and awesome mice and this is no different. The wireless receiver fits nicely in the USB slot, the mouse has a nice feel and size, standard AA battery slot, and comes with a battery pre-installed which is nice. All the usual features are there, left/right click, scroll wheel. The scroll wheel is especially wonderful as it scrolls smoothly. The previous logitech mouse I had (M315) had a more rough scroll wheel in that it felt bumpy when scrolling. This one on the other had feels a lot more smooth and when you increase the amount of scrolling in the windows settings, this feels buttery smooth.

The one thing that annoyed me a lot is that the scroll wheel also has a back/forward function by pushing the wheel left or right. I never had this feature in the past. I usually middle click the scroll wheel in the browser to open new tab when clicking a link, etc. But often, I accidentally push the wheel to the left while doing so which then automatically makes me go one page back. It happened almost all the time making it extremely annoying. The good thing is you can disable this function. The bad thing is you need to download the Logitech SetPoint software to do so, so I have to add another non-vital piece of software and clutter my computer. I knocked out one star for this annoyance.

text: Takes a little getting used to, but I think it has helped the fatigue in my hand and wrist from using the computer all day.

title: It's not perfect (see below)
text:
Let me start by saying that I wish I could give this mouse 4.5 stars, but it was either 4 or 5. It's not perfect (see below). I'm not sure where people are having issues with the latching scroll wheel. I've been using the mouse for a couple of weeks now and it is fine. I'm using it for CAD work in an office and it really performs. I've only had to charge it once so far. There are a few things I do not like about it, however. Firstly, the middle mouse click is pretty hard. I don't know if it was designed this way or if I have a bad model or if it's a result of the latching scroll wheel. But it's kinda tough to press. Not major, but it's annoying.
My other peeve is that the mouse is ONLY wireless. It includes a microUSB cable for charging...and that's it. You can use the mouse while it is plugged in, but it's still working wirelessly. Again, not major, but I wish it were different.
There is also no way to store the USB receiver inside of the mouse, as with some other Logitech mice (usually there's a little door on the back that you can pop open and there's a spot for the USB receiver). I would have liked a way to keep the receiver with the mouse.
Otherwise, it's a treat to use. When Logitech says it tracks on anything, they mean it tracks on ANYTHING except air. Wood, formica, laminate, acrylic, glass, you name it. No mousepad? No problem. If you have the software, you can change any and every button. There is a recent update that even allows you to set application-specific functions for each button. The best thing about this mouse, though, is that it can connect to 3 different devices. I can leave the receiver plugged into my computer at work, bring the mouse home, and use it on my desktop with Bluetooth. Why is every mouse not like this?

title: Comfortable and programmable, not a lot of extra buttons.
text:
Pros:
Comfortable in the hand, ambidextrous design.
Scroll wheel switches between smooth scroll and click-scroll.
Unifying receiver means only 1 dongle for both mouse and keyboard (if both are Logitech).
Accurate mouse movement, even on irregular surfaces.
Great battery life.. 3 months and still going strong, should last at least a year.
Somewhat customizable buttons, via Logitech's software.
Logitech's customization software is pretty easy to use, and more in-depth than basic Windows functionality.

Cons:
No quick DPI changing like on some gaming mice.
Middle click button is a separate button right below the scroll wheel (click the scroll wheel changes from smooth scroll to click scroll). This takes some getting used to, and is slightly less comfortable than regular middle-clicking.
Too easy to accidentally hit the side forward/back buttons with your thumbs.
Only two extra programmable buttons (not including the scroll wheel and middle-click button). Could be one or two more.

Overall, it's a great mouse. It might take some getting used to, and for games that would benefit from more programmable buttons it's not idea, but other than that it's comfortable, somewhat customizable, has good battery life, and is a good value for the money.

title: After 3 years, it's still going strong
text:
I ordered this 3 years ago it's still going strong. The vendor was Dealz Dr at the time, so it probably won't show as verified, but I wanted to give my input anyway

Pros:
- Extremely easy to use. Plug in the adapter, it installs a driver once, and it's ready. Just turn on the headset and it connects in a second.
- Comfortable after hours of use
- Collapsible to save space
- Battery still lasts about 4 hours after a full charge, even after having it for 3 years
- The headset sound is great. It's not highdef, but I don't consider this a professional headset.
- The mic picks up very well. Everyone on the other end has said they can hear my clearly.
- Mic is also bendable and swivels in both directions if you want it on the other side of your head
- Works with bluetooth, so I can use it with my other devices as well

Cons:
- After 3 years, the pads are pretty much completely worn down now in the center, but I may be able to have them replaced with warranty, I just haven't checked yet. Keep this in mind to save the paperwork that comes with it if you order it. I can't find where I put mine, probably threw it out.
- The USB adapter is small. I've almost lost it a couple times. Luckily I can always connect it with bluetooth if I need to. It would be great if they had a place you could store the adapter in the headset when you're not using it.
- A pain to switch back and forth between outputting to external speakers and the headset when the USB adapter is plugged in, even if the headset if off. I have go through sound settings and change it, but I end up just physically unplugging it because it's easier. It would be better if the adapter detected that the headset wasn't on, and would shut off the service without having to unplug it.

Despite the flaws, this headset has served me well, and has been way better in comparison to any others I've owned in the past.

title: Good keyboard at first blush, not actually that loud compared to similarly priced products
text:
Going to leave this as 4 instead of 5 stars, because I just got it, but I wanted to address some of the stuff people have been saying about how loud this keyboard is. I've used this thing for several hours now and just can't come up with any reasonable perspective for acting like this keyboard is exceptionally noisy. I suppose if you came from a terrible keyboard like those flat, membrane hybrid covers / keyboards that are being marketed towards people who will barely use them, this thing is loud. I've gone through several bluetooth keyboards though, and like many that use hard (responsive) keyboards, most of the sound is a result of how the user types. The only exception I could possibly be something like newer Mac Books that have keys with very minimal surrounding structure, and thus less to contact and make noise - but in this case those things are the outliers, not this product. This keyboard simply isn't meaningfully louder than any other out there based on its actuation alone. Press it slowly and like many it makes barely any noise at all, type quickly and you get standard keyboard noise.

If a normal ass sounding keyboard is too loud for you not to be self conscious taking notes in class, consider a stylus or some good old fashion pen and paper because there's not a reasonably price BT keyboard out there that's quieter than this by any reasonable scale of measurement. If your friends and / or loved ones are actively mocking you to the point that you feel the need to return a damn keyboard because of how much it's impacting your relationship with them, RMA the people and not the keyboard - you'll be happier that way. [ No, seriously, if they feel it's okay to make that big a deal over a keyboard, take a step back and consider some things.

Other points from other reviews worth noting:
- Yes, the batteries add a bit of size and weight, but they save a bundle in up front cost and while recharging batteries are great they tend to get real hot any time they're drawn from.
- If your co-workers are giving you crap, point out that they're talking about a bluetooth keyboard, quite literally one of the most boring pieces of modern technology, and that they could be using that time to do whatever work they're putting off to comment on it like tweenage morons.
- Not going to argue the thing is a bit heavy, but if you've carried anything other than an ultrabook around, you'll be fine. I'm also a big guy, and could probably lug around a 60lb bag of sand all day without getting too tired, so take that with a grain of... salt.

title: Adequate overall, but the wheel is a huge failure.
text:
i managed to get through a day at work with this, and i'm considering returning it. It's a refurb, but seems functional enough. It didn't come with everything in the retail package, just the cord, battery, and Unifier plug.

First thing i notice is the scroll wheel.

It seems they've done some work so that the fast scroll offers almost NO resistance. To a degree, this is great. But there are few occasions where i want to see how hard i can flip the scroll wheel, go get a sandwich, and come back when it's done.

The wheel is also set kind of deep between left/right click buttons, so the side-rocker is hard to catch with my index or middle fingers. The smooth surface of the sides of the wheel increases the slippage, to where i often don't get it to register a rocker-action. i've gotten used to the M560's wheel that has enough texture to catch, and has a definitive "notch" where the rocker action registers. Performance MX is missing this, and the rocker spring is a little too resistant.

Lastly about the wheel, the one i purchased is EXTREMELY sensitive. Just moving the mouse around can get the wheel to move, which is beyond annoying. i attribute this to the near-zero resistance of the wheel, and wish they'd have stuck with the M560's design. The balancing is off, so that if i stop the wheel in the wrong spot it will scroll itself slightly as the heavy end sinks to the bottom. Also incredibly annoying. The only fix for this slippage is to toggle into ratchet mode, which i don't like that much.

The scroll toggle button is fine, i guess, but a dedicated button for this is wasteful. The M560 make the wheel-click the toggle, with a programmable button behind the wheel, usually used to replace middle-click from the wheel. i've gotten used to that and find it convenient.

i'm indifferent to the other buttons on the mouse because the wheel is so distracting. Getting used to using my thumb for forward/backward navigation would be fine if the buttons were a little easier to reach. The Zoom button is nearly useless to me, and i bump into it accidentally more than i'd like. The base thumb button is also overkill for my needs, and makes me feel like i can't relax my hand without clicking it by accident.

So why did i bother with this if i like the M560 so much?

* i wanted something a little bigger to fit my ham-fists, which Performance MX does nicely.
* i wanted something that is better on batteries. Performance MX promises months of use on a single battery, which sounds great. Real world usage will obviously change that, but at least i don't have to pop the battery out every few weeks and wait for it to charge like i do with M560. i can attach it to the cable and use it while it charges, then leave it to charge when i'm done.
* i wanted a dark field sensor, but it wasn't a huge priority.

i'm going to give it a few more days to see if i can get used to it. If i start liking it any better i may return it anyway for a new, retail package item. However, odds aren't looking good.

title: G933 Review
text:
Having just upgraded from the G930 (had said headset for ~2.5 years, broke due to a structural flaw), the G933 is a welcome update to its predecessor. It fixes most if not all of the problems I had with the 930, some of which I will go into detail here:

1. Lack of 3.5mm jack: One of the most glaring flaws of the 930 was that it did not include a standard 3.5mm audio connector. This meant that it was unusable with mobile devices and other devices which lacked a USB port or the required software compatibility to run the headset. This has been fixed, as the 933 now includes a 4-conductor 3.5mm audio jack, as well as a control-equipped cable designed to work with it. The headset also includes a "passive mode" function, in which the headset powers off, but can still be used as a standard stereo headset off of the 3.5mm port.

2. Aforementioned structural weakness: My G930 broke due to a slight engineering oversight in the connection point between the earcup assembly and the headband. At this point, the metal headband connector is attached to the earcup swivel assembly by four screws driven through a small plastic plate. Over time, this plate weakens and cracks due to the bending force caused by repeated usage. Eventually, it breaks completely, causing the earcup to detach, only being held on by the internal data wire. This design flaw is addressed on the 933, as the plastic plate has been reinforced and thickened to reduce the chance of breakage. Only time will tell if this fix is effective, but I am confident that it will at least help the problem, if not solve it completely.

3. Earcup design: The earcup padding of the G930 worked relatively well - it was soft, cool, and rather durable. However, it had two problems - one, after extended usage, it tended to become quite warm and caused sweating around the ears, and two, it began to degrade after about a year of use. Now, this is not to say that this was not expected. PU leather is durable, but not indestructible. The earcup padding on the 933, however, is made of a multi-layer fabric mesh, which should prove to be superior in both durability and breathability. In addition, it is now washable in addition to replaceable.

4. Battery accessibility: The battery on the G930 was by no means irreplaceable - it only required the removal of 11 screws - but Logitech decided to simplify it further. The battery on the 933 is now accessible by removing a cover on the right earcup held on by 3 magnets. That's it. No screws, nothing. Just a cover. Pop it off, disconnect the battery, pull it out, put a new one in, and done. It's essentially the equivalent of replacing an old HP laptop battery, but easier.

And that just about covers it. I'll update this review if anything significant comes up, but suffice it to say that Logitech has done an exemplary job with the G933, and it is by far a worthy successor to the G930. Every aspect (sound quality, battery life, durability, appearance, etc.) is equal to or surpasses the attributes of the G930, and I hope to have it last another two or three years, at least until Logitech releases the next model in the line, that is.

EDIT: Just found a minor complaint with the 933's design. Both the 930 and 933 include 3 'G-buttons', programmable buttons that can be used for just about anything. I use them for video/music control when I'm AFK (Left, Space, and Right, respectively). However, since the 933 removed the 'Surround on/off' switch, I now have no way to switch between stereo and surround modes with my current key set. I'll be able to work around it, of course, but it's still a minor annoyance. Still a minor flaw in a otherwise perfect design, though.

title: By Far The Best Underrated Headphone
text:
It saddens me knowing that Beats has nearly 2,300 reviews on their Studios with 4/5 stars. This pair matches the Beats in sound quality, comfort, and style while exceeding them in durability. It's a shame that Logitech stopped production for this headset and focused solely on speakers because I truly believe they have something great going on. If they kept going at it I am confident they could have been a top contender for quality headphones. An example of this would be their gaming line up where they're already one of the best if not the best company to get your gaming gear from.

Sound Quality : The headphones are a fun pair to listen to. I'm not a huge headphone enthusiast which is great because majority of people aren't. So I don't know much about high, mids, lows, treble, bass. The best way I can explain the sound is by going to Best Buy, put on the Studios. Imagine that sound without all the muddy bass, and imagine you paying as low as $50 for it.

Durability/construction : The headphones are similar in Beats in plastic feel but less rattle. The cable used is a soft silicone rubber and the headband has a smooth matte plastic. The combination of matte black and glossy plastic is awesome. The earcups are super plush and can be easily worn for 4 hours without heating up.

Conclusion : They're really a diamond in the rough. You cannot beat the price for what you're getting. Two cables, a carrying case, and audio splitter, and a pair of headphones that match $300 ones. They fold up super compact and are perfect for pretty much anyone.

title: Best investment ever! My life has gotten lazier!
text: This remote is simply amazing. It can connect to every device in the house. No more storing the instructions and playing around with codes. Setup is so easy, just plug it into the computer, and tell it what you got. And if what you got isn't on the list, the remote can learn it. Teach it by using the original remote and the program. I also love the fact that if there isn't a button u need, you can add a button to the screen that's on the remote, so you can have 100% functionality of all your devices. My favorite function, hands down,  are the activities. Activities allow you to control multiple devices at once. Example: I'm watching cable and want to play xbox. I press play games activity, the remote automatically turns off the cable box, changes the tv to the right source, turns the xbox and my soundbar on. And now the remote is set to control the volume of my soundbar, the menu options of my tv, and the buttons to navigate through the xbox menus, without have to flip back and forth between different input buttons on the remote. The remote is 100% customizable, set it up for your own personal needs. It has a back light for every button and automatically illuminates when you pick it up, and fully charges in a couple hours for a weeks worth of battery life. I plug mine in over night every couple days. The ONLY bit of negativity I can come up with is: there's no charging dock for this remote, just a plug and wire. This remote is easy to use, easy to to set up, my entire house loves it, and it's fun to show it off.

title: Great keyboard overall, awesome for Windows and Android, okay for Mac OS
text:
I got this keyboard mainly for my desktop PC (Windows) since I don't have a lot of desk space, and it has worked beautifully. The build feels very solid, and the keys have a nice spring to them.

Build quality:
The keyboard feels very solidly built -- I've used other wireless keyboards that bent easily and made all kinds of unpleasant creaking noises. This one feels like a solid chunk of plastic.

Typing:
It is surprisingly satisfying to type on this keyboard -- the keys have a nice spring to them and feel very responsive. I've used other bluetooth keyboards which have what I would describe as a "mushy" key feel -- this one thankfully avoids that. One caveat -- this keyboard is about 1cm shorter than a "standard" keyboard. It's not a huge difference, and I haven't found it impairs my typing at all, but it's something to be aware of.

Bluetooth:
The ability to save 3 different pairings and toggle between them is a great feature that should really be supported by every bluetooth device -- it makes it trivially easy to switch the keyboard between my tablet and desktop without awkwardly unpairing and repairing.

Compatibility:
The keyboard has the ability to automatically switch between hotkeys for Windows, Mac OS, Android, and iOS. For Windows and Android, this works perfectly, and all the keys are exactly where you expect them to be. For Mac OS, it works *almost* perfectly. The Command and Option keys are properly labeled, but if you've used an Apple keyboard a lot, you'll find that the "fn" and "ctrl" keys are in the opposite positions to where you would expect them to be, so your muscle memory might need a bit of retraining.

All in all, this is the best bluetooth keyboard I've used, and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
