title: Great webcam for the price!
text:
Purchased this webcam to use for video conferencing. I am using it with a Dell Precision M4800 Mobile Workstation laptop which did not come equipped with a webcam. The webcam is being used to record a class in a forty-seat classroom. I purchased it because I wanted the highest resolution available, and I am pleased to report this webcam does record video in full 1080p HD quality using the provided Logitech software.

The webcam has a very nice weight to it, with no external controls, since the camera has a well-designed autofocusing system. No focus dial to fiddle with here! The base for the webcam is heavy enough that it can be placed on a flat surface such as a table or a desk without fear of it tipping over. Additionally, there is a rubber non-skid base on the bottom of the webcam that prevents it from sliding. The base folds open to provide a clamp so that the camera could be mounted on top of a monitor. There is adhesive backing inside the clamp to ensure the camera is securely mounted. I was pleasantly surprised to see a standard tripod mounting screw on the bottom of the camera. This could be very helpful if you would like to mount the camera somewhere where there is not a convenient mounting location. Since this feature is rarely seen on webcams, it was a very welcome addition. The permanently attached USB cable is about seven feet long, which should be plenty long enough to use in a desktop or mobile environment. I might add that this 7 foot length is much longer than the Microsoft webcam that I own for personal use.

Setup took less than 5 minutes overall. Obviously, you have to have an available USB 2.0/3.0 port to plug the webcam into. It only required a few moments to install the driver from Logitech's website, and I was up and running. Though the webcam does come with a CD-ROM, I chose to download the latest version of the drivers to ensure I had the newest software. I always recommend you do this for any product, as the CD-ROM does not always include the latest software. The software for the webcam includes a surprisingly good software suite that runs smoothly, requires very little memory to run, and provides basic, easy-to-use image and video recording functionality.

With the webcam up and running, I did a few test calls with Skype, and recorded a couple videos. The caller on the other end said the microphone sounded great, and the video quality was excellent, with only a little graininess visible. A few photos and recorded video from the webcam showed excellent detail, and surprisingly accurate colors, though perhaps a bit muted, as is normal for a webcam. Even with me standing at the back of the classroom approximately 25 feet away, the person on the other end said they could see my facial features and other details well. They could also still easily hear what I was saying.

In regards to the videoconferencing abilities of this camera: the viewing angle on this camera could be wider, but it works very well in its intended use as a personal webcam. If using this for video conferencing in a conference room with many participants, a wider viewing angle may be desired, but there are very few webcams in this price range that will provide a wider viewing angle.

Overall, I believe you would be hard-pressed to find a better webcam than the Logitech c920, at any price. It's full 1080p resolution capabilities, excellent photo and video quality, and surprisingly decent included software bundle make this a first-rate camera for videoconferencing, Skype video calls, or other uses. The tripod mount was a nice unexpected addition as well, allowing a lot of flexible mounting options.

title: Great keyboard/case for iPad Pro. Well worth it's price for quality, durability, and ease of use.
text: I purchased this keyboard case when I bought my new iPad Pro. I absolutely love it! Very nice quality case, with an excellent keyboard. I am using it to type this review, and it is very comfortable. The keys feel very nice, good response when typing. The keyboard has backlit keys, which are nice when you need that extra bit of light to see in the evenings. The keyboard connects via the smart connector on the iPad and very easily clicks into place. The keyboard uses power from the iPad, so no charging, or Bluetooth, is necessary. I haven't used the keyboard for long periods of time, to really know just how much of a drain it is on the iPad battery. So far, the longest I've used it is about 3 hours in one sitting. It didn't drain down the iPad battery very much for that length of time. I really like the size of the keyboard. Feels almost like a full size keyboard you would normally use with a desktop computer! It's just as good as any laptop keyboard. Plus, this one has a few keys specifically for the iPad. I am still getting used to everything, but so far I am very pleased with everything this keyboard case has to offer. It is a bit heavy, but not bad for the quality of the keyboard and the cover itself. It closes nice and has a snug fit for the iPad. I feel this is probably very adequate protection as is, but I also purchased an inexpensive $15 padded carry case for more ease of portability. This is really more for my own particular needs and preferences.  I really do not have any complaints so far. When you aren't using the keyboard, the iPad easily folds down on top of the keyboard, or even backwards if that's what you prefer. There is no slipping of the iPad once you make the snap in connection to the keyboard. It stays put, and you can type whatever you need to get done with ease. Also, the backlit keys will go off, after about 5 seconds of pausing your typing. This is nice, and it helps save on the iPad  battery. There is plenty of room for resting your wrists, forearms, etc., when typing. I still have a few things to learn how to use concerning the iPad related specific keys. From what I read about them, it seems like they will be a nice addition, and very useful. Overall, I have been very satisfied, and happy with this purchase. I even use the box that the keyboard came in to set the iPad and keyboard/case on, in my lap, while lounging on my bed typing. It works nicely for me for that little bit of extra height I need when it's in my lap. I have also just used the keyboard/case directly on my lap, with no difficulty at all. So, I feel this product is worth the price I paid, for the durability, protection, and ease of use. I would highly recommend this keyboard case to anyone looking for a nice quality addition for their iPad Pro.

title: A useful device - when it works as intended
text:
It's a great idea, and the concept of creating your own macros for controlling A/V electronics is well executed. Thousands of obscure items can be remotely controlled with this remote, and the programmable buttons + lighted screen makes operating it simple.

However, after programming the actions into the remote, it will typically work for a week or two and then the actions stop working. Even with new batteries, it will fail to perform the desired function and pop up the "help" screen. Telling it to resolve the problem works - but the remote does not remember that it needed to fix the command sequence, so the next time you do this it's the same thing all over again. It doesn't matter if you turned on/off the devices manually using the Logitech remote or not - it just stops functioning and you have to navigate through the menus to set up your equipment. Hooking the remote back up to your computer and re-programming it restores the actions. For about a week or so, until it fails again. Note that this is not a complete device reset as some people have experienced - the batteries do not lose contact and all manual functions of the device seem unimpaired. It's just the action macros that seem to vanish.

It is nice not to have to fiddle with multiple remotes, but the net effect is that you have to switch between multiple control modes and manually select all the functions unless you want to go reprogram the remote again every week or so to keep it working properly. Too bad, because if it worked all the time it would be quite a useful little tool.

I have contacted friends who also own this device, and sadly they have seen the same behavior. It does seem to be a design or coding problem in the remote, and as such it needs to be resolved before the device can live up to its billing.

I hate the fact that this niche market got driven out of business by inferior products and people trying to use tablets as alarm clocks, but market realities prevailed.

Features:
The build quality is high and the sound is amazing for a compact mono speaker...on par with expensive bluetooth speakers.
Pandora still works flawlessly to wake me every morning. There are endless alarm configurations on this thing -- you set station (radio, internet, local, or network music...it all works) and can choose any combination of day and time, repeat or one time alarms
There are six present buttons that can be set to any music source
The display and background artwork are beautiful...I wish it was one inch larger, but it works
Full control (turn on off, select source, volume, set/change alarms, etc.) from smartphone, although a workaround is needed for newest android releases
Internet time that works...resets itself after power outage, and doesn't lose ANY settings (stations, alarms, etc.)
Auto-dim/bright display based on ambient light.

I will hate it when/if my units die, or the squeezebox service (no longer supported) actually stops working to connect internet music/radio sources, but I've certainly got my money's worth over the years. as much as I love it, I still wouldn't pay the prices being asked for this used, but would buy a working one at a garage sale at a decent price in an instant.

text:
This is simply awesome, the best I tried so far. It has an automatic switch between the ratcheted and "free spin" scroll mode, it basically detects when you hit the scroll for long spin (e.g., when you want to quickly move down a document) and automatically switches to the free spin mode, when the scroll stops it moves back to the ratcheted mode.
It takes some getting used to, but once you do - it's really missed in other mice. I also use the MX Performance (which is also great), and I tend do find myself missing the auto switch between the modes.
One down side to that - 6 month after I bought it, and I noticed that auto-switch is not working as well as it used to (tend to get stuck on the "free spin" mode and needs to be clicked a few times to go back to the default ratcheted).
The horizontal scroll was designed like a touch pad, the clockwise direction scrolls to the left (it's really counterintuitive) - but luckily that definition can be changed through the Logitech app.
Other than that - it's a great fit to the hand.

title: Great bang for the buck, highly recommended for those with realistic expectations!
text:
I'm working on getting my father to use a home computer on a regular basis, and purchased this set of speakers so he could have some decent sound. After lurking and reading piles of reviews for a couple weeks I decided upon this set for a few reasons, foremost being Logitech's solid name. Secondly was the power factor, for the price range this little system provides good sound and fills a good sized room with ease. It's not a 100 watt system, nor does it sound like one. But you won't find many systems that squeeze this kind of sound from this size and price range.

After hooking it up we went through a few youtube videos, and then I introduced him to the 20GB of music I loaded onto his system and it was on from there. We kept the volume at a reasonable level, no more than half to allow for easy break-in on the speakers and we were both impressed. We'll see how they do over time, but I'm expecting them to only get better.

The remote is slightly clunky and can be a bit of a pain to operate, but we've also both got fairly large hands and I'm used to struggling with lightweight intricate items with my ham fists. If one had a somewhat permanent location decided I would recommended some velcro or something to keep it fixed in one spot. But that's just me and I understand my flaws as well.

Most of my pc speaker background is in 2.1 systems and I really do prefer them for their compact form factor. Sure I may not get surround sound, but I don't want it or need it for my PC. With that in mind, I can't say enough about this set of speakers. I've had or purchased 10 sets of varying computer speakers over the years and these are already in my top 3 for value, sound and construction. I'll update this if things change, but for the time being I can't recommend this set enough.

title: Does what is says it will do ... which is the problem
text:
Bought this to replace my Harmony 650. The 650 had two drawbacks: 1. It is flimsy and cheap-feeling; a few drops and the buttons don't push 'cleanly'. 2. If you have a setup with a cable box, an AVR and a TV, you have to keep the remote pointed at your devices (like Deadwood's Richardson wielding his antlers) while it works through the power on sequence. (For those unfamiliar, the Harmony 650 steps through the power-on sequence for each device in serial fashion - a real user experience breakthrough. Instead of manually switching modes on a typical universal remote as you seek to control each device, the Harmony devices know what you need to do and switches for you, finishing with a set of controls that makes sense - volume controlled by the AVR, channels by the cable box, etc.)

The Harmony Smart control solves the two drawbacks. Its handheld remote is more solid (not like a rock, but not as flimsy and cheap-feeling). And because it sends the command to a relay box instead of to the devices directly, you initiate the sequence and put the remote down; the relay box serially fires off the infrared signals to power on your devices.

That's all good, but the user experience after that is not great: The remote does not have a display, so when using it, you are somewhat back to the 'mode' problem of less-sophisticated universal remotes. For example, there are three buttons that start sequences - listen to music, watch TV and watch a DVD by default. Want to watch Apple TV? Reprogram one of the buttons to initiate Apple TV when you press and hold it. Now memorize which of those buttons you programmed to do that. Want to go to a favorite channel, one of the strengths of the Harmony 650? The designers of the Smart Control system push you to a phone or tablet app to manage that. This is less than ideal. With unlimited space, the user interface designers crammed everything into that, making for a very complex interface. Want to adjust the picture setting on your TV? Find the screen mode in the TV control to open the menu, then swipe to the mode that allows you to control the cursor - before the menu automatically disappears because no input has been detected (in some cases with my TV).

While it is common to use your phone and tablet while watching TV, this system forces you to do so. So now I get to drop my phone instead of my remote. And cobble together a system where I use my phone or tablet for some commands, my relatively dumb new remote for others, or fish for the device-specific remote out of the bin.

The strength of the Harmony 650 was its relative simplicity - which is, after all, the major selling point of a universal remote. The Smart Control does what it says it will do, but it is a step backward in terms of simplifying things. This is a hard user interface problem. This device doesn't solve it, and in some ways, makes it worse.

title: Glad I bought it!
text:
I purchased this product in late December when the official Apple version was out of stock. I was skeptical based on some of the reviews but I have been more than satisfied. It offers great protection and solid functionality to my iPad Pro. One comment that keeps coming up in reviews is how hard it is to install the iPad into the case. I had no problem and never felt like my iPad was in jeopardy of being broken. Yes, you need to apply some pressure to snap the corner into place but nothing unreasonable. Once it's in, it's in! If you need to take the iPad out of the case, bend the corner of the case. It's flexible and unless you store it in a freezer, there is no fear of breaking it.

Having owned a keyboard/case for my old iPad2, I never expected this new keyboard to transform my iPad Pro into a laptop. It simply adds a quality keyboard for word-processing and a good case for protection.

Pros:
- sturdy construction
- excellent grip so there's no fear of it slipping out of my hand
- large keys and good "feel" when typing
- back-lit keys are helpful in low light conditions
- top row of iPad functions are helpful (Home Key is a real plus)

Cons:
- A bit heavy but a fair trade-off for protection
- Really needs a solid surface to maintain contact with smart connector
- Could use an option for keeping the backlighting "on" rather than quickly turning off after a few moments of non-use.

title: Initial thoughts (Updated after use)
text:
I just picked up this case today at Best Buy (out of stock at Amazon). So far my thoughts are positive. This case does add some bulk to the iPad profile but it adds a TON of utility. The keyboard is easy to type on and has a lot of advantages over the Apple Keyboard Cover such as backlit keys, function buttons and coverage for the entire iPad instead of just covering the screen. It isn't hard to open (as some of the previous reviewers have shared) and I really like the fact that the case / keyboard uses the SmartConnector in place of Bluetooth. Aside from being one less thing to worry about charging the assembly creates a very stable setup for lap typing (which cannot be done with the MS Surface). All in all I would highly recommend this case for someone using the iPad Pro for content creation or business purposes.

Follow up thoughts
After owning this case for about a month and a half I have noticed the coating on my iPad Pro showing abrasions and wear due to the case. I also experienced maddening lag on keystrokes. At first I thought it was app specific, but the issue only seemed to get worse as time went on. I finally retired the case and went back to a smart case and carrying a separate Bluetooth keyboard (also Logitech) which performs excellently. I love the concept of this case, but it literally has damaged my iPad and the time it takes to correct keystrokes was enough to push me over the edge. I'll leave my original review for full transparency and to show I have this a legitimate chance.

Update 8/1
Just a final update on this review, I recently purchased the Apple Smart Keyboard Cover and while doing so, I explained to the Apple Store rep my experience with the Logitech Create damaging my iPad. Apparently this is a known issue and the iPad was replaced under warranty.

title: BUYER BEWARE - CASE CAUSES NOTICABLE SCREEN DAMAGE
text:
Just wanted to jump in here and say that I, like many others - was an early(ish) adopter of the iPad Pro and Logitech keyboard. I purchased both on Jan 27 2016 and after months of light use experienced an issue that many others are having - when closed, the connectors at the top and bottom of the keyboard press into your keyboard and cause irreparable damage to the screen. If you do a quick search of "iPad" + "Logitech create" and "scratch" or "damage keyboard" you will find several forums (with photographs) of frustrated customers who love the functionality, support and protection that the case provides (granted it's a bit heavy) but after a month or two of use find that their screens are being damaged.

Even more frustratingly, it appears that people who choose to contact Logitech with this issue are having their claims denied and have to live with the fact that their brand new $1K iPad was damaged by an expensive Apple-endorsed third party product, and they'll likely have to pay out of pocket to have the screen repaired.

But I like to focus on the positive :). On the positive side, you'll also read of many people who go into their local Apple Stores where they purchased the iPad and keyboard and once they point out the damage (and all of the chatter and photos on online forums outlining the same issues) their local Apple stores will happily exchange the IPad and refund the money or offer an alternative keyboard (theirs) - plus any price difference, with little or no questions asked. Such was the case with me.

Some small details: I purchased my iPad Pro on Jan 27 2006 and on the suggestion of the salesperson at the Apple Store, bought the Logitech keyboard instead of the IPad keyboard - he suggested it would protect the back and front of the iPad as well as offering more stability when I wanted to use it in bed or on my lap. I have to admit - I really did love the keyboard - until this month when I noticed the same lines that I saw in the online forums. At first, I thought that I would be able to remove them, but when they were readilly apparent during a presentation I was giving two months later on March 22nd, I knew I had to try to see if Apple could help me.

Yesterday I returned to the Apple Store where I purchased the iPad and showed a repair person the keyboard and links to several forums where folks had the same issues. He was fantastic. After going through the motions of also trying to wipe off the scratches, he immediately set me up with a new iPad, and I paid the difference for the new keyboard.

I should also mention that don't typically carry this iPad around in a bag where it can get compressed by other things. I usually carry it in a sleeve and put it in my purse - so it's not likely any undue compression caused this. Just think the simple act of closing and opening it over time caused it. Bums me out too, because I actually really liked the keyboard.

I'm hoping that Apple realizes that this is an issue and stops selling the keyboard. And hope that Logitech pulls the keyboard until they can resolve the problem.

Hoping others find this helpful. I have to say that I really did like the keyboard a lot. It's just unfortunate that it caused damage to the screen.

Good luck with whatever you choose!!!!

title: Great keyboard that probably will ruin your screen
text:
The keyboard itself is quite decent, if a bit heavy. The iPad Pro comes quite close to a laptop PC experience, just as I hoped. There are some quite irritating key-drops and wonkiness that probably will be resolved in iOS 9.3, so until iOS 9.3 is released you should be warned that this can make the keyboard unuseable for you. But I' m in it for the long run and can wait. The cause for the delay is probably that iOS currently does not support delivery of firmware updates through the proprietary connector. Based on this, it deserves 4 stars.

However, this keyboard is also supposed to be a screen protector. Instead, it will probably end up ruining your screen.
Carrying the device in a moderately full bag will press the lower metal part of the keyboard into the screen. Since the cover is a bit wobbly in the hinge, this metal part wil rub against the screen continously when you walk, making a horizontal matte stripe on your screen over time.

This is easy to see simply by looking at a closed device sideways against a bright light source: The screen rests against the keyboard frame. The rubber wedge that is supposed to prevent this is simply not enough.

The wear is slow, as the screen is tough and the metal is not sharp. However, I expect a lot of users with this complaint in a few moths time. I must say I am very surprised that this could pass QA, and will be interested in having a response from Logitech.

I've owned this case for just under a month at this point. I reserved my comments to give it some time to be used. I want to be as fair and balanced as I can with this review, so I will proceed, pro/con style. If you'd like to save yourself some time, please feel free to jump down to the con list. It's short, but important.

Pros:
• Construction: Overall, the construction of the device is nice. It's weighty, but not unwieldy.
• Key Travel: The key travel is what you would normally expect from an Apple-style keyboard. Nice and solid.
• The nylon cover is nice, and does not feel cheap.
• The magnetic closure works well. I haven't had any issues with the cover falling open.

Cons:
• If you're looking for an efficient method for scratching your iPad screen, this keyboard cover will take care of the task handily.

Seriously, my screen has some nice nicks in it with *careful* use along three weeks. I'm concerned about its continued use, but there are not any immediately available alternatives. I'm disappointed.

Edit / Update: It's not just nicks... The ridge on the front edge of the keyboard has abraded the screen, leaving a cloudy line on the surface that runs the width of the screen. title: Not just worst keyboard, but the worst product I've ever used.
text:
Let me preface this by saying that I've been a heavy user of technology for 25 years - and that prior to this disaster of a keyboard case, Logitech was my favourite brand of keyboard.

I got an iPad Pro to do two main things: word processing for reports, academic papers, etc for my job as a healthcare professional, and for drawing and editing for my job as an educator. Believe it or not, this Logi Create keyboard case not only makes my performance in these activities worse - but as it has irreparably damaged plenty of users' screens - it could potentially independently render my $1000 iPad useless.

It ruins your typing experience: this keyboard has some issues either staying "on", or connecting to the iPad for any period of time - thus as one types, the repeated 'disconnects' makes it so that you get to type half a sentence, stop because your input randomly stops being registered care of a random disconnect, wait for the backlight to come back on to indicate that you are re-connected, then finish typing your sentence (if lucky enough to have it remain connected for the duration of that one sentence. It is an absolute disaster.

It damages your iPad: the keyboard case has two metal areas that are often in contact with your iPad screen when the case is folded closed during transport or storage. Over even short periods of time, the case will erode your screen's protective coating, and start to irreparably etch long lines into the glass of your $1000 iPad screen. Look it up.

Furthermore, despite these two often reported issues, Logitech has yet to create a solution to a) apologize to its users for this expensive mess of a keyboard case, b) address damage done to screens, and c) provide an update (in conjunction with Apple or not - whatever the process is) to address the random disconnects between keyboard and iPad. It's insane. It's poor customer service, and reflects so poorly on Logitech as a company. I've seen Logitech claim that a public beta of iOS 9.3 fixes the issues - IT DOES NOT. Do not be fooled.

Mine is slated for return - and unless you want your expensive tablet damaged, or your productivity to drop precipitously - yours should be too. Give me a good reason why I'm wrong, Logitech.

title: Nice, but WHY NOT BLUETOOTH?!?
text:
This is a great touchpad. Gestures are perfect every time, and it's thin and light. ONE MINOR ISSUE. The glass cracks easily. I shattered mine within a month. It was at the top, so I just threw packing tape over it, but I thought to call Logitech to get a repair cost as well. They sent me another brand new touchpad for FREE! 2 thumbs up to Logitech! If you take your T650 out at all, you're bound to crack it, so keep the number handy: 1 (646) 454-3200. There's almost no hold and you can even keep your old touchpad and receiver, which is nice because even cracked mine was still usable. I gave it to my dad and he doesn't mind the cracks and loves it.

One minor annoyance is the requirement for a Unifying receiver. I know, I know, it's better than bluetooth, yada yada yada, and it saves battery, but damn, when you only have 3 working USB ports, losing one is a killer. Thus, it lost one star. If you have a MacBook Air, this brings you down to ONE USB 2.0/3.0 port, which is absolutely awful in 2016. Pitiful really. Shame on Logitech for not using Bluetooth, or at least not making a BT model available. The Unifying is NICE when transferring between PCs, but I would still wanna see a BT model.

I got mine on eBay for $20 new (damaged box), and that price can't be beat.

When I press a button - for instance turning up the volume on my home theater - the screen will go blank and I cannot operate the remote any further until I pull the batteries out and reinsert them after waiting several seconds. I tried new batteries - same result immediately. I searched around on the internet, and followed a suggestion to "put something (e.g. foam or toilet paper) behind the battery cover" because the battery terminals are not snug - same result. Finally, I synced the remote with the MyHarmony software - same result.

It's a shame. I have received many compliments on how the remote ties everything together in the living room, and up until today I have recommended the 650. Unfortunately, I will no longer praise this product to friends and family. I gave two stars because it worked for almost a year, and if it weren't for an obvious software issue I would continue to use/recommend it.

title: Good initial impression, died after several days
text:
I was initially pleasantly surprised by the headset. I got it as a replacement for a pair of Gamecom 780s that had the headband snap of death several months ago. As a previous 7.1 surround sound junkie I can confirm that this headset has excellent 7.1, and the bass is surprisingly deep for a pair of headphones.

My first disappointment came with the included micro-usb cable, whose "ears" (the locking/reinforcement pins that stick up on the underside of the connector) were so stiff that they gouged a rut in the plastic leading to the micro-usb port on the headset. The other disappointment was discovered upon opening the storage cover for the USB adapter, one of the magnets' glue had come unstuck from the cover and the magnet was attached to its mate on the headset, leaving the glue-pattern exposed and an empty magnet hole on the ear cover.

I enjoyed the sound so much that I grabbed a spare micro-usb connector, set the headphones on a hanger, and let them sit and charge for several days while I went about my business.

Unfortunately tonight I sat down to try and play something with them, and lo and behold they would not power on. Flicking the power button causes the rear LEDs to "breathe" about 2.5 times and then abruptly shut off, as if the headset isn't charging. I tried the recommended trick to unplug the battery, plug the headset into the USB connector and micro-usb and force a firmware update, but the firmware will not update because the headset is not turning on. When the microphone is pulled down no LED light turns on to indicate that it is muted. No combination of battery in/out, USB adapter plugged/unplugged/direct plugged, resets, restarts, and letting it charge/rest between toggles did any good. I've sent the headset back for a replacement and will hopefully get a functioning set to update my review and experience with.

As it stands I'm very disappointed with this headset. It's a fantastic idea, and had all of the features I wanted. I am under the impression that you pay for quality, and this experience flies in the face of that expectation.

title: Simply a wonderful piece of tech!
text:
I don't have a ton to say about this mouse, but I felt it deserved the 5-star anyway.

I'm no "power user". I'm not a video editor nor do I do any work in spreadsheets. I'm just a normal guy with a laptop (MacBook Air) hooked up to a monitor.

Originally I bought a Logitech M320 to use while the laptop was hooked up to the monitor...I liked the 320 just fine, but it's small; it's a travel mouse basically. I won't sit hear and say I have anything but medium sized hands, but now that I've gotten used to having the laptop plugged in to the monitor I was ready for something more "full-sized". I had been eyeing the MX Master for a while..mostly because of YouTube videos like those from MKBHD. Maybe it's the car-guy in me, but seeing them sculpting it out of clay like a vehicle really stuck with me..

To the point, this thing is amazing..in both looks and feel. It fits my hand so well I find myself fondling it for no reason. It's an odd thing I know, but this thing is just so nice. The thumb rest area is very comfortable, and it can come in pretty handy. I don't find the gesture button, as they call it, difficult at all to depress. By default on my MacBook it deploys Mission Control to help switch between apps or open windows and that works just fine for me. The back/forward buttons are also no problem to hit with the joint or tip of my thumb, but my thumb is not your thumb so hopefully it'll work just as well for you!

If you want to treat yourself to a nice mouse that'll do pretty much anything you want, go ahead and do yourself the favor. You don't need to be a business pro, a YouTube-type video editor or whoever it is that works with spreadsheets. This is just a sexy piece of tech anyone can enjoy (assuming you don't need a left-handed mouse). With the Logitech Options app there's a ton of customizability, if you're into that kinda thing. Obviously serious gamers can probably look elsewhere for more suitable devices, but besides that I'd recommend this mouse to anyone!

title: Very happy with upgrading to this mouse.
text:
I've been using this mouse now for 2 months, after having used the Logitech M705 for a couple of years, and I'm loving the MX Master!

Here's what I like:
(1) The shape of the mouse is very ergonomic for my hands, it is much more comfortable for prolonged use. It moves very smoothly on my desk surface.
(2) The automatic free-wheeling feature of the scroll wheel I found surprisingly nice, and I now miss on other mice.
(3) The battery life is fine, I think it lasts me a couple of weeks per charge for work.
(4) You can recharge the mouse while using it, so you never have to worry about battery life!
(5) Flexible connectivity: The mouse can connect to any Logitech Unifying receiver (I used one I already owned) as well as via bluetooth. The button on the bottom of the mouse let's you switch between three pairing modes which I find useful as I have the 1st mode set up to pair with my desktop, and 2nd mode to pair with my laptop. This means you can get more use out of this expensive (but good) mouse.
(6) The software. Logitech's software makes it easy to pair with multiple devices with your Unifying receiver, and it also has a battery low notification for this mouse reminding you to charge it.

Here's what I was concerned about initially, but I'm now okay with:
(1) The awkwardly placed forward button. The back button is easily accessed, but the forward button you have to pick up your thumb and move up. I was worried about this before buying, but because I use the back button much more frequently I have found it doesn't matter for me.
(2) Coming from the M705 which uses regular batteries but lasts about a year per set, I was worried about going back to a mouse that needs regular charging. Since the battery life is pretty good and you can recharge while using it's not a problem.

Here's what I'm neutral on:
The side scroll wheel is nice, but many applications don't support it so it doesn't really matter much for me.

Overall I'm very happy with having spent $75 on this mouse, it's a big improvement over my old one. The biggest thing for me is the ergonomics and good wireless functionality, but there are lots of good features.

text:
I love the wireless headphones. If you've never tried wireless headphones, you should definitely give these a shot. It is night and day not having to worry about a cord touching your arm, hitting your keyboard, or getting caught in your computer chair wheels. The range is about 40 feet (through two walls from my office, through living room, and into the bedroom), at that point the audio would start to cut out.

They're also comfortable. I have an average to larger size head being 6 feet tall. Unlike the cheap computer headsets I've used in the past, these do not put any pressure on the top of my ears. Looking at you, Logitech. Re-make this mouse with a unifying receiver and I will gobble that up in a heart beat.

title: Good Product Overall, But I Still Consider It A Downgrade Compared to the MX Revolution
text:
This would be a joint review of MX Master and MX Performance, both of which I returned with some disappointment. I am a long time user of MX Revolution and have always been looking for a worthy replacement when my MX Revolution started having minor issues after 4 years of use.

I first bought this MX Master, but returned it after trying it in hands in exchange for MX Performance. I browsed the reviews on Amazon and saw that many people share my issues. Thus, I would like to voice my opinions in hope that the Logitech team will tack into account the views of us loyal users, so that the next generation will display improvements.

Overall, MX Master is a very well-built mouse. I think that the design, make, weight, and texture all live up to the now $80-ish price. My problem with it mainly lays in the ergonomics and ease of use. I almost completely agree with Aaron’s three-star review, so I’m just going to quote him.

1. “It's more uncomfortable than my old Revolution MX mouse - my hands aren't large enough, I guess - and it has a sharp ridge between your thumb and index finger (along the palm) if you don't hold it exactly right.”
I agree, this sharp ridge definitely does not feel as great as MX Revolution’s more smooth ridge. I switched down to MX Performance for the reminiscent MX Revolution shape, but found that the design of MX Performance wasn’t quite as comfortable either. It features less support for the ring finger and the pinky finger, as the part where these two fingers rest on are more “taken in” compared to that of MX Revolution.

2. The thumb touch/gesture button: I liked the idea of it, but it is a lot harder to press compared to the same button on MX Performance.

3. “The forward/backward buttons are too close, so you can't just flick your finger and expect to get the behavior you just want.” Exactly. I also want to comment that these two buttons are placed a bit too much towards the back, so they are a bit hard to access and take a bit extra effort to hit precisely.

4. “There's a dedicated horizontal thumb scroll wheel, rather than a tilt on the main scroll wheel like other mice tend to have.” I would very much prefer if this wheel has some “stoppage” like the main wheel (sorry I don’t really know the exact word for this) instead of just having a smooth, continuous scroll. The main reason for this is that when I use it to switch between tabs, it is difficult to have a precise sense of how much scrolling corresponds to how many tabs switched.

5. I don't mind that the battery for MX Master is not replaceable - so long as the battery life does not start shorten after a year or so like the iPhones. However, I did find it convenient that you can kind of store the dongle in the MX Performance by putting it in the battery compartment.

What I liked about the MX Master:
1. The automatic switching between free scroll and normal scroll is back. I noticed that on MX Performance, you’ll need to manually unlock free scroll, while I am used to having my MX Revolution automatically switching to momentum scrolling mode. So it is great that this feature is back.
2. The corded charger instead of the charging port that MX Revolution has.
3. Great battery life. I began to feel this is especially important after I experienced the MX Performance battery problem - the battery level goes critical 20 mins after I unplugged the charging cable.

title: Solid performer - recommended! One small note though.
text:
I must commend the Logitech M510 Wireless Mouse for being a solid-feeling and inexpensive device. The receiver is small enough to work with a laptop and be inconspicuous, and the easy-to-toggle power switch on the bottom makes turning it off to save batteries easy. The mouse feels a little heavier than a wired version with the batteries in - that takes a little getting used to and I had to tweak my windows mouse settings but no big deal there.

The two side-buttons (programmable, of course) - have a soft-push feel to them, not clicky, but are comfy to use. I get a lot of precision when using this mouse and would recommend it for anyone who is just sick of yet another cord in their computer setup. Me, I was tired of my cat laying on the cord when he sleeps between keyboard and monitor. Problem solved!

There are those who will tell you a wireless mouse is terrible for gaming, but I disagree. The real potential problem issue is a little more complex. For example, the third time I used this mouse, when operating it I heard strange scraping sounds from the front yard of my house. I opened the blinds and saw nothing at first, so I went back to using the mouse... heard it again. This time when I looked, I noticed some fir-tree rounds that had been sitting by the rubbish bins from a recent tree we had cut down had been dragged halfway across the lawn and left furrowed trails of moist brown upturned dirt behind. I reached down and gripped the M510 again and moved it left and forward, and watched the sections of wood drag a torn pathway through the rhododendrons growing along the edge of the lawn and then crunch into the side of my neighbor's Land Rover.

Needless to say there was a little bit of insurance paperwork to do, and I had to call in an Earth Wizard from the local council of elders to alter the frequencies of the magical force-lines around my property.

After that - smooth sailing! Can't recommend this mouse enough, but do be careful.

title: This system is AWESOME and EASY TO SETUP...ignore the bad reviews
text:
Not sure why this product has an overall mediocre rating. I've used universal remotes for 15 years, and am so impressed with this system.

PROs:
- setup is user-friendly!!
- setup is fast!!
- app is excellent
- love the included remote, great feel
- great compatibility for AV gear
- highly customizable
IT JUST WORKS!!!!

CONs:
crickets.....

In less than an hour, I unpacked, setup, and configured this harmony remote connected to ** 9 ** systems. It hardly could have been any easier or faster. I spent another few hours tweaking and fine-tuning my configuration, but connecting 9 units with everything working in under 1 hour was just awesome. Hats off to the Logitech UX team...very very well thought out.

Sony Android TV - 2016
Denon AV Surround Sound Receiver (HDMI hub for most of the devices) - 2008
Panasonic Blue Ray - 2008
Xfinity DVR
Xbox One
Apple TV Gen 4
Amazon Fire TV (4K)
Google Chromecast Audio
Whole House Nest

Plus, added specific remote activities inside Android TV included on the Sony TV:
Netflix
YouTube
Google Play

Note the mix of the devices, how two are very old. All of these worked without entering any special codes, only needed to enter the make and model number. All setup in under an hour!

Setup:
The wifi base went right in my AV cabinet. I added the included IR blaster in one other location just for additional coverage. I used the Apple app to install (so smooth).

Started with a helpful video in the app. Then everything after was step by step. No guessing on what to do next. The app provided tests along the way.

The app searches for Hubs and Devices....even easier.

Kudos to Logitech.... this unit was a refurb, previously used. During the initial setup, the instructions clearly called out I should see a blinking red light. Mine was red. What next? The app told me to press the resync button on the back, which was easy to find. And even better, did not require some crazy "press for 10 seconds while pushing another button through a pin hole then praying to a rain god for a reset". No, a one second press of the button that was super easy to find, and the unit was blinking red. I didn't need to restart the process, the app moved along without skipping a beat.

Next I added all 9 devices, after each, the app tests to make sure these work. All the devices connected on the first try except the TV. When looking for the Model, the app returned an error. I just tried a second time and it worked.

Most of the activities worked great right from the start. I did need to add a delay to a few activities as Amazon Fire TV seems to send keep-alives to the TV, and after switching to the new activity, the TV would flip back to Amazon. This problem had nothing to do with Harmony, and the app allowed me to simply apply a fix.

APP:
The app is 5 stars. Easy to use. Connects via wifi to the hub (better than pointing remotes, right) My kids understood it instantly without explanation. They loved the ability to change the volume using their volume rocker on their iphones. My oldest thought that approach was too annoying and instinctively found the screen controls.

Here is one of the very best features..... the app requires absolutely ZERO user registration when loading the app on additional mobile devices. You install the app via the app store, and the app finds the hub and loads the full configuration. No logins required!!! So any guest (grandma, friend) who stops by for a while can control the AV just by connecting to your wifi and a quick app install. No need to share your username and password, and no need to spend 15 minutes explaining "use this remote here...that remote there...." So well thought out by the Logitech team. Awesome work Logitech!!

REMOTE:
Feels great in your hand. Excellent weight distribution, responsive buttons, great grip. Logitech: your design team spent serious cycles refining this remote and it shows. Nice work with the customizable short press/long press buttons. Nothing fancy, just enough buttons to get the job done, intuitively.

UPDATE: Voice control with Alexa is supported. OK, now its time for an Echo.

The remote is missing one feature:
- backlight. I give Logitech a pass here, and in fact believe the lack of a backlight may have been an intentional omission to preserve battery life and/or reduce the overall remote size that is needed for the extra batteries. My last two harmony remotes *** constantly *** needed new batteries (because of the backlight). But, a backlight would be really helpful (often dark when watching TV). My suggestion is to add a dedicated backlight button that turns on the light, with a dedicated battery (if that battery for backlight dies, the remote still works).

Which I will plan to do. My love/hate with harmony remotes over the last 10 years gave me serious pause to buy another. But I'm a big fan again. Great work Logitech in keeping me loving your products!!!

UPDATE 11.27 ----
Still love this remote. I've since purchased an Amazon Echo and am underwhelmed at the integration. Essentially, you can tell Alexa to turn off and turn on activities, but it seems you cannot control functions (like mute, volume down, volume up) and even more importantly, cannot dictate searches within screens (for example, "Alexa, search netflix for Midnight in Paris"). So for now, the Alexa integration is a 2/5 stars. But still love the overall setup of Harmony.

title: Don't bother with any other Blue microphone.
text:
As a small-time streamer, the Blue Yeti is pretty much everything I was looking for in a microphone: sensitive enough to pick up my voice at a decent volume without needing a pre-amp and able to adjust volume on-the-fly. This thing is a 100% improvement over the Snowball, both in sensitivity and in general build quality. If you don't want to screw around with software-based amplification and you don't want to spend hundreds on a pre-amp, this is the microphone you want to get.

Unlike the Snowball, the Yeti offers two key features that make it far less of a nightmare to stream with: a hardware-based amplifier and a headphone jack so you can hear what the microphone is going to be picking up. This largely eliminates the need to deal with software-based amplification and having different settings for different programs. What's also nice is that it removes the need to be raised and lowered in a simple "microphone-on-table" setup. Once it's facing right-side up, the Yeti will pick up everything quite nicely, though you may need an arm stand if you plan on using it for recording a band or something.

The Yeti's default stand is also a lot more sturdy than the Snowball's is - the entire stand is solid metal, and while it weighs far more than the Snowball does, there's no danger of the stand breaking or succumbing to fatigue over time (especially given that you're probably not moving the mic around on the stand a whole lot).

The only downside to this microphone is the price: at over $100, it's definitely an investment compared to the $60 Snowball - but if you plan on doing anything more serious than using it for voicechat, it's well worth it.

This didn't seem to mesh with the other reviews saying it has perfect audio quality and can pick up footsteps from halfway across the room. Upon further inspection, I found that the sensitivity selector switch on the back of the microphone had a plastic plate glued over it and that the switch was in fact not there at all.

Given the other reviews of this microphone, I can't tell if it's a bad batch or if it's broken by design, but in any case I would avoid this microphone and pay the extra $10 for the real Blue Snowball.

16 December update to review::::::
Harmony Hub works great with Echo. I bought my Harmony Hub back in November and it was great having Alexa turn on my audio/video equipment (Apple TV, Roku, Stereo Receiver, Blu-ray player and TV). title: I'm on my 3rd one in 5 years
text:
I have a love/hate relationship with this keyboard. I'm a fan of the look, and the low profile keys, and the solar recharging is great; doesn't eat batteries like other wireless, although you need to keep it in relatively bright light as it ages. It keeps a full charge wonderfully for the first year or so, but after that it needs more and more light to operate.

I have owned 3 in 5 years, and I'm about to buy a 4th today. I have one my workplace that has lasted longer than both of the ones at home, probably because of the 16+ hours of bright light it receives. Once the ones at home hit less than 25%, it's a waiting game as to when they'll die. Just this morning I was using my ~3 year old one at home and all of the sudden I start getting double characters when pressing a key - br fo b, h/ for h. Then the power button stopped responding and the keyboard would not turn off. I tried all support suggestions: remove battery, unpair and repair - which it would no longer pair, uninstall and reinstall driver. Nothing. Keyboard is now dead.

Very frustrating to be sure. Unfortunately, I love the design so much I'm willing to shell $50 out every couple years to keep it.

title: I bought this having owned a previous generation of Logitech ...
text:
I bought this having owned a previous generation of Logitech remote (and two generations of Monster remotes before that using the same backend), but this has been the most consistently frustrating technological experience in recent memory. This remote works perfectly 60% of the time... which lulls you into a sense of technological bliss... and then everything falls apart... leaving you feeling despondent, angry, frustrated and alone. You sit down for a Friday of Netflix and everything turns on but the TV.... "Help" does nothing but turn on other devices you had no interest in (PlayStation, I'm looking at you).

Bonus... I get more exercise getting up from the couch to turn on the TV manually using the little joystick on the back that's only there for people in the year 2040 who still have a Samsung flat screen but lost the remote two moving companies ago. I also now know the difference between OFF, STANDBY, and ON on my Denon receiver... because walking over to it and physically pressing the power button cycles through those. Neat.

Technology. Thanks Logitech.

UPDATE: Decided to go back through my old Amazon reviews and realized that while I was initially negative, this remote has ended up being a workhorse for us. It kinda just works now. I haven't had to update it in months, and it just does what it's supposed to do. To be honest, I've had a couple of moments where it's occurred to me that when this dies, I'll need to shop for a new universal remote, and I dread it :).

We do now use the iOS app more than we used to, and it works well. The remote and the app stay "in sync" as far as current system state quite well.

title: Thoughtless and Arrogant Company
text:
I bought this primarily to work in conjunction with the Apple Remote AirPlay which I use for streaming music to multiple areas of my house. I have four stereo receivers - 2 older Kenwoods, a Yamaha and newer Pioneer - which I am able to control using the Harmony mobile app for iPhones. I am also able to control a Sony TV, a Vizio TV, a PS3 and a very old Panasonic CD/DVD player. There's no universal remote on the market that can compare with this!

I had no problems with the download, installation and set-up on an iMac, iPad, iPod and iPhone but using the computer version is the preferred method for configuring the hub. I bought a second IR blaster and a 25 foot extension cable plus a few adapters to use in a second area of the house and it works with no loss of signal.

I'm not that crazy about the programmable Activities - you have to disable HDMI CEC/ARC - or the handheld remote but they may be more useful to someone with different needs than mine. My rating for this product is really a 4.5, after about a month of testing and usage. I'm hoping in the near future that Logitech and/or Amazon will get this product to work with the Echo, and then it will be a 5.

UPDATE: Over time, I’ve purchased three of these specifically because they worked disconnected from the Internet. Now that Logitech has forced its customers to use an Internet connection - by forced I mean pushing unwanted firmware updates without the customer’s knowledge - I can no longer recommend this or any similar product they make.

title: Shoddy customer service and support cripples a potentially awesome device.
text:
Good theory; poor implementation, worse service.

I used to love my harmony hub. Then I got a PS4. After finding the software update that would let me use my harmony to control the PS4, it's finally hooked up. So. How does it work?

Not well.

Any time I try to switch from my PS4 to anything else, the hub puts the PS4 into "Rest" mode. There is no way to change or disable this. Logitech's customer support has known about the issue for months, and doesn't do anything about it. (Their forums have complaints dating back to June of last year). The worst part is: it's a custom sequence that the system goes through, so it would take about 3 seconds for any competent engineer to fix this, and about 4 minutes to make it a customizable option.

I tried to fix it myself by updating the device, but Logitech's "Harmony Smart Control" center is so dumbed down that you can't set any options yourself, and the options you can set don't work.

I've previously had a lot of issues with the communication between the hub and my Comcast DVR, which I had always blamed on Comcast (because everyone hates Comcast). However, after this, I'm starting to think maybe Logitech is more to blame.

So, final thoughts:
Ease of setup: 3/5 (annoying to get everything working)
Range of devices: 5/5 (the one place it shines)
Usefulness: 2/5 (it works the way one engineer wants it to, but not for the customers)
Customer Support: 0/5.

Final thoughts: Don't buy ... unless you have one TV, one movie player, and one stereo, and just want to be able to control your system from your phone or iPad for "coolness" sake.

I had my doubts whether this was going to work but it is actually working really well. The set-up was extremely easy and took about 10 minutes. The set-up took me through everything step by step and picked sensible default settings. I was surprised to learn that the hub works perfectly fine just from my iphone. Setting up the physical remote is just a last step at the end. I placed the IR blaster that comes with it on top of the amp and it is able to both control my projector on the other side of the room and the amp even though it has no direct line of side to the amps ir receiver. I am very happy with this device and I am recommending it to all my friends and family.

title: This Will Change Everything...
text:
Game changer. I have been running the Logitech G5 with 18 grams of weight for years. Not like 2 years, but like 6. I think the G5 is on its 4th or 5th set of skids (feet). The G5 is still great and functional, but I felt it was time for an upgrade with new features. Things like no mouse acceleration, better DPI, and more buttons.

Well...this mouse is it. I know there's a lot of reviews on this product already, but OMG this sensor. So accurate, so precise, and what feels like zero acceleration. The pointer just goes where you want it. The Logitech Gaming software is great. Lets you adjust all sorts of things and enable extra features. Best part is: If you have other Logitech hardware on your machine, it will detect those too. I have a 1080P, stereo mic, video conference camera from Logitech and it let me adjust new options on it as well. The sniper button seemed pointless at first, then I used it in CS:GO and Overwatch. Turns out it's extremely useful.

In one 2 hour sitting, my accuracy in game increased dramatically. Target tracking is so much better now with no acceleration. You will not regret buying this.

The comfort level is exactly the same as my G5. I was worried it wasn't going to be. The G5 is just such a perfect fit for my hand and that's why I kept it for so long in service. The thumb indent is perfect, the size is a good fit for medium to large size hands. The scroll wheel being either clicky or super smooth with a push of a button is a nice feature.

A few Pro Tips:

1. Get the Logitech software. It allows you to calibrate the sensor for your surface and it DOES make a difference. The lighting effects are cool too.

2. Tweak the DPI setting to what feels good for you. The pre-programmed ones are good, but if you're picky take the 5 minutes to tune it in.

3. Go play some games and feel the difference.

tl:dr - Great mouse. No regrets. Buy it.

title: Very good mouse that broke after a few months of use - managed to figure out what the problem was and make it usable again! YAY
text:
I have been pretty happy with my mouse, until it started behaving strangely, as described below. I really like the mouse despite its shortcomings so I really wanted to figure out what the problem was and get it fixed. If it hadn't failed after such a short time, I would definitely have given it 5 stars despite what I consider to be it's shortcomings :)

I have had the Logitech MX Performance mouse for just over a year now. I have been pretty happy with it, although I did disable all the extra buttons as I kept accidentally pressing them, causing me a great deal of annoyance.

About 3 weeks ago I encountered a problem with the mouse which seemed to be with the left mouse button. While holding the left mouse button to select text or such, the selection is randomly dropped, causing great annoyance and also sometimes resulting in text being moved around in a document etc. - in other words, the mouse is not usable. After browsing the web for info on what the problem might be and not finding anything that made sense or described the problem I was facing, I ended up contacting Logitech support who offered me the option (or non-option in my case) to RMA the mouse through the retailer which is a few thousand miles away from me.

I decided to not bother with RMA as it would probably cost as much or more than the mouse cost me initially and instead dissect the mouse to see if I could figure out what the problem is.

There are videos on YouTube and elsewhere which show how to open up the mice so I won't go into details about how that is done.

The top part of the mouse has those few extra buttons and a battery status / DPI LED indicator on it, which are connected to the main PCB via some wires with a plug on the main PCB end which can be disconnected once you have the mouse open. I started by disconnecting this plug and then tried the mouse again which resulted in the problem having fully disappeared. So it seems that the fault is connected to the charge / DPI setting indicator LEDs, or the extra buttons or related circuitry. I don't use the extra buttons and actually find them to be more of an annoyance than anything else, so I was in fact delighted to find out that this solved the issue. I may dig into it deeper at some point and update this post if I can pinpoint the problem better.

To open up the mouse you need to either remove the PTFE pads/skates from the bottom of the mouse, or figure out where the screw holes are and drill holes in the pads to get to the screws (should be possible to find accurate enough photos of the base somewhere online). It is not easy (or perhaps even impossible) to remove the PTFE pads without ruining the double sided tape that holds it in place.

title: Big dudes rejoice!
text:
I was blown away as soon as i plugged these in. I had been looking forward to an upgrade from my Astro A50's, and after a long time of researching I came across these pair of god sent headphones.

Battery: You can't ask for a better battery on high end headphones like these. On a full charge with lighting off, you get 12 hours which is near perfect for long session gamer's. The battery is replaceable and the box should provide two batteries( mine did not), which means pretty much 24 hours of uninterrupted gaming.

Lighting: This was mainly what I was looking for in a headset, and while it did go beyond my expectations, i don't use it at all in order to prolong my battery life. There are plenty of basic patterns to choose from like color cycle, breathing, solid color, or customize your own. This option could be used to sync your other logitech spectrum rgb lighting support items like the mouse or keyboard.

Comfort: Being mostly a long session and hardcore gamer, i've done short and long sessions from 4-16 hours of playtime mixed with hearing music or watching netflix. These feel really comfortable and i've yet to have an issue with how comfortable they feel. Compared to other headsets i've had like the hyperx clouds, which would get uncomfortable within a few hours. Say goodbye to sweating, shifting sides, taking breaks to relieve the pressure on your ears.

Build: I was sold when i saw all the features, and i wondered if it would fit my head correctly and not be loose. I'm a pretty big dude, 300lbs+, and I'm pretty sure now i need an XXL football helmet(the size of my shirts.) When the headset arrived, I noticed it was a bit small and instantly got really worried. After about three weeks with them I can't even feel them and my ears are having the time of their lives before they go deaf. Now sadly, where I have to slap Logitech's hand is, their build quality. In close up inspection, i noticed my lighting strip was scratched on the right side, and had a little bit of left over building debris on the left. I figured, minor imperfections isn't bad at all for these babies. That's when I decided to put them on, these make a squeak when putting them on or shifting the ear cups to the sides as if i needed WD-40. Once I noticed the squeaks, I noticed the headband cushion is slightly missing out of place, but with enough room it can be easily removed if pulled. It was inserted wrong and the only thing keeping it in place is the adhesive placed throughout the headband to stick the the plastic.

Microphone: I did not physically test this for the purpose of finding a microphone that is so good that it can hear wind moving in your room. I only used it over skype and TS3, where everyone heard me clearly and there was no issue.

Pros: Battery(12-24 hours, or infinite plugged in)
Very comfortable
Price is very affordable considering this is a high end headset.
Sound channels(Dolby 7.1 for movies and music, DTS X for gaming.)
Cord Length: I believe its near 10 ft, it is a Micro USB for those who care.

Cons: Replaceable battery option that is not provided via no extra battery.
Macro buttons: Little to no use, no easy distinction between the three unless programmed by yourself.
Build quality.

title: The logitech MX Master is hands down the best mouse I've owned in the past 20+ years
text:
The logitech MX Master is hands down the best mouse I've owned in the past 20+ years. I love the gestures of my Apple Magic Mouse but my hand cramps and the ergonomics simply don't exist with it. That said, I had to find a replacement and the MX Master fit the bill. I have used this mouse now for several months with my iMac and my Macbook Pro and needless to say it works flawlessly. The software (downloadable via the Logitech site) offers the ability to heavily customize this mouse with gestures, actions and infinite scrolling. It is comfortable to use and the functionality fits well with my workflow. I have used it both with a bluetooth connection and with the unifying dongle. The only hiccup I experienced was with the dongle being in a USB port that is too close to my power supply cord. It causes the mouse to act wonky with random cursor disappearances and slow response time.

My only complaint with this mouse is the battery life. It is rechargeable and can be used while charging. Once the mouse is charged, it lasts about 4-7 days with heavy use (8-10hrs a day). For the pricetag of $99 or so, I would like to see battery life improved as I believe it can be with modern advances in battery life and performance. Overall, this mouse is a win. I wouldn't hesitate to purchase another.

The Logitech Harmony Smart Control is a terrible product and I'm shocked on all of the positive reviews. I have always been a huge fan of Logitech products and owned their universal remotes, mice, keyboards, and speakers. I've always raved about them, until now. This product is a disaster. I am now on my 2nd device after the first one was deemed defective by Logitech product support. I am having the exact same set-up and communication errors trying to set up this one as the last. I have tried so many different ways to get this to work using both a Windows 10 and Windows 7 laptop. I've also tried to setup just through the Harmony app. I have factory reset the hub and updated the firmware multiple times throughout the set up attempts to no avail (btw, for those who need to try this just hit Alt-F9 as the Harmony program is launching on your laptop and walk through the steps). When you buy a product designed to make your life easier, you don't expect it to waste more time than it saves. I am now returning this 2nd device and am very disappointed with Logitech.

On a side note, Amazon has been very good in managing returns throughout.

title: Really silent and a nice comfortable mouse with virtually no setup required.
text:
[[VIDEOID:9812ea950c2cba1f2e730ef5a9a5598d]] The Logitech M330 is not only truly silent, it's truly easy to set up, too. It is bigger than most Laptop Mice so it is really suitable for Desktop and Laptops. It's comfortable in my palm and there was something very cool about that silent factor. It makes the buttons feel substantial. The base of the unit has everything you need to get up and running, including a two year battery. The tiny usb receiver is in there, too.

To use your mouse, remove the USB receiver and plug it into any available usb port on your computer. Turn your mouse on with the switch on the bottom and there is nothing else you need to do (well have something to put under it if your surface is too reflective). It's an optical mouse so the precision is remarkable but can be adjusted with your own computer mouse software (you know things like, scroll speed or if you wanted to assign different functions for the left and right buttons).

I tried this on both Windows and Mac laptop and on both it worked without a second of hesitation.

The signal between the mouse and receiver is really strong. It will shut off automatically so you don't have to flip the switch when you're done. It's made by Logitech when does tend to make very compatible devices for Windows and Mac based machines.

title: Incredible remote when paired with Harmony Home Hub, MUST HAVE
text:
Upgraded my Logitech Home controller with this one. Paired with the Home control base, this remote is VERY powerful, it is effectively now a Ultimate Home Touch setup and got this and the home controller for less than half the price of a Ultimate Home touch setup... not to mention have an extra remote now. I won't comment on this remote without the Home controller.... you are crazy not to buy the Home controller if you have this (unless you only need the really basic IR features... but if you want to control your FireTV or other bluetooth devices, or you Philips hue lights, all can be done with this remote if you have it paired to a Home control base).

I have a rather complex setup that this remote works flawlessly with (again paired with the home hub). I have a 55" 4k Vizio TV, a Sony soundbar, and Xbox one with a TV tuner and a FireTV attached to it's HDMI passthrough, and Phillips hue lighting. (I've also had other devices setup previously, including a TV tuner box before I started using the Xbox tuner).

With activities setup, with one touch I can turn on everything I need to do any task I want (from watching live TV, to the FireTV, to playing games, or listening to music), and I can quickly switch between devices I am controlling (ie. from the Xbox to the Fire TV).

What I also love (probably due to the TV and Sound bar being new), I've previously had issues with smart controllers because if the device was out of sync from what the controller thought it was (ie. you used a different controller or button on the device to change an input or power on/off) the smart controller would get out of sync ALL the time, and be more of a pain than useful. But because my TV ad Sound bar can go to any input directly (so it doesn't matter if the remote accurately knows which one its currently in) not to mention has different ON/OFF signals than just a Toggle ON/OFF, I finally have a complete setup that my smart controller ALWAYS works correctly. **If you are using older devices that don't work like this, pretty much EVERY smart controller will have the same issues, and I know your pain... it may be worth upgrading your hardware, i can't explain how nice this is finally after many years of attempting to use smart controllers. Just make sure you always use the smart controller if you are in this situation.

As I said, I upgraded my Logitech home control's simple remote with this one. I really like the UI on this one, simple buttons and the touchscreen does exactly what I need. Beside the obvious changes, there's a few more things worth mentioning:

1) My old remote for some reason had 1 issue... the volume down worked somewhat badly (I could not figure out why, all other buttons worked perfect, and I even programmed a different button to volume down and that did not fix it... not to mention, you can control the sound bar volume either with the TV volume or directly, and both had same issue). Basically I had to hold down the volume down button for about 2-3 seconds for it to finally lower the volume (all other button, including volume up worked on a simple press almost instantly). With this upgraded remote, finally my volume down works just like everything else.
2) Everything is more responsive. While the original remote was quite adequate in speed, almost instantaneous when pressing buttons, this one is even faster. Everything responds pretty much instantly now. Also, switching between activities/devices is significantly faster now, and definitely much easier with the touch screen showing me exactly my activities (no more memorizing, and having to tell friends which button is which)
3) I finally can control my Philips hue lights from my TV remote. It's easy to change the brightness of any light, as well as switch between scenes... quite happy with this additional functionality.

As I keep saying, the Home hub is basically a must have (and easy to find between $60-$80), paired with this remote, and you now have an Ultimate Home hub setup. While the original remote did it's job, this upgrade was worth every penny (not to mention got a great price on this remote in slightly used, like-new condition). For the combo (with an extra remote) I paid less than $120.... for more hardware than the $300 Ultimate home controller. Also, with the hub, and the amazon echo.. I now have complete voice control over all of my equipment.

title: Great bluetooth wireless mouse
text:
I wanted this mouse specifically because it is bluetooth. My notebook has bluetooth. This means you don't need a little USB plug in piece like the standard wireless mouse.

I've had this mouse for a few months now. It works perfectly. I paired it once and have never had any problems with the connection. It reconnects right away whenever my laptop wakes up. I'm using it with a Lenovo ThinkPad. No problems with battery life, like every Logitech wireless product I've had. The scroll wheel and buttons have very good clickiness. I did not install any special software for the mouse. The buttons are fine with the stock driver: left, right buttons; the scroll wheel scrolls and tilting left and right goes back and forth through the history in a web browser; and the small middle button below the wheel works as a task switcher.

The bottom side has a power switch. I use this when I throw it in a bag to travel, to save power. That way the mouse won't wake up every time it's moved around.

I'd definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a wireless mouse that uses Bluetooth and not a little plug in transceiver.

title: All-rounder. Precise. Solid. Feels like a $100 Mouse without SCREAMING "Gamer, Gamer". Just Perfect.
text:
The Amazon cat dragged in a Proteus Spectrum for around a $97, including $17 shipping. I gotta give it to Amazon. They always ship earlier than promised. Got this in like 5 days to the UAE which is nice.

So far I'm having a good experience; better than my previous G700s

Pros:
- Very solid make. Better than other Logitechs I've had before, including the G700s. Feels the money's worth. You do say it must be a $100 mouse when you see it, feel it and use it.
- Good fit. Not exactly as small as what others suggested, but still not bad. Ideal for: PALM GRIP, not exactly Claw unless you have large hands.
- Lighting is good. Not overdone but not missing either. Logitech is always on the more decent, sophisticated and professional side of things. It doesn't SCREAM "GAMER" so gamers and professionals alike can opt for their gear without second thoughts. RGB Spectrum gives you 16.5 Million colors or whatever.
- Nice soft braided, durable cable.
- Weight balancing options.
- Software.
- Options: multiple switches, sniper DPI button, on the fly settings, continuous or step-by-step scroll adjustment
- Solid buttons and feel.
- Great tactile feedback of almost all the clicks.
- DPI accuracy and precision.
- In short, it's good for gaming, accuracy (Photoshop etc.) and just general use. Not much competition there.

Cons:
- May be a bit on the heavier side, but that's purely because of the components (I think).
- Sniper button is a bit farther than I can easily reach.
- Continuous scroll sometimes keeps moving. Maybe less accurate to control because of that. Scroll wheel is a bit... loose... like generally. Still, no remorse.
- They said it's SMALL or TINY. It's not. I guess it's a good coincidence that it has a good fit for me, otherwise I think there are much smaller mice out there (Abyssus, Krait, Spectre for example, are all much smaller, and though they are a great fit for me, though don't pack as many features as I want to have).

Will share more thoughts as and when necessary, if necessary. So far, this is indeed the best mouse I'VE ever had. I did skip R.A.Ts and Corsair for this so, let's hope I stay happy.
