title: Amazing mouse, but unreliable.
text:
Maaan, I loved this mouse so much. It was hands down, the best mouse I'd ever used. Until it broke after less than a year.
I've had this mouse about 10 months and it's already broken. First of all, I have a few little nitpicks.
This item came with scratches. There were little curved lines in the finish on the LMB and on the palm. It doesn't affect anything, but it was a little disappointing. Another is the braided cable. I'm not sure if it came like it or maybe the cable just doesn't fit in the outer braid correctly, but the braid split randomly and the plastic wire came out. The extra weight on the side the wire popped out made it imbalanced.

Here is why I'm giving it a two-star review rather than a four star. Let me paint a picture for you;

I'm in the middle of a game of Overwatch, and suddenly the screen doesn't move at all. I start testing it, opening the Logitech gaming software, (which I never used past reprogramming the sniper button.) reinstalling drivers, and unplugging the mouse back in and out. I even restarted my computer to no avail. But while I was unplugging it, I noticed something strange. The dpi profile indicators were a static green, and the G logo was pulsing from green to teal up and down at random times. I didn't even have the lights on breathing either. And it was still unresponsive. As far as I know, I didn't think there were green LEDs in this thing. (I can confirm, this wasn't the Spectrum.) So I plugged it back in and the G logo was pulsing from teal to blue. The indicators were still static. I did it again and the G logo was blue and all of the other lights were all gone. Now I have a pretty paperweight that shines blue. In case it's windy I can make it a little bit heavier to make sure the paper doesn't fly off. Yay.

Edit: It's been a year and I decided that I would like to figure out what the heck is wrong with the mouse.

It was such an obscure and random looking issue. Someone had probably seen something like this before! I spent 3 days doing nothing but looking for fixes for this mouse, to no avail. No one has seen the problems that I seem to have. Strange. I contact customer support, and they take a few days, but respond back to me respectfully. Asking for a lot of technical information for the mouse. I don't expect much from this considering my relationship with Logitech Customer Support in the past, but they send me an email another 2 days later saying that they're replacing it for me. They were very respectful and professional. I'm still giving this mouse a three-star because it's not entirely reliable considering it broke within a year the last time. It hasn't come in the mail yet, but I'll come back to this a year later. If it still works, I'll give it a four-star. That would mean that the one I got had some weird factory defect.

Edit: Still using the mouse a few months later. The wire braiding has frayed already, but it's not a problem yet. No bugs I've seen. Still, love it.

Final edit: My journey with the G502 seems to have finally come to a close. The lights started flashing different colors on my replacement model randomly. That doesn't seem like much of a problem, but along with that, the LED's on the DPI indicators stopped working as well. After trying to press buttons to test if they worked I didn't realize that I wouldn't have been able to set it back to my original setting without an annoyingly large amount of experimentation and time that I just didn't care enough to invest, considering I wasn't able to see which DPI setting I was on, let alone the profile. I just sent it back to Logitech and I've requested the Logitech G403. If possible I would have gotten the new Razer mouse, the Basilisk. It's a lot like this mouse, but fewer buttons, lighter, and 10-20 dollars more expensive depending on where you get it. I've heard it was good, and it has some interesting features as well. Obviously I couldn't have gotten that through the warranty because it's a Razer mouse, but I've also heard a lot about the G403. I will make a review on that once it comes in the mail, and put a link to the review on this one as a bit of a continuation.

title: Stay far away.
text:
Logitech makes quality products. I have owned or used mice, keyboards, webcams, and headsets by logitech, and they are all very reliable pieces of technology. This controller, however, is not.

I have owned three of this controller. Yes, it took me three tries to learn that this is not a quality product, and I regret having spent 60 dollars over the course of those three purchases, when I could have just bought an xbox 360 controller, or the F710 for the same price.

In its defense, the controller feels nice, has well placed buttons and responsive sticks. It's a good weight and really reminds me of the PS2 controller. And that's the end of this controller's pros. To be fair, it only has one con, but that con is a game changer: the wiring is faulty. Remember those three controllers I've owned? Each one died thanks to a short in the wire, and none lasted me more than a year. The short in each controller originated very close to or AT the solder point where the wires meet the PCB, so fixing it was either out of the question or extremely difficult in every case.

Save your money. Buy the F710 or an Xbox 360 controller instead, if you absolutely have to have a wire.

And while I have a wireless mouse already (The little Logitech M305, which has sadly been discontinued: [[ASIN:B003HC2FHE Logitech M305 Wireless Mouse (Black)]]), I thought the small size wouldn't be as comfortable to use daily, so I decided to buy a full-sized wireless mouse to replace my desktop mouse.

I first tried a different full-sized mouse from Logitech (I can't remember the model number), but that one made the end of my ring finger go numb. So I bought this one...and hated it. It gave me horrible hand cramps, so I went back to my wired desktop mouse and use my tiny wireless mouse anytime I'm away from my desk. Even though it's small, it's way more comfortable than any of the full sized mice I've tried so far.

This mouse gave me horrible hand cramps for two reasons: its physical shape, and the way it tracks.

1. Its physical shape: it has too narrow of a "waist," which caused me to pinch the sides of my palm together (moving the base of my thumb toward the base of my pinky), and any tool or action that causes me to hold this position for very long invariably makes my hands horribly sore for the next day. There is no way I can use a mouse for a reasonable amount of time if it causes me to assume this position and gives me horrible hand cramps every day.

2. Its tracking: It doesn't seem to track well on the surfaces I need it to (for one, it hates the texture of my desk). I remember I had trouble controlling where the mouse was going, and that was one more reason that led to me holding my mouse with a death grip and led to horrible hand cramps. The movement was jerky and I felt at times the cursor was flying away from me.

I wish I could have returned this thing back when I bought it. Instead, it's been sitting in a drawer wasting space ever since, and every time I see it, a very small part of me gets mad again.

title: I LOVE this thing.. but..
text:
I LOVE this thing!

(Though I thought it was rather pricey)

This is the ONLY Logitech brand product that I own that I actually LIKE*

This is the OLDER model that still contains the older firmware which allows selection and/or entry of NON-LISTED internet radio stations (the newer AE firmware has this great feature REMOVED!).

I use this product OFTEN and it doubles as a nice CLOCK for my bathroom, too :)

I use this product to listen to my own internet radio station, and, for what it is, it sounds GREAT! It has very nice bass (lows) and nice crisp treble (highs) when sitting on my bathroom counter :)

The only things wrong with it are:

1.. it doesn't have THAT great of a battery life- its not bad.. about 4 hours or so.. but, its not super-great either.. (please note: it takes a SPECIAL battery and its NOT INCLUDED!) also, when running on batteries, it won't be a good clock unless you don't mind "waiting for it to turn on"; this can easily take up to THREE MINUTES of time - to read the time... WOW! and...

2.. another thing to keep in mind, is, when you turn it on, it will ALWAYS "call home".. and, thus, DISPLAY YOUR NETWORK'S IP ADDRESS on the Logitech website in Korea which it now REQUIRES access to in order to work (it didn't used to do that.. used to work without logitech.kr peeking in) and Logitech does NOT employ a strong password and/or encryption either.

Oh yeah, and one other VERY ANNOYING thing.. VERY IMPORTANT! Whenever they FORCE an update, ANY security settings (such as setting the SHELL ACCESS PASSWORD, for example...) will be RESET to its default.. This means ANY hacker who has your network's IP address (remember? they can get THAT from the Logitech website!) can LOG INTO the product's SHELL PROMPT and have a LAUNCH ACCESS POINT onto your home network! So, this has to be WATCHED and CHECKED from time to time.. I have had my network "broken into" as a result of this thing receiving updates and resetting the shell access password.. yes! they CAN gain access to this thing via the web right through Logitech's website in KOREA! luckily, at that time, I had it isolated and they didn't get far in, however, they DID have enough access to set up a DDoS node from within my network and caused EXTENSIVE DAMAGE to the network connection itself!

* Other than that, it really IS a GREAT sounding product.. just don't "leave it plugged in, on the net, unattended" for too long.

title: Best Keyboard Ever
text:
I have 2 of these - one at home and one at work. I've been using them for about a year and can confidently proclaim them my favorite keyboard of all time. Why? (1) It's wireless. No more tug of war. Put it anywhere you want. Any time. Simple. (2) It never needs batteries. Ever. No more batteries conking out midstream typing. No more fetching batteries and finding something to stick in a tiny hole so you can re-introduce the wireless to your computer. Simple, again! (3) It's lightweight, well organized and the keys have a nice feel - sort of tight but not overly so. The keys feel a little "deeper" than some, so you know when you've made contact - and there's a satisfying click when you type. If you like a very shallow key feel, maybe you won't love this aspect of it. This part's hard to explain and a matter of preference - but it suits me 100%.

As for the level of light needed - no particular light requirement. This keyboard works perfectly in both my home office and my work office. Neither keyboard sees any direct sunlight. I've never had any problem even on the cloudiest day in the middle of January in New England.

Oh yeah, and it was super easy to set up- just plug in the USB and you are good to go. I love this keyboard! Thanks, Logitech!!

(3) It's lightweight, well organized and the keys have a nice feel - sort of tight but not overly so. The keys feel a little "deeper" than some, so you know when you've made contact - and there's a satisfying click when you type. If you like a very shallow key feel, maybe you won't love this aspect of it. This part's hard to explain and a matter of preference - but it suits me 100%.

As for the level of light needed - no particular light requirement. This keyboard works perfectly in both my home office and my work office. Neither keyboard sees any direct sunlight. I've never had any problem even on the cloudiest day in the middle of January in New England.

Oh yeah, and it was super easy to set up- just plug in the USB and you are good to go. I love this keyboard! Thanks, Logitech!!

title: The updated M510 mouse
text:
This review is for the returning M510 users out there. If you've owned this mouse, you should know that that Logitech has changed the design a little bit. Along with their new logo, the new "2nd Edition" M510 (missed opportunity by not calling it M510S or something) now also sports a "laser-grade" optical sensor, as opposed to the old "actual laser" sensor. After doing a deep dive for some information, the internet scholars on a couple first-page forums have confirmed a few facts for me. First, the optical sensor is not necessarily a downgrade. Laser sensors have inherent issues - some complaints on the old 510 were that it exhibited cursor stutters, jitters, and shakes - and the modified design is likely to address those concerns. That being said, laser sensors have higher a DPI resolution, which should mean that they are more precise. Conventional wisdom might make you hesitant to purchase this new M510S (my nickname for it). Why would the 'newer' model have LESS DPI's? What an outrage!

Well, let's be true millennials and talk about how it feels. The optical sensor feels smooth and rounded, yet agile and lively. It's actually really enjoyable. The cursor "acceleration" on the older version became more pronounced while using them side by side, and it started to get annoying after I actually noticed it. Without subtle wiggles, the overall experience is more precise.

Fortunately, the folks at Logitech seem to be pragmatists and have figured that, while they took away some of the super-awesome DPI's, the mouse actually performs more satisfactorily during real-world use. After doing way more research that I bargained for, I found out that most people would agree too.

I wish the change was more clearly communicated, though. I almost didn't even open the packaging because I thought it was counterfeit, so my first time using it was littered with skepticism. I wrote this review because I don't think I'll be the last person to go through that.

If you currently own or have owned the 1st version M510 and want to replace it or get a second one but are now reluctant because it's a different design, just buy it. That's the beauty about this thing: a mouse is not something worth obsessing over, and it just works well.

title: Not worth the $$$
text:
I cannot believe this thing sells for $350. I received this free from Logitech because the previous model I had battery blew up.

The touch screen is the worst idea conceived. There in no longer a number pad. You have to use the touch screen. About 1 out of 5 times when you press the screen it doesn't select what you pressed. It swipes the screen to the next screen. When it does actually register the selection the delay is excruciatingly long and you end up pressing it twice. It is a standard 1 second delay from when you press a button and when it registers.

At least once every 2-3 days the remote completely freezes up. Typically while your in the middle of fast forwarding is when this happens so your whole show fast forwards to the end.

Actual physical buttons are hard to tell if they register or not.

The design of the remote itself is horrible. It is not flat on the bottom so it rocks on flat surfaces. If it's sitting on something flat you cannot really press the buttons. You have to physically hold the remote to use it. The pause, fast forward and rewind buttons are above the touch screen so when you use them your palm below your thumb touches the screen and presses buttons.

Again, this thing sells for $350. I would seriously expect to pay $25 for this product.

The only value I will admit to is every electronic I searched for with a remote you can program into it.

Bottom line, would not buy again, would not recommend

title: Best Mouse and Keyboard Combo I've Found
text:
Overall Impression:
I bought this combo as part of a new desktop build. I've been very happy with it.

Keyboard:
Part of the reason I bought this keyboard is because of the part at the bottom. It continues the keyboard at a constant angle all the way down to the top of my desk and gives me a very natural place to rest my palms as I type. I also like the small LED screen at the top that notifies you whether the caps lock is on, the volume is muted, whether you are holding down function or not, etc. Note that it is not backlit so seeing it in the dark is tough. The full number pad was also an attraction that made me buy this one specifically.

Mouse:
The mouse is very comfortable and has a nice indentation for my thumb that feels very natural when I hold it. The scroll wheel has a button that lets you spin freely or spin with small clicks so you have a choice of how you control scrolling down the page. It also has forward/back buttons that felt odd at first but now I can't image browsing the web without them.

Other:
The battery life has been amazing on these. I haven't had to replace them yet and it's been 3 years. Also the dongle that you plug in the USB slot if very small which is nice but obviously you need to be careful not to lose it. Also I've noticed the signal doesn't penetrate metal very well (which is to be expected for RF signals in general) so I've gotten the best results with the usb receiver plugged into the front of my computer rather than buried on the backside of my computer where the signal has to penetrate my computer case.

Specific Issues:
The mouse uses a laser and doesn't work well on glass but every other surface I've tried it on it has worked well. There is also a weird bug when I change the audio setting up or down on the keyboard it takes a second for my desktop to register the change. If I move the mouse back and forth a bit it gets the signal and changes the audio. Not sure why that happens but it's a minor annoyance.

title: Design and build quality are excellent, and it feels great to use
text:
Design and build quality are excellent, and it feels great to use. Unfortunatey, it functions as a mouse rather than a Windows 8/10 compliant HID touch device. This means that the two-finger scrolling operates like a scroll wheel on a mouse, where rolling the wheel down causes the page you're viewing to scroll up. While that makes sense for a real mouse, that's not how touch works. On any touchscreen monitor or laptop, or any trackpad built into a laptop, two-finger scroll gestures work the other way--moving your fingers up the screen or up the trackpad will scroll the page up.

I can't understand why Logitech would design this backwards and provide no simple software solution to invert this behavior.

title: but the backlight timeout is highly annoying. Why on earth did anyone think that keeping ...
text:
I got this because I wanted a full bright LED backlit keyboard with touchpad with scroll and I could not find any others that came much closer, but the backlight timeout is highly annoying. Why on earth did anyone think that keeping the backlight on for less than 6 seconds at a time was sooo important that they do not even give you an option to keep it on manually? Totally lame. I don't care about saving energy. I will leave mine plugged in to power all the time anyway. I was going to hack it and I opened up the case and the battery is at 4v, but the "LED bar" is powered at 19v and I could not find a 19v pad to solder the bar to. Also, I think everything is powered off by the microcontroller anyway.
Long story short, I was able to put tape over the LED brightness button (F1 key) to keep it permanently pressed and it keeps the light on permanently. I wanted full brightness, so I manually pressed once, then put tape down to bring it to full brightness. It even remembers the setting if you power it off and then on again. It is a reasonable hack for me.
The other surprising thing about this KB is the 2-finger scroll on the touchpad works on Windows 7, so don't need Win8 for scrolling!

title: UNNATURAL MOVEMENT, INACCURATE MOUSING
text:
On a design standpoint, using the thumb to control is awkward. The index figure is much better for pointing, touching, feeling and doing anything intuitive. When was the last time you used your thumb on your phone to scroll or search a phone number or play a game? You can see from the trail of your mouse, going up and down is more of an S curve than just a straight line or far from it. Also the thumb and rest of the hand has the naturalness to grab so I keep making mistakes of pressing the button and moving off the target. It is also highly inaccurate, using a 4k monitor, along with software like Maya, Lightroom, and anything that requires detailed work.
I have the original Trackman wired from over 10 years ago and it has worked fine, however I need scrolling and wireless. The only thing I liked about this, is it's shaped like a mouse. I got this on sale for 20 bucks here, cost 8 bucks to return. I wish Logitech re-created the Trackman with a scrolling wheel and more buttons. I am going to try the Kensington pro.

title: best mouse I've ever used, hands down
text:
I've never really cared about my computer mice much before this one. I've had a laptop and a Dynex wired USB mouse for years and recently decided to upgrade to something a bit more ergonomic to put less strain on my wrist (and wireless so I don't have to repeatedly coil up the cable). Out of all possible choices I feel like this is an incredibly good one. I use it as a Bluetooth mouse so I don't have to eat up a USB port or worry about losing the dongle and it works perfectly. Even though I use many other Bluetooth devices, I've never had any interference issues. The extra buttons are great and the app-specific programmability is incredibly useful. I don't understand the other reviews that complain about the thumb buttons; in my experience, both are very easy to reach and use. The "gestures" feature has sped up my workflow considerably. The battery has yet to run out (I've had it for about two months now and only charged it on the day I got it and it's still got 2/3 power bars; I use it on average 1 hr a day, though some days I use it for 3 or 4 hours).

All this to say, it's a fantastic mouse. Absolutely recommend to anyone who wants a comfortable, functional mouse that will allow you streamline your workflow.

(sidenote: I also got the Hermitshell case for it. does a great job of keeping the mouse safe in my backpack)

EDIT 2/22/19:
So after 2.5 years this thing has finally bit the dust. Though it was well cared for (it outlived the original hermitshell case which I then replaced with another) the gesture button finally bit the bullet. A few days ago I noticed a small tear in the rubber coating over the button and after a short period the tear worsened until the rubber around the gesture button tore off completely. Since this was one of the main features I loved about the mouse and without it (and its ergonomic rubber coating) the mouse is quite uncomfortable to use I'll be moving on to something new (been eyeing a trackball mouse for a while now anyways). To be fair it lived a good life and was well worth the $70 I paid for it. RIP MX Master. You will always live on in my heart.

title: Great keyboard but eats certain key combos, and sub-par track-pad.
text:
PROS; This is one of the nicest feeling bluetooth keyboard around - it has a metal bottom, and while typing, does not flex at all. The keys have a very nice tactile feel to it, and is on par with some of the old style Thinkpad T series.

CONS;
1) It eats up random windows key combinations - for example, Ctrl-Shift-Left works, but Ctrl-Shift-Right doesn't! Why?? Who knows. Each of the three keys work individually, and yet together, they don't work. This is almost a fatal flaw!!! I'm seriously considering returning this product.
2) There seems to be no way to disable gestures on the trackpad, or to adjust the sensitivity The trackpad has what's called a "tap-to-click" feature, which means that a simple tap of the trackpad will be registered as a single click. The problem is that when you're trying to move the cursor, putting down your finger can be interpreted incorrectly as a tap. So instead of moving the cursor, you find yourself having selected a block of text. Or worse, you've accidentally clicked on some unwanted button. Logitech keyboard/trackpad combos allows you to disable this feature via Fn-LeftButton, but this trackpad doesn't.
3) There's no way to adjust scrolling direction - on Macbooks and newer Lenovos, 2 finger scrolling is in the "natural" direction--i.e., moving two fingers down scrolls up, and vise-versa. Now, I dislike the way this works, but many in my family likes this (un)natural scrolling, and this keyboard doesn't allow it.
4) It doesn't come with Mac or Windows driver software which means that you can't adjust any of the above.

title: Logitech deserves a design award
text:
I was looking to go to Bluetooth with a HTPC/living room setup of mine. Tired of the MS wireless. All I really wanted was stronger range.
But when I stumbled across this unit, I saw that the developers had thought of things I had not yet realized I needed.
The integral touchpad means no separate mouse to handle or mousing surface to find.
The compact size has been an improvement I didn't expect. Easier to carry/handle. No loss in effectiveness or convenience.
The rechargeable Li-ion battery means no more AA's. Plenty of useful life on a single charge.
The (nearly hidden) extra left click button on the upper left is a clever feature that I haven't taught myself to use as often as it would come in handy. And the shortcut/Fn keys are thoughtful/organized enough that for the first time I am actually learning their location.
The two finger scrolling on the touchpad is such an improvement over the touchpad edge scrolling that I am used to with my laptops.
The backlit keys are well thought out also, and even provide a low light level when the unit knows it is in a dark room.
The only problem I have had is with a default setting in Windows. What was happening was the KB would get into a zombie state overnight sometimes. It would show as paired but not connected to the computer, like it was out of range. It appeared to be related to the battery level of the KB, but it would happen before I ever saw the recharge warning on the KB--and was a real pain to make reconnect. But before I gave up the ship I found some good advice online (after the usual 90% bogus advice) that showed a default power management setting was letting Windows 'turn off the device to save power' (but the KB apparently never got that memo). Unclick the check box and no problems, just happiness, since. [Device Mgr>>Bluetooth>>Intel Wireless Bluetooth>>Properties>>Power Mgmt>>uncheck box]

title: Pretty good headset for this price range
text: Reception-wise, it's alright if you're in the immediate vicinity of the USB dongle-- although it's still not the best from there either, compared to most of the more expensive wireless headsets, but at this price-- not "cheap," but cheapER-- it's not expected to compete with those high-end headsets. The range is not that bad, but-- as with most any wireless headsets-- doors, walls, etc, in between the headset and the dongle tends to cause some significant drop-off. In an open area, I was able to move probably about the advertised 40 ft or so, before the quality noticeably dropped off. Comfort-wise-- and again, as with the rest of this review, all I can really compare this headset to is a couple of more expensive headsets-- it's average. It's a lot lighter than what I'm used to-- which is GREAT, but as I'm more used to a "cup" shaped earpiece that goes around my ears, these earpieces sitting directly ON my ears takes some getting used to. That's definitely personal preference though, and some people might prefer that type of fit. Overall, this is a solid headset (Logitech is usually pretty good about making good stuff), that isn't perfect-- but for the price, it's definitely worth looking into. I'll also mention that this worked MUCH better with my phone/iPad (using Skype) than it did with my computer (but the same is true, to a lesser degree, with my other headsets-- so this one isn't much different in that regard.

title: Fails as a cooling pad but comfortable on the lap.
text:
I honestly can't figure out how some people got a reduction in temperature with this product. I test it out on a Macbook Air, Macbook Pro, Dell 15.6 and a Lenovo 11 inch laptop and honestly I would not recommend this product for the "cooling effect".

So for the Macbook Air and the Macbook pro, I used Tunabelly's temperature monitor. Even though Macs run hotter than windows, I generally don't like them going over 80C. This product failed to cool the temperature down in any meaningful way, that I could say with certainty was caused by this product. Even a lowering 3C would have been noticeable. Part of the problem is that this cooler has a dinky little fan in the center of pad that does nothing for the Macbooks. Aside from that the top part of the pad is all plastic that actually insulates the lower metallic surface of the Macs, you know the part that Macbooks use to disperse heat, the part that absolutely should not be insulated.

For the Lenovo I used Core Temp as my temperature monitor software. I had to place the laptop to one side so that the fan was underneath the air ports/vent at the bottom, so that there could be some cooling effect. But placing the laptop to one side, made the whole thing a bit unbalanced. As to the actual cooling, yes I did notice, when the laptop was idle, it was idle at a lower temperature than usual, but any strain and the temperature shot right up with no help from this pad.

For the Dell, again I used the Core temp software and to my disappointment, the pad's performance was subpar.

So the question is, why did I give it two stars instead of one when the cooling part is clearly lacking. Well that's because of the underside of the pad. The underside is a soft cushion that makes it very comfortable to rest the pad and a laptop on your lap while you work on the sofa/chair. That soft underside is the only reason this product isn't a complete failure.

It fails at actual cooling but if you just want something to place your laptop on, it's a good product.......But hang on....your're paying $30-40 for this sucker and all you're getting is a cushioned laptop place mat?

When I selected the Roku 3 on the Harmony remote, it was controlling my older Roku HD, while the Roku 3 was completely unresponsive to it. I tried the "Add or fix command" option in the setup program, but it had no effect. The Harmony remote wouldn't even acknowledge that the commands were received.

I was able to control my DirecTV HR54 with the Harmony, but some of the buttons I use frequently weren't pre-configured - the SkipForward, SkipBack, and Mini-guide buttons. I used the setup program to configure those buttons, but it had no effect. The Harmony remote gave me the “Command received successfully” when I configured those buttons with the setup program, but the buttons still didn’t work afterward.

The Logitech phone support was no help. All they could do was walk me through configuring and re-configuring the remote, but none of it had any effect. I finally gave up and sent it back for a refund.

title: Exactly What I Needed
text:
I purchased this mouse a few weeks ago and I think it's finally time to review it. For starters, I spent days researching which mouse to buy; pouring over review after review here on Amazon and later going to third party sites to get their opinion as well. There were a lot of mice on my list but this is the one I chose. I'm not going to tell you why I chose this mouse, I'm going to tell you why I'm happy with the purchase I made.

For starters, this mouse is a very comfortable fit; important for someone like myself who sometimes holds one for hours at a time without letting go. Comfort is very important. It should be noted that this mouse is only fit for right-handers, it is not ambidextrous. As for features, this mouse has just enough to keep me satisfied without confusing my fingers: two primary buttons and the mousewheel, of course, along with a forward and back button (standard, mostly) and one secret button below where your thumb rests. This secret button seemed rather silly to me at first and I wasn't sure what I would use it for, thankfully logitech's downloadable software solves that question for you and replaces it with another: "How will I decide what this button will do?!" There are so many options and I was rather pleased after settling on it switching between programs for me, quite handy.

Third, and most importantly, is the way this mouse feels as it moves. Let me clarify: I use a 3D graphics program (Blender 3D, for those who care) which requires a lot of use with the mouse, including holding down the middle mouse button while gesturing to move around the 3D environment. Understandably, a mouse must have a very certain "feel" to it as I move in this environment to not slow me down. This mouse is perfect for what I need it to be. It moves smoothly, the mousewheel button doesn't resist too much, and the ratchet on the mousewheel is solid enough that I don't accidentally spin it while pressing down. It is hard to find a mouse this adept for what I need it to be.

Last but not least, you can't argue with the price. I was thinking about spending over $100 to get a decent mouse but I'm glad I found this first. I honestly believe that I'm happier with this mouse, priced under $50, than I would have been with a top-of-the-line expensive mouse. I hope you found this review helpful!

title: Pods are only like $100 too
text:
Word of warning for everyone here, these speakers are very susceptible to lightning damage. They don't have a dedicated ground so if they're on at all and lightning hits they're done...

That said, I've had mine since 2008 and they're going strong. I've lost a sub/amp to lightning and blown a speaker, but other than that they're tough. I've played them past full volume for hours (they go into "boost", and max out at boost 11) smelling the cones on the speakers they were being driven so hard, and never many problems. The blown speaker I had was actually from the lightning! Not from my abuse, lol. They've survived college, apartments while I chased jobs, and now my house. When I had to replace the sub/amp due to lightning another sub was just $130 shipped off ebay, and the speaker was just $40 shipped. Pods are only like $100 too, so if anything goes bad the entire system is modular and you can usually just drop around $100 to fix it. Only computer speakers I've cared about enough to do that with....all my previous speakers, when something happened, in the garbage they went. Not these....they're really something special. They rival my friends' and family's $1000+ home theater systems. I was heartbroken when I went without them after the lightning hit. The best way to use them is actually as a theater.....they sound better than being at a movie theater. DTS with the normalizer off and at like 80-90% volume and its AMAZING. Crashing bass, crazy special effects, you swear you're on a ride at Universal Studios or something. And its more than being boomy, or powerful, the sound is very well balanced and detailed. I have a Soundblaster X-Fi Fatal1ty Pro powering mine and the sound quality is just unreal. I find that using the DAC on the soundcard and outputting analog 6-channel direct is much clearer and stronger than using bitstreaming/SPDIF. And yes, music is amazing, it goes so loud without distorting it hurts my ears before there's any distortion. Its like being at a concert....these babies ROCK. Gaming is also just about perfect, the sound from these speakers greatly add to the immersion. Skyrim, Fallout 4, GTA 5, and more, are all amazing on these. Sounds like being there, in the game.

title: Buyer Beware - poor design/quality control
text:
First pair started acting funny about 2 weeks in, the mute function on the microphone stem would mute when placed up, but would not unmute when pulled back down in front of your mouth. The Headsets also sends static through vcom programs such as discord and teamspeak when it is muted making the muting function worthless. Then the headset started not turning all the way on when the power switch was turned on, as in the mic would turn on but the speakers would not start and I would have to restart the headset multiple times to get the speakers and mic to turn on at the same time. Then finally the headset died about 2 weeks after my return period with amazon. I RMA'd the head set with logitech which took two weeks and received a second pair.

The next pair had the same issue with transmitting static when muted and promptly died within 2 weeks going through the same deterioration as my first pair but in a much shorter time frame. I am currently in process of trying to get a refund from logitech so I can purchase a product from a different company that works.

While the product was actually working the sound was amazing, the noise cancellation was almost too good as I could not hear people talking right next to me.

The sidetone is almost non-existent even while turned all the way up, which paired with the high noise cancellation makes controlling the volume of your voice hard to do. Lastly, Logitech advertises the G933's as having a longer wireless range than the g930's, but this is simply not true. Two headsets and neither one of them reached further than my 3-4 year old g930's. A friend made the same upgrade and he has noted a decreased range from the g930's as well.

The ear and head padding seemed like a decent upgrade over the g930's but for some reason the top strap really started to hurt the top of my head. I don't know if this is specific to the shape of my head or what, but never had the issue with the g930's which I used for 3-4 years.

For the price these are not worth it, I've been a Logitech fanboy for years and my view of Logitech has completely changed with the use of this product.

title: The forward and back gesturing in browsers and file folders is pretty reliable. The middle button (two finger click at ...
text:
A few things with this mouse- it's not a full touch only mouse. The whole mouse is a button and to left click right click, you have to to hold down only that finger in the appropriate area and the whole mouse clicks. This is okay but what you need to understand is that you cannot rest the opposite finger on the touch surface when you actually press the mouse as you would with a typical button mouse setup. Most cases when you have your right finger rested while you left click, a right click box will come up.

The forward and back gesturing in browsers and file folders is pretty reliable. The middle button (two finger click at lower 1/3 of mouse near logo) is very unreliable and only works sometimes. There are options to toggle features and customize a few of the settings with the software that comes with it.

Overall I still use the mouse and I believe it is a step in the right direction. What I would personally like to see is a full touch surface mouse with no mechanical buttons at all.

Over all a good product that is easy to use and setup. Saw this $20 more expensive in Best Buy.

title: Only works on 2.4GHz - And Other Issues
text:
I had this device for about a week before deciding to return it. Hoping this review helps someone else make an informed decision. This is a really great device - in concept. The execution lacks a bit. For one thing, it only operates on the 2.4GHz wireless spectrum. Which may be OK for you, but I recently upgraded to 5GHz because of interference issues. If the device loses wifi signal, it's a useless brick. So the connectivity is really important. And it tended to lose connectivity right in the middle of doing something like turning up the volume. I could turn it up 3 notches but the 4th press would get me nothing, then it was dead for 30+seconds. Beyond frustrating- especially when you have a wife who was already skeptical about the concept of a $90 remote control.

In addition to the 2.4GHz limitations, there are issues with wifi connectivity even if you don't have interference. Google Harmony Hub Red LED to see other users with this issue.

Outside of the connectivity issues, it would occasionally send random commands out. Like, I was watching Amazon video and all of the sudden the Roku switched over to Netflix.

I also found the method for programming "activities" kind of lacking. What I really wanted this device for was a simple task- before bed I turn the screen off on my tv (power saving mode) and set the sleep timer. Then I use SmartThings to shut off the bedroom lights. Since this integrates with SmartThings I wanted to set up a button that would just run that set of commands for me. (I already have a custom macro programmed in a cheap universal remote, but it doesn't work with the lights). The "activities" here required you to start/end with turning a device on/off, which didn't make sense for me because I wanted to trigger it after the tv was already on.

I never got around to the SmartThings integration since I couldn't get the basic functions to work well.

All in all I think it's a neat concept, and if you have a higher tolerance than me for quirks go ahead and try it. But I'm going to wait for the next model and hope it improves.

title: The Harmony 650 looked nice enough, with a cool LCD screen feature
text:
Purchased in mid-January. Quirks by February. Failure in April. I purchased this remote to replace a more standard Logitech universal remote (the indicators and numbers on the buttons had severely worn away, but that's another matter). The Harmony 650 looked nice enough, with a cool LCD screen feature. After about 30 - 40 minutes of registering it with Logitech, downloading software, online key/button assignment and syncing the device, it was finally ready and worked well. I particularly love the backlit feature.
A couple of weeks in and I found that I had to use the "Help" button a few times a week to reset the remote. I've now had the remote for three months and it has FAILED. It does not readily respond to the preset buttons, the screen works sporadically and it turns on alternate devices without my selection. Admittedly, it's taken a drop or two out of bed, to the floor, but what remote hasn't? Having paid $65.00 for this remote, I expected it to have a stronger constitution. Now, I'm back to my old remote, relying on memory to select the right buttons.
Here are a few suggestions to Logitech: 1. Use better quality paint or screening on the buttons, so it doesn't wear away. 2. Develop devices that are practically made and sturdy enough for reasonable usage. 3. Be fair and reasonable with the pricing of the products. I shouldn't have to treat a remote control, something that is handled numerous times a day, like fine china. And I shouldn't have to pay for so much money for a product that fails so quickly.

title: Frustrated and disappointed. Windows 10 users beware.
text:
I bought two of the g933 wireless headsets (one in March 2016, and one in September) back when I still had Windows 7. It was a direct upgrade from my G930 which I loved, but needed to replace because the battery was degrading. My husband initially loved the G933 headset even though it was a bit quirky, thus why I bought a second one for myself. After upgrading to Windows 10 Anniversary, the headsets barely work. Every time we turn on our PCs, we cross our fingers and hope that the headsets will function without needing to spend copious amounts of time tediously trouble shooting to get them working.

The issues seem to vary every time we restart. Sometimes the sound wont work at all, and other times it works but not for certain applications (such as not having audio in voice chat applications). Sometimes the audio works but our microphones are permanently muted. Even on those rare occasions when everything seems to be working fine on boot up, the headset randomly decides to go into sleep mode while we are listening to music or playing games and refuses to "wake up" without rebooting. We have done every thing suggest from Logitech to fix these problems, from reinstalling drivers and gaming software, to using the hard reset button on the dongle and headset, to unconventional recommendations such as uninstalling skype preview. Ultimately, no matter what "solution" we try, these problems inevitably return.

I have never had issues with Logitech before, and that is why I feel so disheartened to give this headset such a low score, but I just can NOT recommend this to anyone using windows 10. The fact that I paid around $175 for each set, and the fact that Windows 10 has been out over a year and Logitech still does not have a fix for these issues is just not okay. My husband and I have very different components in our PCs so this isn't an isolated problem, and you can google "g933 sound issues" and see the hundreds of results confirming what I have written here. I am disappointed to have spent what I consider a lot of money on not one, but two, "premium" headset only to spend an absurd amount of time every day trying to get them to work. This headset is a frustration every time I try to use it. I will update my review if Logitech ever gets around to fixing these issues.

title: Great for some, not for everyone.
text:
I'll start this review with the fact that ultimately I decided to return this headset. It just wasn't the headset for me. I discovered that I love Logitech products, until there is an issue with them. I've been a big fan of Logitech mice and keyboard to the point where they are what I exclusively buy, and still will until proven otherwise. However, there line of high end headsets doesn't meet my expectations. In the end it came down to two factors software and support that lead me to return the headset.

Below are the pros and issues I ran into.

Pros:
Design - The design and integration with the rest of my Logitech products (I use the G910 Keyboard and G502 Mouse) is great and the look of the headset is fantastic.
Sound - The sound quality is great.
Singe Use - This headset is great if you plan on using it for one thing. Wireless to PS4 and or PC this thing is perfect (minus my one comfort issue below).

Cons:
Comfort - For me the headset was to tight. (To the point in which is was giving me headaches to wear it), though this could just be my head size.
Software - The LGS can be buggy at times. I had audio cutting out, mic would stop working things like that until I found a forum post explaining to put your PC into clean mode (i.e. boot up with all services disabled) and reinstall the LGS that way. And that did in fact clear up the software issue. I just found it ridiculous that a headset I paid this much for I had to do that, considering I already had a version of LGS running for my keyboard and mouse with no issues.
Multi Use - Here is where things really started to frustrate me. I could not for the life of me get the pass through feature on the 3.5 mm headset to work with the built in boom mic. The intent is to be able to use the boom mic when I'm plugged into my PS4 controller or Android phone and the feature would not work correctly. And this leads me to my final and biggest problem.
Support - Speed and Communication. This is what Logitech support lacks. Better communication between the customer and what support is doing and why they are doing it.

Communicate. Speak to me like a person, not a ticket.

Overall - If you get the headset and it feels good and you have no issues, keep it, you'll be happy. If you run into problems early be warned. The culmination of little things here and there and lack luster support communication is what made me return this item.

title: Not perfect, but **** near!
text:
I'd like to start this by stating that I would have given it a 4.5 or even a 4.75 if I could (Amazon if you read this, please add this feature).

I have used many mouses in the past, most notably(and most recently as this is a replacement mouse) the SteelSeries Rival. After the scroll wheel started to stick I decided it was time for a new mouse, plus with the new lighting feature I was excited to upgrade to the G502 (I also like new tech and am fortunate enough to be able to buy things like the G502 without too much harm done). I only received the mouse today, however, I have done about 8 hours of testing and have some stuff to say about it. (please note: I will update if my opinion changes or if any problems arise)

-Build quality and packaging:

The packaging is awesome, it even tells me the coefficient of friction... I love physics, and this being included is really awesome, thank you Logitech! :D (also it looks cool, not the nicest thing I've ever unboxed but it's still pretty good)

As for the mouse itself I was pleasantly surprised by it's shape and construction quality. I felt the cheap manufacturing of even the rival but the G502 really gives me a new look at how a mouse I payed a rather large amount of money for "should" feel. Really good job, Logitech!

-Feeling/Comfort:

I am right handed, if you're left handed I can't imagine it'd be all that comfortable as such don't pay attention to this :(

The first thing I thought when I got the mouse in my hands was it was cold and soft in all the right places... the sides have a simply fantastic matt finish, as such it's slightly cold to the touch and also very soft. Seemingly connecting the matt finish in a series of circuits(as you can see from looking at the pictures by logitech) is hard, cold plastic. The plastic really adds personality to the mouse, with it's very strong structure.

The lay-out of the buttons is great because whether or not you touch them is completely up to you(as in resting position you're not going to touch any of the G-keys)

The mouse wheel is simply orgasmic(sorry, but I'm in love), it's made out of I presume either stainless steel or something of that nature and feels really, really sturdy. When you move the wheel it has a very nice click feeling. This along with a very smooth "infinite" scrolling feature I can't think of a single thing wrong with it. Some people may say it's slippery, which I suppose it could be, but coming from the rival with it's rubber roller cover, putting a little extra force on the wheel is a small amount to pay for such a luxury feel.

The adjustable weights are really well implemented, and offer a great deal of customization, both in changing the center of mass of the mouse and in changing it's frictional resistance. I personally just use the mouse without any weights as I got accustomed to the Rival's extremely light design. However having the option is a very nice touch.

-Sensor

Coming from the Rival all I really have to say is it feels very responsive and gives a lot of options for DPI adjustment. I have a 1440p monitor and prefer something around 5000dpi, however I have higher presets for things like flying or driving and then lower presets for sniping. At the presets I have after playing a couple hours of games I didn't experience any issues!

Works very well in FPS games and I would assume in any other game (though if you only play RTS games don't spend 80$ on a mouse, but that's just my 2 cents)

-Features

Unlike many other gamers I do not like to use the G-keys for anything other than DPI shifting and then back and forward for browsing. I don't use multiple profiles and use the "Shift" key sparingly, though I am using it more and more (it's only been a day!).

HOWEVER, the mouse brings a LOT to the table. With more than just customizable G-keys. For example, the shift key being a new addition to my "used" features with it's very ergonomic implementation. Not to mention the fantastic "infinite scroll" feature, which is a really awesome tool to have, it's surprising how often it comes in handy. The features that I do use offer me more than enough to be happy with the mouse, in fact the only button I don't use is the profile switch key. Which, I've gotta say is really awesome! (that I don't have to use all of the keys to really enjoy the mouse)

That said, the Logitech program, while being a bit wanky and laggy, offers a metric **** ton of customization; from a different profile per game along with the 3 customizable profiles to being able to change any and all the buttons to do whatever you feel necessary, the G502 delivers.

-Lighting

So having seen the spectrum on CES 2016 I was instantly hooked on the idea with a mouse that could fit in with my color scheme (green and black as I have a black widow keyboard [highly recommend this, btw]). However, I was disappointed by it's lackluster customize options, you can change the color and whether or not it breaths or shifts between colors. Not to mention the fact that the lighting is done rather poorly, with pretty dim lights it doesn't stand a chance against my keyboard, and then at the same time the lighting is not uniform across the logo. Which is something that is disappointing as the Rival accomplished this goal very well with nice, bright, lights (I forget whether or not the light intensity was customizable). It's for this reason that I deducted .25-.5 points as the whole bases of this upgrade(from core to spectrum, Logitech's upgrade, not mine) was for the new RGB lights and Logitech did a rather poor job of implementing it :(

Conclusion:

I would, as my opinion stands right now, recommend this mouse. I think it's definetely worth the 80$ if you have a use for it's features and or sensor. It's not perfect, but I give props to Logitech and whoever designed it for it's amazing feeling, that mouse wheel made me so happy it's astounding! Also the cable for the mouse is pretty short, Wish it could have been maybe 1-2 feet longer, but oh well.

Thanks for reading, and good luck with your future mouse :D

note: for those wondering I would rank the Rival below this, the G502 feels much better to me, and also a little more responsive.

Written by a gamer, dabbling graphics artist and writer.

I will be using this mouse until it goes out of production.

title: Can't really recommend this unfortunately
text:
Can't really recommend this unfortunately. I had an older Logitech mouse (can't for the life of me remember what specific one, but I'm almost certain they don't make them anymore) and it was loads better.

-The older mouse's movement was a lot smoother. This mouse has more friction than I'm comfortable with.

-The older mouse's scroll wheel was more rigid. This mouse has a loose scroll wheel that's a tad difficult to press.

-The older mouse's tracking was immensely better. I'm a programmer so I do very small movements all the time when I'm working. This new mouse takes more movement to actually move the cursor, and the minimum distance it moves the mouse is more than I need (I've messed with DPI settings and the only thing that's gotten close was applying precision mouse detection). Additionally, this mouse's tracking seems unacceptably jittery. Sometimes it freaks out and jitters a lot when I'm trying to move it, other times vertical or horizontal tracking fail for about 30 seconds which gets incredibly irritating.

-The older mouse seemed more sturdy in its build. This mouse feels a bit loose in some areas.

With that aside let me state the pros:

-I like the rubbery grip along the left side. Your hand never slips on accident.

-Some people might enjoy the hyper-scrolling capability. I don't really use it but perhaps some people put it to good use.

So, in conclusion, should you buy this mouse? I honestly can't give it a recommendation, especially when there are cheaper mice out there (I'm talking <= $10) without all the bells and whistles that certainly perform better than this one (which costs $20). If you want to buy a Logitech mouse, I'd probably go for the M510 (which as of 4/21/2016 is on sale for cheaper than this mouse). People seem a lot happier with that mouse (if you can get past wireless, I know some people are hardcore wired users).

I'd give this mouse a 2.5 out of 5 if I could but I can only rate in whole numbers and 2 is too low in my opinion.

title: DON'T BUY FOR WINDOWS 10
text: I bought this touchpad specifically for the multitouch gestures it supports. After disappointment with apple's bootcamp drivers for the trackpad on my mbp running windows 10, I read that this trackpad will get the job done with smooth scrolling and navigation gestures. I read many reviews and was well aware that it was designed for windows 8. However I bought it anyway because I'd like to use multitouch gestures such as horizontal scroll and zoom for navigating a windows exclusive program. The t650 came in the mail this morning and after disappointment with its windows 10 support, I spent the entire day searching online for solutions to no avail. The only gestures that work with windows 10 are two finger VERTICAL scrolling (which can be done with my logitech m325 mouse), three finger swipe up for start menu (on the rare occasion I want this, I can simply click on it) and 4 finger swipe up and down for maximizing and minimizing windows. In my personal opinion there is no advantage to using a trackpad over a mouse unless it's gestures make navigation and control smoother. I wouldn't even spend $20 for a device that lets me smoothly scroll up and down google chrome. This is a nice piece of hardware, the software developers at logitech need to get their s*** together as windows 10 has been out for almost a year.

As others have stated the adaptive scroll wheel stopped working after about two weeks, which would have been fine with if it had stuck on ratchet mode. Even after reading multiple reviews that stated that the replacement came with the same issues, I almost ordered another one. The adaptive scroll wheel was a great feature while it worked, and I found myself trying to use it with other mice. I decided that if I was going to pay $80 for a mouse, I would have liked all features to work, especially the advertised ones.

While using the mouse with Linux, the Bluetooth address would change after every restart or sleep, which rendered automatic pairing useless. I was unable to find any information from people with similar issues with this mouse (and another Bluetooth mouse I had tried didn't have problems at all). There was no issue with using the wireless dongle.

I honestly want to give this product 3 stars, but I did like it. However, I was weary to use a Logitech product as this mouse's replacement and decided to go with an aLLreLi M910BU. It is less than half the cost, and almost as functional. If the MX Master had been maybe $30-$40 cheaper, I would have endlessly returned the mouse for a replacement until I received a flawless one.

title: Wish I could give this 5 stars
text:
I purchased this product after using the [[ASIN:B00Y09IWGQ Logitech MX Anywhere 2 Wireless Mobile Mouse]] for a while. I love that mouse, and still use it, but wanted a bit of an upgrade, so I purchased the MX Master. It took a while to get used to the controls, being slightly different from the MX Anywhere 2, but once you get comfortable with it, it's not a problem. What I really like about the MX Master is the "smart speed-adaptive scroll wheel" that can switch between ratchet and free "hyper-fast" scrolling automatically. It felt weird at first, but after getting used to it, you'd wish that all scroll wheels had that capability.
Now here comes the bad part. After using this mouse for a week or so, I noticed that the ratchet in the scroll wheel began to feel lighter, like it wasn't getting a good physical connection under the hood. Over just a short period of time, it got looser and looser, until there was no ratchet feel at all, and it felt like it was in hyper-fast mode. I spent several days looking online to find a remedy, but all I could find were software-related suggestions. I decided to take the mouse apart and try to figure out what was wrong. This in itself was a pain because they use Torx (6-pointed star-shaped) screws, which I don't have a screwdriver for. After finally getting in, I searched around to find the problem. There's a portion under the wheel that moves when it switches between ratchet and hyper-fast mode. Repeated movement of this part seems to slowly move itself out of place, which makes it lose contact with the ratchet arm. It's easy to push it back into place, but the problem doesn't stop there. I have to repeat this process OFTEN, like every few weeks to a month depending on how much I use the mouse. I'm trying to figure out a way to permanently keep it from shifting out of place, but haven't found a solution yet. The nylon feet/pads on the underside of the mouse don't stick all too well anymore from the constant removing and replacing I've had to do.
I really want to give this product 5 stars but I can't, just because of this one issue.

title: Beautiful mouse with a FATAL FLAW!
text:
I don't typically write reviews but I just had to for this POS product. The physical problem with the MX Master is that the $75-$100 mouse uses extremely cheap plastic on the inside. The mouse feels fantastic in the hand, but the parts that matter will wear out and fail within days of any type of regular use. I'm a web developer and use this mouse between 3 different systems, so it's used 12+ hours a day.

The physical problem I mentioned above is the failure of the "ratchet" scroll wheel mechanism. The mouse has the ability to change between ratchet scroll (click-to-click) or free-spin scroll (scroll the wheel and it spins freely for long page documents/websites). The ratchet system is so poorly made, and made with some of the cheapest plastic parts you can find, that this mouse will fail to perform and will fail rather quickly. The first MX Master that i purchased lasted less than 24 hours. The second has fared a little better as I've had it a little over a week, however it too has lost the ratchet scroll function.

The other problem I have with this mouse is the company that makes it, Logitech. I've visited their "support" (and I use that term extremely loosely) forums and quickly realized, if they actually reply to an issue, all they want their customers to do is wait for a software update. Seriously? This is far more than a software issue, however they refuse to admit to that, and do nothing more than waste their customers' time.

All that said, I wanted to love this mouse, and in most ways I do (see the "good" and "bad" section below). I've always owned Logitech mice, and all of them have lasted years and years. This one feels absolutely incredible in the hand and has every single feature I want in a mouse, including the ability to use it on multiple systems. The issue remains however that this mouse is sold as a premium mouse but uses some of the cheapest plastics to attempt to make Logitech more money, it's nothing more than that. Obviously with the sheer amount of refurbs being sold on eBay from the point this product hit the public's hands, Logitech didn't actually do any real world stress testing of this mouse. They wanted to push it out the door as quickly as possible, in the process screwing over most of the people who purchase it.

Quick Recap/Overview:

The Good:
-Feels great in the hand, premium materials on the outside
-A plethora of features: thumb scroll wheel, forward/back button within easy thumb reach
-Battery life seems incredibly solid
-Perfectly balanced
-Logitech Options software a huge improvement over previous software and has almost unlimited options with application-specific button mapping
-The option to use the mouse with up to 3 different systems (and the insanely easy way to do so) makes this a huge advantage over all other mice out there)

The Bad:
-Cheap, cheap, cheap plastic on the inside, means this mouse wasn't designed to last
-Logitech "support" is a laughable joke

The good far outweighs the bad, however when a product becomes unusable after just a day or so no amount of "good" is good enough! I'll update this review IF Logitech decides to fix the issue this mouse has.

title: Five Star Mouse With Two Star Software
text:
Knowing what I've learned about the software, is the mouse still good enough that I would purchase it again? Yes. It's that good. Here's the full story.

The mouse ergonomics, scroll wheel, button options, design, ability to use with up to three different computers, are all five star features. Simply the best feeling mouse I've used in my 32 years of mousing around. However, the MX Master, Options 3.20.35 software for Windows 10 is a frustration and I give it two stars. So the overall average is just shy of 4 stars.

The "Options" software is buggy and caused me about an hour's time with phone support until I figured out the problem. The scroll wheel would work on my W7 laptop but failed to work on the W10 desktop computer. Difference was "Options" software that was not loaded on the laptop. Once I uninstalled the software, the problem immediately went away.

One other tip, both support agents I spoke with suggest the following. If you have a Logitech keyboard or mouse and have been having intermittent issues with lag time or unresponsive keyboard key strokes, try this. The problem may be the "balanced" power setting is sending less voltage to the USB receiver. You can fix this by going to: Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Edit Plan Settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings. Then disable "USB selective suspend setting."

Hope this helps you with your buying and/or troubleshooting. We're all in this together!

title: It's okay.
text:
For the price that I got mine at, I'd recommend it. That being said, I got mine at 20 dollars during some kind of a promo.

LOOKS: The Snowball has an individual and very distinguishable look that almost everyone knows. If you don't even know microphones, there's two mics that are almost immediately identifiable; the Shure SM58 and the Blue Snowball.

DURABILITY:It's surprisingly durable. I've dropped it a few times off my desk, and even out of my backpack, and this thing survives. Now we'll see how long the wiring will last compared to my Yeti.

SOUND: It's great, for the price, but even at this price range, I'd still recommend a different mic. The Snowball is a good mic for people who want accentuated bass, smooth mids, and rolled-off treble. If you want something flatter and more balanced, get the [[ASIN:B001R76D42 Samson Go USB Mic]] It's smaller, and it sounds better in good recording conditions.

FOR CLARIFICATION:
This microphone is CARDIOID ONLY. People have written reviews where they thought they were buying the real Blue Snowball, but this microphone only has one condenser instead of two to enable it to record in omnidirectional and figure-8 bidirectional. That's why the Snowball iCE is cheaper than the Snowball.

OVERVIEW: It's an okay mic at best, and like the Blue Yeti and the Snowball, it's overhyped and a tad overpriced for the sound, but people still buy it. It'll last, no doubt, but there are better options for the money out there.

title: Good, but not what I needed
text:
[[VIDEOID:3d715f6d99fe691133a872bb66ee2dc3]] All in all, it's technically a great webcam. The resolution is fantastic, the autofocus is surprisingly helpful, the clip-on base is stable, the rotating head is smooth, and so on. Not to mention I didn't need to download any drivers; I just plugged it in and opened Photo Booth to test it out, and it worked perfectly, giving me clear video without any kind of framerate stutter. However, that all would have been very nice had I purchased it with the intention of regular video.
I primarily intended to use it for stop-motion animation. For those who don't know, that involves taking multiple of an object while moving said object between photographs. Because of this, I need to be able to have full manual control of its settings, primarily focal length and light compensation. If the focus were to automatically shift from the foreground to the background between two frames, or if the light were to adjust itself when a brightly-colored object enters the shot, it would create an unsightly and significantly problematic effect. I have downloaded Logitech Camera Settings from the App Store, which allows me to switch off the autofocus, but the problem remains: between frames, it will automatically adjust itself to compensate for the amount of light in the shot. The result is a horribly unattractive flickering/flashing effect due to some individual frames being brighter or darker than those around it, meaning that every so often, the video will have a split-second flash of light that repeats itself several times per shot. Now, if someone could point me in the direction of an external application that lets me access the manual settings, I would be most grateful. However, until I am able to control the automatic light compensation, it will be mostly unusable.
I am uploading the first video I shot with the webcam; notice that around the edges, there is a constant flickering effect. (And the entire backdrop shifts a tiny bit at one point because I neglected to properly secure it, but that's not the point.)
All in all, excellent webcam, but be careful, depending on its intended use.

The other issue is the back/forward button which takes the back seat to the horizontal scroll (much less used feature in my case). The only reason i bought it as a perfomance mx user is the bluetooth connectivity (to free up usb port on my xps 15 with only 2) but even that doesn't work good: it's choppy. It's easier to grip than perfomance mx, so if you are used to keeping your wrist in mid air, have the need for horizontal scroll, than you could find this mouse pretty good. title: The MX Master is more like an MX Letdown.
text:
I’ve been using a Logitech MX Revolution for many, many years now. I’ve replaced most of the buttons and switches in it just to keep it going. I’ve tried to find a new mouse for years but all have fallen short. I hoped the MX Master could finally let me put my MX Revolution to rest. It did not.

What’s wrong with it?
The thumb buttons aren’t in an ideal place, about a half inch too far back for me. Perhaps they’d feel more natural under the side-scroll wheel rather than behind. As they currently exist, my thumb knuckle sorta rests between them, but they aren’t defined well enough to press without pulling the tip of my thumb back to figure out which button is which.

The lower thumb button (the black padding is a button) feels spongy, soft, and awkward to press. The scroll wheel button and middle button behind it also feel spongy. I’m constantly questioning if I’ve pressed the buttons or not. I like a reasonably firm click on my mice and this doesn’t have it. The left/right buttons are more firm than the rest, but still lacking. The buttons feel more like a rubber keyboard or remote control.

Buttons can be made to emulate a keystroke. Once. No matter how long you press the button, you get a single keystroke. It will not repeat the keystroke without another button press. If you’re hoping to use a button in a game as, say, “move upward”, it’ll be useless. I suppose this is entirely a software issue, but still a letdown compared to the MX Revolution software.

The scroll wheel on mine is not balanced. If you use the wheel in free-spin mode the uneven weight of the wheel will fall to the bottom taking your pages with them. This can be especially inconvenient if you have video players which use the scroll wheel to adjust volume. It’s also quite annoying if you’re doing something crazy like reading and watch the words scroll off the window. I have no interest in using the mouse in other scroll modes. How much could it cost to balance a scroll wheel anyway?

title: A mouse built for professionals
text:
Having gone through some 30 mice over the past 16 years, its nice to finally find one that truly stands out fom the rest. My needs are more business related (programmer) so many of the bells and whistles found in the mice popular on blogs and youtube reviews just arn't approprate. The Logitech MX Master is a real tool designed for folks who spend 50+ hrs a week attached to their systems. When in the office connected to the desktop using the nano receiver Logitech pioneered many years ago, or on the road talking to the laptop over built-in bluetooth support, this mouse hasn't failed in exceeding my expectations once.

When scrolling through thousands of lines of code, the mouse will automaticlly (mechanically) toggle between indented scrolling mode and free spin fast scroll mode allowing you to completly change your workflow and increase productivity in a natural seamless way. This is the first mouse I have ever experienced with this feature and I can never go back to a single mode or manual dual mode scroll wheel again.

The ergonomics of this mouse are also second to none. As someone with large hands, the gentle curves and ample thumb rest fit my hand perfectly causing no strain or palm discomfort even after marathon all day coding sessions. The navigation buttons and horizontal scroll wheel are placed in a natural location alowing for easy control even while moving the mouse. My only gripe is the thumb gesture button is not as sensitive as I would like, but given more time with this mouse, it is becoming more useful than I ever imagined.

If you make your living using a computer or value your physical comfort in any fashion, you will not be disappointed with this mouse (unless your left handed, sorry). Yes this will most likely be the most expensive mouse you will ever purchase, but the craftmanship and shear feature set makes this purchase totally worth every penny. Fantastic job Logitech! I tip my hat to you.

title: Amazing hardware, Horrible software.
text:

Want to vertically scroll with the thumb wheel? NOPE
Want to Pan with the thumb button(s)? NOPE

Even with the latest software for both, none of the thumb remapping even works with Revit.

Also, there is NO option for mouse Acceleration. If you have more than one monitor, you will need to pick up the mouse to traverse; even with mouse sensitivity set to max.

The only reason I gave 3 Stars is because the mouse itself feels great.

title: Still not a full replacement for the MX Revolution
text:
For the longest time I have refused to upgrade from my Logitech Revolution MX. When the button switches started to register 'double clicks' I took it apart and fixed the switches. When the battery started to go out, I took the mouse apart and replaced it. Recently the scroll wheel on my Revolution started to stop registering 'middle mouse' clicks unless I pressed it at specific angle. I decided that while I might be able to fix this issue too, I would first look to see if there was a valid replacement for my beloved mouse first.

Enter the Logitech MX Master mouse.

Benefits of the MX Master over the MX Revolution:
- Battery life is significantly longer and I can charge it while using it
- I thought the gesture button was a gimmick, but I have actually grown to kinda like it

Negatives for the MX Master vs. the MX Revolution:
- Fewer configurable buttons.
- 'Side scroll' wheel rarely works in any application outside of my browser or Excel and you can't really customize what it does. Its feature to 'switch tabs' apparently uses some hard coded keyboard shortcuts which you can't override and again, it rarely works well.
- Back // Forward buttons are small and stacked on top of each other making them hard to press
- Side gesture button might as well not exist. It requires far too much force to push and requires you move your hand around on the mouse
- While the gesture feature allows a lot more customization (essentially 5 more button presses) I have had problems with it not releasing modifier keys (for instance, I have a keyboard shortcut that does ctrl-alt-right arrow, and the 'ctrl' key will get 'stuck' and I need to manually press it to release it)

The back and forward buttons on the side of the mouse are awkwardly placed and I'll end up hitting the wrong button from time to time. Finally, after less than a week of use, the scroll wheel on the mouse lost it's clicky sound and is stuck on the smooth scrolling mode. The shape prioritizes form over function: it is no more comfortable to hold than any regular mouse. I find both the $30 [[ASIN:B00D68ZVY8 Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Mouse (L6V-00001), Black]] and the $20 [[ASIN:B00BIFNTMC Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600DPI, 5 Buttons - Black]] significantly more comfortable to use all-day.

The perfect (non-gaming) mouse in my opinion would have the build-quality, scrolling and tracking of the MX Master and the shape and comfort of the Microsoft Sculpt, and not be significantly more expensive than the latter. Unfortunately, it wouldn't look as nice as the MX Master and so might struggle to sell as well.

title: Amazing mouse to go with a mac
text:
I bought this mouse some time ago because I wanted a good mouse to use with my mac that had a third button. This one seems like it was made with that specific purpose in mind. The horizontal scrolling really adds a lot, especially in media applications and in apps which use multi-touch two-dimensional scrolling. The gesture button is also useful. The fact that you can map the scroll function button to the play button means that you can use this mouse as a media remote. It also holds power very well. A single charge lasts a few weeks, and it works great
The only reason why I gave this mouse four stars instead of five is because the ratchet on the scroll wheel wears out too fast. While this could be a deal-breaker, I found that the other features can compensate well enough for it to still be a good purchase.

No directions except a tiny piece of hieroglyphics. You have to be smart enough (fourth grade?) to figure out that "synchronize applications" just means initialize the mouse to your computer. I've been using the same Microsoft trackball for the past fifteen years and it's had arthritis for awhile now, so I've replaced it with this Logitech wireless. The "receiver" that plugs in to a USB port is so tiny that you can still shut the door (if you're using a tower hard drive, as I do). Rolling is so smooth it's almost too slippery, but I'll get used to it. (This matters when you're trying to highlight or cut and paste something, the cursor can drift a little, so you just need to be sure to take your thumb off the ball before you click.) Very satisfied. From checking around at big box stores, this is still a good deal, even factoring in the hefty ($8) shipping fee.

title: What is pictured is not what you will get
text:
The product that you are about to receive may not be what you expect it to be, what you will get is not the old logitech unifying receiver that was compatible with everything and awesome, and had a rectangular prism on the end of it, but you will get the new one, which is much less great, and tapers down to the usb connector. The big problem with the new unifying receiver is that it only works on windows systems, while the old receiver, which is pictured in the product image, is compatible with Mac OS, Windows, and Linux operating systems.

The big problem with this product is that you will not be receiving the usb receiver that is pictured, but the newer version, which is decidely inferior to the old one, since the old receiver is much more compatible with every type of operating system.
