text:
nice resting position (because the pictures all show it more upright, understand that it does lay almost flat, watch a video of someone using it). Keys are easy to set up through the Logitech Gaming Software (LGS), with many presets already figured out for you, and easy setup of alternate layouts (for example, starcraft 2, it will list the "find worker hotkey" as "Select Idle Worker" instead of "F1"), which is helpful for when you find an action that you didn't know had a hotkey. And can be completely customized with any key or key combination you like, with programmable timing sequences, text blocks, and more being able to be assigned.

One drawback:
If you do go one brand for your peripherals, Logitech is the way to go. The only downside is this, and most people won't even notice it. I game on my laptop, while my wife games on the desktop. I use my laptop for work and school, but I only game at home while plugged in. I also happen to have the Logitech g700s, which is a fantastic mouse. Before I set up my g13, I had used the mouse both on and off my Lenovo one link dock. There's the option to have a button cycle through profile presets, which is kind of nice. Once I had setup the g13, this button no longer worked, since the g13 has the option to select among your profiles right there on the device screen. It's a nice feature, but unplugging from my dock, and taking the laptop and mouse elsewhere, that option to cycle profiles didn't come back. Only annoying if I happened to leave the profile on one of my games, when I have copy/pasta or my password database hotkey programmed to my g-keys (Logitech's name for the programmable buttons).

It's a small inconvenience that will probably only affect very few, but it is there. Everything else links and stitches together wonderfully well.

title: Other nice touches are the automatic scroll wheel adjustment
text:
The arguable successor to the [[ASIN:B002HWRJBM Logitech Wireless Performance Mouse MX for PC and Mac]], the MX Master I think actually positions itself not as a replacement to it but a higher-end alternative. The fact that is has support for Bluetooth AND the proprietary Logitech Unifying receiver means I can leave the latter in my desktop that does not support Bluetooth, and use the former on a Mac laptop. It supports up to three connections, so I do not have to unpair from one and then re-pair to another machine; I just change it from a button at the bottom of the mouse. This alone was worth it to me.

The new Darkfield technology that Logitech says allows you to work on even glass surfaces does work as advertised; I just don't notice that much of an improvement over the previous generation's tech. And the shape of the mouse is quite a bit different in my opinion from the Performance MX; it's a considerably taller mouse, and feels heavier. It does more fully-fit larger palms however, and the thumb-rest is plentifully large. This is definitely a mouse for those who use a full-hand "palm" grip on their mouse, and not the "finger" or "claw" grip that some prefer smaller mice for.

Other nice touches are the automatic scroll wheel adjustment; the flywheel in the scroll wheel will switch from a notched, "clicky" roll to a smooth, free-rolling scroll depending on how fast you are rolling the scroll wheel. This seems to work well so far in practice, though it might trip up those who are trying to quickly but precisely scroll to, say, a selection in a list. You can turn off this feature in the drivers should you install them. There is a second wheel for horizontal scrolling, and a side button, but I find these less commonly used.

If you feel the Performance MX wasn't big enough for your palm-grip use, or want the flexibility of connectivity, I recommend going up to this mouse. Otherwise, owners of the Performance MX should not feel too envious. It's a solid evolutionary upgrade, but it branches out instead of being better guts in the same shell.

title: Many instances of scroll wheel issues, but Logitech doesn't care
text:
This mouse is extremely comfortable, the external materials are wonderful, excellent weight, long battery life, and good functionality. The options of using bluetooth or the Logitech receiver is awesome. There's one serious problem: THE SCROLL WHEEL HAS SERIOUS ISSUES.

I've already had this replaced once, and after I return this second one I won't be purchasing another. The "ratchet" mode of the scroll wheel starts out very clicky and definite as it should, then slowly degrades over a period of 1-2 weeks (with my moderate usage) until it's pretty much indistinguishable from the freespin mode, which is also accompanied by heavy drifting.

Why does this one problem give this product a one star review? Because for one, this severely inhibits the usefulness of this mouse, as scrolling is obviously a critical action most users will be using every few seconds during normal usage. The other is that Logitech refuses to acknowledge this problem despite heaps of reviews here and complaints on their forums asking for a solution.

I seriously wonder if a lot of the single-sentence reviews on this Amazon page were paid for by Logitech to boost their sales. Making the situation even more frustrating is all the video reviewers/unboxers judging the product positively based only on their first impressions of it. If they actually used the product for more than a few hours, the scrolling problem would become much more apparent and maybe Logitech would stop ignoring it and actually pay attention to their users.

As someone who relies on using the computer for their livelihood, the concept of the MX master is my dream, and I'd be willing to pay even twice as much as it costs now to just have it last a long time and be reliable. Sadly, it seems Logitech has gone the cheap route and are likely making a huge profit off this thing considering its MSRP of $99 and its actual street price of around $70 and marketing it as a serious professional mouse.

text: I have a Performance MX at work and love it so I decided to get the Master for my home computer.  I love the feel of the device.  The main thing I was wanting was the frictionless scroll.  Unfortunately, I got a unit with an unbalanced wheel.  It seems to be a common issue.  After stopping the scroll, the wheel might turn about 180 degrees, scrolling up or down, and forcing me to engage the ratcheting mechanism.  Then within a week of use, the ratcheting mechanism just stopped working.  Now the scrollwheel is useless, since it is unbalanced.  I also had interference problems, even if the usb dongle was plugged in on the desk a few inches away from the mouse.  Though I think this is always an issue with wireless mice.  Definately not what I expected from a premium product.  Going to try the M500 instead at 1/4 the price.

title: Great mouse for video editing.
text:
I bought this mouse for video editing mostly and I didn't want a wired mouse anymore. This mouse works great. It's built well. It is very comfortable in my hand, while the actual weight of the mouse is not too heavy but has enough to it for use. The horizontal scroll makes video editing much faster once you get used to it. The battery lasts a very long time, when it does die, just plug in the USB, yes you can still use the mouse while charging... The ratchet scroll actually comes in handy when browsing the web.

My only complaint is that the buttons on the side aren't exactly the easiest to press because they are so far back, it is works but moving the buttons forward would have solved this issue. And the "thumb button" either needs to be easier to press or more foward.
Also, one or two more buttons would be nice.

Overall my favourite mouse to use, definitely not the cheapest mouse but well worth it.

title: Great way to disappoint your dad on Father's day.
text:
I bought this for my Dad as a father's day gift and I'll never buy him a logitech product again. As an engineer he can be very picky when it comes to features on a mouse and the MX master was the closest replacement to his favorite mouse the logitech MX 1100, which was discontinued and is now selling for around $250 on Amazon as of 7/16/16.
While the ergonomics of this mouse are there, everything else is absolutely garbage and a symbol of how a company can ruin a good product. First, there are no instructions at all. The only paper I could find is a diagram on battery replacement on a rechargeable, proprietary battery. Why the switch from standard double or triple A? And to top that off There's no latch to open but a set of 6 torx screws, 4 of which are hidden under the foot pads so if you want to replace your most likely broken battery you're gonna have to butcher this thing a little. Then there's a mysterious watch battery with no description on where it goes.
There is no way a $50+ mouse should be having as many problems as it is. If Logitech was serious about their customers they would have recalled this model until all the bugs were gone but for that much money the amount of failures should be minimal. It is clear to me that they just wanted to update the looks of their mouse lines and functionality was the last thing they were worried about.
And to top it off it stopped working, not from a failure to charge but simply poor or a lack of craftsmanship.
Do not buy from anyone ever.

The sidetone is super nice when talking, meaning I can hear myself and don't end up talking louder due to ambient sounds (including my voice) being muffled due to reasonable sound isolation.

The biggest issue is the headset continually does the same thing the previous generation does, it randomly disconnects and reconnects on it's own. This is a major negative for a "wireless" headset. It happens 5-30 times a day for me. This occurs on multiple OSs, multiple machines, different USB ports/hubs/etc. This issue is worth -2 stars since it makes it unreliable in uses outside of gaming (I can't reliably use this headset when taking a call on skype/google/etc). When gaming, the device seems to be good, and the disconnects aren't nearly as disruptive. This is the reason for 3 instead of 5 stars.

When the disconnect happens, the machine doesn't lose the audio device, it is simply the headset disconnecting/reconnecting to the USB stick. This is the only saving grace when the disconnect happens as it doesn't cause the machine to pick a new audio device.

text:
Build quality is excellent, it's solid, smooth.. it's basically just what I wanted, but it's fatally flawed.

You can't turn off "acceleration" on this device. This is also referred to in windows as "enhance pointer precision." The driver software for this touchpad overrides whatever windows is doing and always has that on. Furthermore, their particular implementation of acceleration is terrible. It makes the cursor feel sluggish, as your smallest movements result in almost no cursor movement whatsoever, so you exaggerate slightly, which causes the cursor to overshoot, again and again. with a quick swipe of about one inch, the cursor will almost travel the entire width of a 1080p screen. In short, it's far too slow for slow movements, and far too fast for fast movements... and you can't adjust it or disable it. At all. period.

As a result it's probably the nicest feeling to the touch, and only slightly less infurating than touchpads on cheap netbooks. I prefer the touchpad built into my MSI GT72, i just wanted something I could use in a different position.

Do not recommend.

title: The Good: - The unifying receiver is great
text:
I have had several of these over the years. From my perspective, here's the scoop.

The Good:
- The unifying receiver is great. I like the one small receiver that I can plug into a USB port and run both the mouse and keyboard from. I also like the fact that I can use the same receiver for a travel mouse and/or keyboard on the same laptop.
- Build quality is solid. It feels just a little plastic-y, but that is a really small nit to pick.
- Key action is nice for me. Sufficiently stiff, with a pretty short through. Not as nice as a true mechanical keyboard, but a nice approximation without the bulk.
- Multi-Function keys. Lots of single key-press options for launching your default browser, email app, settings, managing media, etc. They're nice for when you need that functionality, but they're far enough away from the main keyboard that they don't get in the way of daily work.
- The mouse fits my hand well. It's large enough for someone with pretty beefy hands, while the contours allow for someone with smaller hands to work comfortably as well.
- The multi function buttons on the mouse that let you scroll, move forward and back, and even do a task switch work extremely well, in my opinion. I have never changed the default configuration for these button actions, but the can be customized if you like, which is a nice touch.

The not so good:
- I only have one real complaint with regard to this keyboard. The little plastic "feet" on the back of the keyboard are a bit flimsy. I've found that the larger ones, which give me the level of tilt that I like, break a bit too easily for my taste. I've never actually had the functionality die on one of these. The main reason I've ever had to replace one is when something (often something fairly light) falls on it and breaks this little foot. I will end up living with the lesser tilt of the smaller one for a while, get frustrated and end up buying a new one.

Improvement recommendations:
- Improve the quality on the little "tilt feet". Maybe use a combined combo option as is often done on keyboards today, which might bulk up the strength a bit while keeping the space requirements small.
- About the only other thing I could think of to improve this keyboard/mouse combo would be a switching mechanism that would allow me to choose between a few different unifying receivers for the same keyboard/mouse combo. I have three different docking stations for different machines at my home workstation, and I'm not happy with the KVM options these days. They are either too pricey, or they don't meet my needs. If I could just throw a switch to move from one receiver to the next and just change a monitor input, that would be fabulous. Currently, each receiver can pair with multiple devices, but each device can only pair with a single receiver.

Overall, I think an excellent bargain with good price/performance.

title: Rugged, waterproof, and great bang for your buck.
text:
In the $100 and under price range, this speaker wins my vote as my favorite speaker. I work in a consumer electronics store so I have either owned or had a lot of experience with many other types of speakers.

My favorite part of this speaker is the form factor. Its really small and slim, which makes it super easy to bring literally anywhere. The bungee cord makes it possible to strap it to nearly anything. My normal way of demoing this speaker is by looping it through my belt loop on my pants and walking around with it playing.

The sound quality is pretty decent. You're going to get better sound out of a jbl flip 3, which is comparable cost. But the difference in sound quality is forgivable when you consider how slim the speaker is. This speaker does sound really good though.

I love the fact that its waterproof and rugged. I can take this to the beach and throw it in a bunch of sand, then run into the water with it to wash it off and not worry. This speaker normally hangs from my shower caddy and gets drenched everyday. I cant say enough good about this thing. I actually stopped using my Beats Pill XL once I bought this because it is so convenient.

title: Finally got my Smart Control added to my Harmony Ultimate Home hub!!
text:
Finally, I got my Smart Control added on as a second remote to my Harmony Ultimate Home hub!!

You might wonder why I gave it 5 stars after the torture I went through. Well, it was a simple mistake on my part that created the problem, so I'll take the blame. Ultimately, it works and is such an improvement over the original touch remote that I'm overjoyed. As I like to say: "The first phase of any successful project is lowering customer expectations".

It's so nice to eliminate the need for pointing the remote at the TV. But I still find myself doing that sometimes out of long years of habit.

The Smart Control is just the right size, and has almost the right buttons. As other have commented, one more activity button would be nice. But I used short press/long press on the "listen to music" button and that works fine. My Amazon Fire TV is the short press; Apple TV is the long press.

My mistake:

I so disliked the touch screen remote, that I'd stuffed it away in a deep corner in hopes of never seeing it again. So when I tried to "upgrade" my hub with the new Smart control remote, and the MyHarmony.app prompted me to connect my remote, I started looking for a connector on the Smart Control - and there is none. I dug the hole deeper with a few web searches, which implied that the Smart Control can be programmed via bluetooth.

The solution:

Well that's true, the Smart Control is programmed via bluetooth. But ... you've got to physically connect the original remote to your computer before MyHarmony.app will progress to the new remote. From there it was easy. Only downside is that I'll have to keep the touch remote handy as I refine my setup, add/remove devices, etc.

I also tried using the iPhone app to add the Smart Control. It would make a bit of progress, sometimes to the point of downloading configurations, but didn't seem to be able to finish the job. I wasted time with the alternate methods (bluetooth pairing, IP address). But then I took another trip down another hole when I found a Logitech page that said I couldn't use a 5 GHz network to program it. I was getting ready to dredge up an old 802.11g router and place it in my entertainment unit so I could run a separate network just for the Harmony. Fortunately I stumbled onto the answer above, otherwise I'd have wasted even more time and energy.

I believe it's also made for possibly teaching gorillas to use computer track balls. title: vs Nest
text:
I have this one and I have a Nest camera for my other apartment. Hands down: Buy the nest. Only exception is: You want 24h video history without paying and you’re so poor that you really can’t afford the nest. Or you only use case is live video or 24h recording with NO additional features required.

Here's why (sorted by importance):

App
--------------
Nest is great. Logi is simple (=basic - not in a good way), buggy and a pain in the behind to use, lacking features, not intuitive at all. Why is it always in landscape mode? I don’t understand… it also doesn't do… home/away

Home/Away - Major issue:
------------------------------------------
My nest turns off when my Smartphone that runs the app is near (= me at home). So I don’t record myself, my girlfriend and her boyfriend and his boyfriend etc. - makes it way less creepy to people visiting and to myself. Logi doesn’t have that. You have to turn on/off manual. Also the Circle tells me constantly “Saw someone” - yes it’s me - I’m home.

Alerts:
--------------
Nest can send me a nice mugshot via e-mail or app even without nest aware. No e-mail option here. My camera is setup in a fashion that it sees also the light outside a window turning on. It constantly gets confused by that. Nest solves that by a) a better algorithm and b) activity zones…

Activity Zones:
----------------------------
On nest you can define which parts of the picture to look at for movement. Nope - not with the circle.

Setup:
--------------
I bought both the Nest and the Circle refurbished. Resetting and linking to my account took 5 minutes on the Nest and 1 hour on the Logitech. The instruction don't tell you that you can't reset it when the battery is low. It will beep and all but will not reset and will not allow you to pair. Manual is silent about that.
The purple LED is explained nowhere either.

LED:
--------------
The led blinks when the cam is filming and lights solid when it’s not. 100% of people seeing this will believe I record them. Only solution is turning off the LED completely. Nest is on = recording, off = not recording or completely off.

Build& Construction:
----------------------------
To me, it looks cheap. The nest is also way more flexible in mounting. Super annoying is also that you can't rotate the image by 90deg - just 180. Also, it's very easy to mount the charging ring the wrong way.

Battery:
----------------------------
I have no clue what the use case should be. Where would you put it where no power is nearby but wifi? Just another potential point of failure.

title: The Best Remote Ever
text:
I have complicated home theater cinema with up to 10 electronic equipment. This remote has been a life saver and since I have now used the LOG19 for three months, it is time to provide my feedback:
Pros: Easy to set up even a 5 year old could do it if they had all the info. Just make sure that you have the model number of each device you are adding. Once you add all devices, it is so easy to set up activities. Plus it gives custom option of changing activity name e.g. "instead of watch tv" I just switch to "watch amazon fire" etc. Intuitive, at least for most parts. I like the "help" function i.e. if a device is not responding, you just tap HELP and it walks you through it. The cable that is attached to the hub is very long and can pretty much cover any good size room. One more thing, it works very well with my Lutron Bridge Pro - I control lutron lights directly from the remote. Finally, the remote is connected to my home wifi and I'm able to update software without connecting it to a computer.
Cons:
It does not work well with my Sony HWES40 projector. For this, i give it 4.5 stars but I would buy it again

title: Doesn't Remote an iPhone; Key Features Missing in MyHarmony Software
text:
I ran into multiple difficult setup issues with the hub. Able to get through them, but they were not easy.

I bought this remote hoping to set up an activity to control an iPhone using Tidal. I *thought* that since the iPhone was involved, the remote could control the iPhone. There is an existing Satechi remote that can control the iPhone--I have this remote, it works, and it's available at Amazon. But the hub cannot remote control the iPhone.

So, I went in a different direction to see if this remote could replace my existing Harmony One media room remote. I would probably use a Harmony Ultimate, but since I had this at home I decided to investigate using the new MyHarmony software.

Sadly, the new MyHarmony software has removed key features from the older Harmony Remote Software 7 program. Specifically, you are no longer allowed to modify the shutdown steps to insert a change of input---in my case, I want to switch the TV to InputHDMI3 on shutdown.

Why do I need to do this? When my wife and I watch DirecTV over the TV & TV speakers, we use the DirecTV remote. It's a complicated remote and Harmony does not completely support it--and we are used to it. In every other situation, we use our Harmony One remote. Our DirecTV DVR is hooked up to input HDMI3, so in order for the Harmony One remote to be compatible with the DirecTV remote, every Harmony One remote Activity ends by setting the input to HDMI3. So, if we turn on the TV using the DirecTV remote everything is ready.

So, I looked at workarounds. One approach suggested in Logitech forums was to teach the InputHDMI3 command to the new remote by hand. Then it could be used on shutdown. Sadly, there seems to be no direct way to do this since this particular command is not on any Sony remote. The only way I could think of was to use an older Harmony remote to teach the command to the newer Companion remote. Doesn't seem to be a robust way to do things going forward; what if the older Logitech software stops working?

I want to point out that the Harmony remotes do not exist as the single system in homes. Harmony remotes have to be able to play in the sandbox with other systems. I cannot emphasize enough the need to interact with other systems. Harmony remotes should not be a closed-wall system that is all or nothing.

I currently have 2 aging Harmony One remotes that I have had for many years and love. Each is on it's second battery and are showing signs of recharge fatigue. My decision going forward is to replace these remotes with Harmony 650s, which use the old software and can set the input to HDMI3 on exit. Amazon has the 650s so no problem there. I am returning this Harmony Companion remote.

title: Battery problems
text:
In the nine months we've owned this--using it about as often as we previously used our regular TiVo or XBox remotes--we've replaced the batteries seven times. So, 16 batteries in nine months. We didn't change the batteries in any previous remote more than twice in a year, and I think it was closer to every nine months or so. In addition to the wastefulness and expense, it's also just irritating to have the remote stop working out of nowhere once a month (there is no warning that the batteries are low--it just suddenly begins to reboot itself every time you push any button).

Speaking of that, and possibly related: apparently these units have a problem keeping the batteries stable, with a good connection, and that too can cause the remote to reboot. So anytime the remote slips onto our rug--a very cushy surface--or even bounces off a couch cushion, it resets itself and we have to go through a walk-through instructional sequence of button-pushing to get it to function again. There is no way to cancel this process, you just have to do it every time. Again, this is very irritating because it happens a few times every day with normal usage.

It's very unfortunate, because I love the convenience of having one remote that makes usage across devices fairly intuitive (once the programming is complete), but the battery issues will probably make me move on to a different brand in the future.

title: Amazing keyboard for a multi-tasker!
text:
I am a home health nurse and the company I work for provides a Samsung galaxy tablet for our charting.The k480 fits the tablet (without a case) perfectly. It's so much easier than pecking away at the on-screen tablet. It also leaves enough space to keep my iPhone next to it. I'm able to answer text messages and emails while charting on my tablet.

I had no trouble pairing the keyboard with any of my devices. I even paired it to my MacBook Pro which I have open for personal emails/messaging and homework assignments/discussions. The transition between devices is really seamless with a delay of a fraction of a second. The notifications of connecting/disconnecting show on the different screens so I know when I can start typing again on each. That delay isn't a deal breaker for me. It's a lot more comfortable to type on than keyboard cases I've tried. I found a keyboard key cover to help protect the keys since I am usually snacking when charting. Apparently the cover will mute the keystroke sounds a bit but it's not obnoxiously loud to begin with.

I was concerned about transporting the tablet in my backpack. I carry books for school as well and didn't want to mess up the keys on my keyboard. I found a Hermitshell case for it which I've used for a few days now and it seems to do the job.

I like the fact that it uses batteries and I don't have to worry about forgetting to charge it, or accidentally leaving it on.

I'm super happy with the quality and the price of this keyboard. I've been recommending it to my friends/family/coworkers.

title: Sync fails all the time!
text:
For the most part, I like this product. This remote is simple, easy to set up and has a lot of flexibility. The 650 in particular is just a basic IR remote, which I wanted, and does not have internal rechargeable batteries, so the remote does not need to be kept in a cradle.
The problem that I have is that the SYNC operation fails literally ALL THE TIME! I have a 64-bit computer with Windows 10. Everytime I change settings and try to send the settings to the remote (called Syncing), it stops at 99% and tells me that it has lost communication with the remote. After much trial-and-error, I have been able to get it to Sync completely only after forcing the remote into Safe Mode (requires removing the batteries and holding down the OFF button while re-installing the batteries).
This is EXTREMELY annoying since it happens virtually every time I try to Sync the remote. I have seen many posts online about this problem, but have not seen anything from Logitech that provides a solution. They seem to be satisfied to tell people to use a tech-savvy solution like setting Safe Mode, or re-booting the computer or using another computer (REALLY?). I am extremely dissatisfied at the lack of effort being put into solving this problem by Logitech. This may work OK on older computers, but eventually every PC will be running Windows 10. Logitech, you better shape up or the world will pass you by!

title: Very nice mouse, though will not be my primary driver.
text:
It's a great mouse, really, which is why i am rating it a four. The only reason it is not a five is because, whilst it IS a great mouse to have, it does have a few small issues. at least mine did.... Let me tell you why i recommend this item, regardless of my issues, and then i will tell you what issues i have had.

PROS:
Battery- This thing has a LONG battery life, if you hate changing batteries for a wireless mouse, then this thing has got you covered.
Form- even with my 8 by 4 hand, this thing is comfortable in a palm/fingertip hybrid grip.
Software- Logitech does not mess around. It's software for this mouse is good, it's not fully amazing with bright lights or a coat of paint but it does the trick with anything you might need for a productivity point of view.
Satisfying use- The trackball is well placed and has a very good use. though my own input fails sometimes as i have a VERY twitchy right thumb (too much use out of the G600 i think) whenever I'm not twitching, i feel very much in control and like the mouse. Though settings will vary with user, so my good setting may be too much or too little for you. Software is your friend with this one.

Cons: (some issues for my device only, and some things i noticed between both mine and my friends)
Inconcistant build- My friends device is perfectly rounded with no noticeable bumps other than the usual wear and tear of grease on his mouse, besides the body being beat up the triggers and buttons work and feel just right and where they should be and aligned perfectly. Mine not so much, the triggers are slanted a tad, with the right trigger having a small bump above it's sitting place compared to the main body, and the forward and back buttons seem to get stuck down from time to time unlike my friends
Cleaning: you will be cleaning the trackball, and the pressure points that it sits on, ALOT! with alot of use or hardly any, it will gunk up and feel very sluggish moving the ball around, and i have to clean it either every day or every other day to make sure it stays smooth.
Scroll Wheel: It's not very clicky, and you feel only a small tense vibration whenever it scrolls up or down a notch. not very satisfying and a little off with it's notches i think.

Though the problems may turn some people off, i want to encourage you to either find someone who has it and try yourself, or find it on sale. it is a VERY good wireless mouse, and if you are someone who hates moving their arm a lot, then this thing is DEFINITELY for you, regardless of it's quirks. Logitech's build quality is still very high, even if sometimes the product doesn't always come out perfect. Hey, nothing ever is you know? so instead of asking for perfection at low price, ask for a good product at a fair price, and i think that is what you are getting.

title: Modest price, great performance
text: For a modestly priced universal remote control, the Logitech Harmony 650 is exactly what I needed. it replaced all of my remotes in one. The best features are the ability to press one button, and have the remote turn on all electronics required to perform one function, such as "Watch TV", or "Watch a movie". Not only does the remote turn on all of the required electronics, it also turns them to the correct inputs. If for some reason, there is a glitch in the process, a simple press of the "Help" button allows the remote to fix the problem after answering yes or no on a few questions.When picking up the remote in a dark room, the backlit buttons automatically light up. Tech support is savvy enough to solve problems another remote control manufacturer was unable to solve, which is why I returned the previous "universal" remote. Being able to enter your electronics into the online setup is much easier than entering code after code to search for the right one. Enter your electronics item model number, and you are ready to roll.

title: Quality Product, but Only for Small/Medium-sized Heads
text:
Very nice headset for the money. Sturdy construction, the ear-muffs are made of a composite plastic rather than foam, so they won't naturally peel-off over time. With gentle daily use, I could see these lasting 1-3 years.

However, as another poster mentioned, this headset is ONLY for people with medium/small-sized heads. The plastic headband is very thick and stout, applies more pressure than is necessary to keep itself on the head, and can't be flexed to change the pressure level. I have a larger head, and need to remove it after each and every call, otherwise risk a head/ear-ache.

Also, the ear cups are actually smaller than the ear, which feels a bit strange but is actually nice once you get used to it.

Lastly, I had hoped that the thick section in the middle of the cable was an auto-spooling storage container for the cable. However, it's just a very bulky collar clip with a volume adjuster on it.

I would give the product 5 stars if I had a medium-sized head :)

title: It was hands down the best controller I'd ever used for PC
text:
Unfortunately my Logitech Rumblepad 2 Cordless controller finally died after several years of operation. It was hands down the best controller I'd ever used for PC. They are still available in limited quantities from various sellers though at a significantly higher price of $130-$150 on Amazon and other websites. Subsequently I decided to seek a new wireless controller...

I first tried an Xbox One for PC. I encountered numerous issues with it on both Win 7 x64 and Win 10 Pro x64 and to no avail could I get it to operate correctly with my steam games etc. I then tried the PS4 Dualshock with similar results. Despite being an experienced computer user the drivers and software, in all its multifarious revisions available online, in addition to all personal modifications that were attempted for both controllers it did not help me whatsoever. Many people experienced similiar issues as mine and would sometimes be successful with either of them. It was an infuriating hit and miss situation per person as to whether or not they would work.

I read reviews on the F710 and similarily saw both good and bad experience. Fortunately though for me the controller has proved to be just as good as my previous Rumblepad 2 cordless. The installation was an entirely painfree process compared to the others I mentioned. The only difference between the F710 and the Rumblepad 2 is in their weight, the latter being slightly lighter. This is a negligible issue though and it seems to make up for this by having a better battery life.

I would recommend this to anyone who has suffered similar dilemmas with controllers to try this one. If you encounter any issues, switch its mode from XInput to Directinput (located on top of the controller) and it'll more than likely be solved

text:
This is a really impressive system. Despite being a long time, mostly satisfied, Harmony user, I hesitated buying the hub version because I was convinced it would not work well in my setup where the only practical placement of the the hub is directly on-top of and vertically adjacent to the devices it would be controlling (see picture).

The term "IR blaster" seems appropriate enough in this case. In my case, the hub is placed directly on top of and next to the DirectTV and Receiver, and is actually SEPARATED from the TV by a cabinet with no line of sight at all. Yet, it all works perfectly. It reliably controls these devices.

The minimal remote is nicer than the last few generations of full featured remotes and the RF communications between the hub and remote is rock solid. It's responsive and the smartphone setup is very nicely implemented.

title: LOVE these remotes! Just wish it was backlit.
text:
I own three of them and have given away at least another three of them as gifts. They're the perfect size, the buttons are laid out well, and the set up is very easy with the iPhone app. The best feature is the hub. Unlike other "universal" remotes, this one has an RF (radio) link between the remote and the hub - meaning that you don't have to point it at anything, and it goes through walls, blankets, whatever. Second, the hub does all the "macro" stuff... that is, it sequentially issues all the commands to all the devices. With universal remotes, you have to keep the remote pointed at all these devices while it goes through all the commands.

My only gripe is that there's no backlight. I don't need a color screen (way too expensive) I just need the buttons to light up so I can see them in the dark. I know where most of them are by feel, but sometimes it's still nice to have the light. I know this would drain more battery, which would probably require a AAA cell and make it a little bigger... but it would be worth it.

title: Xfinity / Cable Users Please Read: Easy to Set Up, Works with Smart Things
text:
My second in the house. I feel as though the overall functionality has improved since my initial remote when these first came out (I feel as though it is faster/more responsive). I'm controlling Cable TV, Ambient Music with Chromecast Audio (Speakers wired in ceiling through the house), Sony Smart TV, AppleTV, Denon Receiver with 2 zones and Motion sensor / Room Lights with this one unit (last two via Samsung Smart Things).

I think Logitech could do themselves a world of favor (and massive number of returns) by explaining how these integrate with cable boxes. title: Plays Echo Dot music through your stereo system, yet still allows Echo Dot to work on its own when stereo is off!
text:
This Logitech Bluetooth Audio Adapter works great with the Echo Dot. Now we can listen to the huge library of Internet-streamed music from Amazon, Pandora, Spotify, etc, played through our old but still great-sounding stereo and multi-room speaker setup. There is a key feature which some may not be aware of that makes the combo work great. I'll explain:

Initially, you "pair" the Audio Adapter with the Echo Dot. I used the Alexa App but it can be done strictly with Alexa voice commands too. Once you've done this, sound from the Echo Dot plays through the Bluetooth connection instead of the Dot's tiny internal speaker. The key feature is this: when the Audio Adapter is powered on, it automatically reconnects to the Dot, the Dot internal speaker is muted, and sound is routed through the stereo. When the Audio Adapter is powered off, the Bluetooth is automatically disconnected, and the Echo Dot once more uses its internal speaker.

Pull out your stereo receiver and look on the back for an electrical outlet marked "switched". This is power that turns on when your stereo receiver is turned on, and off when the receiver is turned off. Just plug the power adapter for the Logitech Audio Adapter into this "switched" outlet, not into a regular wall socket. Now when you use your stereo remote, or the front panel switch, to turn on the stereo system, you'll hear a few beeps from the Echo Dot, and presto, its sound is routed through the stereo. Turn off the stereo system, and the Dot works with its internal speaker again for non-music use -- like as a kitchen timer, etc.

This trick is working perfectly for me and hearing any songs we want instantly played through the whole house is a treat. I recommend this device along with the Echo Dot if you have a stereo system and want to play streaming music through it.

title: Windows 10 users beware
text:
PLEASE NOTE: The current version of Logitech's Gaming Software (8.83.85) seems to have a bug with volume control. This makes the headphones very, very quiet on Windows 10 64 bit operating systems. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like Logitech is too motivated to fix this issue either as their customer support has yet to even verify the problem on their support forums.

Purchase this product at your own risk given the above.

That out of the way, please note that I own a G930 that has lasted me for around a year. I consider the G930 to be a decent piece of hardware despite the criticisms it has received. The G933 is not much of an upgrade. The headphones are extremely tight fitting meaning your ears will probably hurt from the constant pressure that is applied while wearing them. Putting them around your neck results in being choked. Note that the decision to focus on lighting is a poor one. Drawing more power from something as superfluous as a lighting system on an audio device that focuses on wireless communication is a big mistake in the electrical and computer engineering worlds. I'm not really sure who approved the idea but they probably should not be involved in future wireless audio endeavors by Logitech.

Adjusting the advanced equalizer settings yields disappointing results. Using the same settings I use on the G930, it would appear that the bass spectrum seems to have been completely neglected. Note that there is now no way to adjust the amplifier setting to fix the static distortion you sometimes hear in music with heavy bass and treble at the same times.

I could go on (the auto turnoff after a set interval of time, poor mic quality, etc.) but I feel the above should be enough to solidify this product as a no go for anyone seriously considering audio peripherals for a computer or home entertainment system. Such a disappointment.

title: Another Logitech WIN!  Great product.  I highly recommend.
text:
I've used Logitech's original trackball (with a cord) for years. Unfortunately years of use and abuse have weakened the cord so that it only works sporadically. I finally gave up fighting with it and decided to order a new one. I was disappointed when I found out they don't make that model anymore. The replacement for it was this model. I was a bit skeptical about it. I've gotten used to the track ball and will never willing go back to using a mouse. So I had no choice if I wanted a new trackball. I've been a fan of Logitech for many years. The M570 was no disappointment. It is fairly lightweight if you pack it with a laptop like I do. The base is weighted just enough to give good stability and the no slip pads on the bottom work great on one most surfaces. It trackball is very responsive to every move and glides like oiled silk on glass ball bearings. (i.e. very smooth). The buttons on just firm enough with a clear tactile click. The (new to me) forward and back browser buttons add a little more versatility. The scroll wheel feels better than on the original trackball. The only downside is the small size of the USB receiver. But in a way, that's a positive because it's low profile allows you to leave it slotted in most bags. If you can't or prefer to remove it, it has a convenient storage compartment on the bottom. The new receiver allows you to connect up to 6 devices through a single USB port. It has a solid feel and feels very functional. If you've never used one, do yourself a favor and switch to a Logitech trackball.

Over all, I like it better than my original Logitech. I'm looking forward to many years of use.

title: "Meh"
text:
I was in the market for a Bluetooth keyboard to clear up the clutter on my desk and purchased this one last November after reading glowing reviews of it.

First, here's what I love about it: it has memory keys so that you can seamlessly switch from one device to another. That means that if you have a laptop and a tv that you want to use the keyboard with, changing back and forth is as simple as the push of a button. Having an Apple Magic Trackpad that I have to switch on and off and re-pair every time I turn off the Bluetooth on my Macbook, that feature is not lost on me.

Here's the problem. After using the keyboard for just a few months, keys started falling off. Even though $90 isn't an insane amount to pay for a Bluetooth keyboard, the build quality of this keyboard is just plain substandard. I have to constantly push keys back down on the keyboard, and after a day or two I notice they've sprung back up again.

So, in short, if you're looking for a decent keyboard that may last you a couple of years, this one is okay. However there are definitely better one's out there. Having used the Apple keyboard I can tell you that that one will definitely last much longer than this one.

However, if this was a perfect world, the balance between price and quality - notably how the former is often artificially inflated to achieve the latter - is a precarious thing to begin with, and even then it's skewed against consumers, but that's not why we're here. I'm going to go ahead and give it four because, frankly, it's cheap and good for what it is.

Not to get too deep in the creek, but I recently got back into gaming after a two-decade absence and eventually purchased a PC because, let's face it, a MacBook won't cut it. I spend most of my time playing the stuff I missed, particularly games made before or around 2005. That is something to note. Quite a few if not most of your older games won't play with this gamepad - apart from some computer tinkering if one swings that way - but that's just how that is and can't be considered a mark against it. Newer stuff usually demand some sort of controller, and there was never any problem there.

That all being said, when I decided to try a gamepad, I went with the F310 knowing a couple things. One, Logitech has always made quality products, in my experience. Granted, my memory may be filling in holes on its own, but I've used speakers, keyboards and other whatnot made by them over the past few years and never got less than what I paid for. Two, I quit using game controllers with the SNES and this new format confuses and frightens me. I did not want to blow 50 bucks on something I couldn't use and the 20 here was just perfect.

So the purchase was made and for several months all were happy. Unfortunately, here's where we get to the three-and-a-half-not-four star business. Again, based on experience, your less expensive Logitech products aren't quite as sturdy as their pricier ones. I have a small dog who apparently thinks I like knocking this controller to the hard-wood floor and, being a good boy, he decides to help me out once in a while. Being a clumsy oaf, this thing hit the floor quite often and, consequently, nine months after purchase, it's battered to a useless degree.

Being cautious and charitable, I'm erring on the side of positive because of that. Perhaps you're not a clumsy oaf. Perhaps you don't live with such a conscientious canine. This, then, might be the controller for you and you might gets years of joy and enjoyment from it. I can't say. I can say, however, that it is a solid, serviceable, affordable gamepad and a good value for its price. It'd also make a good "got a little extra cash" back up or an "Oh, drat, my old gamepad exploded and I can't afford to buy a new one for a while" last-minute thing, as well. I'm going to try something else - perhaps the slightly pricier Logitech F710 - but the F310 is most certainly a quality buy and I am a satisfied customer.

For whatever that's worth. I still haven't gotten used to the new set-up.

title: I like these headphones
text: I like these headphones, warts and all.  The sound is good, excellent when you consider these are wireless.  Range is also impressive as I can walk around the house without any signal loss.  They are reasonably comfortable, though the clamping force is a little excessive initially.  Design wise I appreciate the dongle is stored in the left ear cup (behind a magnetic cover), and the mic arm tucks away and into the same left ear cup out of sight. Style wise, the implementation of the RGB lighting was done with some level of restraint and syncs up with your Logitech Gaming mouse and keyboard, assuming you have them.  The battery life is good for about 11 hours with RGB turned off (though it's advertised as 12), which is a lot longer then I will ever use them in one sitting.  I cannot honestly comment on the mic quality, I do not use it to record my voice, just to chat occasionally on Google Hangouts, but seemed fined for that.  Now for the quirks, which almost prompted me to return them.  The Logitech Gaming  Software program that controls much of the headsets functionality is a bit flaky.  If it is running in the background/taskbar, and I turn on the headset, it almost never recognizes them initially.  I usually have to exit the Logitech Gaming Software program, and restart it, which has always fixed the problem for me  and my headphones show up ( I am running Win10 with Anniversary update).  The second, and more frustrating quirk, is the dongle and headset unpairing.  First couple of days I had no issues with the headset connecting to the dongle, but one day I switched on the power button and got three beeps and green flashing lights.  At the time I did not know it was because the headset could not find the dongle, and I tried trouble shooting by unplugging /powering down/reupdating the firmware.  Re-updating the firmware worked and paired them again, but the issue kept cropping up, after not using the headphones for a few hours or day they would lose the pairing.  The only thing that worked was updating the firmware, each time it lost connection (pretty much every day).  After doing a little research and trial an error, I found a much simpler method to fix the issue, the reset button on the dongle.  Using a paperclip, you reset the connection and almost instantly everything is working again.  Once connected the headphones work great with no issues, but I wish I did not have to continue to do this.  Many will feel this is a dealbreaker, but despite this problem I will keep the headphones and hope a future firmware update resolves it completely.

text:
I have had this trackball for 8 months now. I bought it because I had wrist and hand pain from using a regular mouse. This works great for that. I'd say it reduced my pain at least 90%. The other 10% is because I use a computer all day and get sore towards the end of the day.

I found a forum thread on the manufacturer's website going back 3 years with complaints about this issue. Hundreds of people have experienced it. I haven't decided if I want to chase the warranty or buy a new one yet.

I'd gladly pay double or triple for the same mouse but built with much better quality instead.

Update June 2017:

I'm on my second unit now. Logitech sent me a new one about 8 months ago after going through the short warranty process. This second unit, has just started to fail like the first. The switch on the left click is faulty and will either not register a click, or rapidly fire several clicks. I'm constantly double-clicking on accident and cannot drag anything.

Going to knock another star off because of the poor quality of switches they put in this trackball.

title: Excellent headset with good sound in multiple areas
text:
Logitech has outdone themselves! These headphones are very comfortable to wear.

The pads on the ears fit fully around my ears so there is no discomfort during long gaming sessions. The microphone quality is very good... At least that's what my teammates say, as I have yet to hear it. When making phone calls via Google Voice, the person at the other end of the call also states the sound quality is good. The microphone folds up into the headset when not in use and produces a audible tone when doing so, indicating the mic is being muted or un-muted.

In gaming, the 7.1 surround does make a difference in telling which way sounds are coming from. I am able to identify where the bad guys are aurally, enabling me to have cross hairs waiting in their general direction before they are in view.

The headset features a toggle switch for the power allowing me to easily tell when they are off or on. The previous incarnation, the G930, had a power button that needed to be held to turn off or on. This may be annoying to some, but on power up, they play a little 4 tone jingle indicating they are on. The volume knob on the headset also produces sound when adjusting the volume, a higher tone for up and a lower tone for down. The G buttons on the headset are, by default, bound to functions that change the way you experience the headset. They do require a fair bit of pressure to push. The G1 button cycles through the different lighting effects. G2 toggles surround on or off. G3 cycles through the equalizer presets.

The RGB lighting is an interesting affair. The lights have multiple modes: Breathing (pulsing on and off), Color Cycle, Solid Color, and Cusom Lighting. The Custom Lighting mode allows you to turn on or off the Logitech Logo and side color strips, define a custom color to just be always on, and also adjust the speed and brightness of the Color Cycle and Breathing effects. Outside of a gaming party situation, I can't see them doing anything but decreasing your battery life while you use the headset, as you can't see the lights. It even says on the Logitech product page, that with no lighting you get up to 12 hours of battery. With lighting, only 8. Batteries only have a limited number of charging cycles, so better battery life without lighting = batteries that live a longer life. Mine have the lights turned off and will proabaly stay off. Outside of use, they do light up while charging.

The Equalizer has several presets: FPS, MOBA, Flat, "Drop the Bass," Cinematic Gaming, and Communications. I can hear a difference when switching between the modes, but can't determine why one would be better than the others in specific situations.

In Windows, these are identified as a 7.1 audio device, even without installing the Logitech Gaming Software. When I installed the software and clicked the Experience Surround Sound button, I literally got goosebumps while the demo was playing. The software has the ability to switch between "Dolby Surround Sound" and "DTS Headphone:X" modes. I am unable to tell a difference between the two, but I guess it's nice to be able to choose between those.

Outside of games, the 7.1 audio is very good. Everything from TV shows and movies, to YouTube videos sounds excellent. I previously had a pair of Corsair headphones and they required special software to "enable" 7.1. This resulted in everything that wasn't gaming to sound like the audio source had been sliced and diced before I heard it. In fact, I needed to return the Corsair headset inside of a week of getting them, they were so bad. Not so with these. Everything sounds wonderful.

There was a problem with the Logitech software when playing a new game, The Division, where using this headset would cause input lag on the keyboard. A big problem for a shooting game. Logitech has identified the issue and released a beta version of their software that resolves this issue and will be implementing the fix into their regular software the next time a new release is... released. Excellent support for a higher end product.

The 10 foot braided charging cable that comes with the unit has an excellent feeling to it, and fits into the charging port of the headset very snugly. I'm currently using it with a Samsung USB wall charger. The previous generation, the G930 had the charging cable and USB dongle connection integrated into a single cord with a dock that the two sides of the cables wrapped around when not in use. This is both a good and bad change, depending on your view. The separate charging cables gives you the freedom to plug in wherever you want, while the previous one would only take up one USB port on the computer. The long cable gives me plenty of room to roam around my gaming area without fear of reaching the end of my tether. An interesting thing happens when you plug the headphones into the charging cable and then plug the cable into your PC. Windows will identify them as a USB Input Device and even istall drivers for it. Without the software though, I was unable to get them to do anything the computer recongnized as "input."

My only complaint is the headband, if not worn in the correct position, does have a tendency to slide back on my head, pulling the ear cups away from the front of my ears. That may just be me having to learn to wear them in a less haphazard manor than the G930s.

The G930s I had received about 3 years ago for a Christmas gift. The only reason I moved away from them to the Corsair, and then immediately back to the Logitech, is that they died on me. They just stopped producing sound. I determined it was a failure with the speakers in the headset themselves, as I was able to hear a slight hissing noise in the headset when playing audio and having everything volume wise cranked to max. I am hopeful that the G933s can avoid a similar fate.

Long story short: OH MY GOD I LOVE THESE HEADPHONES!!!

Edit: Logitech has released the update to their official software version fixing the keyboard lag issue.
Edit 2: Turns out the USB device identified when plugging the headset into the PC is used to update the firmware on the headset. Very cool.

title: Perfect for CAD [SolidWorks, Fusion-360, Unity, Cura, etc]
text:
I have been using this mouse for the last 4 months and I am LOVING IT!!
I purchased this primarily for use with SolidWorks, Fusion-360 and Unity <- 3D modeling softwares. I am a power-CAD user: probably spend 6-7 hours a day on CAD (sometimes more). I have tried different brands and keep coming back to Logitech. I was hesitant at first to try the track-ball setup. But after a couple hours of getting used to, it was intuitive and straightforward. It especially goes great with the 3D Connexion SpaceMouse PRO.

SpaceMouse PRO (magical device)+ Logitech M570 (mouse)+ Logitech K310 (keyboard) is now the default setup on all CAD workstations at Carbon Origins. We do a lot of CAD modeling and this setup works like a charm.

If you are looking for a mouse to use with CAD software, you should definitely try this one out. It might not be a good fit for everyone though... A colleague of mine (also a powerCAD user) didn't like it as much. If you don't like it, you can always return it back and switch with a traditional mouse.

Sometimes the trackball gets a bit hard to move as dust collects around the tiny ball bearings (caster balls...) under the trackball. But it is an easy fix. All you need to do is pop the trackball out (very easy- there is a hole in the back for this), wipe the trackball and the bearings and pop the trackball back into the mouse and it's as good as new. I probably do this twice a week. Try to keep your fingers clean while using this and you can minimize the frequency at which you need to clean.

title: Great mouse with tons of features and capabilities
text:
This is the best mouse that I have ever had. It fits very well in your hand and that paired with the ability to tune it to a large range of weights makes it a very well suited mouse. I feared that this mouse would not fit well if someone had large hands, but the mouse is long enough that I believe almost anyone could use it. Upon just plugging it in with no drivers installed from Logitech you can already cycle through a variety of modes with different sensitivities and features. The software that you download from Logitechs website allows you to alter the sensitivity on any of the 3 presets as well as the color scheme of the light and the command buttons on the mouse. This mouse also has a physical button on it that acts as a brake for the scroll wheel. You can turn this break on so that the wheel moves and stops on the next notch down, (like most mouses) or you can turn it off and the wheel will glide easily and move extremely fast.

*Pros*
High customizability with sensitivity and features including weight
Fits in your hand extremely well
Software from Logitech allows you to alter the mouse parameters easily
Looks great especially with the customizable light

*Cons*
Wired mouses can be somewhat annoying if you don't like cable management

Overall I would highly recommend this mouse not only as a gaming mouse but for anyone who wants a mouse that fits comfortably in your hand and looks good doing it.

title: Middle Mouse Click Problems
text:
I was disappointed by this mouse. While playing games online, I always bound the middle mouse click as my push to talk for voice comms. However, I encountered a problem with this setup. The middle mouse wheel supports three different clicks: down for middle click, left for left scroll, and right for right scroll. However, it is extremely easy to accidentally rock either right or left while pushing down on the wheel, entering a dead zone between the mouse click and the scroll to either side. Altering the mouse settings to set the scroll clicks equal to middle mouse click has no effect, because the space between them is truly a dead zone with no input even though you have the wheel pushed down. I have never encountered this problem before, even with cheap mice. I know I can reassign any of the extra buttons to this same function, but I am disappointed that I have to use it in this fashion, changing a binding I have grown accustomed to for years.

I've tried this configuration on two different G502 mice: the proteus core and proteus spectrum. Both have the same issue, so I'm pretty sure it's not a one-off issue.

title: Fun to use mouse just not for First Person Shooters
text:

What truly effects the use of this mouse would have to be the thumb rest for it can in my case effect flick shots greatly and I use a 650 dpi while playing CSGO. For me it didn't feel as great as I thought and caused some hand strain.
Pros:
-Quick and easy DPI changer
-Nice feeling buttons on the mouse
-Free roll mouse scroll wheel

Cons:
-Thumb rest can get in the way
-Weight even without using the extra ones it can with
-Didn't feel that comfortable while gaming due to shape

As long as you are not playing an FPS this mouse is a great addition to any person's hands. Enjoyed the ridiculous customization that came with this mouse.

Comparing the G502 to the G403 for First Person Shooters, the G403 cannot be beat when comparing these two for they both have a similar sensor but the shape and weight of the mouse is what sets the G502 apart from the G403. Currently I am using the G403 as my main mouse and i must say that it is the best mouse to go with if you don't feel like the G502 fits your needs and if you still want to stick to the logitech brand then by all means buy the G403.

For many people this mouse might fit perfectly for you even while playing an FPS.

text:
These headphones.. where do I start!
Well first day, I was a little disappointed with there sound, It was clear but it just wasn't loud enough, but then it turned out that there was another sound option on the actual logitech program, it was set to 75% by default so, 100% it went and I can 100% say its loud enough, and with sound quality it is just amazing, its awesome for music, great base and treble, highs and lows. And with gaming, once you put it on 7.1 dolby surround sound it sounds a little tinny, I could still hear where everyone was and from a fairly long distance to, but it just didnt satisfy me, at first that was, I guess I just wasn't used to 7.1 (I never had put my hands on it before) but now it sounds so much better weirdly, I think I might just have had to play around with my settings because it was configured to my old headphones, but after a few tweaks, I loved the sound and I could listen to a gun shot, and turn directly to there head (CSGO) I also played a bit of Arma 3 with them, sounds great and thee same with CSGO, just amazing quality, I can also say I could sit down for ages playing games without taking off my headset without it getting uncomfortable, the software is also awesome, nothing more I could want there. But one of the biggest problems I had, and made me pretty mad tbh, whenever I hooked up this headset, it would make my mouse macros extremely laggy (I think because my mouse and my headset had to work through 1 program?) and slow to react (the mouse clicks where find though which was really strange) so after a few calls to Logitech to help me fix this, not one of them could help which was annoying, so I looked in the software and I decided I would switch Automatic game detection to on board memory on my mouse (which of course is logitech) and that completely solved it and now the macros work extremely fast just like they used to, although I cant customize it heaps the on board memory options did enough. The headset itself feels extremely premium and its weight is not to heavy
(nothing that even effected me a little) and tbh felt even better with that little bit of extra weight. It has lots of ear room so dont worry about it rubbing against your ears or anything like that! But yeah awesome headset, definitely recommend buying it!

It'd be great if this thing weighed around 90-100g and had the additional custom weights. As it stands, you'd never need them. I think the folks who love this mouse grew up using the big, bulky, gaming mice of the early 2000s, so the weight doesn't bother them. I had nothing to do with the dirt on the pad...which was very minimal IMHO. It was the dumb logictech software. It has 3 surface settings. Logitech G240 Cloth Mouse Pad, Logitech G something Solid Plastic Mouse Pad, and CUSTOM Mouse Pad...It was set to G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad which is correct...so I changed it to CUSTOM Mouse Pad and after finishing the calibration steps it has been working perfectly...not only that, but it moves more accurately than it ever has before. I added 1 more star because bad software.

Recap: Its strange that as the mouse pad acquired a slightly stained look where it was used the most AND also tracked like s*** on the used areas, I would rotate it and try to use fresh parts of the pad to get better tracking. I even found hairs and stuff where the tracking failed....but the normal darkening of the pad where you use it the most is literally untrackable...it seemed to work fine on the clean areas...so strange that changing software settings fixed it...I think it had something to do with the calibration steps but I'm not going to mess with anything now that its working.

So if you have this pad with poor results, try changing your software setting from this pad to a custom pad and follow the steps to finish the process and it might work better than it ever has.

title: Fun and awesome little camera, that can do what it says it does.
text:
Starting with the packaging, I must say, I am impressed. I felt like I was opening a box holding a product that is worth twice as much. Inside contains the camera (soft touch plastic camera body... feels more premium than plain hard plastic), like a display case, and underneath it, holds the accessories:

1 USB wall plug
1 USB cable
1 Magnetic and locking base for mono/tripod mounting
1 Micro SD to SD card adapter

The included 16GB card is pre-installed, and I immediately checked how difficult, or actually, rather easy it is to swap out (to a 64GB), very easy, no sticking, nice little recessed area for depressing your finger and then using that same recessed space to give you a little more grip on the mSD card while taking it out. I spent a good 10 minutes just fiddling with the parts and checking the fit and finish, and I felt there was no faults to be found, the magnetic base made it effortless to attach, and a simple twist locks it in (it covers the micro SD card slot, so there is more than just a press to get it out, but all parts play well together). Okay, enough about the physical appearance, packaging, and design, lets get down to business.

-Connectivity, no issues, everything works great, really. I can't think of much to say here. No random drops, no interference, nothing (so far). I wish my mirrorless camera can just connect to the damn app so I can transfer some photos to my phone sometimes...
-Sound, I would rate it a good solid step above using a phone, the sound recording is pretty clear if just a bit muffled, and do well recording voice (only thing I tried). Background noise seems well controlled. I haven't tried out manually adjusting gain and left it alone in auto gain and felt it just works, good for helping beginners like me get some audio that isn't all distorted and blown out in situations where the sound level may change drastically. Is it perfect? Uh.. probably not??? But its good and satisfying to know that the mic is constantly adapting to the situation.
-Camera, I remember when 4K video recording first came out and there was a huge deal about cropping frames out to use as photos, that was an incredible idea, not sure if it ever took off though... I feel Mevo's concept is very similar, or coincidental, not sure... It is a 4K resolution sensor, that means you have a huge canvas to play with and zoom, pan, crop whatever you want in a huge picture, live. I think 720p is fine, some may disagree, but I am not sure if there is a real advantage here going to 1080p many platform compresses the videos anyway dont they? I wonder if Livestream can release a firmware to allow 1080p recording/streaming and leave it up to the user's digression.
Its not a large sensor, and it doesn't perform like one. It performs like a good small sensor. This means it's not design to work well in the low light or dark, if lowlight recording is your goal, you are looking in the wrong place. Most small sensor cameras (including action cameras) in similar price range won't do much better IMO. Maybe Livestream can make some light attachments in the future as accessories?
-Battery life... Guys, seriously this thing is a size of half a can of redbull... you don't really expect more than a hour of battery life right? I didn't, but at the same time, I wasn't WOW'ed by it. Keeping things in perspective, I think Livestream did a great job on size/weight and capabilities vs battery life. One can always grab a battery brick (who doesnt own one now a days?) and keep it hooked up for longer streams/recordings.

I don't think I've tried everything Mevo camera has to offer yet, but its on to a great start for me. Anyway to wrap things up since I know I went off tangent and kept talking about random things... but this thing makes videos fun and easy! I love the idea of putting the camera in one place and just adjusting framing with your iPhone or iPad. It can make a decent video/stream with minimal effort, and you look like you used some decent rig to make it happen too! But in reality you used a camera that is half the size of a can of redbull and 1/10th the cost of pro gear... to deliver hopefully cool content.

I'd like to see Livestream release some light accessories, maybe a lens protector of some kind, and maybe a firmware to try out 1080p if possible?

Final Verdict: I would recommend this product since it performs well within expectations if not slightly exceeded.

I was looking for a gaming mouse to use at work. I work for a tech-company of sorts, so I spend a lot of time behind my multi-screen setup. I used the Logitech G5 a long time ago and remembered how much I liked that compared to the dime-a-dozen Microsoft business mouses that are lying around at work. After a couple of hours doing some comparison work, I figured it would be either the Logitech G502 or it would be one of the Razor mouses.

My initial reservation with the G502 was the amount of customization. To some this may appeal, but generally for me this is not a plus. The Razor mouses seem simpler. My main selection criteria was that I wanted a mouse that layed nicely in my palm, moved smoothly, higher DPI, and just felt right. I decided to go for the G502 due to my good experiences with the G5, and I have not been disappointed. The movement is so nice compared to business mouses, and I've actually started to use part of the customization that the G502 has to offer.

title: Very nice keyboard, though included battery was a dud on the two K750s I ordered.
text:
I really like this keyboard, I actually bought 2 of them for different machines. It's conformable to type on, and generally works like a keyboard should.

I took away two stars for two reasons. The first is that the battery that it uses to store power was apparently on it's last legs after only a few weeks. I kept seeing the red "low power" LED blink, so (when it wasn't in use) I tried leaving it in a few different places like in a well lit room or near a window where it was getting sunlight. This didn't resolve the low power LED, so I ordered a replacement battery. You have to get a very specific type of rechargeable battery (ML 2032, maybe $6 on Amazon). Since the battery has been replaced, it hasn't shown the low power LED and I've had it now for longer with the replacement battery than without. I don't know if I got one that had been sitting unused for too long or what, but I've noticed this behavior on both keyboards, which either means I'm really unlucky, or this problem is somewhat common. For what it's worth, it never actually stopped working, but I think eventually it would have run out of juice on the old battery.

The second issue is that the application/utility that tells you the information about battery charge and how much power it's currently generating doesn't work on the most recent version of OS X. In fact, it hasn't worked in several versions of OS X. Not a huge deal, but it would be nice to see.

I do like the concept and the keyboard itself. It's just a shame that the batteries weren't any good.

Far more than those wireless keyboards that take AA batteries.
I wondered how the solar panels would do in my setting. I have a large black out curtain covering a big window so my room stays really dark most of the day. I have my light on for a little while, which shows about 30-60 lux i think depending on the angle of my keyboard, before I end up turning it off. so needless to say it does not get near enough light to stay charged all the time. Buy that has never been a problem for me as the battery lasts a really long time. Around the time I get a warning with about 25% battery or so I stick it behind the curtain for a day while I'm at work. When I get home it's usually between 70%-85% and I am set for at least another month.
All in all its a fantastic keyboard and I will be using this mouse and keyboard until I can't use them any more

title: Supurb headset.
text:
WONDERFUL! I've always loved my G930's - and to be honest, I was a little timid about going to the 933's for a few reasons. First - the price. A little steep. Thank you Amazon for putting them on sale! Second, my 930's sounded GREAT - If something works, why fix it? (but they were getting old and the batteries were failing). Lastly - I've seen reviews that show them easily slipping off of people heads when they lean backwards.
Ok - Now I have them. They hug my head nicely. Maybe others had small heads but these actually stay on BETTER than the 930's. Next - the sound quality - Of course there's the initial frustration of getting the equalizer JUST the way I like it. Always true with new headsets - but now that I have? Sound quality PHENOMINAL. I'd say slightly BETTER than the 930's.
The software is SUPERIOR to the old 930 software. I like it. And although the lights may seem "gimmicky" to some - I LIKE THEM. They can also respond to games making player "teams" obvious. Kind of a cool feature.
Another selling point - USER REPLACEABLE BATTERY! I've had THREE 930's. Always replacing due to battery failure (still felt I got my moneys worth. They DID all three last for quite a while). GREAT MOVE Logitech in giving this headset user replaceable batteries. I'm quite pleased with that.
4 stars instead of 5 - I dock Logitech 1 star for 2 reasons. First, the cups could be SLIGHTLY deeper. My big ears hit the inside unless I get them just right. But it's not bad and not a deal breaker. Second - Lack of documentation in the packaging. Maybe it was just my set, but there was no manual or "fast start" guide. I had to figure out that I needed to download the software. Lastly - The charge indicator (which is in the software only) isn't terribly accurate. You sometimes have to unplug and re-plug the dongle to get an accurate reading. Attention Logitech - Look into this issue (I'm not the only one to report it) and make a "Fully Charged" indicator on the headset itself. Heck it has multi-color LED's, can't you make the blue pulse change to red while plugged in to indicate a full charge?
The negatives are quite minor. All in all a GREAT headset. I highly recommend.

- Ron Donofero

The other aspect about the keyboard is the keys. The keys are delicate and if the keyboard should fall or slip and be knocked it is almost impossible to get a popped key reseated.
