title: Absolutely Wonderful - Better than an Apple Chiclet Keyboard
text:
I have been a longtime Windows and Linux user - I don't really like Apple's macOS/OSX. However, for work, I've been using a Mac for the past few months, and fell in love with their chiclet-style keyboard. It feels solid and responsive, and looks attractive. I can't stand the fact that Apple's wireless keyboards aren't full-width (including a full numberpad, full-sized arrow keys, etc) so I've been using a Apple's wired USB keyboard, which is full-width.

I ordered this K750 in an attempt to replicate the typing experience I have at work on the Apple keyboard. Knowing the body wasn't aluminum like Apple's made me hesitate a little bit, honestly. But HOLY. COW.

This isn't just a typing experience AS GOOD AS the Apple keyboard, this is BETTER. The reasons:
-The keyboard is just as solid as any aluminum keyboard would be. It's not cheap-feeling at all.
-The keyboard is wireless, without the normal hassle of being wireless. No batteries to replace, no cables needed for charging. The solar panels keep it charged just fine, and it can be monitored so easily through the solar app that I never have questions.
-The key travel is wonderful and has a satisfying click when each key is pressed. Better, even, than the Apple keyboards I use.
-Each key is slightly concave, allowing your fingers to rest comfortably on the keys. Typing is great.
-Though it is wireless, everything is seamless. The keyboard works in my computer's BIOS, no problems at all. It's just as reliable and behaves as if it was a USB keyboard plugged into the machine.

Note: I don't game, so I don't see a ton of value in the zero-response-time thing that a lot of gamers bring up when complaining about wireless keyboards. I don't notice any lag in response time at all - as soon as a press a key, it is registered instantaneously.

Overall, I'm way more happy with this keyboard than I even expected I would be. No complaints at all!

title: A good keyboard - on the outside
text:
I bought this keyboard because it was cheap and it looked simple and not too over the top. At first glance, I was pretty impressed with it. As soon as I looked closer, though, things did not look as good. First, the writing on the keys is a sticker instead of being printed on. Although I know this feature is less common with budget keyboards, I would have liked it if they had traded out the solar gimmick for better build quality. This leads well into my second problem with this keyboard: it bends. It bends a lot. With the back stands put out, the keyboard bangs against the table with every press. Although this problem can be easily solved with a tissue, it detracts from the experience as a whole. Finally, although the solar panel is a good idea, I think it would be better suited on a more expensive keyboard where there would still be money left in the budget for the rest of it.

Pros:
+ Good typing experience
+ Sleek, polished appearance
+ Very good battery life
+ Price

Cons:
- Bad build quality
- It bends under the lightest of loads
- The keys have stickers instead of being printed
- The glossy finish gets smudged easily
- The solar panel seems like a feature used to sell the keyboard instead of improving the user experience. I mean, how hard is it to replace two AA batteries twice a year?

So, would I recommend this keyboard? Yes, I would. But only if you have a tight budget, and even then I would opt for something with better build quality.

title: like the Razer Deathadder that I’ve grown used to
text:
The two most immediately noticeable thing about the Marathon Mouse are its size and its design. The mouse is expectedly miniature compared to fuller sized mice, like the Razer Deathadder that I’ve grown used to. This makes it so that your wrist, instead of partially touching the mouse and partially touching the mousepad, is now touching the mousepad almost exclusively (depending on the size of your hand). This means the motion comes equally from the fingers as the wrist. While this may be annoying for some (myself included) it’s unlikely to find any mobile mouse with as many of the other benefits without sacrificing size.

The design is excellent, your hand rests naturally on top, while your thumb is cradled into the rest on the left side of the mouse. It looks sleek and streamlined, combining a darker gray chassis with a comfortable, matte black material on either sides, and a strip of shiny, black plastic separating the main chassis from the material on the left side of the mouse. The material on either side of the mouse itself is also great, adding a little grip without sacrificing ease of use and comfort.

The mouse functions well, and is accurate, though I haven’t used it for any type of gaming so far. The features are definitely some of the mouse’s high points. It includes a three-button scroll wheel, allowing left and right scrolling along with the main scroll wheel click common in most mice. Behind the scroll-wheel is a small button that rests between your fingers that changes the scroll-wheel from a more clicky movement to a smoother, free-wheeling motion. On the left side of the mouse where your thumb rests, there are three additional buttons. Two are higher up, above your thumb but still within easy reach, and another that is actually built into the mouse itself, meaning that if you press down on the material where your thumb is resting (you may have to adjust your thumb downward slightly to get better purchase on the button) which is a feature I’ve never seen before, and was impressed with.

Outside of buttons, the mouse also includes a small compartment for the USB dongle within the battery compartment. Finally, the battery compartment is set so the batteries are both facing in the same direction, unlike the usual opposing sides. This is to allow the mouse to function when only one battery is in, giving you some degree of control over the weight of the mouse.

This is an excellent mouse, and one that I found impressive despite the discomfort caused by the size. It’s a well-designed piece of engineering, with several worthwhile features that improve its overall function.

title: A simple fix for the left button double-click problem
text:
This has been my favorite mouse for several years because it is comfortable and has very flexible options that the buttons can be programmed to execute. Until it suddenly developed the too common left button double-click problem experienced by many reviewers here.

My experience gives clues to the cause of the problem and its fix so bear with me as I describe what led to this problem in case you might have a similar experience. I recently moved the laptop that I use it with from my home office to the living area so I could work while watching TV. The mouse didn't work on the glossy surface of the serving tray I was using so I used a sheet of paper as a mouse pad. The double-click problem started within a few days after that.

A web search found many fixes for this problem. Most felt it was a mechanical problem and proposed taking the mouse apart to fix it. Then I ran across one from KACE Tech Review that suggests it is caused by a static electricity problem with a very short simple and easy fix - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o-bUVxlDLaw. I tried that but the problem came back within a few days so I tried again, still didn't hold up.

Then I thought the mouse pad surface might cause an electrical problem. I had used a regular mouse pad in the office but was now using a makeshift paper one. So I replaced the paper pad with the old one from the office and redid the fix, bingo, no more problem!

So the mouse pad surface does seem to be the cause of the problem in my case.

Anyway, after many web page researches I found the way to change my channel setting for my Wi-Fi. Apparently the hub will not work at 5.0 and must be set at 2.4. title: Buyer beware - Defective product - Terrible Support
text:
This headset was touted as the best headset that will work with all modern consoles and PC and it's wireless. Sure, that's all well and good... For the first week or so that it worked.

This headset has progressively gotten worse as time has gone on and Logitech support is atrocious. They are unavailable on weekends and took almost a full week to reply by email to tell me the same troubleshooting steps that are already on their website and did not fix the issue.

When I finally got a hold of a representative I went over that in the week or so I was waiting on a response I got the headset at least semi-working and unbricked. I explained my actual current issue and she just went through the same steps for what is now a third time. Finally she said she would process a replacement. Here's that process:

1. They send me a return label in my email that I have to print. (I have to obtain my own packaging apparently)
2. I send the headset back to them.
3. They get the product and finally process my replacement.
4. I wait another 2-4 days to receive my replacement.

All said and done I'm looking at at least a week before I receive a replacement product. When I said that was unacceptable as I'd be without sound on my PC for a week at that point, she said "well you already have no sound right?" She did not listen to anything I said that it was a MICROPHONE issue and that i had the sound working. I was then told well, that's just the way it's done.

Regardless, there were no attempts to even make me feel any better. No sympathy, not even an apology. She basically said too bad, deal with it.

I'd just return this through Amazon but it's been more than 30 days. (I've had it about 3 months)

I've been buying Logitech problems for 15+ years and this entire experience has soured my taste so much, I will likely never buy another of their products again.

I usually do not write reviews like this, but I feel that people need to know. Had I known, I'd not have bought this product.

The issues were very minor at first, but have escalated terribly over the last 1-2 weeks.

Now they crackle and pop and disconnect every 30 seconds or so and the microphone stays permanently muted.

Do yourself a huge favor and buy something else.

For those who care, I'm fairly confident the issue lies in the wireless receiver as I have basically no issues over 3.5mm but if I didn't want to use wireless I could've bought way cheaper headphones.

In closing, these WILL break, and you WILL need to replace them. Safe yourself a lot of time and hassle.

title: ... this mouse for over 7 years and I'd highly recommend it to anyone
text:
I've had this mouse for over 7 years and I'd highly recommend it to anyone. I can't honestly tell you what the battery life is. I usually keep my mouse settings on the highest sensitivity and it's kept up with no degradation. I'm very rarely impressed by electronic accessories as they are usually made to be thrown away after a 2-3 years. I'm impressed.

Need to know:
Compatability: I clearly have not tested every OS but I know it works on Windows Vista(Yes, that's how old this mouse is), Windows 7, 8, 10, and Ubuntu 11 and later
Battery: 2x AA
Battery Life: >1 year (constant power)
Feel: Comfortable for an average sized hand
Handling: All the precision and accuracy of a gaming mouse without all the buttons
Range: (?) I've used it across a room (15-20 feet) and had zero issues, but I haven't exactly tested it.
Software/Drivers: Plug and play, no CD or Install required just plug the USB nano receiver in.
USB 2.0 and is compatible with 3.0
Quality: Excellent

After nearly 8 years of service I've started to have my first issue. title: Defective Key Mechanics in 2/3 Keyboards, Incompetent (and Slow) Warranty Support Staff
text:
PROS: Looks good, relatively light, 3 year warranty
CONS: poor key action design, incompetent support staff who do not read tickets and take 1 week+ to respond

My first keyboard of this model lasted around 10 months before electrical circuit failures resulted in dead keys. Thereafter, I received 3 warranty replacements: 1 was the wrong model, and 2 had mechanical problems with keyboard action. The design of the keyboard is such that even if the key is fully depressed, there is a chance it does not contact the switch beneath to register a keystroke. One would have to add extra force to ensure the connection was secure-- which over time leads to wrist and forearm pain. Evidently there is a severe design or manufacturing flaw if 2/3 keyboards I've had of this model had this keystroke problem.

As well, due to slow Logitech support staff responses, it took 3 months from the time I made my support ticket to the time I received the correct keyboard (which had mechanical keystroke problems).On average, the support staff would take a full week to respond. When they did respond, it was often without regard to concerns raised. For example, my initial support ticket was accidentally made for a different model-- however they shut down my ticket for the correct model, thinking it was a duplicate of the first (even if they were for two different products). As well, when testing for Bluetooth errors and despite me repeatedly saying I was using an Android device, they were giving me Windows desktop instructions on how change Bluetooth settings.

Disappointing for a company like Logitech. Do not buy this product.

title: Highly Critical 100,000 MP3 Reviewer says BUY THIS SYSTEM if this is in your budget range! Great Job LOGITECH. Bravo!
text: Hi my name is Bobby and I have been an Amazon customer since 2001 and I thought it time I begin writing some reviews given I have purchased 1000's of items on this great site. Great job Jeff Bezos. I loved you when I worked on Wall Street and I love you now. Great business. Ok this is the third type of system that I have owned and I am an audiophile of epic proportions. I read over 100 reviews on these Logitech speakers I just purchased a few weeks ago. For 34 dollars and free shipping you can not go wrong with this system. It is just as awesome as many have described especially for this price. This system is powerful enough to throw a party in any size room. The trebles are fantastic through the 2 small satellite speakers. The bass is rich and combines with the 2 speakers perfectly in my office. The little hand volume dial is perfect the way it sits just left of my laptop. I had read a few tips on previous reviews that prove true. The positioning of the speakers and the weighty sub is everything. I worked for an hour to get the most pure sound. I ended up raising the speakers exactly equal height at about 24 inches high and are 7 feet separated. The sub sits on a hard surface with 6 inches clearance on a low dresser at 18 inches below the speakers. The floor under my desk seemed to not allow to breathe enough and it is nice where it is for my vape battery charger to sit on top within reach. Hard surface over carpet is the biggest improvement. Also I placed it 2 feet to the left of my left raised speaker. The speakers sit 3 feet back from where I sit at the back corners of my L-Shaped desk. I am listening to it while I write this and Logitech should be commended for the pure sound I am getting right now on Pandora Today's Hits Radio. I tested this system on an Iphone, a very high end Android phone, 2 laptops and a desktop. The quality seemed to vary based on the quality of the device. Laptops were definitely the best by far. I highly recommend this system for someone on a limited budget who still want to feel the music cut through them at the high level quality sound that it takes to get that feeling. Just one small criticism which a few others have mentioned. If the sub-woofer had a separate control this would be 10 stars not 5. This will be the best 34 dollars you ever spent. When I lifted the Logitech colorful box out of the brown cardboard AMZN box I immediately noticed the dense weight. I knew right away. Yeup I made the right purchase. And of course it was the sub-woofer. I was like "really?" f"or under 40 bucks the sub weighs like this?" It arrived 3 days early too. Bravo on that Amazon. 5 Stars all the way. Buy this system if you are looking at it!!!Bobby

title: Good option for multi-component home theater systems.
text: I picked up one of these for $10.00 at a yard sale. I have a multi-component home theater system with 4kBluray player, TV, turntable, vhs/dvd recorder, etc. While I have a clutter of several remotes on the coffee table, I was reluctant to consolidate them into a single multipurpose remote, as they usually did not have buttons to control every function, and I also have a rare Sherbourn home theater preamp controlling the whole system and I thought there would not be a multipurpose remote that could be programed for it. I was surprised to learn that, using the internet, there was a program for the Sherbourn and that it had controls for every function of it. Granted it takes time to set this all up, but so far there is nothing in my system it is not able to control or have buttons for. With the main hub in the closet with all the components and the remote blaster near the TV, I have been able to eliminate my previous remote extension setup with all of those blaster next to each component and the master remote receiver next to the TV. I was skeptical of the claim that the main hub in a closet or cabinet and the blaster in the main room would work, but it does, perfectly! The one complaint I do have is that it takes a few seconds before you have full control of the component you have turned on. I think that is because it has to go through every sequence of the particular set up you are using before it is functional. Also, as the Sherbourn also takes time to come on completely, sometimes it will try to open the needed input in that setup before before the Sherbourn completes its warm up cycle and I have to go to the screen to the Sherbourn remote. (However, that is better than plowing through cluster of remotes on the coffee table.)  The other concern I have is that, from what I have researched, it is not possible to up grade this model to one of the more advanced Smart Hub systems by buying just the more advanced remote. It would be nice if Logitech offered that option for those who already have this particular hub (are you listening Logitech?). As I have had difficulty with other multiple purpose remotes, I know I would have never bought this one at the full  price had I not found it for $10 at a yard sale. If this one wears out, I might though in the future.

title: These headphones sound bad.
text:
These headphones sound bad. They have almost no bass and the highs clip making a lot of things sound scratchy. The G230's, Logitech's cheaper stereo headset, sounds better than these do.

I had a pair of G930's, Logitech's older wireless surround sound model, and they were much better than these are. Unfortunately they broke so I had to use my G230's for a while. The main thing I missed about the G930's was that it was wireless so I decided to give Logitech's new headset a chance, they hadn't failed me in the past so I felt pretty good about it. Sadly the speakers in these headphones don't even compare to the sound quality of the 230's. They clip on high frequency sounds making it sound very scratchy at times and the bass is almost nonexistent making them sound very flat.

One of my biggest issue is with the surround sound, and not even the surround sound itself. There are two surround sound options you can choose from, Dolby and DST, and for some reason the one you choose to use effects the sound quality when surround sound it turned off and the headphones are in stereo mode. For the life of me I can't figure out why this is the case. DST mode makes the stereo sound flat while Dolby makes it quieter and I'd say more muffled than bass-y. Both modes have a problem with highs clipping, I'm assuming because the headset speakers suck. Listening to stereo audio while in surround mode makes it sound like you're in a big empty room, and listening to surround sound while in stereo mode makes audio mostly come out of the right ear speaker. These were issues of the G930's and you would think these would be fixed by now.

The equalizer you can adjust in the Logitech Gaming Software doesn't seem to do much, while with my G930's I was able to notice a fairly large difference with the same equalizer.

The programmable buttons on the headset are a very odd choice. Not having them as they were on the G930's and worked well on them, just more of the placement. The G930's had the buttons on the side and were fairly easy to tell apart while these have them on the back and are pretty difficult to tell apart. They tried to make it easier by having different shapes for the buttons but they're not different enough to be able to tell apart without feeling up the buttons for a second or two. Also they buttons are on the left ear cup, which, seeing as they are advertised as gaming headphones, is very strange. I mainly use my left hand for moving around on both controller and keyboard and if I need to do something with my hands I usually use my right had first as aiming is less important than moving around, at least for a few seconds. Having to take my hand off the movement keys to press the buttons on the headset make me not want to do it as much as I might be able to if they were on the right ear cup instead. Again, this was a problem with the G930's that I would have hoped they fixed.

Everything else about the headset is pretty good. They're a bit heavy but they're are comfy enough it doesn't really matter. The ear pads are big and comfy, even with glasses on. The mic retracts into the headset which is probably my favorite feature. You can replace the battery on the go if needed. Having the ability to use a headphone jack and mix multiple audio sources is also really cool. I can't testify about battery life since I haven't even had these long enough to drain the battery, but and 8-10 hour estimate seems right.

Overall this headset is pretty nice if you're willing to sacrifice sound quality, which I wouldn't. They are built well and have some cool features but you can get much better sounding headphones for the same, or even a cheaper price.

text:
UPSIDE: Amazingly easy to get used to, just takes maybe a day to re-adjust your way of thinking from a "normal" mouse and feels very natural in the hand. The main reason that I buy these is that they work unparalleled in small spaces. I use one on my home desk because I often clutter it with work or study materials, and this frees up a surprising amount of space, more than you would think, when overall the mouse itself need not move except to adjust for hand and wrist comfort. It also has the benefit of not being limited by the surface you are on, I can easily sit this on my couch next to me and connect it to my laptop, even the modern high quality laser mouse is not capable of doing this reliably on most surfaces. For that same reason I also use it for the media server and 2nd small computer that I have directly connected to my TV. The function is top quality, the reliability and quality however leave something to be desired, addressed below.

DOWNSIDE: I have owned what will be 3 total of these so far. One for work, one for home, one for my girlfriend at home. For some reason these seem to have more problems than any other. I replaced my one at work finally with a traditional mouse as the trackball would act weird however the left click finally stopped working. I am about to order yet another to replace mine at home as the trackball will work fine, then almost stop moving or move erratically. I often have to clean it out and/or spin the ball at high speed to get it to re-register the movement, however this has become a daily thing now. I have probably 5 other different types of mouse from Logitech even up to and including one that is 5 years old and works fine however, those are all laser, not trackball.

For some reason these trackball ones seem to show far more wear and tear than the others. I will be purchasing my 4th and final one at least from Logitech and, if that one begins to have the same issues as well I will try another manufacturer.

title: Better than the Harmony One
text:
After dropping my Harmony One for the millionth time, the screen finally cracked. I've had two Harmony Ones so far. The first one I had,I spilled beer on it and shorted it out lol. The Harmony one is no longer in production and I wasn't really liking the changes they made with the new touchscreen remotes. So I decided to "downgrade" to the Harmony 700.

Wow, totally impressed with this thing. It basically does everything the One did except for the touchscreen. To be honest, the touchscreen while cool, was more annoying than useful. Can't tell you how many times accidentally pressed the wrong button on the touchscreen. This remote also lack the lacks wallpapers and sounds, not anything I miss.

The reasons why I like this remote more than the One are these:

1. Buttons instead of a touchscreen. Touchscreens make sense for things like tablets and smartphones. For a remote though, I don't want to have to look at the screen. Since this remote imported all my settings from the One, I no longer need to look at the screen to make sure I'm pressing right button.

2. Cheaper. This remote is aroung $70 compared to the $200 I paid for the One. Much better value buying this vs the One or the newer touch models. I i drop this sucker and it breaks, i'm only out $70 more dollars compared to $200.

3. Feels better in the hand. The One had very glossy finish that made it easier to drop (despite the matte finish on the bottom of the remote). This one has a matte finish all around seems to be a little smaller which fits better in my small hands.

4. Physical colored buttons on remote. More actual buttons!

The only thing the remote lacks is a charging cradle but thats not a big deal.

I highly recommend this remote to anyone who wants a solid, no frills universal remote. The only way I can see purchasing a higher end model is if you need to control more than 6-8 devices, need RF, or like touchscreens.

title: Harmony 700 easily solves complex Home Theater setup. Great price. Considered competitive remote controls costing over $200.
text:
Has the right blend of backlit "Hard Buttons" and "Screen Buttons" to make using the remote a joy in a dark Home Theater. The motion sensor to turn on the backlight is a great usability feature. This was a key criteria for me as I do not like the usability of a touchscreen remote without buttons.

Solved a complex Home Theater setup of 6 devices: Samsung TV, Oppo 105D Blu-Ray used as a Digital Processor, Parasound P7 Multichannel Analog Preamp, TiVo Roamio Plus, Roku 3, Apple Mac mini (used for music connected to DAC in Oppo 105D).

Programmed 9 Activities to "Watch TV: TiVo", "Watch TV: OTA" (OTA = Over the Air Broadcast TV), "Spotify: Mac mini", "Netflix: Oppo", "Vudu: Oppo", "Pandora: Oppo", "YouTube: TiVo", "HBONow: Roku", "TWIT: Roku". Unifies selecting different streaming and cable services on the best available device.

The Harmony 700 powers on correct devices and selects appropriate inputs on TV, Oppo Digital Processor and Parasound Analog Preamp and then selects the service of the Activity all with a press of one button. You then push another "Activity button" to change activity.

Initial programming takes about 30 to 45 mins if you have device model numbers prior to starting operation to setup the basic operations. Your configuration is backed up to the Logitech "cloud" and can be transferred to another Harmony remote in the future.

After initial setup you can easily add "Activities", change "Buttons" or "Screen Options" on the remote in the application on your computer (Windows or Mac). You can customize the "Startup Activity" with additional "commands" and insert "delays" if needed. Remote Control has a "Help" function that will try alternative power on, input selection and delays and getting user feedback to see if problem is solved. The Remote Control has a "Learning" function if device or button is not in the extensive Logitech database.

You can add up to 23 "Favorite Channels" with icons for the channels on the screen. Note Logitech does not provide icons but there is a website iconharmony dot com that has most channel icons available. You can also create your own icons by capturing a "jpg" format of your favorite channels.

Overall very easy to do basic programming. To get the most out of your remote you need to embrace the "Activities" model and think through your use cases. Any refinements are easily made in the app and then syncing changes with the remote.

The rechargeable Lithium batteries are a bonus compared to the similar Harmony 650. Battery charge lasts about 1 to 2 weeks before requiring recharge.

I considered alternative remotes but others were either too basic for my setup or required a dealer to do the programming at a fee and then additional fees for changes to the remote. The Logitech Software is simple enough that I could easily make the changes while having my configuration backed up in the Logitech cloud.

My list of changes I'd like to see in the product:

1. I do wish that Logitech gave more information as to what exactly was being done at Power On and Power Off sequences especially when the "Help" function is invoked to correct a problem as well as allowing the user to insert commands or delays into the Activity Startup Command power on and input selection sequence. Logitech allows changes after the Power On and Input Selection sequences but does not allow changes to their command steps. This function could be an "Expert Only" function.

2. The remote has a backlight to all of the buttons below the screen but it would be really helpful to have the Power Off, Help and Activity Buttons above the screen also backlit. Overall this is a minor inconvenience in an otherwise outstanding remote.

3. Allow more than 23 Favorite Channels, although I've only used 17 so far. This appears to be mostly a programming constraint since the only information kept is channel number (4 digits) and icon - 20k to 50k per icon.

Overall a great product well worth the $66 at Amazon. When it is time to replace it I'll buy another Harmony remote control.

title: After 3 great hours of use I was plagued with an issue ...
text:
I was very excited to try my new Logitech G933 headphones just as soon as I could get them out of the box. After 3 great hours of use I was plagued with an issue that causes the headset's sound to cut out completely and the LEDs to begin blinking green. Searching online shows that this problem has not been answered, and Logitech generally just throw new headsets at you until they start to work.

I shouldn't have to be "lucky" to get a working product when I'm spending $150. If this was a 15 buck headset I wouldn't be surprised that there are software issues, but with a company as big as Logitech to charge this much for a product and have it be functionally useless just hours out of the box is truly amazing.

I would not recommend this to anyone unless your latest fortune cookie mentions that you're due for a lucky day.

title: No way to adjust the bass
text:
For the price, these speakers met all sound quality expectations.

Deducting a star for not having any sort of knob or setting to adjust the bass on the subwoofer. There is a wired power and volume control, but there's no way to adjust the bass whatsoever. So you either use the setup as-is, or not at all. The only options are to hope your soundcard has built-in equalizer software to adjust on your PC, set up third-party equalization software (which is NOT as easy as it sounds), or use some sort of physical dampening to muffle the subwoofer (styrofoam underneath and/or a pillow in front, etc). Of course, you can also use media player equalizers, but that won't work for sites like YouTube or Netflix. Just something to know and keep in mind if you live in an apartment or dorms.

title: Surprisingly Good For The Price
text: This little system has genuinely impressed me. I am on a very tight budget and needed a replacement for an old desktop system whose best days were behind it. I find the satellites to be bright, (which I like), but not fatiguing. The sub delivers deep, accurate bass. In fact, the bass may be too overpowering for some people, but as I listen to mostly rock and pop, I like it. There are some mid-range frequencies that don't come through as strongly as I'd like but it is tolerable. I am also noticing some nice crisp highs that I never heard on my previous set-up. The 25W amp is more than adequate for my near-field listening position. I will say that when I was adjusting the volume on the controller there was some crackling which may not bode well for the longevity of the system. However, for daily use, I use my computer's volume control exclusively and only use the controller for on/off so it may not be an issue. Note that these speakers are sensitive to the source. I listen to some low-grade mp3 (128-192) and it is obvious. I also have some higher grade mp3 (256-320) that sounds genuinely decent. Lastly, either my ears are getting used to the new sound or they are breaking in very nicely. Definitely give them a couple of weeks to really open up before you judge them. While this system will never be confused with high-end speakers, if you are on a budget like me, I don't think you will do better.

title: Be prepared to return as defective.
text:
At first, these speakers were great. Solid, beefy sound, a massaging rumble flowing through the desk from the sub, and nice clarity for a desktop computer system. If these speakers continued to work this way, they would be a perfect purchase.

If...

In less than 3 weeks, the hum began. The speakers would slowly build a louder and louder buzz that made anything you were listening to get lost in a swarm of bees. Two days later, the right speaker goes out completely. Not even a buzz out of it, just dead. I double checked the computer by plugging in different speakers. No buzz, stereo sound. Plugged them into a different desktop, and the right speaker was still belly up.

Amazon return policy on holiday orders leaves me sitting on these until February until I can return them. When I receive replacements, I'll come back and update.

title: People who use it either love it or hate it
text:
I was a bit apprehensive about ordering the Logitech G13 after reading some of the reviews. People who use it either love it or hate it. I was initially leaning towards getting the Razer Orbweaver (the Tartarus simply doesn't have enough buttons for me), but, after reading all the issues surrounding its cheap adhesive, I decided to go with the G13. Although my initial impressions weren't great, I'm overall very glad I went with this gamepad. I was a bit lukewarm at first, because I didn't like the feel of the membrane keys after having grown accustomed to a mechanical keyboard. Aside from that, the G13 is really a solid product. The software is pretty straightforward and easy to use, and the keypad really does feel more comfortable than a regular keyboard. The joystick thumb controller is surprisingly much more useful than I thought it would be.

One thing I would like to mention is that I have long fingers, and the keypad fits great for me. I know that some people had issues with the G13 feeling a bit too large. See if you can try it out at a store before you buy. It's also pretty large in size. I actually have to move my keyboard completely out of the way in order to play with a more ergonomic setup.

Anyways, great product, and very happy customer!

title: Software is the best part
text:
I bought this game pad to replace a Nostromo N52 that I had for years. The Nostromo did not have drivers for win 10 and was causing my system to crash.

No CD on the box, I had to go to the Logitech support site and download. Not a big deal, but did take more time than just popping in a cd. Registered the device, but thw software link didnt work after the registration. Would have been 5 stars if not for the hassle.

The game pad iraelf is awesome! After installing the software and plugging in the game pad, the software scanned my system and downloaded a default key mapping for the games I play. That was pretty cool! Very easy to modify the key mappings with drag and drop to reassign. I was up and playing in about 30 minutes.

Besides the software, the pad itself is pretty cool. The thumb stick is smooth, much better than the N52 dpad. The LCD automatically shows in game info. E.g. Morale / Power and location for LoTRO. Can also set timers if you have a spell you need to recast every so often.

My gaming buddies we mocking me for ranting about how cool the game pad was, but I don't care because I was having a blast.

Only used one night so far, so I haven't really gotten in to any advanced features. So far, so good.

I am not a hard core gamer, I play one night per week for about 4 hours. If you play games with a bunch of buttons and controls (LoTRO, WoW, 1st Person Shooters), this will really give you an advantage.

title: Don't Bother
text:
Logitech is one of the least competent makers of drivers, software and hardware -- at least in terms of audio devices. I have logged many, many hundreds of hours using this headset and it's predecessor, G930. Let me preface this with this: I am an IT guy and spend all my professional and personal time troubleshooting technology. So I know more than the average consumer. Lets start with the pros and cons.

Pros:

-Decent comfort. I can wear these for hours and little adjustment is needed. The padding is great. It'll start to become uncomfortable after awhile, but I can't complain for as long as I've been wearing them.

-The sound is great. I'm not an audiophile, so I won't pretend to know what I'm talking about. All I know is that I can clearly tell when you go from these to a lesser tuned device, especially stereo headsets.

-Durability is decent. I've had these for about a year and I use them every day for 2-3 hours at least. Nothing has broken.

-Fairly decent mic, for being a "gaming" headset.

Cons (get ready):

-Will intermittently get wireless interference. Don't get these if you live in an apartment complex where the saturation of wireless signals is going to be a problem. Here's the kicker -- some days it's fine, other days it's so bad it drops signal every other second. G930 had same issue.

-The headset will suddenly reboot, without warning and often enough to be aggravating. At least once every few days, often times several times in a few hours. Not improved since G930.

-7.1 will stop working and will require that you either reboot the software, reboot the headset or unplug/plug the usb receiver. Often all three at the same time. Not improved since G930.

-Software will often-times not recognize your headset. If headset is off, software will show it as "sleeping." Turn it on, and it disappears entirely.

-Unmute/mute function of the mic often does not work correctly. Will get "stuck" in mute. Headset reboot required. Not improved since G930.

-Turn on headset and it'll just not play sound. You need to make sure it does it startup sound.

-If you use USB connection/charge and 3.5mm connections at the same time, you will get horrible feedback. Same with USB 3.5mm passthrough.

-Will sometimes mess up your entire computer's ability to play sound and error out when playing "test" sound. Most of the time, YouTube videos will start to freak out and lose sound.

-God forbid you ever get another instance where you had to run cmdlets to update the firmware on these things to get the 7.1 to function at all. I haven't had this problem in about 9 months, but at the beginning it was the only way to fix them.

Overall: These are a "Don't Buy." Two stars would be a little harsh if I were taking these as a first generation attempt. But many of the G933's problems were carried over from their predecessor's. That's inexcusable. Perhaps the wired versions might be worth it, but I cannot recommend the wireless versions.

title: Sound and the utility it comes with is really nice and really customizable
text:
Sound and the utility it comes with is really nice and really customizable. It's amazing... at first.
After about 2 weeks, my headset wouldn't connect to the wireless adapter. I spent about 2 hours troubleshooting, resetting firmware, reinstalling the logitech gaming utility, reinstalling drivers, nothing worked. I got this specifically for the wireless, and the only fix is to reset the wireless adapter EVERY. SINGLE. TIME I want to connect to it. I then have to go into the utility and reset all of the options for the headset, including the 5 minute sleep option. If I forget, the headset falls asleep and the only way I can wake it up is to reset the wireless adapter again, turn the headset off and back on, and then make sure to go in and tell my headset to not fall asleep.
I can't even customize the sound the way I want it to be, or enable the surround sound(which was amazing) because I'll just have to mess with those settings every single time I get back in. It's just not worth my time to go back in.
Many more issues happened at the same time. The sound quality randomly changes, the mic will mute itself for no reason. At this point, the only good thing about this headset is the battery life.
If my headset had never had these issues, honestly, for the first 2 weeks, I couldn't have been happier. 5/5 stars for the first two weeks. But now, I just need to find an affordable option to replace it because I can't spend 200$ on another headset.

title: ... as an upgrade from the G930 which was the best headset I had ever owned
text:
I bought this headset as an upgrade from the G930 which was the best headset I had ever owned. The hardware of the headset itself is top notch. It feels incredibly comfortable, looks very sleek, and is all around one of the better made headsets I've ever owned. The software and drivers, however, are garbage.

Switching between applications now occasionally causes the headset to stop working, which can only be fixed by going into control panel and enabling it then disabling it. There's no way for it to detect when you turn it on and off for it to automatically switch to your default device when it's on, then back to your speakers when you turn the headset off again. Sometimes, you can't even fix the issue with sound not playing by disabling and re-enabling the headset and must instead go into services and restart the entire Windows Audio service.

When playing games like League, every game you join you will get no sound until you tab out and disable/enable the device again. The faults in the device will occasionally cause Chrome to lock up until audio is restarted entirely, and will prevent any videos from playing. This is all related to the headset as when the speakers are the only thing in use, absolutely none of these issues persist. Further, none of these issues were a problem with the G930 either.

Logitech support has taken weeks to get to the point where they want to send me a replacement, but I've had to suffer through restarting 10 times a day in the meantime and, oh yeah, it's not the hardware! Uninstalling and re-installing all software and drivers for the device as per their support did nothing, but the headset itself is perfectly fine. Maybe somewhere down the line Logitech support will figure this out, but this was a birthday gift that I was very excited about and now it's nothing but a headache to deal with and I'm constantly thinking about just boxing it up and using my old G930 again or moving to a different brand.

If you buy this headset and it works, great! But if you don't, you might as well immediately send it back to Amazon because there's no resolving this issue with Logitech support, apparently. And with 5 day turnarounds on ticket responses and each one just being concerned with trying to swap the hardware and not resolve the issue, I'm not holding my breath that this headset will every be anything more than a shiny paperweight.

Edit: After struggling with Logitech support, they sent me a new one. Worked for a few months, same issues popping up, same support problems with them being unable to resolve the obvious software issue and wanting to replace the hardware. Have to send it in first before getting the replacement shipped to me, so I'm without the headset for work for a week or more. Just going to find a different brand and I suggest everyone else do the same. As usual, best hardware around and they couple it with the worst software on the planet so all you get is a shiny paperweight.

Edit2: At this point they've replaced the headset twice, I'm still facing the same issues, and now I'm no longer getting sound from anything but the left and right channels. No surround at all. It's apparently a known problem as Google search has shown me dozens of people having this same issue for years but there is no fix for it. Never been so disappointed with a headset. 100% do not buy this headset. I say this as a Logitech fan for two decades with a thousand dollars worth of Logitech peripherals.

title: All that you expect out of a controller.
text: I didn't buy this product on amazon, I acquired it used and have had no issues with this rugged controller that seems to hybridize the analog sticks of a playstation with the overall body of a 360 controller.Using AntiMicro to manually adjust the deadzones and maxzones the sticks would center at 0,0 90% of the time, with the maximum x and y range going out to about 32737 for my specific controller and the highest (which only occurs rarely >1% of the time) being at 1600, putting this controller at slightly less then 5% deadzone with it hovering more at the 1% mark most of the time. This is extraordinarily unnoticable while in game and any percieved deadzone from other reviews that I have seen is more probably from software settings (also remember that this controller was used when I bought it so buying it new may yield even better deadzone results.) Its feel in the hand (I take a womens xs glove) feels offf at first due to its unique hybrid design, but within minutes of use is completely unnoticable. Friends commented that the controller feels almost larger then expected when grabbing onto it initially but quickly getting used to it and having no issues. It's triggers have incredibly tight recoil that feels at home in both shooting and racing games. I have used both the stick switching mode as well as its dinput to xinput toggle switch (which requires you to reconnect your controller either by replugging it in or toggling the usb ports power. Its textured thumbgrips and navy blue exterior with texturized plastic that gives it a beautiful matte appearance and a steadiness even with rather slippery hands.Its dpad is far better in my opinion then the xbox 360's dpad, despite looking similar with its coin design it controlled admirably in emulated goldeneye n64 using it for fast fluid movement through levels. The default logitech profiler leaves alot to be desired and I would recommend downloading the free antimicro profiler to further improve your gaming experience. Cons with the dpads coin design it is sometimes possible to actuate a diagonal when you intended a four way movement, however I attribute this more to a sloppy hand then a design error.

title: Gave gaming headsets a 2nd chance but they still seem to dissapoint
text:
Im not an audiophile but I do own a pair of studio headphones with a 3rd party mic so I will make several comparisons.

Comfort
I feel like this is the most important part of any headset/headphone. The comfort on these are quite amazing for the amount of features it has. I honestly expected it to be heavy and hurt the top of my head after several hours of use but it didn't.

Audio Quality
The sound is pretty solid for a gaming headset. They dont really compare to some of my dedicated headphones that I own, but its alright. The bass option in the softwares EQ is pretty intense when gaming. But like I said, its average for a gaming headset.

Mic Quality
Now this is what breaks it for me. The mic on this headset sounds like complete garbage. Its incredibly muddy/low and produces a lot of low sounding static in the background. There is simply no reason a $160 headset should have this poor of a microphone.

Wireless/Battery life
There definitely arent as many disconnects as the g930 but it still does disconnect at least once a day. The battery life is pretty great, it will definitely last you 11 hours if you turn the brightness down on the LEDs.

Conclusion
Honestly, these are far too expensive for it to be even remotely worth it. For $160, you can get a decent pair of studio headphones and pair it with a 3rd party microphone and get a far better experience. The microphone and audio quality are simply not worth it and there are far better alternatives.

title: Low Volume with No Solution, Get Something Better
text:
The sound quality is decent but not stellar, and the distance/location of relative sounds in games if fairly defined; as well as the frequency distribution between highs and base. The primary issue I've had is the volume is low, REALLY LOW. Maxing out the volume while listening to music barely comes to 35%-40% of the Skullcandy PLYR1 headset I'm replacing.
After spending a day going through Logitech's support site there doesn't appear to be a solution, they recommend uninstalling the LGS software which defeats the purpose of having this headset to begin with. Even removing the LGS software only gained me about a ~10% increase in volume.

At this point the closest substitute for a solution I've been able to find is a combination of a sound booster (which does cause distortion) and using DFX Enhancer. And based on the numerous threads I've read on Logitech's support site there isn't a solution and there doesn't appear there will ever be a solution; just a lot of help desk platitudes. As of this comment, the latest software version is LGS v8.88.28, which after installing in the hopes it would resolve the issues caused the volume to drop even more.

So the bottom line is, if you're only gaming you should be OK, but if you're using them across multiple media venues (gaming, music, movies, videos, etc) save your money and get something better.

After that I was thrilled to discover how easy it is to use the headset with nearly any device (including my phone) with or without the Logitech Gaming Software. Using the 3.5mm cable that comes with the headphones you can plug your headphones into any device with the corresponding 3.5mm audio output. You also (like many other "noise canceling" headphones) don't actually need to turn on the headphones to listen to your music. Powering on the headphones is preferred because of the incredible noise cancelation feature as well as the cleaner and more amplified playback. As for the features provided in the gaming software, like all other Logitech Gaming devices, the G933 and G633 are extremely customizable from equalizer presets to LED control. I would love to go into all the features, but seeing as how I haven't used all of them yet and I don't want to write a small novel, I'll leave it to you to explore. title: Comfortable, with a lot of gimmicks and no longevitity.
text:
At first I was floored with this headset, having come from a Creative Evo ZxR wireless headset. This headset is very light and comfortable. The sound is clean but average at best, but audiophiles don't buy gaming headsets for their sonic qualities. One of the main features that is marketed is the 7.1, but this is more of a gimmick and you are better off leaving this feature disabled if the games you are playing feature a native surround sound implementation like Overwatch has with Dolby Atomos support.

For some reason the engineers decided have the headset nag you about battery power being low when in fact its still above 40% and depending on your power savings settings would still be another 4 hours of usage. When enabling all the power saving features, a full 12 hours of usage can be realized. There is no way to disable this and the only way to stop it is to plug it in. Not sure who thought this was a bright idea because if you were actually gaming and in the heat of a match that will really take you out your zone. A smarter idea would have been to let me know that batter is low at like 5-10% and give me the option to turn that off all together. Beyond annoying.

The real deal breaker for me its essentially dead after only owning it for 5-6 months. I purchased this headset on April 16, 2016 and its on October 1, 2016. While I can still plug it in via analog, its a wasted investment as I paid for wireless "7.1" headset with RGB and programmable buttons. Also the sound quality when plugged in via analog, surprisingly enough is degraded, the mic starts to sound very scratchy. Could not get the mic to work at all until I dug up the original 4 pole connector that came with the headset. In the days leading up to the death of the headset, the headset would power cycle itself and/or lose connection to the USB dongle. Now they wont turn on all. They wont charge. They are not recognized by either the dongle or the software. I suspect that the issue may be caused by the battery, which would not surprise me.

Although I can give kudos for the ergonomic design, being light weight and comfortable, I cannot recommended this gaming headset to anyone looking for a flagship model for last them a couple years or actual game with.

I will attempt to RMA but the fact remains this should not happen with the brand new device less than 6 months old. I will update my reviewed based on my results.

Happens usually when I turn the headset on, but sometimes just happens when I'm trying to fix the second problem, more on that shortly. This causes no sound using program or device on my computer to emit any sound. Even after the headset USB dongle is removed and device priority is set to default. Nothing. Nada. Problem is not fixed until I restart my computer.

Second problem: one application I love and use often is Discord. As someone on Reddit posted 8 months ago with no easy fix; muting your mic for 15 to 20 seconds on Discord causes the program to no longer pick up your mic input until you fiddle with your Windows sound devices or restart the program itself. This is to some degree Discord's fault, but mostly Logitech's as it seems this is the only headset that has this particular problem.

Overall, bought a cool headset and ended up with a giant headache.

text:
I had some high hopes for this headset as I've used the G930s for a couple years now. First getting them out of the box liked the idea of having a sliding power switch instead of the soft hard to use button on the 930s. I noticed the cloth ear cuffs help reduce more background noise than the pleather style cuffs on the 930s, it quickly became apparent that the thicker cuff was going to contribute to more heat build up though. The boom on the mic doesn't swing down as far as on the 930 and the muted indicator is harder to see without directly looking at the mic. A shame considering all the fancy led lighting built into the rest of it I would leave off all the time. The mute button being on the back of the headset was a change in the wrong direction I feel as well. The 930s it's on the side and away from the G function buttons, very easy to get to in a hurry before a sneeze if you a live mic. On the 933 it's on the back of the headset and up against the G1 button.
The headset didn't completely function with my Galaxy 6 at first. The in line play/pause button worked playing/pausing the music I couldn't hear at the time so I knew my phone wasn't the issue. I took the headset to my desktop and plugged in the receiver and hard wired the headset via usb. Driver installed fine and logitech gaming software picked up the receiver quickly. The headset would not pair with the receiver though. Found the knowledge base about dead sets and followed instructions. The firmware update found the headset immediately on a manual initiation and v27 was installed. The headset started working with my phone luckily but no improvements with the computer setup. Figured I'd try an older version of the firmware... now the firmware update applications can't find the headset while it's plugged in. One step forward... two steps back. Looks like I'm getting out the faithful 930 again and returning these. Logitech can sure make things pretty these days but functionally I haven't had luck with them. Don't like my recently added harmony ultimate remote over an older 1000 model.

title: *EXPERIENCE WITH SUPPORT* (IN PROCESS FOR REPLACEMENT) - Everything seemed fine until 30 days later.
text:
Upon receiving the headset, there was a firmware update and the only way for the headset to actually update was it needed to be re-synced, didn't look too much into it but whatever. I went to the latest firmware update and used it as anyone person in their right mind would. Fast forward to Day 30. I notice there are no green lights or any lights for that matter other than the red mic light. Found it rather odd and looked up possible solutions and tried every possible fix, 3 of which were posted by Logitech support in response to people who have had the same issue as I am currently having to which there was no success. The headset is dead and won't charge. Amazon will not take the return since I just passed the 30-day mark so I contact Logitech and submit a claim May 8th. To make this quicker to read, I will just give a quick summary of the conversation to speed up to the important part(s):
May 8th: Claim Filed - Explaining the problems I have been having along with what I have done to attempt to fix it.
May 10th: Claim responded - Logitech asks for more info about the purchase (The usual and expected response in a case like this)
May 11th: Respond with all the information asked for along with an image of the sales receipt and box's barcode/serial number.
May 15th: Logitech: "We already processed the replacement. We will be requiring you to send the defective device first before we can send the replacement. A UPS prepaid shipping label will be sent to your email within 24 hours so you can return the defective device. After we receive your defective device, we will be sending the replacement and a UPS tracking number will be sent to your email. Please note, that the tracking number will first be active circa 12 hours after you receive the automated email. Please do not worry, it is expected that until the tracking number become active, it will state "Billing Information Received" or may not function at all. The expected delivery time is 5-7 business days after the warranty replacement has been shipped. Once you have received the tracking number, this case will be automatically set to "Solved"."
So after 4 days of showing proof of purchase and other information about the item, I am told I will receive a shipping label within 24 hours. Normally I would be fine but this is my only source of audio so I really just want to get the ball rolling. I wait until Tuesday afternoon for a label.
May 17th: I respond to confirm that I received the email on Sunday and inform them that there is no label that was sent by Logitech or by UPS (Checked Spam folder too, I'm basically trolling my e-mail once an hour because of the email stating I'm to receive a prepaid label).
May 18th: Logitech responds with: Please be informed that the case is being monitored as of the moment. we will send you notification once update has been provided.
May 20th: Call Logitech's Main Support Line, machine asked for more specific questions about why I am calling, maybe 4 in total? After the questions were answered, I got a representative within 3 seconds. After giving the case number, I was told that the RMA was approved this morning and that I should receive a prepaid shipping label within 24 hours. (Basically the same exact message on Sunday but was approved 5 days later?). I received a label about 4 hours after hanging up.
May 21st: Dropped off package
May 22nd: Sent the UPS drop off receipt to Logitech Support
May 23rd: Support acknowledges and recognizes the tracking update. Package en-route to Logitech.

*Will update as this goes - Currently have no sound because of this problem*

title: The headset itself is very nice, the associated software is broken.
text:
The headset itself is very nice, the problem is logitech can't handle itself with the associated software. Updates bring frequent bugs and the software causes the headset to malfunction. Earlier this fall (2016) the headset suffered a problem where it would not unmute and you had to perform a hardware reset to temporarily fix it. They eventually released a patch to fix it, and it worked for a couple weeks. Recently however a similar bug has recurred and the mic will no longer unmute after raising the arm to auto-mute it. This time it can be fixed by muting and unmuting through the logitech software, but it will occur once again as soon as you raise the arm. In addition, if you have the headset plugged in while in use, it will occasionally (average about once an hour) power cycle itself. You will hear it turn off and then the start up tone as it comes back, losing audio for about fifteen seconds. This problem has persisted for a long time and many others have reported it.

The sound and voice quality is great and the headset is very comfortable with decent battery life, but it's buggy. And if you're going to spend $150+ on a headset, you should absolutely not have to deal with bugs and workarounds. The best part is that it's the software that causes the problems, so getting a replacement solves nothing. Don't waste money on this.

title: Great upgrade from my well-worn G930
text:
Super solid PC headset, was scared after reading some of the reviews but if you're buying this solely for PC use, you're likely to enjoy it as much as I have. As a previous own of the G930 I'll try and do some pros and cons for anyone in a similar situation.

Pros:

- Slightly better audio quality (Both headphones and mic)
- Removable ear cups that allow you to store your receiver for easy travel
- Build quality feels more robust overall, including the receiver
- Zero disconnects
- Foldaway mic
- Good fit (Could be a bit different for everyone else, but in general this fits better than the G930)
- Better looking design

Cons:

- Price tag is a little much
- Mic works fine but it seems like it should be a little longer

All in all, I do think it's a really good upgrade if you've enjoyed the G930 and just wish it didn't have disconnect/software issues, this is certainly a great headset to go for. The design of the headset also allows it to easily be taken on trips without too much worry, even allowing you to store the USB receiver inside of the headset. My only genuine complaint is that the mic appears to be too short. I say appears because people have been able to hear me fine, and in the end that's all that matters, but I still feel like the mic could have been a bit longer just for the sake of versatility and comfort.

This issue I could live with, but when combined with the other two issues it points to a larger problem with this headset.

Make your life better and keep this garbage headset out of it. I've contacted Logitech support so I will update this post if I have massive success in exchanging this headset, but I'm not keeping my hopes very high.

Logitech is aware of this issue and is planning to fix this, but as of today they are unable to give any time estimates regarding when this is planned to be fixed.

When I first noticed this problem and called Logitech, I was told by the staff member (who was kind of rude and seemed to have no idea what he was talking about) that it was a hardware problem. Then later when I called again, I talked to a different customer service representative that it was a problem with the latest OSX update.

Until they fix this issue and/or stop falsely advertising that they're compatible with Mac OS X 10.4 or later, I can not give them more than 1 star. This issue makes this mouse a non-starter.

title: The wireless range is amazing. I live and work in a large two ...
text: I work from home as a full-time telecommuter. I connect through consumer versions of Skype, Zoom, and Google Voice in multiple virtual meetings each day. Most meetings are voice-only, but some are video. All are exclusively through my computer.  Sometimes I will spend as much as 4 to 5 hours a day in virtual calls with people both in the states and overseas. I had previously used both plug-in headphones (Apple earbuds, Shure SE 215-K) and a bluetooth earpiece (Sony MBH10). The Logitech Wireless is a HUGE step up, and has made a major difference in my work flow. The wireless range is amazing. I live and work in a large two bedroom apartment with a rooftop terrace. I can go anywhere in my house with no negative effect on sound quality. I love being able to get a cup of coffee in the kitchen, see who's knocking at my door, or simply pace around the house while in meetings, without being tethered to my desk or its immediate radius.  Voices sound very clear and full to me, and I have been told by others that my voice sounds very clear to them. I read in other reviews that people felt like music didn't sound great. I am no audiophile, but feel that my itunes, spotify, etc. background music that I sometimes play when not in meetings all sound just fine.  I really like having the on-ear volume and muting controls--very handy to adjust in the course of a call without having to return to my computer, if I'm walking around the house. I also like the design of the base, which makes charging very easy and intuitive.  Ive had no quality control issues or technical malfunctions in the 6 months that Ive been using this.  My only complaint is that the on-ear style does feel a bit tiring/less comfortable after a few hours of calls. Overall I am extremely satisfied with my purchase to-date.

title: Works for me despite design flaws.  May or  may not work for you.
text:
I write software for a living. Accumulated computer workstation hours affect my aging body and I've found that seemingly small changes can make a big difference. Switching from a mouse to a touch pad caused my fingers to change position more frequently and eliminated the cramping and wrist pain. I have also come to appreciate some touch gestures that a mouse can not duplicate. That is the case for a touch pad, but why this one?

The field isn't exactly crowded with options and, as a Linux user, I'm drawn to widely used hardware because it is the most likely to have decent driver support. That narrowed the field further to Apple Magic Trackpad, Dell TP317, and Logitech T650. I had experience with the Magic Trackpad and found it smooth and responsive, but Amazon had a refurbished T650 for a quarter of the price so I took a shot. Three months later, I'm still using it regularly. It's clearly inferior to the Magic Trackpad but not sufficiently inferior to drive a change.

What makes it inferior? It's a well-built product on top of some poor design choices. Out of the box (original firmware), it's essentially an upside-down mouse. Left and right clicks are exerting sufficient pressure on a portion of the surface to push a physical button on the underside. Accidentally push the wrong part of the surface and you push the wrong button. I found myself getting right clicks when I really wanted left clicks and making a terrible mess of my work. I also found that my fingers objected to the amount of pressure required to activate the buttons. Thankfully, Logitech addressed the physical awkwardness with a firmware upgrade in 2014.

The upgrade, available at support.logitech.com, provides "tap" gestures to replace the physical clicking. Tap with one finger for a left click. Tap with two fingers for a right click. That's a major improvement and, if Logitech had stopped there, their product would be almost as good as Apple's, but instead they decided to double-down on their original poor design choice and add a third right-click method: tap on the lower right portion of the surface. Consequently, I still found myself right-clicking when I meant to left-click. Ultimately, I resolved this with a hack: placing a stack of three business cards over the right-click area and fixing them to the surface with electrical tape. It's ugly and it causes me to lose surface area, but it eliminated the need to recover from accidental right-clicks.

Another questionable design choice is the lack of a low-battery indicator. This is a particular nuisance because the battery takes at least an hour to recharge to a useful state. I worked around the issue by keeping the device plugged into USB power consistently. If you actually need your touch pad to be wireless for extended periods of time, this could be a deal breaker for you.

As another reviewer noted, the firmware upgrade process will annoy Linux or Mac users. It requires a physical Windows machine or a Chromebook, so I had to install a copy of Windows 7 on an old notebook retrieved from a junk heap in my garage and then muddle through a series of screens that didn't make much sense to me. The upgrade itself, however, was well worth the effort.

Finally, how well the T650 works for you will depend on what you intend to do with it. I do most of my work on the command line or in text editors which require little or nothing from a pointing device. For moving windows around the desktop and switching between them, the touch pad is more than adequate. I also found it perfectly serviceable for manipulating images with GIMP and killing orcs with Battle for Wesnoth. The right-click issues may make it insufficiently precise for serious photo editing or gaming.

All in all, it's good enough for me. It beats a mouse and I'm not sending it back.

title: Great quality for the price
text:
Pros:
good audio quality, no need for phantom power or other equipment. if you're a beginner on a budget or don't need a fancy setup this is a one-and-done buy.

Cons:
depending on your setup the spherical shape can be somewhat bulky and awkward. does not fit a standard shock mount or have an XLR connector. if you're a quiet speaker you may need to keep the mic within about a foot from your face.

Other thoughts:
the pickup pattern on this mic is basically a full hemisphere in front of the mic. so placement is kind of critical as it can and will pick up your PC fans, keyboard clacking, and any other sounds in the room. i was able to filter out the sound of my PC fans pretty easily with software and now it sounds great. I've seen a lot of reviews complaining about the sensitivity to background noise but this pretty much comes with the territory of condenser mics. if you want zero background noise without a soundproof studio or any post-processing, get a dynamic mic.

overall the advantage of this mic is that it's very easy and cheap to set up, requiring no extra hardware/equipment or even software. this makes it a good choice for beginners, but anyone wanting serious, professional audio will probably want to look into a real studio mic

title: Logitech Harmony 950 IR Universal Remote: Over priced and over rated.
text:
I am the sorry owner of 4 of these overhyped and overpriced devices. One is used in a home theater, and two others are intended to run multiple devices other a TV. One simply operates a TV. I am using these devices along with a Direct TV Genie. I have a 4K "Client" and have 4K Netflix service that I can view on an LG OLED 4K 55" set.
The problems with the 950 are multiple. It is impossible to program without a computer and Harmony software is complex and very user unfriendly. The program has no way to identify which 950 you are programming or editing; that's up to the user, a problem if you have multiple remotes as I do. All 27 buttons are small, crammed together in a 2 in X 3 and a half inch space and can be very difficult to identify in dim light. The worse feature is the touch screen which just doesn't work consistently on any of my devices. You can trigger a response by just passing your finger over a number or icon. Often this is not the number or icon you intended to touch. Or sometimes you have to touch an icon or number multiple times to get any response. This can be very frustrating when you are trying to enter a 3 digit channel number. The 950 measures 7 and half inches by 2 and weighs 6.0 onces. Dedicated remotes for your electronic devices, especially the Direct TV Genie remote, are infinitely more user friendly and reliable.
I have had these for 10 days now and have asked both the dealer and Logitech for a refund on my purchase. Logitech won't respond and the dealer simply became very angry with me when I expressed my disappointment.

text:
So you're thinking about purchasing a Snowball Ice microphone from Blue? Let me see if I can help you with that. First off let me say this microphone is excellent! The difference in my audio quality on my YouTube videos is night and day. I highly recommend this microphone if you plan on dabbling in YouTube videos or even use Skype a lot. CONS:

-The light on the front is bright and can be distracting until you get use to it

TIPS:
-Buy a microphone boom and pop filter, you will not regret this small investment
-This microphone can pick up echos in certain rooms - I picked up some sound absorbing material and placed them around my pc desk

If you don't want to spend 160+ bucks on a microphone then I honestly think there's no better choice than this beauty. Do yourself a favor and "JUST DO IT!"

Tried changing mouse batteries, restarting computer, plugging it into all my USB ports to try to get it to work, and even tested on 3 other computers--nothing. Contacted the seller for return or exchange but their one line robot response of "the item is outside the return window" was pretty damn frustrating. title: It works as a controller but sadly it doesn't at the sametime
text:
I have been using this controller for around 4 months as my main way to control an Gaming HTPC I built recently, it boots directly on Steam Big Picture so I'm able to boot up any game on your library without even using a mouse or keyboard and even access certain functions so I thought a wireless controller like this would have been the perfect solution for my current setup, after all I have been gaming mainly on consoles for decades, sadly it isn't an experience as smooth as it should be.

I'm basing this reviews from my 4 months of use playing through following games to completion with only few exceptions: Valkyria Chronicles, Fallout 4, Dishonored, Saint Rows 4, Lethal League, Spelunky, Sonic Generations, Undertale, Freedom Planet, Stardew Valley, One Piece Pirrate Warriors 3, Borderlands The Pre-Sequel and other games.

Overview/Pros:
As a normal controller, it just works completely works,the D-pad feels great to play 2D games like Freedom Planet, Undertale and Spelunky I used mainly the D-pad to play all this games and had no issues with it and its current layout. There's also a mode button that swaps the Left Stick and D-pad functionality, this way you can use it with games with no controller layout options, its an easy turn around that you have access through at any point of the game so you can swap at any time. Those that wished for a PS3 controller with a bit more of weight and size, longer battery life, and actualy good triggers will feel extremely happy with this controller, its only short coming in my personal opinion its the bumpers that feel extremely stiff, feels as stiff as if they were the RS(R3) and LS(L3) buttons that are integrated on the sticks. Its powered by 2 Double A Batteries and they are include and I haven't even replaced them after 4 months of play and comes with a USB extender and a small dongle for it to connect to your PC and has a switch to change it from Dinput to Xinput(Xbox 360 controller) modes and you can turn off vibration at any time with the press off a button and delay isn't noticeable.

The shortcomings:
Besides the Right and Left Bumpers feeling too stiff for my taste. The installation process sadly its not just plug and play if you're currently using Windows 10, I had to go through a guide to just use the controller, assigning drivers and even downloading Microsoft drivers in some cases, etc... Basic things that a person that knows its ways through tech can easily go through but can't say the same for the rest. The range even using the USB extender its just horrible, from the USB dongle to the controller, there's around 6 feet and the controller would disconnect randomly even thought the controller and the dongle are around the same height the way I set it up. Also, Its IMPOSSIBLE to reprogram home button to anything, so Windows 10 and 8.1 users won't be able to access Steam Big Picture options while playing, instead due to this you are going to be greeted by Xbox DVR features, wished Logitech would have given us a work around for this.

Side notes:
-Vibration will automaticaly turn off when your batteries are running low on energy, something to keep on mind, this is not even explained on the manual.
-Those having other 2.4 GHz wireless devices, your range and disconnection issues should be even worse or unstable and this is bound to happen if you get a F710 controller for multiplayer, because you're going to need to use 2 separate dongles.
-You can't customize the controls while on Xinput mode with the Logitech Profiller only on Dinput.

My Recommendation:
If you're looking for a budget priced controller to play from your basic PC desk setup and don't mind taking extra steps to set it up, look no more and just get this controller, if you have an HTPC and want to control your PC from a distance with Steam Big Picture or want to setup multiple controllers for multiplayer or don't want to deal with the setup process, just get an Xbox 360 or Xbox One controller with an adapter, I think for the long run its seems to be a more reliable option, this is not the permanent solution for you.
