title: Great controller overall, bad for Windows 10
text:
It's a great controller, possible one of the best that you can get for PC, but it just simply doesn't work right under Windows 10 and likely Windows 8/8.1. So I could say Logitech are false advertising.

I have a lot of their products, and to be fair, none of them are meant to last, apparently. G19 - the screen broke and is now bright and unreadable. G300 - the wheel is starting to fail. F710 - loses connection OH SO often. I plugged it into every possible USB port, both with and without an extender cable, and it just keeps losing connection and starts to blink in the most intense moments during gameplay. I swapped batteries a couple of times, still the same results.

Also, there are no official/unofficial drivers for Win10. You can install it as a classic Xbox 360 controller and it will work in XInput, but the problem is, you're losing some functionality off the controler, and that extra functionality is nifty. The "Logitech" button in the center for example works VERY well with Steam Big Picture. You want to use this controller under Windows 10 and have all the Big Picture functionality? Too bad. Switch to Windows 7 or something, where it actually all works like intended and you don't even have to do anything. For the newer systems there are no options, I guess. The center button does absolutely nothing, it doesn't bring up the Big Picture when in classic Steam, it doesn't make screenshots or bring up a Big Picture overlay in-game. Kinda funny because F710 was very heavily advertisted for Big Picture back then, and now it's practically useless, and nobody ever cared to make a patch or a compatible driver.

title: UE 900s - Not Perfect But It Does Bring Some Good Value & Sound ...
text:
UE 900s - Not Perfect But It Does Bring Some Good Value & Sound

Packaging 9/10 - Box looks and feels quite premium. Un-boxing makes you feel like you made a good decision with your hard earned cash. Shipped very quickly and is as advertised.

Accessories 8/10 - Huge assortment of ear tips of both silicon and memory foam variety. Excellent layout of the ear tips all sorted by size. There is an inclusion of these plastic holders for all sizes so that you may test out each size to find the perfect fit. Very nice touch and spells out premium quality. However, I knocked off a point because although the ear tips are nice I found that they still do not provide the best fit as other after market memory foams that I have used. Sound signature appears to be modified using the provided ear tips. Read further in sound section for details.

Both of the included cables were good quality. One has the remote the other does not. They feel solid but the construction could have been better. Hence, knocked off another point. They are not 100% perfect and they do not exude "luxury" at this price point. The braided cable leading from the Y-split to the jack feels absolutely great and durable. However there is no strain relief and only a small rubber/plastic cover. From that point on the wires that lead up to the earphones themselves do not feel as nice and in my opinion makes it look a bit cheap for the price you are paying. Providing some rubberizing/casing for it would give it that ultimate feel and durability instead of making you crave for better cables.

Sound 9/10 - Listening to these at first utilizing the included ear tips I felt that the sound appeared slightly veiled. Highs, mids, lows for some reason did not sound a crisp to me. I then switched up the ear tips to after market memory foams and that made the biggest difference. The sound from these are very detailed and balanced. Highs and mids are very good. However, the highs to me can be slightly veiled at times depending on the music but these are definitely very high quality in sound and worth every penny you paid for. The bass is good and present, but it lacks a little less of a punch but it definitely is not bad at all.

Conclusion - The UE 900s represents good value at this price point. The UE sound signature is definitely present. I own their UE 6000 series headphones and when I first bought it 5 years ago it blew my expectations out of the water. The UE 900s sound very nice for this price level and although there are some shortcomings with the included ear tips and wires these are minor quibbles and should not deter anyone looking for a good set of universal in-ear monitors from this reputable manufacturer.

title: Terrible mouse for an engineer.
text:
This mouse is so frustrating to use for anything other than basic computer uses like searching the internet, reading emails, ect.

I bought this mouse thinking that it would be useful for myself, an engineer, due to its many buttons and programmable capabilities. I put brand new batteries in it when I originally got it and plugged the little usb drive in. The mouse is very easy to set up and also very easy to program the buttons. However it wasn't until I began trying to use the mouse in a CAD program that I realized there is no scroll click while pushing the scroll wheel directly in. This feature is needed to rotate a model in almost any CAD program. The mouse has a click between hyper-scrolling and regular scrolling when the scroll wheel is pressed directly down. Not to mention that the "hyper-scrolling" is possibly the most useless feature on any mouse ever. When the hyper-scroll is engaged the wheel literally just continues to spin for like 10 seconds after you roll it. So I managed to work around that feature by making one of the side scroll clicks do that function. A real pain to try to get used to after many years of using a direct click on the scroll wheel.

I used the mouse for a day or two before I noticed that the mouse seemed to lag or stop moving every once in a while. I thought that maybe the batteries I had originally put in were bad. So I replaced them and began using it again. About another two or three days later the same issue began happening again. It basically would lose connection for a split second and whatever button I has holding down or trying to click wouldn't work. Extremely frustrating while trying to model parts and manipulate assemblies. I thought that maybe the mouse just had a bad range and couldn't maintain a strong connection so I moved the computer and usb drive directly next to the mouse hand. same issue occurred. Checked the batteries and the programs says they are 95%.

Overall I believe this mouse would be OKAY to use if it stayed connected the entire time, however it doesn't. I can get over some of the other little issues just by using it a lot and getting used to it. I would not recommend this product to anyone that uses a mouse continuously on a daily work basis. I wouldn't even buy it for my own personal use at home. The lack of a center scroll click ON the wheel is terrible.

title: I really liked the headphones
text:
I teach English on Skype while visiting various countries, and bought one of these in June 2015 to use for work. At first, I really liked the headphones. That was because they were light and very comfortable- instead of cheap foam, the earpieces have nice, soft fabric. Also, the cable was far more robust than the one used on Logitech's lower-end models; I thought this augured well for durability. However, there were some issues. First, the mike was susceptible to wind. When there was a light breeze, it was very audible both on my side and the student's, something which had not been the case with cheaper Logitech headphones. Second, the inline volume adjuster has square edges on it that snagged easily on clothing and hard edges of tables. That leads me to the third issue, which was that because of such a snag, the headphones fell a few inches and broke the flimsily attached microphone tube off, leaving it dangling by a tiny wire. (This issue has been noted by several other buyers.) Fourth, the headphones had a glitch which caused them to make a painfully, nearly damagingly loud CHIRP sound in both ears when using them to listen to music or watch videos.
After returning home for Christmas in 2015, I called Amazon, and they agreed to replace the headphones for free. I got new ones, which exhibited most of the same flaws (there has been no physical breakage yet), plus a new one: the mike simply stopped working. In the middle of Skype calls, my students would tell me, "Hey, I can't hear you". I'd reboot the computer, add updates, log out and log in again on Skype, all to no avail: the headphones only worked for part of each call, and then stopped working. Luckily, I have some non-H650e backups with me, and I now use them. Hopefully I can get a refund, because both of my H650e's have really, really sucked.

title: Grand keyboard, BUT letters and numbers wear off from heavy use.
text:
I purchased this back in 2013 and it's now 2016. The keyboard and mouse are used for work. Overall, it's one of the best wireless keyboards I've ever used. It's still functional and I have yet to change the batteries.

However, there is something that nobody's discussed in reviews that I felt required mentioning. The letters and numbers aren't embedded in the plastic keys, their simply a labeled imprint.

After about a year's use, the letters and numbers wore off from heavy use. Note, I'm a guy, so I tend to be a lead-fingered key puncher and perhaps that contributed to the wear and tear. Regardless, the characters do wear off from use.

Other than the characters wearing from the keys, I'm comfortable with the keyboard and didn't want to buy a new one just because I had to guess which key I was pressing. Due to this dilemma, I had no choice but to use labels and stick the characters back on the keys that wore off. Even then, I have to cover the labels with clear tape to keep the inked letters from wearing off. Granted, this isn't the perfect solution, but it suffices for it's simplicity and function.

As stated, my circumstances maybe unusual because it's used constantly with heavy fingers. Under normal, infrequent use, the keyboard will probably hold it's own for many years. Other than the issue I just mentioned, it's a grand keyboard and well worth the price.

title: Was PAINFUL to set up before it died.
text:
Pros: Tons of integration points and device support. It gracefully turned 6 remotes into 1. It does what it is supposed to do, and after setup it does function as a remote well. I was able to integrate it with my Amazon Echo via IFTT so that I could add voice control to some basic functions on my devices, which did work, but not without issues.

Cons: The device can be slow. Very slow. Whether you're using the remote or sending commands via a phone or other service, you can occasionally see some significant lag which usually resulted in me pressing the button again, sending an additional but unwanted command. For instance, I would go to turn the volume up a few notches, think the hub wasn't receiving commands from the remote, so naturally I would volume up a few more times, and suddenly get blasted once the device suddenly responds to every press. Then there's the setup. It was slow and painful. The process of setting up new devices did not seem very logical, requiring you to tie devices to specific "activities" rather than allowing the user to pick which device specifically they would like to use the remote with. Yes, you can add devices and then not tie them to an activity, but this in effect is useless. This only will allow you to control the device through the phone app, but not the remote. Perhaps I am missing something, which very well could be, as the app interface is not very clear or informative. Sure, it's pretty; there are some good design elements, but it is lacking in substance. Re-adding devices and changing around activities is also PAINFULLY slow. Every time you want to configure something new, or make a change, you are required to wait while the app syncs with the Hub. This happens constantly as changes are made, requiring you to wait up to a minute each time. All of those minutes add up. It took me about 15 minutes to the the Harmony connected to its remote and to my WiFi, then another hour or so just setting up a TV, sound bar, PS4, Roku, and Chromecast. Calibrating the settings for sending commands took another half an hour to get right, and it still was never entirely consistent, but did work.

After a painful set up, it lasted about 5 months before it died unexpectedly. It had been connected to a quality surge protector, I live in a dry region where there is no hazardous weather, and the unit was stored in a place where it went essentially untouched. I attempted to use their website (which is also painful) to come up with a solution. I attempted to reset the device, then finally downloaded their desktop app per the suggestion as a final solution. This did not help either. After many attempts at getting the device to connect to the desktop via USB, following the instructions on their site, I could never get the device to connect. It is now a glossy black paperweight. Prior to it dying, I may have recommended it, but now I would tell all to steer clear until there are some serious revisions to both the product and its app.

title: Setup for MSI z97 gaming motherboards, and boards without color coding.
text:
These are worth $50. They produce excellent Bass, and clear undistorted sound from each speaker. I am using them on my MSI z97 gaming 5 motherboard. The trick to getting them installed is to plug them in correctly. That may not seem like much of a feat, but the z97 doesn't really have color coding, it's one red port for the front speakers and the rest of the ports are black. Also the manual for this sound system doesn't tell you which of these colors are for which speakers.

Here they are:
Front speakers: Green.
Center/Bass: Orange
Rear: Black

My motherboard has labels for each port, so make sure you plug green into the red port, and orange into center port below it. Then the black goes into the rear port. They should be labeled. If not, I have included a picture for reference. If you plug the black into the Surround sound port instead, that will not work as it is only for 7.1 sound. Then all you need to do is make sure your realtek drivers are up to date and that correct output is selected under the playback devices section. You can also download Creative Sound blaster Cinema 2 to tune the sound further and get even better performance. I hope this has helped.

title: Good smart keyboard for the Logitech Harmony devotee.
text:
I am a big fan of Logitech remotes, keyboards and mice and this product didn't disappoint me at all. It was very simple to setup coming from a Harmony 700 and it does what I need it to do, control various streaming boxes using a full-sized keyboard. I am using it with a Roku LT, Amazon Fire TV 1st gen, Apple TV 3rd gen, TiVo Premiere, and a Windows 10 PC. This keyboard does not have backlighting but I always feel deducting points for something it doesn't do, and doesn't advertise it will do, is silly. It is a non-backlit keyboard that works with many IR, RF, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi controlled devices, although not all devices, and it works well.

Compared to other non-backlit keyboards for this purpose, I believe it is the best option, thus the 5-star review. I hope rather than dropping this type of product since it doesn't appear to be a success, Logitech offers one with backlighting.

title: Nice receiver but not for the Amazon Echo device
text: I purchased this in hopes of connecting my home stereo to my Echo Dot using Bluetooth.  Unfortunately, the Logitech receiver (and many other Bluetooth receivers as it turns out) doesn't work well with the Echo because they feature an auto-reconnect function that tries to re-establish a connection when it is "lost".  Connecting it too the Echo was straight-forward and the sound quality was much better than a cheap receiver I tried before.  However, when I told Alexa to disconnect and switch back to the hard-wired connection, she obeyed and her voice immediately switched to the hard-wired speakers.  However, a few seconds later I hear a beep and the Logitech receiver reconnected to the Echo via Bluetooth and the Echo no longer used my hard-wired connection.  No matter what I did I could not disable this auto-reconnect and the Echo always switched back to Bluetooth.  The only solution I've found is to disconnect power to the Logitech receiver when not using it.  So over all, it seems to be a nice Bluetooth receiver but didn't meet my needs and I don't recommend it for use with the Amazon Echo Dot and I would assume the original Echo too.

title: Great Bluetooth Keyboard
text:
Shipping was extremely fast. As soon as the payment went through, it arrived the very next day. The product box was a little dent in places, but my concern was the actual keyboard. It was wonderfully pristine and extremely easy to set up. I wanted this so I didn't have to lug around my laptop to my college classes, especially considering most of them don't approve of laptop use in class anyways, but I wanted to be able to type out anything really quickly without running around campus looking for an available computer.

The bluetooth connectivity is super easy to connect and the sticker it comes with gives you a link to an online manual that's easy to understand. I find it great that it has different channels for 3 devices, that way you don't have to worry about confusing the keyboard on where to connect and having to fiddle with bluetooth on every device you own.

The keyboard itself is fantastic. It responds well and is the size of a standard laptop keyboard. I've always had problems with other bluetooth keyboards being too small and having the keys extremely close together. This keyboard might be bigger than other portable keyboards to keep that natural feel, but it doesn't compromise the size by adding in weight. It weighs only a couple pounds, making it feel more like a standard hardcover book than a fully functional keyboard.

Another reason I specifically chose this keyboard was the groove for your devices. Every other keyboard doesn't have this feature, making you have to buy a stand or bulky case with a stand. Thankfully, this one has a groove wide and deep enough to fit most devices. It's even slanted to keep it from falling. It can easily hold my iPad 3 with a plastic shell case and even my Droid Turbo with it's super bulky case.

The only two things I would recommend is that you have or buy a case to hold both the keyboard and your tablet, especially if you're going to school or taking it with you everywhere on a daily basis. Though that could just be me because I like to have that extra security. The second is carry along extra batteries. It's unfortunate that it isn't rechargeable, but I feel like that would add on extra unneeded pounds. It comes with batteries so it can be used right out of the box, but it's easy to forget when they need to be replaced because the switch and battery indicator are on the bottom. So if you don't make it a habit to switch it off when you're done, those batteries will drain before you know it.

Overall, great keyboard for students and writers, just have a case and extra batteries before you leave.

title: this is a great bluetooth receiver
text:
do not buy this unless you want to lose your mind.

Don't get me wrong, this is a great bluetooth receiver. Good range, clear sound, stays connected, and pairing is easy. But that is the problem. The pairing is too easy. Once you connect a device, it will continue to automatically connect every time it becomes within range until the end of all eternity. There is no option to disable this auto-pairing, and I have had to resort to constantly unplugging it in order to make it stop. Now, this may be great for some situations, like putting this in a garage or shed, or someplace where you know you will be listening to music EVERY time you are there. For my living room, however, it's insanity. I pair my iPhone and MacBook Pro with this. I can't even have bluetooth turned on without it automatically connecting. Even after I click "disconnect," it re-connects with my device a few seconds later. Super annoying. Also, I leave my speakers plugged into this 24/7, so everything is ready to go whenever I want to use it. However, I can't even pull into my garage with out it causing my iPhone to disconnect from my car's bluetooth, and connect to this and blare whatever music I was listening to all throughout the house. (the wife loves that when I come home at 3am).

I still gave this receiver 3 stars because, like I said, it is great at doing exactly what it is advertised to do. However, I would recommend a bluetooth receiver that does not have auto-pairing, so you can be more selectable with your audio and not have your speakers constantly hijacking your audio.

text: I switched from logitech's mx performance mouse to this and do not regret it. The trackball is better on your wrist than a conventional mouse, especially if your a heavy user. The only issue is that overtime the ball gets stuck because of the gunk that accumulates between the ball and the contact surfaces. This is fixed by popping the ball out and clearing the gunk. Pop it in and its good as new! After long term use, the clicking mechanism will start to double click instead of single clicking (most likely happens to the left click button). This causes minor annoyances in operating the computer. If it starts to do this and its not under warranty anymore you can 1. buy the same mouse again, or 2. get the replacement part and solder it in. Quick and easy to do. I would purchase the exact one micro switch(OMRON D2FC-F-7N China). I bought the Japanese made one thinking it would be better but it made the click a bit different. You have to keep the bottom screw holding the housing chassis together (Topmost screw) loose. Otherwise the click is dampened.

title: Awesome Camera - Drop/ Ne$T cam who??
text: Awesome camera. Our Foscam finally died and it was time for a new solution to our home monitoring needs. I did a lot of research before purchasing and unfortunately most of the negative video reviews (CNET, youtube, etc) are from late last year. There have since been several firmware updates, which the camera downloaded upon startup, released that have made this camera a top performer. . The camera was incredibly easy to setup. On as scale of difficulty the Foscam was a 10 and this was a 1. Download the app, turn on camera, tell it your wifi specifics and your done. We purchased two cameras initially and adding the second was as easy as the first.  The app is clean and refined and video history (100% free storage) is well categorized. Each time the camera detects movement the tag label turns to blue. This way it is easy to identify when there was movement and no need to scan through 24 hrs of video. But if you want to watch the whole day, then select  "Day Brief" and watch 24 hrs of video go by in about a minute. The internal batteries of the camera went past 6 hours when off the charging circle but I had no need to go any longer. The only thing I would add is date/time tagging to video files. After downloading video history clips to your phone from the app (which is easy) there is no longer a way to tell what time and what day the video was recorded. This camera can also serve as a baby monitor if you want. The app will stay on the whole time if you desire and the audio/video is clear and crisp. Why pay more for a camera and then pay for cloud storage too? Buy this camera and you won't be disappointed.

text: I received this keyboard folio the first week in March 2016, and initially it worked very well. Nobody makes computers or phones with Bluetooth 2.0 anymore, we're well into 4.0 territory even in older crappier phones. This means you have to rely on the tiny included dongle in order to use it on your computer, and you can absolutely forget using it with your phone. Also, a heads up - keep track of the dongle, as replacements are expensive and difficult to find.

title: Why all the five star reviews? This thing is complete junk
text:
First off, let me say, I NEVER write reviews. But I had to when I received this and it was a complete joke. I seriously don't understand how there are so many 5 star reviews on a system that costs well over $350, when it sounds like a $20 pair of Dell speakers.
I've been loyal to Logitech. I had an old set of speakers and sub I have had hooked up to my computer that only produces 150 watts, but it's super loud. So I expected this system to be even louder....wrong. It maybe put out half the sound my old ones did.
This system is maybe worth $100 because you literally have to turn it all the way up to even get any sound out of it. First off, the description is COMPLETELY misleading. It says the peak power is 1,000 watts, but on the box that it comes it, it clearly states the peak power is 500 watts..not 1,000....and no, not RMS, peak power. Nowadays, 500 watts isn't crap. And it showed. When I say I had to turn the knob all the way up to even get decent sound...I had to turn the knob all the way up to get decent sound. On my old system, I could maybe turn it up a quarter of the way and it was way too much for me to handle.
I read half the reviews and people say you have to go out and buy better speaker wire to make it sound good, and components to give it "full potential". So someone who spends $370 on a speaker system has to go out and buy better wire and components? Where is the logic in that? If it's a surround sound system, it should come with at least a 14 gauge wire, especially at that price. This system comes with a $1 set of 18 gauge wire. I didn't even know they made wire that crappy.
Logitech tried to cut corners by including cheap speaker wire and not giving people the ability to adjust the speaker or subwoofer settings at all. Sure, you can adjust what speakers the sound comes out of, but not levels, or how deep the sub bangs. So you get mediocre, low sound. I put a rap song on when I got these things and the sub did not bump...at all. I maybe got a muffle out of it. My old system shook the whole house when it was turned on. Again, why would someone spend that much money on this system?
Also, the packaging was piss poor. Half the speakers were scratched up when I got it and it was missing a set of speaker wires. The remote looks like something that came out of the 1980s. Cheaply made and looked faded. Something that probably wouldn't last.
I had way higher expectations for a system of this price. Way higher. But man I was disappointed.
I'm literally shocked by all the 5 star reviews. This system is not worth $100. I'm sticking with my old Logitech speakers that produced better sound and I didn't have to go out and buy upgrades to make it sound good.

title: Great Case, Great Keyboard, but Not Great in Portrait
text:
Currently writing this review on the Type+ Keyboard right now. Just got this a couple of days ago, and thus far, it feels very good. The material feels like it is good quality, and the keyboard feels good to type on. The keyboard is a bit on the small side for me, but I am used to typing on a full sized keyboard on my laptop. They keys are spaced pretty well, and the feel very solid and are very responsive. I find that when I'm using the keyboard it really does make my iPad seem more like a laptop, which I enjoy.

Many people complain about the angle of the screen. Personally, I don't find it an issue. I suppose if you are very tall or if you are setting it down on a surface very low to the ground, the angle could be an issue. Right now I'm sitting in my desk chair with my iPad on my lap and it's not an issue for me at all. I just moved it up to my desk and the angle is even better. I suppose that it is possible for the angle to be inconvenient, but I guess I'm not that picky!

Others have said that their space bars don't worry. I guess I am luck to not have that issue!

Now, the reason that I gave this four stars instead of five is that while I do enjoy the ability to view and type in landscape view, I do enjoy to read the news and things in the portrait view. The case is just thick enough that if you fold it and hold it in your hands, it is a but cumbersome and takes way from the nice feel of the thin, light iPad in your hand. This takes a little while to get used to, but my initial reaction was a bit of disappointment. Personally, I think that it is worth the trade off - the case feels very protective, the keyboard is good, and it's only slightly cumbersome to view in portrait. If being able to view in both portrait and landscape is incredibly important to you, I recommend you get one of those keyboard-stand-thingys if you need to be able to type on a keyboard.

Just a quick note, I purchased the "Deep Blue" cover (I would have gotten black but at the time it was ~$20 cheaper), and found that the blue was a bit lighter than what is pictured, as normally happens with Amazon photos. It is not an offensive color so I have no complaints there.

Since I have not had the case for that long, I have not experience the little plastic holders break off on me. Hopefully this won't happen! I will report back if it does. The little holders seem to keep the iPad in place, and they actually feel pretty sturdy to me.

Anyway, I think this case is great. Would definitely recommend to a friend if they just got an iPad Air 2. For what it's worth, my whole family has case-envy!

title: Good for Simple A/V systems
text:
I am generally happy with this remote. The hub approach works well for my mix of IR and WiFi Network controlled devices. The IR signal from the hub is quite strong, and I have placed it on a table top on the far side of the room. I've had no need for additional plug-in IR blasters.

Many users have reported that this remote frequently goes out of sync with devices and inputs. This does happen occasionally and may be related to pressing power or selection keys in improper sequence. Sometimes it seems to happen at random. However, the solution in my case was to program unused keys to provide specific device power toggle and source selection options. Thus I can easily straighten out sync if it goes out of whack.

I prefer the Companion physical remote to the smart phone app. It provides basic functions with logically arranged physical buttons. Lack of a backlight is not an issue for me. The smart phone app is usable, but requires screen after screen of buttons and is not particularly logical in arrangement. It takes a lot of swiping and clicking to do even basic functions.

My system is fairly simple, with only 4 devices to be controlled. I can see that even a few sync problems could become a time consuming struggle for more complex systems. So I believe that this remote is suitable for use mainly with a small number of devices and where a physical remote is preferred. It is a good solution within these limitations.

And by "directly connected" they mean "by wire." Why you would want to do that I don't know. Your computer, if it's a laptop, already has a keyboard. Why doesn't Logitech simply design and build a device that would be what I think many of us are looking for: something like the Harmony remote, but as a keyboard? Anyway, it seems well built. But if you're looking for direct, as in wireless, connection to your TV and using this keyboard to do things like search Netflix or Youtube, this device probably won't work.

title: Pretty much just a keyboard to sign in so I ...
text:
Was looking for something to control my gaming pc when I hook it up to the big tv. Pretty much just a keyboard to sign in so I don't have to move my wired keyboard and mouse. Does that and more. Also finding use as a remote for video programs that don't support media controls, like browser video and radio or Amazon Prime video.
Pros:
Trackpad's nice and responsive. I don't like acceleration on mice, but it seems natural on the K400.
Like the click button in the top corner. Let's you hold it like a big controller, using your thumb on the trackpad and click button, and still be able to drag and drop if you need to (quick fixes like game patches and mods)
Great range. (with exceptions, see below) Was able to use from doorway to another room, probably 50-60 feet with no drops.
Cons:
Feels KINDA cheap for a Logitech product. Haven't bought anything recently, but I've got a cordless mouse man optical that I've had for 10+ years. Don't see this lasting as long.
Originally hooked up the receiver in the back of my computer for controlling a few feet away. Lost signal intermittently. Moved it to the front USB port with slightly better line of sight and it works from there. Of note, I also loose bluetooth connection in that room, so it could some kind of interference. The other rooms I've had it had no issues. (See above comments on range)

text:
Great product! It replaced a stack of remotes which is exactly why I bought it. The reasons it didn't get 5 stars:
1) It took a couple of days to get it working correctly. I had to do some trouble shooting. Kudos to the troubleshooting section of the website. They had the problem description and resolution listed and was easy to follow. The less techy person will have a hard time getting this thing working if they experience problems.
2) the button layout isn't the best. The main area your thumb would naturally contact is taken up by a touch screen. This isn't a huge problem, but I'd rather have the normal buttons I use right under my thumb.
3) The battery life is suspect. It has a marked accelerated battery use when fast forwarding and reversing video. Not that big of a deal either. I just put it back in the cradle when I go to bed each night and there's plenty of battery available for a full day's use the next morning. This might be an issue as it gets older.
All in all, I love the product and look forward to a long relationship with Harmony remotes.

title: So frustrating, sick of being tv tech support
text: I've had this for 7 months now, and I'm officially giving up on it. The concept is great, execution is ok, reliability is terrible. My harmony 900 died after several years, I liked it a lot, it's major issues were slow response from the remote transmitter, and occasional freeze ups of the remote itself, not too bad, and the help function on the touch screen saved me from constantly having to fix things for people who just couldn't handle it, and would some how manage to screw things up in the longish turn on process by not keeping the remote pointed in the right direction. I have a complicated system, with all my equipment mounted in a media closet out of the way tv on the wall with all inwall speakers, my main goal is to hide all wires, keep it clean, and make it as easy as possible to watch tv or Roku without 4 remotes, while using an avr for sound. That said a remote transmitter is absolutely necessary. First issue, the companion remote does not have an ir emitter, this was not mentioned anywhere yay or nay, I just assumed it would be there. So to get around it I had to put the hub on a table near the tv, and extend the remote wired transmitter to get it into my media closet. This worked well except anything put in front of or people walking near the hub made it useless and miss commands.  The companion has no help function to help you sort it out, so if anyone else in my family, or visitors encounter this, they are dead in the water. On my Panasonic tv, they do not have the right input changing codes, know this, will manually fix it in your account for you, but still have not fixed it in the main firmware. So you can't use the setup wizard without manually modifying it every time.... which happens more than i ever thought I would have to do. On my tv, the remote reliably freezes up upon 4 button pushes into its Netflix app. The worst part is it just randomly stops working momentarily.. all the time. Tried everything to resolve... placement, wifi mods and updates,  to no avail. It was a pain to setup correctly just to have to constantly fiddle with it, and to have to be tech support for people who experience the many hiccups. Just got a new avr that does a great job with hdmi arc and controls, it's not perfect, still need the Roku remote, and DVD remote, but it's reliable, and that makes it light years better than the hub and companion remote.

title: Great, unless it has low battery
text:
When it has enough power in the battery, it's a great unit. When using via USB, video and sound is clear, it's easy to set up and our users love it.

Unless the battery is low.

Then it wont work until it gets a nominal amount of charge. So we have users late for conferences as the unit was not turned off (or automatically powered down quick enough - no idea why it doesn't do that sooner) and it has low battery.

Instead of working and slowly charging, it turns on, alerts about low battery, then powers off, all while connected via USB. It's come to a point when I need to keep a fully charged unit as a spare, ready to swap out.

This webcam should be ready to use, regardless of battery level. I thought maybe it was a fault, but we have 5 of them now, and all have the same behaviour

**edit
Seems USB2 does not provide enough power for the device, so it will be constantly discharging under use. It may be ok with USB3 or if you have a charging USB socket on your computer that provides 1A or more.

text:
There's actually a decent amount of space for your hands on this keyboard, and the buttons actually feel pretty nice. All in all it's a pretty neat package on the surface. However it suffers from a few fairly glaring issues.

1) Can't type too fast or it won't recognize key presses. This is a problem with the quality of the circuitry to my knowledge. Unfortunately this means I have to dramatically slow down my typing, but I can still pull around 50 on it without it bogging down.

2) Has a habit of not staying connected, or failing to connect if the tablet has been on too long. This is a pretty common bluetooth problem and you simply have to reboot to fix this.

3) Durability is iffy. The tablet seems more durable than the keyboard case. I unfortunately believe i may have ruined the keyboard by typing on it with slightly wet hands that I had dried off briefly on my pants. This is my own fault, but it's a pretty small mistake I feel and regardless it's a pretty glaring weakness.

Besides that I really enjoyed it while it worked. and may actually get a new one to keep my tablet being usable. But I'm very disappointed that such an easy mistake ruined the keyboard.

title: Simply Awesome, even Better than Triple.Fi10
text:
Long time user of Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10s needing a replacement set of earphones after seven great years and dismayed to find out they are no longer manufactured. I bought these Ultimate Ears UE900s which seem to be the closest replacement. They are Simply Awesome and even a bit better than the TF10s.

Pros: Everything is clear, crisp, full and gorgeous whether I listen to rock, hard rock, alternative, blues or jazz. Just like the TF10s, the sound is outstanding across the entire musical range. But these UE900s pull out some small details that my old TF10s (or even my prior Shures) never could. Best of all, no distortion at all and notes never get clipped or cut. Fit is much better than the old TF10s thanks to the swivel cable and also the size of the earphones.

Cons: The low end of the bass was a shade stronger on the TF10s than on these UE900s: a bit more boom. But the tradeoff of much better fit with the UE900s plus a bit better overall sound is well worth it.

Other Comments: UE includes a pretty thorough fit kit of tips, an extra cable, a hard case, a soft case and also a gel for the swivel joint if ever needed to keep electrical contact clean. I love these earphones. Very happy with the purchase for as much as I enjoy listening to music.

title: Hardware seems good, but account creation/software experience is horrible
text:
Hardware 9/10
Software 1/10

Installed the app on my phone, and during setup opted to use Facebook login for account creation. Got things setup, devices working, etc. I decided to look into getting things setup with IFTTT. When attempting to link the Harmony hub to my IFTTT account via the Facebook link, nothing happened. I went to myharmony.com to login there. This is then things started to go really bad. 'Sign In' there redirects you to download a desktop software, which I did, however this results in a hung install process that never actually finishes. Kill task, go to Add/Remove programs and see that it is installed but "unavailable". Click uninstall, and it disappears from list, but now I can't actually launch the installer again. Double click = nothing happens. Reboot machine. Same experience. Try another machine, same thing. So while I can control things with an app on my phone, I have no way to actually edit my "Harmony" account so that I can enable other items like IFTTT. This software experience overall is absolutely terrible. No way to access my account from within the app on the phone, no way (apparently) to login via their web site, and since I can't get their desktop software installed on any of my PCs, I'm blocked. I bought two of these for home automation purposes, but I haven't unboxed the second one, and at this point I'm seriously considering returning them both. I know that the account problem sounds like a trivial thing to have an issue with, but without being able to look into my actual Harmony account details, I have no way of fixing the Facebook/IFTTT login problems. Frustrating.

title: Definitely Recommend this case!
text:
LOVE IT! I tried a few ipad keyboard cases and have done my research, I'm also a college student so I wasn't looking to spend $$$ on a keyboard, I was looking for something that was a decent price and good quality.
After looking at a ton of keyboards on Amazon, I decided to try this one out because I felt like it had a good stand, case, and wouldn't scratch my ipad.
The outside of the case is very clean and relatively dirt proof, I take it to and from school and use it all the time and so far it hasn't gotten dirty and the material is a little rougher and not like felt so it keeps dirt off the case.
The part to hold the ipad into the case is covered in a rubber material so it won't scratch the ipad and holds it in well. Taking the Ipad in and out of the case is also really easy too so you don't have to worry about damaging the case or Ipad.
Now the keyboard is great, I'm 5'4 woman with small hands so I don't have any problems with the size of the keyboard. My boyfriend is a 200lb 6'2 guy and he uses the keyboard too and i've never heard him complain about the size of the keyboard either so I think it's almost a standard sized keyboard. Now the buttons are awesome, the top row of keys are like a regular macbook keyboard and I love it! There's a home, lock, vol. up/down, individual screens, play/pause, etc buttons.
It's also a magnetic on and shut off ipad so when you close the case (the keyboard doesn't lie flush on the screen of the ipad when you the case is closed so it will prevent from scratching, it turns off the ipad and vice versa. When you open the case and stand it up, a magnetic strip on the case allows ipad to stand up. It's a pretty strong magnetic so you can push on it like a regular touch screen and even pick up the ipad and the keyboard will still be stuck too it. It's a strong enough magnet to handle all the pushing but light enough where you won't struggle to take it off. If you leave the bluetooth on your ipad, it connects automatically and very quickly which is a plus because the other cases that i've tried out have really lagged on connection. It also has great battery life, I bought it about 2 months ago, and use it EVERY day and I have yet to charge it.

Overall this keyboard is definitely recommended! Comes at a great prices and very good quality, even bought one for my dad.

title: Great keyboard and mouse - with a couple minor mouse issues.
text:
I bought this about a year ago from another manufacturer. I can only assume there were some bad batches or versions based on the negative reviews. I've loved this keyboard. I'm a fan of the chicklet keys - though it did take a little getting used to at first. Granted, battery life isn't a major issues with keyboards, but it's nice to never have to worry about it. I use this in an office with fluorescent lights and I'm always at top solar activity and 100% charge. I can even slide my keyboard under my desk - hiding the solar panels and it still works. Light input drops to 15% and presumably the batteries would die soon, but overall, in daily use for about a year, it's always been a great keyboard.
I deduct one star for the mouse. I've always loved Logitech mice and especially the form factor of this and the pro model I had before. The infinity scroll is a nice feature - especially with Windows' occasional scrolling glitches. The additional buttons are also added value - except for the back button. It's easy to hit it sometimes when reaching for the mouse, causing your webpage to go back. This is very annoying on a page that doesn't resubmit properly if you're looking at search results. The biggest problem I've had with the mouse is the batteries. They lasted a long time initially, but now I only get about a month or so out of them before recharging. That said, it's easy enough to recharge with a USB cable and the mouse is usable while connected for charging. Plus, replacing the batteries would probably solve that problem for another year or so. Based on my experience, I highly recommend.

title: Here's the thing - this is a great microphone for what it is and how much it ...
text:
Here's the thing - this is a great microphone for what it is and how much it costs. I was able to pick one up on a lightning deal for $89 and it's well worth that price, however, I've had a few problems with it from day one that have since been rectified. Let's start with the bad.

Number one, I had to ship the first one back because one of the screws that holds the microphone into place was stripped out. This is not anyone's fault however it shows a possible cheapness in the product quality. Metal screws would not have stripped as easily as these screws. Otherwise the product is definitely sturdy and feels like it's a quality product. It has a nice weight to it and a really nice look to it. I do wish that the microphone had a mute button without a light on it. It actually is a bit confusing as to whether or not the mic is muted because you a red light would make you think it's muted -- not with this mic. It is not muted unless the light is blinking. Also, I really don't want another LED shining at my face while I work.

Number two, the microphone itself sometimes has a hard time connecting with my iMac. Every once in a while the microphone will show up in my sound settings but it will not have any audio coming into the computer. I searched some internet forums and this is not uncommon. One workaround I have found is to open up my sound settings and leave them open - this seems to keep the mic working.

Finally we can talk about the good and what should matter most when you are purchasing an expensive USB microphone and that is the sound quality -- it's excellent. If you are streaming a podcast or recording scratch audio for video production like I use it for, this microphone is really great. It has a great clarity that you would expect from a much more expensive microphone. I actually attended an SNL video editing workshop and the editor from Saturday Night Live said that there's been many occasions where the voiceover used in the spots they air on television were recorded at the editing station using this microphone.

title: Here's the thing - this is a great microphone for what it is and how much it ...
text:
Here's the thing - this is a great microphone for what it is and how much it costs. I was able to pick one up on a lightning deal for $89 and it's well worth that price, however, I've had a few problems with it from day one that have since been rectified. Let's start with the bad.

Number one, I had to ship the first one back because one of the screws that holds the microphone into place was stripped out. This is not anyone's fault however it shows a possible cheapness in the product quality. Metal screws would not have stripped as easily as these screws. Otherwise the product is definitely sturdy and feels like it's a quality product. It has a nice weight to it and a really nice look to it. I do wish that the microphone had a mute button without a light on it. It actually is a bit confusing as to whether or not the mic is muted because you a red light would make you think it's muted -- not with this mic. It is not muted unless the light is blinking. Also, I really don't want another LED shining at my face while I work.

Number two, the microphone itself sometimes has a hard time connecting with my iMac. Every once in a while the microphone will show up in my sound settings but it will not have any audio coming into the computer. I searched some internet forums and this is not uncommon. One workaround I have found is to open up my sound settings and leave them open - this seems to keep the mic working.

Finally we can talk about the good and what should matter most when you are purchasing an expensive USB microphone and that is the sound quality -- it's excellent. If you are streaming a podcast or recording scratch audio for video production like I use it for, this microphone is really great. It has a great clarity that you would expect from a much more expensive microphone. I actually attended an SNL video editing workshop and the editor from Saturday Night Live said that there's been many occasions where the voiceover used in the spots they air on television were recorded at the editing station using this microphone.

I definitely recommend getting this if you can afford it and you're looking for ways to improve your sound quality in a convenient package.

Another tip, I use this mic while on FaceTime and phone calls from my computer and it sounds really nice and much better than the built in computer mic.

text:
The sound quality of these speakers is great. And I like that they tie into the volume on my iphone, rather than having their own independent volume as many bluetooth speakers do. But, they have one really annoying feature, and that is that they override whichever other output device I'm using even when I don't want them to. For example, I'll be watching a video through Apple TV, and suddenly it cuts out and switches to these speakers, simply because they are on in the other room. Or I'll be listening to music through my bluetooth headphones, and as I get close to my office (where I have these speakers), the music suddenly cuts out - because it's switched to the speakers. This is stupid, they should not decide for me that I want to listen to them, I should be the one choosing which output device I want to use.

Unfortunately this has gotten to be so annoying that I'm considering returning them. For the price they cost, to have this extremely obnoxious feature really detracts from the value in my opinion. If they didn't do this, I would give them five stars. But this feature has annoyed me to the point that I can only give them two stars. title: Great for marketing production needs
text:
As you might expect based on the rating, I'm a fan of the product. I work in marketing and we use Mevo to produce both scripted demos as well as livestream events. We've broadly been happy with the results, much, much better than filming with iPhone and trying to do a few takes, stitch them together, etc.

A couple things worth noting:

The hardware build quality is very good and has the right amount of heft and durability.
The software has some initial bugs (soon after launch) but they've done a good job at squashing those and steadily improving as people figure out new ways to use the camera.

The hardware/software isn't going to solve your environmental issues (e.g. low light or slow internet connectivity) so be sure to do a couple test runs if you can. I'd also recommend that you use a dedicated device or put into "do not disturb mode" so that app notifications, texts, phone calls, etc don't disrupt you during a shoot.

Battery life was fine for our needs (shorter 5 min videos) but if you are filming longer periods or offsite, the battery pack might be a smart addition.

Good luck!

title: Will not give you control of individual AV devices - you'll need to use the app for that
text:
I really liked the basic Logitech Harmony my parents own. It was simple, intuitive and inexpensive. I opeted for the Harmony Home Control because it was the cheapest one that would work with my devices and control the PS4 as a media playback device (Netflix, Amazon, etc.)

The setup is simple. The remote is lightweight and feels great. I had no problems with it, and I love that I didn't have to point it at anything. However, it will not control my TV. I can't hit a 'TV' button and get into my TV menus. I have to chang the picture setting on my TV frequently to account for a bright room during the day and dark at night; but with the Harmony Home Control I couldn't do that with the remote. Instead, I had to use the app on my phone. The app is fine, but why did I buy a universal remote if I need my phone on me?

I can't comment on the home control features as I was using it for a more traditional AV purpose. I love Logitech's 'Activities' capability, but couldn't get over the fact that I could not access the menus of my devices with it. In the end, I returned it and will just use the basic $40 Logitech. At least with that I can take control of individual devices. There is usually a PS4 controller on the coffee table anyway, so it will get me from 4 to 2 remotes on the table.

title: Could have been a contender, instead it has left me frustrated.
text:
Pros:
1-Very intuitive design
2-Looks great in the living room
3- The keys are great to type on
4- Connectivity is great at a decent distance from the reciever

Cons
1- My daughter broke the power switch very quickly
2- Battery consumption gets expensive
3- The touchpad does not respond well unless the keyboard is perfectly flat with a hard surface behind it.
4- The logitec software EATS system resources, enough to be very noticeable.
5- Had the keyboard just over a year and the thing is failing.

So I bought this at Best Buy because it was the same price at the time. No big deal, thought I was buying something great. I was very wrong. The keyboard does have very good keys and is easy to type on. That's about where I stop with the good. I would say this keyboard's biggest issue is its size. If the keyboard is twisted in any way then the trackpad does not function correctly. The moment the batteries start to fail the touchpad fails in interesting ways. Yes, the touchpad could have been great but the windows 8 experiment failed and the functionality built into this keyboard became obsolete. The software was a great idea that failed miserably. The software to control the touchpad had every option i could think of and allowed me to customise my interface just the way I wanted. But the software also would randomly start taking 80% of my RAM to function, then not release the resources once it had finished messing up the computer. When I looked into those problems, turns out I was not the only one and logitec handled it in typical, large corporation fashion. They ignored the complaints and refused to acknowledge there was a problem. I am a very patient person and I have tried to make the keyboard work for us. I am going to be getting rid of mine now.

Overall, the keyboard could have been a great one. It had a lot going for it but logitec failed to make all those great ideas actually work.

title: AWESOME.
text: This is the first review I've written on Amazon, and I've been a customer for 3 years. I am a pretty indecisive person, and it took me a bit of research and back-and-forth between this and other keyboards (including the Apple Smart Keyboard) before taking the plunge. But, I'm glad I went with this one. Like many other reviewers have noted, this really feels like a protective case/keyboard for your iPad Pro 9.7. Yes, it does add "bulk," but to me it's really minimal, relative to the enhanced sense of security I feel packing this is in my purse, as well as the ease of use and functionality. I'm someone who needs to use e-mail and write reports/word documents frequently, and am a former graduate student who is no stranger to sitting in front of a laptop for hours on end. Now starting my career, I wanted to simplify things by not carrying around a heavy laptop, but also to have everything I need in a compact, accessible device. This has elevated my iPad to that perfect device. Just clicking it into place and not having to worry about Bluetooth connection or anything is satisfying. It basically feels like a sturdy, mini (but not uncomfortably so!) laptop, and I've been able to use this on my lap with just as much ease as on a table. Yes, it wobbles slightly if your legs are moving, but if you're paying attention and being mindful of how you handle your iPad when in this case, it's really not a problem. Sturdy, functional, and still sleek. Definitely worth the purchase!

title: Good no-frills speaker
text:
I was looking for a cheap speaker because I was annoyed with the tinny sound from my cellphone's and laptop's external speakers. Nothing fancy, nothing with Bluetooth technology, nothing ridiculously overpriced, I just wanted a speaker that would get the job done. I've had this Z50 speaker for a couple weeks now, and I'm pretty happy with it. The sound is good for the price, and I like that it plugs directly into an outlet for power and directly into an audio port for sound.
There are a couple things, though, that keep me from giving it a full 5 stars:
- a noticeable "hum" when it's plugged in. It's pretty quiet and not very annoying, but it's still there.
- The cords are shorter than I'd like. The audio cord is only about 32" and the power cord is about 6'.
- The lack of volume controls on the speaker is mildly inconveniencing.
Still, I'm happy with this speaker. I'd give it a 4.4 out of 5.

While it is relatively quiet, if you're looking for a click-free keyboard, this isn't it. However, action on all keys is springy and firm, so keys never feel "sticky".

One sorely needed feature is steady lit LED's. There are no context clues on the keyboard to let you know that caps lock is activated, if the Function variant of keys are active, or which device is selected after long sessions away from the keyboard.

Key placement is also puzzling - it's clearly a PC-oriented keyboard, so use with OS X has the standard PC keyboard layout issues. Pairing with a portable device (tablet/phone) means that you'll be hunting around the keyboard for the correct key for, say, the "Home" button. It seems that the keyboard would have been better served by opting for a dedicated row of keys like volume, track search, home, etc.

My experience with modern devices was that pairing was relatively simple.

Overall this keyboard offers a no-frills approach. It works, but would work much better with persistent LED's and dedicated function keys.
